chapters.en: But Pharaoh hardened his heart this time as well, and he would not let the people go.
chapters.zh: 这一次法老又硬着心，不容百姓去。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and tell him that this is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
chapters.zh: 耶和华吩咐摩西说：「你进去见法老，对他说：『耶和华－希伯来人的上帝这样说：容我的百姓去，好事奉我。

chapters.en: But if you continue to restrain them and refuse to let them go,
chapters.zh: 你若不肯容他们去，仍旧强留他们，

chapters.en: then the hand of the LORD will bring a severe plague on your livestock in the field—on your horses, donkeys, camels, herds, and flocks.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的手加在你田间的牲畜上，就是在马、驴、骆驼、牛群、羊群上，必有重重的瘟疫。

chapters.en: But the LORD will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, so that no animal belonging to the Israelites will die.’”
chapters.zh: 耶和华要分别以色列的牲畜和埃及的牲畜，凡属以色列人的，一样都不死。』」

chapters.en: The LORD set a time, saying, “Tomorrow the LORD will do this in the land.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华就定了时候，说：「明天耶和华必在此地行这事。」

chapters.en: And the next day the LORD did just that. All the livestock of the Egyptians died, but not one animal belonging to the Israelites died.
chapters.zh: 第二天，耶和华就行这事。埃及的牲畜〔几乎〕都死了，只是以色列人的牲畜，一个都没有死。

chapters.en: Pharaoh sent officials and found that none of the livestock of the Israelites had died. But Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not let the people go.
chapters.zh: 法老打发人去〔看〕，谁知以色列人的牲畜连一个都没有死。法老的心却是固执，不容百姓去。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Take handfuls of soot from the furnace; in the sight of Pharaoh, Moses is to toss it into the air.
chapters.zh: 耶和华吩咐摩西、亚伦说：「你们取几捧炉灰，摩西要在法老面前向天扬起来。

chapters.en: It will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and festering boils will break out on man and beast throughout the land.”
chapters.zh: 这灰要在埃及全地变作尘土，在人身上和牲畜身上成了起泡的疮。」

chapters.en: So they took soot from the furnace and stood before Pharaoh. Moses tossed it into the air, and festering boils broke out on man and beast.
chapters.zh: 摩西、亚伦取了炉灰，站在法老面前。摩西向天扬起来，就在人身上和牲畜身上成了起泡的疮。

chapters.en: The magicians could not stand before Moses, because the boils had broken out on them and on all the Egyptians.
chapters.zh: 行法术的在摩西面前站立不住，因为在他们身上和一切埃及人身上都有这疮。

chapters.en: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said to Moses.
chapters.zh: 耶和华使法老的心刚硬，不听他们，正如耶和华对摩西所说的。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Get up early in the morning, stand before Pharaoh, and tell him that this is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你清早起来，站在法老面前，对他说：『耶和华－希伯来人的上帝这样说：容我的百姓去，好事奉我。

chapters.en: Otherwise, I will send all My plagues against you and your officials and your people, so you may know that there is no one like Me in all the earth.
chapters.zh: 因为这一次我要叫一切的灾殃临到你和你臣仆并你百姓的身上，叫你知道在普天下没有像我的。

chapters.en: For by this time I could have stretched out My hand and struck you and your people with a plague to wipe you off the earth.
chapters.zh: 我若伸手用瘟疫攻击你和你的百姓，你早就从地上除灭了。

chapters.en: But I have raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display My power to you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.
chapters.zh: 其实，我叫你存立，是特要向你显我的大能，并要使我的名传遍天下。

chapters.en: Still, you lord it over My people and do not allow them to go.
chapters.zh: 你还向我的百姓自高，不容他们去吗？

chapters.en: Behold, at this time tomorrow I will rain down the worst hail that has ever fallen on Egypt, from the day it was founded until now.
chapters.zh: 到明天约在这时候，我必叫重大的冰雹降下，自从埃及开国以来，没有这样的冰雹。

chapters.en: So give orders now to shelter your livestock and everything you have in the field. Every man or beast that remains in the field and is not brought inside will die when the hail comes down upon them.’”
chapters.zh: 现在你要打发人把你的牲畜和你田间一切所有的催进来；凡在田间不收回家的，无论是人是牲畜，冰雹必降在他们身上，他们就必死。』」

chapters.en: Those among Pharaoh’s officials who feared the word of the LORD hurried to bring their servants and livestock to shelter,
chapters.zh: 法老的臣仆中，惧怕耶和华这话的，便叫他的奴仆和牲畜跑进家来。

chapters.en: but those who disregarded the word of the LORD left their servants and livestock in the field.
chapters.zh: 但那不把耶和华这话放在心上的，就将他的奴仆和牲畜留在田里。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, so that hail may fall on all the land of Egypt—on man and beast and every plant of the field throughout the land of Egypt.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你向天伸杖，使埃及遍地的人身上和牲畜身上，并田间各样菜蔬上，都有冰雹。」

chapters.en: So Moses stretched out his staff toward heaven, and the LORD sent thunder and hail, and lightning struck the earth. So the LORD rained down hail upon the land of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 摩西向天伸杖，耶和华就打雷下雹，有火闪到地上；耶和华下雹在埃及地上。

chapters.en: The hail fell and the lightning continued flashing through it. The hail was so severe that nothing like it had ever been seen in all the land of Egypt from the time it became a nation.
chapters.zh: 那时，雹与火搀杂，甚是厉害，自从埃及成国以来，遍地没有这样的。

chapters.en: Throughout the land of Egypt, the hail struck down everything in the field, both man and beast; it beat down every plant of the field and stripped every tree.
chapters.zh: 在埃及遍地，雹击打了田间所有的人和牲畜，并一切的菜蔬，又打坏田间一切的树木。

chapters.en: The only place where it did not hail was in the land of Goshen, where the Israelites lived.
chapters.zh: 惟独以色列人所住的歌珊地没有冰雹。

chapters.en: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron. “This time I have sinned,” he said. “The LORD is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.
chapters.zh: 法老打发人召摩西、亚伦来，对他们说：「这一次我犯了罪了。耶和华是公义的；我和我的百姓是邪恶的。

chapters.en: Pray to the LORD, for there has been enough of God’s thunder and hail. I will let you go; you do not need to stay any longer.”
chapters.zh: 这雷轰和冰雹已经够了。请你们求耶和华，我就容你们去，不再留住你们。」

chapters.en: Moses said to him, “When I have left the city, I will spread out my hands to the LORD. The thunder will cease, and there will be no more hail, so that you may know that the earth is the LORD’s.
chapters.zh: 摩西对他说：「我一出城，就要向耶和华举手〔祷告〕；雷必止住，也不再有冰雹，叫你知道全地都是属耶和华的。

chapters.en: But as for you and your officials, I know that you still do not fear the LORD our God.”
chapters.zh: 至于你和你的臣仆，我知道你们还是不惧怕耶和华上帝。」

chapters.en: (Now the flax and barley were destroyed, since the barley was ripe and the flax was in bloom;
chapters.zh: （那时，麻和大麦被〔雹〕击打；因为大麦已经吐穗，麻也开了花。

chapters.en: but the wheat and spelt were not destroyed, because they are late crops.)
chapters.zh: 只是小麦和粗麦没有被击打，因为还没有长成。）

chapters.en: Then Moses departed from Pharaoh, went out of the city, and spread out his hands to the LORD. The thunder and hail ceased, and the rain no longer poured down on the land.
chapters.zh: 摩西离了法老出城，向耶和华举手〔祷告〕；雷和雹就止住，雨也不再浇在地上了。

chapters.en: When Pharaoh saw that the rain and hail and thunder had ceased, he sinned again and hardened his heart—he and his officials.
chapters.zh: 法老见雨和雹与雷止住，就越发犯罪；他和他的臣仆都硬着心。

chapters.en: So Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he would not let the Israelites go, just as the LORD had said through Moses.
chapters.zh: 法老的心刚硬，不容以色列人去，正如耶和华藉着摩西所说的。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials, that I may perform these miraculous signs of Mine among them,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你进去见法老。我使他和他臣仆的心刚硬，为要在他们中间显我这些神迹，

chapters.en: and that you may tell your children and grandchildren how severely I dealt with the Egyptians when I performed miraculous signs among them, so that all of you may know that I am the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 并要叫你将我向埃及人所做的事，和在他们中间所行的神迹，传于你儿子和你孙子的耳中，好叫你们知道我是耶和华。」

chapters.en: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and told him, “This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before Me? Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
chapters.zh: 摩西、亚伦就进去见法老，对他说：「耶和华－希伯来人的上帝这样说：『你在我面前不肯自卑要到几时呢？容我的百姓去，好事奉我。

chapters.en: But if you refuse to let My people go, I will bring locusts into your territory tomorrow.
chapters.zh: 你若不肯容我的百姓去，明天我要使蝗虫进入你的境内，

chapters.en: They will cover the face of the land so that no one can see it. They will devour whatever is left after the hail and eat every tree that grows in your fields.
chapters.zh: 遮满地面，甚至看不见地，并且吃那冰雹所剩的和田间所长的一切树木。

chapters.en:
They will fill your houses and the houses of all your officials and every Egyptian—something neither your fathers nor your grandfathers have seen since the day they came into this land.’”
Then Moses turned and left Pharaoh’s presence.
chapters.zh: 你的宫殿和你众臣仆的房屋，并一切埃及人的房屋，都要被蝗虫佔满了；自从你祖宗和你祖宗的祖宗在世以来，直到今日，没有见过这样的〔灾〕。』」摩西就转身离开法老出去。

chapters.en: Pharaoh’s officials asked him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the people go, so that they may worship the LORD their God. Do you not yet realize that Egypt lies in ruins?”
chapters.zh: 法老的臣仆对法老说：「这人为我们的网罗要到几时呢？容这些人去事奉耶和华－他们的上帝吧！埃及已经败坏了，你还不知道吗？」

chapters.en: So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. “Go, worship the LORD your God,” he said. “But who exactly will be going?”
chapters.zh: 于是摩西、亚伦被召回来见法老；法老对他们说：「你们去事奉耶和华－你们的上帝；但那要去的是谁呢？」

chapters.en: “We will go with our young and old,” Moses replied. “We will go with our sons and daughters, and with our flocks and herds, for we must hold a feast to the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 摩西说：「我们要和我们老的少的、儿子女儿同去，且把羊群牛群一同带去，因为我们务要向耶和华守节。」

chapters.en: Then Pharaoh told them, “May the LORD be with you if I ever let you go with your little ones. Clearly you are bent on evil.
chapters.zh: 法老对他们说：「我容你们和你们〔妇人〕孩子去的时候，耶和华与你们同在吧！你们要谨慎；因为有祸在你们眼前〔注：或译：你们存着恶意〕，

chapters.en: No, only the men may go and worship the LORD, since that is what you have been requesting.” And Moses and Aaron were driven from Pharaoh’s presence.
chapters.zh: 不可都去！你们这壮年人去事奉耶和华吧，因为这是你们所求的。」于是把他们从法老面前撵出去。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt, so that the locusts may swarm over it and devour every plant in the land—everything that the hail has left behind.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你向埃及地伸杖，使蝗虫到埃及地上来，吃地上一切的菜蔬，就是冰雹所剩的。」

chapters.en: So Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and throughout that day and night the LORD sent an east wind across the land. By morning the east wind had brought the locusts.
chapters.zh: 摩西就向埃及地伸杖，那一昼一夜，耶和华使东风刮在埃及地上；到了早晨，东风把蝗虫刮了来。

chapters.en: The locusts swarmed across the land and settled over the entire territory of Egypt. Never before had there been so many locusts, and never again will there be.
chapters.zh: 蝗虫上来，落在埃及的四境，甚是厉害；以前没有这样的，以后也必没有。

chapters.en: They covered the face of all the land until it was black, and they consumed all the plants on the ground and all the fruit on the trees that the hail had left behind. Nothing green was left on any tree or plant in all the land of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 因为这蝗虫遮满地面，甚至地都黑暗了，又吃地上一切的菜蔬和冰雹所剩树上的果子。埃及遍地，无论是树木，是田间的菜蔬，连一点青的也没有留下。

chapters.en: Pharaoh quickly summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.
chapters.zh: 于是法老急忙召了摩西、亚伦来，说：「我得罪耶和华－你们的上帝，又得罪了你们。

chapters.en: Now please forgive my sin once more and appeal to the LORD your God, that He may remove this death from me.”
chapters.zh: 现在求你，只这一次，饶恕我的罪，求耶和华－你们的上帝使我脱离这一次的死亡。」

chapters.en: So Moses left Pharaoh’s presence and appealed to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 摩西就离开法老去求耶和华。

chapters.en: And the LORD changed the wind to a very strong west wind that carried off the locusts and blew them into the Red Sea. Not a single locust remained anywhere in Egypt.
chapters.zh: 耶和华转了极大的西风，把蝗虫刮起，吹入红海；在埃及的四境连一个也没有留下。

chapters.en: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let the Israelites go.
chapters.zh: 但耶和华使法老的心刚硬，不容以色列人去。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, so that darkness may spread over the land of Egypt—a palpable darkness.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你向天伸杖，使埃及地黑暗；这黑暗似乎摸得着。」

chapters.en: So Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and total darkness covered all the land of Egypt for three days.
chapters.zh: 摩西向天伸杖，埃及遍地就乌黑了三天。

chapters.en: No one could see anyone else, and for three days no one left his place. Yet all the Israelites had light in their dwellings.
chapters.zh: 三天之久，人不能相见，谁也不敢起来离开本处；惟有以色列人家中都有亮光。

chapters.en: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and said, “Go, worship the LORD. Even your little ones may go with you; only your flocks and herds must stay behind.”
chapters.zh: 法老就召摩西来，说：「你们去事奉耶和华；只是你们的羊群牛群要留下；你们的〔妇人〕孩子可以和你们同去。」

chapters.en: But Moses replied, “You must also provide us with sacrifices and burnt offerings to present to the LORD our God.
chapters.zh: 摩西说：「你总要把祭物和燔祭牲交给我们，使我们可以祭祀耶和华－我们的上帝。

chapters.en: Even our livestock must go with us; not a hoof will be left behind, for we will need some of them to worship the LORD our God, and we will not know how we are to worship the LORD until we arrive.”
chapters.zh: 我们的牲畜也要带去，连一蹄也不留下；因为我们要从其中取出来，事奉耶和华－我们的上帝。我们未到那里，还不知道用什么事奉耶和华。」

chapters.en: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was unwilling to let them go.
chapters.zh: 但耶和华使法老的心刚硬，不肯容他们去。

chapters.en: “Depart from me!” Pharaoh said to Moses. “Make sure you never see my face again, for on the day you see my face, you will die.”
chapters.zh: 法老对摩西说：「你离开我去吧，你要小心，不要再见我的面！因为你见我面的那日你就必死！」

chapters.en: “As you say,” Moses replied, “I will never see your face again.”
chapters.zh: 摩西说：「你说得好！我必不再见你的面了。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “I will bring upon Pharaoh and Egypt one more plague. After that, he will allow you to leave this place. And when he lets you go, he will drive you out completely.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「我再使一样的灾殃临到法老和埃及，然后他必容你们离开这地。他容你们去的时候，总要催逼你们都从这地出去。

chapters.en: Now announce to the people that men and women alike should ask their neighbors for articles of silver and gold.”
chapters.zh: 你要传于百姓的耳中，叫他们男女各人向邻舍要金器银器。」

chapters.en: And the LORD gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover, Moses himself was highly regarded in Egypt by Pharaoh’s officials and by the people.
chapters.zh: 耶和华叫百姓在埃及人眼前蒙恩，并且摩西在埃及地、法老臣仆，和百姓的眼中看为极大。

chapters.en: So Moses declared, “This is what the LORD says: ‘About midnight I will go throughout Egypt,
chapters.zh: 摩西说：「耶和华这样说：『约到半夜，我必出去巡行埃及遍地。

chapters.en: and every firstborn son in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne, to the firstborn of the servant girl behind the hand mill, as well as the firstborn of all the cattle.
chapters.zh: 凡在埃及地，从坐宝座的法老直到磨子后的婢女所有的长子，以及一切头生的牲畜，都必死。

chapters.en: Then a great cry will go out over all the land of Egypt. Such an outcry has never been heard before and will never be heard again.
chapters.zh: 埃及遍地必有大哀号；从前没有这样的，后来也必没有。

chapters.en:
But among all the Israelites, not even a dog will snarl at man or beast.’
Then you will know that the LORD makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel.
chapters.zh: 至于以色列中，无论是人是牲畜，连狗也不敢向他们摇舌，好叫你们知道耶和华是将埃及人和以色列人分别出来。』

chapters.en:
And all these officials of yours will come and bow before me, saying, ‘Go, you and all the people who follow you!’ After that, I will depart.”
And hot with anger, Moses left Pharaoh’s presence.
chapters.zh: 你这一切臣仆都要俯伏来见我，说：『求你和跟从你的百姓都出去』，然后我要出去。」于是，摩西气忿忿地离开法老，出去了。

chapters.en: The LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that My wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「法老必不听你们，使我的奇事在埃及地多起来。」

chapters.en: Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh, but the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart so that he would not let the Israelites go out of his land.
chapters.zh: 摩西、亚伦在法老面前行了这一切奇事；耶和华使法老的心刚硬，不容以色列人出离他的地。

chapters.en: Now the LORD said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt,
chapters.zh: 耶和华在埃及地晓谕摩西、亚伦说：

chapters.en: “This month is the beginning of months for you; it shall be the first month of your year.
chapters.zh: 「你们要以本月为正月，为一年之首。

chapters.en: Tell the whole congregation of Israel that on the tenth day of this month each man must select a lamb for his family, one per household.
chapters.zh: 你们吩咐以色列全会众说：本月初十日，各人要按着父家取羊羔，一家一只。

chapters.en: If the household is too small for a whole lamb, they are to share with the nearest neighbor based on the number of people, and apportion the lamb accordingly.
chapters.zh: 若是一家的人太少，吃不了一只羊羔，本人就要和他隔壁的邻舍共取一只。你们预备羊羔，要按着人数和饭量计算。

chapters.en: Your lamb must be an unblemished year-old male, and you may take it from the sheep or the goats.
chapters.zh: 要无残疾、一岁的公羊羔，你们或从绵羊里取，或从山羊里取，都可以。

chapters.en: You must keep it until the fourteenth day of the month, when the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel will slaughter the animals at twilight.
chapters.zh: 要留到本月十四日，在黄昏的时候，以色列全会众把羊羔宰了。

chapters.en: They are to take some of the blood and put it on the sides and tops of the doorframes of the houses where they eat the lambs.
chapters.zh: 各家要取点血，涂在吃羊羔的房屋左右的门框上和门楣上。

chapters.en: They are to eat the meat that night, roasted over the fire, along with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
chapters.zh: 当夜要吃羊羔的肉；用火烤了，与无酵饼和苦菜同吃。

chapters.en: Do not eat any of the meat raw or cooked in boiling water, but only roasted over the fire—its head and legs and inner parts.
chapters.zh: 不可吃生的，断不可吃水煮的，要带着头、腿、五脏，用火烤了吃。

chapters.en: Do not leave any of it until morning; before the morning you must burn up any part that is left over.
chapters.zh: 不可剩下一点留到早晨；若留到早晨，要用火烧了。

chapters.en: This is how you are to eat it: You must be fully dressed for travel, with your sandals on your feet and your staff in your hand. You are to eat in haste; it is the LORD’s Passover.
chapters.zh: 你们吃羊羔当腰间束带，脚上穿鞋，手中拿杖，赶紧地吃；这是耶和华的逾越节。

chapters.en: On that night I will pass through the land of Egypt and strike down every firstborn male, both man and beast, and I will execute judgment against all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 因为那夜我要巡行埃及地，把埃及地一切头生的，无论是人是牲畜，都击杀了，又要败坏埃及一切的神。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: The blood on the houses where you are staying will be a sign; when I see the blood, I will pass over you. No plague will fall on you to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 这血要在你们所住的房屋上作记号；我一见这血，就越过你们去。我击杀埃及地〔头生〕的时候，灾殃必不临到你们身上灭你们。」

chapters.en: And this day will be a memorial for you, and you are to celebrate it as a feast to the LORD, as a permanent statute for the generations to come.
chapters.zh: 「你们要记念这日，守为耶和华的节，作为你们世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: For seven days you must eat unleavened bread. On the first day you are to remove the leaven from your houses. Whoever eats anything leavened from the first day through the seventh must be cut off from Israel.
chapters.zh: 你们要吃无酵饼七日。头一日要把酵从你们各家中除去；因为从头一日起，到第七日为止，凡吃有酵之饼的，必从以色列中剪除。

chapters.en: On the first day you are to hold a sacred assembly, and another on the seventh day. You must not do any work on those days, except to prepare the meals—that is all you may do.
chapters.zh: 头一日你们当有圣会，第七日也当有圣会。这两日之内，除了预备各人所要吃的以外，无论何工都不可做。

chapters.en: So you are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread, for on this very day I brought your divisions out of the land of Egypt. You must keep this day as a permanent statute for the generations to come.
chapters.zh: 你们要守无酵节，因为我正当这日把你们的军队从埃及地领出来。所以，你们要守这日，作为世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: In the first month you are to eat unleavened bread, from the evening of the fourteenth day until the evening of the twenty-first day.
chapters.zh: 从正月十四日晚上，直到二十一日晚上，你们要吃无酵饼。

chapters.en: For seven days there must be no leaven found in your houses. If anyone eats something leavened, that person, whether a foreigner or native of the land, must be cut off from the congregation of Israel.
chapters.zh: 在你们各家中，七日之内不可有酵；因为凡吃有酵之物的，无论是寄居的，是本地的，必从以色列的会中剪除。

chapters.en: You are not to eat anything leavened; eat unleavened bread in all your homes.”
chapters.zh: 有酵的物，你们都不可吃；在你们一切住处要吃无酵饼。」

chapters.en: Then Moses summoned all the elders of Israel and told them, “Go at once and select for yourselves a lamb for each family, and slaughter the Passover lamb.
chapters.zh: 于是，摩西召了以色列的众长老来，对他们说：「你们要按着家口取出羊羔，把这逾越节〔的羊羔〕宰了。

chapters.en: Take a cluster of hyssop, dip it into the blood in the basin, and brush the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe. None of you shall go out the door of his house until morning.
chapters.zh: 拿一把牛膝草，蘸盆里的血，打在门楣上和左右的门框上。你们谁也不可出自己的房门，直到早晨。

chapters.en: When the LORD passes through to strike down the Egyptians, He will see the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe and will pass over that doorway; so He will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses and strike you down.
chapters.zh: 因为耶和华要巡行击杀埃及人，他看见血在门楣上和左右的门框上，就必越过那门，不容灭命的进你们的房屋，击杀你们。

chapters.en: And you are to keep this command as a permanent statute for you and your descendants.
chapters.zh: 这例，你们要守着，作为你们和你们子孙永远的定例。

chapters.en: When you enter the land that the LORD will give you as He promised, you are to keep this service.
chapters.zh: 日后，你们到了耶和华按着所应许赐给你们的那地，就要守这礼。

chapters.en: When your children ask you, ‘What does this service mean to you?’
chapters.zh: 你们的儿女问你们说：『行这礼是什么意思？』

chapters.en:
you are to reply, ‘It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt when He struck down the Egyptians and spared our homes.’”
Then the people bowed down and worshiped.
chapters.zh: 你们就说：『这是献给耶和华逾越节的祭。当以色列人在埃及的时候，他击杀埃及人，越过以色列人的房屋，救了我们各家。』」于是百姓低头下拜。

chapters.en: And the Israelites went and did just what the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.
chapters.zh: 耶和华怎样吩咐摩西、亚伦，以色列人就怎样行。

chapters.en: Now at midnight the LORD struck down every firstborn male in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sat on his throne, to the firstborn of the prisoner in the dungeon, as well as all the firstborn among the livestock.
chapters.zh: 到了半夜，耶和华把埃及地所有的长子，就是从坐宝座的法老，直到被掳囚在监里之人的长子，以及一切头生的牲畜，尽都杀了。

chapters.en: During the night Pharaoh got up—he and all his officials and all the Egyptians—and there was loud wailing in Egypt; for there was no house without someone dead.
chapters.zh: 法老和一切臣仆，并埃及众人，夜间都起来了。在埃及有大哀号，无一家不死一个人的。

chapters.en: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron by night and said, “Get up, leave my people, both you and the Israelites! Go, worship the LORD as you have requested.
chapters.zh: 夜间，法老召了摩西、亚伦来，说：「起来！连你们带以色列人，从我民中出去，依你们所说的，去事奉耶和华吧！

chapters.en: Take your flocks and herds as well, just as you have said, and depart! And bless me also.”
chapters.zh: 也依你们所说的，连羊群牛群带着走吧！并要为我祝福。」

chapters.en: And in order to send them out of the land quickly, the Egyptians urged the people on. “For otherwise,” they said, “we are all going to die!”
chapters.zh: 埃及人催促百姓，打发他们快快出离那地，因为埃及人说：「我们都要死了。」

chapters.en: So the people took their dough before it was leavened, carrying it on their shoulders in kneading bowls wrapped in clothing.
chapters.zh: 百姓就拿着没有酵的生面，把抟面盆包在衣服中，扛在肩头上。

chapters.en: Furthermore, the Israelites acted on Moses’ word and asked the Egyptians for articles of silver and gold, and for clothing.
chapters.zh: 以色列人照着摩西的话行，向埃及人要金器、银器，和衣裳。

chapters.en: And the LORD gave the people such favor in the sight of the Egyptians that they granted their request. In this way they plundered the Egyptians.
chapters.zh: 耶和华叫百姓在埃及人眼前蒙恩，以致埃及人给他们所要的。他们就把埃及人的〔财物〕夺去了。

chapters.en: The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth with about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children.
chapters.zh: 以色列人从兰塞起行，往疏割去；除了〔妇人〕孩子，步行的男人约有六十万。

chapters.en: And a mixed multitude also went up with them, along with great droves of livestock, both flocks and herds.
chapters.zh: 又有许多闲杂人，并有羊群牛群，和他们一同上去。

chapters.en: Since their dough had no leaven, the people baked what they had brought out of Egypt into unleavened loaves. For when they had been driven out of Egypt, they could not delay and had not prepared any provisions for themselves.
chapters.zh: 他们用埃及带出来的生面烤成无酵饼。这生面原没有发起；因为他们被催逼离开埃及，不能耽延，也没有为自己预备什么食物。

chapters.en: Now the duration of the Israelites’ stay in Egypt was 430 years.
chapters.zh: 以色列人住在埃及共有四百三十年。

chapters.en: At the end of the 430 years, to the very day, all the LORD’s divisions went out of the land of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 正满了四百三十年的那一天，耶和华的军队都从埃及地出来了。

chapters.en: Because the LORD kept a vigil that night to bring them out of the land of Egypt, this same night is to be a vigil to the LORD, to be observed by all the Israelites for the generations to come.
chapters.zh: 这夜是耶和华的夜；因耶和华领他们出了埃及地，所以当向耶和华谨守，是以色列众人世世代代该谨守的。

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the statute of the Passover: No foreigner is to eat of it.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西、亚伦说：「逾越节的例是这样：外邦人都不可吃这羊羔。

chapters.en: But any slave who has been purchased may eat of it, after you have circumcised him.
chapters.zh: 但各人用银子买的奴仆，既受了割礼就可以吃。

chapters.en: A temporary resident or hired hand shall not eat the Passover.
chapters.zh: 寄居的和雇工人都不可吃。

chapters.en: It must be eaten inside one house. You are not to take any of the meat outside the house, and you may not break any of the bones.
chapters.zh: 应当在一个房子里吃；不可把一点肉从房子里带到外头去。羊羔的骨头一根也不可折断。

chapters.en: The whole congregation of Israel must celebrate it.
chapters.zh: 以色列全会众都要守这礼。

chapters.en: If a foreigner resides with you and wants to celebrate the LORD’s Passover, all the males in the household must be circumcised; then he may come near to celebrate it, and he shall be like a native of the land. But no uncircumcised man may eat of it.
chapters.zh: 若有外人寄居在你们中间，愿向耶和华守逾越节，他所有的男子务要受割礼，然后才容他前来遵守，他也就像本地人一样；但未受割礼的，都不可吃这羊羔。

chapters.en: The same law shall apply to both the native and the foreigner who resides among you.”
chapters.zh: 本地人和寄居在你们中间的外人同归一例。」

chapters.en: Then all the Israelites did this—they did just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.
chapters.zh: 耶和华怎样吩咐摩西、亚伦，以色列众人就怎样行了。

chapters.en: And on that very day the LORD brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt by their divisions.
chapters.zh: 正当那日，耶和华将以色列人按着他们的军队，从埃及地领出来。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Consecrate to Me every firstborn male. The firstborn from every womb among the Israelites belongs to Me, both of man and beast.”
chapters.zh: 「以色列中凡头生的，无论是人是牲畜，都是我的，要分别为圣归我。」

chapters.en: So Moses told the people, “Remember this day, the day you came out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery; for the LORD brought you out of it by the strength of His hand. And nothing leavened shall be eaten.
chapters.zh: 摩西对百姓说：「你们要记念从埃及为奴之家出来的这日，因为耶和华用大能的手将你们从这地方领出来。有酵的饼都不可吃。

chapters.en: Today, in the month of Abib, you are leaving.
chapters.zh: 亚笔月间的这日是你们出来的日子。

chapters.en: And when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites—the land He swore to your fathers that He would give you, a land flowing with milk and honey—you shall keep this service in this month.
chapters.zh: 将来耶和华领你进迦南人、赫人、亚摩利人、希未人、耶布斯人之地，就是他向你的祖宗起誓应许给你那流奶与蜜之地，那时你要在这月间守这礼。

chapters.en: For seven days you are to eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a feast to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你要吃无酵饼七日，到第七日要向耶和华守节。

chapters.en: Unleavened bread shall be eaten during those seven days. Nothing leavened may be found among you, nor shall leaven be found anywhere within your borders.
chapters.zh: 这七日之久，要吃无酵饼；在你四境之内不可见有酵的饼，也不可见发酵的物。

chapters.en: And on that day you are to explain to your son, ‘This is because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.’
chapters.zh: 当那日，你要告诉你的儿子说：『这是因耶和华在我出埃及的时候为我所行的事。

chapters.en: It shall be a sign for you on your hand and a reminder on your forehead that the Law of the LORD is to be on your lips. For with a mighty hand the LORD brought you out of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 这要在你手上作记号，在你额上作纪念，使耶和华的律法常在你口中，因为耶和华曾用大能的手将你从埃及领出来。

chapters.en: Therefore you shall keep this statute at the appointed time year after year.
chapters.zh: 所以你每年要按着日期守这例。』」

chapters.en: And after the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites and gives it to you, as He swore to you and your fathers,
chapters.zh: 「将来，耶和华照他向你和你祖宗所起的誓将你领进迦南人之地，把这地赐给你，

chapters.en: you are to present to the LORD the firstborn male of every womb. All the firstborn males of your livestock belong to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 那时你要将一切头生的，并牲畜中头生的，归给耶和华；公的都要属耶和华。

chapters.en: You must redeem every firstborn donkey with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, you are to break its neck. And every firstborn of your sons you must redeem.
chapters.zh: 凡头生的驴，你要用羊羔代赎；若不代赎，就要打折牠的颈项。凡你儿子中头生的都要赎出来。

chapters.en: In the future, when your son asks you, ‘What does this mean?’ you are to tell him, ‘With a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
chapters.zh: 日后，你的儿子问你说：『这是什么意思？』你就说：『耶和华用大能的手将我们从埃及为奴之家领出来。

chapters.en: And when Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both of man and beast. This is why I sacrifice to the LORD the firstborn male of every womb, but I redeem all the firstborn of my sons.’
chapters.zh: 那时法老几乎不容我们去，耶和华就把埃及地所有头生的，无论是人是牲畜，都杀了。因此，我把一切头生的公〔牲畜〕献给耶和华为祭，但将头生的儿子都赎出来。

chapters.en: So it shall serve as a sign on your hand and a symbol on your forehead, for with a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt.”
chapters.zh: 这要在你手上作记号，在你额上作经文，因为耶和华用大能的手将我们从埃及领出来。』」

chapters.en: When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them along the road through the land of the Philistines, though it was shorter. For God said, “If the people face war, they might change their minds and return to Egypt.”
chapters.zh: 法老容百姓去的时候，非利士地的道路虽近，上帝却不领他们从那里走；因为上帝说：「恐怕百姓遇见打仗后悔，就回埃及去。」

chapters.en: So God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea. And the Israelites left the land of Egypt arrayed for battle.
chapters.zh: 所以上帝领百姓绕道而行，走红海旷野的路。以色列人出埃及地，都带着兵器上去。

chapters.en: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him because Joseph had made the sons of Israel swear a solemn oath when he said, “God will surely attend to you, and then you must carry my bones with you from this place.”
chapters.zh: 摩西把约瑟的骸骨一同带去；因为约瑟曾叫以色列人严严地起誓，〔对他们〕说：「上帝必眷顾你们，你们要把我的骸骨从这里一同带上去。」

chapters.en: They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham on the edge of the wilderness.
chapters.zh: 他们从疏割起行，在旷野边的以倘安营。

chapters.en: And the LORD went before them in a pillar of cloud to guide their way by day, and in a pillar of fire to give them light by night, so that they could travel by day or night.
chapters.zh: 日间，耶和华在云柱中领他们的路；夜间，在火柱中光照他们，使他们日夜都可以行走。

chapters.en: Neither the pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night left its place before the people.
chapters.zh: 日间云柱，夜间火柱，总不离开百姓的面前。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Tell the Israelites to turn back and encamp before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. You are to encamp by the sea, directly opposite Baal-zephon.
chapters.zh: 「你吩咐以色列人转回，安营在比‧哈希录前，密夺和海的中间，对着巴力‧洗分，靠近海边安营。

chapters.en: For Pharaoh will say of the Israelites, ‘They are wandering the land in confusion; the wilderness has boxed them in.’
chapters.zh: 法老必说：『以色列人在地中绕迷了，旷野把他们困住了。』

chapters.en:
And I will harden Pharaoh’s heart so that he will pursue them. But I will gain honor by means of Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD.”
So this is what the Israelites did.
chapters.zh: 我要使法老的心刚硬，他要追赶他们，我便在法老和他全军身上得荣耀；埃及人就知道我是耶和华。」于是以色列人这样行了。

chapters.en: When the king of Egypt was told that the people had fled, Pharaoh and his officials changed their minds about them and said, “What have we done? We have released Israel from serving us.”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉埃及王说：「百姓逃跑。」法老和他的臣仆就向百姓变心，说：「我们容以色列人去，不再服事我们，这做的是什么事呢？」

chapters.en: So Pharaoh prepared his chariot and took his army with him.
chapters.zh: 法老就预备他的车辆，带领军兵同去，

chapters.en: He took 600 of the best chariots, and all the other chariots of Egypt, with officers over all of them.
chapters.zh: 并带着六百辆特选的车和埃及所有的车，每辆都有车兵长。

chapters.en: And the LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt so that he pursued the Israelites, who were marching out defiantly.
chapters.zh: 耶和华使埃及王法老的心刚硬，他就追赶以色列人，因为以色列人是昂然无惧地出埃及。

chapters.en: The Egyptians—all Pharaoh’s horses and chariots, horsemen and troops—pursued the Israelites and overtook them as they camped by the sea near Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon.
chapters.zh: 埃及人追赶他们，法老一切的马匹、车辆、马兵，与军兵就在海边上，靠近比‧哈希录，对着巴力‧洗分，在他们安营的地方追上了。

chapters.en: As Pharaoh approached, the Israelites looked up and saw the Egyptians marching after them, and they were terrified and cried out to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 法老临近的时候，以色列人举目看见埃及人赶来，就甚惧怕，向耶和华哀求。

chapters.en: They said to Moses, “Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us into the wilderness to die? What have you done to us by bringing us out of Egypt?
chapters.zh: 他们对摩西说：「难道在埃及没有坟地，你把我们带来死在旷野吗？你为什么这样待我们，将我们从埃及领出来呢？

chapters.en: Did we not say to you in Egypt, ‘Leave us alone so that we may serve the Egyptians’? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.”
chapters.zh: 我们在埃及岂没有对你说过，不要搅扰我们，容我们服事埃及人吗？因为服事埃及人比死在旷野还好。」

chapters.en: But Moses told the people, “Do not be afraid. Stand firm and you will see the LORD’s salvation, which He will accomplish for you today; for the Egyptians you see today, you will never see again.
chapters.zh: 摩西对百姓说：「不要惧怕，只管站住！看耶和华今天向你们所要施行的救恩。因为，你们今天所看见的埃及人必永远不再看见了。

chapters.en: The LORD will fight for you; you need only to be still.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华必为你们争战；你们只管静默，不要作声。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Why are you crying out to Me? Tell the Israelites to go forward.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你为什么向我哀求呢？你吩咐以色列人往前走。

chapters.en: And as for you, lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, so that the Israelites can go through the sea on dry ground.
chapters.zh: 你举手向海伸杖，把水分开。以色列人要下海中走干地。

chapters.en: And I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians so that they will go in after them. Then I will gain honor by means of Pharaoh and all his army and chariots and horsemen.
chapters.zh: 我要使埃及人的心刚硬，他们就跟着下去。我要在法老和他的全军、车辆、马兵上得荣耀。

chapters.en: The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I am honored through Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen.”
chapters.zh: 我在法老和他的车辆、马兵上得荣耀的时候，埃及人就知道我是耶和华了。」

chapters.en: And the angel of God, who had gone before the camp of Israel, withdrew and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from before them and stood behind them,
chapters.zh: 在以色列营前行走上帝的使者，转到他们后边去；云柱也从他们前边转到他们后边立住。

chapters.en: so that it came between the camps of Egypt and Israel. The cloud was there in the darkness, but it lit up the night. So all night long neither camp went near the other.
chapters.zh: 在埃及营和以色列营中间有云柱，一边黑暗，一边发光，终夜两下不得相近。

chapters.en: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the LORD drove back the sea with a strong east wind that turned it into dry land. So the waters were divided,
chapters.zh: 摩西向海伸杖，耶和华便用大东风，使海水一夜退去，水便分开，海就成了干地。

chapters.en: and the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on their right and on their left.
chapters.zh: 以色列人下海中走干地，水在他们的左右作了墙垣。

chapters.en: And the Egyptians chased after them—all Pharaoh’s horses, chariots, and horsemen—and followed them into the sea.
chapters.zh: 埃及人追赶他们，法老一切的马匹、车辆，和马兵都跟着下到海中。

chapters.en: At morning watch, however, the LORD looked down on the army of the Egyptians from the pillar of fire and cloud, and He threw their camp into confusion.
chapters.zh: 到了晨更的时候，耶和华从云火柱中向埃及的军兵观看，使埃及的军兵混乱了；

chapters.en: He caused their chariot wheels to wobble, so that they had difficulty driving. “Let us flee from the Israelites,” said the Egyptians, “for the LORD is fighting for them against Egypt!”
chapters.zh: 又使他们的车轮脱落，难以行走，以致埃及人说：「我们从以色列人面前逃跑吧！因耶和华为他们攻击我们了。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea, so that the waters may flow back over the Egyptians and their chariots and horsemen.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你向海伸杖，叫水仍合在埃及人并他们的车辆、马兵身上。」

chapters.en: So Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and at daybreak the sea returned to its normal state. As the Egyptians were retreating, the LORD swept them into the sea.
chapters.zh: 摩西就向海伸杖，到了天一亮，海水仍旧复原。埃及人避水逃跑的时候，耶和华把他们推翻在海中，

chapters.en: The waters flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen—the entire army of Pharaoh that had chased the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them survived.
chapters.zh: 水就回流，淹没了车辆和马兵。那些跟着以色列人下海法老的全军，连一个也没有剩下。

chapters.en: But the Israelites had walked through the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on their right and on their left.
chapters.zh: 以色列人却在海中走干地；水在他们的左右作了墙垣。

chapters.en: That day the LORD saved Israel from the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the shore.
chapters.zh: 当日，耶和华这样拯救以色列人脱离埃及人的手，以色列人看见埃及人的死尸都在海边了。

chapters.en: When Israel saw the great power that the LORD had exercised over the Egyptians, the people feared the LORD and believed in Him and in His servant Moses.
chapters.zh: 以色列人看见耶和华向埃及人所行的大事，就敬畏耶和华，又信服他和他的仆人摩西。

chapters.en:
Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the LORD:
“I will sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted. The horse and rider He has thrown into the sea.
chapters.zh: 那时，摩西和以色列人向耶和华唱歌说： 我要向耶和华歌唱，因他大大战胜， 将马和骑马的投在海中。

chapters.en: The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation. He is my God, and I will praise Him, my father’s God, and I will exalt Him.
chapters.zh: 耶和华是我的力量，我的诗歌， 也成了我的拯救。 这是我的上帝，我要赞美他， 是我父亲的上帝，我要尊崇他。

chapters.en: The LORD is a warrior, the LORD is His name.
chapters.zh: 耶和华是战士； 他的名是耶和华。

chapters.en: Pharaoh’s chariots and army He has cast into the sea; the finest of his officers are drowned in the Red Sea.
chapters.zh: 法老的车辆、军兵，耶和华已抛在海中； 他特选的军长都沉于红海。

chapters.en: The depths have covered them; they sank there like a stone.
chapters.zh: 深水淹没他们； 他们如同石头坠到深处。

chapters.en: Your right hand, O LORD, is majestic in power; Your right hand, O LORD, has shattered the enemy.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，你的右手施展能力，显出荣耀； 耶和华啊，你的右手摔碎仇敌。

chapters.en: You overthrew Your adversaries by Your great majesty. You unleashed Your burning wrath; it consumed them like stubble.
chapters.zh: 你大发威严，推翻那些起来攻击你的； 你发出烈怒〔如火〕，烧灭他们像烧碎诩一样。

chapters.en: At the blast of Your nostrils the waters piled up; like a wall the currents stood firm; the depths congealed in the heart of the sea.
chapters.zh: 你发鼻中的气，水便聚起成堆， 大水直立如垒， 海中的深水凝结。

chapters.en: The enemy declared, ‘I will pursue, I will overtake. I will divide the spoils; I will gorge myself on them. I will draw my sword; my hand will destroy them.’
chapters.zh: 仇敌说：我要追赶，我要追上； 我要分掳物，我要在他们身上称我的心愿。 我要拔出刀来，亲手杀灭他们。

chapters.en: But You blew with Your breath, and the sea covered them. They sank like lead in the mighty waters.
chapters.zh: 你叫风一吹，海就把他们淹没； 他们如铅沉在大水之中。

chapters.en: Who among the gods is like You, O LORD? Who is like You—majestic in holiness, revered with praises, performing wonders?
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，众神之中，谁能像你？ 谁能像你－至圣至荣， 可颂可畏，施行奇事？

chapters.en: You stretched out Your right hand, and the earth swallowed them up.
chapters.zh: 你伸出右手， 地便吞灭他们。

chapters.en: With loving devotion You will lead the people You have redeemed; with Your strength You will guide them to Your holy dwelling.
chapters.zh: 你凭慈爱领了你所赎的百姓； 你凭能力引他们到了你的圣所。

chapters.en: The nations will hear and tremble; anguish will grip the dwellers of Philistia.
chapters.zh: 外邦人听见就发颤； 疼痛抓住非利士的居民。

chapters.en: Then the chiefs of Edom will be dismayed; trembling will seize the leaders of Moab; those who dwell in Canaan will melt away,
chapters.zh: 那时，以东的族长惊惶， 摩押的英雄被战兢抓住， 迦南的居民〔心〕都消化了。

chapters.en: and terror and dread will fall on them. By the power of Your arm they will be as still as a stone until Your people pass by, O LORD, until the people You have bought pass by.
chapters.zh: 惊骇恐惧临到他们。 耶和华啊，因你膀臂的大能， 他们如石头寂然不动， 等候你的百姓过去， 等候你所赎的百姓过去。

chapters.en: You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance— the place, O LORD, You have prepared for Your dwelling, the sanctuary, O Lord, Your hands have established.
chapters.zh: 你要将他们领进去，栽于你产业的山上－ 耶和华啊，就是你为自己所造的住处； 主啊，就是你手所建立的圣所。

chapters.en: The LORD will reign forever and ever!”
chapters.zh: 耶和华必作王，直到永永远远！

chapters.en: For when Pharaoh’s horses, chariots, and horsemen went into the sea, the LORD brought the waters of the sea back over them. But the Israelites walked through the sea on dry ground.
chapters.zh: 法老的马匹、车辆，和马兵下到海中，耶和华使海水回流，淹没他们；惟有以色列人在海中走干地。

chapters.en: Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron’s sister, took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women followed her with tambourines and dancing.
chapters.zh: 亚伦的姊姊，女先知米利暗，手里拿着鼓；众妇女也跟她出去拿鼓跳舞。

chapters.en:
And Miriam sang back to them:
“Sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted; the horse and rider He has thrown into the sea.”
chapters.zh: 米利暗应声说： 你们要歌颂耶和华，因他大大战胜， 将马和骑马的投在海中。

chapters.en: Then Moses led Israel from the Red Sea, and they went out into the Desert of Shur. For three days they walked in the desert without finding water.
chapters.zh: 摩西领以色列人从红海往前行，到了书珥的旷野，在旷野走了三天，找不着水。

chapters.en: And when they came to Marah, they could not drink the water there because it was bitter. (That is why it was named Marah.)
chapters.zh: 到了玛拉，不能喝那里的水；因为水苦，所以那地名叫玛拉。

chapters.en: So the people grumbled against Moses, saying, “What are we to drink?”
chapters.zh: 百姓就向摩西发怨言，说：「我们喝什么呢？」

chapters.en:
And Moses cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a log. And when he cast it into the waters, they were sweetened.
There the LORD made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there He tested them,
chapters.zh: 摩西呼求耶和华，耶和华指示他一棵树。他把树丢在水里，水就变甜了。 耶和华在那里为他们定了律例、典章，在那里试验他们；

chapters.en: saying, “If you will listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God, and do what is right in His eyes, and pay attention to His commands, and keep all His statutes, then I will not bring on you any of the diseases I inflicted on the Egyptians. For I am the LORD who heals you.”
chapters.zh: 又说：「你若留意听耶和华－你上帝的话，又行我眼中看为正的事，留心听我的诫命，守我一切的律例，我就不将所加与埃及人的疾病加在你身上，因为我－耶和华是医治你的。」

chapters.en: Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the waters.
chapters.zh: 他们到了以琳，在那里有十二股水泉，七十棵棕树；他们就在那里的水边安营。

chapters.en: On the fifteenth day of the second month after they had left the land of Egypt, the whole congregation of Israel set out from Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai.
chapters.zh: 以色列全会众从以琳起行，在出埃及后第二个月十五日到了以琳和西奈中间、汛的旷野。

chapters.en: And there in the desert the whole congregation of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron.
chapters.zh: 以色列全会众在旷野向摩西、亚伦发怨言，

chapters.en: “If only we had died by the LORD’s hand in the land of Egypt!” they said. “There we sat by pots of meat and ate our fill of bread, but you have brought us into this desert to starve this whole assembly to death!”
chapters.zh: 说：「巴不得我们早死在埃及地、耶和华的手下；那时我们坐在肉锅旁边，吃得饱足。你们将我们领出来，到这旷野，是要叫这全会众都饿死啊！」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I will rain down bread from heaven for you. Each day the people are to go out and gather enough for that day. In this way I will test whether or not they will follow My instructions.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「我要将粮食从天降给你们。百姓可以出去，每天收每天的分，我好试验他们遵不遵我的法度。

chapters.en: Then on the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it will be twice as much as they gather on the other days.”
chapters.zh: 到第六天，他们要把所收进来的预备好了，比每天所收的多一倍。」

chapters.en: So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, “This evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt,
chapters.zh: 摩西、亚伦对以色列众人说：「到了晚上，你们要知道是耶和华将你们从埃及地领出来的。

chapters.en: and in the morning you will see the LORD’s glory, because He has heard your grumbling against Him. For who are we, that you should grumble against us?”
chapters.zh: 早晨，你们要看见耶和华的荣耀，因为耶和华听见你们向他所发的怨言了。我们算什么，你们竟向我们发怨言呢？」

chapters.en: And Moses added, “The LORD will give you meat to eat this evening and bread to fill you in the morning, for He has heard your grumbling against Him. Who are we? Your grumblings are not against us but against the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 摩西又说：「耶和华晚上必给你们肉吃，早晨必给你们食物得饱；因为你们向耶和华发的怨言，他都听见了。我们算什么，你们的怨言不是向我们发的，乃是向耶和华发的。」

chapters.en: Then Moses said to Aaron, “Tell the whole congregation of Israel, ‘Come before the LORD, for He has heard your grumbling.’”
chapters.zh: 摩西对亚伦说：「你告诉以色列全会众说：『你们就近耶和华面前，因为他已经听见你们的怨言了。』」

chapters.en: And as Aaron was speaking to the whole congregation of Israel, they looked toward the desert, and there in a cloud the glory of the LORD appeared.
chapters.zh: 亚伦正对以色列全会众说话的时候，他们向旷野观看，不料，耶和华的荣光在云中显现。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Tell them, ‘At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will be filled with bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.’”
chapters.zh: 「我已经听见以色列人的怨言。你告诉他们说：『到黄昏的时候，你们要吃肉，早晨必有食物得饱，你们就知道我是耶和华－你们的上帝。』」

chapters.en: That evening quail came and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
chapters.zh: 到了晚上，有鹌鹑飞来，遮满了营；早晨在营四围的地上有露水。

chapters.en: When the layer of dew had evaporated, there were thin flakes on the desert floor, as fine as frost on the ground.
chapters.zh: 露水上升之后，不料，野地面上有如白霜的小圆物。

chapters.en:
When the Israelites saw it, they asked one another, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was.
So Moses told them, “It is the bread that the LORD has given you to eat.
chapters.zh: 以色列人看见，不知道是什么，就彼此对问说：「这是什么呢？」摩西对他们说：「这就是耶和华给你们吃的食物。

chapters.en: This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Each one is to gather as much as he needs. You may take an omer for each person in your tent.’”
chapters.zh: 耶和华所吩咐的是这样：你们要按着各人的饭量，为帐棚里的人，按着人数收起来，各拿一俄梅珥。」

chapters.en: So the Israelites did this. Some gathered more, and some less.
chapters.zh: 以色列人就这样行；有多收的，有少收的。

chapters.en: When they measured it by the omer, he who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall. Each one gathered as much as he needed to eat.
chapters.zh: 及至用俄梅珥量一量，多收的也没有余，少收的也没有缺；各人按着自己的饭量收取。

chapters.en: Then Moses said to them, “No one may keep any of it until morning.”
chapters.zh: 摩西对他们说：「所收的，不许什么人留到早晨。」

chapters.en: But they did not listen to Moses; some people left part of it until morning, and it became infested with maggots and began to smell. So Moses was angry with them.
chapters.zh: 然而他们不听摩西的话，内中有留到早晨的，就生虫变臭了；摩西便向他们发怒。

chapters.en: Every morning each one gathered as much as was needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away.
chapters.zh: 他们每日早晨，按着各人的饭量收取，日头一发热，就消化了。

chapters.en: On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much food—two omers per person —and all the leaders of the congregation came and reported this to Moses.
chapters.zh: 到第六天，他们收了双倍的食物，每人两俄梅珥。会众的官长来告诉摩西；

chapters.en: He told them, “This is what the LORD has said: ‘Tomorrow is to be a day of complete rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you want to bake, and boil what you want to boil. Then set aside whatever remains and keep it until morning.’”
chapters.zh: 摩西对他们说：「耶和华这样说：『明天是圣安息日，是向耶和华守的圣安息日。你们要烤的就烤了，要煮的就煮了，所剩下的都留到早晨。』」

chapters.en: So they set it aside until morning as Moses had commanded, and it did not smell or contain any maggots.
chapters.zh: 他们就照摩西的吩咐留到早晨，也不臭，里头也没有虫子。

chapters.en: “Eat it today,” Moses said, “because today is a Sabbath to the LORD. Today you will not find anything in the field.
chapters.zh: 摩西说：「你们今天吃这个吧！因为今天是向耶和华守的安息日；你们在田野必找不着了。

chapters.en: For six days you may gather, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, it will not be there.”
chapters.zh: 六天可以收取，第七天乃是安息日，那一天必没有了。」

chapters.en: Yet on the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they did not find anything.
chapters.zh: 第七天，百姓中有人出去收，什么也找不着。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and instructions?
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你们不肯守我的诫命和律法，要到几时呢？

chapters.en: Understand that the LORD has given you the Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day He will give you bread for two days. On the seventh day, everyone must stay where he is; no one may leave his place.”
chapters.zh: 你们看！耶和华既将安息日赐给你们，所以第六天他赐给你们两天的食物，第七天各人要住在自己的地方，不许什么人出去。」

chapters.en: So the people rested on the seventh day.
chapters.zh: 于是百姓第七天安息了。

chapters.en: Now the house of Israel called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.
chapters.zh: 这食物，以色列家叫吗哪；样子像芫荽子，颜色是白的，滋味如同搀蜜的薄饼。

chapters.en: Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Keep an omer of manna for the generations to come, so that they may see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.’”
chapters.zh: 摩西说：「耶和华所吩咐的是这样：『要将一满俄梅珥吗哪留到世世代代，使后人可以看见我当日将你们领出埃及地，在旷野所给你们吃的食物。』」

chapters.en: So Moses told Aaron, “Take a jar and fill it with an omer of manna. Then place it before the LORD to be preserved for the generations to come.”
chapters.zh: 摩西对亚伦说：「你拿一个罐子，盛一满俄梅珥吗哪，存在耶和华面前，要留到世世代代。」

chapters.en: And Aaron placed it in front of the Testimony, to be preserved just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 耶和华怎么吩咐摩西，亚伦就怎么行，把吗哪放在法〔柜〕前存留。

chapters.en: The Israelites ate manna forty years, until they came to a land where they could settle; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.
chapters.zh: 以色列人吃吗哪共四十年，直到进了有人居住之地，就是迦南的境界。

chapters.en: (Now an omer is a tenth of an ephah.)
chapters.zh: （俄梅珥就是伊法十分之一。）

chapters.en: Then the whole congregation of Israel left the Desert of Sin, moving from place to place as the LORD commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
chapters.zh: 以色列全会众都遵耶和华的吩咐，按着站口从汛的旷野往前行，在利非订安营。百姓没有水喝，

chapters.en:
So the people contended with Moses, “Give us water to drink.”
“Why do you contend with me?” Moses replied. “Why do you test the LORD?”
chapters.zh: 所以与摩西争闹，说：「给我们水喝吧！」摩西对他们说：「你们为什么与我争闹？为什么试探耶和华呢？」

chapters.en: But the people thirsted for water there, and they grumbled against Moses: “Why have you brought us out of Egypt—to make us and our children and livestock die of thirst?”
chapters.zh: 百姓在那里甚渴，要喝水，就向摩西发怨言，说：「你为什么将我们从埃及领出来，使我们和我们的儿女并牲畜都渴死呢？」

chapters.en: Then Moses cried out to the LORD, “What should I do with these people? A little more and they will stone me!”
chapters.zh: 摩西就呼求耶和华说：「我向这百姓怎样行呢？他们几乎要拿石头打死我。」

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses, “Walk on ahead of the people and take some of the elders of Israel with you. Take along in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你手里拿着你先前击打河水的杖，带领以色列的几个长老，从百姓面前走过去。

chapters.en:
Behold, I will stand there before you by the rock at Horeb. And when you strike the rock, water will come out of it for the people to drink.”
So Moses did this in the sight of the elders of Israel.
chapters.zh: 我必在何烈的磐石那里，站在你面前。你要击打磐石，从磐石里必有水流出来，使百姓可以喝。」摩西就在以色列的长老眼前这样行了。

chapters.en: He named the place Massah and Meribah because the Israelites quarreled, and because they tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us or not?”
chapters.zh: 他给那地方起名叫玛撒〔注：就是试探的意思〕，又叫米利巴〔注：就是争闹的意思〕；因以色列人争闹，又因他们试探耶和华，说：「耶和华是在我们中间不是？」

chapters.en: After this, the Amalekites came and attacked the Israelites at Rephidim.
chapters.zh: 那时，亚玛力人来在利非订，和以色列人争战。

chapters.en: So Moses said to Joshua, “Choose some of our men and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on the hilltop with the staff of God in my hand.”
chapters.zh: 摩西对约书亚说：「你为我们选出人来，出去和亚玛力人争战。明天我手里要拿着上帝的杖，站在山顶上。」

chapters.en: Joshua did as Moses had instructed him and fought against the Amalekites, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
chapters.zh: 于是约书亚照着摩西对他所说的话行，和亚玛力人争战。摩西、亚伦，与户珥都上了山顶。

chapters.en: As long as Moses held up his hands, Israel prevailed; but when he lowered them, Amalek prevailed.
chapters.zh: 摩西何时举手，以色列人就得胜，何时垂手，亚玛力人就得胜。

chapters.en: When Moses’ hands grew heavy, they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Then Aaron and Hur held his hands up, one on each side, so that his hands remained steady until the sun went down.
chapters.zh: 但摩西的手发沉，他们就搬石头来，放在他以下，他就坐在上面。亚伦与户珥扶着他的手，一个在这边，一个在那边，他的手就稳住，直到日落的时候。

chapters.en: So Joshua overwhelmed Amalek and his army with the sword.
chapters.zh: 约书亚用刀杀了亚玛力王和他的百姓。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this on a scroll as a reminder and recite it to Joshua, because I will utterly blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「我要将亚玛力的名号从天下全然涂抹了；你要将这话写在书上作纪念，又念给约书亚听。」

chapters.en: And Moses built an altar and named it The LORD Is My Banner.
chapters.zh: 摩西筑了一座坛，起名叫「耶和华尼西」〔注：就是耶和华是我旌旗的意思〕，

chapters.en: “Indeed,” he said, “a hand was lifted up toward the throne of the LORD. The LORD will war against Amalek from generation to generation.”
chapters.zh: 又说：「耶和华已经起了誓，必世世代代和亚玛力人争战。」

chapters.en: Now Moses’ father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, heard about all that God had done for Moses and His people Israel, and how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 摩西的岳父，米甸祭司叶忒罗，听见上帝为摩西和上帝的百姓以色列所行的一切事，就是耶和华将以色列从埃及领出来的事，

chapters.en: After Moses had sent back his wife Zipporah, his father-in-law Jethro had received her,
chapters.zh: 便带着摩西的妻子西坡拉，就是摩西从前打发回去的，

chapters.en: along with her two sons. One son was named Gershom, for Moses had said, “I have been a foreigner in a foreign land.”
chapters.zh: 又带着西坡拉的两个儿子，一个名叫革舜，因为摩西说：「我在外邦作了寄居的」；

chapters.en: The other son was named Eliezer, for Moses had said, “The God of my father was my helper and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.”
chapters.zh: 一个名叫以利以谢，因为〔他说〕：「我父亲的上帝帮助了我，救我脱离法老的刀。」

chapters.en: Moses’ father-in-law Jethro, along with Moses’ wife and sons, came to him in the desert, where he was encamped at the mountain of God.
chapters.zh: 摩西的岳父叶忒罗带着摩西的妻子和两个儿子来到上帝的山，就是摩西在旷野安营的地方。

chapters.en: He sent word to Moses, “I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you with your wife and her two sons.”
chapters.zh: 他对摩西说：「我是你岳父叶忒罗，带着你的妻子和两个儿子来到你这里。」

chapters.en: So Moses went out to meet his father-in-law and bowed down and kissed him. They greeted each other and went into the tent.
chapters.zh: 摩西迎接他的岳父，向他下拜，与他亲嘴，彼此问安，都进了帐棚。

chapters.en: Then Moses recounted to his father-in-law all that the LORD had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, all the hardships they had encountered along the way, and how the LORD had delivered them.
chapters.zh: 摩西将耶和华为以色列的缘故向法老和埃及人所行的一切事，以及路上所遭遇的一切艰难，并耶和华怎样搭救他们，都述说与他岳父听。

chapters.en: And Jethro rejoiced over all the good things the LORD had done for Israel, whom He had rescued from the hand of the Egyptians.
chapters.zh: 叶忒罗因耶和华待以色列的一切好处，就是拯救他们脱离埃及人的手，便甚欢喜。

chapters.en: Jethro declared, “Blessed be the LORD, who has delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and of Pharaoh, and who has delivered the people from the hand of the Egyptians.
chapters.zh: 叶忒罗说：「耶和华是应当称颂的；他救了你们脱离埃及人和法老的手，将这百姓从埃及人的手下救出来。

chapters.en: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all other gods, for He did this when they treated Israel with arrogance.”
chapters.zh: 我现今在埃及人向这百姓发狂傲的事上得知，耶和华比万神都大。」

chapters.en: Then Moses’ father-in-law Jethro brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God, and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law in the presence of God.
chapters.zh: 摩西的岳父叶忒罗把燔祭和〔平安〕祭献给上帝。亚伦和以色列的众长老都来了，与摩西的岳父在上帝面前吃饭。

chapters.en: The next day Moses took his seat to judge the people, and they stood around him from morning until evening.
chapters.zh: 第二天，摩西坐着审判百姓，百姓从早到晚都站在摩西的左右。

chapters.en: When his father-in-law saw all that Moses was doing for the people, he asked, “What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone as judge, with all the people standing around you from morning till evening?”
chapters.zh: 摩西的岳父看见他向百姓所做的一切事，就说：「你向百姓做的是什么事呢？你为什么独自坐着，众百姓从早到晚都站在你的左右呢？」

chapters.en: “Because the people come to me to inquire of God,” Moses replied.
chapters.zh: 摩西对岳父说：「这是因百姓到我这里来求问上帝。

chapters.en: “Whenever they have a dispute, it is brought to me to judge between one man and another, and I make known to them the statutes and laws of God.”
chapters.zh: 他们有事的时候就到我这里来，我便在两造之间施行审判；我又叫他们知道上帝的律例和法度。」

chapters.en: But Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “What you are doing is not good.
chapters.zh: 摩西的岳父说：「你这做的不好。

chapters.en: Surely you and these people with you will wear yourselves out, because the task is too heavy for you. You cannot handle it alone.
chapters.zh: 你和这些百姓必都疲惫；因为这事太重，你独自一人办理不了。

chapters.en: Now listen to me; I will give you some advice, and may God be with you. You must be the people’s representative before God and bring their causes to Him.
chapters.zh: 现在你要听我的话。我为你出个主意，愿上帝与你同在。你要替百姓到上帝面前，将案件奏告上帝；

chapters.en: Teach them the statutes and laws, and show them the way to live and the work they must do.
chapters.zh: 又要将律例和法度教训他们，指示他们当行的道，当做的事；

chapters.en: Furthermore, select capable men from among the people—God-fearing, trustworthy men who are averse to dishonest gain. Appoint them over the people as leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.
chapters.zh: 并要从百姓中拣选有才能的人，就是敬畏上帝、诚实无妄、恨不义之财的人，派他们作千夫长、百夫长、五十夫长、十夫长，管理百姓，

chapters.en: Have these men judge the people at all times. Then they can bring you any major issue, but all minor cases they can judge on their own, so that your load may be lightened as they share it with you.
chapters.zh: 叫他们随时审判百姓，大事都要呈到你这里，小事他们自己可以审判。这样，你就轻省些，他们也可以同当此任。

chapters.en: If you follow this advice and God so directs you, then you will be able to endure, and all these people can go home in peace.”
chapters.zh: 你若这样行，上帝也这样吩咐你，你就能受得住，这百姓也都平平安安归回他们的住处。」

chapters.en: Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.
chapters.zh: 于是，摩西听从他岳父的话，按着他所说的去行。

chapters.en: So Moses chose capable men from all Israel and made them heads over the people as leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.
chapters.zh: 摩西从以色列人中拣选了有才能的人，立他们为百姓的首领，作千夫长、百夫长、五十夫长、十夫长。

chapters.en: And they judged the people at all times; they would bring the difficult cases to Moses, but any minor issue they would judge themselves.
chapters.zh: 他们随时审判百姓，有难断的案件就呈到摩西那里，但各样小事他们自己审判。

chapters.en: Then Moses sent his father-in-law on his way, and Jethro returned to his own land.
chapters.zh: 此后，摩西让他的岳父去，他就往本地去了。

chapters.en: In the third month, on the same day of the month that the Israelites had left the land of Egypt, they came to the Wilderness of Sinai.
chapters.zh: 以色列人出埃及地以后，满了三个月的那一天，就来到西奈的旷野。

chapters.en: After they had set out from Rephidim, they entered the Wilderness of Sinai, and Israel camped there in front of the mountain.
chapters.zh: 他们离了利非订，来到西奈的旷野，就在那里的山下安营。

chapters.en: Then Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain, “This is what you are to tell the house of Jacob and explain to the sons of Israel:
chapters.zh: 摩西到上帝那里，耶和华从山上呼唤他说：「你要这样告诉雅各家，晓谕以色列人说：

chapters.en: ‘You have seen for yourselves what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to Myself.
chapters.zh: 『我向埃及人所行的事，你们都看见了，且看见我如鹰将你们背在翅膀上，带来归我。

chapters.en: Now if you will indeed obey My voice and keep My covenant, you will be My treasured possession out of all the nations—for the whole earth is Mine.
chapters.zh: 如今你们若实在听从我的话，遵守我的约，就要在万民中作属我的子民，因为全地都是我的。

chapters.en: And unto Me you shall be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ These are the words that you are to speak to the Israelites.”
chapters.zh: 你们要归我作祭司的国度，为圣洁的国民。』这些话你要告诉以色列人。」

chapters.en: So Moses went back and summoned the elders of the people and set before them all these words that the LORD had commanded him.
chapters.zh: 摩西去召了民间的长老来，将耶和华所吩咐他的话都在他们面前陈明。

chapters.en:
And all the people answered together, “We will do everything that the LORD has spoken.”
So Moses brought their words back to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 百姓都同声回答说：「凡耶和华所说的，我们都要遵行。」摩西就将百姓的话回复耶和华。

chapters.en:
The LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I will come to you in a dense cloud, so that the people will hear when I speak with you, and they will always put their trust in you.”
And Moses relayed to the LORD what the people had said.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「我要在密云中临到你那里，叫百姓在我与你说话的时候可以听见，也可以永远信你了。」 于是，摩西将百姓的话奏告耶和华。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. They must wash their clothes
chapters.zh: 耶和华又对摩西说：「你往百姓那里去，叫他们今天明天自洁，又叫他们洗衣服。

chapters.en: and be prepared by the third day, for on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.
chapters.zh: 到第三天要预备好了，因为第三天耶和华要在众百姓眼前降临在西奈山上。

chapters.en: And you are to set up a boundary for the people around the mountain and tell them, ‘Be careful not to go up on the mountain or touch its base. Whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.
chapters.zh: 你要在山的四围给百姓定界限，说：『你们当谨慎，不可上山去，也不可摸山的边界；凡摸这山的，必要治死他。

chapters.en:
No hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or shot with arrows—whether man or beast, he must not live.’
Only when the ram’s horn sounds a long blast may they approach the mountain. ”
chapters.zh: 不可用手摸他，必用石头打死，或用〔箭〕射透；无论是人是牲畜，都不得活。到角声拖长的时候，他们才可到山根来。』」

chapters.en: When Moses came down from the mountain to the people, he consecrated them, and they washed their clothes.
chapters.zh: 摩西下山往百姓那里去，叫他们自洁，他们就洗衣服。

chapters.en: “Be prepared for the third day,” he said to the people. “Do not draw near to a woman.”
chapters.zh: 他对百姓说：「到第三天要预备好了。不可亲近女人。」

chapters.en: On the third day, when morning came, there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud was upon the mountain, and a very loud blast of the ram’s horn went out, so that all the people in the camp trembled.
chapters.zh: 到了第三天早晨，在山上有雷轰、闪电，和密云，并且角声甚大，营中的百姓尽都发颤。

chapters.en: Then Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet with God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
chapters.zh: 摩西率领百姓出营迎接上帝，都站在山下。

chapters.en: Mount Sinai was completely enveloped in smoke, because the LORD had descended on it in fire. And the smoke rose like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked violently.
chapters.zh: 西奈全山冒烟，因为耶和华在火中降于山上。山的烟气上腾，如烧窑一般，遍山大大地震动。

chapters.en: And as the sound of the ram’s horn grew louder and louder, Moses spoke and God answered him in the thunder.
chapters.zh: 角声渐渐地高而又高，摩西就说话，上帝有声音答应他。

chapters.en: The LORD descended to the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses to the summit. So Moses went up,
chapters.zh: 耶和华降临在西奈山顶上，耶和华召摩西上山顶，摩西就上去。

chapters.en: and the LORD said to him, “Go down and warn the people not to break through to see the LORD, lest many of them perish.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你下去嘱咐百姓，不可闯过来到我面前观看，恐怕他们有多人死亡；

chapters.en: Even the priests who approach the LORD must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out against them.”
chapters.zh: 又叫亲近我的祭司自洁，恐怕我忽然出来〔击杀〕他们。」

chapters.en: But Moses said to the LORD, “The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, for You solemnly warned us, ‘Put a boundary around the mountain and set it apart as holy.’”
chapters.zh: 摩西对耶和华说：「百姓不能上西奈山，因为你已经嘱咐我们说：『要在山的四围定界限，叫山成圣。』」

chapters.en: And the LORD replied, “Go down and bring Aaron with you. But the priests and the people must not break through to come up to the LORD, or He will break out against them.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对他说：「下去吧，你要和亚伦一同上来；只是祭司和百姓不可闯过来上到我面前，恐怕我忽然出来〔击杀〕他们。」

chapters.en: So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.
chapters.zh: 于是摩西下到百姓那里告诉他们。

chapters.en: And God spoke all these words:
chapters.zh: 上帝吩咐这一切的话说：

chapters.en: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
chapters.zh: 「我是耶和华－你的上帝，曾将你从埃及地为奴之家领出来。

chapters.en: You shall have no other gods before Me.
chapters.zh: 「除了我以外，你不可有别的神。

chapters.en: You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.
chapters.zh: 「不可为自己雕刻偶像，也不可做什么形像仿佛上天、下地，和地底下、水中的〔百物〕。

chapters.en: You shall not bow down to them or worship them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me,
chapters.zh: 不可跪拜那些像，也不可事奉它，因为我耶和华－你的上帝是忌邪的上帝。恨我的，我必追讨他的罪，自父及子，直到三四代；

chapters.en: but showing loving devotion to a thousand generations of those who love Me and keep My commandments.
chapters.zh: 爱我、守我诫命的，我必向他们发慈爱，直到千代。

chapters.en: You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain.
chapters.zh: 「不可妄称耶和华－你上帝的名；因为妄称耶和华名的，耶和华必不以他为无罪。

chapters.en: Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.
chapters.zh: 「当记念安息日，守为圣日。

chapters.en: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
chapters.zh: 六日要劳碌做你一切的工，

chapters.en: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God, on which you must not do any work—neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your manservant or maidservant or livestock, nor the foreigner within your gates.
chapters.zh: 但第七日是向耶和华－你上帝当守的安息日。〔这一日〕你和你的儿女、仆婢、牲畜，并你城里寄居的客旅，无论何工都不可做；

chapters.en: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth and the sea and all that is in them, but on the seventh day He rested. Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy.
chapters.zh: 因为六日之内，耶和华造天、地、海，和其中的万物，第七日便安息，所以耶和华赐福与安息日，定为圣日。

chapters.en: Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
chapters.zh: 「当孝敬父母，使你的日子在耶和华－你上帝所赐你的地上得以长久。

chapters.en: You shall not murder.
chapters.zh: 「不可杀人。

chapters.en: You shall not commit adultery.
chapters.zh: 「不可奸淫。

chapters.en: You shall not steal.
chapters.zh: 「不可偷盗。

chapters.en: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
chapters.zh: 「不可作假见证陷害人。

chapters.en: You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, or his manservant or maidservant, or his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.”
chapters.zh: 「不可贪恋人的房屋；也不可贪恋人的妻子、仆婢、牛驴，并他一切所有的。」

chapters.en: When all the people witnessed the thunder and lightning, the sounding of the ram’s horn, and the mountain enveloped in smoke, they trembled and stood at a distance.
chapters.zh: 众百姓见雷轰、闪电、角声、山上冒烟，就都发颤，远远地站立，

chapters.en: “Speak to us yourself and we will listen,” they said to Moses. “But do not let God speak to us, or we will die.”
chapters.zh: 对摩西说：「求你和我们说话，我们必听；不要上帝和我们说话，恐怕我们死亡。」

chapters.en: “Do not be afraid,” Moses replied. “For God has come to test you, so that the fear of Him may be before you, to keep you from sinning.”
chapters.zh: 摩西对百姓说：「不要惧怕；因为上帝降临是要试验你们，叫你们时常敬畏他，不致犯罪。」

chapters.en: And the people stood at a distance as Moses approached the thick darkness where God was.
chapters.zh: 于是百姓远远地站立；摩西就挨近上帝所在的幽暗之中。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “This is what you are to tell the Israelites: ‘You have seen for yourselves that I have spoken to you from heaven.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你要向以色列人这样说：『你们自己看见我从天上和你们说话了。

chapters.en: You are not to make any gods alongside Me; you are not to make for yourselves gods of silver or gold.
chapters.zh: 你们不可做什么〔神像〕与我相配，不可为自己做金银的神像。

chapters.en: You are to make for Me an altar of earth, and sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and peace offerings, your sheep and goats and cattle. In every place where I cause My name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
chapters.zh: 你要为我筑土坛，在上面以牛羊献为燔祭和平安祭。凡记下我名的地方，我必到那里赐福给你。

chapters.en: Now if you make an altar of stones for Me, you must not build it with stones shaped by tools; for if you use a chisel on it, you will defile it.
chapters.zh: 你若为我筑一座石坛，不可用凿成的石头，因你在上头一动家具，就把坛污秽了。

chapters.en: And you must not go up to My altar on steps, lest your nakedness be exposed on it.’
chapters.zh: 你上我的坛，不可用台阶，免得露出你的下体来。』」

chapters.en: “These are the ordinances that you are to set before them:
chapters.zh: 「你在百姓面前所要立的典章是这样：

chapters.en: If you buy a Hebrew servant, he is to serve you for six years. But in the seventh year, he shall go free without paying anything.
chapters.zh: 你若买希伯来人作奴仆，他必服事你六年；第七年他可以自由，白白地出去。

chapters.en: If he arrived alone, he is to leave alone; if he arrived with a wife, she is to leave with him.
chapters.zh: 他若孤身来就可以孤身去；他若有妻，他的妻就可以同他出去。

chapters.en: If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and her children shall belong to her master, and only the man shall go free.
chapters.zh: 他主人若给他妻子，妻子给他生了儿子或女儿，妻子和儿女要归主人，他要独自出去。

chapters.en: But if the servant declares, ‘I love my master and my wife and children; I do not want to go free,’
chapters.zh: 倘或奴仆明说：『我爱我的主人和我的妻子儿女，不愿意自由出去。』

chapters.en: then his master is to bring him before the judges. And he shall take him to the door or doorpost and pierce his ear with an awl. Then he shall serve his master for life.
chapters.zh: 他的主人就要带他到审判官〔注：或译：上帝；下同〕那里，又要带他到门前，靠近门框，用锥子穿他的耳朵，他就永远服事主人。

chapters.en: And if a man sells his daughter as a servant, she is not to go free as the menservants do.
chapters.zh: 「人若卖女儿作婢女，婢女不可像男仆那样出去。

chapters.en: If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master who had designated her for himself, he must allow her to be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to foreigners, since he has broken faith with her.
chapters.zh: 主人选定她归自己，若不喜欢她，就要许她赎身；主人既然用诡诈待她，就没有权柄卖给外邦人。

chapters.en: And if he chooses her for his son, he must deal with her as with a daughter.
chapters.zh: 主人若选定她给自己的儿子，就当待她如同女儿。

chapters.en: If he takes another wife, he must not reduce the food, clothing, or marital rights of his first wife.
chapters.zh: 若另娶一个，那女子的吃食、衣服，并好合的事，仍不可减少。

chapters.en: If, however, he does not provide her with these three things, she is free to go without monetary payment.
chapters.zh: 若不向她行这三样，她就可以不用钱赎，白白地出去。」

chapters.en: Whoever strikes and kills a man must surely be put to death.
chapters.zh: 「打人以致打死的，必要把他治死。

chapters.en: If, however, he did not lie in wait, but God allowed it to happen, then I will appoint for you a place where he may flee.
chapters.zh: 人若不是埋伏着〔杀人〕，乃是上帝交在他手中，我就设下一个地方，他可以往那里逃跑。

chapters.en: But if a man schemes and acts willfully against his neighbor to kill him, you must take him away from My altar to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 人若任意用诡计杀了他的邻舍，就是逃到我的坛那里，也当捉去把他治死。

chapters.en: Whoever strikes his father or mother must surely be put to death.
chapters.zh: 「打父母的，必要把他治死。

chapters.en: Whoever kidnaps another man must be put to death, whether he sells him or the man is found in his possession.
chapters.zh: 「拐带人口，或是把人卖了，或是留在他手下，必要把他治死。

chapters.en: Anyone who curses his father or mother must surely be put to death.
chapters.zh: 「咒骂父母的，必要把他治死。

chapters.en: If men are quarreling and one strikes the other with a stone or a fist, and he does not die but is confined to bed,
chapters.zh: 「人若彼此相争，这个用石头或是拳头打那个，尚且不至于死，不过躺卧在床，

chapters.en: then the one who struck him shall go unpunished, as long as the other can get up and walk around outside with his staff. Nevertheless, he must compensate the man for his lost work and see that he is completely healed.
chapters.zh: 若再能起来扶杖而出，那打他的可算无罪；但要将他耽误的工夫用钱赔补，并要将他全然医好。

chapters.en: If a man strikes his manservant or maidservant with a rod, and the servant dies by his hand, he shall surely be punished.
chapters.zh: 「人若用棍子打奴仆或婢女，立时死在他的手下，他必要受刑。

chapters.en: However, if the servant gets up after a day or two, the owner shall not be punished, since the servant is his property.
chapters.zh: 若过一两天才死，就可以不受刑，因为是用钱买的。

chapters.en: If men who are fighting strike a pregnant woman and her child is born prematurely, but there is no further injury, he shall surely be fined as the woman’s husband demands and as the court allows.
chapters.zh: 「人若彼此争斗，伤害有孕的妇人，甚至坠胎，随后却无别害，那伤害她的，总要按妇人的丈夫所要的，照审判官所断的，受罚。

chapters.en: But if a serious injury results, then you must require a life for a life—
chapters.zh: 若有别害，就要以命偿命，

chapters.en: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
chapters.zh: 以眼还眼，以牙还牙，以手还手，以脚还脚，

chapters.en: burn for burn, wound for wound, and stripe for stripe.
chapters.zh: 以烙还烙，以伤还伤，以打还打。

chapters.en: If a man strikes and blinds the eye of his manservant or maidservant, he must let the servant go free as compensation for the eye.
chapters.zh: 「人若打坏了他奴仆或是婢女的一只眼，就要因他的眼放他去得以自由。

chapters.en: And if he knocks out the tooth of his manservant or maidservant, he must let the servant go free as compensation for the tooth.
chapters.zh: 若打掉了他奴仆或是婢女的一个牙，就要因他的牙放他去得以自由。」

chapters.en: If an ox gores a man or woman to death, the ox must surely be stoned, and its meat must not be eaten. But the owner of the ox shall not be held responsible.
chapters.zh: 「牛若触死男人或是女人，总要用石头打死那牛，却不可吃牠的肉；牛的主人可算无罪。

chapters.en: But if the ox has a habit of goring, and its owner has been warned yet does not restrain it, and it kills a man or woman, then the ox must be stoned and its owner must also be put to death.
chapters.zh: 倘若那牛素来是触人的，有人报告了牛主，他竟不把牛拴着，以致把男人或是女人触死，就要用石头打死那牛，牛主也必治死。

chapters.en: If payment is demanded of him instead, he may redeem his life by paying the full amount demanded of him.
chapters.zh: 若罚他赎〔命〕的价银，他必照所罚的赎他的命。

chapters.en: If the ox gores a son or a daughter, it shall be done to him according to the same rule.
chapters.zh: 牛无论触了人的儿子或是女儿，必照这例办理。

chapters.en: If the ox gores a manservant or maidservant, the owner must pay thirty shekels of silver to the master of that servant, and the ox must be stoned.
chapters.zh: 牛若触了奴仆或是婢女，必将银子三十舍客勒给他们的主人，也要用石头把牛打死。

chapters.en: If a man opens or digs a pit and fails to cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
chapters.zh: 「人若敞着井口，或挖井不遮盖，有牛或驴掉在里头，

chapters.en: the owner of the pit shall make restitution; he must pay its owner, and the dead animal will be his.
chapters.zh: 井主要拿钱赔还本主人，死牲畜要归自己。

chapters.en: If a man’s ox injures his neighbor’s ox and it dies, they must sell the live one and divide the proceeds; they also must divide the dead animal.
chapters.zh: 「这人的牛若伤了那人的牛，以至于死，他们要卖了活牛，平分价值，也要平分死牛。

chapters.en: But if it was known that the ox had a habit of goring, yet its owner failed to restrain it, he shall pay full compensation, ox for ox, and the dead animal will be his.
chapters.zh: 人若知道这牛素来是触人的，主人竟不把牛拴着，他必要以牛还牛，死牛要归自己。」

chapters.en: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters or sells it, he must repay five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.
chapters.zh: 「人若偷牛或羊，无论是宰了，是卖了，他就要以五牛赔一牛，四羊赔一羊。

chapters.en: If a thief is caught breaking in and is beaten to death, no one shall be guilty of bloodshed.
chapters.zh: 人若遇见贼挖窟窿，把贼打了，以至于死，就不能为他有流血的罪。

chapters.en:
But if it happens after sunrise, there is guilt for his bloodshed.
A thief must make full restitution; if he has nothing, he himself shall be sold for his theft.
chapters.zh: 若太阳已经出来，就为他有流血的罪。贼若被拿，总要赔还。若他一无所有，就要被卖，顶他所偷的物。

chapters.en: If what was stolen is actually found alive in his possession—whether ox or donkey or sheep—he must pay back double.
chapters.zh: 若他所偷的，或牛，或驴，或羊，仍在他手下存活，他就要加倍赔还。

chapters.en: If a man grazes his livestock in a field or vineyard and allows them to stray so that they graze in someone else’s field, he must make restitution from the best of his own field or vineyard.
chapters.zh: 「人若在田间或在葡萄园里放牲畜，任凭牲畜上别人的田里去吃，就必拿自己田间上好的和葡萄园上好的赔还。

chapters.en: If a fire breaks out and spreads to thornbushes so that it consumes stacked or standing grain, or the whole field, the one who started the fire must make full restitution.
chapters.zh: 「若点火焚烧荆棘，以致将别人堆积的禾捆，站着的禾稼，或是田园，都烧尽了，那点火的必要赔还。

chapters.en: If a man gives his neighbor money or goods for safekeeping and they are stolen from the neighbor’s house, the thief, if caught, must pay back double.
chapters.zh: 「人若将银钱或家具交付邻舍看守，这物从那人的家被偷去，若把贼找到了，贼要加倍赔还；

chapters.en: If the thief is not found, the owner of the house must appear before the judges to determine whether he has taken his neighbor’s property.
chapters.zh: 若找不到贼，那家主必就近审判官，要〔看看〕他拿了原主的物件没有。

chapters.en: In all cases of illegal possession of an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost item that someone claims, ‘This is mine,’ both parties shall bring their cases before the judges. The one whom the judges find guilty must pay back double to his neighbor.
chapters.zh: 「两个人的案件，无论是为什么过犯，或是为牛，为驴，为羊，为衣裳，或是为什么失掉之物，有一人说：『这是我的』，两造就要将案件禀告审判官，审判官定谁有罪，谁就要加倍赔还。

chapters.en: If a man gives a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any other animal to be cared for by his neighbor, but it dies or is injured or stolen while no one is watching,
chapters.zh: 「人若将驴，或牛，或羊，或别的牲畜，交付邻舍看守，牲畜或死，或受伤，或被赶去，无人看见，

chapters.en: an oath before the LORD shall be made between the parties to determine whether or not the man has taken his neighbor’s property. The owner must accept the oath and require no restitution.
chapters.zh: 那看守的人要凭着耶和华起誓，手里未曾拿邻舍的物，本主就要罢休，看守的人不必赔还。

chapters.en: But if the animal was actually stolen from the neighbor, he must make restitution to the owner.
chapters.zh: 牲畜若从看守的那里被偷去，他就要赔还本主；

chapters.en: If the animal was torn to pieces, he shall bring it as evidence; he need not make restitution for the torn carcass.
chapters.zh: 若被〔野兽〕撕碎，看守的要带来当作证据，所撕的不必赔还。

chapters.en: If a man borrows an animal from his neighbor and it is injured or dies while its owner is not present, he must make full restitution.
chapters.zh: 「人若向邻舍借什么，所借的或受伤，或死，本主没有同在一处，借的人总要赔还；

chapters.en: If the owner was present, no restitution is required. If the animal was rented, the fee covers the loss.
chapters.zh: 若本主同在一处，他就不必赔还；若是雇的，也不必赔还，本是为雇价来的。」

chapters.en: If a man seduces a virgin who is not pledged in marriage and sleeps with her, he must pay the full dowry for her to be his wife.
chapters.zh: 「人若引诱没有受聘的处女，与她行淫，他总要交出聘礼，娶她为妻。

chapters.en: If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, the man still must pay an amount comparable to the bridal price of a virgin.
chapters.zh: 若女子的父亲决不肯将女子给他，他就要按处女的聘礼，交出钱来。

chapters.en: You must not allow a sorceress to live.
chapters.zh: 「行邪术的女人，不可容她存活。

chapters.en: Whoever lies with an animal must surely be put to death.
chapters.zh: 「凡与兽淫合的，总要把他治死。

chapters.en: If anyone sacrifices to any god other than the LORD alone, he must be set apart for destruction.
chapters.zh: 「祭祀别神，不单单祭祀耶和华的，那人必要灭绝。

chapters.en: You must not exploit or oppress a foreign resident, for you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 「不可亏负寄居的，也不可欺压他，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。

chapters.en: You must not mistreat any widow or orphan.
chapters.zh: 不可苦待寡妇和孤儿；

chapters.en: If you do mistreat them, and they cry out to Me in distress, I will surely hear their cry.
chapters.zh: 若是苦待他们一点，他们向我一哀求，我总要听他们的哀声，

chapters.en: My anger will be kindled, and I will kill you with the sword; then your wives will become widows and your children will be fatherless.
chapters.zh: 并要发烈怒，用刀杀你们，使你们的妻子为寡妇，儿女为孤儿。

chapters.en: If you lend money to one of My people among you who is poor, you must not act as a creditor to him; you are not to charge him interest.
chapters.zh: 「我民中有贫穷人与你同住，你若借钱给他，不可如放债的向他取利。

chapters.en: If you take your neighbor’s cloak as collateral, return it to him by sunset,
chapters.zh: 你即或拿邻舍的衣服作当头，必在日落以先归还他；

chapters.en: because his cloak is the only covering he has for his body. What else will he sleep in? And if he cries out to Me, I will hear, for I am compassionate.
chapters.zh: 因他只有这一件当盖头，是他盖身的衣服，〔若是没有〕，他拿什么睡觉呢？他哀求我，我就应允，因为我是有恩惠的。

chapters.en: You must not blaspheme God or curse the ruler of your people.
chapters.zh: 「不可毁谤上帝；也不可毁谤你百姓的官长。

chapters.en: You must not hold back offerings from your granaries or vats. You are to give Me the firstborn of your sons.
chapters.zh: 「你要从你庄稼中的〔谷〕和〔酒〕醡中滴出来的酒拿来献上，不可迟延。 「你要将头生的儿子归给我。

chapters.en: You shall do likewise with your cattle and your sheep. Let them stay with their mothers for seven days, but on the eighth day you are to give them to Me.
chapters.zh: 你牛羊〔头生的〕，也要这样；七天当跟着母，第八天要归给我。

chapters.en: You are to be My holy people. You must not eat the meat of a mauled animal found in the field; you are to throw it to the dogs.
chapters.zh: 「你们要在我面前为圣洁的人。因此，田间被野兽撕裂牲畜的肉，你们不可吃，要丢给狗吃。」

chapters.en: “You shall not spread a false report. Do not join the wicked by being a malicious witness.
chapters.zh: 「不可随伙布散谣言；不可与恶人连手妄作见证。

chapters.en: You shall not follow the crowd in wrongdoing. When you testify in a lawsuit, do not pervert justice by siding with the crowd.
chapters.zh: 不可随众行恶；不可在争讼的事上随众偏行，作见证屈枉〔正直〕；

chapters.en: And do not show favoritism to a poor man in his lawsuit.
chapters.zh: 也不可在争讼的事上偏护穷人。

chapters.en: If you encounter your enemy’s stray ox or donkey, you must return it to him.
chapters.zh: 「若遇见你仇敌的牛或驴失迷了路，总要牵回来交给他。

chapters.en: If you see the donkey of one who hates you fallen under its load, do not leave it there; you must help him with it.
chapters.zh: 若看见恨你人的驴压卧在重驮之下，不可走开，务要和驴主一同抬开〔重驮〕。

chapters.en: You shall not deny justice to the poor in their lawsuits.
chapters.zh: 「不可在穷人争讼的事上屈枉正直。

chapters.en: Stay far away from a false accusation. Do not kill the innocent or the just, for I will not acquit the guilty.
