chapters.en: with forty silver bases to put under the twenty frames—two bases for each frame, one under each tenon.
chapters.zh: 在这二十块板底下又做四十个带卯的银座：两卯接这块板上的两榫，两卯接那块板上的两榫。

chapters.en: For the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, he made twenty frames
chapters.zh: 帐幕的第二面，就是北面，也做板二十块

chapters.en: and forty silver bases—two bases under each frame.
chapters.zh: 和带卯的银座四十个：这板底下有两卯，那板底下也有两卯。

chapters.en: He made six frames for the rear of the tabernacle, the west side,
chapters.zh: 帐幕的后面，就是西面，做板六块。

chapters.en: and two frames for the two back corners of the tabernacle,
chapters.zh: 帐幕后面的拐角做板两块。

chapters.en: coupled together from bottom to top and fitted into a single ring. He made both corners in this way.
chapters.zh: 板的下半截是双的，上半截是整的，直到第一个环子；在帐幕的两个拐角上都是这样做。

chapters.en: So there were eight frames and sixteen silver bases—two under each frame.
chapters.zh: 有八块板和十六个带卯的银座，每块板底下有两卯。

chapters.en: He also made five crossbars of acacia wood for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,
chapters.zh: 他用皂荚木做闩：为帐幕这面的板做五闩，

chapters.en: five for those on the other side, and five for those on the rear side of the tabernacle, to the west.
chapters.zh: 为帐幕那面的板做五闩，又为帐幕后面的板做五闩，

chapters.en: He made the central crossbar to run through the center of the frames, from one end to the other.
chapters.zh: 使板腰间的中闩从这一头通到那一头。

chapters.en: And he overlaid the frames with gold and made gold rings to hold the crossbars. He also overlaid the crossbars with gold.
chapters.zh: 用金子将板包裹，又做板上的金环套闩；闩也用金子包裹。

chapters.en: Next, he made the veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen, with cherubim skillfully worked into it.
chapters.zh: 他用蓝色、紫色、朱红色〔线〕，和撚的细麻织幔子，以巧匠的手工绣上基路伯。

chapters.en: He also made four posts of acacia wood for it and overlaid them with gold, along with gold hooks; and he cast four silver bases for the posts.
chapters.zh: 为幔子做四根皂荚木柱子，用金包裹，柱子上有金钩，又为柱子铸了四个带卯的银座。

chapters.en: For the entrance to the tent, he made a curtain embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen,
chapters.zh: 拿蓝色、紫色、朱红色〔线〕，和撚的细麻，用绣花的手工织帐幕的门帘；

chapters.en:
together with five posts and their hooks.
He overlaid the tops of the posts and their bands with gold, and their five bases were bronze.
chapters.zh: 又为帘子做五根柱子和柱子上的钩子，用金子把柱顶和柱子上的杆子包裹。柱子有五个带卯的座，是铜的。

chapters.en: Bezalel went on to construct the ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
chapters.zh: 比撒列用皂荚木做柜，长二肘半，宽一肘半，高一肘半。

chapters.en: He overlaid it with pure gold, both inside and out, and made a gold molding around it.
chapters.zh: 里外包上精金，四围镶上金牙边，

chapters.en: And he cast four gold rings for its four feet, two rings on one side and two on the other.
chapters.zh: 又铸四个金环，安在柜的四脚上：这边两环，那边两环。

chapters.en: Then he made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
chapters.zh: 用皂荚木做两根杠，用金包裹。

chapters.en: He inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark in order to carry it.
chapters.zh: 把杠穿在柜旁的环内，以便抬柜。

chapters.en: He constructed a mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
chapters.zh: 用精金做施恩座，长二肘半，宽一肘半。

chapters.en: He made two cherubim of hammered gold at the ends of the mercy seat,
chapters.zh: 用金子锤出两个基路伯来，安在施恩座的两头，

chapters.en: one cherub on one end and one on the other, all made from one piece of gold.
chapters.zh: 这头做一个基路伯，那头做一个基路伯，二基路伯接连一块，在施恩座的两头。

chapters.en: And the cherubim had wings that spread upward, overshadowing the mercy seat. The cherubim faced each other, looking toward the mercy seat.
chapters.zh: 二基路伯高张翅膀，遮掩施恩座；基路伯是脸对脸，朝着施恩座。

chapters.en: He also made the table of acacia wood two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
chapters.zh: 他用皂荚木做一张桌子，长二肘，宽一肘，高一肘半，

chapters.en: He overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold molding around it.
chapters.zh: 又包上精金，四围镶上金牙边。

chapters.en: And he made a rim around it a handbreadth wide and put a gold molding on the rim.
chapters.zh: 桌子的四围各做一掌宽的横梁，横梁上镶着金牙边，

chapters.en: He cast four gold rings for the table and fastened them to the four corners at its four legs.
chapters.zh: 又铸了四个金环，安在桌子四脚的四角上。

chapters.en: The rings were placed close to the rim, to serve as holders for the poles used to carry the table.
chapters.zh: 安环子的地方是挨近横梁，可以穿杠抬桌子。

chapters.en: He made the poles of acacia wood for carrying the table and overlaid them with gold.
chapters.zh: 他用皂荚木做两根杠，用金包裹，以便抬桌子；

chapters.en: He also made the utensils for the table out of pure gold: its plates and dishes, as well as its bowls and pitchers for pouring drink offerings.
chapters.zh: 又用精金做桌子上的器皿，就是盘子、调羹，并奠〔酒〕的瓶和爵。

chapters.en: Then he made the lampstand out of pure hammered gold, all of one piece: its base and shaft, its cups, and its buds and petals.
chapters.zh: 他用精金做一个灯台；这灯台的座和干，与杯、球、花，都是接连一块锤出来的。

chapters.en: Six branches extended from the sides, three on one side and three on the other.
chapters.zh: 灯台两旁杈出六个枝子：这旁三个，那旁三个。

chapters.en: There were three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the first branch, each with buds and petals, three on the next branch, and the same for all six branches that extended from the lampstand.
chapters.zh: 这旁每枝上有三个杯，形状像杏花，有球有花；那旁每枝上也有三个杯，形状像杏花，有球有花。从灯台杈出来的六个枝子都是如此。

chapters.en: And on the lampstand were four cups shaped like almond blossoms with buds and petals.
chapters.zh: 灯台上有四个杯，形状像杏花，有球有花。

chapters.en: A bud was under the first pair of branches that extended from the lampstand, a bud under the second pair, and a bud under the third pair.
chapters.zh: 灯台每两个枝子以下有球，与枝子接连一块；灯台杈出的六个枝子都是如此。

chapters.en: The buds and branches were all of one piece with the lampstand, hammered out of pure gold.
chapters.zh: 球和枝子是接连一块，都是一块精金锤出来的。

chapters.en: He also made its seven lamps, its wick trimmers, and trays of pure gold.
chapters.zh: 用精金做灯台的七个灯盏，并灯台的蜡剪和蜡花盘。

chapters.en: He made the lampstand and all its utensils from a talent of pure gold.
chapters.zh: 他用精金一他连得做灯台和灯台的一切器具。

chapters.en: He made the altar of incense out of acacia wood. It was square, a cubit long, a cubit wide, and two cubits high. Its horns were of one piece.
chapters.zh: 他用皂荚木做香坛，是四方的，长一肘，宽一肘，高二肘，坛的四角与坛接连一块；

chapters.en: And he overlaid with pure gold the top and all the sides and horns. Then he made a molding of gold around it.
chapters.zh: 又用精金把坛的上面与坛的四面并坛的四角包裹，又在坛的四围镶上金牙边。

chapters.en: He made two gold rings below the molding on opposite sides to hold the poles used to carry it.
chapters.zh: 做两个金环，安在牙子边以下，在坛的两旁、两根横撑上，作为穿杠的用处，以便抬坛。

chapters.en: And he made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
chapters.zh: 用皂荚木做杠，用金包裹。

chapters.en: He also made the sacred anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer.
chapters.zh: 又按做香之法做圣膏油和馨香料的净香。

chapters.en: Bezalel constructed the altar of burnt offering from acacia wood. It was square, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high.
chapters.zh: 他用皂荚木做燔祭坛，是四方的，长五肘，宽五肘，高三肘，

chapters.en: He made a horn at each of its four corners, so that the horns and altar were of one piece, and he overlaid the altar with bronze.
chapters.zh: 在坛的四拐角上做四个角，与坛接连一块，用铜把坛包裹。

chapters.en: He made all the altar’s utensils of bronze—its pots, shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks, and firepans.
chapters.zh: 他做坛上的盆、铲子、盘子、肉锸子、火鼎；这一切器具都是用铜做的。

chapters.en: He made a grate of bronze mesh for the altar under its ledge, halfway up from the bottom.
chapters.zh: 又为坛做一个铜网，安在坛四面的围腰板以下，从下达到坛的半腰。

chapters.en: At the four corners of the bronze grate he cast four rings as holders for the poles.
chapters.zh: 为铜网的四角铸四个环子，作为穿杠的用处。

chapters.en: And he made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.
chapters.zh: 用皂荚木做杠，用铜包裹，

chapters.en: Then he inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar for carrying it. He made the altar with boards so that it was hollow.
chapters.zh: 把杠穿在坛两旁的环子内，用以抬坛，并用板做坛；坛是空的。

chapters.en: Next he made the bronze basin and its stand from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 他用铜做洗濯盆和盆座，是用会幕门前伺候的妇人之镜子做的。

chapters.en: Then he constructed the courtyard. The south side of the courtyard was a hundred cubits long and had curtains of finely spun linen,
chapters.zh: 他做〔帐幕〕的院子。院子的南面用撚的细麻做帷子，〔宽〕一百肘。

chapters.en: with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and with silver hooks and bands on the posts.
chapters.zh: 帷子的柱子二十根，带卯的铜座二十个；柱子上的钩子和杆子都是用银子做的。

chapters.en: The north side was also a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases. The hooks and bands of the posts were silver.
chapters.zh: 北面也〔有帷子〕，〔宽〕一百肘。帷子的柱子二十根，带卯的铜座二十个；柱子上的钩子和杆子都是用银子做的。

chapters.en: The west side was fifty cubits long and had curtains, with ten posts and ten bases. The hooks and bands of the posts were silver.
chapters.zh: 〔院子的〕西面有帷子，〔宽〕五十肘。帷子的柱子十根，带卯的座十个；柱子的钩子和杆子都是用银子做的。

chapters.en: And the east side, toward the sunrise, was also fifty cubits long.
chapters.zh: 〔院子的〕东面，〔宽〕五十肘。

chapters.en: The curtains on one side of the entrance were fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
And the curtains on the other side were also fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases as well.
chapters.zh: 门这边的帷子十五肘，那边也是一样。帷子的柱子三根，带卯的座三个。在门的左右各有帷子十五肘，帷子的柱子三根，带卯的座三个。

chapters.en: All the curtains around the courtyard were made of finely spun linen.
chapters.zh: 院子四面的帷子都是用撚的细麻做的。

chapters.en: The bases for the posts were bronze, the hooks and bands were silver, and the plating for the tops of the posts was silver. So all the posts of the courtyard were banded with silver.
chapters.zh: 柱子带卯的座是铜的，柱子上的钩子和杆子是银的，柱顶是用银子包的。院子一切的柱子都是用银杆连络的。

chapters.en: The curtain for the entrance to the courtyard was embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen. It was twenty cubits long and, like the curtains of the courtyard, five cubits high,
chapters.zh: 院子的门帘是以绣花的手工，用蓝色、紫色、朱红色〔线〕，和撚的细麻织的，宽二十肘，高五肘，与院子的帷子相配。

chapters.en: with four posts and four bronze bases. Their hooks were silver, as well as the bands and the plating of their tops.
chapters.zh: 帷子的柱子四根，带卯的铜座四个；柱子上的钩子和杆子是银的；柱顶是用银子包的。

chapters.en: All the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the surrounding courtyard were bronze.
chapters.zh: 帐幕一切的橛子和院子四围的橛子都是铜的。

chapters.en: This is the inventory for the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the Testimony, as recorded at Moses’ command by the Levites under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
chapters.zh: 这是法〔柜〕的帐幕中利未人所用〔物件〕的总数，是照摩西的吩咐，经祭司亚伦的儿子以他玛的手数点的。

chapters.en: Bezalel son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything that the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 凡耶和华所吩咐摩西的都是犹大支派户珥的孙子、乌利的儿子比撒列做的。

chapters.en: With him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver, designer, and embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen.
chapters.zh: 与他同工的有但支派中亚希撒抹的儿子亚何利亚伯；他是雕刻匠，又是巧匠，又能用蓝色、紫色、朱红色〔线〕，和细麻绣花。

chapters.en: All the gold from the wave offering used for the work on the sanctuary totaled 29 talents and 730 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
chapters.zh: 为圣所一切工作使用所献的金子，按圣所的平，有二十九他连得并七百三十舍客勒。

chapters.en: The silver from those numbered among the congregation totaled 100 talents and 1,775 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel—
chapters.zh: 会中被数的人所出的银子，按圣所的平，有一百他连得并一千七百七十五舍客勒。

chapters.en: a beka per person, that is, half a shekel, according to the sanctuary shekel, from everyone twenty years of age or older who had crossed over to be numbered, a total of 603,550 men.
chapters.zh: 凡过去归那些被数之人的，从二十岁以外，有六十万零三千五百五十人。按圣所的平，每人出银半舍客勒，就是一比加。

chapters.en: The hundred talents of silver were used to cast the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the veil—100 bases from the 100 talents, one talent per base.
chapters.zh: 用那一百他连得银子铸造圣所带卯的座和幔子〔柱子〕带卯的座；一百他连得共一百带卯的座，每带卯的座用一他连得。

chapters.en: With the 1,775 shekels of silver he made the hooks for the posts, overlaid their tops, and supplied bands for them.
chapters.zh: 用那一千七百七十五〔舍客勒银子〕做柱子上的钩子，包裹柱顶并柱子上的杆子。

chapters.en: The bronze from the wave offering totaled 70 talents and 2,400 shekels.
chapters.zh: 所献的铜有七十他连得并二千四百舍客勒。

chapters.en: He used it to make the bases for the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar and its bronze grating, all the utensils for the altar,
chapters.zh: 用这铜做会幕门带卯的座和铜坛，并坛上的铜网和坛的一切器具，

chapters.en: the bases for the surrounding courtyard and its gate, and all the tent pegs for the tabernacle and its surrounding courtyard.
chapters.zh: 并院子四围带卯的座和院门带卯的座，与帐幕一切的橛子和院子四围所有的橛子。

chapters.en: From the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn they made specially woven garments for ministry in the sanctuary, as well as the holy garments for Aaron, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 比撒列用蓝色、紫色、朱红色〔线〕做精致的衣服，在圣所用以供职，又为亚伦做圣衣，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: Bezalel made the ephod of finely spun linen embroidered with gold, and with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
chapters.zh: 他用金〔线〕和蓝色、紫色、朱红色〔线〕，并撚的细麻做以弗得；

chapters.en: They hammered out thin sheets of gold and cut threads from them to interweave with the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen—the work of a skilled craftsman.
chapters.zh: 把金子锤成薄片，剪出线来，与蓝色、紫色、朱红色〔线〕，用巧匠的手工一同绣上。

chapters.en: They made shoulder pieces for the ephod, which were attached at two of its corners, so it could be fastened.
chapters.zh: 又为以弗得做两条相连的肩带，接连在以弗得的两头。

chapters.en: And the skillfully woven waistband of the ephod was of one piece with the ephod, of the same workmanship—with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 其上巧工织的带子和以弗得一样的做法，用以束上，与以弗得接连一块，是用金〔线〕和蓝色、紫色、朱红色〔线〕，并撚的细麻做的，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: They mounted the onyx stones in gold filigree settings, engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.
chapters.zh: 又琢出两块红玛瑙，镶在金槽上，仿佛刻图书，按着以色列儿子的名字雕刻；

chapters.en: Then they fastened them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 将这两块宝石安在以弗得的两条肩带上，为以色列人做纪念石，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: He made the breastpiece with the same workmanship as the ephod, with gold, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and with finely spun linen.
chapters.zh: 他用巧匠的手工做胸牌，和以弗得一样的做法，用金〔线〕与蓝色、紫色、朱红色〔线〕，并撚的细麻做的。

chapters.en: It was square when folded over double, a span long and a span wide.
chapters.zh: 胸牌是四方的，叠为两层；这两层长一虎口，宽一虎口，

chapters.en:
And they mounted on it four rows of gemstones:
The first row had a ruby, a topaz, and an emerald;
chapters.zh: 上面镶着宝石四行：第一行是红宝石、红璧玺、红玉；

chapters.en: the second row had a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
chapters.zh: 第二行是绿宝石、蓝宝石、金钢石；

chapters.en: the third row had a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
chapters.zh: 第三行是紫玛瑙、白玛瑙、紫晶；

chapters.en:
and the fourth row had a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper.
These stones were mounted in gold filigree settings.
chapters.zh: 第四行是水苍玉、红玛瑙、碧玉。这都镶在金槽中。

chapters.en: The twelve stones corresponded to the names of the sons of Israel. Each stone was engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
chapters.zh: 这些宝石都是按着以色列十二个儿子的名字，仿佛刻图书，刻十二个支派的名字。

chapters.en: For the breastpiece they made braided chains like cords of pure gold.
chapters.zh: 在胸牌上，用精金拧成如绳子的鍊子。

chapters.en: They also made two gold filigree settings and two gold rings, and fastened the two rings to the two corners of the breastpiece.
chapters.zh: 又做两个金槽和两个金环，安在胸牌的两头。

chapters.en: Then they fastened the two gold chains to the two gold rings at the corners of the breastpiece,
chapters.zh: 把那两条拧成的金鍊子穿过胸牌两头的环子，

chapters.en: and they fastened the other ends of the two chains to the two filigree settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
chapters.zh: 又把鍊子的那两头接在两槽上，安在以弗得前面肩带上。

chapters.en: They made two more gold rings and attached them to the other two corners of the breastpiece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.
chapters.zh: 做两个金环，安在胸牌的两头，在以弗得里面的边上，

chapters.en: They made two additional gold rings and attached them to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on its front, near the seam just above its woven waistband.
chapters.zh: 又做两个金环，安在以弗得前面两条肩带的下边，挨近相接之处，在以弗得巧工织的带子以上。

chapters.en: Then they tied the rings of the breastpiece to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue yarn, so that the breastpiece was above the waistband of the ephod and would not swing out from the ephod, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 用一条蓝细带子把胸牌的环子和以弗得的环子系住，使胸牌贴在以弗得巧工织的带子上，不可与以弗得离缝，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: They made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth, the work of a weaver,
chapters.zh: 他用织工做以弗得的外袍，颜色全是蓝的。

chapters.en: with an opening in the center of the robe like that of a garment, with a collar around the opening so that it would not tear.
chapters.zh: 袍上留一领口，口的周围织出领边来，仿佛铠甲的领口，免得破裂。

chapters.en: They made pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen on the lower hem of the robe.
chapters.zh: 在袍子底边上，用蓝色、紫色、朱红色〔线〕，并撚的〔细麻〕做石榴，

chapters.en: They also made bells of pure gold and attached them around the hem between the pomegranates,
chapters.zh: 又用精金做铃铛，把铃铛钉在袍子周围底边上的石榴中间：

chapters.en: alternating the bells and pomegranates around the lower hem of the robe to be worn for ministry, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 一个铃铛一个石榴，一个铃铛一个石榴，在袍子周围底边上用以供职，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: For Aaron and his sons they made tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver,
chapters.zh: 他用织成的细麻布为亚伦和他的儿子做内袍，

chapters.en: as well as the turban of fine linen, the ornate headbands and undergarments of finely spun linen,
chapters.zh: 并用细麻布做冠冕和华美的裹头巾，用撚的细麻布做裤子，

chapters.en: and the sash of finely spun linen, embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 又用蓝色、紫色、朱红色〔线〕，并撚的细麻，以绣花的手工做腰带，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en:
They also made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and they engraved on it, like an inscription on a seal:
HOLY TO THE LORD.
chapters.zh: 他用精金做圣冠上的牌，在上面按刻图书之法，刻着「归耶和华为圣」。

chapters.en: Then they fastened to it a blue cord to mount it on the turban, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 又用一条蓝细带子将牌系在冠冕上，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: So all the work for the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, was completed. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 帐幕，就是会幕，一切的工就这样做完了。凡耶和华所吩咐摩西的，以色列人都照样做了。

chapters.en:
Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses:
the tent with all its furnishings, its clasps, its frames, its crossbars, and its posts and bases;
chapters.zh: 他们送到摩西那里。帐幕和帐幕的一切器具，就是钩子、板、闩、柱子、带卯的座，

chapters.en: the covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, and the veil of the covering;
chapters.zh: 染红公羊皮的盖、海狗皮的顶盖，和遮掩〔柜〕的幔子，

chapters.en: the ark of the Testimony with its poles and the mercy seat;
chapters.zh: 法柜和柜的杠并施恩座，

chapters.en: the table with all its utensils and the Bread of the Presence;
chapters.zh: 桌子和桌子的一切器具并陈设饼，

chapters.en: the pure gold lampstand with its row of lamps and all its utensils, as well as the oil for the light;
chapters.zh: 精〔金〕的灯台和摆列的灯盏，与灯台的一切器具，并点灯的油，

chapters.en: the gold altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance to the tent;
chapters.zh: 金坛、膏油、馨香的香料、会幕的门帘，

chapters.en:
the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles, and all its utensils;
the basin with its stand;
chapters.zh: 铜坛和坛上的铜网，坛的杠并坛的一切器具，洗濯盆和盆座，

chapters.en:
the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases;
the curtain for the gate of the courtyard, its ropes and tent pegs, and all the equipment for the service of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting;
chapters.zh: 院子的帷子和柱子，并带卯的座，院子的门帘、绳子、橛子，并帐幕和会幕中一切使用的器具，

chapters.en: and the woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary, both the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.
chapters.zh: 精工做的礼服，和祭司亚伦并他儿子在圣所用以供祭司职分的圣衣。

chapters.en: The Israelites had done all the work just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 这一切工作都是以色列人照耶和华所吩咐摩西做的。

chapters.en: And Moses inspected all the work and saw that they had accomplished it just as the LORD had commanded. So Moses blessed them.
chapters.zh: 耶和华怎样吩咐的，他们就怎样做了。摩西看见一切的工都做成了，就给他们祝福。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “On the first day of the first month you are to set up the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 「正月初一日，你要立起帐幕，

chapters.en: Put the ark of the Testimony in it and screen off the ark with the veil.
chapters.zh: 把法柜安放在里面，用幔子将柜遮掩。

chapters.en: Then bring in the table and set out its arrangement; bring in the lampstand as well, and set up its lamps.
chapters.zh: 把桌子搬进去，摆设上面的物。把灯台搬进去，点其上的灯。

chapters.en: Place the gold altar of incense in front of the ark of the Testimony, and hang the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 把〔烧〕香的金坛安在法柜前，挂上帐幕的门帘。

chapters.en: Place the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance to the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 把燔祭坛安在帐幕门前。

chapters.en: And place the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
chapters.zh: 把洗濯盆安在会幕和坛的中间，在盆里盛水。

chapters.en: Set up the surrounding courtyard and hang the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard.
chapters.zh: 又在四围立院帷，把院子的门帘挂上。

chapters.en: Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it; consecrate it along with all its furnishings, and it shall be holy.
chapters.zh: 用膏油把帐幕和其中所有的都抹上，使帐幕和一切器具成圣，就都成圣。

chapters.en: Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils; consecrate the altar, and it shall be most holy.
chapters.zh: 又要抹燔祭坛和一切器具，使坛成圣，就都成为至圣。

chapters.en: Anoint the basin and its stand and consecrate them.
chapters.zh: 要抹洗濯盆和盆座，使盆成圣。

chapters.en: Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water.
chapters.zh: 要使亚伦和他儿子到会幕门口来，用水洗身。

chapters.en: And you are to clothe Aaron with the holy garments, anoint him, and consecrate him, so that he may serve Me as a priest.
chapters.zh: 要给亚伦穿上圣衣，又膏他，使他成圣，可以给我供祭司的职分；

chapters.en: Bring his sons forward and clothe them with tunics.
chapters.zh: 又要使他儿子来，给他们穿上内袍。

chapters.en: Anoint them just as you anointed their father, so that they may also serve Me as priests. Their anointing will qualify them for a permanent priesthood throughout their generations.”
chapters.zh: 怎样膏他们的父亲，也要照样膏他们，使他们给我供祭司的职分。他们世世代代凡受膏的，就永远当祭司的职任。」

chapters.en: Moses did everything just as the LORD had commanded him.
chapters.zh: 摩西这样行，都是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: So the tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month of the second year.
chapters.zh: 第二年正月初一日，帐幕就立起来。

chapters.en: When Moses set up the tabernacle, he laid its bases, positioned its frames, inserted its crossbars, and set up its posts.
chapters.zh: 摩西立起帐幕，安上带卯的座，立上板，穿上闩，立起柱子。

chapters.en: Then he spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering over the tent, just as the LORD had commanded him.
chapters.zh: 在帐幕以上搭罩棚，把罩棚的顶盖盖在其上，是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: Moses took the Testimony and placed it in the ark, attaching the poles to the ark; and he set the mercy seat atop the ark.
chapters.zh: 又把法〔版〕放在柜里，把杠穿在柜的两旁，把施恩座安在柜上。

chapters.en: Then he brought the ark into the tabernacle, put up the veil for the screen, and shielded off the ark of the Testimony, just as the LORD had commanded him.
chapters.zh: 把柜抬进帐幕，挂上遮掩〔柜〕的幔子，把法柜遮掩了，是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: Moses placed the table in the Tent of Meeting on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the veil.
chapters.zh: 又把桌子安在会幕内，在帐幕北边，在幔子外。

chapters.en: He arranged the bread on it before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded him.
chapters.zh: 在桌子上将饼陈设在耶和华面前，是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: He also placed the lampstand in the Tent of Meeting opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle
chapters.zh: 又把灯台安在会幕内，在帐幕南边，与桌子相对，

chapters.en: and set up the lamps before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded him.
chapters.zh: 在耶和华面前点灯，是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: Moses placed the gold altar in the Tent of Meeting, in front of the veil,
chapters.zh: 把金坛安在会幕内的幔子前，

chapters.en: and he burned fragrant incense on it, just as the LORD had commanded him.
chapters.zh: 在坛上烧了馨香料做的香，是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: Then he put up the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 又挂上帐幕的门帘。

chapters.en: He placed the altar of burnt offering near the entrance to the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, and offered on it the burnt offering and the grain offering, just as the LORD had commanded him.
chapters.zh: 在会幕的帐幕门前，安设燔祭坛，把燔祭和素祭献在其上，是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: He placed the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar and put water in it for washing;
chapters.zh: 把洗濯盆安在会幕和坛的中间，盆中盛水，以便洗濯。

chapters.en: and from it Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet.
chapters.zh: 摩西和亚伦并亚伦的儿子在这盆里洗手洗脚。

chapters.en: They washed whenever they entered the Tent of Meeting or approached the altar, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 他们进会幕或就近坛的时候，便都洗濯，是照耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: And Moses set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and the altar, and he hung the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard. So Moses finished the work.
chapters.zh: 在帐幕和坛的四围立了院帷，把院子的门帘挂上。这样，摩西就完了工。

chapters.en: Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 当时，云彩遮盖会幕，耶和华的荣光就充满了帐幕。

chapters.en: Moses was unable to enter the Tent of Meeting because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 摩西不能进会幕；因为云彩停在其上，并且耶和华的荣光充满了帐幕。

chapters.en: Whenever the cloud was lifted from above the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out through all the stages of their journey.
chapters.zh: 每逢云彩从帐幕收上去，以色列人就起程前往；

chapters.en: If the cloud was not lifted, they would not set out until the day it was taken up.
chapters.zh: 云彩若不收上去，他们就不起程，直等到云彩收上去。

chapters.en: For the cloud of the LORD was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in the cloud by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel through all their journeys.
chapters.zh: 日间，耶和华的云彩是在帐幕以上；夜间，云中有火，在以色列全家的眼前。在他们所行的路上都是这样。

chapters.en: Then the LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying,
chapters.zh: 耶和华从会幕中呼叫摩西，对他说：

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When any of you brings an offering to the LORD, you may bring as your offering an animal from the herd or the flock.
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：你们中间若有人献供物给耶和华，要从牛群羊群中献牲畜为供物。

chapters.en: If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he is to present an unblemished male. He must bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting for its acceptance before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「他的供物若以牛为燔祭，就要在会幕门口献一只没有残疾的公牛，可以在耶和华面前蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: He is to lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, so it can be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for him.
chapters.zh: 他要按手在燔祭牲的头上，燔祭便蒙悦纳，为他赎罪。

chapters.en: And he shall slaughter the young bull before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons the priests are to present the blood and splatter it on all sides of the altar at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 他要在耶和华面前宰公牛；亚伦子孙作祭司的，要奉上血，把血洒在会幕门口、坛的周围。

chapters.en: Next, he is to skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
chapters.zh: 那人要剥去燔祭牲的皮，把燔祭牲切成块子。

chapters.en: The sons of Aaron the priest shall put a fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
chapters.zh: 祭司亚伦的子孙要把火放在坛上，把柴摆在火上。

chapters.en: Then Aaron’s sons the priests are to arrange the pieces, including the head and the fat, atop the burning wood on the altar.
chapters.zh: 亚伦子孙作祭司的，要把肉块和头并脂油摆在坛上火的柴上。

chapters.en: The entrails and legs must be washed with water, and the priest shall burn all of it on the altar as a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 但燔祭的脏腑与腿要用水洗。祭司就要把一切全烧在坛上，当作燔祭，献与耶和华为馨香的火祭。

chapters.en: If, however, one’s offering is a burnt offering from the flock—from the sheep or goats—he is to present an unblemished male.
chapters.zh: 「人的供物若以绵羊或山羊为燔祭，就要献上没有残疾的公羊。

chapters.en: He shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons the priests are to splatter its blood against the altar on all sides.
chapters.zh: 要把羊宰于坛的北边，在耶和华面前；亚伦子孙作祭司的，要把羊血洒在坛的周围。

chapters.en: He is to cut the animal into pieces, and the priest shall arrange them, including the head and fat, atop the burning wood that is on the altar.
chapters.zh: 要把燔祭牲切成块子，连头和脂油，祭司就要摆在坛上火的柴上；

chapters.en: The entrails and legs must be washed with water, and the priest shall present all of it and burn it on the altar; it is a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 但脏腑与腿要用水洗，祭司就要全然奉献，烧在坛上。这是燔祭，是献与耶和华为馨香的火祭。

chapters.en: If, instead, one’s offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, he is to present a turtledove or a young pigeon.
chapters.zh: 「人奉给耶和华的供物，若以鸟为燔祭，就要献斑鸠或是雏鸽为供物。

chapters.en: Then the priest shall bring it to the altar, twist off its head, and burn it on the altar; its blood should be drained out on the side of the altar.
chapters.zh: 祭司要把鸟拿到坛前，揪下头来，把鸟烧在坛上；鸟的血要流在坛的旁边；

chapters.en: And he is to remove the crop with its contents and throw it to the east side of the altar, in the place for ashes.
chapters.zh: 又要把鸟的嗉子和脏物〔注：脏物：或译翎毛〕除掉，丢在坛的东边〔倒〕灰的地方。

chapters.en: He shall tear it open by its wings, without dividing the bird completely. And the priest is to burn it on the altar atop the burning wood. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 要拿着鸟的两个翅膀，把鸟撕开，只是不可撕断；祭司要在坛上、在火的柴上焚烧。这是燔祭，是献与耶和华为馨香的火祭。」

chapters.en: “When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, his offering must consist of fine flour. He is to pour olive oil on it, put frankincense on it,
chapters.zh: 「若有人献素祭为供物给耶和华，要用细面浇上油，加上乳香，

chapters.en: and bring it to Aaron’s sons the priests. The priest shall take a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the frankincense, and burn this as a memorial portion on the altar, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 带到亚伦子孙作祭司的那里；祭司就要从细面中取出一把来，并取些油和所有的乳香，然后要把所取的这些作为纪念，烧在坛上，是献与耶和华为馨香的火祭。

chapters.en: The remainder of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the food offerings to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 素祭所剩的要归给亚伦和他的子孙；这是献与耶和华的火祭中为至圣的。

chapters.en: Now if you bring an offering of grain baked in an oven, it must consist of fine flour, either unleavened cakes mixed with oil or unleavened wafers coated with oil.
chapters.zh: 「若用炉中烤的物为素祭，就要用调油的无酵细面饼，或是抹油的无酵薄饼。

chapters.en: If your offering is a grain offering prepared on a griddle, it must be unleavened bread made of fine flour mixed with oil.
chapters.zh: 若用铁鏊上做的物为素祭，就要用调油的无酵细面，

chapters.en: Crumble it and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.
chapters.zh: 分成块子，浇上油；这是素祭。

chapters.en: If your offering is a grain offering cooked in a pan, it must consist of fine flour with oil.
chapters.zh: 若用煎盘做的物为素祭，就要用油与细面做成。

chapters.en: When you bring to the LORD the grain offering made in any of these ways, it is to be presented to the priest, and he shall take it to the altar.
chapters.zh: 要把这些东西做的素祭带到耶和华面前，并奉给祭司，带到坛前。

chapters.en: The priest is to remove the memorial portion from the grain offering and burn it on the altar as a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司要从素祭中取出作为纪念的，烧在坛上，是献与耶和华为馨香的火祭。

chapters.en: But the remainder of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the food offerings to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 素祭所剩的要归给亚伦和他的子孙。这是献与耶和华的火祭中为至圣的。

chapters.en: No grain offering that you present to the LORD may be made with leaven, for you are not to burn any leaven or honey as a food offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「凡献给耶和华的素祭都不可有酵；因为你们不可烧一点酵、一点蜜当作火祭献给耶和华。

chapters.en: You may bring them to the LORD as an offering of firstfruits, but they must not go up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
chapters.zh: 这些物要献给耶和华作为初熟的供物，只是不可在坛上献为馨香的祭。

chapters.en: And you shall season each of your grain offerings with salt. You must not leave the salt of the covenant of your God out of your grain offering; you are to add salt to each of your offerings.
chapters.zh: 凡献为素祭的供物都要用盐调和，在素祭上不可缺了你上帝立约的盐。一切的供物都要配盐而献。

chapters.en: If you bring a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, you shall offer crushed heads of new grain roasted on the fire.
chapters.zh: 若向耶和华献初熟之物为素祭，要献上烘了的禾穗子，就是轧了的新穗子，当作初熟之物的素祭。

chapters.en: And you are to put oil and frankincense on it; it is a grain offering.
chapters.zh: 并要抹上油，加上乳香；这是素祭。

chapters.en: The priest shall then burn the memorial portion of the crushed grain and the oil, together with all its frankincense, as a food offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司要把其中作为纪念的，就是一些轧了的禾穗子和一些油，并所有的乳香，都焚烧，是向耶和华献的火祭。」

chapters.en: “If one’s offering is a peace offering and he offers an animal from the herd, whether male or female, he must present it without blemish before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「人献供物为平安祭〔注：平安：或译酬恩；下同〕，若是从牛群中献，无论是公的是母的，必用没有残疾的献在耶和华面前。

chapters.en: He is to lay his hand on the head of the offering and slaughter it at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Then Aaron’s sons the priests shall splatter the blood on all sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 他要按手在供物的头上，宰于会幕门口。亚伦子孙作祭司的，要把血洒在坛的周围。

chapters.en: From the peace offering he is to bring a food offering to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails, all the fat that is on them,
chapters.zh: 从平安祭中，将火祭献给耶和华，也要把盖脏的脂油和脏上所有的脂油，

chapters.en: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys.
chapters.zh: 并两个腰子和腰子上的脂油，就是靠腰两旁的脂油，与肝上的网子和腰子，一概取下。

chapters.en: Then Aaron’s sons are to burn it on the altar atop the burnt offering that is on the burning wood, as a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 亚伦的子孙要把这些烧在坛的燔祭上，就是在火的柴上，是献与耶和华为馨香的火祭。

chapters.en: If, however, one’s peace offering to the LORD is from the flock, he must present a male or female without blemish.
chapters.zh: 「人向耶和华献供物为平安祭，若是从羊群中献，无论是公的是母的，必用没有残疾的。

chapters.en: If he is presenting a lamb for his offering, he must present it before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 若献一只羊羔为供物，必在耶和华面前献上，

chapters.en: He is to lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it in front of the Tent of Meeting. Then Aaron’s sons shall splatter its blood on all sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 并要按手在供物的头上，宰于会幕前。亚伦的子孙要把血洒在坛的周围。

chapters.en: And from the peace offering he shall bring a food offering to the LORD consisting of its fat: the entire fat tail cut off close to the backbone, the fat that covers the entrails, all the fat that is on them,
chapters.zh: 从平安祭中，将火祭献给耶和华，其中的脂油和整肥尾巴都要在靠近脊骨处取下，并要把盖脏的脂油和脏上所有的脂油，

chapters.en: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys.
chapters.zh: 两个腰子和腰子上的脂油，就是靠腰两旁的脂油，并肝上的网子和腰子，一概取下。

chapters.en: Then the priest is to burn them on the altar as food, a food offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司要在坛上焚烧，是献给耶和华为食物的火祭。

chapters.en: If one’s offering is a goat, he is to present it before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「人的供物若是山羊，必在耶和华面前献上。

chapters.en: He must lay his hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the Tent of Meeting. Then Aaron’s sons shall splatter its blood on all sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 要按手在山羊头上，宰于会幕前。亚伦的子孙要把血洒在坛的周围，

chapters.en: And from his offering he shall present a food offering to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails, all the fat that is on them,
both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys.
chapters.zh: 又把盖脏的脂油和脏上所有的脂油，两个腰子和腰子上的脂油，就是靠腰两旁的脂油，并肝上的网子和腰子，一概取下，献给耶和华为火祭。

chapters.en: Then the priest is to burn the food on the altar as a food offering, a pleasing aroma. All the fat is the LORD’s.
chapters.zh: 祭司要在坛上焚烧，作为馨香火祭的食物。脂油都是耶和华的。

chapters.en: This is a permanent statute for the generations to come, wherever you live: You must not eat any fat or any blood.”
chapters.zh: 在你们一切的住处，脂油和血都不可吃；这要成为你们世世代代永远的定例。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Tell the Israelites to do as follows with one who sins unintentionally against any of the LORD’s commandments and does what is forbidden by them:
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：若有人在耶和华所吩咐不可行的什么事上误犯了一件，

chapters.en: If the anointed priest sins, bringing guilt on the people, he must bring to the LORD a young bull without blemish as a sin offering for the sin he has committed.
chapters.zh: 或是受膏的祭司犯罪，使百姓陷在罪里，就当为他所犯的罪把没有残疾的公牛犊献给耶和华为赎罪祭。

chapters.en: He must bring the bull to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting before the LORD, lay his hand on the bull’s head, and slaughter it before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 他要牵公牛到会幕门口，在耶和华面前按手在牛的头上，把牛宰于耶和华面前。

chapters.en: Then the anointed priest shall take some of the bull’s blood and bring it into the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 受膏的祭司要取些公牛的血带到会幕，

chapters.en: The priest is to dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of it seven times before the LORD, in front of the veil of the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 把指头蘸于血中，在耶和华面前对着圣所的幔子弹血七次，

chapters.en: The priest must then put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense that is before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting. And he is to pour out the rest of the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 又要把些血抹在会幕内、耶和华面前香坛的四角上，再把公牛所有的血倒在会幕门口、燔祭坛的脚那里。

chapters.en: Then he shall remove all the fat from the bull of the sin offering—the fat that covers the entrails, all the fat that is on them,
chapters.zh: 要把赎罪祭公牛所有的脂油，乃是盖脏的脂油和脏上所有的脂油，

chapters.en: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys—
chapters.zh: 并两个腰子和腰子上的脂油，就是靠腰两旁的脂油，与肝上的网子和腰子，一概取下，

chapters.en: just as the fat is removed from the ox of the peace offering. Then the priest shall burn them on the altar of burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 与平安祭公牛上所取的一样；祭司要把这些烧在燔祭的坛上。

chapters.en: But the hide of the bull and all its flesh, with its head and legs and its entrails and dung—
chapters.zh: 公牛的皮和所有的肉，并头、腿、脏、腑、粪，

chapters.en: all the rest of the bull—he must take outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place where the ashes are poured out, and there he must burn it on a wood fire on the ash heap.
chapters.zh: 就是全公牛，要搬到营外洁净之地、倒灰之所，用火烧在柴上。

chapters.en: Now if the whole congregation of Israel strays unintentionally and the matter escapes the notice of the assembly so that they violate any of the LORD’s commandments and incur guilt by doing what is forbidden,
chapters.zh: 「以色列全会众若行了耶和华所吩咐不可行的什么事，误犯了罪，是隐而未现、会众看不出来的，

chapters.en: when they become aware of the sin they have committed, then the assembly must bring a young bull as a sin offering and present it before the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 会众一知道所犯的罪就要献一只公牛犊为赎罪祭，牵到会幕前。

chapters.en: The elders of the congregation are to lay their hands on the bull’s head before the LORD, and it shall be slaughtered before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 会中的长老就要在耶和华面前按手在牛的头上，将牛在耶和华面前宰了。

chapters.en: Then the anointed priest is to bring some of the bull’s blood into the Tent of Meeting,
chapters.zh: 受膏的祭司要取些公牛的血带到会幕，

chapters.en: and he is to dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD in front of the veil.
chapters.zh: 把指头蘸于血中，在耶和华面前对着幔子弹血七次，

chapters.en: He is also to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that is before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting, and he must pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 又要把些血抹在会幕内、耶和华面前坛的四角上，再把所有的血倒在会幕门口、燔祭坛的脚那里。

chapters.en: And he is to remove all the fat from it and burn it on the altar.
chapters.zh: 把牛所有的脂油都取下，烧在坛上；

chapters.en: He shall offer this bull just as he did the bull for the sin offering; in this way the priest will make atonement on their behalf, and they will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 收拾这牛，与那赎罪祭的牛一样。祭司要为他们赎罪，他们必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: Then he is to take the bull outside the camp and burn it, just as he burned the first bull. It is the sin offering for the assembly.
chapters.zh: 他要把牛搬到营外烧了，像烧头一个牛一样；这是会众的赎罪祭。

chapters.en: When a leader sins unintentionally and does what is prohibited by any of the commandments of the LORD his God, he incurs guilt.
chapters.zh: 「官长若行了耶和华－他上帝所吩咐不可行的什么事，误犯了罪，

chapters.en: When he becomes aware of the sin he has committed, he must bring an unblemished male goat as his offering.
chapters.zh: 所犯的罪自己知道了，就要牵一只没有残疾的公山羊为供物，

chapters.en: He is to lay his hand on the head of the goat and slaughter it at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the LORD. It is a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 按手在羊的头上，宰于耶和华面前、宰燔祭牲的地方；这是赎罪祭。

chapters.en: Then the priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
chapters.zh: 祭司要用指头蘸些赎罪祭牲的血，抹在燔祭坛的四角上，把血倒在燔祭坛的脚那里。

chapters.en: He must burn all its fat on the altar, like the fat of the peace offerings; thus the priest will make atonement for that man’s sin, and he will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 所有的脂油，祭司都要烧在坛上，正如平安祭的脂油一样。至于他的罪，祭司要为他赎了，他必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: And if one of the common people sins unintentionally and does what is prohibited by any of the LORD’s commandments, he incurs guilt.
chapters.zh: 「民中若有人行了耶和华所吩咐不可行的什么事，误犯了罪，

chapters.en: When he becomes aware of the sin he has committed, he must bring an unblemished female goat as his offering for that sin.
chapters.zh: 所犯的罪自己知道了，就要为所犯的罪牵一只没有残疾的母山羊为供物，

chapters.en: He is to lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it at the place of the burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 按手在赎罪祭牲的头上，在那宰燔祭牲的地方宰了。

chapters.en: Then the priest is to take some of its blood with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
chapters.zh: 祭司要用指头蘸些羊的血，抹在燔祭坛的四角上，所有的血都要倒在坛的脚那里，

chapters.en: Then he is to remove all the fat, just as it is removed from the peace offering, and the priest is to burn it on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. In this way the priest will make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 又要把羊所有的脂油都取下，正如取平安祭牲的脂油一样。祭司要在坛上焚烧，在耶和华面前作为馨香〔的祭〕，为他赎罪，他必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: If, however, he brings a lamb as a sin offering, he must bring an unblemished female.
chapters.zh: 「人若牵一只绵羊羔为赎罪祭的供物，必要牵一只没有残疾的母羊，

chapters.en: And he is to lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it as a sin offering at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
chapters.zh: 按手在赎罪祭牲的头上，在那宰燔祭牲的地方宰了作赎罪祭。

chapters.en: Then the priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.
chapters.zh: 祭司要用指头蘸些赎罪祭牲的血，抹在燔祭坛的四角上，所有的血都要倒在坛的脚那里，

chapters.en: And he shall remove all the fat, just as the fat of the lamb is removed from the peace offerings, and he shall burn it on the altar along with the food offerings to the LORD. In this way the priest will make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 又要把所有的脂油都取下，正如取平安祭羊羔的脂油一样。祭司要按献给耶和华火祭的条例，烧在坛上。至于所犯的罪，祭司要为他赎了，他必蒙赦免。」

chapters.en: “If someone sins by failing to testify when he hears a public charge about something he has witnessed, whether he has seen it or learned of it, he shall bear the iniquity.
chapters.zh: 「若有人听见发誓的声音〔注：或译：若有人听见叫人发誓的声音〕，他本是见证，却不把所看见的、所知道的说出来，这就是罪；他要担当他的罪孽。

chapters.en: Or if a person touches anything unclean—whether the carcass of any unclean wild animal or livestock or crawling creature—even if he is unaware of it, he is unclean and guilty.
chapters.zh: 或是有人摸了不洁的物，无论是不洁的死兽，是不洁的死畜，是不洁的死虫，他却不知道，因此成了不洁，就有了罪。

chapters.en: Or if he touches human uncleanness—anything by which one becomes unclean—even if he is unaware of it, when he realizes it, he is guilty.
chapters.zh: 或是他摸了别人的污秽，无论是染了什么污秽，他却不知道，一知道了就有了罪。

chapters.en: Or if someone swears thoughtlessly with his lips to do anything good or evil—in whatever matter a man may rashly pronounce an oath—even if he is unaware of it, when he realizes it, he is guilty in the matter.
chapters.zh: 或是有人嘴里冒失发誓，要行恶，要行善，无论人在什么事上冒失发誓，他却不知道，一知道了就要在这其中的一件上有了罪。

chapters.en: If someone incurs guilt in one of these ways, he must confess the sin he has committed,
chapters.zh: 他有了罪的时候，就要承认所犯的罪，

chapters.en: and he must bring his guilt offering to the LORD for the sin he has committed: a female lamb or goat from the flock as a sin offering. And the priest will make atonement for him concerning his sin.
chapters.zh: 并要因所犯的罪，把他的赎愆祭牲－就是羊群中的母羊，或是一只羊羔，或是一只山羊－牵到耶和华面前为赎罪祭。至于他的罪，祭司要为他赎了。

chapters.en: If, however, he cannot afford a lamb, he may bring to the LORD as restitution for his sin two turtledoves or two young pigeons—one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 「他的力量若不够献一只羊羔，就要因所犯的罪，把两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽带到耶和华面前为赎愆祭：一只作赎罪祭，一只作燔祭。

chapters.en: He is to bring them to the priest, who shall first present the one for the sin offering. He is to twist its head at the front of its neck without severing it;
chapters.zh: 把这些带到祭司那里，祭司就要先把那赎罪祭献上，从鸟的颈项上揪下头来，只是不可把鸟撕断，

chapters.en: then he is to sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, while the rest of the blood is drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 也把些赎罪祭牲的血弹在坛的旁边，剩下的血要流在坛的脚那里；这是赎罪祭。

chapters.en: And the priest must prepare the second bird as a burnt offering according to the ordinance. In this way the priest will make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 他要照例献第二只为燔祭。至于他所犯的罪，祭司要为他赎了，他必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: But if he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he may bring a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He must not put olive oil or frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 「他的力量若不够献两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽，就要因所犯的罪带供物来，就是细面伊法十分之一为赎罪祭；不可加上油，也不可加上乳香，因为是赎罪祭。

chapters.en: He is to bring it to the priest, who shall take a handful from it as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar atop the food offerings to the LORD; it is a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 他要把供物带到祭司那里，祭司要取出自己的一把来作为纪念，按献给耶和华火祭的条例烧在坛上；这是赎罪祭。

chapters.en: In this way the priest will make atonement for him for any of these sins he has committed, and he will be forgiven. The remainder will belong to the priest, like the grain offering.”
chapters.zh: 至于他在这几件事中所犯的罪，祭司要为他赎了，他必蒙赦免。〔剩下的面〕都归与祭司，和素祭一样。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “If someone acts unfaithfully and sins unintentionally against any of the LORD’s holy things, he must bring his guilt offering to the LORD: an unblemished ram from the flock, of proper value in silver shekels according to the sanctuary shekel; it is a guilt offering.
chapters.zh: 「人若在耶和华的圣物上误犯了罪，有了过犯，就要照你所估的，按圣所的舍客勒拿银子，将赎愆祭牲－就是羊群中一只没有残疾的公绵羊－牵到耶和华面前为赎愆祭；

chapters.en: Regarding any holy thing he has harmed, he must make restitution by adding a fifth of its value to it and giving it to the priest, who will make atonement on his behalf with the ram as a guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 并且他因在圣物上的差错要偿还，另外加五分之一，都给祭司。祭司要用赎愆祭的公绵羊为他赎罪，他必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: If someone sins and violates any of the LORD’s commandments even though he was unaware, he is guilty and shall bear his punishment.
chapters.zh: 「若有人犯罪，行了耶和华所吩咐不可行的什么事，他虽然不知道，还是有了罪，就要担当他的罪孽；

chapters.en: He is to bring to the priest an unblemished ram of proper value from the flock as a guilt offering. Then the priest will make atonement on his behalf for the wrong he has committed in ignorance, and he will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 也要照你所估定的价，从羊群中牵一只没有残疾的公绵羊来，给祭司作赎愆祭。至于他误行的那错事，祭司要为他赎罪，他必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: It is a guilt offering; he was certainly guilty before the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 这是赎愆祭，因他在耶和华面前实在有了罪。」

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “If someone sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving his neighbor in regard to a deposit or security entrusted to him or stolen, or if he extorts his neighbor
chapters.zh: 「若有人犯罪，干犯耶和华，在邻舍交付他的物上，或是在交易上行了诡诈，或是抢夺人的财物，或是欺压邻舍，

chapters.en: or finds lost property and lies about it and swears falsely, or if he commits any such sin that a man might commit—
chapters.zh: 或是在捡了遗失的物上行了诡诈，说谎起誓，在这一切的事上犯了什么罪；

chapters.en: once he has sinned and becomes guilty, he must return what he has stolen or taken by extortion, or the deposit entrusted to him, or the lost property he found,
chapters.zh: 他既犯了罪，有了过犯，就要归还他所抢夺的，或是因欺压所得的，或是人交付他的，或是人遗失他所捡的物，

chapters.en:
or anything else about which he has sworn falsely.
He must make restitution in full, add a fifth of the value, and pay it to the owner on the day he acknowledges his guilt.
chapters.zh: 或是他因什么物起了假誓，就要如数归还，另外加上五分之一，在查出他有罪的日子要交还本主。

chapters.en: Then he must bring to the priest his guilt offering to the LORD: an unblemished ram of proper value from the flock.
chapters.zh: 也要照你所估定的价，把赎愆祭牲－就是羊群中一只没有残疾的公绵羊－牵到耶和华面前，给祭司为赎愆祭。

chapters.en: In this way the priest will make atonement for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for anything he may have done to incur guilt.”
chapters.zh: 祭司要在耶和华面前为他赎罪；他无论行了什么事，使他有了罪，都必蒙赦免。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Command Aaron and his sons that this is the law of the burnt offering: The burnt offering is to remain on the hearth of the altar all night, until morning, and the fire must be kept burning on the altar.
chapters.zh: 「你要吩咐亚伦和他的子孙说，燔祭的条例乃是这样：燔祭要放在坛的柴上，从晚上到天亮，坛上的火要常常烧着。

chapters.en: And the priest shall put on his linen robe and linen undergarments, and he shall remove from the altar the ashes of the burnt offering that the fire has consumed and place them beside it.
chapters.zh: 祭司要穿上细麻布衣服，又要把细麻布裤子穿在身上，把坛上所烧的燔祭灰收起来，倒在坛的旁边；

chapters.en: Then he must take off his garments, put on other clothes, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a ceremonially clean place.
chapters.zh: 随后要脱去这衣服，穿上别的衣服，把灰拿到营外洁净之处。

chapters.en: The fire on the altar shall be kept burning; it must not be extinguished. Every morning the priest is to add wood to the fire, arrange the burnt offering on it, and burn the fat portions of the peace offerings on it.
chapters.zh: 坛上的火要在其上常常烧着，不可熄灭。祭司要每日早晨在上面烧柴，并要把燔祭摆在坛上，在其上烧平安祭牲的脂油。

chapters.en: The fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it must not be extinguished.
chapters.zh: 在坛上必有常常烧着的火，不可熄灭。」

chapters.en: Now this is the law of the grain offering: Aaron’s sons shall present it before the LORD in front of the altar.
chapters.zh: 「素祭的条例乃是这样：亚伦的子孙要在坛前把这祭献在耶和华面前。

chapters.en: The priest is to remove a handful of fine flour and olive oil, together with all the frankincense from the grain offering, and burn the memorial portion on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司要从其中－就是从素祭的细面中－取出自己的一把，又要取些油和素祭上所有的乳香，烧在坛上，奉给耶和华为馨香素祭的纪念。

chapters.en: Aaron and his sons are to eat the remainder. It must be eaten without leaven in a holy place; they are to eat it in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 所剩下的，亚伦和他子孙要吃，必在圣处不带酵而吃，要在会幕的院子里吃。

chapters.en: It must not be baked with leaven; I have assigned it as their portion of My food offerings. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
chapters.zh: 〔烤的时候〕不可搀酵。这是从所献给我的火祭中赐给他们的分，是至圣的，和赎罪祭并赎愆祭一样。

chapters.en: Any male among the sons of Aaron may eat it. This is a permanent portion from the food offerings to the LORD for the generations to come. Anything that touches them will become holy.”
chapters.zh: 凡献给耶和华的火祭，亚伦子孙中的男丁都要吃这一分，直到万代，作他们永得的分。摸这些祭物的，都要成为圣。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “This is the offering that Aaron and his sons must present to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half in the evening.
chapters.zh: 「当亚伦受膏的日子，他和他子孙所要献给耶和华的供物，就是细面伊法十分之一，为常献的素祭：早晨一半，晚上一半。

chapters.en: It shall be prepared with oil on a griddle; you are to bring it well-kneaded and present it as a grain offering broken in pieces, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 要在铁鏊上用油调和做成，调匀了，你就拿进来；烤好了分成块子，献给耶和华为馨香的素祭。

chapters.en: The priest, who is one of Aaron’s sons and will be anointed to take his place, is to prepare it. As a permanent portion for the LORD, it must be burned completely.
chapters.zh: 亚伦的子孙中，接续他为受膏的祭司，要把这素祭献上，要全烧给耶和华。这是永远的定例。

chapters.en: Every grain offering for a priest shall be burned completely; it is not to be eaten.”
chapters.zh: 祭司的素祭都要烧了，却不可吃。」

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Tell Aaron and his sons that this is the law of the sin offering: In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering shall be slaughtered before the LORD; it is most holy.
chapters.zh: 「你对亚伦和他的子孙说，赎罪祭的条例乃是这样：要在耶和华面前、宰燔祭牲的地方宰赎罪祭牲；这是至圣的。

chapters.en: The priest who offers it shall eat it; it must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 为赎罪献这祭的祭司要吃，要在圣处，就是在会幕的院子里吃。

chapters.en: Anything that touches its flesh will become holy, and if any of the blood is spattered on a garment, you must wash it in a holy place.
chapters.zh: 凡摸这祭肉的要成为圣；这祭牲的血若弹在什么衣服上，所弹的那一件要在圣处洗净。

chapters.en: The clay pot in which the sin offering is boiled must be broken; if it is boiled in a bronze pot, the pot must be scoured and rinsed with water.
chapters.zh: 惟有煮祭物的瓦器要打碎；若是煮在铜器里，这铜器要擦磨，在水中涮净。

chapters.en: Any male among the priests may eat it; it is most holy.
chapters.zh: 凡祭司中的男丁都可以吃；这是至圣的。

chapters.en: But no sin offering may be eaten if its blood has been brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place; it must be burned.
chapters.zh: 凡赎罪祭，若将血带进会幕在圣所赎罪，那肉都不可吃，必用火焚烧。」

chapters.en: “Now this is the law of the guilt offering, which is most holy:
chapters.zh: 「赎愆祭的条例乃是如此：这祭是至圣的。

chapters.en: The guilt offering must be slaughtered in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and the priest shall splatter its blood on all sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 人在那里宰燔祭牲，也要在那里宰赎愆祭牲；其血，祭司要洒在坛的周围。

chapters.en: And all the fat from it shall be offered: the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails,
chapters.zh: 又要将肥尾巴和盖脏的脂油，

chapters.en: both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which is to be removed with the kidneys.
chapters.zh: 两个腰子和腰子上的脂油，就是靠腰两旁的脂油，并肝上的网子和腰子，一概取下。

chapters.en: The priest shall burn them on the altar as a food offering to the LORD; it is a guilt offering.
chapters.zh: 祭司要在坛上焚烧，为献给耶和华的火祭，是赎愆祭。

chapters.en: Every male among the priests may eat of it. It must be eaten in a holy place; it is most holy.
chapters.zh: 祭司中的男丁都可以吃这祭物；要在圣处吃，是至圣的。

chapters.en: The guilt offering is like the sin offering; the same law applies to both. It belongs to the priest who makes atonement with it.
chapters.zh: 赎罪祭怎样，赎愆祭也是怎样，两个祭是一个条例。献赎愆祭赎罪的祭司要得这祭物。

chapters.en: As for the priest who presents a burnt offering for anyone, the hide of that offering belongs to him.
chapters.zh: 献燔祭的祭司，无论为谁奉献，要亲自得他所献那燔祭牲的皮。

chapters.en: Likewise, every grain offering that is baked in an oven or cooked in a pan or on a griddle belongs to the priest who presents it,
chapters.zh: 凡在炉中烤的素祭和煎盘中做的，并铁鏊上做的，都要归那献祭的祭司。

chapters.en: and every grain offering, whether dry or mixed with oil, belongs equally to all the sons of Aaron.
chapters.zh: 凡素祭，无论是油调和的是干的，都要归亚伦的子孙，大家均分。」

chapters.en: Now this is the law of the peace offering that one may present to the LORD:
chapters.zh: 「人献与耶和华平安祭的条例乃是这样：

chapters.en: If he offers it in thanksgiving, then along with the sacrifice of thanksgiving he shall offer unleavened cakes mixed with olive oil, unleavened wafers coated with oil, and well-kneaded cakes of fine flour mixed with oil.
chapters.zh: 他若为感谢献上，就要用调油的无酵饼和抹油的无酵薄饼，并用油调匀细面做的饼，与感谢祭一同献上。

chapters.en: Along with his peace offering of thanksgiving he is to present an offering with cakes of leavened bread.
chapters.zh: 要用有酵的饼和为感谢献的平安祭，与供物一同献上。

chapters.en: From the cakes he must present one portion of each offering as a contribution to the LORD. It belongs to the priest who sprinkles the blood of the peace offering.
chapters.zh: 从各样的供物中，他要把一个饼献给耶和华为举祭，是要归给洒平安祭牲血的祭司。

chapters.en: The meat of the sacrifice of his peace offering of thanksgiving must be eaten on the day he offers it; none of it may be left until morning.
chapters.zh: 为感谢献平安祭牲的肉，要在献的日子吃，一点不可留到早晨。

chapters.en: If, however, the sacrifice he offers is a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day he presents his sacrifice, but the remainder may be eaten on the next day.
chapters.zh: 若所献的是为还愿，或是甘心献的，必在献祭的日子吃，所剩下的第二天也可以吃。

chapters.en: But any meat of the sacrifice remaining until the third day must be burned up.
chapters.zh: 但所剩下的祭肉，到第三天要用火焚烧；

chapters.en: If any of the meat from his peace offering is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted. It will not be credited to the one who presented it; it shall be an abomination, and the one who eats of it shall bear his iniquity.
chapters.zh: 第三天若吃了平安祭的肉，这祭必不蒙悦纳，人所献的也不算为祭，反为可憎嫌的，吃这祭肉的，就必担当他的罪孽。

chapters.en: Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten; it is to be burned up. As for any other meat, anyone who is ceremonially clean may eat it.
chapters.zh: 「挨了污秽物的肉就不可吃，要用火焚烧。至于平安祭的肉，凡洁净的人都要吃；

chapters.en: But if anyone who is unclean eats meat from the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people.
chapters.zh: 只是献与耶和华平安祭的肉，人若不洁净而吃了，这人必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: If one touches anything unclean, whether human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean, detestable thing, and then eats any of the meat of the peace offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people.”
chapters.zh: 有人摸了什么不洁净的物，或是人的不洁净，或是不洁净的牲畜，或是不洁可憎之物，吃了献与耶和华平安祭的肉，这人必从民中剪除。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘You are not to eat any of the fat of an ox, a sheep, or a goat.
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：牛的脂油、绵羊的脂油、山羊的脂油，你们都不可吃。

chapters.en: The fat of an animal found dead or mauled by wild beasts may be used for any other purpose, but you must not eat it.
chapters.zh: 自死的和被野兽撕裂的，那脂油可以做别的使用，只是你们万不可吃。

chapters.en: If anyone eats the fat of an animal from which a food offering may be presented to the LORD, the one who eats it must be cut off from his people.
chapters.zh: 无论何人吃了献给耶和华当火祭牲畜的脂油，那人必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: You must not eat the blood of any bird or animal in any of your dwellings.
chapters.zh: 在你们一切的住处，无论是雀鸟的血是野兽的血，你们都不可吃。

chapters.en: If anyone eats blood, that person must be cut off from his people.’”
chapters.zh: 无论是谁吃血，那人必从民中剪除。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘Anyone who presents a peace offering to the LORD must bring it as his sacrifice to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：献平安祭给耶和华的，要从平安祭中取些来奉给耶和华。

chapters.en: With his own hands he is to bring the food offerings to the LORD; he shall bring the fat, together with the breast, and wave the breast as a wave offering before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 他亲手献给耶和华的火祭，就是脂油和胸，要带来，好把胸在耶和华面前作摇祭，摇一摇。

chapters.en: The priest is to burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
chapters.zh: 祭司要把脂油在坛上焚烧，但胸要归亚伦和他的子孙。

chapters.en: And you are to give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your peace offering.
chapters.zh: 你们要从平安祭中把右腿作举祭，奉给祭司。

chapters.en: The son of Aaron who presents the blood and fat of the peace offering shall have the right thigh as a portion.
chapters.zh: 亚伦子孙中，献平安祭牲血和脂油的，要得这右腿为分；

chapters.en: I have taken from the sons of Israel the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution of their peace offerings, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a permanent portion from the sons of Israel.’”
chapters.zh: 因为我从以色列人的平安祭中，取了这摇的胸和举的腿给祭司亚伦和他子孙，作他们从以色列人中所永得的分。」

chapters.en: This is the portion of the food offerings to the LORD for Aaron and his sons since the day they were presented to serve the LORD as priests.
chapters.zh: 这是从耶和华火祭中，作亚伦受膏的分和他子孙受膏的分，正在摩西〔注：原文是他〕叫他们前来给耶和华供祭司职分的日子，

chapters.en: On the day they were anointed, the LORD commanded that this be given them by the sons of Israel. It is a permanent portion for the generations to come.
chapters.zh: 就是在摩西〔注：原文是他〕膏他们的日子，耶和华吩咐以色列人给他们的。这是他们世世代代永得的分。

chapters.en: This is the law of the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the peace offering,
chapters.zh: 这就是燔祭、素祭、赎罪祭、赎愆祭，和平安祭的条例，并承接圣职的礼，

chapters.en: which the LORD gave Moses on Mount Sinai on the day He commanded the Israelites to present their offerings to the LORD in the Wilderness of Sinai.
chapters.zh: 都是耶和华在西奈山所吩咐摩西的，就是他在西奈旷野吩咐以色列人献供物给耶和华之日所说的。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Take Aaron and his sons, their garments, the anointing oil, the bull of the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread,
chapters.zh: 「你将亚伦和他儿子一同带来，并将圣衣、膏油，与赎罪祭的一只公牛、两只公绵羊、一筐无酵饼都带来，

chapters.en: and assemble the whole congregation at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.”
chapters.zh: 又招聚会众到会幕门口。」

chapters.en: So Moses did as the LORD had commanded him, and the assembly gathered at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 摩西就照耶和华所吩咐的行了；于是会众聚集在会幕门口。

chapters.en: And Moses said to them, “This is what the LORD has commanded to be done.”
chapters.zh: 摩西告诉会众说：「这就是耶和华所吩咐当行的事。」

chapters.en: Then Moses presented Aaron and his sons and washed them with water.
chapters.zh: 摩西带了亚伦和他儿子来，用水洗了他们。

chapters.en: He put the tunic on Aaron, tied the sash around him, clothed him with the robe, and put the ephod on him. He tied the woven band of the ephod around him and fastened it to him.
chapters.zh: 给亚伦穿上内袍，束上腰带，穿上外袍，又加上以弗得，用其上巧工织的带子把以弗得系在他身上，

chapters.en: Then he put the breastpiece on him and placed the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece.
chapters.zh: 又给他戴上胸牌，把乌陵和土明放在胸牌内，

chapters.en: Moses also put the turban on Aaron’s head and set the gold plate, the holy diadem, on the front of the turban, as the LORD had commanded him.
chapters.zh: 把冠冕戴在他头上，在冠冕的前面钉上金牌，就是圣冠，都是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: Next, Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it; and so he consecrated them.
chapters.zh: 摩西用膏油抹帐幕和其中所有的，使它成圣；

chapters.en: He sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times, anointing the altar and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand, to consecrate them.
chapters.zh: 又用膏油在坛上弹了七次，又抹了坛和坛的一切器皿，并洗濯盆和盆座，使它成圣；

chapters.en: He also poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head and anointed him to consecrate him.
chapters.zh: 又把膏油倒在亚伦的头上膏他，使他成圣。

chapters.en: Then Moses presented Aaron’s sons, put tunics on them, wrapped sashes around them, and tied headbands on them, just as the LORD had commanded him.
chapters.zh: 摩西带了亚伦的儿子来，给他们穿上内袍，束上腰带，包上裹头巾，都是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: Moses then brought the bull near for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
chapters.zh: 他牵了赎罪祭的公牛来，亚伦和他儿子按手在赎罪祭公牛的头上，

chapters.en: Moses slaughtered the bull, took some of the blood, and applied it with his finger to all four horns of the altar, purifying the altar. He poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar and consecrated it so that atonement could be made on it.
chapters.zh: 就宰了公牛。摩西用指头蘸血，抹在坛上四角的周围，使坛洁净，把血倒在坛的脚那里，使坛成圣，坛就洁净了；

chapters.en: Moses also took all the fat that was on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys and their fat, and burned it all on the altar.
chapters.zh: 又取脏上所有的脂油和肝上的网子，并两个腰子与腰子上的脂油，都烧在坛上；

chapters.en: But the bull with its hide, flesh, and dung he burned outside the camp, as the LORD had commanded him.
chapters.zh: 惟有公牛，连皮带肉并粪，用火烧在营外，都是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: Then Moses presented the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
chapters.zh: 他奉上燔祭的公绵羊；亚伦和他儿子按手在羊的头上，

chapters.en: Moses slaughtered the ram and splattered the blood on all sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 就宰了公羊。摩西把血洒在坛的周围，

chapters.en: He cut the ram into pieces and burned the head, the pieces, and the fat.
chapters.zh: 把羊切成块子，把头和肉块并脂油都烧了。

chapters.en: He washed the entrails and legs with water and burned the entire ram on the altar as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 用水洗了脏腑和腿，就把全羊烧在坛上为馨香的燔祭，是献给耶和华的火祭，都是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: After that, Moses presented the other ram, the ram of ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
chapters.zh: 他又奉上第二只公绵羊，就是承接圣职之礼的羊；亚伦和他儿子按手在羊的头上，

chapters.en: Moses slaughtered the ram and took some of its blood and put it on Aaron’s right earlobe, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
chapters.zh: 就宰了羊。摩西把些血抹在亚伦的右耳垂上和右手的大拇指上，并右脚的大拇指上，

chapters.en: Moses also presented Aaron’s sons and put some of the blood on their right earlobes, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then he splattered the blood on all sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 又带了亚伦的儿子来，把些血抹在他们的右耳垂上和右手的大拇指上，并右脚的大拇指上，又把血洒在坛的周围。

chapters.en: And Moses took the fat—the fat tail, all the fat that was on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and both kidneys with their fat—as well as the right thigh.
chapters.zh: 取脂油和肥尾巴，并脏上一切的脂油与肝上的网子，两个腰子和腰子上的脂油，并右腿，

chapters.en: And from the basket of unleavened bread that was before the LORD, he took one cake of unleavened bread, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer, and he placed them on the fat portions and on the right thigh.
chapters.zh: 再从耶和华面前、盛无酵饼的筐子里取出一个无酵饼，一个油饼，一个薄饼，都放在脂油和右腿上，

chapters.en: He put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved them before the LORD as a wave offering.
chapters.zh: 把这一切放在亚伦的手上和他儿子的手上作摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇。

chapters.en: Then Moses took these from their hands and burned them on the altar with the burnt offering. This was an ordination offering, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 摩西从他们的手上拿下来，烧在坛上的燔祭上，都是为承接圣职献给耶和华馨香的火祭。

chapters.en: He also took the breast—Moses’ portion of the ram of ordination—and waved it before the LORD as a wave offering, as the LORD had commanded him.
chapters.zh: 摩西拿羊的胸作为摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇，是承接圣职之礼，归摩西的分，都是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: Next, Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood that was on the altar and sprinkled them on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. So he consecrated Aaron and his garments, as well as Aaron’s sons and their garments.
chapters.zh: 摩西取点膏油和坛上的血，弹在亚伦和他的衣服上，并他儿子和他儿子的衣服上，使他和他们的衣服一同成圣。

chapters.en: And Moses said to Aaron and his sons, “Boil the meat at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and eat it there with the bread that is in the basket of ordination offerings, as I commanded, saying, ‘Aaron and his sons are to eat it.’
chapters.zh: 摩西对亚伦和他儿子说：「把肉煮在会幕门口，在那里吃，又吃承接圣职筐子里的饼，按我所吩咐的说〔注：或译：按所吩咐我的说〕：『这是亚伦和他儿子要吃的。』

chapters.en: Then you must burn up the remainder of the meat and bread.
chapters.zh: 剩下的肉和饼，你们要用火焚烧。

chapters.en: You must not go outside the entrance to the Tent of Meeting for seven days, until the days of your ordination are complete; for it will take seven days to ordain you.
chapters.zh: 你们七天不可出会幕的门，等到你们承接圣职的日子满了，因为主叫你们七天承接圣职。

chapters.en: What has been done today has been commanded by the LORD in order to make atonement on your behalf.
chapters.zh: 像今天所行的都是耶和华吩咐行的，为你们赎罪。

chapters.en: You must remain at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting day and night for seven days and keep the LORD’s charge so that you will not die, for this is what I have been commanded.”
chapters.zh: 七天你们要昼夜住在会幕门口，遵守耶和华的吩咐，免得你们死亡，因为所吩咐我的就是这样。」

chapters.en: So Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD had commanded through Moses.
chapters.zh: 于是亚伦和他儿子行了耶和华藉着摩西所吩咐的一切事。

chapters.en: On the eighth day Moses summoned Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.
chapters.zh: 到了第八天，摩西召了亚伦和他儿子，并以色列的众长老来，

chapters.en: He said to Aaron, “Take for yourself a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, both without blemish, and present them before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 对亚伦说：「你当取牛群中的一只公牛犊作赎罪祭，一只公绵羊作燔祭，都要没有残疾的，献在耶和华面前。

chapters.en: Then speak to the Israelites and say, ‘Take a male goat for a sin offering, a calf and a lamb—both a year old and without blemish—for a burnt offering,
chapters.zh: 你也要对以色列人说：『你们当取一只公山羊作赎罪祭，又取一只牛犊和一只绵羊羔，都要一岁、没有残疾的，作燔祭，

chapters.en: an ox and a ram for a peace offering to sacrifice before the LORD, and a grain offering mixed with oil. For today the LORD will appear to you.’”
chapters.zh: 又取一只公牛，一只公绵羊作平安祭，献在耶和华面前，并取调油的素祭，因为今天耶和华要向你们显现。』」

chapters.en: So they took what Moses had commanded to the front of the Tent of Meeting, and the whole congregation drew near and stood before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 于是他们把摩西所吩咐的，带到会幕前；全会众都近前来，站在耶和华面前。

chapters.en: And Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you.”
chapters.zh: 摩西说：「这是耶和华吩咐你们所当行的；耶和华的荣光就要向你们显现。」

chapters.en: Then Moses said to Aaron, “Approach the altar and sacrifice your sin offering and your burnt offering to make atonement for yourself and for the people. And sacrifice the people’s offering to make atonement for them, as the LORD has commanded.”
chapters.zh: 摩西对亚伦说：「你就近坛前，献你的赎罪祭和燔祭，为自己与百姓赎罪，又献上百姓的供物，为他们赎罪，都照耶和华所吩咐的。」

chapters.en: So Aaron approached the altar and slaughtered the calf as a sin offering for himself.
chapters.zh: 于是，亚伦就近坛前，宰了为自己作赎罪祭的牛犊。

chapters.en: The sons of Aaron brought the blood to him, and he dipped his finger in the blood and applied it to the horns of the altar. And he poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
chapters.zh: 亚伦的儿子把血奉给他，他就把指头蘸在血中，抹在坛的四角上，又把血倒在坛脚那里。

chapters.en: On the altar he burned the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 惟有赎罪祭的脂油和腰子，并肝上取的网子，都烧在坛上，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的；

chapters.en: But he burned up the flesh and the hide outside the camp.
chapters.zh: 又用火将肉和皮烧在营外。

chapters.en: Then Aaron slaughtered the burnt offering. His sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it on all sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 亚伦宰了燔祭牲，他儿子把血递给他，他就洒在坛的周围，

chapters.en: They brought him the burnt offering piece by piece, including the head, and he burned them on the altar.
chapters.zh: 又把燔祭一块一块地、连头递给他，他都烧在坛上；

chapters.en: He washed the entrails and the legs and burned them atop the burnt offering on the altar.
chapters.zh: 又洗了脏腑和腿，烧在坛上的燔祭上。

chapters.en: Aaron then presented the people’s offering. He took the male goat for the people’s sin offering, slaughtered it, and offered it for sin like the first one.
chapters.zh: 他奉上百姓的供物，把那给百姓作赎罪祭的公山羊宰了，为罪献上，和先献的一样；

chapters.en: He presented the burnt offering and offered it according to the ordinance.
chapters.zh: 也奉上燔祭，照例而献。

chapters.en: Next he presented the grain offering, took a handful of it, and burned it on the altar in addition to the morning’s burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 他又奉上素祭，从其中取一满把，烧在坛上；这是在早晨的燔祭以外。

chapters.en: Then he slaughtered the ox and the ram as the people’s peace offering. His sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it on all sides of the altar.
chapters.zh: 亚伦宰了那给百姓作平安祭的公牛和公绵羊。他儿子把血递给他，他就洒在坛的周围；

chapters.en: They also brought the fat portions from the ox and the ram—the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver—
chapters.zh: 又把公牛和公绵羊的脂油、肥尾巴，并盖〔脏〕的脂油与腰子，和肝上的网子，都递给他；

chapters.en: and placed these on the breasts. Aaron burned the fat portions on the altar,
chapters.zh: 把脂油放在胸上，他就把脂油烧在坛上。

chapters.en: but he waved the breasts and the right thigh as a wave offering before the LORD, as Moses had commanded.
chapters.zh: 胸和右腿，亚伦当作摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇，都是照摩西所吩咐的。

chapters.en: Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people and blessed them. And having made the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offering, he stepped down.
chapters.zh: 亚伦向百姓举手，为他们祝福。他献了赎罪祭、燔祭、平安祭就下来了。

chapters.en: Moses and Aaron then entered the Tent of Meeting. When they came out, they blessed the people, and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.
chapters.zh: 摩西、亚伦进入会幕，又出来为百姓祝福，耶和华的荣光就向众民显现。

chapters.en: Fire came out from the presence of the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar. And when all the people saw it, they shouted for joy and fell facedown.
chapters.zh: 有火从耶和华面前出来，在坛上烧尽燔祭和脂油；众民一见，就都欢呼，俯伏在地。

chapters.en: Now Aaron’s sons Nadab and Abihu took their censers, put fire in them and added incense, and offered unauthorized fire before the LORD, contrary to His command.
chapters.zh: 亚伦的儿子拿答、亚比户各拿自己的香炉，盛上火，加上香，在耶和华面前献上凡火，是耶和华没有吩咐他们的，

chapters.en: So fire came out from the presence of the LORD and consumed them, and they died in the presence of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 就有火从耶和华面前出来，把他们烧灭，他们就死在耶和华面前。

chapters.en:
Then Moses said to Aaron, “This is what the LORD meant when He said:
‘To those who come near Me I will show My holiness, and in the sight of all the people I will reveal My glory.’”
But Aaron remained silent.
chapters.zh: 于是摩西对亚伦说：「这就是耶和华所说：『我在亲近我的人中要显为圣；在众民面前，我要得荣耀。』」亚伦就默默不言。

chapters.en: Moses summoned Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Aaron’s uncle Uzziel, and said to them, “Come here; carry the bodies of your cousins outside the camp, away from the front of the sanctuary.”
chapters.zh: 摩西召了亚伦叔父乌薛的儿子米沙利、以利撒反来，对他们说：「上前来，把你们的亲属从圣所前抬到营外。」

chapters.en: So they came forward and carried them, still in their tunics, outside the camp, as Moses had directed.
chapters.zh: 于是二人上前来，把他们穿着袍子抬到营外，是照摩西所吩咐的。

chapters.en: Then Moses said to Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, “Do not let your hair become disheveled and do not tear your garments, or else you will die, and the LORD will be angry with the whole congregation. But your brothers, the whole house of Israel, may mourn on account of the fire that the LORD has ignited.
chapters.zh: 摩西对亚伦和他儿子以利亚撒、以他玛说：「不可蓬头散发，也不可撕裂衣裳，免得你们死亡，又免得耶和华向会众发怒；只要你们的弟兄以色列全家为耶和华所发的火哀哭。

chapters.en:
You shall not go outside the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, or you will die, for the LORD’s anointing oil is on you.”
So they did as Moses instructed.
chapters.zh: 你们也不可出会幕的门，恐怕你们死亡，因为耶和华的膏油在你们的身上。」他们就照摩西的话行了。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Aaron,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕亚伦说：

chapters.en: “You and your sons are not to drink wine or strong drink when you enter the Tent of Meeting, or else you will die; this is a permanent statute for the generations to come.
chapters.zh: 「你和你儿子进会幕的时候，清酒、浓酒都不可喝，免得你们死亡；这要作你们世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: You must distinguish between the holy and the common, between the clean and the unclean,
chapters.zh: 使你们可以将圣的、俗的，洁净的、不洁净的，分别出来；

chapters.en: so that you may teach the Israelites all the statutes that the LORD has given them through Moses.”
chapters.zh: 又使你们可以将耶和华藉摩西晓谕以色列人的一切律例教训他们。」

chapters.en: And Moses said to Aaron and his remaining sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, “Take the grain offering that remains from the food offerings to the LORD and eat it without leaven beside the altar, because it is most holy.
chapters.zh: 摩西对亚伦和他剩下的儿子以利亚撒、以他玛说：「你们献给耶和华火祭中所剩的素祭，要在坛旁不带酵而吃，因为是至圣的。

chapters.en: You shall eat it in a holy place, because it is your share and your sons’ share of the food offerings to the LORD; for this is what I have been commanded.
chapters.zh: 你们要在圣处吃；因为在献给耶和华的火祭中，这是你的分和你儿子的分；所吩咐我的本是这样。

chapters.en: And you and your sons and daughters may eat the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution in a ceremonially clean place, because these portions have been assigned to you and your children from the peace offerings of the sons of Israel.
chapters.zh: 所摇的胸，所举的腿，你们要在洁净地方吃。你和你的儿女都要同吃；因为这些是从以色列人平安祭中给你，当你的分和你儿子的分。

chapters.en: They are to bring the thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering, together with the fat portions of the food offerings, to wave as a wave offering before the LORD. It will belong permanently to you and your children, as the LORD has commanded.”
chapters.zh: 所举的腿，所摇的胸，他们要与火祭的脂油一同带来当摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇；这要归你和你儿子，当作永得的分，都是照耶和华所吩咐的。」

chapters.en: Later, Moses searched carefully for the goat of the sin offering, and behold, it had been burned up. He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s remaining sons, and asked,
chapters.zh: 当下摩西急切地寻找作赎罪祭的公山羊，谁知已经焚烧了，便向亚伦剩下的儿子以利亚撒、以他玛发怒，说：

chapters.en: “Why didn’t you eat the sin offering in the holy place? For it is most holy; it was given to you to take away the guilt of the congregation by making atonement for them before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「这赎罪祭既是至圣的，主又给了你们，为要你们担当会众的罪孽，在耶和华面前为他们赎罪，你们为何没有在圣所吃呢？

chapters.en: Since its blood was not brought inside the holy place, you should have eaten it in the sanctuary area, as I commanded.”
chapters.zh: 看哪，这祭牲的血并没有拿到圣所里去，你们本当照我所吩咐的，在圣所里吃这祭肉。」

chapters.en: But Aaron replied to Moses, “Behold, this very day they presented their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD. Since these things have happened to me, if I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have been acceptable in the sight of the LORD?”
chapters.zh: 亚伦对摩西说：「今天他们在耶和华面前献上赎罪祭和燔祭，我又遇见这样的灾，若今天吃了赎罪祭，耶和华岂能看为美呢？」

chapters.en: And when Moses heard this explanation, he was satisfied.
chapters.zh: 摩西听见〔这话〕，便以为美。

chapters.en: The LORD spoke again to Moses and Aaron, telling them,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西、亚伦说：

chapters.en: “Say to the Israelites, ‘Of all the beasts of the earth, these ones you may eat:
chapters.zh: 「你们晓谕以色列人说，在地上一切走兽中可吃的乃是这些：

chapters.en: You may eat any animal that has a split hoof completely divided and that chews the cud.
chapters.zh: 凡蹄分两瓣、倒嚼的走兽，你们都可以吃。

chapters.en:
But of those that only chew the cud or only have a divided hoof, you are not to eat the following:
The camel, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 但那倒嚼或分蹄之中不可吃的乃是：骆驼－因为倒嚼不分蹄，就与你们不洁净；

chapters.en: The rock badger, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 沙番－因为倒嚼不分蹄，就与你们不洁净；

chapters.en: The rabbit, though it chews the cud, does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 觠子－因为倒嚼不分蹄，就与你们不洁净；

chapters.en: And the pig, though it has a split hoof completely divided, does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 猪－因为蹄分两瓣，却不倒嚼，就与你们不洁净。

chapters.en: You must not eat their meat or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 这些兽的肉，你们不可吃；死的，你们不可摸，都与你们不洁净。

chapters.en: Of all the creatures that live in the water, whether in the seas or in the streams, you may eat anything with fins and scales.
chapters.zh: 「水中可吃的乃是这些：凡在水里、海里、河里、有翅有鳞的，都可以吃。

chapters.en: But the following among all the teeming life and creatures in the water are detestable to you: everything in the seas or streams that does not have fins and scales.
chapters.zh: 凡在海里、河里，并一切水里游动的活物，无翅无鳞的，你们都当以为可憎。

chapters.en: They shall be an abomination to you; you must not eat their meat, and you must detest their carcasses.
chapters.zh: 这些无翅无鳞、以为可憎的，你们不可吃牠的肉；死的也当以为可憎。

chapters.en: Everything in the water that does not have fins and scales shall be detestable to you.
chapters.zh: 凡水里无翅无鳞的，你们都当以为可憎。

chapters.en:
Additionally, you are to detest the following birds, and they must not be eaten because they are detestable:
the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
chapters.zh: 「雀鸟中你们当以为可憎、不可吃的乃是：鵰、狗头鵰、红头鵰、

chapters.en: the kite, any kind of falcon,
chapters.zh: 鹞鹰、小鹰与其类；

chapters.en: any kind of raven,
chapters.zh: 乌鸦与其类；

chapters.en: the ostrich, the screech owl, the gull, any kind of hawk,
chapters.zh: 鸵鸟、夜鹰、鱼鹰、鹰与其类；

chapters.en: the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
chapters.zh: 鸮鸟、鸬鹚、猫头鹰、

chapters.en: the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
chapters.zh: 角鸱、鹈鹕、秃鵰、

chapters.en:
the stork, any kind of heron,
the hoopoe, and the bat.
chapters.zh: 鹳、鹭鸶与其类；戴鵀与蝙蝠。

chapters.en: All flying insects that walk on all fours are detestable to you.
chapters.zh: 「凡有翅膀用四足爬行的物，你们都当以为可憎。

chapters.en: However, you may eat the following kinds of flying insects that walk on all fours: those having jointed legs above their feet for hopping on the ground.
chapters.zh: 只是有翅膀用四足爬行的物中，有足有腿，在地上蹦跳的，你们还可以吃。

chapters.en: Of these you may eat any kind of locust, katydid, cricket, or grasshopper.
chapters.zh: 其中有蝗虫、蚂蚱、蟋蟀与其类；蚱蜢与其类；这些你们都可以吃。
