chapters.en: All other flying insects that have four legs are detestable to you.
chapters.zh: 但是有翅膀有四足的爬物，你们都当以为可憎。

chapters.en: These creatures will make you unclean. Whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening,
chapters.zh: 「这些都能使你们不洁净。凡摸了死的，必不洁净到晚上。

chapters.en: and whoever picks up one of their carcasses must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 凡拿了死的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服。

chapters.en: Every animal with hooves not completely divided or that does not chew the cud is unclean for you. Whoever touches any of them will be unclean.
chapters.zh: 凡走兽分蹄不成两瓣、也不倒嚼的，是与你们不洁净；凡摸了的就不洁净。

chapters.en: All the four-footed animals that walk on their paws are unclean for you; whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening,
chapters.zh: 凡四足的走兽，用掌行走的，是与你们不洁净；摸其尸的，必不洁净到晚上。

chapters.en: and anyone who picks up a carcass must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 拿其尸的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服。这些是与你们不洁净的。

chapters.en: The following creatures that move along the ground are unclean for you: the mole, the mouse, any kind of great lizard,
chapters.zh: 「地上爬物与你们不洁净的乃是这些：鼬鼠、鼫鼠、蜥蜴与其类；

chapters.en: the gecko, the monitor lizard, the common lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
chapters.zh: 壁虎、龙子、守宫、蛇医、蝘蜓。

chapters.en: These animals are unclean for you among all the crawling creatures. Whoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 这些爬物都是与你们不洁净的。在牠死了以后，凡摸了的，必不洁净到晚上。

chapters.en: When one of them dies and falls on something, that article becomes unclean; any article of wood, clothing, leather, sackcloth, or any implement used for work must be rinsed with water and will remain unclean until evening; then it will be clean.
chapters.zh: 其中死了的，掉在什么东西上，这东西就不洁净，无论是木器、衣服、皮子、口袋，不拘是做什么工用的器皿，须要放在水中，必不洁净到晚上，到晚上才洁净了。

chapters.en: If any of them falls into a clay pot, everything in it will be unclean; you must break the pot.
chapters.zh: 若有死了掉在瓦器里的，其中不拘有什么，就不洁净，你们要把这瓦器打破了。

chapters.en: Any food coming into contact with water from that pot will be unclean, and any drink in such a container will be unclean.
chapters.zh: 其中一切可吃的食物，沾水的就不洁净，并且那样器皿中一切可喝的，也必不洁净。

chapters.en: Anything upon which one of their carcasses falls will be unclean. If it is an oven or cooking pot, it must be smashed; it is unclean and will remain unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 其中已死的，若有一点掉在什么物件上，那物件就不洁净，不拘是炉子，是锅台，就要打碎，都不洁净，也必与你们不洁净。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, a spring or cistern containing water will remain clean, but one who touches a carcass in it will be unclean.
chapters.zh: 但是泉源或是聚水的池子仍是洁净；惟挨了那死的，就不洁净。

chapters.en: If a carcass falls on any seed for sowing, the seed is clean;
chapters.zh: 若是死的，有一点掉在要种的子粒上，子粒仍是洁净；

chapters.en: but if water has been put on the seed and a carcass falls on it, it is unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 若水已经浇在子粒上，那死的有一点掉在上头，这子粒就与你们不洁净。

chapters.en: If an animal that you may eat dies, anyone who touches the carcass will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 「你们可吃的走兽若是死了，有人摸牠，必不洁净到晚上；

chapters.en: Whoever eats from the carcass must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening, and anyone who picks up the carcass must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 有人吃那死了的走兽，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服；拿了死走兽的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服。

chapters.en: Every creature that moves along the ground is detestable; it must not be eaten.
chapters.zh: 「凡地上的爬物是可憎的，都不可吃。

chapters.en: Do not eat any creature that moves along the ground, whether it crawls on its belly or walks on four or more feet; for such creatures are detestable.
chapters.zh: 凡用肚子行走的和用四足行走的，或是有许多足的，就是一切爬在地上的，你们都不可吃，因为是可憎的。

chapters.en: Do not defile yourselves by any crawling creature; do not become unclean or defiled by them.
chapters.zh: 你们不可因什么爬物使自己成为可憎的，也不可因这些使自己不洁净，以致染了污秽。

chapters.en: For I am the LORD your God; consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy, because I am holy. You must not defile yourselves by any creature that crawls along the ground.
chapters.zh: 我是耶和华－你们的上帝；所以你们要成为圣洁，因为我是圣洁的。你们也不可在地上的爬物污秽自己。

chapters.en: For I am the LORD, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt so that I would be your God; therefore be holy, because I am holy.
chapters.zh: 我是把你们从埃及地领出来的耶和华，要作你们的上帝；所以你们要圣洁，因为我是圣洁的。」

chapters.en: This is the law regarding animals, birds, all living creatures that move in the water, and all creatures that crawl along the ground.
chapters.zh: 这是走兽、飞鸟，和水中游动的活物，并地上爬物的条例。

chapters.en: You must distinguish between the unclean and the clean, between animals that may be eaten and those that may not.’”
chapters.zh: 要把洁净的和不洁净的，可吃的与不可吃的活物，都分别出来。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Say to the Israelites, ‘A woman who becomes pregnant and gives birth to a son will be unclean for seven days, as she is during the days of her menstruation.
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：若有妇人怀孕生男孩，她就不洁净七天，像在月经污秽的日子不洁净一样。

chapters.en: And on the eighth day the flesh of the boy’s foreskin is to be circumcised.
chapters.zh: 第八天，要给婴孩行割礼。

chapters.en: The woman shall continue in purification from her bleeding for thirty-three days. She must not touch anything sacred or go into the sanctuary until the days of her purification are complete.
chapters.zh: 妇人在产血不洁之中，要家居三十三天。她洁净的日子未满，不可摸圣物，也不可进入圣所。

chapters.en: If, however, she gives birth to a daughter, the woman will be unclean for two weeks as she is during her menstruation. Then she must continue in purification from her bleeding for sixty-six days.
chapters.zh: 她若生女孩，就不洁净两个七天，像污秽〔的时候〕一样，要在产血不洁之中，家居六十六天。

chapters.en: When the days of her purification are complete, whether for a son or for a daughter, she is to bring to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 「满了洁净的日子，无论是为男孩是为女孩，她要把一岁的羊羔为燔祭，一只雏鸽或是一只斑鸠为赎罪祭，带到会幕门口交给祭司。

chapters.en: And the priest will present them before the LORD and make atonement for her; and she shall be ceremonially cleansed from her flow of blood. This is the law for a woman giving birth, whether to a male or to a female.
chapters.zh: 祭司要献在耶和华面前，为她赎罪，她的血源就洁净了。这条例是为生育的妇人，无论是生男生女。

chapters.en: But if she cannot afford a lamb, she shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. Then the priest will make atonement for her, and she will be clean.’”
chapters.zh: 她的力量若不够献一只羊羔，她就要取两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽，一只为燔祭，一只为赎罪祭。祭司要为她赎罪，她就洁净了。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西、亚伦说：

chapters.en: “When someone has a swelling or rash or bright spot on his skin that may be an infectious skin disease, he must be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who is a priest.
chapters.zh: 「人的肉皮上若长了疖子，或长了癣，或长了火斑，在他肉皮上成了大痲疯的灾病，就要将他带到祭司亚伦或亚伦作祭司的一个子孙面前。

chapters.en: The priest is to examine the infection on his skin, and if the hair in the infection has turned white and the sore appears to be deeper than the skin, it is a skin disease. After the priest examines him, he must pronounce him unclean.
chapters.zh: 祭司要察看肉皮上的灾病，若灾病处的毛已经变白，灾病的现象深于肉上的皮，这便是大痲疯的灾病。祭司要察看他，定他为不洁净。

chapters.en: If, however, the spot on his skin is white and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and the hair in it has not turned white, the priest shall isolate the infected person for seven days.
chapters.zh: 若火斑在他肉皮上是白的，现象不深于皮，其上的毛也没有变白，祭司就要将有灾病的人关锁七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine him, and if he sees that the infection is unchanged and has not spread on the skin, the priest must isolate him for another seven days.
chapters.zh: 第七天，祭司要察看他，若看灾病止住了，没有在皮上发散，祭司还要将他关锁七天。

chapters.en: The priest will examine him again on the seventh day, and if the sore has faded and has not spread on the skin, the priest shall pronounce him clean; it is a rash. The person must wash his clothes and be clean.
chapters.zh: 第七天，祭司要再察看他，若灾病发暗，而且没有在皮上发散，祭司要定他为洁净，原来是癣；那人就要洗衣服，得为洁净。

chapters.en: But if the rash spreads further on his skin after he has shown himself to the priest for his cleansing, he must present himself again to the priest.
chapters.zh: 但他为得洁净，将身体给祭司察看以后，癣若在皮上发散开了，他要再将身体给祭司察看。

chapters.en: The priest will reexamine him, and if the rash has spread on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a skin disease.
chapters.zh: 祭司要察看，癣若在皮上发散，就要定他为不洁净，是大痲疯。

chapters.en: When anyone develops a skin disease, he must be brought to the priest.
chapters.zh: 「人有了大痲疯的灾病，就要将他带到祭司面前。

chapters.en: The priest will examine him, and if there is a white swelling on the skin that has turned the hair white, and there is raw flesh in the swelling,
chapters.zh: 祭司要察看，皮上若长了白疖，使毛变白，在长白疖之处有了红瘀肉，

chapters.en: it is a chronic skin disease and the priest must pronounce him unclean. He need not isolate him, for he is unclean.
chapters.zh: 这是肉皮上的旧大痲疯，祭司要定他为不洁净，不用将他关锁，因为他是不洁净了。

chapters.en: But if the skin disease breaks out all over his skin so that it covers all the skin of the infected person from head to foot, as far as the priest can see,
chapters.zh: 大痲疯若在皮上四外发散，长满了患灾病人的皮，据祭司察看，从头到脚无处不有，

chapters.en: the priest shall examine him, and if the disease has covered his entire body, he is to pronounce the infected person clean. Since it has all turned white, he is clean.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要察看，全身的肉若长满了大痲疯，就要定那患灾病的为洁净；全身都变为白，他乃洁净了。

chapters.en: But whenever raw flesh appears on someone, he will be unclean.
chapters.zh: 但红肉几时显在他的身上就几时不洁净。

chapters.en: When the priest sees the raw flesh, he must pronounce him unclean. The raw flesh is unclean; it is a skin disease.
chapters.zh: 祭司一看那红肉就定他为不洁净。红肉本是不洁净，是大痲疯。

chapters.en: But if the raw flesh changes and turns white, he must go to the priest.
chapters.zh: 红肉若复原，又变白了，他就要来见祭司。

chapters.en: The priest will reexamine him, and if the infection has turned white, the priest is to pronounce the infected person clean; then he is clean.
chapters.zh: 祭司要察看，灾病处若变白了，祭司就要定那患灾病的为洁净，他乃洁净了。

chapters.en: When a boil appears on someone’s skin and it heals,
chapters.zh: 「人若在皮肉上长疮，却治好了，

chapters.en: and a white swelling or a reddish-white spot develops where the boil was, he must present himself to the priest.
chapters.zh: 在长疮之处又起了白疖，或是白中带红的火斑，就要给祭司察看。

chapters.en: The priest shall examine it, and if it appears to be beneath the skin and the hair in it has turned white, the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection that has broken out in the boil.
chapters.zh: 祭司要察看，若现象洼于皮，其上的毛也变白了，就要定他为不洁净，是大痲疯的灾病发在疮中。

chapters.en: But when the priest examines it, if there is no white hair in it, and it is not beneath the skin and has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
chapters.zh: 祭司若察看，其上没有白毛，也没有洼于皮，乃是发暗，就要将他关锁七天。

chapters.en: If it spreads any further on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is an infection.
chapters.zh: 若在皮上发散开了，祭司就要定他为不洁净，是灾病。

chapters.en: But if the spot remains unchanged and does not spread, it is only the scar from the boil, and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
chapters.zh: 火斑若在原处止住，没有发散，便是疮的痕迹，祭司就要定他为洁净。

chapters.en: When there is a burn on someone’s skin and the raw area of the burn becomes reddish-white or white,
chapters.zh: 「人的皮肉上若起了火毒，火毒的瘀〔肉〕成了火斑，或是白中带红的，或是全白的，

chapters.en: the priest must examine it. If the hair in the spot has turned white and the spot appears to be deeper than the skin, it is a disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要察看，火斑中的毛若变白了，现象又深于皮，是大痲疯在火毒中发出，就要定他为不洁净，是大痲疯的灾病。

chapters.en: But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in the spot, and it is not beneath the skin but has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
chapters.zh: 但是祭司察看，在火斑中若没有白毛，也没有洼于皮，乃是发暗，就要将他关锁七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine him, and if it has spread further on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection.
chapters.zh: 到第七天，祭司要察看他，火斑若在皮上发散开了，就要定他为不洁净，是大痲疯的灾病。

chapters.en: But if the spot is unchanged and has not spread on the skin but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn, and the priest is to pronounce him clean; for it is only the scar from the burn.
chapters.zh: 火斑若在原处止住，没有在皮上发散，乃是发暗，是起的火毒，祭司要定他为洁净，不过是火毒的痕迹。

chapters.en: If a man or woman has an infection on the head or chin,
chapters.zh: 「无论男女，若在头上有灾病，或是男人胡须上有灾病，

chapters.en: the priest shall examine the infection, and if it appears to be deeper than the skin and the hair in it is yellow and thin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a scaly outbreak, an infectious disease of the head or chin.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要察看；这灾病现象若深于皮，其间有细黄毛，就要定他为不洁净，这是头疥，是头上或是胡须上的大痲疯。

chapters.en: But if the priest examines the scaly infection and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, the priest shall isolate the infected person for seven days.
chapters.zh: 祭司若察看头疥的灾病，现象不深于皮，其间也没有黑毛，就要将长头疥灾病的关锁七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine the infection, and if the scaly outbreak has not spread and there is no yellow hair in it, and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin,
chapters.zh: 第七天，祭司要察看灾病，若头疥没有发散，其间也没有黄毛，头疥的现象不深于皮，

chapters.en: then the person must shave himself except for the scaly area. Then the priest shall isolate him for another seven days.
chapters.zh: 那人就要剃去须发，但他不可剃头疥之处。祭司要将那长头疥的，再关锁七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day the priest shall examine the scaly outbreak, and if it has not spread on the skin and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, the priest is to pronounce him clean. He must wash his clothes, and he will be clean.
chapters.zh: 第七天，祭司要察看头疥，头疥若没有在皮上发散，现象也不深于皮，就要定他为洁净，他要洗衣服，便成为洁净。

chapters.en: If, however, the scaly outbreak spreads further on the skin after his cleansing,
chapters.zh: 但他得洁净以后，头疥若在皮上发散开了，

chapters.en: the priest is to examine him, and if the scaly outbreak has spread on the skin, the priest need not look for yellow hair; the person is unclean.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要察看他。头疥若在皮上发散，就不必找那黄毛，他是不洁净了。

chapters.en: If, however, in his sight the scaly outbreak is unchanged and black hair has grown in it, then it has healed. He is clean, and the priest is to pronounce him clean.
chapters.zh: 祭司若看头疥已经止住，其间也长了黑毛，头疥已然痊愈，那人是洁净了，就要定他为洁净。

chapters.en: When a man or a woman has white spots on the skin,
chapters.zh: 「无论男女，皮肉上若起了火斑，就是白火斑，

chapters.en: the priest shall examine them, and if the spots are dull white, it is a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin; the person is clean.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要察看，他们肉皮上的火斑若白中带黑，这是皮上发出的白癣，那人是洁净了。

chapters.en: Now if a man loses his hair and is bald, he is still clean.
chapters.zh: 「人头上的发若掉了，他不过是头秃，还是洁净。

chapters.en: Or if his hairline recedes and he is bald on his forehead, he is still clean.
chapters.zh: 他顶前若掉了头发，他不过是顶门秃，还是洁净。

chapters.en: But if there is a reddish-white sore on the bald head or forehead, it is an infectious disease breaking out on it.
chapters.zh: 头秃处或是顶门秃处若有白中带红的灾病，这就是大痲疯发在他头秃处或是顶门秃处，

chapters.en: The priest is to examine him, and if the swelling of the infection on his bald head or forehead is reddish-white like a skin disease,
chapters.zh: 祭司就要察看，他起的那灾病若在头秃处或是顶门秃处有白中带红的，像肉皮上大痲疯的现象，

chapters.en: the man is diseased; he is unclean. The priest must pronounce him unclean because of the infection on his head.
chapters.zh: 那人就是长大痲疯，不洁净的，祭司总要定他为不洁净，他的灾病是在头上。

chapters.en: A diseased person must wear torn clothes and let his hair hang loose, and he must cover his mouth and cry out, ‘Unclean, unclean!’
chapters.zh: 「身上有长大痲疯灾病的，他的衣服要撕裂，也要蓬头散发，蒙着上唇，喊叫说：『不洁净了！不洁净了！』

chapters.en: As long as he has the infection, he remains unclean. He must live alone in a place outside the camp.
chapters.zh: 灾病在他身上的日子，他便是不洁净；他既是不洁净，就要独居营外。」

chapters.en: If any fabric is contaminated with mildew —any wool or linen garment,
chapters.zh: 「染了大痲疯灾病的衣服，无论是羊毛衣服、是麻布衣服，

chapters.en: any weave or knit of linen or wool, or any article of leather—
chapters.zh: 无论是在经上、在纬上，是麻布的、是羊毛的，是在皮子上，或在皮子做的什么物件上，

chapters.en: and if the mark in the fabric, leather, weave, knit, or leather article is green or red, then it is contaminated with mildew and must be shown to the priest.
chapters.zh: 或在衣服上、皮子上，经上、纬上，或在皮子做的什么物件上，这灾病若是发绿，或是发红，是大痲疯的灾病，要给祭司察看。

chapters.en: And the priest is to examine the mildew and isolate the contaminated fabric for seven days.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要察看那灾病，把染了灾病的物件关锁七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day the priest shall reexamine it, and if the mildew has spread in the fabric, weave, knit, or leather, then regardless of how it is used, it is a harmful mildew; the article is unclean.
chapters.zh: 第七天，他要察看那灾病，灾病或在衣服上，经上、纬上，皮子上，若发散，这皮子无论当作何用，这灾病是蚕食的大痲疯，都是不洁净了。

chapters.en: He is to burn the fabric, weave, or knit, whether the contaminated item is wool or linen or leather. Since the mildew is harmful, the article must be burned up.
chapters.zh: 那染了灾病的衣服，或是经上、纬上，羊毛上，麻衣上，或是皮子做的什么物件上，他都要焚烧；因为这是蚕食的大痲疯，必在火中焚烧。

chapters.en: But when the priest reexamines it, if the mildew has not spread in the fabric, weave, knit, or leather article,
chapters.zh: 「祭司要察看，若灾病在衣服上，经上、纬上，或是皮子做的什么物件上，没有发散，

chapters.en: the priest is to order the contaminated article to be washed and isolated for another seven days.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要吩咐他们，把染了灾病的物件洗了，再关锁七天。

chapters.en: After it has been washed, the priest is to reexamine it, and if the mildewed article has not changed in appearance, it is unclean. Even though the mildew has not spread, you must burn it, whether the rot is on the front or back.
chapters.zh: 洗过以后，祭司要察看，那物件若没有变色，灾病也没有消散，那物件就不洁净，是透重的灾病，无论正面反面，都要在火中焚烧。

chapters.en: If the priest examines it and the mildew has faded after it has been washed, he must cut the contaminated section out of the fabric, leather, weave, or knit.
chapters.zh: 洗过以后，祭司要察看，若见那灾病发暗，他就要把那灾病从衣服上，皮子上，经上、纬上，都撕去。

chapters.en: But if it reappears in the fabric, weave, or knit, or on any leather article, it is spreading. You must burn the contaminated article.
chapters.zh: 若仍现在衣服上，或是经上、纬上、皮子做的什么物件上，这就是灾病又发了，必用火焚烧那染灾病的物件。

chapters.en: If the mildew disappears from the fabric, weave, or knit, or any leather article after washing, then it is to be washed again, and it will be clean.
chapters.zh: 所洗的衣服，或是经，或是纬，或是皮子做的什么物件，若灾病离开了，要再洗，就洁净了。」

chapters.en: This is the law concerning a mildew contamination in wool or linen fabric, weave, or knit, or any leather article, for pronouncing it clean or unclean.”
chapters.zh: 这就是大痲疯灾病的条例，无论是在羊毛衣服上，麻布衣服上，经上、纬上，和皮子做的什么物件上，可以定为洁净或是不洁净。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：「

chapters.en: “This is the law for the one afflicted with a skin disease on the day of his cleansing, when he is brought to the priest.
chapters.zh: 长大痲疯得洁净的日子，其例乃是这样：要带他去见祭司；

chapters.en: The priest is to go outside the camp to examine him, and if the skin disease of the afflicted person has healed,
chapters.zh: 祭司要出到营外察看，若见他的大痲疯痊愈了，

chapters.en: the priest shall order that two live clean birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop be brought for the one to be cleansed.
chapters.zh: 就要吩咐人为那求洁净的拿两只洁净的活鸟和香柏木、朱红色〔线〕，并牛膝草来。

chapters.en: Then the priest shall command that one of the birds be slaughtered over fresh water in a clay pot.
chapters.zh: 祭司要吩咐用瓦器盛活水，把一只鸟宰在上面。

chapters.en: And he is to take the live bird together with the cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop, and dip them into the blood of the bird that was slaughtered over the fresh water.
chapters.zh: 至于那只活鸟，祭司要把牠和香柏木、朱红色〔线〕并牛膝草一同蘸于宰在活水上的鸟血中，

chapters.en: Seven times he shall sprinkle the one to be cleansed of the skin disease. Then he shall pronounce him clean and release the live bird into the open field.
chapters.zh: 用以在那长大痲疯求洁净的人身上洒七次，就定他为洁净，又把活鸟放在田野里。

chapters.en: The one being cleansed must wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and bathe with water; then he will be ceremonially clean. Afterward, he may enter the camp, but he must remain outside his tent for seven days.
chapters.zh: 求洁净的人当洗衣服，剃去毛发，用水洗澡，就洁净了；然后可以进营，只是要在自己的帐棚外居住七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day he must shave off all his hair—his head, his beard, his eyebrows, and the rest of his hair. He must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water, and he will be clean.
chapters.zh: 第七天，再把头上所有的头发与胡须、眉毛，并全身的毛，都剃了；又要洗衣服，用水洗身，就洁净了。

chapters.en: On the eighth day he is to bring two unblemished male lambs, an unblemished ewe lamb a year old, a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with olive oil, and one log of olive oil.
chapters.zh: 「第八天，他要取两只没有残疾的公羊羔和一只没有残疾、一岁的母羊羔，又要把调油的细面〔伊法〕十分之三为素祭，并油一罗革，一同取来。

chapters.en: The priest who performs the cleansing shall present the one to be cleansed, together with these offerings, before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 行洁净之礼的祭司要将那求洁净的人和这些东西安置在会幕门口、耶和华面前。

chapters.en: Then the priest is to take one of the male lambs and present it as a guilt offering, along with the log of olive oil; and he must wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司要取一只公羊羔献为赎愆祭，和那一罗革油一同作摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇；

chapters.en: Then he is to slaughter the lamb in the sanctuary area where the sin offering and burnt offering are slaughtered. Like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest; it is most holy.
chapters.zh: 把公羊羔宰于圣地，就是宰赎罪祭牲和燔祭牲之地。赎愆祭要归祭司，与赎罪祭一样，是至圣的。

chapters.en: The priest is to take some of the blood from the guilt offering and put it on the right earlobe of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
chapters.zh: 祭司要取些赎愆祭牲的血，抹在求洁净人的右耳垂上和右手的大拇指上，并右脚的大拇指上。

chapters.en: Then the priest shall take some of the log of olive oil, pour it into his left palm,
chapters.zh: 祭司要从那一罗革油中取些倒在自己的左手掌里，

chapters.en: dip his right forefinger into the oil in his left palm, and sprinkle some of the oil with his finger seven times before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 把右手的一个指头蘸在左手的油里，在耶和华面前用指头弹七次。

chapters.en: And the priest is to put some of the oil remaining in his palm on the right earlobe of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on top of the blood of the guilt offering.
chapters.zh: 将手里所剩的油抹在那求洁净人的右耳垂上和右手的大拇指上，并右脚的大拇指上，就是抹在赎愆祭牲的血上。

chapters.en: The rest of the oil in his palm, the priest is to put on the head of the one to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司手里所剩的油要抹在那求洁净人的头上，在耶和华面前为他赎罪。

chapters.en: Then the priest is to sacrifice the sin offering and make atonement for the one to be cleansed from his uncleanness. After that, the priest shall slaughter the burnt offering
chapters.zh: 祭司要献赎罪祭，为那本不洁净、求洁净的人赎罪；然后要宰燔祭牲，

chapters.en: and offer it on the altar, with the grain offering, to make atonement for him, and he will be clean.
chapters.zh: 把燔祭和素祭献在坛上，为他赎罪，他就洁净了。

chapters.en: If, however, the person is poor and cannot afford these offerings, he is to take one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved to make atonement for him, along with a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with olive oil for a grain offering, a log of olive oil,
chapters.zh: 「他若贫穷不能预备够数，就要取一只公羊羔作赎愆祭，可以摇一摇，为他赎罪；也要把调油的细面〔伊法〕十分之一为素祭，和油一罗革一同取来；

chapters.en: and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford, one to be a sin offering and the other a burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 又照他的力量取两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽，一只作赎罪祭，一只作燔祭。

chapters.en: On the eighth day he is to bring them for his cleansing to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 第八天，要为洁净，把这些带到会幕门口、耶和华面前，交给祭司。

chapters.en: The priest shall take the lamb for the guilt offering, along with the log of olive oil, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司要把赎愆祭的羊羔和那一罗革油一同作摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇。

chapters.en: And after he slaughters the lamb for the guilt offering, the priest is to take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the right earlobe of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
chapters.zh: 要宰了赎愆祭的羊羔，取些赎愆祭牲的血，抹在那求洁净人的右耳垂上和右手的大拇指上，并右脚的大拇指上。

chapters.en: Then the priest is to pour some of the oil into his left palm
chapters.zh: 祭司要把些油倒在自己的左手掌里，

chapters.en: and sprinkle with his right forefinger some of the oil in his left palm seven times before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 把左手里的油，在耶和华面前，用右手的一个指头弹七次，

chapters.en: The priest shall also put some of the oil in his palm on the right earlobe of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot—on the same places as the blood of the guilt offering.
chapters.zh: 又把手里的油抹些在那求洁净人的右耳垂上和右手的大拇指上，并右脚的大拇指上，就是抹赎愆祭之血的原处。

chapters.en: The rest of the oil in his palm, the priest is to put on the head of the one to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司手里所剩的油要抹在那求洁净人的头上，在耶和华面前为他赎罪。

chapters.en: Then he must sacrifice the turtledoves or young pigeons, whichever he can afford,
chapters.zh: 那人又要照他的力量献上一只斑鸠或是一只雏鸽，

chapters.en: one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, together with the grain offering. In this way the priest will make atonement before the LORD for the one to be cleansed.
chapters.zh: 就是他所能办的，一只为赎罪祭，一只为燔祭，与素祭一同献上；祭司要在耶和华面前为他赎罪。

chapters.en: This is the law for someone who has a skin disease and cannot afford the cost of his cleansing.”
chapters.zh: 这是那有大痲疯灾病的人、不能将〔关乎〕得洁净之物预备够数的条例。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西、亚伦说：

chapters.en: “When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as your possession, and I put a contamination of mildew into a house in that land,
chapters.zh: 「你们到了我赐给你们为业的迦南地，我若使你们所得为业之地的房屋中有大痲疯的灾病，

chapters.en: the owner of the house shall come and tell the priest, ‘Something like mildew has appeared in my house.’
chapters.zh: 房主就要去告诉祭司说：『据我看，房屋中似乎有灾病。』

chapters.en: The priest must order that the house be cleared before he enters it to examine the mildew, so that nothing in the house will become unclean. After this, the priest shall go in to inspect the house.
chapters.zh: 祭司还没有进去察看灾病以前，就要吩咐人把房子腾空，免得房子里所有的都成了不洁净；然后祭司要进去察看房子。

chapters.en: He is to examine the house, and if the mildew on the walls consists of green or red depressions that appear to be beneath the surface of the wall,
chapters.zh: 他要察看那灾病，灾病若在房子的墙上有发绿或发红的凹斑纹，现象洼于墙，

chapters.en: the priest shall go outside the doorway of the house and close it up for seven days.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要出到房门外，把房子封锁七天。

chapters.en: On the seventh day the priest is to return and inspect the house. If the mildew has spread on the walls,
chapters.zh: 第七天，祭司要再去察看，灾病若在房子的墙上发散，

chapters.en: he must order that the contaminated stones be pulled out and thrown into an unclean place outside the city.
chapters.zh: 就要吩咐人把那有灾病的石头挖出来，扔在城外不洁净之处；

chapters.en: And he shall have the inside of the house scraped completely and the plaster that is scraped off dumped into an unclean place outside the city.
chapters.zh: 也要叫人刮房内的四围，所刮掉的灰泥要倒在城外不洁净之处；

chapters.en: So different stones must be obtained to replace the contaminated ones, as well as additional mortar to replaster the house.
chapters.zh: 又要用别的石头代替那挖出来的石头，要另用灰泥墁房子。

chapters.en: If the mildew reappears in the house after the stones have been torn out and the house has been scraped and replastered,
chapters.zh: 「他挖出石头，刮了房子，墁了以后，灾病若在房子里又发现，

chapters.en:
the priest must come and inspect it.
If the mildew has spread in the house, it is a destructive mildew; the house is unclean.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要进去察看，灾病若在房子里发散，这就是房内蚕食的大痲疯，是不洁净。

chapters.en: It must be torn down with its stones, its timbers, and all its plaster, and taken outside the city to an unclean place.
chapters.zh: 他就要拆毁房子，把石头、木头、灰泥都搬到城外不洁净之处。

chapters.en: Anyone who enters the house during any of the days that it is closed up will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 在房子封锁的时候，进去的人必不洁净到晚上；

chapters.en: And anyone who sleeps in the house or eats in it must wash his clothes.
chapters.zh: 在房子里躺着的必洗衣服；在房子里吃饭的也必洗衣服。

chapters.en: If, however, the priest comes and inspects it, and the mildew has not spread after the house has been replastered, he shall pronounce the house clean, because the mildew is gone.
chapters.zh: 「房子墁了以后，祭司若进去察看，见灾病在房内没有发散，就要定房子为洁净，因为灾病已经消除。

chapters.en: He is to take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop to purify the house;
chapters.zh: 要为洁净房子取两只鸟和香柏木、朱红色〔线〕并牛膝草，

chapters.en: and he shall slaughter one of the birds over fresh water in a clay pot.
chapters.zh: 用瓦器盛活水，把一只鸟宰在上面，

chapters.en: Then he shall take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet yarn, and the live bird, dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
chapters.zh: 把香柏木、牛膝草、朱红色〔线〕，并那活鸟，都蘸在被宰的鸟血中与活水中，用以洒房子七次。

chapters.en: And he shall cleanse the house with the bird’s blood, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the scarlet yarn.
chapters.zh: 要用鸟血、活水、活鸟、香柏木、牛膝草，并朱红色〔线〕，洁净那房子。

chapters.en: Finally, he is to release the live bird into the open fields outside the city. In this way he will make atonement for the house, and it will be clean.
chapters.zh: 但要把活鸟放在城外田野里。这样洁净房子〔注：原文是为房子赎罪〕，房子就洁净了。」

chapters.en: This is the law for any infectious skin disease, for a scaly outbreak,
chapters.zh: 这是为各类大痲疯的灾病和头疥，

chapters.en: for mildew in clothing or in a house,
chapters.zh: 并衣服与房子的大痲疯，

chapters.en: and for a swelling, rash, or spot,
chapters.zh: 以及疖子、癣、火斑所立的条例，

chapters.en: to determine when something is clean or unclean. This is the law regarding skin diseases and mildew. ”
chapters.zh: 指明何时为洁净，何时为不洁净。这是大痲疯的条例。

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西、亚伦说：

chapters.en: “Say to the Israelites, ‘When any man has a bodily discharge, the discharge is unclean.
chapters.zh: 「你们晓谕以色列人说：人若身患漏症，他因这漏症就不洁净了。

chapters.en: This uncleanness is from his discharge, whether his body allows the discharge to flow or blocks it. So his discharge will bring about uncleanness.
chapters.zh: 他患漏症，无论是下流的，是止住的，都是不洁净。

chapters.en: Any bed on which the man with the discharge lies will be unclean, and any furniture on which he sits will be unclean.
chapters.zh: 他所躺的床都为不洁净，所坐的物也为不洁净。

chapters.en: Anyone who touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 凡摸那床的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: Whoever sits on furniture on which the man with the discharge was sitting must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 那坐患漏症人所坐之物的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: Whoever touches the body of the man with a discharge must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 那摸患漏症人身体的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: If the man with the discharge spits on one who is clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 若患漏症人吐在洁净的人身上，那人必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: Any saddle on which the man with the discharge rides will be unclean.
chapters.zh: 患漏症人所骑的鞍子也为不洁净。

chapters.en: Whoever touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 凡摸了他身下之物的，必不洁净到晚上；拿了那物的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: If the man with the discharge touches anyone without first rinsing his hands with water, the one who was touched must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 患漏症的人没有用水涮手，无论摸了谁，谁必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: Any clay pot that the man with the discharge touches must be broken, and any wooden utensil must be rinsed with water.
chapters.zh: 患漏症人所摸的瓦器就必打破；所摸的一切木器也必用水涮洗。

chapters.en: When the man has been cleansed from his discharge, he must count off seven days for his cleansing, wash his clothes, and bathe himself in fresh water, and he shall be clean.
chapters.zh: 「患漏症的人痊愈了，就要为洁净自己计算七天，也必洗衣服，用活水洗身，就洁净了。

chapters.en: On the eighth day he is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, come before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, and give them to the priest.
chapters.zh: 第八天，要取两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽，来到会幕门口、耶和华面前，把鸟交给祭司。

chapters.en: The priest is to sacrifice them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for the man before the LORD because of his discharge.
chapters.zh: 祭司要献上一只为赎罪祭，一只为燔祭；因那人患的漏症，祭司要在耶和华面前为他赎罪。

chapters.en: When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 「人若〔梦〕遗，他必不洁净到晚上，并要用水洗全身。

chapters.en: Any clothing or leather on which there is an emission of semen must be washed with water, and it will remain unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 无论是衣服是皮子，被精所染，必不洁净到晚上，并要用水洗。

chapters.en: If a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both must bathe with water, and they will remain unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 若男女交合，两个人必不洁净到晚上，并要用水洗澡。

chapters.en: When a woman has a discharge consisting of blood from her body, she will be unclean due to her menstruation for seven days, and anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 「女人行经，必污秽七天；凡摸她的，必不洁净到晚上。

chapters.en: Anything on which she lies or sits during her menstruation will be unclean,
chapters.zh: 女人在污秽之中，凡她所躺的物件都为不洁净，所坐的物件也都不洁净。

chapters.en: and anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 凡摸她床的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: Whoever touches any furniture on which she was sitting must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 凡摸她所坐什么物件的，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: And whether it is a bed or furniture on which she was sitting, whoever touches it will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 在女人的床上，或在她坐的物上，若有别的物件，人一摸了，必不洁净到晚上。

chapters.en: If a man lies with her and her menstrual flow touches him, he will be unclean for seven days, and any bed on which he lies will become unclean.
chapters.zh: 男人若与那女人同房，染了她的污秽，就要七天不洁净；所躺的床也为不洁净。

chapters.en: When a woman has a discharge of her blood for many days at a time other than her menstrual period, or if it continues beyond her period, she will be unclean all the days of her unclean discharge, just as she is during the days of her menstruation.
chapters.zh: 「女人若在经期以外患多日的血漏，或是经期过长，有了漏症，她就因这漏症不洁净，与她在经期不洁净一样。

chapters.en: Any bed on which she lies or any furniture on which she sits during the days of her discharge will be unclean, like her bed during her menstrual period.
chapters.zh: 她在患漏症的日子所躺的床、所坐的物都要看为不洁净，与她月经的时候一样。

chapters.en: Anyone who touches these things will be unclean; he must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening.
chapters.zh: 凡摸这些物件的，就为不洁净，必不洁净到晚上，并要洗衣服，用水洗澡。

chapters.en: When a woman is cleansed of her discharge, she must count off seven days, and after that she will be ceremonially clean.
chapters.zh: 女人的漏症若好了，就要计算七天，然后才为洁净。

chapters.en: On the eighth day she is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 第八天，要取两只斑鸠或是两只雏鸽，带到会幕门口给祭司。

chapters.en: The priest is to sacrifice one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for her before the LORD for her unclean discharge.
chapters.zh: 祭司要献一只为赎罪祭，一只为燔祭；因那人血漏不洁，祭司要在耶和华面前为她赎罪。

chapters.en: You must keep the children of Israel separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die by defiling My tabernacle, which is among them.
chapters.zh: 「你们要这样使以色列人与他们的污秽隔绝，免得他们玷污我的帐幕，就因自己的污秽死亡。」

chapters.en: This is the law of him who has a discharge, of the man who has an emission of semen whereby he is unclean,
chapters.zh: 这是患漏症和〔梦〕遗而不洁净的，

chapters.en: of a woman in her menstrual period, of any male or female who has a discharge, and of a man who lies with an unclean woman.’”
chapters.zh: 并有月经病的和患漏症的，无论男女，并人与不洁净女人同房的条例。

chapters.en: Now the LORD spoke to Moses after the death of two of Aaron’s sons when they approached the presence of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 亚伦的两个儿子近到耶和华面前死了。死了之后，耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses: “Tell your brother Aaron not to enter freely into the Most Holy Place behind the veil in front of the mercy seat on the ark, or else he will die, because I appear in the cloud above the mercy seat.
chapters.zh: 「要告诉你哥哥亚伦，不可随时进圣所的幔子内、到柜上的施恩座前，免得他死亡，因为我要从云中显现在施恩座上。

chapters.en: This is how Aaron is to enter the Holy Place: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 亚伦进圣所，要带一只公牛犊为赎罪祭，一只公绵羊为燔祭。

chapters.en: He is to wear the sacred linen tunic, with linen undergarments. He must tie a linen sash around him and put on the linen turban. These are holy garments, and he must bathe himself with water before he wears them.
chapters.zh: 要穿上细麻布圣内袍，把细麻布裤子穿在身上，腰束细麻布带子，头戴细麻布冠冕；这都是圣服。他要用水洗身，然后穿戴。

chapters.en: And he shall take from the congregation of Israel two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 要从以色列会众取两只公山羊为赎罪祭，一只公绵羊为燔祭。

chapters.en: Aaron is to present the bull for his sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household.
chapters.zh: 「亚伦要把赎罪祭的公牛奉上，为自己和本家赎罪；

chapters.en: Then he shall take the two goats and present them before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 也要把两只公山羊安置在会幕门口、耶和华面前，

chapters.en: After Aaron casts lots for the two goats, one for the LORD and the other for the scapegoat,
chapters.zh: 为那两只羊拈鬮，一鬮归与耶和华，一鬮归与阿撒泻勒。

chapters.en: he shall present the goat chosen by lot for the LORD and sacrifice it as a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 亚伦要把那拈鬮归与耶和华的羊献为赎罪祭，

chapters.en: But the goat chosen by lot as the scapegoat shall be presented alive before the LORD to make atonement by sending it into the wilderness as the scapegoat.
chapters.zh: 但那拈鬮归与阿撒泻勒的羊要活着安置在耶和华面前，用以赎罪，打发〔人送〕到旷野去，归与阿撒泻勒。

chapters.en: When Aaron presents the bull for his sin offering and makes atonement for himself and his household, he is to slaughter the bull for his own sin offering.
chapters.zh: 「亚伦要把赎罪祭的公牛牵来宰了，为自己和本家赎罪；

chapters.en: Then he must take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD, and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense, and take them inside the veil.
chapters.zh: 拿香炉，从耶和华面前的坛上盛满火炭，又拿一捧捣细的香料，都带入幔子内，

chapters.en: He is to put the incense on the fire before the LORD, and the cloud of incense will cover the mercy seat above the Testimony, so that he will not die.
chapters.zh: 在耶和华面前，把香放在火上，使香的烟云遮掩法〔柜〕上的施恩座，免得他死亡；

chapters.en: And he is to take some of the bull’s blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the east side of the mercy seat; then he shall sprinkle some of it with his finger seven times before the mercy seat.
chapters.zh: 也要取些公牛的血，用指头弹在施恩座的东面，又在施恩座的前面弹血七次。

chapters.en: Aaron shall then slaughter the goat for the sin offering for the people and bring its blood behind the veil, and with its blood he must do as he did with the bull’s blood: He is to sprinkle it against the mercy seat and in front of it.
chapters.zh: 「随后他要宰那为百姓作赎罪祭的公山羊，把羊的血带入幔子内，弹在施恩座的上面和前面，好像弹公牛的血一样。

chapters.en: So he shall make atonement for the Most Holy Place because of the impurities and rebellious acts of the Israelites in regard to all their sins. He is to do the same for the Tent of Meeting which abides among them in the midst of their impurities.
chapters.zh: 他因以色列人诸般的污秽、过犯，就是他们一切的罪愆，当这样在圣所行赎罪之礼，并因会幕在他们污秽之中，也要照样而行。

chapters.en: No one may be in the Tent of Meeting from the time Aaron goes in to make atonement in the Most Holy Place until he leaves, after he has made atonement for himself, his household, and the whole assembly of Israel.
chapters.zh: 他进圣所赎罪的时候，会幕里不可有人，直等到他为自己和本家并以色列全会众赎了罪出来。

chapters.en: Then he shall go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He is to take some of the bull’s blood and some of the goat’s blood and put it on all the horns of the altar.
chapters.zh: 他出来，要到耶和华面前的坛那里，在坛上行赎罪之礼，又要取些公牛的血和公山羊的血，抹在坛上四角的周围；

chapters.en: He is to sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times to cleanse it and consecrate it from the uncleanness of the Israelites.
chapters.zh: 也要用指头把血弹在坛上七次，洁净了坛，从坛上除掉以色列人诸般的污秽，使坛成圣。」

chapters.en: When Aaron has finished purifying the Most Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, he is to bring forward the live goat.
chapters.zh: 「亚伦为圣所和会幕并坛献完了赎罪祭，就要把那只活着的公山羊奉上。

chapters.en: Then he is to lay both hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities and rebellious acts of the Israelites in regard to all their sins. He is to put them on the goat’s head and send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a man appointed for the task.
chapters.zh: 两手按在羊头上，承认以色列人诸般的罪孽过犯，就是他们一切的罪愆，把这罪都归在羊的头上，藉着所派之人的手，送到旷野去。

chapters.en: The goat will carry on itself all their iniquities into a solitary place, and the man will release it into the wilderness.
chapters.zh: 要把这羊放在旷野，这羊要担当他们一切的罪孽，带到无人之地。

chapters.en: Then Aaron is to enter the Tent of Meeting, take off the linen garments he put on before entering the Most Holy Place, and leave them there.
chapters.zh: 「亚伦要进会幕，把他进圣所时所穿的细麻布衣服脱下，放在那里，

chapters.en: He is to bathe himself with water in a holy place and put on his own clothes. Then he must go out and sacrifice his burnt offering and the people’s burnt offering to make atonement for himself and for the people.
chapters.zh: 又要在圣处用水洗身，穿上衣服，出来，把自己的燔祭和百姓的燔祭献上，为自己和百姓赎罪。

chapters.en: He is also to burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
chapters.zh: 赎罪祭牲的脂油要在坛上焚烧。

chapters.en: The man who released the goat as the scapegoat must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water; afterward he may reenter the camp.
chapters.zh: 那放羊归与阿撒泻勒的人要洗衣服，用水洗身，然后进营。

chapters.en: The bull for the sin offering and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought into the Most Holy Place to make atonement, must be taken outside the camp; and their hides, flesh, and dung must be burned up.
chapters.zh: 作赎罪祭的公牛和公山羊的血既带入圣所赎罪，这牛羊就要搬到营外，将皮、肉、粪用火焚烧。

chapters.en: The one who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water, and afterward he may reenter the camp.
chapters.zh: 焚烧的人要洗衣服，用水洗身，然后进营。」

chapters.en: This is to be a permanent statute for you: On the tenth day of the seventh month, you shall humble yourselves and not do any work—whether the native or the foreigner who resides among you—
chapters.zh: 「每逢七月初十日，你们要刻苦己心，无论是本地人，是寄居在你们中间的外人，什么工都不可做；这要作你们永远的定例。

chapters.en: because on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you, and you will be clean from all your sins before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 因在这日要为你们赎罪，使你们洁净。你们要在耶和华面前得以洁净，脱尽一切的罪愆。

chapters.en: It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, that you may humble yourselves; it is a permanent statute.
chapters.zh: 这日你们要守为圣安息日，要刻苦己心；这为永远的定例。

chapters.en: The priest who is anointed and ordained to succeed his father as high priest shall make atonement. He will put on the sacred linen garments
chapters.zh: 那受膏、接续他父亲承接圣职的祭司要穿上细麻布的圣衣，行赎罪之礼。

chapters.en: and make atonement for the Most Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, and for the priests and all the people of the assembly.
chapters.zh: 他要在至圣所和会幕与坛行赎罪之礼，并要为众祭司和会众的百姓赎罪。

chapters.en:
This is to be a permanent statute for you, to make atonement once a year for the Israelites because of all their sins.”
And all this was done as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 这要作你们永远的定例－就是因以色列人一切的罪，要一年一次为他们赎罪。」 于是，亚伦照耶和华所吩咐摩西的行了。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites and tell them this is what the LORD has commanded:
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕亚伦和他儿子并以色列众人说，耶和华所吩咐的乃是这样：

chapters.en: ‘Anyone from the house of Israel who slaughters an ox, a lamb, or a goat in the camp or outside of it
chapters.zh: 凡以色列家中的人宰公牛，或是绵羊羔，或是山羊，不拘宰于营内营外，

chapters.en: instead of bringing it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before His tabernacle—that man shall incur bloodguilt. He has shed blood and must be cut off from among his people.
chapters.zh: 若未曾牵到会幕门口、耶和华的帐幕前献给耶和华为供物，流血的罪必归到那人身上。他流了血，要从民中剪除。

chapters.en: For this reason the Israelites will bring to the LORD the sacrifices they have been offering in the open fields. They are to bring them to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and offer them as sacrifices of peace offerings to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 这是为要使以色列人把他们在田野里所献的祭带到会幕门口、耶和华面前，交给祭司，献与耶和华为平安祭。

chapters.en: The priest will then splatter the blood on the altar of the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司要把血洒在会幕门口、耶和华的坛上，把脂油焚烧，献给耶和华为馨香的祭。

chapters.en: They must no longer offer their sacrifices to the goat demons to which they have prostituted themselves. This will be a permanent statute for them for the generations to come.’
chapters.zh: 他们不可再献祭给他们行邪淫所随从的鬼魔〔注：原文是公山羊〕；这要作他们世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: Tell them that if anyone from the house of Israel or any foreigner living among them offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice
chapters.zh: 「你要晓谕他们说：凡以色列家中的人，或是寄居在他们中间的外人，献燔祭或是〔平安〕祭，

chapters.en: but does not bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting to sacrifice it to the LORD, that man must be cut off from his people.
chapters.zh: 若不带到会幕门口献给耶和华，那人必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: If anyone from the house of Israel or a foreigner living among them eats any blood, I will set My face against that person and cut him off from among his people.
chapters.zh: 「凡以色列家中的人，或是寄居在他们中间的外人，若吃什么血，我必向那吃血的人变脸，把他从民中剪除。

chapters.en: For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you to make atonement for your souls upon the altar; for it is the blood that makes atonement for the soul.
chapters.zh: 因为活物的生命是在血中。我把这血赐给你们，可以在坛上为你们的生命赎罪；因血里有生命，所以能赎罪。

chapters.en: Therefore I say to the Israelites, ‘None of you may eat blood, nor may any foreigner living among you eat blood.’
chapters.zh: 因此，我对以色列人说：你们都不可吃血；寄居在你们中间的外人也不可吃血。

chapters.en: And if any Israelite or foreigner living among them hunts down a wild animal or bird that may be eaten, he must drain its blood and cover it with dirt.
chapters.zh: 凡以色列人，或是寄居在他们中间的外人，若打猎得了可吃的禽兽，必放出牠的血来，用土掩盖。

chapters.en: For the life of all flesh is its blood. Therefore I have told the Israelites, ‘You must not eat the blood of any living thing, because the life of all flesh is its blood; whoever eats it must be cut off.’
chapters.zh: 「论到一切活物的生命，就在血中。所以我对以色列人说：无论什么活物的血，你们都不可吃，因为一切活物的血就是他的生命。凡吃了血的，必被剪除。

chapters.en: And any person, whether native or foreigner, who eats anything found dead or mauled by wild beasts must wash his clothes and bathe with water, and he will be unclean until evening; then he will be clean.
chapters.zh: 凡吃自死的，或是被野兽撕裂的，无论是本地人，是寄居的，必不洁净到晚上，都要洗衣服，用水洗身，到了晚上才为洁净。

chapters.en: But if he does not wash his clothes and bathe himself, then he shall bear his iniquity.”
chapters.zh: 但他若不洗衣服，也不洗身，就必担当他的罪孽。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：我是耶和华－你们的上帝。

chapters.en: You must not follow the practices of the land of Egypt, where you used to live, and you must not follow the practices of the land of Canaan, into which I am bringing you. You must not walk in their customs.
chapters.zh: 你们从前住的埃及地，那里人的行为，你们不可效法，我要领你们到的迦南地，那里人的行为也不可效法，也不可照他们的恶俗行。

chapters.en: You are to practice My judgments and keep My statutes by walking in them. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 你们要遵我的典章，守我的律例，按此而行。我是耶和华－你们的上帝。

chapters.en: Keep My statutes and My judgments, for the man who does these things will live by them. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们要守我的律例典章；人若遵行，就必因此活着。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: None of you are to approach any close relative to have sexual relations. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「你们都不可露骨肉之亲的下体，亲近他们。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: You must not expose the nakedness of your father by having sexual relations with your mother. She is your mother; you must not have sexual relations with her.
chapters.zh: 不可露你母亲的下体，羞辱了你父亲。她是你的母亲，不可露她的下体。

chapters.en: You must not have sexual relations with your father’s wife; it would dishonor your father.
chapters.zh: 不可露你继母的下体；这本是你父亲的下体。

chapters.en: You must not have sexual relations with your sister, either your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter, whether she was born in the same home or elsewhere.
chapters.zh: 你的姊妹，不拘是异母同父的，是异父同母的，无论是生在家生在外的，都不可露她们的下体。

chapters.en: You must not have sexual relations with your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, for that would shame your family.
chapters.zh: 不可露你孙女或是外孙女的下体，露了她们的下体就是露了自己的下体。

chapters.en: You must not have sexual relations with the daughter of your father’s wife, born to your father; she is your sister.
chapters.zh: 你继母从你父亲生的女儿本是你的妹妹，不可露她的下体。

chapters.en: You must not have sexual relations with your father’s sister; she is your father’s close relative.
chapters.zh: 不可露你姑母的下体；她是你父亲的骨肉之亲。

chapters.en: You must not have sexual relations with your mother’s sister, for she is your mother’s close relative.
chapters.zh: 不可露你姨母的下体；她是你母亲的骨肉之亲。

chapters.en: You must not dishonor your father’s brother by approaching his wife to have sexual relations with her; she is your aunt.
chapters.zh: 不可亲近你伯叔之妻，羞辱了你伯叔；她是你的伯叔母。

chapters.en: You must not have sexual relations with your daughter-in-law. She is your son’s wife; you are not to have sexual relations with her.
chapters.zh: 不可露你儿妇的下体；她是你儿子的妻，不可露她的下体。

chapters.en: You must not have sexual relations with your brother’s wife; that would shame your brother.
chapters.zh: 不可露你弟兄妻子的下体；这本是你弟兄的下体。

chapters.en: You must not have sexual relations with both a woman and her daughter. You are not to marry her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter and have sexual relations with her. They are close relatives; it is depraved.
chapters.zh: 不可露了妇人的下体，又露她女儿的下体，也不可娶她孙女或是外孙女，露她们的下体；她们是骨肉之亲，这本是大恶。

chapters.en: You must not take your wife’s sister as a rival wife and have sexual relations with her while your wife is still alive.
chapters.zh: 你妻还在的时候，不可另娶她的姊妹作对头，露她的下体。

chapters.en: You must not approach a woman to have sexual relations with her during her menstrual period.
chapters.zh: 「女人行经不洁净的时候，不可露她的下体，与她亲近。

chapters.en: You must not lie carnally with your neighbor’s wife and thus defile yourself with her.
chapters.zh: 不可与邻舍的妻行淫，玷污自己。

chapters.en: You must not give any of your children to be sacrificed to Molech, for you must not profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可使你的儿女经火归与摩洛，也不可亵渎你上帝的名。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: You must not lie with a man as with a woman; that is an abomination.
chapters.zh: 不可与男人苟合，像与女人一样；这本是可憎恶的。

chapters.en: You must not lie carnally with any animal, thus defiling yourself with it; a woman must not stand before an animal to mate with it; that is a perversion.
chapters.zh: 不可与兽淫合，玷污自己。女人也不可站在兽前，与牠淫合；这本是逆性的事。

chapters.en: Do not defile yourselves by any of these practices, for by all these things the nations I am driving out before you have defiled themselves.
chapters.zh: 「在这一切的事上，你们都不可玷污自己；因为我在你们面前所逐出的列邦，在这一切的事上玷污了自己；

chapters.en: Even the land has become defiled, so I am punishing it for its sin, and the land will vomit out its inhabitants.
chapters.zh: 连地也玷污了，所以我追讨那地的罪孽，那地也吐出它的居民。

chapters.en: But you are to keep My statutes and ordinances, and you must not commit any of these abominations—neither your native-born nor the foreigner who lives among you.
chapters.zh: 故此，你们要守我的律例典章。这一切可憎恶的事，无论是本地人，是寄居在你们中间的外人，都不可行，

chapters.en: For the men who were in the land before you committed all these abominations, and the land has become defiled.
chapters.zh: （在你们以先居住那地的人行了这一切可憎恶的事，地就玷污了，）

chapters.en: So if you defile the land, it will vomit you out as it spewed out the nations before you.
chapters.zh: 免得你们玷污那地的时候，地就把你们吐出，像吐出在你们以先的国民一样。

chapters.en: Therefore anyone who commits any of these abominations must be cut off from among his people.
chapters.zh: 无论什么人，行了其中可憎的一件事，必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: You must keep My charge not to practice any of the abominable customs that were practiced before you, so that you do not defile yourselves by them. I am the LORD your God.”
chapters.zh: 所以，你们要守我所吩咐的，免得你们随从那些可憎的恶俗，就是在你们以先〔的人〕所常行的，以致玷污了自己。我是耶和华－你们的上帝。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to the whole congregation of Israel and tell them: Be holy because I, the LORD your God, am holy.
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列全会众说：你们要圣洁，因为我耶和华－你们的上帝是圣洁的。

chapters.en: Each of you must respect his mother and father, and you must keep My Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 你们各人都当孝敬父母，也要守我的安息日。我是耶和华－你们的上帝。

chapters.en: Do not turn to idols or make for yourselves molten gods. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 你们不可偏向虚无的神，也不可为自己铸造神〔像〕。我是耶和华－你们的上帝。

chapters.en: When you sacrifice a peace offering to the LORD, you shall offer it for your acceptance.
chapters.zh: 你们献平安祭给耶和华的时候，要献得可蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it, or on the next day; but what remains on the third day must be burned up.
chapters.zh: 这祭物要在献的那一天和第二天吃，若有剩到第三天的，就必用火焚烧。

chapters.en: If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is tainted and will not be accepted.
chapters.zh: 第三天若再吃，这就为可憎恶的，必不蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: Whoever eats it will bear his iniquity, for he has profaned what is holy to the LORD. That person must be cut off from his people.
chapters.zh: 凡吃的人必担当他的罪孽；因为他亵渎了耶和华的圣物，那人必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: When you reap the harvest of your land, you are not to reap to the very edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest.
chapters.zh: 「在你们的地收割庄稼，不可割尽田角，也不可拾取所遗落的。

chapters.en: You must not strip your vineyard bare or gather its fallen grapes. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 不可摘尽葡萄园的果子，也不可拾取葡萄园所掉的果子；要留给穷人和寄居的。我是耶和华－你们的上帝。

chapters.en: You must not steal. You must not lie or deceive one another.
chapters.zh: 「你们不可偷盗，不可欺骗，也不可彼此说谎。

chapters.en: You must not swear falsely by My name and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可指着我的名起假誓，亵渎你上帝的名。我是耶和华。

chapters.en:
You must not defraud your neighbor or rob him.
You must not withhold until morning the wages due a hired hand.
chapters.zh: 「不可欺压你的邻舍，也不可抢夺他的物。雇工人的工价，不可在你那里过夜，留到早晨。

chapters.en: You must not curse the deaf or place a stumbling block before the blind, but you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可咒骂聋子，也不可将绊脚石放在瞎子面前，只要敬畏你的上帝。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: You must not pervert justice; you must not show partiality to the poor or favoritism to the rich; you are to judge your neighbor fairly.
chapters.zh: 「你们施行审判，不可行不义；不可偏护穷人，也不可重看有势力的人，只要按着公义审判你的邻舍。

chapters.en:
You must not go about spreading slander among your people.
You must not endanger the life of your neighbor. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可在民中往来搬弄是非，也不可与邻舍为敌，置之于死〔注：原文是流他的血〕。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: You must not harbor hatred against your brother in your heart. Directly rebuke your neighbor, so that you will not incur guilt on account of him.
chapters.zh: 「不可心里恨你的弟兄；总要指摘你的邻舍，免得因他担罪。

chapters.en: Do not seek revenge or bear a grudge against any of your people, but love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可报仇，也不可埋怨你本国的子民，却要爱人如己。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: You are to keep My statutes. You shall not crossbreed two different kinds of livestock; you shall not sow your fields with two kinds of seed; and you shall not wear clothing made of two kinds of material.
chapters.zh: 「你们要守我的律例。不可叫你的牲畜与异类配合；不可用两样搀杂的种种你的地，也不可用两样搀杂的料做衣服穿在身上。

chapters.en: If a man lies carnally with a slave girl promised to another man but who has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there must be due punishment. But they are not to be put to death, because she had not been freed.
chapters.zh: 「婢女许配了丈夫，还没有被赎、得释放，人若与她行淫，二人要受刑罚，却不把他们治死，因为婢女还没有得自由。

chapters.en: The man, however, must bring a ram to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting as his guilt offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 那人要把赎愆祭，就是一只公绵羊牵到会幕门口、耶和华面前。

chapters.en: The priest shall make atonement on his behalf before the LORD with the ram of the guilt offering for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven the sin he has committed.
chapters.zh: 祭司要用赎愆祭的羊在耶和华面前赎他所犯的罪，他的罪就必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: When you enter the land and plant any kind of tree for food, you shall regard the fruit as forbidden. For three years it will be forbidden to you and must not be eaten.
chapters.zh: 「你们到了迦南地，栽种各样结果子的树木，就要以所结的果子如未受割礼的一样。三年之久，你们要以这些果子，如未受割礼的，是不可吃的。

chapters.en: In the fourth year all its fruit must be consecrated as a praise offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 但第四年所结的果子全要成为圣，用以赞美耶和华。

chapters.en: But in the fifth year you may eat its fruit; thus your harvest will be increased. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 第五年，你们要吃那树上的果子，好叫树给你们结果子更多。我是耶和华－你们的上帝。

chapters.en:
You must not eat anything with blood still in it.
You must not practice divination or sorcery.
chapters.zh: 「你们不可吃带血的物；不可用法术，也不可观兆。

chapters.en: You must not cut off the hair at the sides of your head or clip off the edges of your beard.
chapters.zh: 头的周围〔注：或译：两鬓〕不可剃，胡须的周围也不可损坏。

chapters.en: You must not make any cuts in your bodies for the dead or put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可为死人用刀划身，也不可在身上刺花纹。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: You must not defile your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will be prostituted and filled with depravity.
chapters.zh: 「不可辱没你的女儿，使她为娼妓，恐怕地上〔的人〕专向淫乱，地就满了大恶。

chapters.en: You must keep My Sabbaths and have reverence for My sanctuary. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你们要守我的安息日，敬我的圣所。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: You must not turn to mediums or spiritists; do not seek them out, or you will be defiled by them. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 「不可偏向那些交鬼的和行巫术的；不可求问他们，以致被他们玷污了。我是耶和华－你们的上帝。

chapters.en: You are to rise in the presence of the elderly, honor the aged, and fear your God. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「在白发的人面前，你要站起来；也要尊敬老人，又要敬畏你的上帝。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: When a foreigner resides with you in your land, you must not oppress him.
chapters.zh: 「若有外人在你们国中和你同居，就不可欺负他。

chapters.en: You must treat the foreigner living among you as native-born and love him as yourself, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 和你们同居的外人，你们要看他如本地人一样，并要爱他如己，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。我是耶和华－你们的上帝。

chapters.en: You must not use dishonest measures of length, weight, or volume.
chapters.zh: 「你们施行审判，不可行不义；在尺、秤、升、斗上也是如此。

chapters.en: You shall maintain honest scales and weights, an honest ephah, and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 要用公道天平、公道法码、公道升斗、公道秤。我是耶和华－你们的上帝，曾把你们从埃及地领出来的。

chapters.en: You must keep all My statutes and all My ordinances and follow them. I am the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 你们要谨守遵行我一切的律例典章。我是耶和华。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Tell the Israelites, ‘Any Israelite or foreigner living in Israel who gives any of his children to Molech must be put to death. The people of the land are to stone him.
chapters.zh: 「你还要晓谕以色列人说：凡以色列人，或是在以色列中寄居的外人，把自己的儿女献给摩洛的，总要治死他；本地人要用石头把他打死。

chapters.en: And I will set My face against that man and cut him off from his people, because by giving his offspring to Molech, he has defiled My sanctuary and profaned My holy name.
chapters.zh: 我也要向那人变脸，把他从民中剪除；因为他把儿女献给摩洛，玷污我的圣所，亵渎我的圣名。

chapters.en: And if the people of the land ever hide their eyes and fail to put to death the man who gives one of his children to Molech,
chapters.zh: 那人把儿女献给摩洛，本地人若佯为不见，不把他治死，

chapters.en: then I will set My face against that man and his family and cut off from among their people both him and all who follow him in prostituting themselves with Molech.
chapters.zh: 我就要向这人和他的家变脸，把他和一切随他与摩洛行邪淫的人都从民中剪除。

chapters.en: Whoever turns to mediums or spiritists to prostitute himself with them, I will also set My face against that person and cut him off from his people.
chapters.zh: 「人偏向交鬼的和行巫术的，随他们行邪淫，我要向那人变脸，把他从民中剪除。

chapters.en: Consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 所以你们要自洁成圣，因为我是耶和华－你们的上帝。

chapters.en: And you shall keep My statutes and practice them. I am the LORD who sanctifies you.
chapters.zh: 你们要谨守遵行我的律例；我是叫你们成圣的耶和华。

chapters.en: If anyone curses his father or mother, he must be put to death. He has cursed his father or mother; his blood shall be upon him.
chapters.zh: 凡咒骂父母的，总要治死他；他咒骂了父母，他的罪〔注：原文是血；本章同〕要归到他身上。

chapters.en: If a man commits adultery with another man’s wife—with the wife of his neighbor—both the adulterer and the adulteress must surely be put to death.
chapters.zh: 「与邻舍之妻行淫的，奸夫淫妇都必治死。

chapters.en: If a man lies with his father’s wife, he has uncovered his father’s nakedness. Both must surely be put to death; their blood is upon them.
chapters.zh: 与继母行淫的，就是羞辱了他父亲，总要把他们二人治死，罪要归到他们身上。

chapters.en: If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both must surely be put to death. They have acted perversely; their blood is upon them.
chapters.zh: 与儿妇同房的，总要把他们二人治死；他们行了逆伦的事，罪要归到他们身上。

chapters.en: If a man lies with a man as with a woman, they have both committed an abomination. They must surely be put to death; their blood is upon them.
chapters.zh: 人若与男人苟合，像与女人一样，他们二人行了可憎的事，总要把他们治死，罪要归到他们身上。

chapters.en: If a man marries both a woman and her mother, it is depraved. Both he and they must be burned in the fire, so that there will be no depravity among you.
chapters.zh: 人若娶妻，并娶其母，便是大恶，要把这三人用火焚烧，使你们中间免去大恶。

chapters.en: If a man lies carnally with an animal, he must be put to death. And you are also to kill the animal.
chapters.zh: 人若与兽淫合，总要治死他，也要杀那兽。

chapters.en: If a woman approaches any animal to mate with it, you must kill both the woman and the animal. They must surely be put to death; their blood is upon them.
chapters.zh: 女人若与兽亲近，与牠淫合，你要杀那女人和那兽，总要把他们治死，罪要归到他们身上。

chapters.en: If a man marries his sister, whether the daughter of his father or of his mother, and they have sexual relations, it is a disgrace. They must be cut off in the sight of their people. He has uncovered the nakedness of his sister; he shall bear his iniquity.
chapters.zh: 「人若娶他的姊妹，无论是异母同父的，是异父同母的，彼此见了下体，这是可耻的事；他们必在本民的眼前被剪除。他露了姊妹的下体，必担当自己的罪孽。

chapters.en: If a man lies with a menstruating woman and has sexual relations with her, he has exposed the source of her flow, and she has uncovered the source of her blood. Both of them must be cut off from among their people.
chapters.zh: 妇人有月经，若与她同房，露了她的下体，就是露了妇人的血源，妇人也露了自己的血源，二人必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: You must not have sexual relations with the sister of your mother or your father, for it is exposing one’s own kin; both shall bear their iniquity.
chapters.zh: 不可露姨母或是姑母的下体，这是露了骨肉之亲的下体；二人必担当自己的罪孽。

chapters.en: If a man lies with his uncle’s wife, he has uncovered the nakedness of his uncle. They will bear their sin; they shall die childless.
chapters.zh: 人若与伯叔之妻同房，就羞辱了他的伯叔；二人要担当自己的罪，必无子女而死。

chapters.en: If a man marries his brother’s wife, it is an act of impurity. He has uncovered the nakedness of his brother; they shall be childless.
chapters.zh: 人若娶弟兄之妻，这本是污秽的事，羞辱了他的弟兄；二人必无子女。

chapters.en: You are therefore to keep all My statutes and ordinances, so that the land where I am bringing you to live will not vomit you out.
chapters.zh: 「所以，你们要谨守遵行我一切的律例典章，免得我领你们去住的那地把你们吐出。

chapters.en: You must not follow the statutes of the nations I am driving out before you. Because they did all these things, I abhorred them.
chapters.zh: 我在你们面前所逐出的国民，你们不可随从他们的风俗；因为他们行了这一切的事，所以我厌恶他们。

chapters.en: But I have told you that you will inherit their land, since I will give it to you as an inheritance—a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God, who has set you apart from the peoples.
chapters.zh: 但我对你们说过，你们要承受他们的地，就是我要赐给你们为业、流奶与蜜之地。我是耶和华－你们的上帝，使你们与万民有分别的。

chapters.en: You are therefore to distinguish between clean and unclean animals and birds. Do not become contaminated by any animal or bird, or by anything that crawls on the ground; I have set these apart as unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们要把洁净和不洁净的禽兽分别出来；不可因我给你们分为不洁净的禽兽，或是滋生在地上的活物，使自己成为可憎恶的。

chapters.en: You are to be holy to Me because I, the LORD, am holy, and I have set you apart from the nations to be My own.
chapters.zh: 你们要归我为圣，因为我－耶和华是圣的，并叫你们与万民有分别，使你们作我的民。

chapters.en: A man or a woman who is a medium or spiritist must surely be put to death. They shall be stoned; their blood is upon them.’”
chapters.zh: 「无论男女，是交鬼的或行巫术的，总要治死他们。人必用石头把他们打死，罪要归到他们身上。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to Aaron’s sons, the priests, and tell them that a priest is not to defile himself for a dead person among his people,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你告诉亚伦子孙作祭司的说：祭司不可为民中的死人沾染自己，

chapters.en: except for his immediate family—his mother, father, son, daughter, or brother,
chapters.zh: 除非为他骨肉之亲的父母、儿女、弟兄，

chapters.en: or his unmarried sister who is near to him, since she has no husband.
chapters.zh: 和未曾出嫁、作处女的姊妹，才可以沾染自己。

chapters.en: He is not to defile himself for those related to him by marriage, and so profane himself.
chapters.zh: 祭司既在民中为首，就不可从俗沾染自己。

chapters.en: Priests must not make bald spots on their heads, shave off the edges of their beards, or make cuts in their bodies.
chapters.zh: 不可使头光秃；不可剃除胡须的周围，也不可用刀划身。

chapters.en: They must be holy to their God and not profane the name of their God. Because they present to the LORD the food offerings, the food of their God, they must be holy.
chapters.zh: 要归上帝为圣，不可亵渎上帝的名；因为耶和华的火祭，就是上帝的食物，是他们献的，所以他们要成为圣。

chapters.en: A priest must not marry a woman defiled by prostitution or divorced by her husband, for the priest is holy to his God.
chapters.zh: 不可娶妓女或被污的女人为妻，也不可娶被休的妇人为妻，因为祭司是归上帝为圣。

chapters.en: You are to regard him as holy, since he presents the food of your God. He shall be holy to you, because I the LORD am holy—I who set you apart.
chapters.zh: 所以你要使他成圣，因为他奉献你上帝的食物；你要以他为圣，因为我－使你们成圣的耶和华－是圣的。

chapters.en: If a priest’s daughter defiles herself by prostituting herself, she profanes her father; she must be burned in the fire.
chapters.zh: 祭司的女儿若行淫辱没自己，就辱没了父亲，必用火将她焚烧。

chapters.en: The priest who is highest among his brothers, who has had the anointing oil poured on his head and has been ordained to wear the priestly garments, must not let his hair hang loose or tear his garments.
chapters.zh: 「在弟兄中作大祭司、头上倒了膏油、又承接圣职、穿了〔圣〕衣的，不可蓬头散发，也不可撕裂衣服。

chapters.en: He must not go near any dead body; he must not defile himself, even for his father or mother.
chapters.zh: 不可挨近死尸，也不可为父母沾染自己。

chapters.en: He must not leave or desecrate the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可出圣所，也不可亵渎上帝的圣所，因为上帝膏油的冠冕在他头上。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: The woman he marries must be a virgin.
chapters.zh: 他要娶处女为妻。

chapters.en: He is not to marry a widow, a divorced woman, or one defiled by prostitution. He is to marry a virgin from his own people,
chapters.zh: 寡妇或是被休的妇人，或是被污为妓的女人，都不可娶；只可娶本民中的处女为妻。

chapters.en: so that he does not defile his offspring among his people, for I am the LORD who sanctifies him.”
chapters.zh: 不可在民中辱没他的儿女，因为我是叫他成圣的耶和华。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Say to Aaron, ‘For the generations to come, none of your descendants who has a physical defect may approach to offer the food of his God.
chapters.zh: 「你告诉亚伦说：你世世代代的后裔，凡有残疾的，都不可近前来献他上帝的食物。

chapters.en: No man who has any defect may approach—no man who is blind, lame, disfigured, or deformed;
chapters.zh: 因为凡有残疾的，无论是瞎眼的、瘸腿的、塌鼻子的、肢体有余的、

chapters.en: no man who has a broken foot or hand,
chapters.zh: 折脚折手的、

chapters.en: or who is a hunchback or dwarf, or who has an eye defect, a festering rash, scabs, or a crushed testicle.
chapters.zh: 驼背的、矮矬的、眼睛有毛病的、长癣的、长疥的，或是损坏肾子的，都不可近前来。

chapters.en: No descendant of Aaron the priest who has a defect shall approach to present the food offerings to the LORD. Since he has a defect, he is not to come near to offer the food of his God.
chapters.zh: 祭司亚伦的后裔，凡有残疾的，都不可近前来，将火祭献给耶和华。他有残疾，不可近前来献上帝的食物。

chapters.en: He may eat the most holy food of his God as well as the holy food,
chapters.zh: 上帝的食物，无论是圣的，至圣的，他都可以吃。

chapters.en: but because he has a defect, he must not go near the veil or approach the altar, so as not to desecrate My sanctuaries. For I am the LORD who sanctifies them.’”
chapters.zh: 但不可进到幔子前，也不可就近坛前；因为他有残疾，免得亵渎我的圣所。我是叫他成圣的耶和华。」

chapters.en: Moses told this to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites.
chapters.zh: 于是，摩西晓谕亚伦和亚伦的子孙，并以色列众人。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Tell Aaron and his sons to treat with respect the sacred offerings that the Israelites have consecrated to Me, so that they do not profane My holy name. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「你吩咐亚伦和他子孙说：要远离以色列人所分别为圣、归给我的圣物，免得亵渎我的圣名。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: Tell them that for the generations to come, if any of their descendants in a state of uncleanness approaches the sacred offerings that the Israelites consecrate to the LORD, that person must be cut off from My presence. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你要对他们说：你们世世代代的后裔，凡身上有污秽、亲近以色列人所分别为圣、归耶和华圣物的，那人必在我面前剪除。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: If a descendant of Aaron has a skin disease or a discharge, he may not eat the sacred offerings until he is clean. Whoever touches anything defiled by a corpse or by a man who has an emission of semen,
chapters.zh: 亚伦的后裔，凡长大痲疯的，或是有漏症的，不可吃圣物，直等他洁净了。无论谁摸那因死尸不洁净的物〔注：或译：人〕，或是遗精的人，

chapters.en: or whoever touches a crawling creature or a person that makes him unclean, whatever the uncleanness may be—
chapters.zh: 或是摸什么使他不洁净的爬物，或是摸那使他不洁净的人（不拘那人有什么不洁净），

chapters.en: the man who touches any of these will remain unclean until evening. He must not eat from the sacred offerings unless he has bathed himself with water.
chapters.zh: 摸了这些人、物的，必不洁净到晚上；若不用水洗身，就不可吃圣物。

chapters.en: When the sun has set, he will become clean, and then he may eat from the sacred offerings, for they are his food.
chapters.zh: 日落的时候，他就洁净了，然后可以吃圣物，因为这是他的食物。

chapters.en: He must not eat anything found dead or torn by wild animals, which would make him unclean. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 自死的或是被野兽撕裂的，他不可吃，因此污秽自己。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: The priests must keep My charge, lest they bear the guilt and die because they profane it. I am the LORD who sanctifies them.
chapters.zh: 所以他们要守我所吩咐的，免得轻忽了，因此担罪而死。我是叫他们成圣的耶和华。

chapters.en: No one outside a priest’s family may eat the sacred offering, nor may the guest of a priest or his hired hand eat it.
chapters.zh: 「凡外人不可吃圣物；寄居在祭司家的，或是雇工人，都不可吃圣物；

chapters.en: But if a priest buys a slave with his own money, or if a slave is born in his household, that slave may eat his food.
chapters.zh: 倘若祭司买人，是他的钱买的，那人就可以吃圣物；生在他家的人也可以吃。

chapters.en: If the priest’s daughter is married to a man other than a priest, she is not to eat of the sacred contributions.
chapters.zh: 祭司的女儿若嫁外人，就不可吃举祭的圣物。

chapters.en: But if a priest’s daughter with no children becomes widowed or divorced and returns to her father’s house, she may share her father’s food as in her youth. But no outsider may share it.
chapters.zh: 但祭司的女儿若是寡妇，或是被休的，没有孩子，又归回父家，与她青年一样，就可以吃她父亲的食物；只是外人不可吃。

chapters.en: If anyone eats a sacred offering in error, he must add a fifth to its value and give the sacred offering to the priest.
chapters.zh: 若有人误吃了圣物，要照圣物的原数加上五分之一交给祭司。

chapters.en: The priests must not profane the sacred offerings that the Israelites present to the LORD
chapters.zh: 祭司不可亵渎以色列人所献给耶和华的圣物，

chapters.en: by allowing the people to eat the sacred offerings and thus to bear the punishment for guilt. For I am the LORD who sanctifies them.”
chapters.zh: 免得他们在吃圣物上自取罪孽，因为我是叫他们成圣的耶和华。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to Aaron and his sons and all the Israelites and tell them, ‘Any man of the house of Israel or any foreign resident who presents a gift for a burnt offering to the LORD, whether to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering,
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕亚伦和他子孙，并以色列众人说：以色列家中的人，或在以色列中寄居的，凡献供物，无论是所许的愿，是甘心献的，就是献给耶和华作燔祭的，

chapters.en: must offer an unblemished male from the cattle, sheep, or goats in order for it to be accepted on your behalf.
chapters.zh: 要将没有残疾的公牛，或是绵羊，或是山羊〔献上〕，如此方蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: You must not present anything with a defect, because it will not be accepted on your behalf.
chapters.zh: 凡有残疾的，你们不可献上，因为这不蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: When a man presents a peace offering to the LORD from the herd or flock to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, it must be without blemish or defect to be acceptable.
chapters.zh: 凡从牛群或是羊群中，将平安祭献给耶和华，为要还特许的愿，或是作甘心献的，所献的必纯全无残疾的才蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: You are not to present to the LORD any animal that is blind, injured, or maimed, or anything with a running sore, a festering rash, or a scab; you must not put any of these on the altar as a food offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 瞎眼的、折伤的、残废的、有瘤子的、长癣的、长疥的都不可献给耶和华，也不可在坛上作为火祭献给耶和华。

chapters.en: You may present as a freewill offering an ox or sheep that has a deformed or stunted limb, but it is not acceptable in fulfillment of a vow.
chapters.zh: 无论是公牛是绵羊羔，若肢体有余的，或是缺少的，只可作甘心祭献上；用以还愿，却不蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: You are not to present to the LORD an animal whose testicles are bruised, crushed, torn, or cut; you are not to sacrifice them in your land.
chapters.zh: 肾子损伤的，或是压碎的，或是破裂的，或是骟了的，不可献给耶和华，在你们的地上也不可〔这样〕行。

chapters.en: Neither you nor a foreigner shall present food to your God from any such animal. They will not be accepted on your behalf, because they are deformed and flawed.’”
chapters.zh: 这类的物，你们从外人的手，一样也不可接受作你们上帝的食物献上；因为这些都有损坏，有残疾，不蒙悦纳。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “When an ox, a sheep, or a goat is born, it must remain with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day on, it will be acceptable as a food offering presented to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「才生的公牛，或是绵羊或是山羊，七天当跟着母；从第八天以后，可以当供物蒙悦纳，作为耶和华的火祭。

chapters.en: But you must not slaughter an ox or a sheep on the same day as its young.
chapters.zh: 无论是母牛是母羊，不可同日宰母和子。

chapters.en: When you sacrifice a thank offering to the LORD, offer it so that it may be acceptable on your behalf.
chapters.zh: 你们献感谢祭给耶和华，要献得可蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: It must be eaten that same day. Do not leave any of it until morning. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 要当天吃，一点不可留到早晨。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: You are to keep My commandments and practice them. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「你们要谨守遵行我的诫命。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: You must not profane My holy name. I must be acknowledged as holy among the Israelites. I am the LORD who sanctifies you,
chapters.zh: 你们不可亵渎我的圣名；我在以色列人中，却要被尊为圣。我是叫你们成圣的耶和华，

chapters.en: who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 把你们从埃及地领出来，作你们的上帝。我是耶和华。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them, ‘These are My appointed feasts, the feasts of the LORD that you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies.
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：耶和华的节期，你们要宣告为圣会的节期。

chapters.en: For six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, a day of sacred assembly. You must not do any work; wherever you live, it is a Sabbath to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 六日要做工，第七日是圣安息日，当有圣会；你们什么工都不可做。这是在你们一切的住处向耶和华守的安息日。

chapters.en: These are the LORD’s appointed feasts, the sacred assemblies you are to proclaim at their appointed times.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的节期，就是你们到了日期要宣告为圣会的，乃是这些。」

chapters.en: The Passover to the LORD begins at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month.
chapters.zh: 「正月十四日，黄昏的时候，是耶和华的逾越节。

chapters.en: On the fifteenth day of the same month begins the Feast of Unleavened Bread to the LORD. For seven days you must eat unleavened bread.
chapters.zh: 这月十五日是向耶和华守的无酵节；你们要吃无酵饼七日。

chapters.en: On the first day you are to hold a sacred assembly; you are not to do any regular work.
chapters.zh: 第一日当有圣会，什么劳碌的工都不可做；

chapters.en: For seven days you are to present a food offering to the LORD. On the seventh day there shall be a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work.’”
chapters.zh: 要将火祭献给耶和华七日。第七日是圣会，什么劳碌的工都不可做。」

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘When you enter the land that I am giving you and you reap its harvest, you are to bring to the priest a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest.
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：你们到了我赐给你们的地，收割庄稼的时候，要将初熟的庄稼一捆带给祭司。

chapters.en: And he shall wave the sheaf before the LORD so that it may be accepted on your behalf; the priest is to wave it on the day after the Sabbath.
chapters.zh: 他要把这一捆在耶和华面前摇一摇，使你们得蒙悦纳。祭司要在安息日的次日把这捆摇一摇。

chapters.en: On the day you wave the sheaf, you shall offer a year-old lamb without blemish as a burnt offering to the LORD,
chapters.zh: 摇这捆的日子，你们要把一岁、没有残疾的公绵羊羔献给耶和华为燔祭。

chapters.en: along with its grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil—a food offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma—and its drink offering of a quarter hin of wine.
chapters.zh: 同献的素祭，就是调油的细面〔伊法〕十分之二，作为馨香的火祭，献给耶和华。同献的奠祭，要酒一欣四分之一。

chapters.en: You must not eat any bread or roasted or new grain until the very day you have brought this offering to your God. This is to be a permanent statute for the generations to come, wherever you live.
chapters.zh: 无论是饼，是烘的子粒，是新穗子，你们都不可吃，直等到把你们献给上帝的供物带来的那一天才可以吃。这在你们一切的住处作为世世代代永远的定例。」

chapters.en: From the day after the Sabbath, the day you brought the sheaf of the wave offering, you are to count off seven full weeks.
chapters.zh: 「你们要从安息日的次日，献禾捆为摇祭的那日算起，要满了七个安息日。

chapters.en: You shall count off fifty days until the day after the seventh Sabbath, and then present an offering of new grain to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 到第七个安息日的次日，共计五十天，又要将新素祭献给耶和华。

chapters.en: Bring two loaves of bread from your dwellings as a wave offering, each made from two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour, baked with leaven, as the firstfruits to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 要从你们的住处取出细面〔伊法〕十分之二，加酵，烤成两个摇祭的饼，当作初熟之物献给耶和华。

chapters.en: Along with the bread you are to present seven unblemished male lambs a year old, one young bull, and two rams. They will be a burnt offering to the LORD, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings—a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 又要将一岁、没有残疾的羊羔七只、公牛犊一只、公绵羊两只，和饼一同奉上。这些与同献的素祭和奠祭要作为燔祭献给耶和华，就是作馨香的火祭献给耶和华。

chapters.en: You shall also prepare one male goat as a sin offering and two male lambs a year old as a peace offering.
chapters.zh: 你们要献一只公山羊为赎罪祭，两只一岁的公绵羊羔为平安祭。

chapters.en: The priest is to wave the lambs as a wave offering before the LORD, together with the bread of the firstfruits. The bread and the two lambs shall be holy to the LORD for the priest.
chapters.zh: 祭司要把这些和初熟〔麦子做〕的饼一同作摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇；这是献与耶和华为圣物归给祭司的。

chapters.en: On that same day you are to proclaim a sacred assembly, and you must not do any regular work. This is to be a permanent statute wherever you live for the generations to come.
chapters.zh: 当这日，你们要宣告圣会；什么劳碌的工都不可做。这在你们一切的住处作为世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap all the way to the edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest. Leave them for the poor and the foreign resident. I am the LORD your God.’”
chapters.zh: 「在你们的地收割庄稼，不可割尽田角，也不可拾取所遗落的；要留给穷人和寄居的。我是耶和华－你们的上帝。」

chapters.en: The LORD also said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘On the first day of the seventh month you are to have a day of rest, a sacred assembly announced by trumpet blasts.
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：七月初一，你们要守为圣安息日，要吹角作纪念，当有圣会。

chapters.en: You must not do any regular work, but you are to present a food offering to the LORD.’”
chapters.zh: 什么劳碌的工都不可做；要将火祭献给耶和华。」

chapters.en: Again the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “The tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. You shall hold a sacred assembly and humble yourselves, and present a food offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「七月初十是赎罪日；你们要守为圣会，并要刻苦己心，也要将火祭献给耶和华。

chapters.en: On this day you are not to do any work, for it is the Day of Atonement, when atonement is made for you before the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 当这日，什么工都不可做；因为是赎罪日，要在耶和华－你们的上帝面前赎罪。

chapters.en: If anyone does not humble himself on this day, he must be cut off from his people.
