chapters.zh: 当这日，凡不刻苦己心的，必从民中剪除。

chapters.en: I will destroy from among his people anyone who does any work on this day.
chapters.zh: 凡这日做什么工的，我必将他从民中除灭。

chapters.en: You are not to do any work at all. This is a permanent statute for the generations to come, wherever you live.
chapters.zh: 你们什么工都不可做。这在你们一切的住处作为世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: It will be a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall humble yourselves. From the evening of the ninth day of the month until the following evening you are to keep your Sabbath.”
chapters.zh: 你们要守这日为圣安息日，并要刻苦己心。从这月初九日晚上到〔次日〕晚上，要守为安息日。」

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say, ‘On the fifteenth day of the seventh month the Feast of Tabernacles to the LORD begins, and it continues for seven days.
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：这七月十五日是住棚节，要在耶和华面前守这节七日。

chapters.en: On the first day there shall be a sacred assembly. You must not do any regular work.
chapters.zh: 第一日当有圣会，什么劳碌的工都不可做。

chapters.en: For seven days you are to present a food offering to the LORD. On the eighth day you are to hold a sacred assembly and present a food offering to the LORD. It is a solemn assembly; you must not do any regular work.
chapters.zh: 七日内要将火祭献给耶和华。第八日当守圣会，要将火祭献给耶和华。这是严肃会，什么劳碌的工都不可做。

chapters.en: These are the LORD’s appointed feasts, which you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies for presenting food offerings to the LORD—burnt offerings and grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings, each on its designated day.
chapters.zh: 「这是耶和华的节期，就是你们要宣告为圣会的节期；要将火祭、燔祭、素祭、祭物，并奠祭，各归各日，献给耶和华。

chapters.en: These offerings are in addition to the offerings for the LORD’s Sabbaths, and in addition to your gifts, to all your vow offerings, and to all the freewill offerings you give to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 这是在耶和华的安息日以外，又在你们的供物和所许的愿，并甘心献给耶和华的以外。

chapters.en: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, after you have gathered the produce of the land, you are to celebrate a feast to the LORD for seven days. There shall be complete rest on the first day and also on the eighth day.
chapters.zh: 「你们收藏了地的出产，就从七月十五日起，要守耶和华的节七日。第一日为圣安息；第八日也为圣安息。

chapters.en: On the first day you are to gather the fruit of majestic trees, the branches of palm trees, and the boughs of leafy trees and of willows of the brook. And you are to rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.
chapters.zh: 第一日要拿美好树上的果子和棕树上的枝子，与茂密树的枝条并河旁的柳枝，在耶和华－你们的上帝面前欢乐七日。

chapters.en: You are to celebrate this as a feast to the LORD for seven days each year. This is a permanent statute for the generations to come; you are to celebrate it in the seventh month.
chapters.zh: 每年七月间，要向耶和华守这节七日。这为你们世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: You are to dwell in booths for seven days. All the native-born of Israel must dwell in booths,
chapters.zh: 你们要住在棚里七日；凡以色列家的人都要住在棚里，

chapters.en: so that your descendants may know that I made the Israelites dwell in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.’”
chapters.zh: 好叫你们世世代代知道，我领以色列人出埃及地的时候曾使他们住在棚里。我是耶和华－你们的上帝。」

chapters.en: So Moses announced to the Israelites the appointed feasts of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 于是，摩西将耶和华的节期传给以色列人。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, to keep the lamps burning continually.
chapters.zh: 「要吩咐以色列人，把那为点灯捣成的清橄榄油拿来给你，使灯常常点着。

chapters.en: Outside the veil of the Testimony in the Tent of Meeting, Aaron is to tend the lamps continually before the LORD from evening until morning. This is to be a permanent statute for the generations to come.
chapters.zh: 在会幕中法〔柜〕的幔子外，亚伦从晚上到早晨必在耶和华面前经理这灯。这要作你们世世代代永远的定例。

chapters.en: He shall tend the lamps on the pure gold lampstand before the LORD continually.
chapters.zh: 他要在耶和华面前常收拾精〔金〕灯台上的灯。」

chapters.en: You are also to take fine flour and bake twelve loaves, using two-tenths of an ephah for each loaf,
chapters.zh: 「你要取细面，烤成十二个饼，每饼用面〔伊法〕十分之二。

chapters.en: and set them in two rows—six per row—on the table of pure gold before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 要把饼摆列两行〔注：或译：摞；下同〕，每行六个，在耶和华面前精〔金〕的桌子上；

chapters.en: And you are to place pure frankincense near each row, so that it may serve as a memorial portion for the bread, a food offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 又要把净乳香放在每行饼上，作为纪念，就是作为火祭献给耶和华。

chapters.en: Every Sabbath day the bread is to be set out before the LORD on behalf of the Israelites as a permanent covenant.
chapters.zh: 每安息日要常摆在耶和华面前；这为以色列人作永远的约。

chapters.en: It belongs to Aaron and his sons, who are to eat it in a holy place; for it is to him a most holy part of the food offerings to the LORD—his portion forever.”
chapters.zh: 这饼是要给亚伦和他子孙的；他们要在圣处吃，为永远的定例，因为在献给耶和华的火祭中是至圣的。」

chapters.en: Now the son of an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father went out among the Israelites, and a fight broke out in the camp between him and an Israelite.
chapters.zh: 有一个以色列妇人的儿子，他父亲是埃及人，〔一日〕闲游在以色列人中。这以色列妇人的儿子和一个以色列人在营里争斗。

chapters.en: The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name with a curse. So they brought him to Moses. (His mother’s name was Shelomith daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.)
chapters.zh: 这以色列妇人的儿子亵渎了〔圣〕名，并且咒诅，就有人把他送到摩西那里。（他母亲名叫示罗密，是但支派底伯利的女儿。）

chapters.en: They placed him in custody until the will of the LORD should be made clear to them.
chapters.zh: 他们把那人收在监里，要得耶和华所指示的话。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Take the blasphemer outside the camp, and have all who heard him lay their hands on his head; then have the whole assembly stone him.
chapters.zh: 「把那咒诅〔圣名〕的人带到营外。叫听见的人都放手在他头上；全会众就要用石头打死他。

chapters.en: And you are to tell the Israelites, ‘If anyone curses his God, he shall bear the consequences of his sin.
chapters.zh: 你要晓谕以色列人说：凡咒诅上帝的，必担当他的罪。

chapters.en: Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD must surely be put to death; the whole assembly must surely stone him, whether he is a foreign resident or native; if he blasphemes the Name, he must be put to death.
chapters.zh: 那亵渎耶和华名的，必被治死；全会众总要用石头打死他。不管是寄居的是本地人，他亵渎〔耶和华〕名的时候，必被治死。

chapters.en: And if a man takes the life of anyone else, he must surely be put to death.
chapters.zh: 打死人的，必被治死；

chapters.en: Whoever kills an animal must make restitution—life for life.
chapters.zh: 打死牲畜的，必赔上牲畜，以命偿命。

chapters.en: If anyone injures his neighbor, whatever he has done must be done to him:
chapters.zh: 人若使他邻舍的身体有残疾，他怎样行，也要照样向他行：

chapters.en: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. Just as he injured the other person, the same must be inflicted on him.
chapters.zh: 以伤还伤，以眼还眼，以牙还牙。他怎样叫人的身体有残疾，也要照样向他行。

chapters.en: Whoever kills an animal must make restitution, but whoever kills a man must be put to death.
chapters.zh: 打死牲畜的，必赔上牲畜；打死人的，必被治死。

chapters.en: You are to have the same standard of law for the foreign resident and the native; for I am the LORD your God.’”
chapters.zh: 不管是寄居的是本地人，同归一例。我是耶和华－你们的上帝。」

chapters.en: Then Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they took the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him. So the Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 于是，摩西晓谕以色列人，他们就把那咒诅〔圣名〕的人带到营外，用石头打死。以色列人就照耶和华所吩咐摩西的行了。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses on Mount Sinai,
chapters.zh: 耶和华在西奈山对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land that I am giving you, the land itself must observe a Sabbath to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：你们到了我所赐你们那地的时候，地就要向耶和华守安息。

chapters.en: For six years you may sow your field and prune your vineyard and gather its crops.
chapters.zh: 六年要耕种田地，也要修理葡萄园，收藏地的出产。

chapters.en:
But in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land—a Sabbath to the LORD.
You are not to sow your field or prune your vineyard.
chapters.zh: 第七年，地要守圣安息，就是向耶和华守的安息，不可耕种田地，也不可修理葡萄园。

chapters.en: You are not to reap the aftergrowth of your harvest or gather the grapes of your untended vines. The land must have a year of complete rest.
chapters.zh: 遗落自长的庄稼不可收割；没有修理的葡萄树也不可摘取葡萄。这年，地要守圣安息。

chapters.en: Whatever the land yields during the Sabbath year shall be food for you—for yourself, your manservant and maidservant, the hired hand or foreigner who stays with you,
chapters.zh: 地在安息年所出的，要给你和你的仆人、婢女、雇工人，并寄居的外人当食物。

chapters.en: and for your livestock and the wild animals in your land. All its growth may serve as food.
chapters.zh: 这年的土产也要给你的牲畜和你地上的走兽当食物。」

chapters.en: And you shall count off seven Sabbaths of years—seven times seven years—so that the seven Sabbaths of years amount to forty-nine years.
chapters.zh: 「你要计算七个安息年，就是七七年。这便为你成了七个安息年，共是四十九年。

chapters.en: Then you are to sound the horn far and wide on the tenth day of the seventh month, the Day of Atonement. You shall sound it throughout your land.
chapters.zh: 当年七月初十日，你要大发角声；这日就是赎罪日，要在遍地发出角声。

chapters.en: So you are to consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty in the land for all its inhabitants. It shall be your Jubilee, when each of you is to return to his property and to his clan.
chapters.zh: 第五十年，你们要当作圣年，在遍地给一切的居民宣告自由。这年必为你们的禧年，各人要归自己的产业，各归本家。

chapters.en: The fiftieth year will be a Jubilee for you; you are not to sow the land or reap its aftergrowth or harvest the untended vines.
chapters.zh: 第五十年要作为你们的禧年。这年不可耕种；地中自长的，不可收割；没有修理的葡萄树也不可摘取〔葡萄〕。

chapters.en: For it is a Jubilee; it shall be holy to you. You may eat only the crops taken directly from the field.
chapters.zh: 因为这是禧年，你们要当作圣年，吃地中〔自出〕的土产。

chapters.en: In this Year of Jubilee, each of you shall return to his own property.
chapters.zh: 「这禧年，你们各人要归自己的地业。

chapters.en: If you make a sale to your neighbor or a purchase from him, you must not take advantage of each other.
chapters.zh: 你若卖什么给邻舍，或是从邻舍的手中买什么，彼此不可亏负。

chapters.en: You are to buy from your neighbor according to the number of years since the last Jubilee; he is to sell to you according to the number of harvest years remaining.
chapters.zh: 你要按禧年以后的年数向邻舍买；他也要按年数的收成卖给你。

chapters.en: You shall increase the price in proportion to a greater number of years, or decrease it in proportion to a lesser number of years; for he is selling you a given number of harvests.
chapters.zh: 年岁若多，要照数加添价值；年岁若少，要照数减去价值，因为他照收成的数目卖给你。

chapters.en: Do not take advantage of each other, but fear your God; for I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 你们彼此不可亏负，只要敬畏你们的上帝，因为我是耶和华－你们的上帝。」

chapters.en: You are to keep My statutes and carefully observe My judgments, so that you may dwell securely in the land.
chapters.zh: 「我的律例，你们要遵行，我的典章，你们要谨守，就可以在那地上安然居住。

chapters.en: Then the land will yield its fruit, so that you can eat your fill and dwell in safety in the land.
chapters.zh: 地必出土产，你们就要吃饱，在那地上安然居住。

chapters.en: Now you may wonder, ‘What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not sow or gather our produce?’
chapters.zh: 你们若说：『这第七年我们不耕种，也不收藏土产，吃什么呢？』

chapters.en: But I will send My blessing upon you in the sixth year, so that the land will yield a crop sufficient for three years.
chapters.zh: 我必在第六年将我所命的福赐给你们，地便生三年的土产。

chapters.en: While you are sowing in the eighth year, you will be eating from the previous harvest, until the ninth year’s harvest comes in.
chapters.zh: 第八年，你们要耕种，也要吃陈粮，等到第九年出产收来的时候，你们还吃陈粮。」

chapters.en: The land must not be sold permanently, because it is Mine, and you are but foreigners and residents with Me.
chapters.zh: 「地不可永卖，因为地是我的；你们在我面前是客旅，是寄居的。

chapters.en: Thus for every piece of property you possess, you must provide for the redemption of the land.
chapters.zh: 在你们所得为业的全地，也要准人将地赎回。

chapters.en: If your brother becomes impoverished and sells some of his property, his nearest of kin may come and redeem what his brother has sold.
chapters.zh: 你的弟兄〔注：弟兄是指本国人说；下同〕若渐渐穷乏，卖了几分地业，他至近的亲属就要来把弟兄所卖的赎回。

chapters.en: Or if a man has no one to redeem it for him, but he prospers and acquires enough to redeem his land,
chapters.zh: 若没有能给他赎回的，他自己渐渐富足，能够赎回，

chapters.en: he shall calculate the years since its sale, repay the balance to the man to whom he sold it, and return to his property.
chapters.zh: 就要算出卖地的年数，把余剩年数的价值还那买主，自己便归回自己的地业。

chapters.en: But if he cannot obtain enough to repay him, what he sold will remain in possession of the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee, however, it is to be released, so that he may return to his property.
chapters.zh: 倘若不能为自己得回所卖的，仍要存在买主的手里直到禧年；到了禧年，地业要出〔买主的手〕，自己便归回自己的地业。

chapters.en: If a man sells a house in a walled city, he retains his right of redemption until a full year after its sale; during that year it may be redeemed.
chapters.zh: 「人若卖城内的住宅，卖了以后，一年之内可以赎回；在一整年，必有赎回的权柄。

chapters.en: If it is not redeemed by the end of a full year, then the house in the walled city is permanently transferred to its buyer and his descendants. It is not to be released in the Jubilee.
chapters.zh: 若在一整年之内不赎回，这城内的房屋就定准永归买主，世世代代为业；在禧年也不得出〔买主的手〕。

chapters.en: But houses in villages with no walls around them are to be considered as open fields. They may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the Jubilee.
chapters.zh: 但房屋在无城墙的村庄里，要看如乡下的田地一样，可以赎回；到了禧年，都要出〔买主的手〕。

chapters.en: As for the cities of the Levites, the Levites always have the right to redeem their houses in the cities they possess.
chapters.zh: 然而利未人所得为业的城邑，其中的房屋，利未人可以随时赎回。

chapters.en: So whatever belongs to the Levites may be redeemed—a house sold in a city they possess—and must be released in the Jubilee, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the Israelites.
chapters.zh: 若是一个利未人不将所卖的房屋赎回，是在所得为业的城内，到了禧年就要出〔买主的手〕，因为利未人城邑的房屋是他们在以色列人中的产业。

chapters.en: But the open pastureland around their cities may not be sold, for this is their permanent possession.
chapters.zh: 只是他们各城郊野之地不可卖，因为是他们永远的产业。」

chapters.en: Now if your countryman becomes destitute and cannot support himself among you, then you are to help him as you would a foreigner or stranger, so that he can continue to live among you.
chapters.zh: 「你的弟兄在你那里若渐渐贫穷，手中缺乏，你就要帮补他，使他与你同住，像外人和寄居的一样。

chapters.en: Do not take any interest or profit from him, but fear your God, that your countryman may live among you.
chapters.zh: 不可向他取利，也不可向他多要；只要敬畏你的上帝，使你的弟兄与你同住。

chapters.en: You must not lend him your silver at interest or sell him your food for profit.
chapters.zh: 你借钱给他，不可向他取利；借粮给他，也不可向他多要。

chapters.en: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
chapters.zh: 我是耶和华－你们的上帝，曾领你们从埃及地出来，为要把迦南地赐给你们，要作你们的上帝。」

chapters.en: If a countryman among you becomes destitute and sells himself to you, then you must not force him into slave labor.
chapters.zh: 「你的弟兄若在你那里渐渐穷乏，将自己卖给你，不可叫他像奴仆服事你。

chapters.en: Let him stay with you as a hired worker or temporary resident; he is to work for you until the Year of Jubilee.
chapters.zh: 他要在你那里像雇工人和寄居的一样，要服事你直到禧年。

chapters.en: Then he and his children are to be released, and he may return to his clan and to the property of his fathers.
chapters.zh: 到了禧年，他和他儿女要离开你，一同出去归回本家，到他祖宗的地业那里去。

chapters.en: Because the Israelites are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt, they are not to be sold as slaves.
chapters.zh: 因为他们是我的仆人，是我从埃及地领出来的，不可卖为奴仆。

chapters.en: You are not to rule over them harshly, but you shall fear your God.
chapters.zh: 不可严严地辖管他，只要敬畏你的上帝。

chapters.en: Your menservants and maidservants shall come from the nations around you, from whom you may purchase them.
chapters.zh: 至于你的奴仆、婢女，可以从你四围的国中买。

chapters.en: You may also purchase them from the foreigners residing among you or their clans living among you who are born in your land. These may become your property.
chapters.zh: 并且那寄居在你们中间的外人和他们的家属，在你们地上所生的，你们也可以从其中买人；他们要作你们的产业。

chapters.en: You may leave them to your sons after you to inherit as property; you can make them slaves for life. But as for your brothers, the Israelites, no man may rule harshly over his brother.
chapters.zh: 你们要将他们遗留给你们的子孙为产业，要永远从他们中间拣出奴仆；只是你们的弟兄以色列人，你们不可严严地辖管。

chapters.en: If a foreigner residing among you prospers, but your countryman dwelling near him becomes destitute and sells himself to the foreigner or to a member of his clan,
chapters.zh: 「住在你那里的外人，或是寄居的，若渐渐富足，你的弟兄却渐渐穷乏，将自己卖给那外人，或是寄居的，或是外人的宗族，

chapters.en: he retains the right of redemption after he has sold himself. One of his brothers may redeem him:
chapters.zh: 卖了以后，可以将他赎回。无论是他的弟兄，

chapters.en: either his uncle or cousin or any close relative from his clan may redeem him. Or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.
chapters.zh: 或伯叔、伯叔的儿子，本家的近支，都可以赎他。他自己若渐渐富足，也可以自赎。

chapters.en: He and his purchaser will then count the time from the year he sold himself up to the Year of Jubilee. The price of his sale will be determined by the number of years, based on the daily wages of a hired hand.
chapters.zh: 他要和买主计算，从卖自己的那年起，算到禧年；所卖的价值照着年数多少，好像工人每年的工价。

chapters.en: If many years remain, he must pay for his redemption in proportion to his purchase price.
chapters.zh: 若缺少的年数多，就要按着年数从买价中偿还他的赎价。

chapters.en: If only a few years remain until the Year of Jubilee, he is to calculate and pay his redemption according to his remaining years.
chapters.zh: 若到禧年只缺少几年，就要按着年数和买主计算，偿还他的赎价。

chapters.en: He shall be treated like a man hired from year to year, but a foreign owner must not rule over him harshly in your sight.
chapters.zh: 他和买主同住，要像每年雇的工人，买主不可严严地辖管他。

chapters.en: Even if he is not redeemed in any of these ways, he and his children shall be released in the Year of Jubilee.
chapters.zh: 他若不这样被赎，到了禧年，要和他的儿女一同出去。

chapters.en: For the Israelites are My servants. They are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 因为以色列人都是我的仆人，是我从埃及地领出来的。我是耶和华－你们的上帝。」

chapters.en: “You must not make idols for yourselves or set up a carved image or sacred pillar; you must not place a sculpted stone in your land to bow down to it. For I am the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 「你们不可做什么虚无的神〔像〕，不可立雕刻的偶像或是柱像，也不可在你们的地上安什么錾成的石像，向它跪拜，因为我是耶和华－你们的上帝。

chapters.en: You must keep My Sabbaths and have reverence for My sanctuary. I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你们要守我的安息日，敬我的圣所。我是耶和华。

chapters.en: If you follow My statutes and carefully keep My commandments,
chapters.zh: 「你们若遵行我的律例，谨守我的诫命，

chapters.en: I will give you rains in their season, and the land will yield its produce, and the trees of the field will bear their fruit.
chapters.zh: 我就给你们降下时雨，叫地生出土产，田野的树木结果子。

chapters.en: Your threshing will continue until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will continue until sowing time; you will have your fill of food to eat and will dwell securely in your land.
chapters.zh: 你们打粮食要打到摘葡萄的时候，摘葡萄要摘到撒种的时候；并且要吃得饱足，在你们的地上安然居住。

chapters.en: And I will give peace to the land, and you will lie down with nothing to fear. I will rid the land of dangerous animals, and no sword will pass through your land.
chapters.zh: 我要赐平安在〔你们的〕地上；你们躺卧，无人惊吓。我要叫恶兽从〔你们的〕地上熄灭；刀剑也必不经过你们的地。

chapters.en: You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall by the sword before you.
chapters.zh: 你们要追赶仇敌，他们必倒在你们刀下。

chapters.en: Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand, and your enemies will fall by the sword before you.
chapters.zh: 你们五个人要追赶一百人，一百人要追赶一万人；仇敌必倒在你们刀下。

chapters.en: I will turn toward you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will establish My covenant with you.
chapters.zh: 我要眷顾你们，使你们生养众多，也要与你们坚定所立的约。

chapters.en: You will still be eating the old supply of grain when you need to clear it out to make room for the new.
chapters.zh: 你们要吃陈粮，又因新粮挪开陈粮。

chapters.en: And I will make My dwelling place among you, and My soul will not despise you.
chapters.zh: 我要在你们中间立我的帐幕；我的心也不厌恶你们。

chapters.en: I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be My people.
chapters.zh: 我要在你们中间行走；我要作你们的上帝，你们要作我的子民。

chapters.en: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be slaves to the Egyptians. I broke the bars of your yoke and enabled you to walk in uprightness.
chapters.zh: 我是耶和华－你们的上帝，曾将你们从埃及地领出来，使你们不作埃及人的奴仆；我也折断你们所负的轭，叫你们挺身而走。」

chapters.en: If, however, you fail to obey Me and to carry out all these commandments,
chapters.zh: 「你们若不听从我，不遵行我的诫命，

chapters.en: and if you reject My statutes, despise My ordinances, and neglect to carry out all My commandments, and so break My covenant,
chapters.zh: 厌弃我的律例，厌恶我的典章，不遵行我一切的诫命，背弃我的约，

chapters.en: then this is what I will do to you: I will bring upon you sudden terror, wasting disease, and fever that will destroy your sight and drain your life. You will sow your seed in vain, because your enemies will eat it.
chapters.zh: 我待你们就要这样：我必命定惊惶，叫眼目干瘪、精神消耗的痨病热病辖制你们。你们也要白白地撒种，因为仇敌要吃你们所种的。

chapters.en: And I will set My face against you, so that you will be defeated by your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee when no one pursues you.
chapters.zh: 我要向你们变脸，你们就要败在仇敌面前。恨恶你们的，必辖管你们；无人追赶，你们却要逃跑。

chapters.en: And if after all this you will not obey Me, I will proceed to punish you sevenfold for your sins.
chapters.zh: 你们因这些事若还不听从我，我就要为你们的罪加七倍惩罚你们。

chapters.en: I will break down your stubborn pride and make your sky like iron and your land like bronze,
chapters.zh: 我必断绝你们因势力而有的骄傲，又要使〔覆〕你们的天如铁，〔载〕你们的地如铜。

chapters.en: and your strength will be spent in vain. For your land will not yield its produce, and the trees of the land will not bear their fruit.
chapters.zh: 你们要白白地劳力；因为你们的地不出土产，其上的树木也不结果子。

chapters.en: If you walk in hostility toward Me and refuse to obey Me, I will multiply your plagues seven times, according to your sins.
chapters.zh: 「你们行事若与我反对，不肯听从我，我就要按你们的罪加七倍降灾与你们。

chapters.en: I will send wild animals against you to rob you of your children, destroy your livestock, and reduce your numbers, until your roads lie desolate.
chapters.zh: 我也要打发野地的走兽到你们中间，抢吃你们的儿女，吞灭你们的牲畜，使你们的人数减少，道路荒凉。

chapters.en: And if in spite of these things you do not accept My discipline, but continue to walk in hostility toward Me,
chapters.zh: 「你们因这些事若仍不改正归我，行事与我反对，

chapters.en: then I will act with hostility toward you, and I will strike you sevenfold for your sins.
chapters.zh: 我就要行事与你们反对，因你们的罪击打你们七次。

chapters.en: And I will bring a sword against you to execute the vengeance of the covenant. Though you withdraw into your cities, I will send a plague among you, and you will be delivered into the hand of the enemy.
chapters.zh: 我又要使刀剑临到你们，报复你们背约的仇；聚集你们在各城内，降瘟疫在你们中间，也必将你们交在仇敌的手中。

chapters.en: When I cut off your supply of bread, ten women will bake your bread in a single oven and dole out your bread by weight, so that you will eat but not be satisfied.
chapters.zh: 我要折断你们的杖，就是断绝你们的粮。那时，必有十个女人在一个炉子给你们烤饼，按分量秤给你们；你们要吃，也吃不饱。

chapters.en: But if in spite of all this you do not obey Me, but continue to walk in hostility toward Me,
chapters.zh: 「你们因这一切的事若不听从我，却行事与我反对，

chapters.en: then I will walk in fury against you, and I, even I, will punish you sevenfold for your sins.
chapters.zh: 我就要发烈怒，行事与你们反对，又因你们的罪惩罚你们七次。

chapters.en: You will eat the flesh of your own sons and daughters.
chapters.zh: 并且你们要吃儿子的肉，也要吃女儿的肉。

chapters.en: I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars, and heap your lifeless bodies on the lifeless remains of your idols; and My soul will despise you.
chapters.zh: 我又要毁坏你们的邱坛，砍下你们的日像，把你们的尸首扔在你们偶像的身上；我的心也必厌恶你们。

chapters.en: I will reduce your cities to rubble and lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will refuse to smell the pleasing aroma of your sacrifices.
chapters.zh: 我要使你们的城邑变为荒凉，使你们的众圣所成为荒场；我也不闻你们馨香的香气。

chapters.en: And I will lay waste the land, so that your enemies who dwell in it will be appalled.
chapters.zh: 我要使地成为荒场，住在其上的仇敌就因此诧异。

chapters.en: But I will scatter you among the nations and will draw out a sword after you as your land becomes desolate and your cities are laid waste.
chapters.zh: 我要把你们散在列邦中；我也要拔刀追赶你们。你们的地要成为荒场；你们的城邑要变为荒凉。

chapters.en: Then the land shall enjoy its Sabbaths all the days it lies desolate, while you are in the land of your enemies. At that time the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
chapters.zh: 「你们在仇敌之地居住的时候，你们的地荒凉，要享受众安息；正在那时候，地要歇息，享受安息。

chapters.en: As long as it lies desolate, the land will have the rest it did not receive during the Sabbaths when you lived in it.
chapters.zh: 地多时为荒场，就要多时歇息；地这样歇息，是你们住在其上的安息年所不能得的。

chapters.en: As for those of you who survive, I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies, so that even the sound of a windblown leaf will put them to flight. And they will flee as one flees the sword, and fall when no one pursues them.
chapters.zh: 至于你们剩下的人，我要使他们在仇敌之地心惊胆怯。叶子被风吹的响声，要追赶他们；他们要逃避，像人逃避刀剑，无人追赶，却要跌倒。

chapters.en: They will stumble over one another as before the sword, though no one is behind them. So you will not be able to stand against your enemies.
chapters.zh: 无人追赶，他们要彼此撞跌，像在刀剑之前。你们在仇敌面前也必站立不住。

chapters.en: You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will consume you.
chapters.zh: 你们要在列邦中灭亡；仇敌之地要吞吃你们。

chapters.en: Those of you who survive in the lands of your enemies will waste away in their iniquity and will decay in the sins of their fathers.
chapters.zh: 你们剩下的人必因自己的罪孽和祖宗的罪孽在仇敌之地消灭。

chapters.en: But if they will confess their iniquity and that of their fathers in the unfaithfulness that they practiced against Me, by which they have also walked in hostility toward Me—
chapters.zh: 「他们要承认自己的罪和他们祖宗的罪，就是干犯我的那罪，并且承认自己行事与我反对，

chapters.en: and I acted with hostility toward them and brought them into the land of their enemies—and if their uncircumcised hearts will be humbled and they will make amends for their iniquity,
chapters.zh: 我所以行事与他们反对，把他们带到仇敌之地。那时，他们未受割礼的心若谦卑了，他们也服了罪孽的刑罚，

chapters.en: then I will remember My covenant with Jacob and My covenant with Isaac and My covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.
chapters.zh: 我就要记念我与雅各所立的约，与以撒所立的约，与亚伯拉罕所立的约，并要记念这地。

chapters.en: For the land will be abandoned by them, and it will enjoy its Sabbaths by lying desolate without them. And they will pay the penalty for their iniquity, because they rejected My ordinances and abhorred My statutes.
chapters.zh: 他们离开这地，地在荒废无人的时候就要享受安息。并且他们要服罪孽的刑罚；因为他们厌弃了我的典章，心中厌恶了我的律例。

chapters.en: Yet in spite of this, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject or despise them so as to destroy them and break My covenant with them; for I am the LORD their God.
chapters.zh: 虽是这样，他们在仇敌之地，我却不厌弃他们，也不厌恶他们，将他们尽行灭绝，也不背弃我与他们所立的约，因为我是耶和华－他们的上帝。

chapters.en: But for their sake I will remember the covenant with their fathers, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God. I am the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 我却要为他们的缘故记念我与他们先祖所立的约。他们的先祖是我在列邦人眼前、从埃及地领出来的，为要作他们的上帝。我是耶和华。」

chapters.en: These are the statutes, ordinances, and laws that the LORD established between Himself and the Israelites through Moses on Mount Sinai.
chapters.zh: 这些律例、典章，和法度是耶和华与以色列人在西奈山藉着摩西立的。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them, ‘When someone makes a special vow to the LORD involving the value of persons,
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：人还特许的愿，被许的人要按你所估的价值归给耶和华。

chapters.en: if the valuation concerns a male from twenty to sixty years of age, then your valuation shall be fifty shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel.
chapters.zh: 你估定的，从二十岁到六十岁的男人，要按圣所的平，估定价银五十舍客勒。

chapters.en: Or if it is a female, then your valuation shall be thirty shekels.
chapters.zh: 若是女人，你要估定三十舍客勒。

chapters.en: And if the person is from five to twenty years of age, then your valuation for the male shall be twenty shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
chapters.zh: 若是从五岁到二十岁，男子你要估定二十舍客勒，女子估定十舍客勒。

chapters.en: Now if the person is from one month to five years of age, then your valuation for the male shall be five shekels of silver, and for the female three shekels of silver.
chapters.zh: 若是从一月到五岁，男子你要估定五舍客勒，女子估定三舍客勒。

chapters.en: And if the person is sixty years of age or older, then your valuation shall be fifteen shekels for the male and ten shekels for the female.
chapters.zh: 若是从六十岁以上，男人你要估定十五舍客勒，女人估定十舍客勒。

chapters.en: But if the one making the vow is too poor to pay the valuation, he is to present the person before the priest, who shall set the value according to what the one making the vow can afford.
chapters.zh: 他若贫穷，不能照你所估定的价，就要把他带到祭司面前，祭司要按许愿人的力量估定他的价。

chapters.en: If he vows an animal that may be brought as an offering to the LORD, any such animal given to the LORD shall be holy.
chapters.zh: 「〔所许的〕若是牲畜，就是人献给耶和华为供物的，凡这一类献给耶和华的，都要成为圣。

chapters.en: He must not replace it or exchange it, either good for bad or bad for good. But if he does substitute one animal for another, both that animal and its substitute will be holy.
chapters.zh: 人不可改换，也不可更换，或是好的换坏的，或是坏的换好的。若以牲畜更换牲畜，所许的与所换的都要成为圣。

chapters.en: But if the vow involves any of the unclean animals that may not be brought as an offering to the LORD, the animal must be presented before the priest.
chapters.zh: 若牲畜不洁净，是不可献给耶和华为供物的，就要把牲畜安置在祭司面前。

chapters.en: The priest shall set its value, whether high or low; as the priest values it, the price will be set.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要估定价值；牲畜是好是坏，祭司怎样估定，就要以怎样为是。

chapters.en: If, however, the owner decides to redeem the animal, he must add a fifth to its value.
chapters.zh: 他若一定要赎回，就要在你所估定的价值以外加上五分之一。

chapters.en: Now if a man consecrates his house as holy to the LORD, then the priest shall value it either as good or bad. The price will stand just as the priest values it.
chapters.zh: 「人将房屋分别为圣，归给耶和华，祭司就要估定价值。房屋是好是坏，祭司怎样估定，就要以怎样为定。

chapters.en: But if he who consecrated his house redeems it, he must add a fifth to the assessed value, and it will belong to him.
chapters.zh: 将房屋分别为圣的人，若要赎回房屋，就必在你所估定的价值以外加上五分之一，房屋仍旧归他。

chapters.en: If a man consecrates to the LORD a parcel of his land, then your valuation shall be proportional to the seed required for it—fifty shekels of silver for every homer of barley seed.
chapters.zh: 「人若将承受为业的几分地分别为圣，归给耶和华，你要按这地撒种多少估定价值，若撒大麦一贺梅珥，〔要估〕价五十舍客勒。

chapters.en: If he consecrates his field during the Year of Jubilee, the price will stand according to your valuation.
chapters.zh: 他若从禧年将地分别为圣，就要以你所估定的价为定。

chapters.en: But if he consecrates his field after the Jubilee, the priest is to calculate the price in proportion to the years left until the next Year of Jubilee, so that your valuation will be reduced.
chapters.zh: 倘若他在禧年以后将地分别为圣，祭司就要按着未到禧年所剩的年数推算价值，也要从你所估的减去价值。

chapters.en: And if the one who consecrated the field decides to redeem it, he must add a fifth to the assessed value, and it shall belong to him.
chapters.zh: 将地分别为圣的人若定要把地赎回，他便要在你所估的价值以外加上五分之一，地就准定归他。

chapters.en: If, however, he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold it to another man, it may no longer be redeemed.
chapters.zh: 他若不赎回那地，或是将地卖给别人，就再不能赎了。

chapters.en: When the field is released in the Jubilee, it will become holy, like a field devoted to the LORD; it becomes the property of the priests.
chapters.zh: 但到了禧年，那地从〔买主手下〕出来的时候，就要归耶和华为圣，和永献的地一样，要归祭司为业。

chapters.en: Now if a man consecrates to the LORD a field he has purchased, which is not a part of his own property,
chapters.zh: 他若将所买的一块地，不是承受为业的，分别为圣归给耶和华，

chapters.en: then the priest shall calculate for him the value up to the Year of Jubilee, and the man shall pay the assessed value on that day as a sacred offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 祭司就要将你所估的价值给他推算到禧年。当日，他要以你所估的价银为圣，归给耶和华。

chapters.en: In the Year of Jubilee the field shall return to the one from whom it was bought—the original owner of the land.
chapters.zh: 到了禧年，那地要归卖主，就是那承受为业的原主。

chapters.en: Every valuation will be according to the sanctuary shekel, twenty gerahs to the shekel.
chapters.zh: 凡你所估定的价银都要按着圣所的平：二十季拉为一舍客勒。

chapters.en: But no one may consecrate a firstborn of the livestock, because a firstborn belongs to the LORD. Whether it is an ox or a sheep, it is the LORD’s.
chapters.zh: 「惟独牲畜中头生的，无论是牛是羊，既归耶和华，谁也不可再分别为圣，因为这是耶和华的。

chapters.en: But if it is among the unclean animals, then he may redeem it according to your valuation and add a fifth of its value. If it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold according to your valuation.
chapters.zh: 若是不洁净的牲畜生的，就要按你所估定的价值加上五分之一赎回；若不赎回，就要按你所估定的价值卖了。

chapters.en: Nothing that a man sets apart to the LORD from all he owns—whether a man, an animal, or his inherited land—can be sold or redeemed; everything so devoted is most holy to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「但一切永献的，就是人从他所有永献给耶和华的，无论是人，是牲畜，是他承受为业的地，都不可卖，也不可赎。凡永献的是归给耶和华为至圣。

chapters.en: No person set apart for destruction may be ransomed; he must surely be put to death.
chapters.zh: 凡从人中当灭的都不可赎，必被治死。」

chapters.en: Thus any tithe from the land, whether from the seed of the land or the fruit of the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「地上所有的，无论是地上的种子是树上的果子，十分之一是耶和华的，是归给耶和华为圣的。

chapters.en: If a man wishes to redeem part of his tithe, he must add a fifth to its value.
chapters.zh: 人若要赎这十分之一的什么物，就要加上五分之一。

chapters.en: Every tenth animal from the herd or flock that passes under the shepherd’s rod will be holy to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 凡牛群羊群中，一切从杖下经过的，每第十只要归给耶和华为圣。

chapters.en: He must not inspect whether it is good or bad, and he shall not make any substitution. But if he does make a substitution, both the animal and its substitute shall become holy; they cannot be redeemed.’”
chapters.zh: 不可问是好是坏，也不可更换；若定要更换，所更换的与本来的牲畜都要成为圣，不可赎回。」

chapters.en: These are the commandments that the LORD gave to Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
chapters.zh: 这就是耶和华在西奈山为以色列人所吩咐摩西的命令。

chapters.en: On the first day of the second month of the second year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the Tent of Meeting in the Wilderness of Sinai. He said:
chapters.zh: 以色列人出埃及地后，第二年二月初一日，耶和华在西奈的旷野、会幕中晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Take a census of the whole congregation of Israel by their clans and families, listing every man by name, one by one.
chapters.zh: 「你要按以色列全会众的家室、宗族、人名的数目计算所有的男丁。

chapters.en: You and Aaron are to number those who are twenty years of age or older by their divisions—everyone who can serve in Israel’s army.
chapters.zh: 凡以色列中，从二十岁以外，能出去打仗的，你和亚伦要照他们的军队数点。

chapters.en: And one man from each tribe, the head of each family, must be there with you.
chapters.zh: 每支派中必有一人作本支派的族长，帮助你们。

chapters.en:
These are the names of the men who are to assist you:
From the tribe of Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
chapters.zh: 他们的名字：属吕便的，有示丢珥的儿子以利蓿；

chapters.en: from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
chapters.zh: 属西缅的，有苏利沙代的儿子示路蔑；

chapters.en: from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
chapters.zh: 属犹大的，有亚米拿达的儿子拿顺；

chapters.en: from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
chapters.zh: 属以萨迦的，有苏押的儿子拿坦业；

chapters.en: from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
chapters.zh: 属西布伦的，有希伦的儿子以利押；
约瑟子孙、属以法莲的，有亚米忽的儿子以利沙玛；属玛拿西的，有比大蓿的儿子迦玛列；

chapters.en: from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
chapters.zh: 属便雅悯的，有基多尼的儿子亚比但；

chapters.en: from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
chapters.zh: 属但的，有亚米沙代的儿子亚希以谢；

chapters.en: from Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran;
chapters.zh: 属亚设的，有俄兰的儿子帕结；

chapters.en: from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel;
chapters.zh: 属迦得的，有丢珥的儿子以利雅萨；

chapters.en: and from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.”
chapters.zh: 属拿弗他利的，有以南的儿子亚希拉。

chapters.en: These men were appointed from the congregation; they were the leaders of the tribes of their fathers, the heads of the clans of Israel.
chapters.zh: 这都是从会中选召的，各作本支派的首领，都是以色列军中的统领。」

chapters.en: So Moses and Aaron took these men who had been designated by name,
chapters.zh: 于是，摩西、亚伦带着这些按名指定的人，

chapters.en: and on the first day of the second month they assembled the whole congregation and recorded their ancestry by clans and families, counting one by one the names of those twenty years of age or older,
chapters.zh: 当二月初一日招聚全会众。会众就照他们的家室、宗族、人名的数目，从二十岁以外的，都述说自己的家谱。

chapters.en:
just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
So Moses numbered them in the Wilderness of Sinai:
chapters.zh: 耶和华怎样吩咐摩西，他就怎样在西奈的旷野数点他们。

chapters.en: From the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, according to the records of their clans and families, counting one by one the names of every male twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,
those registered to the tribe of Reuben numbered 46,500.
chapters.zh: 以色列的长子，吕便子孙的后代，照着家室、宗族、人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗、被数的男丁，共有四万六千五百名。

chapters.en: From the sons of Simeon, according to the records of their clans and families, counting one by one the names of every male twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,
those registered to the tribe of Simeon numbered 59,300.
chapters.zh: 西缅子孙的后代，照着家室、宗族、人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗、被数的男丁，共有五万九千三百名。

chapters.en: From the sons of Gad, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,
those registered to the tribe of Gad numbered 45,650.
chapters.zh: 迦得子孙的后代，照着家室、宗族、人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗、被数的，共有四万五千六百五十名。

chapters.en: From the sons of Judah, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,
those registered to the tribe of Judah numbered 74,600.
chapters.zh: 犹大子孙的后代，照着家室、宗族、人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗、被数的，共有七万四千六百名。

chapters.en: From the sons of Issachar, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,
those registered to the tribe of Issachar numbered 54,400.
chapters.zh: 以萨迦子孙的后代，照着家室、宗族、人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗、被数的，共有五万四千四百名。

chapters.en: From the sons of Zebulun, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,
those registered to the tribe of Zebulun numbered 57,400.
chapters.zh: 西布伦子孙的后代，照着家室、宗族、人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗、被数的，共有五万七千四百名。

chapters.en:
From the sons of Joseph:
From the sons of Ephraim, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,
those registered to the tribe of Ephraim numbered 40,500.
chapters.zh: 约瑟子孙属以法莲子孙的后代，照着家室、宗族、人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗、被数的，共有四万零五百名。

chapters.en: And from the sons of Manasseh, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,
those registered to the tribe of Manasseh numbered 32,200.
chapters.zh: 玛拿西子孙的后代，照着家室、宗族、人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗、被数的，共有三万二千二百名。

chapters.en: From the sons of Benjamin, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,
those registered to the tribe of Benjamin numbered 35,400.
chapters.zh: 便雅悯子孙的后代，照着家室、宗族、人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗、被数的，共有三万五千四百名。

chapters.en: From the sons of Dan, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,
those registered to the tribe of Dan numbered 62,700.
chapters.zh: 但子孙的后代，照着家室、宗族、人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗、被数的，共有六万二千七百名。

chapters.en: From the sons of Asher, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,
those registered to the tribe of Asher numbered 41,500.
chapters.zh: 亚设子孙的后代，照着家室、宗族、人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗、被数的，共有四万一千五百名。

chapters.en: From the sons of Naphtali, according to the records of their clans and families, counting the names of all those twenty years of age or older who could serve in the army,
those registered to the tribe of Naphtali numbered 53,400.
chapters.zh: 拿弗他利子孙的后代，照着家室、宗族、人名的数目，从二十岁以外，凡能出去打仗、被数的，共有五万三千四百名。

chapters.en: These were the men numbered by Moses and Aaron, with the assistance of the twelve leaders of Israel, each one representing his family.
chapters.zh: 这些就是被数点的，是摩西、亚伦，和以色列中十二个首领所数点的；这十二个人各作各宗族的代表。

chapters.en: So all the Israelites twenty years of age or older who could serve in Israel’s army were counted according to their families.
And all those counted totaled 603,550.
chapters.zh: 这样，凡以色列人中被数的，照着宗族，从二十岁以外，能出去打仗、被数的，共有六十万零三千五百五十名。

chapters.en: The Levites, however, were not numbered along with them by the tribe of their fathers.
chapters.zh: 利未人却没有按着支派数在其中，

chapters.en: For the LORD had said to Moses:
chapters.zh: 因为耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Do not number the tribe of Levi in the census with the other Israelites.
chapters.zh: 「惟独利未支派你不可数点，也不可在以色列人中计算他们的总数。

chapters.en: Instead, you are to appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of the Testimony, all its furnishings, and everything in it. They shall carry the tabernacle and all its articles, care for it, and camp around it.
chapters.zh: 只要派利未人管法〔柜〕的帐幕和其中的器具，并属乎帐幕的；他们要抬〔注：或译：搬运〕帐幕和其中的器具，并要办理帐幕的事，在帐幕的四围安营。

chapters.en: Whenever the tabernacle is to move, the Levites are to take it down, and whenever it is to be pitched, the Levites are to set it up. Any outsider who goes near it must be put to death.
chapters.zh: 帐幕将往前行的时候，利未人要拆卸；将支搭的时候，利未人要竖起。近前来的外人必被治死。

chapters.en: The Israelites are to camp by their divisions, each man in his own camp and under his own standard.
chapters.zh: 以色列人支搭帐棚，要照他们的军队，各归本营，各归本纛。

chapters.en: But the Levites are to camp around the tabernacle of the Testimony and watch over it, so that no wrath will fall on the congregation of Israel. So the Levites are responsible for the tabernacle of the Testimony.”
chapters.zh: 但利未人要在法〔柜〕帐幕的四围安营，免得忿怒临到以色列会众；利未人并要谨守法〔柜〕的帐幕。」

chapters.en: Thus the Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 以色列人就这样行。凡耶和华所吩咐摩西的，他们就照样行了。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西、亚伦说：

chapters.en: “The Israelites are to camp around the Tent of Meeting at a distance from it, each man under his standard, with the banners of his family.
chapters.zh: 「以色列人要各归自己的纛下，在本族的旗号那里，对着会幕的四围安营。

chapters.en:
On the east side, toward the sunrise, the divisions of Judah are to camp under their standard:
The leader of the Judahites is Nahshon son of Amminadab,
chapters.zh: 在东边，向日出之地，照着军队安营的是犹大营的纛。有亚米拿达的儿子拿顺作犹大人的首领。

chapters.en: and his division numbers 74,600.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有七万四千六百名。

chapters.en: The tribe of Issachar will camp next to it. The leader of the Issacharites is Nethanel son of Zuar,
chapters.zh: 挨着他安营的是以萨迦支派。有苏押的儿子拿坦业作以萨迦人的首领。

chapters.en: and his division numbers 54,400.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有五万四千四百名。

chapters.en: Next will be the tribe of Zebulun. The leader of the Zebulunites is Eliab son of Helon,
chapters.zh: 又有西布伦支派。希伦的儿子以利押作西布伦人的首领。

chapters.en: and his division numbers 57,400.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有五万七千四百名。

chapters.en: The total number of men in the divisions of the camp of Judah is 186,400; they shall set out first.
chapters.zh: 凡属犹大营、按着军队被数的，共有十八万六千四百名，要作第一队往前行。

chapters.en:
On the south side, the divisions of Reuben are to camp under their standard:
The leader of the Reubenites is Elizur son of Shedeur,
chapters.zh: 「在南边，按着军队是吕便营的纛。有示丢珥的儿子以利蓿作吕便人的首领。

chapters.en: and his division numbers 46,500.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有四万六千五百名。

chapters.en: The tribe of Simeon will camp next to it. The leader of the Simeonites is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai,
chapters.zh: 挨着他安营的是西缅支派。苏利沙代的儿子示路蔑作西缅人的首领。

chapters.en: and his division numbers 59,300.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有五万九千三百名。

chapters.en: Next will be the tribe of Gad. The leader of the Gadites is Eliasaph son of Deuel,
chapters.zh: 又有迦得支派。丢珥的儿子以利雅萨作迦得人的首领。

chapters.en: and his division numbers 45,650.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有四万五千六百五十名，

chapters.en: The total number of men in the divisions of the camp of Reuben is 151,450; they shall set out second.
chapters.zh: 凡属吕便营、按着军队被数的，共有十五万一千四百五十名，要作第二队往前行。

chapters.en: In the middle of the camps, the Tent of Meeting is to travel with the camp of the Levites. They are to set out in the order they encamped, each in his own place under his standard.
chapters.zh: 「随后，会幕要往前行，有利未营在诸营中间。他们怎样安营就怎样往前行，各按本位，各归本纛。

chapters.en:
On the west side, the divisions of Ephraim are to camp under their standard:
The leader of the Ephraimites is Elishama son of Ammihud,
chapters.zh: 「在西边，按着军队是以法莲营的纛。亚米忽的儿子以利沙玛作以法莲人的首领。

chapters.en: and his division numbers 40,500.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有四万零五百名。

chapters.en: The tribe of Manasseh will be next to it. The leader of the Manassites is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur,
chapters.zh: 挨着他的是玛拿西支派。比大蓿的儿子迦玛列作玛拿西人的首领。

chapters.en: and his division numbers 32,200.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有三万二千二百名。

chapters.en: Next will be the tribe of Benjamin. The leader of the Benjamites is Abidan son of Gideoni,
chapters.zh: 又有便雅悯支派。基多尼的儿子亚比但作便雅悯人的首领。

chapters.en: and his division numbers 35,400.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有三万五千四百名。

chapters.en: The total number of men in the divisions of the camp of Ephraim is 108,100; they shall set out third.
chapters.zh: 凡属以法莲营、按着军队被数的，共有十万零八千一百名，要作第三队往前行。

chapters.en:
On the north side, the divisions of Dan are to camp under their standard:
The leader of the Danites is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai,
chapters.zh: 「在北边，按着军队是但营的纛。亚米沙代的儿子亚希以谢作但人的首领。

chapters.en: and his division numbers 62,700.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有六万二千七百名。

chapters.en: The tribe of Asher will camp next to it. The leader of the Asherites is Pagiel son of Ocran,
chapters.zh: 挨着他安营的是亚设支派。俄兰的儿子帕结作亚设人的首领。

chapters.en: and his division numbers 41,500.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有四万一千五百名。

chapters.en: Next will be the tribe of Naphtali. The leader of the Naphtalites is Ahira son of Enan,
chapters.zh: 又有拿弗他利支派。以南的儿子亚希拉作拿弗他利人的首领。

chapters.en: and his division numbers 53,400.
chapters.zh: 他军队被数的，共有五万三千四百名。

chapters.en: The total number of men in the camp of Dan is 157,600; they shall set out last, under their standards.”
chapters.zh: 凡但营被数的，共有十五万七千六百名，要归本纛作末队往前行。」

chapters.en: These are the Israelites, numbered according to their families. The total of those counted in the camps, by their divisions, was 603,550.
chapters.zh: 这些以色列人，照他们的宗族，按他们的军队，在诸营中被数的，共有六十万零三千五百五十名。

chapters.en: But the Levites were not counted among the other Israelites, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 惟独利未人没有数在以色列人中，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: So the Israelites did everything the LORD commanded Moses; they camped under their standards in this way and set out in the same way, each man with his clan and his family.
chapters.zh: 以色列人就这样行，各人照他们的家室、宗族归于本纛，安营起行，都是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。

chapters.en: This is the account of Aaron and Moses at the time the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
chapters.zh: 耶和华在西奈山晓谕摩西的日子，亚伦和摩西的后代如下：

chapters.en: These are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab the firstborn, then Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
chapters.zh: 亚伦的儿子，长子名叫拿答，还有亚比户、以利亚撒、以他玛。

chapters.en: These were Aaron’s sons, the anointed priests, who were ordained to serve as priests.
chapters.zh: 这是亚伦儿子的名字，都是受膏的祭司，是摩西叫他们承接圣职供祭司职分的。

chapters.en: Nadab and Abihu, however, died in the presence of the LORD when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the Wilderness of Sinai. And since they had no sons, only Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests during the lifetime of their father Aaron.
chapters.zh: 拿答、亚比户在西奈的旷野向耶和华献凡火的时候就死在耶和华面前了。他们也没有儿子。以利亚撒、以他玛在他们的父亲亚伦面前供祭司的职分。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Bring the tribe of Levi and present them to Aaron the priest to assist him.
chapters.zh: 「你使利未支派近前来，站在祭司亚伦面前好服事他，

chapters.en: They are to perform duties for him and for the whole congregation before the Tent of Meeting, attending to the service of the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 替他和会众在会幕前守所吩咐的，办理帐幕的事。

chapters.en: They shall take care of all the furnishings of the Tent of Meeting and fulfill obligations for the Israelites by attending to the service of the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 又要看守会幕的器具，并守所吩咐以色列人的，办理帐幕的事。

chapters.en: Assign the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they have been given exclusively to him from among the Israelites.
chapters.zh: 你要将利未人给亚伦和他的儿子，因为他们是从以色列人中选出来给他的。

chapters.en: So you shall appoint Aaron and his sons to carry out the duties of the priesthood; but any outsider who approaches the tabernacle must be put to death.”
chapters.zh: 你要嘱咐亚伦和他的儿子谨守自己祭司的职任。近前来的外人必被治死。」

chapters.en: Again the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel in place of every firstborn Israelite from the womb. The Levites belong to Me,
chapters.zh: 「我从以色列人中拣选了利未人，代替以色列人一切头生的；利未人要归我。

chapters.en: for all the firstborn are Mine. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to Myself all the firstborn in Israel, both man and beast. They are Mine; I am the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 因为凡头生的是我的；我在埃及地击杀一切头生的那日就把以色列中一切头生的，连人带牲畜都分别为圣归我；他们定要属我。我是耶和华。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD spoke to Moses in the Wilderness of Sinai, saying,
chapters.zh: 耶和华在西奈的旷野晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Number the Levites by their families and clans. You are to count every male a month old or more.”
chapters.zh: 「你要照利未人的宗族、家室数点他们。凡一个月以外的男子都要数点。」

chapters.en: So Moses numbered them according to the word of the LORD, as he had been commanded.
chapters.zh: 于是摩西照耶和华所吩咐的数点他们。

chapters.en: These were the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
chapters.zh: 利未众子的名字是革顺、哥辖、米拉利。

chapters.en: These were the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.
chapters.zh: 革顺的儿子，按着家室，是立尼、示每。

chapters.en: The sons of Kohath by their clans were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
chapters.zh: 哥辖的儿子，按着家室，是暗兰、以斯哈、希伯伦、乌薛。

chapters.en: And the sons of Merari by their clans were Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of the Levites, according to their families.
chapters.zh: 米拉利的儿子，按着家室，是抹利、母示。这些按着宗族是利未人的家室。

chapters.en: From Gershon came the Libnite clan and the Shimeite clan; these were the Gershonite clans.
chapters.zh: 属革顺的，有立尼族、示每族。这是革顺的二族。

chapters.en: The number of all the males a month old or more was 7,500.
chapters.zh: 其中被数、从一个月以外所有的男子共有七千五百名。

chapters.en: The Gershonite clans were to camp on the west, behind the tabernacle,
chapters.zh: 这革顺的二族要在帐幕后西边安营。

chapters.en: and the leader of the families of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.
chapters.zh: 拉伊勒的儿子以利雅萨作革顺人宗族的首领。

chapters.en: The duties of the Gershonites at the Tent of Meeting were the tabernacle and tent, its covering, the curtain for the entrance to the Tent of Meeting,
chapters.zh: 革顺的子孙在会幕中所要看守的，就是帐幕和罩棚，并罩棚的盖与会幕的门帘，

chapters.en: the curtains of the courtyard, the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard that surrounds the tabernacle and altar, and the cords—all the service for these items.
chapters.zh: 院子的帷子和门帘（院子是围帐幕和坛的），并一切使用的绳子。

chapters.en: From Kohath came the clans of the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites; these were the clans of the Kohathites.
chapters.zh: 属哥辖的，有暗兰族、以斯哈族、希伯伦族、乌薛族。这是哥辖的诸族。

chapters.en: The number of all the males a month old or more was 8,600. They were responsible for the duties of the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 按所有男子的数目，从一个月以外看守圣所的，共有八千六百名。

chapters.en: The clans of the Kohathites were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle,
chapters.zh: 哥辖儿子的诸族要在帐幕的南边安营。

chapters.en: and the leader of the families of the Kohathites was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
chapters.zh: 乌薛的儿子以利撒反作哥辖宗族家室的首领。

chapters.en: Their duties were the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the articles of the sanctuary used with them, and the curtain—all the service for these items.
chapters.zh: 他们所要看守的是〔约〕柜、桌子、灯台、两座坛与圣所内使用的器皿，并帘子和一切使用之物。

chapters.en: The chief of the leaders of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest; he oversaw those responsible for the duties of the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 祭司亚伦的儿子以利亚撒作利未人众首领的领袖，要监察那些看守圣所的人。

chapters.en: From Merari came the clans of the Mahlites and Mushites; these were the Merarite clans.
chapters.zh: 属米拉利的，有抹利族、母示族。这是米拉利的二族。

chapters.en: The number of all the males a month old or more was 6,200.
chapters.zh: 他们被数的，按所有男子的数目，从一个月以外的，共有六千二百名。

chapters.en: The leader of the families of the Merarites was Zuriel son of Abihail; they were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 亚比亥的儿子苏列作米拉利二宗族的首领。他们要在帐幕的北边安营。

chapters.en: The duties assigned to the sons of Merari were the tabernacle’s frames, crossbars, posts, bases, and all its equipment—all the service for these items,
chapters.zh: 米拉利子孙的职分是看守帐幕的板、闩、柱子、带卯的座，和帐幕一切所使用的器具，

chapters.en: as well as the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, tent pegs, and ropes.
chapters.zh: 院子四围的柱子、带卯的座、橛子，和绳子。

chapters.en: Moses, Aaron, and Aaron’s sons were to camp to the east of the tabernacle, toward the sunrise, before the Tent of Meeting. They were to perform the duties of the sanctuary as a service on behalf of the Israelites; but any outsider who approached the sanctuary was to be put to death.
chapters.zh: 在帐幕前东边，向日出之地安营的是摩西、亚伦，和亚伦的儿子。他们看守圣所，替以色列人守〔耶和华〕所吩咐的。近前来的外人必被治死。

chapters.en: The total number of Levites that Moses and Aaron counted by their clans at the LORD’s command, including all the males a month old or more, was 22,000.
chapters.zh: 凡被数的利未人，就是摩西、亚伦照耶和华吩咐所数的，按着家室，从一个月以外的男子，共有二万二千名。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Number every firstborn male of the Israelites a month old or more, and list their names.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你要从以色列人中数点一个月以外、凡头生的男子，把他们的名字记下。

chapters.en: You are to take the Levites for Me—I am the LORD—in place of all the firstborn of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the livestock of the Israelites.”
chapters.zh: 我是耶和华。你要拣选利未人归我，代替以色列人所有头生的，也取利未人的牲畜代替以色列所有头生的牲畜。」

chapters.en: So Moses numbered all the firstborn of the Israelites, as the LORD had commanded him.
chapters.zh: 摩西就照耶和华所吩咐的把以色列人头生的都数点了。

chapters.en: The total number of the firstborn males a month old or more, listed by name, was 22,273.
chapters.zh: 按人名的数目，从一个月以外、凡头生的男子，共有二万二千二百七十三名。

chapters.en: Again the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites belong to Me; I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「你拣选利未人代替以色列人所有头生的，也取利未人的牲畜代替以色列人的牲畜。利未人要归我；我是耶和华。

chapters.en: To redeem the 273 firstborn Israelites who outnumber the Levites,
chapters.zh: 以色列人中头生的男子比利未人多二百七十三个，必当将他们赎出来。

chapters.en: you are to collect five shekels for each one, according to the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs.
chapters.zh: 你要按人丁，照圣所的平，每人取赎银五舍客勒（一舍客勒是二十季拉），

chapters.en: Give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for the excess among the Israelites.”
chapters.zh: 把那多余之人的赎银交给亚伦和他的儿子。」

chapters.en: So Moses collected the redemption money from those in excess of the number redeemed by the Levites.
chapters.zh: 于是摩西从那被利未人所赎以外的人取了赎银。

chapters.en: He collected the money from the firstborn of the Israelites: 1,365 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
chapters.zh: 从以色列人头生的所取之银，按圣所的平，有一千三百六十五〔舍客勒〕。

chapters.en: And Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons in obedience to the word of the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded him.
chapters.zh: 摩西照耶和华的话把这赎银给亚伦和他的儿子，正如耶和华所吩咐的。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西、亚伦说：

chapters.en: “Take a census of the Kohathites among the Levites by their clans and families,
chapters.zh: 「你从利未人中，将哥辖子孙的总数，照他们的家室、宗族，

chapters.en: men from thirty to fifty years old—everyone who is qualified to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 从三十岁直到五十岁，凡前来任职、在会幕里办事的，全都计算。

chapters.en: This service of the Kohathites at the Tent of Meeting regards the most holy things.
chapters.zh: 哥辖子孙在会幕〔搬运〕至圣之物，所办的事乃是这样：

chapters.en: Whenever the camp sets out, Aaron and his sons are to go in, take down the veil of the curtain, and cover the ark of the Testimony with it.
chapters.zh: 起营的时候，亚伦和他儿子要进去摘下遮掩〔柜〕的幔子，用以蒙盖法柜，

chapters.en: They are to place over this a covering of fine leather, spread a solid blue cloth over it, and insert its poles.
chapters.zh: 又用海狗皮盖在上头，再蒙上纯蓝色的毯子，把杠穿上。

chapters.en: Over the table of the Presence they are to spread a blue cloth and place the plates and cups on it, along with the bowls and pitchers for the drink offering. The regular bread offering is to remain on it.
chapters.zh: 又用蓝色毯子铺在陈设饼的桌子上，将盘子、调羹、奠〔酒〕的爵，和杯摆在上头。桌子上也必有常〔设的〕饼。

chapters.en: And they shall spread a scarlet cloth over them, cover them with fine leather, and insert the poles.
chapters.zh: 在其上又要蒙朱红色的毯子，再蒙上海狗皮，把杠穿上。

chapters.en: They are to take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand used for light, together with its lamps, wick trimmers, and trays, as well as the jars of oil with which to supply it.
chapters.zh: 要拿蓝色毯子，把灯台和灯台上所用的灯盏、剪子、蜡花盘，并一切盛油的器皿，全都遮盖。

chapters.en: Then they shall wrap it and all its utensils inside a covering of fine leather and put it on the carrying frame.
chapters.zh: 又要把灯台和灯台的一切器具包在海狗皮里，放在抬架上。

chapters.en: Over the gold altar they are to spread a blue cloth, cover it with fine leather, and insert the poles.
chapters.zh: 在金坛上要铺蓝色毯子，蒙上海狗皮，把杠穿上。

chapters.en: They are to take all the utensils for serving in the sanctuary, place them in a blue cloth, cover them with fine leather, and put them on the carrying frame.
chapters.zh: 又要把圣所用的一切器具包在蓝色毯子里，用海狗皮蒙上，放在抬架上。

chapters.en: Then they shall remove the ashes from the bronze altar, spread a purple cloth over it,
chapters.zh: 要收去坛上的灰，把紫色毯子铺在坛上；

chapters.en: and place on it all the vessels used to serve there: the firepans, meat forks, shovels, and sprinkling bowls—all the equipment of the altar. They are to spread over it a covering of fine leather and insert the poles.
chapters.zh: 又要把所用的一切器具，就是火鼎、肉锸子、铲子、盘子，一切属坛的器具都摆在坛上，又蒙上海狗皮，把杠穿上。

chapters.en: When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy objects and all their equipment, as soon as the camp is ready to move, the Kohathites shall come and do the carrying. But they must not touch the holy objects, or they will die. These are the transportation duties of the Kohathites regarding the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 将要起营的时候，亚伦和他儿子把圣所和圣所的一切器具遮盖完了，哥辖的子孙就要来抬，只是不可摸圣物，免得他们死亡。会幕里这些物件是哥辖子孙所当抬的。

chapters.en: Eleazar son of Aaron the priest shall oversee the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the daily grain offering, and the anointing oil. He has oversight of the entire tabernacle and everything in it, including the holy objects and their utensils.”
chapters.zh: 「祭司亚伦的儿子以利亚撒所要看守的是点灯的油与香料，并当献的素祭和膏油，也要看守全帐幕与其中所有的，并圣所和圣所的器具。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西、亚伦说：

chapters.en: “Do not allow the Kohathite tribal clans to be cut off from among the Levites.
chapters.zh: 「你们不可将哥辖人的支派从利未人中剪除。

chapters.en: In order that they may live and not die when they come near the most holy things, do this for them: Aaron and his sons are to go in and assign each man his task and what he is to carry.
chapters.zh: 他们挨近至圣物的时候，亚伦和他儿子要进去派他们各人所当办的，所当抬的。这样待他们，好使他们活着，不致死亡。

chapters.en: But the Kohathites are not to go in and look at the holy objects, even for a moment, or they will die.”
chapters.zh: 只是他们连片时不可进去观看圣所，免得他们死亡。」

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Take a census of the Gershonites as well, by their families and clans,
chapters.zh: 「你要将革顺子孙的总数，照着宗族、家室，

chapters.en: from thirty to fifty years old, counting everyone who comes to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 从三十岁直到五十岁，凡前来任职、在会幕里办事的，全都数点。

chapters.en: This is the service of the Gershonite clans regarding work and transport:
chapters.zh: 革顺人各族所办的事、所抬的物乃是这样：

chapters.en: They are to carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting with the covering of fine leather over it, the curtains for the entrance to the Tent of Meeting,
chapters.zh: 他们要抬帐幕的幔子和会幕，并会幕的盖与其上的海狗皮，和会幕的门帘，

chapters.en: the curtains of the courtyard, and the curtains for the entrance at the gate of the courtyard that surrounds the tabernacle and altar, along with their ropes and all the equipment for their service. The Gershonites will do all that needs to be done with these items.
chapters.zh: 院子的帷子和门帘（院子是围帐幕和坛的）、绳子，并所用的器具，不论是做什么用的，他们都要经理。

chapters.en: All the service of the Gershonites—all their transport duties and other work—is to be done at the direction of Aaron and his sons; you are to assign to them all that they are responsible to carry.
chapters.zh: 革顺的子孙在一切抬物办事之上都要凭亚伦和他儿子的吩咐；他们所当抬的，要派他们看守。

chapters.en: This is the service of the Gershonite clans at the Tent of Meeting, and their duties shall be under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
chapters.zh: 这是革顺子孙的各族在会幕里所办的事；他们所看守的，必在祭司亚伦儿子以他玛的手下。」

chapters.en: As for the sons of Merari, you are to number them by their clans and families,
chapters.zh: 「至于米拉利的子孙，你要照着家室、宗族把他们数点。

chapters.en: from thirty to fifty years old, counting everyone who comes to serve in the work of the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 从三十岁直到五十岁，凡前来任职、在会幕里办事的，你都要数点。

chapters.en: This is the duty for all their service at the Tent of Meeting: to carry the frames of the tabernacle with its crossbars, posts, and bases,
chapters.zh: 他们办理会幕的事，就是抬帐幕的板、闩、柱子，和带卯的座，

chapters.en: and the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, tent pegs, and ropes, including all their equipment and everything related to their use. You shall assign by name the items that they are responsible to carry.
chapters.zh: 院子四围的柱子和其上带卯的座、橛子、绳子，并一切使用的器具。他们所抬的器具，你们要按名指定。

chapters.en: This is the service of the Merarite clans according to all their work at the Tent of Meeting, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.”
chapters.zh: 这是米拉利子孙各族在会幕里所办的事，都在祭司亚伦儿子以他玛的手下。」

chapters.en: So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the congregation numbered the Kohathites by their clans and families,
chapters.zh: 摩西、亚伦与会众的诸首领将哥辖的子孙，照着家室、宗族，

chapters.en: everyone from thirty to fifty years old who came to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 从三十岁直到五十岁，凡前来任职、在会幕里办事的，都数点了。

chapters.en: And those numbered by their clans totaled 2,750.
chapters.zh: 被数的共有二千七百五十名。

chapters.en: These were counted from the Kohathite clans, everyone who could serve at the Tent of Meeting. Moses and Aaron numbered them according to the command of the LORD through Moses.
chapters.zh: 这是哥辖各族中被数的，是在会幕里办事的，就是摩西、亚伦照耶和华藉摩西所吩咐数点的。

chapters.en: Then the Gershonites were numbered by their clans and families,
chapters.zh: 革顺子孙被数的，照着家室、宗族，

chapters.en: everyone from thirty to fifty years old who came to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
And those numbered by their clans and families totaled 2,630.
chapters.zh: 从三十岁直到五十岁，凡前来任职、在会幕里办事的，共有二千六百三十名。

chapters.en: These were counted from the Gershonite clans who served at the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the LORD’s command.
chapters.zh: 这是革顺子孙各族中被数的，是在会幕里办事的，就是摩西、亚伦照耶和华藉摩西所吩咐数点的。

chapters.en: And the Merarites were numbered by their clans and families,
chapters.zh: 米拉利子孙中各族被数的，照着家室、宗族，

chapters.en: everyone from thirty to fifty years old who came to serve in the work at the Tent of Meeting.
The men registered by their clans numbered 3,200.
chapters.zh: 从三十岁直到五十岁，凡前来任职、在会幕里办事的，共有三千二百名。

chapters.en: These were counted from the Merarite clans, whom Moses and Aaron numbered at the LORD’s command through Moses.
chapters.zh: 这是米拉利子孙各族中被数的，就是摩西、亚伦照耶和华藉摩西所吩咐数点的。

chapters.en: So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel numbered by their clans and families all the Levites
chapters.zh: 凡被数的利未人，就是摩西、亚伦并以色列众首领，照着家室、宗族所数点的，

chapters.en: from thirty to fifty years old who came to do the work of serving and carrying the Tent of Meeting.
And the number of men was 8,580.
chapters.zh: 从三十岁直到五十岁，凡前来任职、在会幕里做抬物之工的，共有八千五百八十名。

chapters.en: At the LORD’s command through Moses they were numbered, and each one was assigned his work and burden, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 摩西按他们所办的事、所抬的物，凭耶和华的吩咐数点他们；他们这样被摩西数点，正如耶和华所吩咐他的。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Command the Israelites to send away from the camp anyone with a skin disease, anyone who has a bodily discharge, and anyone who is defiled by a dead body.
chapters.zh: 「你吩咐以色列人，使一切长大痲疯的，患漏症的，并因死尸不洁净的，都出营外去。

chapters.en: You must send away male and female alike; send them outside the camp so they will not defile their camp, where I dwell among them.”
chapters.zh: 无论男女都要使他们出到营外，免得污秽他们的营；这营是我所住的。」

chapters.en: So the Israelites did this, sending such people outside the camp. They did just as the LORD had instructed Moses.
chapters.zh: 以色列人就这样行，使他们出到营外。耶和华怎样吩咐摩西，以色列人就怎样行了。

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Tell the Israelites that when a man or woman acts unfaithfully against the LORD by committing any sin against another, that person is guilty
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：无论男女，若犯了人所常犯的罪，以致干犯耶和华，那人就有了罪。

chapters.en: and must confess the sin he has committed. He must make full restitution, add a fifth to its value, and give all this to the one he has wronged.
chapters.zh: 他要承认所犯的罪，将所亏负人的，如数赔还，另外加上五分之一，也归与所亏负的人。

chapters.en: But if the man has no relative to whom restitution can be made for the wrong, the restitution belongs to the LORD and must be given to the priest along with the ram of atonement, by which the atonement is made for him.
chapters.zh: 那人若没有亲属可受所赔还的，那所赔还的就要归与服事耶和华的祭司；至于那为他赎罪的公羊是在外。

chapters.en: Every sacred contribution the Israelites bring to the priest shall belong to him.
chapters.zh: 以色列人一切的圣物中，所奉给祭司的举祭都要归与祭司。

chapters.en: Each man’s sacred gifts are his own, but whatever he gives to the priest will belong to the priest.”
chapters.zh: 各人所分别为圣的物，无论是什么，都要归给祭司。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them that if any man’s wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：人的妻若有邪行，得罪她丈夫，

chapters.en: by sleeping with another man, and it is concealed from her husband and her impurity is undetected (since there is no witness against her and she was not caught in the act),
chapters.zh: 有人与她行淫，事情严密，瞒过她丈夫，而且她被玷污，没有作见证的人，当她行淫的时候也没有被捉住，

chapters.en: and if a feeling of jealousy comes over her husband and he suspects his wife who has defiled herself—or if a feeling of jealousy comes over him and he suspects her even though she has not defiled herself—
chapters.zh: 她丈夫生了疑恨的心，疑恨她，她是被玷污，或是她丈夫生了疑恨的心，疑恨她，她并没有被玷污，

chapters.en:
then he is to bring his wife to the priest.
He must also bring for her an offering of a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He is not to pour oil over it or put frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, an offering of memorial as a reminder of iniquity.
chapters.zh: 这人就要将妻送到祭司那里，又为她带着大麦面伊法十分之一作供物，不可浇上油，也不可加上乳香；因为这是疑恨的素祭，是思念的素祭，使人思念罪孽。

chapters.en: The priest is to bring the wife forward and have her stand before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「祭司要使那妇人近前来，站在耶和华面前。

chapters.en: Then he is to take some holy water in a clay jar and put some of the dust from the tabernacle floor into the water.
chapters.zh: 祭司要把圣水盛在瓦器里，又从帐幕的地上取点尘土，放在水中。

chapters.en: After the priest has the woman stand before the LORD, he is to let down her hair and place in her hands the grain offering of memorial, which is the grain offering for jealousy. The priest is to hold the bitter water that brings a curse.
chapters.zh: 祭司要叫那妇人蓬头散发，站在耶和华面前，把思念的素祭，就是疑恨的素祭，放在她手中。祭司手里拿着致咒诅的苦水，

chapters.en: And he is to put the woman under oath and say to her, ‘If no other man has slept with you and you have not gone astray and become defiled while under your husband’s authority, may you be immune to this bitter water that brings a curse.
chapters.zh: 要叫妇人起誓，对她说：『若没有人与你行淫，也未曾背着丈夫做污秽的事，你就免受这致咒诅苦水的灾。

chapters.en: But if you have gone astray while under your husband’s authority and have defiled yourself and lain carnally with a man other than your husband’—
chapters.zh: 你若背着丈夫行了污秽的事，在你丈夫以外有人与你行淫，

chapters.en: and the priest shall have the woman swear under the oath of the curse—‘then may the LORD make you an attested curse among your people by making your thigh shrivel and your belly swell.
chapters.zh: （祭司叫妇人发咒起誓），愿耶和华叫你大腿消瘦，肚腹发胀，使你在你民中被人咒诅，成了誓语；

chapters.en:
May this water that brings a curse enter your stomach and cause your belly to swell and your thigh to shrivel.’
Then the woman is to say, ‘Amen, Amen.’
chapters.zh: 并且这致咒诅的水入你的肠中，要叫你的肚腹发胀，大腿消瘦。』妇人要回答说：『阿们，阿们。』

chapters.en: And the priest shall write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the bitter water.
chapters.zh: 「祭司要写这咒诅的话，将所写的字抹在苦水里，

chapters.en: He is to have the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and it will enter her and may cause her bitter suffering.
chapters.zh: 又叫妇人喝这致咒诅的苦水；这水要进入她里面〔变〕苦了。

chapters.en: The priest shall take from her hand the grain offering for jealousy, wave it before the LORD, and bring it to the altar.
chapters.zh: 祭司要从妇人的手中取那疑恨的素祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇，拿到坛前；

chapters.en: Then the priest is to take a handful of the grain offering as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar; after that he is to have the woman drink the water.
chapters.zh: 又要从素祭中取出一把，作为这事的纪念，烧在坛上，然后叫妇人喝这水。

chapters.en: When he has made her drink the water, if she has defiled herself and been unfaithful to her husband, then the water that brings a curse will enter her and cause bitter suffering; her belly will swell, her thigh will shrivel, and she will become accursed among her people.
chapters.zh: 叫她喝了以后，她若被玷污，得罪了丈夫，这致咒诅的水必进入她里面〔变〕苦了，她的肚腹就要发胀，大腿就要消瘦，那妇人便要在他民中被人咒诅。

chapters.en: But if the woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she will be unaffected and able to conceive children.
chapters.zh: 若妇人没有被玷污，却是清洁的，就要免受这灾，且要怀孕。

chapters.en: This is the law of jealousy when a wife goes astray and defiles herself while under her husband’s authority,
chapters.zh: 「妻子背着丈夫行了污秽的事，

chapters.en: or when a feeling of jealousy comes over a husband and he suspects his wife. He is to have the woman stand before the LORD, and the priest is to apply to her this entire law.
chapters.zh: 或是人生了疑恨的心，疑恨他的妻，就有这疑恨的条例。那时他要叫妇人站在耶和华面前，祭司要在她身上照这条例而行。

chapters.en: The husband will be free from guilt, but the woman shall bear her iniquity.”
chapters.zh: 男人就为无罪，妇人必担当自己的罪孽。」

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them that if a man or woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the LORD,
chapters.zh: 「你晓谕以色列人说：无论男女许了特别的愿，就是拿细耳人的愿〔注：拿细耳就是归主的意思；下同〕，要离俗归耶和华。

chapters.en: he is to abstain from wine and strong drink. He must not drink vinegar made from wine or strong drink, and he must not drink any grape juice or eat fresh grapes or raisins.
chapters.zh: 他就要远离清酒浓酒，也不可喝什么清酒浓酒做的醋；不可喝什么葡萄汁，也不可吃鲜葡萄和干葡萄。

chapters.en: All the days of his separation, he is not to eat anything that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or skins.
chapters.zh: 在一切离俗的日子，凡葡萄树上结的，自核至皮所做的物，都不可吃。

chapters.en: For the entire period of his vow of separation, no razor shall touch his head. He must be holy until the time of his separation to the LORD is complete; he must let the hair of his head grow long.
chapters.zh: 「在他一切许愿离俗的日子，不可用剃头刀剃头，要由发绺长长了。他要圣洁，直到离俗归耶和华的日子满了。

chapters.en: Throughout the days of his separation to the LORD, he must not go near a dead body.
chapters.zh: 在他离俗归耶和华的一切日子，不可挨近死尸。

chapters.en: Even if his father or mother or brother or sister should die, he is not to defile himself, because the symbol of consecration to his God is upon his head.
chapters.zh: 他的父母或是弟兄姊妹死了的时候，他不可因他们使自己不洁净，因为那离俗归上帝的〔凭据〕是在他头上。

chapters.en: Throughout the time of his separation, he is holy to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 在他一切离俗的日子是归耶和华为圣。

chapters.en: If someone suddenly dies in his presence and defiles his consecrated head of hair, he must shave his head on the day of his cleansing—the seventh day.
chapters.zh: 「若在他旁边忽然有人死了，以致沾染了他离俗的头，他要在第七日，得洁净的时候，剃头。

chapters.en: On the eighth day he must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
chapters.zh: 第八日，他要把两只斑鸠或两只雏鸽带到会幕门口，交给祭司。

chapters.en: And the priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to make atonement for him, because he has sinned by being in the presence of the dead body. On that day he must consecrate his head again.
chapters.zh: 祭司要献一只作赎罪祭，一只作燔祭，为他赎那因死尸而有的罪，并要当日使他的头成为圣洁。

chapters.en: He must rededicate his time of separation to the LORD and bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. But the preceding days shall not be counted, because his separation was defiled.
chapters.zh: 他要另选离俗归耶和华的日子，又要牵一只一岁的公羊羔来作赎愆祭；但先前的日子要归徒然，因为他在离俗之间被玷污了。

chapters.en: Now this is the law of the Nazirite when his time of separation is complete: He must be brought to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting,
chapters.zh: 「拿细耳人满了离俗的日子乃有这条例：人要领他到会幕门口，

chapters.en: and he is to present an offering to the LORD of an unblemished year-old male lamb as a burnt offering, an unblemished year-old female lamb as a sin offering, and an unblemished ram as a peace offering—
chapters.zh: 他要将供物奉给耶和华，就是一只没有残疾、一岁的公羊羔作燔祭，一只没有残疾、一岁的母羊羔作赎罪祭，和一只没有残疾的公绵羊作平安祭，

chapters.en: together with their grain offerings and drink offerings—and a basket of unleavened cakes made from fine flour mixed with oil and unleavened wafers coated with oil.
chapters.zh: 并一筐子无酵调油的细面饼，与抹油的无酵薄饼，并同献的素祭和奠祭。

chapters.en: The priest is to present all these before the LORD and make the sin offering and the burnt offering.
chapters.zh: 祭司要在耶和华面前献那人的赎罪祭和燔祭；

chapters.en: He shall also offer the ram as a peace offering to the LORD, along with the basket of unleavened bread. And the priest is to offer the accompanying grain offering and drink offering.
chapters.zh: 也要把那只公羊和那筐无酵饼献给耶和华作平安祭，又要将同献的素祭和奠祭献上。

chapters.en: Then at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the Nazirite is to shave his consecrated head, take the hair, and put it on the fire under the peace offering.
chapters.zh: 拿细耳人要在会幕门口剃离俗的头，把离俗头上的发放在平安祭下的火上。

chapters.en: And the priest is to take the boiled shoulder from the ram, one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and put them into the hands of the Nazirite who has just shaved the hair of his consecration.
chapters.zh: 他剃了以后，祭司就要取那已煮的公羊一条前腿，又从筐子里取一个无酵饼和一个无酵薄饼，都放在他手上。

chapters.en: The priest shall then wave them as a wave offering before the LORD. This is a holy portion for the priest, in addition to the breast of the wave offering and the thigh that was presented. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine.
chapters.zh: 祭司要拿这些作为摇祭，在耶和华面前摇一摇；这与所摇的胸、所举的腿同为圣物，归给祭司。然后拿细耳人可以喝酒。

chapters.en: This is the law of the Nazirite who vows his offering to the LORD for his separation, in addition to whatever else he can afford; he must fulfill whatever vow he makes, according to the law of his separation.”
chapters.zh: 「许愿的拿细耳人为离俗所献的供物，和他以外所能得的献给耶和华，就有这条例。他怎样许愿就当照离俗的条例行。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:
chapters.zh: 「你告诉亚伦和他儿子说：你们要这样为以色列人祝福，说：

chapters.en: ‘May the LORD bless you and keep you;
chapters.zh: 『愿耶和华赐福给你，保护你。

chapters.en: may the LORD cause His face to shine upon you and be gracious to you;
chapters.zh: 愿耶和华使他的脸光照你，赐恩给你。

chapters.en: may the LORD lift up His countenance toward you and give you peace.’
chapters.zh: 愿耶和华向你仰脸，赐你平安。』

chapters.en: So they shall put My name on the Israelites, and I will bless them.”
chapters.zh: 他们要如此奉我的名为以色列人祝福；我也要赐福给他们。」

chapters.en: On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed and consecrated it and all its furnishings, along with the altar and all its utensils.
chapters.zh: 摩西立完了帐幕，就把帐幕用膏抹了，使它成圣，又把其中的器具和坛，并坛上的器具，都抹了，使它成圣。

chapters.en: And the leaders of Israel, the heads of their families, presented an offering. These men were the tribal leaders who had supervised the registration.
chapters.zh: 当天，以色列的众首领，就是各族的族长，都来奉献。他们是各支派的首领，管理那些被数的人。

chapters.en: They brought as their offering before the LORD six covered carts and twelve oxen—an ox from each leader and a cart from every two leaders—and presented them before the tabernacle.
chapters.zh: 他们把自己的供物送到耶和华面前，就是六辆篷子车和十二只公牛。每两个首领奉献一辆车，每首领奉献一只牛。他们把这些都奉到帐幕前。

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Accept these gifts from them, that they may be used in the work of the Tent of Meeting. And give them to the Levites, to each man according to his service.”
chapters.zh: 「你要收下这些，好作会幕的使用，都要照利未人所办的事交给他们。」

chapters.en: So Moses took the carts and oxen and gave them to the Levites.
chapters.zh: 于是摩西收了车和牛，交给利未人，

chapters.en: He gave the Gershonites two carts and four oxen, as their service required,
chapters.zh: 把两辆车，四只牛，照革顺子孙所办的事交给他们，

chapters.en: and he gave the Merarites four carts and eight oxen, as their service required, all under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
chapters.zh: 又把四辆车，八只牛，照米拉利子孙所办的事交给他们；他们都在祭司亚伦的儿子以他玛手下。

chapters.en: But he did not give any to the Kohathites, since they were to carry on their shoulders the holy objects for which they were responsible.
chapters.zh: 但车与牛都没有交给哥辖子孙；因为他们办的是圣所的事，在肩头上抬圣物。

chapters.en: When the altar was anointed, the leaders approached with their offerings for its dedication and presented them before the altar.
chapters.zh: 用膏抹坛的日子，首领都来行奉献坛的礼，众首领就在坛前献供物。

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Moses, “Each day one leader is to present his offering for the dedication of the altar.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「众首领为行奉献坛的礼，要每天一个首领来献供物。」

chapters.en: On the first day Nahshon son of Amminadab from the tribe of Judah drew near with his offering.
chapters.zh: 头一日献供物的是犹大支派的亚米拿达的儿子拿顺。

chapters.en: His offering was one silver platter weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, both according to the sanctuary shekel and filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
chapters.zh: 他的供物是：一个银盘子，重一百三十〔舍客勒〕，一个银碗，重七十舍客勒，都是按圣所的平，也都盛满了调油的细面作素祭；

chapters.en: one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense;
chapters.zh: 一个金盂，重十〔舍客勒〕，盛满了香；

chapters.en: one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
chapters.zh: 一只公牛犊，一只公绵羊，一只一岁的公羊羔作燔祭；

chapters.en: one male goat for a sin offering;
chapters.zh: 一只公山羊作赎罪祭；

chapters.en: and a peace offering of two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.

chapters.en: So these were the offerings from the leaders of Israel for the dedication of the altar when it was anointed: twelve silver platters, twelve silver bowls, and twelve gold dishes.
chapters.zh: 用膏抹坛的日子，以色列的众首领为行献坛之礼所献的是：银盘子十二个，银碗十二个，金盂十二个；

chapters.en: Each silver platter weighed a hundred and thirty shekels, and each silver bowl seventy shekels. The total weight of the silver articles was two thousand four hundred shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
chapters.zh: 每盘子〔重〕一百三十〔舍客勒〕，每碗重七十〔舍客勒〕。一切器皿的银子，按圣所的平，共有二千四百〔舍客勒〕。

chapters.en: The twelve gold dishes filled with incense weighed ten shekels each, according to the sanctuary shekel. The total weight of the gold dishes was a hundred and twenty shekels.
chapters.zh: 十二个金盂盛满了香，按圣所的平，每盂重十〔舍客勒〕，所有的金子共一百二十〔舍客勒〕。

chapters.en: All the livestock for the burnt offering totaled twelve bulls, twelve rams, and twelve male lambs a year old—together with their grain offerings—and twelve male goats for the sin offering.
chapters.zh: 作燔祭的，共有公牛十二只，公羊十二只，一岁的公羊羔十二只，并同献的素祭作赎罪祭的公山羊十二只；

chapters.en: All the livestock sacrificed for the peace offering totaled twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty male lambs a year old. This was the dedication offering for the altar after it was anointed.
chapters.zh: 作平安祭的，共有公牛二十四只，公绵羊六十只，公山羊六十只，一岁的公羊羔六十只。这就是用膏抹坛之后，为行奉献坛之礼所献的。

chapters.en: When Moses entered the Tent of Meeting to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from between the two cherubim above the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony. Thus the LORD spoke to him.
chapters.zh: 摩西进会幕要与耶和华说话的时候，听见法柜的施恩座以上、二基路伯中间有与他说话的声音，就是耶和华与他说话。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Moses,
chapters.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：

chapters.en: “Speak to Aaron and tell him: ‘When you set up the seven lamps, they are to light the area in front of the lampstand.’”
chapters.zh: 「你告诉亚伦说：点灯的时候，七盏灯都要向灯台前面发光。」

chapters.en: And Aaron did so; he set up the lamps facing toward the front of the lampstand, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
chapters.zh: 亚伦便这样行。他点灯台上的灯，〔使灯〕向前〔发光〕，是照耶和华所吩咐摩西的。
