chapters.en: and what He did in the midst of all the Israelites to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab the Reubenite, when the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, their tents, and every living thing that belonged to them.
chapters.zh: 也没有看见他怎样待吕便子孙以利押的儿子大坍、亚比兰，地怎样在以色列人中间开口，吞了他们和他们的家眷，并帐棚与跟他们的一切活物。

chapters.en: For it is your own eyes that have seen every great work that the LORD has done.
chapters.zh: 惟有你们亲眼看见耶和华所做的一切大事。」

chapters.en: You shall therefore keep every commandment I am giving you today, so that you may have the strength to go in and possess the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess,
chapters.zh: 「所以，你们要守我今日所吩咐的一切诫命，使你们胆壮，能以进去，得你们所要得的那地，

chapters.en: and so that you may live long in the land that the LORD swore to your fathers to give them and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
chapters.zh: 并使你们的日子在耶和华向你们列祖起誓、应许给他们和他们后裔的地上得以长久；那是流奶与蜜之地。

chapters.en: For the land that you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt, from which you have come, where you sowed your seed and irrigated on foot, like a vegetable garden.
chapters.zh: 你要进去得为业的那地，本不像你出来的埃及地。你在那里撒种，用脚浇灌，像浇灌菜园一样。

chapters.en: But the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess is a land of mountains and valleys that drinks in the rain from heaven.
chapters.zh: 你们要过去得为业的那地乃是有山有谷、雨水滋润之地，

chapters.en: It is a land for which the LORD your God cares; the eyes of the LORD your God are always on it, from the beginning to the end of the year.
chapters.zh: 是耶和华－你上帝所眷顾的；从岁首到年终，耶和华－你上帝的眼目时常看顾那地。

chapters.en: So if you carefully obey the commandments I am giving you today, to love the LORD your God and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul,
chapters.zh: 「你们若留意听从我今日所吩咐的诫命，爱耶和华－你们的上帝，尽心尽性事奉他，

chapters.en: then I will provide rain for your land in season, the autumn and spring rains, that you may gather your grain, new wine, and oil.
chapters.zh: 他〔注：原文是我〕必按时降秋雨春雨在你们的地上，使你们可以收藏五谷、新酒，和油，

chapters.en: And I will provide grass in the fields for your livestock, and you will eat and be satisfied.
chapters.zh: 也必使你吃得饱足，并使田野为你的牲畜长草。

chapters.en: But be careful that you are not enticed to turn aside to worship and bow down to other gods,
chapters.zh: 你们要谨慎，免得心中受迷惑，就偏离〔正路〕，去事奉敬拜别神。

chapters.en: or the anger of the LORD will be kindled against you. He will shut the heavens so that there will be no rain, nor will the land yield its produce, and you will soon perish from the good land that the LORD is giving you.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的怒气向你们发作，就使天闭塞不下雨，地也不出产，使你们在耶和华所赐给你们的美地上速速灭亡。

chapters.en: Fix these words of mine in your hearts and minds; tie them as reminders on your hands and bind them on your foreheads.
chapters.zh: 「你们要将我这话存在心内，留在意中，系在手上为记号，戴在额上为经文；

chapters.en: Teach them to your children, speaking about them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
chapters.zh: 也要教训你们的儿女，无论坐在家里，行在路上，躺下，起来，都要谈论；

chapters.en: Write them on the doorposts of your houses and on your gates,
chapters.zh: 又要写在房屋的门框上，并城门上，

chapters.en: so that as long as the heavens are above the earth, your days and those of your children may be multiplied in the land that the LORD swore to give your fathers.
chapters.zh: 使你们和你们子孙的日子在耶和华向你们列祖起誓、应许给他们的地上得以增多，如天覆地的日子那样多。

chapters.en: For if you carefully keep all these commandments I am giving you to follow—to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, and to hold fast to Him—
chapters.zh: 你们若留意谨守遵行我所吩咐这一切的诫命，爱耶和华－你们的上帝，行他的道，专靠他，

chapters.en: then the LORD will drive out all these nations before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and stronger than you.
chapters.zh: 他必从你们面前赶出这一切国民，就是比你们更大更强的国民，你们也要得他们的地。

chapters.en: Every place where the sole of your foot treads will be yours. Your territory will extend from the wilderness to Lebanon, and from the Euphrates River to the Western Sea.
chapters.zh: 凡你们脚掌所踏之地都必归你们；从旷野和黎巴嫩，并幼发拉底大河，直到西海，都要作你们的境界。

chapters.en: No man will be able to stand against you; the LORD your God will put the fear and dread of you upon all the land, wherever you set foot, as He has promised you.
chapters.zh: 必无一人能在你们面前站立得住；耶和华－你们的上帝必照他所说的，使惧怕惊恐临到你们所踏之地的居民。

chapters.en: See, today I am setting before you a blessing and a curse—
chapters.zh: 「看哪，我今日将祝福与咒诅的话都陈明在你们面前。

chapters.en: a blessing if you obey the commandments of the LORD your God that I am giving you today,
chapters.zh: 你们若听从耶和华－你们上帝的诫命，就是我今日所吩咐你们的，就必蒙福。

chapters.en: but a curse if you disobey the commandments of the LORD your God and turn aside from the path I command you today by following other gods, which you have not known.
chapters.zh: 你们若不听从耶和华－你们上帝的诫命，偏离我今日所吩咐你们的道，去事奉你们素来所不认识的别神，就必受祸。

chapters.en: When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess, you are to proclaim the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
chapters.zh: 及至耶和华－你的上帝领你进入要去得为业的那地，你就要将祝福的话陈明在基利心山上，将咒诅的话陈明在以巴路山上。

chapters.en: Are not these mountains across the Jordan, west of the road toward the sunset, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah opposite Gilgal near the Oak of Moreh?
chapters.zh: 这二山岂不是在约旦河那边，日落之处，在住亚拉巴的迦南人之地与吉甲相对，靠近摩利橡树吗？

chapters.en: For you are about to cross the Jordan to enter and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you. When you take possession of it and settle in it,
chapters.zh: 你们要过约旦河，进去得耶和华－你们上帝所赐你们为业之地，在那地居住。

chapters.en: be careful to follow all the statutes and ordinances that I am setting before you today.
chapters.zh: 你们要谨守遵行我今日在你们面前所陈明的一切律例典章。」

chapters.en: These are the statutes and ordinances you must be careful to follow all the days you live in the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you to possess.
chapters.zh: 「你们存活于世的日子，在耶和华－你们列祖的上帝所赐你们为业的地上，要谨守遵行的律例典章乃是这些：

chapters.en: Destroy completely all the places where the nations you are dispossessing have served their gods—atop the high mountains, on the hills, and under every green tree.
chapters.zh: 你们要将所赶出的国民事奉神的各地方，无论是在高山，在小山，在各青翠树下，都毁坏了；

chapters.en: Tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, burn up their Asherah poles, cut down the idols of their gods, and wipe out their names from every place.
chapters.zh: 也要拆毁他们的祭坛，打碎他们的柱像，用火焚烧他们的木偶，砍下他们雕刻的神像，并将其名从那地方除灭。

chapters.en: You shall not worship the LORD your God in this way.
chapters.zh: 你们不可照他们那样事奉耶和华－你们的上帝。

chapters.en: Instead, you must seek the place the LORD your God will choose from among all your tribes to establish as a dwelling for His Name, and there you must go.
chapters.zh: 但耶和华－你们的上帝从你们各支派中选择何处为立他名的居所，你们就当往那里去求问，

chapters.en: To that place you are to bring your burnt offerings and sacrifices, your tithes and heave offerings, your vow offerings and freewill offerings, as well as the firstborn of your herds and flocks.
chapters.zh: 将你们的燔祭、〔平安〕祭、十分取一之物，和手中的举祭，并还愿祭、甘心祭，以及牛群羊群中头生的，都奉到那里。

chapters.en: There, in the presence of the LORD your God, you and your households shall eat and rejoice in all you do, because the LORD your God has blessed you.
chapters.zh: 在那里，耶和华－你们上帝的面前，你们和你们的家属都可以吃，并且因你手所办的一切事蒙耶和华－你的上帝赐福，就都欢乐。

chapters.en: You are not to do as we are doing here today, where everyone does what seems right in his own eyes.
chapters.zh: 我们今日在这里所行的是各人行自己眼中看为正的事，你们将来不可这样行；

chapters.en: For you have not yet come to the resting place and the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.
chapters.zh: 因为你们还没有到耶和华－你上帝所赐你的安息〔地〕，所给你的产业。

chapters.en: When you cross the Jordan and live in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and He gives you rest from all the enemies around you and you dwell securely,
chapters.zh: 但你们过了约旦河，得以住在耶和华－你们上帝使你们承受为业之地，又使你们太平，不被四围的一切仇敌扰乱，安然居住。

chapters.en: then the LORD your God will choose a dwelling for His Name. And there you are to bring everything I command you: your burnt offerings and sacrifices, your tithes and special gifts, and all the choice offerings you vow to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 那时要将我所吩咐你们的燔祭、〔平安〕祭、十分取一之物，和手中的举祭，并向耶和华许愿献的一切美祭，都奉到耶和华－你们上帝所选择要立为他名的居所。

chapters.en: And you shall rejoice before the LORD your God—you, your sons and daughters, your menservants and maidservants, and the Levite within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.
chapters.zh: 你们和儿女、仆婢，并住在你们城里无分无业的利未人，都要在耶和华－你们的上帝面前欢乐。

chapters.en: Be careful not to offer your burnt offerings in just any place you see;
chapters.zh: 你要谨慎，不可在你所看中的各处献燔祭。

chapters.en: you must offer them only in the place the LORD will choose in one of your tribal territories, and there you shall do all that I command you.
chapters.zh: 惟独耶和华从你那一支派中所选择的地方，你就要在那里献燔祭，行我一切所吩咐你的。

chapters.en: But whenever you want, you may slaughter and eat meat within any of your gates, according to the blessing the LORD your God has given you. Both the ceremonially clean and unclean may eat it as they would a gazelle or deer,
chapters.zh: 「然而，在你各城里都可以照耶和华－你上帝所赐你的福分，随心所欲宰牲吃肉；无论洁净人不洁净人都可以吃，就如吃羚羊与鹿一般。

chapters.en: but you must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.
chapters.zh: 只是不可吃血，要倒在地上，如同倒水一样。

chapters.en: Within your gates you must not eat the tithe of your grain or new wine or oil, the firstborn of your herds or flocks, any of the offerings that you have vowed to give, or your freewill offerings or special gifts.
chapters.zh: 你的五谷、新酒，和油的十分之一，或是牛群羊群中头生的，或是你许愿献的，甘心献的，或是手中的举祭，都不可在你城里吃。

chapters.en: Instead, you must eat them in the presence of the LORD your God at the place the LORD your God will choose—you, your sons and daughters, your menservants and maidservants, and the Levite within your gates. Rejoice before the LORD your God in all you do,
chapters.zh: 但要在耶和华－你的上帝面前吃，在耶和华－你上帝所要选择的地方，你和儿女、仆婢，并住在你城里的利未人，都可以吃；也要因你手所办的，在耶和华－你上帝面前欢乐。

chapters.en: and be careful not to neglect the Levites as long as you live in your land.
chapters.zh: 你要谨慎，在你所住的地方永不可丢弃利未人。

chapters.en: When the LORD your God expands your territory as He has promised, and you crave meat and say, “I want to eat meat,” you may eat it whenever you want.
chapters.zh: 「耶和华－你的上帝照他所应许扩张你境界的时候，你心里想要吃肉，说：『我要吃肉』，就可以随心所欲地吃肉。

chapters.en: If the place where the LORD your God chooses to put His Name is too far from you, then you may slaughter any of the herd or flock He has given you, as I have commanded you, and you may eat it within your gates whenever you want.
chapters.zh: 耶和华－你上帝所选择要立他名的地方若离你太远，就可以照我所吩咐的，将耶和华赐给你的牛羊取些宰了，可以随心所欲在你城里吃。

chapters.en: Indeed, you may eat it as you would eat a gazelle or deer; both the ceremonially unclean and the clean may eat it.
chapters.zh: 你吃那肉，要像吃羚羊与鹿一般；无论洁净人不洁净人都可以吃。

chapters.en: Only be sure not to eat the blood, because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.
chapters.zh: 只是你要心意坚定，不可吃血，因为血是生命；不可将血〔注：原文是生命〕与肉同吃。

chapters.en: You must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.
chapters.zh: 不可吃血，要倒在地上，如同倒水一样。

chapters.en: Do not eat it, so that it may go well with you and your children after you, because you will be doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 不可吃血。这样，你行耶和华眼中看为正的事，你和你的子孙就可以得福。

chapters.en: But you are to take your holy things and your vow offerings and go to the place the LORD will choose.
chapters.zh: 只是你分别为圣的物和你的还愿祭要奉到耶和华所选择的地方去。

chapters.en: Present the meat and blood of your burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD your God. The blood of your other sacrifices must be poured out beside the altar of the LORD your God, but you may eat the meat.
chapters.zh: 你的燔祭，连肉带血，都要献在耶和华－你上帝的坛上。〔平安〕祭的血要倒在耶和华－你上帝的坛上；〔平安〕祭的肉，你自己可以吃。

chapters.en: Be careful to obey all these things I command you, so that it may always go well with you and your children after you, because you will be doing what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 你要谨守听从我所吩咐的一切话，行耶和华－你上帝眼中看为善，看为正的事。这样，你和你的子孙就可以永远享福。」

chapters.en: When the LORD your God cuts off before you the nations you are entering to dispossess, and you drive them out and live in their land,
chapters.zh: 「耶和华－你上帝将你要去赶出的国民从你面前剪除，你得了他们的地居住，

chapters.en: be careful not to be ensnared by their ways after they have been destroyed before you. Do not inquire about their gods, asking, “How do these nations serve their gods? I will do likewise.”
chapters.zh: 那时就要谨慎，不可在他们除灭之后随从他们〔的恶〕俗，陷入网罗，也不可访问他们的神说：『这些国民怎样事奉他们的神，我也要照样行。』

chapters.en: You must not worship the LORD your God in this way, because they practice for their gods every abomination which the LORD hates. They even burn their sons and daughters in the fire as sacrifices to their gods.
chapters.zh: 你不可向耶和华－你的上帝这样行，因为他们向他们的神行了耶和华所憎嫌所恨恶的一切事，甚至将自己的儿女用火焚烧，献与他们的神。

chapters.en: See that you do everything I command you; do not add to it or subtract from it.
chapters.zh: 凡我所吩咐的，你们都要谨守遵行，不可加添，也不可删减。

chapters.en: If a prophet or dreamer of dreams arises among you and proclaims a sign or wonder to you,
chapters.zh: 「你们中间若有先知或是做梦的起来，向你显个神迹奇事，

chapters.en: and if the sign or wonder he has spoken to you comes about, but he says, “Let us follow other gods (which you have not known) and let us worship them,”
chapters.zh: 对你说：『我们去随从你素来所不认识的别神，事奉它吧。』他所显的神迹奇事虽有应验，

chapters.en: you must not listen to the words of that prophet or dreamer. For the LORD your God is testing you to find out whether you love Him with all your heart and with all your soul.
chapters.zh: 你也不可听那先知或是那做梦之人的话；因为这是耶和华－你们的上帝试验你们，要知道你们是尽心尽性爱耶和华－你们的上帝不是。

chapters.en: You are to follow the LORD your God and fear Him. Keep His commandments and listen to His voice; serve Him and hold fast to Him.
chapters.zh: 你们要顺从耶和华－你们的上帝，敬畏他，谨守他的诫命，听从他的话，事奉他，专靠他。

chapters.en: Such a prophet or dreamer must be put to death, because he has advocated rebellion against the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery; he has tried to turn you from the way in which the LORD your God has commanded you to walk. So you must purge the evil from among you.
chapters.zh: 那先知或是那做梦的既用言语叛逆那领你们出埃及地、救赎你脱离为奴之家的耶和华－你们的上帝，要勾引你离开耶和华－你上帝所吩咐你行的道，你便要将他治死。这样，就把那恶从你们中间除掉。

chapters.en: If your very own brother, or your son or daughter, or the wife you embrace, or your closest friend secretly entices you, saying, “Let us go and worship other gods” (which neither you nor your fathers have known,
chapters.zh: 「你的同胞弟兄，或是你的儿女，或是你怀中的妻，或是如同你性命的朋友，若暗中引诱你，说：『我们不如去事奉你和你列祖素来所不认识的别神－

chapters.en: the gods of the peoples around you, whether near or far, whether from one end of the earth or the other),
chapters.zh: 是你四围列国的神。』无论是离你近，离你远，从地这边到地那边的神，

chapters.en: you must not yield to him or listen to him. Show him no pity, and do not spare him or shield him.
chapters.zh: 你不可依从他，也不可听从他，眼不可顾惜他。你不可怜恤他，也不可遮庇他，

chapters.en: Instead, you must surely kill him. Your hand must be the first against him to put him to death, and then the hands of all the people.
chapters.zh: 总要杀他；你先下手，然后众民也下手，将他治死。

chapters.en: Stone him to death for trying to turn you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
chapters.zh: 要用石头打死他，因为他想要勾引你离开那领你出埃及地为奴之家的耶和华－你的上帝。

chapters.en: Then all Israel will hear and be afraid, and will never again do such a wicked thing among you.
chapters.zh: 以色列众人都要听见害怕，就不敢在你们中间再行这样的恶了。

chapters.en: If, regarding one of the cities the LORD your God is giving you to inhabit, you hear it said
that wicked men have arisen from among you and have led the people of their city astray, saying, “Let us go and serve other gods” (which you have not known),
chapters.zh: 「在耶和华－你上帝所赐你居住的各城中，你若听人说，有些匪类从你们中间的一座城出来勾引本城的居民，说：『我们不如去事奉你们素来所不认识的别神』；

chapters.en: then you must inquire, investigate, and interrogate thoroughly. And if it is established with certainty that this abomination has been committed among you,
chapters.zh: 你就要探听，查究，细细地访问，果然是真，准有这可憎恶的事行在你们中间，

chapters.en: you must surely put the inhabitants of that city to the sword. Devote to destruction all its people and livestock.
chapters.zh: 你必要用刀杀那城里的居民，把城里所有的，连牲畜，都用刀杀尽。

chapters.en: And you are to gather all its plunder in the middle of the public square, and completely burn the city and all its plunder as a whole burnt offering to the LORD your God. The city must remain a mound of ruins forever, never to be rebuilt.
chapters.zh: 你从那城里所夺的财物都要堆积在街市上，用火将城和其内所夺的财物都在耶和华－你上帝面前烧尽；那城就永为荒堆，不可再建造。

chapters.en: Nothing devoted to destruction shall cling to your hands, so that the LORD will turn from His fierce anger, grant you mercy, show you compassion, and multiply you as He swore to your fathers,
because you obey the LORD your God, keeping all His commandments I am giving you today and doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 那当毁灭的物连一点都不可粘你的手。你要听从耶和华－你上帝的话，遵守我今日所吩咐你的一切诫命，行耶和华－你上帝眼中看为正的事，耶和华就必转意，不发烈怒，恩待你，怜恤你，照他向你列祖所起的誓使你人数增多。」

chapters.en: You are sons of the LORD your God; do not cut yourselves or shave your foreheads on behalf of the dead,
chapters.zh: 「你们是耶和华－你们上帝的儿女。不可为死人用刀划身，也不可将额上剃光；

chapters.en: for you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD has chosen you to be a people for His prized possession out of all the peoples on the face of the earth.
chapters.zh: 因为你归耶和华－你上帝为圣洁的民，耶和华从地上的万民中拣选你特作自己的子民。」

chapters.en: You must not eat any detestable thing.
chapters.zh: 「凡可憎的物都不可吃。

chapters.en:
These are the animals that you may eat:
The ox, the sheep, the goat,
chapters.zh: 可吃的牲畜就是牛、绵羊、山羊、

chapters.en:
the deer, the gazelle, the roe deer,
the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope,
and the mountain sheep.
chapters.zh: 鹿、羚羊、誁子、野山羊、麋鹿、黄羊、青羊。

chapters.en: You may eat any animal that has a split hoof divided in two and that chews the cud.
chapters.zh: 凡分蹄成为两瓣又倒嚼的走兽，你们都可以吃。

chapters.en:
But of those that chew the cud or have a completely divided hoof, you are not to eat the following:
the camel,
the rabbit,
or the rock badger.
Although they chew the cud, they do not have a divided hoof. They are unclean for you,
chapters.zh: 但那些倒嚼或是分蹄之中不可吃的乃是骆驼、觠子、沙番－因为是倒嚼不分蹄，就与你们不洁净；

chapters.en: as well as the pig; though it has a divided hoof, it does not chew the cud. It is unclean for you. You must not eat its meat or touch its carcass.
chapters.zh: 猪－因为是分蹄却不倒嚼，就与你们不洁净。这些兽的肉，你们不可吃，死的也不可摸。

chapters.en: Of all the creatures that live in the water, you may eat anything with fins and scales,
chapters.zh: 「水中可吃的乃是这些：凡有翅有鳞的都可以吃；

chapters.en: but you may not eat anything that does not have fins and scales; it is unclean for you.
chapters.zh: 凡无翅无鳞的都不可吃，是与你们不洁净。

chapters.en: You may eat any clean bird,
chapters.zh: 「凡洁净的鸟，你们都可以吃。

chapters.en:
but these you may not eat:
the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
chapters.zh: 不可吃的乃是鵰、狗头鵰、红头鵰、

chapters.en: the red kite, the falcon, any kind of kite,
chapters.zh: 鹯、小鹰、鹞鹰与其类，

chapters.en: any kind of raven,
chapters.zh: 乌鸦与其类，

chapters.en: the ostrich, the screech owl, the gull, any kind of hawk,
chapters.zh: 鸵鸟、夜鹰、鱼鹰、鹰与其类，

chapters.en: the little owl, the great owl, the white owl,
chapters.zh: 鸮鸟、猫头鹰、角鸱、

chapters.en: the desert owl, the osprey, the cormorant,
chapters.zh: 鹈鹕、秃鵰、鸬鹚、

chapters.en:
the stork, any kind of heron,
the hoopoe, or the bat.
chapters.zh: 鹳、鹭鸶与其类，戴鵀与蝙蝠。

chapters.en: All flying insects are unclean for you; they may not be eaten.
chapters.zh: 凡有翅膀爬行的物是与你们不洁净，都不可吃。

chapters.en: But you may eat any clean bird.
chapters.zh: 凡洁净的鸟，你们都可以吃。

chapters.en:
You are not to eat any carcass; you may give it to the foreigner residing within your gates, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner. For you are a holy people belonging to the LORD your God.
You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.
chapters.zh: 「凡自死的，你们都不可吃，可以给你城里寄居的吃，或卖与外人吃，因为你是归耶和华－你上帝为圣洁的民。 「不可用山羊羔母的奶煮山羊羔。」

chapters.en: You must be sure to set aside a tenth of all the produce brought forth each year from your fields.
chapters.zh: 「你要把你撒种所产的，就是你田地每年所出的，十分取一分；

chapters.en: And you are to eat a tenth of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks, in the presence of the LORD your God at the place He will choose as a dwelling for His Name, so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God always.
chapters.zh: 又要把你的五谷、新酒、和油的十分之一，并牛群羊群中头生的，吃在耶和华－你上帝面前，就是他所选择要立为他名的居所。这样，你可以学习时常敬畏耶和华－你的上帝。

chapters.en: But if the distance is too great for you to carry that with which the LORD your God has blessed you, because the place where the LORD your God will choose to put His Name is too far away,
chapters.zh: 当耶和华－你上帝赐福与你的时候，耶和华－你上帝所选择要立为他名的地方若离你太远，那路也太长，使你不能把这物带到那里去，

chapters.en: then exchange it for money, take the money in your hand, and go to the place the LORD your God will choose.
chapters.zh: 你就可以换成银子，将银子包起来，拿在手中，往耶和华－你上帝所要选择的地方去。

chapters.en: Then you may spend the money on anything you desire: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink, or anything you wish. You are to feast there in the presence of the LORD your God and rejoice with your household.
chapters.zh: 你用这银子，随心所欲，或买牛羊，或买清酒浓酒，凡你心所想的都可以买；你和你的家属在耶和华－你上帝的面前吃喝快乐。

chapters.en: And do not neglect the Levite within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.
chapters.zh: 「住在你城里的利未人，你不可丢弃他，因为他在你们中间无分无业。

chapters.en: At the end of every three years, bring a tenth of all your produce for that year and lay it up within your gates.
chapters.zh: 每逢三年的末一年，你要将本年的土产十分之一都取出来，积存在你的城中。

chapters.en: Then the Levite (because he has no portion or inheritance among you), the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow within your gates may come and eat and be satisfied. And the LORD your God will bless you in all the work of your hands.
chapters.zh: 在你城里无分无业的利未人，和你城里寄居的，并孤儿寡妇，都可以来，吃得饱足。这样，耶和华－你的上帝必在你手里所办的一切事上赐福与你。」

chapters.en: At the end of every seven years you must cancel debts.
chapters.zh: 「每逢七年末一年，你要施行豁免。

chapters.en: This is the manner of remission: Every creditor shall cancel what he has loaned to his neighbor. He is not to collect anything from his neighbor or brother, because the LORD’s time of release has been proclaimed.
chapters.zh: 豁免的定例乃是这样：凡债主要把所借给邻舍的豁免了；不可向邻舍和弟兄追讨，因为耶和华的豁免〔年〕已经宣告了。

chapters.en: You may collect something from a foreigner, but you must forgive whatever your brother owes you.
chapters.zh: 若借给外邦人，你可以向他追讨；但借给你弟兄，无论是什么，你要松手豁免了。

chapters.en: There will be no poor among you, however, because the LORD will surely bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess as an inheritance,
if only you obey the LORD your God and are careful to follow all these commandments I am giving you today.
chapters.zh: 你若留意听从耶和华－你上帝的话，谨守遵行我今日所吩咐你这一切的命令，就必在你们中间没有穷人了（在耶和华－你上帝所赐你为业的地上，耶和华必大大赐福与你。）

chapters.en: When the LORD your God blesses you as He has promised, you will lend to many nations but borrow from none; you will rule over many nations but be ruled by none.
chapters.zh: 因为耶和华－你的上帝必照他所应许你的赐福与你。你必借给许多国民，却不致向〔他们〕借贷；你必管辖许多国民，他们却不能管辖你。

chapters.en: If there is a poor man among your brothers within any of the gates in the land that the LORD your God is giving you, then you are not to harden your heart or shut your hand from your poor brother.
chapters.zh: 「在耶和华－你上帝所赐你的地上，无论哪一座城里，你弟兄中若有一个穷人，你不可忍着心、揝着手不帮补你穷乏的弟兄。

chapters.en: Instead, you are to open your hand to him and freely loan him whatever he needs.
chapters.zh: 总要向他松开手，照他所缺乏的借给他，补他的不足。

chapters.en: Be careful not to harbor this wicked thought in your heart: “The seventh year, the year of release, is near,” so that you look upon your poor brother begrudgingly and give him nothing. He will cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
chapters.zh: 你要谨慎，不可心里起恶念，说：『第七年的豁免年快到了』，你便恶眼看你穷乏的弟兄，什么都不给他，以致他因你求告耶和华，罪便归于你了。

chapters.en: Give generously to him, and do not let your heart be grieved when you do so. And because of this the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything to which you put your hand.
chapters.zh: 你总要给他，给他的时候心里不可愁烦；因耶和华－你的上帝必在你这一切所行的，并你手里所办的事上，赐福与你。

chapters.en: For there will never cease to be poor in the land; that is why I am commanding you to open wide your hand to your brother and to the poor and needy in your land.
chapters.zh: 原来那地上的穷人永不断绝；所以我吩咐你说：『总要向你地上困苦穷乏的弟兄松开手。』」

chapters.en: If a fellow Hebrew, a man or a woman, is sold to you and serves you six years, then in the seventh year you must set him free.
chapters.zh: 「你弟兄中，若有一个希伯来男人或希伯来女人被卖给你，服事你六年，到第七年就要任他自由出去。

chapters.en: And when you release him, do not send him away empty-handed.
chapters.zh: 你任他自由的时候，不可使他空手而去，

chapters.en: You are to furnish him liberally from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. You shall give to him as the LORD your God has blessed you.
chapters.zh: 要从你羊群、禾场、酒醡之中多多地给他；耶和华－你的上帝怎样赐福与你，你也要照样给他。

chapters.en: Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you; that is why I am giving you this command today.
chapters.zh: 要记念你在埃及地作过奴仆，耶和华－你的上帝将你救赎；因此，我今日吩咐你这件事。

chapters.en: But if your servant says to you, ‘I do not want to leave you,’ because he loves you and your household and is well off with you,
chapters.zh: 他若对你说：『我不愿意离开你』，是因他爱你和你的家，且因在你那里很好，

chapters.en: then take an awl and pierce it through his ear into the door, and he will become your servant for life. And treat your maidservant the same way.
chapters.zh: 你就要拿锥子将他的耳朵在门上刺透，他便永为你的奴仆了。你待婢女也要这样。

chapters.en: Do not regard it as a hardship to set your servant free, because his six years of service were worth twice the wages of a hired hand. And the LORD your God will bless you in all you do.
chapters.zh: 你任他自由的时候，不可以为难事，因他服事你六年，较比雇工的工价多加一倍了。耶和华－你的上帝就必在你所做的一切事上赐福与你。」

chapters.en: You must set apart to the LORD your God every firstborn male produced by your herds and flocks. You are not to put the firstborn of your oxen to work, nor are you to shear the firstborn of your flock.
chapters.zh: 「你牛群羊群中头生的，凡是公的，都要分别为圣，归耶和华－你的上帝。牛群中头生的，不可用牠耕地；羊群中头生的，不可剪毛。

chapters.en: Each year you and your household are to eat it before the LORD your God in the place the LORD will choose.
chapters.zh: 这头生的，你和你的家属，每年要在耶和华所选择的地方，在耶和华－你上帝面前吃。

chapters.en: But if an animal has a defect, is lame or blind, or has any serious flaw, you must not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 这头生的若有什么残疾，〔就如〕瘸腿的、瞎眼的，无论有什么恶残疾，都不可献给耶和华－你的上帝；

chapters.en: Eat it within your gates; both the ceremonially unclean and clean may eat it as they would a gazelle or a deer.
chapters.zh: 可以在你城里吃；洁净人与不洁净人都〔可以吃〕，就如吃羚羊与鹿一般。

chapters.en: But you must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.
chapters.zh: 只是不可吃牠的血；要倒在地上，如同倒水一样。」

chapters.en: Observe the month of Abib and celebrate the Passover to the LORD your God, because in the month of Abib the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
chapters.zh: 「你要注意亚笔月，向耶和华－你的上帝守逾越节，因为耶和华－你的上帝在亚笔月夜间领你出埃及。

chapters.en: You are to offer to the LORD your God the Passover sacrifice from the herd or flock in the place the LORD will choose as a dwelling for His Name.
chapters.zh: 你当在耶和华所选择要立为他名的居所，从牛群羊群中，将逾越〔节的祭牲〕献给耶和华－你的上帝。

chapters.en: You must not eat leavened bread with it; for seven days you are to eat with it unleavened bread, the bread of affliction, because you left the land of Egypt in haste—so that you may remember for the rest of your life the day you left the land of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 你吃〔这祭牲〕，不可吃有酵的饼；七日之内要吃无酵饼，就是困苦饼－你本是急忙出了埃及地－要叫你一生一世记念你从埃及地出来的日子。

chapters.en: No leaven is to be found in all your land for seven days, and none of the meat you sacrifice in the evening of the first day shall remain until morning.
chapters.zh: 在你四境之内，七日不可见面酵，头一日晚上所献的肉，一点不可留到早晨。

chapters.en: You are not to sacrifice the Passover animal in any of the towns that the LORD your God is giving you.
chapters.zh: 在耶和华－你上帝所赐的各城中，你不可献逾越〔节的祭〕；

chapters.en: You must only offer the Passover sacrifice at the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for His Name. Do this in the evening as the sun sets, at the same time you departed from Egypt.
chapters.zh: 只当在耶和华－你上帝所选择要立为他名的居所，晚上日落的时候，乃是你出埃及的时候，献逾越〔节的祭〕。

chapters.en: And you shall roast it and eat it in the place the LORD your God will choose, and in the morning you shall return to your tents.
chapters.zh: 当在耶和华－你上帝所选择的地方把肉烤了吃〔注：烤：或译煮〕，次日早晨就回到你的帐棚去。

chapters.en: For six days you must eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day you shall hold a solemn assembly to the LORD your God, and you must not do any work.
chapters.zh: 你要吃无酵饼六日，第七日要向耶和华－你的上帝守严肃会，不可做工。」

chapters.en: You are to count off seven weeks from the time you first put the sickle to the standing grain.
chapters.zh: 「你要计算七七日：从你开镰收割禾稼时算起，共计七七日。

chapters.en: And you shall celebrate the Feast of Weeks to the LORD your God with a freewill offering that you give in proportion to how the LORD your God has blessed you,
chapters.zh: 你要照耶和华－你上帝所赐你的福，手里拿着甘心祭，献在耶和华－你的上帝面前，守七七节。

chapters.en: and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God in the place He will choose as a dwelling for His Name—you, your sons and daughters, your menservants and maidservants, and the Levite within your gates, as well as the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widows among you.
chapters.zh: 你和你儿女、仆婢，并住在你城里的利未人，以及在你们中间寄居的与孤儿寡妇，都要在耶和华－你上帝所选择立为他名的居所，在耶和华－你的上帝面前欢乐。

chapters.en: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and carefully follow these statutes.
chapters.zh: 你也要记念你在埃及作过奴仆。你要谨守遵行这些律例。」

chapters.en: You are to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days after you have gathered the produce of your threshing floor and your winepress.
chapters.zh: 「你把禾场的〔谷〕、酒醡的〔酒〕收藏以后，就要守住棚节七日。

chapters.en: And you shall rejoice in your feast—you, your sons and daughters, your menservants and maidservants, and the Levite, as well as the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widows among you.
chapters.zh: 守节的时候，你和你儿女、仆婢，并住在你城里的利未人，以及寄居的与孤儿寡妇，都要欢乐。

chapters.en: For seven days you shall celebrate a feast to the LORD your God in the place He will choose, because the LORD your God will bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, so that your joy will be complete.
chapters.zh: 在耶和华所选择的地方，你当向耶和华－你的上帝守节七日；因为耶和华－你上帝在你一切的土产上和你手里所办的事上要赐福与你，你就非常地欢乐。

chapters.en: Three times a year all your men are to appear before the LORD your God in the place He will choose: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles. No one should appear before the LORD empty-handed.
chapters.zh: 你一切的男丁要在除酵节、七七节、住棚节，一年三次，在耶和华－你上帝所选择的地方朝见他，却不可空手朝见。

chapters.en: Everyone must appear with a gift as he is able, according to the blessing the LORD your God has given you.
chapters.zh: 各人要按自己的力量，照耶和华－你上帝所赐的福分，奉献礼物。」

chapters.en: You are to appoint judges and officials for your tribes in every town that the LORD your God is giving you. They are to judge the people with righteous judgment.
chapters.zh: 「你要在耶和华－你上帝所赐的各城里，按着各支派设立审判官和官长。他们必按公义的审判判断百姓。

chapters.en: Do not deny justice or show partiality. Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
chapters.zh: 不可屈枉正直；不可看人的外貌。也不可受贿赂；因为贿赂能叫智慧人的眼变瞎了，又能颠倒义人的话。

chapters.en: Pursue justice, and justice alone, so that you may live, and you may possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
chapters.zh: 你要追求至公至义，好叫你存活，承受耶和华－你上帝所赐你的地。

chapters.en: Do not set up any wooden Asherah pole next to the altar you will build for the LORD your God,
chapters.zh: 「你为耶和华－你的上帝筑坛，不可在坛旁栽什么树木作为木偶。

chapters.en: and do not set up for yourselves a sacred pillar, which the LORD your God hates.
chapters.zh: 也不可为自己设立柱像；这是耶和华－你上帝所恨恶的。

chapters.en: You shall not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep with any defect or serious flaw, for that is detestable to the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 「凡有残疾，或有什么恶病的牛羊，你都不可献给耶和华－你的上帝，因为这是耶和华－你上帝所憎恶的。

chapters.en: If a man or woman among you in one of the towns that the LORD your God gives you is found doing evil in the sight of the LORD your God by transgressing His covenant
chapters.zh: 「在你们中间，在耶和华－你上帝所赐你的诸城中，无论哪座城里，若有人，或男或女，行耶和华－你上帝眼中看为恶的事，违背了他的约，

chapters.en: and going to worship other gods, bowing down to them or to the sun or moon or any of the host of heaven—which I have forbidden—
chapters.zh: 去事奉敬拜别神，或拜日头，或拜月亮，或拜天象，是主不曾吩咐的；

chapters.en:
and if it is reported and you hear about it, you must investigate it thoroughly.
If the report is true and such an abomination has happened in Israel,
chapters.zh: 有人告诉你，你也听见了，就要细细地探听，果然是真，准有这可憎恶的事行在以色列中，

chapters.en: you must bring out to your gates the man or woman who has done this evil thing, and you must stone that person to death.
chapters.zh: 你就要将行这恶事的男人或女人拉到城门〔外〕，用石头将他打死。

chapters.en: On the testimony of two or three witnesses a man shall be put to death, but he shall not be executed on the testimony of a lone witness.
chapters.zh: 要凭两三个人的口作见证将那当死的人治死；不可凭一个人的口作见证将他治死。

chapters.en: The hands of the witnesses shall be the first in putting him to death, and after that, the hands of all the people. So you must purge the evil from among you.
chapters.zh: 见证人要先下手，然后众民也下手将他治死。这样，就把那恶从你们中间除掉。

chapters.en: If a case is too difficult for you to judge, whether the controversy within your gates is regarding bloodshed, lawsuits, or assaults, you must go up to the place the LORD your God will choose.
chapters.zh: 「你城中若起了争讼的事，或因流血，或因争竞，或因殴打，是你难断的案件，你就当起来，往耶和华－你上帝所选择的地方

chapters.en: You are to go to the Levitical priests and to the judge who presides at that time. Inquire of them, and they will give you a verdict in the case.
chapters.zh: 去见祭司利未人，并当时的审判官，求问他们，他们必将判语指示你。

chapters.en: You must abide by the verdict they give you at the place the LORD will choose. Be careful to do everything they instruct you,
chapters.zh: 他们在耶和华所选择的地方指示你的判语，你必照着他们所指教你的一切话谨守遵行。

chapters.en: according to the terms of law they give and the verdict they proclaim. Do not turn aside to the right or to the left from the decision they declare to you.
chapters.zh: 要按他们所指教你的律法，照他们所断定的去行；他们所指示你的判语，你不可偏离左右。

chapters.en: But the man who acts presumptuously, refusing to listen either to the priest who stands there to serve the LORD your God, or to the judge, must be put to death. You must purge the evil from Israel.
chapters.zh: 若有人擅敢不听从那侍立在耶和华－你上帝面前的祭司，或不听从审判官，那人就必治死；这样，便将那恶从以色列中除掉。

chapters.en: Then all the people will hear and be afraid, and will no longer behave arrogantly.
chapters.zh: 众百姓都要听见害怕，不再擅敢行事。」

chapters.en: When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you and have taken possession of it and settled in it, and you say, “Let us set a king over us like all the nations around us,”
chapters.zh: 「到了耶和华－你上帝所赐你的地，得了那地居住的时候，若说：『我要立王治理我，像四围的国一样。』

chapters.en: you are to appoint over yourselves the king whom the LORD your God shall choose. Appoint a king from among your brothers; you are not to set over yourselves a foreigner who is not one of your brothers.
chapters.zh: 你总要立耶和华－你上帝所拣选的人为王。必从你弟兄中立一人；不可立你弟兄以外的人为王。

chapters.en: But the king must not acquire many horses for himself or send the people back to Egypt to acquire more horses, for the LORD has said, ‘You are never to go back that way again.’
chapters.zh: 只是王不可为自己加添马匹，也不可使百姓回埃及去，为要加添他的马匹，因耶和华曾吩咐你们说：『不可再回那条路去。』

chapters.en: He must not take many wives for himself, lest his heart go astray. He must not accumulate for himself large amounts of silver and gold.
chapters.zh: 他也不可为自己多立妃嫔，恐怕他的心偏邪；也不可为自己多积金银。

chapters.en: When he is seated on his royal throne, he must write for himself a copy of this instruction on a scroll in the presence of the Levitical priests.
chapters.zh: 他登了国位，就要将祭司利未人面前的这律法〔书〕，为自己抄录一本，

chapters.en: It is to remain with him, and he is to read from it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God by carefully observing all the words of this instruction and these statutes.
chapters.zh: 存在他那里，要平生诵读，好学习敬畏耶和华－他的上帝，谨守遵行这律法〔书〕上的一切言语和这些律例，

chapters.en: Then his heart will not be exalted above his countrymen, and he will not turn aside from the commandment, to the right or to the left, in order that he and his sons may reign many years over his kingdom in Israel.
chapters.zh: 免得他向弟兄心高气傲，偏左偏右，离了这诫命。这样，他和他的子孙便可在以色列中，在国位上年长日久。」

chapters.en: The Levitical priests—indeed the whole tribe of Levi—shall have no portion or inheritance with Israel. They are to eat the food offerings to the LORD; that is their inheritance.
chapters.zh: 「祭司利未人和利未全支派必在以色列中无分无业；他们所吃用的就是献给耶和华的火祭和一切所捐的。

chapters.en: Although they have no inheritance among their brothers, the LORD is their inheritance, as He promised them.
chapters.zh: 他们在弟兄中必没有产业；耶和华是他们的产业，正如耶和华所应许他们的。

chapters.en: This shall be the priests’ share from the people who offer a sacrifice, whether a bull or a sheep: the priests are to be given the shoulder, the jowls, and the stomach.
chapters.zh: 祭司从百姓所当得的分乃是这样：凡献牛或羊为祭的，要把前腿和两腮并脾胃给祭司。

chapters.en: You are to give them the firstfruits of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the first wool sheared from your flock.
chapters.zh: 初收的五谷、新酒和油，并初剪的羊毛，也要给他；

chapters.en: For the LORD your God has chosen Levi and his sons out of all your tribes to stand and minister in His name for all time.
chapters.zh: 因为耶和华－你的上帝从你各支派中将他拣选出来，使他和他子孙永远奉耶和华的名侍立，事奉。

chapters.en: Now if a Levite moves from any town of residence throughout Israel and comes in all earnestness to the place the LORD will choose,
chapters.zh: 「利未人无论寄居在以色列中的哪一座城，若从那里出来，一心愿意到耶和华所选择的地方，

chapters.en: then he shall serve in the name of the LORD his God like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 就要奉耶和华－他上帝的名事奉，像他众弟兄利未人侍立在耶和华面前事奉一样。

chapters.en: They shall eat equal portions, even though he has received money from the sale of his father’s estate.
chapters.zh: 除了他卖祖父产业所得的以外，还要得一分祭物与他们同吃。」

chapters.en: When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, do not imitate the detestable ways of the nations there.
chapters.zh: 「你到了耶和华－你上帝所赐之地，那些国民所行可憎恶的事，你不可学着行。

chapters.en: Let no one be found among you who sacrifices his son or daughter in the fire, practices divination or conjury, interprets omens, practices sorcery,
chapters.zh: 你们中间不可有人使儿女经火，也不可有占卜的、观兆的、用法术的、行邪术的、

chapters.en: casts spells, consults a medium or spiritist, or inquires of the dead.
chapters.zh: 用迷术的、交鬼的、行巫术的、过阴的。

chapters.en: For whoever does these things is detestable to the LORD. And because of these detestable things, the LORD your God is driving out the nations before you.
chapters.zh: 凡行这些事的都为耶和华所憎恶；因那些国民行这可憎恶的事，所以耶和华－你的上帝将他们从你面前赶出。

chapters.en: You must be blameless before the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 你要在耶和华－你的上帝面前作完全人。」

chapters.en: Though these nations, which you will dispossess, listen to conjurers and diviners, the LORD your God has not permitted you to do so.
chapters.zh: 「因你所要赶出的那些国民都听信观兆的和占卜的，至于你，耶和华－你的上帝从来不许你这样行。

chapters.en: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You must listen to him.
chapters.zh: 耶和华－你的上帝要从你们弟兄中间给你兴起一位先知，像我，你们要听从他。

chapters.en: This is what you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, “Let us not hear the voice of the LORD our God or see this great fire anymore, so that we will not die!”
chapters.zh: 正如你在何烈山大会的日子求耶和华－你上帝一切的话，说：『求你不再叫我听见耶和华－我上帝的声音，也不再叫我看见这大火，免得我死亡。』

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to me, “They have spoken well.
chapters.zh: 耶和华就对我说：『他们所说的是。

chapters.en: I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers. I will put My words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him.
chapters.zh: 我必在他们弟兄中间给他们兴起一位先知，像你。我要将当说的话传给他；他要将我一切所吩咐的都传给他们。

chapters.en: And I will hold accountable anyone who does not listen to My words that the prophet speaks in My name.
chapters.zh: 谁不听他奉我名所说的话，我必讨谁的罪。

chapters.en: But if any prophet dares to speak a message in My name that I have not commanded him to speak, or to speak in the name of other gods, that prophet must be put to death.”
chapters.zh: 若有先知擅敢讬我的名说我所未曾吩咐他说的话，或是奉别神的名说话，那先知就必治死。』

chapters.en: You may ask in your heart, “How can we recognize a message that the LORD has not spoken?”
chapters.zh: 你心里若说：『耶和华所未曾吩咐的话，我们怎能知道呢？』

chapters.en: When a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the message does not come to pass or come true, that is a message the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken presumptuously. Do not be afraid of him.
chapters.zh: 先知讬耶和华的名说话，所说的若不成就，也无效验，这就是耶和华所未曾吩咐的，是那先知擅自说的，你不要怕他。」

chapters.en: When the LORD your God has cut off the nations whose land He is giving you, and when you have driven them out and settled in their cities and houses,
chapters.zh: 「耶和华－你上帝将列国之民剪除的时候，耶和华－你上帝也将他们的地赐给你，你接着住他们的城邑并他们的房屋，

chapters.en: then you are to set apart for yourselves three cities within the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
chapters.zh: 就要在耶和华－你上帝所赐你为业的地上分定三座城。

chapters.en: You are to build roads for yourselves and divide into three regions the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, so that any manslayer can flee to these cities.
chapters.zh: 要将耶和华－你上帝使你承受为业的地分为三段；又要预备道路，使误杀人的，都可以逃到那里去。

chapters.en: Now this is the situation regarding the manslayer who flees to one of these cities to save his life, having killed his neighbor accidentally, without intending to harm him:
chapters.zh: 「误杀人的逃到那里可以存活，定例乃是这样：凡素无仇恨，无心杀了人的，

chapters.en: If he goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut timber and swings his axe to chop down a tree, but the blade flies off the handle and strikes and kills his neighbor, he may flee to one of these cities to save his life.
chapters.zh: 就如人与邻舍同入树林砍伐树木，手拿斧子一砍，本想砍下树木，不料，斧头脱了把，飞落在邻舍身上，以致于死，这人逃到那些城的一座城，就可以存活，

chapters.en: Otherwise, the avenger of blood might pursue the manslayer in a rage, overtake him if the distance is great, and strike him dead though he did not deserve to die, since he did not intend any harm.
chapters.zh: 免得报血仇的，心中火热追赶他，因路远就追上，将他杀死；其实他不该死，因为他与被杀的素无仇恨。

chapters.en: This is why I am commanding you to set apart for yourselves three cities.
chapters.zh: 所以我吩咐你说，要分定三座城。

chapters.en: And if the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as He swore to your fathers, and gives you all the land He promised them,
chapters.zh: 耶和华－你上帝若照他向你列祖所起的誓扩张你的境界，将所应许赐你列祖的地全然给你，

chapters.en: and if you carefully keep all these commandments I am giving you today, loving the LORD your God and walking in His ways at all times, then you are to add three more cities to these three.
chapters.zh: 你若谨守遵行我今日所吩咐的这一切诫命，爱耶和华－你的上帝，常常遵行他的道，就要在这三座城之外，再添三座城，

chapters.en: Thus innocent blood will not be shed in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, so that you will not be guilty of bloodshed.
chapters.zh: 免得无辜之人的血流在耶和华－你上帝所赐你为业的地上，流血的罪就归于你。

chapters.en: If, however, a man hates his neighbor and lies in wait, attacks him and kills him, and then flees to one of these cities,
chapters.zh: 「若有人恨他的邻舍，埋伏着起来击杀他，以致于死，便逃到这些城的一座城，

chapters.en: the elders of his city must send for him, bring him back, and hand him over to the avenger of blood to die.
chapters.zh: 本城的长老就要打发人去，从那里带出他来，交在报血仇的手中，将他治死。

chapters.en: You must show him no pity. You are to purge from Israel the guilt of shedding innocent blood, that it may go well with you.
chapters.zh: 你眼不可顾惜他，却要从以色列中除掉流无辜血的罪，使你可以得福。」

chapters.en: You must not move your neighbor’s boundary marker, which was set up by your ancestors to mark the inheritance you shall receive in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
chapters.zh: 「在耶和华－你上帝所赐你承受为业之地，不可挪移你邻舍的地界，那是先人所定的。」

chapters.en: A lone witness is not sufficient to establish any wrongdoing or sin against a man, regardless of what offense he may have committed. A matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
chapters.zh: 「人无论犯什么罪，作什么恶，不可凭一个人的口作见证，总要凭两三个人的口作见证才可定案。

chapters.en: If a false witness testifies against someone, accusing him of a crime,
chapters.zh: 若有凶恶的见证人起来，见证某人作恶，

chapters.en: both parties to the dispute must stand in the presence of the LORD, before the priests and judges who are in office at that time.
chapters.zh: 这两个争讼的人就要站在耶和华面前，和当时的祭司，并审判官面前，

chapters.en: The judges shall investigate thoroughly, and if the witness is proven to be a liar who has falsely accused his brother,
chapters.zh: 审判官要细细地查究，若见证人果然是作假见证的，以假见证陷害弟兄，

chapters.en: you must do to him as he intended to do to his brother. So you must purge the evil from among you.
chapters.zh: 你们就要待他如同他想要待的弟兄。这样，就把那恶从你们中间除掉。

chapters.en: Then the rest of the people will hear and be afraid, and they will never again do anything so evil among you.
chapters.zh: 别人听见都要害怕，就不敢在你们中间再行这样的恶了。

chapters.en: You must show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, and foot for foot.
chapters.zh: 你眼不可顾惜，要以命偿命，以眼还眼，以牙还牙，以手还手，以脚还脚。」

chapters.en: When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses, chariots, and an army larger than yours, do not be afraid of them; for the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, is with you.
chapters.zh: 「你出去与仇敌争战的时候，看见马匹、车辆，并有比你多的人民，不要怕他们，因为领你出埃及地的耶和华－你上帝与你同在。

chapters.en: When you are about to go into battle, the priest is to come forward and address the army,
chapters.zh: 你们将要上阵的时候，祭司要到百姓面前宣告

chapters.en: saying to them, “Hear, O Israel, today you are going into battle with your enemies. Do not be fainthearted or afraid; do not be alarmed or terrified because of them.
chapters.zh: 说：『以色列人哪，你们当听，你们今日将要与仇敌争战，不要胆怯，不要惧怕战兢，也不要因他们惊恐；

chapters.en: For the LORD your God goes with you to fight for you against your enemies, to give you the victory.”
chapters.zh: 因为耶和华－你们的上帝与你们同去，要为你们与仇敌争战，拯救你们。』

chapters.en: Furthermore, the officers are to address the army, saying, “Has any man built a new house and not dedicated it? Let him return home, or he may die in battle and another man dedicate it.
chapters.zh: 官长也要对百姓宣告说：『谁建造房屋，尚未奉献，他可以回家去，恐怕他阵亡，别人去奉献。

chapters.en: Has any man planted a vineyard and not begun to enjoy its fruit? Let him return home, or he may die in battle and another man enjoy its fruit.
chapters.zh: 谁种葡萄园，尚未用所结的果子，他可以回家去，恐怕他阵亡，别人去用。

chapters.en: Has any man become pledged to a woman and not married her? Let him return home, or he may die in battle and another man marry her.”
chapters.zh: 谁聘定了妻，尚未迎娶，他可以回家去，恐怕他阵亡，别人去娶。』

chapters.en: Then the officers shall speak further to the army, saying, “Is any man afraid or fainthearted? Let him return home, so that the hearts of his brothers will not melt like his own.”
chapters.zh: 官长又要对百姓宣告说：『谁惧怕胆怯，他可以回家去，恐怕他弟兄的心消化，和他一样。』

chapters.en: When the officers have finished addressing the army, they are to appoint commanders to lead it.
chapters.zh: 官长对百姓宣告完了，就当派军长率领他们。

chapters.en: When you approach a city to fight against it, you are to make an offer of peace.
chapters.zh: 「你临近一座城、要攻打的时候，先要对城〔里的民〕宣告和睦的话。

chapters.en: If they accept your offer of peace and open their gates, all the people there will become forced laborers to serve you.
chapters.zh: 他们若以和睦的话回答你，给你开了城，城里所有的人都要给你效劳，服事你；

chapters.en: But if they refuse to make peace with you and wage war against you, lay siege to that city.
chapters.zh: 若不肯与你和好，反要与你打仗，你就要围困那城。

chapters.en: When the LORD your God has delivered it into your hand, you must put every male to the sword.
chapters.zh: 耶和华－你的上帝把城交付你手，你就要用刀杀尽这城的男丁。

chapters.en: But the women, children, livestock, and whatever else is in the city—all its spoil—you may take as plunder, and you shall use the spoil of your enemies that the LORD your God gives you.
chapters.zh: 惟有妇女、孩子、牲畜，和城内一切的财物，你可以取为自己的掠物。耶和华－你上帝把你仇敌的财物赐给你，你可以吃用。

chapters.en: This is how you are to treat all the cities that are far away from you and do not belong to the nations nearby.
chapters.zh: 离你甚远的各城，不是这些国民的城，你都要这样待他。

chapters.en: However, in the cities of the nations that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you must not leave alive anything that breathes.
chapters.zh: 但这些国民的城，耶和华－你上帝既赐你为业，其中凡有气息的，一个不可存留；

chapters.en: For you must devote them to complete destruction —the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—as the LORD your God has commanded you,
chapters.zh: 只要照耶和华－你上帝所吩咐的将这赫人、亚摩利人、迦南人、比利洗人、希未人、耶布斯人都灭绝净尽，

chapters.en: so that they cannot teach you to do all the detestable things they do for their gods, and so cause you to sin against the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 免得他们教导你们学习一切可憎恶的事，就是他们向自己神所行的，以致你们得罪耶和华－你们的上帝。

chapters.en: When you lay siege to a city for an extended time while fighting against it to capture it, you must not destroy its trees by putting an axe to them, because you can eat their fruit. You must not cut them down. Are the trees of the field human, that you should besiege them?
chapters.zh: 「你若许久围困、攻打所要取的一座城，就不可举斧子砍坏树木；因为你可以吃那树上的果子，不可砍伐。田间的树木岂是人，叫你糟蹋吗？

chapters.en: But you may destroy the trees that you know do not produce fruit. Use them to build siege works against the city that is waging war against you, until it falls.
chapters.zh: 惟独你所知道不是结果子的树木可以毁坏、砍伐，用以修筑营垒，攻击那与你打仗的城，直到攻塌了。」

chapters.en: If one is found slain, lying in a field in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess, and it is not known who killed him,
chapters.zh: 「在耶和华－你上帝所赐你为业的地上，若遇见被杀的人倒在田野，不知道是谁杀的，

chapters.en: your elders and judges must come out and measure the distance from the victim to the neighboring cities.
chapters.zh: 长老和审判官就要出去，从被杀的人那里量起，直量到四围的城邑，

chapters.en: Then the elders of the city nearest the victim shall take a heifer that has never been yoked or used for work,
chapters.zh: 看哪城离被杀的人最近，那城的长老就要从牛群中取一只未曾耕地、未曾负轭的母牛犊，

chapters.en: bring the heifer to a valley with running water that has not been plowed or sown, and break its neck there by the stream.
chapters.zh: 把母牛犊牵到流水、未曾耕种的山谷去，在谷中打折母牛犊的颈项。

chapters.en: And the priests, the sons of Levi, shall come forward, for the LORD your God has chosen them to serve Him and pronounce blessings in His name and to give a ruling in every dispute and case of assault.
chapters.zh: 祭司利未的子孙要近前来；因为耶和华－你的上帝拣选了他们事奉他，奉耶和华的名祝福，所有争讼殴打的事都要凭他们判断。

chapters.en: Then all the elders of the city nearest the victim shall wash their hands by the stream over the heifer whose neck has been broken,
chapters.zh: 那城的众长老，就是离被杀的人最近的，要在那山谷中，在所打折颈项的母牛犊以上洗手，

chapters.en: and they shall declare, “Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes see it.
chapters.zh: 祷告〔注：原文是回答〕说：『我们的手未曾流这〔人的〕血；我们的眼也未曾看见这事。

chapters.en:
Accept this atonement, O LORD, for Your people Israel whom You have redeemed, and do not hold the shedding of innocent blood against them.”
And the bloodshed will be atoned for.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你赦免你所救赎的以色列民，不要使流无辜血的罪归在你的百姓以色列中间。』这样，流血的罪必得赦免。

chapters.en: So you shall purge from among you the guilt of shedding innocent blood, since you have done what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你行耶和华眼中看为正的事，就可以从你们中间除掉流无辜血的罪。」

chapters.en: When you go to war against your enemies and the LORD your God delivers them into your hand and you take them captive,
chapters.zh: 「你出去与仇敌争战的时候，耶和华－你的上帝将他们交在你手中，你就掳了他们去。

chapters.en: if you see a beautiful woman among them, and you desire her and want to take her as your wife,
chapters.zh: 若在被掳的人中见有美貌的女子，恋慕她，要娶她为妻，

chapters.en: then you shall bring her into your house. She must shave her head, trim her nails,
chapters.zh: 就可以领她到你家里去；她便要剃头发，修指甲，

chapters.en:
and put aside the clothing of her captivity.
After she has lived in your house a full month and mourned her father and mother, you may have relations with her and be her husband, and she shall be your wife.
chapters.zh: 脱去被掳时所穿的衣服，住在你家里哀哭父母一个整月，然后可以与她同房。你作她的丈夫，她作你的妻子。

chapters.en: And if you are not pleased with her, you are to let her go wherever she wishes. But you must not sell her for money or treat her as a slave, since you have dishonored her.
chapters.zh: 后来你若不喜悦她，就要由她随意出去，决不可为钱卖她，也不可当婢女待她，因为你玷污了她。」

chapters.en: If a man has two wives, one beloved and the other unloved, and both bear him sons, but the unloved wife has the firstborn son,
chapters.zh: 「人若有二妻，一为所爱，一为所恶，所爱的、所恶的都给他生了儿子，但长子是所恶之妻生的。

chapters.en: when that man assigns his inheritance to his sons he must not appoint the son of the beloved wife as the firstborn over the son of the unloved wife.
chapters.zh: 到了把产业分给儿子承受的时候，不可将所爱之妻生的儿子立为长子，在所恶之妻生的儿子以上，

chapters.en: Instead, he must acknowledge the firstborn, the son of his unloved wife, by giving him a double portion of all that he has. For that son is the firstfruits of his father’s strength; the right of the firstborn belongs to him.
chapters.zh: 却要认所恶之妻生的儿子为长子，将产业多加一分给他；因这儿子是他力量强壮的时候生的，长子的名分本当归他。」

chapters.en: If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who does not obey his father and mother and does not listen to them when disciplined,
chapters.zh: 「人若有顽梗悖逆的儿子，不听从父母的话，他们虽惩治他，他仍不听从，

chapters.en: his father and mother are to lay hold of him and bring him to the elders of his city, to the gate of his hometown,
chapters.zh: 父母就要抓住他，将他带到本地的城门、本城的长老那里，

chapters.en: and say to the elders, “This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious; he does not obey us. He is a glutton and a drunkard.”
chapters.zh: 对长老说：『我们这儿子顽梗悖逆，不听从我们的话，是贪食好酒的人。』

chapters.en: Then all the men of his city will stone him to death. So you must purge the evil from among you, and all Israel will hear and be afraid.
chapters.zh: 本城的众人就要用石头将他打死。这样，就把那恶从你们中间除掉，以色列众人都要听见害怕。」

chapters.en: If a man has committed a sin worthy of death, and he is executed, and you hang his body on a tree,
chapters.zh: 「人若犯该死的罪，被治死了，你将他挂在木头上，

chapters.en: you must not leave the body on the tree overnight, but you must be sure to bury him that day, because anyone who is hung on a tree is under God’s curse. You must not defile the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
chapters.zh: 他的尸首不可留在木头上过夜，必要当日将他葬埋，免得玷污了耶和华－你上帝所赐你为业之地。因为被挂的人是在上帝面前受咒诅的。

chapters.en: If you see your brother’s ox or sheep straying, you must not ignore it; be sure to return it to your brother.
chapters.zh: 「你若看见弟兄的牛或羊失迷了路，不可佯为不见，总要把牠牵回来交给你的弟兄。

chapters.en: If your brother does not live near you, or if you do not know who he is, you are to take the animal home to remain with you until your brother comes seeking it; then you can return it to him.
chapters.zh: 你弟兄若离你远，或是你不认识他，就要牵到你家去，留在你那里，等你弟兄来寻找就还给他。

chapters.en: And you shall do the same for his donkey, his cloak, or anything your brother has lost and you have found. You must not ignore it.
chapters.zh: 你的弟兄无论失落什么，或是驴，或是衣服，你若遇见，都要这样行，不可佯为不见。

chapters.en: If you see your brother’s donkey or ox fallen on the road, you must not ignore it; you must help him lift it up.
chapters.zh: 你若看见弟兄的牛或驴跌倒在路上，不可佯为不见，总要帮助他拉起来。

chapters.en: A woman must not wear men’s clothing, and a man must not wear women’s clothing, for whoever does these things is detestable to the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 「妇女不可穿戴男子所穿戴的，男子也不可穿妇女的衣服，因为这样行都是耶和华－你上帝所憎恶的。

chapters.en: If you come across a bird’s nest with chicks or eggs, either in a tree or on the ground along the road, and the mother is sitting on the chicks or eggs, you must not take the mother along with the young.
chapters.zh: 「你若路上遇见鸟窝，或在树上或在地上，里头有雏或有蛋，母鸟伏在雏上或在蛋上，你不可连母带雏一并取去。

chapters.en: You may take the young, but be sure to let the mother go, so that it may be well with you and that you may prolong your days.
chapters.zh: 总要放母，只可取雏；这样你就可以享福，日子得以长久。

chapters.en: If you build a new house, you are to construct a railing around your roof, so that you do not bring bloodguilt on your house if someone falls from it.
chapters.zh: 「你若建造房屋，要在房上的四围安栏杆，免得有人从房上掉下来，流血的罪就归于你家。

chapters.en: Do not plant your vineyard with two types of seed; if you do, the entire harvest will be defiled —both the crop you plant and the fruit of your vineyard.
chapters.zh: 「不可把两样种子种在你的葡萄园里，免得你撒种所结的和葡萄园的果子都要充公。

chapters.en: Do not plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together.
chapters.zh: 不可并用牛、驴耕地。

chapters.en: Do not wear clothes of wool and linen woven together.
chapters.zh: 不可穿羊毛、细麻两样搀杂料做的衣服。

chapters.en: You are to make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wear.
chapters.zh: 「你要在所披的外衣上四围做繸子。」

chapters.en: Suppose a man marries a woman, has relations with her, and comes to hate her,
chapters.zh: 「人若娶妻，与她同房之后恨恶她，

chapters.en: and he then accuses her of shameful conduct and gives her a bad name, saying, “I married this woman and had relations with her, but I discovered she was not a virgin.”
chapters.zh: 信口说她，将丑名加在她身上，说：『我娶了这女子，与她同房，见她没有贞洁的凭据』；

chapters.en: Then the young woman’s father and mother shall bring the proof of her virginity to the city elders at the gate
chapters.zh: 女子的父母就要把女子贞洁的凭据拿出来，带到本城门长老那里。

chapters.en: and say to the elders, “I gave my daughter in marriage to this man, but he has come to hate her.
chapters.zh: 女子的父亲要对长老说：『我将我的女儿给这人为妻，他恨恶她，

chapters.en: And now he has accused her of shameful conduct, saying, ‘I discovered that your daughter was not a virgin.’ But here is the proof of her virginity.” And they shall spread out the cloth before the city elders.
chapters.zh: 信口说她，说：我见你的女儿没有贞洁的凭据；其实这就是我女儿贞洁的凭据。』父母就把那布铺在本城的长老面前。

chapters.en: Then the elders of that city shall take the man and punish him.
chapters.zh: 本城的长老要拿住那人，惩治他，

chapters.en: They are also to fine him a hundred shekels of silver and give them to the young woman’s father, because this man has given a virgin of Israel a bad name. And she shall remain his wife; he must not divorce her as long as he lives.
chapters.zh: 并要罚他一百〔舍客勒〕银子，给女子的父亲，因为他将丑名加在以色列的一个处女身上。女子仍作他的妻，终身不可休她。

chapters.en: If, however, this accusation is true, and no proof of the young woman’s virginity can be found,
chapters.zh: 但这事若是真的，女子没有贞洁的凭据，

chapters.en: she shall be brought to the door of her father’s house, and there the men of her city will stone her to death. For she has committed an outrage in Israel by being promiscuous in her father’s house. So you must purge the evil from among you.
chapters.zh: 就要将女子带到她父家的门口，本城的人要用石头将她打死；因为她在父家行了淫乱，在以色列中做了丑事。这样，就把那恶从你们中间除掉。

chapters.en: If a man is found lying with another man’s wife, both the man who slept with her and the woman must die. You must purge the evil from Israel.
chapters.zh: 「若遇见人与有丈夫的妇人行淫，就要将奸夫淫妇一并治死。这样，就把那恶从以色列中除掉。

chapters.en: If there is a virgin pledged in marriage to a man, and another man encounters her in the city and sleeps with her,
chapters.zh: 「若有处女已经许配丈夫，有人在城里遇见她，与她行淫，

chapters.en: you must take both of them out to the gate of that city and stone them to death—the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he has violated his neighbor’s wife. So you must purge the evil from among you.
chapters.zh: 你们就要把这二人带到本城门，用石头打死－女子是因为虽在城里却没有喊叫；男子是因为玷污别人的妻。这样，就把那恶从你们中间除掉。

chapters.en: But if the man encounters a betrothed woman in the open country, and he overpowers her and lies with her, only the man who has done this must die.
chapters.zh: 「若有男子在田野遇见已经许配人的女子，强与她行淫，只要将那男子治死。

chapters.en: Do nothing to the young woman, because she has committed no sin worthy of death. This case is just like one in which a man attacks his neighbor and murders him.
chapters.zh: 但不可办女子；她本没有该死的罪，这事就类乎人起来攻击邻舍，将他杀了一样。

chapters.en: When he found her in the field, the betrothed woman cried out, but there was no one to save her.
chapters.zh: 因为男子是在田野遇见那已经许配人的女子，女子喊叫，并无人救她。

chapters.en: If a man encounters a virgin who is not pledged in marriage, and he seizes her and lies with her, and they are discovered,
chapters.zh: 「若有男子遇见没有许配人的处女，抓住她，与她行淫，被人看见，

chapters.en: then the man who lay with her must pay the young woman’s father fifty shekels of silver, and she must become his wife because he has violated her. He must not divorce her as long as he lives.
chapters.zh: 这男子就要拿五十〔舍客勒〕银子给女子的父亲；因他玷污了这女子，就要娶她为妻，终身不可休她。

chapters.en: A man is not to marry his father’s wife, so that he will not dishonor his father’s marriage bed.
chapters.zh: 「人不可娶继母为妻；不可掀开他父亲的衣襟。」

chapters.en: No man with crushed or severed genitals may enter the assembly of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「凡外肾受伤的，或被阉割的，不可入耶和华的会。

chapters.en: No one of illegitimate birth may enter the assembly of the LORD, nor may any of his descendants, even to the tenth generation.
chapters.zh: 「私生子不可入耶和华的会；他的子孙，直到十代，也不可入耶和华的会。

chapters.en: No Ammonite or Moabite or any of their descendants may enter the assembly of the LORD, even to the tenth generation.
chapters.zh: 「亚扪人或是摩押人不可入耶和华的会；他们的子孙，虽过十代，也永不可入耶和华的会。

chapters.en: For they did not meet you with food and water on your way out of Egypt, and they hired Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Aram-naharaim to curse you.
chapters.zh: 因为你们出埃及的时候，他们没有拿食物和水在路上迎接你们，又因他们雇了美索不达米亚的毗夺人比珥的儿子巴兰来咒诅你们。

chapters.en: Yet the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam, and the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loves you.
chapters.zh: 然而耶和华－你的上帝不肯听从巴兰，却使那咒诅的言语变为祝福的话，因为耶和华－你的上帝爱你。

chapters.en: You are not to seek peace or prosperity from them as long as you live.
chapters.zh: 你一生一世永不可求他们的平安和他们的利益。

chapters.en: Do not despise an Edomite, for he is your brother. Do not despise an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.
chapters.zh: 「不可憎恶以东人，因为他是你的弟兄。不可憎恶埃及人，因为你在他的地上作过寄居的。

chapters.en: The third generation of children born to them may enter the assembly of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 他们第三代子孙可以入耶和华的会。」

chapters.en: When you are encamped against your enemies, then you shall keep yourself from every wicked thing.
chapters.zh: 「你出兵攻打仇敌，就要远避诸恶。

chapters.en: If any man among you becomes unclean because of a nocturnal emission, he must leave the camp and stay outside.
chapters.zh: 「你们中间，若有人夜间偶然梦遗，不洁净，就要出到营外，不可入营；

chapters.en: When evening approaches, he must wash with water, and when the sun sets he may return to the camp.
chapters.zh: 到傍晚的时候，他要用水洗澡，及至日落了才可以入营。

chapters.en: You must have a place outside the camp to go and relieve yourself.
chapters.zh: 「你在营外也该定出一个地方作为便所。

chapters.en: And you must have a digging tool in your equipment so that when you relieve yourself you can dig a hole and cover up your excrement.
chapters.zh: 在你器械之中当预备一把锹，你出营外便溺以后，用以铲土，转身掩盖。

chapters.en: For the LORD your God walks throughout your camp to protect you and deliver your enemies to you. Your camp must be holy, lest He see anything unclean among you and turn away from you.
chapters.zh: 因为耶和华－你的上帝常在你营中行走，要救护你，将仇敌交给你，所以你的营理当圣洁，免得他见你那里有污秽，就离开你。」

chapters.en: Do not return a slave to his master if he has taken refuge with you.
chapters.zh: 「若有奴仆脱了主人的手，逃到你那里，你不可将他交付他的主人。

chapters.en: Let him live among you wherever he chooses, in the town of his pleasing. Do not oppress him.
chapters.zh: 他必在你那里与你同住，在你的城邑中，要由他选择一个所喜悦的地方居住；你不可欺负他。

chapters.en: No daughter or son of Israel is to be a shrine prostitute.
chapters.zh: 「以色列的女子中不可有妓女；以色列的男子中不可有娈童。

chapters.en: You must not bring the wages of a prostitute, whether female or male, into the house of the LORD your God to fulfill any vow, because both are detestable to the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 娼妓所得的钱，或娈童〔注：原文是狗〕所得的价，你不可带入耶和华－你上帝的殿还愿，因为这两样都是耶和华－你上帝所憎恶的。

chapters.en: Do not charge your brother interest on money, food, or any other type of loan.
chapters.zh: 「你借给你弟兄的，或是钱财或是粮食，无论什么可生利的物，都不可取利。

chapters.en: You may charge a foreigner interest, but not your brother, so that the LORD your God may bless you in everything to which you put your hand in the land that you are entering to possess.
chapters.zh: 借给外邦人可以取利，只是借给你弟兄不可取利。这样，耶和华－你上帝必在你所去得为业的地上和你手里所办的一切事上赐福与你。

chapters.en: If you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not be slow to keep it, because He will surely require it of you, and you will be guilty of sin.
chapters.zh: 「你向耶和华－你的上帝许愿，偿还不可迟延；因为耶和华－你的上帝必定向你追讨，你不偿还就有罪。

chapters.en: But if you refrain from making a vow, you will not be guilty of sin.
chapters.zh: 你若不许愿，倒无罪。

chapters.en: Be careful to follow through on what comes from your lips, because you have freely vowed to the LORD your God with your own mouth.
chapters.zh: 你嘴里所出的，就是你口中应许甘心所献的，要照你向耶和华－你上帝所许的愿谨守遵行。

chapters.en: When you enter your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat your fill of grapes, but you must not put any in your basket.
chapters.zh: 「你进了邻舍的葡萄园，可以随意吃饱了葡萄，只是不可装在器皿中。

chapters.en: When you enter your neighbor’s grainfield, you may pluck the heads of grain with your hand, but you must not put a sickle to your neighbor’s grain.
chapters.zh: 你进了邻舍站着的禾稼，可以用手摘穗子，只是不可用镰刀割取禾稼。」

chapters.en: If a man marries a woman, but she becomes displeasing to him because he finds some indecency in her, he may write her a certificate of divorce, hand it to her, and send her away from his house.
chapters.zh: 「人若娶妻以后，见她有什么不合理的事，不喜悦她，就可以写休书交在她手中，打发她离开夫家。

chapters.en: If, after leaving his house, she goes and becomes another man’s wife,
chapters.zh: 妇人离开夫家以后，可以去嫁别人。

chapters.en: and the second man hates her, writes her a certificate of divorce, hands it to her, and sends her away from his house, or if he dies,
chapters.zh: 后夫若恨恶她，写休书交在她手中，打发她离开夫家，或是娶她为妻的后夫死了，

chapters.en: then the husband who divorced her first may not remarry her after she has been defiled, for that is an abomination to the LORD. You must not bring sin upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
chapters.zh: 打发她去的前夫不可在妇人玷污之后再娶她为妻，因为这是耶和华所憎恶的；不可使耶和华－你上帝所赐为业之地被玷污了。」

chapters.en: If a man is newly married, he must not be sent to war or be pressed into any duty. For one year he is free to stay at home and bring joy to the wife he has married.
chapters.zh: 「新娶妻之人不可从军出征，也不可讬他办理什么公事，可以在家清闲一年，使他所娶的妻快活。

chapters.en: Do not take a pair of millstones or even an upper millstone as security for a debt, because that would be taking one’s livelihood as security.
chapters.zh: 「不可拿人的〔全〕盘磨石或是上磨石作当头，因为这是拿〔人的〕命作当头。

chapters.en: If a man is caught kidnapping one of his Israelite brothers, whether he treats him as a slave or sells him, the kidnapper must die. So you must purge the evil from among you.
chapters.zh: 「若遇见人拐带以色列中的一个弟兄，当奴才待他，或是卖了他，那拐带人的就必治死。这样，便将那恶从你们中间除掉。

chapters.en: In cases of infectious skin diseases, be careful to diligently follow everything the Levitical priests instruct you. Be careful to do as I have commanded them.
chapters.zh: 「在大痲疯的灾病上，你们要谨慎，照祭司利未人一切所指教你们的留意遵行。我怎样吩咐他们，你们要怎样遵行。

chapters.en: Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the journey after you came out of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 当记念出埃及后，在路上，耶和华－你上帝向米利暗所行的事。

chapters.en: When you lend anything to your neighbor, do not enter his house to collect security.
chapters.zh: 「你借给邻舍，不拘是什么，不可进他家拿他的当头。

chapters.en: You are to stand outside while the man to whom you are lending brings the security out to you.
chapters.zh: 要站在外面，等那向你借贷的人把当头拿出来交给你。

chapters.en: If he is a poor man, you must not go to sleep with the security in your possession;
chapters.zh: 他若是穷人，你不可留他的当头过夜。

chapters.en: be sure to return it to him by sunset, so that he may sleep in his own cloak and bless you, and this will be credited to you as righteousness before the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 日落的时候，总要把当头还他，使他用那件衣服盖着睡觉，他就为你祝福；这在耶和华－你上帝面前就是你的义了。

chapters.en: Do not oppress a hired hand who is poor and needy, whether he is a brother or a foreigner residing in one of your towns.
chapters.zh: 「困苦穷乏的雇工，无论是你的弟兄或是在你城里寄居的，你不可欺负他。

chapters.en: You are to pay his wages each day before sunset, because he is poor and depends on them. Otherwise he may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
chapters.zh: 要当日给他工价，不可等到日落－因为他穷苦，把心放在工价上－恐怕他因你求告耶和华，罪便归你了。

chapters.en: Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin.
chapters.zh: 「不可因子杀父，也不可因父杀子；凡被杀的都为本身的罪。

chapters.en: Do not deny justice to the foreigner or the fatherless, and do not take a widow’s cloak as security.
chapters.zh: 「你不可向寄居的和孤儿屈枉正直，也不可拿寡妇的衣裳作当头。

chapters.en: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from that place. Therefore I am commanding you to do this.
chapters.zh: 要记念你在埃及作过奴仆。耶和华－你的上帝从那里将你救赎，所以我吩咐你这样行。

chapters.en: If you are harvesting in your field and forget a sheaf there, do not go back to get it. It is to be left for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
chapters.zh: 「你在田间收割庄稼，若忘下一捆，不可回去再取，要留给寄居的与孤儿寡妇。这样，耶和华－你上帝必在你手里所办的一切事上赐福与你。

chapters.en: When you beat the olives from your trees, you must not go over the branches again. What remains will be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
chapters.zh: 你打橄榄树，枝上剩下的，不可再打；要留给寄居的与孤儿寡妇。

chapters.en: When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, you must not go over the vines again. What remains will be for the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
chapters.zh: 你摘葡萄园的〔葡萄〕，所剩下的，不可再摘；要留给寄居的与孤儿寡妇。

chapters.en: Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt. Therefore I am commanding you to do this.
chapters.zh: 你也要记念你在埃及地作过奴仆，所以我吩咐你这样行。

chapters.en: If there is a dispute between men, they are to go to court to be judged, so that the innocent may be acquitted and the guilty condemned.
chapters.zh: 「人若有争讼，来听审判，〔审判官〕就要定义人有理，定恶人有罪。

chapters.en: If the guilty man deserves to be beaten, the judge shall have him lie down and be flogged in his presence with the number of lashes his crime warrants.
chapters.zh: 恶人若该受责打，审判官就要叫他当面伏在地上，按着他的罪照数责打。

chapters.en: He may receive no more than forty lashes, lest your brother be beaten any more than that and be degraded in your sight.
chapters.zh: 只可打他四十下，不可过数；若过数，便是轻贱你的弟兄了。

chapters.en: Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.
chapters.zh: 「牛在场上踹谷的时候，不可笼住牠的嘴。」

chapters.en: When brothers dwell together and one of them dies without a son, the widow must not marry outside the family. Her husband’s brother is to take her as his wife and fulfill the duty of a brother-in-law for her.
chapters.zh: 「弟兄同居，若死了一个，没有儿子，死人的妻不可出嫁外人，她丈夫的兄弟当尽弟兄的本分，娶她为妻，与她同房。

chapters.en: The first son she bears will carry on the name of the dead brother, so that his name will not be blotted out from Israel.
chapters.zh: 妇人生的长子必归死兄的名下，免得他的名在以色列中涂抹了。

chapters.en: But if the man does not want to marry his brother’s widow, she is to go to the elders at the city gate and say, “My husband’s brother refuses to preserve his brother’s name in Israel. He is not willing to perform the duty of a brother-in-law for me.”
chapters.zh: 那人若不愿意娶他哥哥的妻，他哥哥的妻就要到城门长老那里，说：『我丈夫的兄弟不肯在以色列中兴起他哥哥的名字，不给我尽弟兄的本分。』

chapters.en: Then the elders of his city shall summon him and speak with him. If he persists and says, “I do not want to marry her,”
chapters.zh: 本城的长老就要召那人来问他，他若执意说：『我不愿意娶她』，

chapters.en: his brother’s widow shall go up to him in the presence of the elders, remove his sandal, spit in his face, and declare, “This is what is done to the man who will not maintain his brother’s line.”
chapters.zh: 他哥哥的妻就要当着长老到那人的跟前，脱了他的鞋，吐唾沫在他脸上，说：『凡不为哥哥建立家室的都要这样待他。』

chapters.en: And his family name in Israel will be called “The House of the Unsandaled.”
chapters.zh: 在以色列中，他的名必称为脱鞋之家。」

chapters.en: If two men are fighting, and the wife of one comes to rescue her husband from the one striking him, and she reaches out her hand and grabs his genitals,
chapters.zh: 「若有二人争斗，这人的妻近前来，要救她丈夫脱离那打她丈夫之人的手，抓住那人的下体，

chapters.en: you are to cut off her hand. You must show her no pity.
chapters.zh: 就要砍断妇人的手，眼不可顾惜她。

chapters.en: You shall not have two differing weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.
chapters.zh: 「你囊中不可有一大一小两样的法码。

chapters.en: You shall not have two differing measures in your house, one large and one small.
chapters.zh: 你家里不可有一大一小两样的升斗。

chapters.en: You must maintain accurate and honest weights and measures, so that you may live long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
chapters.zh: 当用对准公平的法码，公平的升斗。这样，在耶和华－你上帝所赐你的地上，你的日子就可以长久。

chapters.en: For everyone who behaves dishonestly in regard to these things is detestable to the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 因为行非义之事的人都是耶和华－你上帝所憎恶的。」

chapters.en: Remember what the Amalekites did to you along your way from Egypt,
chapters.zh: 「你要记念你们出埃及的时候，亚玛力人在路上怎样待你。

chapters.en: how they met you on your journey when you were tired and weary, and they attacked all your stragglers; they had no fear of God.
chapters.zh: 他们在路上遇见你，趁你疲乏困倦击杀你尽后边软弱的人，并不敬畏上帝。

chapters.en: When the LORD your God gives you rest from the enemies around you in the land that He is giving you to possess as an inheritance, you are to blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget!
chapters.zh: 所以耶和华－你上帝使你不被四围一切的仇敌扰乱，在耶和华－你上帝赐你为业的地上得享平安。那时，你要将亚玛力的名号从天下涂抹了，不可忘记。」

chapters.en: When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and you take possession of it and settle in it,
chapters.zh: 「你进去得了耶和华－你上帝所赐你为业之地居住，

chapters.en: you are to take some of the firstfruits of all your produce from the soil of the land that the LORD your God is giving you and put them in a basket. Then go to the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for His Name,
chapters.zh: 就要从耶和华－你上帝赐你的地上将所收的各种初熟的土产取些来，盛在筐子里，往耶和华－你上帝所选择要立为他名的居所去，

chapters.en: to the priest who is serving at that time, and say to him, “I declare today to the LORD your God that I have entered the land that the LORD swore to our fathers to give us.”
chapters.zh: 见当时作祭司的，对他说：『我今日向耶和华－你上帝明认，我已来到耶和华向我们列祖起誓应许赐给我们的地。』

chapters.en: Then the priest shall take the basket from your hands and place it before the altar of the LORD your God,
chapters.zh: 祭司就从你手里取过筐子来，放在耶和华－你上帝的坛前。

chapters.en: and you are to declare before the LORD your God, “My father was a wandering Aramean, and he went down to Egypt few in number and lived there and became a great nation, mighty and numerous.
chapters.zh: 你要在耶和华－你上帝面前说：『我祖原是一个将亡的亚兰人，下到埃及寄居。他人口稀少，在那里却成了又大又强、人数很多的国民。

chapters.en: But the Egyptians mistreated us and afflicted us, putting us to hard labor.
chapters.zh: 埃及人恶待我们，苦害我们，将苦工加在我们身上。

chapters.en: So we called out to the LORD, the God of our fathers; and the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, toil, and oppression.
chapters.zh: 于是我们哀求耶和华－我们列祖的上帝，耶和华听见我们的声音，看见我们所受的困苦、劳碌、欺压，

chapters.en: Then the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, signs, and wonders.
chapters.zh: 他就用大能的手和伸出来的膀臂，并大可畏的事与神迹奇事，领我们出了埃及，

chapters.en: And He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
chapters.zh: 将我们领进这地方，把这流奶与蜜之地赐给我们。

chapters.en:
And now, behold, I have brought the firstfruits of the land that You, O LORD, have given me.”
Then you are to place the basket before the LORD your God and bow down before Him.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，现在我把你所赐给我地上初熟的土产奉了来。』随后你要把筐子放在耶和华－你上帝面前，向耶和华－你的上帝下拜。

chapters.en: So you shall rejoice—you, the Levite, and the foreigner dwelling among you—in all the good things the LORD your God has given to you and your household.
chapters.zh: 你和利未人，并在你们中间寄居的，要因耶和华－你上帝所赐你和你家的一切福分欢乐。

chapters.en: When you have finished laying aside a tenth of all your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, you are to give it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, that they may eat and be filled within your gates.
chapters.zh: 「每逢三年，就是十分取一之年，你取完了一切土产的十分之一，要分给利未人和寄居的，与孤儿寡妇，使他们在你城中可以吃得饱足。

chapters.en: Then you shall declare in the presence of the LORD your God, “I have removed from my house the sacred portion and have given it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, according to all the commandments You have given me. I have not transgressed or forgotten Your commandments.
chapters.zh: 你又要在耶和华－你上帝面前说：『我已将圣物从我家里拿出来，给了利未人和寄居的，与孤儿寡妇，是照你所吩咐我的一切命令。你的命令我都没有违背，也没有忘记。

chapters.en: I have not eaten any of the sacred portion while in mourning, or removed any of it while unclean, or offered any of it for the dead. I have obeyed the LORD my God; I have done everything You commanded me.
chapters.zh: 我守丧的时候，没有吃这圣物；不洁净的时候，也没有拿出来，又没有为死人送去。我听从了耶和华－我上帝的话，都照你所吩咐的行了。

chapters.en: Look down from Your holy habitation, from heaven, and bless Your people Israel and the land You have given us as You swore to our fathers—a land flowing with milk and honey.”
chapters.zh: 求你从天上、你的圣所垂看，赐福给你的百姓以色列与你所赐给我们的地，就是你向我们列祖起誓赐我们流奶与蜜之地。』」

chapters.en: The LORD your God commands you this day to follow these statutes and ordinances. You must be careful to follow them with all your heart and with all your soul.
chapters.zh: 「耶和华－你的上帝今日吩咐你行这些律例典章，所以你要尽心尽性谨守遵行。

chapters.en: Today you have proclaimed that the LORD is your God and that you will walk in His ways, keep His statutes and commandments and ordinances, and listen to His voice.
chapters.zh: 你今日认耶和华为你的上帝，应许遵行他的道，谨守他的律例、诫命、典章，听从他的话。

chapters.en: And today the LORD has proclaimed that you are His people and treasured possession as He promised, that you are to keep all His commandments,
chapters.zh: 耶和华今日照他所应许你的，也认你为他的子民，使你谨守他的一切诫命，

chapters.en: that He will set you high in praise and name and honor above all the nations He has made, and that you will be a holy people to the LORD your God, as He has promised.
chapters.zh: 又使你得称赞、美名、尊荣，超乎他所造的万民之上，并照他所应许的使你归耶和华－你上帝为圣洁的民。」

chapters.en: Then Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people: “Keep all the commandments I am giving you today.
chapters.zh: 摩西和以色列的众长老吩咐百姓说：「你们要遵守我今日所吩咐的一切诫命。

chapters.en: And on the day you cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, set up large stones and coat them with plaster.
chapters.zh: 你们过约旦河，到了耶和华－你上帝所赐给你的地，当天要立起几块大石头，墁上石灰，

chapters.en: Write on them all the words of this law when you have crossed over to enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, has promised you.
chapters.zh: 把这律法的一切话写在石头上。你过了河，可以进入耶和华－你上帝所赐你流奶与蜜之地，正如耶和华－你列祖之上帝所应许你的。

chapters.en: And when you have crossed the Jordan, you are to set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I am commanding you today, and you are to coat them with plaster.
chapters.zh: 你们过了约旦河，就要在以巴路山上照我今日所吩咐的，将这些石头立起来，墁上石灰。

chapters.en: Moreover, you are to build there an altar to the LORD your God, an altar of stones. You must not use any iron tool on them.
chapters.zh: 在那里要为耶和华－你的上帝筑一座石坛；在石头上不可动铁〔器〕。

chapters.en: You shall build the altar of the LORD your God with uncut stones and offer upon it burnt offerings to the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 要用没有凿过的石头筑耶和华－你上帝的坛，在坛上要将燔祭献给耶和华－你的上帝。

chapters.en: There you are to sacrifice your peace offerings, eating them and rejoicing in the presence of the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 又要献平安祭，且在那里吃，在耶和华－你的上帝面前欢乐。

chapters.en: And you shall write distinctly upon these stones all the words of this law.”
chapters.zh: 你要将这律法的一切话明明地写在石头上。」

chapters.en: Then Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel: “Be silent, O Israel, and listen! This day you have become the people of the LORD your God.
chapters.zh: 摩西和祭司利未人晓谕以色列众人说：「以色列啊，要默默静听。你今日成为耶和华－你上帝的百姓了。

chapters.en: You shall therefore obey the voice of the LORD your God and follow His commandments and statutes I am giving you today.”
chapters.zh: 所以要听从耶和华－你上帝的话，遵行他的诫命律例，就是我今日所吩咐你的。」

chapters.en: On that day Moses commanded the people:
chapters.zh: 当日，摩西嘱咐百姓说：

chapters.en: “When you have crossed the Jordan, these tribes shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
chapters.zh: 「你们过了约旦河，西缅、利未、犹大、以萨迦、约瑟、便雅悯六个支派的人都要站在基利心山上为百姓祝福。

chapters.en: And these tribes shall stand on Mount Ebal to deliver the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
chapters.zh: 吕便、迦得、亚设、西布伦、但、拿弗他利六个支派的人都要站在以巴路山上宣布咒诅。

chapters.en: Then the Levites shall proclaim in a loud voice to every Israelite:
chapters.zh: 利未人要向以色列众人高声说：

chapters.en: ‘Cursed is the man who makes a carved idol or molten image—an abomination to the LORD, the work of the hands of a craftsman—and sets it up in secret.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’
chapters.zh: 「『有人制造耶和华所憎恶的偶像，或雕刻，或铸造，就是工匠手所做的，在暗中设立，那人必受咒诅！』百姓都要答应说：『阿们！』

chapters.en: ‘Cursed is he who dishonors his father or mother.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’
chapters.zh: 「『轻慢父母的，必受咒诅！』百姓都要说：『阿们！』

chapters.en: ‘Cursed is he who moves his neighbor’s boundary stone.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’
chapters.zh: 「『挪移邻舍地界的，必受咒诅！』百姓都要说：『阿们！』

chapters.en: ‘Cursed is he who lets a blind man wander in the road.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’
chapters.zh: 「『使瞎子走差路的，必受咒诅！』百姓都要说：『阿们！』

chapters.en: ‘Cursed is he who withholds justice from the foreigner, the fatherless, or the widow.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’
chapters.zh: 「『向寄居的和孤儿寡妇屈枉正直的，必受咒诅！』百姓都要说：『阿们！』

chapters.en: ‘Cursed is he who sleeps with his father’s wife, for he has violated his father’s marriage bed.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’
chapters.zh: 「『与继母行淫的，必受咒诅！因为掀开他父亲的衣襟。』百姓都要说：『阿们！』

chapters.en: ‘Cursed is he who lies with any animal.’ And let all the people say, ‘Amen!’
chapters.zh: 「『与兽淫合的，必受咒诅！』百姓都要说：『阿们！』
