chapters.en: “Very well,” said Jonathan, “we will cross over toward these men and show ourselves to them.
chapters.zh: 约拿单说：「我们要过到那些人那里去，使他们看见我们。

chapters.en: If they say, ‘Wait until we come to you,’ then we will stay where we are and will not go up to them.
chapters.zh: 他们若对我们说：『你们站住，等我们到你们那里去』，我们就站住，不上他们那里去。

chapters.en: But if they say, ‘Come on up,’ then we will go up, because this will be our sign that the LORD has delivered them into our hands.”
chapters.zh: 他们若说：『你们上到我们这里来』，这话就是我们的证据；我们便上去，因为耶和华将他们交在我们手里了。」

chapters.en: So the two of them showed themselves to the outpost of the Philistines, who exclaimed, “Look, the Hebrews are coming out of the holes in which they were hiding!”
chapters.zh: 二人就使非利士的防兵看见。非利士人说：「希伯来人从所藏的洞穴里出来了！」

chapters.en:
So the men of the outpost called out to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, “Come on up, and we will teach you a lesson!”
“Follow me,” Jonathan told his armor-bearer, “for the LORD has delivered them into the hand of Israel.”
chapters.zh: 防兵对约拿单和拿兵器的人说：「你们上到这里来，我们有一件事指示你们。」约拿单就对拿兵器的人说：「你跟随我上去，因为耶和华将他们交在以色列人手里了。」

chapters.en: So Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer behind him. And the Philistines fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer followed and finished them off.
chapters.zh: 约拿单就爬上去，拿兵器的人跟随他。约拿单杀倒非利士人，拿兵器的人也随着杀他们。

chapters.en: In that first assault, Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about twenty men in about half an acre of land.
chapters.zh: 约拿单和拿兵器的人起头所杀的约有二十人，都在一亩地的半诓沟之内。

chapters.en: Then panic struck the Philistines in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. Even those in the outposts and raiding parties trembled. Indeed, the earth quaked, and panic spread from God.
chapters.zh: 于是在营中、在田野、在众民内都有战兢，防兵和掠兵也都战兢，地也震动，战兢之势甚大。

chapters.en: Now when Saul’s watchmen at Gibeah in Benjamin looked and saw the troops melting away and scattering in every direction,
chapters.zh: 在便雅悯的基比亚，扫罗的守望兵看见非利士的军众溃散，四围乱窜。

chapters.en:
Saul said to the troops who were with him, “Call the roll and see who has left us.”
And when they had called the roll, they saw that Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.
chapters.zh: 扫罗就对跟随他的民说：「你们查点查点，看从我们这里出去的是谁？」他们一查点，就知道约拿单和拿兵器的人没有在这里。

chapters.en: Then Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring the ark of God.” (For at that time it was with the Israelites.)
chapters.zh: 那时上帝的〔约〕柜在以色列人那里。扫罗对亚希亚说：「你将上帝的〔约〕柜运了来。」

chapters.en: While Saul was talking to the priest, the commotion in the Philistine camp continued to increase. So Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗正与祭司说话的时候，非利士营中的喧嚷越发大了；扫罗就对祭司说：「停手吧！」

chapters.en: Then Saul and all his troops assembled and marched to the battle, and they found the Philistines in total confusion, with each man wielding the sword against his neighbor.
chapters.zh: 扫罗和跟随他的人都聚集，来到战场，看见非利士人用刀互相击杀，大大惶乱。

chapters.en: And the Hebrews who had previously gone up into the surrounding camps to join the Philistines now went over to the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.
chapters.zh: 从前由四方来跟随非利士军的希伯来人现在也转过来，帮助跟随扫罗和约拿单的以色列人了。

chapters.en: When all the Israelites who had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines were fleeing, they also joined the battle in close pursuit.
chapters.zh: 那藏在以法莲山地的以色列人听说非利士人逃跑，就出来紧紧地追杀他们。

chapters.en: So the LORD saved Israel that day, and the battle moved on beyond Beth-aven.
chapters.zh: 那日，耶和华使以色列人得胜，一直战到伯‧亚文。

chapters.en: Now the men of Israel were in distress that day, for Saul had placed the troops under an oath, saying, “Cursed is the man who eats any food before evening, before I have taken vengeance on my enemies.” So none of the troops tasted any food.
chapters.zh: 扫罗叫百姓起誓说，凡不等到晚上向敌人报完了仇吃什么的，必受咒诅。因此这日百姓没有吃什么，就极其困惫。

chapters.en: Then all the troops entered the forest, and there was honey on the ground.
chapters.zh: 众民进入树林，见有蜜在地上。

chapters.en: And when they entered the forest and saw the flowing honey, not one of them put his hand to his mouth, because they feared the oath.
chapters.zh: 他们进了树林，见有蜜流下来，却没有人敢用手〔取蜜〕入口，因为他们怕那誓言。

chapters.en: Jonathan, however, had not heard that his father had bound the people with the oath. So he reached out the end of the staff in his hand, dipped it into the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth, and his eyes brightened.
chapters.zh: 约拿单没有听见他父亲叫百姓起誓，所以伸手中的杖，用杖头蘸在蜂房里，转手送入口内，眼睛就明亮了。

chapters.en: Then one of the soldiers told him, “Your father bound the troops with a solemn oath, saying, ‘Cursed is the man who eats food today.’ That is why the people are faint.”
chapters.zh: 百姓中有一人对他说：「你父亲曾叫百姓严严地起誓说，今日吃什么的，必受咒诅；因此百姓就疲乏了。」

chapters.en: “My father has brought trouble to the land,” Jonathan replied. “Just look at how my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.
chapters.zh: 约拿单说：「我父亲连累你们了。你看，我尝了这一点蜜，眼睛就明亮了。

chapters.en: How much better it would have been if the troops had eaten freely today from the plunder they took from their enemies! Would not the slaughter of the Philistines have been much greater?”
chapters.zh: 今日百姓若任意吃了从仇敌所夺的物，击杀的非利士人岂不更多吗？」

chapters.en: That day, after the Israelites had struck down the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon, the people were very faint.
chapters.zh: 这日，以色列人击杀非利士人，从密抹直到亚雅崙。百姓甚是疲乏，

chapters.en: So they rushed greedily to the plunder, taking sheep, cattle, and calves. They slaughtered them on the ground and ate meat with the blood still in it.
chapters.zh: 就急忙将所夺的牛羊和牛犊宰于地上，肉还带血就吃了。

chapters.en:
Then someone reported to Saul: “Look, the troops are sinning against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it.”
“You have broken faith,” said Saul. “Roll a large stone over here at once.”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉扫罗说：「百姓吃带血的肉，得罪耶和华了。」扫罗说：「你们有罪了，今日要将大石头滚到我这里来。」

chapters.en:
Then he said, “Go among the troops and tell them, ‘Each man must bring me his ox or his sheep, slaughter them in this place, and then eat. Do not sin against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it.’”
So that night everyone brought his ox and slaughtered it there.
chapters.zh: 扫罗又说：「你们散在百姓中，对他们说，你们各人将牛羊牵到我这里来宰了吃，不可吃带血的肉得罪耶和华。」这夜，百姓就把牛羊牵到那里宰了。

chapters.en: Then Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first time he had built an altar to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 扫罗为耶和华筑了一座坛，这是他初次为耶和华筑的坛。

chapters.en:
And Saul said, “Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder them until dawn, leaving no man alive!”
“Do what seems good to you,” the troops replied.
But the priest said, “We must consult God here.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗说：「我们不如夜里下去追赶非利士人，抢掠他们，直到天亮，不留他们一人。」众民说：「你看怎样好就去行吧！」祭司说：「我们先当亲近上帝。」

chapters.en:
So Saul inquired of God, “Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will You give them into the hand of Israel?”
But God did not answer him that day.
chapters.zh: 扫罗求问上帝说：「我下去追赶非利士人可以不可以？你将他们交在以色列人手里不交？」这日上帝没有回答他。

chapters.en: Therefore Saul said, “Come here, all you leaders of the troops, and let us investigate how this sin has occurred today.
chapters.zh: 扫罗说：「你们百姓中的长老都上这里来，查明今日是谁犯了罪。

chapters.en:
As surely as the LORD who saves Israel lives, even if it is my son Jonathan, he must die!”
But not one of the troops said a word.
chapters.zh: 我指着救以色列－永生的耶和华起誓，就是我儿子约拿单犯了罪，他也必死。」但百姓中无一人回答他。

chapters.en:
Then Saul said to all Israel, “You stand on one side, and I and my son Jonathan will stand on the other side.”
“Do what seems good to you,” the troops replied.
chapters.zh: 扫罗就对以色列众人说：「你们站在一边，我与我儿子约拿单也站在一边。」百姓对扫罗说：「你看怎样好就去行吧！」

chapters.en: So Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, “Why have You not answered Your servant this day? If the fault is with me or my son Jonathan, respond with Urim, but if the fault is with the men of Israel, respond with Thummim.” And Jonathan and Saul were selected, but the people were cleared of the charge.
chapters.zh: 扫罗祷告耶和华－以色列的上帝说：「求你指示实情。」于是〔掣签〕掣出扫罗和约拿单来；百姓尽都无事。

chapters.en: Then Saul said, “Cast the lot between me and my son Jonathan.” And Jonathan was selected.
chapters.zh: 扫罗说：「你们再〔掣签〕，看是我，是我儿子约拿单」，就掣出约拿单来。

chapters.en:
“Tell me what you have done,” Saul commanded him.
So Jonathan told him, “I only tasted a little honey with the end of the staff that was in my hand. And now I must die?”
chapters.zh: 扫罗对约拿单说：「你告诉我，你做了什么事？」约拿单说：「我实在以手里的杖，用杖头蘸了一点蜜尝了一尝。这样我就死吗〔注：或译：吧！〕？」

chapters.en: And Saul declared, “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if you, Jonathan, do not surely die!”
chapters.zh: 扫罗说：「约拿单哪，你定要死！若不然，愿上帝重重地降罚与我。」

chapters.en:
But the people said to Saul, “Must Jonathan die—he who accomplished such a great deliverance for Israel? Never! As surely as the LORD lives, not a hair of his head will fall to the ground, for with God’s help he has accomplished this today.”
So the people rescued Jonathan, and he did not die.
chapters.zh: 百姓对扫罗说：「约拿单在以色列人中这样大行拯救，岂可使他死呢？断乎不可！我们指着永生的耶和华起誓，连他的一根头发也不可落地，因为他今日与上帝一同做事。」于是百姓救约拿单免了死亡。

chapters.en: Then Saul gave up his pursuit of the Philistines, and the Philistines returned to their own land.
chapters.zh: 扫罗回去，不追赶非利士人；非利士人也回本地去了。

chapters.en: After Saul had assumed the kingship over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side—the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. Wherever he turned, he routed them.
chapters.zh: 扫罗执掌以色列的国权，常常攻击他四围的一切仇敌，就是摩押人、亚扪人、以东人，和琐巴诸王，并非利士人。他无论往何处去，都打败仇敌。

chapters.en: He fought valiantly and defeated the Amalekites, delivering Israel from the hands of its plunderers.
chapters.zh: 扫罗奋勇攻击亚玛力人，救了以色列人脱离抢掠他们之人的手。

chapters.en: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua. His two daughters were named Merab (his firstborn) and Michal (his younger daughter).
chapters.zh: 扫罗的儿子是约拿单、亦施韦、麦基舒亚。他的两个女儿：长女名米拉，次女名米甲。

chapters.en: His wife’s name was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. The name of the commander of his army was Abner, the son of Saul’s uncle Ner.
chapters.zh: 扫罗的妻名叫亚希暖，是亚希玛斯的女儿。扫罗的元帅名叫押尼珥，是尼珥的儿子；尼珥是扫罗的叔叔。

chapters.en: Saul’s father Kish and Abner’s father Ner were sons of Abiel.
chapters.zh: 扫罗的父亲基士，押尼珥的父亲尼珥，都是亚别的儿子。

chapters.en: And the war with the Philistines was fierce for all the days of Saul. So whenever he noticed any strong or brave man, Saul would enlist him.
chapters.zh: 扫罗平生常与非利士人大大争战。扫罗遇见有能力的人或勇士，都招募了来跟随他。

chapters.en: Then Samuel said to Saul, “The LORD sent me to anoint you king over His people Israel. Now therefore, listen to the words of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳对扫罗说：「耶和华差遣我膏你为王，治理他的百姓以色列；所以你当听从耶和华的话。

chapters.en: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘I witnessed what the Amalekites did to the Israelites when they opposed them on their way up from Egypt.
chapters.zh: 万军之耶和华如此说：『以色列人出埃及的时候，在路上亚玛力人怎样待他们，怎样抵挡他们，我都没忘。

chapters.en: Now go and attack the Amalekites and devote to destruction all that belongs to them. Do not spare them, but put to death men and women, children and infants, oxen and sheep, camels and donkeys.’”
chapters.zh: 现在你要去击打亚玛力人，灭尽他们所有的，不可怜惜他们，将男女、孩童、吃奶的，并牛、羊、骆驼，和驴尽行杀死。』」

chapters.en: So Saul summoned the troops and numbered them at Telaim—200,000 foot soldiers and 10,000 men of Judah.
chapters.zh: 于是扫罗招聚百姓在提拉因，数点他们，共有步兵二十万，另有犹大人一万。

chapters.en: Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the valley.
chapters.zh: 扫罗到了亚玛力的〔京〕城，在谷中设下埋伏。

chapters.en:
And he warned the Kenites, “Since you showed kindness to all the Israelites when they came up out of Egypt, go on and get away from the Amalekites. Otherwise I will sweep you away with them.”
So the Kenites moved away from the Amalekites.
chapters.zh: 扫罗对基尼人说：「你们离开亚玛力人下去吧，恐怕我将你们和亚玛力人一同杀灭；因为以色列人出埃及的时候，你们曾恩待他们。」于是基尼人离开亚玛力人去了。

chapters.en: Then Saul struck down the Amalekites all the way from Havilah to Shur, which is east of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 扫罗击打亚玛力人，从哈腓拉直到埃及前的书珥，

chapters.en: He captured Agag king of Amalek alive, but devoted all the others to destruction with the sword.
chapters.zh: 生擒了亚玛力王亚甲，用刀杀尽亚玛力的众民。

chapters.en: Saul and his troops spared Agag, along with the best of the sheep and cattle, the fat calves and lambs, and the best of everything else. They were unwilling to devote them to destruction, but they devoted to destruction all that was despised and worthless.
chapters.zh: 扫罗和百姓却怜惜亚甲，也爱惜上好的牛、羊、牛犊、羊羔，并一切美物，不肯灭绝。凡下贱瘦弱的，尽都杀了。

chapters.en: Then the word of the LORD came to Samuel, saying,
chapters.zh: 耶和华的话临到撒母耳说：

chapters.en:
“I regret that I have made Saul king, for he has turned away from following Me and has not carried out My instructions.”
And Samuel was distressed and cried out to the LORD all that night.
chapters.zh: 「我立扫罗为王，我后悔了；因为他转去不跟从我，不遵守我的命令。」撒母耳便甚忧愁，终夜哀求耶和华。

chapters.en: Early in the morning Samuel got up to confront Saul, but he was told, “Saul has gone to Carmel, and behold, he has set up a monument for himself and has turned and gone down to Gilgal.”
chapters.zh: 撒母耳清早起来，迎接扫罗。有人告诉撒母耳说：「扫罗到了迦密，在那里立了纪念碑，又转身下到吉甲。」

chapters.en: When Samuel reached him, Saul said to him, “May the LORD bless you. I have carried out the LORD’s instructions.”
chapters.zh: 撒母耳到了扫罗那里，扫罗对他说：「愿耶和华赐福与你，耶和华的命令我已遵守了。」

chapters.en: But Samuel replied, “Then what is this bleating of sheep and lowing of cattle that I hear?”
chapters.zh: 撒母耳说：「我耳中听见有羊叫、牛鸣，是从哪里来的呢？」

chapters.en: Saul answered, “The troops brought them from the Amalekites; they spared the best sheep and cattle to sacrifice to the LORD your God, but the rest we devoted to destruction.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗说：「这是百姓从亚玛力人那里带来的；因为他们爱惜上好的牛羊，要献与耶和华－你的上帝；其余的，我们都灭尽了。」

chapters.en:
“Stop!” exclaimed Samuel. “Let me tell you what the LORD said to me last night.”
“Tell me,” Saul replied.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳对扫罗说：「你住口吧！等我将耶和华昨夜向我所说的话告诉你。」扫罗说：「请讲。」

chapters.en: And Samuel said, “Although you were once small in your own eyes, have you not become the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel
chapters.zh: 撒母耳对扫罗说：「从前你虽然以自己为小，岂不是被立为以色列支派的元首吗？耶和华膏你作以色列的王。

chapters.en: and sent you on a mission, saying, ‘Go and devote to destruction the sinful Amalekites. Fight against them until you have wiped them out.’
chapters.zh: 耶和华差遣你，吩咐你说，你去击打那些犯罪的亚玛力人，将他们灭绝净尽。

chapters.en: So why did you not obey the LORD? Why did you rush upon the plunder and do evil in the sight of the LORD?”
chapters.zh: 你为何没有听从耶和华的命令，急忙掳掠财物，行耶和华眼中看为恶的事呢？」

chapters.en: “But I did obey the LORD,” Saul replied. “I went on the mission that the LORD gave me. I brought back Agag king of Amalek and devoted the Amalekites to destruction.
chapters.zh: 扫罗对撒母耳说：「我实在听从了耶和华的命令，行了耶和华所差遣我行的路，擒了亚玛力王亚甲来，灭尽了亚玛力人。

chapters.en: The troops took sheep and cattle from the plunder, the best of the things devoted to destruction, in order to sacrifice them to the LORD your God at Gilgal.”
chapters.zh: 百姓却在所当灭的物中，取了最好的牛羊，要在吉甲献与耶和华－你的上帝。」

chapters.en:
But Samuel declared:
“Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obedience to His voice? Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice, and attentiveness is better than the fat of rams.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳说： 耶和华喜悦燔祭和〔平安〕祭， 岂如喜悦人听从他的话呢？ 听命胜于献祭； 顺从胜于公羊的脂油。

chapters.en: For rebellion is like the sin of divination, and arrogance is like the wickedness of idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, He has rejected you as king.”
chapters.zh: 悖逆的罪与行邪术的罪相等； 顽梗的罪与拜虚神和偶像的罪相同。 你既厌弃耶和华的命令， 耶和华也厌弃你作王。

chapters.en: Then Saul said to Samuel, “I have sinned; I have transgressed the LORD’s commandment and your instructions, because I feared the people and obeyed their voice.
chapters.zh: 扫罗对撒母耳说：「我有罪了，我因惧怕百姓，听从他们的话，就违背了耶和华的命令和你的言语。

chapters.en: Now therefore, please forgive my sin and return with me so I can worship the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 现在求你赦免我的罪，同我回去，我好敬拜耶和华。」

chapters.en: “I will not return with you,” Samuel replied. “For you have rejected the word of the LORD, and He has rejected you as king over Israel.”
chapters.zh: 撒母耳对扫罗说：「我不同你回去；因为你厌弃耶和华的命令，耶和华也厌弃你作以色列的王。」

chapters.en: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the hem of his robe, and it tore.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳转身要走，扫罗就扯住他外袍的衣襟，衣襟就撕断了。

chapters.en: So Samuel said to him, “The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to your neighbor who is better than you.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳对他说：「如此，今日耶和华使以色列国与你断绝，将这国赐与比你更好的人。

chapters.en: Moreover, the Glory of Israel does not lie or change His mind, for He is not a man, that He should change His mind.”
chapters.zh: 以色列的大能者必不致说谎，也不致后悔；因为他迥非世人，决不后悔。」

chapters.en: “I have sinned,” Saul replied. “Please honor me now before the elders of my people and before Israel. Come back with me, so that I may worship the LORD your God.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗说：「我有罪了，虽然如此，求你在我百姓的长老和以色列人面前抬举我，同我回去，我好敬拜耶和华－你的上帝。」

chapters.en: So Samuel went back with Saul, and Saul worshiped the LORD.
chapters.zh: 于是撒母耳转身跟随扫罗回去，扫罗就敬拜耶和华。

chapters.en:
Then Samuel said, “Bring me Agag king of the Amalekites.”
Agag came to him cheerfully, for he thought, “Surely the bitterness of death is past.”
chapters.zh: 撒母耳说：「要把亚玛力王亚甲带到我这里来。」亚甲就欢欢喜喜地来到他面前，心里说，死亡的苦难必定过去了。

chapters.en:
But Samuel declared:
“As your sword has made women childless, so your mother will be childless among women.”
And Samuel hacked Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳说：「你既用刀使妇人丧子，这样，你母亲在妇人中也必丧子。」于是，撒母耳在吉甲耶和华面前将亚甲杀死。

chapters.en: Then Samuel went to Ramah, but Saul went up to his home in Gibeah of Saul.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳回了拉玛。扫罗上他所住的基比亚，回自己的家去了。

chapters.en: And to the day of his death, Samuel never again visited Saul. Samuel mourned for Saul, and the LORD regretted that He had made Saul king over Israel.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳直到死的日子，再没有见扫罗；但撒母耳为扫罗悲伤，是因耶和华后悔立他为以色列的王。

chapters.en: Now the LORD said to Samuel, “How long are you going to mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem, for I have selected from his sons a king for Myself.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对撒母耳说：「我既厌弃扫罗作以色列的王，你为他悲伤要到几时呢？你将膏油盛满了角，我差遣你往伯利恒人耶西那里去；因为我在他众子之内，预定一个作王的。」

chapters.en:
“How can I go?” Samuel asked. “Saul will hear of it and kill me!”
The LORD answered, “Take a heifer with you and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.’
chapters.zh: 撒母耳说：「我怎能去呢？扫罗若听见，必要杀我。」耶和华说：「你可以带一只牛犊去，就说：『我来是要向耶和华献祭。』

chapters.en: Then invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you are to do. You are to anoint for Me the one I indicate.”
chapters.zh: 你要请耶西来吃祭肉，我就指示你所当行的事。我所指给你的人，你要膏他。」

chapters.en: So Samuel did what the LORD had said and went to Bethlehem. When the elders of the town met him, they trembled and asked, “Do you come in peace?”
chapters.zh: 撒母耳就照耶和华的话去行。到了伯利恒，那城里的长老都战战兢兢地出来迎接他，问他说：「你是为平安来的吗？」

chapters.en:
“In peace,” he replied. “I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.”
Then he consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.
chapters.zh: 他说：「为平安来的，我是给耶和华献祭。你们当自洁，来与我同吃祭肉。」撒母耳就使耶西和他众子自洁，请他们来吃祭肉。

chapters.en: When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab and said, “Surely here before the LORD is His anointed.”
chapters.zh: 他们来的时候，撒母耳看见以利押，就心里说，耶和华的受膏者必定在他面前。

chapters.en: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Do not consider his appearance or height, for I have rejected him; the LORD does not see as man does. For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华却对撒母耳说：「不要看他的外貌和他身材高大，我不拣选他。因为，〔耶和华〕不像人看人：人是看外貌；耶和华是看内心。」

chapters.en: Then Jesse called Abinadab and presented him to Samuel, who said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”
chapters.zh: 耶西叫亚比拿达从撒母耳面前经过，撒母耳说：「耶和华也不拣选他。」

chapters.en: Next Jesse presented Shammah, but Samuel said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”
chapters.zh: 耶西又叫沙玛从撒母耳面前经过，撒母耳说：「耶和华也不拣选他。」

chapters.en: Thus Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, but Samuel told him, “The LORD has not chosen any of these.”
chapters.zh: 耶西叫他七个儿子都从撒母耳面前经过，撒母耳说：「这都不是耶和华所拣选的。」

chapters.en:
And Samuel asked him, “Are these all the sons you have?”
“There is still the youngest,” Jesse replied, “but he is tending the sheep.”
“Send for him,” Samuel replied. “For we will not sit down to eat until he arrives.”
chapters.zh: 撒母耳对耶西说：「你的儿子都在这里吗？」他回答说：「还有个小的，现在放羊。」撒母耳对耶西说：「你打发人去叫他来；他若不来，我们必不坐席。」

chapters.en: So Jesse sent for his youngest son and brought him in. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance. And the LORD said, “Rise and anoint him, for he is the one.”
chapters.zh: 耶西就打发人去叫了他来。他面色光红，双目清秀，容貌俊美。耶和华说：「这就是他，你起来膏他。」

chapters.en: So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward. Then Samuel set out and went to Ramah.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳就用角里的膏油，在他诸兄中膏了他。从这日起，耶和华的灵就大大感动大卫。撒母耳起身回拉玛去了。

chapters.en: Now the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and a spirit of distress from the LORD began to torment him.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的灵离开扫罗，有恶魔从耶和华那里来扰乱他。

chapters.en: Saul’s servants said to him, “Surely a spirit of distress from God is tormenting you.
chapters.zh: 扫罗的臣仆对他说：「现在有恶魔从上帝那里来扰乱你。

chapters.en: Let our lord command your servants here to seek out someone who can skillfully play the harp. Whenever the spirit of distress from God is upon you, he is to play it, and you will be well.”
chapters.zh: 我们的主可以吩咐面前的臣仆，找一个善于弹琴的来，等上帝那里来的恶魔临到你身上的时候，使他用手弹琴，你就好了。」

chapters.en: And Saul commanded his servants, “Find me someone who plays well, and bring him to me.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗对臣仆说：「你们可以为我找一个善于弹琴的，带到我这里来。」

chapters.en: One of the servants answered, “I have seen a son of Jesse of Bethlehem who knows how to play the harp. He is a mighty man of valor, a warrior, eloquent and handsome, and the LORD is with him.”
chapters.zh: 其中有一个少年人说：「我曾见伯利恒人耶西的一个儿子善于弹琴，是大有勇敢的战士，说话合宜，容貌俊美，耶和华也与他同在。」

chapters.en: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, “Send me your son David, who is with the sheep.”
chapters.zh: 于是扫罗差遣使者去见耶西，说：「请你打发你放羊的儿子大卫到我这里来。」

chapters.en: And Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a skin of wine, and one young goat and sent them to Saul with his son David.
chapters.zh: 耶西就把几个饼和一皮袋酒，并一只山羊羔，都驮在驴上，交给他儿子大卫，送与扫罗。

chapters.en: When David came to Saul and entered his service, Saul loved him very much, and David became his armor-bearer.
chapters.zh: 大卫到了扫罗那里，就侍立在扫罗面前。扫罗甚喜爱他，他就作了扫罗拿兵器的人。

chapters.en: Then Saul sent word to Jesse, saying, “Let David remain in my service, for I am pleased with him.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗差遣人去见耶西，说：「求你容大卫侍立在我面前，因为他在我眼前蒙了恩。」

chapters.en: And whenever the spirit from God came upon Saul, David would pick up his harp and play. Then Saul would find relief and feel better, and the spirit of distress would depart from him.
chapters.zh: 从上帝那里来的恶魔临到扫罗身上的时候，大卫就拿琴，用手而弹，扫罗便舒畅爽快，恶魔离了他。

chapters.en: Now the Philistines gathered their forces for war at Socoh in Judah, and they camped between Socoh and Azekah in Ephes-dammim.
chapters.zh: 非利士人招聚他们的军旅，要来争战；聚集在属犹大的梭哥，安营在梭哥和亚西加中间的以弗‧大悯。

chapters.en: Saul and the men of Israel assembled and camped in the Valley of Elah, arraying themselves for battle against the Philistines.
chapters.zh: 扫罗和以色列人也聚集，在以拉谷安营，摆列队伍，要与非利士人打仗。

chapters.en: The Philistines stood on one hill and the Israelites stood on another, with the valley between them.
chapters.zh: 非利士人站在这边山上，以色列人站在那边山上，当中有谷。

chapters.en: Then a champion named Goliath, who was from Gath, came out from the Philistine camp. He was six cubits and a span in height,
chapters.zh: 从非利士营中出来一个讨战的人，名叫歌利亚，是迦特人，身高六肘零一虎口；

chapters.en: and he had a bronze helmet on his head. He wore a bronze coat of mail weighing five thousand shekels,
chapters.zh: 头戴铜盔，身穿铠甲，甲重五千舍客勒；

chapters.en: and he had armor of bronze on his legs and a javelin of bronze slung between his shoulders.
chapters.zh: 腿上有铜护膝，两肩之中背负铜戟；

chapters.en: The shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and its iron point weighed six hundred shekels. In addition, his shield bearer went before him.
chapters.zh: 枪杆粗如织布的机轴，铁枪头重六百舍客勒。有一个拿盾牌的人在他前面走。

chapters.en: And Goliath stood and shouted to the ranks of Israel, “Why do you come out and array yourselves for battle? Am I not a Philistine, and are you not servants of Saul? Choose one of your men and have him come down against me.
chapters.zh: 歌利亚对着以色列的军队站立，呼叫说：「你们出来摆列队伍做什么呢？我不是非利士人吗？你们不是扫罗的仆人吗？可以从你们中间拣选一人，使他下到我这里来。

chapters.en: If he is able to fight me and kill me, then we will be your servants. But if I prevail against him and kill him, then you shall be our servants and work for us.”
chapters.zh: 他若能与我战斗，将我杀死，我们就作你们的仆人；我若胜了他，将他杀死，你们就作我们的仆人，服事我们。」

chapters.en: Then the Philistine said, “I defy the ranks of Israel this day! Give me a man to fight!”
chapters.zh: 那非利士人又说：「我今日向以色列人的军队骂阵。你们叫一个人出来，与我战斗。」

chapters.en: On hearing the words of the Philistine, Saul and all the Israelites were dismayed and greatly afraid.
chapters.zh: 扫罗和以色列众人听见非利士人的这些话，就惊惶，极其害怕。

chapters.en: Now David was the son of a man named Jesse, an Ephrathite from Bethlehem of Judah who had eight sons. And in the days of Saul, Jesse was old and well along in years.
chapters.zh: 大卫是犹大伯利恒的以法他人耶西的儿子。耶西有八个儿子。当扫罗的时候，耶西已经老迈。

chapters.en: The three older sons of Jesse had followed Saul into battle: The firstborn was Eliab, the second was Abinadab, and the third was Shammah.
chapters.zh: 耶西的三个大儿子跟随扫罗出征。这出征的三个儿子：长子名叫以利押，次子名叫亚比拿达，三子名叫沙玛。

chapters.en:
And David was the youngest.
The three oldest had followed Saul,
chapters.zh: 大卫是最小的；那三个大儿子跟随扫罗。

chapters.en: but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father’s sheep in Bethlehem.
chapters.zh: 大卫有时离开扫罗，回伯利恒放他父亲的羊。

chapters.en: For forty days the Philistine came forward every morning and evening to take his stand.
chapters.zh: 那非利士人早晚都出来站着，如此四十日。

chapters.en: One day Jesse said to his son David, “Take this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread for your brothers and hurry to their camp.
chapters.zh: 一日，耶西对他儿子大卫说：「你拿一伊法烘了的穗子和十个饼，速速地送到营里去，交给你哥哥们；

chapters.en: Take also these ten portions of cheese to the commander of their unit. Check on the welfare of your brothers and bring back an assurance from them.
chapters.zh: 再拿这十块奶饼，送给他们的千夫长，且问你哥哥们好，向他们要一封信来。」

chapters.en: They are with Saul and all the men of Israel in the Valley of Elah, fighting against the Philistines.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗与大卫的三个哥哥和以色列众人，在以拉谷与非利士人打仗。

chapters.en: So David got up early in the morning, left the flock with a keeper, loaded up, and set out as Jesse had instructed him. He reached the camp as the army was marching out to its position and shouting the battle cry.
chapters.zh: 大卫早晨起来，将羊交讬一个看守的人，照着他父亲所吩咐的话，带着食物去了。到了辎重营，军兵刚出到战场，吶喊要战。

chapters.en: And Israel and the Philistines arrayed in formation against each other.
chapters.zh: 以色列人和非利士人都摆列队伍，彼此相对。

chapters.en: Then David left his supplies in the care of the quartermaster and ran to the battle line. When he arrived, he asked his brothers how they were doing.
chapters.zh: 大卫把他带来的食物留在看守物件人的手下，跑到战场，问他哥哥们安。

chapters.en: And as he was speaking with them, suddenly the champion named Goliath, the Philistine from Gath, came forward from the ranks of the Philistines and shouted his usual words, which David also heard.
chapters.zh: 与他们说话的时候，那讨战的，就是属迦特的非利士人歌利亚，从非利士队中出来，说从前所说的话；大卫都听见了。

chapters.en: When all the men of Israel saw Goliath, they fled from him in great fear.
chapters.zh: 以色列众人看见那人，就逃跑，极其害怕。

chapters.en: Now the men of Israel had been saying, “Do you see how this man keeps coming out to defy Israel? To the man who kills him the king will give great riches. And he will give him his daughter in marriage and exempt his father’s house from taxation in Israel.”
chapters.zh: 以色列人彼此说：「这上来的人你看见了吗？他上来是要向以色列人骂阵。若有能杀他的，王必赏赐他大财，将自己的女儿给他为妻，并在以色列人中免他父家纳粮当差。」

chapters.en: David asked the men who were standing with him, “What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and removes this disgrace from Israel? Just who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?”
chapters.zh: 大卫问站在旁边的人说：「有人杀这非利士人，除掉以色列人的耻辱，怎样待他呢？这未受割礼的非利士人是谁呢？竟敢向永生上帝的军队骂阵吗？」

chapters.en: The people told him about the offer, saying, “That is what will be done for the man who kills him.”
chapters.zh: 百姓照先前的话回答他说：「有人能杀这非利士人，必如此如此待他。」

chapters.en: Now when David’s oldest brother Eliab heard him speaking to the men, his anger burned against David. “Why have you come down here?” he asked. “And with whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your pride and wickedness of heart—you have come down to see the battle!”
chapters.zh: 大卫的长兄以利押听见大卫与他们所说的话，就向他发怒，说：「你下来做什么呢？在旷野的那几只羊，你交讬了谁呢？我知道你的骄傲和你心里的恶意，你下来特为要看争战！」

chapters.en: “What have I done now?” said David. “Was it not just a question?”
chapters.zh: 大卫说：「我做了什么呢？我来岂没有缘故吗？」

chapters.en: Then he turned from him toward another and asked about the offer, and those people answered him just as the first ones had answered.
chapters.zh: 大卫就离开他转向别人，照先前的话而问；百姓仍照先前的话回答他。

chapters.en: Now David’s words were overheard and reported to Saul, who sent for him.
chapters.zh: 有人听见大卫所说的话，就告诉了扫罗；扫罗便打发人叫他来。

chapters.en: And David said to Saul, “Let no man’s heart fail on account of this Philistine. Your servant will go and fight him!”
chapters.zh: 大卫对扫罗说：「人都不必因那非利士人胆怯。你的仆人要去与那非利士人战斗。」

chapters.en: But Saul replied, “You cannot go out against this Philistine to fight him. You are just a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗对大卫说：「你不能去与那非利士人战斗；因为你年纪太轻，他自幼就作战士。」

chapters.en: David replied, “Your servant has been tending his father’s sheep, and whenever a lion or a bear came and carried off a lamb from the flock,
chapters.zh: 大卫对扫罗说：「你仆人为父亲放羊，有时来了狮子，有时来了熊，从群中啣一只羊羔去。

chapters.en: I went after it, struck it down, and delivered the lamb from its mouth. If it reared up against me, I would grab it by its fur, strike it down, and kill it.
chapters.zh: 我就追赶牠，击打牠，将羊羔从牠口中救出来。牠起来要害我，我就揪着牠的胡子，将牠打死。

chapters.en: Your servant has killed lions and bears; this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, for he has defied the armies of the living God.”
chapters.zh: 你仆人曾打死狮子和熊，这未受割礼的非利士人向永生上帝的军队骂阵，也必像狮子和熊一般。」

chapters.en:
David added, “The LORD, who delivered me from the claws of the lion and the bear, will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine.”
“Go,” said Saul, “and may the LORD be with you.”
chapters.zh: 大卫又说：「耶和华救我脱离狮子和熊的爪，也必救我脱离这非利士人的手。」扫罗对大卫说：「你可以去吧！耶和华必与你同在。」

chapters.en: Then Saul clothed David in his own tunic, put a bronze helmet on his head, and dressed him in armor.
chapters.zh: 扫罗就把自己的战衣给大卫穿上，将铜盔给他戴上，又给他穿上铠甲。

chapters.en:
David strapped his sword over the tunic and tried to walk, but he was not accustomed to them.
“I cannot walk in these,” David said to Saul. “I am not accustomed to them.” So David took them off.
chapters.zh: 大卫把刀跨在战衣外，试试能走不能走；因为素来没有穿惯，就对扫罗说：「我穿戴这些不能走，因为素来没有穿惯。」于是摘脱了。

chapters.en: And David took his staff in his hand, selected five smooth stones from the brook, and put them in the pouch of his shepherd’s bag. And with his sling in hand, he approached the Philistine.
chapters.zh: 他手中拿杖，又在溪中挑选了五块光滑石子，放在袋里，就是牧人带的囊里；手中拿着甩石的机弦，就去迎那非利士人。

chapters.en: Now the Philistine came closer and closer to David, with his shield-bearer before him.
chapters.zh: 非利士人也渐渐地迎着大卫来，拿盾牌的走在前头。

chapters.en: When the Philistine looked and saw David, he despised him because he was just a boy, ruddy and handsome.
chapters.zh: 非利士人观看，见了大卫，就藐视他；因为他年轻，面色光红，容貌俊美。

chapters.en: “Am I a dog,” he said to David, “that you come at me with sticks?” And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
chapters.zh: 非利士人对大卫说：「你拿杖到我这里来，我岂是狗呢？」非利士人就指着自己的神咒诅大卫。

chapters.en: “Come here,” he called to David, “and I will give your flesh to the birds of the air and the beasts of the field!”
chapters.zh: 非利士人又对大卫说：「来吧！我将你的肉给空中的飞鸟、田野的走兽吃。」

chapters.en: But David said to the Philistine, “You come against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the LORD of Hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.
chapters.zh: 大卫对非利士人说：「你来攻击我，是靠着刀枪和〔铜〕戟；我来攻击你，是靠着万军之耶和华的名，就是你所怒骂带领以色列军队的上帝。

chapters.en: This day the LORD will deliver you into my hand. This day I will strike you down, cut off your head, and give the carcasses of the Philistine army to the birds of the air and the creatures of the earth. Then the whole world will know that there is a God in Israel.
chapters.zh: 今日耶和华必将你交在我手里。我必杀你，斩你的头，又将非利士军兵的尸首给空中的飞鸟、地上的野兽吃，使普天下的人都知道以色列中有上帝；

chapters.en: And all those assembled here will know that it is not by sword or spear that the LORD saves; for the battle is the LORD’s, and He will give all of you into our hands.”
chapters.zh: 又使这众人知道耶和华使人得胜，不是用刀用枪，因为争战的胜败全在乎耶和华。他必将你们交在我们手里。」

chapters.en: As the Philistine started forward to attack him, David ran quickly toward the battle line to meet him.
chapters.zh: 非利士人起身，迎着大卫前来。大卫急忙迎着非利士人，往战场跑去。

chapters.en: Then David reached into his bag, took out a stone, and slung it, striking the Philistine on the forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell facedown on the ground.
chapters.zh: 大卫用手从囊中掏出一块石子来，用机弦甩去，打中非利士人的额，石子进入额内，他就仆倒，面伏于地。

chapters.en: Thus David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone; without a sword in his hand he struck down the Philistine and killed him.
chapters.zh: 这样，大卫用机弦甩石，胜了那非利士人，打死他；大卫手中却没有刀。

chapters.en:
David ran and stood over him. He grabbed the Philistine’s sword and pulled it from its sheath and killed him, and he cut off his head with the sword.
When the Philistines saw that their hero was dead, they turned and ran.
chapters.zh: 大卫跑去，站在非利士人身旁，将他的刀从鞘中拔出来，杀死他，割了他的头。非利士众人看见他们讨战的勇士死了，就都逃跑。

chapters.en: Then the men of Israel and Judah charged forward with a shout and pursued the Philistines to the entrance of Gath and to the gates of Ekron. And the bodies of the Philistines were strewn along the Shaaraim road to Gath and Ekron.
chapters.zh: 以色列人和犹大人便起身吶喊，追赶非利士人，直到迦特〔注：或译：该〕和以革伦的城门。被杀的非利士人倒在沙拉音的路上，直到迦特和以革伦。

chapters.en: When the Israelites returned from their pursuit of the Philistines, they plundered their camps.
chapters.zh: 以色列人追赶非利士人回来，就夺了他们的营盘。

chapters.en: David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, and he put Goliath’s weapons in his own tent.
chapters.zh: 大卫将那非利士人的头拿到耶路撒冷，却将他军装放在自己的帐棚里。

chapters.en:
As Saul had watched David going out to confront the Philistine, he said to Abner the commander of the army, “Abner, whose son is this young man?”
“As surely as you live, O king,” Abner replied, “I do not know.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗看见大卫去攻击非利士人，就问元帅押尼珥说：「押尼珥啊，那少年人是谁的儿子？」押尼珥说：「我敢在王面前起誓，我不知道。」

chapters.en: “Find out whose son this young man is!” said the king.
chapters.zh: 王说：「你可以问问那幼年人是谁的儿子。」

chapters.en: So when David returned from killing the Philistine, still holding his head in his hand, Abner took him and brought him before Saul.
chapters.zh: 大卫打死非利士人回来，押尼珥领他到扫罗面前，他手中拿着非利士人的头。

chapters.en:
“Whose son are you, young man?” asked Saul.
“I am the son of your servant Jesse of Bethlehem,” David replied.
chapters.zh: 扫罗问他说：「少年人哪，你是谁的儿子？」大卫说：「我是你仆人伯利恒人耶西的儿子。」

chapters.en: After David had finished speaking with Saul, the souls of Jonathan and David were knit together, and Jonathan loved him as himself.
chapters.zh: 大卫对扫罗说完了话，约拿单的心与大卫的心深相契合。约拿单爱大卫，如同爱自己的性命。

chapters.en: And from that day Saul kept David with him and did not let him return to his father’s house.
chapters.zh: 那日扫罗留住大卫，不容他再回父家。

chapters.en: Then Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself.
chapters.zh: 约拿单爱大卫如同爱自己的性命，就与他结盟。

chapters.en: And Jonathan removed the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his tunic, his sword, his bow, and his belt.
chapters.zh: 约拿单从身上脱下外袍，给了大卫，又将战衣、刀、弓、腰带都给了他。

chapters.en: So David marched out and prospered in everything Saul sent him to do, and Saul set him over the men of war. And this was pleasing in the sight of all the people, and of Saul’s officers as well.
chapters.zh: 扫罗无论差遣大卫往何处去，他都做事精明。扫罗就立他作战士长，众百姓和扫罗的臣仆无不喜悦。

chapters.en: As the troops were returning home after David had killed the Philistine, the women came out of all the cities of Israel to meet King Saul with singing and dancing, with joyful songs, and with tambourines and other instruments.
chapters.zh: 大卫打死了那非利士人，同众人回来的时候，妇女们从以色列各城里出来，欢欢喜喜，打鼓击磬，歌唱跳舞，迎接扫罗王。

chapters.en:
And as the women danced, they sang out:
“Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands.”
chapters.zh: 众妇女舞蹈唱和，说：「扫罗杀死千千，大卫杀死万万。」

chapters.en: And Saul was furious and resented this song. “They have ascribed tens of thousands to David,” he said, “but only thousands to me. What more can he have but the kingdom?”
chapters.zh: 扫罗甚发怒，不喜悦这话，就说：「将万万归大卫，千千归我，只剩下王位没有给他了。」

chapters.en: And from that day forward Saul kept a jealous eye on David.
chapters.zh: 从这日起，扫罗就怒视大卫。

chapters.en: The next day a spirit of distress sent from God came upon Saul, and he prophesied inside the house while David played the harp as usual. Now Saul was holding a spear,
chapters.zh: 次日，从上帝那里来的恶魔大大降在扫罗身上，他就在家中胡言乱语。大卫照常弹琴，扫罗手里拿着枪。

chapters.en: and he hurled it, thinking, “I will pin David to the wall.” But David eluded him twice.
chapters.zh: 扫罗把枪一抡，心里说，我要将大卫刺透，钉在墙上。大卫躲避他两次。

chapters.en: So Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with David but had departed from Saul.
chapters.zh: 扫罗惧怕大卫；因为耶和华离开自己，与大卫同在。

chapters.en: Therefore Saul sent David away and gave him command of a thousand men. David led the troops out to battle and back,
chapters.zh: 所以扫罗使大卫离开自己，立他为千夫长，他就领兵出入。

chapters.en: and he continued to prosper in all his ways, because the LORD was with him.
chapters.zh: 大卫做事无不精明，耶和华也与他同在。

chapters.en: When Saul saw that David was very successful, he was afraid of him.
chapters.zh: 扫罗见大卫做事精明，就甚怕他。

chapters.en: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he was leading them out to battle and back.
chapters.zh: 但以色列和犹大众人都爱大卫，因为他领他们出入。

chapters.en: Then Saul said to David, “Here is my older daughter Merab. I will give her to you in marriage. Only be valiant for me and fight the LORD’s battles.” But Saul was thinking, “I need not raise my hand against him; let the hand of the Philistines be against him.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗对大卫说：「我将大女儿米拉给你为妻，只要你为我奋勇，为耶和华争战。」扫罗心里说：「我不好亲手害他，要藉非利士人的手害他。」

chapters.en: And David said to Saul, “Who am I, and what is my family or my father’s clan in Israel, that I should become the son-in-law of the king?”
chapters.zh: 大卫对扫罗说：「我是谁，我是什么出身，我父家在以色列中是何等的家，岂敢作王的女婿呢？」

chapters.en: So when it was time to give Saul’s daughter Merab to David, she was given in marriage to Adriel of Meholah.
chapters.zh: 扫罗的女儿米拉到了当给大卫的时候，扫罗却给了米何拉人亚得列为妻。

chapters.en: Now Saul’s daughter Michal loved David, and when this was reported to Saul, it pleased him.
chapters.zh: 扫罗的次女米甲爱大卫。有人告诉扫罗，扫罗就喜悦。

chapters.en: “I will give her to David,” Saul thought, “so that she may be a snare to him, and the hand of the Philistines may be against him.” So Saul said to David, “For a second time now you can be my son-in-law.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗心里说：「我将这女儿给大卫，作他的网罗，好藉非利士人的手害他。」所以扫罗对大卫说：「你今日可以第二次作我的女婿。」

chapters.en: Then Saul ordered his servants, “Speak to David privately and tell him, ‘Behold, the king is pleased with you, and all his servants love you. Now therefore, become his son-in-law.’”
chapters.zh: 扫罗吩咐臣仆〔说〕：「你们暗中对大卫说：『王喜悦你，王的臣仆也都喜爱你，所以你当作王的女婿。』」

chapters.en: But when Saul’s servants relayed these words to David, he replied, “Does it seem trivial in your sight to be the son-in-law of the king? I am a poor man and lightly esteemed.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗的臣仆就照这话说给大卫听。大卫说：「你们以为作王的女婿是一件小事吗？我是贫穷卑微的人。」

chapters.en: And the servants told Saul what David had said.
chapters.zh: 扫罗的臣仆回奏说，大卫所说的如此如此。

chapters.en: Saul replied, “Say to David, ‘The king desires no other dowry but a hundred Philistine foreskins as revenge on his enemies.’” But Saul intended to cause David’s death at the hands of the Philistines.
chapters.zh: 扫罗说：「你们要对大卫这样说：『王不要什么聘礼，只要一百非利士人的阳皮，好在王的仇敌身上报仇。』」扫罗的意思要使大卫丧在非利士人的手里。

chapters.en: When the servants reported these terms to David, he was pleased to become the king’s son-in-law. Before the wedding day arrived,
chapters.zh: 扫罗的臣仆将这话告诉大卫，大卫就欢喜作王的女婿。日期还没有到，

chapters.en: David and his men went out and killed two hundred Philistines. He brought their foreskins and presented them as payment in full to become the king’s son-in-law. Then Saul gave his daughter Michal to David in marriage.
chapters.zh: 大卫和跟随他的人起身前往，杀了二百非利士人，将阳皮满数交给王，为要作王的女婿。于是扫罗将女儿米甲给大卫为妻。

chapters.en: When Saul realized that the LORD was with David and that his daughter Michal loved David,
chapters.zh: 扫罗见耶和华与大卫同在，又知道女儿米甲爱大卫，

chapters.en: he grew even more afraid of David. So from then on Saul was David’s enemy.
chapters.zh: 就更怕大卫，常作大卫的仇敌。

chapters.en: Every time the Philistine commanders came out for battle, David was more successful than all of Saul’s officers, so that his name was highly esteemed.
chapters.zh: 每逢非利士军长出来〔打仗〕，大卫比扫罗的臣仆做事精明，因此他的名被人尊重。

chapters.en:
Then Saul ordered his son Jonathan and all his servants to kill David.
But Jonathan delighted greatly in David,
chapters.zh: 扫罗对他儿子约拿单和众臣仆说，要杀大卫；扫罗的儿子约拿单却甚喜爱大卫。

chapters.en: so he warned David, saying, “My father Saul intends to kill you. Be on your guard in the morning; find a secret place and hide there.
chapters.zh: 约拿单告诉大卫说：「我父扫罗想要杀你，所以明日早晨你要小心，到一个僻静地方藏身。

chapters.en: I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, so I can ask about you. And if I find out anything, I will tell you.”
chapters.zh: 我就出到你所藏的田里，站在我父亲旁边与他谈论。我看他情形怎样，我必告诉你。」

chapters.en: Then Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul and said to him, “The king should not sin against his servant David; he has not sinned against you. In fact, his actions have been highly beneficial to you.
chapters.zh: 约拿单向他父亲扫罗替大卫说好话，说：「王不可得罪王的仆人大卫；因为他未曾得罪你，他所行的都与你大有益处。

chapters.en: He took his life in his hands when he struck down the Philistine, and the LORD worked a great salvation for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced, so why would you sin against innocent blood by killing David for no reason?”
chapters.zh: 他拼命杀那非利士人，耶和华为以色列众人大行拯救；那时你看见，甚是欢喜，现在为何无故要杀大卫，流无辜人的血，自己取罪呢？」

chapters.en: Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan and swore an oath: “As surely as the LORD lives, David will not be put to death.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗听了约拿单的话，就指着永生的耶和华起誓说：「我必不杀他。」

chapters.en: So Jonathan summoned David and told him all these things. Then Jonathan brought David to Saul, and David was with Saul as before.
chapters.zh: 约拿单叫大卫来，把这一切事告诉他，带他去见扫罗。他就仍然侍立在扫罗面前。

chapters.en: When war broke out again, David went out and fought the Philistines and struck them with such a mighty blow that they fled before him.
chapters.zh: 此后又有争战的事。大卫出去与非利士人打仗，大大杀败他们，他们就在他面前逃跑。

chapters.en: But as Saul was sitting in his house with his spear in his hand, a spirit of distress from the LORD came upon him. While David was playing the harp,
chapters.zh: 从耶和华那里来的恶魔又降在扫罗身上（扫罗手里拿枪坐在屋里），大卫就用手弹琴。

chapters.en: Saul tried to pin him to the wall with his spear. But David eluded him and the spear struck the wall. And David fled and escaped that night.
chapters.zh: 扫罗用枪想要刺透大卫，钉在墙上，他却躲开，扫罗的枪刺入墙内。当夜大卫逃走，躲避了。

chapters.en: Then Saul sent messengers to David’s house to watch him and kill him in the morning. But David’s wife Michal warned him, “If you do not run for your life tonight, tomorrow you will be dead!”
chapters.zh: 扫罗打发人到大卫的房屋那里窥探他，要等到天亮杀他。大卫的妻米甲对他说：「你今夜若不逃命，明日你要被杀。」

chapters.en: So Michal lowered David from the window, and he ran away and escaped.
chapters.zh: 于是米甲将大卫从窗户里缒下去，大卫就逃走，躲避了。

chapters.en: Then Michal took a household idol and laid it in the bed, placed some goat hair on its head, and covered it with a garment.
chapters.zh: 米甲把家中的神像放在床上，头枕在山羊毛装的枕头上，用被遮盖。

chapters.en: When Saul sent the messengers to seize David, Michal said, “He is ill.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗打发人去捉拿大卫，米甲说：「他病了。」

chapters.en: But Saul sent the messengers back to see David and told them, “Bring him up to me in his bed so I can kill him.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗又打发人去看大卫，说：「当连床将他抬来，我好杀他。」

chapters.en: And when the messengers entered, there was the idol in the bed with the goat hair on its head.
chapters.zh: 使者进去，看见床上有神像，头枕在山羊毛装的枕头上。

chapters.en:
And Saul said to Michal, “Why did you deceive me like this? You sent my enemy away, and he has escaped!”
Michal replied, “He said to me, ‘Help me get away, or I will kill you!’”
chapters.zh: 扫罗对米甲说：「你为什么这样欺哄我，放我仇敌逃走呢？」米甲回答说：「他对我说：『你放我走，不然我要杀你。』」

chapters.en: So David ran away and escaped. And he went to Samuel at Ramah and told him all that Saul had done to him. Then he and Samuel went to Naioth and stayed there.
chapters.zh: 大卫逃避，来到拉玛见撒母耳，将扫罗向他所行的事述说了一遍。他和撒母耳就往拿约去居住。

chapters.en: When Saul was told that David was at Naioth in Ramah,
chapters.zh: 有人告诉扫罗，说大卫在拉玛的拿约。

chapters.en: he sent messengers to seize him. But when they saw the group of prophets prophesying, with Samuel leading them, the Spirit of God came upon them, and Saul’s messengers also began to prophesy.
chapters.zh: 扫罗打发人去捉拿大卫。去的人见有一班先知都受感说话，撒母耳站在其中监管他们；打发去的人也受上帝的灵感动说话。

chapters.en:
When this was reported to Saul, he sent more messengers, but they began to prophesy as well.
So Saul tried again and sent messengers a third time, and even they began to prophesy.
chapters.zh: 有人将这事告诉扫罗，他又打发人去，他们也受感说话。扫罗第三次打发人去，他们也受感说话。

chapters.en:
Finally, Saul himself left for Ramah and came to the large cistern at Secu, where he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?”
“At Naioth in Ramah,” he was told.
chapters.zh: 然后扫罗自己往拉玛去，到了西沽的大井，问人说：「撒母耳和大卫在哪里呢？」有人说：「在拉玛的拿约。」

chapters.en: So Saul went to Naioth in Ramah. But the Spirit of God came upon even Saul, and he walked along prophesying until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
chapters.zh: 他就往拉玛的拿约去。上帝的灵也感动他，一面走一面说话，直到拉玛的拿约。

chapters.en: Then Saul stripped off his robes and also prophesied before Samuel. And he collapsed and lay naked all that day and night. That is why it is said, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
chapters.zh: 他就脱了衣服，在撒母耳面前受感说话，一昼一夜露体躺卧。因此有句俗语说：「扫罗也列在先知中吗？」

chapters.en: Then David fled from Naioth in Ramah. He came to Jonathan and asked, “What have I done? What is my iniquity? How have I sinned against your father, that he wants to take my life?”
chapters.zh: 大卫从拉玛的拿约逃跑，来到约拿单那里，对他说：「我做了什么？有什么罪孽呢？在你父亲面前犯了什么罪，他竟寻索我的性命呢？」

chapters.en: “Far from it!” Jonathan replied. “You will not die. Indeed, my father does nothing, great or small, without telling me. So why would he hide this matter from me? This cannot be true!”
chapters.zh: 约拿单回答说：「断然不是！你必不致死。我父做事，无论大小，没有不叫我知道的。怎么独有这事隐瞒我呢？决不如此。」

chapters.en: But David again vowed, “Your father knows very well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he has said, ‘Jonathan must not know of this, or he will be grieved.’ As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, there is but a step between me and death.”
chapters.zh: 大卫又起誓说：「你父亲准知我在你眼前蒙恩。他心里说，不如不叫约拿单知道，恐怕他愁烦。我指着永生的耶和华，又敢在你面前起誓，我离死不过一步。」

chapters.en: Then Jonathan said to David, “Whatever you desire, I will do for you.”
chapters.zh: 约拿单对大卫说：「你心里所求的，我必为你成就。」

chapters.en: So David told him, “Look, tomorrow is the New Moon, and I am supposed to dine with the king. Instead, let me go and hide in the field until the third evening from now.
chapters.zh: 大卫对约拿单说：「明日是初一，我当与王同席，求你容我去藏在田野，直到第三日晚上。

chapters.en: If your father misses me at all, tell him, ‘David urgently requested my permission to hurry to Bethlehem, his hometown, because there is an annual sacrifice for his whole clan.’
chapters.zh: 你父亲若见我不在席上，你就说：『大卫切求我许他回本城伯利恒去，因为他全家在那里献年祭。』

chapters.en: If he says, ‘Good,’ then your servant is safe, but if he is enraged, you will know he has evil intentions.
chapters.zh: 你父亲若说好，仆人就平安了；他若发怒，你就知道他决意要害我。

chapters.en: Therefore show kindness to your servant, for you have brought me into a covenant with you before the LORD. If there is iniquity in me, then kill me yourself; why should you bring me to your father?”
chapters.zh: 求你施恩与仆人，因你在耶和华面前曾与仆人结盟。我若有罪，不如你自己杀我，何必将我交给你父亲呢？」

chapters.en: “Never!” Jonathan replied. “If I ever found out that my father had evil intentions against you, would I not tell you?”
chapters.zh: 约拿单说：「断无此事！我若知道我父亲决意害你，我岂不告诉你呢？」

chapters.en: Then David asked Jonathan, “Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?”
chapters.zh: 大卫对约拿单说：「你父亲若用厉言回答你，谁来告诉我呢？」

chapters.en:
“Come,” he replied, “let us go out to the field.”
So the two of them went out into the field,
chapters.zh: 约拿单对大卫说：「你我且往田野去。」二人就往田野去了。

chapters.en: and Jonathan said, “By the LORD, the God of Israel, I will sound out my father by this time tomorrow or the next day. If he is favorable toward you, will I not send for you and tell you?
chapters.zh: 约拿单对大卫说：「愿耶和华－以色列的上帝〔为证〕。明日约在这时候，或第三日，我探我父亲的意思，若向你有好意，我岂不打发人告诉你吗？

chapters.en: But if my father intends to bring evil on you, then may the LORD punish me, and ever so severely, if I do not tell you and send you on your way in safety. May the LORD be with you, just as He has been with my father.
chapters.zh: 我父亲若有意害你，我不告诉你使你平平安安地走，愿耶和华重重地降罚与我。愿耶和华与你同在，如同从前与我父亲同在一样。

chapters.en: And as long as I live, treat me with the LORD’s loving devotion, that I may not die,
chapters.zh: 你要照耶和华的慈爱恩待我，不但我活着的时候免我死亡，

chapters.en: and do not ever cut off your loving devotion from my household—not even when the LORD cuts off every one of David’s enemies from the face of the earth.”
chapters.zh: 就是我死后，耶和华从地上剪除你仇敌的时候，你也永不可向我家绝了恩惠。」

chapters.en: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, “May the LORD hold David’s enemies accountable.”
chapters.zh: 于是约拿单与大卫家结盟，〔说〕：「愿耶和华藉大卫的仇敌追讨〔背约〕的罪。」

chapters.en: And Jonathan had David reaffirm his vow out of love for him, for Jonathan loved David as he loved himself.
chapters.zh: 约拿单因爱大卫如同爱自己的性命，就使他再起誓。

chapters.en: Then Jonathan said to David, “Tomorrow is the New Moon, and you will be missed, because your seat will be empty.
chapters.zh: 约拿单对他说：「明日是初一，你的座位空设，人必理会你不在那里。

chapters.en: When you have stayed three days, hurry down to the place you hid on the day this trouble began, and remain beside the stone Ezel.
chapters.zh: 你等三日，就要速速下去，到你从前遇事所藏的地方，在以色磐石那里等候。

chapters.en: I will shoot three arrows to the side of it, as if I were aiming at a target.
chapters.zh: 我要向磐石旁边射三箭，如同射箭靶一样。

chapters.en: Then I will send a boy and say, ‘Go, find the arrows!’ Now, if I expressly say to him, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you; bring them,’ then come, because as surely as the LORD lives, it is safe for you, and there is no danger.
chapters.zh: 我要打发童子，〔说〕：『去把箭找来。』我若对童子说：『箭在后头，把箭拿来』，你就可以回来；我指着永生的耶和华起誓，你必平安无事。

chapters.en: But if I say to the young man, ‘Look, the arrows are beyond you,’ then you must go, for the LORD has sent you away.
chapters.zh: 我若对童子说：『箭在前头』，你就要去，因为是耶和华打发你去的。

chapters.en: And as for the matter you and I have discussed, the LORD is a witness between you and me forever.”
chapters.zh: 至于你我今日所说的话，有耶和华在你我中间〔为证〕，直到永远。」

chapters.en: So David hid in the field, and when the New Moon had come, the king sat down to eat.
chapters.zh: 大卫就去藏在田野。到了初一日，王坐席要吃饭。

chapters.en: He sat in his usual place by the wall, opposite Jonathan and beside Abner, but David’s place was empty.
chapters.zh: 王照常坐在靠墙的位上，约拿单侍立，押尼珥坐在扫罗旁边，大卫的座位空设。

chapters.en: Saul said nothing that day because he thought, “Something has happened to David to make him ceremonially unclean—surely he is unclean.”
chapters.zh: 然而这日扫罗没有说什么，他想大卫遇事，偶染不洁，他必定是不洁。

chapters.en: But on the day after the New Moon, the second day, David’s place was still empty, and Saul asked his son Jonathan, “Why hasn’t the son of Jesse come to the meal either yesterday or today?”
chapters.zh: 初二日大卫的座位还空设。扫罗问他儿子约拿单说：「耶西的儿子为何昨日、今日没有来吃饭呢？」

chapters.en: Jonathan answered, “David urgently requested my permission to go to Bethlehem,
chapters.zh: 约拿单回答扫罗说：「大卫切求我容他往伯利恒去。

chapters.en: saying, ‘Please let me go, because our clan is holding a sacrifice in the city, and my brother has told me to be there. So now, if I have found favor in your eyes, please let me go and see my brothers.’ That is why he has not come to the king’s table.”
chapters.zh: 他说：『求你容我去，因为我家在城里有献祭的事；我长兄吩咐我去。如今我若在你眼前蒙恩，求你容我去见我的弟兄』；所以大卫没有赴王的席。」

chapters.en: Then Saul’s anger burned against Jonathan, and he said to him, “You son of a perverse and rebellious woman! Do I not know that you have chosen the son of Jesse to your own shame and to the shame of the mother who bore you?
chapters.zh: 扫罗向约拿单发怒，对他说：「你这顽梗背逆之妇人所生的，我岂不知道你喜悦耶西的儿子，自取羞辱，以致你母亲露体蒙羞吗？

chapters.en: For as long as the son of Jesse lives on this earth, neither you nor your kingdom shall be established. Now send for him and bring him to me, for he must surely die!”
chapters.zh: 耶西的儿子若在世间活着，你和你的国位必站立不住。现在你要打发人去，将他捉拿交给我；他是该死的。」

chapters.en: “Why must he be put to death?” Jonathan replied. “What has he done?”
chapters.zh: 约拿单对父亲扫罗说：「他为什么该死呢？他做了什么呢？」

chapters.en: Then Saul hurled his spear at Jonathan to kill him. So Jonathan knew that his father was determined to kill David.
chapters.zh: 扫罗向约拿单抡枪要刺他，约拿单就知道他父亲决意要杀大卫。

chapters.en: Jonathan got up from the table in fierce anger and did not eat any food that second day of the month, for he was grieved by his father’s shameful treatment of David.
chapters.zh: 于是约拿单气忿忿地从席上起来，在这初二日没有吃饭。他因见父亲羞辱大卫，就为大卫愁烦。

chapters.en: In the morning Jonathan went out to the field for the appointment with David, and a small boy was with him.
chapters.zh: 次日早晨，约拿单按着与大卫约会的时候出到田野，有一个童子跟随。

chapters.en: He said to the boy, “Run and find the arrows I shoot.” And as the boy ran, Jonathan shot an arrow beyond him.
chapters.zh: 约拿单对童子说：「你跑去，把我所射的箭找来。」童子跑去，约拿单就把箭射在童子前头。

chapters.en: When the boy reached the place where Jonathan’s arrow had fallen, Jonathan called to him, “Isn’t the arrow beyond you?”
chapters.zh: 童子到了约拿单落箭之地，约拿单呼叫童子说：「箭不是在你前头吗？」

chapters.en: Then Jonathan cried out, “Hurry! Make haste! Do not delay!” So the boy picked up the arrow and returned to his master.
chapters.zh: 约拿单又呼叫童子说：「速速地去，不要迟延！」童子就拾起箭来，回到主人那里。

chapters.en: But the boy did not know anything; only Jonathan and David knew the arrangement.
chapters.zh: 童子却不知道这是什么意思，只有约拿单和大卫知道。

chapters.en: Then Jonathan gave his equipment to the boy and said, “Go, take it back to the city.”
chapters.zh: 约拿单将弓箭交给童子，吩咐说：「你拿到城里去。」

chapters.en: When the young man had gone, David got up from the south side of the stone, fell facedown, and bowed three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and wept together—though David wept more.
chapters.zh: 童子一去，大卫就从〔磐石〕的南边出来，俯伏在地，拜了三拜；二人亲嘴，彼此哭泣，大卫哭得更恸。

chapters.en: And Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace, for the two of us have sworn in the name of the LORD, saying, ‘May the LORD be a witness between you and me, and between your descendants and mine forever.’” Then David got up and departed, and Jonathan went back into the city.
chapters.zh: 约拿单对大卫说：「我们二人曾指着耶和华的名起誓说：『愿耶和华在你我中间，并你我后裔中间〔为证〕，直到永远。』如今你平平安安地去吧！」大卫就起身走了；约拿单也回城里去了。

chapters.en: Then David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. And when Ahimelech met David, he trembled and asked him, “Why are you alone? Why is no one with you?”
chapters.zh: 大卫到了挪伯祭司亚希米勒那里，亚希米勒战战兢兢地出来迎接他，问他说：「你为什么独自来，没有人跟随呢？」

chapters.en: “The king has given me a mission,” David replied. “He told me no one is to know about the mission on which I am sending you. And I have directed my young men to meet me at a certain place.
chapters.zh: 大卫回答祭司亚希米勒说：「王吩咐我一件事说：『我差遣你委托你的这件事，不要使人知道。』故此我已派定少年人在某处等候我。

chapters.en: Now then, what do you have on hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever can be found.”
chapters.zh: 现在你手下有什么？求你给我五个饼或是别样的食物。」

chapters.en: “There is no common bread on hand,” the priest replied, “but there is some consecrated bread—provided that the young men have kept themselves from women.”
chapters.zh: 祭司对大卫说：「我手下没有寻常的饼，只有圣饼；若少年人没有亲近妇人才可以给。」

chapters.en: David answered, “Women have indeed been kept from us, as is usual when I set out. And the bodies of the young men are holy even on common missions. How much more so today!”
chapters.zh: 大卫对祭司说：「实在约有三日我们没有亲近妇人；我出来的时候，虽是寻常行路，少年人的器皿还是洁净的；何况今日不更是洁净吗？」

chapters.en: So the priest gave him the consecrated bread, since there was no bread there but the Bread of the Presence, which had been removed from before the LORD and replaced with hot bread on the day it was taken away.
chapters.zh: 祭司就拿圣〔饼〕给他；因为在那里没有别样饼，只有更换新饼，从耶和华面前撤下来的陈设饼。

chapters.en: Now one of Saul’s servants was there that day, detained before the LORD. And his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief shepherd for Saul.
chapters.zh: （当日有扫罗的一个臣子留在耶和华面前。他名叫多益，是以东人，作扫罗的司牧长。）

chapters.en: Then David asked Ahimelech, “Is there not a spear or sword on hand here? For I have brought neither my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king’s mission was urgent.”
chapters.zh: 大卫问亚希米勒说：「你手下有枪有刀没有？因为王的事甚急，连刀剑器械我都没有带。」

chapters.en:
The priest replied, “The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you killed in the Valley of Elah, is here; it is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you want, you may take it. For there is no other but this one here.”
And David said, “There is none like it; give it to me.”
chapters.zh: 祭司说：「你在以拉谷杀非利士人歌利亚的那刀在这里，裹在布中，放在以弗得后边，你要就可以拿去；除此以外，再没有别的。」大卫说：「这刀没有可比的！求你给我。」

chapters.en: That day David fled from Saul and went to Achish king of Gath.
chapters.zh: 那日大卫起来，躲避扫罗，逃到迦特王亚吉那里。

chapters.en:
But the servants of Achish said to him, “Is this not David, the king of the land? Did they not sing about him in their dances, saying:
‘Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands’?”
chapters.zh: 亚吉的臣仆对亚吉说：「这不是〔以色列〕国王大卫吗？那里的妇女跳舞唱和，不是指着他说『扫罗杀死千千，大卫杀死万万』吗？」

chapters.en: Now David took these words to heart and was very much afraid of Achish the king of Gath.
chapters.zh: 大卫将这话放在心里，甚惧怕迦特王亚吉，

chapters.en: So he changed his behavior before them and feigned madness in their hands; he scratched on the doors of the gate and let his saliva run down his beard.
chapters.zh: 就在众人面前改变了寻常的举动，在他们手下假装疯癫，在城门的门扇上胡写乱画，使唾沫流在胡子上。

chapters.en: Then Achish said to his servants, “Look, you can see that the man is insane! Why have you brought him to me?
chapters.zh: 亚吉对臣仆说：「你们看，这人是疯子。为什么带他到我这里来呢？

chapters.en: Am I in need of madmen, that you have brought this man to rave in my presence? Must this man come into my house?”
chapters.zh: 我岂缺少疯子，你们带这人来在我面前疯癫吗？这人岂可进我的家呢？」

chapters.en: So David left Gath and took refuge in the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and the rest of his father’s household heard about it, they went down to him there.
chapters.zh: 大卫就离开那里，逃到亚杜兰洞。他的弟兄和他父亲的全家听见了，就都下到他那里。

chapters.en: And all who were distressed or indebted or discontented rallied around him, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him.
chapters.zh: 凡受窘迫的、欠债的、心里苦恼的都聚集到大卫那里；大卫就作他们的头目，跟随他的约有四百人。

chapters.en: From there David went to Mizpeh of Moab, where he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and mother stay with you until I learn what God will do for me.”
chapters.zh: 大卫从那里往摩押的米斯巴去，对摩押王说：「求你容我父母搬来，住在你们这里，等我知道上帝要为我怎样行。」

chapters.en: So he left them in the care of the king of Moab, and they stayed with him the whole time David was in the stronghold.
chapters.zh: 大卫领他父母到摩押王面前。大卫住山寨多少日子，他父母也住摩押王那里多少日子。

chapters.en: Then the prophet Gad said to David, “Do not stay in the stronghold. Depart and go into the land of Judah.” So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.
chapters.zh: 先知迦得对大卫说：「你不要住在山寨，要往犹大地去。」大卫就离开那里，进入哈列的树林。

chapters.en: Soon Saul learned that David and his men had been discovered. At that time Saul was sitting under the tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibeah, with his spear in hand and all his servants standing around him.
chapters.zh: 扫罗在基比亚的拉玛，坐在垂丝柳树下，手里拿着枪，众臣仆侍立在左右。扫罗听见大卫和跟随他的人在何处，

chapters.en: Then Saul said to his servants, “Listen, men of Benjamin! Is the son of Jesse giving all of you fields and vineyards and making you commanders of thousands or hundreds?
chapters.zh: 就对左右侍立的臣仆说：「便雅悯人哪，你们要听我的话！耶西的儿子能将田地和葡萄园赐给你们各人吗？能立你们各人作千夫长百夫长吗？

chapters.en: Is that why all of you have conspired against me? Not one of you told me that my own son had made a covenant with the son of Jesse. Not one of you has shown concern for me or revealed to me that my son has stirred up my own servant to lie in wait against me, as is the case today.”
chapters.zh: 你们竟都结党害我！我的儿子与耶西的儿子结盟的时候，无人告诉我；我的儿子挑唆我的臣子谋害我，就如今日的光景，也无人告诉我，为我忧虑。」

chapters.en: But Doeg the Edomite, who had stationed himself with Saul’s servants, answered: “I saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob.
chapters.zh: 那时以东人多益站在扫罗的臣仆中，对他说：「我曾看见耶西的儿子到了挪伯，亚希突的儿子亚希米勒那里。

chapters.en: Ahimelech inquired of the LORD for him and gave him provisions. He also gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”
chapters.zh: 亚希米勒为他求问耶和华，又给他食物，并给他〔杀〕非利士人歌利亚的刀。」

chapters.en: Then the king sent messengers to summon Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and his father’s whole family, who were priests at Nob. And all of them came to the king.
chapters.zh: 王就打发人将祭司亚希突的儿子亚希米勒和他父亲的全家，就是住挪伯的祭司都召了来；他们就来见王。

chapters.en:
“Listen now, son of Ahitub,” said Saul.
“Here I am, my lord,” he replied.
chapters.zh: 扫罗说：「亚希突的儿子，要听我的话！」他回答说：「主啊，我在这里。」

chapters.en: And Saul asked him, “Why have you and the son of Jesse conspired against me? You gave him bread and a sword and inquired of God for him so that he could rise up against me to lie in wait, as he is doing today.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗对他说：「你为什么与耶西的儿子结党害我，将食物和刀给他，又为他求问上帝，使他起来谋害我，就如今日的光景？」

chapters.en: Ahimelech answered the king, “Who among all your servants is as faithful as David, the king’s son-in-law, the captain of your bodyguard and honored in your house?
chapters.zh: 亚希米勒回答王说：「王的臣仆中有谁比大卫忠心呢？他是王的女婿，又是王的参谋，并且在王家中是尊贵的。

chapters.en: Was that day the first time I inquired of God for him? Far be it from me! Let not the king accuse your servant or any of my father’s household, for your servant knew nothing of this whole affair—not in part or in whole.”
chapters.zh: 我岂是从今日才为他求问上帝呢？断不是这样！王不要将罪归我和我父的全家；因为这事，无论大小，仆人都不知道。」

chapters.en: But the king replied, “You will surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house!”
chapters.zh: 王说：「亚希米勒啊，你和你父的全家都是该死的！」

chapters.en:
Then the king ordered the guards at his side, “Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because they too sided with David. For they knew he was fleeing, but they did not tell me.”
But the king’s servants would not lift a hand to strike the priests of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 王就吩咐左右的侍卫说：「你们去杀耶和华的祭司；因为他们帮助大卫，又知道大卫逃跑，竟没有告诉我。」扫罗的臣子却不肯伸手杀耶和华的祭司。

chapters.en:
So the king ordered Doeg, “You turn and strike down the priests!”
And Doeg the Edomite turned and struck down the priests himself. On that day he killed eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.
chapters.zh: 王吩咐多益说：「你去杀祭司吧！」以东人多益就去杀祭司，那日杀了穿细麻布以弗得的八十五人；

chapters.en: He also put to the sword Nob, the city of the priests, with its men and women, children and infants, oxen, donkeys, and sheep.
chapters.zh: 又用刀将祭司城挪伯中的男女、孩童、吃奶的，和牛、羊、驴尽都杀灭。

chapters.en: But one of the sons of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped. His name was Abiathar, and he fled to David.
chapters.zh: 亚希突的儿子亚希米勒有一个儿子，名叫亚比亚他，逃到大卫那里。

chapters.en: And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 亚比亚他将扫罗杀耶和华祭司的事告诉大卫。

chapters.en: Then David said to Abiathar, “I knew that Doeg the Edomite was there that day, and that he was sure to tell Saul. I myself am responsible for the lives of everyone in your father’s house.
chapters.zh: 大卫对亚比亚他说：「那日我见以东人多益在那里，就知道他必告诉扫罗。你父的全家〔丧〕命，都是因我的缘故。

chapters.en: Stay with me; do not be afraid, for he who seeks your life is seeking mine as well. You will be safe with me.”
chapters.zh: 你可以住在我这里，不要惧怕。因为寻索你命的就是寻索我的命；你在我这里可得保全。」

chapters.en: Now it was reported to David, “Look, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and looting the threshing floors.”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉大卫说：「非利士人攻击基伊拉，抢夺禾场。」

chapters.en:
So David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go and attack these Philistines?”
And the LORD said to David, “Go and attack the Philistines and save Keilah.”
chapters.zh: 所以大卫求问耶和华说：「我去攻打那些非利士人可以不可以？」耶和华对大卫说：「你可以去攻打非利士人，拯救基伊拉。」

chapters.en: But David’s men said to him, “Look, we are afraid here in Judah; how much more if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?”
chapters.zh: 跟随大卫的人对他说：「我们在犹大地这里尚且惧怕，何况往基伊拉去攻打非利士人的军旅呢？」

chapters.en: Once again, David inquired of the LORD, and the LORD answered him: “Go at once to Keilah, for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand.”
chapters.zh: 大卫又求问耶和华。耶和华回答说：「你起身下基伊拉去，我必将非利士人交在你手里。」

chapters.en: Then David and his men went to Keilah, fought against the Philistines, and carried off their livestock, striking them with a mighty blow. So David saved the people of Keilah.
chapters.zh: 大卫和跟随他的人往基伊拉去，与非利士人打仗，大大杀败他们，又夺获他们的牲畜。这样，大卫救了基伊拉的居民。

chapters.en: (Now Abiathar son of Ahimelech had brought the ephod with him when he fled to David at Keilah.)
chapters.zh: 亚希米勒的儿子亚比亚他逃到基伊拉见大卫的时候，手里拿着以弗得。

chapters.en: When Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah, he said, “God has delivered him into my hand, for he has trapped himself by entering a town with gates and bars.”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉扫罗说：「大卫到了基伊拉。」扫罗说：「他进了有门有闩的城，困闭在里头；这是上帝将他交在我手里了。」

chapters.en: Then Saul summoned all his troops to go to war at Keilah and besiege David and his men.
chapters.zh: 于是扫罗招聚众民，要下去攻打基伊拉城，围困大卫和跟随他的人。

chapters.en: When David learned that Saul was plotting evil against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod.”
chapters.zh: 大卫知道扫罗设计谋害他，就对祭司亚比亚他说：「将以弗得拿过来。」

chapters.en: And David said, “O LORD, God of Israel, Your servant has heard that Saul intends to come to Keilah and destroy the city on my account.
chapters.zh: 大卫祷告说：「耶和华－以色列的上帝啊，你仆人听真了扫罗要往基伊拉来，为我的缘故灭城。

chapters.en:
Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me into his hand? Will Saul come down, as Your servant has heard? O LORD, God of Israel, please tell Your servant.”
“He will,” said the LORD.
chapters.zh: 基伊拉人将我交在扫罗手里不交？扫罗照着你仆人所听的话下来不下来？耶和华－以色列的上帝啊，求你指示仆人！」耶和华说：「扫罗必下来。」

chapters.en:
So David asked, “Will the citizens of Keilah surrender me and my men into the hand of Saul?”
“They will,” said the LORD.
chapters.zh: 大卫又说：「基伊拉人将我和跟随我的人交在扫罗手里不交？」耶和华说：「必交出来。」

chapters.en: Then David and his men, about six hundred strong, set out and departed from Keilah, moving from place to place. When Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, he declined to go forth.
chapters.zh: 大卫和跟随他的约有六百人，就起身出了基伊拉，往他们所能往的地方去。有人告诉扫罗，大卫离开基伊拉逃走；于是扫罗不出来了。

chapters.en: And David stayed in the wilderness strongholds and in the hill country of the Wilderness of Ziph. Day after day Saul searched for him, but God would not deliver David into his hand.
chapters.zh: 大卫住在旷野的山寨里，常在西弗旷野的山地。扫罗天天寻索大卫，上帝却不将大卫交在他手里。

chapters.en: While David was in Horesh in the Wilderness of Ziph, he saw that Saul had come out to take his life.
chapters.zh: 大卫知道扫罗出来寻索他的命。那时，他住在西弗旷野的树林里；

chapters.en: And Saul’s son Jonathan came to David in Horesh and strengthened his hand in God,
chapters.zh: 扫罗的儿子约拿单起身，往那树林里去见大卫，使他倚靠上帝得以坚固，

chapters.en: saying, “Do not be afraid, for my father Saul will never lay a hand on you. And you will be king over Israel, and I will be your second-in-command. Even my father Saul knows this is true.”
chapters.zh: 对他说：「不要惧怕！我父扫罗的手必不加害于你；你必作以色列的王，我也作你的宰相。这事我父扫罗知道了。」

chapters.en: So the two of them made a covenant before the LORD. And David remained in Horesh, while Jonathan went home.
chapters.zh: 于是二人在耶和华面前立约。大卫仍住在树林里，约拿单回家去了。

chapters.en: Then the Ziphites came up to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Is not David hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah south of Jeshimon?
chapters.zh: 西弗人上到基比亚见扫罗，说：「大卫不是在我们那里的树林里山寨中、旷野南边的哈基拉山藏着吗？

chapters.en: Now, O king, come down whenever your soul desires, and we will be responsible for delivering him into your hand.”
chapters.zh: 王啊，请你随你的心愿下来，我们必亲自将他交在王的手里。」

chapters.en: “May you be blessed by the LORD,” replied Saul, “for you have had compassion on me.
chapters.zh: 扫罗说：「愿耶和华赐福与你们，因你们顾恤我。

chapters.en: Please go and prepare further. Investigate and watch carefully where he goes and who has seen him there, for I am told that he is extremely cunning.
chapters.zh: 请你们回去，再确实查明他的住处和行踪，是谁看见他在那里，因为我听见人说他甚狡猾。

chapters.en: Observe and find out all the places where he hides. Then come back to me with certainty, and I will go with you. If he is in the land, I will search him out among all the clans of Judah.”
chapters.zh: 所以要看准他藏匿的地方，回来据实地告诉我，我就与你们同去。他若在犹大的境内，我必从千门万户中搜出他来。」

chapters.en: So they set out and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the Wilderness of Maon in the Arabah south of Jeshimon,
chapters.zh: 西弗人就起身，在扫罗以先往西弗去。 大卫和跟随他的人却在玛云旷野南边的亚拉巴。

chapters.en: and Saul and his men went to seek him. When David was told about it, he went down to the rock and stayed in the Wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard of this, he pursued David there.
chapters.zh: 扫罗和跟随他的人去寻找大卫；有人告诉大卫，他就下到磐石，住在玛云的旷野。扫罗听见，便在玛云的旷野追赶大卫。

chapters.en: Saul was proceeding along one side of the mountain, and David and his men along the other side. Even though David was hurrying to get away, Saul and his men were closing in on David and his men to capture them.
chapters.zh: 扫罗在山这边走，大卫和跟随他的人在山那边走。大卫急忙躲避扫罗；因为扫罗和跟随他的人，四面围住大卫和跟随他的人，要拿获他们。

chapters.en: Then a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Come quickly, for the Philistines have raided the land!”
chapters.zh: 忽有使者来报告扫罗说：「非利士人犯境抢掠，请王快快回去！」

chapters.en: So Saul broke off his pursuit of David and went to meet the Philistines. That is why that place is called Sela-hammahlekoth.
chapters.zh: 于是扫罗不追赶大卫，回去攻打非利士人。因此那地方名叫西拉‧哈玛希罗结。

chapters.en: And David went up from there and lived in the strongholds of En-gedi.
chapters.zh: 大卫从那里上去，住在隐‧基底的山寨里。

chapters.en: After Saul had returned from pursuing the Philistines, he was told, “David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.”
chapters.zh: 扫罗追赶非利士人回来，有人告诉他说：「大卫在隐‧基底的旷野。」

chapters.en: So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to look for David and his men in the region of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
chapters.zh: 扫罗就从以色列人中挑选三千精兵，率领他们往野羊的磐石去，寻索大卫和跟随他的人。

chapters.en: Soon Saul came to the sheepfolds along the road, where there was a cave, and he went in to relieve himself. And David and his men were hiding in the recesses of the cave.
chapters.zh: 到了路旁的羊圈，在那里有洞，扫罗进去大解。大卫和跟随他的人正藏在洞里的深处。

chapters.en:
So David’s men said to him, “This is the day about which the LORD said to you, ‘Behold, I will deliver your enemy into your hand, that you may do with him as you wish.’”
Then David crept up and stealthily cut off a corner of Saul’s robe.
chapters.zh: 跟随的人对大卫说：「耶和华曾应许你说：『我要将你的仇敌交在你手里，你可以任意待他。』如今时候到了！」大卫就起来，悄悄地割下扫罗外袍的衣襟。

chapters.en: Afterward, David’s conscience was stricken because he had cut off the corner of Saul’s robe.
chapters.zh: 随后大卫心中自责，因为割下扫罗的衣襟；

chapters.en: So he said to his men, “The LORD forbid that I should do such a thing to my master, the LORD’s anointed. May I never lift my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed.”
chapters.zh: 对跟随他的人说：「我的主乃是耶和华的受膏者，我在耶和华面前万不敢伸手害他，因他是耶和华的受膏者。」

chapters.en: With these words David restrained his men, and he did not let them rise up against Saul. Then Saul left the cave and went on his way.
chapters.zh: 大卫用这话拦住跟随他的人，不容他们起来害扫罗。扫罗起来，从洞里出去行路。

chapters.en:
After that, David got up, went out of the cave, and called out to Saul, “My lord the king!”
When Saul looked behind him, David bowed facedown in reverence
chapters.zh: 随后大卫也起来，从洞里出去，呼叫扫罗说：「我主，我王！」扫罗回头观看，大卫就屈身、脸伏于地下拜。

chapters.en: and said to Saul, “Why do you listen to the words of men who say, ‘Look, David intends to harm you’?
chapters.zh: 大卫对扫罗说：「你为何听信人的谗言，说大卫想要害你呢？

chapters.en: Behold, this day you have seen with your own eyes that the LORD delivered you into my hand in the cave. I was told to kill you, but I spared you and said, ‘I will not lift my hand against my lord, since he is the LORD’s anointed.’
chapters.zh: 今日你亲眼看见在洞中，耶和华将你交在我手里；有人叫我杀你，我却爱惜你，说：『我不敢伸手害我的主，因为他是耶和华的受膏者。』

chapters.en: See, my father, look at the corner of your robe in my hand. For I cut it off, but I did not kill you. Know and see that there is no evil or rebellion in my hands. I have not sinned against you, even though you are hunting me down to take my life.
chapters.zh: 我父啊，看看你外袍的衣襟在我手中。我割下你的衣襟，没有杀你；你由此可以知道我没有恶意叛逆你。你虽然猎取我的命，我却没有得罪你。

chapters.en: May the LORD judge between you and me, and may the LORD take vengeance on you, but my hand will never be against you.
chapters.zh: 愿耶和华在你我中间判断是非，在你身上为我伸冤，我却不亲手加害于你。

chapters.en: As the old proverb says, ‘Wickedness proceeds from the wicked.’ But my hand will never be against you.
chapters.zh: 古人有句俗语说：『恶事出于恶人。』我却不亲手加害于你。

chapters.en: Against whom has the king of Israel come out? Whom are you pursuing? A dead dog? A flea?
chapters.zh: 以色列王出来要寻找谁呢？追赶谁呢？不过追赶一条死狗，一个虼蚤就是了。

chapters.en: May the LORD be our judge and decide between you and me. May He take notice and plead my case and deliver me from your hand.”
chapters.zh: 愿耶和华在你我中间施行审判，断定是非，并且鉴察，为我伸冤，救我脱离你的手。」

chapters.en:
When David had finished saying these things, Saul called back, “Is that your voice, David my son?”
Then Saul wept aloud
chapters.zh: 大卫向扫罗说完这话，扫罗说：「我儿大卫，这是你的声音吗？」就放声大哭，

chapters.en: and said to David, “You are more righteous than I, for you have rewarded me with good, though I have rewarded you with evil.
chapters.zh: 对大卫说：「你比我公义；因为你以善待我，我却以恶待你。

chapters.en: And you have declared this day how you have treated me well, for when the LORD delivered me into your hand, you did not kill me.
chapters.zh: 你今日显明是以善待我；因为耶和华将我交在你手里，你却没有杀我。

chapters.en: When a man finds his enemy, does he let him go away unharmed? May the LORD reward you with good for what you have done for me this day.
chapters.zh: 人若遇见仇敌，岂肯放他平安无事地去呢？愿耶和华因你今日向我所行的，以善报你。

chapters.en: Now I know for sure that you will be king and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hands.
chapters.zh: 我也知道你必要作王，以色列的国必坚立在你手里。

chapters.en: So now, swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my descendants or wipe out my name from my father’s house.”
chapters.zh: 现在你要指着耶和华向我起誓，不剪除我的后裔，在我父家不灭没我的名。」

chapters.en: So David gave his oath to Saul. Then Saul returned home, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.
chapters.zh: 于是大卫向扫罗起誓，扫罗就回家去；大卫和跟随他的人上山寨去了。

chapters.en:
When Samuel died, all Israel gathered to mourn for him; and they buried him at his home in Ramah.
Then David set out and went down to the Wilderness of Paran.
chapters.zh: 撒母耳死了，以色列众人聚集，为他哀哭，将他葬在拉玛－他自己的坟墓〔注：原文是房屋〕里。 大卫起身，下到巴兰的旷野。

chapters.en: Now there was a man in Maon whose business was in Carmel. He was a very wealthy man with a thousand goats and three thousand sheep, which he was shearing in Carmel.
chapters.zh: 在玛云有一个人，他的产业在迦密，是一个大富户，有三千绵羊，一千山羊；他正在迦密剪羊毛。

chapters.en: His name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail. She was an intelligent and beautiful woman, but her husband, a Calebite, was harsh and evil in his dealings.
chapters.zh: 那人名叫拿八，是迦勒族的人；他的妻名叫亚比该，是聪明俊美的妇人。拿八为人刚愎凶恶。

chapters.en: While David was in the wilderness, he heard that Nabal was shearing sheep.
chapters.zh: 大卫在旷野听见说拿八剪羊毛，

chapters.en: So David sent ten young men and instructed them, “Go up to Nabal at Carmel. Greet him in my name
chapters.zh: 大卫就打发十个仆人，吩咐他们说：「你们上迦密去见拿八，提我的名问他安。

chapters.en: and say to him, ‘Long life to you, and peace to you and to your house and to all that belongs to you.
chapters.zh: 要对那富户如此说：『愿你平安，愿你家平安，愿你一切所有的都平安。

chapters.en: Now I hear that it is time for shearing. When your shepherds were with us, we did not harass them, and nothing of theirs was missing the whole time they were in Carmel.
chapters.zh: 现在我听说有人为你剪羊毛，你的牧人在迦密的时候和我们在一处，我们没有欺负他们，他们也未曾失落什么。

chapters.en: Ask your young men, and they will tell you. So let my young men find favor with you, for we have come on the day of a feast. Please give whatever you can spare to your servants and to your son David.’”
chapters.zh: 可以问你的仆人，他们必告诉你。所以愿我的仆人在你眼前蒙恩，因为是在好日子来的。求你随手取点赐与仆人和你儿子大卫。』」

chapters.en: When David’s young men arrived, they relayed all these words to Nabal on behalf of David. Then they waited.
chapters.zh: 大卫的仆人到了，将这话提大卫的名都告诉了拿八，就住了口。

chapters.en: But Nabal asked them, “Who is David? Who is this son of Jesse? Many servants these days are breaking away from their masters.
chapters.zh: 拿八回答大卫的仆人说：「大卫是谁？耶西的儿子是谁？近来悖逆主人奔逃的仆人甚多，

chapters.en: Why should I take my bread and water and the meat I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give them to these men whose origin I do not know?”
chapters.zh: 我岂可将饮食和为我剪羊毛人所宰的肉给我不知道从哪里来的人呢？」

chapters.en: So David’s men turned around and went back, and they relayed to him all these words.
chapters.zh: 大卫的仆人就转身从原路回去，照这话告诉大卫。

chapters.en: And David said to his men, “Strap on your swords!” So David and all his men strapped on their swords, and about four hundred men followed David, while two hundred stayed with the supplies.
chapters.zh: 大卫向跟随他的人说：「你们各人都要带上刀！」众人就都带上刀，大卫也带上刀。跟随大卫上去的约有四百人，留下二百人看守器具。

chapters.en: Meanwhile, one of Nabal’s young men informed Nabal’s wife Abigail, “Look, David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, but he screamed at them.
chapters.zh: 有拿八的一个仆人告诉拿八的妻亚比该说：「大卫从旷野打发使者来问我主人的安，主人却辱骂他们。

chapters.en: Yet these men were very good to us. When we were in the field, we were not harassed, and nothing of ours went missing the whole time we lived among them.
chapters.zh: 但是那些人待我们甚好；我们在田野与他们来往的时候，没有受他们的欺负，也未曾失落什么。

chapters.en: They were a wall around us, both day and night, the whole time we were herding our sheep near them.
chapters.zh: 我们在他们那里牧羊的时候，他们昼夜作我们的保障。

chapters.en: Now consider carefully what you must do, because disaster looms over our master and all his household. For he is such a scoundrel that nobody can speak to him!”
chapters.zh: 所以你当筹划，看怎样行才好；不然，祸患定要临到我主人和他全家。他性情凶暴，无人敢与他说话。」

chapters.en: Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five butchered sheep, five seahs of roasted grain, a hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs. She loaded them on donkeys
chapters.zh: 亚比该急忙将二百饼，两皮袋酒，五只收拾好了的羊，五细亚烘好了的穗子，一百葡萄饼，二百无花果饼，都驮在驴上，

chapters.en: and said to her young men, “Go ahead of me. I will be right behind you.” But she did not tell her husband Nabal.
chapters.zh: 对仆人说：「你们前头走，我随着你们去。」这事她却没有告诉丈夫拿八。

chapters.en: As Abigail came riding her donkey into a mountain ravine, she saw David and his men coming down toward her, and she met them.
chapters.zh: 亚比该骑着驴，正下山坡，见大卫和跟随他的人从对面下来，亚比该就迎接他们。

chapters.en: Now David had just said, “In vain I have protected all that belonged to this man in the wilderness. Nothing that belongs to him has gone missing, yet he has paid me back evil for good.
chapters.zh: 大卫曾说：「我在旷野为那人看守所有的，以致他一样不失落，实在是徒然了！他向我以恶报善。

chapters.en: May God punish David, and ever so severely, if I let one male belonging to Nabal survive until morning.”
chapters.zh: 凡属拿八的男丁，我若留一个到明日早晨，愿上帝重重降罚与我！」

chapters.en: When Abigail saw David, she quickly got off the donkey, fell facedown, and bowed before him.
chapters.zh: 亚比该见大卫，便急忙下驴，在大卫面前脸伏于地叩拜，

chapters.en: She fell at his feet and said, “My lord, may the blame be on me alone, but please let your servant speak to you; hear the words of your servant.
chapters.zh: 俯伏在大卫的脚前，说：「我主啊，愿这罪归我！求你容婢女向你进言，更求你听婢女的话。

chapters.en: My lord should pay no attention to this scoundrel Nabal, for he lives up to his name: His name means Fool, and folly accompanies him. I, your servant, did not see my lord’s young men whom you sent.
chapters.zh: 我主不要理这坏人拿八，他的性情与他的名相称；他名叫拿八〔注：就是愚顽的意思〕，他为人果然愚顽。但我主所打发的仆人，婢女并没有看见。

chapters.en: Now, my lord, as surely as the LORD lives and you yourself live, since the LORD has held you back from bloodshed and from avenging yourself with your own hand, may your enemies and those who seek harm for my lord be like Nabal.
chapters.zh: 我主啊，耶和华既然阻止你亲手报仇，取流血的罪，所以我指着永生的耶和华、又敢在你面前起誓说：『愿你的仇敌和谋害你的人都像拿八一样。』

chapters.en: Now let this gift your servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who follow you.
chapters.zh: 如今求你将婢女送来的礼物给跟随你的仆人。

chapters.en: Please forgive your servant’s offense, for the LORD will surely make a lasting dynasty for my lord, because he fights the LORD’s battles. May no evil be found in you as long as you live.
chapters.zh: 求你饶恕婢女的罪过。耶和华必为我主建立坚固的家，因我主为耶和华争战；并且在你平生的日子查不出有什么过来。

chapters.en: And should someone pursue you and seek your life, then the life of my lord will be bound securely by the LORD your God in the bundle of the living. But He shall fling away the lives of your enemies like stones from a sling.
chapters.zh: 虽有人起来追逼你，寻索你的性命，你的性命却在耶和华－你的上帝那里蒙保护，如包裹宝器一样；你仇敌的性命，耶和华必抛去，如用机弦甩石一样。

chapters.en: When the LORD has done for my lord all the good He promised, and when He has appointed you ruler over Israel,
then my lord will have no remorse or guilt of conscience over needless bloodshed and revenge. And when the LORD has dealt well with my lord, may you remember your servant.”
chapters.zh: 我主现在若不亲手报仇流无辜人的血，到了耶和华照所应许你的话赐福与你，立你作以色列的王，那时我主必不致心里不安，觉得良心有亏。耶和华赐福与我主的时候，求你记念婢女。」

chapters.en: Then David said to Abigail, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me this day!
chapters.zh: 大卫对亚比该说：「耶和华－以色列的上帝是应当称颂的，因为他今日使你来迎接我。
