chapters.zh: 次日早晨，大卫写信与约押，交乌利亚随手带去。

chapters.en: In the letter he wrote: “Put Uriah at the front of the fiercest battle; then withdraw from him, so that he may be struck down and killed.”
chapters.zh: 信内写着说：「要派乌利亚前进，到阵势极险之处，你们便退后，使他被杀。」

chapters.en: So as Joab besieged the city, he assigned Uriah to a place where he knew the strongest enemy soldiers were.
chapters.zh: 约押围城的时候，知道敌人那里有勇士，便将乌利亚派在那里。

chapters.en: And when the men of the city came out and fought against Joab, some of David’s servants fell, and Uriah the Hittite also died.
chapters.zh: 城里的人出来和约押打仗；大卫的仆人中有几个被杀的，赫人乌利亚也死了。

chapters.en: Joab sent to David a full account of the battle
chapters.zh: 于是，约押差人去将争战的一切事告诉大卫，

chapters.en: and instructed the messenger, “When you have finished giving the king a full account of the battle,
chapters.zh: 又嘱咐使者说：「你把争战的一切事对王说完了，

chapters.en: if the king’s anger flares, he may ask you, ‘Why did you get so close to the city to fight? Did you not realize they would shoot from atop the wall?
chapters.zh: 王若发怒，问你说：『你们打仗为什么挨近城墙呢？岂不知敌人必从城上射箭吗？

chapters.en:
Who struck Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth ? Was it not a woman who dropped an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died in Thebez? Why did you get so close to the wall?’
If he asks you this, then you are to say, ‘Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.’”
chapters.zh: 从前打死耶路‧比设〔注：就是耶路‧巴力，见士师记九章一节〕儿子亚比米勒的是谁呢？岂不是一个妇人从城上抛下一块上磨石来，打在他身上，他就死在提备斯吗？你们为什么挨近城墙呢？』你就说：『王的仆人－赫人乌利亚也死了。』」

chapters.en: So the messenger set out and reported to David all that Joab had sent him to say.
chapters.zh: 使者起身，来见大卫，照着约押所吩咐他的话奏告大卫。

chapters.en: The messenger said to David, “The men overpowered us and came out against us in the field, but we drove them back to the entrance of the gate.
chapters.zh: 使者对大卫说：「敌人强过我们，出到郊野与我们打仗，我们追杀他们，直到城门口。

chapters.en: Then the archers shot at your servants from the wall, and some of the king’s servants were killed. And your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.”
chapters.zh: 射箭的从城上射王的仆人，射死几个，赫人乌利亚也死了。」

chapters.en: Then David told the messenger, “Say this to Joab: ‘Do not let this matter upset you, for the sword devours one as well as another. Strengthen your attack against the city and demolish it.’ Encourage him with these words.”
chapters.zh: 王向使者说：「你告诉约押说：『不要因这事愁闷，刀剑或吞灭这人或吞灭那人，没有一定的；你只管竭力攻城，将城倾覆。』可以用这话勉励约押。」

chapters.en: When Uriah’s wife heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him.
chapters.zh: 乌利亚的妻听见丈夫乌利亚死了，就为他哀哭。

chapters.en:
And when the time of mourning was over, David had her brought to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son.
But the thing that David had done was evil in the sight of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 哀哭的日子过了，大卫差人将她接到宫里，她就作了大卫的妻，给大卫生了一个儿子。但大卫所行的这事，耶和华甚不喜悦。

chapters.en: Then the LORD sent Nathan to David, and when he arrived, he said, “There were two men in a certain city, one rich and the other poor.
chapters.zh: 耶和华差遣拿单去见大卫。拿单到了大卫那里，对他说：「在一座城里有两个人：一个是富户，一个是穷人。

chapters.en: The rich man had a great number of sheep and cattle,
chapters.zh: 富户有许多牛群羊群；

chapters.en: but the poor man had nothing except one small ewe lamb that he had bought. He raised it, and it grew up with him and his children. It shared his food and drank from his cup; it slept in his arms and was like a daughter to him.
chapters.zh: 穷人除了所买来养活的一只小母羊羔之外，别无所有。羊羔在他家里和他儿女一同长大，吃他所吃的，喝他所喝的，睡在他怀中，在他看来如同女儿一样。

chapters.en: Now a traveler came to the rich man, who refrained from taking one of his own sheep or cattle to prepare for the traveler who had come to him. Instead, he took the poor man’s lamb and prepared it for his guest.”
chapters.zh: 有一客人来到这富户家里；富户舍不得从自己的牛群羊群中取一只预备给客人吃，却取了那穷人的羊羔，预备给客人吃。」

chapters.en: David burned with anger against the man and said to Nathan: “As surely as the LORD lives, the man who did this deserves to die!
chapters.zh: 大卫就甚恼怒那人，对拿单说：「我指着永生的耶和华起誓，行这事的人该死！

chapters.en: Because he has done this thing and has shown no pity, he must pay for the lamb four times over.”
chapters.zh: 他必偿还羊羔四倍；因为他行这事，没有怜恤的心。」

chapters.en: Then Nathan said to David, “You are that man! This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul.
chapters.zh: 拿单对大卫说：「你就是那人！耶和华－以色列的上帝如此说：『我膏你作以色列的王，救你脱离扫罗的手。

chapters.en: I gave your master’s house to you and your master’s wives into your arms. I gave you the house of Israel and Judah, and if that was not enough, I would have given you even more.
chapters.zh: 我将你主人的家业赐给你，将你主人的妻交在你怀里，又将以色列和犹大家赐给你；你若还以为不足，我早就加倍地赐给你。

chapters.en: Why then have you despised the command of the LORD by doing evil in His sight? You put Uriah the Hittite to the sword and took his wife as your own. You have slain him with the sword of the Ammonites.
chapters.zh: 你为什么藐视耶和华的命令，行他眼中看为恶的事呢？你借亚扪人的刀杀害赫人乌利亚，又娶了他的妻为妻。

chapters.en: Now, therefore, the sword will never depart from your house, because you have despised Me and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your own.’
chapters.zh: 你既藐视我，娶了赫人乌利亚的妻为妻，所以刀剑必永不离开你的家。』

chapters.en: This is what the LORD says: ‘I will raise up adversity against you from your own house. Before your very eyes I will take your wives and give them to another, and he will lie with them in broad daylight.
chapters.zh: 耶和华如此说：『我必从你家中兴起祸患攻击你；我必在你眼前把你的妃嫔赐给别人，他在日光之下就与她们同寝。

chapters.en: You have acted in secret, but I will do this thing in broad daylight before all Israel.’”
chapters.zh: 你在暗中行这事，我却要在以色列众人面前，日光之下，报应你。』」

chapters.en:
Then David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against the LORD.”
“The LORD has taken away your sin,” Nathan replied. “You will not die.
chapters.zh: 大卫对拿单说：「我得罪耶和华了！」拿单说：「耶和华已经除掉你的罪，你必不至于死。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, because by this deed you have shown utter contempt for the word of the LORD, the son born to you will surely die.”
chapters.zh: 只是你行这事，叫耶和华的仇敌大得亵渎的机会，故此，你所得的孩子必定要死。」

chapters.en: After Nathan had gone home, the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s wife had borne to David, and he became ill.
chapters.zh: 拿单就回家去了。 耶和华击打乌利亚妻给大卫所生的孩子，使他得重病。

chapters.en: David pleaded with God for the boy. He fasted and went into his house and spent the night lying in sackcloth on the ground.
chapters.zh: 所以大卫为这孩子恳求上帝，而且禁食，进入〔内室〕，终夜躺在地上。

chapters.en: The elders of his household stood beside him to help him up from the ground, but he was unwilling and would not eat anything with them.
chapters.zh: 他家中的老臣来到他旁边，要把他从地上扶起来，他却不肯起来，也不同他们吃饭。

chapters.en: On the seventh day the child died. But David’s servants were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, “Look, while the child was alive, we spoke to him, and he would not listen to us. So how can we tell him the child is dead? He may even harm himself.”
chapters.zh: 到第七日，孩子死了。大卫的臣仆不敢告诉他孩子死了，因他们说：「孩子还活着的时候，我们劝他，他尚且不肯听我们的话，若告诉他孩子死了，岂不更加忧伤吗？」

chapters.en:
When David saw that his servants were whispering to one another, he perceived that the child was dead. So he asked his servants, “Is the child dead?”
“He is dead,” they replied.
chapters.zh: 大卫见臣仆彼此低声说话，就知道孩子死了，问臣仆说：「孩子死了吗？」他们说：「死了。」

chapters.en: Then David got up from the ground, washed and anointed himself, changed his clothes, and went into the house of the LORD and worshiped. Then he went to his own house, and at his request they set food before him, and he ate.
chapters.zh: 大卫就从地上起来，沐浴，抹膏，换了衣裳，进耶和华的殿敬拜；然后回宫，吩咐人摆饭，他便吃了。

chapters.en: “What is this you have done?” his servants asked. “While the child was alive, you fasted and wept, but when he died, you got up and ate.”
chapters.zh: 臣仆问他说：「你所行的是什么意思？孩子活着的时候，你禁食哭泣；孩子死了，你倒起来吃饭。」

chapters.en: David answered, “While the child was alive, I fasted and wept, for I said, ‘Who knows? The LORD may be gracious to me and let him live.’
chapters.zh: 大卫说：「孩子还活着，我禁食哭泣；因为我想，或者耶和华怜恤我，使孩子不死也未可知。

chapters.en: But now that he is dead, why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me.”
chapters.zh: 孩子死了，我何必禁食，我岂能使他返回呢？我必往他那里去，他却不能回我这里来。」

chapters.en:
Then David comforted his wife Bathsheba, and he went to her and lay with her. So she gave birth to a son, and they named him Solomon.
Now the LORD loved the child
chapters.zh: 大卫安慰他的妻拔示巴，与她同寝，她就生了儿子，给他起名叫所罗门。耶和华也喜爱他，

chapters.en: and sent word through Nathan the prophet to name him Jedidiah because the LORD loved him.
chapters.zh: 就藉先知拿单赐他一个名字，叫耶底底亚，因为耶和华〔爱他〕。

chapters.en: Meanwhile, Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and captured the royal fortress.
chapters.zh: 约押攻取亚扪人的京城拉巴。

chapters.en: Then Joab sent messengers to David to say, “I have fought against Rabbah and have captured the water supply of the city.
chapters.zh: 约押打发使者去见大卫，说：「我攻打拉巴，取其水城。

chapters.en: Now, therefore, assemble the rest of the troops, lay siege to the city, and capture it. Otherwise I will capture the city, and it will be named after me.”
chapters.zh: 现在你要聚集其余的军兵来，安营围攻这城，恐怕我取了这城，人就以我的名叫这城。」

chapters.en: So David assembled all the troops and went to Rabbah; and he fought against it and captured it.
chapters.zh: 于是大卫聚集众军，往拉巴去攻城，就取了这城，

chapters.en: Then he took the crown from the head of their king. It weighed a talent of gold and was set with precious stones, and it was placed on David’s head. And David took a great amount of plunder from the city.
chapters.zh: 夺了亚扪人之王所戴的金冠冕〔注：王：或译玛勒堪；玛勒堪就是米勒公，又名摩洛，亚扪族之神名〕，其上的金子重一他连得，又嵌着宝石。人将这冠冕戴在大卫头上。大卫从城里夺了许多财物，

chapters.en: David brought out the people who were there and put them to work with saws, iron picks, and axes, and he made them work at the brick kilns. He did the same to all the Ammonite cities. Then David and all his troops returned to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 将城里的人拉出来，放在锯下，或铁耙下，或铁斧下，或叫他经过砖窑〔注：或译：强他们用锯，或用打粮食的铁器，或用铁斧做工，或使在砖窑里服役〕；大卫待亚扪各城的居民都是如此。其后，大卫和众军都回耶路撒冷去了。

chapters.en: After some time, David’s son Amnon fell in love with Tamar, the beautiful sister of David’s son Absalom.
chapters.zh: 大卫的儿子押沙龙有一个美貌的妹子，名叫她玛。大卫的儿子暗嫩爱她。

chapters.en: Amnon was sick with frustration over his sister Tamar, for she was a virgin, and it seemed implausible for him to do anything to her.
chapters.zh: 暗嫩为他妹子她玛忧急成病。她玛还是处女，暗嫩以为难向她行事。

chapters.en: Now Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of David’s brother Shimeah. Jonadab was a very shrewd man,
chapters.zh: 暗嫩有一个朋友，名叫约拿达，是大卫长兄示米亚的儿子。这约拿达为人极其狡猾；

chapters.en:
and he asked Amnon, “Why are you, the son of the king, so depressed morning after morning? Won’t you tell me?”
Amnon replied, “I am in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.”
chapters.zh: 他问暗嫩说：「王的儿子啊，为何一天比一天瘦弱呢？请你告诉我。」暗嫩回答说：「我爱我兄弟押沙龙的妹子她玛。」

chapters.en: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend you are ill. When your father comes to see you, say to him, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come and give me something to eat. Let her prepare it in my sight so I may watch her and eat it from her hand.’”
chapters.zh: 约拿达说：「你不如躺在床上装病；你父亲来看你，就对他说：『求父叫我妹子她玛来，在我眼前预备食物，递给我吃，使我看见，好从她手里接过来吃。』」

chapters.en: So Amnon lay down and feigned illness. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of cakes in my sight, so that I may eat from her hand.”
chapters.zh: 于是暗嫩躺卧装病。王来看他，他对王说：「求父叫我妹子她玛来，在我眼前为我做两个饼，我好从她手里接过来吃。」

chapters.en: Then David sent word to Tamar at the palace: “Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare a meal for him.”
chapters.zh: 大卫就打发人到宫里，对她玛说：「你往你哥哥暗嫩的屋里去，为他预备食物。」

chapters.en: So Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon, who was lying down. She took some dough, kneaded it, made cakes in his sight, and baked them.
chapters.zh: 她玛就到她哥哥暗嫩的屋里；暗嫩正躺卧。她玛抟面，在他眼前做饼，且烤熟了，

chapters.en: Then she brought the pan and set it down before him, but he refused to eat. “Send everyone away!” said Amnon. And everyone went out.
chapters.zh: 在他面前将饼从锅里倒出来，他却不肯吃，便说：「众人离开我出去吧！」众人就都离开他，出去了。

chapters.en:
Then Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food into the bedroom, so that I may eat it from your hand.”
Tamar took the cakes she had made and went to her brother Amnon’s bedroom.
chapters.zh: 暗嫩对她玛说：「你把食物拿进卧房，我好从你手里接过来吃。」她玛就把所做的饼拿进卧房，到她哥哥暗嫩那里，

chapters.en: And when she had brought them to him to eat, he took hold of her and said, “Come lie with me, my sister!”
chapters.zh: 拿着饼上前给他吃，他便拉住她玛，说：「我妹妹，你来与我同寝。」

chapters.en: “No, my brother!” she cried. “Do not violate me, for such a thing should never be done in Israel. Do not do this disgraceful thing!
chapters.zh: 她玛说：「我哥哥，不要玷辱我。以色列人中不当这样行，你不要做这丑事；

chapters.en: Where could I ever take my shame? And you would be like one of the fools in Israel! Please speak to the king, for he will not withhold me from you.”
chapters.zh: 你〔玷辱了我〕，我何以掩盖我的羞耻呢？你在以色列中也成了愚妄人。你可以求王，他必不禁止我归你。」

chapters.en: But Amnon refused to listen to her, and being stronger, he violated her and lay with her.
chapters.zh: 但暗嫩不肯听她的话，因比她力大，就玷辱她，与她同寝。

chapters.en: Then Amnon hated Tamar with such intensity that his hatred was greater than the love he previously had. “Get up!” he said to her. “Be gone!”
chapters.zh: 随后，暗嫩极其恨她，那恨她的心比先前爱她的心更甚，对她说：「你起来，去吧！」

chapters.en:
“No,” she replied, “sending me away is worse than this great wrong you have already done to me!”
But he refused to listen to her.
chapters.zh: 她玛说：「不要这样！你赶出我去的这罪比你才行的更重！」但暗嫩不肯听她的话，

chapters.en: Instead, he called to his attendant and said, “Throw this woman out and bolt the door behind her!”
chapters.zh: 就叫伺候自己的仆人来，说：「将这个女子赶出去！她一出去，你就关门，上闩。」

chapters.en: So Amnon’s attendant threw her out and bolted the door behind her. Now Tamar was wearing a robe of many colors, because this is what the king’s virgin daughters wore.
chapters.zh: 那时她玛穿着彩衣，因为没有出嫁的公主都是这样穿。暗嫩的仆人就把她赶出去，关门上闩。

chapters.en: And Tamar put ashes on her head and tore her robe. And putting her hand on her head, she went away crying aloud.
chapters.zh: 她玛把灰尘撒在头上，撕裂所穿的彩衣，以手抱头，一面行走，一面哭喊。

chapters.en:
Her brother Absalom said to her, “Has your brother Amnon been with you? Be quiet for now, my sister. He is your brother. Do not take this thing to heart.”
So Tamar lived as a desolate woman in the house of her brother Absalom.
chapters.zh: 她胞兄押沙龙问她说：「莫非你哥哥暗嫩与你亲近了吗？我妹妹，暂且不要作声，他是你的哥哥，不要将这事放在心上。」她玛就孤孤单单地住在她胞兄押沙龙家里。

chapters.en: When King David heard all this, he was furious.
chapters.zh: 大卫王听见这事，就甚发怒。

chapters.en: And Absalom never said a word to Amnon, either good or bad, because he hated Amnon for violating his sister Tamar.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙并不和他哥哥暗嫩说好说歹；因为暗嫩玷辱他妹妹她玛，所以押沙龙恨恶他。

chapters.en: Two years later, when Absalom’s sheepshearers were at Baal-hazor near Ephraim, he invited all the sons of the king.
chapters.zh: 过了二年，在靠近以法莲的巴力‧夏琐有人为押沙龙剪羊毛；押沙龙请王的众子与他同去。

chapters.en: And he went to the king and said, “Your servant has just hired shearers. Will the king and his servants please come with me?”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙来见王，说：「现在有人为仆人剪羊毛，请王和王的臣仆与仆人同去。」

chapters.en: “No, my son,” the king replied, “we should not all go, or we would be a burden to you.” Although Absalom urged him, he was not willing to go, but gave him his blessing.
chapters.zh: 王对押沙龙说：「我儿，我们不必都去，恐怕使你耗费太多。」押沙龙再三请王，王仍是不肯去，只为他祝福。

chapters.en:
“If not,” said Absalom, “please let my brother Amnon go with us.”
“Why should he go with you?” the king asked.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙说：「王若不去，求王许我哥哥暗嫩同去。」王说：「何必要他去呢？」

chapters.en: But Absalom urged him, so the king sent Amnon and the rest of his sons.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙再三求王，王就许暗嫩和王的众子与他同去。

chapters.en: Now Absalom had ordered his young men, “Watch Amnon until his heart is merry with wine, and when I order you to strike Amnon down, you are to kill him. Do not be afraid. Have I not commanded you? Be courageous and valiant!”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙吩咐仆人说：「你们注意，看暗嫩饮酒畅快的时候，我对你们说杀暗嫩，你们便杀他，不要惧怕。这不是我吩咐你们的吗？你们只管壮胆奋勇！」

chapters.en: So Absalom’s young men did to Amnon just as Absalom had ordered. Then all the other sons of the king got up, and each one fled on his mule.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙的仆人就照押沙龙所吩咐的，向暗嫩行了。王的众子都起来，各人骑上骡子，逃跑了。

chapters.en: While they were on the way, a report reached David: “Absalom has struck down all the sons of the king; not one of them is left!”
chapters.zh: 他们还在路上，有风声传到大卫那里，说：「押沙龙将王的众子都杀了，没有留下一个。」

chapters.en: Then the king stood up, tore his clothes, and lay down on the ground. And all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.
chapters.zh: 王就起来，撕裂衣服，躺在地上。王的臣仆也都撕裂衣服，站在旁边。

chapters.en: But Jonadab, the son of David’s brother Shimeah, spoke up: “My lord must not think they have killed all the sons of the king, for only Amnon is dead. In fact, Absalom has planned this since the day Amnon violated his sister Tamar.
chapters.zh: 大卫的长兄，示米亚的儿子约拿达说：「我主，不要以为王的众子－少年人都杀了，只有暗嫩一个人死了。自从暗嫩玷辱押沙龙妹子她玛的那日，押沙龙就定意杀暗嫩了。

chapters.en: So now, my lord the king, do not take to heart the report that all the sons of the king are dead. Only Amnon is dead.”
chapters.zh: 现在，我主我王，不要把这事放在心上，以为王的众子都死了，只有暗嫩一个人死了。」

chapters.en: Meanwhile, Absalom had fled. When the young man standing watch looked up, he saw many people coming down the road west of him, along the side of the hill. And the watchman went and reported to the king, “I see men coming from the direction of Horonaim, along the side of the hill.”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙逃跑了。 守望的少年人举目观看，见有许多人从山坡的路上来。

chapters.en: So Jonadab said to the king, “Look, the sons of the king have arrived! It is just as your servant said.”
chapters.zh: 约拿达对王说：「看哪，王的众子都来了，果然与你仆人所说的相合。」

chapters.en: And as he finished speaking, the sons of the king came in, wailing loudly. Then the king and all his servants also wept very bitterly.
chapters.zh: 话才说完，王的众子都到了，放声大哭；王和臣仆也都哭得甚恸。

chapters.en: Now Absalom fled and went to Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. But David mourned for his son every day.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙逃到基述王亚米忽的儿子达买那里去了。大卫天天为他儿子悲哀。

chapters.en: After Absalom had fled and gone to Geshur, he stayed there three years.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙逃到基述，在那里住了三年。

chapters.en: And King David longed to go to Absalom, for he had been consoled over Amnon’s death.
chapters.zh: 暗嫩死了以后，大卫王得了安慰，心里切切想念押沙龙。

chapters.en: Now Joab son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart longed for Absalom.
chapters.zh: 洗鲁雅的儿子约押，知道王心里想念押沙龙，

chapters.en: So Joab sent to Tekoa to bring a wise woman from there. He told her, “Please pretend to be a mourner; put on clothes for mourning and do not anoint yourself with oil. Act like a woman who has mourned for the dead a long time.
chapters.zh: 就打发人往提哥亚去，从那里叫了一个聪明的妇人来，对她说：「请你假装居丧的，穿上孝衣，不要用膏抹身，要装作为死者许久悲哀的妇人；

chapters.en: Then go to the king and speak these words to him.” And Joab put the words in her mouth.
chapters.zh: 进去见王，对王如此如此说。」于是约押将当说的话教导了妇人。

chapters.en: When the woman from Tekoa went to the king, she fell facedown in homage and said, “Help me, O king!”
chapters.zh: 提哥亚妇人到王面前，伏地叩拜，说：「王啊，求你拯救！」

chapters.en:
“What troubles you?” the king asked her.
“Indeed,” she said, “I am a widow, for my husband is dead.
chapters.zh: 王问她说：「你有什么事呢？」回答说：「婢女实在是寡妇，我丈夫死了。

chapters.en: And your maidservant had two sons who were fighting in the field with no one to separate them, and one struck the other and killed him.
chapters.zh: 我有两个儿子，一日在田间争斗，没有人解劝，这个就打死那个。

chapters.en: Now the whole clan has risen up against your maidservant and said, ‘Hand over the one who struck down his brother, that we may put him to death for the life of the brother whom he killed. Then we will cut off the heir as well!’ So they would extinguish my one remaining ember by not preserving my husband’s name or posterity on the earth.”
chapters.zh: 现在全家的人都起来攻击婢女，说：『你将那打死兄弟的交出来，我们好治死他，偿他打死兄弟的命，灭绝那承受家业的。』这样，他们要将我剩下的炭火灭尽，不与我丈夫留名留后在世上。」

chapters.en: “Go home,” the king said to the woman, “and I will give orders on your behalf.”
chapters.zh: 王对妇人说：「你回家去吧！我必为你下令。」

chapters.en: But the woman of Tekoa said to the king, “My lord the king, may any blame be on me and on my father’s house, and may the king and his throne be guiltless.”
chapters.zh: 提哥亚妇人又对王说：「我主我王，愿这罪归我和我父家，与王和王的位无干。」

chapters.en: “If anyone speaks to you,” said the king, “bring him to me, and he will not trouble you again!”
chapters.zh: 王说：「凡难为你的，你就带他到我这里来，他必不再搅扰你。」

chapters.en:
“Please,” she replied, “may the king invoke the LORD your God to prevent the avenger of blood from increasing the devastation, so that my son may not be destroyed!”
“As surely as the LORD lives,” he vowed, “not a hair of your son’s head will fall to the ground.”
chapters.zh: 妇人说：「愿王记念耶和华－你的上帝，不许报血仇的人施行灭绝，恐怕他们灭绝我的儿子。」王说：「我指着永生的耶和华起誓：你的儿子连一根头发也不致落在地上。」

chapters.en:
Then the woman said, “Please, may your servant speak a word to my lord the king?”
“Speak,” he replied.
chapters.zh: 妇人说：「求我主我王容婢女再说一句话。」王说：「你说吧！」

chapters.en: The woman asked, “Why have you devised a thing like this against the people of God? When the king says this, does he not convict himself, since he has not brought back his own banished son?
chapters.zh: 妇人说：「王为何也起意要害上帝的民呢？王不使那逃亡的人回来，王的这话就是自证己错了！

chapters.en: For we will surely die and be like water poured out on the ground, which cannot be recovered. Yet God does not take away a life, but He devises ways that the banished one may not be cast out from Him.
chapters.zh: 我们都是必死的，如同水泼在地上，不能收回。上帝并不夺取人的性命，乃设法使逃亡的人不致成为赶出、回不来的。

chapters.en: Now therefore, I have come to present this matter to my lord the king because the people have made me afraid. Your servant thought, ‘I will speak to the king. Perhaps he will grant the request of his maidservant.
chapters.zh: 我来将这话告诉我主我王，是因百姓使我惧怕。婢女想，不如将这话告诉王，或者王成就婢女所求的。

chapters.en: For the king will hear and deliver his maidservant from the hand of the man who would cut off both me and my son from God’s inheritance.’
chapters.zh: 人要将我和我儿子从上帝的地业上一同除灭，王必应允救我脱离他的手。

chapters.en: And now your servant says, ‘May the word of my lord the king bring me rest, for my lord the king is able to discern good and evil, just like the angel of God. May the LORD your God be with you.’”
chapters.zh: 婢女又想，我主我王的话必安慰我；因为我主我王能辨别是非，如同上帝的使者一样。惟愿耶和华－你的上帝与你同在！」

chapters.en:
Then the king said to the woman, “I am going to ask you something; do not conceal it from me!”
“Let my lord the king speak,” she replied.
chapters.zh: 王对妇人说：「我要问你一句话，你一点不要瞒我。」妇人说：「愿我主我王说。」

chapters.en:
So the king asked, “Is the hand of Joab behind all this?”
The woman answered, “As surely as you live, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything that my lord the king says. Yes, your servant Joab is the one who gave me orders; he told your maidservant exactly what to say.
chapters.zh: 王说：「你这些话莫非是约押的主意吗？」妇人说：「我敢在我主我王面前起誓：王的话正对，不偏左右，是王的仆人约押吩咐我的，这些话是他教导我的。

chapters.en: Joab your servant has done this to bring about this change of affairs, but my lord has wisdom like the wisdom of the angel of God, to know everything that happens in the land.”
chapters.zh: 王的仆人约押如此行，为要挽回这事。我主的智慧却如上帝使者的智慧，能知世上一切事。」

chapters.en: Then the king said to Joab, “I hereby grant this request. Go, bring back the young man Absalom.”
chapters.zh: 王对约押说：「我应允你这事。你可以去，把那少年人押沙龙带回来。」

chapters.en: Joab fell facedown in homage and blessed the king. “Today,” said Joab, “your servant knows that he has found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, because the king has granted his request.”
chapters.zh: 约押就面伏于地叩拜，祝谢于王，又说：「王既应允仆人所求的，仆人今日知道在我主我王眼前蒙恩了。」

chapters.en: So Joab got up, went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 于是约押起身往基述去，将押沙龙带回耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: But the king added, “He may return to his house, but he must not see my face.” So Absalom returned to his own house, but he did not see the face of the king.
chapters.zh: 王说：「使他回自己家里去，不要见我的面。」押沙龙就回自己家里去，没有见王的面。

chapters.en: Now there was not a man in all Israel as handsome and highly praised as Absalom. From the sole of his foot to the top of his head, he did not have a single flaw.
chapters.zh: 以色列全地之中，无人像押沙龙那样俊美，得人的称赞，从脚底到头顶毫无瑕疵。

chapters.en: And when he cut the hair of his head—he shaved it every year because his hair got so heavy—he would weigh it out to be two hundred shekels, according to the royal standard.
chapters.zh: 他的头发甚重，每到年底剪发一次；所剪下来的，按王的平称一称，重二百舍客勒。

chapters.en: Three sons were born to Absalom, and a daughter named Tamar, who was a beautiful woman.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙生了三个儿子，一个女儿。女儿名叫她玛，是个容貌俊美的女子。

chapters.en: Now Absalom lived in Jerusalem two years without seeing the face of the king.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙住在耶路撒冷足有二年，没有见王的面。

chapters.en:
Then he sent for Joab to send him to the king, but Joab refused to come to him.
So Absalom sent a second time, but Joab still would not come.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙打发人去叫约押来，要讬他去见王，约押却不肯来。第二次打发人去叫他，他仍不肯来。

chapters.en:
Then Absalom said to his servants, “Look, Joab’s field is next to mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire!”
And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
chapters.zh: 所以押沙龙对仆人说：「你们看，约押有一块田，与我的田相近，其中有大麦，你们去放火烧了。」押沙龙的仆人就去放火烧了那田。

chapters.en: Then Joab came to Absalom’s house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
chapters.zh: 于是约押起来，到了押沙龙家里，问他说：「你的仆人为何放火烧了我的田呢？」

chapters.en: “Look,” said Absalom, “I sent for you and said, ‘Come here. I want to send you to the king to ask: Why have I come back from Geshur? It would be better for me if I were still there.’ So now, let me see the king’s face, and if there is iniquity in me, let him kill me.”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙回答约押说：「我打发人去请你来，好讬你去见王，替我说：『我为何从基述回来呢？不如仍在那里。』现在要许我见王的面；我若有罪，任凭王杀我就是了。」

chapters.en: So Joab went and told the king, and David summoned Absalom, who came to him and bowed facedown before him. Then the king kissed Absalom.
chapters.zh: 于是约押去见王，将这话奏告王，王便叫押沙龙来。押沙龙来见王，在王面前俯伏于地，王就与押沙龙亲嘴。

chapters.en: Some time later, Absalom provided for himself a chariot with horses and fifty men to run ahead of him.
chapters.zh: 此后，押沙龙为自己预备车马，又派五十人在他前头奔走。

chapters.en:
He would get up early and stand beside the road leading to the city gate.
Whenever anyone had a grievance to bring before the king for a decision, Absalom would call out and ask, “What city are you from?” And if he replied, “Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel,”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙常常早晨起来，站在城门的道旁，凡有争讼要去求王判断的，押沙龙就叫他过来，问他说：「你是哪一城的人？」回答说：「仆人是以色列某支派的人。」

chapters.en: Absalom would say, “Look, your claims are good and right, but the king has no deputy to hear you.”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙对他说：「你的事有情有理，无奈王没有委人听你伸诉。」

chapters.en: And he would add, “If only someone would appoint me judge in the land, then everyone with a grievance or dispute could come to me, and I would give him justice.”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙又说：「恨不得我作国中的士师！凡有争讼求审判的到我这里来，我必秉公判断。」

chapters.en: Also, when anyone approached to bow down to him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him, and kiss him.
chapters.zh: 若有人近前来要拜押沙龙，押沙龙就伸手拉住他，与他亲嘴。

chapters.en: Absalom did this to all the Israelites who came to the king for justice. In this way he stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
chapters.zh: 以色列人中，凡去见王求判断的，押沙龙都是如此待他们。这样，押沙龙暗中得了以色列人的心。

chapters.en: After four years had passed, Absalom said to the king, “Please let me go to Hebron to fulfill a vow I have made to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 满了四十年〔注：有作四年的〕，押沙龙对王说：「求你准我往希伯崙去，还我向耶和华所许的愿。

chapters.en: For your servant made a vow while dwelling in Geshur of Aram, saying: ‘If indeed the LORD brings me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the LORD in Hebron.’ ”
chapters.zh: 因为仆人住在亚兰的基述，曾许愿说：『耶和华若使我再回耶路撒冷，我必事奉他。』」

chapters.en: “Go in peace,” said the king. So Absalom got up and went to Hebron.
chapters.zh: 王说：「你平平安安地去吧！」押沙龙就起身，往希伯崙去了。

chapters.en: Then Absalom sent spies throughout the tribes of Israel with this message: “When you hear the sound of the horn, you are to say, ‘Absalom reigns in Hebron!’”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙打发探子走遍以色列各支派，说：「你们一听见角声就说：『押沙龙在希伯崙作王了！』」

chapters.en: Two hundred men from Jerusalem accompanied Absalom. They had been invited as guests and they went along innocently, for they knew nothing about the matter.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙在耶路撒冷请了二百人与他同去，都是诚诚实实去的，并不知道其中的真情。

chapters.en:
While Absalom was offering the sacrifices, he sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, to come from his hometown of Giloh.
So the conspiracy gained strength, and Absalom’s following kept increasing.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙献祭的时候，打发人去将大卫的谋士、基罗人亚希多弗从他本城请了来。于是叛逆的势派甚大；因为随从押沙龙的人民，日渐增多。

chapters.en: Then a messenger came to David and reported, “The hearts of the men of Israel are with Absalom.”
chapters.zh: 有人报告大卫说：「以色列人的心都归向押沙龙了！」

chapters.en: And David said to all the servants with him in Jerusalem, “Arise and let us flee, or we will not escape from Absalom! We must leave quickly, or he will soon overtake us, heap disaster on us, and put the city to the sword.”
chapters.zh: 大卫就对耶路撒冷跟随他的臣仆说：「我们要起来逃走，不然都不能躲避押沙龙了；要速速地去，恐怕他忽然来到，加害于我们，用刀杀尽合城的人。」

chapters.en: The king’s servants replied, “Whatever our lord the king decides, we are your servants.”
chapters.zh: 王的臣仆对王说：「我主我王所定的，仆人都愿遵行。」

chapters.en: Then the king set out, and his entire household followed him. But he left behind ten concubines to take care of the palace.
chapters.zh: 于是王带着全家的人出去了，但留下十个妃嫔看守宫殿。

chapters.en: So the king set out with all the people following him. He stopped at the last house,
chapters.zh: 王出去，众民都跟随他，到伯墨哈，就住下了。

chapters.en: and all his servants marched past him—all the Cherethites and Pelethites, and six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gath.
chapters.zh: 王的臣仆都在他面前过去。基利提人、比利提人，就是从迦特跟随王来的六百人，也都在他面前过去。

chapters.en: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why should you also go with us? Go back and stay with the new king, since you are both a foreigner and an exile from your homeland.
chapters.zh: 王对迦特人以太说：「你是外邦逃来的人，为什么与我们同去呢？你可以回去与〔新〕王同住，〔或者回〕你本地去吧！

chapters.en: In fact, you arrived only yesterday; should I make you wander around with us today while I do not know where I am going? Go back and take your brothers with you. May the LORD show you loving devotion and faithfulness. ”
chapters.zh: 你来的日子不多，我今日怎好叫你与我们一同飘流、没有一定的住处呢？你不如带你的弟兄回去吧！〔愿耶和华〕用慈爱诚实待你。」

chapters.en: But Ittai answered the king, “As surely as the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be!”
chapters.zh: 以太对王说：「我指着永生的耶和华起誓，又敢在王面前起誓：无论生死，王在哪里，仆人也必在那里。」

chapters.en: “March on then,” said David to Ittai. So Ittai the Gittite marched past with all his men and all the little ones who were with him.
chapters.zh: 大卫对以太说：「你前去过〔河〕吧！」于是迦特人以太带着跟随他的人和所有的〔妇人〕孩子，就都过去了。

chapters.en: Everyone in the countryside was weeping loudly as all the people passed by. And as the king crossed the Kidron Valley, all the people also passed toward the way of the wilderness.
chapters.zh: 本地的人都放声大哭。众民尽都过去，王也过了汲沦溪；众民往旷野去了。

chapters.en: Zadok was also there, and all the Levites with him were carrying the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until all the people had passed out of the city.
chapters.zh: 撒督和抬上帝约柜的利未人也一同来了，将上帝的〔约〕柜放下。亚比亚他上来，等着众民从城里出来过去。

chapters.en: Then the king said to Zadok, “Return the ark of God to the city. If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back and let me see both it and His dwelling place again.
chapters.zh: 王对撒督说：「你将上帝的〔约〕柜抬回城去。我若在耶和华眼前蒙恩，他必使我回来，再见〔约〕柜和他的居所。

chapters.en: But if He should say, ‘I do not delight in you,’ then here I am; let Him do to me whatever seems good to Him.”
chapters.zh: 倘若他说：『我不喜悦你』，看哪，我在这里，愿他凭自己的意旨待我！」

chapters.en: The king also said to Zadok the priest, “Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace—you with your son Ahimaaz, and Abiathar with his son Jonathan.
chapters.zh: 王又对祭司撒督说：「你不是先见吗？你可以安然回城；你儿子亚希玛斯和亚比亚他的儿子约拿单都可以与你同去。

chapters.en: See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”
chapters.zh: 我在旷野的渡口那里等你们报信给我。」

chapters.en: So Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem and stayed there.
chapters.zh: 于是撒督和亚比亚他将上帝的〔约〕柜抬回耶路撒冷，他们就住在那里。

chapters.en: But David continued up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went up. His head was covered, and he was walking barefoot. And all the people with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went.
chapters.zh: 大卫蒙头赤脚上橄榄山，一面上一面哭。跟随他的人也都蒙头哭着上去；

chapters.en:
Now someone told David: “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.”
So David pleaded, “O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉大卫说：「亚希多弗也在叛党之中，随从押沙龙。」大卫祷告说：「耶和华啊，求你使亚希多弗的计谋变为愚拙！」

chapters.en: When David came to the summit, where he used to worship God, Hushai the Archite was there to meet him with his robe torn and dust on his head.
chapters.zh: 大卫到了〔山〕顶、敬拜上帝的地方，见亚基人户筛，衣服撕裂，头蒙灰尘来迎接他。

chapters.en: David said to him, “If you go on with me, you will be a burden to me.
chapters.zh: 大卫对他说：「你若与我同去，必累赘我；

chapters.en: But you can thwart the counsel of Ahithophel for me if you return to the city and say to Absalom: ‘I will be your servant, my king; in the past I was your father’s servant, but now I will be your servant.’
chapters.zh: 你若回城去，对押沙龙说：『王啊，我愿作你的仆人；我向来作你父亲的仆人，现在我也照样作你的仆人。』这样，你就可以为我破坏亚希多弗的计谋。

chapters.en: Will not Zadok and Abiathar the priests be there with you? Report to them everything you hear from the king’s palace.
chapters.zh: 祭司撒督和亚比亚他岂不都在那里吗？你在王宫里听见什么，就要告诉祭司撒督和亚比亚他。

chapters.en: Indeed, their two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them. Send them to me with everything you hear.”
chapters.zh: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯，亚比亚他的儿子约拿单，也都在那里。凡你们所听见的可以讬这二人来报告我。」

chapters.en: So David’s friend Hushai arrived in Jerusalem just as Absalom was entering the city.
chapters.zh: 于是，大卫的朋友户筛进了城；押沙龙也进了耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: When David had gone a little beyond the summit, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth was there to meet him. He had a pair of saddled donkeys loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred clusters of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.
chapters.zh: 大卫刚过〔山〕顶，见米非波设的仆人洗巴拉着备好了的两匹驴，驴上驮着二百面饼，一百葡萄饼，一百个夏天的果饼，一皮袋酒来迎接他。

chapters.en:
“Why do you have these?” asked the king.
Ziba replied, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride, the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness.”
chapters.zh: 王问洗巴说：「你带这些来是什么意思呢？」洗巴说：「驴是给王的家眷骑的；面饼和夏天的果饼是给少年人吃的；酒是给在旷野疲乏人喝的。」

chapters.en:
“Where is your master’s grandson?” asked the king.
And Ziba answered, “Indeed, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he has said, ‘Today, the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my grandfather.’”
chapters.zh: 王问说：「你主人的儿子在哪里呢？」洗巴回答王说：「他仍在耶路撒冷，因他说：『以色列人今日必将我父的国归还我。』」

chapters.en:
So the king said to Ziba, “All that belongs to Mephibosheth is now yours!”
“I humbly bow before you,” said Ziba. “May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king!”
chapters.zh: 王对洗巴说：「凡属米非波设的都归你了。」洗巴说：「我叩拜我主我王，愿我在你眼前蒙恩。」

chapters.en: As King David approached Bahurim, a man from the family of the house of Saul was just coming out. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and as he approached, he kept yelling out curses.
chapters.zh: 大卫王到了巴户琳，见有一个人出来，是扫罗族基拉的儿子，名叫示每。他一面走一面咒骂，

chapters.en: He threw stones at David and at all the servants of the king, though the troops and all the mighty men were on David’s right and left.
chapters.zh: 又拿石头砍大卫王和王的臣仆；众民和勇士都在王的左右。

chapters.en: And as he yelled curses, Shimei said, “Get out, get out, you worthless man of bloodshed!
chapters.zh: 示每咒骂说：「你这流人血的坏人哪，去吧去吧！

chapters.en: The LORD has paid you back for all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and the LORD has delivered the kingdom into the hand of your son Absalom. See, you have come to ruin because you are a man of bloodshed!”
chapters.zh: 你流扫罗全家的血，接续他作王；耶和华把这罪归在你身上，将这国交给你儿子押沙龙。现在你自取其祸，因为你是流人血的人。」

chapters.en: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and cut off his head!”
chapters.zh: 洗鲁雅的儿子亚比筛对王说：「这死狗岂可咒骂我主我王呢？求你容我过去，割下他的头来。」

chapters.en: But the king replied, “What have I to do with you, O sons of Zeruiah? If he curses me because the LORD told him, ‘Curse David,’ who can ask, ‘Why did you do this?’”
chapters.zh: 王说：「洗鲁雅的儿子，我与你们有何关涉呢？他咒骂是因耶和华吩咐他说：『你要咒骂大卫。』如此，谁敢说你为什么这样行呢？」

chapters.en: Then David said to Abishai and to all his servants, “Behold, my own son, my own flesh and blood, seeks my life. How much more, then, this Benjamite! Leave him alone and let him curse me, for the LORD has told him so.
chapters.zh: 大卫又对亚比筛和众臣仆说：「我亲生的儿子尚且寻索我的性命，何况这便雅悯人呢？由他咒骂吧！因为这是耶和华吩咐他的。

chapters.en: Perhaps the LORD will see my affliction and repay me with good for the cursing I receive today.”
chapters.zh: 或者耶和华见我遭难，为我今日被这人咒骂，就施恩与我。」

chapters.en: So David and his men proceeded along the road as Shimei went along the ridge of the hill opposite him. As Shimei went, he yelled curses, threw stones, and flung dust at David.
chapters.zh: 于是大卫和跟随他的人往前行走。示每在大卫对面山坡，一面行走一面咒骂，又拿石头砍他，拿土扬他。

chapters.en: Finally, the king and all the people with him arrived, exhausted. And there he refreshed himself.
chapters.zh: 王和跟随他的众人疲疲乏乏地到了一个地方，就在那里歇息歇息。

chapters.en: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙和以色列众人来到耶路撒冷；亚希多弗也与他同来。

chapters.en: And David’s friend Hushai the Archite went to Absalom and said to him, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
chapters.zh: 大卫的朋友亚基人户筛去见押沙龙，对他说：「愿王万岁！愿王万岁！」

chapters.en: “Is this the loyalty you show your friend?” Absalom replied. “Why did you not go with your friend?”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙问户筛说：「这是你恩待朋友吗？为什么不与你的朋友同去呢？」

chapters.en: “Not at all,” Hushai answered. “For the one chosen by the LORD, by this people, and by all the men of Israel—his I will be, and with him I will remain.
chapters.zh: 户筛对押沙龙说：「不然，耶和华和这民，并以色列众人所拣选的，我必归顺他，与他同住。

chapters.en: Furthermore, whom should I serve if not his son? As I served in your father’s presence, so also I will serve in yours.”
chapters.zh: 再者，我当服事谁呢？岂不是前王的儿子吗？我怎样服事你父亲，也必照样服事你。」

chapters.en: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, “Give me counsel. What should we do?”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙对亚希多弗说：「你们出个主意，我们怎样行才好？」

chapters.en: Ahithophel replied, “Sleep with your father’s concubines, whom he has left to take care of the palace. When all Israel hears that you have become a stench to your father, then the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened.”
chapters.zh: 亚希多弗对押沙龙说：「你父所留下看守宫殿的妃嫔，你可以与她们亲近。以色列众人听见你父亲憎恶你，凡归顺你人的手就更坚强。」

chapters.en: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and he slept with his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
chapters.zh: 于是人为押沙龙在宫殿的平顶上支搭帐棚；押沙龙在以色列众人眼前，与他父的妃嫔亲近。

chapters.en: Now in those days the advice of Ahithophel was like the consultation of the word of God. Such was the regard that both David and Absalom had for Ahithophel’s advice.
chapters.zh: 那时亚希多弗所出的主意好像人问上帝的话一样；他昔日给大卫，今日给押沙龙所出的主意，都是这样。

chapters.en: Furthermore, Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Let me choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of David.
chapters.zh: 亚希多弗又对押沙龙说：「求你准我挑选一万二千人，今夜我就起身追赶大卫，

chapters.en: I will attack him while he is weak and weary; I will throw him into a panic, and all the people with him will flee; I will strike down only the king
chapters.zh: 趁他疲乏手软，我忽然追上他，使他惊惶；跟随他的民必都逃跑，我就单杀王一人，

chapters.en: and bring all the people back to you as a bride returning to her husband. You seek the life of only one man; then all the people will be at peace.”
chapters.zh: 使众民都归顺你。你所寻找的人〔既然死了〕，众民就如已经归顺你；这样，也都平安无事了。」

chapters.en: This proposal seemed good to Absalom and all the elders of Israel.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙和以色列的长老都以这话为美。

chapters.en: Then Absalom said, “Summon Hushai the Archite as well, and let us hear what he too has to say.”
chapters.zh: 押沙龙说：「要召亚基人户筛来，我们也要听他怎样说。」

chapters.en: So Hushai came to Absalom, who told him, “Ahithophel has spoken this proposal. Should we carry it out? If not, what do you say?”
chapters.zh: 户筛到了押沙龙面前，押沙龙向他说：「亚希多弗是如此如此说的，我们照着他的话行可以不可以？若不可，你就说吧！」

chapters.en: Hushai replied, “This time the advice of Ahithophel is not sound.”
chapters.zh: 户筛对押沙龙说：「亚希多弗这次所定的谋不善。」

chapters.en: He continued, “You know your father and his men. They are mighty men, and as fierce as a wild bear robbed of her cubs. Moreover, your father is a man of war who will not spend the night with the troops.
chapters.zh: 户筛又说：「你知道，你父亲和跟随他的人都是勇士，现在他们心里恼怒，如同田野丢崽子的母熊一般，而且你父亲是个战士，必不和民一同住宿。

chapters.en: Surely by now he is hiding in a cave or some other location. If some of your troops fall first, whoever hears of it will say, ‘There has been a slaughter among the troops who follow Absalom.’
chapters.zh: 他现今或藏在坑中或在别处，若有人首先被杀，凡听见的必说：『跟随押沙龙的民被杀了。』

chapters.en: Then even the most valiant soldier with the heart of a lion will melt with fear, because all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man who has valiant men with him.
chapters.zh: 虽有人胆大如狮子，他的心也必消化；因为以色列人都知道你父亲是英雄，跟随他的人也都是勇士。

chapters.en: Instead, I advise that all Israel from Dan to Beersheba—a multitude like the sand on the seashore—be gathered to you, and that you yourself lead them into battle.
chapters.zh: 依我之计，不如将以色列众人－从但直到别是巴，如同海边的沙那样多－聚集到你这里来，你也亲自率领他们出战。

chapters.en: Then we will attack David wherever we find him, and we will descend on him like dew on the ground. And of all the men with him, not even one will remain.
chapters.zh: 这样，我们在何处遇见他，就下到他那里，如同露水下在地上一般，连他带跟随他的人，一个也不留下。

chapters.en: If he retreats to a city, all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down to the valley until not even a pebble can be found there.”
chapters.zh: 他若进了哪一座城，以色列众人必带绳子去，将那城拉到河里，甚至连一块小石头都不剩下。」

chapters.en: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The advice of Hushai the Archite is better than that of Ahithophel.” For the LORD had purposed to thwart the good counsel of Ahithophel in order to bring disaster on Absalom.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙和以色列众人说：「亚基人户筛的计谋比亚希多弗的计谋更好！」这是因耶和华定意破坏亚希多弗的良谋，为要降祸与押沙龙。

chapters.en: So Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, “This is what Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the elders of Israel, and this is what I have advised.
chapters.zh: 户筛对祭司撒督和亚比亚他说：「亚希多弗为押沙龙和以色列的长老所定的计谋是如此如此，我所定的计谋是如此如此。

chapters.en: Now send quickly and tell David, ‘Do not spend the night at the fords of the wilderness, but be sure to cross over. Otherwise the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.’”
chapters.zh: 现在你们要急速打发人去，告诉大卫说：『今夜不可住在旷野的渡口，务要过河，免得王和跟随他的人都被吞灭。』」

chapters.en: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel, where a servant girl would come and pass along information to them. They in turn would go and inform King David, for they dared not be seen entering the city.
chapters.zh: 那时，约拿单和亚希玛斯在隐‧罗结那里等候，不敢进城，恐怕被人看见。有一个使女出来，将这话告诉他们，他们就去报信给大卫王。

chapters.en: But a young man did see them and told Absalom. So the two left quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim. He had a well in his courtyard, and they climbed down into it.
chapters.zh: 然而有一个童子看见他们，就去告诉押沙龙。他们急忙跑到巴户琳某人的家里；那人院中有一口井，他们就下到井里。

chapters.en: Then the man’s wife took a covering, spread it over the mouth of the well, and scattered grain over it so nobody would know a thing.
chapters.zh: 那家的妇人用盖盖上井口，又在上头铺上碎麦，事就没有洩漏。

chapters.en:
When Absalom’s servants came to the woman at the house, they asked, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?”
“They have crossed over the brook,” she replied. The men searched but did not find them, so they returned to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙的仆人来到那家，问妇人说：「亚希玛斯和约拿单在哪里？」妇人说：「他们过了河了。」 仆人找他们，找不着，就回耶路撒冷去了。

chapters.en: After the men had gone, Ahimaaz and Jonathan climbed up out of the well and went to inform King David, saying, “Get up and cross over the river at once, for Ahithophel has given this advice against you.”
chapters.zh: 他们走后，二人从井里上来，去告诉大卫王说：「亚希多弗如此如此定计害你，你们务要起来，快快过河。」

chapters.en: So David and all the people with him got up and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak, there was no one left who had not crossed the Jordan.
chapters.zh: 于是大卫和跟随他的人都起来，过约旦河。到了天亮，无一人不过约旦河的。

chapters.en: When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his house in his hometown. He put his affairs in order and hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father’s tomb.
chapters.zh: 亚希多弗见不依从他的计谋，就备上驴，归回本城；到了家，留下遗言，便吊死了，葬在他父亲的坟墓里。

chapters.en: Then David went to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.
chapters.zh: 大卫到了玛哈念，押沙龙和跟随他的以色列人也都过了约旦河。

chapters.en: Absalom had appointed Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra, the Ishmaelite who had married Abigail, the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah the mother of Joab.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙立亚玛撒作元帅，代替约押。亚玛撒是〔以实玛利〕人〔注：又作以色列人〕以特拉的儿子。以特拉曾与拿辖的女儿亚比该亲近；这亚比该与约押的母亲洗鲁雅是姊妹。

chapters.en: So the Israelites and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙和以色列人都安营在基列地。

chapters.en: When David came to Mahanaim, he was met by Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim.
chapters.zh: 大卫到了玛哈念，亚扪族的拉巴人拿辖的儿子朔比，罗‧底巴人亚‧米利的儿子玛吉，基列的罗基琳人巴西莱，

chapters.en: They brought beds, basins, and earthen vessels, as well as wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils,
chapters.zh: 带着被、褥、盆、碗、瓦器、小麦、大麦、麦面、炒〔谷〕、豆子、红豆、炒〔豆〕、

chapters.en: honey, curds, sheep, and cheese from the herd for David and his people to eat. For they said, “The people have become hungry, exhausted, and thirsty in the wilderness.”
chapters.zh: 蜂蜜、奶油、绵羊、奶饼，供给大卫和跟随他的人吃；他们说：「民在旷野，必饥渴困乏了。」

chapters.en: Then David reviewed his troops and appointed over them commanders of thousands and of hundreds.
chapters.zh: 大卫数点跟随他的人，立千夫长、百夫长率领他们。

chapters.en: He sent out the troops, a third under Joab, a third under Joab’s brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the troops, “I will surely march out with you as well.”
chapters.zh: 大卫打发军兵出战，分为三队：一队在约押手下，一队在洗鲁雅的儿子、约押兄弟亚比筛手下，一队在迦特人以太手下。大卫对军兵说：「我必与你们一同出战。」

chapters.en: But the people pleaded, “You must not go out! For if we have to flee, they will not care about us. Even if half of us die, they will not care. But you are worth ten thousand of us. It is better now if you support us from the city.”
chapters.zh: 军兵却说：「你不可出战。若是我们逃跑，敌人必不介意；我们阵亡一半，敌人也不介意。因为你一人强似我们万人，你不如在城里预备帮助我们。」

chapters.en: “I will do whatever seems best to you,” the king replied. So he stood beside the gate, while all the troops marched out by hundreds and by thousands.
chapters.zh: 王向他们说：「你们以为怎样好，我就怎样行。」于是王站在城门旁，军兵或百或千地挨次出去了。

chapters.en: Now the king had commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, “Treat the young man Absalom gently for my sake.” And all the people heard the king’s orders to each of the commanders regarding Absalom.
chapters.zh: 王嘱咐约押、亚比筛、以太说：「你们要为我的缘故宽待那少年人押沙龙。」王为押沙龙嘱咐众将的话，兵都听见了。

chapters.en: So David’s army marched into the field to engage Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
chapters.zh: 兵就出到田野迎着以色列人，在以法莲树林里交战。

chapters.en: There the people of Israel were defeated by David’s servants, and the slaughter was great that day—twenty thousand men.
chapters.zh: 以色列人败在大卫的仆人面前；那日阵亡的甚多，共有二万人。

chapters.en: The battle spread over the whole countryside, and that day the forest devoured more people than the sword.
chapters.zh: 因为在那里四面打仗，死于树林的比死于刀剑的更多。

chapters.en: Now Absalom was riding on his mule when he met the servants of David, and as the mule went under the thick branches of a large oak, Absalom’s head was caught fast in the tree. The mule under him kept going, so that he was suspended in midair.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙偶然遇见大卫的仆人。押沙龙骑着骡子，从大橡树密枝底下经过，他的头〔发〕被树枝绕住，就悬挂起来，所骑的骡子便离他去了。

chapters.en: When one of the men saw this, he told Joab, “I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree!”
chapters.zh: 有个人看见，就告诉约押说：「我看见押沙龙挂在橡树上了。」

chapters.en: “You just saw him!” Joab exclaimed. “Why did you not strike him to the ground right there? I would have given you ten shekels of silver and a warrior’s belt!”
chapters.zh: 约押对报信的人说：「你既看见他，为什么不将他打死落在地上呢？〔你若打死他〕，我就赏你十〔舍客勒〕银子，一条带子。」

chapters.en: The man replied, “Even if a thousand shekels of silver were weighed out into my hands, I would not raise my hand against the son of the king. For we heard the king command you and Abishai and Ittai, ‘Protect the young man Absalom for my sake. ’
chapters.zh: 那人对约押说：「我就是得你一千〔舍客勒〕银子，我也不敢伸手害王的儿子；因为我们听见王嘱咐你和亚比筛并以太说：『你们要谨慎，不可害那少年人押沙龙。』

chapters.en: If I had jeopardized my own life —and nothing is hidden from the king—you would have abandoned me.”
chapters.zh: 我若妄为害了他的性命，就是你自己也必与我为敌（原来，无论何事都瞒不过王。）」

chapters.en: But Joab declared, “I am not going to wait like this with you!” And he took three spears in his hand and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the oak tree.
chapters.zh: 约押说：「我不能与你留连。」约押手拿三杆短枪，趁押沙龙在橡树上还活着，就刺透他的心。

chapters.en: And ten young men who carried Joab’s armor surrounded Absalom, struck him, and killed him.
chapters.zh: 给约押拿兵器的十个少年人围绕押沙龙，将他杀死。

chapters.en: Then Joab blew the ram’s horn, and the troops broke off their pursuit of Israel because Joab had restrained them.
chapters.zh: 约押吹角，拦阻众人，他们就回来，不再追赶以色列人。

chapters.en: They took Absalom, cast him into a large pit in the forest, and piled a huge mound of stones over him. Meanwhile, all the Israelites fled, each to his home.
chapters.zh: 他们将押沙龙丢在林中一个大坑里，上头堆起一大堆石头。以色列众人都逃跑，各回各家去了。

chapters.en: During his lifetime, Absalom had set up for himself a pillar in the King’s Valley, for he had said, “I have no son to preserve the memory of my name.” So he gave the pillar his name, and to this day it is called Absalom’s Monument.
chapters.zh: 押沙龙活着的时候，在王谷立了一根〔石〕柱，因他说：「我没有儿子为我留名。」他就以自己的名称那〔石〕柱叫押沙龙柱，直到今日。

chapters.en: Then Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, “Please let me run and tell the king the good news that the LORD has avenged him of his enemies.”
chapters.zh: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯说：「容我跑去，将耶和华向仇敌给王报仇的信息报与王知。」

chapters.en: But Joab replied, “You are not the man to take good news today. You may do it another day, but you must not do so today, because the king’s son is dead.”
chapters.zh: 约押对他说：「你今日不可去报信，改日可以报信；因为今日王的儿子死了，所以你不可去报信。」

chapters.en: So Joab said to a Cushite, “Go, tell the king what you have seen.” The Cushite bowed to Joab and took off running.
chapters.zh: 约押对古示人说：「你去将你所看见的告诉王。」古示人在约押面前下拜，就跑去了。

chapters.en:
Ahimaaz son of Zadok, however, persisted and said to Joab, “No matter what, please let me also run behind the Cushite!”
“My son,” Joab replied, “why do you want to run, since you will not receive a reward?”
chapters.zh: 撒督的儿子亚希玛斯又对约押说：「无论怎样，求你容我随着古示人跑去。」约押说：「我儿，你报这信息，既不得赏赐，何必要跑去呢？」

chapters.en:
“No matter what, I want to run!” he replied.
“Then run!” Joab told him.
So Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.
chapters.zh: 他〔又说〕：「无论怎样，我要跑去。」约押说：「你跑去吧！」亚希玛斯就从平原往前跑，跑过古示人去了。

chapters.en: Now David was sitting between the two gates when the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall, looked out, and saw a man running alone.
chapters.zh: 大卫正坐在城甕里。守望的人上城门楼的顶上，举目观看，见有一个人独自跑来。

chapters.en:
So he called out and told the king.
“If he is alone,” the king replied, “he bears good news.”
As the first runner drew near,
chapters.zh: 守望的人就大声告诉王。王说：「他若独自来，必是报口信的。」那人跑得渐渐近了。

chapters.en:
the watchman saw another man running, and he called out to the gatekeeper, “Look! Another man is running alone!”
“This one also brings good news,” said the king.
chapters.zh: 守望的人又见一人跑来，就对守城门的人说：「又有一人独自跑来。」王说：「这也必是报信的。」

chapters.en:
The watchman said, “The first man appears to me to be running like Ahimaaz son of Zadok.”
“This is a good man,” said the king. “He comes with good news.”
chapters.zh: 守望的人说：「我看前头人的跑法，好像撒督的儿子亚希玛斯的跑法一样。」王说：「他是个好人，必是报好信息。」

chapters.en:
Then Ahimaaz called out to the king, “All is well!” And he bowed facedown before the king.
He continued, “Blessed be the LORD your God! He has delivered up the men who raised their hands against my lord the king.”
chapters.zh: 亚希玛斯向王呼叫说：「平安了！」就在王面前脸伏于地叩拜，说：「耶和华－你的上帝是应当称颂的，因他已将那举手攻击我主我王的人交给王了。」

chapters.en:
The king asked, “Is the young man Absalom all right?”
And Ahimaaz replied, “When Joab sent the king’s servant and your servant, I saw a great tumult, but I do not know what it was.”
chapters.zh: 王问说：「少年人押沙龙平安不平安？」亚希玛斯回答说：「约押打发王的仆人，那时仆人听见众民大声喧哗，却不知道是什么事。」

chapters.en:
“Move aside,” said the king, “and stand here.”
So he stepped aside.
chapters.zh: 王说：「你退去，站在旁边。」他就退去，站在旁边。

chapters.en: Just then the Cushite came and said, “May my lord the king hear the good news: Today the LORD has avenged you of all who rose up against you!”
chapters.zh: 古示人也来到，说：「有信息报给我主我王！耶和华今日向一切兴起攻击你的人给你报仇了。」

chapters.en:
The king asked the Cushite, “Is the young man Absalom all right?”
And the Cushite replied, “May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up against you to harm you be like that young man.”
chapters.zh: 王问古示人说：「少年人押沙龙平安不平安？」古示人回答说：「愿我主我王的仇敌，和一切兴起要杀害你的人，都与那少年人一样。」

chapters.en: The king was shaken and went up to the chamber over the gate and wept. And as he walked, he cried out, “O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you, O Absalom, my son, my son!”
chapters.zh: 王就心里伤恸，上城门楼去哀哭，一面走一面说：「我儿押沙龙啊！我儿，我儿押沙龙啊！我恨不得替你死，押沙龙啊，我儿！我儿！」

chapters.en: Then it was reported to Joab, “The king is weeping and mourning over Absalom.”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉约押说：「王为押沙龙哭泣悲哀。」

chapters.en: And that day’s victory was turned into mourning for all the people, because on that day they were told, “The king is grieving over his son.”
chapters.zh: 众民听说王为他儿子忧愁，他们得胜的欢乐却变成悲哀。

chapters.en: So they returned to the city quietly that day, as people steal away in humiliation after fleeing a battle.
chapters.zh: 那日众民暗暗地进城，就如败阵逃跑、惭愧的民一般。

chapters.en: But the king covered his face and cried out at the top of his voice, “O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!”
chapters.zh: 王蒙着脸，大声哭号说：「我儿押沙龙啊！押沙龙，我儿，我儿啊！」

chapters.en: Then Joab went into the house and said to the king, “Today you have disgraced all your servants who have saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters, of your wives, and of your concubines.
chapters.zh: 约押进去见王，说：「你今日使你一切仆人脸面惭愧了！他们今日救了你的性命和你儿女妻妾的性命，

chapters.en: You love those who hate you and hate those who love you! For you have made it clear today that the commanders and soldiers mean nothing to you. I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead, it would have pleased you!
chapters.zh: 你却爱那恨你的人，恨那爱你的人。你今日明明地不以将帅、仆人为念。我今日看明，若押沙龙活着，我们都死亡，你就喜悦了。

chapters.en: Now therefore get up! Go out and speak comfort to your servants, for I swear by the LORD that if you do not go out, not a man will remain with you tonight. This will be worse for you than all the adversity that has befallen you from your youth until now!”
chapters.zh: 现在你当出去，安慰你仆人的心。我指着耶和华起誓：你若不出去，今夜必无一人与你同在一处；这祸患就比你从幼年到如今所遭的更甚！」

chapters.en:
So the king got up and sat in the gate, and all the people were told: “Behold, the king is sitting in the gate.” So they all came before the king.
Meanwhile, the Israelites had fled, each man to his home.
chapters.zh: 于是王起来，坐在城门口。众民听说王坐在城门口，就都到王面前。 以色列人已经逃跑，各回各家去了。

chapters.en: And all the people throughout the tribes of Israel were arguing, “The king rescued us from the hand of our enemies and delivered us from the hand of the Philistines, but now he has fled the land because of Absalom.
chapters.zh: 以色列众支派的人纷纷议论说：「王曾救我们脱离仇敌的手，又救我们脱离非利士人的手，现在他躲避押沙龙逃走了。

chapters.en: But Absalom, the man we anointed over us, has died in battle. So why do you say nothing about restoring the king?”
chapters.zh: 我们膏押沙龙治理我们，他已经阵亡。现在为什么不出一言请王回来呢？」

chapters.en: Then King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests: “Say to the elders of Judah, ‘Why should you be the last to restore the king to his palace, since the talk of all Israel has reached the king at his quarters?
chapters.zh: 大卫王差人去见祭司撒督和亚比亚他，说：「你们当向犹大长老说：『以色列众人已经有话请王回宫，你们为什么落在他们后头呢？

chapters.en: You are my brothers, my own flesh and blood. So why should you be the last to restore the king?’
chapters.zh: 你们是我的弟兄，是我的骨肉，为什么在人后头请王回来呢？』

chapters.en: And say to Amasa, ‘Aren’t you my flesh and blood? May God punish me, and ever so severely, if from now on you are not the commander of my army in place of Joab!’”
chapters.zh: 也要对亚玛撒说：『你不是我的骨肉吗？我若不立你替约押常作元帅，愿上帝重重地降罚与我！』」

chapters.en: So he swayed the hearts of all the men of Judah as though they were one man, and they sent word to the king: “Return, you and all your servants.”
chapters.zh: 如此就挽回犹大众人的心，如同一人的心。他们便打发人去见王，说：「请王和王的一切臣仆回来。」

chapters.en: So the king returned, and when he arrived at the Jordan, the men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet him and escort him across the Jordan.
chapters.zh: 王就回来，到了约旦河。犹大人来到吉甲，要去迎接王，请他过约旦河。

chapters.en: Then Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David,
chapters.zh: 巴户琳的便雅悯人、基拉的儿子示每急忙与犹大人一同下去迎接大卫王。

chapters.en:
along with a thousand men of Benjamin, as well as Ziba the steward of the house of Saul and his fifteen sons and twenty servants.
They rushed down to the Jordan before the king
chapters.zh: 跟从示每的有一千便雅悯人，还有扫罗家的仆人洗巴和他十五个儿子，二十个仆人；他们都诜过约旦河迎接王。

chapters.en:
and crossed at the ford to carry over the king’s household and to do what was good in his sight.
When Shimei son of Gera crossed the Jordan, he fell down before the king
chapters.zh: 有摆渡船过去，渡王的家眷，任王使用。 王要过约旦河的时候，基拉的儿子示每就俯伏在王面前，

chapters.en: and said, “My lord, do not hold me guilty, and do not remember your servant’s wrongdoing on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem. May the king not take it to heart.
chapters.zh: 对王说：「我主我王出耶路撒冷的时候，仆人行悖逆的事，现在求我主不要因此加罪与仆人，不要记念，也不要放在心上。

chapters.en: For your servant knows that I have sinned, so here I am today as the first of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet my lord the king.”
chapters.zh: 仆人明知自己有罪，所以约瑟全家之中，今日我首先下来迎接我主我王。」

chapters.en: But Abishai son of Zeruiah said, “Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD’s anointed?”
chapters.zh: 洗鲁雅的儿子亚比筛说：「示每既咒骂耶和华的受膏者，不应当治死他吗？」

chapters.en: And David replied, “Sons of Zeruiah, what have I to do with you, that you should be my adversaries today? Should any man be put to death in Israel today? Am I not indeed aware that today I am king over Israel?”
chapters.zh: 大卫说：「洗鲁雅的儿子，我与你们有何关涉，使你们今日与我反对呢？今日在以色列中岂可治死人呢？我岂不知今日我作以色列的王吗？」

chapters.en: So the king said to Shimei, “You shall not die.” And the king swore an oath to him.
chapters.zh: 于是王对示每说：「你必不死。」王就向他起誓。

chapters.en: Then Mephibosheth, Saul’s grandson, went down to meet the king. He had not cared for his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes from the day the king had left until the day he returned safely.
chapters.zh: 扫罗的孙子米非波设也下去迎接王。他自从王去的日子，直到王平平安安地回来，没有修脚，没有剃胡须，也没有洗衣服。

chapters.en: And he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, who asked him, “Mephibosheth, why did you not go with me?”
chapters.zh: 他来到耶路撒冷迎接王的时候，王问他说：「米非波设，你为什么没有与我同去呢？」

chapters.en: “My lord the king,” he replied, “because I am lame, I said, ‘I will have my donkey saddled so that I may ride on it and go with the king.’ But my servant Ziba deceived me,
chapters.zh: 他回答说：「我主我王，仆人是瘸腿的。那日我想要备驴骑上，与王同去，无奈我的仆人欺哄了我，

chapters.en:
and he has slandered your servant to my lord the king.
Yet my lord the king is like the angel of God, so do what is good in your eyes.
chapters.zh: 又在我主我王面前谗毁我。然而我主我王如同上帝的使者一般，你看怎样好，就怎样行吧！

chapters.en: For all the house of my grandfather deserves death from my lord the king, yet you have set your servant among those who eat at your table. What further right, then, do I have to keep appealing to the king?”
chapters.zh: 因为我祖全家的人，在我主我王面前都算为死人，王却使仆人在王的席上同人吃饭，我现在向王还能辨理诉冤吗？」

chapters.en: The king replied, “Why say any more? I hereby declare that you and Ziba are to divide the land.”
chapters.zh: 王对他说：「你何必再提你的事呢？我说，你与洗巴均分地土。」

chapters.en: And Mephibosheth said to the king, “Instead, since my lord the king has safely come to his own house, let Ziba take it all!”
chapters.zh: 米非波设对王说：「我主我王既平平安安地回宫，就任凭洗巴都取了也可以。」

chapters.en: Now Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim to cross the Jordan with the king and send him on his way from there.
chapters.zh: 基列人巴西莱从罗基琳下来，要送王过约旦河，就与王一同过了约旦河。

chapters.en: Barzillai was quite old, eighty years of age, and since he was a very wealthy man, he had provided for the king while he stayed in Mahanaim.
chapters.zh: 巴西莱年纪老迈，已经八十岁了。王住在玛哈念的时候，他就拿食物来供给王；他原是大富户。

chapters.en: The king said to Barzillai, “Cross over with me, and I will provide for you at my side in Jerusalem.”
chapters.zh: 王对巴西莱说：「你与我同去，我要在耶路撒冷那里养你的老。」

chapters.en: But Barzillai replied, “How many years of my life remain, that I should go up to Jerusalem with the king?
chapters.zh: 巴西莱对王说：「我在世的年日还能有多少，使我与王同上耶路撒冷呢？

chapters.en: I am now eighty years old. Can I discern what is good and what is not? Can your servant taste what he eats or drinks? Can I still hear the voice of singing men and women? Why should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king?
chapters.zh: 仆人现在八十岁了，还能尝出饮食的滋味、辨别美恶吗？还能听男女歌唱的声音吗？仆人何必累赘我主我王呢？

chapters.en: Your servant will go with the king only a short distance past the Jordan; why should the king repay me with such a reward?
chapters.zh: 仆人只要送王过约旦河，王何必赐我这样的恩典呢？

chapters.en: Please let your servant return, that I may die in my own city near the tomb of my father and mother. But here is your servant Chimham. Let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your sight.”
chapters.zh: 求你准我回去，好死在我本城，〔葬在〕我父母的墓旁。这里有王的仆人金罕，让他同我主我王过去，可以随意待他。」

chapters.en: The king replied, “Chimham will cross over with me, and I will do for him what is good in your sight, and I will do for you whatever you desire of me.”
chapters.zh: 王说：「金罕可以与我同去，我必照你的心愿待他。你向我求什么，我都必为你成就。」

chapters.en: So all the people crossed the Jordan, and then the king crossed over. The king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and Barzillai returned home.
chapters.zh: 于是众民过约旦河，王也过去。王与巴西莱亲嘴，为他祝福，巴西莱就回本地去了。

chapters.en: Then the king crossed over to Gilgal, and Chimham crossed over with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel escorted the king.
chapters.zh: 王过去，到了吉甲，金罕也跟他过去。犹大众民和以色列民的一半也都送王过去。

chapters.en: Soon all the men of Israel came to the king and asked, “Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, take you away secretly and bring the king and his household across the Jordan, together with all of David’s men?”
chapters.zh: 以色列众人来见王，对他说：「我们弟兄犹大人为什么暗暗送王和王的家眷，并跟随王的人过约旦河？」

chapters.en: And all the men of Judah replied to the men of Israel, “We did this because the king is our relative. Why does this anger you? Have we ever eaten at the king’s expense or received anything for ourselves?”
chapters.zh: 犹大众人回答以色列人说：「因为王与我们是亲属，你们为何因这事发怒呢？我们吃了王的什么呢？王赏赐了我们什么呢？」

chapters.en:
“We have ten shares in the king,” answered the men of Israel, “so we have more claim to David than you. Why then do you despise us? Were we not the first to speak of restoring our king?”
But the men of Judah spoke more fiercely than the men of Israel.
chapters.zh: 以色列人回答犹大人说：「按支派，我们与王有十分的情分；在大卫身上，我们也比你们更有情分。你们为何藐视我们，请王回来不先与我们商量呢？」 但犹大人的话比以色列人的话更硬。

chapters.en:
Now a worthless man named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjamite, happened to be there, and he blew the ram’s horn and shouted:
“We have no share in David, no inheritance in Jesse’s son. Every man to his tent, O Israel!”
chapters.zh: 在那里恰巧有一个匪徒，名叫示巴，是便雅悯人比基利的儿子。他吹角，说：「我们与大卫无分，与耶西的儿子无涉。以色列人哪，你们各回各家去吧！」

chapters.en: So all the men of Israel deserted David to follow Sheba son of Bichri. But the men of Judah stayed by their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 于是以色列人都离开大卫，跟随比基利的儿子示巴。但犹大人从约旦河直到耶路撒冷，都紧紧跟随他们的王。

chapters.en: When David returned to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to take care of the palace, and he placed them in a house under guard. He provided for them, but he no longer slept with them. They were confined until the day of their death, living as widows.
chapters.zh: 大卫王来到耶路撒冷，进了宫殿，就把从前留下看守宫殿的十个妃嫔禁闭在〔冷宫〕，养活她们，不与她们亲近。她们如同寡妇被禁，直到死的日子。

chapters.en: Then the king said to Amasa, “Summon the men of Judah to come to me within three days, and be here yourself.”
chapters.zh: 王对亚玛撒说：「你要在三日之内将犹大人招聚了来，你也回到这里来。」

chapters.en: So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he took longer than the time allotted him.
chapters.zh: 亚玛撒就去招聚犹大人，却耽延过了王所限的日期。

chapters.en: And David said to Abishai, “Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. Take your lord’s servants and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities and elude us. ”
chapters.zh: 大卫对亚比筛说：「现在恐怕比基利的儿子示巴加害于我们比押沙龙更甚。你要带领你主的仆人追赶他，免得他得了坚固城，躲避我们。」

chapters.en: So Joab’s men, along with the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men, marched out of Jerusalem in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.
chapters.zh: 约押的人和基利提人、比利提人，并所有的勇士，都跟着亚比筛，从耶路撒冷出去追赶比基利的儿子示巴。

chapters.en:
And while they were at the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa joined them.
Now Joab was dressed in military attire, with a dagger strapped to his belt. And as he stepped forward, he slipped the dagger from its sheath.
chapters.zh: 他们到了基遍的大磐石那里，亚玛撒来迎接他们。那时约押穿着战衣，腰束佩刀的带子，刀在鞘内；约押前行，刀从鞘内掉出来。

chapters.en: “Are you well, my brother?” Joab asked Amasa. And with his right hand Joab grabbed Amasa by the beard to kiss him.
chapters.zh: 约押〔左手拾起刀来〕，对亚玛撒说：「我兄弟，你好啊！」就用右手抓住亚玛撒的胡子，要与他亲嘴。

chapters.en: Amasa was not on guard against the dagger in Joab’s hand, and Joab stabbed him in the stomach and spilled out his intestines on the ground. And Joab did not need to strike him again, for Amasa was dead. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bichri.
chapters.zh: 亚玛撒没有防备约押手里所拿的刀；约押用刀刺入他的肚腹，他的肠子流在地上，没有再刺他，就死了。 约押和他兄弟亚比筛往前追赶比基利的儿子示巴。

chapters.en: One of Joab’s young men stood near Amasa and said, “Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David, let him follow Joab!”
chapters.zh: 有约押的一个少年人站在亚玛撒尸身旁边，〔对众人〕说：「谁喜悦约押，谁归顺大卫，就当跟随约押去。」

chapters.en: But Amasa wallowed in his blood in the middle of the road, and when the man saw that all the troops were stopping there, he dragged the body off the road into a field and threw a garment over it.
chapters.zh: 亚玛撒在道路上滚在自己的血里。那人见众民〔经过〕都站住，就把亚玛撒的尸身从路上挪到田间，用衣服遮盖。

chapters.en: As soon as Amasa’s body was removed from the road, all the men went on with Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.
chapters.zh: 尸身从路上挪移之后，众民就都跟随约押去追赶比基利的儿子示巴。

chapters.en: Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel-beth-maacah and through the entire region of the Berites, who gathered together and followed him.
chapters.zh: 他走遍以色列各支派，直到伯‧玛迦的亚比拉，并比利人的全地；那些地方的人也都聚集跟随他。

chapters.en:
And Joab’s troops came and besieged Sheba in Abel-beth-maacah and built a siege ramp against the outer rampart of the city.
As all the troops with Joab were battering the wall to topple it,
chapters.zh: 约押和跟随的人到了伯‧玛迦的亚比拉，围困示巴，就对着城筑垒；跟随约押的众民〔用锤〕撞城，要使城塌陷。

chapters.en: a wise woman called out from the city, “Listen! Listen! Please tell Joab to come here so that I may speak with him.”
chapters.zh: 有一个聪明妇人从城上呼叫说：「听啊，听啊，请约押近前来，我好与他说话。」

chapters.en:
When he had come near to her, the woman asked, “Are you Joab?”
“I am,” he replied.
“Listen to the words of your servant,” she said.
“I am listening,” he answered.
chapters.zh: 约押就近前来，妇人问他说：「你是约押不是？」他说：「我是。」妇人说：「求你听婢女的话。」约押说：「我听。」

chapters.en: Then the woman said, “Long ago they used to say, ‘Seek counsel at Abel,’ and that is how disputes were settled.
chapters.zh: 妇人说：「古时有话说，当先在亚比拉求问，然后事就定妥。

chapters.en: I am among the peaceable and faithful in Israel, but you are trying to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up the LORD’s inheritance?”
chapters.zh: 我们这城的人在以色列人中是和平、忠厚的。你为何要毁坏以色列中的大城，吞灭耶和华的产业呢？」

chapters.en: “Far be it!” Joab declared. “Far be it from me to swallow up or destroy!
chapters.zh: 约押回答说：「我决不吞灭毁坏，

chapters.en:
That is not the case. But a man named Sheba son of Bichri, from the hill country of Ephraim, has lifted up his hand against the king, against David. Deliver him alone, and I will depart from the city.”
“Look,” the woman replied, “his head will be thrown to you over the wall.”
chapters.zh: 乃因以法莲山地的一个人－比基利的儿子示巴－举手攻击大卫王，你们若将他一人交出来，我便离城而去。」妇人对约押说：「那人的首级必从城墙上丢给你。」

chapters.en: Then the woman went to all the people with her wise counsel, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it to Joab. So he blew the ram’s horn and his men dispersed from the city, each to his own home. And Joab returned to the king in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 妇人就凭她的智慧去劝众人。他们便割下比基利的儿子示巴的首级，丢给约押。约押吹角，众人就离城而散，各归各家去了。约押回耶路撒冷，到王那里。

chapters.en: Now Joab was over the whole army of Israel; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites;
chapters.zh: 约押作以色列全军的元帅；耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅统辖基利提人和比利提人；

chapters.en: Adoram was in charge of the forced labor; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
chapters.zh: 亚多兰掌管服苦的人；亚希律的儿子约沙法作史官；

chapters.en: Sheva was the scribe; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
chapters.zh: 示法作书记；撒督和亚比亚他作祭司〔长〕；

chapters.en: and Ira the Jairite was David’s priest.
chapters.zh: 睚珥人以拉作大卫的宰相。

chapters.en:
During the reign of David there was a famine for three successive years, and David sought the face of the LORD.
And the LORD said, “It is because of the blood shed by Saul and his family, because he killed the Gibeonites.”
chapters.zh: 大卫年间有饥荒，一连三年，大卫就求问耶和华。耶和华说：「这饥荒是因扫罗和他流人血之家杀死基遍人。」

chapters.en: At this, David summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them. (Now the Gibeonites were not Israelites, but a remnant of the Amorites. The Israelites had taken an oath concerning them, but in his zeal for Israel and Judah, Saul had sought to kill them.)
chapters.zh: 原来这基遍人不是以色列人，乃是亚摩利人中所剩的；以色列人曾向他们起誓，〔不杀灭他们〕，扫罗却为以色列人和犹大人发热心，想要杀灭他们。大卫王召了他们来，

chapters.en: So David asked the Gibeonites, “What shall I do for you? How can I make amends so that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD?”
chapters.zh: 问他们说：「我当为你们怎样行呢？可用什么赎这罪，使你们为耶和华的产业祝福呢？」

chapters.en:
The Gibeonites said to him, “We need no silver or gold from Saul or his house, nor should you put to death anyone in Israel for us.”
“Whatever you ask, I will do for you,” he replied.
chapters.zh: 基遍人回答说：「我们和扫罗与他家的事并不关乎金银，也不要因我们的缘故杀一个以色列人。」大卫说：「你们怎样说，我就为你们怎样行。」

chapters.en: And they answered the king, “As for the man who consumed us and plotted against us to exterminate us from existing within any border of Israel,
chapters.zh: 他们对王说：「那从前谋害我们、要灭我们、使我们不得再住以色列境内的人，

chapters.en:
let seven of his male descendants be delivered to us so that we may hang them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the LORD.”
“I will give them to you,” said the king.
chapters.zh: 现在愿将他的子孙七人交给我们，我们好在耶和华面前，将他们悬挂在耶和华拣选扫罗的基比亚。」王说：「我必交给你们。」

chapters.en: Now the king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the oath before the LORD between David and Jonathan son of Saul.
chapters.zh: 王因为曾与扫罗的儿子约拿单指着耶和华起誓〔结盟〕，就爱惜扫罗的孙子、约拿单的儿子米非波设，〔不交出来〕，

chapters.en: But the king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the two sons whom Rizpah daughter of Aiah had borne to Saul, as well as the five sons whom Merab daughter of Saul had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite.
chapters.zh: 却把爱雅的女儿利斯巴给扫罗所生的两个儿子亚摩尼、米非波设，和扫罗女儿米甲〔的姊姊〕给米何拉人巴西莱儿子亚得列所生的五个儿子

chapters.en: And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the hill before the LORD. So all seven of them fell together; they were put to death in the first days of the harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest.
chapters.zh: 交在基遍人的手里。基遍人就把他们，在耶和华面前，悬挂在山上，这七人就一同死亡。被杀的时候正是收割的日子，就是动手割大麦的时候。

chapters.en: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on a rock. From the beginning of the harvest until the rain from heaven poured down on the bodies, she did not allow the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
chapters.zh: 爱雅的女儿利斯巴用麻布在磐石上搭棚，从动手收割的时候直到天降雨在尸身上的时候，日间不容空中的雀鸟落在尸身上，夜间不让田野的走兽前来糟践。

chapters.en: When David was told what Saul’s concubine Rizpah, daughter of Aiah, had done,
chapters.zh: 有人将扫罗的妃嫔爱雅女儿利斯巴所行的这事告诉大卫。

chapters.en: he went and took the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen them from the public square of Beth-shan where the Philistines had hung the bodies after they had struck down Saul at Gilboa.
chapters.zh: 大卫就去，从基列‧雅比人那里将扫罗和他儿子约拿单的骸骨搬了来（是因非利士人从前在基利波杀扫罗，将尸身悬挂在伯‧珊的街市上，基列‧雅比人把尸身偷了去。）

chapters.en: So David had the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan brought from there, and they also gathered the bones of those who had been hanged.
chapters.zh: 大卫将扫罗和他儿子约拿单的骸骨从那里搬了来，又收殓被悬挂七人的骸骨，

chapters.en:
And they buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in Zela in the land of Benjamin, in the tomb of Saul’s father Kish.
After they had done everything the king had commanded, God answered their prayers for the land.
chapters.zh: 将扫罗和他儿子约拿单的骸骨葬在便雅悯的洗拉，在扫罗父亲基士的坟墓里；众人行了王所吩咐的。此后上帝垂听国民所求的。

chapters.en: Once again the Philistines waged war against Israel, and David and his servants went down and fought against the Philistines. But David became exhausted.
chapters.zh: 非利士人与以色列人打仗；大卫带领仆人下去，与非利士人接战，大卫就疲乏了。

chapters.en: Then Ishbi-benob, a descendant of Rapha, whose bronze spear weighed three hundred shekels and who was bearing a new sword, resolved to kill David.
chapters.zh: 伟人的一个儿子以实‧比诺要杀大卫；他的铜枪重三百〔舍客勒〕，又佩着新〔刀〕。

chapters.en:
But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his aid, struck the Philistine, and killed him.
Then David’s men swore to him, “You must never again go out with us to battle, so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished.”
chapters.zh: 但洗鲁雅的儿子亚比筛帮助大卫，攻打非利士人，将他杀死。当日，跟随大卫的人向大卫起誓说：「以后你不可再与我们一同出战，恐怕熄灭以色列的灯。」

chapters.en: Some time later at Gob, there was another battle with the Philistines. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph, a descendant of Rapha.
chapters.zh: 后来，以色列人在歌伯与非利士人打仗，户沙人西比该杀了伟人的一个儿子撒弗。

chapters.en: Once again there was a battle with the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan son of Jair the Bethlehemite killed the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.
chapters.zh: 又在歌伯与非利士人打仗，伯利恒人雅雷俄珥金的儿子伊勒哈难杀了迦特人歌利亚。这人的枪杆粗如织布的机轴。

chapters.en: And there was also a battle at Gath, where there was a man of great stature with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot—twenty-four in all. He too was descended from Rapha,
chapters.zh: 又在迦特打仗，那里有一个身量高大的人，手脚都是六指，共有二十四个指头；他也是伟人的儿子。

chapters.en: and when he taunted Israel, Jonathan the son of David’s brother Shimei killed him.
chapters.zh: 这人向以色列人骂阵，大卫的哥哥示米亚的儿子约拿单就杀了他。

chapters.en: So these four descendants of Rapha in Gath fell at the hands of David and his servants.
chapters.zh: 这四个人是迦特伟人的儿子，都死在大卫和他仆人的手下。

chapters.en: And David sang this song to the LORD on the day the LORD had delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
chapters.zh: 当耶和华救大卫脱离一切仇敌和扫罗之手的日子，他向耶和华念这诗，

chapters.en:
He said:
“The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer.
chapters.zh: 说： 耶和华是我的巖石， 我的山寨，我的救主，

chapters.en: My God is my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield, and the horn of my salvation. My stronghold, my refuge, and my Savior, You save me from violence.
chapters.zh: 我的上帝，我的磐石，我所投靠的。 他是我的盾牌，是拯救我的角， 是我的高台，是我的避难所。 我的救主啊，你是救我脱离强暴的。

chapters.en: I will call upon the LORD, who is worthy to be praised; so shall I be saved from my enemies.
chapters.zh: 我要求告当赞美的耶和华， 这样，我必从仇敌手中被救出来。

chapters.en: For the waves of death engulfed me; the torrents of chaos overwhelmed me.
chapters.zh: 曾有死亡的波浪环绕我， 匪类的急流使我惊惧，

chapters.en: The cords of Sheol entangled me; the snares of death confronted me.
chapters.zh: 阴间的绳索缠绕我， 死亡的网罗临到我。

chapters.en: In my distress I called upon the LORD; I cried out to my God. And from His temple He heard my voice, and my cry for help reached His ears.
chapters.zh: 我在急难中求告耶和华， 向我的上帝呼求。 他从殿中听了我的声音； 我的呼求入了他的耳中。

chapters.en:
Then the earth shook and quaked; the foundations of the heavens trembled;
they were shaken because He burned with anger.
chapters.zh: 那时因他发怒，地就摇撼战抖； 天的根基也震动摇撼。

chapters.en:
Smoke rose from His nostrils, and consuming fire came from His mouth;
glowing coals blazed forth.
chapters.zh: 从他鼻孔冒烟上腾； 从他口中发火焚烧，连炭也着了。

chapters.en: He parted the heavens and came down with dark clouds beneath His feet.
chapters.zh: 他又使天下垂，亲自降临； 有黑云在他脚下。

chapters.en: He mounted a cherub and flew; He soared on the wings of the wind.
chapters.zh: 他坐着基路伯飞行， 在风的翅膀上显现。

chapters.en: He made darkness a canopy around Him, a gathering of water and thick clouds.
chapters.zh: 他以黑暗和聚集的水、 天空的厚云为他四围的行宫。

chapters.en: From the brightness of His presence coals of fire blazed forth.
chapters.zh: 因他面前的光辉炭都着了。

chapters.en: The LORD thundered from heaven; the voice of the Most High resounded.
chapters.zh: 耶和华从天上打雷； 至高者发出声音。

chapters.en: He shot His arrows and scattered the foes; He hurled lightning and routed them.
chapters.zh: 他射出箭来，使仇敌四散， 发出闪电，使他们扰乱。

chapters.en: The channels of the sea appeared, and the foundations of the world were exposed at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of His nostrils.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的斥责一发，鼻孔的气一出， 海底就出现，大地的根基也显露。

chapters.en: He reached down from on high and took hold of me; He drew me out of deep waters.
chapters.zh: 他从高天伸手抓住我， 把我从大水中拉上来。

chapters.en: He rescued me from my powerful enemy, from foes too mighty for me.
chapters.zh: 他救我脱离我的劲敌和那些恨我的人， 因为他们比我强盛。

chapters.en: They confronted me in my day of calamity, but the LORD was my support.
chapters.zh: 我遭遇灾难的日子，他们来攻击我； 但耶和华是我的倚靠。

chapters.en: He brought me out into the open; He rescued me because He delighted in me.
chapters.zh: 他又领我到宽阔之处； 他救拔我，因他喜悦我。

chapters.en: The LORD has rewarded me according to my righteousness; He has repaid me according to the cleanness of my hands.
chapters.zh: 耶和华按着我的公义报答我， 按着我手中的清洁赏赐我。

chapters.en: For I have kept the ways of the LORD and have not wickedly departed from my God.
chapters.zh: 因为我遵守了耶和华的道， 未曾作恶离开我的上帝。

chapters.en: For all His ordinances are before me; I have not disregarded His statutes.
chapters.zh: 他的一切典章常在我面前； 他的律例，我也未曾离弃。

chapters.en: And I have been blameless before Him and kept myself from iniquity.
chapters.zh: 我在他面前作了完全人； 我也保守自己远离我的罪孽。

chapters.en: So the LORD has repaid me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness in His sight.
chapters.zh: 所以耶和华按我的公义， 按我在他眼前的清洁赏赐我。

chapters.en: To the faithful You show Yourself faithful, to the blameless You show Yourself blameless;
chapters.zh: 慈爱的人，你以慈爱待他； 完全的人，你以完全待他；

chapters.en: to the pure You show Yourself pure, but to the crooked You show Yourself shrewd.
chapters.zh: 清洁的人，你以清洁待他； 乖僻的人，你以弯曲待他。

chapters.en: You save an afflicted people, but Your eyes are on the haughty to bring them down.
chapters.zh: 困苦的百姓，你必拯救； 但你的眼目察看高傲的人，使他降卑。

chapters.en: For You, O LORD, are my lamp; the LORD lights up my darkness.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，你是我的灯； 耶和华必照明我的黑暗。

chapters.en: For in You I can charge an army; with my God I can scale a wall.
chapters.zh: 我藉着你冲入敌军， 藉着我的上帝跳过墙垣。

chapters.en: As for God, His way is perfect; the word of the LORD is flawless. He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him.
chapters.zh: 至于上帝，他的道是完全的； 耶和华的话是炼净的。 凡投靠他的，他便作他们的盾牌。

chapters.en: For who is God besides the LORD? And who is the Rock except our God?
chapters.zh: 除了耶和华，谁是上帝呢？ 除了我们的上帝，谁是磐石呢？

chapters.en: God is my strong fortress, and He makes my way clear.
chapters.zh: 上帝是我坚固的保障； 他引导完全人行他的路。

chapters.en: He makes my feet like those of a deer and stations me upon the heights.
chapters.zh: 他使我的脚快如母鹿的〔蹄〕， 又使我在高处安稳。

chapters.en: He trains my hands for battle; my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
chapters.zh: 他教导我的手能以争战， 甚至我的膀臂能开铜弓。

chapters.en: You have given me Your shield of salvation, and Your gentleness exalts me.
chapters.zh: 你把你的救恩给我作盾牌； 你的温和使我为大。

chapters.en: You broaden the path beneath me so that my ankles do not give way.
chapters.zh: 你使我脚下的地步宽阔； 我的脚未曾滑跌。

chapters.en: I pursued my enemies and destroyed them; I did not turn back until they were consumed.
chapters.zh: 我追赶我的仇敌，灭绝了他们， 未灭以先，我没有归回。

chapters.en: I devoured and crushed them so they could not rise; they have fallen under my feet.
chapters.zh: 我灭绝了他们， 打伤了他们，使他们不能起来； 他们都倒在我的脚下。

chapters.en: You have armed me with strength for battle; You have subdued my foes beneath me.
chapters.zh: 因为你曾以力量束我的腰，使我能争战； 你也使那起来攻击我的都服在我以下。

chapters.en: You have made my enemies retreat before me; I destroyed those who hated me.
chapters.zh: 你又使我的仇敌在我面前转背逃跑， 叫我能以剪除那恨我的人。

chapters.en: They looked, but there was no one to save them— to the LORD, but He did not answer.
chapters.zh: 他们仰望，却无人拯救； 就是呼求耶和华，他也不应允。

chapters.en: I ground them as the dust of the earth; I crushed and trampled them like mud in the streets.
chapters.zh: 我捣碎他们，如同地上的灰尘， 践踏他们，四散在地，如同街上的泥土。

chapters.en:
You have delivered me from the strife of my people; You have preserved me as the head of nations;
a people I had not known shall serve me.
chapters.zh: 你救我脱离我百姓的争竞， 保护我作列国的元首； 我素不认识的民必事奉我。

chapters.en: Foreigners cower before me; when they hear me, they obey me.
chapters.zh: 外邦人要投降我， 一听见我的名声就必顺从我。

chapters.en: Foreigners lose heart and come trembling from their strongholds.
chapters.zh: 外邦人要衰残， 战战兢兢地出他们的营寨。
