chapters.en: The LORD lives, and blessed be my Rock! And may God, the Rock of my salvation, be exalted—
chapters.zh: 耶和华是活神，愿我的磐石被人称颂！ 愿上帝－那拯救我的磐石被人尊崇！

chapters.en: the God who avenges me and brings down nations beneath me,
chapters.zh: 这位上帝就是那为我伸冤、 使众民服在我以下的。

chapters.en: who frees me from my enemies. You exalt me above my foes; You rescue me from violent men.
chapters.zh: 你救我脱离仇敌， 又把我举起，高过那些起来攻击我的； 你救我脱离强暴的人。

chapters.en: Therefore I will praise You, O LORD, among the nations; I will sing praises to Your name.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，因此我要在外邦中称谢你， 歌颂你的名。

chapters.en:
Great salvation He brings to His king. He shows loving devotion to His anointed,
to David and his descendants forever.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华赐极大的救恩给他〔所立〕的王， 施慈爱给他的受膏者， 就是给大卫和他的后裔， 直到永远！

chapters.en:
These are the last words of David:
“The oracle of David son of Jesse, the oracle of the man raised on high, the one anointed by the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel:
chapters.zh: 以下是大卫末了的话。耶西的儿子大卫得居高位，是雅各上帝所膏的，作以色列的美歌者，说：

chapters.en: The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; His word was on my tongue.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的灵藉着我说： 他的话在我口中。

chapters.en: The God of Israel spoke; the Rock of Israel said to me, ‘He who rules the people with justice, who rules in the fear of God,
chapters.zh: 以色列的上帝、 以色列的磐石晓谕我说： 那以公义治理人民的， 敬畏上帝执掌权柄，

chapters.en: is like the light of the morning at sunrise of a cloudless dawn, the glistening after the rain on the sprouting grass of the earth.’
chapters.zh: 他必像日出的晨光， 如无云的清晨， 雨后的晴光， 使地〔发生〕嫩草。

chapters.en: Is not my house right with God? For He has established with me an everlasting covenant, ordered and secured in every part. Will He not bring about my full salvation and my every desire?
chapters.zh: 我家在上帝面前并非如此； 上帝却与我立永远的约。 这约凡事坚稳， 关乎我的一切救恩和我一切所想望的， 他岂不为我成就吗？

chapters.en: But the worthless are all like thorns raked aside, for they can never be gathered by hand.
chapters.zh: 但匪类都必像荆棘被丢弃； 人不敢用手拿它；

chapters.en: The man who touches them must be armed with iron or with the shaft of a spear. The fire burns them to ashes in the place where they lie.”
chapters.zh: 拿它的人必带铁器和枪杆， 终久它必被火焚烧。

chapters.en:
These are the names of David’s mighty men:
Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite was chief of the Three. He wielded his spear against eight hundred men, whom he killed at one time.
chapters.zh: 大卫勇士的名字记在下面：他革扪人约设‧巴设，又称伊斯尼人亚底挪，他是军长的统领，一时击杀了八百人。

chapters.en: Next in command was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite. As one of the three mighty men, he went with David to taunt the Philistines who had gathered for battle at Pas-dammim. The men of Israel retreated,
chapters.zh: 其次是亚合人朵多的儿子以利亚撒。从前非利士人聚集要打仗，以色列人迎着上去，有跟随大卫的三个勇士向非利士人骂阵，其中有以利亚撒。

chapters.en: but Eleazar stood his ground and struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary and stuck to his sword. The LORD brought about a great victory that day. Then the troops returned to him, but only to plunder the dead.
chapters.zh: 他起来击杀非利士人，直到手臂疲乏，手黏住刀把。那日耶和华使〔以色列〕人大获全胜；众民在以利亚撒后头专夺财物。

chapters.en: And after him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. When the Philistines had banded together near a field full of lentils, Israel’s troops fled from them.
chapters.zh: 其次是哈拉人亚基的儿子沙玛。一日，非利士人聚集成群，在一块长满红豆的田里，众民就在非利士人面前逃跑。

chapters.en: But Shammah took his stand in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines. So the LORD brought about a great victory.
chapters.zh: 沙玛却站在那田间击杀非利士人，救护了那田。耶和华使〔以色列〕人大获全胜。

chapters.en: At harvest time, three of the thirty chief men went down to David at the cave of Adullam, while a company of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.
chapters.zh: 收割的时候，有三十个勇士中的三个人下到亚杜兰洞见大卫。非利士的军兵在利乏音谷安营。

chapters.en: At that time David was in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was at Bethlehem.
chapters.zh: 那时大卫在山寨，非利士人的防营在伯利恒。

chapters.en: David longed for water and said, “Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!”
chapters.zh: 大卫渴想，说：「甚愿有人将伯利恒城门旁、井里的水打来给我喝。」

chapters.en: So the three mighty men broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem, and brought it back to David. But he refused to drink it; instead, he poured it out to the LORD,
chapters.zh: 这三个勇士就闯过非利士人的营盘，从伯利恒城门旁的井里打水，拿来奉给大卫。他却不肯喝，将水奠在耶和华面前，

chapters.en:
saying, “Far be it from me, O LORD, to do this! Is this not the blood of the men who risked their lives?” So he refused to drink it.
Such were the exploits of the three mighty men.
chapters.zh: 说：「耶和华啊，这三个人冒死〔去打水〕；〔这水〕好像他们的血一般，我断不敢喝。」如此，大卫不肯喝。这是三个勇士所做的事。

chapters.en: Now Abishai, the brother of Joab and son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Three, and he wielded his spear against three hundred men, killed them, and won a name along with the Three.
chapters.zh: 洗鲁雅的儿子、约押的兄弟亚比筛是这三个勇士的首领；他举枪杀了三百人，就在三个勇士里得了名。

chapters.en: Was he not more honored than the Three? And he became their commander, even though he was not included among the Three.
chapters.zh: 他在这三个勇士里是最尊贵的，所以作他们的首领，只是不及前三个勇士。

chapters.en: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a man of valor from Kabzeel, a man of many exploits. He struck down two champions of Moab, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
chapters.zh: 有甲薛勇士耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅行过大能的事；他杀了摩押人亚利伊勒的两个儿子，又在下雪的时候下坑里去，杀了一个狮子，

chapters.en: He also struck down an Egyptian, a huge man. Although the Egyptian had a spear in his hand, Benaiah went against him with a club, snatched the spear from his hand, and killed the Egyptian with his own spear.
chapters.zh: 又杀了一个强壮的埃及人；埃及人手里拿着枪，比拿雅只拿着棍子下去，从埃及人手里夺过枪来，用那枪将他杀死。

chapters.en: These were the exploits of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who won a name along with the three mighty men.
chapters.zh: 这是耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅所行的事，就在三个勇士里得了名。

chapters.en: He was most honored among the Thirty, but he did not become one of the Three. And David appointed him over his guard.
chapters.zh: 他比那三十个勇士都尊贵，只是不及前三个勇士。大卫立他作护卫长。

chapters.en:
Now these were members of the Thirty:
Asahel the brother of Joab,
Elhanan son of Dodo of Bethlehem,
chapters.zh: 三十个勇士里有约押的兄弟亚撒黑，伯利恒人朵多的儿子伊勒哈难，

chapters.en:
Shammah the Harodite,
Elika the Harodite,
chapters.zh: 哈律人沙玛，哈律人以利加，

chapters.en:
Helez the Paltite,
Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
chapters.zh: 帕勒提人希利斯，提哥亚人益吉的儿子以拉，

chapters.en:
Abiezer the Anathothite,
Mebunnai the Hushathite,
chapters.zh: 亚拿突人亚比以谢，户沙人米本乃，

chapters.en:
Zalmon the Ahohite,
Maharai the Netophathite,
chapters.zh: 亚合人撒们，尼陀法人玛哈莱，

chapters.en:
Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite,
Ittai son of Ribai from Gibeah of the Benjamites,
chapters.zh: 尼陀法人巴拿的儿子希立，便雅悯族、基比亚人利拜的儿子以太，

chapters.en:
Benaiah the Pirathonite,
Hiddai from the brooks of Gaash,
chapters.zh: 比拉顿人比拿雅，迦实溪人希太，

chapters.en:
Abi-albon the Arbathite,
Azmaveth the Barhumite,
chapters.zh: 伯亚拉巴人亚比亚本，巴鲁米人押斯玛弗，

chapters.en:
Eliahba the Shaalbonite,
the sons of Jashen,
Jonathan
chapters.zh: 沙本人以利雅哈巴，雅善儿子中的约拿单，

chapters.en:
son of Shammah the Hararite,
Ahiam son of Sharar the Hararite,
chapters.zh: 哈拉人沙玛，哈拉人沙拉的儿子亚希暗，

chapters.en:
Eliphelet son of Ahasbai the Maacathite,
Eliam son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
chapters.zh: 玛迦人亚哈拜的儿子以利法列，基罗人亚希多弗的儿子以连，

chapters.en:
Hezro the Carmelite,
Paarai the Arbite,
chapters.zh: 迦密人希斯莱，亚巴人帕莱，

chapters.en:
Igal son of Nathan of Zobah,
Bani the Gadite,
chapters.zh: 琐巴人拿单的儿子以甲，迦得人巴尼，

chapters.en:
Zelek the Ammonite,
Naharai the Beerothite, the armor-bearer of Joab son of Zeruiah,
chapters.zh: 亚扪人洗勒，比录人拿哈莱（是给洗鲁雅的儿子约押拿兵器的），

chapters.en:
Ira the Ithrite,
Gareb the Ithrite,
chapters.zh: 以帖人以拉，以帖人迦立，

chapters.en:
and Uriah the Hittite.
There were thirty-seven in all.
chapters.zh: 赫人乌利亚，共有三十七人。

chapters.en: Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He stirred up David against them, saying, “Go and take a census of Israel and Judah.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华又向以色列人发怒，就激动大卫，使他吩咐人去数点以色列人和犹大人。

chapters.en: So the king said to Joab the commander of his army, who was with him, “Go now throughout the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba and register the troops, so that I may know their number.”
chapters.zh: 大卫就吩咐跟随他的元帅约押说：「你去走遍以色列众支派，从但直到别是巴，数点百姓，我好知道他们的数目。」

chapters.en: But Joab replied to the king, “May the LORD your God multiply the troops a hundred times over, and may the eyes of my lord the king see it. But why does my lord the king want to do such a thing?”
chapters.zh: 约押对王说：「无论百姓多少，愿耶和华－你的上帝再加增百倍，使我主我王亲眼得见。我主我王何必喜悦行这事呢？」

chapters.en: Nevertheless, the king’s word prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army departed from the presence of the king to register the troops of Israel.
chapters.zh: 但王的命令胜过约押和众军长。约押和众军长就从王面前出去，数点以色列的百姓。

chapters.en: They crossed the Jordan and camped near Aroer, south of the town in the middle of the valley, and proceeded toward Gad and Jazer.
chapters.zh: 他们过了约旦河，在迦得谷中、城的右边亚罗珥安营，与雅谢相对，

chapters.en: Then they went to Gilead and the land of Tahtim-hodshi, and on to Dan-jaan and around to Sidon.
chapters.zh: 又到了基列和他停‧合示地，又到了但‧雅安，绕到西顿，

chapters.en: They went toward the fortress of Tyre and all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites. Finally, they went on to the Negev of Judah, to Beersheba.
chapters.zh: 来到泰尔的保障，并希未人和迦南人的各城，又到犹大南方的别是巴。

chapters.en: At the end of nine months and twenty days, having gone through the whole land, they returned to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 他们走遍全地，过了九个月零二十天，就回到耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: And Joab reported to the king the total number of the troops. In Israel there were 800,000 men of valor who drew the sword, and in Judah there were 500,000.
chapters.zh: 约押将百姓的总数奏告于王：以色列拿刀的勇士有八十万；犹大有五十万。

chapters.en: After David had numbered the troops, his conscience was stricken and he said to the LORD, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done. Now, O LORD, I beg You to take away the iniquity of Your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.”
chapters.zh: 大卫数点百姓以后，就心中自责，祷告耶和华说：「我行这事大有罪了。耶和华啊，求你除掉仆人的罪孽，因我所行的甚是愚昧。」

chapters.en: When David got up in the morning, the word of the LORD had come to Gad the prophet, David’s seer:
chapters.zh: 大卫早晨起来，耶和华的话临到先知迦得，就是大卫的先见，说：

chapters.en: “Go and tell David that this is what the LORD says: ‘I am offering you three options. Choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you.’”
chapters.zh: 「你去告诉大卫，说耶和华如此说：『我有三样灾，随你选择一样，我好降与你。』」

chapters.en: So Gad went and said to David, “Do you choose to endure three years of famine in your land, three months of fleeing the pursuit of your enemies, or three days of plague upon your land? Now then, think it over and decide how I should reply to Him who sent me.”
chapters.zh: 于是迦得来见大卫，对他说：「你愿意国中有七年的饥荒呢？是在你敌人面前逃跑，被追赶三个月呢？是在你国中有三日的瘟疫呢？现在你要揣摩思想，我好回复那差我来的。」

chapters.en: David answered Gad, “I am deeply distressed. Please, let us fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are great; but do not let me fall into the hands of men.”
chapters.zh: 大卫对迦得说：「我甚为难！我愿落在耶和华的手里，因为他有丰盛的怜悯。我不愿落在人的手里。」

chapters.en: So the LORD sent a plague upon Israel from that morning until the appointed time, and seventy thousand of the people from Dan to Beersheba died.
chapters.zh: 于是，耶和华降瘟疫与以色列人，自早晨到所定的时候；从但直到别是巴，民间死了七万人。

chapters.en: But when the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD relented from the calamity and said to the angel who was destroying the people, “Enough! Withdraw your hand now!” At that time the angel of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
chapters.zh: 天使向耶路撒冷伸手要灭城的时候，耶和华后悔，就不降这灾了，吩咐灭民的天使说：「够了！住手吧！」那时耶和华的使者在耶布斯人亚劳拿的禾场那里。

chapters.en: When David saw the angel striking down the people, he said to the LORD, “Surely I, the shepherd, have sinned and acted wickedly. But these sheep, what have they done? Please, let Your hand fall upon me and my father’s house.”
chapters.zh: 大卫看见灭民的天使，就祷告耶和华说：「我犯了罪，行了恶；但这群羊做了什么呢？愿你的手攻击我和我的父家。」

chapters.en: And that day Gad came to David and said to him, “Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”
chapters.zh: 当日，迦得来见大卫，对他说：「你上去，在耶布斯人亚劳拿的禾场上为耶和华筑一座坛。」

chapters.en: So David went up at the word of Gad, just as the LORD had commanded.
chapters.zh: 大卫就照着迦得奉耶和华名所说的话上去了。

chapters.en: When Araunah looked out and saw the king and his servants coming toward him, he went out and bowed facedown before the king.
chapters.zh: 亚劳拿观看，见王和他臣仆前来，就迎接出去，脸伏于地，向王下拜，

chapters.en:
“Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” Araunah said.
“To buy your threshing floor,” David replied, “that I may build an altar to the LORD, so that the plague upon the people may be halted.”
chapters.zh: 说：「我主我王为何来到仆人这里呢？」大卫说：「我要买你这禾场，为耶和华筑一座坛，使民间的瘟疫止住。」

chapters.en: Araunah said to David, “May my lord the king take whatever seems good to him and offer it up. Here are the oxen for a burnt offering and the threshing sledges and ox yokes for the wood.
chapters.zh: 亚劳拿对大卫说：「我主我王，你喜悦用什么，就拿去献祭。看哪，这里有牛可以作燔祭，有打粮的器具和套牛的轭可以当柴烧。

chapters.en: O king, Araunah gives all these to the king.” He also said to the king, “May the LORD your God accept you.”
chapters.zh: 王啊，这一切，我亚劳拿都奉给你」；又对王说：「愿耶和华－你的上帝悦纳你。」

chapters.en:
“No,” replied the king, “I insist on paying a price, for I will not offer to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing.”
So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
chapters.zh: 王对亚劳拿说：「不然。我必要按着价值向你买；我不肯用白得之物作燔祭献给耶和华－我的上帝。」大卫就用五十舍客勒银子买了那禾场与牛。

chapters.en:
And there he built an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.
Then the LORD answered the prayers on behalf of the land, and the plague upon Israel was halted.
chapters.zh: 大卫在那里为耶和华筑了一座坛，献燔祭和平安祭。如此，耶和华垂听国民所求的，瘟疫在以色列人中就止住了。

chapters.en: Now King David was old and well along in years, and though they covered him with blankets, he could not keep warm.
chapters.zh: 大卫王年纪老迈，虽用被遮盖，仍不觉暖。

chapters.en: So his servants said to him, “Let us search for a young virgin for our lord the king, to attend to him and care for him and lie by his side to keep him warm.”
chapters.zh: 所以臣仆对他说：「不如为我主我王寻找一个处女，使她伺候王，奉养王，睡在王的怀中，好叫我主我王得暖。」

chapters.en: Then they searched throughout Israel for a beautiful girl, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.
chapters.zh: 于是在以色列全境寻找美貌的童女，寻得书念的一个童女亚比煞，就带到王那里。

chapters.en: The girl was unsurpassed in beauty; she cared for the king and served him, but he had no relations with her.
chapters.zh: 这童女极其美貌，她奉养王，伺候王，王却没有与她亲近。

chapters.en: At that time Adonijah, David’s son by Haggith, began to exalt himself, saying, “I will be king!” And he acquired chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run ahead of him.
chapters.zh: 那时，哈及的儿子亚多尼雅自尊，说：「我必作王」，就为自己预备车辆、马兵，又派五十人在他前头奔走。

chapters.en: (His father had never once reprimanded him by saying, “Why do you act this way?” Adonijah was also very handsome, born next after Absalom.)
chapters.zh: 他父亲素来没有使他忧闷，说：「你是做什么呢？」他甚俊美，生在押沙龙之后。

chapters.en: So Adonijah conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, who supported him.
chapters.zh: 亚多尼雅与洗鲁雅的儿子约押，和祭司亚比亚他商议；二人就顺从他，帮助他。

chapters.en: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David’s mighty men would not join Adonijah.
chapters.zh: 但祭司撒督、耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅、先知拿单、示每、利以，并大卫的勇士都不顺从亚多尼雅。

chapters.en: And Adonijah sacrificed sheep, oxen, and fattened calves near the stone of Zoheleth, which is next to En-rogel. He invited all his royal brothers and all the men of Judah who were servants of the king.
chapters.zh: 一日，亚多尼雅在隐‧罗结旁、琐希列磐石那里宰了牛羊、肥犊，请他的诸弟兄，就是王的众子，并所有作王臣仆的犹大人；

chapters.en: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, or his brother Solomon.
chapters.zh: 惟独先知拿单和比拿雅并勇士，与他的兄弟所罗门，他都没有请。

chapters.en: Then Nathan said to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, “Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David does not know it?
chapters.zh: 拿单对所罗门的母亲拔示巴说：「哈及的儿子亚多尼雅作王了，你没有听见吗？我们的主大卫却不知道。

chapters.en: Now please, come and let me advise you. Save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.
chapters.zh: 现在我可以给你出个主意，好保全你和你儿子所罗门的性命。

chapters.en: Go at once to King David and say, ‘My lord the king, did you not swear to your maidservant, “Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne”? Why then has Adonijah become king?’
chapters.zh: 你进去见大卫王，对他说：『我主我王啊，你不曾向婢女起誓说：你儿子所罗门必接续我作王，坐在我的位上吗？现在亚多尼雅怎么作了王呢？』

chapters.en: Then, while you are still there speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words.”
chapters.zh: 你还与王说话的时候，我也随后进去，证实你的话。」

chapters.en: So Bathsheba went to see the king in his bedroom. Since the king was very old, Abishag the Shunammite was serving him.
chapters.zh: 拔示巴进入内室见王，王甚老迈，书念的童女亚比煞正伺候王。

chapters.en: And Bathsheba bowed down in homage to the king, who asked, “What is your desire?”
chapters.zh: 拔示巴向王屈身下拜；王说：「你要什么？」

chapters.en: “My lord,” she replied, “you yourself swore to your maidservant by the LORD your God: ‘Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne.’
chapters.zh: 她说：「我主啊，你曾向婢女指着耶和华－你的上帝起誓〔说〕：『你儿子所罗门必接续我作王，坐在我的位上。』

chapters.en: But now, behold, Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, do not know it.
chapters.zh: 现在亚多尼雅作王了，我主我王却不知道。

chapters.en: And he has sacrificed an abundance of oxen, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the other sons of the king, as well as Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander of the army. But he has not invited your servant Solomon.
chapters.zh: 他宰了许多牛羊、肥犊，请了王的众子和祭司亚比亚他，并元帅约押；惟独王的仆人所罗门，他没有请。

chapters.en: And as for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are upon you to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
chapters.zh: 我主我王啊，以色列众人的眼目都仰望你，等你晓谕他们，在我主我王之后谁坐你的位。

chapters.en: Otherwise, when my lord the king rests with his fathers, I and my son Solomon will be counted as criminals.”
chapters.zh: 若不然，到我主我王与列祖同睡以后，我和我儿子所罗门必算为罪人了。」

chapters.en: And just then, while Bathsheba was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.
chapters.zh: 拔示巴还与王说话的时候，先知拿单也进来了。

chapters.en: So the king was told, “Nathan the prophet is here.” And Nathan went in and bowed facedown before the king.
chapters.zh: 有人奏告王说：「先知拿单来了。」拿单进到王前，脸伏于地。

chapters.en: “My lord the king,” said Nathan, “did you say, ‘Adonijah will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne’?
chapters.zh: 拿单说：「我主我王果然应许亚多尼雅说『你必接续我作王，坐在我的位上』吗？

chapters.en: For today he has gone down and sacrificed an abundance of oxen, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the sons of the king, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest. And behold, they are eating and drinking before him, saying, ‘Long live King Adonijah!’
chapters.zh: 他今日下去，宰了许多牛羊、肥犊，请了王的众子和军长，并祭司亚比亚他；他们正在亚多尼雅面前吃喝，说：『愿亚多尼雅王万岁！』

chapters.en: But me your servant he has not invited, nor Zadok the priest, nor Benaiah son of Jehoiada, nor your servant Solomon.
chapters.zh: 惟独我，就是你的仆人和祭司撒督，耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅，并王的仆人所罗门，他都没有请。

chapters.en: Has my lord the king let this happen without informing your servant who should sit on the throne after my lord the king?”
chapters.zh: 这事果然出乎我主我王吗？王却没有告诉仆人们，在我主我王之后谁坐你的位。」

chapters.en: Then King David said, “Call in Bathsheba for me.” So she came into the king’s presence and stood before him.
chapters.zh: 大卫王吩咐说：「叫拔示巴来。」拔示巴就进来，站在王面前。

chapters.en: And the king swore an oath, saying, “As surely as the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from all distress,
chapters.zh: 王起誓说：「我指着救我性命脱离一切苦难、永生的耶和华起誓。

chapters.en: I will carry out this very day exactly what I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel: Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne in my place.”
chapters.zh: 我既然指着耶和华－以色列的上帝向你起誓说：你儿子所罗门必接续我作王，坐在我的位上。我今日就必照这话而行。」

chapters.en: Bathsheba bowed facedown in homage to the king and said, “May my lord King David live forever!”
chapters.zh: 于是，拔示巴脸伏于地，向王下拜，说：「愿我主大卫王万岁！」

chapters.en: Then King David said, “Call in for me Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada.” So they came before the king.
chapters.zh: 大卫王又吩咐说：「将祭司撒督、先知拿单、耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅召来！」他们就都来到王面前。

chapters.en: “Take my servants with you,” said the king. “Set my son Solomon on my own mule and take him down to Gihon.
chapters.zh: 王对他们说：「要带领你们主的仆人，使我儿子所罗门骑我的骡子，送他下到基训；

chapters.en: There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint him king over Israel. You are to blow the ram’s horn and declare, ‘Long live King Solomon!’
chapters.zh: 在那里，祭司撒督和先知拿单要膏他作以色列的王；你们也要吹角，说：『愿所罗门王万岁！』

chapters.en: Then you shall go up with him, and he is to come and sit on my throne and reign in my place. For I have appointed him ruler over Israel and Judah.”
chapters.zh: 然后要跟随他上来，使他坐在我的位上，接续我作王。我已立他作以色列和犹大的君。」

chapters.en: “Amen,” replied Benaiah son of Jehoiada. “May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, so declare it.
chapters.zh: 耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅对王说：「阿们！愿耶和华－我主我王的上帝也这样命定。

chapters.en: Just as the LORD was with my lord the king, so may He be with Solomon and make his throne even greater than that of my lord King David.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华怎样与我主我王同在，愿他照样与所罗门同在，使他的国位比我主大卫王的国位更大。」

chapters.en: Then Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, along with the Cherethites and Pelethites, went down and set Solomon on King David’s mule, and they escorted him to Gihon.
chapters.zh: 于是，祭司撒督、先知拿单、耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅，和基利提人、比利提人都下去使所罗门骑大卫王的骡子，将他送到基训。

chapters.en: Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tabernacle and anointed Solomon. Then they blew the ram’s horn, and all the people proclaimed, “Long live King Solomon!”
chapters.zh: 祭司撒督就从帐幕中取了盛膏油的角来，用膏膏所罗门。人就吹角，众民都说：「愿所罗门王万岁！」

chapters.en: All the people followed him, playing flutes and rejoicing with such a great joy that the earth was split by the sound.
chapters.zh: 众民跟随他上来，且吹笛，大大欢呼，声音震地。

chapters.en: Now Adonijah and all his guests were finishing their feast when they heard the sound of the ram’s horn. “Why is the city in such a loud uproar?” asked Joab.
chapters.zh: 亚多尼雅和所请的众客筵宴方毕，听见这声音；约押听见角声就说：「城中为何有这响声呢？」

chapters.en: As he was speaking, suddenly Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest arrived. “Come in,” said Adonijah, “for you are a man of valor. You must be bringing good news.”
chapters.zh: 他正说话的时候，祭司亚比亚他的儿子约拿单来了。亚多尼雅对他说：「进来吧！你是个忠义的人，必是报好信息。」

chapters.en: “Not at all,” Jonathan replied. “Our lord King David has made Solomon king.
chapters.zh: 约拿单对亚多尼雅说：「我们的主大卫王诚然立所罗门为王了。

chapters.en: And with Solomon, the king has sent Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada, along with the Cherethites and Pelethites, and they have set him on the king’s mule.
chapters.zh: 王差遣祭司撒督、先知拿单、耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅，和基利提人、比利提人都去使所罗门骑王的骡子。

chapters.en: Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king at Gihon, and they have gone up from there with rejoicing that rings out in the city. That is the noise you hear.
chapters.zh: 祭司撒督和先知拿单在基训已经膏他作王。众人都从那里欢呼着上来，声音使城震动，这就是你们所听见的声音；

chapters.en: Moreover, Solomon has taken his seat on the royal throne.
chapters.zh: 并且所罗门登了国位。

chapters.en:
The king’s servants have also gone to congratulate our lord King David, saying, ‘May your God make the name of Solomon more famous than your own name, and may He make his throne greater than your throne.’
And the king has bowed in worship on his bed,
chapters.zh: 王的臣仆也来为我们的主大卫王祝福，说：『愿王的上帝使所罗门的名比王的名更尊荣；使他的国位比王的国位更大。』王就在床上屈身下拜。

chapters.en: saying, ‘Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel! Today He has provided one to sit on my throne, and my eyes have seen it.’”
chapters.zh: 王又说：『耶和华－以色列的上帝是应当称颂的；因他赐我一人今日坐在我的位上，我也亲眼看见了。』」

chapters.en: At this, all the guests of Adonijah arose in terror and scattered.
chapters.zh: 亚多尼雅的众客〔听见这话〕就都惊惧，起来四散。

chapters.en: But Adonijah, in fear of Solomon, got up and went to take hold of the horns of the altar.
chapters.zh: 亚多尼雅惧怕所罗门，就起来，去抓住祭坛的角。

chapters.en: It was reported to Solomon: “Behold, Adonijah fears King Solomon, and he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, ‘Let King Solomon first swear to me not to put his servant to the sword.’”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉所罗门说：「亚多尼雅惧怕所罗门王，现在抓住祭坛的角，说：『愿所罗门王今日向我起誓，必不用刀杀仆人。』」

chapters.en: And Solomon replied, “If he is a man of character, not a single hair of his will fall to the ground. But if evil is found in him, he will die.”
chapters.zh: 所罗门说：「他若作忠义的人，连一根头发也不致落在地上；他若行恶，必要死亡。」

chapters.en: So King Solomon summoned Adonijah down from the altar, and he came and bowed down before King Solomon, who said to him, “Go to your home.”
chapters.zh: 于是所罗门王差遣人，使亚多尼雅从坛上下来，他就来，向所罗门王下拜；所罗门对他说：「你回家去吧！」

chapters.en: As the time drew near for David to die, he charged his son Solomon,
chapters.zh: 大卫的死期临近了，就嘱咐他儿子所罗门说：

chapters.en: “I am about to go the way of all the earth. So be strong and prove yourself a man.
chapters.zh: 「我现在要走世人必走的路。所以，你当刚强，作大丈夫，

chapters.en: And keep the charge of the LORD your God to walk in His ways and to keep His statutes, commandments, ordinances, and decrees, as written in the Law of Moses, so that you may prosper in all you do and wherever you turn,
chapters.zh: 遵守耶和华－你上帝所吩咐的，照着摩西律法上所写的行主的道，谨守他的律例、诫命、典章、法度。这样，你无论做什么事，不拘往何处去，尽都亨通。

chapters.en: and so that the LORD may fulfill His promise to me: ‘If your descendants take heed to walk faithfully before Me with all their heart and soul, you will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.’
chapters.zh: 耶和华必成就向我所应许的话说：『你的子孙若谨慎自己的行为，尽心尽意诚诚实实地行在我面前，就不断人坐以色列的国位。』

chapters.en: Moreover, you know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me—what he did to Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, the two commanders of the armies of Israel. He killed them in peacetime to avenge the blood of war. He stained with the blood of war the belt around his waist and the sandals on his feet.
chapters.zh: 你知道洗鲁雅的儿子约押向我所行的，就是杀了以色列的两个元帅：尼珥的儿子押尼珥和益帖的儿子亚玛撒。他在太平之时流这二人的血，如在争战之时一样，将这血染了腰间束的带和脚上穿的鞋。

chapters.en: So act according to your wisdom, and do not let his gray head go down to Sheol in peace.
chapters.zh: 所以你要照你的智慧行，不容他白头安然下阴间。

chapters.en: But show loving devotion to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, because they stood by me when I fled from your brother Absalom.
chapters.zh: 你当恩待基列人巴西莱的众子，使他们常与你同席吃饭；因为我躲避你哥哥押沙龙的时候，他们〔拿食物〕来迎接我。

chapters.en: Keep an eye on Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite from Bahurim who is with you. He called down bitter curses against me on the day I went to Mahanaim, but when he came down to meet me at the Jordan, I swore to him by the LORD: ‘I will never put you to the sword.’
chapters.zh: 在你这里有巴户琳的便雅悯人，基拉的儿子示每；我往玛哈念去的那日，他用狠毒的言语咒骂我，后来却下约旦河迎接我，我就指着耶和华向他起誓说：『我必不用刀杀你。』

chapters.en: Now therefore, do not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man. You know what you ought to do to him to bring his gray head down to Sheol in blood.”
chapters.zh: 现在你不要以他为无罪。你是聪明人，必知道怎样待他，使他白头见杀，流血下到阴间。」

chapters.en: Then David rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.
chapters.zh: 大卫与他列祖同睡，葬在大卫城。

chapters.en: The length of David’s reign over Israel was forty years—seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 大卫作以色列王四十年：在希伯崙作王七年，在耶路撒冷作王三十三年。

chapters.en: So Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was firmly established.
chapters.zh: 所罗门坐他父亲大卫的位，他的国甚是坚固。

chapters.en:
Now Adonijah son of Haggith went to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon, and she asked, “Do you come in peace?”
“Yes, in peace,” he replied.
chapters.zh: 哈及的儿子亚多尼雅去见所罗门的母亲拔示巴，拔示巴问他说：「你来是为平安吗？」回答说：「是为平安」；

chapters.en:
Then he said, “I have something to tell you.”
“Say it,” she answered.
chapters.zh: 又说：「我有话对你说。」拔示巴说：「你说吧。」

chapters.en: “You know that the kingship was mine,” he said. “All Israel expected that I should reign, but the kingship has turned to my brother, for it has come to him from the LORD.
chapters.zh: 亚多尼雅说：「你知道国原是归我的，以色列众人也都仰望我作王，不料，国反归了我兄弟，因他得国是出乎耶和华。

chapters.en:
So now I have just one request of you; do not deny me.”
“State your request,” she told him.
chapters.zh: 现在我有一件事求你，望你不要推辞。」拔示巴说：「你说吧。」

chapters.en: Adonijah replied, “Please speak to King Solomon, since he will not turn you down. Let him give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife.”
chapters.zh: 他说：「求你请所罗门王将书念的女子亚比煞赐我为妻，因他必不推辞你。」

chapters.en: “Very well,” Bathsheba replied. “I will speak to the king for you.”
chapters.zh: 拔示巴说：「好，我必为你对王提说。」

chapters.en: So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. The king stood up to greet her, bowed to her, and sat down on his throne. Then the king had a throne brought for his mother, who sat down at his right hand.
chapters.zh: 于是，拔示巴去见所罗门王，要为亚多尼雅提说；王起来迎接，向她下拜，就坐在位上，吩咐人为王母设一座位，她便坐在王的右边。

chapters.en:
“I have just one small request of you,” she said. “Do not deny me.”
“Make your request, my mother,” the king replied, “for I will not deny you.”
chapters.zh: 拔示巴说：「我有一件小事求你，望你不要推辞。」王说：「请母亲说，我必不推辞。」

chapters.en: So Bathsheba said, “Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife.”
chapters.zh: 拔示巴说：「求你将书念的女子亚比煞赐给你哥哥亚多尼雅为妻。」

chapters.en: King Solomon answered his mother, “Why do you request Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Since he is my older brother, you might as well request the kingdom for him and for Abiathar the priest and for Joab son of Zeruiah!”
chapters.zh: 所罗门王对他母亲说：「为何单替他求书念的女子亚比煞呢？也可以为他求国吧！他是我的哥哥，他有祭司亚比亚他和洗鲁雅的儿子约押〔为辅佐〕。」

chapters.en: Then King Solomon swore by the LORD: “May God punish me, and ever so severely, if Adonijah has not made this request at the expense of his life.
chapters.zh: 所罗门王就指着耶和华起誓说：「亚多尼雅这话是自己送命，不然，愿上帝重重地降罚与我。

chapters.en: And now, as surely as the LORD lives—the One who established me, who set me on the throne of my father David, and who founded for me a dynasty as He promised—surely Adonijah shall be put to death today!”
chapters.zh: 耶和华坚立我，使我坐在父亲大卫的位上，照着所应许的话为我建立家室；现在我指着永生的耶和华起誓，亚多尼雅今日必被治死。」

chapters.en: So King Solomon gave orders to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he struck down Adonijah and he died.
chapters.zh: 于是所罗门王差遣耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅，将亚多尼雅杀死。

chapters.en: Then the king said to Abiathar the priest, “Go back to your fields in Anathoth. Even though you deserve to die, I will not put you to death at this time, since you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before my father David, and you suffered through all that my father suffered.”
chapters.zh: 王对祭司亚比亚他说：「你回亚拿突归自己的田地去吧！你本是该死的，但因你在我父亲大卫面前抬过主耶和华的〔约〕柜，又与我父亲同受一切苦难，所以我今日不将你杀死。」

chapters.en: So Solomon banished Abiathar from the priesthood of the LORD and thus fulfilled the word that the LORD had spoken at Shiloh against the house of Eli.
chapters.zh: 所罗门就革除亚比亚他，不许他作耶和华的祭司。这样，便应验耶和华在示罗论以利家所说的话。

chapters.en: When the news reached Joab, who had conspired with Adonijah but not with Absalom, he fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.
chapters.zh: 约押虽然没有归从押沙龙，却归从了亚多尼雅。他听见这风声，就逃到耶和华的帐幕，抓住祭坛的角。

chapters.en:
It was reported to King Solomon: “Joab has fled to the tent of the LORD and is now beside the altar.”
So Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, “Go, strike him down!”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉所罗门王说：「约押逃到耶和华的帐幕，现今在祭坛的旁边。」所罗门就差遣耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅，说：「你去将他杀死。」

chapters.en:
And Benaiah entered the tent of the LORD and said to Joab, “The king says, ‘Come out!’”
But Joab replied, “No, I will die here.”
So Benaiah relayed the message to the king, saying, “This is how Joab answered me.”
chapters.zh: 比拿雅来到耶和华的帐幕，对约押说：「王吩咐说，你出来吧！」他说：「我不出去，我要死在这里。」比拿雅就去回复王，说约押如此如此回答我。

chapters.en: And the king replied, “Do just as he says. Strike him down and bury him, and so remove from me and from the house of my father the innocent blood that Joab shed.
chapters.zh: 王说：「你可以照着他的话行，杀死他，将他葬埋，好叫约押流无辜人血的罪不归我和我的父家了。

chapters.en: The LORD will bring his bloodshed back upon his own head, for without the knowledge of my father David he struck down two men more righteous and better than he when he put to the sword Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel’s army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah’s army.
chapters.zh: 耶和华必使约押流人血的罪归到他自己的头上；因为他用刀杀了两个比他又义又好的人，就是以色列元帅尼珥的儿子押尼珥和犹大元帅益帖的儿子亚玛撒，我父亲大卫却不知道。

chapters.en: Their blood will come back upon the heads of Joab and his descendants forever; but for David, his descendants, his house, and his throne, there shall be peace from the LORD forever.”
chapters.zh: 故此，流这二人血的罪必归到约押和他后裔的头上，直到永远；惟有大卫和他的后裔，并他的家与国，必从耶和华那里得平安，直到永远。」

chapters.en: So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up, struck down Joab, and killed him. He was buried at his own home in the wilderness.
chapters.zh: 于是耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅上去，将约押杀死，葬在旷野约押自己的坟墓〔注：原文是房屋〕里。

chapters.en: And the king appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada in Joab’s place over the army, and he appointed Zadok the priest in Abiathar’s place.
chapters.zh: 王就立耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅作元帅，代替约押，又使祭司撒督代替亚比亚他。

chapters.en: Then the king summoned Shimei and said to him, “Build a house for yourself in Jerusalem and live there, but do not go anywhere else.
chapters.zh: 王差遣人将示每召来，对他说：「你要在耶路撒冷建造房屋居住，不可出来往别处去。

chapters.en: On the day you go out and cross the Kidron Valley, know for sure that you will die; your blood will be on your own head.”
chapters.zh: 你当确实地知道，你何日出来过汲沦溪，何日必死！你的罪〔注：原文是血〕必归到自己的头上。」

chapters.en: “The sentence is fair,” Shimei replied. “Your servant will do as my lord the king has spoken.” And Shimei lived in Jerusalem for a long time.
chapters.zh: 示每对王说：「这话甚好！我主我王怎样说，仆人必怎样行。」于是示每多日住在耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: After three years, however, two of Shimei’s slaves ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. And Shimei was told, “Look, your slaves are in Gath.”
chapters.zh: 过了三年，示每的两个仆人逃到迦特王玛迦的儿子亚吉那里去。有人告诉示每说：「你的仆人在迦特。」

chapters.en: So Shimei saddled his donkey and set out to Achish at Gath in search of his slaves, and he brought them back from Gath.
chapters.zh: 示每起来，备上驴，往迦特到亚吉那里去找他的仆人，就从迦特带他仆人回来。

chapters.en: When Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned,
chapters.zh: 有人告诉所罗门说：「示每出耶路撒冷往迦特去，回来了。」

chapters.en: the king summoned Shimei and said to him, “Did I not make you swear by the LORD and warn you, ‘On the day you leave and go elsewhere, know for sure that you will die’? And you told me, ‘The sentence is fair; I will comply.’
chapters.zh: 王就差遣人将示每召了来，对他说：「我岂不是叫你指着耶和华起誓，并且警戒你说『你当确实地知道，你哪日出来往别处去，那日必死』吗？你也对我说：『这话甚好，我必听从。』

chapters.en: So why have you not kept your oath to the LORD and the command that I gave you?”
chapters.zh: 现在你为何不遵守你指着耶和华起的誓和我所吩咐你的命令呢？」

chapters.en: The king also said, “You know in your heart all the evil that you did to my father David. Therefore the LORD will bring your evil back upon your head.
chapters.zh: 王又对示每说：「你向我父亲大卫所行的一切恶事，你自己心里也知道，所以耶和华必使你的罪恶归到自己的头上；

chapters.en: But King Solomon will be blessed and David’s throne will remain secure before the LORD forever.”
chapters.zh: 惟有所罗门王必得福，并且大卫的国位必在耶和华面前坚定，直到永远。」

chapters.en: Then the king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck Shimei down, and he died. Thus the kingdom was firmly established in the hand of Solomon.
chapters.zh: 于是王吩咐耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅，他就去杀死示每。这样，便坚定了所罗门的国位。

chapters.en: Later, Solomon formed an alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt by marrying his daughter. Solomon brought her to the City of David until he had finished building his palace and the house of the LORD, as well as the wall around Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 所罗门与埃及王法老结亲，娶了法老的女儿为妻，接她进入大卫城，直等到造完了自己的宫和耶和华的殿，并耶路撒冷周围的城墙。

chapters.en: The people, however, were still sacrificing on the high places because a house for the Name of the LORD had not yet been built.
chapters.zh: 当那些日子，百姓仍在邱坛献祭，因为还没有为耶和华的名建殿。

chapters.en: And Solomon loved the LORD and walked in the statutes of his father David, except that he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
chapters.zh: 所罗门爱耶和华，遵行他父亲大卫的律例，只是还在邱坛献祭烧香。

chapters.en: Now the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for it was the great high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on the altar there.
chapters.zh: 所罗门王上基遍去献祭；因为在那里有极大〔注：或译：出名〕的邱坛，他在那坛上献一千牺牲作燔祭。

chapters.en: One night at Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream, and God said, “Ask, and I will give it to you!”
chapters.zh: 在基遍，夜间梦中，耶和华向所罗门显现，对他说：「你愿我赐你什么？你可以求。」

chapters.en: Solomon replied, “You have shown much loving devotion to Your servant, my father David, because he walked before You in faithfulness, righteousness, and uprightness of heart. And You have maintained this loving devotion by giving him a son to sit on his throne this very day.
chapters.zh: 所罗门说：「你仆人－我父亲大卫用诚实、公义、正直的心行在你面前，你就向他大施恩典，又为他存留大恩，赐他一个儿子坐在他的位上，正如今日一样。

chapters.en: And now, O LORD my God, You have made Your servant king in my father David’s place. But I am only a little child, not knowing how to go out or come in.
chapters.zh: 耶和华－我的上帝啊，如今你使仆人接续我父亲大卫作王；但我是幼童，不知道应当怎样出入。

chapters.en: Your servant is here among the people You have chosen, a people too numerous to count or number.
chapters.zh: 仆人住在你所拣选的民中，这民多得不可胜数。

chapters.en: Therefore give Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people and to discern between good and evil. For who is able to govern this great people of Yours?”
chapters.zh: 所以求你赐我智慧，可以判断你的民，能辨别是非。不然，谁能判断这众多的民呢？」

chapters.en: Now it pleased the Lord that Solomon had made this request.
chapters.zh: 所罗门因为求这事，就蒙主喜悦。

chapters.en: So God said to him, “Since you have asked for this instead of requesting long life or wealth for yourself or death for your enemies—but you have asked for discernment to administer justice—
chapters.zh: 上帝对他说：「你既然求这事，不为自己求寿、求富，也不求灭绝你仇敌的性命，单求智慧可以听讼，

chapters.en: behold, I will do what you have asked. I will give you a wise and discerning heart, so that there will never have been another like you, nor will there ever be.
chapters.zh: 我就应允你所求的，赐你聪明智慧，甚至在你以前没有像你的，在你以后也没有像你的。

chapters.en: Moreover, I will give you what you did not request—both riches and honor—so that during all your days no man in any kingdom will be your equal.
chapters.zh: 你所没有求的，我也赐给你，就是富足、尊荣，使你在世的日子，列王中没有一个能比你的。

chapters.en: So if you walk in My ways and keep My statutes and commandments, just as your father David did, I will prolong your days.”
chapters.zh: 你若效法你父亲大卫，遵行我的道，谨守我的律例、诫命，我必使你长寿。」

chapters.en: Then Solomon awoke, and indeed it had been a dream. So he returned to Jerusalem, stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then he held a feast for all his servants.
chapters.zh: 所罗门醒了，不料是个梦。他就回到耶路撒冷，站在耶和华的约柜前，献燔祭和平安祭，又为他众臣仆设摆筵席。

chapters.en: At that time two prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.
chapters.zh: 一日，有两个妓女来，站在王面前。

chapters.en: One woman said, “Please, my lord, this woman and I live in the same house, and I gave birth while she was in the house.
chapters.zh: 一个说：「我主啊，我和这妇人同住一房；她在房中的时候，我生了一个男孩。

chapters.en: On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also had a baby. We were alone, with no one in the house but the two of us.
chapters.zh: 我生孩子后第三日，这妇人也生了孩子。我们是同住的，除了我们二人之外，房中再没有别人。

chapters.en: During the night this woman’s son died because she rolled over on him.
chapters.zh: 夜间，这妇人睡着的时候，压死了她的孩子。

chapters.en: So she got up in the middle of the night and took my son from my side while I was asleep. She laid him in her bosom and put her dead son at my bosom.
chapters.zh: 她半夜起来，趁我睡着，从我旁边把我的孩子抱去，放在她怀里，将她的死孩子放在我怀里。

chapters.en: The next morning, when I got up to nurse my son, I discovered he was dead. But when I examined him, I realized that he was not the son I had borne.”
chapters.zh: 天要亮的时候，我起来要给我的孩子吃奶，不料，孩子死了；及至天亮，我细细地察看，不是我所生的孩子。」

chapters.en:
“No,” said the other woman, “the living one is my son and the dead one is your son.”
But the first woman insisted, “No, the dead one is yours and the living one is mine.” So they argued before the king.
chapters.zh: 那妇人说：「不然，活孩子是我的，死孩子是你的。」这妇人说：「不然，死孩子是你的，活孩子是我的。」她们在王面前如此争论。

chapters.en: Then the king replied, “This woman says, ‘My son is alive and yours is dead,’ but that woman says, ‘No, your son is dead and mine is alive.’”
chapters.zh: 王说：「这妇人说『活孩子是我的，死孩子是你的』，那妇人说『不然，死孩子是你的，活孩子是我的』」，

chapters.en: The king continued, “Bring me a sword.” So they brought him a sword,
chapters.zh: 就吩咐说：「拿刀来！」人就拿刀来。

chapters.en: and the king declared, “Cut the living child in two and give half to one and half to the other.”
chapters.zh: 王说：「将活孩子劈成两半，一半给那妇人，一半给这妇人。」

chapters.en:
Then the woman whose son was alive spoke to the king because she yearned with compassion for her son. “Please, my lord,” she said, “give her the living baby. Do not kill him!”
But the other woman said, “He will be neither mine nor yours. Cut him in two!”
chapters.zh: 活孩子的母亲为自己的孩子心里急痛，就说：「求我主将活孩子给那妇人吧，万不可杀他！」那妇人说：「这孩子也不归我，也不归你，把他劈了吧！」

chapters.en: Then the king gave his ruling: “Give the living baby to the first woman. By no means should you kill him; she is his mother.”
chapters.zh: 王说：「将活孩子给这妇人，万不可杀他；这妇人实在是他的母亲。」

chapters.en: When all Israel heard of the judgment the king had given, they stood in awe of him, for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to administer justice.
chapters.zh: 以色列众人听见王这样判断，就都敬畏他；因为见他心里有上帝的智慧，能以断案。

chapters.en: So King Solomon ruled over Israel,
chapters.zh: 所罗门作以色列众人的王。

chapters.en:
and these were his chief officials:
Azariah son of Zadok was the priest;
chapters.zh: 他的臣子记在下面：撒督的儿子亚撒利雅作祭司，

chapters.en:
Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, were secretaries;
Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
chapters.zh: 示沙的两个儿子以利何烈、亚希亚作书记，亚希律的儿子约沙法作史官，

chapters.en:
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the army;
Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
chapters.zh: 耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅作元帅，撒督和亚比亚他作祭司〔长〕，

chapters.en:
Azariah son of Nathan was in charge of the governors;
Zabud son of Nathan was a priest and adviser to the king;
chapters.zh: 拿单的儿子亚撒利雅作众吏长，王的朋友拿单的儿子撒布得作领袖，

chapters.en:
Ahishar was in charge of the palace;
and Adoniram son of Abda was in charge of the forced labor.
chapters.zh: 亚希煞作家宰，亚比大的儿子亚多尼兰掌管服苦的人。

chapters.en: Solomon had twelve governors over all Israel to provide food for the king and his household. Each one would arrange provisions for one month of the year,
chapters.zh: 所罗门在以色列全地立了十二个官吏，使他们供给王和王家的食物，每年各人供给一月。

chapters.en:
and these were their names:
Ben-hur in the hill country of Ephraim;
chapters.zh: 他们的名字记在下面：在以法莲山地有便‧户珥；

chapters.en: Ben-deker in Makaz, in Shaalbim, in Beth-shemesh, and in Elon-beth-hanan;
chapters.zh: 在玛迦斯、沙宾、伯‧示麦、以伦‧伯‧哈南有便‧底甲；

chapters.en: Ben-hesed in Arubboth (Socoh and all the land of Hepher belonged to him);
chapters.zh: 在亚鲁泊有便‧希悉，他管理梭哥和希弗全地；

chapters.en: Ben-abinadab in Naphath-dor (Taphath, a daughter of Solomon, was his wife);
chapters.zh: 在多珥山冈〔注：或译：全境〕有便‧亚比拿达，他娶了所罗门的女儿她法为妻；

chapters.en: Baana son of Ahilud in Taanach, in Megiddo, and in all of Beth-shean next to Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah and on past Jokmeam;
chapters.zh: 在他纳和米吉多，并靠近撒拉他拿、耶斯列下边的伯‧善全地，从伯‧善到亚伯‧米何拉直到约念之外，有亚希律的儿子巴拿；

chapters.en: Ben-geber in Ramoth-gilead (the villages of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead belonged to him, as well as the region of Argob in Bashan with its sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars);
chapters.zh: 在基列的拉末有便‧基别，他管理在基列的玛拿西子孙睚珥的城邑，巴珊的亚珥歌伯地的大城六十座，都有城墙和铜闩；

chapters.en: Ahinadab son of Iddo in Mahanaim;
chapters.zh: 在玛哈念有易多的儿子亚希拿达；

chapters.en: Ahimaaz in Naphtali (he had married Basemath, a daughter of Solomon);
chapters.zh: 在拿弗他利有亚希玛斯，他也娶了所罗门的一个女儿巴实抹为妻；

chapters.en: Baana son of Hushai in Asher and in Aloth;
chapters.zh: 在亚设和亚禄有户筛的儿子巴拿；

chapters.en: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah in Issachar;
chapters.zh: 在以萨迦有帕路亚的儿子约沙法；

chapters.en: Shimei son of Ela in Benjamin;
chapters.zh: 在便雅悯有以拉的儿子示每；

chapters.en:
Geber son of Uri in the land of Gilead, including the territories of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan.
There was also one governor in the land of Judah.
chapters.zh: 在基列地，就是〔从前属〕亚摩利王西宏和巴珊王噩之地，有乌利的儿子基别一人管理。

chapters.en: The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore, and they were eating and drinking and rejoicing.
chapters.zh: 犹大人和以色列人如同海边的沙那样多，都吃喝快乐。

chapters.en: And Solomon reigned over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt. These kingdoms offered tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.
chapters.zh: 所罗门统管诸国，从大河到非利士地，直到埃及的边界。所罗门在世的日子，这些国都进贡服事他。

chapters.en: Solomon’s provisions for a single day were thirty cors of fine flour, sixty cors of meal,
chapters.zh: 所罗门每日所用的食物：细面三十歌珥，粗面六十歌珥，

chapters.en: ten fat oxen, twenty range oxen, and a hundred sheep, as well as deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened poultry.
chapters.zh: 肥牛十只，草场的牛二十只，羊一百只，还有鹿、羚羊、誁子，并肥禽。

chapters.en: For Solomon had dominion over everything west of the Euphrates —over all the kingdoms from Tiphsah to Gaza—and he had peace on all sides.
chapters.zh: 所罗门管理大河西边的诸王，以及从提弗萨直到迦萨的全地，四境尽都平安。

chapters.en: Throughout the days of Solomon, Judah and Israel dwelt securely from Dan to Beersheba, each man under his own vine and his own fig tree.
chapters.zh: 所罗门在世的日子，从但到别是巴的犹大人和以色列人都在自己的葡萄树下和无花果树下安然居住。

chapters.en: Solomon had 4,000 stalls for his chariot horses and 12,000 horses.
chapters.zh: 所罗门有套车的马四万，还有马兵一万二千。

chapters.en: Each month the governors in turn provided food for King Solomon and all who came to his table. They saw to it that nothing was lacking.
chapters.zh: 那十二个官吏各按各月供给所罗门王，并一切与他同席之人的食物，一无所缺。

chapters.en: Each one also brought to the required place their quotas of barley and straw for the chariot horses and other horses.
chapters.zh: 众人各按各分，将养马与快马的大麦和干草送到〔官吏〕那里。

chapters.en: And God gave Solomon wisdom, exceedingly deep insight, and understanding beyond measure, like the sand on the seashore.
chapters.zh: 上帝赐给所罗门极大的智慧聪明和广大的心，如同海沙〔不可测量〕。

chapters.en: Solomon’s wisdom was greater than that of all the men of the East, greater than all the wisdom of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 所罗门的智慧超过东方人和埃及人的一切智慧。

chapters.en: He was wiser than all men—wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and wiser than Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. And his fame spread throughout the surrounding nations.
chapters.zh: 他的智慧胜过万人，胜过以斯拉人以探，并玛曷的儿子希幔、甲各、达大的智慧。他的名声传扬在四围的列国。

chapters.en: Solomon composed three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered a thousand and five.
chapters.zh: 他作箴言三千句，诗歌一千零五首。

chapters.en: He spoke of trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing in the wall, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.
chapters.zh: 他讲论草木，自黎巴嫩的香柏树直到墙上长的牛膝草，又讲论飞禽走兽、昆虫水族。

chapters.en: So men of all nations came to listen to Solomon’s wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.
chapters.zh: 天下列王听见所罗门的智慧，就都差人来听他的智慧话。

chapters.en: Now when Hiram king of Tyre heard that Solomon had been anointed king in his father’s place, he sent envoys to Solomon; for Hiram had always been a friend of David.
chapters.zh: 泰尔王希兰，平素爱大卫；他听见以色列人膏所罗门，接续他父亲作王，就差遣臣仆来见他。

chapters.en: And Solomon relayed this message to Hiram:
chapters.zh: 所罗门也差遣人去见希兰，说：

chapters.en: “As you are well aware, due to the wars waged on all sides against my father David, he could not build a house for the Name of the LORD his God until the LORD had put his enemies under his feet.
chapters.zh: 「你知道我父亲大卫因四围的争战，不能为耶和华－他上帝的名建殿，直等到耶和华使仇敌都服在他脚下。

chapters.en: But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side, and there is no adversary or crisis.
chapters.zh: 现在耶和华－我的上帝使我四围平安，没有仇敌，没有灾祸。

chapters.en: So behold, I plan to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God, according to what the LORD said to my father David: ‘I will put your son on your throne in your place, and he will build the house for My Name.’
chapters.zh: 我定意要为耶和华－我上帝的名建殿，是照耶和华应许我父亲大卫的话说：『我必使你儿子接续你坐你的位，他必为我的名建殿。』

chapters.en: Now therefore, order that cedars of Lebanon be cut down for me. My servants will be with your servants, and I will pay your servants whatever wages you set, for you know that there are none among us as skilled in logging as the Sidonians.”
chapters.zh: 所以求你吩咐你的仆人在黎巴嫩为我砍伐香柏木，我的仆人也必帮助他们，我必照你所定的，给你仆人的工价；因为你知道，在我们中间没有人像西顿人善于砍伐树木。」

chapters.en: When Hiram received Solomon’s message, he rejoiced greatly and said, “Blessed be the LORD this day! He has given David a wise son over this great people!”
chapters.zh: 希兰听见所罗门的话，就甚喜悦，说：「今日应当称颂耶和华；因他赐给大卫一个有智慧的儿子，治理这众多的民。」

chapters.en:
Then Hiram sent a reply to Solomon, saying:
“I have received your message; I will do all you desire regarding the cedar and cypress timber.
chapters.zh: 希兰打发人去见所罗门，说：「你差遣人向我所提的那事，我都听见了；论到香柏木和松木，我必照你的心愿而行。

chapters.en: My servants will haul the logs from Lebanon to the Sea, and I will float them as rafts by sea to the place you specify. There I will separate the logs, and you can take them away. And in exchange, you can meet my needs by providing my household with food.”
chapters.zh: 我的仆人必将这木料从黎巴嫩运到海里，扎成筏子，浮海运到你所指定我的地方，在那里拆开，你就可以收取；你也要成全我的心愿，将食物给我的家。」

chapters.en: So Hiram provided Solomon with all the cedar and cypress timber he wanted,
chapters.zh: 于是希兰照着所罗门所要的，给他香柏木和松木；

chapters.en: and year after year Solomon would provide Hiram with 20,000 cors of wheat as food for his household, as well as 20,000 baths of pure olive oil.
chapters.zh: 所罗门给希兰麦子二万歌珥，清油二十歌珥，作他家的食物。所罗门每年都是这样给希兰。

chapters.en: And the LORD gave Solomon wisdom, as He had promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a treaty.
chapters.zh: 耶和华照着所应许的赐智慧给所罗门。希兰与所罗门和好，彼此立约。

chapters.en: Then King Solomon conscripted a labor force of 30,000 men from all Israel.
chapters.zh: 所罗门王从以色列人中挑取服苦的人共有三万，

chapters.en: He sent them to Lebanon in monthly shifts of 10,000 men, so that they would spend one month in Lebanon and two months at home. And Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor.
chapters.zh: 派他们轮流每月一万人上黎巴嫩去；一个月在黎巴嫩，两个月在家里。亚多尼兰掌管他们。

chapters.en: Solomon had 70,000 porters and 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains,
chapters.zh: 所罗门用七万扛抬的，八万在山上凿石头的。

chapters.en: not including his 3,300 foremen who supervised the workers.
chapters.zh: 此外，所罗门用三千三百督工的，监管工人。

chapters.en: And the king commanded them to quarry large, costly stones to lay the foundation of the temple with dressed stones.
chapters.zh: 王下令，人就凿出又大又宝贵的石头来，用以立殿的根基。

chapters.en: So Solomon’s and Hiram’s builders, along with the Gebalites, quarried the stone and prepared the timber and stone for the construction of the temple.
chapters.zh: 所罗门的匠人和希兰的匠人，并迦巴勒人，都将石头凿好，预备木料和石头建殿。

chapters.en: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, the second month, he began to build the house of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 以色列人出埃及地后四百八十年，所罗门作以色列王第四年西弗月，就是二月，开工建造耶和华的殿。

chapters.en: The house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
chapters.zh: 所罗门王为耶和华所建的殿，长六十肘，宽二十肘，高三十肘。

chapters.en: The portico at the front of the main hall of the temple was twenty cubits long, extending across the width of the temple and projecting out ten cubits in front of the temple.
chapters.zh: 殿前的廊子长二十肘，与殿的宽窄一样，阔十肘；

chapters.en: He also had narrow windows framed high in the temple.
chapters.zh: 又为殿做了严紧的窗櫺。

chapters.en: Against the walls of the temple and the inner sanctuary, Solomon built a chambered structure around the temple, in which he constructed the side rooms.
chapters.zh: 靠着殿墙，围着外殿内殿，造了三层旁屋；

chapters.en: The bottom floor was five cubits wide, the middle floor six cubits, and the third floor seven cubits. He also placed offset ledges around the outside of the temple, so that nothing would be inserted into its walls.
chapters.zh: 下层宽五肘，中层宽六肘，上层宽七肘。殿外旁屋〔的梁木〕搁在殿墙坎上，免得插入殿墙。

chapters.en: The temple was constructed using finished stones cut at the quarry, so that no hammer or chisel or any other iron tool was heard in the temple while it was being built.
chapters.zh: 建殿是用山中凿成的石头。建殿的时候，锤子、斧子，和别样铁器的响声都没有听见。

chapters.en: The entrance to the bottom floor was on the south side of the temple. A stairway led up to the middle level, and from there to the third floor.
chapters.zh: 在殿右边当中的旁屋有门，门内有旋螺的楼梯，可以上到第二层，从第二层可以上到第三层。

chapters.en: So Solomon built the temple and finished it, roofing it with beams and planks of cedar.
chapters.zh: 所罗门建殿，安置香柏木的栋梁，又用香柏木板遮盖。

chapters.en: He built chambers all along the temple, each five cubits high and attached to the temple with beams of cedar.
chapters.zh: 靠着殿所造的旁屋，每层高五肘，香柏木的栋梁搁在殿墙〔坎上〕。

chapters.en: Then the word of the LORD came to Solomon, saying:
chapters.zh: 耶和华的话临到所罗门说：

chapters.en: “As for this temple you are building, if you walk in My statutes, carry out My ordinances, and keep all My commandments by walking in them, I will fulfill through you the promise I made to your father David.
chapters.zh: 「论到你所建的这殿，你若遵行我的律例，谨守我的典章，遵从我的一切诫命，我必向你应验我所应许你父亲大卫的话。

chapters.en: And I will dwell among the Israelites and will not abandon My people Israel.”
chapters.zh: 我必住在以色列人中间，并不丢弃我民以色列。」

chapters.en: So Solomon built the temple and finished it.
chapters.zh: 所罗门建造殿宇。

chapters.en: He lined the interior walls with cedar paneling from the floor of the temple to the ceiling, and he covered the floor with cypress boards.
chapters.zh: 殿里面用香柏木板贴墙，从地到棚顶都用木板遮蔽，又用松木板铺地。

chapters.en: He partitioned off the twenty cubits at the rear of the temple with cedar boards from floor to ceiling to form within the temple an inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
chapters.zh: 内殿，就是至圣所，长二十肘，从地到〔棚顶〕用香柏木板遮蔽〔注：或译：隔断〕。

chapters.en: And the main hall in front of this room was forty cubits long.
chapters.zh: 内殿前的外殿，长四十肘。

chapters.en: The cedar paneling inside the temple was carved with gourds and open flowers. Everything was cedar; not a stone could be seen.
chapters.zh: 殿里一点石头都不显露，一概用香柏木遮蔽；上面刻着野瓜和初开的花。

chapters.en: Solomon also prepared the inner sanctuary within the temple to set the ark of the covenant of the LORD there.
chapters.zh: 殿里预备了内殿，好安放耶和华的约柜。

chapters.en: The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold, and he also overlaid the altar of cedar.
chapters.zh: 内殿长二十肘，宽二十肘，高二十肘，墙面都贴上精金；又用香柏木做坛，包上精金。

chapters.en: So Solomon overlaid the inside of the temple with pure gold, and he extended gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary, which was overlaid with gold.
chapters.zh: 所罗门用精金贴了殿内的墙，又用金鍊子挂在内殿前〔门扇〕，用金包裹。

chapters.en: So he overlaid with gold the whole interior of the temple, until everything was completely finished. He also overlaid with gold the entire altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 全殿都贴上金子，直到贴完；内殿前的坛，也都用金包裹。

chapters.en: In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim, each ten cubits high, out of olive wood.
chapters.zh: 他用橄榄木做两个基路伯，各高十肘，安在内殿。

chapters.en: One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long, and the other wing was five cubits long as well. So the full wingspan was ten cubits.
chapters.zh: 这一个基路伯有两个翅膀，各长五肘，从这翅膀尖到那翅膀尖共有十肘；

chapters.en: The second cherub also measured ten cubits; both cherubim had the same size and shape,
chapters.zh: 那一个基路伯〔的两个翅膀〕也是十肘，两个基路伯的尺寸、形像都是一样。

chapters.en: and the height of each cherub was ten cubits.
chapters.zh: 这基路伯高十肘，那基路伯也是如此。

chapters.en: And he placed the cherubim inside the innermost room of the temple. Since their wings were spread out, the wing of the first cherub touched one wall, while the wing of the second cherub touched the other wall, and in the middle of the room their wingtips touched.
chapters.zh: 他将两个基路伯安在内殿里；基路伯的翅膀是张开的，这基路伯的一个翅膀挨着这边的墙，那基路伯的一个翅膀挨着那边的墙，里边的两个翅膀在殿中间彼此相接；

chapters.en: He also overlaid the cherubim with gold.
chapters.zh: 又用金子包裹二基路伯。

chapters.en: Then he carved the walls all around the temple, in both the inner and outer sanctuaries, with carved engravings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.
chapters.zh: 内殿、外殿周围的墙上都刻着基路伯、棕树，和初开的花。

chapters.en: And he overlaid the temple floor with gold in both the inner and outer sanctuaries.
chapters.zh: 内殿、外殿的地板都贴上金子。

chapters.en: For the entrance to the inner sanctuary, Solomon constructed doors of olive wood with five-sided doorposts.
chapters.zh: 又用橄榄木制造内殿的门扇、门楣、门框；门口〔有墙的〕五分之一。

chapters.en: The double doors were made of olive wood, and he carved into them cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers and overlaid the cherubim and palm trees with hammered gold.
chapters.zh: 在橄榄木做的两门扇上刻着基路伯、棕树，和初开的花，都贴上金子。

chapters.en: In the same way he made four-sided doorposts of olive wood for the sanctuary entrance.
chapters.zh: 又用橄榄木制造外殿的门框，门口有〔墙的〕四分之一。

chapters.en: The two doors were made of cypress wood, and each had two folding panels.
chapters.zh: 用松木做门两扇。这扇分两扇，是折叠的；那扇分两扇，也是折叠的。

chapters.en: He carved into them cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and he overlaid them with gold hammered evenly over the carvings.
chapters.zh: 上面刻着基路伯、棕树，和初开的花，都用金子贴了。

chapters.en: Solomon built the inner courtyard with three rows of dressed stone and one row of trimmed cedar beams.
chapters.zh: 他又用凿成的石头三层、香柏木一层建筑内院。

chapters.en: The foundation of the house of the LORD was laid in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign, in the month of Ziv.
chapters.zh: 〔所罗门在位〕第四年西弗月，立了耶和华殿的根基。

chapters.en: In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, the eighth month, the temple was finished in every detail and according to every specification. So he built the temple in seven years.
chapters.zh: 到十一年布勒月，就是八月，殿和一切属殿的都按着样式造成。他建殿的工夫共有七年。

chapters.en: Solomon, however, took thirteen years to complete the construction of his entire palace.
chapters.zh: 所罗门为自己建造宫室，十三年方才造成；

chapters.en: He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high, with four rows of cedar pillars supporting the cedar beams.
chapters.zh: 又建造黎巴嫩林宫，长一百肘，宽五十肘，高三十肘，有香柏木柱三〔注：原文是四〕行，柱上有香柏木柁梁。

chapters.en: The house was roofed with cedar above the beams that rested on the pillars—forty-five beams, fifteen per row.
chapters.zh: 其上以香柏木为盖，每行柱子十五根，共有四十五根。

chapters.en: There were three rows of high windows facing one another in three tiers.
chapters.zh: 有窗户三层，窗与窗相对。

chapters.en: All the doorways had rectangular frames, with the openings facing one another in three tiers.
chapters.zh: 所有的门框都是厚木见方的，有窗户三层，窗与窗相对。

chapters.en: Solomon made his colonnade fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide, with a portico in front of it and a canopy with pillars in front of the portico.
chapters.zh: 并建造有柱子的廊子，长五十肘，宽三十肘；在这廊前又有廊子，廊外有柱子和台阶。

chapters.en: In addition, he built a hall for the throne, the Hall of Justice, where he was to judge. It was paneled with cedar from floor to ceiling.
chapters.zh: 又建造一廊，其中设立审判的座位，这廊从地到顶都用香柏木遮蔽。

chapters.en: And the palace where Solomon would live, set further back, was of similar construction. He also made a palace like this hall for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom he had married.
chapters.zh: 廊后院内有所罗门住的宫室；工作与这工作相同。所罗门又为所娶法老的女儿建造一宫，做法与这廊子一样。

chapters.en: All these buildings were constructed with costly stones, cut to size and trimmed with saws inside and out from the foundation to the eaves, and from the outside to the great courtyard.
chapters.zh: 建造这一切所用的石头都是宝贵的，是按着尺寸凿成的，是用锯里外锯齐的；从根基直到檐石，从外头直到大院，都是如此。

chapters.en: The foundations were laid with large, costly stones, some ten cubits long and some eight cubits long.
chapters.zh: 根基是宝贵的大石头，有长十肘的，有长八肘的；

chapters.en: Above these were costly stones, cut to size, and cedar beams.
chapters.zh: 上面有香柏木和按着尺寸凿成宝贵的石头。

chapters.en: The great courtyard was surrounded by three rows of dressed stone and a row of trimmed cedar beams, as were the inner courtyard and portico of the house of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 大院周围有凿成的石头三层、香柏木一层，都照耶和华殿的内院和殿廊的样式。

chapters.en: Now King Solomon sent to bring Huram from Tyre.
chapters.zh: 所罗门王差遣人往泰尔去，将户兰召了来。

chapters.en: He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a craftsman in bronze. Huram had great skill, understanding, and knowledge for every kind of bronze work. So he came to King Solomon and carried out all his work.
chapters.zh: 他是拿弗他利支派中一个寡妇的儿子，他父亲是泰尔人，作铜匠的。户兰满有智慧、聪明、技能，善于各样铜作。他来到所罗门王那里，做王一切所要做的。

chapters.en: He cast two pillars of bronze, each eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference.
chapters.zh: 他制造两根铜柱，每根高十八肘，围十二肘；

chapters.en: He also made two capitals of cast bronze to set on top of the pillars, each capital five cubits high.
chapters.zh: 又用铜铸了两个柱顶安在柱上，各高五肘。

chapters.en: For the capitals on top of the pillars he made a network of lattice, with wreaths of chainwork, seven for each capital.
chapters.zh: 柱顶上有装修的网子和拧成的鍊索，每顶七个。

chapters.en: Likewise, he made the pillars with two rows of pomegranates around each grating to cover each capital atop the pillars.
chapters.zh: 网子周围有两行〔石榴〕遮盖柱顶，两个柱顶都是如此。

chapters.en: And the capitals atop the pillars in the portico were shaped like lilies, four cubits high.
chapters.zh: 廊子的柱顶径四肘，刻着百合花。

chapters.en: On the capitals of both pillars, just above the rounded projection next to the network, were the two hundred pomegranates in rows encircling each capital.
chapters.zh: 两柱顶的鼓肚上挨着网子，各有两行石榴环绕，两行共有二百。

chapters.en: Thus he set up the pillars at the portico of the temple. The pillar to the south he named Jachin, and the pillar to the north he named Boaz.
chapters.zh: 他将两根柱子立在殿廊前头：右边立一根，起名叫雅斤；左边立一根，起名叫波阿斯。

chapters.en: And the tops of the pillars were shaped like lilies. So the work of the pillars was completed.
chapters.zh: 在柱顶上刻着百合花。这样，造柱子的工就完毕了。

chapters.en: He also made the Sea of cast metal. It was circular in shape, measuring ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits in height, and thirty cubits in circumference.
chapters.zh: 他又铸一个铜海，样式是圆的，高五肘，径十肘，围三十肘。

chapters.en: Below the rim, ornamental buds encircled it, ten per cubit all the way around the Sea, cast in two rows as a part of the Sea.
chapters.zh: 在海边之下，周围有野瓜的样式；每肘十瓜，共有两行，是铸海的时候铸上的。

chapters.en: The Sea stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea rested on them, with all their hindquarters toward the center.
chapters.zh: 有十二只〔铜〕牛驮海：三只向北，三只向西，三只向南，三只向东；海在牛上，牛尾都向内。

chapters.en: It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It could hold two thousand baths.
chapters.zh: 海厚一掌，边如杯边，又如百合花，可容二千罢特。

chapters.en: In addition, he made ten movable stands of bronze, each four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits high.
chapters.zh: 他用铜制造十个〔盆〕座，每座长四肘，宽四肘，高三肘。

chapters.en: This was the design of the stands: They had side panels attached to uprights,
chapters.zh: 座的造法是这样：四面都有心子，心子在边子当中，

chapters.en: and on the panels between the uprights were lions, oxen, and cherubim. On the uprights was a pedestal above, and below the lions and oxen were wreaths of beveled work.
chapters.zh: 心子上有狮子和牛，并基路伯；边上有〔小〕座，狮子和牛以下有垂下的璎珞。

chapters.en: Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles and a basin resting on four supports, with wreaths at each side.
chapters.zh: 每〔盆〕座有四个铜轮和铜轴。〔小〕座的四角上在盆以下，有铸成的盆架，其旁都有璎珞。

chapters.en: The opening to each stand inside the crown at the top was one cubit deep, with a round opening like the design of a pedestal, a cubit and a half wide. And around its opening were engravings, but the panels of the stands were square, not round.
chapters.zh: 小座高一肘，口是圆的，仿佛座的样式，〔径〕一肘半，在口上有雕工，心子是方的，不是圆的。

chapters.en: There were four wheels under the panels, and the axles of the wheels were attached to the stand; each wheel was a cubit and a half in diameter.
chapters.zh: 四个轮子在心子以下，轮轴与座相连，每轮高一肘半。

chapters.en: The wheels were made like chariot wheels; their axles, rims, spokes, and hubs were all of cast metal.
chapters.zh: 轮的样式如同车轮；轴、辋、辐、毂都是铸的。

chapters.en: Each stand had four handles, one for each corner, projecting from the stand.
chapters.zh: 每座四角上都有盆架，是与座一同铸成的。

chapters.en: At the top of each stand was a circular band half a cubit high. The supports and panels were cast as a unit with the top of the stand.
chapters.zh: 座上有圆架，高半肘；座上有撑子和心子，是与座一同铸的。

chapters.en: He engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees on the surfaces of the supports and panels, wherever each had space, with wreaths all around.
chapters.zh: 在撑子和心子上刻着基路伯、狮子，和棕树，周围有璎珞。

chapters.en: In this way he made the ten stands, each with the same casting, dimensions, and shape.
chapters.zh: 十个盆座都是这样，铸法、尺寸、样式相同。

chapters.en: He also made ten bronze basins, each holding forty baths and measuring four cubits across, one basin for each of the ten stands.
chapters.zh: 又用铜制造十个盆，每盆可容四十罢特。盆径四肘，在那十座上，每座安设一盆。

chapters.en: He set five stands on the south side of the temple and five on the north, and he put the Sea on the south side, at the southeast corner of the temple.
chapters.zh: 五个安在殿门的右边，五个放在殿〔门〕的左边；又将海放在殿〔门〕的右旁，就是南边。

chapters.en:
Additionally, Huram made the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls.
So Huram finished all the work that he had undertaken for King Solomon in the house of the LORD:
chapters.zh: 户兰又造了盆、铲子，和盘子。这样，他为所罗门王做完了耶和华殿的一切工。
所〔造的〕就是：两根柱子和柱上两个如球的顶；并两个盖柱顶的网子；

chapters.en: the four hundred pomegranates for the two sets of network (two rows of pomegranates for each network covering both the bowl-shaped capitals atop the pillars);
chapters.zh: 和四百石榴，安在两个网子上，每网两行，盖着两个柱上如球的顶；

chapters.en:
the ten stands;
the ten basins on the stands;
chapters.zh: 十个座和其上的十个盆；

chapters.en:
the Sea;
the twelve oxen underneath the Sea;
chapters.zh: 海和海下的十二只牛；

chapters.en:
and the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls.
All the articles that Huram made for King Solomon in the house of the LORD were made of burnished bronze.
chapters.zh: 盆、铲子、盘子。这一切都是户兰给所罗门王用光亮的铜为耶和华的殿造成的，

chapters.en: The king had them cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan between Succoth and Zarethan.
chapters.zh: 是〔遵〕王〔命〕在约旦平原、疏割和撒拉但中间藉胶泥铸成的。

chapters.en: Solomon left all these articles unweighed, because there were so many. The weight of the bronze could not be determined.
chapters.zh: 这一切所罗门都没有〔过秤〕；因为甚多，铜的轻重也无法可查。
所罗门又造耶和华殿里的金坛和陈设饼的金桌子；

chapters.en:
the lampstands of pure gold in front of the inner sanctuary, five on the right side and five on the left;
the gold flowers, lamps, and tongs;
chapters.zh: 内殿前的精金灯台：右边五个，左边五个，并其上的金花、灯盏、蜡剪，

chapters.en:
the pure gold basins, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, ladles, and censers;
and the gold hinges for the doors of the inner temple (that is, the Most Holy Place ) as well as for the doors of the main hall of the temple.
chapters.zh: 与精金的杯、盘、镊子、调羹、火鼎，以及至圣所、内殿的门枢，和外殿的门枢。

chapters.en:
So all the work that King Solomon had performed for the house of the LORD was completed.
Then Solomon brought in the items his father David had dedicated—the silver, the gold, and the furnishings—and he placed them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 所罗门王做完了耶和华殿的一切工，就把他父大卫分别为圣的金银和器皿都带来放在耶和华殿的府库里。

chapters.en: At that time Solomon assembled before him in Jerusalem the elders of Israel—all the tribal heads and family leaders of the Israelites—to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Zion, the City of David.
chapters.zh: 那时，所罗门将以色列的长老和各支派的首领，并以色列的族长，招聚到耶路撒冷，要把耶和华的约柜从大卫城－就是锡安－运上来。

chapters.en: And all the men of Israel came together to King Solomon at the feast in the seventh month, the month of Ethanim.
chapters.zh: 以他念月，就是七月，在节前，以色列人都聚集到所罗门王那里。

chapters.en: When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the priests took up the ark,
chapters.zh: 以色列长老来到，祭司便抬起〔约〕柜，

chapters.en: and they brought up the ark of the LORD and the Tent of Meeting with all its sacred furnishings. So the priests and Levites carried them up.
chapters.zh: 祭司和利未人将耶和华的〔约〕柜运上来，又将会幕和会幕的一切圣器具都带上来。

chapters.en: There, before the ark, King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel who had assembled with him sacrificed so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.
chapters.zh: 所罗门王和聚集到他那里的以色列全会众，一同在〔约〕柜前献牛羊为祭，多得不可胜数。

chapters.en: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place in the inner sanctuary of the temple, the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
chapters.zh: 祭司将耶和华的约柜抬进内殿，就是至圣所，放在两个基路伯的翅膀底下。

chapters.en: For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark and overshadowed the ark and its poles.
chapters.zh: 基路伯张着翅膀在〔约〕柜之上，遮掩〔约〕柜和抬柜的杠。

chapters.en: The poles extended far enough that their ends were visible from the Holy Place in front of the inner sanctuary, but not from outside the Holy Place; and they are there to this day.
chapters.zh: 这杠甚长，杠头在内殿前的圣所可以看见，在殿外却不能看见，直到如今还在那里。

chapters.en: There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed in it at Horeb, where the LORD had made a covenant with the Israelites after they had come out of the land of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 约柜里惟有两块石版，就是以色列人出埃及地后，耶和华与他们立约的时候摩西在何烈山所放的。除此以外，并无别物。

chapters.en: And when the priests came out of the Holy Place, the cloud filled the house of the LORD
chapters.zh: 祭司从圣所出来的时候，有云充满耶和华的殿；

chapters.en: so that the priests could not stand there to minister because of the cloud. For the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 甚至祭司不能站立供职，因为耶和华的荣光充满了殿。

chapters.en:
Then Solomon declared:
“The LORD has said that He would dwell in the thick cloud.
chapters.zh: 那时所罗门说： 耶和华曾说， 他必住在幽暗之处。

chapters.en: I have indeed built You an exalted house, a place for You to dwell forever.”
chapters.zh: 我已经建造殿宇作你的居所， 为你永远的住处。

chapters.en: And as the whole assembly of Israel stood there, the king turned around and blessed them all
chapters.zh: 王转脸为以色列会众祝福，以色列会众就都站立。

chapters.en:
and said:
“Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has fulfilled with His own hand what He spoke with His mouth to my father David, saying,
chapters.zh: 所罗门说：「耶和华－以色列的上帝是应当称颂的！因他亲口向我父大卫所应许的，也亲手成就了。

chapters.en: ‘Since the day I brought My people Israel out of Egypt, I have not chosen a city from any tribe of Israel in which to build a house so that My Name would be there. But I have chosen David to be over My people Israel.’
chapters.zh: 他说：『自从我领我民以色列出埃及以来，我未曾在以色列各支派中选择一城建造殿宇－为我名的〔居所〕，但拣选大卫治理我民以色列。』」

chapters.en: Now it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
chapters.zh: 所罗门说：「我父大卫曾立意，要为耶和华－以色列上帝的名建殿。

chapters.en: But the LORD said to my father David, ‘Since it was in your heart to build a house for My Name, you have done well to have this in your heart.
chapters.zh: 耶和华却对我父大卫说：『你立意为我的名建殿，这意思甚好。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, you are not the one to build it; but your son, your own offspring, will build the house for My Name.’
chapters.zh: 只是你不可建殿，惟你所生的儿子必为我名建殿。』

chapters.en: Now the LORD has fulfilled the word that He spoke. I have succeeded my father David, and I sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised. I have built the house for the Name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
chapters.zh: 现在耶和华成就了他所应许的话，使我接续我父大卫坐以色列的国位，又为耶和华－以色列上帝的名建造了殿。

chapters.en: And there I have provided a place for the ark, which contains the covenant of the LORD that He made with our fathers when He brought them out of the land of Egypt.”
chapters.zh: 我也在其中为〔约〕柜预备一处。〔约〕柜内有耶和华的约，就是他领我们列祖出埃及地的时候，与他们所立的约。」

chapters.en: Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel, spread out his hands toward heaven,
chapters.zh: 所罗门当着以色列会众，站在耶和华的坛前，向天举手说：

chapters.en:
and said:
“O LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven above or on earth below, keeping Your covenant of loving devotion with Your servants who walk before You with all their hearts.
chapters.zh: 「耶和华－以色列的上帝啊，天上地下没有神可比你的！你向那尽心行在你面前的仆人守约施慈爱；

chapters.en: You have kept Your promise to Your servant, my father David. What You spoke with Your mouth You have fulfilled with Your hand this day.
chapters.zh: 向你仆人－我父大卫所应许的话现在应验了。你亲口应许，亲手成就，正如今日一样。

chapters.en: Therefore now, O LORD, God of Israel, keep for Your servant, my father David, what You promised when You said: ‘You will never fail to have a man to sit before Me on the throne of Israel, if only your descendants guard their way to walk before Me as you have done.’
chapters.zh: 耶和华－以色列的上帝啊，你所应许你仆人－我父大卫的话说：『你的子孙若谨慎自己的行为，在我面前行事像你所行的一样，就不断人坐以色列的国位。』现在求你应验这话。

chapters.en: And now, O God of Israel, please confirm what You promised to Your servant, my father David.
chapters.zh: 以色列的上帝啊，求你成就向你仆人－我父大卫所应许的话。

chapters.en: But will God indeed dwell upon the earth? The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built.
chapters.zh: 「上帝果真住在地上吗？看哪，天和天上的天尚且不足你居住的，何况我所建的这殿呢？

chapters.en: Yet regard the prayer and plea of Your servant, O LORD my God, so that You may hear the cry and the prayer that Your servant is praying before You today.
chapters.zh: 惟求耶和华－我的上帝垂顾仆人的祷告祈求，俯听仆人今日在你面前的祈祷呼吁。

chapters.en: May Your eyes be open toward this temple night and day, toward the place of which You said, ‘My Name shall be there,’ so that You may hear the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.
chapters.zh: 愿你昼夜看顾这殿，就是你应许立为你名的居所；求你垂听仆人向此处祷告的话。

chapters.en: Hear the plea of Your servant and of Your people Israel when they pray toward this place. May You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place. May You hear and forgive.
chapters.zh: 你仆人和你民以色列向此处祈祷的时候，求你在天上你的居所垂听，垂听而赦免。

chapters.en: When a man sins against his neighbor and is required to take an oath, and he comes to take an oath before Your altar in this temple,
chapters.zh: 「人若得罪邻舍，有人叫他起誓，他来到这殿在你的坛前起誓，

chapters.en: then may You hear from heaven and act. May You judge Your servants, condemning the wicked man by bringing down on his own head what he has done, and justifying the righteous man by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
chapters.zh: 求你在天上垂听，判断你的仆人：定恶人有罪，照他所行的报应在他头上；定义人有理，照他的义赏赐他。

chapters.en: When Your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and they return to You and confess Your name, praying and pleading with You in this temple,
chapters.zh: 「你的民以色列若得罪你，败在仇敌面前，又归向你，承认你的名，在这殿里祈求祷告，

chapters.en: then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your people Israel. May You restore them to the land You gave to their fathers.
chapters.zh: 求你在天上垂听，赦免你民以色列的罪，使他们归回你赐给他们列祖之地。

chapters.en: When the skies are shut and there is no rain because Your people have sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and confess Your name, and they turn from their sins because You have afflicted them,
chapters.zh: 「你的民因得罪你，你惩罚他们，使天闭塞不下雨；他们若向此处祷告，承认你的名，离开他们的罪，

chapters.en: then may You hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your servants, Your people Israel, so that You may teach them the good way in which they should walk. May You send rain on the land that You gave Your people as an inheritance.
chapters.zh: 求你在天上垂听，赦免你仆人以色列民的罪，将当行的善道指教他们，且降雨在你的地，就是你赐给你民为业之地。

chapters.en: When famine or plague comes upon the land, or blight or mildew or locusts or grasshoppers, or when their enemy besieges them in their cities, whatever plague or sickness may come,
chapters.zh: 「国中若有饥荒、瘟疫、旱风、霉烂、蝗虫、蚂蚱，或有仇敌犯境围困城邑，无论遭遇什么灾祸疾病，

chapters.en: then may whatever prayer or petition Your people Israel make—each knowing his own afflictions and spreading out his hands toward this temple—
chapters.zh: 你的民以色列，或是众人，或是一人，自觉有罪〔注：原文是灾〕，向这殿举手，无论祈求什么，祷告什么，

chapters.en: be heard by You from heaven, Your dwelling place. And may You forgive and act, and repay each man according to all his ways, since You know his heart—for You alone know the hearts of all men—
chapters.zh: 求你在天上你的居所垂听赦免。你是知道人心的，要照各人所行的待他们（惟有你知道世人的心），

chapters.en: so that they may fear You all the days they live in the land that You gave to our fathers.
chapters.zh: 使他们在你赐给我们列祖之地上一生一世敬畏你。

chapters.en: And as for the foreigner who is not of Your people Israel but has come from a distant land because of Your name—
chapters.zh: 「论到不属你民以色列的外邦人，为你名从远方而来，

chapters.en: for they will hear of Your great name and mighty hand and outstretched arm—when he comes and prays toward this temple,
chapters.zh: （他们听人论说你的大名和大能的手，并伸出来的膀臂）向这殿祷告，

chapters.en: then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to You. Then all the peoples of the earth will know Your name and fear You, as do Your people Israel, and they will know that this house I have built is called by Your Name.
chapters.zh: 求你在天上你的居所垂听，照着外邦人所祈求的而行，使天下万民都认识你的名，敬畏你像你的民以色列一样；又使他们知道我建造的这殿是称为你名下的。

chapters.en: When Your people go to war against their enemies, wherever You send them, and when they pray to the LORD in the direction of the city You have chosen and the house I have built for Your Name,
chapters.zh: 「你的民若奉你的差遣，无论往何处去与仇敌争战，向耶和华所选择的城与我为你名所建造的殿祷告，

chapters.en: then may You hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and may You uphold their cause.
chapters.zh: 求你在天上垂听他们的祷告祈求，使他们得胜。

chapters.en: When they sin against You—for there is no one who does not sin—and You become angry with them and deliver them to an enemy who takes them as captives to his own land, whether far or near,
chapters.zh: 「你的民若得罪你（世上没有不犯罪的人），你向他们发怒，将他们交给仇敌掳到仇敌之地，或远或近，

chapters.en: and when they come to their senses in the land to which they were taken, and they repent and plead with You in the land of their captors, saying, ‘We have sinned and done wrong; we have acted wickedly,’
chapters.zh: 他们若在掳到之地想起罪来，回心转意，恳求你说：『我们有罪了，我们悖逆了，我们作恶了』；

chapters.en: and when they return to You with all their heart and soul in the land of the enemies who took them captive, and when they pray to You in the direction of the land that You gave to their fathers, the city You have chosen, and the house I have built for Your Name,
chapters.zh: 他们若在掳到之地尽心尽性归服你，又向自己的地，就是你赐给他们列祖之地和你所选择的城，并我为你名所建造的殿祷告，

chapters.en: then may You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, their prayer and petition, and may You uphold their cause.
chapters.zh: 求你在天上你的居所垂听他们的祷告祈求，为他们伸冤；

chapters.en: May You forgive Your people who have sinned against You and all the transgressions they have committed against You, and may You grant them compassion in the eyes of their captors to show them mercy.
chapters.zh: 饶恕得罪你的民，赦免他们的一切过犯，使他们在掳他们的人面前蒙怜恤。

chapters.en: For they are Your people and Your inheritance; You brought them out of Egypt, out of the furnace for iron.
chapters.zh: 因为他们是你的子民，你的产业，是你从埃及领出来脱离铁炉的。

chapters.en: May Your eyes be open to the pleas of Your servant and of Your people Israel, and may You listen to them whenever they call to You.
chapters.zh: 愿你的眼目看顾仆人，听你民以色列的祈求，无论何时向你祈求，愿你垂听。

chapters.en: For You, O Lord GOD, have set them apart from all the peoples of the earth as Your inheritance, as You spoke through Your servant Moses when You brought our fathers out of Egypt.”
chapters.zh: 主耶和华啊，你将他们从地上的万民中分别出来作你的产业，是照你领我们列祖出埃及的时候，藉你仆人摩西所应许的话。」

chapters.en: Now when Solomon had finished praying this entire prayer and petition to the LORD, he got up before the altar of the LORD, where he had been kneeling with his hands spread out toward heaven.
chapters.zh: 所罗门在耶和华的坛前屈膝跪着，向天举手，在耶和华面前祷告祈求已毕，就起来，

chapters.en: And he stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice, saying:
chapters.zh: 站着，大声为以色列全会众祝福，说：

chapters.en: “Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to His people Israel according to all that He promised. Not one word has failed of all the good promises He made through His servant Moses.
chapters.zh: 「耶和华是应当称颂的！因为他照着一切所应许的赐平安给他的民以色列人，凡藉他仆人摩西应许赐福的话，一句都没有落空。

chapters.en: May the LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers. May He never leave us or forsake us.
chapters.zh: 愿耶和华－我们的上帝与我们同在，像与我们列祖同在一样，不撇下我们，不丢弃我们，

chapters.en: May He incline our hearts to Himself, to walk in all His ways and to keep the commandments and statutes and ordinances He commanded our fathers.
chapters.zh: 使我们的心归向他，遵行他的道，谨守他吩咐我们列祖的诫命、律例、典章。

chapters.en: And may these words with which I have made my petition before the LORD be near to the LORD our God day and night, so that He may uphold the cause of His servant and of His people Israel as each day requires,
chapters.zh: 我在耶和华面前祈求的这些话，愿耶和华－我们的上帝昼夜垂念，每日为他仆人与他民以色列伸冤，

chapters.en: so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God. There is no other!
chapters.zh: 使地上的万民都知道惟独耶和华是上帝，并无别神。

chapters.en: So let your heart be fully devoted to the LORD our God, as it is this day, to walk in His statutes and to keep His commandments.”
chapters.zh: 所以你们当向耶和华－我们的上帝存诚实的心，遵行他的律例，谨守他的诫命，〔至终〕如今日一样。」

chapters.en: Then the king and all Israel with him offered sacrifices before the LORD.
chapters.zh: 王和以色列众民一同在耶和华面前献祭。

chapters.en: And Solomon offered as peace offerings to the LORD 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep. So the king and all the Israelites dedicated the house of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 所罗门向耶和华献平安祭，用牛二万二千，羊十二万。这样，王和以色列众民为耶和华的殿行奉献之礼。

chapters.en: On that same day the king consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD, and there he offered the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings, since the bronze altar before the LORD was too small to contain all these offerings.
