chapters.en: You were patient with them for many years, and Your Spirit admonished them through Your prophets. Yet they would not listen, so You gave them into the hands of the neighboring peoples.
chapters.zh: 但你多年宽容他们，又用你的灵藉众先知劝戒他们，他们仍不听从，所以你将他们交在列国之民的手中。

chapters.en: But in Your great compassion, You did not put an end to them; nor did You forsake them, for You are a gracious and compassionate God.
chapters.zh: 然而你大发怜悯，不全然灭绝他们，也不丢弃他们；因为你是有恩典、有怜悯的上帝。

chapters.en: So now, our God, the great and mighty and awesome God who keeps His gracious covenant, do not view lightly all the hardship that has come upon us, and upon our kings and leaders, our priests and prophets, our ancestors and all Your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria until today.
chapters.zh: 「我们的上帝啊，你是至大、至能、至可畏、守约施慈爱的上帝。我们的君王、首领、祭司、先知、列祖，和你的众民，从亚述列王的时候直到今日所遭遇的苦难，现在求你不要以为小。

chapters.en:
You are just in all that has befallen us, because You have acted faithfully,
while we have acted wickedly.
chapters.zh: 在一切临到我们的事上，你却是公义的；因你所行的是诚实，我们所做的是邪恶。

chapters.en: Our kings and leaders and priests and fathers did not obey Your law or listen to Your commandments and warnings that You gave them.
chapters.zh: 我们的君王、首领、祭司、列祖都不遵守你的律法，不听从你的诫命和你警戒他们的话。

chapters.en:
For even while they were in their kingdom, with the abundant goodness
that You had given them, and in the spacious and fertile land that You had set before them, they would not serve You or turn from their wicked ways.
chapters.zh: 他们在本国里沾你大恩的时候，在你所赐给他们这广大肥美之地上不事奉你，也不转离他们的恶行。

chapters.en:
So here we are today as slaves in the land You gave our fathers to enjoy its fruit and goodness—
here we are as slaves!
chapters.zh: 我们现今作了奴仆；至于你所赐给我们列祖享受其上的土产，并美物之地，看哪，我们在这地上作了奴仆！

chapters.en: Its abundant harvest goes to the kings You have set over us because of our sins. And they rule over our bodies and our livestock as they please. We are in great distress.
chapters.zh: 这地许多出产归了列王，就是你因我们的罪所派辖制我们的。他们任意辖制我们的身体和牲畜，我们遭了大难。」

chapters.en: In view of all this, we make a binding agreement, putting it in writing and sealing it with the names of our leaders, Levites, and priests.”
chapters.zh: 因这一切的事，我们立确实的约，写在册上。我们的首领、利未人，和祭司都签了名。

chapters.en:
Now these were the ones who sealed the document:
Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah,
and also Zedekiah,
chapters.zh: 签名的是：哈迦利亚的儿子－省长尼希米，和西底家；

chapters.en: Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah,
chapters.zh: 祭司：西莱雅、亚撒利雅、耶利米、

chapters.en: Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah,
chapters.zh: 巴施户珥、亚玛利雅、玛基雅、

chapters.en: Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch,
chapters.zh: 哈突、示巴尼、玛鹿、

chapters.en: Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah,
chapters.zh: 哈琳、米利末、俄巴底亚、

chapters.en: Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch,
chapters.zh: 但以理、近顿、巴录、

chapters.en: Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin,
chapters.zh: 米书兰、亚比雅、米雅民、

chapters.en:
Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah.
These were the priests.
chapters.zh: 玛西亚、璧该、示玛雅；

chapters.en:
The Levites:
Jeshua son of Azaniah,
Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel,
chapters.zh: 又有利未人，就是亚散尼的儿子耶书亚、希拿达的子孙宾内、甲篾；

chapters.en: and their associates: Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
chapters.zh: 还有他们的弟兄示巴尼、荷第雅、基利他、毗莱雅、哈难、

chapters.en: Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah,
chapters.zh: 米迦、利合、哈沙比雅、

chapters.en: Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,
chapters.zh: 撒刻、示利比、示巴尼、

chapters.en: Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.
chapters.zh: 荷第雅、巴尼、比尼努；

chapters.en:
And the leaders of the people:
Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,
chapters.zh: 又有民的首领，就是巴录、巴赫‧摩押、以拦、萨土、巴尼、

chapters.en: Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,
chapters.zh: 布尼、押甲、比拜、

chapters.en: Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,
chapters.zh: 亚多尼雅、比革瓦伊、亚丁、

chapters.en: Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur,
chapters.zh: 亚特、希西家、押朔、

chapters.en: Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,
chapters.zh: 荷第雅、哈顺、比赛、

chapters.en: Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai,
chapters.zh: 哈拉、亚拿突、尼拜、

chapters.en: Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,
chapters.zh: 抹比押、米书兰、希悉、

chapters.en: Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,
chapters.zh: 米示萨别、撒督、押杜亚、

chapters.en: Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,
chapters.zh: 毗拉提、哈难、亚奈雅、

chapters.en: Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub,
chapters.zh: 何细亚、哈拿尼雅、哈述、

chapters.en: Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek,
chapters.zh: 哈罗黑、毗利哈、朔百、

chapters.en: Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,
chapters.zh: 利宏、哈沙拿、玛西雅、

chapters.en: Ahijah, Hanan, Anan,
chapters.zh: 亚希雅、哈难、亚难、

chapters.en: Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.
chapters.zh: 玛鹿、哈琳、巴拿。

chapters.en: “The rest of the people—the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and all who had separated themselves from the people of the land to obey the Law of God—along with their wives and all their sons and daughters who are able to understand,
chapters.zh: 其余的民、祭司、利未人、守门的、歌唱的、尼提宁，和一切离绝邻邦居民归服上帝律法的，并他们的妻子、儿女，凡有知识能明白的，

chapters.en: hereby join with their noble brothers and commit themselves with a sworn oath to follow the Law of God given through His servant Moses and to obey carefully all the commandments, ordinances, and statutes of the LORD our Lord.
chapters.zh: 都随从他们贵胄的弟兄，发咒起誓，必遵行上帝藉他仆人摩西所传的律法，谨守遵行耶和华－我们主的一切诫命、典章、律例；

chapters.en: We will not give our daughters in marriage to the people of the land, and we will not take their daughters for our sons.
chapters.zh: 并不将我们的女儿嫁给这地的居民，也不为我们的儿子娶他们的女儿。

chapters.en: When the people of the land bring merchandise or any kind of grain to sell on the Sabbath day, we will not buy from them on a Sabbath or holy day. Every seventh year we will let the fields lie fallow and will cancel every debt.
chapters.zh: 这地的居民若在安息日，或什么圣日，带了货物或粮食来卖给我们，我们必不买。每逢第七年必不耕种，凡欠我们债的必不追讨。

chapters.en: We also place ourselves under the obligation to contribute a third of a shekel yearly for the service of the house of our God:
chapters.zh: 我们又为自己定例，每年各人捐银一舍客勒三分之一，为我们上帝殿的使用，

chapters.en: for the showbread, for the regular grain offerings and burnt offerings, for the Sabbath offerings, for the New Moons and appointed feasts, for the holy offerings, for the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and for all the duties of the house of our God.
chapters.zh: 就是为陈设饼、常献的素祭，和燔祭，安息日、月朔、节期所献的与圣物，并以色列人的赎罪祭，以及我们上帝殿里一切的费用。

chapters.en: We have cast lots among the priests, Levites, and people for the donation of wood by our families at the appointed times each year. They are to bring it to the house of our God to burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as it is written in the Law.
chapters.zh: 我们的祭司、利未人，和百姓都掣签，看每年是哪一族按定期将〔献祭的〕柴奉到我们上帝的殿里，照着律法上所写的，烧在耶和华－我们上帝的坛上。

chapters.en: We will also bring the firstfruits of our land and of every fruit tree to the house of the LORD year by year.
chapters.zh: 又定每年将我们地上初熟的土产和各样树上初熟的果子都奉到耶和华的殿里。

chapters.en: And we will bring the firstborn of our sons and our livestock, as it is written in the Law, and will bring the firstborn of our herds and flocks to the house of our God, to the priests who minister in the house of our God.
chapters.zh: 又照律法上所写的，将我们头胎的儿子和首生的牛羊都奉到我们上帝的殿，交给我们上帝殿里供职的祭司；

chapters.en: Moreover, we will bring to the priests at the storerooms of the house of our God the firstfruits of our dough, of our grain offerings, of the fruit of all our trees, and of our new wine and oil. A tenth of our produce belongs to the Levites, so that they shall receive tithes in all the towns where we labor.
chapters.zh: 并将初熟之麦子所磨的面和举祭、各样树上〔初熟〕的果子、新酒与油奉给祭司，收在我们上帝殿的库房里，把我们地上所产的十分之一奉给利未人，因利未人在我们一切城邑的土产中当取十分之一。

chapters.en: A priest of Aaron’s line is to accompany the Levites when they collect the tenth, and the Levites are to bring a tenth of these tithes to the storerooms of the treasury in the house of our God.
chapters.zh: 利未人取十分之一的时候，亚伦的子孙中，当有一个祭司与利未人同在。利未人也当从十分之一中取十分之一，奉到我们上帝殿的屋子里，收在库房中。

chapters.en:
For the Israelites and the Levites are to bring the contributions of grain, new wine, and oil to the storerooms where the articles of the sanctuary are kept and where the ministering priests, the gatekeepers, and the singers stay.
Thus we will not neglect the house of our God.”
chapters.zh: 以色列人和利未人要将五谷、新酒，和油为举祭，奉到收存圣所器皿的屋子里，就是供职的祭司、守门的、歌唱的所住的屋子。这样，我们就不离弃我们上帝的殿。

chapters.en: Now the leaders of the people settled in Jerusalem, and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of ten to live in the holy city of Jerusalem, while the remaining nine were to dwell in their own towns.
chapters.zh: 百姓的首领住在耶路撒冷。其余的百姓掣签，每十人中使一人来住在圣城耶路撒冷，那九人住在〔别的〕城邑。

chapters.en: And the people blessed all the men who volunteered to live in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 凡甘心乐意住在耶路撒冷的，百姓都为他们祝福。

chapters.en: These are the heads of the provinces who settled in Jerusalem. (In the villages of Judah, however, each lived on his own property in their towns—the Israelites, priests, Levites, temple servants, and descendants of Solomon’s servants—
chapters.zh: 以色列人、祭司、利未人、尼提宁，和所罗门仆人的后裔都住在犹大城邑，各在自己的地业中。本省的首领住在耶路撒冷的记在下面：
其中有些犹大人和便雅悯人。犹大人中有法勒斯的子孙、乌西雅的儿子亚他雅。乌西雅是撒迦利雅的儿子；撒迦利雅是亚玛利雅的儿子；亚玛利雅是示法提雅的儿子；示法提雅是玛勒列的儿子。

chapters.en: and Maaseiah son of Baruch, the son of Col-hozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, a descendant of Shelah.
chapters.zh: 又有巴录的儿子玛西雅。巴录是谷何西的儿子；谷何西是哈赛雅的儿子；哈赛雅是亚大雅的儿子；亚大雅是约雅立的儿子；约雅立是撒迦利雅的儿子；撒迦利雅是示罗尼的儿子。

chapters.en: The descendants of Perez who settled in Jerusalem totaled 468 men of valor.
chapters.zh: 住在耶路撒冷、法勒斯的子孙共四百六十八名，都是勇士。

chapters.en:
From the descendants of Benjamin:
Sallu son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jeshaiah;
chapters.zh: 便雅悯人中有米书兰的儿子撒路。米书兰是约叶的儿子；约叶是毗大雅的儿子；毗大雅是哥赖雅的儿子；哥赖雅是玛西雅的儿子；玛西雅是以铁的儿子；以铁是耶筛亚的儿子。

chapters.en: and his followers Gabbai and Sallai—928 men.
chapters.zh: 其次有迦拜、撒来〔的子孙〕，共九百二十八名。

chapters.en: Joel son of Zichri was the officer over them, and Judah son of Hassenuah was over the Second District of the city.
chapters.zh: 细基利的儿子约珥是他们的长官。哈西努亚的儿子犹大是耶路撒冷的副官。

chapters.en:
From the priests:
Jedaiah son of Joiarib; Jachin;
chapters.zh: 祭司中有雅斤，又有约雅立的儿子耶大雅；

chapters.en: Seraiah son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the chief official of the house of God;
chapters.zh: 还有管理上帝殿的西莱雅。西莱雅是希勒家的儿子；希勒家是米书兰的儿子；米书兰是撒督的儿子；撒督是米拉约的儿子；米拉约是亚希突的儿子。

chapters.en:
and their associates who did the work at the temple—822 men;
Adaiah son of Jeroham, the son of Pelaliah, the son of Amzi, the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah;
chapters.zh: 还有他们的弟兄在殿里供职的，共八百二十二名；又有耶罗罕的儿子亚大雅。耶罗罕是毗拉利的儿子；毗拉利是暗洗的儿子；暗洗是撒迦利亚的儿子；撒迦利亚是巴施户珥的儿子；巴施户珥是玛基雅的儿子。

chapters.en:
and his associates, the leaders of families—242 men;
Amashai son of Azarel, the son of Ahzai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer;
chapters.zh: 还有他的弟兄作族长的，二百四十二名；又有亚萨列的儿子亚玛帅。亚萨列是亚哈赛的儿子；亚哈赛是米实利末的儿子；米实利末是音麦的儿子。

chapters.en: and his associates —128 mighty men of valor. Zabdiel son of Haggedolim was their overseer.
chapters.zh: 还有他们弟兄、大能的勇士共一百二十八名。哈基多琳的儿子撒巴第业是他们的长官。

chapters.en:
From the Levites:
Shemaiah son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Bunni;
chapters.zh: 利未人中有哈述的儿子示玛雅。哈述是押利甘的儿子；押利甘是哈沙比雅的儿子；哈沙比雅是布尼的儿子。

chapters.en: Shabbethai and Jozabad, two leaders of the Levites, who supervised the work outside the house of God;
chapters.zh: 又有利未人的族长沙比太和约撒拔管理上帝殿的外事。

chapters.en: Mattaniah son of Mica, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, who led in thanksgiving and prayer; Bakbukiah, second among his associates; and Abda son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun.
chapters.zh: 祈祷的时候，为称谢领首的是米迦的儿子玛他尼。米迦是撒底的儿子；撒底是亚萨的儿子；又有玛他尼弟兄中的八布迦为副。还有沙母亚的儿子押大。沙母亚是加拉的儿子；加拉是耶杜顿的儿子。

chapters.en: The Levites in the holy city totaled 284.
chapters.zh: 在圣城的利未人共二百八十四名。

chapters.en:
And the gatekeepers:
Akkub, Talmon, and their associates, who kept watch at the gates—172 men.
chapters.zh: 守门的是亚谷和达们，并守门的弟兄，共一百七十二名。

chapters.en: The rest of the Israelites, with the priests and Levites, were in all the villages of Judah, each on his own inheritance.
chapters.zh: 其余的以色列人、祭司、利未人都住在犹大的一切城邑，各在自己的地业中。

chapters.en: The temple servants lived on the hill of Ophel, with Ziha and Gishpa over them.
chapters.zh: 尼提宁却住在俄斐勒；西哈和基斯帕管理他们。

chapters.en: Now the overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Mica. He was one of Asaph’s descendants, who were the singers in charge of the service of the house of God.
chapters.zh: 在耶路撒冷、利未人的长官，管理上帝殿事务的是歌唱者亚萨的子孙、巴尼的儿子乌西。巴尼是哈沙比雅的儿子；哈沙比雅是玛他尼的儿子；玛他尼是米迦的儿子。

chapters.en: For there was a command from the king concerning the singers, an ordinance regulating their daily activities.
chapters.zh: 王为歌唱的出命令，每日供给他们必有一定之粮。

chapters.en: Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, a descendant of Zerah son of Judah, was the king’s agent in every matter concerning the people.
chapters.zh: 犹大儿子谢拉的子孙、米示萨别的儿子毗他希雅辅助王办理犹大民的事。

chapters.en: As for the villages with their fields, some of the people of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba, Dibon, Jekabzeel, and their villages;
chapters.zh: 至于村庄和属村庄的田地，有犹大人住在基列‧亚巴和属基列‧亚巴的乡村；底本和属底本的乡村；叶甲薛和属叶甲薛的村庄；

chapters.en: in Jeshua, Moladah, and Beth-pelet;
chapters.zh: 耶书亚、摩拉大、伯‧帕列、

chapters.en: in Hazar-shual; in Beersheba and its villages;
chapters.zh: 哈萨‧书亚、别是巴，和属别是巴的乡村；

chapters.en: in Ziklag; in Meconah and its villages;
chapters.zh: 洗革拉、米哥拿，和属米哥拿的乡村；

chapters.en: in En-rimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth,
chapters.zh: 音‧临门、琐拉、耶末、

chapters.en: Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages; in Lachish and its fields; and in Azekah and its villages. So they settled from Beersheba all the way to the Valley of Hinnom.
chapters.zh: 撒挪亚、亚杜兰，和属这两处的村庄；拉吉和属拉吉的田地；亚西加和属亚西加的乡村。他们所住的地方是从别是巴直到欣嫩谷。

chapters.en: The descendants of Benjamin from Geba lived in Michmash, Aija, and Bethel with its villages;
chapters.zh: 便雅悯人从迦巴起，住在密抹、亚雅、伯特利和属伯特利的乡村。

chapters.en: in Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
chapters.zh: 亚拿突、挪伯、亚难雅、

chapters.en: Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
chapters.zh: 夏琐、拉玛、基他音、

chapters.en: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
chapters.zh: 哈叠、洗编、尼八拉、

chapters.en: Lod, and Ono; and in the Valley of the Craftsmen.
chapters.zh: 罗德、阿挪、匠人之谷。

chapters.en: And some divisions of the Levites of Judah settled in Benjamin.
chapters.zh: 利未人中有几班曾住在犹大地归于便雅悯的。

chapters.en:
Now these are the priests and Levites who went up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and with Jeshua:
Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
chapters.zh: 同着撒拉铁的儿子所罗巴伯和耶书亚回来的祭司与利未人记在下面：祭司是西莱雅、耶利米、以斯拉、

chapters.en: Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
chapters.zh: 亚玛利雅、玛鹿、哈突、

chapters.en: Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
chapters.zh: 示迦尼、利宏、米利末、

chapters.en: Iddo, Ginnethon, Abijah,
chapters.zh: 易多、近顿、亚比雅、

chapters.en: Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
chapters.zh: 米雅民、玛底雅、璧迦、

chapters.en: Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
chapters.zh: 示玛雅、约雅立、耶大雅、

chapters.en:
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah.
These were the leaders of the priests and their associates in the days of Jeshua.
chapters.zh: 撒路、亚木、希勒家、耶大雅。这些人在耶书亚的时候作祭司和他们弟兄的首领。

chapters.en: The Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, who, with his associates, led the songs of thanksgiving.
chapters.zh: 利未人是耶书亚、宾内、甲篾、示利比、犹大、玛他尼。这玛他尼和他的弟兄管理称谢的事。

chapters.en: Bakbukiah and Unni, their associates, stood across from them in the services.
chapters.zh: 他们的弟兄八布迦和乌尼照自己的班次与他们相对。

chapters.en:
Jeshua was the father of Joiakim,
Joiakim was the father of Eliashib,
Eliashib was the father of Joiada,
chapters.zh: 耶书亚生约雅金；约雅金生以利亚实；以利亚实生耶何耶大；

chapters.en:
Joiada was the father of Jonathan,
and Jonathan was the father of Jaddua.
chapters.zh: 耶何耶大生约拿单；约拿单生押杜亚。
在约雅金的时候，祭司作族长的西莱雅族〔注：或译：班；本段同〕有米拉雅；耶利米族有哈拿尼雅；

chapters.en:
of Ezra, Meshullam;
of Amariah, Jehohanan;
chapters.zh: 以斯拉族有米书兰；亚玛利雅族有约哈难；

chapters.en:
of Malluchi, Jonathan;
of Shebaniah, Joseph;
chapters.zh: 米利古族有约拿单；示巴尼族有约瑟；

chapters.en:
of Harim, Adna;
of Meraioth, Helkai;
chapters.zh: 哈琳族有押拿；米拉约族有希勒恺；

chapters.en:
of Iddo, Zechariah;
of Ginnethon, Meshullam;
chapters.zh: 易多族有撒迦利亚；近顿族有米书兰；

chapters.en:
of Abijah, Zichri;
of Miniamin and of Moadiah, Piltai;
chapters.zh: 亚比雅族有细基利；米拿民族〔某〕；摩亚底族有毗勒太；

chapters.en:
of Bilgah, Shammua;
of Shemaiah, Jonathan;
chapters.zh: 璧迦族有沙母亚；示玛雅族有约拿单；

chapters.en:
of Joiarib, Mattenai;
of Jedaiah, Uzzi;
chapters.zh: 约雅立族有玛特乃；耶大雅族有乌西；

chapters.en:
of Sallai, Kallai;
of Amok, Eber;
chapters.zh: 撒来族有加莱；亚木族有希伯；

chapters.en:
of Hilkiah, Hashabiah;
and of Jedaiah, Nethanel.
chapters.zh: 希勒家族有哈沙比雅；耶大雅族有拿坦业。

chapters.en: In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, during the reign of Darius the Persian, the heads of the families of the Levites and priests were recorded.
chapters.zh: 至于利未人，当以利亚实、耶何耶大、约哈难、押杜亚的时候，他们的族长记在册上。波斯王大流士在位的时候，〔作族长的〕祭司也记在册上。

chapters.en: As for the descendants of Levi, the family heads up to the days of Johanan son of Eliashib were recorded in the Book of the Chronicles.
chapters.zh: 利未人作族长的记在历史上，直到以利亚实的儿子约哈难的时候。

chapters.en: The leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua son of Kadmiel, along with their associates, who stood across from them to give praise and thanksgiving as one section alternated with the other, as prescribed by David the man of God.
chapters.zh: 利未人的族长是哈沙比雅、示利比、甲篾的儿子耶书亚，与他们弟兄的班次相对，照着神人大卫的命令一班一班地赞美称谢。

chapters.en: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers who guarded the storerooms at the gates.
chapters.zh: 玛他尼、八布迦、俄巴底亚、米书兰、达们、亚谷是守门的，就是在库房那里守门。

chapters.en: They served in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe.
chapters.zh: 这都是在约撒达的孙子、耶书亚的儿子约雅金和省长尼希米，并祭司文士以斯拉的时候，〔有职任的〕。

chapters.en: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, the Levites were sought out from all their homes and brought to Jerusalem to celebrate the joyous dedication with thanksgiving and singing, accompanied by cymbals, harps, and lyres.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷城墙告成的时候，众民就把各处的利未人招到耶路撒冷，要称谢、歌唱、敲钹、鼓瑟、弹琴，欢欢喜喜地行告成之礼。

chapters.en: The singers were also assembled from the region around Jerusalem, from the villages of the Netophathites,
from Beth-gilgal, and from the fields of Geba and Azmaveth, for they had built villages for themselves around Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 歌唱的人从耶路撒冷的周围和尼陀法的村庄与伯‧吉甲，又从迦巴和押玛弗的田地聚集，因为歌唱的人在耶路撒冷四围为自己立了村庄。

chapters.en: After the priests and Levites had purified themselves, they purified the people, the gates, and the wall.
chapters.zh: 祭司和利未人就洁净自己，也洁净百姓和城门，并城墙。

chapters.en: Then I brought the leaders of Judah up on the wall, and I appointed two great thanksgiving choirs. One was to proceed along the top of the wall to the right, toward the Dung Gate.
chapters.zh: 我带犹大的首领上城，使称谢的人分为两大队，排列而行：第一队在城上往右边向粪厂门行走，

chapters.en: Hoshaiah and half the leaders of Judah followed,
chapters.zh: 在他们后头的有何沙雅与犹大首领的一半，

chapters.en: along with Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
chapters.zh: 又有亚撒利雅、以斯拉、米书兰、

chapters.en: Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, Jeremiah,
chapters.zh: 犹大、便雅悯、示玛雅、耶利米。

chapters.en: and some of the priests with trumpets, and also Zechariah son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Micaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph,
chapters.zh: 还有些吹号之祭司的子孙，约拿单的儿子撒迦利亚。约拿单是示玛雅的儿子；示玛雅是玛他尼的儿子；玛他尼是米该亚的儿子；米该亚是撒刻的儿子；撒刻是亚萨的儿子；

chapters.en: and his associates—Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani—with the musical instruments prescribed by David the man of God. Ezra the scribe led the procession.
chapters.zh: 又有撒迦利亚的弟兄示玛雅、亚撒利、米拉莱、基拉莱、玛艾、拿坦业、犹大、哈拿尼，都拿着神人大卫的乐器，文士以斯拉引领他们。

chapters.en: At the Fountain Gate they went directly up the steps of the City of David on the ascent to the wall and passed above the house of David to the Water Gate on the east.
chapters.zh: 他们经过泉门往前，从大卫城的台阶随地势而上，在大卫宫殿以上，直行到朝东的水门。

chapters.en: The second thanksgiving choir proceeded to the left, and I followed it with half the people along the top of the wall, past the Tower of the Ovens to the Broad Wall,
chapters.zh: 第二队称谢的人要与那一队相迎而行。我和民的一半跟随他们，在城墙上过了炉楼，直到宽墙；

chapters.en: over the Gate of Ephraim, the Jeshanah Gate, the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate. And they stopped at the Gate of the Guard.
chapters.zh: 又过了以法莲门、古门、鱼门、哈楠业楼、哈米亚楼，直到羊门，就在护卫门站住。

chapters.en: The two thanksgiving choirs then stood in the house of God, as did I, along with the half of the officials accompanying me,
chapters.zh: 于是，这两队称谢的人连我和官长的一半，站在上帝的殿里。

chapters.en: as well as the priests with their trumpets—Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah—
chapters.zh: 还有祭司以利亚金、玛西雅、米拿民、米该亚、以利约乃、撒迦利亚、哈楠尼亚吹号；

chapters.en: and also Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. Then the choirs sang out under the direction of Jezrahiah.
chapters.zh: 又有玛西雅、示玛雅、以利亚撒、乌西、约哈难、玛基雅、以拦，和以谢〔奏乐〕。歌唱的就大声歌唱，伊斯拉希雅管理他们。

chapters.en: On that day they offered great sacrifices, rejoicing because God had given them great joy. The women and children also rejoiced, so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard from afar.
chapters.zh: 那日，众人献大祭而欢乐；因为上帝使他们大大欢乐，连妇女带孩童也都欢乐，甚至耶路撒冷中的欢声听到远处。

chapters.en: And on that same day men were appointed over the rooms that housed the supplies, contributions, firstfruits, and tithes. The portions specified by the Law for the priests and Levites were gathered into these storerooms from the fields of the villages, because Judah rejoiced over the priests and Levites who were serving.
chapters.zh: 当日，派人管理库房，将举祭、初熟之物和所取的十分之一，就是按各城田地，照律法所定归给祭司和利未人的分，都收在里头。犹大人因祭司和利未人供职，就欢乐了。

chapters.en: They performed the service of their God and the service of purification, along with the singers and gatekeepers, as David and his son Solomon had prescribed.
chapters.zh: 祭司利未人遵守上帝所吩咐的，并守洁净的礼。歌唱的、守门的，照着大卫和他儿子所罗门的命令〔也如此行〕。

chapters.en: For long ago, in the days of David and Asaph, there were directors for the singers and for the songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.
chapters.zh: 古时，在大卫和亚萨的日子，有歌唱的伶长，并有赞美称谢上帝的诗歌。

chapters.en: So in the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, all Israel contributed the daily portions for the singers and gatekeepers. They also set aside daily portions for the Levites, and the Levites set aside daily portions for the descendants of Aaron.
chapters.zh: 当所罗巴伯和尼希米的时候，以色列众人将歌唱的、守门的，每日所当得的分供给他们，又给利未人当得的分；利未人又给亚伦的子孙当得的分。

chapters.en: At that time the Book of Moses was read aloud in the hearing of the people, and in it they found the passage stating that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God,
chapters.zh: 当日，人念摩西的〔律法〕书给百姓听，遇见书上写着说，亚扪人和摩押人永不可入上帝的会；

chapters.en: because they had not met the Israelites with food and water, but had hired Balaam to call down a curse against them (although our God had turned the curse into a blessing).
chapters.zh: 因为他们没有拿食物和水来迎接以色列人，且雇了巴兰咒诅他们，但我们的上帝使那咒诅变为祝福。

chapters.en: As soon as the people heard this law, they excluded from Israel all of foreign descent.
chapters.zh: 以色列民听见这律法，就与一切闲杂人绝交。

chapters.en: Now before this, Eliashib the priest, a relative of Tobiah, had been put in charge of the storerooms of the house of our God
chapters.zh: 先是蒙派管理我们上帝殿中库房的祭司以利亚实与多比雅结亲，

chapters.en: and had prepared for Tobiah a large room where they had previously stored the grain offerings, the frankincense, the temple articles, and the tithes of grain, new wine, and oil prescribed for the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, along with the contributions for the priests.
chapters.zh: 便为他预备一间大屋子，就是从前收存素祭、乳香、器皿，和照命令供给利未人、歌唱的、守门的五谷、新酒，和油的十分之一，并归祭司举祭的屋子。

chapters.en: While all this was happening, I was not in Jerusalem, because I had returned to Artaxerxes king of Babylon in the thirty-second year of his reign. Some time later I obtained leave from the king
chapters.zh: 那时我不在耶路撒冷；因为巴比伦王亚达薛西三十二年，我回到王那里。过了多日，我向王告假。

chapters.en: to return to Jerusalem. Then I discovered the evil that Eliashib had done on behalf of Tobiah by providing him a room in the courts of the house of God.
chapters.zh: 我来到耶路撒冷，就知道以利亚实为多比雅在上帝殿的院内预备屋子的那件恶事。

chapters.en: And I was greatly displeased and threw all of Tobiah’s household goods out of the room.
chapters.zh: 我甚恼怒，就把多比雅的一切家具从屋里都抛出去，

chapters.en: Then I ordered that the rooms be purified, and I had the articles of the house of God restored to them, along with the grain offerings and frankincense.
chapters.zh: 吩咐人洁净这屋子，遂将上帝殿的器皿和素祭、乳香又搬进去。

chapters.en: I also learned that because the portions for the Levites had not been given to them, all the Levites and singers responsible for performing the service had gone back to their own fields.
chapters.zh: 我见利未人所当得的分无人供给他们，甚至供职的利未人与歌唱的俱各奔回自己的田地去了。

chapters.en:
So I rebuked the officials and asked, “Why has the house of God been neglected?”
Then I gathered the Levites and singers together and stationed them at their posts,
chapters.zh: 我就斥责官长说：「为何离弃上帝的殿呢？」我便招聚利未人，使他们照旧供职。

chapters.en: and all Judah brought a tenth of the grain, new wine, and oil into the storerooms.
chapters.zh: 犹大众人就把五谷、新酒，和油的十分之一送入库房。

chapters.en: I appointed as treasurers over the storerooms Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, with Hanan son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah, to assist them, because they were considered trustworthy. They were responsible for distributing the supplies to their fellow Levites.
chapters.zh: 我派祭司示利米雅、文士撒督，和利未人毗大雅作库官管理库房；副官是哈难。哈难是撒刻的儿子；撒刻是玛他尼的儿子。这些人都是忠信的，他们的职分是将〔所供给的〕分给他们的弟兄。

chapters.en: Remember me for this, O my God, and do not blot out my deeds of loving devotion for the house of my God and for its services.
chapters.zh: 我的上帝啊，求你因这事记念我，不要涂抹我为上帝的殿与其中的礼节所行的善。

chapters.en: In those days I saw people in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath and bringing in grain and loading it on donkeys, along with wine, grapes, and figs. All kinds of goods were being brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. So I warned them against selling food on that day.
chapters.zh: 那些日子，我在犹大见有人在安息日醡酒〔注：原文是踹酒醡〕，搬运禾捆驮在驴上，又把酒、葡萄、无花果，和各样的担子在安息日担入耶路撒冷，我就在他们卖食物的那日警戒他们。

chapters.en: Additionally, men of Tyre who lived there were importing fish and all kinds of merchandise and selling them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 又有泰尔人住在耶路撒冷；他们把鱼和各样货物运进来，在安息日卖给犹大人。

chapters.en: Then I rebuked the nobles of Judah and asked, “What is this evil you are doing—profaning the Sabbath day?
chapters.zh: 我就斥责犹大的贵胄说：「你们怎么行这恶事犯了安息日呢？

chapters.en: Did not your forefathers do the same things, so that our God brought all this disaster on us and on this city? And now you are rekindling His wrath against Israel by profaning the Sabbath!”
chapters.zh: 从前你们列祖岂不是这样行，以致我们上帝使一切灾祸临到我们和这城吗？现在你们还犯安息日，使忿怒越发临到以色列！」

chapters.en: When the evening shadows began to fall on the gates of Jerusalem, just before the Sabbath, I ordered that the gates be shut and not opened until after the Sabbath. I posted some of my servants at the gates so that no load could enter on the Sabbath day.
chapters.zh: 在安息日的前一日，耶路撒冷城门有黑影的时候，我就吩咐人将门关锁，不过安息日不准开放。我又派我几个仆人管理城门，免得有人在安息日担什么担子进城。

chapters.en: Once or twice, the merchants and those who sell all kinds of goods camped outside Jerusalem,
chapters.zh: 于是商人和贩卖各样货物的，一两次住宿在耶路撒冷城外。

chapters.en: but I warned them, “Why are you camping in front of the wall? If you do it again, I will lay hands on you.” From that time on, they did not return on the Sabbath.
chapters.zh: 我就警戒他们说：「你们为何在城外住宿呢？若再这样，我必下手拿办你们。」从此以后，他们在安息日不再来了。

chapters.en:
Then I instructed the Levites to purify themselves and guard the gates in order to keep the Sabbath day holy.
Remember me for this as well, O my God, and show me mercy according to Your abundant loving devotion.
chapters.zh: 我吩咐利未人洁净自己，来守城门，使安息日为圣。我的上帝啊，求你因这事记念我，照你的大慈爱怜恤我。

chapters.en: In those days I also saw Jews who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
chapters.zh: 那些日子，我也见犹大人娶了亚实突、亚扪、摩押的女子为妻。

chapters.en: Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod or of the other peoples, but could not speak the language of Judah.
chapters.zh: 他们的儿女说话，一半是亚实突的话，不会说犹大的话，所说的是照着各族的方言。

chapters.en:
I rebuked them and called down curses on them. I beat some of these men and pulled out their hair.
Then I made them take an oath before God and said, “You must not give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters as wives for your sons or for yourselves!
chapters.zh: 我就斥责他们，咒诅他们，打了他们几个人，拔下他们的头发，叫他们指着上帝起誓，必不将自己的女儿嫁给外邦人的儿子，也不为自己和儿子娶他们的女儿。

chapters.en: Did not King Solomon of Israel sin in matters like this? There was not a king like him among many nations, and he was loved by his God, who made him king over all Israel—yet foreign women drew him into sin.
chapters.zh: 我〔又说〕：「以色列王所罗门不是在这样的事上犯罪吗？在多国中并没有一王像他，且蒙他上帝所爱，上帝立他作以色列全国的王；然而连他也被外邦女子引诱犯罪。

chapters.en: Must we now hear that you too are doing all this terrible evil and acting unfaithfully against our God by marrying foreign women?”
chapters.zh: 如此，我岂听你们行这大恶，娶外邦女子干犯我们的上帝呢？」

chapters.en: Even one of the sons of Jehoiada son of Eliashib the high priest had become a son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite. Therefore I drove him away from me.
chapters.zh: 大祭司以利亚实的孙子、耶何耶大的一个儿子是和伦人参巴拉的女婿，我就从我这里把他赶出去。

chapters.en: Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.
chapters.zh: 我的上帝啊，求你记念他们的罪；因为他们玷污了祭司的职任，违背你与祭司利未人所立的约。

chapters.en: Thus I purified the priests and Levites from everything foreign, and I assigned specific duties to each of the priests and Levites.
chapters.zh: 这样，我洁净他们，使他们离绝一切外邦人，派定祭司和利未人的班次，使他们各尽其职。

chapters.en:
I also arranged for contributions of wood at the appointed times, and for the firstfruits.
Remember me, O my God, with favor.
chapters.zh: 我又派〔百姓〕按定期献柴和初熟的土产。我的上帝啊，求你记念我，施恩与我。

chapters.en: This is what happened in the days of Xerxes, who reigned over 127 provinces from India to Cush.
chapters.zh: 亚哈随鲁作王，从印度直到古实，统管一百二十七省。

chapters.en: In those days King Xerxes sat on his royal throne in the citadel of Susa.
chapters.zh: 亚哈随鲁王在书珊城的宫登基；

chapters.en: In the third year of his reign, Xerxes held a feast for all his officials and servants. The military leaders of Persia and Media were there, along with the nobles and princes of the provinces.
chapters.zh: 在位第三年，为他一切首领臣仆设摆筵席，有波斯和米底亚的权贵，就是各省的贵胄与首领，在他面前。

chapters.en: And for a full 180 days he displayed the glorious riches of his kingdom and the magnificent splendor of his greatness.
chapters.zh: 他把他荣耀之国的丰富和他美好威严的尊贵给他们看了许多日，就是一百八十日。

chapters.en: At the end of this time, in the garden court of the royal palace, the king held a seven-day feast for all the people in the citadel of Susa, from the least to the greatest.
chapters.zh: 这日子满了，又为所有住书珊城的大小人民在御园的院子里设摆筵席七日。

chapters.en: Hangings of white and blue linen were fastened with cords of fine white and purple material to silver rings on the marble pillars. Gold and silver couches were arranged on a mosaic pavement of porphyry, marble, mother-of-pearl, and other costly stones.
chapters.zh: 有白色、绿色、蓝色的〔帐子〕，用细麻绳、紫色绳从银环内系在白玉石柱上；有金银的床榻摆在红、白、黄、黑玉石的铺石地上。

chapters.en: Beverages were served in an array of goblets of gold, each with a different design, and the royal wine flowed freely, according to the king’s bounty.
chapters.zh: 用金器皿赐酒，器皿各有不同。御酒甚多，足显王的厚意。

chapters.en: By order of the king, no limit was placed on the drinking, and every official of his household was to serve each man whatever he desired.
chapters.zh: 喝酒有例，不准勉强人，因王吩咐宫里的一切臣宰，让人各随己意。

chapters.en: Queen Vashti also gave a banquet for the women in the royal palace of King Xerxes.
chapters.zh: 王后瓦实提在亚哈随鲁王的宫内也为妇女设摆筵席。

chapters.en: On the seventh day, when the king’s heart was merry with wine, he ordered the seven eunuchs who served him—Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas—
chapters.zh: 第七日，亚哈随鲁王饮酒，心中快乐，就吩咐在他面前侍立的七个太监米户幔、比斯他、哈波拿、比革他、亚拔他、西达、甲迦，

chapters.en: to bring Queen Vashti before him, wearing her royal crown, to display her beauty to the people and officials. For she was beautiful to behold.
chapters.zh: 请王后瓦实提头戴王后的冠冕到王面前，使各等臣民看她的美貌，因为她容貌甚美。

chapters.en: Queen Vashti, however, refused to come at the king’s command brought by his eunuchs. And the king became furious, and his anger burned within him.
chapters.zh: 王后瓦实提却不肯遵太监所传的王命而来，所以王甚发怒，心如火烧。

chapters.en: Then the king consulted the wise men who knew the times, for it was customary for him to confer with the experts in law and justice.

His closest advisors were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media who had personal access to the king and ranked highest in the kingdom.
chapters.zh: 那时，在王左右常见王面、国中坐高位的，有波斯和米底亚的七个大臣，就是甲示拿、示达、押玛他、他施斯、米力、玛西拿、米母干，都是达时务的明哲人。按王的常规，办事必先询问知例明法的人。王问他们说：

chapters.en: “According to law,” he asked, “what should be done with Queen Vashti, since she refused to obey the command of King Xerxes delivered by the eunuchs?”
chapters.zh: 「王后瓦实提不遵太监所传的王命，照例应当怎样办理呢？」

chapters.en: And in the presence of the king and his princes, Memucan replied, “Queen Vashti has wronged not only the king, but all the princes and the peoples in all the provinces of King Xerxes.
chapters.zh: 米母干在王和众首领面前回答说：「王后瓦实提这事，不但得罪王，并且有害于王各省的臣民；

chapters.en: For the conduct of the queen will become known to all women, causing them to despise their husbands and say, ‘King Xerxes ordered Queen Vashti to be brought before him, but she did not come.’
chapters.zh: 因为王后这事必传到众妇人的耳中，说：『亚哈随鲁王吩咐王后瓦实提到王面前，她却不来』，她们就藐视自己的丈夫。

chapters.en: This very day the noble women of Persia and Media who have heard about the queen’s conduct will say the same thing to all the king’s officials, resulting in much contempt and wrath.
chapters.zh: 今日波斯和米底亚的众夫人听见王后这事，必向王的大臣〔照样〕行；从此必大开藐视和忿怒之端。

chapters.en: So if it pleases the king, let him issue a royal decree, and let it be recorded in the laws of Persia and Media so that it cannot be repealed, that Vashti shall never again enter the presence of King Xerxes, and that her royal position shall be given to a woman better than she.
chapters.zh: 王若以为美，就降旨写在波斯和米底亚人的例中，永不更改，不准瓦实提再到王面前，将她王后的位分赐给比她还好的人。

chapters.en: The edict the king issues will be heard throughout his vast kingdom—and so all women, from the least to the greatest, will honor their husbands.”
chapters.zh: 所降的旨意传遍通国（国度本来广大），所有的妇人，无论丈夫贵贱都必尊敬他。」

chapters.en: The king and his princes were pleased with this counsel; so the king did as Memucan advised.
chapters.zh: 王和众首领都以米母干的话为美，王就照这话去行，

chapters.en: He sent letters to all the provinces of the kingdom, to each province in its own script and to each people in their own language, proclaiming that every man should be master of his own household.
chapters.zh: 发诏书，用各省的文字、各族的方言通知各省，使为丈夫的在家中作主，各说本地的方言。

chapters.en: Some time later, when the anger of King Xerxes had subsided, he remembered Vashti and what she had done, and what had been decreed against her.
chapters.zh: 这事以后，亚哈随鲁王的忿怒止息，就想念瓦实提和她所行的，并怎样降旨办她。

chapters.en: Then the king’s attendants proposed, “Let a search be made for beautiful young virgins for the king,
chapters.zh: 于是王的侍臣对王说：「不如为王寻找美貌的处女。

chapters.en: and let the king appoint commissioners in each province of his kingdom to assemble all the beautiful young women into the harem at the citadel of Susa. Let them be placed under the care of Hegai, the king’s eunuch in charge of the women, and let them be given beauty treatments.
chapters.zh: 王可以派官在国中的各省招聚美貌的处女到书珊城〔注：或译：宫〕的女院，交给掌管女子的太监希该，给她们当用的香品。

chapters.en:
Then let the young woman who pleases the king become queen in place of Vashti.”
This suggestion pleased the king, and he acted accordingly.
chapters.zh: 王所喜爱的女子可以立为王后，代替瓦实提。」王以这事为美，就如此行。

chapters.en: Now there was at the citadel of Susa a Jewish man from the tribe of Benjamin named Mordecai son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish.
chapters.zh: 书珊城有一个犹大人，名叫末底改，是便雅悯人基士的曾孙，示每的孙子，睚珥的儿子。

chapters.en: He had been carried into exile from Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon among those taken captive with Jeconiah king of Judah.
chapters.zh: 从前巴比伦王尼布甲尼撒将犹大王耶哥尼雅〔注：又名约雅斤〕和百姓从耶路撒冷掳去，末底改也在其内。

chapters.en: And Mordecai had brought up Hadassah (that is, Esther), the daughter of his uncle, because she did not have a father or mother. The young woman was lovely in form and appearance, and when her father and mother had died, Mordecai had taken her as his own daughter.
chapters.zh: 末底改抚养他叔叔的女儿哈大沙（后名以斯帖），因为她没有父母。这女子又容貌俊美；她父母死了，末底改就收她为自己的女儿。

chapters.en: When the king’s command and edict had been proclaimed, many young women gathered at the citadel of Susa under the care of Hegai. Esther was also taken to the palace and placed under the care of Hegai, the custodian of the women.
chapters.zh: 王的谕旨传出，就招聚许多女子到书珊城，交给掌管女子的希该；以斯帖也送入王宫，交付希该。

chapters.en: And the young woman pleased him and obtained his favor, so he quickly provided her with beauty treatments and the special diet. He assigned to her seven select maidservants from the palace and transferred her with them to the best place in the harem.
chapters.zh: 希该喜悦以斯帖，就恩待她，急忙给她需用的香品和她所当得的分，又派所当得的七个宫女服事她，使她和她的宫女搬入女院上好的房屋。

chapters.en: Esther did not reveal her people or her lineage, because Mordecai had instructed her not to do so.
chapters.zh: 以斯帖未曾将籍贯宗族告诉人，因为末底改嘱咐她不可叫人知道。

chapters.en: And every day Mordecai would walk back and forth in front of the court of the harem to learn about Esther’s welfare and what was happening to her.
chapters.zh: 末底改天天在女院前边行走，要知道以斯帖平安不平安，并后事如何。

chapters.en: In the twelve months before her turn to go to King Xerxes, the harem regulation required each young woman to receive beauty treatments with oil of myrrh for six months, and then with perfumes and cosmetics for another six months.
chapters.zh: 众女子照例先洁净身体十二个月：六个月用没药油，六个月用香料和洁身之物。满了日期，然后挨次进去见亚哈随鲁王。

chapters.en: When the young woman would go to the king, she was given whatever she requested to take with her from the harem to the king’s palace.
chapters.zh: 女子进去见王是这样：从女院到王宫的时候，凡她所要的都必给她。

chapters.en: She would go there in the evening, and in the morning she would return to a second harem under the care of Shaashgaz, the king’s eunuch in charge of the concubines. She would not return to the king unless he delighted in her and summoned her by name.
chapters.zh: 晚上进去，次日回到女子第二院，交给掌管妃嫔的太监沙甲；除非王喜爱她，再提名召她，就不再进去见王。

chapters.en: Now Esther was the daughter of Abihail, the uncle from whom Mordecai had adopted her as his own daughter. And when it was her turn to go to the king, she did not ask for anything except what Hegai, the king’s trusted official in charge of the harem, had advised. And Esther found favor in the eyes of everyone who saw her.
chapters.zh: 末底改叔叔亚比孩的女儿，就是末底改收为自己女儿的以斯帖，按次序当进去见王的时候，除了掌管女子的太监希该所派定给她的，她别无所求。凡看见以斯帖的都喜悦她。

chapters.en: She was taken to King Xerxes in the royal palace in the tenth month, the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
chapters.zh: 亚哈随鲁王第七年十月，就是提别月，以斯帖被引入宫见王。

chapters.en: And the king loved Esther more than all the other women, and she found grace and favor in his sight more than all of the other virgins. So he placed the royal crown upon her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.
chapters.zh: 王爱以斯帖过于爱众女，她在王眼前蒙宠爱比众处女更甚。王就把王后的冠冕戴在她头上，立她为王后，代替瓦实提。

chapters.en: Then the king held a great banquet, Esther’s banquet, for all his officials and servants. He proclaimed a tax holiday in the provinces and gave gifts worthy of the king’s bounty.
chapters.zh: 王因以斯帖的缘故给众首领和臣仆设摆大筵席，又豁免各省的〔租税〕，并照王的厚意大颁赏赐。

chapters.en: When the virgins were assembled a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king’s gate.
chapters.zh: 第二次招聚处女的时候，末底改坐在朝门。

chapters.en: Esther still had not revealed her lineage or her people, just as Mordecai had instructed. She obeyed Mordecai’s command, as she had done under his care.
chapters.zh: 以斯帖照着末底改所嘱咐的，还没有将籍贯宗族告诉人；因为以斯帖遵*末底改的命，如抚养她的时候一样。

chapters.en: In those days, while Mordecai was sitting at the king’s gate, Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs who guarded the entrance, grew angry and conspired to assassinate King Xerxes.
chapters.zh: 当那时候，末底改坐在朝门，王的太监中有两个守门的，辟探和提列，恼恨亚哈随鲁王，想要下手害他。

chapters.en: When Mordecai learned of the plot, he reported it to Queen Esther, and she informed the king on Mordecai’s behalf.
chapters.zh: 末底改知道了，就告诉王后以斯帖。以斯帖奉末底改的名，报告于王；

chapters.en: After the report had been investigated and verified, both officials were hanged on the gallows. And all this was recorded in the Book of the Chronicles in the presence of the king.
chapters.zh: 究察这事，果然是实，就把二人挂在木头上，将这事在王面前写于历史上。

chapters.en: After these events, King Xerxes honored Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, elevating him to a position above all the princes who were with him.
chapters.zh: 这事以后，亚哈随鲁王抬举亚甲族哈米大他的儿子哈曼，使他高升，叫他的爵位超过与他同事的一切臣宰。

chapters.en: All the royal servants at the king’s gate bowed down and paid homage to Haman, because the king had commanded that this be done for him. But Mordecai would not bow down or pay homage.
chapters.zh: 在朝门的一切臣仆都跪拜哈曼，因为王如此吩咐；惟独末底改不跪不拜。

chapters.en: Then the royal servants at the king’s gate asked Mordecai, “Why do you disobey the command of the king?”
chapters.zh: 在朝门的臣仆问末底改说：「你为何违背王的命令呢？」

chapters.en: Day after day they warned him, but he would not comply. So they reported it to Haman to see whether Mordecai’s behavior would be tolerated, since he had told them he was a Jew.
chapters.zh: 他们天天劝他，他还是不听，他们就告诉哈曼，要看末底改的事站得住站不住，因他已经告诉他们自己是犹大人。

chapters.en: When Haman saw that Mordecai would not bow down or pay him homage, he was filled with rage.
chapters.zh: 哈曼见末底改不跪不拜，他就怒气填胸。

chapters.en: And when he learned the identity of Mordecai’s people, he scorned the notion of laying hands on Mordecai alone. Instead, he sought to destroy all of Mordecai’s people, the Jews, throughout the kingdom of Xerxes.
chapters.zh: 他们已将末底改的本族告诉哈曼；他以为下手害末底改一人是小事，就要灭绝亚哈随鲁王通国所有的犹大人，就是末底改的本族。

chapters.en: In the twelfth year of King Xerxes, in the first month, the month of Nisan, the Pur (that is, the lot) was cast before Haman to determine a day and month. And the lot fell on the twelfth month, the month of Adar.
chapters.zh: 亚哈随鲁王十二年正月，就是尼散月，人在哈曼面前，按日日月月掣普珥，就是掣签，要定何月何日为吉，择定了十二月，就是亚达月。

chapters.en: Then Haman informed King Xerxes, “There is a certain people scattered and dispersed among the peoples of every province of your kingdom. Their laws are different from everyone else’s, and they do not obey the king’s laws. So it is not in the king’s best interest to tolerate them.
chapters.zh: 哈曼对亚哈随鲁王说：「有一种民散居在王国各省的民中；他们的律例与万民的律例不同，也不守王的律例，所以容留他们与王无益。

chapters.en: If it pleases the king, let a decree be issued to destroy them, and I will deposit ten thousand talents of silver into the royal treasury to pay those who carry it out.”
chapters.zh: 王若以为美，请下旨意灭绝他们；我就捐一万他连得银子交给掌管国帑的人，纳入王的府库。」

chapters.en: So the king removed the signet ring from his finger and gave it to Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.
chapters.zh: 于是王从自己手上摘下戒指给犹大人的仇敌－亚甲族哈米大他的儿子哈曼。

chapters.en: “Keep your money,” said the king to Haman. “These people are given to you to do with them as you please.”
chapters.zh: 王对哈曼说：「这银子仍赐给你，这民也交给你，你可以随意待他们。」

chapters.en: On the thirteenth day of the first month, the royal scribes were summoned and the order was written exactly as Haman commanded the royal satraps, the governors of each province, and the officials of each people, in the script of each province and the language of every people. It was written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with the royal signet ring.
chapters.zh: 正月十三日，就召了王的书记来，照着哈曼一切所吩咐的，用各省的文字、各族的方言，奉亚哈随鲁王的名写旨意，传与总督和各省的省长，并各族的首领；又用王的戒指盖印，

chapters.en: And the letters were sent by couriers to each of the royal provinces with the order to destroy, kill, and annihilate all the Jews—young and old, women and children—and to plunder their possessions on a single day, the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month.
chapters.zh: 交给驿卒传到王的各省，吩咐将犹大人，无论老少妇女孩子，在一日之间，十二月，就是亚达月十三日，全然剪除，杀戮灭绝，并夺他们的财为掠物。

chapters.en: A copy of the text of the edict was to be issued in every province and published to all the people, so that they would be ready on that day.
chapters.zh: 抄录这旨意，颁行各省，宣告各族，使他们预备等候那日。

chapters.en: The couriers left, spurred on by the king’s command, and the edict was issued in the citadel of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Susa was in confusion.
chapters.zh: 驿卒奉王命急忙起行，旨意也传遍书珊城。王同哈曼坐下饮〔酒〕，书珊城的民却都慌乱。

chapters.en: When Mordecai learned of all that had happened, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the middle of the city, wailing loudly and bitterly.
chapters.zh: 末底改知道所做的这一切事，就撕裂衣服，穿麻衣，蒙灰尘，在城中行走，痛哭哀号。

chapters.en: But he went only as far as the king’s gate, because the law prohibited anyone wearing sackcloth from entering that gate.
chapters.zh: 到了朝门前〔停住脚步〕，因为穿麻衣的不可进朝门。

chapters.en: In every province to which the king’s command and edict came, there was great mourning among the Jews. They fasted, wept, and lamented, and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
chapters.zh: 王的谕旨所到的各省各处，犹大人大大悲哀，禁食哭泣哀号，穿麻衣躺在灰中的甚多。

chapters.en: When Esther’s maidens and eunuchs came and told her about Mordecai, the queen was overcome with distress. She sent clothes for Mordecai to wear instead of his sackcloth, but he would not accept them.
chapters.zh: 王后以斯帖的宫女和太监来把这事告诉以斯帖，她甚是忧愁，就送衣服给末底改穿，要他脱下麻衣，他却不受。

chapters.en: Then Esther summoned Hathach, one of the king’s eunuchs appointed to her, and she dispatched him to Mordecai to learn what was troubling him and why.
chapters.zh: 以斯帖就把王所派伺候她的一个太监，名叫哈他革召来，吩咐他去见末底改，要知道这是什么事，是什么缘故。

chapters.en: So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the city square in front of the king’s gate,
chapters.zh: 于是哈他革出到朝门前的宽阔处见末底改。

chapters.en: and Mordecai told him all that had happened to him, including the exact amount of money that Haman had promised to pay into the royal treasury in order to destroy the Jews.
chapters.zh: 末底改将自己所遇的事，并哈曼为灭绝犹大人应许捐入王库的银数都告诉了他；

chapters.en: Mordecai also gave Hathach a copy of the written decree issued in Susa for the destruction of the Jews, to show and explain to Esther, urging her to approach the king, implore his favor, and plead before him for her people.
chapters.zh: 又将所抄写传遍书珊城要灭绝犹大人的旨意交给哈他革，要给以斯帖看，又要给她说明，并嘱咐她进去见王，为本族的人在王面前恳切祈求。

chapters.en: So Hathach went back and relayed Mordecai’s response to Esther.
chapters.zh: 哈他革回来，将末底改的话告诉以斯帖；

chapters.en: Then Esther spoke to Hathach and instructed him to tell Mordecai,
chapters.zh: 以斯帖就吩咐哈他革去见末底改，〔说〕：

chapters.en: “All the royal officials and the people of the king’s provinces know that one law applies to every man or woman who approaches the king in the inner court without being summoned—that he be put to death. Only if the king extends the gold scepter may that person live. But I have not been summoned to appear before the king for the past thirty days.”
chapters.zh: 「王的一切臣仆和各省的人民都知道有一个定例：若不蒙召，擅入内院见王的，无论男女必被治死；除非王向他伸出金杖，不得存活。现在我没有蒙召进去见王已经三十日了。」

chapters.en: When Esther’s words were relayed to Mordecai,
chapters.zh: 人就把以斯帖这话告诉末底改。

chapters.en: he sent back to her this reply: “Do not imagine that because you are in the king’s palace you alone will escape the fate of all the Jews.
chapters.zh: 末底改讬人回复以斯帖说：「你莫想在王宫里强过一切犹大人，得免这祸。

chapters.en: For if you remain silent at this time, relief and deliverance for the Jews will arise from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. And who knows if perhaps you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”
chapters.zh: 此时你若闭口不言，犹大人必从别处得解脱，蒙拯救；你和你父家必致灭亡。焉知你得了王后的位分不是为现今的机会吗？」

chapters.en: Then Esther sent this reply to Mordecai:
chapters.zh: 以斯帖就吩咐人回报末底改说：

chapters.en: “Go and assemble all the Jews who can be found in Susa, and fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day, and I and my maidens will fast as you do. After that, I will go to the king, even though it is against the law. And if I perish, I perish! ”
chapters.zh: 「你当去招聚书珊城所有的犹大人，为我禁食三昼三夜，不吃不喝；我和我的宫女也要这样禁食。然后我违例进去见王，我若死就死吧！」

chapters.en: So Mordecai went and did all that Esther had instructed him.
chapters.zh: 于是末底改照以斯帖一切所吩咐的去行。

chapters.en: On the third day, Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner court of the palace across from the king’s quarters. The king was sitting on his royal throne in the royal courtroom, facing the entrance.
chapters.zh: 第三日，以斯帖穿上朝服，进王宫的内院，对殿站立。王在殿里坐在宝座上，对着殿门。

chapters.en: As soon as the king saw Queen Esther standing in the court, she found favor in his sight. The king extended the gold scepter in his hand toward Esther, and she approached and touched the tip of the scepter.
chapters.zh: 王见王后以斯帖站在院内，就施恩于她，向她伸出手中的金杖；以斯帖便向前摸杖头。

chapters.en: “What is it, Queen Esther?” the king inquired. “What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be given to you.”
chapters.zh: 王对她说：「王后以斯帖啊，你要什么？你求什么，就是国的一半也必赐给你。」

chapters.en: “If it pleases the king,” Esther replied, “may the king and Haman come today to the banquet I have prepared for the king.”
chapters.zh: 以斯帖说：「王若以为美，就请王带着哈曼今日赴我所预备的筵席。」

chapters.en:
“Hurry,” commanded the king, “and bring Haman, so we can do as Esther has requested.”
So the king and Haman went to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
chapters.zh: 王说：「叫哈曼速速照以斯帖的话去行。」于是王带着哈曼赴以斯帖所预备的筵席。

chapters.en: And as they drank their wine, the king said to Esther, “What is your petition? It will be given to you. What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be fulfilled.”
chapters.zh: 在酒席筵前，王又问以斯帖说：「你要什么，我必赐给你；你求什么，就是国的一半也必〔为你〕成就。」

chapters.en: Esther replied, “This is my petition and my request:
chapters.zh: 以斯帖回答说：「我有所要，我有所求。

chapters.en: If I have found favor in the sight of the king, and if it pleases the king to grant my petition and fulfill my request, may the king and Haman come tomorrow to the banquet I will prepare for them. Then I will answer the king’s question.”
chapters.zh: 我若在王眼前蒙恩，王若愿意赐我所要的，准我所求的，就请王带着哈曼再赴我所要预备的筵席。明日我必照王所问的说明。」

chapters.en: That day Haman went out full of joy and glad of heart. At the king’s gate, however, he saw Mordecai, who did not rise or tremble in fear at his presence. And Haman was filled with rage toward Mordecai.
chapters.zh: 那日哈曼心中快乐，欢欢喜喜地出来；但见末底改在朝门不站起来，连身也不动，就满心恼怒末底改。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, Haman restrained himself and went home. And calling for his friends and his wife Zeresh,
chapters.zh: 哈曼暂且忍耐回家，叫人请他朋友和他妻子细利斯来。

chapters.en: Haman recounted to them his glorious wealth, his many sons, and all the ways the king had honored and promoted him over the other officials and servants.
chapters.zh: 哈曼将他富厚的荣耀、众多的儿女，和王抬举他使他超乎首领臣仆之上，都述说给他们听。

chapters.en: “What is more,” Haman added, “Queen Esther invited no one but me to join the king at the banquet she prepared, and I am invited back tomorrow along with the king.
chapters.zh: 哈曼又说：「王后以斯帖预备筵席，除了我之外不许别人随王赴席。明日王后又请我随王赴席；

chapters.en: Yet none of this satisfies me as long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king’s gate.”
chapters.zh: 只是我见犹大人末底改坐在朝门，虽有这一切〔荣耀〕，也与我无益。」

chapters.en:
His wife Zeresh and all his friends told him, “Have them build a gallows fifty cubits high, and ask the king in the morning to have Mordecai hanged on it. Then go to the banquet with the king and enjoy yourself.”
The advice pleased Haman, and he had the gallows constructed.
chapters.zh: 他的妻细利斯和他一切的朋友对他说：「不如立一个五丈高的木架，明早求王将末底改挂在其上，然后你可以欢欢喜喜地随王赴席。」哈曼以这话为美，就叫人做了木架。

chapters.en: That night sleep escaped the king; so he ordered the Book of Records, the Chronicles, to be brought in and read to him.
chapters.zh: 那夜王睡不着觉，就吩咐人取历史来，念给他听。

chapters.en: And there it was found recorded that Mordecai had exposed Bigthana and Teresh, two of the eunuchs who guarded the king’s entrance, when they had conspired to assassinate King Xerxes.
chapters.zh: 正遇见书上写着〔说〕：王的太监中有两个守门的，辟探和提列，想要下手害亚哈随鲁王，末底改将这事告诉〔王后〕。

chapters.en:
The king inquired, “What honor or dignity has been bestowed on Mordecai for this act?”
“Nothing has been done for him,” replied the king’s attendants.
chapters.zh: 王说：「末底改行了这事，赐他什么尊荣爵位没有？」伺候王的臣仆回答说：「没有赐他什么。」

chapters.en:
“Who is in the court?” the king asked.
Now Haman had just entered the outer court of the palace to ask the king to hang Mordecai on the gallows he had prepared for him.
chapters.zh: 王说：「谁在院子里？」（那时哈曼正进王宫的外院，要求王将末底改挂在他所预备的木架上。）

chapters.en:
So the king’s attendants answered him, “Haman is there, standing in the court.”
“Bring him in,” ordered the king.
chapters.zh: 臣仆说：「哈曼站在院内。」王说：「叫他进来。」

chapters.en:
Haman entered, and the king asked him, “What should be done for the man whom the king is delighted to honor?”
Now Haman thought to himself, “Whom would the king be delighted to honor more than me?”
chapters.zh: 哈曼就进去。王问他说：「王所喜悦尊荣的人，当如何待他呢？」哈曼心里说：「王所喜悦尊荣的，不是我是谁呢？」

chapters.en: And Haman told the king, “For the man whom the king is delighted to honor,
chapters.zh: 哈曼就回答说：「王所喜悦尊荣的，

chapters.en: have them bring a royal robe that the king himself has worn and a horse on which the king himself has ridden—one with a royal crest placed on its head.
chapters.zh: 当将王常穿的朝服和戴冠的御马，

chapters.en: Let the robe and the horse be entrusted to one of the king’s most noble princes. Let them array the man the king wants to honor and parade him on the horse through the city square, proclaiming before him, ‘This is what is done for the man whom the king is delighted to honor!’”
chapters.zh: 都交给王极尊贵的一个大臣，命他将衣服给王所喜悦尊荣的人穿上，使他骑上马，走遍城里的街市，在他面前宣告说：王所喜悦尊荣的人，就如此待他。」

chapters.en: “Hurry,” said the king to Haman, “and do just as you proposed. Take the robe and the horse to Mordecai the Jew, who is sitting at the king’s gate. Do not neglect anything that you have suggested.”
chapters.zh: 王对哈曼说：「你速速将这衣服和马，照你所说的，向坐在朝门的犹大人末底改去行。凡你所说的，一样不可缺。」

chapters.en: So Haman took the robe and the horse, arrayed Mordecai, and paraded him through the city square, crying out before him, “This is what is done for the man whom the king is delighted to honor!”
chapters.zh: 于是哈曼将朝服给末底改穿上，使他骑上马，走遍城里的街市，在他面前宣告说：「王所喜悦尊荣的人，就如此待他。」

chapters.en: Then Mordecai returned to the king’s gate. But Haman rushed home, with his head covered in grief.
chapters.zh: 末底改仍回到朝门，哈曼却忧忧闷闷地蒙着头，急忙回家去了，

chapters.en: Haman told his wife Zeresh and all his friends everything that had happened. His advisers and his wife Zeresh said to him, “Since Mordecai, before whom your downfall has begun, is Jewish, you will not prevail against him—for surely you will fall before him.”
chapters.zh: 将所遇的一切事详细说给他的妻细利斯和他的众朋友听。他的智慧人和他的妻细利斯对他说：「你在末底改面前始而败落，他如果是犹大人，你必不能胜他，终必在他面前败落。」

chapters.en: While they were still speaking with Haman, the king’s eunuchs arrived and rushed him to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
chapters.zh: 他们还与哈曼说话的时候，王的太监来催哈曼快去赴以斯帖所预备的筵席。

chapters.en: So the king and Haman went to dine with Esther the queen,
chapters.zh: 王带着哈曼来赴王后以斯帖的筵席。

chapters.en: and as they drank their wine on that second day, the king asked once more, “Queen Esther, what is your petition? It will be given to you. What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be fulfilled.”
chapters.zh: 这第二次在酒席筵前，王又问以斯帖说：「王后以斯帖啊，你要什么，我必赐给你；你求什么，*就是国的一半也必〔为你〕成就。」

chapters.en: Queen Esther replied, “If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it pleases the king, grant me my life as my petition, and the lives of my people as my request.
chapters.zh: 王后以斯帖回答说：「我若在王眼前蒙恩，王若以为美，我所愿的，是愿王将我的性命赐给我；我所求的，是求王将我的本族赐给我。

chapters.en: For my people and I have been sold out to destruction, death, and annihilation. If we had merely been sold as menservants and maidservants, I would have remained silent, because no such distress would justify burdening the king.”
chapters.zh: 因我和我的本族被卖了，要剪除杀戮灭绝我们。我们若被卖为奴为婢，我也闭口不言；但王的损失，敌人万不能补足。」

chapters.en: Then King Xerxes spoke up and asked Queen Esther, “Who is this, and where is the one who would devise such a scheme?”
chapters.zh: 亚哈随鲁王问王后以斯帖说：「擅敢起意如此行的是谁？这人在哪里呢？」

chapters.en:
Esther replied, “The adversary and enemy is this wicked man—Haman!”
And Haman stood in terror before the king and queen.
chapters.zh: 以斯帖说：「仇人敌人就是这恶人哈曼！」 哈曼在王和王后面前就甚惊惶。

chapters.en: In his fury, the king arose from drinking his wine and went to the palace garden, while Haman stayed behind to beg Queen Esther for his life, for he realized that the king was planning a terrible fate for him.
chapters.zh: 王便大怒，起来离开酒席往御园去了。哈曼见王定意要加罪与他，就起来，求王后以斯帖救命。

chapters.en:
Just as the king returned from the palace garden to the banquet hall, Haman was falling on the couch where Esther was reclining. The king exclaimed, “Would he actually assault the queen while I am in the palace?”
As soon as the words had left the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.
chapters.zh: 王从御园回到酒席之处，见哈曼伏在以斯帖所靠的榻上；王说：「他竟敢在宫内、在我面前凌辱王后吗？」这话一出王口，人就蒙了哈曼的脸。

chapters.en:
Then Harbonah, one of the eunuchs attending the king, said: “There is a gallows fifty cubits high at Haman’s house. He had it built for Mordecai, who gave the report that saved the king.”
“Hang him on it!” declared the king.
chapters.zh: 伺候王的一个太监名叫哈波拿，说：「哈曼为那救王有功的末底改做了五丈高的木架，现今立在哈曼家里。」王说：「把哈曼挂在其上。」

chapters.en: So they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the fury of the king subsided.
chapters.zh: 于是人将哈曼挂在他为末底改所预备的木架上。王的忿怒这才止息。

chapters.en: That same day King Xerxes awarded Queen Esther the estate of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. And Mordecai entered the king’s presence because Esther had revealed his relation to her.
chapters.zh: 当日，亚哈随鲁王把犹大人仇敌哈曼的家产赐给王后以斯帖。末底改也来到王面前，因为以斯帖已经告诉王，末底改是她的亲属。

chapters.en: The king removed the signet ring he had recovered from Haman and presented it to Mordecai. And Esther appointed Mordecai over the estate of Haman.
chapters.zh: 王摘下自己的戒指，就是从哈曼追回的，给了末底改。以斯帖派末底改管理哈曼的家产。

chapters.en: And once again, Esther addressed the king. She fell at his feet weeping and begged him to revoke the evil scheme of Haman the Agagite, which he had devised against the Jews.
chapters.zh: 以斯帖又俯伏在王脚前，流泪哀告，求他除掉亚甲族哈曼害犹大人的恶谋。

chapters.en: The king extended the gold scepter toward Esther, and she arose and stood before the king.
chapters.zh: 王向以斯帖伸出金杖；以斯帖就起来，站在王前，

chapters.en: “If it pleases the king,” she said, “and if I have found favor in his sight, and the matter seems proper to the king, and I am pleasing in his sight, may an order be written to revoke the letters that the scheming Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, wrote to destroy the Jews in all the king’s provinces.
chapters.zh: 说：「亚甲族哈米大他的儿子哈曼设谋传旨，要杀灭在王各省的犹大人。现今王若愿意，我若在王眼前蒙恩，王若以为美，若喜悦我，请王另下旨意，废除哈曼所传的那旨意。

chapters.en: For how could I bear to see the disaster that would befall my people? How could I bear to see the destruction of my kindred?”
chapters.zh: 我何忍见我本族的人受害？何忍见我同宗的人被灭呢？」

chapters.en: So King Xerxes said to Esther the Queen and Mordecai the Jew, “Behold, I have given Haman’s estate to Esther, and he was hanged on the gallows because he attacked the Jews.
chapters.zh: 亚哈随鲁王对王后以斯帖和犹大人末底改说：「因哈曼要下手害犹大人，我已将他的家产赐给以斯帖，人也将哈曼挂在木架上。

chapters.en: Now you may write in the king’s name as you please regarding the Jews, and seal it with the royal signet ring. For a decree that is written in the name of the king and sealed with the royal signet ring cannot be revoked.”
chapters.zh: 现在你们可以随意奉王的名写谕旨给犹大人，用王的戒指盖印；因为奉王名所写、用王戒指盖印的谕旨，人都不能废除。」

chapters.en: At once the royal scribes were summoned, and on the twenty-third day of the third month (the month of Sivan ), they recorded all of Mordecai’s orders to the Jews and to the satraps, governors, and princes of the 127 provinces from India to Cush —writing to each province in its own script, to every people in their own language, and to the Jews in their own script and language.
chapters.zh: 三月，就是西弯月二十三日，将王的书记召来，按着末底改所吩咐的，用各省的文字、各族的方言，并犹大人的文字方言写谕旨，传给那从印度直到古实一百二十七省的犹大人和总督省长首领。

chapters.en: Mordecai wrote in the name of King Xerxes and sealed it with the royal signet ring. He sent the documents by mounted couriers riding on swift horses bred from the royal mares.
chapters.zh: 末底改奉亚哈随鲁王的名写谕旨，用王的戒指盖印，交给骑御马圈快马的驿卒，传〔到各处〕。

chapters.en: By these letters the king permitted the Jews in each and every city the right to assemble and defend themselves, to destroy, kill, and annihilate all the forces of any people or province hostile to them, including women and children, and to plunder their possessions.
The single day appointed throughout all the provinces of King Xerxes was the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar.
chapters.zh: 谕旨中，王准各省各城的犹大人在一日之间，十二月，就是亚达月十三日，聚集保护性命，剪除杀戮灭绝那要攻击犹大人的一切仇敌和他们的妻子儿女，夺取他们的财为掠物。

chapters.en: A copy of the text of the edict was to be issued in every province and published to all the people, so that the Jews would be ready on that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.
chapters.zh: 抄录这谕旨，颁行各省，宣告各族，使犹大人预备等候那日，在仇敌身上报仇。

chapters.en: The couriers rode out in haste on their royal horses, pressed on by the command of the king. And the edict was also issued in the citadel of Susa.
chapters.zh: 于是骑快马的驿卒被王命催促，急忙起行；谕旨也传遍书珊城。

chapters.en: Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal garments of blue and white, with a large gold crown and a purple robe of fine linen. And the city of Susa shouted and rejoiced.
chapters.zh: 末底改穿着蓝色白色的朝服，头戴大金冠冕，又穿紫色细麻布的外袍，从王面前出来；书珊城的人民都欢呼快乐。

chapters.en: For the Jews it was a time of light and gladness, of joy and honor.
chapters.zh: 犹大人有光荣，欢喜快乐而得尊贵。

chapters.en: In every province and every city, wherever the king’s edict and decree reached, there was joy and gladness among the Jews, with feasting and celebrating. And many of the people of the land themselves became Jews, because the fear of the Jews had fallen upon them.
chapters.zh: 王的谕旨所到的各省各城，犹大人都欢喜快乐，设摆筵宴，以那日为吉日。那国的人民，有许多因惧怕犹大人，就入了犹大籍。

chapters.en: On the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, the king’s command and edict were to be executed. On this day the enemies of the Jews had hoped to overpower them, but their plan was overturned and the Jews overpowered those who hated them.
chapters.zh: 十二月，乃亚达月十三日，王的谕旨将要举行，就是犹大人的仇敌盼望辖制他们的日子，犹大人反倒辖制恨他们的人。

chapters.en: In each of the provinces of King Xerxes, the Jews assembled in their cities to attack those who sought to harm them. No man could withstand them, because the fear of them had fallen upon all peoples.
chapters.zh: 犹大人在亚哈随鲁王各省的城里聚集，下手击杀那要害他们的人。无人能敌挡他们，因为各族都惧怕他们。

chapters.en: And all the officials of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and the king’s administrators helped the Jews, because the fear of Mordecai had fallen upon them.
chapters.zh: 各省的首领、总督、省长，和办理王事的人，因惧怕末底改，就都帮助犹大人。

chapters.en: For Mordecai exercised great power in the palace, and his fame spread throughout the provinces as he became more and more powerful.
chapters.zh: 末底改在朝中为大，名声传遍各省，日渐昌盛。

chapters.en: The Jews put all their enemies to the sword, killing and destroying them, and they did as they pleased to those who hated them.
chapters.zh: 犹大人用刀击杀一切仇敌，任意杀灭恨他们的人。

chapters.en: In the citadel of Susa, the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men,
chapters.zh: 在书珊城，犹大人杀灭了五百人；

chapters.en: including Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,
chapters.zh: 又杀巴珊大他、达分、亚斯帕他、

chapters.en: Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,
chapters.zh: 破拉他、亚大利雅、亚利大他、

chapters.en: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha.
chapters.zh: 帕玛斯他、亚利赛、亚利代、瓦耶撒他；

chapters.en: They killed these ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews, but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.
chapters.zh: 这十人都是哈米大他的孙子、犹大人仇敌哈曼的儿子。犹大人却没有下手夺取财物。

chapters.en: On that day the number of those killed in the citadel of Susa was reported to the king,
chapters.zh: 当日，将书珊城被杀的人数呈在王前。

chapters.en: who said to Queen Esther, “In the citadel of Susa the Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men, including Haman’s ten sons. What have they done in the rest of the royal provinces? Now what is your petition? It will be given to you. And what further do you request? It will be fulfilled.”
chapters.zh: 王对王后以斯帖说：「犹大人在书珊城杀灭了五百人，又杀了哈曼的十个儿子，在王的各省不知如何呢？现在你要什么，我必赐给你；你还求什么，也必〔为你〕成就。」

chapters.en: Esther replied, “If it pleases the king, may the Jews in Susa also have tomorrow to carry out today’s edict, and may the bodies of Haman’s ten sons be hanged on the gallows.”
chapters.zh: 以斯帖说：「王若以为美，求你准书珊的犹大人，明日也照今日的旨意行，并将哈曼十个儿子的尸首挂在木架上。」

chapters.en: So the king commanded that this be done. An edict was issued in Susa, and they hanged the ten sons of Haman.
chapters.zh: 王便允准如此行。旨意传在书珊，人就把哈曼十个儿子的尸首挂起来了。

chapters.en: On the fourteenth day of the month of Adar, the Jews in Susa came together again and put to death three hundred men there, but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.
chapters.zh: 亚达月十四日，书珊的犹大人又聚集在书珊，杀了三百人，却没有下手夺取财物。

chapters.en: The rest of the Jews in the royal provinces also assembled to defend themselves and rid themselves of their enemies. They killed 75,000 who hated them, but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.
chapters.zh: 在王各省其余的犹大人也都聚集保护性命，杀了恨他们的人七万五千，却没有下手夺取财物。这样，就脱离仇敌，得享平安。

chapters.en: This was done on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, and on the fourteenth day they rested, making it a day of feasting and joy.
chapters.zh: 亚达月十三日，〔行了这事〕；十四日安息，以这日为设筵欢乐的日子。

chapters.en: The Jews in Susa, however, had assembled on the thirteenth and the fourteenth days of the month. So they rested on the fifteenth day, making it a day of feasting and joy.
chapters.zh: 但书珊的犹大人，这十三日、十四日聚集〔杀戮仇敌〕；十五日安息，以这日为设筵欢乐的日子。

chapters.en: This is why the rural Jews, who live in the villages, observe the fourteenth day of the month of Adar as a day of joy and feasting. It is a holiday for sending gifts to one another.
chapters.zh: 所以住无城墙乡村的犹大人，如今都以亚达月十四日为设筵欢乐的吉日，彼此餽送礼物。

chapters.en: Mordecai recorded these events and sent letters to all the Jews in all the provinces of King Xerxes, both near and far,
chapters.zh: 末底改记录这事，写信与亚哈随鲁王各省远近所有的犹大人，

chapters.en: to establish among them an annual celebration on the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar
chapters.zh: 嘱咐他们每年守亚达月十四、十五两日，

chapters.en: as the days on which the Jews gained rest from their enemies and the month in which their sorrow turned to joy and their mourning into a holiday. He wrote that these were to be days of feasting and joy, of sending gifts to one another and to the poor.
chapters.zh: 以这月的两日为犹大人脱离仇敌得平安、转忧为喜、转悲为乐的吉日。在这两日设筵欢乐，彼此餽送礼物，赒济穷人。

chapters.en: So the Jews agreed to continue the custom they had started, as Mordecai had written to them.
chapters.zh: 于是，犹大人按着末底改所写与他们的信，应承照初次所守的守为永例；

chapters.en: For Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them and had cast the Pur (that is, the lot) to crush and destroy them.
chapters.zh: 是因犹大人的仇敌亚甲族哈米大他的儿子哈曼设谋杀害犹大人，掣普珥，就是掣签，为要杀尽灭绝他们；

chapters.en: But when it came before the king, he commanded by letter that the wicked scheme which Haman had devised against the Jews should come back upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
chapters.zh: 这事报告于王，王便降旨使哈曼谋害犹大人的恶事归到他自己的头上，并吩咐把他和他的众子都挂在木架上。

chapters.en:
Therefore these days are called Purim, from the word Pur.
Because of all the instructions in this letter, and because of all they had seen and experienced,
chapters.zh: 照着普珥的名字，犹大人就称这两日为「普珥日」。他们因这信上的话，又因所看见所遇见的事，

chapters.en: the Jews bound themselves to establish the custom that they and their descendants and all who join them should not fail to celebrate these two days at the appointed time each and every year, according to their regulation.
chapters.zh: 就应承自己与后裔，并归附他们的人，每年按时必守这两日，永远不废。

chapters.en: These days should be remembered and celebrated by every generation, family, province, and city, so that these days of Purim should not fail to be observed among the Jews, nor should the memory of them fade from their descendants.
chapters.zh: 各省各城、家家户户、世世代代纪念遵守这两日，使这「普珥日」在犹大人中不可废掉，在他们后裔中也不可忘记。

chapters.en: So Queen Esther daughter of Abihail, along with Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter concerning Purim.
chapters.zh: 亚比孩的女儿－王后以斯帖和犹大人末底改以全权写第二封信，坚嘱犹大人守这「普珥日」，

chapters.en: And Mordecai sent letters with words of peace and truth to all the Jews in the 127 provinces of the kingdom of Xerxes,
chapters.zh: 用和平诚实话写信给亚哈随鲁〔王〕国中一百二十七省所有的犹大人，

chapters.en: in order to confirm these days of Purim at their appointed time, just as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had established them and had committed themselves and their descendants to the times of fasting and lamentation.
chapters.zh: 劝他们按时守这「普珥日」，禁食呼求，是照犹大人末底改和王后以斯帖所嘱咐的，也照犹大人为自己与后裔所应承的。

chapters.en: So Esther’s decree confirmed these regulations about Purim, which were written into the record.
chapters.zh: 以斯帖命定守「普珥日」，这事也记录在书上。

chapters.en: Now King Xerxes imposed tribute throughout the land, even to its farthest shores.
chapters.zh: 亚哈随鲁王使旱地和海岛的人民都进贡。

chapters.en: And all of Mordecai’s powerful and magnificent accomplishments, together with the full account of the greatness to which the king had raised him, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Media and Persia?
chapters.zh: 他以权柄能力所行的，并他抬举末底改使他高升的事，岂不都写在米底亚和波斯王的历史上吗？

chapters.en: For Mordecai the Jew was second only to King Xerxes, preeminent among the Jews and highly favored by his many kinsmen, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all his countrymen.
chapters.zh: 犹大人末底改作亚哈随鲁王的宰相，在犹大人中为大，得他众弟兄的喜悦，为本族的人求好处，向他们说和平的话。

chapters.en: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. And this man was blameless and upright, fearing God and shunning evil.
chapters.zh: 乌斯地有一个人名叫约伯；那人完全正直，敬畏上帝，远离恶事。

chapters.en: He had seven sons and three daughters,
chapters.zh: 他生了七个儿子，三个女儿。

chapters.en: and he owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 yoke of oxen, 500 female donkeys, and a very large number of servants. Job was the greatest man of all the people of the East.
chapters.zh: 他的家产有七千羊，三千骆驼，五百对牛，五百母驴，并有许多仆婢。这人在东方人中就为至大。

chapters.en: Job’s sons would take turns holding feasts in their homes, and they would invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
chapters.zh: 他的儿子按着日子各在自己家里设摆筵宴，就打发人去，请了他们的三个姊妹来，与他们一同吃喝。

chapters.en: And when the days of feasting were over, Job would send for his children to purify them, rising early in the morning to offer burnt offerings for all of them. For Job thought, “Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.” This was Job’s regular practice.
chapters.zh: 筵宴的日子过了，约伯打发人去叫他们自洁。他清早起来，按着他们众人的数目献燔祭；因为他说：「恐怕我儿子犯了罪，心中弃掉上帝。」约伯常常这样行。

chapters.en: One day the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came with them.
chapters.zh: 有一天，上帝的众子来侍立在耶和华面前，撒但也来在其中。

chapters.en:
“Where have you come from?” said the LORD to Satan.
“From roaming through the earth,” he replied, “and walking back and forth in it.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华问撒但说：「你从哪里来？」撒但回答说：「我从地上走来走去，往返而来。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered My servant Job? For there is no one on earth like him, a man who is blameless and upright, who fears God and shuns evil.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华问撒但说：「你曾用心察看我的仆人约伯没有？地上再没有人像他完全正直，敬畏上帝，远离恶事。」

chapters.en: Satan answered the LORD, “Does Job fear God for nothing?
chapters.zh: 撒但回答耶和华说：「约伯敬畏上帝，岂是无故呢？

chapters.en: Have You not placed a hedge on every side around him and his household and all that he owns? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have increased in the land.
chapters.zh: 你岂不是四面圈上篱笆围护他和他的家，并他一切所有的吗？他手所做的都蒙你赐福；他的家产也在地上增多。

chapters.en: But stretch out Your hand and strike all that he has, and he will surely curse You to Your face.”
chapters.zh: 你且伸手毁他一切所有的；他必当面弃掉你。」

chapters.en:
“Very well,” said the LORD to Satan. “Everything he has is in your hands, but you must not lay a hand on the man himself.”
Then Satan went out from the presence of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对撒但说：「凡他所有的都在你手中；只是不可伸手加害于他。」于是撒但从耶和华面前退去。

chapters.en: One day, while Job’s sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,
chapters.zh: 有一天，约伯的儿女正在他们长兄的家里吃饭喝酒，

chapters.en: a messenger came and reported to Job: “While the oxen were plowing and the donkeys were grazing nearby,
chapters.zh: 有报信的来见约伯，说：「牛正耕地，驴在旁边吃草，

chapters.en: the Sabeans swooped down and took them away. They put the servants to the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
chapters.zh: 示巴人忽然闯来，把牲畜掳去，并用刀杀了仆人；惟有我一人逃脱，来报信给你。」

chapters.en: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and reported: “The fire of God fell from heaven. It burned and consumed the sheep and the servants, and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
chapters.zh: 他还说话的时候，又有人来说：「上帝从天上降下火来，将群羊和仆人都烧灭了；惟有我一人逃脱，来报信给你。」

chapters.en: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and reported: “The Chaldeans formed three bands, raided the camels, and took them away. They put the servants to the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
chapters.zh: 他还说话的时候，又有人来说：「迦勒底人分作三队忽然闯来，把骆驼掳去，并用刀杀了仆人；惟有我一人逃脱，来报信给你。」

chapters.en: While he was still speaking, another messenger came and reported: “Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,
chapters.zh: 他还说话的时候，又有人来说：「你的儿女正在他们长兄的家里吃饭喝酒，

chapters.en: when suddenly a mighty wind swept in from the desert and struck the four corners of the house. It collapsed on the young people and they are dead, and I alone have escaped to tell you!”
chapters.zh: 不料，有狂风从旷野刮来，击打房屋的四角，房屋倒塌在少年人身上，他们就都死了；惟有我一人逃脱，来报信给你。」

chapters.en: Then Job stood up, tore his robe, and shaved his head. He fell to the ground and worshiped,
chapters.zh: 约伯便起来，撕裂外袍，剃了头，伏在地上下拜，

chapters.en:
saying:
“Naked I came from my mother’s womb, and naked I will return. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the name of the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 说：「我赤身出于母胎，也必赤身归回；赏赐的是耶和华，收取的也是耶和华。耶和华的名是应当称颂的。」

chapters.en: In all this, Job did not sin or charge God with wrongdoing.
chapters.zh: 在这一切的事上约伯并不犯罪，也不以上帝为愚妄〔注：或译：也不妄评上帝〕。

chapters.en: On another day the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came with them to present himself before Him.
chapters.zh: 又有一天，上帝的众子来侍立在耶和华面前，撒但也来在其中。

chapters.en:
“Where have you come from?” said the LORD to Satan.
“From roaming through the earth,” he replied, “and walking back and forth in it.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华问撒但说：「你从哪里来？」撒但回答说：「我从地上走来走去，往返而来。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered My servant Job? For there is no one on earth like him, a man who is blameless and upright, who fears God and shuns evil. He still retains his integrity, even though you incited Me against him to ruin him without cause.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华问撒但说：「你曾用心察看我的仆人约伯没有？地上再没有人像他完全正直，敬畏上帝，远离恶事。你虽激动我攻击他，无故地毁灭他，他仍然持守他的纯正。」

chapters.en: “Skin for skin!” Satan replied. “A man will give up all he owns in exchange for his life.
chapters.zh: 撒但回答耶和华说：「人以皮代皮，情愿舍去一切所有的，保全性命。

chapters.en: But stretch out Your hand and strike his flesh and bones, and he will surely curse You to Your face.”
chapters.zh: 你且伸手伤他的骨头和他的肉，他必当面弃掉你。」

chapters.en: “Very well,” said the LORD to Satan. “He is in your hands, but you must spare his life.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华对撒但说：「他在你手中，只要存留他的性命。」

chapters.en: So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD and infected Job with terrible boils from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head.
chapters.zh: 于是撒但从耶和华面前退去，击打约伯，使他从脚掌到头顶长毒疮。

chapters.en: And Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself as he sat among the ashes.
chapters.zh: 约伯就坐在炉灰中，拿瓦片刮身体。

chapters.en: Then Job’s wife said to him, “Do you still retain your integrity? Curse God and die!”
chapters.zh: 他的妻子对他说：「你仍然持守你的纯正吗？你弃掉上帝，死了吧！」

chapters.en:
“You speak as a foolish woman speaks,” he told her. “Should we accept from God only good and not adversity?”
In all this, Job did not sin in what he said.
chapters.zh: 约伯却对她说：「你说话像愚顽的妇人一样。嗳！难道我们从上帝手里得福，不也受祸吗？」在这一切的事上约伯并不以口犯罪。

chapters.en: Now when Job’s three friends—Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite—heard about all this adversity that had come upon him, each of them came from his home, and they met together to go and sympathize with Job and comfort him.
chapters.zh: 约伯的三个朋友－提幔人以利法、书亚人比勒达、拿玛人琐法－听说有这一切的灾祸临到他身上，各人就从本处约会同来，为他悲伤，安慰他。

chapters.en: When they lifted up their eyes from afar, they could barely recognize Job. They began to weep aloud, and each man tore his robe and threw dust in the air over his head.
chapters.zh: 他们远远地举目观看，认不出他来，就放声大哭。各人撕裂外袍，把尘土向天扬起来，落在自己的头上。

chapters.en: Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights, but no one spoke a word to him because they saw how intense his suffering was.
chapters.zh: 他们就同他七天七夜坐在地上，一个人也不向他说句话，因为他极其痛苦。

chapters.en: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
chapters.zh: 此后，约伯开口咒诅自己的〔生〕日，

chapters.en: And this is what he said:
chapters.zh: 说：

chapters.en:
“May the day of my birth perish, and the night it was said,
‘A boy is conceived.’
chapters.zh: 愿我生的那日 和说怀了男胎的那夜都灭没。

chapters.en:
If only that day had turned to darkness! May God above disregard it;
may no light shine upon it.
chapters.zh: 愿那日变为黑暗； 愿上帝不从上面寻找它； 愿亮光不照于其上。

chapters.en:
May darkness and gloom reclaim it, and a cloud settle over it;
may the blackness of the day overwhelm it.
chapters.zh: 愿黑暗和死荫索取那日； 愿密云停在其上； 愿日蚀恐吓它。

chapters.en:
If only darkness had taken that night away! May it not appear among the days of the year;
may it never be entered in any of the months.
chapters.zh: 愿那夜被幽暗夺取， 不在年中的日子同乐， 也不入月中的数目。

chapters.en: Behold, may that night be barren; may no joyful voice come into it.
chapters.zh: 愿那夜没有生育， 其间也没有欢乐的声音。

chapters.en: May it be cursed by those who curse the day — those prepared to rouse Leviathan.
chapters.zh: 愿那咒诅日子且能惹动鳄鱼的 咒诅那夜。

chapters.en:
May its morning stars grow dark; may it wait in vain for daylight;
may it not see the breaking of dawn.
chapters.zh: 愿那夜黎明的星宿变为黑暗， 盼亮却不亮， 也不见早晨的光线〔注：原文是眼皮〕；

chapters.en: For that night did not shut the doors of the womb to hide the sorrow from my eyes.
chapters.zh: 因没有把怀我胎的门关闭， 也没有将患难对我的眼隐藏。

chapters.en: Why did I not perish at birth; why did I not die as I came from the womb?
chapters.zh: 我为何不出〔母〕胎而死？ 为何不出〔母〕腹绝气？

chapters.en: Why were there knees to receive me, and breasts that I should be nursed?
chapters.zh: 为何有膝接收我？ 为何有奶哺养我？

chapters.en: For now I would be lying down in peace; I would be asleep and at rest
chapters.zh: 不然，我就早已躺卧安睡，

chapters.en: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built for themselves cities now in ruins,
chapters.zh: 和地上为自己重造荒邱的君王、谋士，

chapters.en: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.
chapters.zh: 或与有金子、将银子装满了房屋的王子 一同安息；

chapters.en: Or why was I not hidden like a stillborn child, like an infant who never sees daylight?
chapters.zh: 或像隐而未现、不到期而落的胎， 归于无有，如同未见光的婴孩。

chapters.en: There the wicked cease from raging, and there the weary find rest.
chapters.zh: 在那里恶人止息搅扰， 困乏人得享安息，

chapters.en: The captives enjoy their ease; they do not hear the voice of the oppressor.
chapters.zh: 被囚的人同得安逸， 不听见督工的声音。

chapters.en: Both small and great are there, and the slave is freed from his master.
chapters.zh: 大小都在那里； 奴仆脱离主人的辖制。

chapters.en: Why is light given to the miserable, and life to the bitter of soul,
chapters.zh: 受患难的人为何有光赐给他呢？ 心中愁苦的人为何有生命赐给他呢？

chapters.en: who long for death that does not come, and search for it like hidden treasure,
chapters.zh: 他们切望死，却不得死； 求死，胜于求隐藏的珍宝。

chapters.en: who rejoice and greatly exult when they reach the grave?
chapters.zh: 他们寻见坟墓就快乐， 极其欢喜。

chapters.en: Why is life given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
chapters.zh: 人的道路既然遮隐， 上帝又把他四面围困， 〔为何有光赐给〕他呢？

chapters.en: I sigh when food is put before me, and my groans pour out like water.
chapters.zh: 我未曾吃饭就发出叹息； 我唉哼〔的声音〕涌出如水。

chapters.en: For the thing I feared has overtaken me, and what I dreaded has befallen me.
chapters.zh: 因我所恐惧的临到我身， 我所惧怕的迎我而来。

chapters.en: I am not at ease or quiet; I have no rest, for trouble has come.”
chapters.zh: 我不得安逸，不得平静， 也不得安息，却有患难来到。

chapters.en: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:
chapters.zh: 提幔人以利法回答说：

chapters.en: “If one ventures a word with you, will you be wearied? Yet who can keep from speaking?
chapters.zh: 人若想与你说话，你就厌烦吗？ 但谁能忍住不说呢？

chapters.en: Surely you have instructed many, and have strengthened their feeble hands.
chapters.zh: 你素来教导许多的人， 又坚固软弱的手。

chapters.en: Your words have steadied those who stumbled; you have braced the knees that were buckling.
chapters.zh: 你的言语曾扶助那将要跌倒的人； 你又使软弱的膝稳固。

chapters.en: But now trouble has come upon you, and you are weary. It strikes you, and you are dismayed.
chapters.zh: 但现在祸患临到你，你就昏迷， 挨近你，你便惊惶。

chapters.en: Is your reverence not your confidence, and the uprightness of your ways your hope?
chapters.zh: 你的倚靠不是在你敬畏〔上帝〕吗？ 你的盼望不是在你行事纯正吗？

chapters.en:
Consider now, I plead:
Who, being innocent, has ever perished? Or where have the upright been destroyed?
chapters.zh: 请你追想：无辜的人有谁灭亡？ 正直的人在何处剪除？

chapters.en: As I have observed, those who plow iniquity and those who sow trouble reap the same.
chapters.zh: 按我所见，耕罪孽、种毒害的人 都照样收割。

chapters.en: By the breath of God they perish, and by the blast of His anger they are consumed.
chapters.zh: 上帝一出气，他们就灭亡； 上帝一发怒，他们就消没。
