chapters.en: The lion may roar, and the fierce lion may growl, yet the teeth of the young lions are broken.
chapters.zh: 狮子的吼叫和猛狮的声音〔尽都止息〕； 少壮狮子的牙齿也都敲掉。

chapters.en: The old lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
chapters.zh: 老狮子因绝食而死； 母狮之子也都离散。

chapters.en: Now a word came to me secretly; my ears caught a whisper of it.
chapters.zh: 我暗暗地得了默示； 我耳朵也听其细微的声音。

chapters.en: In disquieting visions in the night, when deep sleep falls on men,
chapters.zh: 在思念夜中、异象之间， 世人沉睡的时候，

chapters.en: fear and trembling came over me and made all my bones shudder.
chapters.zh: 恐惧、战兢临到我身， 使我百骨打战。

chapters.en: Then a spirit glided past my face, and the hair on my body bristled.
chapters.zh: 有灵从我面前经过， 我身上的毫毛直立。

chapters.en: It stood still, but I could not discern its appearance; a form loomed before my eyes, and I heard a whispering voice:
chapters.zh: 那灵停住， 我却不能辨其形状； 有影像在我眼前。 我在静默中听见有声音〔说〕：

chapters.en: ‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God, or a man more pure than his Maker?
chapters.zh: 必死的人岂能比上帝公义吗？ 人岂能比造他的主洁净吗？

chapters.en: If God puts no trust in His servants, and He charges His angels with error,
chapters.zh: 主不信靠他的臣仆， 并且指他的使者为愚昧；

chapters.en:
how much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundations are in the dust,
who can be crushed like a moth!
chapters.zh: 何况那住在土房、根基在尘土里、 被蠹虫所毁坏的人呢？

chapters.en: They are smashed to pieces from dawn to dusk; unnoticed, they perish forever.
chapters.zh: 早晚之间，就被毁灭， 永归无有，无人理会。

chapters.en: Are not their tent cords pulled up, so that they die without wisdom?’
chapters.zh: 他帐棚的绳索岂不从中抽出来呢？ 他死，且是无智慧而死。

chapters.en: “Call out if you please, but who will answer? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
chapters.zh: 你且呼求，有谁答应你？ 诸圣者之中，你转向哪一位呢？

chapters.en: For resentment kills a fool, and envy slays the simple.
chapters.zh: 忿怒害死愚妄人； 嫉妒杀死痴迷人。

chapters.en: I have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly his house was cursed.
chapters.zh: 我曾见愚妄人扎下根， 但我忽然咒诅他的住处。

chapters.en: His sons are far from safety, crushed in court without a defender.
chapters.zh: 他的儿女远离稳妥的地步， 在城门口被压，并无人搭救。

chapters.en:
The hungry consume his harvest, taking it even from the thorns,
and the thirsty pant after his wealth.
chapters.zh: 他的庄稼有饥饿的人吃尽了， 就是在荆棘里的也抢去了； 他的财宝有网罗张口吞灭了。

chapters.en: For distress does not spring from the dust, and trouble does not sprout from the ground.
chapters.zh: 祸患原不是从土中出来； 患难也不是从地里发生。

chapters.en: Yet man is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.
chapters.zh: 人生在世必遇患难， 如同火星飞腾。

chapters.en: However, if I were you, I would appeal to God and lay my cause before Him—
chapters.zh: 至于我，我必仰望上帝， 把我的事情托付他。

chapters.en: the One who does great and unsearchable things, wonders without number.
chapters.zh: 他行大事不可测度， 行奇事不可胜数：

chapters.en: He gives rain to the earth and sends water upon the fields.
chapters.zh: 降雨在地上， 赐水于田里；

chapters.en: He sets the lowly on high, so that mourners are lifted to safety.
chapters.zh: 将卑微的安置在高处， 将哀痛的举到稳妥之地；

chapters.en: He thwarts the schemes of the crafty, so that their hands find no success.
chapters.zh: 破坏狡猾人的计谋， 使他们所谋的不得成就。

chapters.en: He catches the wise in their craftiness, and sweeps away the plans of the cunning.
chapters.zh: 他叫有智慧的中了自己的诡计， 使狡诈人的计谋速速灭亡。

chapters.en: They encounter darkness by day and grope at noon as in the night.
chapters.zh: 他们白昼遇见黑暗， 午间摸索如在夜间。

chapters.en: He saves the needy from the sword in their mouth and from the clutches of the powerful.
chapters.zh: 上帝拯救穷乏人 脱离他们口中的刀和强暴人的手。

chapters.en: So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.
chapters.zh: 这样，贫寒的人有指望， 罪孽之辈必塞口无言。

chapters.en: Blessed indeed is the man whom God corrects; so do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.
chapters.zh: 上帝所惩治的人是有福的！ 所以你不可轻看全能者的管教。

chapters.en: For He wounds, but He also binds; He strikes, but His hands also heal.
chapters.zh: 因为他打破，又缠裹； 他击伤，用手医治。

chapters.en: He will rescue you from six calamities; no harm will touch you in seven.
chapters.zh: 你六次遭难，他必救你； 就是七次，灾祸也无法害你。

chapters.en: In famine He will redeem you from death, and in battle from the stroke of the sword.
chapters.zh: 在饥荒中，他必救你脱离死亡； 在争战中，他必救你脱离刀剑的权力。

chapters.en: You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, and will not fear havoc when it comes.
chapters.zh: 你必被隐藏，不受口舌之害； 灾殃临到，你也不惧怕。

chapters.en: You will laugh at destruction and famine, and need not fear the beasts of the earth.
chapters.zh: 你遇见灾害饥馑，就必嬉笑； 地上的野兽，你也不惧怕。

chapters.en: For you will have a covenant with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you.
chapters.zh: 因为你必与田间的石头立约； 田里的野兽也必与你和好。

chapters.en: You will know that your tent is secure, and find nothing amiss when inspecting your home.
chapters.zh: 你必知道你帐棚平安， 要查看你的羊圈，一无所失；

chapters.en: You will know that your offspring will be many, your descendants like the grass of the earth.
chapters.zh: 也必知道你的后裔将来发达， 你的子孙像地上的青草。

chapters.en: You will come to the grave in full vigor, like a sheaf of grain gathered in season.
chapters.zh: 你必寿高年迈才归坟墓， 好像禾捆到时收藏。

chapters.en: Indeed, we have investigated, and it is true! So hear it and know for yourself.”
chapters.zh: 这理，我们已经考察，本是如此。 你须要听，要知道是与自己有益。

chapters.en: Then Job replied:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说：

chapters.en: “If only my grief could be weighed and placed with my calamity on the scales.
chapters.zh: 惟愿我的烦恼称一称， 我一切的灾害放在天平里；

chapters.en: For then it would outweigh the sand of the seas— no wonder my words have been rash.
chapters.zh: 现今都比海沙更重， 所以我的言语急躁。

chapters.en:
For the arrows of the Almighty have pierced me; my spirit drinks in their poison;
the terrors of God are arrayed against me.
chapters.zh: 因全能者的箭射入我身； 其毒，我的灵喝尽了； 上帝的惊吓摆阵攻击我。

chapters.en: Does a wild donkey bray over fresh grass, or an ox low over its fodder?
chapters.zh: 野驴有草岂能叫唤？ 牛有料岂能吼叫？

chapters.en: Is tasteless food eaten without salt, or is there flavor in the white of an egg ?
chapters.zh: 物淡而无盐岂可吃吗？ 蛋青有什么滋味呢？

chapters.en: My soul refuses to touch them; they are loathsome food to me.
chapters.zh: 看为可厌的食物， 我心不肯挨近。

chapters.en: If only my request were granted and God would fulfill my hope:
chapters.zh: 惟愿我得着所求的， 愿上帝赐我所切望的；

chapters.en: that God would be willing to crush me, to unleash His hand and cut me off!
chapters.zh: 就是愿上帝把我压碎， 伸手将我剪除。

chapters.en: It still brings me comfort, and joy through unrelenting pain, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
chapters.zh: 我因没有违弃那圣者的言语， 就仍以此为安慰， 在不止息的痛苦中还可踊跃。

chapters.en: What strength do I have, that I should still hope? What is my future, that I should be patient?
chapters.zh: 我有什么气力使我等候？ 我有什么结局使我忍耐？

chapters.en: Is my strength like that of stone, or my flesh made of bronze?
chapters.zh: 我的气力岂是石头的气力？ 我的肉身岂是铜的呢？

chapters.en: Is there any help within me now that success is driven from me?
chapters.zh: 在我岂不是毫无帮助吗？ 智慧岂不是从我心中赶出净尽吗？

chapters.en: A despairing man should have the kindness of his friend, even if he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
chapters.zh: 那将要灰心、离弃全能者、 不敬畏上帝的人， 他的朋友当以慈爱待他。

chapters.en: But my brothers are as faithless as wadis, as seasonal streams that overflow,
chapters.zh: 我的弟兄诡诈，好像溪水， 又像溪水流干的河道。

chapters.en: darkened because of the ice and the inflow of melting snow,
chapters.zh: 这河因结冰发黑， 有雪藏在其中；

chapters.en: but ceasing in the dry season and vanishing from their channels in the heat.
chapters.zh: 天气渐暖就随时消化， 日头炎热便从原处干涸。

chapters.en: Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go into the wasteland and perish.
chapters.zh: 结伴的客旅〔离弃大道〕， 顺河偏行，到荒野之地死亡。

chapters.en: The caravans of Tema look for water; the travelers of Sheba hope to find it.
chapters.zh: 提玛结伴的客旅瞻望； 示巴同伙的人等候。

chapters.en: They are confounded because they had hoped; their arrival brings disappointment.
chapters.zh: 他们因失了盼望就抱愧， 来到那里便蒙羞。

chapters.en: For now you are of no help; you see terror, and you are afraid.
chapters.zh: 现在你们正是这样， 看见惊吓的事便惧怕。

chapters.en: Have I ever said, ‘Give me something; offer me a bribe from your wealth;
chapters.zh: 我岂说：请你们供给我， 从你们的财物中送礼物给我？

chapters.en: deliver me from the hand of the enemy; redeem me from the grasp of the ruthless’?
chapters.zh: 岂说：拯救我脱离敌人的手吗？ 救赎我脱离强暴人的手吗？

chapters.en: Teach me, and I will be silent. Help me understand how I have erred.
chapters.zh: 请你们教导我，我便不作声； 使我明白在何事上有错。

chapters.en: How painful are honest words! But what does your argument prove?
chapters.zh: 正直的言语力量何其大！ 但你们责备是责备什么呢？

chapters.en: Do you intend to correct my words, and treat as wind my cry of despair?
chapters.zh: 绝望人的讲论既然如风， 你们还想要驳正言语吗？

chapters.en: You would even cast lots for an orphan and barter away your friend.
chapters.zh: 你们想为孤儿拈鬮， 以朋友当货物。

chapters.en: But now, please look at me. Would I lie to your face?
chapters.zh: 现在请你们看看我， 我决不当面说谎。

chapters.en: Reconsider; do not be unjust. Reconsider, for my righteousness is at stake.
chapters.zh: 请你们转意，不要不公； 请再转意，我的事有理。

chapters.en: Is there iniquity on my tongue? Can my mouth not discern malice?
chapters.zh: 我的舌上岂有不义吗？ 我的口里岂不辨奸恶吗？

chapters.en: “Is not man consigned to labor on earth? Are not his days like those of a hired hand?
chapters.zh: 人在世上岂无争战吗？ 他的日子不像雇工人的日子吗？

chapters.en: Like a slave he longs for shade; like a hireling he waits for his wages.
chapters.zh: 像奴仆切慕黑影， 像雇工人盼望工价；

chapters.en: So I am allotted months of futility, and nights of misery are appointed to me.
chapters.zh: 我也照样经过困苦的日月， 夜间的疲乏为我而定。

chapters.en: When I lie down I think: ‘When will I get up?’ But the night drags on, and I toss and turn until dawn.
chapters.zh: 我躺卧的时候便说： 我何时起来，黑夜就过去呢？ 我尽是反来覆去，直到天亮。

chapters.en:
My flesh is clothed with worms and encrusted with dirt;
my skin is cracked and festering.
chapters.zh: 我的肉体以虫子和尘土为衣； 我的皮肤才收了口又重新破裂。

chapters.en: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle; they come to an end without hope.
chapters.zh: 我的日子比梭更快， 都消耗在无指望之中。

chapters.en: Remember that my life is but a breath. My eyes will never again see happiness.
chapters.zh: 求你想念，我的生命不过是一口气； 我的眼睛必不再见福乐。

chapters.en: The eye that beholds me will no longer see me. You will look for me, but I will be no more.
chapters.zh: 观看我的人，他的眼必不再见我； 你的眼目要看我，我却不在了。

chapters.en: As a cloud vanishes and is gone, so he who goes down to Sheol does not come back up.
chapters.zh: 云彩消散而过； 照样，人下阴间也不再上来。

chapters.en: He never returns to his house; his place remembers him no more.
chapters.zh: 他不再回自己的家； 故土也不再认识他。

chapters.en:
Therefore I will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit;
I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
chapters.zh: 我不禁止我口； 我灵愁苦，要发出言语； 我心苦恼，要吐露哀情。

chapters.en: Am I the sea, or the monster of the deep, that You must keep me under guard?
chapters.zh: 我〔对上帝说〕：我岂是洋海， 岂是大鱼，你竟防守我呢？

chapters.en: When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaint,
chapters.zh: 若说：我的床必安慰我， 我的榻必解释我的苦情，

chapters.en: then You frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions,
chapters.zh: 你就用梦惊骇我， 用异象恐吓我，

chapters.en: so that I would prefer strangling and death over my life in this body.
chapters.zh: 甚至我宁肯噎死，宁肯死亡， 胜似留我〔这一身的〕骨头。

chapters.en: I loathe my life! I would not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are but a breath.
chapters.zh: 我厌弃〔性命〕，不愿永活。 你任凭我吧，因我的日子都是虚空。

chapters.en: What is man that You should exalt him, that You should set Your heart upon him,
chapters.zh: 人算什么，你竟看他为大， 将他放在心上？

chapters.en: that You attend to him every morning, and test him every moment?
chapters.zh: 每早鉴察他， 时刻试验他？

chapters.en: Will You never look away from me, or leave me alone to swallow my spittle?
chapters.zh: 你到何时才转眼不看我， 才任凭我咽下唾沫呢？

chapters.en: If I have sinned, what have I done to You, O watcher of mankind? Why have You made me Your target, so that I am a burden to You ?
chapters.zh: 鉴察人的主啊，我若有罪，于你何妨？ 为何以我当你的箭靶子， 使我厌弃自己的性命？

chapters.en: Why do You not pardon my transgression and take away my iniquity? For soon I will lie down in the dust; You will seek me, but I will be no more.”
chapters.zh: 为何不赦免我的过犯， 除掉我的罪孽？ 我现今要躺卧在尘土中； 你要殷勤地寻找我，我却不在了。

chapters.en: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:
chapters.zh: 书亚人比勒达回答说：

chapters.en: “How long will you go on saying such things? The words of your mouth are a blustering wind.
chapters.zh: 这些话你要说到几时？ 口中的言语〔如〕狂风〔要到几时呢〕？

chapters.en: Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty pervert what is right?
chapters.zh: 上帝岂能偏离公平？ 全能者岂能偏离公义？

chapters.en: When your children sinned against Him, He gave them over to their rebellion.
chapters.zh: 或者你的儿女得罪了他； 他使他们受报应。

chapters.en: But if you would earnestly seek God and ask the Almighty for mercy,
chapters.zh: 你若殷勤地寻求上帝， 向全能者恳求；

chapters.en:
if you are pure and upright, even now He will rouse Himself on your behalf
and restore your righteous estate.
chapters.zh: 你若清洁正直， 他必定为你起来， 使你公义的居所兴旺。

chapters.en: Though your beginnings were modest, your latter days will flourish.
chapters.zh: 你起初虽然微小， 终久必甚发达。

chapters.en: Please inquire of past generations and consider the discoveries of their fathers.
chapters.zh: 请你考问前代， 追念他们的列祖所查究的。

chapters.en: For we were born yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are but a shadow.
chapters.zh: 我们不过从昨日才有，一无所知； 我们在世的日子好像影儿。

chapters.en: Will they not teach you and tell you, and speak from their understanding?
chapters.zh: 他们岂不指教你，告诉你， 从心里发出言语来呢？

chapters.en: Does papyrus grow where there is no marsh? Do reeds flourish without water?
chapters.zh: 蒲草没有泥岂能发长？ 芦荻没有水岂能生发？

chapters.en: While the shoots are still uncut, they dry up more quickly than grass.
chapters.zh: 尚青的时候，还没有割下， 比百样的草先枯槁。

chapters.en: Such is the destiny of all who forget God; so the hope of the godless will perish.
chapters.zh: 凡忘记上帝的人，景况也是这样； 不虔敬人的指望要灭没。

chapters.en: His confidence is fragile; his security is in a spider’s web.
chapters.zh: 他所仰赖的必折断； 他所倚靠的是蜘蛛网。

chapters.en: He leans on his web, but it gives way; he holds fast, but it does not endure.
chapters.zh: 他要倚靠房屋，房屋却站立不住； 他要抓住房屋，房屋却不能存留。

chapters.en: He is a well-watered plant in the sunshine, spreading its shoots over the garden.
chapters.zh: 他在日光之下发青， 蔓子爬满了园子；

chapters.en: His roots wrap around the rock heap; he looks for a home among the stones.
chapters.zh: 他的根盘绕〔石〕堆， 扎入石地。

chapters.en: If he is uprooted from his place, it will disown him, saying, ‘I never saw you.’
chapters.zh: 他若从本地被拔出， 那地就不认识他，〔说〕： 我没有见过你。

chapters.en: Surely this is the joy of his way; yet others will spring from the dust.
chapters.zh: 看哪，这就是他道中之乐； 以后必另有人从地而生。

chapters.en: Behold, God does not reject the blameless, nor will He strengthen the hand of evildoers.
chapters.zh: 上帝必不丢弃完全人， 也不扶助邪恶人。

chapters.en: He will yet fill your mouth with laughter, and your lips with a shout of joy.
chapters.zh: 他还要以喜笑充满你的口， 以欢呼充满你的嘴。

chapters.en: Your enemies will be clothed in shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.”
chapters.zh: 恨恶你的要披戴惭愧； 恶人的帐棚必归于无有。

chapters.en: Then Job answered:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说：

chapters.en: “Yes, I know that it is so, but how can a mortal be righteous before God?
chapters.zh: 我真知道是这样； 但人在上帝面前怎能成为义呢？

chapters.en: If one wished to contend with God, he could not answer Him one time out of a thousand.
chapters.zh: 若愿意与他争辩， 千中之一也不能回答。

chapters.en: God is wise in heart and mighty in strength. Who has resisted Him and prospered?
chapters.zh: 他心里有智慧，且大有能力。 谁向上帝刚硬而得亨通呢？

chapters.en: He moves mountains without their knowledge and overturns them in His anger.
chapters.zh: 他发怒，把山翻倒挪移， 山并不知觉。

chapters.en: He shakes the earth from its place, so that its foundations tremble.
chapters.zh: 他使地震动，离其本位， 地的柱子就摇撼。

chapters.en: He commands the sun not to shine; He seals off the stars.
chapters.zh: 他吩咐日头不出来，就不出来， 又封闭众星。

chapters.en: He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea.
chapters.zh: 他独自铺张苍天， 步行在海浪之上。

chapters.en: He is the Maker of the Bear and Orion, of the Pleiades and the constellations of the south.
chapters.zh: 他造北斗、参星、昴星， 并南方的密宫；

chapters.en: He does great things beyond searching out, and wonders without number.
chapters.zh: 他行大事，不可测度， 行奇事，不可胜数。

chapters.en: Were He to pass by me, I would not see Him; were He to move, I would not recognize Him.
chapters.zh: 他从我旁边经过，我却不看见； 他在我面前行走，我倒不知觉。

chapters.en: If He takes away, who can stop Him? Who dares to ask Him, ‘What are You doing?’
chapters.zh: 他夺取，谁能阻挡？ 谁敢问他：你做什么？

chapters.en: God does not restrain His anger; the helpers of Rahab cower beneath Him.
chapters.zh: 上帝必不收回他的怒气； 扶助拉哈伯的，屈身在他以下。

chapters.en: How then can I answer Him or choose my arguments against Him?
chapters.zh: 既是这样，我怎敢回答他， 怎敢选择言语与他〔辩论呢〕？

chapters.en: For even if I were right, I could not answer. I could only beg my Judge for mercy.
chapters.zh: 我虽有义，也不回答他， 只要向那审判我的恳求。

chapters.en: If I summoned Him and He answered me, I do not believe He would listen to my voice.
chapters.zh: 我若呼吁，他应允我； 我仍不信他真听我的声音。

chapters.en: For He would crush me with a tempest and multiply my wounds without cause.
chapters.zh: 他用暴风折断我， 无故地加增我的损伤。

chapters.en: He does not let me catch my breath, but overwhelms me with bitterness.
chapters.zh: 我就是喘一口气，他都不容， 倒使我满心苦恼。

chapters.en: If it is a matter of strength, He is indeed mighty! If it is a matter of justice, who can summon Him ?
chapters.zh: 〔若论〕力量，〔他真有〕能力！ 若论审判，〔他说〕谁能将我传来呢？

chapters.en: Even if I were righteous, my mouth would condemn me; if I were blameless, it would declare me guilty.
chapters.zh: 我虽有义，自己的口要定我为有罪； 我虽完全，我口必显我为弯曲。

chapters.en: Though I am blameless, I have no concern for myself; I despise my own life.
chapters.zh: 我本完全，不顾自己； 我厌恶我的性命。

chapters.en: It is all the same, and so I say, ‘He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.’
chapters.zh: 〔善恶无分〕，都是一样； 所以我说，完全人和恶人，他都灭绝。

chapters.en: When the scourge brings sudden death, He mocks the despair of the innocent.
chapters.zh: 若忽然遭杀害之祸， 他必戏笑无辜的人遇难。

chapters.en:
The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; He blindfolds its judges.
If it is not He, then who is it?
chapters.zh: 世界交在恶人手中； 蒙蔽世界审判官的脸， 若不是他，是谁呢？

chapters.en: My days are swifter than a runner; they flee without seeing good.
chapters.zh: 我的日子比跑信的更快， 急速过去，不见福乐。

chapters.en: They sweep by like boats of papyrus, like an eagle swooping down on its prey.
chapters.zh: 我的日子过去如快船， 如急落抓食的鹰。

chapters.en: If I were to say, ‘I will forget my complaint and change my expression and smile,’
chapters.zh: 我若说：我要忘记我的哀情， 除去我的〔愁容〕，心中畅快；

chapters.en: I would still dread all my sufferings; I know that You will not acquit me.
chapters.zh: 我因愁苦而惧怕， 知道你必不以我为无辜。

chapters.en: Since I am already found guilty, why should I labor in vain?
chapters.zh: 我必被你定为有罪， 我何必徒然劳苦呢？

chapters.en: If I should wash myself with snow and cleanse my hands with lye,
chapters.zh: 我若用雪水洗身， 用碱洁净我的手，

chapters.en: then You would plunge me into the pit, and even my own clothes would despise me.
chapters.zh: 你还要扔我在坑里， 我的衣服都憎恶我。

chapters.en: For He is not a man like me, that I can answer Him, that we can take each other to court.
chapters.zh: 他本不像我是人，使我可以回答他， 又使我们可以同听审判。

chapters.en: Nor is there a mediator between us, to lay his hand upon us both.
chapters.zh: 我们中间没有听讼的人 可以向我们两造按手。

chapters.en: Let Him remove His rod from me, so that His terror will no longer frighten me.
chapters.zh: 愿他把杖离开我， 不使惊惶威吓我。

chapters.en: Then I would speak without fear of Him. But as it is, I am on my own.
chapters.zh: 我就说话，也不惧怕他， 现在我却不是那样。

chapters.en:
“I loathe my own life; I will express my complaint
and speak in the bitterness of my soul.
chapters.zh: 我厌烦我的性命， 必由着自己述说我的哀情； 因心里苦恼，我要说话，

chapters.en:
I will say to God: Do not condemn me!
Let me know why You prosecute me.
chapters.zh: 对上帝说：不要定我有罪， 要指示我，你为何与我争辩？

chapters.en:
Does it please You to oppress me, to reject the work of Your hands
and favor the schemes of the wicked?
chapters.zh: 你手所造的， 你又欺压，又藐视， 却光照恶人的计谋。 这事你以为美吗？

chapters.en: Do You have eyes of flesh? Do You see as man sees?
chapters.zh: 你的眼岂是肉眼？ 你查看岂像人查看吗？

chapters.en: Are Your days like those of a mortal, or Your years like those of a man,
chapters.zh: 你的日子岂像人的日子， 你的年岁岂像人的年岁，

chapters.en: that You should seek my iniquity and search out my sin—
chapters.zh: 就追问我的罪孽， 寻察我的罪过吗？

chapters.en: though You know that I am not guilty, and there is no deliverance from Your hand?
chapters.zh: 其实，你知道我没有罪恶， 并没有能救〔我〕脱离你手的。

chapters.en: Your hands shaped me and altogether formed me. Would You now turn and destroy me?
chapters.zh: 你的手创造我，造就我的四肢百体， 你还要毁灭我。

chapters.en: Please remember that You molded me like clay. Would You now return me to dust?
chapters.zh: 求你记念－制造我如抟泥一般， 你还要使我归于尘土吗？

chapters.en: Did You not pour me out like milk, and curdle me like cheese?
chapters.zh: 你不是倒出我来好像奶， 使我凝结如同奶饼吗？

chapters.en: You clothed me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews.
chapters.zh: 你以皮和肉为衣给我穿上， 用骨与筋把我全体联络。

chapters.en: You have granted me life and loving devotion, and Your care has preserved my spirit.
chapters.zh: 你将生命和慈爱赐给我； 你也眷顾保全我的心灵。

chapters.en: Yet You concealed these things in Your heart, and I know that this was in Your mind:
chapters.zh: 然而，你〔待我的〕这些事早已藏在你心里； 我知道你久有此意。

chapters.en: If I sinned, You would take note, and would not acquit me of my iniquity.
chapters.zh: 我若犯罪，你就察看我， 并不赦免我的罪孽。

chapters.en: If I am guilty, woe to me! And even if I am righteous, I cannot lift my head. I am full of shame and aware of my affliction.
chapters.zh: 我若行恶，便有了祸； 我若为义，也不敢抬头， 正是满心羞愧， 眼见我的苦情。

chapters.en:
Should I hold my head high, You would hunt me like a lion,
and again display Your power against me.
chapters.zh: 我若昂首自得，你就追捕我如狮子， 又在我身上显出奇能。

chapters.en: You produce new witnesses against me and multiply Your anger toward me. Hardships assault me in wave after wave.
chapters.zh: 你重立见证攻击我， 向我加增恼怒， 如军兵更换着攻击我。

chapters.en: Why then did You bring me from the womb? Oh, that I had died, and no eye had seen me!
chapters.zh: 你为何使我出母胎呢？ 不如我当时气绝，无人得见我；

chapters.en: If only I had never come to be, but had been carried from the womb to the grave.
chapters.zh: 这样，就如没有我一般， 一出母胎就被送入坟墓。

chapters.en: Are my days not few? Withdraw from me, that I may have a little comfort,
before I go—never to return— to a land of darkness and gloom,
chapters.zh: 我的日子不是甚少吗？ 求你停手宽容我， 叫我在往而不返之先－ 就是往黑暗和死荫之地以先－ 可以稍得畅快。

chapters.en:
to a land of utter darkness, of deep shadow and disorder,
where even the light is like darkness.”
chapters.zh: 那地甚是幽暗，是死荫混沌〔之地〕； 那里的光好像幽暗。

chapters.en: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:
chapters.zh: 拿玛人琐法回答说：

chapters.en: “Should this stream of words go unanswered and such a speaker be vindicated?
chapters.zh: 这许多的言语岂不该回答吗？ 多嘴多舌的人岂可称为义吗？

chapters.en: Should your babbling put others to silence? Will you scoff without rebuke?
chapters.zh: 你夸大的话岂能使人不作声吗？ 你戏笑的时候岂没有人叫你害羞吗？

chapters.en: You have said, ‘My doctrine is sound, and I am pure in Your sight.’
chapters.zh: 你说：我的道理纯全； 我在你眼前洁净。

chapters.en: But if only God would speak and open His lips against you,
chapters.zh: 惟愿上帝说话； 愿他开口攻击你，

chapters.en: and disclose to you the secrets of wisdom, for true wisdom has two sides. Know then that God exacts from you less than your iniquity deserves.
chapters.zh: 并将智慧的奥祕指示你； 他有诸般的智识。 所以当知道上帝追讨你 比你罪孽该得的还少。

chapters.en: Can you fathom the deep things of God or discover the limits of the Almighty?
chapters.zh: 你考察就能测透上帝吗？ 你岂能尽情测透全能者吗？

chapters.en: They are higher than the heavens—what can you do? They are deeper than Sheol—what can you know?
chapters.zh: 他〔的智慧〕高于天，你还能做什么？ 深于阴间，你还能知道什么？

chapters.en: Their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.
chapters.zh: 其量比地长， 比海宽。

chapters.en: If He comes along to imprison you, or convenes a court, who can stop Him?
chapters.zh: 他若经过，将人拘禁， 招人受审，谁能阻挡他呢？

chapters.en: Surely He knows the deceit of men. If He sees iniquity, does He not take note?
chapters.zh: 他本知道虚妄的人； 人的罪孽，他虽不留意，还是无所不见。

chapters.en: But a witless man can no more become wise than the colt of a wild donkey can be born a man!
chapters.zh: 空虚的人却毫无知识； 人生在世〔好像〕野驴的驹子。

chapters.en: As for you, if you direct your heart and lift up your hands to Him,
chapters.zh: 你若将心安正， 又向主举手；

chapters.en: if you put away the iniquity in your hand, and allow no injustice to dwell in your tents,
chapters.zh: 你手里若有罪孽， 就当远远地除掉， 也不容非义住在你帐棚之中。

chapters.en: then indeed you will lift up your face without blemish; you will stand firm and unafraid.
chapters.zh: 那时，你必仰起脸来毫无斑点； 你也必坚固，无所惧怕。

chapters.en: For you will forget your misery, recalling it only as waters gone by.
chapters.zh: 你必忘记你的苦楚， 就是想起也如流过去的水一样。

chapters.en: Your life will be brighter than noonday; its darkness will be like the morning.
chapters.zh: 你在世的日子要比正午更明， 虽有黑暗仍像早晨。

chapters.en: You will be secure, because there is hope, and you will look around and lie down in safety.
chapters.zh: 你因有指望就必稳固， 也必〔四围〕巡查，坦然安息。

chapters.en: You will lie down without fear, and many will court your favor.
chapters.zh: 你躺卧，无人惊吓， 且有许多人向你求恩。

chapters.en:
But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will elude them;
they will hope for their last breath.”
chapters.zh: 但恶人的眼目必要失明。 他们无路可逃； 他们的指望就是气绝。

chapters.en: Then Job answered:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说：

chapters.en: “Truly then you are the people with whom wisdom itself will die!
chapters.zh: 你们真是子民哪， 你们死亡，智慧也就灭没了。

chapters.en:
But I also have a mind; I am not inferior to you.
Who does not know such things as these?
chapters.zh: 但我也有聪明，与你们一样， 并非不及你们。 你们所说的，谁不知道呢？

chapters.en:
I am a laughingstock to my friends, though I called on God, and He answered.
The righteous and upright man is a laughingstock.
chapters.zh: 我这求告上帝、蒙他应允的人 竟成了朋友所讥笑的； 公义完全人竟受了人的讥笑。

chapters.en: The one at ease scorns misfortune as the fate of those whose feet are slipping.
chapters.zh: 安逸的人心里藐视灾祸； 这灾祸常常等待滑脚的人。

chapters.en:
The tents of robbers are safe, and those who provoke God are secure—
those who carry their god in their hands.
chapters.zh: 强盗的帐棚兴旺， 惹上帝的人稳固， 上帝〔多将财物〕送到他们手中。

chapters.en: But ask the animals, and they will instruct you; ask the birds of the air, and they will tell you.
chapters.zh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你； 又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你；

chapters.en: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you; let the fish of the sea inform you.
chapters.zh: 或与地说话，地必指教你； 海中的鱼也必向你说明。

chapters.en: Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?
chapters.zh: 看这一切， 谁不知道是耶和华的手做成的呢？

chapters.en: The life of every living thing is in His hand, as well as the breath of all mankind.
chapters.zh: 凡活物的生命和人类的气息都在他手中。

chapters.en: Does not the ear test words as the tongue tastes its food?
chapters.zh: 耳朵岂不试验言语， 正如上膛尝食物吗？

chapters.en: Wisdom is found with the elderly, and understanding comes with long life.
chapters.zh: 年老的有智慧； 寿高的有知识。

chapters.en: Wisdom and strength belong to God; counsel and understanding are His.
chapters.zh: 在上帝有智慧和能力； 他有谋略和知识。

chapters.en: What He tears down cannot be rebuilt; the man He imprisons cannot be released.
chapters.zh: 他拆毁的，就不能再建造； 他捆住人，便不得开释。

chapters.en: If He holds back the waters, they dry up, and if He releases them, they overwhelm the land.
chapters.zh: 他把水留住，水便枯干； 他再发出水来，水就翻地。

chapters.en: True wisdom and power belong to Him. The deceived and the deceiver are His.
chapters.zh: 在他有能力和智慧， 被诱惑的与诱惑人的都是属他。

chapters.en: He leads counselors away barefoot and makes fools of judges.
chapters.zh: 他把谋士剥衣掳去， 又使审判官变成愚人。

chapters.en: He loosens the bonds placed by kings and fastens a belt around their waists.
chapters.zh: 他放松君王的绑， 又用带子捆他们的腰。

chapters.en: He leads priests away barefoot and overthrows the established.
chapters.zh: 他把祭司剥衣掳去， 又使有能的人倾败。

chapters.en: He deprives the trusted of speech and takes away the discernment of elders.
chapters.zh: 他废去忠信人的讲论， 又夺去老人的聪明。

chapters.en: He pours out contempt on nobles and disarms the mighty.
chapters.zh: 他使君王蒙羞被辱， 放松有力之人的腰带。

chapters.en: He reveals the deep things of darkness and brings deep shadows into light.
chapters.zh: 他将深奥的事从黑暗中彰显， 使死荫显为光明。

chapters.en: He makes nations great and destroys them; He enlarges nations, then disperses them.
chapters.zh: 他使邦国兴旺而又毁灭； 他使邦国开广而又掳去。

chapters.en: He deprives the earth’s leaders of reason and makes them wander in a trackless wasteland.
chapters.zh: 他将地上民中首领的聪明夺去， 使他们在荒废无路之地漂流；

chapters.en: They grope in the darkness without light; He makes them stagger like drunkards.
chapters.zh: 他们无光，在黑暗中摸索， 又使他们东倒西歪，像醉酒的人一样。

chapters.en: “Indeed, my eyes have seen all this; my ears have heard and understood.
chapters.zh: 这一切，我眼都见过； 我耳都听过，而且明白。

chapters.en: What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.
chapters.zh: 你们所知道的，我也知道， 并非不及你们。

chapters.en: Yet I desire to speak to the Almighty and argue my case before God.
chapters.zh: 我真要对全能者说话； 我愿与上帝理论。

chapters.en: You, however, smear with lies; you are all worthless physicians.
chapters.zh: 你们是编造谎言的， 都是无用的医生。

chapters.en: If only you would remain silent; for that would be your wisdom!
chapters.zh: 惟愿你们全然不作声； 这就算为你们的智慧！

chapters.en: Hear now my argument, and listen to the plea of my lips.
chapters.zh: 请你们听我的辩论， 留心听我口中的分诉。

chapters.en: Will you speak wickedly on God’s behalf or speak deceitfully for Him?
chapters.zh: 你们要为上帝说不义的话吗？ 为他说诡诈的言语吗？

chapters.en: Would you show Him partiality or argue in His defense?
chapters.zh: 你们要为上帝徇情吗？ 要为他争论吗？

chapters.en: Would it be well when He examined you? Could you deceive Him as you would deceive a man?
chapters.zh: 他查出你们来，这岂是好吗？ 人欺哄人，你们也要照样欺哄他吗？

chapters.en: Surely He would rebuke you if you secretly showed partiality.
chapters.zh: 你们若暗中徇情， 他必要责备你们。

chapters.en: Would His majesty not terrify you? Would the dread of Him not fall upon you?
chapters.zh: 他的尊荣岂不叫你们惧怕吗？ 他的惊吓岂不临到你们吗？

chapters.en: Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.
chapters.zh: 你们以为可记念的箴言是炉灰的箴言； 你们以为可靠的坚垒是淤泥的坚垒。

chapters.en: Be silent, and I will speak. Then let come to me what may.
chapters.zh: 你们不要作声，任凭我吧！ 让我说话，无论如何我都承当。

chapters.en: Why do I put myself at risk and take my life in my own hands?
chapters.zh: 我何必把我的肉挂在牙上， 将我的命放在手中。

chapters.en: Though He slay me, I will hope in Him. I will still defend my ways to His face.
chapters.zh: 他必杀我；我虽无指望， 然而我在他面前还要辩明我所行的。

chapters.en: Moreover, this will be my salvation, for no godless man can appear before Him.
chapters.zh: 这要成为我的拯救， 因为不虔诚的人不得到他面前。

chapters.en: Listen carefully to my words; let my declaration ring in your ears.
chapters.zh: 你们要细听我的言语， 使我所辩论的入你们的耳中。

chapters.en: See now, I have prepared my case; I know that I will be vindicated.
chapters.zh: 我已陈明我的案， 知道自己有义。

chapters.en: Can anyone indict me? If so, I will be silent and die.
chapters.zh: 有谁与我争论， 我就情愿缄默不言，气绝而亡。

chapters.en: Only grant these two things to me, so that I need not hide from You:
chapters.zh: 惟有两件不要向我施行， 我就不躲开你的面：

chapters.en: Withdraw Your hand from me, and do not let Your terror frighten me.
chapters.zh: 就是把你的手缩回，远离我身； 又不使你的惊惶威吓我。

chapters.en: Then call me, and I will answer, or let me speak, and You can reply.
chapters.zh: 这样，你呼叫，我就回答； 或是让我说话，你回答我。

chapters.en: How many are my iniquities and sins? Reveal to me my transgression and sin.
chapters.zh: 我的罪孽和罪过有多少呢？ 求你叫我知道我的过犯与罪愆。

chapters.en: Why do You hide Your face and consider me as Your enemy?
chapters.zh: 你为何掩面、 拿我当仇敌呢？

chapters.en: Would You frighten a windblown leaf? Would You chase after dry chaff?
chapters.zh: 你要惊动被风吹的叶子吗？ 要追赶枯干的碎诩吗？

chapters.en: For You record bitter accusations against me and bequeath to me the iniquities of my youth.
chapters.zh: 你按罪状刑罚我， 又使我担当幼年的罪孽；

chapters.en: You put my feet in the stocks and stand watch over all my paths; You set a limit for the soles of my feet.
chapters.zh: 也把我的脚上了木狗， 并窥察我一切的道路， 为我的脚掌划定界限。

chapters.en: So man wastes away like something rotten, like a moth-eaten garment.
chapters.zh: 我已经像灭绝的烂物， 像虫蛀的衣裳。

chapters.en: “Man, who is born of woman, is short of days and full of trouble.
chapters.zh: 人为妇人所生， 日子短少，多有患难；

chapters.en: Like a flower, he comes forth, then withers away; like a fleeting shadow, he does not endure.
chapters.zh: 出来如花，又被割下， 飞去如影，不能存留。

chapters.en: Do You open Your eyes to one like this? Will You bring him into judgment before You?
chapters.zh: 这样的人你岂睁眼看他吗？ 又叫我来受审吗？

chapters.en: Who can bring out clean from unclean? No one!
chapters.zh: 谁能使洁净之物出于污秽之中呢？ 无论谁也不能！

chapters.en: Since his days are determined and the number of his months is with You, and since You have set limits that he cannot exceed,
chapters.zh: 人的日子既然限定， 他的月数在你那里， 你也派定他的界限，使他不能越过，

chapters.en: look away from him and let him rest, so he can enjoy his day as a hired hand.
chapters.zh: 便求你转眼不看他，使他得歇息， 直等他像雇工人完毕他的日子。

chapters.en:
For there is hope for a tree: If it is cut down, it will sprout again,
and its tender shoots will not fail.
chapters.zh: 树若被砍下， 还可指望发芽， 嫩枝生长不息；

chapters.en: If its roots grow old in the ground and its stump dies in the soil,
chapters.zh: 其根虽然衰老在地里， 干也死在土中，

chapters.en: at the scent of water it will bud and put forth twigs like a sapling.
chapters.zh: 及至得了水汽，还要发芽， 又长枝条，像新栽的树一样。

chapters.en: But a man dies and is laid low; he breathes his last, and where is he?
chapters.zh: 但人死亡而消灭； 他气绝，竟在何处呢？

chapters.en: As water disappears from the sea and a river becomes parched and dry,
chapters.zh: 海中的水绝尽， 江河消散干涸。

chapters.en: so a man lies down and does not rise. Until the heavens are no more, he will not be awakened or roused from sleep.
chapters.zh: 人也是如此，躺下不再起来， 等到天没有了，仍不得复醒， 也不得从睡中唤醒。

chapters.en: If only You would hide me in Sheol and conceal me until Your anger has passed! If only You would appoint a time for me and then remember me!
chapters.zh: 惟愿你把我藏在阴间， 存于隐密处，等你的忿怒过去； 愿你为我定了日期，记念我。

chapters.en:
When a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I will wait,
until my renewal comes.
chapters.zh: 人若死了岂能〔再〕活呢？ 我只要在我一切争战的日子， 等我被释放〔注：或译：改变〕的时候来到。

chapters.en: You will call, and I will answer; You will desire the work of Your hands.
chapters.zh: 你呼叫，我便回答； 你手所做的，你必羨慕。

chapters.en: For then You would count my steps, but would not keep track of my sin.
chapters.zh: 但如今你数点我的脚步， 岂不窥察我的罪过吗？

chapters.en: My transgression would be sealed in a bag, and You would cover over my iniquity.
chapters.zh: 我的过犯被你封在囊中， 也缝严了我的罪孽。

chapters.en: But as a mountain erodes and crumbles and a rock is dislodged from its place,
chapters.zh: 山崩变为无有； 磐石挪开原处。

chapters.en:
as water wears away the stones and torrents wash away the soil,
so You destroy a man’s hope.
chapters.zh: 水流消磨石头， 所流溢的洗去地上的尘土； 你也照样灭绝人的指望。

chapters.en: You forever overpower him, and he passes on; You change his countenance and send him away.
chapters.zh: 你攻击人常常得胜，使他去世； 你改变他的容貌，叫他往而不回。

chapters.en: If his sons receive honor, he does not know it; if they are brought low, he is unaware.
chapters.zh: 他儿子得尊荣，他也不知道， 降为卑，他也不觉得。

chapters.en: He feels only the pain of his own body and mourns only for himself.”
chapters.zh: 但知身上疼痛， 心中悲哀。

chapters.en: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:
chapters.zh: 提幔人以利法回答说：

chapters.en: “Does a wise man answer with empty counsel or fill his belly with the hot east wind?
chapters.zh: 智慧人岂可用虚空的知识回答， 用东风充满肚腹呢？

chapters.en: Should he argue with useless words or speeches that serve no purpose?
chapters.zh: 他岂可用无益的话 和无济于事的言语理论呢？

chapters.en: But you even undermine the fear of God and hinder meditation before Him.
chapters.zh: 你是废弃敬畏的意， 在上帝面前阻止敬虔的心。

chapters.en: For your iniquity instructs your mouth, and you choose the language of the crafty.
chapters.zh: 你的罪孽指教你的口； 你选用诡诈人的舌头。

chapters.en: Your own mouth, not mine, condemns you; your own lips testify against you.
chapters.zh: 你自己的口定你有罪，并非是我； 你自己的嘴见证你的不是。

chapters.en: Were you the first man ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills?
chapters.zh: 你岂是头一个被生的人吗？ 你受造在诸山之先吗？

chapters.en: Do you listen in on the council of God or limit wisdom to yourself?
chapters.zh: 你曾听见上帝的密旨吗？ 你还将智慧独自得尽吗？

chapters.en: What do you know that we do not? What do you understand that is not clear to us?
chapters.zh: 你知道什么是我们不知道的呢？ 你明白什么是我们不明白的呢？

chapters.en: Both the gray-haired and the aged are on our side— men much older than your father.
chapters.zh: 我们这里有白发的和年纪老迈的， 比你父亲还老。

chapters.en: Are the consolations of God not enough for you, even words spoken gently to you?
chapters.zh: 上帝用温和的话安慰你， 你以为太小吗？

chapters.en: Why has your heart carried you away, and why do your eyes flash,
chapters.zh: 你的心为何将你逼去？ 你的眼为何冒出火星，

chapters.en: so that you turn your spirit against God and pour such words from your mouth?
chapters.zh: 使你的灵反对上帝， 也任你的口发这言语？

chapters.en: What is man, that he should be pure, or one born of woman, that he should be righteous?
chapters.zh: 人是什么，竟算为洁净呢？ 妇人所生的是什么，竟算为义呢？

chapters.en: If God puts no trust in His holy ones, if even the heavens are not pure in His eyes,
chapters.zh: 上帝不信靠他的众圣者； 在他眼前，天也不洁净，

chapters.en: how much less man, who is vile and corrupt, who drinks injustice like water?
chapters.zh: 何况那污秽可憎、 喝罪孽如水的世人呢！

chapters.en: Listen to me and I will inform you. I will describe what I have seen,
chapters.zh: 我指示你，你要听； 我要述说所看见的，

chapters.en: what was declared by wise men and was not concealed from their fathers,
chapters.zh: 就是智慧人从列祖所受， 传说而不隐瞒的。

chapters.en: to whom alone the land was given when no foreigner passed among them.
chapters.zh: （这地惟独赐给他们， 并没有外人从他们中间经过。）

chapters.en: A wicked man writhes in pain all his days; only a few years are reserved for the ruthless.
chapters.zh: 恶人一生之日劬劳痛苦； 强暴人一生的年数也是如此。

chapters.en: Sounds of terror fill his ears; in his prosperity the destroyer attacks him.
chapters.zh: 惊吓的声音常在他耳中； 在平安时，抢夺的必临到他那里。

chapters.en: He despairs of his return from darkness; he is marked for the sword.
chapters.zh: 他不信自己能从黑暗中转回； 他被刀剑等候。

chapters.en: He wanders about as food for vultures; he knows the day of darkness is at hand.
chapters.zh: 他漂流在外求食，〔说〕：哪里有食物呢？ 他知道黑暗的日子在他手边预备好了。

chapters.en: Distress and anguish terrify him, overwhelming him like a king poised to attack.
chapters.zh: 急难困苦叫他害怕， 而且胜了他，好像君王预备上阵一样。

chapters.en: For he has stretched out his hand against God and has vaunted himself against the Almighty,
chapters.zh: 他伸手攻击上帝， 以骄傲攻击全能者，

chapters.en: rushing headlong at Him with a thick, studded shield.
chapters.zh: 挺〔着〕颈项， 用盾牌的厚凸面向全能者直闯；

chapters.en: Though his face is covered with fat and his waistline bulges with flesh,
chapters.zh: 是因他的脸蒙上脂油， 腰积成肥肉。

chapters.en: he will dwell in ruined cities, in abandoned houses destined to become rubble.
chapters.zh: 他曾住在荒凉城邑， 无人居住、将成乱堆的房屋。

chapters.en: He will no longer be rich; his wealth will not endure. His possessions will not overspread the land.
chapters.zh: 他不得富足，财物不得常存， 产业在地上也不加增。

chapters.en: He will not escape from the darkness; the flame will wither his shoots, and the breath of God’s mouth will carry him away.
chapters.zh: 他不得出离黑暗。 火焰要将他的枝子烧干； 因上帝口中的气，他要灭亡〔注：原文是走去〕。

chapters.en: Let him not deceive himself with trust in emptiness, for emptiness will be his reward.
chapters.zh: 他不用倚靠虚假欺哄自己， 因虚假必成为他的报应。

chapters.en: It will be paid in full before his time, and his branch will not flourish.
chapters.zh: 他的日期未到之先，这事必成就； 他的枝子不得青绿。

chapters.en: He will be like a vine stripped of its unripe grapes, like an olive tree that sheds its blossoms.
chapters.zh: 他必像葡萄树的葡萄，未熟而落； 又像橄榄树的花，一开而谢。

chapters.en: For the company of the godless will be barren, and fire will consume the tents of bribery.
chapters.zh: 原来不敬虔之辈必无生育； 受贿赂之人的帐棚必被火烧。

chapters.en: They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb is pregnant with deceit.”
chapters.zh: 他们所怀的是毒害，所生的是罪孽； 心里所预备的是诡诈。

chapters.en: Then Job answered:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说：

chapters.en: “I have heard many things like these; miserable comforters are you all.
chapters.zh: 这样的话我听了许多； 你们安慰人，反叫人愁烦。

chapters.en: Is there no end to your long-winded speeches? What provokes you to continue testifying?
chapters.zh: 虚空的言语有穷尽吗？ 有什么话惹动你回答呢？

chapters.en: I could also speak like you if you were in my place; I could heap up words against you and shake my head at you.
chapters.zh: 我也能说你们那样的话； 你们若处在我的境遇， 我也会联络言语攻击你们， 又能向你们摇头。

chapters.en: But I would encourage you with my mouth, and the consolation of my lips would bring relief.
chapters.zh: 但我必用口坚固你们， 用嘴消解〔你们的忧愁〕。

chapters.en: Even if I speak, my pain is not relieved, and if I hold back, how will it go away?
chapters.zh: 我虽说话，忧愁仍不得消解； 我虽停住不说，忧愁就离开我吗？

chapters.en: Surely He has now exhausted me; You have devastated all my family.
chapters.zh: 但现在上帝使我困倦， 使亲友远离我，

chapters.en: You have bound me, and it has become a witness; my frailty rises up and testifies against me.
chapters.zh: 又抓住我，作见证〔攻击我〕； 我身体的枯瘦也当面见证我的不是。

chapters.en:
His anger has torn me and opposed me; He gnashes His teeth at me.
My adversary pierces me with His eyes.
chapters.zh: 主发怒撕裂我，逼迫我， 向我切齿； 我的敌人怒目看我。

chapters.en:
They open their mouths against me and strike my cheeks with contempt;
they join together against me.
chapters.zh: 他们向我开口， 打我的脸羞辱我， 聚会攻击我。

chapters.en: God has delivered me to unjust men; He has thrown me to the clutches of the wicked.
chapters.zh: 上帝把我交给不敬虔的人， 把我扔到恶人的手中。

chapters.en: I was at ease, but He shattered me; He seized me by the neck and crushed me. He has set me up as His target;
chapters.zh: 我素来安逸，他折断我， 掐住我的颈项，把我摔碎， 又立我为他的箭靶子。

chapters.en: His archers surround me. He pierces my kidneys without mercy and spills my gall on the ground.
chapters.zh: 他的弓箭手四面围绕我； 他破裂我的肺腑，并不留情， 把我的胆倾倒在地上，

chapters.en: He breaks me with wound upon wound; He rushes me like a mighty warrior.
chapters.zh: 将我破裂又破裂， 如同勇士向我直闯。

chapters.en: I have sewn sackcloth over my skin; I have buried my horn in the dust.
chapters.zh: 我缝麻布在我皮肤上， 把我的角放在尘土中。

chapters.en: My face is red with weeping, and deep shadows ring my eyes;
chapters.zh: 我的脸因哭泣发紫， 在我的眼皮上有死荫。

chapters.en: yet my hands are free of violence and my prayer is pure.
chapters.zh: 我的手中却无强暴； 我的祈祷也是清洁。

chapters.en: O earth, do not cover my blood; may my cry for help never be laid to rest.
chapters.zh: 地啊，不要遮盖我的血！ 不要〔阻挡〕我的哀求！

chapters.en: Even now my witness is in heaven, and my advocate is on high.
chapters.zh: 现今，在天有我的见证， 在上有我的中保。

chapters.en: My friends are my scoffers as my eyes pour out tears to God.
chapters.zh: 我的朋友讥诮我， 我却向上帝眼泪汪汪。

chapters.en: Oh, that a man might plead with God as he pleads with his neighbor!
chapters.zh: 愿人得与上帝辩白， 如同人与朋友辩白一样；

chapters.en: For when only a few years are past I will go the way of no return.
chapters.zh: 因为再过几年， 我必走那往而不返之路。

chapters.en: “My spirit is broken; my days are extinguished; the grave awaits me.
chapters.zh: 我的心灵消耗，我的日子灭尽； 坟墓为我〔预备〕好了。

chapters.en: Surely mockers surround me, and my eyes must gaze at their rebellion.
chapters.zh: 真有戏笑我的在我这里， 我眼常见他们惹动我。

chapters.en: Give me, I pray, the pledge You demand. Who else will be my guarantor?
chapters.zh: 愿主拿凭据给我，自己为我作保。 〔在你以外〕谁肯与我击掌呢？

chapters.en: You have closed their minds to understanding; therefore You will not exalt them.
chapters.zh: 因你使他们心不明理， 所以你必不高举他们。

chapters.en: If a man denounces his friends for a price, the eyes of his children will fail.
chapters.zh: 控告他的朋友、以朋友为可抢夺的， 连他儿女的眼睛也要失明。

chapters.en: He has made me a byword among the people, a man in whose face they spit.
chapters.zh: 上帝使我作了民中的笑谈； 他们也吐唾沫在我脸上。

chapters.en: My eyes have grown dim with grief, and my whole body is but a shadow.
chapters.zh: 我的眼睛因忧愁昏花； 我的百体好像影儿。

chapters.en: The upright are appalled at this, and the innocent are stirred against the godless.
chapters.zh: 正直人因此必惊奇； 无辜的人要兴起攻击不敬虔之辈。

chapters.en: Yet a righteous one holds to his way, and the one with clean hands grows stronger.
chapters.zh: 然而，义人要持守所行的道； 手洁的人要力上加力。

chapters.en: But come back and try again, all of you. For I will not find a wise man among you.
chapters.zh: 至于你们众人，可以再来〔辩论〕吧！ 你们中间，我找不着一个智慧人。

chapters.en: My days have passed; my plans are broken off— even the desires of my heart.
chapters.zh: 我的日子已经过了； 我的谋算、我心所想望的已经断绝。

chapters.en: They have turned night into day, making light seem near in the face of darkness.
chapters.zh: 他们以黑夜为白昼， 〔说〕：亮光近乎黑暗。

chapters.en: If I look for Sheol as my home, if I spread out my bed in darkness,
chapters.zh: 我若盼望阴间为我的房屋， 若下榻在黑暗中，

chapters.en: and say to corruption, ‘You are my father,’ and to the worm, ‘My mother,’ or ‘My sister,’
chapters.zh: 若对朽坏说：你是我的父； 对虫说：你是我的母亲姊妹；

chapters.en: where then is my hope? Who can see any hope for me?
chapters.zh: 这样，我的指望在哪里呢？ 我所指望的谁能看见呢？

chapters.en: Will it go down to the gates of Sheol? Will we go down together into the dust?”
chapters.zh: 等到安息在尘土中， 这指望必下到阴间的门闩那里了。

chapters.en: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:
chapters.zh: 书亚人比勒达回答说：

chapters.en: “How long until you end these speeches? Show some sense, and then we can talk.
chapters.zh: 你寻索言语要到几时呢？ 你可以揣摩思想，然后我们就说话。

chapters.en: Why are we regarded as cattle, as stupid in your sight?
chapters.zh: 我们为何算为畜生， 在你眼中看作污秽呢？

chapters.en:
You who tear yourself in anger— should the earth be forsaken on your account,
or the rocks be moved from their place?
chapters.zh: 你这恼怒将自己撕裂的， 难道大地为你见弃、 磐石挪开原处吗？

chapters.en: Indeed, the lamp of the wicked is extinguished; the flame of his fire does not glow.
chapters.zh: 恶人的亮光必要熄灭； 他的火焰必不照耀。

chapters.en: The light in his tent grows dark, and the lamp beside him goes out.
chapters.zh: 他帐棚中的亮光要变为黑暗； 他以上的灯也必熄灭。

chapters.en: His vigorous stride is shortened, and his own schemes trip him up.
chapters.zh: 他坚强的脚步必见狭窄； 自己的计谋必将他绊倒。

chapters.en: For his own feet lead him into a net, and he wanders into its mesh.
chapters.zh: 因为他被自己的脚陷入网中， 走在缠人的网罗上。

chapters.en: A trap seizes his heel; a snare grips him.
chapters.zh: 圈套必抓住他的脚跟； 机关必擒获他。

chapters.en: A noose is hidden in the ground, and a trap lies in his path.
chapters.zh: 活扣为他藏在土内； 羁绊为他藏在路上。

chapters.en: Terrors frighten him on every side and harass his every step.
chapters.zh: 四面的惊吓要使他害怕， 并且追赶他的脚跟。

chapters.en: His strength is depleted, and calamity is ready at his side.
chapters.zh: 他的力量必因饥饿衰败； 祸患要在他旁边等候。

chapters.en: It devours patches of his skin; the firstborn of death devours his limbs.
chapters.zh: 他本身的肢体要被吞吃； 死亡的长子要吞吃他的肢体。

chapters.en: He is torn from the shelter of his tent and is marched off to the king of terrors.
chapters.zh: 他要从所倚靠的帐棚被拔出来， 带到惊吓的王那里。

chapters.en: Fire resides in his tent; burning sulfur rains down on his dwelling.
chapters.zh: 不属他的必住在他的帐棚里； 硫磺必撒在他所住之处。

chapters.en: The roots beneath him dry up, and the branches above him wither away.
chapters.zh: 下边，他的根本要枯干； 上边，他的枝子要剪除。

chapters.en: The memory of him perishes from the earth, and he has no name in the land.
chapters.zh: 他的记念在地上必然灭亡； 他的名字在街上也不存留。

chapters.en: He is driven from light into darkness and is chased from the inhabited world.
chapters.zh: 他必从光明中被撵到黑暗里， 必被赶出世界。

chapters.en: He has no offspring or posterity among his people, no survivor where he once lived.
chapters.zh: 在本民中必无子无孙； 在寄居之地也无一人存留。

chapters.en: Those in the west are appalled at his fate, while those in the east tremble in horror.
chapters.zh: 以后来的要惊奇他的日子， 好像以前去的受了惊骇。

chapters.en: Surely such is the dwelling of the wicked and the place of one who does not know God.”
chapters.zh: 不义之人的住处总是这样； 此乃不认识上帝之人的地步。

chapters.en: Then Job answered:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说：

chapters.en: “How long will you torment me and crush me with your words?
chapters.zh: 你们搅扰我的心， 用言语压碎我要到几时呢？

chapters.en: Ten times now you have reproached me; you shamelessly mistreat me.
chapters.zh: 你们这十次羞辱我； 你们苦待我也不以为耻。

chapters.en: Even if I have truly gone astray, my error concerns me alone.
chapters.zh: 果真我有错， 这错乃是在我。

chapters.en: If indeed you would exalt yourselves above me and use my disgrace against me,
chapters.zh: 你们果然要向我夸大， 以我的羞辱为证指责我，

chapters.en: then understand that it is God who has wronged me and drawn His net around me.
chapters.zh: 就该知道是上帝倾覆我， 用网罗围绕我。

chapters.en: Though I cry out, ‘Violence!’ I get no response; though I call for help, there is no justice.
chapters.zh: 我因委曲呼叫，却不蒙应允； 我呼求，却不得公断。

chapters.en: He has blocked my way so I cannot pass; He has veiled my paths with darkness.
chapters.zh: 上帝用篱笆拦住我的道路，使我不得经过； 又使我的路径黑暗。

chapters.en: He has stripped me of my honor and removed the crown from my head.
chapters.zh: 他剥去我的荣光， 摘去我头上的冠冕。

chapters.en: He tears me down on every side until I am gone; He uproots my hope like a tree.
chapters.zh: 他在四围攻击我，我便归于死亡， 将我的指望如树拔出来。

chapters.en: His anger burns against me, and He counts me among His enemies.
chapters.zh: 他的忿怒向我发作， 以我为敌人。

chapters.en:
His troops advance together; they construct a ramp against me
and encamp around my tent.
chapters.zh: 他的军旅一齐上来， 修筑战路攻击我， 在我帐棚的四围安营。

chapters.en: He has removed my brothers from me; my acquaintances have abandoned me.
chapters.zh: 他把我的弟兄隔在远处， 使我所认识的全然与我生疏。

chapters.en: My kinsmen have failed me, and my friends have forgotten me.
chapters.zh: 我的亲戚与我断绝； 我的密友都忘记我。

chapters.en: My guests and maidservants count me as a stranger; I am a foreigner in their sight.
chapters.zh: 在我家寄居的， 和我的使女都以我为外人； 我在他们眼中看为外邦人。

chapters.en: I call for my servant, but he does not answer, though I implore him with my own mouth.
chapters.zh: 我呼唤仆人， 虽用口求他，他还是不回答。

chapters.en: My breath is repulsive to my wife, and I am loathsome to my own family.
chapters.zh: 我口的气味，我妻子厌恶； 我的恳求，我同胞也憎嫌。

chapters.en: Even little boys scorn me; when I appear, they deride me.
chapters.zh: 连小孩子也藐视我； 我若起来，他们都嘲笑我。

chapters.en: All my best friends despise me, and those I love have turned against me.
chapters.zh: 我的密友都憎恶我； 我平日所爱的人向我翻脸。

chapters.en: My skin and flesh cling to my bones; I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
chapters.zh: 我的皮肉紧贴骨头； 我只剩牙皮逃脱了。

chapters.en: Have pity on me, my friends, have pity, for the hand of God has struck me.
chapters.zh: 我朋友啊，可怜我！可怜我！ 因为上帝的手攻击我。

chapters.en: Why do you persecute me as God does? Will you never get enough of my flesh?
chapters.zh: 你们为什么仿佛上帝逼迫我， 吃我的肉还以为不足呢？

chapters.en: I wish that my words were recorded and inscribed in a book,
chapters.zh: 惟愿我的言语现在写上， 都记录在书上；

chapters.en: by an iron stylus on lead, or chiseled in stone forever.
chapters.zh: 用铁笔镌刻， 用铅灌在磐石上，直存到永远。

chapters.en: But I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end He will stand upon the earth.
chapters.zh: 我知道我的救赎主活着， 末了必站立在地上。

chapters.en: Even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God.
chapters.zh: 我这皮肉灭绝之后， 我必在肉体之外得见上帝。

chapters.en:
I will see Him for myself; my eyes will behold Him, and not as a stranger.
How my heart yearns within me!
chapters.zh: 我自己要见他， 亲眼要看他，并不像外人。 我的心肠在我里面消灭了！

chapters.en: If you say, ‘Let us persecute him, since the root of the matter lies with him, ’
chapters.zh: 你们若说：我们逼迫他要何等地重呢？ 〔惹〕事的根乃在乎他；

chapters.en:
then you should fear the sword yourselves, because wrath brings punishment by the sword,
so that you may know there is a judgment.”
chapters.zh: 你们就当惧怕刀剑； 因为忿怒〔惹动〕刀剑的刑罚， 使你们知道有报应〔注：原文是审判〕。

chapters.en: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied:
chapters.zh: 拿玛人琐法回答说：

chapters.en: “So my anxious thoughts compel me to answer, because of the turmoil within me.
chapters.zh: 我心中急躁， 所以我的思念叫我回答。

chapters.en: I have heard a rebuke that insults me, and my understanding prompts a reply.
chapters.zh: 我已听见那羞辱我，责备我的话； 我的悟性叫我回答。

chapters.en: Do you not know that from antiquity, since man was placed on the earth,
chapters.zh: 你岂不知亘古以来， 自从人生在地，

chapters.en: the triumph of the wicked has been brief and the joy of the godless momentary?
chapters.zh: 恶人夸胜是暂时的， 不敬虔人的喜乐不过转眼之间吗？

chapters.en: Though his arrogance reaches the heavens, and his head touches the clouds,
chapters.zh: 他的尊荣虽达到天上， 头虽顶到云中，

chapters.en: he will perish forever, like his own dung; those who had seen him will ask, ‘Where is he?’
chapters.zh: 他终必灭亡，像自己的粪一样； 素来见他的人要说：他在哪里呢？

chapters.en: He will fly away like a dream, never to be found; he will be chased away like a vision in the night.
chapters.zh: 他必飞去如梦，不再寻见， 速被赶去，如夜间的异象。

chapters.en: The eye that saw him will see him no more, and his place will no longer behold him.
chapters.zh: 亲眼见过他的，必不再见他； 他的本处也再见不着他。

chapters.en: His sons will seek the favor of the poor, for his own hands must return his wealth.
chapters.zh: 他的儿女要求穷人的恩； 他的手要赔还〔不义〕之财。

chapters.en: The youthful vigor that fills his bones will lie down with him in the dust.
chapters.zh: 他的骨头虽然有青年〔之力〕， 却要和他一同躺卧在尘土中。

chapters.en: Though evil is sweet in his mouth and he conceals it under his tongue,
chapters.zh: 他口内虽以恶为甘甜， 藏在舌头底下，

chapters.en: though he cannot bear to let it go and keeps it in his mouth,
chapters.zh: 爱恋不舍，含在口中；

chapters.en: yet in his stomach his food sours into the venom of cobras within him.
chapters.zh: 他的食物在肚里却要化为酸， 在他里面成为虺蛇的恶毒。

chapters.en: He swallows wealth but vomits it out; God will force it from his stomach.
chapters.zh: 他吞了财宝，还要吐出； 上帝要从他腹中掏出来。

chapters.en: He will suck the poison of cobras; the fangs of a viper will kill him.
chapters.zh: 他必吸饮虺蛇的毒气； 蝮蛇的舌头也必杀他。

chapters.en: He will not enjoy the streams, the rivers flowing with honey and cream.
chapters.zh: 流奶与蜜之河， 他不得再见。

chapters.en: He must return the fruit of his labor without consuming it; he cannot enjoy the profits of his trading.
chapters.zh: 他劳碌得来的要赔还，不得享用〔注：原文是吞下〕； 不能照所得的财货欢乐。

chapters.en: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor; he has seized houses he did not build.
chapters.zh: 他欺压穷人，且又离弃； 强取非自己所盖的房屋〔注：或译：强取房屋不得再建造〕。

chapters.en: Because his appetite is never satisfied, he cannot escape with his treasure.
chapters.zh: 他因贪而无厌， 所喜悦的连一样也不能保守。

chapters.en: Nothing is left for him to consume; thus his prosperity will not endure.
chapters.zh: 其余的没有一样他不吞灭， 所以他的福乐不能长久。

chapters.en: In the midst of his plenty, he will be distressed; the full force of misery will come upon him.
chapters.zh: 他在满足有余的时候，必到狭窄的地步； 凡受苦楚的人都必加手在他身上。

chapters.en:
When he has filled his stomach, God will vent His fury upon him,
raining it down on him as he eats.
chapters.zh: 他正要充满肚腹的时候， 上帝必将猛烈的忿怒降在他身上； 正在他吃饭的时候， 要将这忿怒像雨降在他身上。

chapters.en: Though he flees from an iron weapon, a bronze-tipped arrow will pierce him.
chapters.zh: 他要躲避铁器； 铜弓〔的箭〕要将他射透。

chapters.en:
It is drawn out of his back, the gleaming point from his liver.
Terrors come over him.
chapters.zh: 他把箭一抽，就从他身上出来； 发光的箭头从他胆中出来， 有惊惶临在他身上。

chapters.en:
Total darkness is reserved for his treasures. A fire unfanned will consume him
and devour what is left in his tent.
chapters.zh: 他的财宝归于黑暗； 〔人〕所不吹的火要把他烧灭， 要把他帐棚中所剩下的烧毁。

chapters.en: The heavens will expose his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.
chapters.zh: 天要显明他的罪孽； 地要兴起攻击他。

chapters.en: The possessions of his house will be removed, flowing away on the day of God’s wrath.
chapters.zh: 他的家产必然过去； 上帝发怒的日子，〔他的货物〕都要消灭。

chapters.en: This is the wicked man’s portion from God, the inheritance God has appointed him.”
chapters.zh: 这是恶人从上帝所得的分， 是上帝为他所定的产业。

chapters.en: Then Job answered:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说：

chapters.en: “Listen carefully to my words; let this be your consolation to me.
chapters.zh: 你们要细听我的言语， 就算是你们安慰我。

chapters.en: Bear with me while I speak; then, after I have spoken, you may go on mocking.
chapters.zh: 请宽容我，我又要说话； 说了以后，任凭你们嗤笑吧！

chapters.en: Is my complaint against a man? Then why should I not be impatient?
chapters.zh: 我岂是向人诉冤？ 为何不焦急呢？

chapters.en: Look at me and be appalled; put your hand over your mouth.
chapters.zh: 你们要看着我而惊奇， 用手捂口。

chapters.en: When I remember, terror takes hold, and my body trembles in horror.
chapters.zh: 我每逢思想，心就惊惶， 浑身战兢。

chapters.en: Why do the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power?
chapters.zh: 恶人为何存活， 享大寿数，势力强盛呢？

chapters.en: Their descendants are established around them, and their offspring before their eyes.
chapters.zh: 他们眼见儿孙， 和他们一同坚立。

chapters.en: Their homes are safe from fear; no rod of punishment from God is upon them.
chapters.zh: 他们的家宅平安无惧； 上帝的杖也不加在他们身上。

chapters.en: Their bulls breed without fail; their cows bear calves and do not miscarry.
chapters.zh: 他们的公牛孳生而不断绝； 母牛下犊而不掉胎。

chapters.en: They send forth their little ones like a flock; their children skip about,
chapters.zh: 他们打发小孩子出去，〔多〕如羊群； 他们的儿女踊跃跳舞。

chapters.en: singing to the tambourine and lyre and making merry at the sound of the flute.
chapters.zh: 他们随着琴鼓歌唱， 又因箫声欢喜。

chapters.en: They spend their days in prosperity and go down to Sheol in peace.
chapters.zh: 他们度日诸事亨通， 转眼下入阴间。

chapters.en: Yet they say to God: ‘Leave us alone! For we have no desire to know Your ways.
chapters.zh: 他们对上帝说：离开我们吧！ 我们不愿晓得你的道。

chapters.en: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him, and what would we gain if we pray to Him?’
chapters.zh: 全能者是谁，我们何必事奉他呢？ 求告他有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: Still, their prosperity is not in their own hands, so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.
chapters.zh: 看哪，他们亨通不在乎自己； 恶人所谋定的离我好远。

chapters.en:
How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? Does disaster come upon them?
Does God, in His anger, apportion destruction?
chapters.zh: 恶人的灯何尝熄灭？ 患难何尝临到他们呢？ 上帝何尝发怒，〔向他们〕分散灾祸呢？

chapters.en: Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm?
chapters.zh: 他们何尝像风前的碎诩， 如暴风刮去的糠秕呢？

chapters.en: It is said that God lays up one’s punishment for his children. Let God repay the man himself, so he will know it.
chapters.zh: 〔你们说〕：上帝为恶人的儿女积蓄罪孽； 〔我说〕：不如本人受报，好使他亲自知道。

chapters.en: Let his eyes see his own destruction; let him drink for himself the wrath of the Almighty.
chapters.zh: 愿他亲眼看见自己败亡， 亲自饮全能者的忿怒。

chapters.en: For what does he care about his household after him, when the number of his months has run out?
chapters.zh: 他的岁月既尽， 他还顾他本家吗？

chapters.en: Can anyone teach knowledge to God, since He judges those on high?
chapters.zh: 上帝既审判那在高位的， 谁能将知识教训他呢？

chapters.en: One man dies full of vigor, completely secure and at ease.
chapters.zh: 有人至死身体强壮， 尽得平靖安逸；

chapters.en: His body is well nourished, and his bones are rich with marrow.
chapters.zh: 他的奶桶充满， 他的骨髓滋润。

chapters.en: Yet another man dies in the bitterness of his soul, having never tasted prosperity.
chapters.zh: 有人至死心中痛苦， 终身未尝福乐的滋味；

chapters.en: But together they lie down in the dust, and worms cover them both.
chapters.zh: 他们一样躺卧在尘土中， 都被虫子遮盖。

chapters.en: Behold, I know your thoughts full well, the schemes by which you would wrong me.
chapters.zh: 我知道你们的意思， 并诬害我的计谋。

chapters.en: For you say, ‘Where now is the nobleman’s house, and where are the tents in which the wicked dwell?’
chapters.zh: 你们说：霸者的房屋在哪里？ 恶人住过的帐棚在哪里？

chapters.en: Have you never asked those who travel the roads? Do you not accept their reports?
chapters.zh: 你们岂没有询问过路的人吗？ 不知道他们所引的证据吗？

chapters.en: Indeed, the evil man is spared from the day of calamity, delivered from the day of wrath.
chapters.zh: 就是恶人在祸患的日子得存留， 在发怒的日子得逃脱。

chapters.en: Who denounces his behavior to his face? Who repays him for what he has done?
chapters.zh: 他所行的，有谁当面给他说明？ 他所做的，有谁报应他呢？

chapters.en: He is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.
chapters.zh: 然而他要被抬到茔地； 并有人看守坟墓。

chapters.en:
The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows behind him,
and those before him are without number.
chapters.zh: 他要以谷中的土块为甘甜； 在他以先去的无数， 在他以后去的更多。

chapters.en: So how can you comfort me with empty words? For your answers remain full of falsehood.”
chapters.zh: 你们对答的话中既都错谬， 怎么徒然安慰我呢？

chapters.en: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:
chapters.zh: 提幔人以利法回答说：

chapters.en: “Can a man be of use to God? Can even a wise man benefit Him?
chapters.zh: 人岂能使上帝有益呢？ 智慧人但能有益于己。

chapters.en: Does it delight the Almighty that you are righteous? Does He profit if your ways are blameless?
chapters.zh: 你为人公义，岂叫全能者喜悦呢？ 你行为完全，岂能使他得利呢？

chapters.en: Is it for your reverence that He rebukes you and enters into judgment against you?
chapters.zh: 岂是因你敬畏他 就责备你、审判你吗？

chapters.en: Is not your wickedness great? Are not your iniquities endless?
chapters.zh: 你的罪恶岂不是大吗？ 你的罪孽也没有穷尽；

chapters.en: For you needlessly demanded security from your brothers and deprived the naked of their clothing.
chapters.zh: 因你无故强取弟兄的物为当头， 剥去贫寒人的衣服。

chapters.en: You gave no water to the weary and withheld food from the famished,
chapters.zh: 困乏的人，你没有给他水喝； 饥饿的人，你没有给他食物。

chapters.en: while the land belonged to a mighty man, and a man of honor lived on it.
chapters.zh: 有能力的人就得地土； 尊贵的人也住在其中。

chapters.en: You sent widows away empty-handed, and the strength of the fatherless was crushed.
chapters.zh: 你打发寡妇空手回去， 折断孤儿的膀臂。

chapters.en: Therefore snares surround you, and sudden peril terrifies you;
chapters.zh: 因此，有网罗环绕你， 有恐惧忽然使你惊惶；

chapters.en: it is so dark you cannot see, and a flood of water covers you.
chapters.zh: 或有黑暗蒙蔽你， 并有洪水淹没你。

chapters.en: Is not God as high as the heavens? Look at the highest stars, how lofty they are!
chapters.zh: 上帝岂不是在高天吗？ 你看星宿何其高呢！

chapters.en: Yet you say: ‘What does God know? Does He judge through thick darkness?
chapters.zh: 你说：上帝知道什么？ 他岂能看透幽暗施行审判呢？

chapters.en: Thick clouds veil Him so He does not see us as He traverses the vault of heaven. ’
chapters.zh: 密云将他遮盖，使他不能看见； 他周游穹苍。

chapters.en: Will you stay on the ancient path that wicked men have trod?
chapters.zh: 你要依从上古的道吗？ 这道是恶人所行的。

chapters.en: They were snatched away before their time, and their foundations were swept away by a flood.
chapters.zh: 他们未到死期，忽然除灭； 根基毁坏，好像被江河冲去。

chapters.en: They said to God, ‘Depart from us. What can the Almighty do to us?’
chapters.zh: 他们向上帝说：离开我们吧！ 又〔说〕：全能者能把我们怎么样呢？

chapters.en: But it was He who filled their houses with good things; so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.
chapters.zh: 哪知上帝以美物充满他们的房屋； 但恶人所谋定的离我好远。

chapters.en: The righteous see it and are glad; the innocent mock them:
chapters.zh: 义人看见他们的〔结局〕就欢喜； 无辜的人嗤笑他们，

chapters.en: ‘Surely our foes are destroyed, and fire has consumed their excess.’
chapters.zh: 说：那起来攻击我们的果然被剪除， 其余的都被火烧灭。

chapters.en: Reconcile now and be at peace with Him; thereby good will come to you.
chapters.zh: 你要认识上帝，就得平安； 福气也必临到你。

chapters.en: Receive instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart.
chapters.zh: 你当领受他口中的教训， 将他的言语存在心里。

chapters.en: If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored. If you remove injustice from your tents
chapters.zh: 你若归向全能者，从你帐棚中远除不义， 就必得建立。

chapters.en: and consign your gold to the dust and the gold of Ophir to the stones of the ravines,
chapters.zh: 要将〔你的〕珍宝丢在尘土里， 将俄斐的〔黄金〕丢在溪河石头之间；

chapters.en: then the Almighty will be your gold and the finest silver for you.
chapters.zh: 全能者就必为你的珍宝， 作你的宝银。

chapters.en: Surely then you will delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
chapters.zh: 你就要以全能者为喜乐， 向上帝仰起脸来。

chapters.en: You will pray to Him, and He will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.
chapters.zh: 你要祷告他，他就听你； 你也要还你的愿。

chapters.en: Your decisions will be carried out, and light will shine on your ways.
chapters.zh: 你定意要做何事，必然给你成就； 亮光也必照耀你的路。

chapters.en: When men are brought low and you say, ‘Lift them up!’ then He will save the lowly.
chapters.zh: 人使〔你〕降卑，你仍可说：〔必得〕高升； 谦卑的人，上帝必然拯救。

chapters.en: He will deliver even one who is not innocent, rescuing him through the cleanness of your hands.”
chapters.zh: 人非无辜，上帝且要搭救他； 他因你手中清洁，必蒙拯救。

chapters.en: Then Job answered:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说：

chapters.en: “Even today my complaint is bitter. His hand is heavy despite my groaning.
chapters.zh: 如今我的哀告还算为悖逆； 我的责罚比我的唉哼还重。

chapters.en: If only I knew where to find Him, so that I could go to His seat.
chapters.zh: 惟愿我能知道在哪里可以寻见上帝， 能到他的台前，

chapters.en: I would plead my case before Him and fill my mouth with arguments.
chapters.zh: 我就在他面前将我的案件陈明， 满口辩白。

chapters.en: I would learn how He would answer, and consider what He would say.
chapters.zh: 我必知道他回答我的言语， 明白他向我所说的话。

chapters.en: Would He contend with me in His great power? No, He would certainly take note of me.
chapters.zh: 他岂用大能与我争辩吗？ 必不这样！他必理会我。

chapters.en: Then an upright man could reason with Him, and I would be delivered forever from my Judge.
chapters.zh: 在他那里正直人可以与他辩论； 这样，我必永远脱离那审判我的。

chapters.en: If I go east, He is not there, and if I go west, I cannot find Him.
chapters.zh: 只是，我往前行，他不〔在那里〕， 往后退，也不能见他。

chapters.en: When He is at work in the north, I cannot behold Him; when He turns to the south, I cannot see Him.
chapters.zh: 他在左边行事，我却不能看见， 在右边隐藏，我也不能见他。

chapters.en: Yet He knows the way I have taken; when He has tested me, I will come forth as gold.
chapters.zh: 然而他知道我所行的路； 他试炼我之后，我必如精金。

chapters.en: My feet have followed in His tracks; I have kept His way without turning aside.
chapters.zh: 我脚追随他的步履； 我谨守他的道，并不偏离。

chapters.en:
I have not departed from the command of His lips; I have treasured the words of His mouth
more than my daily bread.
chapters.zh: 他嘴唇的命令，我未曾背弃； 我看重他口中的言语，过于我需用的饮食。

chapters.en: But He is unchangeable, and who can oppose Him? He does what He desires.
chapters.zh: 只是他〔心志〕已定，谁能使他转意呢？ 他心里所愿的，就行出来。

chapters.en: For He carries out His decree against me, and He has many such plans.
chapters.zh: 他向我所定的，就必做成； 这类的事他还有许多。

chapters.en: Therefore I am terrified in His presence; when I consider this, I fear Him.
chapters.zh: 所以我在他面前惊惶； 我思念〔这事〕便惧怕他。

chapters.en: God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me.
chapters.zh: 上帝使我丧胆； 全能者使我惊惶。

chapters.en: Yet I am not silenced by the darkness, by the thick darkness that covers my face.
chapters.zh: 我的恐惧不是因为黑暗， 也不是因为幽暗蒙蔽我的脸。

chapters.en: “Why does the Almighty not reserve times for judgment? Why may those who know Him never see His days?
chapters.zh: 全能者既定期〔罚恶〕， 为何不使认识他的人看见那日子呢？

chapters.en: Men move boundary stones; they pasture stolen flocks.
chapters.zh: 有人挪移地界， 抢夺群畜而牧养。

chapters.en: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless and take the widow’s ox in pledge.
chapters.zh: 他们拉去孤儿的驴， 强取寡妇的牛为当头。

chapters.en: They push the needy off the road and force all the poor of the land into hiding.
chapters.zh: 他们使穷人离开正道； 世上的贫民尽都隐藏。

chapters.en:
Indeed, like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go to work foraging for food;
the wasteland is food for their children.
chapters.zh: 这些贫穷人如同野驴出到旷野，殷勤寻找食物； 他们〔靠着〕野地给儿女糊口，

chapters.en: They gather fodder in the fields and glean the vineyards of the wicked.
chapters.zh: 收割〔别人〕田间的禾稼， 摘取恶人余剩的葡萄，

chapters.en: Without clothing, they spend the night naked; they have no covering against the cold.
chapters.zh: 终夜赤身无衣， 天气寒冷毫无遮盖，

chapters.en: Drenched by mountain rains, they huddle against the rocks for want of shelter.
chapters.zh: 在山上被大雨淋湿， 因没有避身之处就挨近磐石。

chapters.en: The fatherless infant is snatched from the breast; the nursing child of the poor is seized for a debt.
chapters.zh: 又有人从母怀中抢夺孤儿， 强取穷人的〔衣服〕为当头，

chapters.en: Without clothing, they wander about naked. They carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.
chapters.zh: 使人赤身无衣，到处流行， 且因饥饿扛抬禾捆，

chapters.en: They crush olives within their walls; they tread the winepresses, but go thirsty.
chapters.zh: 在那些人的围墙内造油，醡酒， 自己还口渴。

chapters.en:
From the city, men groan, and the souls of the wounded cry out,
yet God charges no one with wrongdoing.
chapters.zh: 在多民的城内有人唉哼， 受伤的人哀号； 上帝却不理会〔那恶人〕的愚妄。

chapters.en: Then there are those who rebel against the light, not knowing its ways or staying on its paths.
chapters.zh: 又有人背弃光明， 不认识光明的道， 不住在光明的路上。

chapters.en:
When daylight is gone, the murderer rises to kill the poor and needy;
in the night he is like a thief.
chapters.zh: 杀人的黎明起来， 杀害困苦穷乏人， 夜间又作盗贼。

chapters.en: The eye of the adulterer watches for twilight. Thinking, ‘No eye will see me,’ he covers his face.
chapters.zh: 奸夫等候黄昏， 说：必无眼能见我， 就把脸蒙蔽。

chapters.en:
In the dark they dig through houses; by day they shut themselves in,
never to experience the light.
chapters.zh: 盗贼黑夜挖窟窿； 白日躲藏， 并不认识光明。

chapters.en: For to them, deep darkness is their morning; surely they are friends with the terrors of darkness!
chapters.zh: 他们看早晨如幽暗， 因为他们晓得幽暗的惊骇。

chapters.en:
They are but foam on the surface of the water; their portion of the land is cursed,
so that no one turns toward their vineyards.
chapters.zh: 〔这些恶人犹如浮萍〕快快〔飘去〕。 他们所得的分在世上被咒诅； 他们不得再走葡萄园的路。

chapters.en: As drought and heat consume the melting snow, so Sheol steals those who have sinned.
chapters.zh: 干旱炎热消没雪水； 阴间也如此〔消没〕犯罪之辈。

chapters.en: The womb forgets them; the worm feeds on them; they are remembered no more. So injustice is broken like a tree.
chapters.zh: 怀他的母〔注：原文是胎〕要忘记他； 虫子要吃他，觉得甘甜； 他不再被人记念。 不义〔的人〕必如树折断。

chapters.en: They prey on the barren and childless, and show no kindness to the widow.
chapters.zh: 他恶待〔注：或译：他吞灭〕不怀孕不生养的妇人， 不善待寡妇。

chapters.en: Yet by His power, God drags away the mighty; though rising up, they have no assurance of life.
chapters.zh: 然而上帝用能力保全有势力的人； 那性命难保的人仍然兴起。

chapters.en: He gives them a sense of security, but His eyes are on their ways.
chapters.zh: 上帝使他们安稳，他们就有所倚靠； 上帝的眼目也看顾他们的道路。

chapters.en: They are exalted for a moment, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.
chapters.zh: 他们被高举，不过片时就没有了； 他们降为卑，被除灭，与众人一样， 又如谷穗被割。

chapters.en: If this is not so, then who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?”
chapters.zh: 若不是这样，谁能证实我是说谎的， 将我的言语驳为虚空呢？

chapters.en: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:
chapters.zh: 书亚人比勒达回答说：

chapters.en: “Dominion and awe belong to God; He establishes harmony in the heights of heaven.
chapters.zh: 上帝有治理之权，有威严可畏； 他在高处施行和平。

chapters.en: Can His troops be numbered? On whom does His light not rise?
chapters.zh: 他的诸军岂能数算？ 他的光亮一发，谁不蒙照呢？

chapters.en: How then can a man be just before God? How can one born of woman be pure?
chapters.zh: 这样在上帝面前，人怎能称义？ 妇人所生的怎能洁净？

chapters.en: If even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not pure in His sight,
chapters.zh: 在上帝眼前，月亮也无光亮， 星宿也不清洁。

chapters.en: how much less man, who is but a maggot, and the son of man, who is but a worm!”
chapters.zh: 何况如虫的人， 如蛆的世人呢！

chapters.en: Then Job answered:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答说：

chapters.en: “How you have helped the powerless and saved the arm that is feeble!
chapters.zh: 无能的人蒙你何等的帮助！ 膀臂无力的人蒙你何等的拯救！

chapters.en: How you have counseled the unwise and provided fully sound insight!
chapters.zh: 无智慧的人蒙你何等的指教！ 你向他多显大知识！

chapters.en: To whom have you uttered these words? And whose spirit spoke through you?
chapters.zh: 你向谁发出言语来？ 谁的灵从你而出？

chapters.en: The dead tremble— those beneath the waters and those who dwell in them.
chapters.zh: 在大水和水族以下的阴魂战兢。

chapters.en: Sheol is naked before God, and Abaddon has no covering.
chapters.zh: 在上帝面前，阴间显露； 灭亡也不得遮掩。

chapters.en: He stretches out the north over empty space; He hangs the earth upon nothing.
chapters.zh: 上帝将北极铺在空中， 将大地悬在虚空；

chapters.en: He wraps up the waters in His clouds, yet the clouds do not burst under their own weight.
chapters.zh: 将水包在密云中， 云却不破裂；

chapters.en: He covers the face of the full moon, spreading over it His cloud.
chapters.zh: 遮蔽他的宝座， 将云铺在其上；

chapters.en: He has inscribed a horizon on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness.
chapters.zh: 在水面的周围划出界限， 直到光明黑暗的交界。

chapters.en: The foundations of heaven quake, astounded at His rebuke.
chapters.zh: 天的柱子因他的斥责震动惊奇。

chapters.en: By His power He stirred the sea; by His understanding He shattered Rahab.
chapters.zh: 他以能力搅动〔注：或译：平静〕大海； 他藉知识打伤拉哈伯，

chapters.en: By His breath the skies were cleared; His hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
chapters.zh: 藉他的灵使天有妆饰； 他的手刺杀快蛇。

chapters.en: Indeed, these are but the fringes of His ways; how faint is the whisper we hear of Him! Who then can understand the thunder of His power?”
chapters.zh: 看哪，这不过是上帝工作的些微； 我们所听于他的是何等细微的声音！ 他大能的雷声谁能明透呢？

chapters.en: Job continued his discourse:
chapters.zh: 约伯接着说：

chapters.en: “As surely as God lives, who has deprived me of justice— the Almighty, who has embittered my soul—
chapters.zh: 上帝夺去我的理，全能者使我心中愁苦。 我指着永生的上帝起誓：

chapters.en: as long as my breath is still within me and the breath of God remains in my nostrils,
chapters.zh: 我的生命尚在我里面； 上帝所赐呼吸之气仍在我的鼻孔内。

chapters.en: my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will not utter deceit.
chapters.zh: 我的嘴决不说非义之言； 我的舌也不说诡诈之语。

chapters.en: I will never say that you are right; I will maintain my integrity until I die.
chapters.zh: 我断不以你们为是； 我至死必不以自己为不正！

chapters.en: I will cling to my righteousness and never let go. As long as I live, my conscience will not accuse me.
chapters.zh: 我持定我的义，必不放松； 在世的日子，我心必不责备我。

chapters.en: May my enemy be like the wicked and my opponent like the unjust.
chapters.zh: 愿我的仇敌如恶人一样； 愿那起来攻击我的，如不义之人一般。

chapters.en: For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
chapters.zh: 不敬虔的人虽然得利， 上帝夺取其命的时候还有什么指望呢？

chapters.en: Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?
chapters.zh: 患难临到他， 上帝岂能听他的呼求？

chapters.en: Will he delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?
chapters.zh: 他岂以全能者为乐， 随时求告上帝呢？

chapters.en: I will instruct you in the power of God. I will not conceal the ways of the Almighty.
chapters.zh: 上帝的作为，我要指教你们； 全能者所行的，我也不隐瞒。

chapters.en: Surely all of you have seen it for yourselves. Why then do you keep up this empty talk?
chapters.zh: 你们自己也都见过， 为何全然变为虚妄呢？

chapters.en: This is the wicked man’s portion from God— the heritage the ruthless receive from the Almighty.
chapters.zh: 上帝为恶人所定的分， 强暴人从全能者所得的报〔注：原文是产业〕乃是这样：

chapters.en: Though his sons are many, they are destined for the sword; and his offspring will never have enough food.
chapters.zh: 倘或他的儿女增多，还是被刀所杀； 他的子孙必不得饱食。

chapters.en: His survivors will be buried by the plague, and their widows will not weep for them.
chapters.zh: 他所遗留的人必死而埋葬； 他的寡妇也不哀哭。

chapters.en: Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up a wardrobe like clay,
chapters.zh: 他虽积蓄银子如尘沙， 预备衣服如泥土；

chapters.en: what he lays up, the righteous will wear, and his silver will be divided by the innocent.
chapters.zh: 他只管预备，义人却要穿上； 他的银子，无辜的人要分取。

chapters.en: The house he built is like a moth’s cocoon, like a hut set up by a watchman.
chapters.zh: 他建造房屋如虫做窝， 又如守望者所搭的棚。

chapters.en: He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone.
chapters.zh: 他虽富足躺卧，却不得收殓， 转眼之间就不在了。

chapters.en: Terrors overtake him like a flood; a tempest sweeps him away in the night.
chapters.zh: 惊恐如波涛将他追上； 暴风在夜间将他刮去。

chapters.en: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.
chapters.zh: 东风把他飘去， 又刮他离开本处。

chapters.en: It hurls itself against him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power.
chapters.zh: 上帝要向他射箭，并不留情； 他恨不得逃脱上帝的手。

chapters.en: It claps its hands at him and hisses him out of his place.
chapters.zh: 人要向他拍掌， 并要发叱声，使他离开本处。

chapters.en: “Surely there is a mine for silver and a place where gold is refined.
chapters.zh: 银子有矿； 炼金有方。

chapters.en: Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from ore.
chapters.zh: 铁从地里挖出； 铜从石中镕化。

chapters.en:
Man puts an end to the darkness; he probes the farthest recesses
for ore in deepest darkness.
chapters.zh: 人为黑暗定界限， 查究幽暗阴翳的石头，直到极处，

chapters.en:
Far from human habitation he cuts a shaft in places forgotten by the foot of man.
Far from men he dangles and sways.
chapters.zh: 在无人居住之处刨开矿穴， 〔过路的人〕也想不到他们； 又与人远离，悬在空中摇来摇去。

chapters.en: Food may come from the earth, but from below it is transformed as by fire.
chapters.zh: 至于地，能出粮食， 地内好像被火翻起来。

chapters.en: Its rocks are the source of sapphires, containing flecks of gold.
chapters.zh: 地中的石头有蓝宝石， 并有金沙。

chapters.en: No bird of prey knows that path; no falcon’s eye has seen it.
chapters.zh: 矿中的路鸷鸟不得知道； 鹰眼也未见过。

chapters.en: Proud beasts have never trodden it; no lion has ever prowled over it.
chapters.zh: 狂傲的野兽未曾行过； 猛烈的狮子也未曾经过。

chapters.en: The miner strikes the flint; he overturns mountains at their base.
chapters.zh: 人伸手凿开坚石， 倾倒山根，

chapters.en: He hews out channels in the rocks, and his eyes spot every treasure.
chapters.zh: 在磐石中凿出水道， 亲眼看见各样宝物。

chapters.en: He stops up the sources of the streams to bring what is hidden to light.
chapters.zh: 他封闭水不得滴流， 使隐藏的物显露出来。

chapters.en: But where can wisdom be found, and where does understanding dwell?
chapters.zh: 然而，智慧有何处可寻？ 聪明之处在哪里呢？

chapters.en: No man can know its value, nor is it found in the land of the living.
chapters.zh: 智慧的价值无人能知， 在活人之地也无处可寻。

chapters.en: The ocean depths say, ‘It is not in me,’ while the sea declares, ‘It is not with me.’
chapters.zh: 深渊说：不在我内； 沧海说：不在我中。

chapters.en: It cannot be bought with gold, nor can its price be weighed out in silver.
chapters.zh: 智慧非用黄金可得， 也不能平白银为它的价值。

chapters.en: It cannot be valued in the gold of Ophir, in precious onyx or sapphire.
chapters.zh: 俄斐金和贵重的红玛瑙， 并蓝宝石，不足与较量；

chapters.en: Neither gold nor crystal can compare to it, nor jewels of fine gold be exchanged for it.
chapters.zh: 黄金和玻璃不足与比较； 精金的器皿不足与兑换。

chapters.en: Coral and quartz are unworthy of mention; the price of wisdom is beyond rubies.
chapters.zh: 珊瑚、水晶都不足论； 智慧的价值胜过珍珠〔注：或译：红宝石〕。

chapters.en: Topaz from Cush cannot compare to it, nor can it be valued in pure gold.
chapters.zh: 古实的红璧玺不足与比较； 精金也不足与较量。

chapters.en: From where, then, does wisdom come, and where does understanding dwell?
chapters.zh: 智慧从何处来呢？ 聪明之处在哪里呢？

chapters.en: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing and concealed from the birds of the air.
chapters.zh: 是向一切有生命的眼目隐藏， 向空中的飞鸟掩蔽。

chapters.en: Abaddon and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor about it.’
chapters.zh: 灭没和死亡说： 我们风闻其名。

chapters.en: But God understands its way, and He knows its place.
chapters.zh: 上帝明白智慧的道路， 晓得智慧的所在。

chapters.en: For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.
chapters.zh: 因他鉴察直到地极， 遍观普天之下，

chapters.en: When God fixed the weight of the wind and measured out the waters,
chapters.zh: 要为风定轻重， 又度量诸水；

chapters.en: when He set a limit for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,
chapters.zh: 他为雨露定命令， 为雷电定道路。

chapters.en: then He looked at wisdom and appraised it; He established it and searched it out.
chapters.zh: 那时他看见智慧，而且述说； 他坚定，并且查究。

chapters.en:
And He said to man, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom,
and to turn away from evil is understanding.’”
chapters.zh: 他对人说：敬畏主就是智慧； 远离恶便是聪明。

chapters.en: And Job continued his discourse:
chapters.zh: 约伯又接着说：

chapters.en: “How I long for the months gone by, for the days when God watched over me,
chapters.zh: 惟愿我〔的景况〕如从前的月份， 如上帝保守我的日子。

chapters.en: when His lamp shone above my head, and by His light I walked through the darkness,
chapters.zh: 那时他的灯照在我头上； 我藉他的光行过黑暗。

chapters.en: when I was in my prime, when the friendship of God rested on my tent,
chapters.zh: 我愿如壮年的时候： 那时我在帐棚中， 上帝待我有密友之情；

chapters.en: when the Almighty was still with me and my children were around me,
chapters.zh: 全能者仍与我同在； 我的儿女都环绕我。

chapters.en: when my steps were bathed in cream and the rock poured out for me streams of oil!
chapters.zh: 奶多可洗我的脚； 磐石为我出油成河。

chapters.en: When I went out to the city gate and took my seat in the public square,
chapters.zh: 我出到城门， 在街上设立座位；

chapters.en: the young men saw me and withdrew, and the old men rose to their feet.
chapters.zh: 少年人见我而回避， 老年人也起身站立；

chapters.en: The princes refrained from speaking and covered their mouths with their hands.
chapters.zh: 王子都停止说话， 用手捂口；

chapters.en: The voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.
chapters.zh: 首领静默无声， 舌头贴住上膛。

chapters.en: For those who heard me called me blessed, and those who saw me commended me,
chapters.zh: 耳朵听我的，就称我有福； 眼睛看我的，便称赞我；

chapters.en: because I rescued the poor who cried out and the fatherless who had no helper.
chapters.zh: 因我拯救哀求的困苦人 和无人帮助的孤儿。

chapters.en: The dying man blessed me, and I made the widow’s heart sing for joy.
chapters.zh: 将要灭亡的为我祝福； 我也使寡妇心中欢乐。

chapters.en: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and my turban.
chapters.zh: 我以公义为衣服， 以公平为外袍和冠冕。

chapters.en: I served as eyes to the blind and as feet to the lame.
chapters.zh: 我为瞎子的眼， 瘸子的脚。

chapters.en: I was a father to the needy, and I took up the case of the stranger.
chapters.zh: 我为穷乏人的父； 素不认识的人，我查明他的案件。

chapters.en: I shattered the fangs of the unjust and snatched the prey from his teeth.
chapters.zh: 我打破不义之人的牙床， 从他牙齿中夺了所抢的。

chapters.en: So I thought: ‘I will die in my nest and multiply my days as the sand.
chapters.zh: 我便说：我必死在家中〔注：原文是窝中〕， 必增添我的日子，多如尘沙。

chapters.en: My roots will spread out to the waters, and the dew will rest nightly on my branches.
chapters.zh: 我的根长到水边； 露水终夜霑在我的枝上。

chapters.en: My glory is ever new within me, and my bow is renewed in my hand.’
chapters.zh: 我的荣耀在身上增新； 我的弓在手中日强。

chapters.en: Men listened to me with expectation, waiting silently for my counsel.
chapters.zh: 人听见我而仰望， 静默等候我的指教。

chapters.en: After my words, they spoke no more; my speech settled on them like dew.
chapters.zh: 我说话之后，他们就不再说； 我的言语〔像雨露〕滴在他们身上。

chapters.en: They waited for me as for rain and drank in my words like spring showers.
chapters.zh: 他们仰望我如仰望雨， 又张开口如切慕春雨。

chapters.en: If I smiled at them, they did not believe it; the light of my countenance was precious.
chapters.zh: 他们不敢自信，我就向他们含笑； 他们不使我脸上的光改变。

chapters.en:
I chose their course and presided as chief. So I dwelt as a king among his troops,
as a comforter of the mourners.
chapters.zh: 我为他们选择道路，又坐首位； 我如君王在军队中居住， 又如吊丧的安慰伤心的人。
