chapters.en: “But now they mock me, men younger than I am, whose fathers I would have refused to put with my sheep dogs.
chapters.zh: 但如今，比我年少的人戏笑我； 其人之父我曾藐视， 不肯安在看守我羊群的狗中。

chapters.en: What use to me was the strength of their hands, since their vigor had left them?
chapters.zh: 他们壮年的气力既已衰败， 其手之力与我何益呢？

chapters.en:
Gaunt from poverty and hunger, they gnawed the dry land,
and the desolate wasteland by night.
chapters.zh: 他们因穷乏饥饿，身体枯瘦， 在荒废凄凉的幽暗中龈干燥之地，

chapters.en: They plucked mallow among the shrubs, and the roots of the broom tree were their food.
chapters.zh: 在草丛之中采咸草， 罗腾〔注：小树名，松类〕的根为他们的食物。

chapters.en: They were banished from among men, shouted at like thieves,
chapters.zh: 他们从人中被赶出； 人追喊他们如贼一般，

chapters.en: so that they lived on the slopes of the wadis, among the rocks and in holes in the ground.
chapters.zh: 以致他们住在荒谷之间， 在地洞和巖穴中；

chapters.en: They cried out among the shrubs and huddled beneath the nettles.
chapters.zh: 在草丛中叫唤， 在荆棘下聚集。

chapters.en: A senseless and nameless brood, they were driven off the land.
chapters.zh: 这都是愚顽下贱人的儿女； 他们被鞭打，赶出境外。

chapters.en: And now they mock me in song; I have become a byword among them.
chapters.zh: 现在这些人以我为歌曲， 以我为笑谈。

chapters.en: They abhor me and keep far from me; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.
chapters.zh: 他们厌恶我，躲在旁边站着， 不住地吐唾沫在我脸上。

chapters.en: Because God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they have cast off restraint in my presence.
chapters.zh: 松开他们的绳索苦待我， 在我面前脱去辔头。

chapters.en:
The rabble arises at my right; they lay snares for my feet
and build siege ramps against me.
chapters.zh: 这等下流人在我右边起来， 推开我的脚，筑成战路来攻击我。

chapters.en:
They tear up my path; they profit from my destruction,
with no one to restrain them.
chapters.zh: 这些无人帮助的， 毁坏我的道，加增我的灾。

chapters.en: They advance as through a wide breach; through the ruins they keep rolling in.
chapters.zh: 他们来如同闯进大破口， 在毁坏之间滚〔在我身上〕。

chapters.en:
Terrors are turned loose against me; they drive away my dignity as by the wind,
and my prosperity has passed like a cloud.
chapters.zh: 惊恐临到我， 驱逐我的尊荣如风； 我的福禄如云过去。

chapters.en: And now my soul is poured out within me; days of affliction grip me.
chapters.zh: 现在我心极其悲伤； 困苦的日子将我抓住。

chapters.en: Night pierces my bones, and my gnawing pains never rest.
chapters.zh: 夜间，我里面的骨头刺我， 〔疼痛〕不止，好像龈我。

chapters.en: With great force He grasps my garment; He seizes me by the collar of my tunic.
chapters.zh: 因〔上帝〕的大力，我的外衣污秽不堪， 又如里衣的领子将我缠住。

chapters.en: He throws me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
chapters.zh: 上帝把我扔在淤泥中， 我就像尘土和炉灰一般。

chapters.en: I cry out to You for help, but You do not answer; when I stand up, You merely look at me.
chapters.zh: 〔主啊〕，我呼求你，你不应允我； 我站起来，你就定睛看我。

chapters.en: You have ruthlessly turned on me; You oppose me with Your strong hand.
chapters.zh: 你向我变心，待我残忍， 又用大能追逼我，

chapters.en:
You snatch me up into the wind and drive me before it;
You toss me about in the storm.
chapters.zh: 把我提在风中，使我驾风而行， 又使我消灭在烈风中。

chapters.en: Yes, I know that You will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living.
chapters.zh: 我知道要使我临到死地， 到那为众生所定的阴宅。

chapters.en: Yet no one stretches out his hand against a ruined man when he cries for help in his distress.
chapters.zh: 然而，人仆倒岂不伸手？ 遇灾难岂不求救呢？

chapters.en: Have I not wept for those in trouble? Has my soul not grieved for the needy?
chapters.zh: 人遭难，我岂不为他哭泣呢？ 人穷乏，我岂不为他忧愁呢？

chapters.en: But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I looked for light, darkness fell.
chapters.zh: 我仰望得好处，灾祸就到了； 我等待光明，黑暗便来了。

chapters.en: I am churning within and cannot rest; days of affliction confront me.
chapters.zh: 我心里烦扰不安， 困苦的日子临到我身。

chapters.en: I go about blackened, but not by the sun. I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
chapters.zh: 我没有日光就哀哭行去〔注：或译：我面发黑并非因日晒〕； 我在会中站着求救。

chapters.en: I have become a brother of jackals, a companion of ostriches.
chapters.zh: 我与野狗为弟兄， 与鸵鸟为同伴。

chapters.en: My skin grows black and peels, and my bones burn with fever.
chapters.zh: 我的皮肤黑〔而脱落〕； 我的骨头因热烧焦。

chapters.en: My harp is tuned to mourning and my flute to the sound of weeping.
chapters.zh: 所以，我的琴音〔变〕为悲音； 我的箫声〔变〕为哭声。

chapters.en: “I have made a covenant with my eyes. How then could I gaze with desire at a virgin?
chapters.zh: 我与眼睛立约， 怎能恋恋瞻望处女呢？

chapters.en: For what is the allotment of God from above, or the heritage from the Almighty on high?
chapters.zh: 从至上的上帝所得之分， 从至高全能者所得之业是什么呢？

chapters.en: Does not disaster come to the unjust and calamity to the workers of iniquity?
chapters.zh: 岂不是祸患临到不义的， 灾害临到作孽的呢？

chapters.en: Does He not see my ways and count my every step?
chapters.zh: 上帝岂不是察看我的道路， 数点我的脚步呢？

chapters.en: If I have walked in falsehood or my foot has rushed to deceit,
chapters.zh: 我若与虚谎同行， 脚若追随诡诈；

chapters.en: let God weigh me with honest scales, that He may know my integrity.
chapters.zh: （我若被公道的天平称度， 使上帝可以知道我的纯正；）

chapters.en:
If my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has followed my eyes,
or if impurity has stuck to my hands,
chapters.zh: 我的脚步若偏离正路， 我的心若随着我的眼目， 若有玷污粘在我手上；

chapters.en: then may another eat what I have sown, and may my crops be uprooted.
chapters.zh: 就愿我所种的有别人吃， 我田所产的被拔出来。

chapters.en: If my heart has been enticed by my neighbor’s wife, or I have lurked at his door,
chapters.zh: 我若受迷惑，向妇人〔起淫念〕， 在邻舍的门外蹲伏，

chapters.en: then may my own wife grind grain for another, and may other men sleep with her.
chapters.zh: 就愿我的妻子给别人推磨， 别人也与她同室。

chapters.en: For that would be a heinous crime, an iniquity to be judged.
chapters.zh: 因为这是大罪， 是审判官〔当罚的〕罪孽。

chapters.en: For it is a fire that burns down to Abaddon; it would root out my entire harvest.
chapters.zh: 这本是火焚烧，直到毁灭， 必拔除我所有的家产。

chapters.en: If I have rejected the cause of my manservant or maidservant when they made a complaint against me,
chapters.zh: 我的仆婢与我争辩的时候， 我若藐视不听他们的情节；

chapters.en: what will I do when God rises to judge? How will I answer when called to account?
chapters.zh: 上帝兴起，我怎样行呢？ 他察问，我怎样回答呢？

chapters.en: Did not He who made me in the womb also make them? Did not the same One form us in the womb?
chapters.zh: 造我在腹中的，不也是造他吗？ 将他与我抟在腹中的岂不是一位吗？

chapters.en: If I have denied the desires of the poor or allowed the widow’s eyes to fail,
chapters.zh: 我若不容贫寒人得其所愿， 或叫寡妇眼中失望，

chapters.en: if I have eaten my morsel alone, not sharing it with the fatherless—
chapters.zh: 或独自吃我一点食物， 孤儿没有与我同吃；

chapters.en: though from my youth I reared him as would a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow—
chapters.zh: （从幼年时孤儿与我同长，好像父子一样； 我从出母腹就扶助〔注：原文是引领〕寡妇。）

chapters.en: if I have seen one perish for lack of clothing, or a needy man without a cloak,
chapters.zh: 我若见人因无衣死亡， 或见穷乏人身无遮盖；

chapters.en: if his heart has not blessed me for warming him with the fleece of my sheep,
chapters.zh: 我若不使他因我羊的毛得暖， 为我祝福；

chapters.en: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless because I saw that I had support in the gate,
chapters.zh: 我若在城门口见有帮助我的， 举手攻击孤儿；

chapters.en: then may my arm fall from my shoulder and be torn from its socket.
chapters.zh: 情愿我的肩头从缺盆骨脱落， 我的膀臂从羊矢骨折断。

chapters.en: For calamity from God terrifies me, and His splendor I cannot overpower.
chapters.zh: 因上帝降的灾祸使我恐惧； 因他的威严，我不能妄为。

chapters.en: If I have put my trust in gold or called pure gold my security,
chapters.zh: 我若以黄金为指望， 对精金说：〔你是〕我的倚靠；

chapters.en: if I have rejoiced in my great wealth because my hand had gained so much,
chapters.zh: 我若因财物丰裕， 因我手多得资财而欢喜；

chapters.en: if I have beheld the sun in its radiance or the moon moving in splendor,
chapters.zh: 我若见太阳发光， 明月行在空中，

chapters.en: so that my heart was secretly enticed and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,
chapters.zh: 心就暗暗被引诱， 口便亲手；

chapters.en: this would also be an iniquity to be judged, for I would have denied God on high.
chapters.zh: 这也是审判官〔当罚的〕罪孽， 又是我背弃在上的上帝。

chapters.en: If I have rejoiced in my enemy’s ruin, or exulted when evil befell him—
chapters.zh: 我若见恨我的遭报就欢喜， 见他遭灾便高兴；

chapters.en: I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking for his life with a curse—
chapters.zh: （我没有容口犯罪， 咒诅他的生命；）

chapters.en: if the men of my house have not said, ‘Who is there who has not had his fill?’—
chapters.zh: 若我帐棚的人未尝说， 谁不以主人的食物吃饱呢？

chapters.en: but no stranger had to lodge on the street, for my door has been open to the traveler—
chapters.zh: （从来我没有容客旅在街上住宿， 却开门迎接行路的人；）

chapters.en: if I have covered my transgressions like Adam by hiding my guilt in my heart,
chapters.zh: 我若像亚当〔注：或译：别人〕遮掩我的过犯， 将罪孽藏在怀中；

chapters.en: because I greatly feared the crowds and the contempt of the clans terrified me, so that I kept silent and would not go outside—
chapters.zh: 因惧怕大众， 又因宗族藐视我使我惊恐， 以致闭口无言，杜门不出；

chapters.en: (Oh, that I had one to hear me! Here is my signature. Let the Almighty answer me; let my accuser compose an indictment.
chapters.zh: 惟愿有一位肯听我！ （看哪，在这里有我所划的押， 愿全能者回答我！）

chapters.en: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder and wear it like a crown.
chapters.zh: 愿那敌我者所写的状词〔在我这里〕！ 我必带在肩上，又绑在头上为冠冕。

chapters.en: I would give account of all my steps; I would approach Him like a prince.)—
chapters.zh: 我必向他述说我脚步的数目， 必如君王进到他面前。

chapters.en: if my land cries out against me and its furrows weep together,
chapters.zh: 我若〔夺取〕田地，这地向我喊冤， 诓沟一同哭泣；

chapters.en: if I have devoured its produce without payment or broken the spirit of its tenants,
chapters.zh: 我若吃地的出产不给价值， 或叫原主丧命；

chapters.en:
then let briers grow instead of wheat and stinkweed instead of barley.”
Thus conclude the words of Job.
chapters.zh: 愿这地长蒺藜代替麦子， 长恶草代替大麦。 约伯的话说完了。

chapters.en: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
chapters.zh: 于是这三个人，因约伯自以为义就不再回答他。

chapters.en: This kindled the anger of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram. He burned with anger against Job for justifying himself rather than God,
chapters.zh: 那时有布西人兰族巴拉迦的儿子以利户向约伯发怒；因约伯自以为义，不以上帝为义。

chapters.en: and he burned with anger against Job’s three friends because they had failed to refute Job, and yet had condemned him.
chapters.zh: 他又向约伯的三个朋友发怒；因为他们想不出回答的话来，仍以约伯为有罪。

chapters.en: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job because the others were older than he.
chapters.zh: 以利户要与约伯说话，就等候他们，因为他们比自己年老。

chapters.en: But when he saw that the three men had no further reply, his anger was kindled.
chapters.zh: 以利户见这三个人口中无话回答，就怒气发作。

chapters.en:
So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite declared:
“I am young in years, while you are old; that is why I was timid and afraid to tell you what I know.
chapters.zh: 布西人巴拉迦的儿子以利户回答说： 我年轻，你们老迈； 因此我退让，不敢向你们陈说我的意见。

chapters.en: I thought that age should speak, and many years should teach wisdom.
chapters.zh: 我说，年老的当先说话； 寿高的当以智慧教训人。

chapters.en:
But there is a spirit in a man, the breath of the Almighty,
that gives him understanding.
chapters.zh: 但在人里面有灵； 全能者的气使人有聪明。

chapters.en: It is not only the old who are wise, or the elderly who understand justice.
chapters.zh: 尊贵的不都有智慧； 寿高的不都能明白公平。

chapters.en: Therefore I say, ‘Listen to me; I too will declare what I know.’
chapters.zh: 因此我说：你们要听我言； 我也要陈说我的意见。

chapters.en: Indeed, I waited while you spoke; I listened to your reasoning; as you searched for words,
chapters.zh: 你们查究所要说的话； 那时我等候你们的话， 侧耳听你们的辩论，

chapters.en: I paid you full attention. But no one proved Job wrong; not one of you rebutted his arguments.
chapters.zh: 留心听你们； 谁知你们中间无一人折服约伯， 驳倒他的话。

chapters.en: So do not claim, ‘We have found wisdom; let God, not man, refute him.’
chapters.zh: 你们切不可说：我们寻得智慧； 上帝能胜他，人却不能。

chapters.en: But Job has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.
chapters.zh: 约伯没有向我争辩； 我也不用你们的话回答他。

chapters.en: Job’s friends are dismayed, with no more to say; words have escaped them.
chapters.zh: 他们惊奇不再回答， 一言不发。

chapters.en: Must I wait, now that they are silent, now that they stand and no longer reply?
chapters.zh: 我岂因他们不说话， 站住不再回答，仍旧等候呢？

chapters.en: I too will answer; yes, I will declare what I know.
chapters.zh: 我也要回答我的一分话， 陈说我的意见。

chapters.en: For I am full of words, and my spirit within me compels me.
chapters.zh: 因为我的言语满怀； 我里面的灵激动我。

chapters.en: Behold, my belly is like unvented wine; it is about to burst like a new wineskin.
chapters.zh: 我的胸怀如盛酒〔之囊〕没有出气之缝， 又如新皮袋快要破裂。

chapters.en: I must speak and find relief; I must open my lips and respond.
chapters.zh: 我要说话，使我舒畅； 我要开口回答。

chapters.en: I will be partial to no one, nor will I flatter any man.
chapters.zh: 我必不看人的情面， 也不奉承人。

chapters.en: For I do not know how to flatter, or my Maker would remove me in an instant.
chapters.zh: 我不晓得奉承； 〔若奉承〕，造我的主必快快除灭我。

chapters.en: “But now, O Job, hear my speech, and listen to all my words.
chapters.zh: 约伯啊，请听我的话， 留心听我一切的言语。

chapters.en: Behold, I will open my mouth; my address is on the tip of my tongue.
chapters.zh: 我现在开口， 用舌发言。

chapters.en: My words are from an upright heart, and my lips speak sincerely what I know.
chapters.zh: 我的言语〔要发明〕心中所存的正直； 我所知道的，我嘴唇要诚实地说出。

chapters.en: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
chapters.zh: 上帝的灵造我； 全能者的气使我得生。

chapters.en: Refute me if you can; prepare your case and confront me.
chapters.zh: 你若回答我， 就站起来，在我面前陈明。

chapters.en: I am just like you before God; I was also formed from clay.
chapters.zh: 我在上帝面前与你一样， 也是用土造成。

chapters.en: Surely no fear of me should terrify you; nor will my hand be heavy upon you.
chapters.zh: 我不用威严惊吓你， 也不用势力重压你。

chapters.en: Surely you have spoken in my hearing, and I have heard these very words:
chapters.zh: 你所说的，我听见了， 也听见你的言语，〔说〕：

chapters.en: ‘I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, with no iniquity in me.
chapters.zh: 我是清洁无过的，我是无辜的； 在我里面也没有罪孽。

chapters.en: Yet God finds occasions against me; He counts me as His enemy.
chapters.zh: 上帝找机会攻击我， 以我为仇敌，

chapters.en: He puts my feet in the stocks; He watches over all my paths.’
chapters.zh: 把我的脚上了木狗， 窥察我一切的道路。

chapters.en: Behold, you are not right in this matter. I will answer you, for God is greater than man.
chapters.zh: 我要回答你说：你这话无理， 因上帝比世人更大。

chapters.en: Why do you complain to Him that He answers nothing a man asks?
chapters.zh: 你为何与他争论呢？ 因他的事都不对人解说？

chapters.en: For God speaks in one way and in another, yet no one notices.
chapters.zh: 上帝说一次、两次， 〔世人〕却不理会。

chapters.en: In a dream, in a vision in the night, when deep sleep falls upon men as they slumber on their beds,
chapters.zh: 人躺在床上沉睡的时候， 上帝就用梦和夜间的异象，

chapters.en: He opens their ears and terrifies them with warnings
chapters.zh: 开通他们的耳朵， 将当受的教训印在他们心上，

chapters.en: to turn a man from wrongdoing and keep him from pride,
chapters.zh: 好叫人不从自己的谋算， 不行骄傲的事〔注：原文是将骄傲向人隐藏〕，

chapters.en: to preserve his soul from the Pit and his life from perishing by the sword.
chapters.zh: 拦阻人不陷于坑里， 不死在刀下。

chapters.en: A man is also chastened on his bed with pain and constant distress in his bones,
chapters.zh: 人在床上被惩治， 骨头中不住地疼痛，

chapters.en: so that he detests his bread, and his soul loathes his favorite food.
chapters.zh: 以致他的口厌弃食物， 心厌恶美味。

chapters.en: His flesh wastes away from sight, and his hidden bones protrude.
chapters.zh: 他的肉消瘦，不得再见； 先前不见的骨头都凸出来。

chapters.en: He draws near to the Pit, and his life to the messengers of death.
chapters.zh: 他的灵魂临近深坑； 他的生命近于灭命的。

chapters.en: Yet if there is a messenger on his side, one mediator in a thousand, to tell a man what is right for him,
chapters.zh: 一千天使中， 若有一个作传话的与上帝同在， 指示人所当行的事，

chapters.en: to be gracious to him and say, ‘Spare him from going down to the Pit; I have found his ransom,’
chapters.zh: 上帝就给他开恩， 说：救赎他免得下坑； 我已经得了赎价。

chapters.en: then his flesh is refreshed like a child’s; he returns to the days of his youth.
chapters.zh: 他的肉要比孩童的肉更嫩； 他就返老还童。

chapters.en: He prays to God and finds favor; he sees God’s face and shouts for joy, and God restores His righteousness to that man.
chapters.zh: 他祷告上帝， 上帝就喜悦他， 使他欢呼朝见上帝的面； 上帝又看他为义。

chapters.en: Then he sings before men with these words: ‘I have sinned and perverted what was right; yet I did not get what I deserved.
chapters.zh: 他在人前歌唱说： 我犯了罪，颠倒是非， 这竟与我无益。

chapters.en: He redeemed my soul from going down to the Pit, and I will live to see the light.’
chapters.zh: 上帝救赎我的灵魂免入深坑； 我的生命也必见光。

chapters.en: Behold, all these things God does to a man, two or even three times,
chapters.zh: 上帝两次、三次向人行这一切的事，

chapters.en: to bring back his soul from the Pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of life.
chapters.zh: 为要从深坑救回人的灵魂， 使他被光照耀，与活人一样。

chapters.en: Pay attention, Job, and listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
chapters.zh: 约伯啊，你当侧耳听我的话， 不要作声，等我讲说。

chapters.en: But if you have something to say, answer me; speak up, for I would like to vindicate you.
chapters.zh: 你若有话说，就可以回答我； 你只管说，因我愿以你为是。

chapters.en: But if not, then listen to me; be quiet, and I will teach you wisdom.”
chapters.zh: 若不然，你就听我说； 你不要作声，我便将智慧教训你。

chapters.en: Then Elihu continued:
chapters.zh: 以利户又说：

chapters.en: “Hear my words, O wise men; give ear to me, O men of learning.
chapters.zh: 你们智慧人要听我的话； 有知识的人要留心听我说。

chapters.en: For the ear tests words as the mouth tastes food.
chapters.zh: 因为耳朵试验话语， 好像上膛尝食物。

chapters.en: Let us choose for ourselves what is right; let us learn together what is good.
chapters.zh: 我们当选择何为是， 彼此知道何为善。

chapters.en: For Job has declared, ‘I am righteous, yet God has deprived me of justice.
chapters.zh: 约伯曾说：我是公义， 上帝夺去我的理；

chapters.en:
Would I lie about my case? My wound is incurable,
though I am without transgression.’
chapters.zh: 我虽有理，还〔算为〕说谎言的； 我虽无过，受的伤还不能医治。

chapters.en: What man is like Job, who drinks up derision like water?
chapters.zh: 谁像约伯， 喝讥诮如同喝水呢？

chapters.en: He keeps company with evildoers and walks with wicked men.
chapters.zh: 他与作孽的结伴， 和恶人同行。

chapters.en: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight in God.’
chapters.zh: 他说：人以上帝为乐， 总是无益。

chapters.en: Therefore listen to me, O men of understanding. Far be it from God to do wrong, and from the Almighty to act unjustly.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们明理的人要听我的话。 上帝断不致行恶； 全能者断不致作孽。

chapters.en: For according to a man’s deeds He repays him; according to a man’s ways He brings consequences.
chapters.zh: 他必按人所做的报应人， 使各人照所行的得报。

chapters.en: Indeed, it is true that God does not act wickedly, and the Almighty does not pervert justice.
chapters.zh: 上帝必不作恶； 全能者也不偏离公平。

chapters.en: Who gave Him charge over the earth? Who appointed Him over the whole world?
chapters.zh: 谁派他治理地， 安定全世界呢？

chapters.en: If He were to set His heart to it and withdraw His Spirit and breath,
chapters.zh: 他若专心为己， 将灵和气收归自己，

chapters.en: all flesh would perish together and mankind would return to the dust.
chapters.zh: 凡有血气的就必一同死亡； 世人必仍归尘土。

chapters.en: If you have understanding, hear this; listen to my words.
chapters.zh: 你若明理，就当听我的话， 留心听我言语的声音。

chapters.en: Could one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the just and mighty One,
chapters.zh: 难道恨恶公平的可以掌权吗？ 那有公义的、有大能的，岂可定他有罪吗？

chapters.en: who says to kings, ‘You are worthless!’ and to nobles, ‘You are wicked,’
chapters.zh: 他对君王说：〔你是〕鄙陋的； 对贵臣说：〔你是〕邪恶的。

chapters.en:
who is not partial to princes and does not favor rich over poor?
For they are all the work of His hands.
chapters.zh: 他待王子不徇情面， 也不看重富足的过于贫穷的， 因为都是他手所造。

chapters.en: They die in an instant, in the middle of the night. The people convulse and pass away; the mighty are removed without human hand.
chapters.zh: 在转眼之间，半夜之中， 他们就死亡。 百姓被震动而去世； 有权力的被夺去非借人手。

chapters.en: For His eyes are on the ways of a man, and He sees his every step.
chapters.zh: 上帝注目观看人的道路， 看明人的脚步。

chapters.en: There is no darkness or deep shadow where the workers of iniquity can hide.
chapters.zh: 没有黑暗、阴翳能给作孽的藏身。

chapters.en: For God need not examine a man further or have him approach for judgment.
chapters.zh: 上帝审判人，不必使人到他面前再三鉴察。

chapters.en: He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets up others in their place.
chapters.zh: 他用难测之法打破有能力的人， 设立别人代替他们。

chapters.en: Therefore, He recognizes their deeds; He overthrows them in the night and they are crushed.
chapters.zh: 他原知道他们的行为， 使他们在夜间倾倒灭亡。

chapters.en: He strikes them for their wickedness in full view,
chapters.zh: 他在众人眼前击打他们， 如同击打恶人一样。

chapters.en: because they turned aside from Him and had no regard for any of His ways.
chapters.zh: 因为他们偏行不跟从他， 也不留心他的道，

chapters.en: They caused the cry of the poor to come before Him, and He heard the outcry of the afflicted.
chapters.zh: 甚至使贫穷人的哀声达到他那里； 他也听了困苦人的哀声。

chapters.en: But when He remains silent, who can condemn Him? When He hides His face, who can see Him? Yet He watches over both man and nation,
chapters.zh: 他使人安静，谁能扰乱〔注：或译：定罪〕呢？ 他掩面，谁能见他呢？ 无论待一国或一人都是如此－

chapters.en:
that godless men should not rule
or lay snares for the people.
chapters.zh: 使不虔敬的人不得作王， 免得有人牢笼百姓。

chapters.en: Suppose someone says to God, ‘I have endured my punishment; I will offend no more.
chapters.zh: 有谁对上帝说： 我受了〔责罚〕，不再犯罪；

chapters.en: Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again.’
chapters.zh: 我所看不明的，求你指教我； 我若作了孽，必不再作？

chapters.en: Should God repay you on your own terms when you have disavowed Him? You must choose, not I; so tell me what you know.
chapters.zh: 他施行报应， 岂要随你的心愿、叫你推辞不受吗？ 选定的是你，不是我。 你所知道的只管说吧！

chapters.en: Men of understanding will declare to me, and the wise men who hear me will say:
chapters.zh: 明理的人和听我话的智慧人必对我说：

chapters.en: ‘Job speaks without knowledge; his words lack insight.’
chapters.zh: 约伯说话没有知识， 言语中毫无智慧。

chapters.en: If only Job were tried to the utmost for answering like a wicked man.
chapters.zh: 愿约伯被试验到底， 因他回答像恶人一样。

chapters.en:
For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us
and multiplies his words against God.”
chapters.zh: 他在罪上又加悖逆； 在我们中间拍手， 用许多言语轻慢上帝。

chapters.en: And Elihu went on to say:
chapters.zh: 以利户又说：

chapters.en: “Do you think this is just? You say, ‘I am more righteous than God.’
chapters.zh: 你以为有理， 或以为你的公义胜于上帝的公义，

chapters.en: For you ask, ‘What does it profit me, and what benefit do I gain apart from sin?’
chapters.zh: 才说这与我有什么益处？ 〔我不犯罪〕比犯罪有什么好处呢？

chapters.en: I will reply to you and to your friends as well.
chapters.zh: 我要回答你和在你这里的朋友。

chapters.en: Look to the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds high above you.
chapters.zh: 你要向天观看， 瞻望那高于你的穹苍。

chapters.en: If you sin, what do you accomplish against Him? If you multiply your transgressions, what do you do to Him?
chapters.zh: 你若犯罪，能使上帝受何害呢？ 你的过犯加增，能使上帝受何损呢？

chapters.en: If you are righteous, what do you give Him, or what does He receive from your hand?
chapters.zh: 你若是公义，还能加增他什么呢？ 他从你手里还接受什么呢？

chapters.en: Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself, and your righteousness only a son of man.
chapters.zh: 你的过恶〔或能害〕你这类的人； 你的公义〔或能叫〕世人〔得益处〕。

chapters.en: Men cry out under great oppression; they plead for relief from the arm of the mighty.
chapters.zh: 人因多受欺压就哀求， 因受能者的辖制〔注：原文是膀臂〕便求救，

chapters.en: But no one asks, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives us songs in the night,
chapters.zh: 却无人说：造我的上帝在哪里？ 他使人夜间歌唱，

chapters.en: who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the air?’
chapters.zh: 教训我们胜于地上的走兽， 使我们有聪明胜于空中的飞鸟。

chapters.en: There they cry out, but He does not answer, because of the pride of evil men.
chapters.zh: 他们在那里， 因恶人的骄傲呼求，却无人答应。

chapters.en: Surely God does not listen to empty pleas, and the Almighty does not take note of it.
chapters.zh: 虚妄的〔呼求〕，上帝必不垂听； 全能者也必不眷顾。

chapters.en: How much less, then, when you say that you do not see Him, that your case is before Him and you must wait for Him,
chapters.zh: 何况你说，你不得见他； 你的案件在他面前，你等候他吧。

chapters.en: and further, that in His anger He has not punished or taken much notice of folly!
chapters.zh: 但如今因他未曾发怒降罚， 也不甚理会狂傲，

chapters.en: So Job opens his mouth in vain and multiplies words without knowledge.”
chapters.zh: 所以约伯开口说虚妄的话， 多发无知识的言语。

chapters.en: And Elihu continued:
chapters.zh: 以利户又接着说：

chapters.en: “Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you that there is more to be said on God’s behalf.
chapters.zh: 你再容我片时，我就指示你， 因我还有话为上帝说。

chapters.en: I get my knowledge from afar, and I will ascribe justice to my Maker.
chapters.zh: 我要将所知道的从远处引来， 将公义归给造我的主。

chapters.en: For truly my words are free of falsehood; one perfect in knowledge is with you.
chapters.zh: 我的言语真不虚谎； 有知识全备的与你同在。

chapters.en: Indeed, God is mighty, but He despises no one; He is mighty in strength of understanding.
chapters.zh: 上帝有大能，并不藐视人； 他的智慧甚广。

chapters.en: He does not keep the wicked alive, but He grants justice to the afflicted.
chapters.zh: 他不保护恶人的性命， 却为困苦人伸冤。

chapters.en:
He does not take His eyes off the righteous, but He enthrones them with kings
and exalts them forever.
chapters.zh: 他时常看顾义人， 使他们和君王同坐宝座， 永远要被高举。

chapters.en: And if men are bound with chains, caught in cords of affliction,
chapters.zh: 他们若被锁鍊捆住， 被苦难的绳索缠住，

chapters.en: then He tells them their deeds and how arrogantly they have transgressed.
chapters.zh: 他就把他们的作为和过犯指示他们， 叫他们知道有骄傲的行动。

chapters.en: He opens their ears to correction and commands that they turn from iniquity.
chapters.zh: 他也开通他们的耳朵得受教训， 吩咐他们离开罪孽转回。

chapters.en:
If they obey and serve Him, then they end their days in prosperity
and their years in happiness.
chapters.zh: 他们若听从事奉他， 就必度日亨通，历年福乐；

chapters.en:
But if they do not obey, then they perish by the sword
and die without knowledge.
chapters.zh: 若不听从， 就要被刀杀灭，无知无识而死。

chapters.en: The godless in heart harbor resentment; even when He binds them, they do not cry for help.
chapters.zh: 那心中不敬虔的人积蓄怒气； 上帝捆绑他们，他们竟不求救；

chapters.en: They die in their youth, among the male shrine prostitutes.
chapters.zh: 必在青年时死亡， 与污秽人一样〔丧命〕。

chapters.en: God rescues the afflicted by their affliction and opens their ears in oppression.
chapters.zh: 上帝藉着困苦救拔困苦人， 趁他们受欺压开通他们的耳朵。

chapters.en:
Indeed, He drew you from the jaws of distress to a spacious and broad place,
to a table full of richness.
chapters.zh: 上帝也必引你出离患难， 进入宽阔不狭窄之地； 摆在你席上的必满有肥甘。

chapters.en: But now you are laden with the judgment due the wicked; judgment and justice have seized you.
chapters.zh: 但你满口有恶人批评的言语； 判断和刑罚抓住你。

chapters.en: Be careful that no one lures you with riches; do not let a large bribe lead you astray.
chapters.zh: 不可容忿怒触动你，使你不服责罚； 也不可因赎价大就偏行。

chapters.en: Can your wealth or all your mighty effort keep you from distress?
chapters.zh: 你的呼求〔注：或译：资财〕，或是你一切的势力， 果有灵验，叫你不受患难吗？

chapters.en: Do not long for the night, when people vanish from their homes.
chapters.zh: 不要切慕黑夜， 就是众民在本处被除灭的时候。

chapters.en: Be careful not to turn to iniquity, for this you have preferred to affliction.
chapters.zh: 你要谨慎，不可重看罪孽， 因你选择罪孽过于选择苦难。

chapters.en: Behold, God is exalted in His power. Who is a teacher like Him?
chapters.zh: 上帝行事有高大的能力； 教训人的有谁像他呢？

chapters.en: Who has appointed His way for Him, or told Him, ‘You have done wrong’?
chapters.zh: 谁派定他的道路？ 谁能说：你所行的不义？

chapters.en: Remember to magnify His work, which men have praised in song.
chapters.zh: 你不可忘记称赞他所行的为大， 就是人所歌颂的。

chapters.en: All mankind has seen it; men behold it from afar.
chapters.zh: 他所行的，万人都看见； 世人也从远处观看。

chapters.en: Indeed, God is great—beyond our knowledge; the number of His years is unsearchable.
chapters.zh: 上帝为大，我们不能全知； 他的年数不能测度。

chapters.en: For He draws up drops of water which distill the rain from the mist,
chapters.zh: 他吸取水点， 这水点从云雾中就变成雨；

chapters.en: which the clouds pour out and shower abundantly on mankind.
chapters.zh: 云彩将雨落下，沛然降与世人。

chapters.en: Furthermore, who can understand how the clouds spread out, how the thunder roars from His pavilion?
chapters.zh: 谁能明白云彩如何铺张， 和上帝行宫的雷声呢？

chapters.en: See how He scatters His lightning around Him and covers the depths of the sea.
chapters.zh: 他将亮光普照在自己的四围； 他又遮覆海底。

chapters.en: For by these He judges the nations and provides food in abundance.
chapters.zh: 他用这些审判众民， 且赐丰富的粮食。

chapters.en: He fills His hands with lightning and commands it to strike its mark.
chapters.zh: 他以电光遮手， 命闪电击中敌人〔注：或译：中了靶子〕。

chapters.en: The thunder declares His presence; even the cattle regard the rising storm.
chapters.zh: 所发的雷声显明他的〔作为〕， 又向牲畜指明要起〔暴风〕。

chapters.en: “At this my heart also pounds and leaps from its place.
chapters.zh: 因此我心战兢， 从原处移动。

chapters.en: Listen closely to the thunder of His voice and the rumbling that comes from His mouth.
chapters.zh: 听啊，上帝轰轰的声音 是他口中所发的响声。

chapters.en: He unleashes His lightning beneath the whole sky and sends it to the ends of the earth.
chapters.zh: 他发响声震遍天下， 发电光闪到地极。

chapters.en: Then there comes a roaring sound; He thunders with His majestic voice. He does not restrain the lightning when His voice resounds.
chapters.zh: 随后人听见有雷声轰轰，大发威严， 雷电接连不断。

chapters.en: God thunders wondrously with His voice; He does great things we cannot comprehend.
chapters.zh: 上帝发出奇妙的雷声； 他行大事，我们不能测透。

chapters.en: For He says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth,’ and to the gentle rain, ‘Pour out a mighty downpour.’
chapters.zh: 他对雪说：要降在地上； 对大雨和暴雨也是这样说。

chapters.en: He seals up the hand of every man, so that all men may know His work.
chapters.zh: 他封住各人的手， 叫所造的万人都晓得他的作为。

chapters.en: The wild animals enter their lairs; they settle down in their dens.
chapters.zh: 百兽进入穴中， 卧在洞内。

chapters.en: The tempest comes from its chamber, and the cold from the driving north winds.
chapters.zh: 暴风出于〔南〕宫； 寒冷出于北方。

chapters.en: By the breath of God the ice is formed and the watery expanses are frozen.
chapters.zh: 上帝嘘气成冰； 宽阔之水也都凝结。

chapters.en: He loads the clouds with moisture; He scatters His lightning through them.
chapters.zh: 他使密云盛满水汽， 布散电光之云；

chapters.en: They swirl about, whirling at His direction, accomplishing all that He commands over the face of all the earth.
chapters.zh: 这云是藉他的指引游行旋转， 得以在全地面上行他一切所吩咐的，

chapters.en: Whether for punishment or for His land, He accomplishes this in His loving devotion.
chapters.zh: 或为责罚，或为〔润〕地， 或为施行慈爱。

chapters.en: Listen to this, O Job; stand still and consider the wonders of God.
chapters.zh: 约伯啊，你要留心听， 要站立思想上帝奇妙的作为。

chapters.en: Do you know how God dispatches the clouds or makes the lightning flash?
chapters.zh: 上帝如何〔吩咐〕这些， 如何使云中的电光照耀，你知道吗？

chapters.en: Do you understand how the clouds float, those wonders of Him who is perfect in knowledge?
chapters.zh: 云彩如何浮于空中， 那知识全备者奇妙的作为，你知道吗？

chapters.en: You whose clothes get hot when the land lies hushed under the south wind,
chapters.zh: 南〔风〕使地寂静， 你的衣服就如火热，你知道吗？

chapters.en: can you, like Him, spread out the skies, as strong as a mirror of bronze?
chapters.zh: 你岂能与上帝同铺穹苍吗？ 这穹苍坚硬，如同铸成的镜子。

chapters.en: Teach us what we should say to Him; we cannot draw up our case because of our darkness.
chapters.zh: 我们愚昧不能陈说； 请你指教我们该对他说什么话。

chapters.en: Should He be told that I want to speak? Would a man ask to be swallowed up ?
chapters.zh: 人岂可说：我愿与他说话？ 岂有人自愿灭亡吗？

chapters.en:
Now no one can gaze at the sun when it is bright in the skies
after the wind has swept them clean.
chapters.zh: 现在〔有云遮蔽〕，人不得见穹苍的光亮； 但风吹过，天又发晴。

chapters.en: Out of the north He comes in golden splendor; awesome majesty surrounds Him.
chapters.zh: 金光出于北方， 在上帝那里有可怕的威严。

chapters.en: The Almighty is beyond our reach; He is exalted in power! In His justice and great righteousness He does not oppress.
chapters.zh: 论到全能者，我们不能测度； 他大有能力，有公平和大义， 必不苦待人。

chapters.en: Therefore, men fear Him, for He is not partial to the wise in heart.”
chapters.zh: 所以，人敬畏他； 凡自〔以为〕心中有智慧的人，他都不顾念。

chapters.en: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
chapters.zh: 那时，耶和华从旋风中回答约伯说：

chapters.en: “Who is this who obscures My counsel by words without knowledge?
chapters.zh: 谁用无知的言语使〔我的〕旨意暗昧不明？

chapters.en: Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.
chapters.zh: 你要如勇士束腰； 我问你，你可以指示我。

chapters.en: Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell Me, if you have understanding.
chapters.zh: 我立大地根基的时候，你在哪里呢？ 你若有聪明，只管说吧！

chapters.en: Who fixed its measurements? Surely you know! Or who stretched a measuring line across it?
chapters.zh: 你若晓得〔就说〕，是谁定地的尺度？ 是谁把准绳拉在其上？

chapters.en: On what were its foundations set, or who laid its cornerstone,
chapters.zh: 地的根基安置在何处？ 地的角石是谁安放的？

chapters.en: while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
chapters.zh: 那时，晨星一同歌唱； 上帝的众子也都欢呼。

chapters.en: Who enclosed the sea behind doors when it burst forth from the womb,
chapters.zh: 海水冲出，如出胎胞， 那时谁将它关闭呢？

chapters.en: when I made the clouds its garment and thick darkness its blanket,
chapters.zh: 是我用云彩当海的衣服， 用幽暗当包裹它的布，

chapters.en: when I fixed its boundaries and set in place its bars and doors,
chapters.zh: 为它定界限， 又安门和闩，

chapters.en: and I declared: ‘You may come this far, but no farther; here your proud waves must stop’?
chapters.zh: 说：你只可到这里，不可越过； 你狂傲的浪要到此止住。

chapters.en: In your days, have you commanded the morning or assigned the dawn its place,
chapters.zh: 你自生以来，曾命定晨光， 使清晨的日光知道本位，

chapters.en: that it might spread to the ends of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
chapters.zh: 叫这光普照地的四极， 将恶人从其中驱逐出来吗？

chapters.en: The earth takes shape like clay under a seal; its hills stand out like the folds of a garment.
chapters.zh: 因〔这光〕，地面改变如泥上印印， 〔万物〕出现如衣服一样。

chapters.en: Light is withheld from the wicked, and their upraised arm is broken.
chapters.zh: 亮光不照恶人； 强横的膀臂也必折断。

chapters.en: Have you journeyed to the vents of the sea or walked in the trenches of the deep?
chapters.zh: 你曾进到海源， 或在深渊的隐密处行走吗？

chapters.en: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
chapters.zh: 死亡的门曾向你显露吗？ 死荫的门你曾见过吗？

chapters.en: Have you surveyed the extent of the earth? Tell Me, if you know all this.
chapters.zh: 地的广大你能明透吗？ 你若全知道，只管说吧！

chapters.en: Where is the way to the home of light? Do you know where darkness resides,
chapters.zh: 光明的居所从何而至？ 黑暗的本位在于何处？

chapters.en: so you can lead it back to its border? Do you know the paths to its home?
chapters.zh: 你能带到本境， 能看明其室之路吗？

chapters.en: Surely you know, for you were already born! And the number of your days is great!
chapters.zh: 你总知道， 因为你早已生在世上， 你日子的数目也多。

chapters.en: Have you entered the storehouses of snow or observed the storehouses of hail,
chapters.zh: 你曾进入雪库， 或见过雹仓吗？

chapters.en: which I hold in reserve for times of trouble, for the day of war and battle?
chapters.zh: 这雪雹乃是我为降灾， 并打仗和争战的日子所预备的。

chapters.en: In which direction is the lightning dispersed, or the east wind scattered over the earth?
chapters.zh: 光亮从何路分开？ 东风从何路分散遍地？

chapters.en: Who cuts a channel for the flood or clears a path for the thunderbolt,
chapters.zh: 谁为雨水分道？ 谁为雷电开路？

chapters.en: to bring rain on a barren land, on a desert where no man lives,
chapters.zh: 使雨降在无人之地、 无人居住的旷野？

chapters.en: to satisfy the parched wasteland and make it sprout with tender grass?
chapters.zh: 使荒废凄凉〔之地〕得以丰足， 青草得以发生？

chapters.en: Does the rain have a father? Who has begotten the drops of dew?
chapters.zh: 雨有父吗？ 露水珠是谁生的呢？

chapters.en: From whose womb does the ice emerge? Who gives birth to the frost from heaven,
chapters.zh: 冰出于谁的胎？ 天上的霜是谁生的呢？

chapters.en: when the waters become hard as stone and the surface of the deep is frozen?
chapters.zh: 诸水坚硬〔注：或译：隐藏〕如石头； 深渊之面凝结成冰。

chapters.en: Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the belt of Orion?
chapters.zh: 你能系住昴星的结吗？ 能解开参星的带吗？

chapters.en: Can you bring forth the constellations in their seasons or lead out the Bear and her cubs?
chapters.zh: 你能按时领出十二宫吗？ 能引导北斗和随它的众星〔注：星：原文是子〕吗？

chapters.en: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you set their dominion over the earth?
chapters.zh: 你知道天的定例吗？ 能使地归在天的权下吗？

chapters.en: Can you command the clouds so that a flood of water covers you?
chapters.zh: 你能向云彩扬起声来， 使倾盆的雨遮盖你吗？

chapters.en: Can you send the lightning bolts on their way? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are’?
chapters.zh: 你能发出闪电，叫它行去， 使它对你说：我们在这里？

chapters.en: Who has put wisdom in the heart or given understanding to the mind?
chapters.zh: 谁将智慧放在怀中？ 谁将聪明赐于心内？

chapters.en: Who has the wisdom to count the clouds? Or who can tilt the water jars of the heavens
when the dust hardens into a mass and the clods of earth stick together?
chapters.zh: 谁能用智慧数算云彩呢？ 尘土聚集成团，土块紧紧结连； 那时，谁能倾倒天上的瓶呢？

chapters.en: Can you hunt the prey for a lioness or satisfy the hunger of young lions
when they crouch in their dens and lie in wait in the thicket?
chapters.zh: 母狮子在洞中蹲伏， 少壮狮子在隐密处埋伏； 你能为牠们抓取食物， 使牠们饱足吗？

chapters.en:
Who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God
as they wander about for lack of food?
chapters.zh: 乌鸦之雏因无食物飞来飞去，哀告上帝； 那时，谁为牠预备食物呢？

chapters.en: “Do you know when mountain goats give birth? Have you watched the doe bear her fawn?
chapters.zh: 山巖间的野山羊几时生产，你知道吗？ 母鹿下犊之期，你能察定吗？

chapters.en: Can you count the months they are pregnant? Do you know the time they give birth?
chapters.zh: 牠们怀胎的月数，你能数算吗？ 牠们几时生产，你能晓得吗？

chapters.en: They crouch down and bring forth their young; they deliver their newborn.
chapters.zh: 牠们屈身，将子生下， 就除掉疼痛。

chapters.en: Their young ones thrive and grow up in the open field; they leave and do not return.
chapters.zh: 这子渐渐肥壮，在荒野长大， 去而不回。

chapters.en: Who set the wild donkey free? Who released the swift donkey from the harness?
chapters.zh: 谁放野驴出去自由？ 谁解开快驴的绳索？

chapters.en: I made the wilderness his home and the salt flats his dwelling.
chapters.zh: 我使旷野作牠的住处， 使咸地当牠的居所。

chapters.en: He scorns the tumult of the city and never hears the shouts of a driver.
chapters.zh: 牠嗤笑城内的喧嚷， 不听赶牲口的喝声。

chapters.en: He roams the mountains for pasture, searching for any green thing.
chapters.zh: 遍山是牠的草场； 牠寻找各样青绿之物。

chapters.en: Will the wild ox consent to serve you? Will he stay by your manger at night?
chapters.zh: 野牛岂肯服事你？ 岂肯住在你的槽旁？

chapters.en: Can you hold him to the furrow with a harness? Will he plow the valleys behind you?
chapters.zh: 你岂能用套绳将野牛笼在诓沟之间？ 牠岂肯随你耙山谷之地？

chapters.en: Can you rely on his great strength? Will you leave your hard work to him?
chapters.zh: 岂可因牠的力大就倚靠牠？ 岂可把你的工交给牠做吗？

chapters.en: Can you trust him to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
chapters.zh: 岂可信靠牠把你的粮食运到家， 又收聚你禾场上的谷吗？

chapters.en: The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully, but cannot match the pinions and feathers of the stork.
chapters.zh: 鸵鸟的翅膀欢然扇展， 岂是显慈爱的翎毛和羽毛吗？

chapters.en: For she leaves her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand.
chapters.zh: 因牠把蛋留在地上， 在尘土中使得温暖；

chapters.en: She forgets that a foot may crush them, or a wild animal may trample them.
chapters.zh: 却想不到被脚踹碎， 或被野兽践踏。

chapters.en: She treats her young harshly, as if not her own, with no concern that her labor was in vain.
chapters.zh: 牠忍心待雏，似乎不是自己的； 虽然徒受劳苦，也不〔为雏〕惧怕；

chapters.en: For God has deprived her of wisdom; He has not endowed her with understanding.
chapters.zh: 因为上帝使牠没有智慧， 也未将悟性赐给牠。

chapters.en: Yet when she proudly spreads her wings, she laughs at the horse and its rider.
chapters.zh: 牠几时挺身展开翅膀， 就嗤笑马和骑马的人。

chapters.en: Do you give strength to the horse or adorn his neck with a mane?
chapters.zh: 马的大力是你所赐的吗？ 牠颈项上挓挲的誃是你给牠披上的吗？

chapters.en: Do you make him leap like a locust, striking terror with his proud snorting?
chapters.zh: 是你叫牠跳跃像蝗虫吗？ 牠喷气之威使人惊惶。

chapters.en: He paws in the valley and rejoices in his strength; he charges into battle.
chapters.zh: 牠在谷中刨地，自喜其力； 牠出去迎接佩带兵器的人。

chapters.en: He laughs at fear, frightened of nothing; he does not turn back from the sword.
chapters.zh: 牠嗤笑可怕的事并不惊惶， 也不因刀剑退回。

chapters.en: A quiver rattles at his side, along with a flashing spear and lance.
chapters.zh: 箭袋和发亮的枪， 并短枪在牠身上铮铮有声。

chapters.en: Trembling with excitement, he devours the distance; he cannot stand still when the ram’s horn sounds.
chapters.zh: 牠发猛烈的怒气将地吞下； 一听角声就不耐站立。

chapters.en:
At the blast of the horn, he snorts with fervor. He catches the scent of battle from afar,
the shouts of captains and the cry of war.
chapters.zh: 角每发声，牠说呵哈； 牠从远处闻着战气， 又听见军长大发雷声和〔兵丁〕吶喊。

chapters.en: Does the hawk take flight by your understanding and spread his wings toward the south?
chapters.zh: 鹰雀飞翔，展开翅膀一直向南， 岂是藉你的智慧吗？

chapters.en: Does the eagle soar at your command and make his nest on high?
chapters.zh: 大鹰上腾在高处搭窝， 岂是听你的吩咐吗？

chapters.en: He dwells on a cliff and lodges there; his stronghold is on a rocky crag.
chapters.zh: 牠住在山巖， 以山峰和坚固之所为家，

chapters.en: From there he spies out food; his eyes see it from afar.
chapters.zh: 从那里窥看食物， 眼睛远远观望。

chapters.en: His young ones feast on blood; and where the slain are, there he is.”
chapters.zh: 牠的雏也咂血； 被杀的人在哪里，牠也在那里。

chapters.en: And the LORD said to Job:
chapters.zh: 耶和华又对约伯说：

chapters.en: “Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who argues with God give an answer.”
chapters.zh: 强辩的岂可与全能者争论吗？ 与上帝辩驳的可以回答这些吧！

chapters.en: Then Job answered the LORD:
chapters.zh: 于是，约伯回答耶和华说：

chapters.en: “Behold, I am insignificant. How can I reply to You? I place my hand over my mouth.
chapters.zh: 我是卑贱的！我用什么回答你呢？ 只好用手捂口。

chapters.en: I have spoken once, but I have no answer— twice, but I have nothing to add.”
chapters.zh: 我说了一次，再不回答； 说了两次，就不再说。

chapters.en: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
chapters.zh: 于是，耶和华从旋风中回答约伯说：

chapters.en: “Now brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform Me.
chapters.zh: 你要如勇士束腰； 我问你，你可以指示我。

chapters.en: Would you really annul My justice? Would you condemn Me to justify yourself?
chapters.zh: 你岂可废弃我所拟定的？ 岂可定我有罪，好显自己为义吗？

chapters.en: Do you have an arm like God’s? Can you thunder with a voice like His?
chapters.zh: 你有上帝那样的膀臂吗？ 你能像他发雷声吗？

chapters.en: Then adorn yourself with majesty and splendor, and clothe yourself with honor and glory.
chapters.zh: 你要以荣耀庄严为妆饰， 以尊荣威严为衣服；

chapters.en: Unleash the fury of your wrath; look on every proud man and bring him low.
chapters.zh: 要发出你满溢的怒气， 见一切骄傲的人，使他降卑；

chapters.en: Look on every proud man and humble him; trample the wicked where they stand.
chapters.zh: 见一切骄傲的人，将他制伏， 把恶人践踏在本处；

chapters.en: Bury them together in the dust; imprison them in the grave.
chapters.zh: 将他们一同隐藏在尘土中， 把他们的脸蒙蔽在隐密处；

chapters.en: Then I will confess to you that your own right hand can save you.
chapters.zh: 我就认你右手能以救自己。

chapters.en: Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you. He feeds on grass like an ox.
chapters.zh: 你且观看河马； 我造你也造牠。 牠吃草与牛一样；

chapters.en: See the strength of his loins and the power in the muscles of his belly.
chapters.zh: 牠的气力在腰间， 能力在肚腹的筋上。

chapters.en: His tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are tightly knit.
chapters.zh: 牠摇动尾巴如香柏树； 牠大腿的筋互相联络。

chapters.en: His bones are tubes of bronze; his limbs are rods of iron.
chapters.zh: 牠的骨头〔好像〕铜管； 牠的肢体仿佛铁棍。

chapters.en: He is the foremost of God’s works; only his Maker can draw the sword against him.
chapters.zh: 牠在上帝所造的物中为首； 创造牠的给牠刀剑。

chapters.en: The hills yield him their produce, while all the beasts of the field play nearby.
chapters.zh: 诸山给牠出食物， 也是百兽游玩之处。

chapters.en: He lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds of the marsh.
chapters.zh: 牠伏在莲叶之下， 卧在芦苇隐密处和水洼子里。

chapters.en: The lotus plants conceal him in their shade; the willows of the brook surround him.
chapters.zh: 莲叶的阴凉遮蔽牠； 溪旁的柳树环绕牠。

chapters.en: Though the river rages, Behemoth is unafraid; he remains secure, though the Jordan surges to his mouth.
chapters.zh: 河水泛滥，牠不发战； 就是约旦河的水涨到牠口边，也是安然。

chapters.en: Can anyone capture him as he looks on, or pierce his nose with a snare?
chapters.zh: 在牠防备的时候，谁能捉拿牠？ 谁能牢笼牠穿牠的鼻子呢？

chapters.en: “Can you pull in Leviathan with a hook or tie down his tongue with a rope?
chapters.zh: 你能用鱼钩钓上鳄鱼吗？ 能用绳子压下牠的舌头吗？

chapters.en: Can you put a cord through his nose or pierce his jaw with a hook?
chapters.zh: 你能用绳索穿牠的鼻子吗？ 能用钩穿牠的腮骨吗？

chapters.en: Will he beg you for mercy or speak to you softly?
chapters.zh: 牠岂向你连连恳求， 说柔和的话吗？

chapters.en: Will he make a covenant with you to take him as a slave for life?
chapters.zh: 岂肯与你立约， 使你拿牠永远作奴仆吗？

chapters.en: Can you pet him like a bird or put him on a leash for your maidens?
chapters.zh: 你岂可拿牠当雀鸟玩耍吗？ 岂可为你的幼女将牠拴住吗？

chapters.en: Will traders barter for him or divide him among the merchants?
chapters.zh: 搭伙的〔渔夫〕岂可拿牠当货物吗？ 能把牠分给商人吗？

chapters.en: Can you fill his hide with harpoons or his head with fishing spears?
chapters.zh: 你能用倒钩枪扎满牠的皮， 能用鱼叉叉满牠的头吗？

chapters.en: If you lay a hand on him, you will remember the battle and never repeat it!
chapters.zh: 你按手在牠身上，想与牠争战， 就不再这样行吧！

chapters.en: Surely hope of overcoming him is false. Is not the sight of him overwhelming?
chapters.zh: 人指望捉拿牠是徒然的； 一见牠，岂不丧胆吗？

chapters.en: No one is so fierce as to rouse Leviathan. Then who is able to stand against Me?
chapters.zh: 没有那么兇猛的人敢惹牠。 这样，谁能在我面前站立得住呢？

chapters.en: Who has given to Me that I should repay him? Everything under heaven is Mine.
chapters.zh: 谁先给我什么，使我偿还呢？ 天下〔万物〕都是我的。

chapters.en: I cannot keep silent about his limbs, his power and graceful form.
chapters.zh: 论到鳄鱼的肢体和其大力，并美好的骨骼， 我不能缄默不言。

chapters.en: Who can strip off his outer coat? Who can approach him with a bridle?
chapters.zh: 谁能剥牠的外衣？ 谁能进牠上下牙骨之间呢？

chapters.en: Who can open his jaws, ringed by his fearsome teeth?
chapters.zh: 谁能开牠的腮颊？ 牠牙齿四围是可畏的。

chapters.en: His rows of scales are his pride, tightly sealed together.
chapters.zh: 牠以坚固的鳞甲为可夸， 紧紧合闭，封得严密。

chapters.en: One scale is so near to another that no air can pass between them.
chapters.zh: 这鳞甲一一相连， 甚至气不得透入其间，

chapters.en: They are joined to one another; they clasp and cannot be separated.
chapters.zh: 都是互相联络、胶结， 不能分离。

chapters.en: His snorting flashes with light, and his eyes are like the rays of dawn.
chapters.zh: 牠打喷嚏就发出光来； 牠眼睛好像早晨的光线〔注：原文是眼皮〕。

chapters.en: Firebrands stream from his mouth; fiery sparks shoot forth!
chapters.zh: 从牠口中发出烧着的火把， 与飞迸的火星；

chapters.en: Smoke billows from his nostrils as from a boiling pot over burning reeds.
chapters.zh: 从牠鼻孔冒出烟来， 如烧开的锅和〔点着〕的芦苇。

chapters.en: His breath sets coals ablaze, and flames pour from his mouth.
chapters.zh: 牠的气点着煤炭， 有火焰从牠口中发出。

chapters.en: Strength resides in his neck, and dismay leaps before him.
chapters.zh: 牠颈项中存着劲力； 在牠面前的都恐吓蹦跳。

chapters.en: The folds of his flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable.
chapters.zh: 牠的肉块互相联络， 紧贴其身，不能摇动。

chapters.en: His chest is as hard as a rock, as hard as a lower millstone!
chapters.zh: 牠的心结实如石头， 如下磨石那样结实。

chapters.en: When Leviathan rises up, the mighty are terrified; they withdraw before his thrashing.
chapters.zh: 牠一起来，勇士都惊恐， 心里慌乱，便都昏迷。

chapters.en: The sword that reaches him has no effect, nor does the spear or dart or arrow.
chapters.zh: 人若用刀，用枪，用标枪， 用尖枪扎牠，都是无用。

chapters.en: He regards iron as straw and bronze as rotten wood.
chapters.zh: 牠以铁为干草， 以铜为烂木。

chapters.en: No arrow can make him flee; slingstones become like chaff to him.
chapters.zh: 箭不能〔恐吓牠〕使牠逃避； 弹石在牠看为碎诩。

chapters.en: A club is regarded as straw, and he laughs at the sound of the lance.
chapters.zh: 棍棒算为禾诩； 牠嗤笑短枪飕的响声。

chapters.en: His undersides are jagged potsherds, spreading out the mud like a threshing sledge.
chapters.zh: 牠肚腹下〔如〕尖瓦片； 牠如钉耙经过淤泥。

chapters.en: He makes the depths seethe like a cauldron; he makes the sea like a jar of ointment.
chapters.zh: 牠使深渊开滚如锅， 使洋海如锅中的膏油。

chapters.en: He leaves a glistening wake behind him; one would think the deep had white hair!
chapters.zh: 牠行的路随后发光， 令人想深渊如同白发。

chapters.en: Nothing on earth is his equal— a creature devoid of fear!
chapters.zh: 在地上没有像牠造的那样， 无所惧怕。

chapters.en: He looks down on all the haughty; he is king over all the proud.”
chapters.zh: 凡高大的，牠无不藐视； 牠在骄傲的水族上作王。

chapters.en: Then Job replied to the LORD:
chapters.zh: 约伯回答耶和华说：

chapters.en: “I know that You can do all things and that no plan of Yours can be thwarted.
chapters.zh: 我知道，你万事都能做； 你的旨意不能拦阻。

chapters.en: You asked, ‘Who is this who conceals My counsel without knowledge?’ Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, things too wonderful for me to know.
chapters.zh: 谁用无知的言语使〔你的〕旨意隐藏呢？ 我所说的是我不明白的； 这些事太奇妙，是我不知道的。

chapters.en: You said, ‘Listen now, and I will speak. I will question you, and you shall inform Me.’
chapters.zh: 求你听我，我要说话； 我问你，求你指示我。

chapters.en: My ears had heard of You, but now my eyes have seen You.
chapters.zh: 我从前风闻有你， 现在亲眼看见你。

chapters.en: Therefore I despise myself, and I repent in dust and ashes.”
chapters.zh: 因此我厌恶自己〔注：或译：我的言语〕， 在尘土和炉灰中懊悔。

chapters.en: After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, He said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you and your two friends. For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对约伯说话以后，就对提幔人以利法说：「我的怒气向你和你两个朋友发作，因为你们议论我不如我的仆人约伯说的是。

chapters.en: So now, take seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and sacrifice a burnt offering for yourselves. Then My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken accurately about Me, as My servant Job has.”
chapters.zh: 现在你们要取七只公牛，七只公羊，到我仆人约伯那里去，为自己献上燔祭，我的仆人约伯就为你们祈祷。我因悦纳他，就不按你们的愚妄办你们。你们议论我，不如我的仆人约伯说的是。」

chapters.en: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them; and the LORD accepted Job’s prayer.
chapters.zh: 于是提幔人以利法、书亚人比勒达、拿玛人琐法照着耶和华所吩咐的去行；耶和华就悦纳约伯。

chapters.en: After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions.
chapters.zh: 约伯为他的朋友祈祷。耶和华就使约伯从苦境〔注：原文是掳掠〕转回，并且耶和华赐给他的比他从前所有的加倍。

chapters.en: All his brothers and sisters and prior acquaintances came and dined with him in his house. They consoled him and comforted him over all the adversity that the LORD had brought upon him. And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.
chapters.zh: 约伯的弟兄、姊妹，和以先所认识的人都来见他，在他家里一同吃饭；又论到耶和华所降与他的一切灾祸，都为他悲伤安慰他。每人也送他一块〔银子〕和一个金环。

chapters.en: So the LORD blessed Job’s latter days more than his first. He owned 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.
chapters.zh: 这样，耶和华后来赐福给约伯比先前更多。他有一万四千羊，六千骆驼，一千对牛，一千母驴。

chapters.en: And he also had seven sons and three daughters.
chapters.zh: 他也有七个儿子，三个女儿。

chapters.en: He named his first daughter Jemimah, his second Keziah, and his third Keren-happuch.
chapters.zh: 他给长女起名叫耶米玛，次女叫基洗亚，三女叫基连‧哈朴。

chapters.en: No women as beautiful as Job’s daughters could be found in all the land, and their father granted them an inheritance among their brothers.
chapters.zh: 在那全地的妇女中找不着像约伯的女儿那样美貌。她们的父亲使她们在弟兄中得产业。

chapters.en: After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.
chapters.zh: 此后，约伯又活了一百四十年，得见他的儿孙，直到四代。

chapters.en: And so Job died, old and full of years.
chapters.zh: 这样，约伯年纪老迈，日子满足而死。

chapters.en: Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, or set foot on the path of sinners, or sit in the seat of mockers.
chapters.zh: 不从恶人的计谋， 不站罪人的道路， 不坐亵慢人的座位，

chapters.en: But his delight is in the Law of the LORD, and on His law he meditates day and night.
chapters.zh: 惟喜爱耶和华的律法， 昼夜思想， 这人便为有福！

chapters.en: He is like a tree planted by streams of water, yielding its fruit in season, whose leaf does not wither, and who prospers in all he does.
chapters.zh: 他要像一棵树栽在溪水旁， 按时候结果子， 叶子也不枯干。 凡他所做的尽都顺利。

chapters.en: Not so the wicked! For they are like chaff driven off by the wind.
chapters.zh: 恶人并不是这样， 乃像糠秕被风吹散。

chapters.en: Therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous.
chapters.zh: 因此，当审判的时候，恶人必站立不住； 罪人在义人的会中也是如此。

chapters.en: For the LORD guards the path of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish.
chapters.zh: 因为耶和华知道义人的道路； 恶人的道路却必灭亡。

chapters.en: Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?
chapters.zh: 外邦为什么争闹？ 万民为什么谋算虚妄的事？

chapters.en: The kings of the earth take their stand and the rulers gather together, against the LORD and against His Anointed One:
chapters.zh: 世上的君王一齐起来， 臣宰一同商议， 要敌挡耶和华并他的受膏者，

chapters.en: “Let us break Their chains and cast away Their cords.”
chapters.zh: 说：我们要挣开他们的捆绑， 脱去他们的绳索。

chapters.en: The One enthroned in heaven laughs; the Lord taunts them.
chapters.zh: 那坐在天上的必发笑； 主必嗤笑他们。

chapters.en: Then He rebukes them in His anger, and terrifies them in His fury:
chapters.zh: 那时，他要在怒中责备他们， 在烈怒中惊吓他们，

chapters.en: “I have installed My King on Zion, upon My holy mountain.”
chapters.zh: 说：我已经立我的君 在锡安－我的圣山上了。

chapters.en: I will proclaim the decree spoken to Me by the LORD: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.
chapters.zh: 〔受膏者说〕：我要传〔圣〕旨。 耶和华曾对我说：你是我的儿子， 我今日生你。

chapters.en: Ask Me, and I will make the nations Your inheritance, the ends of the earth Your possession.
chapters.zh: 你求我，我就将列国赐你为基业， 将地极赐你为田产。

chapters.en: You will break them with an iron scepter; You will shatter them like pottery. ”
chapters.zh: 你必用铁杖打破他们； 你必将他们如同窑匠的瓦器摔碎。

chapters.en: Therefore be wise, O kings; be admonished, O judges of the earth.
chapters.zh: 现在，你们君王应当省悟！ 你们世上的审判官该受管教！

chapters.en: Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
chapters.zh: 当存畏惧事奉耶和华， 又当存战兢而快乐。

chapters.en:
Kiss the Son, lest He be angry and you perish in your rebellion,
when His wrath ignites in an instant.
Blessed are all who take refuge in Him.
chapters.zh: 当以嘴亲子，恐怕他发怒， 你们便在道中灭亡， 因为他的怒气快要发作。 凡投靠他的，都是有福的。

chapters.en: O LORD, how my foes have increased! How many rise up against me!
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，我的敌人何其加增； 有许多人起来攻击我。

chapters.en: Many say of me, “God will not deliver him.” Selah
chapters.zh: 有许多人议论我说： 他得不着上帝的帮助。（细拉）

chapters.en: But You, O LORD, are a shield around me, my glory, and the One who lifts my head.
chapters.zh: 但你－耶和华是我四围的盾牌， 是我的荣耀，又是叫我抬起头来的。

chapters.en: To the LORD I cry aloud, and He answers me from His holy mountain. Selah
chapters.zh: 我用我的声音求告耶和华， 他就从他的圣山上应允我。（细拉）

chapters.en: I lie down and sleep; I wake again, for the LORD sustains me.
chapters.zh: 我躺下睡觉，我醒着， 耶和华都保佑我。

chapters.en: I will not fear the myriads set against me on every side.
chapters.zh: 虽有成万的百姓来周围攻击我， 我也不怕。

chapters.en: Arise, O LORD! Save me, O my God! Strike all my enemies on the jaw; break the teeth of the wicked.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你起来！ 我的上帝啊，求你救我！ 因为你打了我一切仇敌的腮骨， 敲碎了恶人的牙齿。

chapters.en: Salvation belongs to the LORD; may Your blessing be on Your people. Selah
chapters.zh: 救恩属乎耶和华； 愿你赐福给你的百姓。（细拉）

chapters.en: Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness! You have relieved my distress; show me grace and hear my prayer.
chapters.zh: 显我为义的上帝啊， 我呼吁的时候，求你应允我！ 我在困苦中，你曾使我宽广； 现在求你怜恤我，听我的祷告！

chapters.en: How long, O men, will my honor be maligned? How long will you love vanity and seek after lies ? Selah
chapters.zh: 你们这上流人哪，你们将我的尊荣变为羞辱〔要到几时呢〕？ 你们喜爱虚妄，寻找虚假，要到几时呢？（细拉）

chapters.en: Know that the LORD has set apart the godly for Himself; the LORD hears when I call to Him.
chapters.zh: 你们要知道，耶和华已经分别虔诚人归他自己； 我求告耶和华，他必听我。

chapters.en: Be angry, yet do not sin; on your bed, search your heart and be still. Selah
chapters.zh: 你们应当畏惧，不可犯罪； 在床上的时候，要心里思想，并要肃静。（细拉）

chapters.en: Offer the sacrifices of the righteous and trust in the LORD.
chapters.zh: 当献上公义的祭， 又当倚靠耶和华。

chapters.en: Many ask, “Who can show us the good?” Shine the light of Your face upon us, O LORD.
chapters.zh: 有许多人说：谁能指示我们什么好处？ 耶和华啊，求你仰起脸来，光照我们。

chapters.en: You have filled my heart with more joy than when grain and new wine abound.
chapters.zh: 你使我心里快乐， 胜过那丰收五谷新酒的人。

chapters.en: I will lie down and sleep in peace, for You alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety.
chapters.zh: 我必安然躺下睡觉， 因为独有你－耶和华使我安然居住。

chapters.en: Give ear to my words, O LORD; consider my groaning.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你留心听我的言语， 顾念我的心思！

chapters.en:
Attend to the sound of my cry, my King and my God,
for to You I pray.
chapters.zh: 我的王我的上帝啊，求你垂听我呼求的声音！ 因为我向你祈祷。

chapters.en:
In the morning, O LORD, You hear my voice; at daybreak I lay my plea before You
and wait in expectation.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，早晨你必听我的声音； 早晨我必向你陈明〔我的心意〕，并要警醒！

chapters.en: For You are not a God who delights in wickedness; no evil can dwell with You.
chapters.zh: 因为你不是喜悦恶事的上帝， 恶人不能与你同居。

chapters.en: The boastful cannot stand in Your presence; You hate all workers of iniquity.
chapters.zh: 狂傲人不能站在你眼前； 凡作孽的，都是你所恨恶的。

chapters.en: You destroy those who tell lies; the LORD abhors the man of bloodshed and deceit.
chapters.zh: 说谎言的，你必灭绝； 好流人血弄诡诈的，都为耶和华所憎恶。

chapters.en: But I will enter Your house by the abundance of Your loving devotion; in reverence I will bow down toward Your holy temple.
chapters.zh: 至于我，我必凭你丰盛的慈爱进入你的居所； 我必存敬畏你的心向你的圣殿下拜。

chapters.en:
Lead me, O LORD, in Your righteousness because of my enemies;
make straight Your way before me.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你因我的仇敌，凭你的公义引领我， 使你的道路在我面前正直。

chapters.en: For not a word they speak can be trusted; destruction lies within them. Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit.
chapters.zh: 因为，他们的口中没有诚实； 他们的心里满有邪恶； 他们的喉咙是敞开的坟墓； 他们用舌头谄媚人。

chapters.en: Declare them guilty, O God; let them fall by their own devices. Drive them out for their many transgressions, for they have rebelled against You.
chapters.zh: 上帝啊，求你定他们的罪！ 愿他们因自己的计谋跌倒； 愿你在他们许多的过犯中把他们逐出， 因为他们背叛了你。

chapters.en: But let all who take refuge in You rejoice; let them ever shout for joy. May You shelter them, that those who love Your name may rejoice in You.
chapters.zh: 凡投靠你的，愿他们喜乐，时常欢呼， 因为你护庇他们； 又愿那爱你名的人都靠你欢欣。

chapters.en: For surely You, O LORD, bless the righteous; You surround them with the shield of Your favor.
chapters.zh: 因为你必赐福与义人； 耶和华啊，你必用恩惠如同盾牌四面护卫他。

chapters.en: O LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger or discipline me in Your wrath.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你不要在怒中责备我， 也不要在烈怒中惩罚我！

chapters.en: Be merciful to me, O LORD, for I am frail; heal me, O LORD, for my bones are in agony.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你可怜我，因为我软弱。 耶和华啊，求你医治我，因为我的骨头发战。

chapters.en: My soul is deeply distressed. How long, O LORD, how long?
chapters.zh: 我心也大大地惊惶。 耶和华啊，你要到几时〔才救我〕呢？

chapters.en: Turn, O LORD, and deliver my soul; save me because of Your loving devotion.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你转回搭救我！ 因你的慈爱拯救我。

chapters.en: For there is no mention of You in death; who can praise You from Sheol?
chapters.zh: 因为，在死地无人记念你， 在阴间有谁称谢你？

chapters.en:
I am weary from groaning; all night I flood my bed with weeping
and drench my couch with tears.
chapters.zh: 我因唉哼而困乏； 我每夜流泪，把床榻漂起， 把褥子湿透。

chapters.en: My eyes fail from grief; they grow dim because of all my foes.
chapters.zh: 我因忧愁眼睛干瘪， 又因我一切的敌人眼睛昏花。

chapters.en: Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity, for the LORD has heard my weeping.
chapters.zh: 你们一切作孽的人，离开我吧！ 因为耶和华听了我哀哭的声音。

chapters.en: The LORD has heard my cry for mercy; the LORD accepts my prayer.
chapters.zh: 耶和华听了我的恳求； 耶和华必收纳我的祷告。

chapters.en: All my enemies will be ashamed and dismayed; they will turn back in sudden disgrace.
chapters.zh: 我的一切仇敌都必羞愧，大大惊惶； 他们必要退后，忽然羞愧。

chapters.en: O LORD my God, I take refuge in You; save me and deliver me from all my pursuers,
chapters.zh: 耶和华－我的上帝啊，我投靠你！ 求你救我脱离一切追赶我的人，将我救拔出来！

chapters.en: or they will shred my soul like a lion and tear me to pieces with no one to rescue me.
chapters.zh: 恐怕他们像狮子撕裂我， 甚至撕碎，无人搭救。

chapters.en: O LORD my God, if I have done this, if injustice is on my hands,
chapters.zh: 耶和华－我的上帝啊，我若行了这事， 若有罪孽在我手里，

chapters.en: if I have rewarded my ally with evil, if I have plundered my foe without cause,
chapters.zh: 我若以恶报那与我交好的人－ 连那无故与我为敌的，我也救了他，

chapters.en:
then may my enemy pursue me and overtake me; may he trample me to the ground
and leave my honor in the dust. Selah
chapters.zh: 就任凭仇敌追赶我，直到追上， 将我的性命踏在地下， 使我的荣耀归于灰尘。（细拉）

chapters.en:
Arise, O LORD, in Your anger; rise up against the fury of my enemies.
Awake, my God, and ordain judgment.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你在怒中起来， 挺身而立，抵挡我敌人的暴怒！ 求你为我兴起！你已经命定施行审判！

chapters.en: Let the assembled peoples gather around You; take Your seat over them on high.
chapters.zh: 愿众民的会环绕你！ 愿你从其上归于高位！

chapters.en:
The LORD judges the peoples; vindicate me, O LORD,
according to my righteousness and integrity.
chapters.zh: 耶和华向众民施行审判； 耶和华啊，求你按我的公义和我心中的纯正判断我。

chapters.en:
Put an end to the evil of the wicked, but establish the righteous,
O righteous God who searches hearts and minds.
chapters.zh: 愿恶人的恶断绝！ 愿你坚立义人！ 因为公义的上帝察验人的心肠肺腑。

chapters.en: My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.
chapters.zh: 上帝是我的盾牌； 他拯救心里正直的人。

chapters.en: God is a righteous judge and a God who feels indignation each day.
chapters.zh: 上帝是公义的审判者， 又是天天〔向恶人〕发怒的上帝。

chapters.en:
If one does not repent, God will sharpen His sword;
He has bent and strung His bow.
chapters.zh: 若有人不回头，他的刀必磨快， 弓必上弦，预备妥当了。

chapters.en: He has prepared His deadly weapons; He ordains His arrows with fire.
chapters.zh: 他也预备了杀人的器械； 他所射的是火〔箭〕。

chapters.en: Behold, the wicked man travails with evil; he conceives trouble and births falsehood.
chapters.zh: 试看恶人因奸恶而劬劳， 所怀的是毒害，所生的是虚假。

chapters.en: He has dug a hole and hollowed it out; he has fallen into a pit of his own making.
chapters.zh: 他掘了坑，又挖深了， 竟掉在自己所挖的阱里。

chapters.en: His trouble recoils on himself, and his violence falls on his own head.
chapters.zh: 他的毒害必临到他自己的头上； 他的强暴必落到他自己的脑袋上。

chapters.en: I will thank the LORD for His righteousness and sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.
chapters.zh: 我要照着耶和华的公义称谢他， 歌颂耶和华至高者的名。

chapters.en:
O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!
You have set Your glory above the heavens.
chapters.zh: 耶和华－我们的主啊， 你的名在全地何其美！ 你将你的荣耀彰显于天。

chapters.en: From the mouths of children and infants You have ordained praise on account of Your adversaries, to silence the enemy and avenger.
chapters.zh: 你因敌人的缘故， 从婴孩和吃奶的口中， 建立了能力， 使仇敌和报仇的闭口无言。

chapters.en: When I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars, which You have set in place—
chapters.zh: 我观看你指头所造的天， 并你所陈设的月亮星宿，

chapters.en: what is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?
chapters.zh: 〔便说〕：人算什么，你竟顾念他！ 世人算什么，你竟眷顾他！

chapters.en: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor.
chapters.zh: 你叫他比天使〔注：或译：上帝〕微小一点， 并赐他荣耀尊贵为冠冕。

chapters.en: You made him ruler of the works of Your hands; You have placed everything under his feet:
all sheep and oxen, and even the beasts of the field,
the birds of the air and the fish of the sea, all that swim the paths of the seas.
chapters.zh: 你派他管理你手所造的， 使万物，就是一切的牛羊、 田野的兽、空中的鸟、海里的鱼， 凡经行海道的，都服在他的脚下。

chapters.en: O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!
chapters.zh: 耶和华－我们的主啊， 你的名在全地何其美！

chapters.en: I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart; I will recount all Your wonders.
chapters.zh: 我要一心称谢耶和华； 我要传扬你一切奇妙的作为。

chapters.en: I will be glad and rejoice in You; I will sing praise to Your name, O Most High.
chapters.zh: 我要因你欢喜快乐； 至高者啊，我要歌颂你的名！

chapters.en: When my enemies retreat, they stumble and perish before You.
chapters.zh: 我的仇敌转身退去的时候， 他们一见你的面就跌倒灭亡。

chapters.en: For You have upheld my just cause; You sit on Your throne judging righteously.
chapters.zh: 因你已经为我伸冤，为我辨屈； 你坐在宝座上，按公义审判。

chapters.en:
You have rebuked the nations; You have destroyed the wicked;
You have erased their name forever and ever.
chapters.zh: 你曾斥责外邦，你曾灭绝恶人； 你曾涂抹他们的名，直到永永远远。

chapters.en:
The enemy has come to eternal ruin, and You have uprooted their cities;
the very memory of them has vanished.
chapters.zh: 仇敌到了尽头； 他们被毁坏，直到永远。 你拆毁他们的城邑， 连他们的名号都归于无有。

chapters.en: But the LORD abides forever; He has established His throne for judgment.
chapters.zh: 惟耶和华坐着〔为王〕，直到永远； 他已经为审判设摆他的宝座。

chapters.en: He judges the world with justice; He governs the people with equity.
chapters.zh: 他要按公义审判世界， 按正直判断万民。

chapters.en: The LORD is a refuge for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble.
chapters.zh: 耶和华又要给受欺压的人作高台， 在患难的时候作高台。

chapters.en: Those who know Your name trust in You, for You, O LORD, have not forsaken those who seek You.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，认识你名的人要倚靠你， 因你没有离弃寻求你的人。

chapters.en: Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion; proclaim His deeds among the nations.
chapters.zh: 应当歌颂居锡安的耶和华， 将他所行的传扬在众民中。

chapters.en: For the Avenger of bloodshed remembers; He does not ignore the cry of the afflicted.
chapters.zh: 因为那追讨流人血之罪的－他记念受屈的人， 不忘记困苦人的哀求。

chapters.en: Be merciful to me, O LORD; see how my enemies afflict me! Lift me up from the gates of death,
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，你是从死门把我提拔起来的； 求你怜恤我，看那恨我的人所加给我的苦难，

chapters.en: that I may declare all Your praises— that within the gates of Daughter Zion I may rejoice in Your salvation.
chapters.zh: 好叫我述说你一切的美德； 我必在锡安城〔注：原文是女子〕的门因你的救恩欢乐。

chapters.en: The nations have fallen into a pit of their making; their feet are caught in the net they have hidden.
chapters.zh: 外邦人陷在自己所掘的坑中； 他们的脚在自己暗设的网罗里缠住了。

chapters.en: The LORD is known by the justice He brings; the wicked are ensnared by the work of their hands. Higgaion Selah
chapters.zh: 耶和华已将自己显明了，他已施行审判； 恶人被自己手所做的缠住了 〔注：或译：他叫恶人被自己手所做的累住了〕。（细拉）

chapters.en: The wicked will return to Sheol— all the nations who forget God.
chapters.zh: 恶人，就是忘记上帝的外邦人， 都必归到阴间。

chapters.en: For the needy will not always be forgotten; nor the hope of the oppressed forever dashed.
chapters.zh: 穷乏人必不永久被忘； 困苦人的指望必不永远落空。

chapters.en: Rise up, O LORD, do not let man prevail; let the nations be judged in Your presence.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你起来，不容人得胜！ 愿外邦人在你面前受审判！

chapters.en: Lay terror upon them, O LORD; let the nations know they are but men. Selah
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你使外邦人恐惧； 愿他们知道自己不过是人。（细拉）

chapters.en: Why, O LORD, do You stand far off? Why do You hide in times of trouble?
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，你为什么站在远处？ 在患难的时候为什么隐藏？

chapters.en: In pride the wicked pursue the needy; let them be caught in the schemes they devise.
chapters.zh: 恶人在骄横中把困苦人追得火急； 愿他们陷在自己所设的计谋里。

chapters.en: For the wicked man boasts in the cravings of his heart; he blesses the greedy and reviles the LORD.
chapters.zh: 因为恶人以心愿自夸； 贪财的背弃耶和华，并且轻慢他〔注：或译：他祝福贪财的，却轻慢耶和华〕。

chapters.en: In his pride the wicked man does not seek Him; in all his schemes there is no God.
chapters.zh: 恶人面带骄傲，〔说〕：耶和华必不追究； 他一切所想的都以为没有上帝。

chapters.en:
He is secure in his ways at all times; Your lofty judgments are far from him;
he sneers at all his foes.
chapters.zh: 凡他所做的，时常稳固； 你的审判超过他的眼界。 至于他一切的敌人， 他都向他们喷气。

chapters.en: He says to himself, “I will not be moved; from age to age I am free of distress.”
chapters.zh: 他心里说：我必不动摇， 世世代代不遭灾难。

chapters.en: His mouth is full of cursing, deceit, and violence; trouble and malice are under his tongue.
chapters.zh: 他满口是咒骂、诡诈、欺压， 舌底是毒害、奸恶。

chapters.en:
He lies in wait near the villages; in ambush he slays the innocent;
his eyes watch in stealth for the helpless.
chapters.zh: 他在村庄埋伏等候； 他在隐密处杀害无辜的人。 他的眼睛窥探无倚无靠的人；

chapters.en:
He lies in wait like a lion in a thicket; he lurks to seize the oppressed;
he catches the lowly in his net.
chapters.zh: 他埋伏在暗地，如狮子蹲在洞中。 他埋伏，要掳去困苦人； 他拉网，就把困苦人掳去。

chapters.en: They are crushed and beaten down; the helpless fall prey to his strength.
chapters.zh: 他屈身蹲伏， 无倚无靠的人就倒在他爪牙〔注：爪牙：或译强暴人〕之下。

chapters.en: He says to himself, “God has forgotten; He hides His face and never sees.”
chapters.zh: 他心里说：上帝竟忘记了； 他掩面永不观看。

chapters.en: Arise, O LORD! Lift up Your hand, O God! Do not forget the helpless.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你起来！ 上帝啊，求你举手，不要忘记困苦人！

chapters.en: Why has the wicked man renounced God? He says to himself, “You will never call me to account.”
chapters.zh: 恶人为何轻慢上帝， 心里说：你必不追究？

chapters.en: But You have regarded trouble and grief; You see to repay it by Your hand. The victim entrusts himself to You; You are the helper of the fatherless.
chapters.zh: 〔其实〕你已经观看； 因为奸恶毒害，你都看见了， 为要以手施行报应。 无倚无靠的人把〔自己〕交讬你； 你向来是帮助孤儿的。

chapters.en:
Break the arm of the wicked and evildoer; call him to account for his wickedness
until none is left to be found.
chapters.zh: 愿你打断恶人的膀臂； 至于坏人，愿你追究他的恶，直到净尽。

chapters.en: The LORD is King forever and ever; the nations perish from His land.
chapters.zh: 耶和华永永远远为王； 外邦人从他的地已经灭绝了。

chapters.en: You have heard, O LORD, the desire of the humble; You will strengthen their hearts. You will incline Your ear,
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，谦卑人的心愿， 你早已知道〔注：原文是听见〕。 你必预备他们的心， 也必侧耳听他们〔的祈求〕，

chapters.en: to vindicate the fatherless and oppressed, that the men of the earth may strike terror no more.
chapters.zh: 为要给孤儿和受欺压的人伸冤， 使强横的人不再威吓他们。

chapters.en:
In the LORD I take refuge. How then can you say to me:
“Flee like a bird to your mountain!
chapters.zh: 我是投靠耶和华； 你们怎么对我说：你当像鸟飞往你的山去。

chapters.en: For behold, the wicked bend their bows. They set their arrow on the string to shoot from the shadows at the upright in heart.
chapters.zh: 看哪，恶人弯弓，把箭搭在弦上， 要在暗中射那心里正直的人。

chapters.en: If the foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do?”
chapters.zh: 根基若毁坏， 义人还能做什么呢？

chapters.en: The LORD is in His holy temple; the LORD is on His heavenly throne. His eyes are watching closely; they examine the sons of men.
chapters.zh: 耶和华在他的圣殿里； 耶和华的宝座在天上； 他的慧眼察看世人。

chapters.en: The LORD tests the righteous and the wicked; His soul hates the lover of violence.
chapters.zh: 耶和华试验义人； 惟有恶人和喜爱强暴的人，他心里恨恶。

chapters.en: On the wicked He will rain down fiery coals and sulfur; a scorching wind will be their portion.
chapters.zh: 他要向恶人密布网罗； 有烈火、硫磺、热风，作他们杯中的分。

chapters.en: For the LORD is righteous; He loves justice. The upright will see His face.
chapters.zh: 因为耶和华是公义的，他喜爱公义； 正直人必得见他的面。

chapters.en: Help, O LORD, for the godly are no more; the faithful have vanished from among men.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你帮助，因虔诚人断绝了； 世人中间的忠信人没有了。

chapters.en: They lie to one another; they speak with flattering lips and a double heart.
chapters.zh: 人人向邻舍说谎； 他们说话，是嘴唇油滑，心口不一。

chapters.en: May the LORD cut off all flattering lips and every boastful tongue.
chapters.zh: 凡油滑的嘴唇和夸大的舌头， 耶和华必要剪除。

chapters.en: They say, “With our tongues we will prevail. We own our lips—who can be our master?”
chapters.zh: 他们曾说：我们必能以舌头得胜； 我们的嘴唇是我们自己的， 谁能作我们的主呢？

chapters.en: “For the cause of the oppressed and for the groaning of the needy, I will now arise,” says the LORD. “I will bring safety to him who yearns.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华说：因为困苦人的冤屈 和贫穷人的叹息， 我现在要起来， 把他安置在他所切慕的稳妥之地。

chapters.en:
The words of the LORD are flawless, like silver refined in a furnace,
like gold purified sevenfold.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的言语是纯净的言语， 如同银子在泥炉中炼过七次。

chapters.en: You, O LORD, will keep us; You will forever guard us from this generation.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，你必保护他们； 你必保佑他们永远脱离这世代的人。

chapters.en: The wicked wander freely, and vileness is exalted among men.
chapters.zh: 下流人在世人中升高， 就有恶人到处游行。

chapters.en:
How long, O LORD? Will You forget me forever?
How long will You hide Your face from me?
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，你忘记我要到几时呢？要到永远吗？ 你掩面不顾我要到几时呢？

chapters.en:
How long must I wrestle in my soul, with sorrow in my heart each day?
How long will my enemy dominate me?
chapters.zh: 我心里筹算，终日愁苦，要到几时呢？ 我的仇敌升高压制我，要到几时呢？

chapters.en: Consider me and respond, O LORD my God. Give light to my eyes, lest I sleep in death,
chapters.zh: 耶和华－我的上帝啊，求你看顾我，应允我！ 使我眼目光明，免得我沉睡至死；

chapters.en: lest my enemy say, “I have overcome him,” and my foes rejoice when I fall.
chapters.zh: 免得我的仇敌说：我胜了他； 免得我的敌人在我摇动的时候喜乐。

chapters.en: But I have trusted in Your loving devotion; my heart will rejoice in Your salvation.
chapters.zh: 但我倚靠你的慈爱； 我的心因你的救恩快乐。

chapters.en: I will sing to the LORD, for He has been good to me.
chapters.zh: 我要向耶和华歌唱， 因他用厚恩待我。

chapters.en:
The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.”
They are corrupt; their acts are vile. There is no one who does good.
chapters.zh: 愚顽人心里说：没有上帝。 他们都是邪恶，行了可憎恶的事； 没有一个人行善。

chapters.en: The LORD looks down from heaven upon the sons of men to see if any understand, if any seek God.
chapters.zh: 耶和华从天上垂看世人， 要看有明白的没有， 有寻求上帝的没有。

chapters.en: All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
chapters.zh: 他们都偏离正路， 一同变为污秽； 并没有行善的， 连一个也没有。

chapters.en:
Will the workers of iniquity never learn?
They devour my people like bread; they refuse to call upon the LORD.
chapters.zh: 作孽的都没有知识吗？ 他们吞吃我的百姓，〔如同〕吃饭一样， 并不求告耶和华。

chapters.en: There they are, overwhelmed with dread, for God is in the company of the righteous.
chapters.zh: 他们在那里大大地害怕， 因为上帝在义人的族类中。

chapters.en: You sinners frustrate the plans of the oppressed, yet the LORD is their shelter.
chapters.zh: 你们叫困苦人的谋算变为羞辱； 然而耶和华是他的避难所。

chapters.en:
Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion!
When the LORD restores His captive people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad!
chapters.zh: 但愿以色列的救恩从锡安而出。 耶和华救回他被掳的子民那时， 雅各要快乐，以色列要欢喜。

chapters.en: O LORD, who may abide in Your tent? Who may dwell on Your holy mountain?
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，谁能寄居你的帐幕？ 谁能住在你的圣山？

chapters.en:
He who walks with integrity and practices righteousness,
who speaks the truth from his heart,
chapters.zh: 就是行为正直、做事公义、 心里说实话的人。

chapters.en:
who has no slander on his tongue, who does no harm to his neighbor,
who casts no scorn on his friend,
chapters.zh: 他不以舌头谗谤人， 不恶待朋友， 也不随伙毁谤邻里。

chapters.en:
who despises the vile but honors those who fear the LORD,
who does not revise a costly oath,
chapters.zh: 他眼中藐视匪类， 却尊重那敬畏耶和华的人。 他发了誓，虽然自己吃亏也不更改。

chapters.en:
who lends his money without interest and refuses a bribe against the innocent.
He who does these things will never be shaken.
chapters.zh: 他不放债取利， 不受贿赂以害无辜。 行这些事的人必永不动摇。

chapters.en: Preserve me, O God, for in You I take refuge.
chapters.zh: 上帝啊，求你保佑我， 因为我投靠你。

chapters.en: I said to the LORD, “You are my Lord; apart from You I have no good thing.”
chapters.zh: 〔我的心哪〕，你曾对耶和华说：你是我的主； 我的好处不在你以外。

chapters.en:
As for the saints in the land, they are the excellence
in whom all my delight resides.
chapters.zh: 论到世上的圣民，他们又美又善， 是我最喜悦的。

chapters.en: Sorrows will multiply to those who chase other gods. I will not pour out their libations of blood, or speak their names with my lips.
chapters.zh: 以别〔神〕代替〔耶和华〕的〔注：或译：送礼物给别神的〕， 他们的愁苦必加增； 他们所浇奠的血我不献上； 我嘴唇也不提别神的名号。

chapters.en: The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup; You have made my lot secure.
chapters.zh: 耶和华是我的产业， 是我杯中的分； 我所得的，你为我持守。

chapters.en: The lines of my boundary have fallen in pleasant places; surely my inheritance is delightful.
chapters.zh: 用绳量给我的地界，坐落在佳美之处； 我的产业实在美好。

chapters.en: I will bless the LORD who counsels me; even at night my conscience instructs me.
chapters.zh: 我必称颂那指教我的耶和华； 我的心肠在夜间也警戒我。

chapters.en: I have set the LORD always before me. Because He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
chapters.zh: 我将耶和华常摆在我面前， 因他在我右边，我便不致摇动。

chapters.en: Therefore my heart is glad and my tongue rejoices; my body also will dwell securely.
chapters.zh: 因此，我的心欢喜，我的灵〔注：原文是荣耀〕快乐； 我的肉身也要安然居住。

chapters.en: For You will not abandon my soul to Sheol, nor will You let Your Holy One see decay.
chapters.zh: 因为你必不将我的灵魂撇在阴间， 也不叫你的圣者见朽坏。

chapters.en:
You have made known to me the path of life; You will fill me with joy in Your presence,
with eternal pleasures at Your right hand.
chapters.zh: 你必将生命的道路指示我。 在你面前有满足的喜乐； 在你右手中有永远的福乐。

chapters.en: Hear, O LORD, my righteous plea; listen to my cry. Give ear to my prayer— it comes from lips free of deceit.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你听闻公义， 侧耳听我的呼吁！ 求你留心听我这不出于诡诈嘴唇的祈祷！

chapters.en: May my vindication come from Your presence; may Your eyes see what is right.
chapters.zh: 愿我的判语从你面前发出； 愿你的眼睛观看公正。

chapters.en: You have tried my heart; You have visited me in the night. You have tested me and found no evil; I have resolved not to sin with my mouth.
chapters.zh: 你已经试验我的心； 你在夜间鉴察我； 你熬炼我，却找不着什么； 我立志叫我口中没有过失。

chapters.en:
As for the deeds of men— by the word of Your lips
I have avoided the ways of the violent.
chapters.zh: 论到人的行为，我藉着你嘴唇的言语自己谨守， 不行强暴人的道路。

chapters.en: My steps have held to Your paths; my feet have not slipped.
chapters.zh: 我的脚踏定了你的路径； 我的两脚未曾滑跌。

chapters.en: I call on You, O God, for You will answer me. Incline Your ear to me; hear my words.
chapters.zh: 上帝啊，我曾求告你，因为你必应允我； 求你向我侧耳，听我的言语。

chapters.en:
Show the wonders of Your loving devotion, You who save by Your right hand
those who seek refuge from their foes.
chapters.zh: 求你显出你奇妙的慈爱来； 你是那用右手拯救投靠你的脱离起来攻击他们的人。

chapters.en: Keep me as the apple of Your eye; hide me in the shadow of Your wings
chapters.zh: 求你保护我，如同保护眼中的瞳人； 将我隐藏在你翅膀的荫下，

chapters.en: from the wicked who assail me, from my mortal enemies who surround me.
chapters.zh: 使我脱离那欺压我的恶人， 就是围困我要害我命的仇敌。

chapters.en: They have closed their callous hearts; their mouths speak with arrogance.
chapters.zh: 他们的心被脂油包裹； 他们用口说骄傲的话。

chapters.en: They have tracked us down, and now surround us; their eyes are set to cast us to the ground,
chapters.zh: 他们围困了我们的脚步； 他们瞪着眼，要把我们推倒在地。

chapters.en: like a lion greedy for prey, like a young lion lurking in ambush.
chapters.zh: 他像狮子急要抓食， 又像少壮狮子蹲伏在暗处。

chapters.en: Arise, O LORD, confront them! Bring them to their knees; deliver me from the wicked by Your sword,
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你起来，前去迎敌，将他打倒！ 用你的刀救护我命脱离恶人。

chapters.en: from such men, O LORD, by Your hand— from men of the world whose portion is in this life. May You fill the bellies of Your treasured ones and satisfy their sons, so they leave their abundance to their children.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，求你用手救我脱离〔世〕人， 脱离那只在今生有福分的世人！ 你把你的财宝充满他们的肚腹； 他们因有儿女就心满意足， 将其余的财物留给他们的婴孩。

chapters.en: As for me, I will behold Your face in righteousness; when I awake, I will be satisfied in Your presence.
chapters.zh: 至于我，我必在义中见你的面； 我醒了的时候，得见〔注：或译：着〕你的形像就心满意足了。

chapters.en: I love You, O LORD, my strength.
chapters.zh: 耶和华，我的力量啊，我爱你！

chapters.en: The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer. My God is my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold.
chapters.zh: 耶和华是我的巖石，我的山寨，我的救主， 我的上帝，我的磐石，我所投靠的。 他是我的盾牌， 是拯救我的角，是我的高台。

chapters.en: I will call upon the LORD, who is worthy to be praised; so shall I be saved from my enemies.
chapters.zh: 我要求告当赞美的耶和华； 这样我必从仇敌手中被救出来。

chapters.en: The cords of death encompassed me; the torrents of chaos overwhelmed me.
chapters.zh: 曾有死亡的绳索缠绕我， 匪类的急流使我惊惧，

chapters.en: The cords of Sheol entangled me; the snares of death confronted me.
chapters.zh: 阴间的绳索缠绕我， 死亡的网罗临到我。

chapters.en: In my distress I called upon the LORD; I cried to my God for help. From His temple He heard my voice, and my cry for His help reached His ears.
chapters.zh: 我在急难中求告耶和华， 向我的上帝呼求。 他从殿中听了我的声音； 我在他面前的呼求入了他的耳中。

chapters.en:
Then the earth shook and quaked, and the foundations of the mountains trembled;
they were shaken because He burned with anger.
chapters.zh: 那时，因他发怒，地就摇撼战抖； 山的根基也震动摇撼。

chapters.en:
Smoke rose from His nostrils, and consuming fire came from His mouth;
glowing coals blazed forth.
chapters.zh: 从他鼻孔冒烟上腾； 从他口中发火焚烧，连炭也着了。

chapters.en: He parted the heavens and came down with dark clouds beneath His feet.
chapters.zh: 他又使天下垂，亲自降临， 有黑云在他脚下。

chapters.en: He mounted a cherub and flew; He soared on the wings of the wind.
chapters.zh: 他坐着基路伯飞行； 他藉着风的翅膀快飞。

chapters.en: He made darkness His hiding place, and storm clouds a canopy around Him.
chapters.zh: 他以黑暗为藏身之处， 以水的黑暗、天空的厚云为他四围的行宫。

chapters.en:
From the brightness of His presence His clouds advanced—
hailstones and coals of fire.
chapters.zh: 因他面前的光辉， 他的厚云行过便有冰雹火炭。

chapters.en:
The LORD thundered from heaven; the voice of the Most High resounded—
hailstones and coals of fire.
chapters.zh: 耶和华也在天上打雷； 至高者发出声音便有冰雹火炭。

chapters.en: He shot His arrows and scattered the foes; He hurled lightning and routed them.
chapters.zh: 他射出箭来，使仇敌四散； 多多发出闪电，使他们扰乱。

chapters.en: The channels of the sea appeared, and the foundations of the world were exposed, at Your rebuke, O LORD, at the blast of the breath of Your nostrils.
chapters.zh: 耶和华啊，你的斥责一发， 你鼻孔的气一出， 海底就出现， 大地的根基也显露。

chapters.en: He reached down from on high and took hold of me; He drew me out of deep waters.
chapters.zh: 他从高天伸手抓住我， 把我从大水中拉上来。

chapters.en: He rescued me from my powerful enemy, from foes too mighty for me.
chapters.zh: 他救我脱离我的劲敌和那些恨我的人， 因为他们比我强盛。

chapters.en: They confronted me in my day of calamity, but the LORD was my support.
chapters.zh: 我遭遇灾难的日子，他们来攻击我； 但耶和华是我的倚靠。

chapters.en: He brought me out into the open; He rescued me because He delighted in me.
chapters.zh: 他又领我到宽阔之处； 他救拔我，因他喜悦我。

chapters.en: The LORD has rewarded me according to my righteousness; He has repaid me according to the cleanness of my hands.
chapters.zh: 耶和华按着我的公义报答我， 按着我手中的清洁赏赐我。

chapters.en: For I have kept the ways of the LORD and have not wickedly departed from my God.
chapters.zh: 因为我遵守了耶和华的道， 未曾作恶离开我的上帝。

chapters.en: For all His ordinances are before me; I have not disregarded His statutes.
chapters.zh: 他的一切典章常在我面前； 他的律例我也未曾丢弃。

chapters.en: And I have been blameless before Him and kept myself from iniquity.
chapters.zh: 我在他面前作了完全人； 我也保守自己远离我的罪孽。

chapters.en: So the LORD has repaid me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in His sight.
chapters.zh: 所以，耶和华按我的公义， 按我在他眼前手中的清洁偿还我。

chapters.en: To the faithful You show Yourself faithful, to the blameless You show Yourself blameless;
chapters.zh: 慈爱的人，你以慈爱待他； 完全的人，你以完全待他。

chapters.en: to the pure You show Yourself pure, but to the crooked You show Yourself shrewd.
