chapters.en: Long life is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor.
chapters.zh: 她右手有长寿， 左手有富贵。

chapters.en: All her ways are pleasant, and all her paths are peaceful.
chapters.zh: 她的道是安乐； 她的路全是平安。

chapters.en: She is a tree of life to those who embrace her, and those who lay hold of her are blessed.
chapters.zh: 她与持守她的作生命树； 持定她的，俱各有福。

chapters.en: The LORD founded the earth by wisdom and established the heavens by understanding.
chapters.zh: 耶和华以智慧立地， 以聪明定天，

chapters.en: By His knowledge the watery depths were broken open, and the clouds dripped with dew.
chapters.zh: 以知识使深渊裂开， 使天空滴下甘露。

chapters.en: My son, do not lose sight of this: Preserve sound judgment and discernment.
chapters.zh: 我儿，要谨守真智慧和谋略， 不可使她离开你的眼目。

chapters.en: They will be life to your soul and adornment to your neck.
chapters.zh: 这样，她必作你的生命， 颈项的美饰。

chapters.en: Then you will go on your way in safety, and your foot will not stumble.
chapters.zh: 你就坦然行路， 不致碰脚。

chapters.en: When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet.
chapters.zh: 你躺下，必不惧怕； 你躺卧，睡得香甜。

chapters.en: Do not fear sudden danger or the ruin that overtakes the wicked,
chapters.zh: 忽然来的惊恐，不要害怕； 恶人遭毁灭，也不要恐惧。

chapters.en: for the LORD will be your confidence and will keep your foot from the snare.
chapters.zh: 因为耶和华是你所倚靠的； 他必保守你的脚不陷入网罗。

chapters.en: Do not withhold good from the deserving when it is within your power to act.
chapters.zh: 你手若有行善的力量，不可推辞， 就当向那应得的人施行。

chapters.en:
Do not tell your neighbor, “Come back tomorrow and I will provide”—
when you already have the means.
chapters.zh: 你那里若有现成的，不可对邻舍说： 去吧，明天再来，我必给你。

chapters.en: Do not devise evil against your neighbor, for he trustfully dwells beside you.
chapters.zh: 你的邻舍既在你附近安居， 你不可设计害他。

chapters.en: Do not accuse a man without cause, when he has done you no harm.
chapters.zh: 人未曾加害与你， 不可无故与他相争。

chapters.en: Do not envy a violent man or choose any of his ways;
chapters.zh: 不可嫉妒强暴的人， 也不可选择他所行的路。

chapters.en: for the LORD detests the perverse, but He is a friend to the upright.
chapters.zh: 因为，乖僻人为耶和华所憎恶； 正直人为他所亲密。

chapters.en: The curse of the LORD is on the house of the wicked, but He blesses the home of the righteous.
chapters.zh: 耶和华咒诅恶人的家庭， 赐福与义人的居所。

chapters.en: He mocks the mockers, but gives grace to the humble.
chapters.zh: 他讥诮那好讥诮的人， 赐恩给谦卑的人。

chapters.en: The wise will inherit honor, but fools are held up to shame.
chapters.zh: 智慧人必承受尊荣； 愚昧人高升也成为羞辱。

chapters.en: Listen, my sons, to a father’s instruction; pay attention and gain understanding.
chapters.zh: 众子啊，要听父亲的教训， 留心得知聪明。

chapters.en: For I give you sound teaching; do not abandon my directive.
chapters.zh: 因我所给你们的是好教训； 不可离弃我的法则〔注：或译：指教〕。

chapters.en: When I was a son to my father, tender and the only child of my mother,
chapters.zh: 我在父亲面前为孝子， 在母亲眼中为独一的娇儿。

chapters.en:
he taught me and said, “Let your heart lay hold of my words;
keep my commands and you will live.
chapters.zh: 父亲教训我说：你心要存记我的言语， 遵守我的命令，便得存活。

chapters.en: Get wisdom, get understanding; do not forget my words or turn from them.
chapters.zh: 要得智慧，要得聪明，不可忘记， 也不可偏离我口中的言语。

chapters.en: Do not forsake wisdom, and she will preserve you; love her, and she will guard you.
chapters.zh: 不可离弃智慧，智慧就护卫你； 要爱她，她就保守你。

chapters.en: Wisdom is supreme; so acquire wisdom. And whatever you may acquire, gain understanding.
chapters.zh: 智慧为首； 〔所以〕，要得智慧。 在你一切所得之内必得聪明〔注：或译：用你一切所得的去换聪明〕。

chapters.en: Prize her, and she will exalt you; if you embrace her, she will honor you.
chapters.zh: 高举智慧，她就使你高升； 怀抱智慧，她就使你尊荣。

chapters.en: She will set a garland of grace on your head; she will present you with a crown of beauty.”
chapters.zh: 她必将华冠加在你头上， 把荣冕交给你。

chapters.en: Listen, my son, and receive my words, and the years of your life will be many.
chapters.zh: 我儿，你要听受我的言语， 就必延年益寿。

chapters.en: I will guide you in the way of wisdom; I will lead you on straight paths.
chapters.zh: 我已指教你走智慧的道， 引导你行正直的路。

chapters.en: When you walk, your steps will not be impeded; when you run, you will not stumble.
chapters.zh: 你行走，脚步必不致狭窄； 你奔跑，也不致跌倒。

chapters.en: Hold on to instruction; do not let go. Guard it, for it is your life.
chapters.zh: 要持定训诲，不可放松； 必当谨守，因为它是你的生命。

chapters.en: Do not set foot on the path of the wicked or walk in the way of evildoers.
chapters.zh: 不可行恶人的路； 不要走坏人的道。

chapters.en: Avoid it; do not travel on it. Turn from it and pass on by.
chapters.zh: 要躲避，不可经过； 要转身而去。

chapters.en: For they cannot sleep unless they do evil; they are deprived of slumber until they make someone fall.
chapters.zh: 这等人若不行恶，不得睡觉； 不使人跌倒，睡卧不安；

chapters.en: For they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence.
chapters.zh: 因为他们以奸恶吃饼， 以强暴喝酒。

chapters.en: The path of the righteous is like the first gleam of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until midday.
chapters.zh: 但义人的路好像黎明的光， 越照越明，直到日午。

chapters.en: But the way of the wicked is like the darkest gloom; they do not know what makes them stumble.
chapters.zh: 恶人的道好像幽暗， 自己不知因什么跌倒。

chapters.en: My son, pay attention to my words; incline your ear to my sayings.
chapters.zh: 我儿，要留心听我的言词， 侧耳听我的话语，

chapters.en: Do not lose sight of them; keep them within your heart.
chapters.zh: 都不可离你的眼目， 要存记在你心中。

chapters.en: For they are life to those who find them, and health to the whole body.
chapters.zh: 因为得着它的，就得了生命， 又得了医全体的良药。

chapters.en: Guard your heart with all diligence, for from it flow springs of life.
chapters.zh: 你要保守你心，胜过保守一切〔注：或译：你要切切保守你心〕， 因为一生的果效是由心发出。

chapters.en: Put away deception from your mouth; keep your lips from perverse speech.
chapters.zh: 你要除掉邪僻的口， 弃绝乖谬的嘴。

chapters.en: Let your eyes look forward; fix your gaze straight ahead.
chapters.zh: 你的眼目要向前正看； 你的眼睛〔注：原文是皮〕当向前直观。

chapters.en: Make a level path for your feet, and all your ways will be sure.
chapters.zh: 要修平你脚下的路， 坚定你一切的道。

chapters.en: Do not swerve to the right or to the left; turn your feet away from evil.
chapters.zh: 不可偏向左右； 要使你的脚离开邪恶。

chapters.en: My son, pay attention to my wisdom; incline your ear to my insight,
chapters.zh: 我儿，要留心我智慧的话语， 侧耳听我聪明的言词，

chapters.en: that you may maintain discretion and your lips may preserve knowledge.
chapters.zh: 为要使你谨守谋略， 嘴唇保存知识。

chapters.en: Though the lips of the forbidden woman drip honey and her speech is smoother than oil,
chapters.zh: 因为淫妇的嘴滴下蜂蜜； 她的口比油更滑，

chapters.en: in the end she is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a double-edged sword.
chapters.zh: 至终却苦似茵蔯， 快如两刃的刀。

chapters.en: Her feet go down to death; her steps lead straight to Sheol.
chapters.zh: 她的脚下入死地； 她脚步踏住阴间，

chapters.en: She does not consider the path of life; she does not know that her ways are unstable.
chapters.zh: 以致她找不着生命平坦的道。 她的路变迁不定， 自己还不知道。

chapters.en: So now, my sons, listen to me, and do not turn aside from the words of my mouth.
chapters.zh: 众子啊，现在要听从我； 不可离弃我口中的话。

chapters.en: Keep your path far from her; do not go near the door of her house,
chapters.zh: 你所行的道要离她远， 不可就近她的房门，

chapters.en: lest you concede your vigor to others, and your years to one who is cruel;
chapters.zh: 恐怕将你的尊荣给别人， 将你的岁月给残忍的人；

chapters.en: lest strangers feast on your wealth, and your labors enrich the house of a foreigner.
chapters.zh: 恐怕外人满得你的力量， 你劳碌得来的，归入外人的家；

chapters.en: At the end of your life you will groan when your flesh and your body are spent,
chapters.zh: 终久，你皮肉和身体消毁， 你就悲叹，

chapters.en: and you will say, “How I hated discipline, and my heart despised reproof!
chapters.zh: 说：我怎么恨恶训诲， 心中藐视责备，

chapters.en: I did not listen to the voice of my teachers or incline my ear to my mentors.
chapters.zh: 也不听从我师傅的话， 又不侧耳听那教训我的人？

chapters.en: I am on the brink of utter ruin in the midst of the whole assembly.”
chapters.zh: 我在〔圣〕会里， 几乎落在诸般恶中。

chapters.en: Drink water from your own cistern, and running water from your own well.
chapters.zh: 你要喝自己池中的水， 饮自己井里的活水。

chapters.en: Why should your springs flow in the streets, your streams of water in the public squares?
chapters.zh: 你的泉源岂可涨溢在外？ 你的河水岂可流在街上？

chapters.en: Let them be yours alone, never to be shared with strangers.
chapters.zh: 惟独归你一人， 不可与外人同用。

chapters.en: May your fountain be blessed, and may you rejoice in the wife of your youth:
chapters.zh: 要使你的泉源蒙福； 要喜悦你幼年所娶的妻。

chapters.en:
A loving doe, a graceful fawn— may her breasts satisfy you always;
may you be captivated by her love forever.
chapters.zh: 她如可爱的麀鹿，可喜的母鹿； 愿她的胸怀使你时时知足， 她的爱情使你常常恋慕。

chapters.en: Why be captivated, my son, by an adulteress, or embrace the bosom of a stranger?
chapters.zh: 我儿，你为何恋慕淫妇？ 为何抱外女的胸怀？

chapters.en: For a man’s ways are before the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD examines all his paths.
chapters.zh: 因为，人所行的道都在耶和华眼前； 他也修平人一切的路。

chapters.en: The iniquities of a wicked man entrap him; the cords of his sin entangle him.
chapters.zh: 恶人必被自己的罪孽捉住； 他必被自己的罪恶如绳索缠绕。

chapters.en: He dies for lack of discipline, led astray by his own great folly.
chapters.zh: 他因不受训诲就必死亡； 又因愚昧过甚，必走差了路。

chapters.en: My son, if you have put up security for your neighbor, if you have struck hands in pledge with a stranger,
chapters.zh: 我儿，你若为朋友作保， 替外人击掌，

chapters.en: if you have been trapped by the words of your lips, ensnared by the words of your mouth,
chapters.zh: 你就被口中的话语缠住， 被嘴里的言语捉住。

chapters.en: then do this, my son, to free yourself, for you have fallen into your neighbor’s hands: Go, humble yourself, and press your plea with your neighbor.
chapters.zh: 我儿，你既落在朋友手中， 就当这样行才可救自己： 你要自卑，去恳求你的朋友。

chapters.en: Allow no sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids.
chapters.zh: 不要容你的眼睛睡觉； 不要容你的眼皮打盹。

chapters.en: Free yourself, like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler.
chapters.zh: 要救自己，如鹿脱离〔猎户的〕手， 如鸟脱离捕鸟人的手。

chapters.en: Walk in the manner of the ant, O slacker; observe its ways and become wise.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人哪， 你去察看蚂蚁的动作就可得智慧。

chapters.en: Without a commander, without an overseer or ruler,
chapters.zh: 蚂蚁没有元帅， 没有官长，没有君王，

chapters.en: it prepares its provisions in summer; it gathers its food at harvest.
chapters.zh: 尚且在夏天预备食物， 在收割时聚敛粮食。

chapters.en: How long will you lie there, O slacker? When will you get up from your sleep?
chapters.zh: 懒惰人哪，你要睡到几时呢？ 你何时睡醒呢？

chapters.en: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,
chapters.zh: 再睡片时，打盹片时， 抱着手躺卧片时，

chapters.en: and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit.
chapters.zh: 你的贫穷就必如强盗速来， 你的缺乏仿佛拿兵器的人来到。

chapters.en: A worthless person, a wicked man, walks with a perverse mouth,
chapters.zh: 无赖的恶徒， 行动就用乖僻的口，

chapters.en: winking his eyes, speaking with his feet, and pointing with his fingers.
chapters.zh: 用眼传神， 用脚示意， 用指点划，

chapters.en: With deceit in his heart he devises evil; he continually sows discord.
chapters.zh: 心中乖僻， 常设恶谋， 布散纷争。

chapters.en: Therefore calamity will come upon him suddenly; in an instant he will be shattered beyond recovery.
chapters.zh: 所以，灾难必忽然临到他身； 他必顷刻败坏，无法可治。

chapters.en: There are six things that the LORD hates, seven that are detestable to Him:
chapters.zh: 耶和华所恨恶的有六样， 连他心所憎恶的共有七样：

chapters.en:
haughty eyes,
a lying tongue,
hands that shed innocent blood,
chapters.zh: 就是高傲的眼， 撒谎的舌， 流无辜人血的手，

chapters.en:
a heart that devises wicked schemes,
feet that run swiftly to evil,
chapters.zh: 图谋恶计的心， 飞跑行恶的脚，

chapters.en:
a false witness who gives false testimony,
and one who stirs up discord among brothers.
chapters.zh: 吐谎言的假见证， 并弟兄中布散纷争的人。

chapters.en: My son, keep your father’s commandment, and do not forsake your mother’s teaching.
chapters.zh: 我儿，要谨守你父亲的诫命； 不可离弃你母亲的法则〔注：或译：指教〕，

chapters.en: Bind them always upon your heart; tie them around your neck.
chapters.zh: 要常系在你心上， 挂在你项上。

chapters.en:
When you walk, they will guide you; when you lie down, they will watch over you;
when you awake, they will speak to you.
chapters.zh: 你行走，它必引导你； 你躺卧，它必保守你； 你睡醒，它必与你谈论。

chapters.en: For this commandment is a lamp, this teaching is a light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way to life,
chapters.zh: 因为诫命是灯，法则〔注：或译：指教〕是光， 训诲的责备是生命的道，

chapters.en: to keep you from the evil woman, from the smooth tongue of the adulteress.
chapters.zh: 能保你远离恶妇， 远离外女谄媚的舌头。

chapters.en: Do not lust in your heart for her beauty or let her captivate you with her eyes.
chapters.zh: 你心中不要恋慕她的美色， 也不要被她眼皮勾引。

chapters.en: For the levy of the prostitute is poverty, and the adulteress preys upon your very life.
chapters.zh: 因为，妓女〔能使人〕只剩一块饼； 淫妇猎取人宝贵的生命。

chapters.en: Can a man embrace fire and his clothes not be burned?
chapters.zh: 人若怀里搋火， 衣服岂能不烧呢？

chapters.en: Can a man walk on hot coals without scorching his feet?
chapters.zh: 人若在火炭上走， 脚岂能不烫呢？

chapters.en: So is he who sleeps with another man’s wife; no one who touches her will go unpunished.
chapters.zh: 亲近邻舍之妻的，也是如此； 凡挨近她的，不免受罚。

chapters.en: Men do not despise the thief if he steals to satisfy his hunger.
chapters.zh: 贼因饥饿偷窃充饥， 人不藐视他，

chapters.en: Yet if caught, he must pay sevenfold; he must give up all the wealth of his house.
chapters.zh: 若被找着，他必赔还七倍， 必将家中所有的尽都偿还。

chapters.en: He who commits adultery lacks judgment; whoever does so destroys himself.
chapters.zh: 与妇人行淫的，便是无知； 行这事的，必丧掉生命。

chapters.en: Wounds and dishonor will befall him, and his reproach will never be wiped away.
chapters.zh: 他必受伤损，必被凌辱； 他的羞耻不得涂抹。

chapters.en: For jealousy enrages a husband, and he will show no mercy in the day of vengeance.
chapters.zh: 因为人的嫉恨成了烈怒， 报仇的时候决不留情。

chapters.en: He will not be appeased by any ransom, or persuaded by lavish gifts.
chapters.zh: 什么赎价，他都不顾； 你虽送许多礼物，他也不肯干休。

chapters.en: My son, keep my words and treasure my commandments within you.
chapters.zh: 我儿，你要遵守我的言语， 将我的命令存记在心。

chapters.en: Keep my commandments and live; guard my teachings as the apple of your eye.
chapters.zh: 遵守我的命令就得存活； 保守我的法则〔注：或译：指教〕， 好像保守眼中的瞳人，

chapters.en: Tie them to your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.
chapters.zh: 系在你指头上， 刻在你心版上。

chapters.en: Say to wisdom, “You are my sister,” and call understanding your kinsman,
chapters.zh: 对智慧说：你是我的姊妹， 称呼聪明为你的亲人，

chapters.en: that they may keep you from the adulteress, from the stranger with seductive words.
chapters.zh: 她就保你远离淫妇， 远离说谄媚话的外女。

chapters.en: For at the window of my house I looked through the lattice.
chapters.zh: 我曾在我房屋的窗户内， 从我窗棂之间往外观看：

chapters.en:
I saw among the simple, I noticed among the youths,
a young man lacking judgment,
chapters.zh: 见愚蒙人内，少年人中， 分明有一个无知的少年人，

chapters.en: crossing the street near her corner, strolling down the road to her house,
chapters.zh: 从街上经过，走近淫妇的巷口， 直往通她家的路去，

chapters.en: at twilight, as the day was fading into the dark of the night.
chapters.zh: 在黄昏，或晚上， 或半夜，或黑暗之中。

chapters.en: Then a woman came out to meet him, with the attire of a harlot and cunning of heart.
chapters.zh: 看哪，有一个妇人来迎接他， 是妓女的打扮，有诡诈的心思。

chapters.en: She is loud and defiant; her feet do not remain at home.
chapters.zh: 这妇人喧嚷，不守约束， 在家里停不住脚，

chapters.en: Now in the street, now in the squares, she lurks at every corner.
chapters.zh: 有时在街市上，有时在宽阔处， 或在各巷口蹲伏，

chapters.en: She seizes him and kisses him; she brazenly says to him:
chapters.zh: 拉住那少年人，与他亲嘴， 脸无羞耻对他说：

chapters.en: “I have made my peace offerings; today I have paid my vows.
chapters.zh: 平安祭在我这里， 今日才还了我所许的愿。

chapters.en: So I came out to meet you; I sought you, and I have found you.
chapters.zh: 因此，我出来迎接你， 恳切求见你的面，恰巧遇见了你。

chapters.en: I have decked my bed with coverings, with colored linen from Egypt.
chapters.zh: 我已经用绣花毯子 和埃及线织的花纹布铺了我的床。

chapters.en: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, with aloes, and with cinnamon.
chapters.zh: 我又用没药、沉香、桂皮 薰了我的榻。

chapters.en: Come, let us take our fill of love till morning. Let us delight in loving caresses!
chapters.zh: 你来，我们可以饱享爱情，直到早晨； 我们可以彼此亲爱欢乐。

chapters.en: For my husband is not at home; he has gone on a long journey.
chapters.zh: 因为我丈夫不在家，出门行远路；

chapters.en: He took with him a bag of money and will not return till the moon is full.”
chapters.zh: 他手拿银囊，必到月望才回家。

chapters.en: With her great persuasion she entices him; with her flattering lips she lures him.
chapters.zh: 淫妇用许多巧言诱他随从， 用谄媚的嘴逼他同行。

chapters.en:
He follows her on impulse, like an ox going to the slaughter,
like a deer bounding into a trap,
chapters.zh: 少年人立刻跟随她，好像牛往宰杀之地； 又像愚昧人带锁鍊去受刑罚，

chapters.en:
until an arrow pierces his liver, like a bird darting into a snare—
not knowing it will cost him his life.
chapters.zh: 直等箭穿他的肝； 如同雀鸟急入网罗，却不知是自丧己命。

chapters.en: Now, my sons, listen to me, and attend to the words of my mouth.
chapters.zh: 众子啊，现在要听从我， 留心听我口中的话。

chapters.en: Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways; do not stray into her paths.
chapters.zh: 你的心不可偏向淫妇的道， 不要入她的迷途。

chapters.en: For she has brought many down to death; her slain are many in number.
chapters.zh: 因为，被她伤害仆倒的不少； 被她杀戮的而且甚多。

chapters.en: Her house is the road to Sheol, descending to the chambers of death.
chapters.zh: 她的家是在阴间之路， 下到死亡之宫。

chapters.en: Does not wisdom call out, and understanding raise her voice?
chapters.zh: 智慧岂不呼叫？ 聪明岂不发声？

chapters.en: On the heights overlooking the road, at the crossroads she takes her stand.
chapters.zh: 她在道旁高处的顶上， 在十字路口站立，

chapters.en: Beside the gates to the city, at the entrances she cries out:
chapters.zh: 在城门旁，在城门口， 在城门洞，大声说：

chapters.en: “To you, O men, I call out, and my cry is to the sons of men.
chapters.zh: 众人哪，我呼叫你们， 我向世人发声。

chapters.en: O simple ones, learn to be shrewd; O fools, gain understanding.
chapters.zh: 说：愚蒙人哪，你们要会悟灵明； 愚昧人哪，你们当心里明白。

chapters.en: Listen, for I speak of noble things, and the opening of my lips will reveal right.
chapters.zh: 你们当听，因我要说极美的话； 我张嘴要论正直的事。

chapters.en: For my mouth will speak the truth, and wickedness is detestable to my lips.
chapters.zh: 我的口要发出真理； 我的嘴憎恶邪恶。

chapters.en: All the words of my mouth are righteous; none are crooked or perverse.
chapters.zh: 我口中的言语都是公义， 并无弯曲乖僻。

chapters.en: They are all plain to the discerning, and upright to those who find knowledge.
chapters.zh: 有聪明的，以为明显， 得知识的，以为正直。

chapters.en: Receive my instruction instead of silver, and knowledge rather than pure gold.
chapters.zh: 你们当受我的教训，不受白银； 宁得知识，胜过黄金。

chapters.en: For wisdom is more precious than rubies, and nothing you desire compares with her.
chapters.zh: 因为智慧比珍珠〔注：或译：红宝石〕更美； 一切可喜爱的都不足与比较。

chapters.en: I, wisdom, dwell together with prudence, and I find knowledge and discretion.
chapters.zh: 我－智慧以灵明为居所， 又寻得知识和谋略。

chapters.en: To fear the LORD is to hate evil; I hate arrogant pride, evil conduct, and perverse speech.
chapters.zh: 敬畏耶和华在乎恨恶邪恶； 那骄傲、狂妄，并恶道， 以及乖谬的口，都为我所恨恶。

chapters.en: Counsel and sound judgment are mine; I have insight and strength.
chapters.zh: 我有谋略和真知识； 我乃聪明，我有能力。

chapters.en: By me kings reign, and rulers enact just laws;
chapters.zh: 帝王藉我坐国位； 君王藉我定公平。

chapters.en: By me princes rule, and all nobles who govern justly.
chapters.zh: 王子和首领， 世上一切的审判官，都是藉我掌权。

chapters.en: I love those who love me, and those who seek me early shall find me.
chapters.zh: 爱我的，我也爱他； 恳切寻求我的，必寻得见。

chapters.en: With me are riches and honor, enduring wealth and righteousness.
chapters.zh: 丰富尊荣在我； 恒久的财并公义也在我。

chapters.en: My fruit is better than gold, pure gold, and my harvest surpasses choice silver.
chapters.zh: 我的果实胜过黄金，强如精金； 我的出产超乎高银。

chapters.en: I walk in the way of righteousness, along the paths of justice,
chapters.zh: 我在公义的道上走， 在公平的路中行，

chapters.en: bestowing wealth on those who love me and making their treasuries full.
chapters.zh: 使爱我的，承受货财， 并充满他们的府库。

chapters.en: The LORD created me as His first course, before His works of old.
chapters.zh: 在耶和华造化的起头， 在太初创造万物之先，就有了我。

chapters.en: From everlasting I was established, from the beginning, before the earth began.
chapters.zh: 从亘古，从太初， 未有世界以前，我已被立。

chapters.en: When there were no watery depths, I was brought forth, when no springs were overflowing with water.
chapters.zh: 没有深渊， 没有大水的泉源，我已生出。

chapters.en: Before the mountains were settled, before the hills, I was brought forth,
chapters.zh: 大山未曾奠定， 小山未有之先，我已生出。

chapters.en: before He made the land or fields, or any of the dust of the earth.
chapters.zh: 耶和华还没有创造大地和田野， 并世上的土质，我已生出。

chapters.en: I was there when He established the heavens, when He inscribed a circle on the face of the deep,
chapters.zh: 他立高天，我在那里； 他在渊面的周围，划出圆圈。

chapters.en: when He established the clouds above, when the fountains of the deep gushed forth,
chapters.zh: 上使穹苍坚硬， 下使渊源稳固，

chapters.en:
when He set a boundary for the sea, so that the waters would not surpass His command,
when He marked out the foundations of the earth.
chapters.zh: 为沧海定出界限，使水不越过他的命令， 立定大地的根基。

chapters.en:
Then I was a skilled craftsman at His side, and His delight day by day,
rejoicing always in His presence.
chapters.zh: 那时，我在他那里为工师， 日日为他所喜爱， 常常在他面前踊跃，

chapters.en: I was rejoicing in His whole world, delighting together in the sons of men.
chapters.zh: 踊跃在他为人〔预备〕可住之地， 也喜悦住在世人之间。

chapters.en: Now therefore, my sons, listen to me, for blessed are those who keep my ways.
chapters.zh: 众子啊，现在要听从我， 因为谨守我道的，便为有福。

chapters.en: Listen to instruction and be wise; do not ignore it.
chapters.zh: 要听教训就得智慧， 不可弃绝。

chapters.en:
Blessed is the man who listens to me, watching daily at my doors,
waiting at the posts of my doorway.
chapters.zh: 听从我、日日在我门口仰望、 在我门框旁边等候的，那人便为有福。

chapters.en: For whoever finds me finds life and obtains the favor of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 因为寻得我的，就寻得生命， 也必蒙耶和华的恩惠。

chapters.en: But he who fails to find me harms himself; all who hate me love death.”
chapters.zh: 得罪我的，却害了自己的性命； 恨恶我的，都喜爱死亡。

chapters.en: Wisdom has built her house; she has carved out her seven pillars.
chapters.zh: 智慧建造房屋， 凿成七根柱子，

chapters.en: She has prepared her meat and mixed her wine; she has also set her table.
chapters.zh: 宰杀牲畜， 调和旨酒， 设摆筵席；

chapters.en: She has sent out her maidservants; she calls out from the heights of the city.
chapters.zh: 打发使女出去， 自己在城中至高处呼叫，

chapters.en: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” she says to him who lacks judgment.
chapters.zh: 说：谁是愚蒙人，可以转到这里来！ 又对那无知的人说：

chapters.en: “Come, eat my bread and drink the wine I have mixed.
chapters.zh: 你们来，吃我的饼， 喝我调和的酒。

chapters.en: Leave your folly behind, and you will live; walk in the way of understanding.”
chapters.zh: 你们愚蒙人，要舍弃〔愚蒙〕， 就得存活，并要走光明的道。

chapters.en: He who corrects a mocker brings shame on himself; he who rebukes a wicked man taints himself.
chapters.zh: 指斥亵慢人的，必受辱骂； 责备恶人的，必被玷污。

chapters.en: Do not rebuke a mocker, or he will hate you; rebuke a wise man, and he will love you.
chapters.zh: 不要责备亵慢人，恐怕他恨你； 要责备智慧人，他必爱你。

chapters.en: Instruct a wise man, and he will be wiser still; teach a righteous man, and he will increase his learning.
chapters.zh: 〔教导〕智慧人，他就越发有智慧； 指示义人，他就增长学问。

chapters.en: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
chapters.zh: 敬畏耶和华是智慧的开端； 认识至圣者便是聪明。

chapters.en: For through wisdom your days will be multiplied, and years will be added to your life.
chapters.zh: 你藉着我，日子必增多， 年岁也必加添。

chapters.en: If you are wise, you are wise to your own advantage; but if you scoff, you alone will bear the consequences.
chapters.zh: 你若有智慧，是与自己有益； 你若亵慢，就必独自担当。

chapters.en: The woman named Folly is loud; she is naive and knows nothing.
chapters.zh: 愚昧的妇人喧嚷； 她是愚蒙，一无所知。

chapters.en: She sits at the door of her house, on a seat in the heights of the city,
chapters.zh: 她坐在自己的家门口， 坐在城中高处的座位上，

chapters.en: calling out to those who pass by, who make their paths straight.
chapters.zh: 呼叫过路的， 就是直行其道的人，

chapters.en: “Whoever is simple, let him turn in here!” she says to him who lacks judgment.
chapters.zh: 说：谁是愚蒙人，可以转到这里来！ 又对那无知的人说：

chapters.en: “Stolen water is sweet, and bread eaten in secret is tasty!”
chapters.zh: 偷来的水是甜的， 暗〔吃的〕饼是好的。

chapters.en: But they do not know that the dead are there, that her guests are in the depths of Sheol.
chapters.zh: 人却不知有阴魂在她那里； 她的客在阴间的深处。

chapters.en:
The proverbs of Solomon:
A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son grief to his mother.
chapters.zh: 所罗门的箴言： 智慧之子使父亲欢乐； 愚昧之子叫母亲担忧。

chapters.en: Ill-gotten treasures profit nothing, but righteousness brings deliverance from death.
chapters.zh: 不义之财毫无益处； 惟有公义能救人脱离死亡。

chapters.en: The LORD does not let the righteous go hungry, but He denies the craving of the wicked.
chapters.zh: 耶和华不使义人受饥饿； 恶人所欲的，他必推开。

chapters.en: Idle hands make one poor, but diligent hands bring wealth.
chapters.zh: 手懒的，要受贫穷； 手勤的，却要富足。

chapters.en: He who gathers in summer is a wise son, but he who sleeps during harvest is a disgraceful son.
chapters.zh: 夏天聚敛的，是智慧之子； 收割时沉睡的，是贻羞之子。

chapters.en: Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
chapters.zh: 福祉临到义人的头； 强暴蒙蔽恶人的口。

chapters.en: The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.
chapters.zh: 义人的纪念被称赞； 恶人的名字必朽烂。

chapters.en: A wise heart will receive commandments, but foolish lips will come to ruin.
chapters.zh: 心中智慧的，必受命令； 口里愚妄的，必致倾倒。

chapters.en: He who walks in integrity walks securely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.
chapters.zh: 行正直路的，步步安稳； 走弯曲道的，必致败露。

chapters.en: He who winks the eye causes grief, and foolish lips will come to ruin.
chapters.zh: 以眼传神的，使人忧患； 口里愚妄的，必致倾倒。

chapters.en: The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
chapters.zh: 义人的口是生命的泉源； 强暴蒙蔽恶人的口。

chapters.en: Hatred stirs up dissension, but love covers all transgressions.
chapters.zh: 恨能挑启争端； 爱能遮掩一切过错。

chapters.en: Wisdom is found on the lips of the discerning, but a rod is for the back of him who lacks judgment.
chapters.zh: 明哲人嘴里有智慧； 无知人背上受刑杖。

chapters.en: The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of the fool invites destruction.
chapters.zh: 智慧人积存知识； 愚妄人的口速致败坏。

chapters.en: The wealth of the rich man is his fortified city, but poverty is the ruin of the poor.
chapters.zh: 富户的财物是他的坚城； 穷人的贫乏是他的败坏。

chapters.en: The labor of the righteous leads to life, but the gain of the wicked brings punishment.
chapters.zh: 义人的勤劳致生； 恶人的进项致死〔注：死：原文是罪〕。

chapters.en: Whoever heeds instruction is on the path to life, but he who ignores reproof goes astray.
chapters.zh: 谨守训诲的，乃在生命的道上； 违弃责备的，便失迷了路。

chapters.en: The one who conceals hatred has lying lips, and whoever spreads slander is a fool.
chapters.zh: 隐藏怨恨的，有说谎的嘴； 口出谗谤的，是愚妄的人。

chapters.en: When words are many, sin is unavoidable, but he who restrains his lips is wise.
chapters.zh: 多言多语难免有过； 禁止嘴唇是有智慧。

chapters.en: The tongue of the righteous is choice silver, but the heart of the wicked has little worth.
chapters.zh: 义人的舌乃〔似〕高银； 恶人的心所值无几。

chapters.en: The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of judgment.
chapters.zh: 义人的口教养多人； 愚昧人因无知而死亡。

chapters.en: The blessing of the LORD enriches, and He adds no sorrow to it.
chapters.zh: 耶和华所赐的福使人富足， 并不加上忧虑。

chapters.en: The fool delights in shameful conduct, but a man of understanding has wisdom.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人以行恶为戏耍； 明哲人却以智慧为乐。

chapters.en: What the wicked man dreads will overtake him, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.
chapters.zh: 恶人所怕的，必临到他； 义人所愿的，必蒙应允。

chapters.en: When the whirlwind passes, the wicked are no more, but the righteous are secure forever.
chapters.zh: 暴风一过，恶人归于无有； 义人的根基却是永久。

chapters.en: Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is the slacker to those who send him.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人叫差他的人 如醋倒牙，如烟薰目。

chapters.en: The fear of the LORD prolongs life, but the years of the wicked will be cut short.
chapters.zh: 敬畏耶和华使人日子加多； 但恶人的年岁必被减少。

chapters.en: The hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectations of the wicked will perish.
chapters.zh: 义人的盼望〔必得〕喜乐； 恶人的指望必致灭没。

chapters.en: The way of the LORD is a refuge to the upright, but destruction awaits those who do evil.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的道是正直人的保障， 却成了作孽人的败坏。

chapters.en: The righteous will never be shaken, but the wicked will not inhabit the land.
chapters.zh: 义人永不挪移； 恶人不得住在地上。

chapters.en: The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but a perverse tongue will be cut out.
chapters.zh: 义人的口滋生智慧； 乖谬的舌必被割断。

chapters.en: The lips of the righteous know what is fitting, but the mouth of the wicked is perverse.
chapters.zh: 义人的嘴能令人喜悦； 恶人的口〔说〕乖谬的话。

chapters.en: Dishonest scales are an abomination to the LORD, but an accurate weight is His delight.
chapters.zh: 诡诈的天平为耶和华所憎恶； 公平的法码为他所喜悦。

chapters.en: When pride comes, disgrace follows, but with humility comes wisdom.
chapters.zh: 骄傲来，羞耻也来； 谦逊人却有智慧。

chapters.en: The integrity of the upright guides them, but the perversity of the faithless destroys them.
chapters.zh: 正直人的纯正必引导自己； 奸诈人的乖僻必毁灭自己。

chapters.en: Riches are worthless in the day of wrath, but righteousness brings deliverance from death.
chapters.zh: 发怒的日子资财无益； 惟有公义能救人脱离死亡。

chapters.en: The righteousness of the blameless directs their path, but the wicked fall by their own wickedness.
chapters.zh: 完全人的义必指引他的路； 但恶人必因自己的恶跌倒。

chapters.en: The righteousness of the upright delivers them, but the faithless are trapped by their own desires.
chapters.zh: 正直人的义必拯救自己； 奸诈人必陷在自己的罪孽中。

chapters.en: When the wicked man dies, his hope perishes, and the hope of his strength vanishes.
chapters.zh: 恶人一死，他的指望必灭绝； 罪人的盼望也必灭没。

chapters.en: The righteous man is delivered from trouble; in his place the wicked man goes in.
chapters.zh: 义人得脱离患难， 有恶人来代替他。

chapters.en: With his mouth the ungodly man destroys his neighbor, but through knowledge the righteous are rescued.
chapters.zh: 不虔敬的人用口败坏邻舍； 义人却因知识得救。

chapters.en: When the righteous thrive, the city rejoices, and when the wicked perish, there are shouts of joy.
chapters.zh: 义人享福，合城喜乐； 恶人灭亡，人都欢呼。

chapters.en: By the blessing of the upright a city is built up, but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn down.
chapters.zh: 城因正直人祝福便高举， 却因邪恶人的口就倾覆。

chapters.en: Whoever shows contempt for his neighbor lacks judgment, but a man of understanding remains silent.
chapters.zh: 藐视邻舍的，毫无智慧； 明哲人却静默不言。

chapters.en: A gossip reveals a secret, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.
chapters.zh: 往来传舌的，洩漏密事； 心中诚实的，遮隐事情。

chapters.en: For lack of guidance, a nation falls, but with many counselors comes deliverance.
chapters.zh: 无智谋，民就败落； 谋士多，人便安居。

chapters.en: He who puts up security for a stranger will surely suffer, but the one who hates indebtedness is secure.
chapters.zh: 为外人作保的，必受亏损； 恨恶击掌的，却得安稳。

chapters.en: A gracious woman attains honor, but ruthless men gain only wealth.
chapters.zh: 恩德的妇女得尊荣； 强暴的男子得资财。

chapters.en: A kind man benefits himself, but a cruel man brings trouble on himself.
chapters.zh: 仁慈的人善待自己； 残忍的人扰害己身。

chapters.en: The wicked man earns an empty wage, but he who sows righteousness reaps a true reward.
chapters.zh: 恶人经营，得虚浮的工价； 撒义种的，得实在的果效。

chapters.en: Genuine righteousness leads to life, but the pursuit of evil brings death.
chapters.zh: 恒心为义的，〔必得〕生命； 追求邪恶的，〔必致〕死亡。

chapters.en: The perverse in heart are an abomination to the LORD, but the blameless in their walk are His delight.
chapters.zh: 心中乖僻的，为耶和华所憎恶； 行事完全的，为他所喜悦。

chapters.en: Be assured that the wicked will not go unpunished, but the offspring of the righteous will escape.
chapters.zh: 恶人〔虽然〕连手，必不免受罚； 义人的后裔必得拯救。

chapters.en: Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.
chapters.zh: 妇女美貌而无见识， 〔如同〕金环带在猪鼻上。

chapters.en: The desire of the righteous leads only to good, but the hope of the wicked brings wrath.
chapters.zh: 义人的心愿尽得好处； 恶人的指望致干忿怒。

chapters.en: One gives freely, yet gains even more; another withholds what is right, only to become poor.
chapters.zh: 有施散的，却更增添； 有吝惜过度的，反致穷乏。

chapters.en: A generous soul will prosper, and he who refreshes others will himself be refreshed.
chapters.zh: 好施舍的，必得丰裕； 滋润人的，必得滋润。

chapters.en: The people will curse the hoarder of grain, but blessing will crown the one who sells it.
chapters.zh: 屯粮不卖的，民必咒诅他； 情愿出卖的，人必为他祝福。

chapters.en: He who searches out good finds favor, but evil will come to him who seeks it.
chapters.zh: 恳切求善的，就求得恩惠； 惟独求恶的，恶必临到他身。

chapters.en: He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous will thrive like foliage.
chapters.zh: 倚仗自己财物的，必跌倒； 义人必发旺，如青叶。

chapters.en: He who brings trouble on his house will inherit the wind, and the fool will be servant to the wise of heart.
chapters.zh: 扰害己家的，必承受清风； 愚昧人必作慧心人的仆人。

chapters.en: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise.
chapters.zh: 义人所结的果子就是生命树； 有智慧的，必能得人。

chapters.en: If the righteous receive their due on earth, how much more the ungodly and the sinner!
chapters.zh: 看哪，义人在世尚且受报， 何况恶人和罪人呢？

chapters.en: Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but he who hates correction is stupid.
chapters.zh: 喜爱管教的，就是喜爱知识； 恨恶责备的，却是畜类。

chapters.en: The good man obtains favor from the LORD, but the LORD condemns a man who devises evil.
chapters.zh: 善人必蒙耶和华的恩惠； 设诡计的人，耶和华必定他的罪。

chapters.en: A man cannot be established through wickedness, but the righteous cannot be uprooted.
chapters.zh: 人靠恶行不能坚立； 义人的根必不动摇。

chapters.en: A wife of noble character is her husband’s crown, but she who causes shame is like decay in his bones.
chapters.zh: 才德的妇人是丈夫的冠冕； 贻羞的妇人如同朽烂在她丈夫的骨中。

chapters.en: The plans of the righteous are just, but the counsel of the wicked leads to deceit.
chapters.zh: 义人的思念是公平； 恶人的计谋是诡诈。

chapters.en: The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood, but the speech of the upright rescues them.
chapters.zh: 恶人的言论是埋伏流人的血； 正直人的口必拯救人。

chapters.en: The wicked are overthrown and perish, but the house of the righteous will stand.
chapters.zh: 恶人倾覆，归于无有； 义人的家必站得住。

chapters.en: A man is praised according to his wisdom, but a twisted mind is despised.
chapters.zh: 人必按自己的智慧被称赞； 心中乖谬的，必被藐视。

chapters.en: Better to be lightly esteemed yet have a servant, than to be self-important but lack food.
chapters.zh: 被人轻贱，却有仆人， 强如自尊，缺少食物。

chapters.en: A righteous man regards the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are only cruelty.
chapters.zh: 义人顾惜他牲畜的命； 恶人的怜悯也是残忍。

chapters.en: The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies lacks judgment.
chapters.zh: 耕种自己田地的，必得饱食； 追随虚浮的，却是无知。

chapters.en: The wicked desire the plunder of evil men, but the root of the righteous flourishes.
chapters.zh: 恶人想得坏人的网罗； 义人的根得以结实。

chapters.en: An evil man is trapped by his rebellious speech, but a righteous man escapes from trouble.
chapters.zh: 恶人嘴中的过错是自己的网罗； 但义人必脱离患难。

chapters.en: By fruitful speech a man is filled with good things, and the work of his hands returns to him.
chapters.zh: 人因口所结的果子，必饱得美福； 人手所做的，必为自己的报应。

chapters.en: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but a wise man listens to counsel.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人所行的，在自己眼中看为正直； 惟智慧人肯听人的劝教。

chapters.en: A fool’s anger is known at once, but a prudent man overlooks an insult.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人的恼怒立时显露； 通达人能忍辱藏羞。

chapters.en: He who speaks the truth declares what is right, but a false witness speaks deceit.
chapters.zh: 说出真话的，显明公义； 作假见证的，显出诡诈。

chapters.en: Speaking rashly is like a piercing sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
chapters.zh: 说话浮躁的，如刀刺人； 智慧人的舌头却为医人的良药。

chapters.en: Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
chapters.zh: 口吐真言，永远坚立； 舌说谎话，只存片时。

chapters.en: Deceit is in the hearts of those who devise evil, but the counselors of peace have joy.
chapters.zh: 图谋恶事的，心存诡诈； 劝人和睦的，便得喜乐。

chapters.en: No harm befalls the righteous, but the wicked are filled with trouble.
chapters.zh: 义人不遭灾害；恶人满受祸患。

chapters.en: Lying lips are detestable to the LORD, but those who deal faithfully are His delight.
chapters.zh: 说谎言的嘴为耶和华所憎恶； 行事诚实的，为他所喜悦。

chapters.en: A shrewd man keeps his knowledge to himself, but a foolish heart proclaims its folly.
chapters.zh: 通达人隐藏知识； 愚昧人的心彰显愚昧。

chapters.en: The hand of the diligent will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor.
chapters.zh: 殷勤人的手必掌权； 懒惰的人必服苦。

chapters.en: Anxiety weighs down the heart of a man, but a good word cheers it up.
chapters.zh: 人心忧虑，屈而不伸； 一句良言，使心欢乐。

chapters.en: A righteous man is cautious in friendship, but the ways of the wicked lead them astray.
chapters.zh: 义人引导他的邻舍； 恶人的道叫人失迷。

chapters.en: A lazy man does not roast his game, but a diligent man prizes his possession.
chapters.zh: 懒惰的人不烤打猎所得的； 殷勤的人却得宝贵的财物。

chapters.en: There is life in the path of righteousness, but another path leads to death.
chapters.zh: 在公义的道上有生命； 其路之中并无死亡。

chapters.en: A wise son heeds his father’s discipline, but a mocker does not listen to rebuke.
chapters.zh: 智慧子〔听〕父亲的教训； 亵慢人不听责备。

chapters.en: From the fruit of his lips a man enjoys good things, but the desire of the faithless is violence.
chapters.zh: 人因口所结的果子，必享美福； 奸诈人〔必遭〕强暴。

chapters.en: He who guards his mouth protects his life, but the one who opens his lips invites his own ruin.
chapters.zh: 谨守口的，得保生命； 大张嘴的，必致败亡。

chapters.en: The slacker craves yet has nothing, but the soul of the diligent is fully satisfied.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人羨慕，却无所得； 殷勤人必得丰裕。

chapters.en: The righteous hate falsehood, but the wicked bring shame and disgrace.
chapters.zh: 义人恨恶谎言； 恶人有臭名，且致惭愧。

chapters.en: Righteousness guards the man of integrity, but wickedness undermines the sinner.
chapters.zh: 行为正直的，有公义保守； 犯罪的，被邪恶倾覆。

chapters.en: One pretends to be rich, but has nothing; another pretends to be poor, yet has great wealth.
chapters.zh: 假作富足的，却一无所有； 装作穷乏的，却广有财物。

chapters.en: Riches may ransom a man’s life, but a poor man hears no threat.
chapters.zh: 人的资财是他生命的赎价； 穷乏人却听不见威吓的话。

chapters.en: The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked is extinguished.
chapters.zh: 义人的光明亮〔注：原文是欢喜〕； 恶人的灯要熄灭。

chapters.en: Arrogance leads only to strife, but wisdom is with the well-advised.
chapters.zh: 骄傲只启争竞； 听劝言的，却有智慧。

chapters.en: Dishonest wealth will dwindle, but what is earned through hard work will be multiplied.
chapters.zh: 不劳而得之财必然消耗； 勤劳积蓄的，必见加增。

chapters.en: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.
chapters.zh: 所盼望的迟延未得，令人心忧； 所愿意的临到，却是生命树。

chapters.en: He who despises instruction will pay the penalty, but the one who respects a command will be rewarded.
chapters.zh: 藐视训言的，自取灭亡； 敬畏诫命的，必得善报。

chapters.en: The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life, turning one from the snares of death.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的法则〔注：或译：指教〕是生命的泉源， 可以使人离开死亡的网罗。

chapters.en: Good understanding wins favor, but the way of the faithless is difficult.
chapters.zh: 美好的聪明使人蒙恩； 奸诈人的道路崎岖难行。

chapters.en: Every prudent man acts with knowledge, but a fool displays his folly.
chapters.zh: 凡通达人都凭知识行事； 愚昧人张扬自己的愚昧。

chapters.en: A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
chapters.zh: 奸恶的使者必陷在祸患里； 忠信的使臣乃医人的良药。

chapters.en: Poverty and shame come to him who ignores discipline, but whoever heeds correction is honored.
chapters.zh: 弃绝管教的，〔必致〕贫受辱； 领受责备的，必得尊荣。

chapters.en: Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning from evil is detestable to fools.
chapters.zh: 所欲的成就，心觉甘甜； 远离恶事，为愚昧人所憎恶。

chapters.en: He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.
chapters.zh: 与智慧人同行的，必得智慧； 和愚昧人作伴的，必受亏损。

chapters.en: Disaster pursues sinners, but prosperity is the reward of the righteous.
chapters.zh: 祸患追赶罪人； 义人必得善报。

chapters.en: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the sinner’s wealth is passed to the righteous.
chapters.zh: 善人给子孙遗留产业； 罪人为义人积存资财。

chapters.en: Abundant food is in the fallow ground of the poor, but without justice it is swept away.
chapters.zh: 穷人耕种多得粮食， 但因不义，有消灭的。

chapters.en: He who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him diligently.
chapters.zh: 不忍用杖打儿子的，是恨恶他； 疼爱儿子的，随时管教。

chapters.en: A righteous man eats to his heart’s content, but the stomach of the wicked is empty.
chapters.zh: 义人吃得饱足； 恶人肚腹缺粮。

chapters.en: Every wise woman builds her house, but a foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
chapters.zh: 智慧妇人建立家室； 愚妄妇人亲手拆毁。

chapters.en: He who walks in uprightness fears the LORD, but the one who is devious in his ways despises Him.
chapters.zh: 行动正直的，敬畏耶和华； 行事乖僻的，却藐视他。

chapters.en: The proud speech of a fool brings a rod to his back, but the lips of the wise protect them.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人口中骄傲，如杖责打己身； 智慧人的嘴必保守自己。

chapters.en: Where there are no oxen, the manger is empty, but an abundant harvest comes through the strength of the ox.
chapters.zh: 家里无牛，槽头干净； 土产加多乃凭牛力。

chapters.en: An honest witness does not deceive, but a dishonest witness pours forth lies.
chapters.zh: 诚实见证人不说谎话； 假见证人吐出谎言。

chapters.en: A mocker seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
chapters.zh: 亵慢人寻智慧，却寻不着； 聪明人易得知识。

chapters.en: Stay away from a foolish man; you will gain no knowledge from his speech.
chapters.zh: 到愚昧人面前， 不见他嘴中有知识。

chapters.en: The wisdom of the prudent is to discern his way, but the folly of fools deceives them.
chapters.zh: 通达人的智慧在乎明白己道； 愚昧人的愚妄乃是诡诈〔注：或译：自欺〕。

chapters.en: Fools mock the making of amends, but goodwill is found among the upright.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人犯罪，以为戏耍〔注：或译：赎愆祭愚弄愚妄人〕； 正直人互相喜悦。

chapters.en: The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares in its joy.
chapters.zh: 心中的苦楚，自己知道； 心里的喜乐，外人无干。

chapters.en: The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
chapters.zh: 奸恶人的房屋必倾倒； 正直人的帐棚必兴盛。

chapters.en: There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.
chapters.zh: 有一条路，人以为正， 至终成为死亡之路。

chapters.en: Even in laughter the heart may ache, and joy may end in sorrow.
chapters.zh: 人在喜笑中，心也忧愁； 快乐至极就生愁苦。

chapters.en: The backslider in heart receives the fill of his own ways, but a good man is rewarded for his ways.
chapters.zh: 心中背道的，必满得自己的结果； 善人必从自己〔的行为得以知足〕。

chapters.en: The simple man believes every word, but the prudent man watches his steps.
chapters.zh: 愚蒙人是话都信； 通达人步步谨慎。

chapters.en: A wise man fears and turns from evil, but a fool is careless and reckless.
chapters.zh: 智慧人惧怕，就远离恶事； 愚妄人却狂傲自恃。

chapters.en: A quick-tempered man acts foolishly, and a devious man is hated.
chapters.zh: 轻易发怒的，行事愚妄； 设立诡计的，被人恨恶。

chapters.en: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
chapters.zh: 愚蒙人得愚昧为产业； 通达人得知识为冠冕。

chapters.en: The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
chapters.zh: 坏人俯伏在善人面前； 恶人俯伏在义人门口。

chapters.en: The poor man is hated even by his neighbor, but many are those who love the rich.
chapters.zh: 贫穷人连邻舍也恨他； 富足人朋友最多。

chapters.en: He who despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is he who shows kindness to the poor.
chapters.zh: 藐视邻舍的，这人有罪； 怜悯贫穷的，这人有福。

chapters.en: Do not those who contrive evil go astray? But those who plan goodness find loving devotion and faithfulness.
chapters.zh: 谋恶的，岂非走入迷途吗？ 谋善的，〔必得〕慈爱和诚实。

chapters.en: There is profit in all labor, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
chapters.zh: 诸般勤劳都有益处； 嘴上多言乃致穷乏。

chapters.en: The crown of the wise is their wealth, but the effort of fools is folly.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的财为自己的冠冕； 愚妄人的愚昧终是愚昧。

chapters.en: A truthful witness saves lives, but one who utters lies is deceitful.
chapters.zh: 作真见证的，救人性命； 吐出谎言的，〔施行〕诡诈。

chapters.en: He who fears the LORD is secure in confidence, and his children shall have a place of refuge.
chapters.zh: 敬畏耶和华的，大有倚靠； 他的儿女也有避难所。

chapters.en: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a man from the snares of death.
chapters.zh: 敬畏耶和华就是生命的泉源， 可以使人离开死亡的网罗。

chapters.en: A large population is a king’s splendor, but a lack of subjects is a prince’s ruin.
chapters.zh: 帝王荣耀在乎民多； 君王衰败在乎民少。

chapters.en: A patient man has great understanding, but a quick-tempered man promotes folly.
chapters.zh: 不轻易发怒的，大有聪明； 性情暴躁的，大显愚妄。

chapters.en: A tranquil heart is life to the body, but envy rots the bones.
chapters.zh: 心中安静是肉体的生命； 嫉妒是骨中的朽烂。

chapters.en: Whoever oppresses the poor taunts their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors Him.
chapters.zh: 欺压贫寒的，是辱没造他的主； 怜悯穷乏的，乃是尊敬主。

chapters.en: The wicked man is thrown down by his own sin, but the righteous man has a refuge even in death.
chapters.zh: 恶人在所行的恶上必被推倒； 义人临死，有所投靠。

chapters.en: Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning; even among fools she is known.
chapters.zh: 智慧存在聪明人心中； 愚昧人心里所存的，显而易见。

chapters.en: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
chapters.zh: 公义使邦国高举； 罪恶是人民的羞辱。

chapters.en: A king delights in a wise servant, but his anger falls on the shameful.
chapters.zh: 智慧的臣子蒙王恩惠； 贻羞的仆人遭其震怒。

chapters.en: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
chapters.zh: 回答柔和，使怒消退； 言语暴戾，触动怒气。

chapters.en: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouth of the fool spouts folly.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的舌善发知识； 愚昧人的口吐出愚昧。

chapters.en: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, observing the evil and the good.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的眼目无处不在； 恶人善人，他都鉴察。

chapters.en: A soothing tongue is a tree of life, but a perverse tongue crushes the spirit.
chapters.zh: 温良的舌是生命树； 乖谬的嘴使人心碎。

chapters.en: A fool rejects his father’s discipline, but whoever heeds correction is prudent.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人藐视父亲的管教； 领受责备的，得着见识。

chapters.en: The house of the righteous has great treasure, but the income of the wicked is trouble.
chapters.zh: 义人家中多有财宝； 恶人得利反受扰害。

chapters.en: The lips of the wise spread knowledge, but not so the hearts of fools.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的嘴播扬知识； 愚昧人的心并不如此。

chapters.en: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is His delight.
chapters.zh: 恶人献祭，为耶和华所憎恶； 正直人祈祷，为他所喜悦。

chapters.en: The LORD detests the way of the wicked, but He loves those who pursue righteousness.
chapters.zh: 恶人的道路，为耶和华所憎恶； 追求公义的，为他所喜爱。

chapters.en: Discipline is harsh for him who leaves the path; he who hates correction will die.
chapters.zh: 舍弃正路的，必受严刑； 恨恶责备的，必致死亡。

chapters.en: Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD— how much more the hearts of men!
chapters.zh: 阴间和灭亡尚在耶和华眼前， 何况世人的心呢？

chapters.en: A mocker does not love to be reproved, nor will he consult the wise.
chapters.zh: 亵慢人不爱受责备； 他也不就近智慧人。

chapters.en: A joyful heart makes a cheerful countenance, but sorrow of the heart crushes the spirit.
chapters.zh: 心中喜乐，面带笑容； 心里忧愁，灵被损伤。

chapters.en: A discerning heart seeks knowledge, but the mouth of a fool feeds on folly.
chapters.zh: 聪明人心求知识； 愚昧人口吃愚昧。

chapters.en: All the days of the oppressed are bad, but a cheerful heart has a continual feast.
chapters.zh: 困苦人的日子都是愁苦； 心中欢畅的，常享丰筵。

chapters.en: Better a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure with turmoil.
chapters.zh: 少有财宝，敬畏耶和华， 强如多有财宝，烦乱不安。

chapters.en: Better a dish of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox with hatred.
chapters.zh: 吃素菜，彼此相爱， 强如吃肥牛，彼此相恨。

chapters.en: A hot-tempered man stirs up strife, but he who is slow to anger calms dispute.
chapters.zh: 暴怒的人挑启争端； 忍怒的人止息纷争。

chapters.en: The way of the slacker is like a hedge of thorns, but the path of the upright is a highway.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人的道像荆棘的篱笆； 正直人的路是平坦的大道。

chapters.en: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish man despises his mother.
chapters.zh: 智慧子使父亲喜乐； 愚昧人藐视母亲。

chapters.en: Folly is joy to one who lacks judgment, but a man of understanding walks a straight path.
chapters.zh: 无知的人以愚妄为乐； 聪明的人按正直而行。

chapters.en: Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.
chapters.zh: 不先商议，所谋无效； 谋士众多，所谋乃成。

chapters.en: A man takes joy in a fitting reply— and how good is a timely word!
chapters.zh: 口善应对，自觉喜乐； 话合其时，何等美好。

chapters.en: The path of life leads upward for the wise, that he may avoid going down to Sheol.
chapters.zh: 智慧人从生命的道上升， 使他远离在下的阴间。

chapters.en: The LORD tears down the house of the proud, but He protects the boundaries of the widow.
chapters.zh: 耶和华必拆毁骄傲人的家， 却要立定寡妇的地界。

chapters.en: The LORD detests the thoughts of the wicked, but the words of the pure are pleasant to Him.
chapters.zh: 恶谋为耶和华所憎恶； 良言乃为纯净。

chapters.en: He who is greedy for unjust gain brings trouble on his household, but he who hates bribes will live.
chapters.zh: 贪恋财利的，扰害己家； 恨恶贿赂的，必得存活。

chapters.en: The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked blurts out evil.
chapters.zh: 义人的心，思量如何回答； 恶人的口吐出恶言。

chapters.en: The LORD is far from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous.
chapters.zh: 耶和华远离恶人， 却听义人的祷告。

chapters.en: The light of the eyes cheers the heart, and good news nourishes the bones.
chapters.zh: 眼有光，使心喜乐； 好信息，使骨滋润。

chapters.en: He who listens to life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise.
chapters.zh: 听从生命责备的， 必常在智慧人中。

chapters.en: He who ignores discipline despises himself, but whoever heeds correction gains understanding.
chapters.zh: 弃绝管教的，轻看自己的生命； 听从责备的，却得智慧。

chapters.en: The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom, and humility comes before honor.
chapters.zh: 敬畏耶和华是智慧的训诲； 尊荣以前，必有谦卑。

chapters.en: The plans of the heart belong to man, but the reply of the tongue is from the LORD.
chapters.zh: 心中的谋算在乎人； 舌头的应对由于耶和华。

chapters.en: All a man’s ways are pure in his own eyes, but his motives are weighed out by the LORD.
chapters.zh: 人一切所行的，在自己眼中看为清洁； 惟有耶和华衡量人心。

chapters.en: Commit your works to the LORD and your plans will be achieved.
chapters.zh: 你所做的，要交讬耶和华， 你所谋的，就必成立。

chapters.en: The LORD has made everything for His purpose— even the wicked for the day of disaster.
chapters.zh: 耶和华所造的，各适其用； 就是恶人也为祸患的日子所造。

chapters.en: Everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD; be assured that he will not go unpunished.
chapters.zh: 凡心里骄傲的，为耶和华所憎恶； 〔虽然〕连手，他必不免受罚。

chapters.en: By loving devotion and faithfulness iniquity is atoned for, and by the fear of the LORD one turns aside from evil.
chapters.zh: 因怜悯诚实，罪孽得赎； 敬畏耶和华的，远离恶事。

chapters.en: When a man’s ways please the LORD, He makes even the man’s enemies live at peace with him.
chapters.zh: 人所行的，若蒙耶和华喜悦， 耶和华也使他的仇敌与他和好。

chapters.en: Better a little with righteousness than great gain with injustice.
chapters.zh: 多有财利，行事不义， 不如少有财利，行事公义。

chapters.en: A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD determines his steps.
chapters.zh: 人心筹算自己的道路； 惟耶和华指引他的脚步。

chapters.en: A divine verdict is on the lips of a king; his mouth must not betray justice.
chapters.zh: 王的嘴中有神语， 审判之时，他的口必不差错。

chapters.en: Honest scales and balances are from the LORD; all the weights in the bag are His concern.
chapters.zh: 公道的天平和秤都属耶和华； 囊中一切法码都为他所定。

chapters.en: Wicked behavior is detestable for kings, for a throne is established through righteousness.
chapters.zh: 作恶，为王所憎恶， 因国位是靠公义坚立。

chapters.en: Righteous lips are a king’s delight, and he who speaks honestly is beloved.
chapters.zh: 公义的嘴为王所喜悦； 说正直话的，为王所喜爱。

chapters.en: The wrath of a king is a messenger of death, but a wise man will pacify it.
chapters.zh: 王的震怒如杀人的使者； 但智慧人能止息王怒。

chapters.en: When a king’s face brightens, there is life; his favor is like a rain cloud in spring.
chapters.zh: 王的脸光使人有生命； 王的恩典好像春云时雨。

chapters.en: How much better to acquire wisdom than gold! To gain understanding is more desirable than silver.
chapters.zh: 得智慧胜似得金子； 选聪明强如选银子。

chapters.en: The highway of the upright leads away from evil; he who guards his way protects his life.
chapters.zh: 正直人的道是远离恶事； 谨守己路的，是保全性命。

chapters.en: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
chapters.zh: 骄傲在败坏以先； 狂心在跌倒之前。

chapters.en: It is better to be lowly in spirit among the humble than to divide the spoil with the proud.
chapters.zh: 心里谦卑与穷乏人来往， 强如将掳物与骄傲人同分。

chapters.en: Whoever heeds instruction will find success, and blessed is he who trusts in the LORD.
chapters.zh: 谨守训言的，必得好处； 倚靠耶和华的，便为有福。

chapters.en: The wise in heart are called discerning, and pleasant speech promotes instruction.
chapters.zh: 心中有智慧，必称为通达人； 嘴中的甜言，加增人的学问。

chapters.en: Understanding is a fountain of life to its possessor, but the discipline of fools is folly.
chapters.zh: 人有智慧就有生命的泉源； 愚昧人必被愚昧惩治。

chapters.en: The heart of the wise man instructs his mouth and adds persuasiveness to his lips.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的心教训他的口， 又使他的嘴增长学问。

chapters.en: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
chapters.zh: 良言〔如同〕蜂房， 使心觉甘甜，使骨得医治。

chapters.en: There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.
chapters.zh: 有一条路，人以为正， 至终成为死亡之路。

chapters.en: A worker’s appetite works for him because his hunger drives him onward.
chapters.zh: 劳力人的胃口使他劳力， 因为他的口腹催逼他。

chapters.en: A worthless man digs up evil, and his speech is like a scorching fire.
chapters.zh: 匪徒图谋奸恶， 嘴上仿佛有烧焦的火。

chapters.en: A perverse man spreads dissension, and a gossip divides close friends.
chapters.zh: 乖僻人播散纷争； 传舌的，离间密友。

chapters.en: A violent man entices his neighbor and leads him down a path that is not good.
chapters.zh: 强暴人诱惑邻舍， 领他走不善之道。

chapters.en: He who winks his eye devises perversity; he who purses his lips is bent on evil.
chapters.zh: 眼目紧合的，图谋乖僻； 嘴唇紧闭的，成就邪恶。

chapters.en: Gray hair is a crown of glory; it is attained along the path of righteousness.
chapters.zh: 白发是荣耀的冠冕， 在公义的道上必能得着。

chapters.en: He who is slow to anger is better than a warrior, and he who controls his temper is greater than one who captures a city.
chapters.zh: 不轻易发怒的，胜过勇士； 治服己心的，强如取城。

chapters.en: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.
chapters.zh: 籤放在怀里， 定事由耶和华。

chapters.en: Better a dry morsel in quietness than a house full of feasting with strife.
chapters.zh: 设筵满屋，大家相争， 不如有块干饼，大家相安。

chapters.en: A wise servant will rule over a disgraceful son and share his inheritance as one of the brothers.
chapters.zh: 仆人办事聪明，必管辖贻羞之子， 又在众子中同分产业。

chapters.en: A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but the LORD is the tester of hearts.
chapters.zh: 鼎为炼银，炉为炼金； 惟有耶和华熬炼人心。

chapters.en: A wicked man listens to evil lips; a liar gives ear to a destructive tongue.
chapters.zh: 行恶的，留心听奸诈之言； 说谎的，侧耳听邪恶之语。

chapters.en: He who mocks the poor insults their Maker; whoever gloats over calamity will not go unpunished.
chapters.zh: 戏笑穷人的，是辱没造他的主； 幸灾乐祸的，必不免受罚。

chapters.en: Grandchildren are the crown of the aged, and the glory of a son is his father.
chapters.zh: 子孙为老人的冠冕； 父亲是儿女的荣耀。

chapters.en: Eloquent words are unfit for a fool; how much worse are lying lips to a ruler!
chapters.zh: 愚顽人说美言本不相宜， 何况君王说谎话呢？

chapters.en: A bribe is a charm to its giver; wherever he turns, he succeeds.
chapters.zh: 贿赂在餽送的人眼中看为宝玉， 随处运动都得顺利。

chapters.en: Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends.
chapters.zh: 遮掩人过的，寻求人爱； 屡次挑错的，离间密友。

chapters.en: A rebuke cuts into a man of discernment deeper than a hundred lashes cut into a fool.
chapters.zh: 一句责备话深入聪明人的心， 强如责打愚昧人一百下。

chapters.en: An evil man seeks only rebellion; a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
chapters.zh: 恶人只寻背叛， 所以必有严厉的使者奉差攻击他。

chapters.en: It is better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool in his folly.
chapters.zh: 宁可遇见丢崽子的母熊， 不可遇见正行愚妄的愚昧人。

chapters.en: If anyone returns evil for good, evil will never leave his house.
chapters.zh: 以恶报善的， 祸患必不离他的家。

chapters.en: To start a quarrel is to release a flood; so abandon the dispute before it breaks out.
chapters.zh: 纷争的起头〔如〕水放开， 所以，在争闹之先必当止息争竞。

chapters.en: Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous— both are detestable to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 定恶人为义的，定义人为恶的， 这都为耶和华所憎恶。

chapters.en: Why should the fool have money in his hand with no intention of buying wisdom?
chapters.zh: 愚昧人既无聪明， 为何手拿价银买智慧呢？

chapters.en: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
chapters.zh: 朋友乃时常亲爱， 弟兄为患难而生。

chapters.en: A man lacking judgment strikes hands in pledge and puts up security for his neighbor.
chapters.zh: 在邻舍面前击掌作保 乃是无知的人。

chapters.en: He who loves transgression loves strife; he who builds his gate high invites destruction.
chapters.zh: 喜爱争竞的，是喜爱过犯； 高立家门的，乃自取败坏。

chapters.en: The one with a perverse heart finds no good, and he whose tongue is deceitful falls into trouble.
chapters.zh: 心存邪僻的，寻不着好处； 舌弄是非的，陷在祸患中。

chapters.en: A man fathers a fool to his own grief; the father of a fool has no joy.
chapters.zh: 生愚昧子的，必自愁苦； 愚顽人的父毫无喜乐。

chapters.en: A joyful heart is good medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones.
chapters.zh: 喜乐的心乃是良药； 忧伤的灵使骨枯干。

chapters.en: A wicked man takes a covert bribe to subvert the course of justice.
chapters.zh: 恶人暗中受贿赂， 为要颠倒判断。

chapters.en: Wisdom is the focus of the discerning, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.
chapters.zh: 明哲人眼前有智慧； 愚昧人眼望地极。

chapters.en: A foolish son brings grief to his father and bitterness to her who bore him.
chapters.zh: 愚昧子使父亲愁烦， 使母亲忧苦。

chapters.en: It is surely not good to punish the innocent or to flog a noble for his honesty.
chapters.zh: 刑罚义人为不善； 责打君子为不义。

chapters.en: A man of knowledge restrains his words, and a man of understanding maintains a calm spirit.
chapters.zh: 寡少言语的，有知识； 性情温良的，有聪明。

chapters.en: Even a fool is considered wise if he keeps silent, and discerning when he holds his tongue.
chapters.zh: 愚昧人若静默不言也可算为智慧； 闭口不说也可算为聪明。

chapters.en: He who isolates himself pursues selfish desires; he rebels against all sound judgment.
chapters.zh: 与众寡合的，独自寻求心愿， 并恼恨一切真智慧。

chapters.en: A fool does not delight in understanding, but only in airing his opinions.
chapters.zh: 愚昧人不喜爱明哲， 只喜爱显露心意。

chapters.en: With a wicked man comes contempt as well, and shame is accompanied by disgrace.
chapters.zh: 恶人来，藐视随来； 羞耻到，辱骂同到。

chapters.en: The words of a man’s mouth are deep waters; the fountain of wisdom is a bubbling brook.
chapters.zh: 人口中的言语如同深水； 智慧的泉源好像涌流的河水。

chapters.en: Showing partiality to the wicked is not good, nor is depriving the innocent of justice.
chapters.zh: 瞻徇恶人的情面， 偏断义人的案件，都为不善。

chapters.en: A fool’s lips bring him strife, and his mouth invites a beating.
chapters.zh: 愚昧人张嘴启争端， 开口招鞭打。

chapters.en: A fool’s mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a snare to his soul.
chapters.zh: 愚昧人的口自取败坏； 他的嘴是他生命的网罗。

chapters.en: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.
chapters.zh: 传舌人的言语如同美食， 深入人的心腹。

chapters.en: Whoever is slothful in his work is brother to him who destroys.
chapters.zh: 做工懈怠的， 与浪费人为弟兄。

chapters.en: The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are safe.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的名是坚固台； 义人奔入便得安稳。

chapters.en: A rich man’s wealth is his fortified city; it is like a high wall in his imagination.
chapters.zh: 富足人的财物是他的坚城， 在他心想，犹如高墙。

chapters.en: Before his downfall a man’s heart is proud, but humility comes before honor.
chapters.zh: 败坏之先，人心骄傲； 尊荣以前，必有谦卑。

chapters.en: He who answers a matter before he hears it— this is folly and disgrace to him.
chapters.zh: 未曾听完先回答的， 便是他的愚昧和羞辱。

chapters.en: The spirit of a man can endure his sickness, but who can survive a broken spirit?
chapters.zh: 人有疾病，心能忍耐； 心灵忧伤，谁能承当呢？

chapters.en: The heart of the discerning acquires knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks it out.
chapters.zh: 聪明人的心得知识； 智慧人的耳求知识。

chapters.en: A man’s gift opens doors for him, and brings him before great men.
chapters.zh: 人的礼物为他开路， 引他到高位的人面前。

chapters.en: The first to state his case seems right until another comes and cross-examines him.
chapters.zh: 先诉情由的，似乎有理； 但邻舍来到，就察出实情。

chapters.en: Casting the lot ends quarrels and separates strong opponents.
chapters.zh: 掣签能止息争竞， 也能解散强胜的人。

chapters.en: An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city, and disputes are like the bars of a castle.
chapters.zh: 弟兄结怨，〔劝他和好〕，比取坚固城还难； 〔这样的〕争竞如同坚寨的门闩。

chapters.en: From the fruit of his mouth a man’s belly is filled; with the harvest from his lips he is satisfied.
chapters.zh: 人口中所结的果子，必充满肚腹； 他嘴所出的，必使他饱足。

chapters.en: Life and death are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
chapters.zh: 生死在舌头的权下， 喜爱它的，必吃它所结的果子。

chapters.en: He who finds a wife finds a good thing and obtains favor from the LORD.
chapters.zh: 得着〔贤〕妻的，是得着好处， 也是蒙了耶和华的恩惠。

chapters.en: The poor man pleads for mercy, but the rich man answers harshly.
chapters.zh: 贫穷人说哀求的话； 富足人用威吓的话回答。

chapters.en: A man of many companions may come to ruin, but there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.
chapters.zh: 滥交朋友的，自取败坏； 但有一朋友比弟兄更亲密。

chapters.en: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a fool whose lips are perverse.
chapters.zh: 行为纯正的贫穷人 胜过乖谬愚妄的〔富足〕人。

chapters.en: Even zeal is no good without knowledge, and he who hurries his footsteps misses the mark.
chapters.zh: 心无知识的，乃为不善； 脚步急快的，难免犯罪。

chapters.en: A man’s own folly subverts his way, yet his heart rages against the LORD.
chapters.zh: 人的愚昧倾败他的道； 他的心也抱怨耶和华。

chapters.en: Wealth attracts many friends, but a poor man is deserted by his friend.
chapters.zh: 财物使朋友增多； 但穷人朋友远离。

chapters.en: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who utters lies will not escape.
chapters.zh: 作假见证的，必不免受罚； 吐出谎言的，终不能逃脱。

chapters.en: Many seek the favor of the prince, and everyone is a friend of the gift giver.
chapters.zh: 好施散的，有多人求他的恩情； 爱送礼的，人都为他的朋友。

chapters.en: All the brothers of a poor man hate him— how much more do his friends avoid him! He may pursue them with pleading, but they are nowhere to be found.
chapters.zh: 贫穷人，弟兄都恨他； 何况他的朋友，更远离他！ 他用言语追随，他们却走了。

chapters.en: He who acquires wisdom loves himself; one who safeguards understanding will find success.
chapters.zh: 得着智慧的，爱惜生命； 保守聪明的，必得好处。

chapters.en: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who pours out lies will perish.
chapters.zh: 作假见证的，不免受罚； 吐出谎言的，也必灭亡。

chapters.en: Luxury is unseemly for a fool— how much worse for a slave to rule over princes!
chapters.zh: 愚昧人宴乐度日是不合宜的； 何况仆人管辖王子呢？

chapters.en: A man’s insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to overlook an offense.
chapters.zh: 人有见识就不轻易发怒； 宽恕人的过失便是自己的荣耀。

chapters.en: A king’s rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
chapters.zh: 王的忿怒好像狮子吼叫； 他的恩典却如草上的甘露。

chapters.en: A foolish son is his father’s ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping.
chapters.zh: 愚昧的儿子是父亲的祸患； 妻子的争吵〔如雨〕连连滴漏。

chapters.en: Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.
chapters.zh: 房屋钱财是祖宗所遗留的； 惟有贤慧的妻是耶和华所赐的。

chapters.en: Laziness brings on deep sleep, and an idle soul will suffer hunger.
chapters.zh: 懒惰使人沉睡； 懈怠的人必受饥饿。

chapters.en: He who keeps a commandment preserves his soul, but he who is careless in his ways will die.
chapters.zh: 谨守诫命的，保全生命； 轻忽己路的，必致死亡。

chapters.en: Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender.
chapters.zh: 怜悯贫穷的，就是借给耶和华； 他的善行，耶和华必偿还。

chapters.en: Discipline your son, for in that there is hope; do not be party to his death.
chapters.zh: 趁有指望，管教你的儿子； 你的心不可任他死亡。

chapters.en: A man of great anger must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do so again.
chapters.zh: 暴怒的人必受刑罚； 你若救他，必须再救。

chapters.en: Listen to counsel and accept discipline, that you may be wise the rest of your days.
chapters.zh: 你要听劝教，受训诲， 使你终久有智慧。

chapters.en: Many plans are in a man’s heart, but the purpose of the LORD will prevail.
chapters.zh: 人心多有计谋； 惟有耶和华的筹算才能立定。

chapters.en: The desire of a man is loving devotion; better to be poor than a liar.
chapters.zh: 施行仁慈的，令人爱慕； 穷人强如说谎言的。

chapters.en: The fear of the LORD leads to life, that one may rest content, without visitation from harm.
chapters.zh: 敬畏耶和华的，〔得着〕生命； 他必恒久知足，不遭祸患。

chapters.en: The slacker buries his hand in the dish; he will not even bring it back to his mouth.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人放手在盘子里， 就是向口撤回，他也不肯。

chapters.en: Strike a mocker, and the simple will beware; rebuke the discerning man, and he will gain knowledge.
chapters.zh: 鞭打亵慢人，愚蒙人必长见识； 责备明哲人，他就明白知识。

chapters.en: He who assaults his father or evicts his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
chapters.zh: 虐待父亲、撵出母亲的， 是贻羞致辱之子。

chapters.en: If you cease to hear instruction, my son, you will stray from the words of knowledge.
chapters.zh: 我儿，不可听了教训 而又偏离知识的言语。

chapters.en: A corrupt witness mocks justice, and a wicked mouth swallows iniquity.
chapters.zh: 匪徒作见证戏笑公平； 恶人的口吞下罪孽。

chapters.en: Judgments are prepared for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools.
chapters.zh: 刑罚是为亵慢人预备的； 鞭打是为愚昧人的背预备的。

chapters.en: Wine is a mocker, strong drink is a brawler, and whoever is led astray by them is not wise.
chapters.zh: 酒能使人亵慢，浓酒使人喧嚷； 凡因酒错误的，就无智慧。

chapters.en: The terror of a king is like the roar of a lion; whoever provokes him forfeits his own life.
chapters.zh: 王的威吓如同狮子吼叫； 惹动他怒的，是自害己命。

chapters.en: It is honorable for a man to resolve a dispute, but any fool will quarrel.
chapters.zh: 远离纷争是人的尊荣； 愚妄人都爱争闹。

chapters.en: The slacker does not plow in season; at harvest time he looks, but nothing is there.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人因冬寒不肯耕种， 到收割的时候，他必讨饭而无所得。

chapters.en: The intentions of a man’s heart are deep waters, but a man of understanding draws them out.
chapters.zh: 人心怀藏谋略，好像深水， 惟明哲人才能汲引出来。

chapters.en: Many a man proclaims his loving devotion, but who can find a trustworthy man?
chapters.zh: 人多述说自己的仁慈， 但忠信人谁能遇着呢？

chapters.en: The righteous man walks with integrity; blessed are his children after him.
chapters.zh: 行为纯正的义人， 他的子孙是有福的！

chapters.en: A king who sits on a throne to judge sifts out all evil with his eyes.
chapters.zh: 王坐在审判的位上， 以眼目驱散诸恶。

chapters.en: Who can say, “I have kept my heart pure; I am cleansed from my sin”?
chapters.zh: 谁能说，我洁净了我的心， 我脱净了我的罪？

chapters.en: Differing weights and unequal measures — both are detestable to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 两样的法码，两样的升斗， 都为耶和华所憎恶。

chapters.en: Even a young man is known by his actions— whether his conduct is pure and upright.
chapters.zh: 孩童的动作是清洁，是正直， 都显明他的本性。

chapters.en: Ears that hear and eyes that see— the LORD has made them both.
chapters.zh: 能听的耳，能看的眼， 都是耶和华所造的。

chapters.en: Do not love sleep, or you will grow poor; open your eyes, and you will have plenty of food.
chapters.zh: 不要贪睡，免致贫穷； 眼要睁开，你就吃饱。

chapters.en: “Worthless, worthless!” says the buyer, but on the way out, he gloats.
chapters.zh: 买物的说：不好，不好； 及至〔买〕去，他便自夸。

chapters.en: There is an abundance of gold and rubies, but lips of knowledge are a rare treasure.
chapters.zh: 有金子和许多珍珠〔注：或译：红宝石〕， 惟有知识的嘴乃为贵重的珍宝。

chapters.en: Take the garment of the one who posts security for a stranger; get collateral if it is for a foreigner.
chapters.zh: 谁为生人作保，就拿谁的衣服； 谁为外人〔作保〕，谁就要承当。

chapters.en: Food gained by fraud is sweet to a man, but later his mouth is full of gravel.
chapters.zh: 以虚谎而得的食物，人觉甘甜； 但后来，他的口必充满尘沙。

chapters.en: Set plans by consultation, and wage war under sound guidance.
chapters.zh: 计谋都凭筹算立定； 打仗要凭智谋。

chapters.en: He who reveals secrets is a constant gossip; avoid the one who babbles with his lips.
chapters.zh: 往来传舌的，洩漏密事； 大张嘴的，不可与他结交。

chapters.en: Whoever curses his father or mother, his lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness.
chapters.zh: 咒骂父母的，他的灯必灭， 变为漆黑的黑暗。

chapters.en: An inheritance gained quickly will not be blessed in the end.
chapters.zh: 起初速得的产业， 终久却不为福。

chapters.en: Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!” Wait on the LORD, and He will save you.
chapters.zh: 你不要说，我要以恶报恶； 要等候耶和华，他必拯救你。

chapters.en: Unequal weights are detestable to the LORD, and dishonest scales are no good.
chapters.zh: 两样的法码为耶和华所憎恶； 诡诈的天平也为不善。

chapters.en: A man’s steps are from the LORD, so how can anyone understand his own way?
chapters.zh: 人的脚步为耶和华所定； 人岂能明白自己的路呢？

chapters.en: It is a trap for a man to dedicate something rashly, only later to reconsider his vows.
chapters.zh: 人冒失说，〔这是〕圣物， 许愿之后才查问，就是自陷网罗。

chapters.en: A wise king separates out the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them.
chapters.zh: 智慧的王簸散恶人， 用碌碡滚轧他们。

chapters.en: The spirit of a man is the lamp of the LORD, searching out his inmost being.
chapters.zh: 人的灵是耶和华的灯， 鉴察人的心腹。

chapters.en: Loving devotion and faithfulness preserve a king; by these he maintains his throne.
chapters.zh: 王因仁慈和诚实得以保全他的国位， 也因仁慈立稳。

chapters.en: The glory of young men is their strength, and gray hair is the splendor of the old.
chapters.zh: 强壮乃少年人的荣耀； 白发为老年人的尊荣。

chapters.en: Lashes and wounds scour evil, and beatings cleanse the inmost parts.
chapters.zh: 鞭伤除净人的罪恶； 责打〔能入〕人的心腹。

chapters.en: The king’s heart is a waterway in the hand of the LORD; He directs it where He pleases.
chapters.zh: 王的心在耶和华手中， 好像陇沟的水随意流转。

chapters.en: All a man’s ways seem right to him, but the LORD weighs the heart.
chapters.zh: 人所行的，在自己眼中都看为正； 惟有耶和华衡量人心。

chapters.en: To do righteousness and justice is more desirable to the LORD than sacrifice.
chapters.zh: 行仁义公平 比献祭更蒙耶和华悦纳。

chapters.en: Haughty eyes and a proud heart— the guides of the wicked—are sin.
chapters.zh: 恶人发达〔注：发达：原文是灯〕，眼高心傲， 这乃是罪。

chapters.en: The plans of the diligent bring plenty, as surely as haste leads to poverty.
chapters.zh: 殷勤筹划的，足致丰裕； 行事急躁的，都必缺乏。

chapters.en: Making a fortune by a lying tongue is a vanishing mist, a deadly pursuit.
chapters.zh: 用诡诈之舌求财的，就是自己取死； 所得之财乃是吹来吹去的浮云。

chapters.en: The violence of the wicked will sweep them away because they refuse to do what is just.
chapters.zh: 恶人的强暴必将自己扫除， 因他们不肯按公平行事。

chapters.en: The way of a guilty man is crooked, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.
chapters.zh: 负罪之人的路甚是弯曲； 至于清洁的人，他所行的乃是正直。

chapters.en: Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
chapters.zh: 宁可住在房顶的角上， 不在宽阔的房屋与争吵的妇人同住。

chapters.en: The soul of the wicked man craves evil; his neighbor finds no favor in his eyes.
chapters.zh: 恶人的心乐人受祸； 他眼并不怜恤邻舍。

chapters.en: When a mocker is punished, the simple gain wisdom; and when a wise man is instructed, he acquires knowledge.
chapters.zh: 亵慢的人受刑罚，愚蒙的人就得智慧； 智慧人受训诲，便得知识。

chapters.en: The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked and brings the wicked to ruin.
chapters.zh: 义人思想恶人的家， 知道恶人倾倒，必致灭亡。

chapters.en: Whoever shuts his ears to the cry of the poor, he too shall cry out and receive no answer.
chapters.zh: 塞耳不听穷人哀求的， 他将来呼吁也不蒙应允。

chapters.en: A gift in secret soothes anger, and a covert bribe pacifies great wrath.
chapters.zh: 暗中送的礼物挽回怒气； 怀中搋的贿赂止息暴怒。

chapters.en: Justice executed is a joy to the righteous, but a terror to the workers of iniquity.
chapters.zh: 秉公行义使义人喜乐， 使作孽的人败坏。

chapters.en: The man who strays from the path of understanding will rest in the assembly of the dead.
chapters.zh: 迷离通达道路的， 必住在阴魂的会中。

chapters.en: He who loves pleasure will become poor; the one who loves wine and oil will never be rich.
chapters.zh: 爱宴乐的，必致穷乏； 好酒，爱膏油的，必不富足。

chapters.en: The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the faithless for the upright.
chapters.zh: 恶人作了义人的赎价； 奸诈人代替正直人。

chapters.en: Better to live in the desert than with a contentious and ill-tempered wife.
chapters.zh: 宁可住在旷野， 不与争吵使气的妇人同住。

chapters.en: Precious treasures and oil are in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish man consumes them.
chapters.zh: 智慧人家中〔积蓄〕宝物膏油； 愚昧人随得来随吞下。

chapters.en: He who pursues righteousness and loving devotion finds life, righteousness, and honor.
chapters.zh: 追求公义仁慈的， 就寻得生命、公义，和尊荣。

chapters.en: A wise man scales the city of the mighty and pulls down the stronghold in which they trust.
chapters.zh: 智慧人爬上勇士的城墙， 倾覆他所倚靠的坚垒。

chapters.en: He who guards his mouth and tongue keeps his soul from distress.
chapters.zh: 谨守口与舌的， 就保守自己免受灾难。

chapters.en: Mocker is the name of the proud and arrogant man— of him who acts with excessive pride.
chapters.zh: 心骄气傲的人名叫亵慢； 他行事狂妄，都出于骄傲。

chapters.en: The craving of the slacker kills him because his hands refuse to work.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人的心愿将他杀害， 因为他手不肯做工。

chapters.en: All day long he covets more, but the righteous give without restraint.
chapters.zh: 有终日贪得无餍的； 义人施舍而不吝惜。

chapters.en: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable— how much more so when brought with ill intent!
chapters.zh: 恶人的祭物是可憎的； 何况他存恶意来献呢？

chapters.en: A lying witness will perish, but the man who listens to truth will speak forever.
chapters.zh: 作假见证的必灭亡； 惟有听真情而言的，其言长存。

chapters.en: A wicked man hardens his face, but the upright man makes his way sure.
chapters.zh: 恶人脸无羞耻； 正直人行事坚定。

chapters.en: There is no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel that can prevail against the LORD.
chapters.zh: 没有人能以智慧、聪明、 谋略敌挡耶和华。

chapters.en: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory is of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 马是为打仗之日预备的； 得胜乃在乎耶和华。

chapters.en: A good name is more desirable than great riches; favor is better than silver and gold.
chapters.zh: 美名胜过大财； 恩宠强如金银。

chapters.en: The rich and the poor have this in common: The LORD is Maker of them all.
chapters.zh: 富户穷人在世相遇， 都为耶和华所造。

chapters.en: The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and suffer the consequences.
chapters.zh: 通达人见祸藏躲； 愚蒙人前往受害。

chapters.en: The rewards of humility and the fear of the LORD are wealth and honor and life.
chapters.zh: 敬畏耶和华心存谦卑， 就得富有、尊荣、生命为赏赐。

chapters.en: Thorns and snares lie on the path of the perverse; he who guards his soul stays far from them.
chapters.zh: 乖僻人的路上有荆棘和网罗； 保守自己生命的，必要远离。

chapters.en: Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.
chapters.zh: 教养孩童，使他走当行的道， 就是到老他也不偏离。

chapters.en: The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is slave to the lender.
chapters.zh: 富户管辖穷人； 欠债的是债主的仆人。

chapters.en: He who sows injustice will reap disaster, and the rod of his fury will be destroyed.
chapters.zh: 撒罪孽的，必收灾祸； 他逞怒的杖也必废掉。

chapters.en: A generous man will be blessed, for he shares his bread with the poor.
chapters.zh: 眼目慈善的，就必蒙福， 因他将食物分给穷人。

chapters.en: Drive out the mocker, and conflict will depart; even quarreling and insults will cease.
chapters.zh: 赶出亵慢人，争端就消除； 纷争和羞辱也必止息。

chapters.en: He who loves a pure heart and gracious lips will have the king for a friend.
chapters.zh: 喜爱清心的人因他嘴上的恩言， 王必与他为友。

chapters.en: The LORD’s eyes keep watch over knowledge, but He frustrates the words of the faithless.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的眼目眷顾聪明人， 却倾败奸诈人的言语。

chapters.en: The slacker says, “There is a lion outside! I will be slain in the streets!”
chapters.zh: 懒惰人说：外头有狮子； 我在街上就必被杀。

chapters.en: The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; he who is under the wrath of the LORD will fall into it.
chapters.zh: 淫妇的口为深坑； 耶和华所憎恶的，必陷在其中。

chapters.en: Foolishness is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline drives it far from him.
chapters.zh: 愚蒙迷住孩童的心， 用管教的杖可以远远赶除。

chapters.en: Oppressing the poor to enrich oneself or giving gifts to the rich will surely lead to poverty.
chapters.zh: 欺压贫穷为要利己的， 并送〔礼〕与富户的，都必缺乏。

chapters.en: Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise— apply your mind to my knowledge—
chapters.zh: 你须侧耳听受智慧人的言语， 留心领会我的知识。

chapters.en: for it is pleasing when you keep them within you and they are constantly on your lips.
chapters.zh: 你若心中存记， 嘴上咬定，这便为美。

chapters.en: So that your trust may be in the LORD, I instruct you today—yes, you.
chapters.zh: 我今日以此特特指教你， 为要使你倚靠耶和华。

chapters.en: Have I not written for you thirty sayings about counsel and knowledge,
chapters.zh: 谋略和知识的美事， 我岂没有写给你吗？

chapters.en: to show you true and reliable words, that you may soundly answer those who sent you?
chapters.zh: 要使你知道真言的实理， 你好将真言回复那打发你来的人。

chapters.en: Do not rob a poor man because he is poor, and do not crush the afflicted at the gate,
chapters.zh: 贫穷人，你不可因他贫穷就抢夺他的物， 也不可在城门口欺压困苦人；

chapters.en: for the LORD will take up their case and will plunder those who rob them.
chapters.zh: 因耶和华必为他辨屈； 抢夺他的，耶和华必夺取那人的命。

chapters.en: Do not make friends with an angry man, and do not associate with a hot-tempered man,
chapters.zh: 好生气的人，不可与他结交； 暴怒的人，不可与他来往；

chapters.en: or you may learn his ways and entangle yourself in a snare.
chapters.zh: 恐怕你效法他的行为， 自己就陷在网罗里。

chapters.en: Do not be one who gives pledges, who puts up security for debts.
chapters.zh: 不要与人击掌， 不要为欠债的作保。

chapters.en: If you have nothing with which to pay, why should your bed be taken from under you?
chapters.zh: 你若没有什么偿还， 何必使人夺去你睡卧的床呢？

chapters.en: Do not move an ancient boundary stone which your fathers have placed.
chapters.zh: 你先祖所立的地界， 你不可挪移。

chapters.en:
Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will be stationed in the presence of kings;
he will not stand before obscure men.
chapters.zh: 你看见办事殷勤的人吗？ 他必站在君王面前， 必不站在下贱人面前。

chapters.en: When you sit down to dine with a ruler, consider carefully what is set before you,
chapters.zh: 你若与官长坐席， 要留意在你面前的是谁。

chapters.en: and put a knife to your throat if you possess a great appetite.
chapters.zh: 你若是贪食的， 就当拿刀放在喉咙上。

chapters.en: Do not crave his delicacies, for that food is deceptive.
chapters.zh: 不可贪恋他的美食， 因为是哄人的食物。

chapters.en: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; be wise enough to restrain yourself.
chapters.zh: 不要劳碌求富， 休仗自己的聪明。

chapters.en:
When you glance at wealth, it disappears, for it makes wings for itself
and flies like an eagle to the sky.
chapters.zh: 你岂要定睛在虚无的〔钱财〕上吗？ 因〔钱财〕必长翅膀，如鹰向天飞去。

chapters.en: Do not eat the bread of a stingy man, and do not crave his delicacies;
chapters.zh: 不要吃恶眼人的饭， 也不要贪他的美味；

chapters.en: for he is keeping track, inwardly counting the cost. “Eat and drink,” he says to you, but his heart is not with you.
chapters.zh: 因为他心怎样思量， 他为人就是怎样。 他虽对你说，请吃，请喝， 他的心却与你相背。

chapters.en: You will vomit up what little you have eaten and waste your pleasant words.
chapters.zh: 你所吃的那点食物必吐出来； 你所说的甘美言语也必落空。

chapters.en: Do not speak to a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words.
chapters.zh: 你不要说话给愚昧人听， 因他必藐视你智慧的言语。

chapters.en: Do not move an ancient boundary stone or encroach on the fields of the fatherless,
chapters.zh: 不可挪移古时的地界， 也不可侵入孤儿的田地；

chapters.en: for their Redeemer is strong; He will take up their case against you.
chapters.zh: 因他们的救赎主大有能力， 他必向你为他们辨屈。

chapters.en: Apply your heart to instruction and your ears to words of knowledge.
chapters.zh: 你要留心领受训诲， 侧耳听从知识的言语。

chapters.en: Do not withhold discipline from a child; although you strike him with a rod, he will not die.
chapters.zh: 不可不管教孩童； 你用杖打他，他必不至于死。

chapters.en: Strike him with a rod, and you will deliver his soul from Sheol.
chapters.zh: 你要用杖打他， 就可以救他的灵魂免下阴间。

chapters.en: My son, if your heart is wise, my own heart will indeed rejoice.
chapters.zh: 我儿，你心若存智慧， 我的心也甚欢喜。

chapters.en: My inmost being will rejoice when your lips speak what is right.
chapters.zh: 你的嘴若说正直话， 我的心肠也必快乐。

chapters.en: Do not let your heart envy sinners, but always continue in the fear of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你心中不要嫉妒罪人， 只要终日敬畏耶和华；

chapters.en: For surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
chapters.zh: 因为至终必有善报， 你的指望也不致断绝。

chapters.en: Listen, my son, and be wise, and guide your heart on the right course.
chapters.zh: 我儿，你当听，当存智慧， 好在正道上引导你的心。

chapters.en: Do not join those who drink too much wine or gorge themselves on meat.
chapters.zh: 好饮酒的，好吃肉的， 不要与他们来往；

chapters.en: For the drunkard and the glutton will come to poverty, and drowsiness will clothe them in rags.
chapters.zh: 因为好酒贪食的，必致贫穷； 好睡觉的，必穿破烂衣服。

chapters.en: Listen to your father who gave you life, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
chapters.zh: 你要听从生你的父亲； 你母亲老了，也不可藐视她。

chapters.en: Invest in truth and never sell it— in wisdom and instruction and understanding.
chapters.zh: 你当买真理； 就是智慧、训诲，和聪明也都不可卖。

chapters.en: The father of a righteous man will greatly rejoice, and he who fathers a wise son will delight in him.
chapters.zh: 义人的父亲必大得快乐； 人生智慧的儿子，必因他欢喜。

chapters.en: May your father and mother be glad, and may she who gave you birth rejoice!
chapters.zh: 你要使父母欢喜， 使生你的快乐。

chapters.en: My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes delight in my ways.
chapters.zh: 我儿，要将你的心归我； 你的眼目也要喜悦我的道路。

chapters.en: For a prostitute is a deep pit, and an adulteress is a narrow well.
chapters.zh: 妓女是深坑； 外女是窄阱。

chapters.en: Like a robber she lies in wait and multiplies the faithless among men.
chapters.zh: 她埋伏好像强盗； 她使人中多有奸诈的。

chapters.en:
Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has contentions? Who has complaints?
Who has needless wounds? Who has bloodshot eyes?
chapters.zh: 谁有祸患？谁有忧愁？ 谁有争斗？谁有哀叹〔注：或译：怨言〕？ 谁无故受伤？谁眼目红赤？

chapters.en: Those who linger over wine, who go to taste mixed drinks.
chapters.zh: 就是那流连饮酒、 常去寻找调和酒的人。

chapters.en:
Do not gaze at wine while it is red, when it sparkles in the cup
and goes down smoothly.
In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper.
chapters.zh: 酒发红，在杯中闪烁， 你不可观看， 〔虽然〕下咽舒畅， 终久是咬你如蛇，刺你如毒蛇。

chapters.en: Your eyes will see strange things, and your mind will utter perversities.
chapters.zh: 你眼必看见异怪的事〔注：或译：淫妇〕； 你心必发出乖谬的话。

chapters.en: You will be like one sleeping on the high seas or lying on the top of a mast:
chapters.zh: 你必像躺在海中， 或像卧在桅杆上。

chapters.en: “They struck me, but I feel no pain! They beat me, but I did not know it! When can I wake up to search for another drink?”
chapters.zh: 〔你必〕说：人打我，我却未受伤； 人鞭打我，我竟不觉得。 我几时清醒，我仍去寻酒。

chapters.en: Do not envy wicked men or desire their company;
chapters.zh: 你不要嫉妒恶人， 也不要起意与他们相处；
