chapters.en: for their hearts devise violence, and their lips declare trouble.
chapters.zh: 因为，他们的心图谋强暴， 他们的口谈论奸恶。

chapters.en: By wisdom a house is built and by understanding it is established;
chapters.zh: 房屋因智慧建造， 又因聪明立稳；

chapters.en: through knowledge its rooms are filled with every precious and beautiful treasure.
chapters.zh: 其中因知识充满各样美好宝贵的财物。

chapters.en: A wise man is strong, and a man of knowledge enhances his strength.
chapters.zh: 智慧人大有能力； 有知识的人力上加力。

chapters.en: Only with sound guidance should you wage war, and victory lies in a multitude of counselors.
chapters.zh: 你去打仗，要凭智谋； 谋士众多，人便得胜。

chapters.en: Wisdom is too high for a fool; he does not open his mouth in the meeting place.
chapters.zh: 智慧极高，非愚昧人所能及， 所以在城门内不敢开口。

chapters.en: He who plots evil will be called a schemer.
chapters.zh: 设计作恶的， 必称为奸人。

chapters.en: A foolish scheme is sin, and a mocker is detestable to men.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人的思念乃是罪恶； 亵慢者为人所憎恶。

chapters.en: If you faint in the day of distress, how small is your strength!
chapters.zh: 你在患难之日若胆怯， 你的力量就微小。

chapters.en: Rescue those being led away to death, and restrain those stumbling toward the slaughter.
chapters.zh: 人被拉到死地，你要解救； 人将被杀，你须拦阻。

chapters.en: If you say, “Behold, we did not know about this,” does not He who weighs hearts consider it? Does not the One who guards your life know? Will He not repay a man according to his deeds?
chapters.zh: 你若说：这事我未曾知道， 那衡量人心的岂不明白吗？ 保守你命的岂不知道吗？ 他岂不按各人所行的报应各人吗？

chapters.en: Eat honey, my son, for it is good, and the honeycomb is sweet to your taste.
chapters.zh: 我儿，你要吃蜜，因为是好的； 吃蜂房下滴的蜜便觉甘甜。

chapters.en:
Know therefore that wisdom is sweet to your soul. If you find it, there is a future for you,
and your hope will never be cut off.
chapters.zh: 你心得了智慧，也必觉得如此。 你若找着，至终必有善报； 你的指望也不致断绝。

chapters.en: Do not lie in wait, O wicked man, near the dwelling of the righteous; do not destroy his resting place.
chapters.zh: 你这恶人，不要埋伏攻击义人的家； 不要毁坏他安居之所。

chapters.en: For though a righteous man may fall seven times, he still gets up; but the wicked stumble in bad times.
chapters.zh: 因为，义人虽七次跌倒，仍必兴起； 恶人却被祸患倾倒。

chapters.en: Do not gloat when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart rejoice when he stumbles,
chapters.zh: 你仇敌跌倒，你不要欢喜； 他倾倒，你心不要快乐；

chapters.en: or the LORD will see and disapprove, and turn His wrath away from him.
chapters.zh: 恐怕耶和华看见就不喜悦， 将怒气从仇敌身上转过来。

chapters.en: Do not fret over evildoers, and do not be envious of the wicked.
chapters.zh: 不要为作恶的心怀不平， 也不要嫉妒恶人；

chapters.en: For the evil man has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
chapters.zh: 因为，恶人终不得善报； 恶人的灯也必熄灭。

chapters.en: My son, fear the LORD and the king, and do not associate with the rebellious.
chapters.zh: 我儿，你要敬畏耶和华与君王， 不要与反覆无常的人结交，

chapters.en: For they will bring sudden destruction. Who knows what ruin they can bring?
chapters.zh: 因为他们的灾难必忽然而起。 耶和华与君王所施行的毁灭， 谁能知道呢？

chapters.en: These also are sayings of the wise: To show partiality in judgment is not good.
chapters.zh: 以下也是智慧人的〔箴言〕： 审判时看人情面是不好的。

chapters.en: Whoever tells the guilty, “You are innocent”— peoples will curse him, and nations will denounce him;
chapters.zh: 对恶人说「你是义人」的， 这人万民必咒诅，列邦必憎恶。

chapters.en: but it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and rich blessing will come upon them.
chapters.zh: 责备〔恶人的〕，必得喜悦； 美好的福也必临到他。

chapters.en: An honest answer given is like a kiss on the lips.
chapters.zh: 应对正直的，犹如与人亲嘴。

chapters.en: Complete your outdoor work and prepare your field; after that, you may build your house.
chapters.zh: 你要在外头预备工料， 在田间办理整齐， 然后建造房屋。

chapters.en: Do not testify against your neighbor without cause, and do not deceive with your lips.
chapters.zh: 不可无故作见证陷害邻舍， 也不可用嘴欺骗人。

chapters.en: Do not say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”
chapters.zh: 不可说：人怎样待我，我也怎样待他； 我必照他所行的报复他。

chapters.en: I went past the field of a slacker and by the vineyard of a man lacking judgment.
chapters.zh: 我经过懒惰人的田地、 无知人的葡萄园，

chapters.en:
Thorns had grown up everywhere, thistles had covered the ground,
and the stone wall was broken down.
chapters.zh: 荆棘长满了地皮， 刺草遮盖了田面， 石墙也坍塌了。

chapters.en: I observed and took it to heart; I looked and received instruction:
chapters.zh: 我看见就留心思想； 我看着就领了训诲。

chapters.en: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,
chapters.zh: 再睡片时，打盹片时， 抱着手躺卧片时，

chapters.en: and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit.
chapters.zh: 你的贫穷就必如强盗速来， 你的缺乏仿佛拿兵器的人来到。

chapters.en: These are additional proverbs of Solomon, which were copied by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah:
chapters.zh: 以下也是所罗门的箴言，是犹大王希西家的人所誊录的。

chapters.en: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter and the glory of kings to search it out.
chapters.zh: 将事隐祕乃上帝的荣耀； 将事察清乃君王的荣耀。

chapters.en: As the heavens are high and the earth is deep, so the hearts of kings cannot be searched.
chapters.zh: 天之高，地之厚， 君王之心也测不透。

chapters.en: Remove the dross from the silver, and a vessel for a silversmith will come forth.
chapters.zh: 除去银子的渣滓就有〔银子〕出来， 银匠能以做器皿。

chapters.en: Remove the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
chapters.zh: 除去王面前的恶人， 国位就靠公义坚立。

chapters.en: Do not exalt yourself in the presence of the king, and do not stand in the place of great men;
chapters.zh: 不要在王面前妄自尊大； 不要在大人的位上站立。

chapters.en:
for it is better to be told, “Come up here!” than to be demoted in the presence of the prince.
Even what you have seen with your own eyes,
chapters.zh: 宁可有人说：请你上来， 强如在你觐见的王子面前叫你退下。

chapters.en: do not bring hastily to court. Otherwise, what will you do in the end when your neighbor puts you to shame?
chapters.zh: 不要冒失出去与人争竞， 免得至终被他羞辱， 你就〔不知道〕怎样行了。

chapters.en: Argue your case with your neighbor without betraying another’s confidence,
chapters.zh: 你与邻舍争讼， 要与他一人辩论， 不可洩漏人的密事，

chapters.en: lest he who hears you bring shame upon you, and your infamy never go away.
chapters.zh: 恐怕听见的人骂你， 你的臭名就难以脱离。

chapters.en: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
chapters.zh: 一句话说得合宜， 就如金苹果在银网子里。

chapters.en: Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold is a wise man’s rebuke to a listening ear.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的劝戒，在顺从的人耳中， 好像金耳环和精金的妆饰。

chapters.en:
Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him;
he refreshes the soul of his masters.
chapters.zh: 忠信的使者叫差他的人心里舒畅， 就如在收割时有冰雪的凉气。

chapters.en: Like clouds and wind without rain is the man who boasts of gifts never given.
chapters.zh: 空夸赠送礼物的， 好像无雨的风云。

chapters.en: Through patience a ruler can be persuaded, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.
chapters.zh: 恒常忍耐可以劝动君王； 柔和的舌头能折断骨头。

chapters.en: If you find honey, eat just what you need, lest you have too much and vomit it up.
chapters.zh: 你得了蜜吗？只可吃够而已， 恐怕你过饱就呕吐出来。

chapters.en: Seldom set foot in your neighbor’s house, lest he grow weary and hate you.
chapters.zh: 你的脚要少进邻舍的家， 恐怕他厌烦你，恨恶你。

chapters.en: Like a club or sword or sharp arrow is a man who bears false witness against his neighbor.
chapters.zh: 作假见证陷害邻舍的， 就是大槌，是利刀，是快箭。

chapters.en: Like a broken tooth or a foot out of joint is confidence in a faithless man in time of trouble.
chapters.zh: 患难时倚靠不忠诚的人， 好像破坏的牙，错骨缝的脚。

chapters.en:
Like one who removes a garment on a cold day or vinegar poured on a wound
is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
chapters.zh: 对伤心的人唱歌， 就如冷天脱衣服， 又如碱上倒醋。

chapters.en: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
chapters.zh: 你的仇敌若饿了，就给他饭吃； 若渴了，就给他水喝；

chapters.en: For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
chapters.zh: 因为，你〔这样行〕就是把炭火堆在他的头上； 耶和华也必赏赐你。

chapters.en: As the north wind brings forth rain, so a backbiting tongue brings angry looks.
chapters.zh: 北风生雨， 谗谤人的舌头也生怒容。

chapters.en: Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
chapters.zh: 宁可住在房顶的角上， 不在宽阔的房屋与争吵的妇人同住。

chapters.en: Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.
chapters.zh: 有好消息从远方来， 就如拿凉水给口渴的人喝。

chapters.en: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous man who gives way to the wicked.
chapters.zh: 义人在恶人面前退缩， 好像诜浑之泉，弄浊之井。

chapters.en: It is not good to eat too much honey or to search out one’s own glory.
chapters.zh: 吃蜜过多是不好的； 考究自己的荣耀也是可厌的。

chapters.en: Like a city whose walls are broken down is a man who does not control his temper.
chapters.zh: 人不制伏自己的心， 好像毁坏的城邑没有墙垣。

chapters.en: Like snow in summer and rain at harvest, honor does not befit a fool.
chapters.zh: 夏天落雪，收割时下雨，都不相宜； 愚昧人得尊荣也是如此。

chapters.en: Like a fluttering sparrow or darting swallow, an undeserved curse does not come to rest.
chapters.zh: 麻雀往来，燕子翻飞； 这样，无故的咒诅也必不临到。

chapters.en: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools!
chapters.zh: 鞭子是为打马，辔头是为勒驴； 刑杖是为打愚昧人的背。

chapters.en: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, or you yourself will be like him.
chapters.zh: 不要照愚昧人的愚妄话回答他， 恐怕你与他一样。

chapters.en: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he become wise in his own eyes.
chapters.zh: 要照愚昧人的愚妄话回答他， 免得他自以为有智慧。

chapters.en: Like cutting off one’s own feet or drinking violence is the sending of a message by the hand of a fool.
chapters.zh: 藉愚昧人手寄信的， 是砍断〔自己的〕脚，自受〔注：原文是：喝〕损害。

chapters.en: Like lame legs hanging limp is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
chapters.zh: 瘸子的脚空存无用； 箴言在愚昧人的口中也是如此。

chapters.en: Like binding a stone into a sling is the giving of honor to a fool.
chapters.zh: 将尊荣给愚昧人的， 好像人把石子包在机弦里。

chapters.en: Like a thorn that goes into the hand of a drunkard is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
chapters.zh: 箴言在愚昧人的口中， 好像荆棘刺入醉汉的手。

chapters.en: Like an archer who wounds at random is he who hires a fool or passerby.
chapters.zh: 雇愚昧人的，与雇过路人的， 就像射伤众人的弓箭手。

chapters.en: As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly.
chapters.zh: 愚昧人行愚妄事，行了又行， 就如狗转过来吃牠所吐的。

chapters.en: Do you see a man who is wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
chapters.zh: 你见自以为有智慧的人吗？ 愚昧人比他更有指望。

chapters.en: The slacker says, “A lion is in the road! A fierce lion roams the public square!”
chapters.zh: 懒惰人说：道上有猛狮， 街上有壮狮。

chapters.en: As a door turns on its hinges, so the slacker turns on his bed.
chapters.zh: 门在枢纽转动， 懒惰人在床上也是如此。

chapters.en: The slacker buries his hand in the dish; it wearies him to bring it back to his mouth.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人放手在盘子里， 就是向口撤回也以为劳乏。

chapters.en: The slacker is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer discreetly.
chapters.zh: 懒惰人看自己比七个善于应对的人更有智慧。

chapters.en: Like one who grabs a dog by the ears is a passerby who meddles in a quarrel not his own.
chapters.zh: 过路被事激动，管理不干己的争竞， 好像人揪住狗耳。

chapters.en: Like a madman shooting firebrands and deadly arrows,
so is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “I was only joking!”
chapters.zh: 人欺凌邻舍，却说： 我岂不是戏耍吗？ 他就像疯狂的人抛掷火把、利箭， 与杀人的兵器〔注：原文是死亡〕。

chapters.en: Without wood, a fire goes out; without gossip, a conflict ceases.
chapters.zh: 火缺了柴就必熄灭； 无人传舌，争竞便止息。

chapters.en: Like charcoal for embers and wood for fire, so is a quarrelsome man for kindling strife.
chapters.zh: 好争竞的人煽惑争端， 就如余火加炭，火上加柴一样。

chapters.en: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.
chapters.zh: 传舌人的言语，如同美食， 深入人的心腹。

chapters.en: Like glaze covering an earthen vessel are burning lips and a wicked heart.
chapters.zh: 火热的嘴，奸恶的心， 好像银渣包的瓦器。

chapters.en:
A hateful man disguises himself with his speech,
but he lays up deceit in his heart.
chapters.zh: 怨恨人的，用嘴粉饰， 心里却藏着诡诈；

chapters.en: When he speaks graciously, do not believe him, for seven abominations fill his heart.
chapters.zh: 他用甜言蜜语，你不可信他， 因为他心中有七样可憎恶的。

chapters.en: Though his hatred is concealed by deception, his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.
chapters.zh: 他虽用诡诈遮掩自己的怨恨， 他的邪恶必在会中显露。

chapters.en: He who digs a pit will fall into it, and he who rolls a stone will have it roll back on him.
chapters.zh: 挖陷坑的，自己必掉在其中； 滚石头的，石头必反滚在他身上。

chapters.en: A lying tongue hates those it crushes, and a flattering mouth causes ruin.
chapters.zh: 虚谎的舌恨他所压伤的人； 谄媚的口败坏人的事。

chapters.en: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
chapters.zh: 不要为明日自夸， 因为一日要生何事，你尚且不能知道。

chapters.en: Let another praise you, and not your own mouth— a stranger, and not your own lips.
chapters.zh: 要别人夸奖你，不可用口自夸； 等外人称赞你，不可用嘴自称。

chapters.en: A stone is heavy and sand is a burden, but aggravation from a fool outweighs them both.
chapters.zh: 石头重，沙土沉， 愚妄人的恼怒比这两样更重。

chapters.en: Wrath is cruel and anger is like a flood, but who can withstand jealousy?
chapters.zh: 忿怒为残忍，怒气为狂澜， 惟有嫉妒，谁能敌得住呢？

chapters.en: Better an open rebuke than love that is concealed.
chapters.zh: 当面的责备强如背地的爱情。

chapters.en: The wounds of a friend are faithful, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
chapters.zh: 朋友加的伤痕出于忠诚； 仇敌连连亲嘴却是多余。

chapters.en: The soul that is full loathes honey, but to a hungry soul, any bitter thing is sweet.
chapters.zh: 人吃饱了，厌恶蜂房的蜜； 人饥饿了，一切苦物都觉甘甜。

chapters.en: Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who wanders from his home.
chapters.zh: 人离本处飘流， 好像雀鸟离窝游飞。

chapters.en: Oil and incense bring joy to the heart, and the counsel of a friend is sweetness to the soul.
chapters.zh: 膏油与香料使人心喜悦； 朋友诚实的劝教也是如此甘美。

chapters.en:
Do not forsake your friend or your father’s friend, and do not go to your brother’s house
in the day of your calamity; better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away.
chapters.zh: 你的朋友和父亲的朋友， 你都不可离弃。 你遭难的日子，不要上弟兄的家去； 相近的邻舍强如远方的弟兄。

chapters.en: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, so that I can answer him who taunts me.
chapters.zh: 我儿，你要作智慧人，好叫我的心欢喜， 使我可以回答那讥诮我的人。

chapters.en: The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
chapters.zh: 通达人见祸藏躲； 愚蒙人前往受害。

chapters.en: Take the garment of him who posts security for a stranger; get collateral if it is for a foreigner.
chapters.zh: 谁为生人作保，就拿谁的衣服； 谁为外女〔作保〕，谁就承当。

chapters.en: If one blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be counted to him as a curse.
chapters.zh: 清晨起来，大声给朋友祝福的， 就算是咒诅他。

chapters.en: A constant dripping on a rainy day and a contentious woman are alike—
chapters.zh: 大雨之日连连滴漏， 和争吵的妇人一样；

chapters.en: restraining her is like holding back the wind or grasping oil with one’s right hand.
chapters.zh: 想拦阻她的，便是拦阻风， 也是右手抓油。

chapters.en: As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.
chapters.zh: 铁磨铁，磨出刃来； 朋友相感〔注：原文是磨朋友的脸〕也是如此。

chapters.en: Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and he who looks after his master will be honored.
chapters.zh: 看守无花果树的，必吃树上的果子； 敬奉主人的，必得尊荣。

chapters.en: As water reflects the face, so the heart reflects the true man.
chapters.zh: 水中照脸，彼此〔相符〕； 人与人，心也〔相对〕。

chapters.en: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.
chapters.zh: 阴间和灭亡永不满足； 人的眼目也是如此。

chapters.en: A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but a man is tested by the praise accorded him.
chapters.zh: 鼎为炼银，炉为炼金， 人的称赞也〔试炼〕人。

chapters.en: Though you grind a fool like grain with mortar and a pestle, yet his folly will not depart from him.
chapters.zh: 你虽用杵将愚妄人与打碎的麦子一同捣在臼中， 他的愚妄还是离不了他。

chapters.en: Be sure to know the state of your flocks, and pay close attention to your herds;
chapters.zh: 你要详细知道你羊群的景况， 留心料理你的牛群；

chapters.en: for riches are not forever, nor does a crown endure to every generation.
chapters.zh: 因为资财不能永有， 冠冕岂能存到万代？

chapters.en: When hay is removed and new growth appears and the grass from the hills is gathered,
chapters.zh: 干草割去，嫩草发现， 山上的菜蔬也被收敛。

chapters.en: the lambs will provide you with clothing, and the goats with the price of a field.
chapters.zh: 羊羔〔之毛〕是为你作衣服； 山羊是为作田地的价值，

chapters.en:
You will have plenty of goats’ milk to feed you— food for your household
and nourishment for your maidservants.
chapters.zh: 并有母山羊奶够你吃， 也够你的家眷吃， 且够养你的婢女。

chapters.en: The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
chapters.zh: 恶人虽无人追赶也逃跑； 义人却胆壮像狮子。

chapters.en: A land in rebellion has many rulers, but a man of understanding and knowledge maintains order.
chapters.zh: 邦国因有罪过，君王就多〔更换〕； 因有聪明知识的人，国必长存。

chapters.en: A destitute leader who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain that leaves no food.
chapters.zh: 穷人欺压贫民， 好像暴雨〔冲〕没粮食。

chapters.en: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but those who keep the law resist them.
chapters.zh: 违弃律法的，夸奖恶人； 遵守律法的，却与恶人相争。

chapters.en: Evil men do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD comprehend fully.
chapters.zh: 坏人不明白公义； 惟有寻求耶和华的，无不明白。

chapters.en: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a rich man whose ways are perverse.
chapters.zh: 行为纯正的穷乏人 胜过行事乖僻的富足人。

chapters.en: A discerning son keeps the law, but a companion of gluttons disgraces his father.
chapters.zh: 谨守律法的，是智慧之子； 与贪食人作伴的，却羞辱其父。

chapters.en: He who increases his wealth by interest and usury lays it up for one who is kind to the poor.
chapters.zh: 人以〔厚〕利加增财物， 是给那怜悯穷人者积蓄的。

chapters.en: Whoever turns his ear away from hearing the law, even his prayer is detestable.
chapters.zh: 转耳不听律法的， 他的祈祷也为可憎。

chapters.en: He who leads the upright along the path of evil will fall into his own pit, but the blameless will inherit what is good.
chapters.zh: 诱惑正直人行恶道的，必掉在自己的坑里； 惟有完全人必承受福分。

chapters.en: A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but a poor man with discernment sees through him.
chapters.zh: 富足人自以为有智慧， 但聪明的贫穷人能将他查透。

chapters.en: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory, but when the wicked rise, men hide themselves.
chapters.zh: 义人得志，有大荣耀； 恶人兴起，人就躲藏。

chapters.en: He who conceals his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them will find mercy.
chapters.zh: 遮掩自己罪过的，必不亨通； 承认离弃罪过的，必蒙怜恤。

chapters.en: Blessed is the man who is always reverent, but he who hardens his heart falls into trouble.
chapters.zh: 常存敬畏的，便为有福； 心存刚硬的，必陷在祸患里。

chapters.en: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
chapters.zh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民， 好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

chapters.en: A leader who lacks judgment is also a great oppressor, but he who hates dishonest profit will prolong his days.
chapters.zh: 无知的君多行暴虐； 以贪财为可恨的，必年长日久。

chapters.en: A man burdened by bloodguilt will flee into the Pit; let no one support him.
chapters.zh: 背负流人血之罪的，必往坑里奔跑， 谁也不可拦阻他。

chapters.en: He who walks with integrity will be kept safe, but whoever is perverse in his ways will suddenly fall.
chapters.zh: 行动正直的，必蒙拯救； 行事弯曲的，立时跌倒。

chapters.en: The one who works his land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases fantasies will have his fill of poverty.
chapters.zh: 耕种自己田地的，必得饱食； 追随虚浮的，足受穷乏。

chapters.en: A faithful man will abound with blessings, but one eager to be rich will not go unpunished.
chapters.zh: 诚实人必多得福； 想要急速发财的，不免受罚。

chapters.en: To show partiality is not good, yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.
chapters.zh: 看人的情面乃为不好； 人因一块饼枉法也为不好。

chapters.en: A stingy man hastens after wealth and does not know that poverty awaits him.
chapters.zh: 人有恶眼想要急速发财， 却不知穷乏必临到他身。

chapters.en: He who rebukes a man will later find more favor than one who flatters with his tongue.
chapters.zh: 责备人的，后来蒙人喜悦， 多于那用舌头谄媚人的。

chapters.en: He who robs his father or mother, saying, “It is not wrong,” is a companion to the man who destroys.
chapters.zh: 偷窃父母的，说：这不是罪， 此人就是与强盗同类。

chapters.en: A greedy man stirs up strife, but he who trusts in the LORD will prosper.
chapters.zh: 心中贪婪的，挑起争端； 倚靠耶和华的，必得丰裕。

chapters.en: He who trusts in himself is a fool, but one who walks in wisdom will be safe.
chapters.zh: 心中自是的，便是愚昧人； 凭智慧行事的，必蒙拯救。

chapters.en: Whoever gives to the poor will not be in need, but he who hides his eyes will receive many curses.
chapters.zh: 赒济贫穷的，不致缺乏； 佯为不见的，必多受咒诅。

chapters.en: When the wicked come to power, people hide themselves; but when they perish, the righteous flourish.
chapters.zh: 恶人兴起，人就躲藏； 恶人败亡，义人增多。

chapters.en: A man who remains stiff-necked after much reproof will suddenly be shattered beyond recovery.
chapters.zh: 人屡次受责罚，仍然硬着颈项； 他必顷刻败坏，无法可治。

chapters.en: When the righteous flourish, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
chapters.zh: 义人增多，民就喜乐； 恶人掌权，民就叹息。

chapters.en: A man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a companion of prostitutes squanders his wealth.
chapters.zh: 爱慕智慧的，使父亲喜乐； 与妓女结交的，却浪费钱财。

chapters.en: By justice a king brings stability to the land, but a man who exacts tribute demolishes it.
chapters.zh: 王藉公平，使国坚定； 索要贿赂，使国倾败。

chapters.en: A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.
chapters.zh: 谄媚邻舍的， 就是设网罗绊他的脚。

chapters.en: An evil man is caught by his own sin, but a righteous one sings and rejoices.
chapters.zh: 恶人犯罪，自陷网罗； 惟独义人欢呼喜乐。

chapters.en: The righteous consider the cause of the poor, but the wicked have no regard for such concerns.
chapters.zh: 义人知道查明穷人的案； 恶人没有聪明，就不得而知。

chapters.en: Mockers inflame a city, but the wise turn away anger.
chapters.zh: 亵慢人煽惑通城； 智慧人止息众怒。

chapters.en: If a wise man goes to court with a fool, there will be raving and laughing with no resolution.
chapters.zh: 智慧人与愚妄人相争， 或怒或笑，总不能使他止息。

chapters.en: Men of bloodshed hate a blameless man, but the upright care for his life.
chapters.zh: 好流人血的，恨恶完全人， 索取正直人的性命。

chapters.en: A fool vents all his anger, but a wise man holds it back.
chapters.zh: 愚妄人怒气全发； 智慧人忍气含怒。

chapters.en: If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials will be wicked.
chapters.zh: 君王若听谎言， 他一切臣仆都是奸恶。

chapters.en: The poor man and the oppressor have this in common: The LORD gives light to the eyes of both.
chapters.zh: 贫穷人、强暴人在世相遇； 他们的眼目都蒙耶和华光照。

chapters.en: A king who judges the poor with fairness— his throne will be established forever.
chapters.zh: 君王凭诚实判断穷人； 他的国位必永远坚立。

chapters.en: A rod of correction imparts wisdom, but a child left to himself disgraces his mother.
chapters.zh: 杖打和责备能加增智慧； 放纵的儿子使母亲羞愧。

chapters.en: When the wicked thrive, rebellion increases; but the righteous will see their downfall.
chapters.zh: 恶人加多，过犯也加多， 义人必看见他们跌倒。

chapters.en: Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will bring delight to your soul.
chapters.zh: 管教你的儿子，他就使你得安息， 也必使你心里喜乐。

chapters.en: Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint; but blessed is he who keeps the Law.
chapters.zh: 没有异象〔注：或译：默示〕，民就放肆； 惟遵守律法的，便为有福。

chapters.en: A servant cannot be corrected by words alone; though he understands, he will not respond.
chapters.zh: 只用言语，仆人不肯受管教； 他虽然明白，也不留意。

chapters.en: Do you see a man who speaks in haste? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
chapters.zh: 你见言语急躁的人吗？ 愚昧人比他更有指望。

chapters.en: A servant pampered from his youth will bring grief in the end.
chapters.zh: 人将仆人从小娇养， 这仆人终久必成了他的儿子。

chapters.en: An angry man stirs up dissension, and a hot-tempered man abounds in transgression.
chapters.zh: 好气的人挑启争端； 暴怒的人多多犯罪。

chapters.en: A man’s pride will bring him low, but a humble spirit will obtain honor.
chapters.zh: 人的高傲必使他卑下； 心里谦逊的，必得尊荣。

chapters.en: A partner to a thief hates his own soul; he receives the oath but does not testify.
chapters.zh: 人与盗贼分赃，是恨恶自己的性命； 他听见叫人发誓的声音，却不言语。

chapters.en: The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.
chapters.zh: 惧怕人的，陷入网罗； 惟有倚靠耶和华的，必得安稳。

chapters.en: Many seek the ruler’s favor, but a man receives justice from the LORD.
chapters.zh: 求王恩的人多； 定人事乃在耶和华。

chapters.en: An unjust man is detestable to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is detestable to the wicked.
chapters.zh: 为非作歹的，被义人憎嫌； 行事正直的，被恶人憎恶。

chapters.en:
These are the words of Agur son of Jakeh—the burden that this man declared to Ithiel:
“I am weary, O God, and worn out.
chapters.zh: 雅基的儿子亚古珥的言语就是真言。 这人对以铁和乌甲说：

chapters.en: Surely I am the most ignorant of men, and I lack the understanding of a man.
chapters.zh: 我比众人更蠢笨， 也没有人的聪明。

chapters.en: I have not learned wisdom, and I have no knowledge of the Holy One.
chapters.zh: 我没有学好智慧， 也不认识至圣者。

chapters.en: Who has ascended to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in His hands? Who has bound up the waters in His cloak? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is His name, and what is the name of His Son— surely you know!
chapters.zh: 谁升天又降下来？ 谁聚风在掌握中？ 谁包水在衣服里？ 谁立定地的四极？ 他名叫什么？ 他儿子名叫什么？ 你知道吗？

chapters.en: Every word of God is flawless; He is a shield to those who take refuge in Him.
chapters.zh: 上帝的言语句句都是炼净的； 投靠他的，他便作他们的盾牌。

chapters.en: Do not add to His words, lest He rebuke you and prove you a liar.
chapters.zh: 他的言语，你不可加添， 恐怕他责备你，你就显为说谎言的。

chapters.en: Two things I ask of You— do not refuse me before I die:
chapters.zh: 我求你两件事， 在我未死之先，不要不赐给我：

chapters.en:
Keep falsehood and deceitful words far from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches;
feed me with the bread that is my portion.
chapters.zh: 求你使虚假和谎言远离我； 使我也不贫穷也不富足； 赐给我需用的饮食，

chapters.en: Otherwise, I may have too much and deny You, saying, ‘Who is the LORD?’ Or I may become poor and steal, profaning the name of my God.
chapters.zh: 恐怕我饱足不认〔你〕，说： 耶和华是谁呢？ 又恐怕我贫穷就偷窃， 以致亵渎我上帝的名。

chapters.en: Do not slander a servant to his master, or he will curse you, and you will bear the guilt.
chapters.zh: 你不要向主人谗谤仆人， 恐怕他咒诅你，你便算为有罪。

chapters.en: There is a generation of those who curse their fathers and do not bless their mothers.
chapters.zh: 有一宗人〔注：宗：原文是代；下同〕，咒诅父亲， 不给母亲祝福。

chapters.en: There is a generation of those who are pure in their own eyes and yet unwashed of their filth.
chapters.zh: 有一宗人，自以为清洁， 却没有洗去自己的污秽。

chapters.en: There is a generation—how haughty are their eyes and pretentious are their glances—
chapters.zh: 有一宗人，眼目何其高傲， 眼皮也是高举。

chapters.en: there is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose jaws are knives, devouring the oppressed from the earth and the needy from among men.
chapters.zh: 有一宗人，牙如剑，齿如刀， 要吞灭地上的困苦人和世间的穷乏人。

chapters.en:
The leech has two daughters: Give and Give.
There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say, ‘Enough!’:
chapters.zh: 蚂蟥有两个女儿， 〔常说〕：给呀，给呀！ 有三样不知足的， 连不说「够的」共有四样：

chapters.en:
Sheol,
the barren womb,
land never satisfied with water,
and fire that never says, ‘Enough!’
chapters.zh: 就是阴间和石胎， 浸水不足的地，并火。

chapters.en: As for the eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience to a mother, may the ravens of the valley pluck it out and young vultures devour it.
chapters.zh: 戏笑父亲、藐视而不听从母亲的， 他的眼睛必为谷中的乌鸦啄出来，为鹰雏所吃。

chapters.en: There are three things too wonderful for me, four that I cannot understand:
chapters.zh: 我所测不透的奇妙有三样， 连我所不知道的共有四样：

chapters.en:
the way of an eagle in the sky,
the way of a snake on a rock,
the way of a ship at sea,
and the way of a man with a maiden.
chapters.zh: 就是鹰在空中飞的道； 蛇在磐石上爬的道； 船在海中行的道； 男与女交合的道。

chapters.en:
This is the way of an adulteress: She eats and wipes her mouth
and says, ‘I have done nothing wrong.’
chapters.zh: 淫妇的道也是这样： 她吃了，把嘴一擦就说： 我没有行恶。

chapters.en: Under three things the earth trembles, under four it cannot bear up:
chapters.zh: 使地震动的有三样， 连地担不起的共有四样：

chapters.en:
a servant who becomes king,
a fool who is filled with food,
chapters.zh: 就是仆人作王； 愚顽人吃饱；

chapters.en:
an unloved woman who marries,
and a maidservant who supplants her mistress.
chapters.zh: 丑恶的女子出嫁； 婢女接续主母。

chapters.en: Four things on earth are small, yet they are exceedingly wise:
chapters.zh: 地上有四样小物，却甚聪明：

chapters.en: The ants are creatures of little strength, yet they store up their food in the summer;
chapters.zh: 蚂蚁是无力之类， 却在夏天预备粮食。

chapters.en: the rock badgers are creatures of little power, yet they make their homes in the rocks;
chapters.zh: 沙番是软弱之类， 却在磐石中造房。

chapters.en: the locusts have no king, yet they all advance in formation;
chapters.zh: 蝗虫没有君王， 却分队而出。

chapters.en: and the lizard can be caught in one’s hands, yet it is found in the palaces of kings.
chapters.zh: 守宫用爪抓〔墙〕， 却住在王宫。

chapters.en: There are three things that are stately in their stride, and four that are impressive in their walk:
chapters.zh: 步行威武的有三样， 连行走威武的共有四样：

chapters.en: a lion, mighty among beasts, refusing to retreat before anything;
chapters.zh: 就是狮子－乃百兽中最为猛烈、无所躲避的，
猎狗，公山羊，和无人能敌的君王。

chapters.en:
If you have foolishly exalted yourself or if you have plotted evil,
put your hand over your mouth.
chapters.zh: 你若行事愚顽，自高自傲， 或是怀了恶念，就当用手〔捂口〕。

chapters.en:
For as the churning of milk yields butter, and the twisting of the nose draws blood,
so the stirring of anger brings forth strife.”
chapters.zh: 摇牛奶必成奶油； 扭鼻子必出血。 照样，激动怒气必起争端。

chapters.en: These are the words of King Lemuel—the burden that his mother taught him:
chapters.zh: 利慕伊勒王的言语，是他母亲教训他的真言。

chapters.en:
What shall I say, O my son? What, O son of my womb?
What, O son of my vows?
chapters.zh: 我的儿啊，我腹中生的儿啊， 我许愿得的儿啊！我当怎样〔教训〕你呢？

chapters.en: Do not spend your strength on women or your vigor on those who ruin kings.
chapters.zh: 不要将你的精力给妇女； 也不要有败坏君王的行为。

chapters.en:
It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine,
or for rulers to crave strong drink,
chapters.zh: 利慕伊勒啊，君王喝酒，君王喝酒不相宜； 王子说浓酒在那里也不相宜；

chapters.en: lest they drink and forget what is decreed, depriving all the oppressed of justice.
chapters.zh: 恐怕喝了就忘记律例， 颠倒一切困苦人的是非。

chapters.en: Give strong drink to one who is perishing, and wine to the bitter in soul.
chapters.zh: 可以把浓酒给将亡的人喝， 把〔清〕酒给苦心的人喝，

chapters.en: Let him drink and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
chapters.zh: 让他喝了，就忘记他的贫穷， 不再记念他的苦楚。

chapters.en: Open your mouth for those with no voice, for the cause of all the dispossessed.
chapters.zh: 你当为哑巴〔注：或译：不能自辩的〕开口， 为一切孤独的伸冤。

chapters.en: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and defend the cause of the poor and needy.
chapters.zh: 你当开口按公义判断， 为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

chapters.en: A wife of noble character, who can find? She is far more precious than rubies.
chapters.zh: 才德的妇人谁能得着呢？ 她的价值远胜过珍珠。

chapters.en: The heart of her husband trusts in her, and he lacks nothing of value.
chapters.zh: 她丈夫心里倚靠她， 必不缺少利益；

chapters.en: She brings him good and not harm all the days of her life.
chapters.zh: 她一生使丈夫有益无损。

chapters.en: She selects wool and flax and works with eager hands.
chapters.zh: 她寻找羊羢和麻， 甘心用手做工。

chapters.en: She is like the merchant ships, bringing her food from afar.
chapters.zh: 她好像商船从远方运粮来，

chapters.en:
She rises while it is still night to provide food for her household
and portions for her maidservants.
chapters.zh: 未到黎明她就起来， 把食物分给家中的人， 将当做的工分派婢女。

chapters.en: She appraises a field and buys it; from her earnings she plants a vineyard.
chapters.zh: 她想得田地就买来； 用手所得之利栽种葡萄园。

chapters.en: She girds herself with strength and shows that her arms are strong.
chapters.zh: 她以能力束腰， 使膀臂有力。

chapters.en: She sees that her gain is good, and her lamp is not extinguished at night.
chapters.zh: 她觉得所经营的有利； 她的灯终夜不灭。

chapters.en: She stretches out her hands to the distaff and grasps the spindle with her fingers.
chapters.zh: 她手拿撚线竿， 手把纺线车。

chapters.en: She opens her arms to the poor and reaches out her hands to the needy.
chapters.zh: 她张手赒济困苦人， 伸手帮补穷乏人。

chapters.en: When it snows, she has no fear for her household, for they are all clothed in scarlet.
chapters.zh: 她不因下雪为家里的人担心， 因为全家都穿着朱红衣服。

chapters.en: She makes coverings for her bed; her clothing is fine linen and purple.
chapters.zh: 她为自己制作绣花毯子； 她的衣服是细麻和紫色布做的。

chapters.en: Her husband is known at the city gates, where he sits among the elders of the land.
chapters.zh: 她丈夫在城门口与本地的长老同坐， 为众人所认识。

chapters.en: She makes linen garments and sells them; she delivers sashes to the merchants.
chapters.zh: 她做细麻布衣裳出卖， 又将腰带卖与商家。

chapters.en: Strength and honor are her clothing, and she can laugh at the days to come.
chapters.zh: 能力和威仪是她的衣服； 她〔想到〕日后的景况就喜笑。

chapters.en: She opens her mouth with wisdom, and faithful instruction is on her tongue.
chapters.zh: 她开口就发智慧； 她舌上有仁慈的法则。

chapters.en: She watches over the affairs of her household and does not eat the bread of idleness.
chapters.zh: 她观察家务， 并不吃闲饭。

chapters.en: Her children rise up and call her blessed; her husband praises her as well:
chapters.zh: 她的儿女起来称她有福； 她的丈夫也称赞她，

chapters.en: “Many daughters have done noble things, but you surpass them all!”
chapters.zh: 说：才德的女子很多， 惟独你超过一切。

chapters.en: Charm is deceptive and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.
chapters.zh: 艳丽是虚假的，美容是虚浮的； 惟敬畏耶和华的妇女必得称赞。

chapters.en: Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her at the gates.
chapters.zh: 愿她享受操作所得的； 愿她的工作在城门口荣耀她。

chapters.en: These are the words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem:
chapters.zh: 在耶路撒冷作王、大卫的儿子、传道者的言语。

chapters.en: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher, “futility of futilities! Everything is futile!”
chapters.zh: 传道者说：虚空的虚空， 虚空的虚空，凡事都是虚空。

chapters.en: What does a man gain from all his labor, at which he toils under the sun?
chapters.zh: 人一切的劳碌， 就是他在日光之下的劳碌，有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: Generations come and generations go, but the earth remains forever.
chapters.zh: 一代过去，一代又来， 地却永远长存。

chapters.en: The sun rises and the sun sets; it hurries back to where it rises.
chapters.zh: 日头出来，日头落下， 急归所出之地。

chapters.en: The wind blows southward, then turns northward; round and round it swirls, ever returning on its course.
chapters.zh: 风往南刮，又向北转， 不住地旋转，而且返回转行原道。

chapters.en: All the rivers flow into the sea, yet the sea is never full; to the place from which the streams come, there again they flow.
chapters.zh: 江河都往海里流，海却不满； 江河从何处流，仍归还何处。

chapters.en: All things are wearisome, more than one can describe; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear content with hearing.
chapters.zh: 万事令人厌烦〔注：或译：万物满有困乏〕， 人不能说尽。 眼看，看不饱； 耳听，听不足。

chapters.en:
What has been will be again, and what has been done will be done again;
there is nothing new under the sun.
chapters.zh: 已有的事后必再有； 已行的事后必再行。 日光之下并无新事。

chapters.en: Is there a case where one can say, “Look, this is new”? It has already existed in the ages before us.
chapters.zh: 岂有一件事人能指着说这是新的？ 〔哪知〕，在我们以前的世代早已有了。

chapters.en: There is no remembrance of those who came before, and those yet to come will not be remembered by those who follow after.
chapters.zh: 已过的〔世代〕，无人记念； 将来的〔世代〕，后来的人也不记念。

chapters.en: I, the Teacher, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 我传道者在耶路撒冷作过以色列的王。

chapters.en: And I set my mind to seek and explore by wisdom all that is done under heaven. What a miserable task God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them!
chapters.zh: 我专心用智慧寻求、查究天下所做的一切事，〔乃知〕上帝叫世人所经练的是极重的劳苦。

chapters.en: I have seen all the things that are done under the sun, and have found them all to be futile, a pursuit of the wind.
chapters.zh: 我见日光之下所做的一切事，都是虚空，都是捕风。

chapters.en: What is crooked cannot be straightened, and what is lacking cannot be counted.
chapters.zh: 弯曲的，不能变直； 缺少的，不能足数。

chapters.en: I said to myself, “Behold, I have grown and increased in wisdom beyond all those before me who were over Jerusalem, and my mind has observed a wealth of wisdom and knowledge.”
chapters.zh: 我心里议论说：我得了大智慧，胜过我以前在耶路撒冷的众人，而且我心中多经历智慧和知识的事。

chapters.en: So I set my mind to know wisdom and madness and folly; I learned that this, too, is a pursuit of the wind.
chapters.zh: 我又专心察明智慧、狂妄，和愚昧，乃知这也是捕风。

chapters.en: For with much wisdom comes much sorrow, and as knowledge grows, grief increases.
chapters.zh: 因为多有智慧，就多有愁烦； 加增知识的，就加增忧伤。

chapters.en:
I said to myself, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure; enjoy what is good!”
But it proved to be futile.
chapters.zh: 我心里说：「来吧，我以喜乐试试你，你好享福！」谁知，这也是虚空。

chapters.en: I said of laughter, “It is folly,” and of pleasure, “What does it accomplish?”
chapters.zh: 我指嬉笑说：「这是狂妄。」论喜乐说：「有何功效呢？」

chapters.en: I sought to cheer my body with wine and to embrace folly—my mind still guiding me with wisdom—until I could see what was worthwhile for men to do under heaven during the few days of their lives.
chapters.zh: 我心里察究，如何用酒使我肉体舒畅，我心却仍以智慧引导〔我〕；又如何持住愚昧，等我看明世人，在天下一生当行何事为美。

chapters.en: I expanded my pursuits. I built houses and planted vineyards for myself.
chapters.zh: 我为自己动大工程，建造房屋，栽种葡萄园，

chapters.en: I made gardens and parks for myself, where I planted all kinds of fruit trees.
chapters.zh: 修造园囿，在其中栽种各样果木树；

chapters.en: I built reservoirs to water my groves of flourishing trees.
chapters.zh: 挖造水池，用以浇灌嫩小的树木。

chapters.en: I acquired menservants and maidservants, and servants were born in my house. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone in Jerusalem before me,
chapters.zh: 我买了仆婢，也有生在家中的仆婢；又有许多牛群羊群，胜过以前在耶路撒冷众人所有的。

chapters.en: and I accumulated for myself silver and gold and the treasure of kings and provinces. I gathered to myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of men—many concubines.
chapters.zh: 我又为自己积蓄金银和君王的财宝，并各省的财宝；又得唱歌的男女和世人所喜爱的物，并许多的妃嫔。

chapters.en: So I became great and surpassed all in Jerusalem who had preceded me; and my wisdom remained with me.
chapters.zh: 这样，我就日见昌盛，胜过以前在耶路撒冷的众人。我的智慧仍然存留。

chapters.en: Anything my eyes desired, I did not deny myself. I refused my heart no pleasure. For my heart took delight in all my work, and this was the reward for all my labor.
chapters.zh: 凡我眼所求的，我没有留下不给它的；我心所乐的，我没有禁止不享受的；因我的心为我一切所劳碌的快乐，这就是我从劳碌中所得的分。

chapters.en: Yet when I considered all the works that my hands had accomplished and what I had toiled to achieve, I found everything to be futile, a pursuit of the wind; there was nothing to be gained under the sun.
chapters.zh: 后来，我察看我手所经营的一切事和我劳碌所成的功。谁知都是虚空，都是捕风；在日光之下毫无益处。

chapters.en: Then I turned to consider wisdom and madness and folly; for what more can the king’s successor do than what has already been accomplished?
chapters.zh: 我转念观看智慧、狂妄，和愚昧。在王以后而来的人还能做什么呢？也不过行早先所行的就是了。

chapters.en: And I saw that wisdom exceeds folly, just as light exceeds darkness:
chapters.zh: 我便看出智慧胜过愚昧，如同光明胜过黑暗。

chapters.en:
The wise man has eyes in his head, but the fool walks in darkness.
Yet I also came to realize that one fate overcomes them both.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的眼目光明〔注：光明：原文是在他头上〕，愚昧人在黑暗里行。我却看明有一件事，这两等人都必遇见。

chapters.en:
So I said to myself, “The fate of the fool will also befall me. What then have I gained by being wise?”
And I said to myself that this too is futile.
chapters.zh: 我就心里说：「愚昧人所遇见的，我也必遇见，我为何更有智慧呢？」我心里说，这也是虚空。

chapters.en: For there is no lasting remembrance of the wise, just as with the fool, seeing that both will be forgotten in the days to come. Alas, the wise man will die just like the fool!
chapters.zh: 智慧人和愚昧人一样，永远无人记念，因为日后都被忘记；可叹智慧人死亡，与愚昧人无异。

chapters.en: So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was grievous to me. For everything is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
chapters.zh: 我所以恨恶生命；因为在日光之下所行的事我都以为烦恼，都是虚空，都是捕风。

chapters.en: I hated all for which I had toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.
chapters.zh: 我恨恶一切的劳碌，就是我在日光之下的劳碌，因为我得来的必留给我以后的人。

chapters.en: And who knows whether that man will be wise or foolish? Yet he will take over all the labor at which I have worked skillfully under the sun. This too is futile.
chapters.zh: 那人是智慧是愚昧，谁能知道？他竟要管理我劳碌所得的，就是我在日光之下用智慧所得的。这也是虚空。

chapters.en: So my heart began to despair over all the labor that I had done under the sun.
chapters.zh: 故此，我转想我在日光之下所劳碌的一切工作，心便绝望。

chapters.en: When there is a man who has labored with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, and he must give his portion to a man who has not worked for it, this too is futile and a great evil.
chapters.zh: 因为有人用智慧、知识、灵巧所劳碌得来的，却要留给未曾劳碌的人为分。这也是虚空，也是大患。

chapters.en: For what does a man get for all the toil and striving with which he labors under the sun?
chapters.zh: 人在日光之下劳碌累心，在他一切的劳碌上得着什么呢？

chapters.en: Indeed, all his days are filled with grief, and his task is sorrowful; even at night, his mind does not rest. This too is futile.
chapters.zh: 因为他日日忧虑，他的劳苦成为愁烦，连夜间心也不安。这也是虚空。

chapters.en: Nothing is better for a man than to eat and drink and enjoy his work. I have also seen that this is from the hand of God.
chapters.zh: 人莫强如吃喝，且在劳碌中享福，我看这也是出于上帝的手。

chapters.en: For apart from Him, who can eat and who can find enjoyment?
chapters.zh: 论到吃用、享福，谁能胜过我呢？

chapters.en: To the man who is pleasing in His sight, He gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner He assigns the task of gathering and accumulating that which he will hand over to one who pleases God. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
chapters.zh: 上帝喜悦谁，就给谁智慧、知识，和喜乐；惟有罪人，上帝使他劳苦，叫他将所收聚的、所堆积的归给上帝所喜悦的人。这也是虚空，也是捕风。

chapters.en: To everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven:
chapters.zh: 凡事都有定期， 天下万务都有定时。

chapters.en: a time to be born and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot,
chapters.zh: 生有时，死有时； 栽种有时，拔出所栽种的也有时；

chapters.en: a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to break down and a time to build,
chapters.zh: 杀戮有时，医治有时； 拆毁有时，建造有时；

chapters.en: a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to mourn and a time to dance,
chapters.zh: 哭有时，笑有时； 哀恸有时，跳舞有时；

chapters.en: a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together, a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing,
chapters.zh: 抛掷石头有时，堆聚石头有时； 怀抱有时，不怀抱有时；

chapters.en: a time to search and a time to count as lost, a time to keep and a time to discard,
chapters.zh: 寻找有时，失落有时； 保守有时，舍弃有时；

chapters.en: a time to tear and a time to mend, a time to be silent and a time to speak,
chapters.zh: 撕裂有时，缝补有时； 静默有时，言语有时；

chapters.en: a time to love and a time to hate, a time for war and a time for peace.
chapters.zh: 喜爱有时，恨恶有时； 争战有时，和好有时。

chapters.en: What does the worker gain from his toil?
chapters.zh: 〔这样看来〕，做事的人在他的劳碌上有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: I have seen the burden that God has laid upon the sons of men to occupy them.
chapters.zh: 我见上帝叫世人劳苦，使他们在其中受经练。

chapters.en: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in the hearts of men, yet they cannot fathom the work that God has done from beginning to end.
chapters.zh: 上帝造万物，各按其时成为美好，又将永生〔注：原文是永远〕安置在世人心里。然而上帝从始至终的作为，人不能参透。

chapters.en: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and do good while they live,
chapters.zh: 我知道世人，莫强如终身喜乐行善；

chapters.en: and also that every man should eat and drink and find satisfaction in all his labor—this is the gift of God.
chapters.zh: 并且人人吃喝，在他一切劳碌中享福，这也是上帝的恩赐。

chapters.en: I know that everything God does endures forever; nothing can be added to it or taken from it. God does it so that they should fear Him.
chapters.zh: 我知道上帝一切所做的都必永存；无所增添，无所减少。上帝这样行，是要人在他面前存敬畏的心。

chapters.en: What exists has already been, and what will be has already been, for God will call to account what has passed.
chapters.zh: 现今的事早先就有了，将来的事早已也有了，并且上帝使已过的事重新再来〔注：或译：并且上帝再寻回已过的事〕。

chapters.en: Furthermore, I saw under the sun that in the place of judgment there is wickedness, and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.
chapters.zh: 我又见日光之下，在审判之处有奸恶，在公义之处也有奸恶。

chapters.en: I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked, since there is a time for every activity and every deed.”
chapters.zh: 我心里说，上帝必审判义人和恶人；因为在那里，各样事务，一切工作，都有定时。

chapters.en: I said to myself, “As for the sons of men, God tests them so that they may see for themselves that they are but beasts.”
chapters.zh: 我心里说，〔这乃〕为世人的缘故，是上帝要试验他们，使他们觉得自己〔不过像〕兽一样。

chapters.en: For the fates of both men and beasts are the same: As one dies, so dies the other—they all have the same breath. Man has no advantage over the animals, since everything is futile.
chapters.zh: 因为世人遭遇的，兽也遭遇，所遭遇的都是一样：这个怎样死，那个也怎样死，气息都是一样。人不能强于兽，都是虚空。

chapters.en: All go to one place; all come from dust, and all return to dust.
chapters.zh: 都归一处，都是出于尘土，也都归于尘土。

chapters.en: Who knows if the spirit of man rises upward and the spirit of the animal descends into the earth?
chapters.zh: 谁知道人的灵是往上升，兽的魂是下入地呢？

chapters.en: I have seen that there is nothing better for a man than to enjoy his work, because that is his lot. For who can bring him to see what will come after him?
chapters.zh: 故此，我见人莫强如在他经营的事上喜乐，因为这是他的分。他身后的事谁能使他回来得见呢？

chapters.en: Again I looked, and I considered all the oppression taking place under the sun. I saw the tears of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; the power lay in the hands of their oppressors, and there was no comforter.
chapters.zh: 我又转念，见日光之下所行的一切欺压。看哪，受欺压的流泪，且无人安慰；欺压他们的有势力，也无人安慰他们。

chapters.en: So I admired the dead, who had already died, above the living, who are still alive.
chapters.zh: 因此，我赞叹那早已死的死人，胜过那还活着的活人。

chapters.en: But better than both is he who has not yet existed, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.
chapters.zh: 并且我以为那未曾生的，就是未见过日光之下恶事的，比这两等人更强。

chapters.en: I saw that all labor and success spring from a man’s envy of his neighbor. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
chapters.zh: 我又见人为一切的劳碌和各样灵巧的工作就被邻舍嫉妒。这也是虚空，也是捕风。

chapters.en: The fool folds his hands and consumes his own flesh.
chapters.zh: 愚昧人抱着手，吃自己的肉。

chapters.en: Better one handful with tranquility than two handfuls with toil and pursuit of the wind.
chapters.zh: 满了一把，得享安静，强如满了两把，劳碌捕风。

chapters.en: Again, I saw futility under the sun.
chapters.zh: 我又转念，见日光之下有一件虚空的事：

chapters.en: There is a man all alone, without even a son or brother. And though there is no end to his labor, his eyes are still not content with his wealth: “For whom do I toil and bereave my soul of enjoyment?” This too is futile—a miserable task.
chapters.zh: 有人孤单无二，无子无兄，竟劳碌不息，眼目也不以钱财为足。〔他说〕：「我劳劳碌碌，刻苦自己，不享福乐，到底是为谁呢？」这也是虚空，是极重的劳苦。

chapters.en: Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor.
chapters.zh: 两个人总比一个人好，因为二人劳碌同得美好的果效。

chapters.en: For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!
chapters.zh: 若是跌倒，这人可以扶起他的同伴；若是孤身跌倒，没有别人扶起他来，这人就有祸了。

chapters.en: Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; but how can one keep warm alone?
chapters.zh: 再者，二人同睡就都暖和，一人独睡怎能暖和呢？

chapters.en: And though one may be overpowered, two can resist. Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken.
chapters.zh: 有人攻胜孤身一人，若有二人便能敌挡他；三股合成的绳子不容易折断。

chapters.en: Better is a poor but wise youth than an old but foolish king who no longer knows how to take a warning.
chapters.zh: 贫穷而有智慧的少年人胜过年老不肯纳谏的愚昧王。

chapters.en: For the youth has come from the prison to the kingship, though he was born poor in his own kingdom.
chapters.zh: 这人是从监牢中出来作王，在他国中，生来原是贫穷的。

chapters.en: I saw that all who lived and walked under the sun followed this second one, the youth who succeeded the king.
chapters.zh: 我见日光之下一切行动的活人都随从那第二位，就是起来代替老王的少年人。

chapters.en: There is no limit to all the people who were before them. Yet the successor will not be celebrated by those who come even later. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
chapters.zh: 他所治理的众人就是他的百姓，多得无数；在他后来的人尚且不喜悦他。这真是虚空，也是捕风。

chapters.en: Guard your steps when you go to the house of God. Draw near to listen rather than to offer the sacrifice of fools, who do not know that they do wrong.
chapters.zh: 你到上帝的殿要谨慎脚步；因为近前听，胜过愚昧人献祭〔注：或译：胜过献愚昧人的祭〕，他们本不知道所做的是恶。

chapters.en: Do not be quick to speak, and do not be hasty in your heart to utter a word before God. For God is in heaven and you are on earth. So let your words be few.
chapters.zh: 你在上帝面前不可冒失开口，也不可心急发言；因为上帝在天上，你在地下，所以你的言语要寡少。

chapters.en: As a dream comes through many cares, so the speech of a fool comes with many words.
chapters.zh: 事务多，就令人做梦；言语多，就显出愚昧。

chapters.en: When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it, because He takes no pleasure in fools. Fulfill your vow.
chapters.zh: 你向上帝许愿，偿还不可迟延，因他不喜悦愚昧人，所以你许的愿应当偿还。

chapters.en: It is better not to vow than to make a vow and not fulfill it.
chapters.zh: 你许愿不还，不如不许。

chapters.en: Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not tell the messenger that your vow was a mistake. Why should God be angry with your words and destroy the work of your hands?
chapters.zh: 不可任你的口使肉体犯罪，也不可在祭司〔注：原文是使者〕面前说是错许了。为何使上帝因你的声音发怒，败坏你手所做的呢？

chapters.en: For as many dreams bring futility, so do many words. Therefore, fear God.
chapters.zh: 多梦和多言，其中多有虚幻，你只要敬畏上帝。

chapters.en: If you see the oppression of the poor and the denial of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be astonished at the matter; for one official is watched by a superior, and others higher still are over them.
chapters.zh: 你若在一省之中见穷人受欺压，并夺去公义公平的事，不要因此诧异；因有一位高过居高位的鉴察，在他们以上还有更高的。

chapters.en: The produce of the earth is taken by all; the king himself profits from the fields.
chapters.zh: 况且地的益处归众人，就是君王也受田地的供应。

chapters.en: He who loves money is never satisfied by money, and he who loves wealth is never satisfied by income. This too is futile.
chapters.zh: 贪爱银子的，不因得银子知足；贪爱丰富的，也不因得利益知足。这也是虚空。

chapters.en: When good things increase, so do those who consume them; what then is the profit to the owner, except to behold them with his eyes?
chapters.zh: 货物增添，吃的人也增添，物主得什么益处呢？不过眼看而已！

chapters.en: The sleep of the worker is sweet, whether he eats little or much, but the abundance of the rich man permits him no sleep.
chapters.zh: 劳碌的人不拘吃多吃少，睡得香甜；富足人的丰满却不容他睡觉。

chapters.en: There is a grievous evil I have seen under the sun: wealth hoarded to the harm of its owner,
chapters.zh: 我见日光之下有一宗大祸患，就是财主积存资财，反害自己。

chapters.en: or wealth lost in a failed venture, so when that man has a son there is nothing to pass on.
chapters.zh: 因遭遇祸患，这些资财就消灭；那人若生了儿子，手里也一无所有。

chapters.en: As a man came from his mother’s womb, so he will depart again, naked as he arrived. He takes nothing for his labor to carry in his hands.
chapters.zh: 他怎样从母胎赤身而来，也必照样赤身而去；他所劳碌得来的，手中分毫不能带去。

chapters.en: This too is a grievous affliction: Exactly as a man is born, so he will depart. What does he gain as he toils for the wind?
chapters.zh: 他来的情形怎样，他去的情形也怎样。这也是一宗大祸患。他为风劳碌有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: Moreover, all his days he eats in darkness, with much sorrow, sickness, and anger.
chapters.zh: 并且他终身在黑暗中吃喝，多有烦恼，又有病患呕气。

chapters.en: Here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat and drink, and to find satisfaction in all the labor one does under the sun during the few days of life that God has given him—for this is his lot.
chapters.zh: 我所见为善为美的，就是人在上帝赐他一生的日子吃喝，享受日光之下劳碌得来的好处，因为这是他的分。

chapters.en: Furthermore, God has given riches and wealth to every man, and He has enabled him to enjoy them, to accept his lot, and to rejoice in his labor. This is a gift from God.
chapters.zh: 上帝赐人资财丰富，使他能以吃用，能取自己的分，在他劳碌中喜乐，这乃是上帝的恩赐。

chapters.en: For a man seldom considers the days of his life, because God keeps him occupied with the joy of his heart.
chapters.zh: 他不多思念自己一生的年日，因为上帝应他的心使他喜乐。

chapters.en: There is another evil I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily upon mankind:
chapters.zh: 我见日光之下有一宗祸患重压在人身上，

chapters.en: God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing his heart desires; but God does not allow him to enjoy them. Instead, a stranger will enjoy them. This is futile and a grievous affliction.
chapters.zh: 就是人蒙上帝赐他资财、丰富、尊荣，以致他心里所愿的一样都不缺，只是上帝使他不能吃用，反有外人来吃用。这是虚空，也是祸患。

chapters.en: A man may father a hundred children and live for many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he is unsatisfied with his prosperity and does not even receive a proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.
chapters.zh: 人若生一百个儿子，活许多岁数，以致他的年日甚多，心里却不得满享福乐，又不得埋葬；据我说，那不到期而落的胎比他倒好。

chapters.en: For a stillborn child enters in futility and departs in darkness, and his name is shrouded in obscurity.
chapters.zh: 因为虚虚而来，暗暗而去，名字被黑暗遮蔽，

chapters.en: The child, though neither seeing the sun nor knowing anything, has more rest than that man,
chapters.zh: 并且没有见过天日，也毫无知觉；这胎，比那人倒享安息。

chapters.en: even if he lives a thousand years twice over but fails to enjoy his prosperity. Do not all go to the same place?
chapters.zh: 那人虽然活千年，再活千年，却不享福，众人岂不都归一个地方去吗？

chapters.en: All a man’s labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied.
chapters.zh: 人的劳碌都为口腹，心里却不知足。

chapters.en: What advantage, then, has the wise man over the fool? What gain comes to the poor man who knows how to conduct himself before others?
chapters.zh: 这样看来，智慧人比愚昧人有什么长处呢？穷人在众人面前知道如何行，有什么长处呢？

chapters.en: Better what the eye can see than the wandering of desire. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
chapters.zh: 眼睛所看的比心里妄想的倒好。这也是虚空，也是捕风。

chapters.en: Whatever exists was named long ago, and it is known what man is; but he cannot contend with one stronger than he.
chapters.zh: 先前所有的，早已起了名，并知道何为人，他也不能与那比自己力大的相争。

chapters.en: For the more words, the more futility—and how does that profit anyone?
chapters.zh: 加增虚浮的事既多，这与人有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: For who knows what is good for a man during the few days in which he passes through his fleeting life like a shadow? Who can tell a man what will come after him under the sun?
chapters.zh: 人一生虚度的日子，就如影儿经过，谁知道什么与他有益呢？谁能告诉他身后在日光之下有什么事呢？

chapters.en: A good name is better than fine perfume, and one’s day of death is better than his day of birth.
chapters.zh: 名誉强如美好的膏油；人死的日子胜过人生的日子。

chapters.en: It is better to enter a house of mourning than a house of feasting, since death is the end of every man, and the living should take this to heart.
chapters.zh: 往遭丧的家去， 强如往宴乐的家去； 因为〔死〕是众人的结局， 活人也必将这事放在心上。

chapters.en: Sorrow is better than laughter, for a sad countenance is good for the heart.
chapters.zh: 忧愁强如喜笑； 因为面带愁容，终必使心喜乐。

chapters.en: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, but the heart of fools is in the house of pleasure.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的心在遭丧之家； 愚昧人的心在快乐之家。

chapters.en: It is better to heed a wise man’s rebuke than to listen to the song of fools.
chapters.zh: 听智慧人的责备， 强如听愚昧人的歌唱。

chapters.en: For like the crackling of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This too is futile.
chapters.zh: 愚昧人的笑声， 好像锅下烧荆棘的爆声； 这也是虚空。

chapters.en: Surely extortion turns a wise man into a fool, and a bribe corrupts the heart.
chapters.zh: 勒索使智慧人变为愚妄； 贿赂能败坏人的慧心。

chapters.en: The end of a matter is better than the beginning, and a patient spirit is better than a proud one.
chapters.zh: 事情的终局强如事情的起头； 存心忍耐的，胜过居心骄傲的。

chapters.en: Do not be quickly provoked in your spirit, for anger settles in the lap of a fool.
chapters.zh: 你不要心里急躁恼怒， 因为恼怒存在愚昧人的怀中。

chapters.en: Do not say, “Why were the old days better than these?” For it is unwise of you to ask about this.
chapters.zh: 不要说： 先前的日子强过如今的日子， 是什么缘故呢？ 你这样问，不是出于智慧。

chapters.en: Wisdom, like an inheritance, is good, and it benefits those who see the sun.
chapters.zh: 智慧和产业并好， 而且见天日的人得智慧更为有益。

chapters.en:
For wisdom, like money, is a shelter, and the advantage of knowledge
is that wisdom preserves the life of its owner.
chapters.zh: 因为智慧护庇人， 好像银钱护庇人一样。 惟独智慧能保全智慧人的生命。 这就是知识的益处。

chapters.en: Consider the work of God: Who can straighten what He has bent?
chapters.zh: 你要察看上帝的作为； 因上帝使为曲的，谁能变为直呢？

chapters.en:
In the day of prosperity, be joyful, but in the day of adversity, consider this: God has made one of these along with the other, so that a man cannot discover
anything that will come after him.
chapters.zh: 遇亨通的日子你当喜乐；遭患难的日子你当思想；因为上帝使这两样并列，为的是叫人查不出身后有什么事。

chapters.en:
In my futile life I have seen both of these:
A righteous man perishing in his righteousness,
and a wicked man living long in his wickedness.
chapters.zh: 有义人行义，反致灭亡；有恶人行恶，倒享长寿。这都是我在虚度之日中所见过的。

chapters.en: Do not be overly righteous, and do not make yourself too wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
chapters.zh: 不要行义过分，也不要过于自逞智慧，何必自取败亡呢？

chapters.en: Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be a fool. Why should you die before your time?
chapters.zh: 不要行恶过分，也不要为人愚昧，何必不到期而死呢？

chapters.en: It is good to grasp the one and not let the other slip from your hand. For he who fears God will follow both warnings.
chapters.zh: 你持守这个为美，那个也不要松手；因为敬畏上帝的人，必从这两样出来。

chapters.en: Wisdom makes the wise man stronger than ten rulers in a city.
chapters.zh: 智慧使有智慧的人比城中十个官长更有能力。

chapters.en: Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.
chapters.zh: 时常行善而不犯罪的义人，世上实在没有。

chapters.en: Do not pay attention to every word that is spoken, or you may hear your servant cursing you.
chapters.zh: 人所说的一切话，你不要放在心上，恐怕听见你的仆人咒诅你。

chapters.en: For you know in your heart that many times you yourself have cursed others.
chapters.zh: 因为你心里知道，自己也曾屡次咒诅别人。

chapters.en: All this I tested by wisdom, saying, “I resolve to be wise.” But it was beyond me.
chapters.zh: 我曾用智慧试验这一切事；我说，要得智慧，智慧却离我远。

chapters.en: What exists is out of reach and very deep. Who can fathom it?
chapters.zh: 万事〔之理〕，离〔我〕甚远，而且最深，谁能测透呢？

chapters.en: I directed my mind to understand, to explore, to search out wisdom and explanations, and to understand the stupidity of wickedness and the folly of madness.
chapters.zh: 我转念，一心要知道，要考察，要寻求智慧和〔万事的〕理由；又要知道邪恶为愚昧，愚昧为狂妄。

chapters.en: And I find more bitter than death the woman who is a snare, whose heart is a net, and whose hands are chains. The man who pleases God escapes her, but the sinner is ensnared.
chapters.zh: 我得知有等妇人比死还苦：她的心是网罗，手是锁鍊。凡蒙上帝喜悦的人必能躲避她；有罪的人却被她缠住了。

chapters.en: “Behold,” says the Teacher, “I have discovered this by adding one thing to another to find an explanation.
While my soul was still searching but not finding, among a thousand I have found one upright man, but among all these I have not found one such woman.
chapters.zh: 传道者说：「看哪，一千男子中，我找到一个〔正直人〕，但众女子中，没有找到一个。」我〔将这事〕一一比较，要寻求其理，我心仍要寻找，却未曾找到。

chapters.en: Only this have I found: I have discovered that God made mankind upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”
chapters.zh: 我所找到的只有一件，就是上帝造人原是正直，但他们寻出许多巧计。

chapters.en: Who is like the wise man? Who knows the interpretation of a matter? A man’s wisdom brightens his face, and the sternness of his face is changed.
chapters.zh: 谁如智慧人呢？ 谁知道事情的解释呢？ 人的智慧使他的脸发光， 并使他脸上的暴气改变。

chapters.en: Keep the king’s command, I say, because of your oath before God.
chapters.zh: 我〔劝你〕遵守王的命令；既指上帝起誓，理当如此。

chapters.en: Do not hasten to leave his presence, and do not persist in a bad cause, for he will do whatever he pleases.
chapters.zh: 不要急躁离开王的面前，不要固执行恶，因为他凡事都随自己的心意而行。

chapters.en: For the king’s word is supreme, and who can say to him, “What are you doing?”
chapters.zh: 王的话本有权力，谁敢问他说「你做什么」呢？

chapters.en: Whoever keeps his command will come to no harm, and a wise heart knows the right time and procedure.
chapters.zh: 凡遵守命令的，必不经历祸患；智慧人的心能辨明时候和定理〔注：原文是审判；下节同〕。

chapters.en: For there is a right time and procedure to every purpose, though a man’s misery weighs heavily upon him.
chapters.zh: 各样事务〔成就〕都有时候和定理，因为人的苦难重压在他身上。

chapters.en: Since no one knows what will happen, who can tell him what is to come?
chapters.zh: 他不知道将来的事，因为将来如何，谁能告诉他呢？

chapters.en: As no man has power over the wind to contain it, so no one has authority over his day of death. As no one can be discharged in wartime, so wickedness will not release those who practice it.
chapters.zh: 无人有权力掌管生命，将生命留住；也无人有权力掌管死期；这场争战，无人能免；邪恶也不能救那好行邪恶的人。

chapters.en: All this I have seen, applying my mind to every deed that is done under the sun; there is a time when one man lords it over another to his own detriment.
chapters.zh: 这一切我都见过，也专心查考日光之下所做的一切事。有时这人管辖那人，令人受害。

chapters.en: Then too, I saw the burial of the wicked who used to go in and out of the holy place, and they were praised in the city where they had done so. This too is futile.
chapters.zh: 我见恶人埋葬，归入〔坟墓〕；又见行正直事的离开圣地，在城中被人忘记。这也是虚空。

chapters.en: When the sentence for a crime is not speedily executed, the hearts of men become fully set on doing evil.
chapters.zh: 因为断定罪名不立刻施刑，所以世人满心作恶。

chapters.en: Although a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives long, yet I also know that it will go well with those who fear God, who are reverent in His presence.
chapters.zh: 罪人虽然作恶百次，倒享长久的年日；然而我准知道，敬畏上帝的，就是在他面前敬畏的人，终久必得福乐。

chapters.en: Yet because the wicked do not fear God, it will not go well with them, and their days will not lengthen like a shadow.
chapters.zh: 恶人却不得福乐，也不得长久的年日；这年日好像影儿，因他不敬畏上帝。

chapters.en: There is a futility that is done on the earth: There are righteous men who get what the actions of the wicked deserve, and there are wicked men who get what the actions of the righteous deserve. I say that this too is futile.
chapters.zh: 世上有一件虚空的事，就是义人所遭遇的，反照恶人所行的；又有恶人所遭遇的，反照义人所行的。我说，这也是虚空。

chapters.en: So I commended the enjoyment of life, because there is nothing better for a man under the sun than to eat and drink and be merry. For this joy will accompany him in his labor during the days of his life that God gives him under the sun.
chapters.zh: 我就称赞快乐，原来人在日光之下，莫强如吃喝快乐；因为他在日光之下，上帝赐他一生的年日，要从劳碌中，时常享受所得的。

chapters.en: When I applied my mind to know wisdom and to observe the task that one performs on the earth—though his eyes do not see sleep in the day or even in the night—
chapters.zh: 我专心求智慧，要看世上所做的事。（有昼夜不睡觉不合眼的。）

chapters.en: I saw every work of God, and that a man is unable to comprehend the work that is done under the sun. Despite his efforts to search it out, he cannot find its meaning; even if the wise man claims to know, he is unable to comprehend.
chapters.zh: 我就看明上帝一切的作为，知道人查不出日光之下所做的事；任凭他费多少力寻查，都查不出来，就是智慧人虽想知道，也是查不出来。

chapters.en: So I took all this to heart and concluded that the righteous and the wise, as well as their deeds, are in God’s hands. Man does not know what lies ahead, whether love or hate.
chapters.zh: 我将这一切事放在心上，详细考究，就知道义人和智慧人，并他们的作为都在上帝手中；或是爱，或是恨，都在他们的前面，人不能知道。

chapters.en: It is the same for all: There is a common fate for the righteous and the wicked, for the good and the bad, for the clean and the unclean, for the one who sacrifices and the one who does not. As it is for the good, so it is for the sinner; as it is for the one who makes a vow, so it is for the one who refuses to take a vow.
chapters.zh: 凡临到众人的事都是一样：义人和恶人都遭遇一样的事；好人，洁净人和不洁净人，献祭的与不献祭的，也是一样。好人如何，罪人也如何；起誓的如何，怕起誓的也如何。

chapters.en: This is an evil in everything that is done under the sun: There is one fate for everyone. Furthermore, the hearts of men are full of evil and madness while they are alive, and afterward they join the dead.
chapters.zh: 在日光之下所行的一切事上有一件祸患，就是众人所遭遇的都是一样，并且世人的心充满了恶；活着的时候心里狂妄，后来就归死人那里去了。

chapters.en: There is hope, however, for anyone who is among the living; for even a live dog is better than a dead lion.
chapters.zh: 与一切活人相连的，那人还有指望，因为活着的狗比死了的狮子更强。

chapters.en: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, because the memory of them is forgotten.
chapters.zh: 活着的人知道必死；死了的人毫无所知，也不再得赏赐；他们的名无人记念。

chapters.en: Their love, their hate, and their envy have already vanished, and they will never again have a share in all that is done under the sun.
chapters.zh: 他们的爱，他们的恨，他们的嫉妒，早都消灭了。在日光之下所行的一切事上，他们永不再有分了。

chapters.en: Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, for God has already approved your works:
chapters.zh: 你只管去欢欢喜喜吃你的饭，心中快乐喝你的酒，因为上帝已经悦纳你的作为。

chapters.en: Let your garments always be white, and never spare the oil for your head.
chapters.zh: 你的衣服当时常洁白，你头上也不要缺少膏油。

chapters.en: Enjoy life with your beloved wife all the days of the fleeting life that God has given you under the sun—all your fleeting days. For this is your portion in life and in your labor under the sun.
chapters.zh: 在你一生虚空的年日，就是上帝赐你在日光之下虚空的年日，当同你所爱的妻，快活度日，因为那是你生前在日光之下劳碌的事上所得的分。

chapters.en: Whatever you find to do with your hands, do it with all your might, for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.
chapters.zh: 凡你手所当做的事要尽力去做；因为在你所必去的阴间没有工作，没有谋算，没有知识，也没有智慧。

chapters.en: I saw something else under the sun: The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong; neither is the bread to the wise, nor the wealth to the intelligent, nor the favor to the skillful. For time and chance happen to all.
chapters.zh: 我又转念：见日光之下，快跑的未必能赢；力战的未必得胜；智慧的未必得粮食；明哲的未必得资财；灵巧的未必得喜悦。所临到众人的是在乎当时的机会。

chapters.en: For surely no man knows his time: Like fish caught in a cruel net or birds trapped in a snare, so men are ensnared in an evil time that suddenly falls upon them.
chapters.zh: 原来人也不知道自己的定期。鱼被恶网圈住，鸟被网罗捉住，祸患忽然临到的时候，世人陷在其中也是如此。

chapters.en: I have also seen this wisdom under the sun, and it was great to me:
chapters.zh: 我见日光之下有一样智慧，据我看乃是广大，

chapters.en: There was a small city with few men. A mighty king came against it, surrounded it, and built large siege ramps against it.
chapters.zh: 就是有一小城，其中的人数稀少，有大君王来攻击，修筑营垒，将城围困。

chapters.en: Now a poor wise man was found in the city, and he saved the city by his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man.
chapters.zh: 城中有一个贫穷的智慧人，他用智慧救了那城，却没有人记念那穷人。

chapters.en: And I said, “Wisdom is better than strength, but the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are not heeded.”
chapters.zh: 我就说，智慧胜过勇力；然而那贫穷人的智慧被人藐视，他的话也无人听从。

chapters.en: The calm words of the wise are heeded over the shouts of a ruler among fools.
chapters.zh: 宁可在安静之中听智慧人的言语，不听掌管愚昧人的喊声。

chapters.en: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.
chapters.zh: 智慧胜过打仗的兵器；但一个罪人能败坏许多善事。

chapters.en: As dead flies bring a stench to the perfumer’s oil, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
chapters.zh: 死苍蝇使做香的膏油发出臭气； 〔这样〕，一点愚昧也能败坏智慧和尊荣。

chapters.en: A wise man’s heart inclines to the right, but the heart of a fool to the left.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的心居右； 愚昧人的心居左。

chapters.en: Even as the fool walks along the road, his sense is lacking, and he shows everyone that he is a fool.
chapters.zh: 并且愚昧人行路显出无知， 对众人说，他是愚昧人。

chapters.en: If the ruler’s temper flares against you, do not abandon your post, for calmness lays great offenses to rest.
chapters.zh: 掌权者的心若向你发怒， 不要离开你的本位， 因为柔和能免大过。

chapters.en: There is an evil I have seen under the sun— an error that proceeds from the ruler:
chapters.zh: 我见日光之下有一件祸患， 似乎出于掌权的错误，

chapters.en: Folly is appointed to great heights, but the rich sit in lowly positions.
chapters.zh: 就是愚昧人立在高位； 富足人坐在低位。

chapters.en: I have seen slaves on horseback, while princes go on foot like slaves.
chapters.zh: 我见过仆人骑马， 王子像仆人在地上步行。

chapters.en: He who digs a pit may fall into it, and he who breaches a wall may be bitten by a snake.
chapters.zh: 挖陷坑的，自己必掉在其中； 拆墙垣的，必为蛇所咬。

chapters.en: The one who quarries stones may be injured by them, and he who splits logs endangers himself.
chapters.zh: 凿开〔注：或译：挪移〕石头的，必受损伤； 劈开木头的，必遭危险。

chapters.en:
If the axe is dull and the blade unsharpened, more strength must be exerted,
but skill produces success.
chapters.zh: 铁器钝了，若不将刃磨快，就必多费气力； 但得智慧指教，便有益处。

chapters.en: If the snake bites before it is charmed, there is no profit for the charmer.
chapters.zh: 未行法术以先，蛇若咬人， 后行法术也是无益。

chapters.en: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious, but the lips of a fool consume him.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的口说出恩言； 愚昧人的嘴吞灭自己。

chapters.en: The beginning of his talk is folly, and the end of his speech is evil madness.
chapters.zh: 他口中的言语起头是愚昧； 他话的末尾是奸恶的狂妄。

chapters.en:
Yet the fool multiplies words. No one knows what is coming,
and who can tell him what will come after him?
chapters.zh: 愚昧人多有言语， 人却不知将来有什么事； 他身后的事谁能告诉他呢？

chapters.en: The toil of a fool wearies him, for he does not know the way to the city.
chapters.zh: 凡愚昧人，他的劳碌使自己困乏， 因为连进城的路，他也不知道。

chapters.en: Woe to you, O land whose king is a youth, and whose princes feast in the morning.
chapters.zh: 邦国啊，你的王若是孩童， 你的群臣早晨宴乐， 你就有祸了！

chapters.en:
Blessed are you, O land whose king is a son of nobles, and whose princes feast at the proper time—
for strength and not for drunkenness.
chapters.zh: 邦国啊，你的王若是贵胄之子， 你的群臣按时吃喝， 为要补力，不为酒醉， 你就有福了！

chapters.en: Through laziness the roof caves in, and in the hands of the idle, the house leaks.
chapters.zh: 因人懒惰，房顶塌下； 因人手懒，房屋滴漏。

chapters.en: A feast is prepared for laughter, and wine makes life merry, but money is the answer for everything.
chapters.zh: 设摆筵席是为喜笑。 酒能使人快活； 钱能叫万事应心。

chapters.en: Do not curse the king even in your thoughts, or curse the rich even in your bedroom, for a bird of the air may carry your words, and a winged creature may report your speech.
chapters.zh: 你不可咒诅君王， 也不可心怀此念； 在你卧房也不可咒诅富户。 因为空中的鸟必传扬这声音， 有翅膀的也必述说这事。

chapters.en: Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again.
chapters.zh: 当将你的粮食撒在水面， 因为日久必能得着。

chapters.en: Divide your portion among seven, or even eight, for you do not know what disaster may befall the land.
chapters.zh: 你要分给七人，或分给八人， 因为你不知道将来有什么灾祸临到地上。

chapters.en: If the clouds are full, they will pour out rain upon the earth; whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where it falls, there it will lie.
chapters.zh: 云若满了雨，就必倾倒在地上。 树若向南倒，或向北倒， 树倒在何处，就存在何处。

chapters.en: He who watches the wind will fail to sow, and he who observes the clouds will fail to reap.
chapters.zh: 看风的，必不撒种； 望云的，必不收割。

chapters.en: As you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones are formed in a mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the work of God, the Maker of all things.
chapters.zh: 风从何道来，骨头在怀孕妇人的胎中如何长成，你尚且不得知道；这样，行万事之上帝的作为，你更不得知道。

chapters.en: Sow your seed in the morning, and do not rest your hands in the evening, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or if both will equally prosper.
chapters.zh: 早晨要撒你的种，晚上也不要歇你的手，因为你不知道哪一样发旺；或是早撒的，或是晚撒的，或是两样都好。

chapters.en: Light is sweet, and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.
chapters.zh: 光本是佳美的，眼见日光也是可悦的。

chapters.en:
So if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all. But let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many.
Everything to come is futile.
chapters.zh: 人活多年，就当快乐多年；然而也当想到黑暗的日子。因为这日子必多，所要来的都是虚空。

chapters.en: Rejoice, O young man, while you are young, and let your heart be glad in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, but know that for all these things God will bring you to judgment.
chapters.zh: 少年人哪，你在幼年时当快乐。在幼年的日子，使你的心欢畅，行你心所愿行的，看你眼所爱看的；却要知道，为这一切的事，上帝必审问你。

chapters.en:
So banish sorrow from your heart, and cast off pain from your body,
for youth and vigor are fleeting.
chapters.zh: 所以，你当从心中除掉愁烦，从肉体克去邪恶；因为一生的开端和幼年之时，都是虚空的。

chapters.en: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of adversity come and the years approach of which you will say, “I find no pleasure in them,”
chapters.zh: 你趁着年幼、衰败的日子尚未来到，就是你所说，我毫无喜乐的那些年日未曾临近之先，当记念造你的主。

chapters.en: before the light of the sun, moon, and stars is darkened, and the clouds return after the rain,
chapters.zh: 不要等到日头、光明、月亮、星宿变为黑暗，雨后云彩反回，

chapters.en: on the day the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men stoop, when those grinding cease because they are few and those watching through windows see dimly,
chapters.zh: 看守房屋的发颤，有力的屈身，推磨的稀少就止息，从窗户往外看的都昏暗；

chapters.en: when the doors to the street are shut and the sound of the mill fades away, when one rises at the sound of a bird and all the daughters of song grow faint,
chapters.zh: 街门关闭，推磨的响声微小，雀鸟一叫，人就起来，唱歌的女子也都衰微。

chapters.en: when men fear the heights and dangers of the road, when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper loses its spring, and the caper berry shrivels— for then man goes to his eternal home and mourners walk the streets.
chapters.zh: 人怕高处，路上有惊慌，杏树开花，蚱蜢成为重担，人所愿的也都废掉；因为人归他永远的家，吊丧的在街上往来。

chapters.en: Remember Him before the silver cord is snapped and the golden bowl is crushed, before the pitcher is shattered at the spring and the wheel is broken at the well,
chapters.zh: 银鍊折断，金罐破裂，瓶子在泉旁损坏，水轮在井口破烂，

chapters.en: before the dust returns to the ground from which it came and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
chapters.zh: 尘土仍归于地，灵仍归于赐灵的上帝。

chapters.en: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher. “Everything is futile!”
chapters.zh: 传道者说：「虚空的虚空，凡事都是虚空。」

chapters.en: Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also taught the people knowledge; he pondered, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.
chapters.zh: 再者，传道者因有智慧，仍将知识教训众人；又默想，又考查，又陈说许多箴言。

chapters.en: The Teacher searched to find delightful sayings and to record accurate words of truth.
chapters.zh: 传道者专心寻求可喜悦的言语，是凭正直写的诚实话。

chapters.en: The words of the wise are like goads, and the anthologies of the masters are like firmly embedded nails driven by a single Shepherd.
chapters.zh: 智慧人的言语好像刺棍；会中之师的〔言语〕又像钉稳的钉子，都是一个牧者所赐的。

chapters.en: And by these, my son, be further warned: There is no end to the making of many books, and much study wearies the body.
chapters.zh: 我儿，还有一层，你当受劝戒：著书多，没有穷尽；读书多，身体疲倦。

chapters.en: When all has been heard, the conclusion of the matter is this: Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man.
chapters.zh: 这些事都已听见了，总意就是：敬畏上帝，谨守他的诫命，这是人所当尽的〔本分〕〔注：或译：这是众人的本分〕。

chapters.en: For God will bring every deed into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.
chapters.zh: 因为人所做的事，连一切隐藏的事，无论是善是恶，上帝都必审问。

chapters.en: This is Solomon’s Song of Songs.
chapters.zh: 所罗门的歌，是歌中的雅歌。

chapters.en: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! For your love is more delightful than wine.
chapters.zh: 愿他用口与我亲嘴； 因你的爱情比酒更美。

chapters.en:
The fragrance of your perfume is pleasing; your name is like perfume poured out.
No wonder the maidens adore you.
chapters.zh: 你的膏油馨香； 你的名〔如同〕倒出来的〔香〕膏， 所以众童女都爱你。

chapters.en:
Take me away with you—let us hurry! May the king bring me to his chambers. The Friends
We will rejoice and delight in you; we will praise your love more than wine. The Bride
It is only right that they adore you.
chapters.zh: 愿你吸引我，我们就快跑跟随你。 王带我进了内室， 我们必因你欢喜快乐。 我们要称赞你的爱情， 胜似称赞〔美〕酒。 他们爱你是理所当然的。

chapters.en: I am dark, yet lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtains of Solomon.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷的众女子啊， 我虽然黑，却是秀美， 如同基达的帐棚， 好像所罗门的幔子。

chapters.en:
Do not stare because I am dark, for the sun has gazed upon me. My mother’s sons were angry with me; they made me a keeper of the vineyards,
but my own vineyard I have neglected.
chapters.zh: 不要因日头把我晒黑了就轻看我。 我同母的弟兄向我发怒， 他们使我看守葡萄园； 我自己的葡萄园却没有看守。

chapters.en:
Tell me, O one I love, where do you pasture your sheep?
Where do you rest them at midday? Why should I be like a veiled woman beside the flocks of your companions?
chapters.zh: 我心所爱的啊，求你告诉我， 你在何处牧羊？ 晌午在何处使羊歇卧？ 我何必在你同伴的羊群旁边 好像蒙着脸的人呢？

chapters.en: If you do not know, O fairest of women, follow the tracks of the flock, and graze your young goats near the tents of the shepherds.
chapters.zh: 你这女子中极美丽的， 你若不知道， 只管跟随羊群的脚踪去， 把你的山羊羔牧放在牧人帐棚的旁边。

chapters.en: I compare you, my darling, to a mare among Pharaoh’s chariots.
chapters.zh: 我的佳偶， 我将你比法老车上套的骏马。

chapters.en: Your cheeks are beautiful with ornaments, your neck with strings of jewels.
chapters.zh: 你的两腮因发辫而秀美； 你的颈项因珠串而华丽。

chapters.en: We will make you ornaments of gold, studded with beads of silver.
chapters.zh: 我们要为你编上金辫，镶上银钉。

chapters.en: While the king was at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.
chapters.zh: 王正坐席的时候， 我的哪哒香膏发出香味。

chapters.en: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts.
chapters.zh: 我以我的良人为一袋没药， 常在我怀中。

chapters.en: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-gedi.
chapters.zh: 我以我的良人为一棵凤仙花， 在隐‧基底葡萄园中。

chapters.en:
How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how very beautiful!
Your eyes are like doves.
chapters.zh: 我的佳偶，你甚美丽！你甚美丽！ 你的眼〔好像〕鸽子眼。

chapters.en:
How handsome you are, my beloved! Oh, how delightful!
The soft grass is our bed.
chapters.zh: 我的良人哪，你甚美丽可爱！ 我们以青草为床榻，

chapters.en: The beams of our house are cedars; our rafters are fragrant firs.
chapters.zh: 以香柏树为房屋的栋梁， 以松树为椽子。

chapters.en: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valley.
chapters.zh: 我是沙崙的玫瑰花〔注：或译：水仙花〕， 是谷中的百合花。

chapters.en: Like a lily among the thorns is my darling among the maidens.
chapters.zh: 我的佳偶在女子中， 好像百合花在荆棘内。

chapters.en: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest is my beloved among the young men. I delight to sit in his shade, and his fruit is sweet to my taste.
chapters.zh: 我的良人在男子中， 如同苹果树在树林中。 我欢欢喜喜坐在他的荫下， 尝他果子的滋味，觉得甘甜。

chapters.en: He has brought me to the house of wine, and his banner over me is love.
chapters.zh: 他带我入筵宴所， 以爱为旗在我以上。

chapters.en:
Sustain me with raisins; refresh me with apples,
for I am faint with love.
chapters.zh: 求你们给我葡萄干增补我力， 给我苹果畅快我心， 因我思爱成病。

chapters.en: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.
chapters.zh: 他的左手在我头下； 他的右手将我抱住。

chapters.en: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷的众女子啊， 我指着羚羊或田野的母鹿嘱咐你们： 不要惊动、不要叫醒我所亲爱的， 等他自己情愿〔注：不要叫醒......情愿：或译不要激动爱情，等它自发〕。

chapters.en: Listen! My beloved approaches. Look! Here he comes, leaping across the mountains, bounding over the hills.
chapters.zh: 〔听啊〕！是我良人的声音； 看哪！他蹿山越岭而来。

chapters.en: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young stag. Look, he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice.
chapters.zh: 我的良人好像羚羊，或像小鹿。 他站在我们墙壁后， 从窗户往里观看， 从窗棂往里窥探。

chapters.en:
My beloved calls to me, “Arise, my darling.
Come away with me, my beautiful one.
chapters.zh: 我良人对我说： 我的佳偶，我的美人， 起来，与我同去！

chapters.en: For now the winter is past; the rain is over and gone.
chapters.zh: 因为冬天已往， 雨水止住过去了。

chapters.en: The flowers have appeared in the countryside; the season of singing has come, and the cooing of turtledoves is heard in our land.
chapters.zh: 地上百花开放， 〔百鸟〕鸣叫的时候〔注：或译：修理葡萄树的时候〕已经来到； 斑鸠的声音在我们境内也听见了。

chapters.en: The fig tree ripens its figs; the blossoming vines spread their fragrance. Arise, come away, my darling; come away with me, my beautiful one.”
chapters.zh: 无花果树的果子渐渐成熟； 葡萄树开花放香。 我的佳偶，我的美人， 起来，与我同去！

chapters.en: O my dove in the clefts of the rock, in the crevices of the cliff, let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your countenance is lovely.
chapters.zh: 我的鸽子啊，你在磐石穴中， 在陡巖的隐密处。 求你容我得见你的面貌， 得听你的声音； 因为你的声音柔和， 你的面貌秀美。

chapters.en:
Catch for us the foxes— the little foxes that ruin the vineyards—
for our vineyards are in bloom.
chapters.zh: 要给我们擒拿狐狸， 就是毁坏葡萄园的小狐狸， 因为我们的葡萄正在开花。

chapters.en: My beloved is mine and I am his; he pastures his flock among the lilies.
chapters.zh: 良人属我，我也属他； 他在百合花中牧放〔群羊〕。

chapters.en: Before the day breaks and shadows flee, turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of Bether.
chapters.zh: 我的良人哪， 求你等到天起凉风、 日影飞去的时候， 你要转回，好像羚羊， 或像小鹿在比特山上。

chapters.en: On my bed at night I sought the one I love; I sought him, but did not find him.
chapters.zh: 我夜间躺卧在床上， 寻找我心所爱的； 我寻找他，却寻不见。

chapters.en: I will arise now and go about the city, through the streets and squares. I will seek the one I love. So I sought him but did not find him.
chapters.zh: 我说：我要起来，游行城中， 在街市上，在宽阔处， 寻找我心所爱的。 我寻找他，却寻不见。

chapters.en: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city: “Have you seen the one I love?”
chapters.zh: 城中巡逻看守的人遇见我； 〔我问他们〕：你们看见我心所爱的没有？

chapters.en: I had just passed them when I found the one I love. I held him and would not let go until I had brought him to my mother’s house, to the chamber of the one who conceived me.
chapters.zh: 我刚离开他们就遇见我心所爱的。 我拉住他，不容他走， 领他入我母家， 到怀我者的内室。

chapters.en: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you by the gazelles and does of the field: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷的众女子啊， 我指着羚羊或田野的母鹿嘱咐你们： 不要惊动、不要叫醒我所亲爱的， 等他自己情愿〔注：不要叫醒......情愿：或译不要激动爱情，等它自发〕。

chapters.en: Who is this coming up from the wilderness like a column of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense from all the spices of the merchant?
chapters.zh: 那从旷野上来、形状如烟柱、 以没药和乳香并商人各样香粉薰的是谁呢？

chapters.en: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage, escorted by sixty of the mightiest men of Israel.
chapters.zh: 看哪，是所罗门的轿； 四围有六十个勇士， 都是以色列中的勇士；

chapters.en: All are skilled with the sword, experienced in warfare. Each has his sword at his side prepared for the terror of the night.
chapters.zh: 手都持刀，善于争战， 腰间佩刀，防备夜间有惊慌。

chapters.en: King Solomon has made his carriage out of the timber of Lebanon.
chapters.zh: 所罗门王用黎巴嫩木 为自己制造一乘华轿。

chapters.en: He has made its posts of silver, its base of gold, its seat of purple fabric. Its interior is inlaid with love by the daughters of Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 轿柱是用银做的， 轿底是用金做的； 坐垫是紫色的， 其中所铺的乃耶路撒冷众女子的爱情。

chapters.en:
Come out, O daughters of Zion, and gaze at King Solomon, wearing the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding—
the day of his heart’s rejoicing.
chapters.zh: 锡安的众女子啊， 你们出去观看所罗门王！ 头戴冠冕，就是在他婚筵的日子、 心中喜乐的时候，他母亲给他戴上的。

chapters.en: How beautiful you are, my darling— how very beautiful! Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down Mount Gilead.
chapters.zh: 我的佳偶，你甚美丽！你甚美丽！ 你的眼在帕子内〔好像〕鸽子眼。 你的头发如同山羊群卧在基列山旁。

chapters.en: Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.
