chapters.zh: 你的牙齿如〔新〕剪毛的一群〔母〕羊， 洗净上来，个个都有双生， 没有一只丧掉子的。

chapters.en: Your lips are like a scarlet ribbon, and your mouth is lovely. Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.
chapters.zh: 你的唇好像一条朱红线； 你的嘴也秀美。 你的两太阳在帕子内， 如同一块石榴。

chapters.en: Your neck is like the tower of David, built with rows of stones; on it hang a thousand shields, all of them shields of warriors.
chapters.zh: 你的颈项好像大卫建造收藏军器的高台， 其上悬挂一千盾牌， 都是勇士的籐牌。

chapters.en: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle grazing among the lilies.
chapters.zh: 你的两乳好像百合花中吃草的一对小鹿， 就是母鹿双生的。

chapters.en: Before the day breaks and the shadows flee, I will make my way to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
chapters.zh: 我要往没药山和乳香冈去， 直等到天起凉风、 日影飞去的时候〔回来〕。

chapters.en: You are altogether beautiful, my darling; in you there is no flaw.
chapters.zh: 我的佳偶，你全然美丽， 毫无瑕疵！

chapters.en: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon! Descend from the peak of Amana, from the summits of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of the lions, from the mountains of the leopards.
chapters.zh: 我的新妇，求你与我一同离开黎巴嫩， 与我一同离开黎巴嫩。 从亚玛拿顶， 从示尼珥与黑门顶， 从有狮子的洞， 从有豹子的山往下观看。

chapters.en: You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride; you have stolen my heart with one glance of your eyes, with one jewel of your neck.
chapters.zh: 我妹子，我新妇， 你夺了我的心。 你用眼一看， 用你项上的一条〔金〕鍊， 夺了我的心！

chapters.en: How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love is much better than wine, and the fragrance of your perfume than all spices.
chapters.zh: 我妹子，我新妇， 你的爱情何其美！ 你的爱情比酒更美！ 你膏油的香气胜过一切香品！

chapters.en:
Your lips, my bride, drip sweetness like the honeycomb; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments
is like the aroma of Lebanon.
chapters.zh: 我新妇，你的嘴唇滴蜜， 好像蜂房滴蜜； 你的舌下有蜜，有奶。 你衣服的香气如黎巴嫩的香气。

chapters.en: My sister, my bride, you are a garden locked up, a spring enclosed, a fountain sealed.
chapters.zh: 我妹子，我新妇， 乃是关锁的园， 禁闭的井，封闭的泉源。

chapters.en: Your branches are an orchard of pomegranates with the choicest of fruits, with henna and nard,
chapters.zh: 你园内所种的结了石榴， 有佳美的果子， 并凤仙花与哪哒树。

chapters.en: with nard and saffron, with calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of frankincense tree, with myrrh and aloes, with all the finest spices.
chapters.zh: 有哪哒和番红花， 菖蒲和桂树， 并各样乳香木、没药、沉香， 与一切上等的果品。

chapters.en:
You are a garden spring, a well of fresh water
flowing down from Lebanon.
chapters.zh: 你是园中的泉，活水的井， 从黎巴嫩流下来的溪水。

chapters.en: Awake, O north wind, and come, O south wind. Breathe on my garden and spread the fragrance of its spices. Let my beloved come into his garden and taste its choicest fruits.
chapters.zh: 北风啊，兴起！ 南风啊，吹来！ 吹在我的园内， 使其中的香气发出来。 愿我的良人进入自己园里， 吃他佳美的果子。

chapters.en:
I have come to my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. The Friends
Eat, O friends, and drink; drink freely, O beloved.
chapters.zh: 我妹子，我新妇， 我进了我的园中， 采了我的没药和香料， 吃了我的蜜房和蜂蜜， 喝了我的酒和奶。 我的朋友们，请吃！ 我所亲爱的，请喝，且多多地喝！

chapters.en: I sleep, but my heart is awake. A sound! My beloved is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the dampness of the night.”
chapters.zh: 我身睡卧，我心却醒。 这是我良人的声音； 他敲门〔说〕： 我的妹子，我的佳偶， 我的鸽子，我的完全人， 求你给我开门； 因我的头满了露水， 我的头发被夜露滴湿。

chapters.en: I have taken off my robe— must I put it back on? I have washed my feet— must I soil them again?
chapters.zh: 〔我回答说〕： 我脱了衣裳，怎能再穿上呢？ 我洗了脚，怎能再玷污呢？

chapters.en: My beloved put his hand to the latch; my heart pounded for him.
chapters.zh: 我的良人从〔门〕孔里伸进手来， 我便因他动了心。

chapters.en: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh on the handles of the bolt.
chapters.zh: 我起来，要给我良人开门。 我的两手滴下没药； 我的指头有没药汁滴在门闩上。

chapters.en:
I opened for my beloved, but he had turned and gone. My heart sank at his departure. I sought him but did not find him.
I called, but he did not answer.
chapters.zh: 我给我的良人开了门； 我的良人却已转身走了。 他说话的时候，我神不守舍； 我寻找他，竟寻不见； 我呼叫他，他却不回答。

chapters.en: I encountered the watchmen on their rounds of the city. They beat me and bruised me; they took away my cloak, those guardians of the walls.
chapters.zh: 城中巡逻看守的人遇见我， 打了我，伤了我； 看守城墙的人夺去我的披肩。

chapters.en:
O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you, if you find my beloved,
tell him I am sick with love.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷的众女子啊，我嘱咐你们： 若遇见我的良人， 要告诉他，我因思爱成病。

chapters.en: How is your beloved better than others, O most beautiful among women? How is your beloved better than another, that you charge us so?
chapters.zh: 你这女子中极美丽的， 你的良人比别人的良人有何强处？ 你的良人比别人的良人有何强处， 你就这样嘱咐我们？

chapters.en: My beloved is dazzling and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.
chapters.zh: 我的良人白而且红， 超乎万人之上。

chapters.en: His head is purest gold; his hair is wavy and black as a raven.
chapters.zh: 他的头〔像〕至精的金子； 他的头发厚密累垂，黑如乌鸦。

chapters.en: His eyes are like doves beside the streams of water, bathed in milk and mounted like jewels.
chapters.zh: 他的眼如溪水旁的鸽子〔眼〕， 用奶洗净，安得合式。

chapters.en: His cheeks are like beds of spice, towers of perfume. His lips are like lilies, dripping with flowing myrrh.
chapters.zh: 他的两腮如香花畦， 如香草台； 他的嘴唇〔像〕百合花， 且滴下没药汁。

chapters.en: His arms are rods of gold set with beryl. His body is polished ivory bedecked with sapphires.
chapters.zh: 他的两手〔好像〕金管， 镶嵌水苍玉； 他的身体〔如同〕雕刻的象牙， 周围镶嵌蓝宝石。

chapters.en: His legs are pillars of marble set on bases of pure gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, as majestic as the cedars.
chapters.zh: 他的腿〔好像〕白玉石柱， 安在精金座上； 他的形状如黎巴嫩， 且佳美如香柏树。

chapters.en: His mouth is most sweet; he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 他的口极其甘甜； 他全然可爱。 耶路撒冷的众女子啊， 这是我的良人； 这是我的朋友。

chapters.en: Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? Which way has he turned? We will seek him with you.
chapters.zh: 你这女子中极美丽的， 你的良人往何处去了？ 你的良人转向何处去了， 我们好与你同去寻找他。

chapters.en: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens and to gather lilies.
chapters.zh: 我的良人下入自己园中， 到香花畦， 在园内牧放〔群羊〕， 采百合花。

chapters.en: I belong to my beloved and he belongs to me; he pastures his flock among the lilies.
chapters.zh: 我属我的良人， 我的良人也属我； 他在百合花中牧放〔群羊〕。

chapters.en:
You are as beautiful, my darling, as Tirzah, as lovely as Jerusalem,
as majestic as troops with banners.
chapters.zh: 我的佳偶啊，你美丽如得撒， 秀美如耶路撒冷， 威武如展开旌旗的军队。

chapters.en: Turn your eyes away from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats streaming down from Gilead.
chapters.zh: 求你掉转眼目不看我， 因你的眼目使我惊乱。 你的头发如同山羊群卧在基列山旁。

chapters.en: Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing; each has its twin, and not one of them is lost.
chapters.zh: 你的牙齿如一群母羊 洗净上来，个个都有双生， 没有一只丧掉子的。

chapters.en: Your brow behind your veil is like a slice of pomegranate.
chapters.zh: 你的两太阳在帕子内， 如同一块石榴。

chapters.en: There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and maidens without number,
chapters.zh: 有六十王后八十妃嫔， 并有无数的童女。

chapters.en: but my dove, my perfect one, is unique, the favorite of the mother who bore her. The maidens see her and call her blessed; the queens and concubines sing her praises.
chapters.zh: 我的鸽子，我的完全人， 只有这一个是她母亲独生的， 是生养她者所宝爱的。 众女子见了就称她有福； 王后妃嫔见了也赞美她。

chapters.en: Who is this who shines like the dawn, as fair as the moon, as bright as the sun, as majestic as the stars in procession?
chapters.zh: 那向外观看、如晨光发现、 美丽如月亮、皎洁如日头、 威武如展开旌旗军队的是谁呢？

chapters.en: I went down to the walnut grove to see the blossoms of the valley, to see if the vines were budding or the pomegranates were in bloom.
chapters.zh: 我下入核桃园， 要看谷中青绿的植物， 要看葡萄发芽没有， 石榴开花没有。

chapters.en: Before I realized it, my desire had set me among the royal chariots of my people.
chapters.zh: 不知不觉， 我的心将我安置在我尊长的车中。

chapters.en:
Come back, come back, O Shulammite! Come back, come back, that we may gaze upon you. The Bridegroom
Why do you look at the Shulammite, as on the dance of Mahanaim ?
chapters.zh: 回来，回来，书拉密女； 你回来，你回来，使我们得观看你。 你们为何要观看书拉密女， 像观看玛哈念跳舞的呢？

chapters.en: How beautiful are your sandaled feet, O daughter of the prince! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the handiwork of a master.
chapters.zh: 王女啊，你的脚在鞋中何其美好！ 你的大腿圆润，好像美玉， 是巧匠的手做成的。

chapters.en: Your navel is a rounded goblet; it never lacks blended wine. Your waist is a mound of wheat encircled by the lilies.
chapters.zh: 你的肚脐〔如〕圆杯， 不缺调和的酒； 你的腰如一堆麦子， 周围有百合花。

chapters.en: Your breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
chapters.zh: 你的两乳好像一对小鹿， 就是母鹿双生的。

chapters.en: Your neck is like a tower made of ivory; your eyes are like the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim; your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, facing toward Damascus.
chapters.zh: 你的颈项如象牙台； 你的眼目〔像〕希实本、巴特‧拉并门旁的水池； 你的鼻子仿佛朝大马士革的黎巴嫩塔。

chapters.en:
Your head crowns you like Mount Carmel, the hair of your head like purple threads;
the king is captured in your tresses.
chapters.zh: 你的头在你身上好像迦密山； 你头上的发是紫黑色； 王的心因这下垂的发绺系住了。

chapters.en: How fair and pleasant you are, O love, with your delights!
chapters.zh: 我所爱的，你何其美好！ 何其可悦，使人欢畅喜乐！

chapters.en: Your stature is like a palm tree; your breasts are clusters of fruit.
chapters.zh: 你的身量好像棕树； 你的两乳如同其上的果子，累累下垂。

chapters.en: I said, “I will climb the palm tree; I will take hold of its fruit.” May your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the fragrance of your breath like apples,
chapters.zh: 我说：我要上这棕树，抓住枝子。 愿你的两乳好像葡萄累累下垂， 你鼻子的气味香如苹果；

chapters.en:
and your mouth like the finest wine. The Bride
May it flow smoothly to my beloved, gliding gently over lips and teeth.
chapters.zh: 你的口如上好的酒。 〔女子说〕：为我的良人下咽舒畅， 流入睡觉人的嘴中。

chapters.en: I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me.
chapters.zh: 我属我的良人， 他也恋慕我。

chapters.en:
Come, my beloved, let us go to the countryside;
let us spend the night among the wildflowers.
chapters.zh: 我的良人，来吧！ 你我可以往田间去； 你我可以在村庄住宿。

chapters.en:
Let us go early to the vineyards to see if the vine has budded, if the blossom has opened, if the pomegranates are in bloom—
there I will give you my love.
chapters.zh: 我们早晨起来往葡萄园去， 看看葡萄发芽开花没有， 石榴放蕊没有； 我在那里要将我的爱情给你。

chapters.en: The mandrakes send forth a fragrance, and at our door is every delicacy, new as well as old, that I have treasured up for you, my beloved.
chapters.zh: 风茄放香， 在我们的门内有各样新陈佳美的果子； 我的良人，这都是我为你存留的。

chapters.en: O that you were to me like a brother who nursed at my mother’s breasts! If I found you outdoors, I would kiss you, and no one would despise me.
chapters.zh: 巴不得你像我的兄弟， 像吃我母亲奶的兄弟； 我在外头遇见你就与你亲嘴， 谁也不轻看我。

chapters.en: I would lead you and bring you to the house of my mother who taught me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the nectar of my pomegranates.
chapters.zh: 我必引导你， 领你进我母亲的家； 我可以领受教训， 也就使你喝石榴汁酿的香酒。

chapters.en: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.
chapters.zh: 他的左手必在我头下； 他的右手必将我抱住。

chapters.en:
O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you: Do not arouse or awaken love
until the time is right.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷的众女子啊， 我嘱咐你们： 不要惊动、不要叫醒我所亲爱的， 等他自己情愿〔注：不要叫醒......情愿：或译不要激动爱情，等它自发〕。
那靠着良人从旷野上来的是谁呢？ 我在苹果树下叫醒你。 你母亲在那里为你劬劳； 生养你的在那里〔为你〕劬劳。

chapters.en: Set me as a seal over your heart, as a seal upon your arm. For love is as strong as death, its jealousy as unrelenting as Sheol. Its sparks are fiery flames, the fiercest blaze of all.
chapters.zh: 求你将我放在你心上如印记， 带在你臂上如戳记。 因为爱情如死之坚强， 嫉恨如阴间之残忍； 所发的电光是火焰的电光， 是耶和华的烈焰。

chapters.en: Mighty waters cannot quench love; rivers cannot sweep it away. If a man were to give all the wealth of his house for love, his offer would be utterly scorned.
chapters.zh: 爱情，众水不能熄灭， 大水也不能淹没。 若有人拿家中所有的财宝要换爱情， 就全被藐视。

chapters.en: We have a little sister, and her breasts are not yet grown. What shall we do for our sister on the day she is spoken for?
chapters.zh: 我们有一小妹； 她的两乳尚未长成， 人来提亲的日子， 我们当为她怎样办理？

chapters.en: If she is a wall, we will build a tower of silver upon her. If she is a door, we will enclose her with panels of cedar.
chapters.zh: 她若是墙， 我们要在其上建造银塔； 她若是门， 我们要用香柏木板围护她。

chapters.en: I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. So I have become in his eyes like one who brings peace.
chapters.zh: 我是墙； 我两乳像〔其上的〕楼。 那时，我在他眼中像得平安的人。

chapters.en: Solomon had a vineyard in Baal-hamon. He leased it to the tenants. For its fruit, each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver.
chapters.zh: 所罗门在巴力‧哈们有一葡萄园； 他将这葡萄园交给看守的人， 为其中的果子必交一千〔舍客勒〕银子。

chapters.en:
But my own vineyard is mine to give; the thousand shekels are for you, O Solomon,
and two hundred are for those who tend its fruit.
chapters.zh: 我自己的葡萄园在我面前。 所罗门哪，一千〔舍客勒〕归你， 二百〔舍客勒〕归看守果子的人。

chapters.en:
You who dwell in the gardens, my companions are listening for your voice.
Let me hear it!
chapters.zh: 你这住在园中的， 同伴都要听你的声音， 求你使我也得听见。

chapters.en: Come away, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices.
chapters.zh: 我的良人哪，求你快来！ 如羚羊或小鹿在香草山上。

chapters.en: This is the vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem that Isaiah son of Amoz saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
chapters.zh: 当乌西雅、约坦、亚哈斯、希西家作犹大王的时候，亚摩斯的儿子以赛亚得默示，论到犹大和耶路撒冷。

chapters.en:
Listen, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the LORD has spoken:
“I have raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against Me.
chapters.zh: 天哪，要听！地啊，侧耳而听！ 因为耶和华说： 我养育儿女，将他们养大， 他们竟悖逆我。

chapters.en: The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master’s manger, but Israel does not know; My people do not understand.”
chapters.zh: 牛认识主人， 驴认识主人的槽， 以色列却不认识； 我的民却不留意。

chapters.en:
Alas, O sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a brood of evildoers, children who act corruptly! They have forsaken the LORD; they have despised the Holy One of Israel
and turned their backs on Him.
chapters.zh: 嗐！犯罪的国民， 担着罪孽的百姓； 行恶的种类， 败坏的儿女！ 他们离弃耶和华， 藐视以色列的圣者， 与他生疏，往后退步。

chapters.en: Why do you want more beatings? Why do you keep rebelling? Your head has a massive wound, and your whole heart is afflicted.
chapters.zh: 你们为什么屡次悖逆， 还要受责打吗？ 你们已经满头疼痛， 全心发昏。

chapters.en: From the sole of your foot to the top of your head, there is no soundness— only wounds and welts and festering sores neither cleansed nor bandaged nor soothed with oil.
chapters.zh: 从脚掌到头顶， 没有一处完全的， 尽是伤口、青肿，与新打的伤痕， 都没有收口，没有缠裹， 也没有用膏滋润。

chapters.en: Your land is desolate; your cities are burned with fire. Foreigners devour your fields before you— a desolation demolished by strangers.
chapters.zh: 你们的地土已经荒凉； 你们的城邑被火焚毁。 你们的田地在你们眼前为外邦人所侵吞， 既被外邦人倾覆就成为荒凉。

chapters.en: And the Daughter of Zion is abandoned like a shelter in a vineyard, like a shack in a cucumber field, like a city besieged.
chapters.zh: 仅存锡安城〔注：原文是女子〕， 好像葡萄园的草棚， 瓜田的茅屋， 被围困的城邑。

chapters.en: Unless the LORD of Hosts had left us a few survivors, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.
chapters.zh: 若不是万军之耶和华给我们稍留余种， 我们早已像所多玛、蛾摩拉的样子了。

chapters.en: Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
chapters.zh: 你们这所多玛的官长啊， 要听耶和华的话！ 你们这蛾摩拉的百姓啊， 要侧耳听我们上帝的训诲！

chapters.en: “What good to Me is your multitude of sacrifices?” says the LORD. “I am full from the burnt offerings of rams and the fat of well-fed cattle; I take no delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats.
chapters.zh: 耶和华说： 你们所献的许多祭物与我何益呢？ 公绵羊的燔祭和肥畜的脂油， 我已经够了； 公牛的血，羊羔的血，公山羊的血， 我都不喜悦。

chapters.en:
When you come to appear before Me, who has required this of you—
this trampling of My courts?
chapters.zh: 你们来朝见我， 谁向你们讨这些， 使你们践踏我的院宇呢？

chapters.en: Bring your worthless offerings no more; your incense is detestable to Me. New Moons, Sabbaths, and convocations— I cannot endure iniquity in a solemn assembly.
chapters.zh: 你们不要再献虚浮的供物。 香品是我所憎恶的； 月朔和安息日，并宣召的大会， 也是我所憎恶的； 作罪孽，又守严肃会， 我也不能容忍。

chapters.en: I hate your New Moons and your appointed feasts. They have become a burden to Me; I am weary of bearing them.
chapters.zh: 你们的月朔和节期，我心里恨恶， 我都以为麻烦； 我担当，便不耐烦。

chapters.en:
When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you multiply your prayers, I will not listen.
Your hands are covered with blood.
chapters.zh: 你们举手祷告，我必遮眼不看； 就是你们多多地祈祷，我也不听。 你们的手都满了〔杀人的〕血。

chapters.en:
Wash and cleanse yourselves. Remove your evil deeds from My sight.
Stop doing evil!
chapters.zh: 你们要洗濯、自洁， 从我眼前除掉你们的恶行， 要止住作恶，

chapters.en: Learn to do right; seek justice and correct the oppressor. Defend the fatherless and plead the case of the widow.”
chapters.zh: 学习行善， 寻求公平， 解救受欺压的； 给孤儿伸冤， 为寡妇辨屈。

chapters.en: “Come now, let us reason together,” says the LORD. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow; though they are as red as crimson, they will become like wool.
chapters.zh: 耶和华说： 你们来，我们彼此辩论。 你们的罪虽像朱红，必变成雪白； 虽红如丹颜，必白如羊毛。

chapters.en: If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the best of the land.
chapters.zh: 你们若甘心听从， 必吃地上的美物，

chapters.en: But if you resist and rebel, you will be devoured by the sword.” For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
chapters.zh: 若不听从，反倒悖逆， 必被刀剑吞灭。 这是耶和华亲口说的。

chapters.en: See how the faithful city has become a harlot! She once was full of justice; righteousness resided within her, but now only murderers!
chapters.zh: 可叹，忠信的城变为妓女！ 从前充满了公平， 公义居在其中， 现今却有凶手居住。

chapters.en: Your silver has become dross; your fine wine is diluted with water.
chapters.zh: 你的银子变为渣滓； 你的酒用水搀对。

chapters.en: Your rulers are rebels, friends of thieves. They all love bribes and chasing after rewards. They do not defend the fatherless, and the plea of the widow never comes before them.
chapters.zh: 你的官长居心悖逆， 与盗贼作伴， 各都喜爱贿赂， 追求赃私。 他们不为孤儿伸冤； 寡妇的案件也不得呈到他们面前。

chapters.en:
Therefore the Lord GOD of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, declares:
“Ah, I will be relieved of My foes and avenge Myself on My enemies.
chapters.zh: 因此，主－万军之耶和华、 以色列的大能者说： 哎！我要向我的对头雪恨， 向我的敌人报仇。

chapters.en:
I will turn My hand against you; I will thoroughly purge your dross;
I will remove all your impurities.
chapters.zh: 我必反手加在你身上， 炼尽你的渣滓， 除净你的杂质。

chapters.en: I will restore your judges as at first, and your counselors as at the beginning. After that you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City.”
chapters.zh: 我也必复还你的审判官，像起初一样， 复还你的谋士，像起先一般。 然后，你必称为公义之城， 忠信之邑。

chapters.en: Zion will be redeemed with justice, her repentant ones with righteousness.
chapters.zh: 锡安必因公平得蒙救赎； 其中归正的人必因公义得蒙救赎。

chapters.en: But rebels and sinners will together be shattered, and those who forsake the LORD will perish.
chapters.zh: 但悖逆的和犯罪的必一同败亡； 离弃耶和华的必致消灭。

chapters.en: Surely you will be ashamed of the sacred oaks in which you have delighted; you will be embarrassed by the gardens that you have chosen.
chapters.zh: 那等人必因你们所喜爱的橡树抱愧； 你们必因所选择的园子蒙羞。

chapters.en: For you will become like an oak whose leaves are withered, like a garden without water.
chapters.zh: 因为，你们必如叶子枯干的橡树， 好像无水〔浇灌〕的园子。

chapters.en: The strong man will become tinder and his work will be a spark; both will burn together, with no one to quench the flames.
chapters.zh: 有权势的必如麻瓤； 他的工作好像火星， 都要一同焚毁，无人扑灭。

chapters.en: This is the message that was revealed to Isaiah son of Amoz concerning Judah and Jerusalem:
chapters.zh: 亚摩斯的儿子以赛亚得默示，论到犹大和耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: In the last days the mountain of the house of the LORD will be established as the chief of the mountains; it will be raised above the hills, and all nations will stream to it.
chapters.zh: 末后的日子，耶和华殿的山必坚立， 超乎诸山，高举过于万岭； 万民都要流归这山。

chapters.en:
And many peoples will come and say:
“Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us His ways so that we may walk in His paths.”
For the law will go forth from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 必有许多国的民前往，说： 来吧，我们登耶和华的山， 奔雅各上帝的殿。 主必将他的道教训我们； 我们也要行他的路。 因为训诲必出于锡安； 耶和华的言语必出于耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: Then He will judge between the nations and arbitrate for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor train anymore for war.
chapters.zh: 他必在列国中施行审判， 为许多国民断定是非。 他们要将刀打成诓头， 把枪打成镰刀。 这国不举刀攻击那国； 他们也不再学习战事。

chapters.en: Come, O house of Jacob, let us walk in the light of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 雅各家啊，来吧！ 我们在耶和华的光明中行走。

chapters.en: For You have abandoned Your people, the house of Jacob, because they are filled with influences from the east; they are soothsayers like the Philistines; they strike hands with the children of foreigners.
chapters.zh: 〔耶和华〕，你离弃了你百姓雅各家， 是因他们充满了东方的〔风俗〕， 作观兆的，像非利士人一样， 并与外邦人击掌。

chapters.en: Their land is full of silver and gold, with no limit to their treasures; their land is full of horses, with no limit to their chariots.
chapters.zh: 他们的国满了金银， 财宝也无穷； 他们的地满了马匹， 车辆也无数。

chapters.en:
Their land is full of idols; they bow down to the work of their hands,
to what their fingers have made.
chapters.zh: 他们的地满了偶像； 他们跪拜自己手所造的， 就是自己指头所做的。

chapters.en:
So mankind is brought low, and man is humbled—
do not forgive them!
chapters.zh: 卑贱人屈膝； 尊贵人下跪； 所以不可饶恕他们。

chapters.en: Go into the rocks and hide in the dust from the terror of the LORD and the splendor of His majesty.
chapters.zh: 你当进入巖穴，藏在土中， 躲避耶和华的惊吓和他威严的荣光。

chapters.en:
The proud look of man will be humbled, and the loftiness of men brought low;
the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.
chapters.zh: 到那日，眼目高傲的必降为卑； 性情狂傲的都必屈膝； 惟独耶和华被尊崇。

chapters.en: For the Day of the LORD of Hosts will come against all the proud and lofty, against all that is exalted— it will be humbled—
chapters.zh: 必有万军耶和华〔降罚〕的一个日子， 要临到骄傲狂妄的； 一切自高的都必降为卑；

chapters.en: against all the cedars of Lebanon, lofty and lifted up, against all the oaks of Bashan,
chapters.zh: 又临到黎巴嫩高大的香柏树和巴珊的橡树；

chapters.en: against all the tall mountains, against all the high hills,
chapters.zh: 又临到一切高山的峻岭；

chapters.en: against every high tower, against every fortified wall,
chapters.zh: 又临到高台和坚固城墙；

chapters.en: against every ship of Tarshish, and against every stately vessel.
chapters.zh: 又临到他施的船只并一切可爱的美物。

chapters.en: So the pride of man will be brought low, and the loftiness of men will be humbled; the LORD alone will be exalted in that day,
chapters.zh: 骄傲的必屈膝； 狂妄的必降卑。 在那日，惟独耶和华被尊崇；

chapters.en: and the idols will vanish completely.
chapters.zh: 偶像必全然废弃。

chapters.en:
Men will flee to caves in the rocks and holes in the ground, away from the terror of the LORD and from the splendor of His majesty,
when He rises to shake the earth.
chapters.zh: 耶和华兴起，使地大震动的时候， 人就进入石洞，进入土穴， 躲避耶和华的惊吓和他威严的荣光。

chapters.en: In that day men will cast away to the moles and bats their idols of silver and gold— the idols they made to worship.
chapters.zh: 到那日，人必将为拜而造的金偶像、银偶像 抛给田鼠和蝙蝠。

chapters.en:
They will flee to caverns in the rocks and crevices in the cliffs, away from the terror of the LORD and from the splendor of His majesty,
when He rises to shake the earth.
chapters.zh: 到耶和华兴起，使地大震动的时候， 人好进入磐石洞中和巖石穴里， 躲避耶和华的惊吓和他威严的荣光。

chapters.en:
Put no more trust in man, who has only the breath in his nostrils.
Of what account is he?
chapters.zh: 你们休要〔倚靠〕世人。 他鼻孔里不过有气息； 他在一切事上可算什么呢？

chapters.en: For behold, the Lord GOD of Hosts is about to remove from Jerusalem and Judah both supply and support: the whole supply of food and water,
chapters.zh: 主－万军之耶和华从耶路撒冷和犹大， 除掉众人所倚靠的，所仗赖的， 就是所倚靠的粮，所仗赖的水；

chapters.en: the mighty man and the warrior, the judge and the prophet, the soothsayer and the elder,
chapters.zh: 除掉勇士和战士， 审判官和先知， 占卜的和长老，

chapters.en: the commander of fifty and the dignitary, the counselor, the cunning magician, and the clever enchanter.
chapters.zh: 五十夫长和尊贵人， 谋士和有巧艺的， 以及妙行法术的。

chapters.en: “I will make mere lads their leaders, and children will rule over them.”
chapters.zh: 〔主说〕：我必使孩童作他们的首领， 使婴孩辖管他们。

chapters.en: The people will oppress one another, man against man, neighbor against neighbor; the young will rise up against the old, and the base against the honorable.
chapters.zh: 百姓要彼此欺压； 各人受邻舍的欺压。 少年人必侮慢老年人； 卑贱人必侮慢尊贵人。

chapters.en: A man will seize his brother within his father’s house: “You have a cloak—you be our leader! Take charge of this heap of rubble.”
chapters.zh: 人在父家拉住弟兄，〔说〕： 你有衣服，可以作我们的官长。 这败落的事归在你手下吧！

chapters.en: On that day he will cry aloud: “I am not a healer. I have no food or clothing in my house. Do not make me leader of the people!”
chapters.zh: 那时，他必扬声说： 我不作医治你们的人； 因我家中没有粮食，也没有衣服， 你们不可立我作百姓的官长。

chapters.en: For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen because they spoke and acted against the LORD, defying His glorious presence.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷败落， 犹大倾倒； 因为他们的舌头和行为与耶和华反对， 惹了他荣光的眼目。

chapters.en:
The expression on their faces testifies against them, and like Sodom they flaunt their sin;
they do not conceal it. Woe to them, for they have brought disaster upon themselves.
chapters.zh: 他们的面色证明自己的不正； 他们述说自己的罪恶，并不隐瞒， 好像所多玛一样。 他们有祸了！因为作恶自害。

chapters.en: Tell the righteous it will be well with them, for they will enjoy the fruit of their labor.
chapters.zh: 你们要论义人说：他必享福乐， 因为要吃自己行为所结的果子。

chapters.en: Woe to the wicked; disaster is upon them! For they will be repaid with what their hands have done.
chapters.zh: 恶人有祸了！他必遭灾难！ 因为要照自己手所行的受报应。

chapters.en: Youths oppress My people, and women rule over them. O My people, your guides mislead you; they turn you from your paths.
chapters.zh: 至于我的百姓， 孩童欺压他们， 妇女辖管他们。 我的百姓啊，引导你的使你走错， 并毁坏你所行的道路。

chapters.en: The LORD arises to contend; He stands to judge the people.
chapters.zh: 耶和华起来辩论， 站着审判众民。

chapters.en: The LORD brings this charge against the elders and leaders of His people: “You have devoured the vineyard; the plunder of the poor is in your houses.
chapters.zh: 耶和华必审问他民中的长老和首领，〔说〕： 吃尽葡萄园果子的就是你们； 向贫穷人所夺的都在你们家中。

chapters.en: Why do you crush My people and grind the faces of the poor?” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts.
chapters.zh: 主－万军之耶和华说： 你们为何压制我的百姓， 搓磨贫穷人的脸呢？

chapters.en:
The LORD also says:
“Because the daughters of Zion are haughty— walking with heads held high
and wanton eyes, prancing and skipping as they go, jingling the bracelets on their ankles—
chapters.zh: 耶和华又说： 因为锡安的女子狂傲， 行走挺项，卖弄眼目， 俏步徐行，脚下玎珰，

chapters.en:
the Lord will bring sores on the heads of the daughters of Zion,
and the LORD will make their foreheads bare. ”
chapters.zh: 所以，主必使锡安的女子头长秃疮； 耶和华又使她们赤露下体。

chapters.en: In that day the Lord will take away their finery: their anklets and headbands and crescents;
chapters.zh: 到那日，主必除掉她们华美的脚钏、发网、月牙圈、

chapters.en: their pendants, bracelets, and veils;
chapters.zh: 耳环、手镯、蒙脸的帕子、

chapters.en: their headdresses, ankle chains, and sashes; their perfume bottles and charms;
chapters.zh: 华冠、足鍊、华带、香盒、符囊、

chapters.en: their signet rings and nose rings;
chapters.zh: 戒指、鼻环、

chapters.en: their festive robes, capes, cloaks, and purses;
chapters.zh: 吉服、外套、云肩、荷包、

chapters.en: and their mirrors, linen garments, tiaras, and shawls.
chapters.zh: 手镜、细麻衣、裹头巾、蒙身的帕子。

chapters.en: Instead of fragrance there will be a stench; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of styled hair, baldness; instead of fine clothing, sackcloth; instead of beauty, shame.
chapters.zh: 必有臭烂代替馨香， 绳子代替腰带， 光秃代替美发， 麻衣系腰代替华服， 烙伤代替美容。

chapters.en: Your men will fall by the sword, and your warriors in battle.
chapters.zh: 你的男丁必倒在刀下； 你的勇士必死在阵上。

chapters.en: And the gates of Zion will lament and mourn; destitute, she will sit on the ground.
chapters.zh: 锡安〔注：原文是她〕的城门必悲伤、哀号； 她必荒凉坐在地上。

chapters.en: In that day seven women will take hold of one man and say, “We will eat our own bread and provide our own clothes. Just let us be called by your name. Take away our disgrace!”
chapters.zh: 在那日，七个女人必拉住一个男人，说：「我们吃自己的食物，穿自己的衣服，但求你许我们归你名下；求你除掉我们的羞耻。」

chapters.en: On that day the Branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the pride and glory of Israel’s survivors.
chapters.zh: 到那日，耶和华发生的苗必华美尊荣，地的出产必为以色列逃脱的人显为荣华茂盛。

chapters.en: Whoever remains in Zion and whoever is left in Jerusalem will be called holy— all in Jerusalem who are recorded among the living—
when the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and cleansed the bloodstains from the heart of Jerusalem by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of fire.
chapters.zh: 主以公义的灵和焚烧的灵，将锡安女子的污秽洗去，又将耶路撒冷中〔杀人〕的血除净。那时，剩在锡安、留在耶路撒冷的，就是一切住耶路撒冷、在生命册上记名的，必称为圣。

chapters.en: Then the LORD will create over all of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud of smoke by day and a glowing flame of fire by night. For over all the glory there will be a canopy,
chapters.zh: 耶和华也必在锡安全山，并各会众以上，使白日有烟云，黑夜有火焰的光。因为在全荣耀之上必有遮蔽。

chapters.en: a shelter to give shade from the heat by day, and a refuge and hiding place from the storm and the rain.
chapters.zh: 必有亭子，白日可以得荫避暑，也可以作为藏身之处，躲避狂风暴雨。

chapters.en:
I will sing for my beloved a song of his vineyard:
My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill.
chapters.zh: 我要为我所亲爱的唱歌， 是我所爱者的歌，论他葡萄园的事： 我所亲爱的有葡萄园在肥美的山冈上。

chapters.en:
He dug it up and cleared the stones and planted the finest vines. He built a watchtower in the middle and dug out a winepress as well.
He waited for the vineyard to yield good grapes, but the fruit it produced was sour!
chapters.zh: 他刨挖园子，捡去石头， 栽种上等的葡萄树， 在园中盖了一座楼， 又凿出压酒池； 指望结〔好〕葡萄， 反倒结了野葡萄。

chapters.en: “And now, O dwellers of Jerusalem and men of Judah, I exhort you to judge between Me and My vineyard.
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷的居民和犹大人哪， 请你们现今在我与我的葡萄园中，断定是非。

chapters.en: What more could have been done for My vineyard than I have done for it? Why, when I expected sweet grapes, did it bring forth sour fruit?
chapters.zh: 我为我葡萄园所做之外， 还有什么可做的呢？ 我指望结〔好〕葡萄， 怎么倒结了野葡萄呢？

chapters.en:
Now I will tell you what I am about to do to My vineyard:
I will take away its hedge, and it will be consumed; I will tear down its wall, and it will be trampled.
chapters.zh: 现在我告诉你们， 我要向我葡萄园怎样行： 我必撤去篱笆，使它被吞灭， 拆毁墙垣，使它被践踏。

chapters.en:
I will make it a wasteland, neither pruned nor cultivated,
and thorns and briers will grow up. I will command the clouds that rain shall not fall on it.”
chapters.zh: 我必使它荒废，不再修理， 不再锄刨，荆棘蒺藜倒要生长。 我也必命云不降雨在其上。

chapters.en: For the vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are the plant of His delight. He looked for justice, but saw bloodshed; for righteousness, but heard a cry of distress.
chapters.zh: 万军之耶和华的葡萄园就是以色列家； 他所喜爱的树就是犹大人。 他指望的是公平， 谁知倒有暴虐〔注：或译：倒流人血〕； 指望的是公义， 谁知倒有冤声。

chapters.en: Woe to you who add house to house and join field to field until no place is left and you live alone in the land.
chapters.zh: 祸哉！那些以房接房， 以地连地， 以致不留余地的， 只顾自己独居境内。

chapters.en:
I heard the LORD of Hosts declare:
“Surely many houses will become desolate, great mansions left unoccupied.
chapters.zh: 我耳闻万军之耶和华〔说〕： 必有许多又大又美的房屋 成为荒凉，无人居住。

chapters.en: For ten acres of vineyard will yield but a bath of wine, and a homer of seed only an ephah of grain. ”
chapters.zh: 三十亩葡萄园只出一罢特〔酒〕； 一贺梅珥谷种只结一伊法〔粮食〕。

chapters.en: Woe to those who rise early in the morning in pursuit of strong drink, who linger into the evening, to be inflamed by wine.
chapters.zh: 祸哉！那些清早起来追求浓酒， 留连到夜深，甚至因酒发烧的人。

chapters.en: At their feasts are the lyre and harp, tambourines and flutes and wine. They disregard the actions of the LORD and fail to see the work of His hands.
chapters.zh: 他们在筵席上 弹琴，鼓瑟，击鼓，吹笛，饮酒， 却不顾念耶和华的作为， 也不留心他手所做的。

chapters.en: Therefore My people will go into exile for their lack of understanding; their dignitaries are starving and their masses are parched with thirst.
chapters.zh: 所以，我的百姓因无知就被掳去； 他们的尊贵人甚是饥饿， 群众极其干渴。

chapters.en: Therefore Sheol enlarges its throat and opens wide its enormous jaws, and down go Zion’s nobles and masses, her revelers and carousers!
chapters.zh: 故此，阴间扩张其欲， 开了无限量的口； 他们的荣耀、群众、繁华， 并快乐的人都落〔在其中〕。

chapters.en: So mankind will be brought low, and each man humbled; the arrogant will lower their eyes.
chapters.zh: 卑贱人被压服； 尊贵人降为卑； 眼目高傲的人也降为卑。

chapters.en: But the LORD of Hosts will be exalted by His justice, and the holy God will show Himself holy in righteousness.
chapters.zh: 惟有万军之耶和华因公平而崇高； 圣者上帝因公义显为圣。

chapters.en: Lambs will graze as in their own pastures, and strangers will feed in the ruins of the wealthy.
chapters.zh: 那时，羊羔必来吃草，如同在自己的草场； 丰肥人的荒场被游行的人吃尽。

chapters.en: Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of deceit and pull sin along with cart ropes,
chapters.zh: 祸哉！那些以虚假之细绳牵罪孽的人！ 他们又像以套绳拉罪恶，

chapters.en: to those who say, “Let Him hurry and hasten His work so that we may see it! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come so that we may know it!”
chapters.zh: 说：任他急速行，赶快成就他的作为， 使我们看看； 任以色列圣者所谋划的临近成就， 使我们知道。

chapters.en: Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who turn darkness to light and light to darkness, who replace bitter with sweet and sweet with bitter.
chapters.zh: 祸哉！那些称恶为善，称善为恶， 以暗为光，以光为暗， 以苦为甜，以甜为苦的人。

chapters.en: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight.
chapters.zh: 祸哉！那些自以为有智慧， 自看为通达的人。

chapters.en: Woe to those who are heroes in drinking wine and champions in mixing strong drink,
chapters.zh: 祸哉！那些勇于饮酒， 以能力调浓酒的人。

chapters.en: who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of justice.
chapters.zh: 他们因受贿赂，就称恶人为义， 将义人的义夺去。

chapters.en: Therefore, as a tongue of fire consumes the straw, and as dry grass shrivels in the flame, so their roots will decay and their blossoms will blow away like dust; for they have rejected the instruction of the LORD of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
chapters.zh: 火苗怎样吞灭碎诩， 干草怎样落在火焰之中， 照样，他们的根必像朽〔物〕， 他们的花必像灰尘飞腾； 因为他们厌弃万军之耶和华的训诲， 藐视以色列圣者的言语。

chapters.en:
Therefore the anger of the LORD burns against His people; His hand is raised against them to strike them down. The mountains quake, and the corpses lie like refuse in the streets.
Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
chapters.zh: 所以，耶和华的怒气向他的百姓发作。 他的手伸出攻击他们，山岭就震动； 他们的尸首在街市上好像粪土。 虽然如此，他的怒气还未转消； 他的手仍伸不缩。

chapters.en:
He lifts a banner for the distant nations and whistles for those at the ends of the earth.
Behold—how speedily and swiftly they come!
chapters.zh: 他必竖立大旗，招远方的国民， 发嘶声叫他们从地极而来； 看哪，他们必急速奔来。

chapters.en: None of them grows weary or stumbles; no one slumbers or sleeps. No belt is loose and no sandal strap is broken.
chapters.zh: 其中没有疲倦的，绊跌的； 没有打盹的，睡觉的； 腰带并不放松， 鞋带也不折断。

chapters.en: Their arrows are sharpened, and all their bows are strung. The hooves of their horses are like flint; their chariot wheels are like a whirlwind.
chapters.zh: 他们的箭快利， 弓也上了弦。 马蹄算如坚石， 车轮好像旋风。

chapters.en: Their roaring is like that of a lion; they roar like young lions. They growl and seize their prey; they carry it away, and no one can rescue it.
chapters.zh: 他们要吼叫，像母狮子， 咆哮，像少壮狮子； 他们要咆哮抓食， 坦然叼去，无人救回。

chapters.en:
In that day they will roar over it, like the roaring of the sea. If one looks over the land, he will see darkness and distress;
even the light will be obscured by clouds.
chapters.zh: 那日，他们要向以色列人吼叫， 像海浪匉訇； 人若望地，只见黑暗艰难， 光明在云中变为昏暗。

chapters.en: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted; and the train of His robe filled the temple.
chapters.zh: 当乌西雅王崩的那年，我见主坐在高高的宝座上。他的衣裳垂下，遮满圣殿。

chapters.en: Above Him stood seraphim, each having six wings: With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they were flying.
chapters.zh: 其上有撒拉弗侍立，各有六个翅膀：用两个翅膀遮脸，两个翅膀遮脚，两个翅膀飞翔；

chapters.en:
And they were calling out to one another:
“Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory.”
chapters.zh: 彼此呼喊说： 圣哉！圣哉！圣哉！万军之耶和华； 他的荣光充满全地！

chapters.en: At the sound of their voices the doorposts and thresholds shook, and the temple was filled with smoke.
chapters.zh: 因呼喊者的声音，门槛的根基震动，殿充满了烟云。

chapters.en:
Then I said:
“Woe is me, for I am ruined, because I am a man of unclean lips dwelling among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts.”
chapters.zh: 那时我说：「祸哉！我灭亡了！因为我是嘴唇不洁的人，又住在嘴唇不洁的民中，又因我眼见大君王－万军之耶和华。」

chapters.en: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.
chapters.zh: 有一撒拉弗飞到我跟前，手里拿着红炭，是用火剪从坛上取下来的，

chapters.en:
And with it he touched my mouth and said:
“Now that this has touched your lips, your iniquity is removed
and your sin is atoned for.”
chapters.zh: 将炭沾我的口，说：「看哪，这炭沾了你的嘴，你的罪孽便除掉，你的罪恶就赦免了。」

chapters.en:
Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying:
“Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?”
And I said:
“Here am I. Send me!”
chapters.zh: 我又听见主的声音说：「我可以差遣谁呢？谁肯为我们去呢？」我说：「我在这里，请差遣我！」
他说：「你去告诉这百姓说： 你们听是要听见，却不明白； 看是要看见，却不晓得。

chapters.en:
Make the hearts of this people calloused; deafen their ears and close their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears,
understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed. ”
chapters.zh: 要使这百姓心蒙脂油， 耳朵发沉， 眼睛昏迷； 恐怕眼睛看见， 耳朵听见， 心里明白， 回转过来，便得医治。」

chapters.en:
Then I asked:
“How long, O Lord?”
And He replied:
“Until the cities lie ruined
and without inhabitant,
until the houses are left unoccupied and the land is desolate and ravaged,
chapters.zh: 我就说：「主啊，这到几时为止呢？」他说： 直到城邑荒凉，无人居住， 房屋〔空闲〕无人，地土极其荒凉。

chapters.en: until the LORD has driven men far away and the land is utterly forsaken.
chapters.zh: 并且耶和华将人迁到远方， 在这境内撇下的地土很多。

chapters.en: And though a tenth remains in the land, it will be burned again. As the terebinth and oak leave stumps when felled, so the holy seed will be a stump in the land.”
chapters.zh: 境内剩下的〔人〕若还有十分之一， 也必被吞灭， 像栗树、橡树虽被砍伐， 树触子却仍存留。 这圣洁的种类在国中也是如此。

chapters.en: Now in the days that Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, was king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram marched up to wage war against Jerusalem. He was accompanied by Pekah son of Remaliah the king of Israel, but he could not overpower the city.
chapters.zh: 乌西雅的孙子、约坦的儿子、犹大王亚哈斯〔在位〕的时候，亚兰王利汛和利玛利的儿子、以色列王比加上来攻打耶路撒冷，却不能攻取。

chapters.en: When it was reported to the house of David that Aram was in league with Ephraim, the hearts of Ahaz and his people trembled like trees in the forest shaken by the wind.
chapters.zh: 有人告诉大卫家说：「亚兰与以法莲已经同盟。」王的心和百姓的心就都跳动，好像林中的树被风吹动一样。

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to Isaiah, “Go out with your son Shear-jashub to meet Ahaz at the end of the aqueduct that feeds the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field,
chapters.zh: 耶和华对以赛亚说：「你和你的儿子施亚雅述出去，到上池的水沟头，在漂布地的大路上，去迎接亚哈斯，

chapters.en: and say to him: Calm down and be quiet. Do not be afraid or disheartened over these two smoldering stubs of firewood—over the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram and of the son of Remaliah.
chapters.zh: 对他说：『你要谨慎安静，不要因亚兰〔王〕利汛和利玛利的儿子这两个冒烟的火把头所发的烈怒害怕，也不要心里胆怯。

chapters.en: For Aram, along with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted your ruin, saying:
chapters.zh: 因为亚兰和以法莲，并利玛利的儿子，设恶谋害你，

chapters.en: ‘Let us invade Judah, terrorize it, and divide it among ourselves. Then we can install the son of Tabeal over it as king.’
chapters.zh: 说：我们可以上去攻击犹大，扰乱它，攻破它，在其中立他比勒的儿子为王。

chapters.en:
But this is what the Lord GOD says:
‘It will not arise; it will not happen.
chapters.zh: 所以主耶和华如此说： 这所谋的必立不住， 也不得成就。

chapters.en: For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered as a people.
chapters.zh: 原来亚兰的首城是大马士革； 大马士革的首领是利汛。 （六十五年之内，以法莲必然破坏，不再成为国民。）

chapters.en: The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in your faith, then you will not stand at all.’”
chapters.zh: 以法莲的首城是撒马利亚； 撒马利亚的首领是利玛利的儿子。 你们若是不信， 定然不得立稳。』」

chapters.en: Again the LORD spoke to Ahaz, saying,
chapters.zh: 耶和华又晓谕亚哈斯说：

chapters.en: “Ask for a sign from the LORD your God, whether from the depths of Sheol or the heights of heaven.”
chapters.zh: 「你向耶和华－你的上帝求一个兆头：或求〔显〕在深处，或求〔显〕在高处。」

chapters.en: But Ahaz replied, “I will not ask; I will not test the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 亚哈斯说：「我不求；我不试探耶和华。」

chapters.en: Then Isaiah said, “Hear now, O house of David! Is it not enough to try the patience of men? Will you try the patience of my God as well?
chapters.zh: 以赛亚说：「大卫家啊，你们当听！你们使人厌烦岂算小事，还要使我的上帝厌烦吗？

chapters.en: Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: Behold, the virgin will be with child and give birth to a son, and will call Him Immanuel.
chapters.zh: 因此，主自己要给你们一个兆头，必有童女怀孕生子，给他起名叫以马内利〔注：就是上帝与我们同在的意思〕。

chapters.en: By the time He knows enough to reject evil and choose good, He will be eating curds and honey.
chapters.zh: 到他晓得弃恶择善的时候，他必吃奶油与蜂蜜。

chapters.en: For before the boy knows enough to reject evil and choose good, the land of the two kings you dread will be laid waste.
chapters.zh: 因为在这孩子还不晓得弃恶择善之先，你所憎恶的那二王之地必致见弃。

chapters.en: The LORD will bring on you and on your people and on the house of your father a time unlike any since the day Ephraim separated from Judah—He will bring the king of Assyria.”
chapters.zh: 耶和华必使亚述王〔攻击你〕的日子临到你和你的百姓，并你的父家，自从以法莲离开犹大以来，未曾有这样的日子。

chapters.en: On that day the LORD will whistle to the flies at the farthest streams of the Nile and to the bees in the land of Assyria.
chapters.zh: 「那时，耶和华要发嘶声，使埃及江河源头的苍蝇和亚述地的蜂子飞来；

chapters.en:
And they will all come and settle in the steep ravines and clefts of the rocks,
in all the thornbushes and watering holes.
chapters.zh: 都必飞来，落在荒凉的谷内、磐石的穴里，和一切荆棘篱笆中，并一切的草场上。

chapters.en: On that day the Lord will use a razor hired from beyond the Euphrates —the king of Assyria—to shave your head and the hair of your legs, and to remove your beard as well.
chapters.zh: 「那时，主必用大河外赁的剃头刀，就是亚述王，剃去头发和脚上的毛，并要剃净胡须。

chapters.en: On that day a man will raise a young cow and two sheep,
chapters.zh: 「那时，一个人要养活一只母牛犊，两只母绵羊；

chapters.en: and from the abundance of milk they give, he will eat curds; for all who remain in the land will eat curds and honey.
chapters.zh: 因为出的奶多，他就得吃奶油，在境内所剩的人都要吃奶油与蜂蜜。

chapters.en: And on that day, in every place that had a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels of silver, only briers and thorns will be found.
chapters.zh: 「从前，凡种一千棵葡萄树、值银一千〔舍客勒〕的地方，到那时必长荆棘和蒺藜。

chapters.en: Men will go there with bow and arrow, for the land will be covered with briers and thorns.
chapters.zh: 人上那里去，必带弓箭，因为遍地满了荆棘和蒺藜。

chapters.en: For fear of the briers and thorns, you will no longer traverse the hills once tilled by the hoe; they will become places for oxen to graze and sheep to trample.
chapters.zh: 所有用锄刨挖的山地，你因怕荆棘和蒺藜，不敢上那里去；只可成了放牛之处，为羊践踏之地。」

chapters.en: Then the LORD said to me, “Take a large scroll and write on it with an ordinary stylus: Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对我说：「你取一个大牌，拿人所用的笔〔注：或译：人常用的字〕，写上『玛黑珥‧沙拉勒‧哈施‧罢斯』〔注：就是掳掠速临、抢夺快到的意思〕。

chapters.en: And I will appoint for Myself trustworthy witnesses—Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberekiah.”
chapters.zh: 我要用诚实的见证人，祭司乌利亚和耶比利家的儿子撒迦利亚记录这事。」

chapters.en: And I had relations with the prophetess, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. The LORD said to me, “Name him Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
chapters.zh: 我－〔以赛亚〕与妻子〔注：原文是女先知〕同室；她怀孕生子，耶和华就对我说：「给他起名叫玛黑珥‧沙拉勒‧哈施‧罢斯；

chapters.en: For before the boy knows how to cry ‘Father’ or ‘Mother,’ the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off by the king of Assyria.”
chapters.zh: 因为在这小孩子不晓得叫父叫母之先，大马士革的财宝和撒马利亚的掳物必在亚述王面前搬了去。」

chapters.en: And the LORD spoke to me further:
chapters.zh: 耶和华又晓谕我说：

chapters.en: “Because this people has rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah and rejoiced in Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
chapters.zh: 「这百姓既厌弃西罗亚缓流的水，喜悦利汛和利玛利的儿子；

chapters.en:
the Lord will surely bring against them the mighty floodwaters of the Euphrates —
the king of Assyria and all his pomp.
It will overflow its channels and overrun its banks.
chapters.zh: 因此，主必使大河翻腾的水猛然冲来，就是亚述王和他所有的威势，必漫过一切的水道，涨过两岸；

chapters.en:
It will pour into Judah, swirling and sweeping over it,
reaching up to the neck; its spreading streams will cover your entire land, O Immanuel!
chapters.zh: 必冲入犹大，涨溢泛滥，直到颈项。以马内利啊，他展开翅膀，遍满你的地。」

chapters.en: Huddle together, O peoples, and be shattered; pay attention, all you distant lands; prepare for battle, and be shattered; prepare for battle, and be shattered!
chapters.zh: 列国的人民哪，任凭你们喧嚷，终必破坏； 远方的众人哪，当侧耳而听！ 任凭你们束起腰来，终必破坏； 你们束起腰来，终必破坏。

chapters.en:
Devise a plan, but it will be thwarted; state a proposal, but it will not happen.
For God is with us. ”
chapters.zh: 任凭你们同谋，终归无有； 任凭你们言定，终不成立； 因为上帝与我们同在。

chapters.en: For this is what the LORD has spoken to me with a strong hand, instructing me not to walk in the way of this people:
chapters.zh: 耶和华以大能的手，指教我不可行这百姓所行的道，对我这样说：

chapters.en: “Do not call conspiracy everything these people regard as conspiracy. Do not fear what they fear; do not live in dread.
chapters.zh: 「这百姓说同谋背叛，你们不要说同谋背叛。他们所怕的，你们不要怕，也不要畏惧。

chapters.en: The LORD of Hosts is the One you shall regard as holy. Only He should be feared; only He should be dreaded.
chapters.zh: 但要尊万军之耶和华为圣，以他为你们所当怕的，所当畏惧的。

chapters.en: And He will be a sanctuary— but to both houses of Israel a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, to the dwellers of Jerusalem a trap and a snare.
chapters.zh: 他必作为圣所，却向以色列两家作绊脚的石头，跌人的磐石；向耶路撒冷的居民作为圈套和网罗。

chapters.en:
Many will stumble over these; they will fall and be broken;
they will be ensnared and captured.”
chapters.zh: 许多人必在其上绊脚跌倒，而且跌碎，并陷入网罗，被缠住。」

chapters.en: Bind up the testimony and seal the law among my disciples.
chapters.zh: 你要卷起律法〔书〕，在我门徒中间封住训诲。

chapters.en:
I will wait for the LORD, who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob.
I will put my trust in Him.
chapters.zh: 我要等候那掩面不顾雅各家的耶和华；我也要仰望他。

chapters.en: Here am I, and the children the LORD has given me as signs and symbols in Israel from the LORD of Hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.
chapters.zh: 看哪，我与耶和华所给我的儿女，就是从住在锡安山万军之耶和华来的，在以色列中作为预兆和奇迹。

chapters.en: When men tell you to consult mediums and spiritists who whisper and mutter, shouldn’t a people consult their God instead? Why consult the dead on behalf of the living?
chapters.zh: 有人对你们说：「当求问那些交鬼的和行巫术的，就是声音绵蛮，言语微细的。」〔你们便回答说〕：「百姓不当求问自己的上帝吗？岂可为活人〔求问〕死人呢？」

chapters.en: To the law and to the testimony! If they do not speak according to this word, they have no light of dawn.
chapters.zh: 人当以训诲和法度为标准；他们所说的，若不与此相符，必不得见晨光。

chapters.en: They will roam the land, dejected and hungry. When they are famished, they will become enraged; and looking upward, they will curse their king and their God.
chapters.zh: 他们必经过这地，受艰难，受饥饿；饥饿的时候，心中焦躁，咒骂自己的君王和自己的上帝。

chapters.en: Then they will look to the earth and see only distress and darkness and the gloom of anguish. And they will be driven into utter darkness.
chapters.zh: 仰观上天，俯察下地，不料，尽是艰难、黑暗，和幽暗的痛苦。〔他们必〕被赶入乌黑的黑暗中去。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, there will be no more gloom for those in distress. In the past He humbled the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the future He will honor the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations:
chapters.zh: 但那受过痛苦的必不再见幽暗。 从前上帝使西布伦地和拿弗他利地被藐视，末后却使这沿海的路，约旦河外，外邦人的加利利地得着荣耀。

chapters.en: The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned.
chapters.zh: 在黑暗中行走的百姓看见了大光； 住在死荫之地的人有光照耀他们。

chapters.en:
You have enlarged the nation and increased its joy. The people rejoice before You as they rejoice at harvest time,
as men rejoice in dividing the plunder.
chapters.zh: 你使这国民繁多， 加增他们的喜乐； 他们在你面前欢喜， 好像收割的欢喜， 像人分掳物那样的快乐。

chapters.en: For as in the day of Midian You have shattered the yoke of their burden, the bar across their shoulders, and the rod of their oppressor.
chapters.zh: 因为他们所负的重轭 和肩头上的杖， 并欺压他们人的棍， 你都已经折断， 好像在米甸的日子一样。

chapters.en:
For every trampling boot of battle and every garment rolled in blood
will be burned as fuel for the fire.
chapters.zh: 战士在乱杀之间所穿戴的盔甲， 并那滚在血中的衣服， 都必作为可烧的， 当作火柴。

chapters.en:
For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given,
and the government will be upon His shoulders. And He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God,
Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
chapters.zh: 因有一婴孩为我们而生； 有一子赐给我们。 政权必担在他的肩头上； 他名称为「奇妙策士、全能的上帝、永在的父、和平的君」。

chapters.en:
Of the increase of His government and peace there will be no end. He will reign on the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish and sustain it with justice and righteousness
from that time and forevermore.
The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.
chapters.zh: 他的政权与平安必加增无穷。 他必在大卫的宝座上治理他的国， 以公平公义使国坚定稳固， 从今直到永远。 万军之耶和华的热心必成就这事。

chapters.en: The Lord has sent a message against Jacob, and it has fallen upon Israel.
chapters.zh: 主使一言入于雅各〔家〕， 落于以色列〔家〕。

chapters.en: All the people will know it— Ephraim and the dwellers of Samaria. With pride and arrogance of heart they will say:
chapters.zh: 这众百姓，就是以法莲 和撒马利亚的居民，都要知道； 他们凭骄傲自大的心说：

chapters.en: “The bricks have fallen, but we will rebuild with finished stone; the sycamores have been felled, but we will replace them with cedars.”
chapters.zh: 砖〔墙〕塌了，我们却要凿石头建筑； 桑树砍了，我们却要换香柏树。

chapters.en: The LORD has raised up the foes of Rezin against him and joined his enemies together.
chapters.zh: 因此，耶和华要高举利汛的敌人 来攻击以色列， 并要激动以色列的仇敌。

chapters.en:
Aram from the east and Philistia from the west have devoured Israel with open mouths.
Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
chapters.zh: 东有亚兰人，西有非利士人； 他们张口要吞吃以色列。 虽然如此，耶和华的怒气还未转消； 他的手仍伸不缩。

chapters.en: But the people did not return to Him who struck them; they did not seek the LORD of Hosts.
chapters.zh: 这百姓还没有归向击打他们的主， 也没有寻求万军之耶和华。

chapters.en: So the LORD will cut off Israel’s head and tail, both palm branch and reed in a single day.
chapters.zh: 因此，耶和华一日之间 必从以色列中剪除头与尾， 棕枝与芦苇－

chapters.en: The head is the elder and honorable man, and the tail is the prophet who teaches lies.
chapters.zh: 长老和尊贵人就是头， 以谎言教人的先知就是尾。

chapters.en: For those who guide this people mislead them, and those they mislead are swallowed up.
chapters.zh: 因为，引导这百姓的使他们走错了路； 被引导的都必败亡。

chapters.en:
Therefore the Lord takes no pleasure in their young men; He has no compassion on their fatherless and widows. For every one of them is godless and wicked, and every mouth speaks folly.
Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
chapters.zh: 所以，主必不喜悦他们的少年人， 也不怜恤他们的孤儿寡妇； 因为，各人是亵渎的，是行恶的， 并且各人的口都说愚妄的话。 虽然如此，耶和华的怒气还未转消； 他的手仍伸不缩。

chapters.en: For wickedness burns like a fire that consumes the thorns and briers and kindles the forest thickets, which roll upward in billows of smoke.
chapters.zh: 邪恶像火焚烧， 烧灭荆棘和蒺藜， 在稠密的树林中着起来， 就成为烟柱，旋转上腾。

chapters.en: By the wrath of the LORD of Hosts the land is scorched, and the people are fuel for the fire. No man even spares his brother.
chapters.zh: 因万军之耶和华的烈怒，地都烧遍； 百姓成为火柴； 无人怜爱弟兄。

chapters.en:
They carve out what is on the right, but they are still hungry; they eat what is on the left, but they are still not satisfied.
Each one devours the flesh of his own offspring.
chapters.zh: 有人右边抢夺，仍受饥饿， 左边吞吃，仍不饱足； 各人吃自己膀臂上的肉。
玛拿西〔吞吃〕〔注：或译：攻击；下同〕以法莲； 以法莲〔吞吃〕玛拿西， 又一同攻击犹大。 虽然如此，耶和华的怒气还未转消； 他的手仍伸不缩。

chapters.en: Woe to those who enact unjust statutes and issue oppressive decrees,
chapters.zh: 祸哉！那些设立不义之律例的 和记录奸诈之判语的，

chapters.en: to deprive the poor of fair treatment and withhold justice from the oppressed of My people, to make widows their prey and orphans their plunder.
chapters.zh: 为要屈枉穷乏人， 夺去我民中困苦人的理， 以寡妇当作掳物， 以孤儿当作掠物。

chapters.en: What will you do on the day of reckoning when devastation comes from afar? To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave your wealth?
chapters.zh: 到降罚的日子，有灾祸从远方临到， 那时，你们怎样行呢？ 你们向谁逃奔求救呢？ 你们的荣耀〔注：或译：财宝〕存留何处呢？

chapters.en:
Nothing will remain but to crouch among the captives or fall among the slain.
Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
chapters.zh: 他们只得屈身在被掳的人以下， 仆倒在被杀的人以下。 虽然如此，耶和华的怒气还未转消； 他的手仍伸不缩。

chapters.en: Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger; the staff in their hands is My wrath.
chapters.zh: 亚述是我怒气的棍， 手中拿我恼恨的杖。

chapters.en: I will send him against a godless nation; I will dispatch him against a people destined for My rage, to take spoils and seize plunder, and to trample them down like clay in the streets.
chapters.zh: 我要打发他攻击亵渎的国民， 吩咐他攻击我所恼怒的百姓， 抢财为掳物，夺货为掠物， 将他们践踏，像街上的泥土一样。

chapters.en: But this is not his intention; this is not his plan. For it is in his heart to destroy and cut off many nations.
chapters.zh: 然而，他不是这样的意思； 他心也不这样打算。 他心里倒想毁灭， 剪除不少的国。

chapters.en: “Are not all my commanders kings?” he says.
chapters.zh: 他说：我的臣仆岂不都是王吗？

chapters.en: “Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?
chapters.zh: 迦勒挪岂不像迦基米施吗？ 哈马岂不像亚珥拔吗？ 撒马利亚岂不像大马士革吗？

chapters.en: As my hand seized the idolatrous kingdoms whose images surpassed those of Jerusalem and Samaria,
chapters.zh: 我手已经搆到有偶像的国； 这些国雕刻的偶像 过于耶路撒冷和撒马利亚的偶像。

chapters.en: and as I have done to Samaria and its idols, will I not also do to Jerusalem and her idols?”
chapters.zh: 我怎样待撒马利亚和其中的偶像， 岂不照样待耶路撒冷和其中的偶像吗？

chapters.en: So when the Lord has completed all His work against Mount Zion and Jerusalem, He will say, “I will punish the king of Assyria for the fruit of his arrogant heart and the proud look in his eyes.
chapters.zh: 主在锡安山和耶路撒冷成就他一切工作的时候，〔主说〕：「我必罚亚述王自大的心和他高傲眼目的荣耀。」
因为他说： 我所成就的事是靠我手的能力 和我的智慧， 我本有聪明。 我挪移列国的地界， 抢夺他们所积蓄的财宝； 并且我像勇士，使坐宝座的降为卑。

chapters.en: My hand reached as into a nest to seize the wealth of the nations. Like one gathering abandoned eggs, I gathered all the earth. No wing fluttered, no beak opened or chirped.’”
chapters.zh: 我的手搆到列国的财宝， 好像人搆到鸟窝； 我也得了全地， 好像人拾起所弃的雀蛋。 没有动翅膀的； 没有张嘴的，也没有鸣叫的。

chapters.en: Does an axe raise itself above the one who swings it? Does a saw boast over him who saws with it? It would be like a rod waving the one who lifts it, or a staff lifting him who is not wood!
chapters.zh: 斧岂可向用斧砍木的自夸呢？ 锯岂可向用锯的自大呢？ 好比棍抡起那举棍的， 好比杖举起那非木的人。

chapters.en: Therefore the Lord GOD of Hosts will send a wasting disease among Assyria’s stout warriors, and under his pomp will be kindled a fire like a burning flame.
chapters.zh: 因此，主－万军之耶和华 必使亚述王的肥壮人变为瘦弱， 在他的荣华之下必有火着起， 如同焚烧一样。

chapters.en: And the Light of Israel will become a fire, and its Holy One a flame. In a single day it will burn and devour Assyria’s thorns and thistles.
chapters.zh: 以色列的光必如火； 他的圣者必如火焰。 在一日之间，将亚述王的荆棘 和蒺藜焚烧净尽；

chapters.en: The splendor of its forests and orchards, both soul and body, it will completely destroy, as a sickness consumes a man.
chapters.zh: 又将他树林和肥田的荣耀全然烧尽， 好像拿军旗的昏过去一样。

chapters.en: The remaining trees of its forests will be so few that a child could count them.
chapters.zh: 他林中剩下的树必稀少， 就是孩子也能写其数。

chapters.en: On that day the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob will no longer depend on him who struck them, but they will truly rely on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
chapters.zh: 到那日，以色列所剩下的和雅各家所逃脱的，不再倚靠那击打他们的，却要诚实倚靠耶和华－以色列的圣者。

chapters.en: A remnant will return —a remnant of Jacob— to the Mighty God.
chapters.zh: 所剩下的，就是雅各〔家〕所剩下的，必归回全能的上帝。

chapters.en: Though your people, O Israel, be like the sand of the sea, only a remnant will return. Destruction has been decreed, overflowing with righteousness.
chapters.zh: 以色列啊，你的百姓虽多如海沙，〔惟有〕剩下的归回。原来灭绝的事已定，必有公义施行，如水涨溢。

chapters.en: For the Lord GOD of Hosts will carry out the destruction decreed upon the whole land.
chapters.zh: 因为主－万军之耶和华在全地之中必成就所定规的结局。

chapters.en:
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD of Hosts says:
“O My people who dwell in Zion, do not fear Assyria, who strikes you with a rod and lifts his staff against you
as the Egyptians did.
chapters.zh: 所以，主－万军之耶和华如此说：「住锡安我的百姓啊，亚述王虽然用棍击打你，又照埃及的样子举杖攻击你，你却不要怕他。

chapters.en:
For in just a little while My fury against you will subside,
and My anger will turn to their destruction.”
chapters.zh: 因为还有一点点时候，〔向你们〕发的忿恨就要完毕，我的怒气要向他〔发作〕，使他灭亡。

chapters.en: And the LORD of Hosts will brandish a whip against them, as when He struck Midian at the rock of Oreb. He will raise His staff over the sea, as He did in Egypt.
chapters.zh: 万军之耶和华要兴起鞭来攻击他，好像在俄立磐石那里杀戮米甸人一样。耶和华的杖要向海伸出，把杖举起，像在埃及一样。

chapters.en: On that day the burden will be lifted from your shoulders, and the yoke from your neck. The yoke will be broken because your neck will be too large.
chapters.zh: 到那日，亚述王的重担必离开你的肩头；他的轭必离开你的颈项；那轭也必因肥壮的缘故撑断〔注：或译：因膏油的缘故毁坏〕。」

chapters.en:
Assyria has entered Aiath and passed through Migron,
storing their supplies at Michmash.
chapters.zh: 亚述王来到亚叶， 经过米矶崙， 在密抹安放辎重。

chapters.en: They have crossed at the ford: “We will spend the night at Geba.” Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul flees.
chapters.zh: 他们过了隘口， 在迦巴住宿。 拉玛人战兢； 扫罗的基比亚人逃跑。

chapters.en:
Cry aloud, O Daughter of Gallim! Listen, O Laishah!
O wretched Anathoth!
chapters.zh: 迦琳的居民〔注：原文是女子〕哪，要高声呼喊！ 莱煞人哪，须听！ 哀哉！困苦的亚拿突啊。

chapters.en: Madmenah flees; the people of Gebim take refuge.
chapters.zh: 玛得米那人躲避； 基柄的居民逃遁。

chapters.en:
Yet today they will halt at Nob, shaking a fist at the mount of Daughter Zion,
at the hill of Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 当那日，亚述王要在挪伯歇兵， 向锡安女子的山－ 就是耶路撒冷的山－抡手〔攻他〕。

chapters.en: Behold, the Lord GOD of Hosts will lop off the branches with terrifying power. The tall trees will be cut down, the lofty ones will be felled.
chapters.zh: 看哪，主－万军之耶和华 以惊吓削去树枝； 长高的必被砍下， 高大的必被伐倒。

chapters.en: He will clear the forest thickets with an axe, and Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One.
chapters.zh: 稠密的树林，他要用铁器砍下； 黎巴嫩〔的树木〕必被大能者伐倒。

chapters.en: Then a shoot will spring up from the stump of Jesse, and a Branch from his roots will bear fruit.
chapters.zh: 从耶西的本〔注：原文是触〕必发一条； 从他根生的枝子必结果实。

chapters.en:
The Spirit of the LORD will rest on Him— the Spirit of wisdom and understanding,
the Spirit of counsel and strength,
the Spirit of knowledge and fear of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的灵必住在他身上， 就是使他有智慧和聪明的灵， 谋略和能力的灵， 知识和敬畏耶和华的灵。

chapters.en:
And He will delight in the fear of the LORD.
He will not judge by what His eyes see, and He will not decide by what His ears hear,
chapters.zh: 他必以敬畏耶和华为乐； 行审判不凭眼见， 断是非也不凭耳闻；

chapters.en: but with righteousness He will judge the poor, and with equity He will decide for the lowly of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of His mouth and slay the wicked with the breath of His lips.
chapters.zh: 却要以公义审判贫穷人， 以正直判断世上的谦卑人， 以口中的杖击打世界， 以嘴里的气杀戮恶人。

chapters.en: Righteousness will be the belt around His hips, and faithfulness the sash around His waist.
chapters.zh: 公义必当他的腰带； 信实必当他胁下的带子。

chapters.en: The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the goat; the calf and young lion and fatling will be together, and a little child will lead them.
chapters.zh: 豺狼必与绵羊羔同居， 豹子与山羊羔同卧； 少壮狮子与牛犊并肥畜同群； 小孩子要牵引牠们。

chapters.en:
The cow will graze with the bear, their young will lie down together,
and the lion will eat straw like the ox.
chapters.zh: 牛必与熊同食； 牛犊必与小熊同卧； 狮子必吃草，与牛一样。

chapters.en: The infant will play by the cobra’s den, and the toddler will reach into the viper’s nest.
chapters.zh: 吃奶的孩子必玩耍在虺蛇的洞口； 断奶的婴儿必按手在毒蛇的穴上。

chapters.en: They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain, for the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the sea is full of water.
chapters.zh: 在我圣山的遍处， 这一切都不伤人，不害物； 因为认识耶和华的知识要充满遍地， 好像水充满洋海一般。

chapters.en: On that day the Root of Jesse will stand as a banner for the peoples. The nations will seek Him, and His place of rest will be glorious.
chapters.zh: 到那日，耶西的根立作万民的大旗；外邦人必寻求他，他安息之所大有荣耀。

chapters.en: On that day the Lord will extend His hand a second time to recover the remnant of His people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.
chapters.zh: 当那日，主必二次伸手救回自己百姓中所余剩的，就是在亚述、埃及、巴忒罗、古实、以拦、示拿、哈马，并众海岛所剩下的。

chapters.en: He will raise a banner for the nations and gather the exiles of Israel; He will collect the scattered of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
chapters.zh: 他必向列国竖立大旗， 招回以色列被赶散的人， 又从地的四方聚集分散的犹大人。

chapters.en: Then the jealousy of Ephraim will depart, and the adversaries of Judah will be cut off. Ephraim will no longer envy Judah, nor will Judah harass Ephraim.
chapters.zh: 以法莲的嫉妒就必消散； 扰害犹大的必被剪除。 以法莲必不嫉妒犹大， 犹大也不扰害以法莲。

chapters.en: They will swoop down on the slopes of the Philistines to the west; together they will plunder the sons of the east. They will lay their hands on Edom and Moab, and the Ammonites will be subject to them.
chapters.zh: 他们要向西飞， 扑在非利士人的肩头上〔注：肩头上：或译西界〕， 一同掳掠东方人， 伸手按住以东和摩押； 亚扪人也必顺服他们。

chapters.en: The LORD will devote to destruction the gulf of the Sea of Egypt; with a scorching wind He will sweep His hand over the Euphrates. He will split it into seven streams for men to cross with dry sandals.
chapters.zh: 耶和华必使埃及海汊枯干， 抡手用暴热的风使大河分为七条， 令人过去不致湿脚。

chapters.en: There will be a highway for the remnant of His people who remain from Assyria, as there was for Israel when they came up from the land of Egypt.
chapters.zh: 为主余剩的百姓， 就是从亚述剩下回来的， 必有一条大道， 如当日以色列从埃及地上来一样。

chapters.en:
In that day you will say:
“O LORD, I will praise You. Although You were angry with me, Your anger has turned away, and You have comforted me.
chapters.zh: 到那日，你必说： 耶和华啊，我要称谢你！ 因为你虽然向我发怒， 你的怒气却已转消； 你又安慰了我。

chapters.en: Surely God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid. For the LORD GOD is my strength and my song, and He also has become my salvation.”
chapters.zh: 看哪！上帝是我的拯救； 我要倚靠他，并不惧怕。 因为主耶和华是我的力量， 是我的诗歌， 他也成了我的拯救。

chapters.en: With joy you will draw water from the springs of salvation,
chapters.zh: 所以，你们必从救恩的泉源欢然取水。

chapters.en:
and on that day you will say:
“Give praise to the LORD; proclaim His name! Make His works known among the peoples; declare that His name is exalted.
chapters.zh: 在那日，你们要说： 当称谢耶和华，求告他的名； 将他所行的传扬在万民中， 提说他的名已被尊崇。

chapters.en: Sing to the LORD, for He has done glorious things. Let this be known in all the earth.
chapters.zh: 你们要向耶和华唱歌， 因他所行的甚是美好； 但愿这事普传天下。

chapters.en: Cry out and sing, O citizen of Zion, for great among you is the Holy One of Israel.”
chapters.zh: 锡安的居民哪，当扬声欢呼， 因为在你们中间的以色列圣者乃为至大。

chapters.en: This is the burden against Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz received:
chapters.zh: 亚摩斯的儿子以赛亚得默示，论巴比伦。

chapters.en: Raise a banner on a barren hilltop; call aloud to them. Wave your hand, that they may enter the gates of the nobles.
chapters.zh: 应当在净光的山竖立大旗， 向群众扬声招手， 使他们进入贵胄的门。

chapters.en: I have commanded My sanctified ones; I have even summoned My warriors to execute My wrath and exult in My triumph.
chapters.zh: 我吩咐我所挑出来的人； 我招呼我的勇士－ 就是那矜夸高傲之辈， 为要成就我怒中所定的。

chapters.en: Listen, a tumult on the mountains, like that of a great multitude! Listen, an uproar among the kingdoms, like nations gathered together! The LORD of Hosts is mobilizing an army for war.
chapters.zh: 山间有多人的声音， 好像是大国人民。 有许多国的民聚集鬨嚷的声音； 这是万军之耶和华点齐军队，预备打仗。

chapters.en: They are coming from faraway lands, from the ends of the heavens— the LORD and the weapons of His wrath— to destroy the whole country.
chapters.zh: 他们从远方来， 从天边来， 就是耶和华并他恼恨的兵器 要毁灭这全地。

chapters.en: Wail, for the Day of the LORD is near; it will come as destruction from the Almighty.
chapters.zh: 你们要哀号， 因为耶和华的日子临近了！ 这日来到， 好像毁灭从全能者来到。

chapters.en: Therefore all hands will fall limp, and every man’s heart will melt.
chapters.zh: 所以，人手都必软弱； 人心都必消化。

chapters.en: Terror, pain, and anguish will seize them; they will writhe like a woman in labor. They will look at one another, their faces flushed with fear.
chapters.zh: 他们必惊惶悲痛； 愁苦必将他们抓住。 他们疼痛，好像产难的妇人一样， 彼此惊奇相看，脸如火焰。

chapters.en: Behold, the Day of the LORD is coming— cruel, with fury and burning anger— to make the earth a desolation and to destroy the sinners within it.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的日子临到， 必有残忍、忿恨、烈怒， 使这地荒凉， 从其中除灭罪人。

chapters.en: For the stars of heaven and their constellations will not give their light. The rising sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.
chapters.zh: 天上的众星群宿都不发光； 日头一出就变黑暗； 月亮也不放光。

chapters.en: I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their iniquity. I will end the haughtiness of the arrogant and lay low the pride of the ruthless.
chapters.zh: 我必因邪恶刑罚世界， 因罪孽刑罚恶人， 使骄傲人的狂妄止息， 制伏强暴人的狂傲。

chapters.en: I will make man scarcer than pure gold, and mankind rarer than the gold of Ophir.
chapters.zh: 我必使人比精金还少， 使人比俄斐纯金更少。

chapters.en: Therefore I will make the heavens tremble, and the earth will be shaken from its place at the wrath of the LORD of Hosts on the day of His burning anger.
chapters.zh: 我－万军之耶和华在忿恨中发烈怒的日子， 必使天震动， 使地摇撼，离其本位。

chapters.en: Like a hunted gazelle, like a sheep without a shepherd, each will return to his own people, each will flee to his native land.
chapters.zh: 人必像被追赶的鹿， 像无人收聚的羊， 各归回本族， 各逃到本土。

chapters.en: Whoever is caught will be stabbed, and whoever is captured will die by the sword.
chapters.zh: 凡被〔仇敌〕追上的必被刺死； 凡被捉住的必被刀杀。

chapters.en: Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes, their houses will be looted, and their wives will be ravished.
chapters.zh: 他们的婴孩必在他们眼前摔碎； 他们的房屋必被抢夺； 他们的妻子必被玷污。

chapters.en:
Behold, I will stir up against them the Medes, who have no regard for silver
and no desire for gold.
chapters.zh: 我必激动米底亚人来攻击他们。 米底亚人不注重银子， 也不喜爱金子。

chapters.en:
Their bows will dash young men to pieces; they will have no mercy on the fruit of the womb;
they will not look with pity on the children.
chapters.zh: 他们必用弓击碎少年人， 不怜悯妇人所生的， 眼也不顾惜孩子。

chapters.en: And Babylon, the jewel of the kingdoms, the glory of the pride of the Chaldeans, will be overthrown by God like Sodom and Gomorrah.
chapters.zh: 巴比伦素来为列国的荣耀， 为迦勒底人所矜夸的华美， 必像上帝所倾覆的所多玛、蛾摩拉一样。

chapters.en: She will never be inhabited or settled from generation to generation; no nomad will pitch his tent there, no shepherd will rest his flock there.
chapters.zh: 其内必永无人烟， 世世代代无人居住。 阿拉伯人也不在那里支搭帐棚； 牧羊的人也不使羊群卧在那里。

chapters.en: But desert creatures will lie down there, and howling creatures will fill her houses. Ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will leap about.
chapters.zh: 只有旷野的走兽卧在那里； 咆哮的兽满了房屋。 鸵鸟住在那里； 野山羊在那里跳舞。

chapters.en: Hyenas will howl in her fortresses and jackals in her luxurious palaces. Babylon’s time is at hand, and her days will not be prolonged.
chapters.zh: 豺狼必在它宫中呼号； 野狗必在它华美殿内吼叫。 巴比伦〔受罚〕的时候临近； 它的日子必不长久。

chapters.en: For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob; once again He will choose Israel and settle them in their own land. The foreigner will join them and unite with the house of Jacob.
chapters.zh: 耶和华要怜恤雅各，必再拣选以色列，将他们安置在本地。寄居的必与他们联合，紧贴雅各家。

chapters.en:
The nations will escort Israel and bring it to its homeland.
Then the house of Israel will possess the nations as menservants and maidservants in the LORD’s land. They will make captives of their captors and rule over their oppressors.
chapters.zh: 外邦人必将他们带回本土；以色列家必在耶和华的地上得外邦人为仆婢，也要掳掠先前掳掠他们的，辖制先前欺压他们的。

chapters.en: On the day that the LORD gives you rest from your pain and torment, and from the hard labor into which you were forced,
chapters.zh: 当耶和华使你脱离愁苦、烦恼，并人勉强你做的苦工，得享安息的日子，

chapters.en:
you will sing this song of contempt against the king of Babylon:
How the oppressor has ceased, and how his fury has ended!
chapters.zh: 你必题这诗歌论巴比伦王说： 欺压人的何竟熄灭？ 强暴的何竟止息？

chapters.en: The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of the rulers.
chapters.zh: 耶和华折断了恶人的杖， 辖制人的圭，

chapters.en: It struck the peoples in anger with unceasing blows; it subdued the nations in rage with relentless persecution.
chapters.zh: 就是在忿怒中连连攻击众民的， 在怒气中辖制列国， 行逼迫无人阻止的。

chapters.en: All the earth is at peace and at rest; they break out in song.
chapters.zh: 现在全地得安息，享平静； 人皆发声欢呼。

chapters.en: Even the cypresses and cedars of Lebanon exult over you: “Since you have been laid low, no woodcutter comes against us.”
chapters.zh: 松树和黎巴嫩的香柏树 都因你欢乐，〔说〕： 自从你仆倒， 再无人上来砍伐我们。

chapters.en: Sheol beneath is eager to meet you upon your arrival. It stirs the spirits of the dead to greet you— all the rulers of the earth. It makes all the kings of the nations rise from their thrones.
chapters.zh: 你下到阴间， 阴间就因你震动来迎接你， 又因你惊动在世曾为首领的阴魂， 并使那曾为列国君王的， 都离位站起。

chapters.en:
They will all respond to you, saying, “You too have become weak, as we are;
you have become like us!”
chapters.zh: 他们都要发言对你说： 你也变为软弱像我们一样吗？ 你也成了我们的样子吗？

chapters.en: Your pomp has been brought down to Sheol, along with the music of your harps. Maggots are your bed and worms your blanket.
chapters.zh: 你的威势和你琴瑟的声音都下到阴间。 你下铺的是虫，上盖的是蛆。

chapters.en: How you have fallen from heaven, O day star, son of the dawn! You have been cut down to the ground, O destroyer of nations.
chapters.zh: 明亮之星，早晨之子啊， 你何竟从天坠落？ 你这攻败列国的何竟被砍倒在地上？

chapters.en: You said in your heart: “I will ascend to the heavens; I will raise my throne above the stars of God. I will sit on the mount of assembly, in the far reaches of the north.
chapters.zh: 你心里曾说： 我要升到天上； 我要高举我的宝座在上帝众星以上； 我要坐在聚会的山上，在北方的极处。

chapters.en: I will ascend above the tops of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High.”
chapters.zh: 我要升到高云之上； 我要与至上者同等。

chapters.en: But you will be brought down to Sheol, to the lowest depths of the Pit.
chapters.zh: 然而，你必坠落阴间， 到坑中极深之处。

chapters.en: Those who see you will stare; they will ponder your fate: “Is this the man who shook the earth and made the kingdoms tremble,
chapters.zh: 凡看见你的都要定睛看你， 留意看你，〔说〕： 使大地战抖， 使列国震动，

chapters.en: who turned the world into a desert and destroyed its cities, who refused to let the captives return to their homes?”
chapters.zh: 使世界如同荒野， 使城邑倾覆， 不释放被掳的人归家， 是这个人吗？

chapters.en: All the kings of the nations lie in state, each in his own tomb.
chapters.zh: 列国的君王 俱各在自己阴宅的荣耀中安睡。

chapters.en: But you are cast out of your grave like a rejected branch, covered by those slain with the sword, and dumped into a rocky pit like a carcass trampled underfoot.
chapters.zh: 惟独你被抛弃， 不得入你的坟墓， 好像可憎的枝子， 以被杀的人为衣， 就是被刀刺透， 坠落坑中石头那里的； 你又像被践踏的尸首一样。

chapters.en:
You will not join them in burial, since you have destroyed your land
and slaughtered your own people. The offspring of the wicked will never again be mentioned.
chapters.zh: 你不得与君王同葬； 因为你败坏你的国，杀戮你的民。 恶人后裔的名，必永不提说。

chapters.en: Prepare a place to slaughter his sons for the iniquities of their forefathers. They will never rise up to possess a land or cover the earth with their cities.
chapters.zh: 先人既有罪孽， 就要预备杀戮他的子孙， 免得他们兴起来，得了遍地， 在世上修满城邑。

chapters.en:
“I will rise up against them,” declares the LORD of Hosts. “I will cut off from Babylon her name and her remnant,
her offspring and her posterity,” declares the LORD.
chapters.zh: 万军之耶和华说： 我必兴起攻击他们， 将巴比伦的名号和所余剩的人， 连子带孙一并剪除。 这是耶和华说的。

chapters.en:
“I will make her a place for owls and for swamplands; I will sweep her away with the broom of destruction,”
declares the LORD of Hosts.
chapters.zh: 我必使巴比伦为箭猪所得， 又变为水池； 我要用灭亡的扫帚扫净它。 这是万军之耶和华说的。

chapters.en:
The LORD of Hosts has sworn:
“Surely, as I have planned, so will it be; as I have purposed, so will it stand.
chapters.zh: 万军之耶和华起誓说： 我怎样思想，必照样成就； 我怎样定意，必照样成立，

chapters.en: I will break Assyria in My land; I will trample him on My mountain. His yoke will be taken off My people, and his burden removed from their shoulders.”
chapters.zh: 就是在我地上打折亚述人， 在我山上将他践踏。 他加的轭必离开以色列人； 他加的重担必离开他们的肩头。

chapters.en: This is the plan devised for the whole earth, and this is the hand stretched out over all the nations.
chapters.zh: 这是向全地所定的旨意； 这是向万国所伸出的手。

chapters.en: The LORD of Hosts has purposed, and who can thwart Him? His hand is outstretched, so who can turn it back?
chapters.zh: 万军之耶和华既然定意，谁能废弃呢？ 他的手已经伸出，谁能转回呢？

chapters.en: In the year that King Ahaz died, this burden was received:
chapters.zh: 亚哈斯王崩的那年，就有以下的默示：

chapters.en: Do not rejoice, all you Philistines, that the rod that struck you is broken. For a viper will spring from the root of the snake, and a flying serpent from its egg.
chapters.zh: 非利士全地啊， 不要因击打你的杖折断就喜乐。 因为从蛇的根必生出毒蛇； 牠所生的是火焰的飞龙。

chapters.en: Then the firstborn of the poor will find pasture, and the needy will lie down in safety, but I will kill your root by famine, and your remnant will be slain.
chapters.zh: 贫寒人的长子必有所食； 穷乏人必安然躺卧。 我必以饥荒治死你的根； 你所余剩的人必被杀戮。

chapters.en: Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city! Melt away, all you Philistines! For a cloud of smoke comes from the north, and there are no stragglers in its ranks.
chapters.zh: 门哪，应当哀号！ 城啊，应当呼喊！ 非利士全地啊，你都消化了！ 因为有烟从北方出来， 他行伍中并无乱队的。

chapters.en: What answer will be given to the envoys of that nation? “The LORD has founded Zion, where His afflicted people will find refuge.”
chapters.zh: 可怎样回答外邦〔注：或指非利士〕的使者呢？ 必说：耶和华建立了锡安； 他百姓中的困苦人必投奔在其中。

chapters.en:
This is the burden against Moab:
Ar in Moab is ruined, destroyed in a night! Kir in Moab is devastated, destroyed in a night!
chapters.zh: 论摩押的默示： 一夜之间，摩押的亚珥变为荒废， 归于无有； 一夜之间，摩押的基珥变为荒废， 归于无有。

chapters.en:
Dibon goes up to its temple to weep at its high places. Moab wails over Nebo, as well as over Medeba.
Every head is shaved, every beard is cut off.
chapters.zh: 他们上巴益，又往底本， 到高处去哭泣。 摩押人因尼波和米底巴哀号， 各人头上光秃， 胡须剃净。

chapters.en:
In its streets they wear sackcloth; on the rooftops and in the public squares
they all wail, falling down weeping.
chapters.zh: 他们在街市上都腰束麻布， 在房顶上和宽阔处俱各哀号， 眼泪汪汪。

chapters.en: Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; their voices are heard as far as Jahaz. Therefore the soldiers of Moab cry out; their souls tremble within.
chapters.zh: 希实本和以利亚利悲哀的声音达到雅杂， 所以摩押带兵器的高声喊嚷， 人心战兢。

chapters.en:
My heart cries out over Moab; her fugitives flee as far as Zoar,
as far as Eglath-shelishiyah. With weeping they ascend the slope of Luhith; they lament their destruction on the road to Horonaim.
chapters.zh: 我心为摩押悲哀； 他的贵胄〔注：或译：逃民〕〔逃〕到琐珥， 到伊基拉‧施利施亚。 他们上鲁希坡，随走随哭； 在何罗念的路上，因毁灭举起哀声。

chapters.en: The waters of Nimrim are dried up, and the grass is withered; the vegetation is gone, and the greenery is no more.
chapters.zh: 因为宁林的水成为干涸， 青草枯干，嫩草灭没， 青绿之物，一无所有。

chapters.en: So they carry their wealth and belongings over the Brook of the Willows.
chapters.zh: 因此，摩押人所得的财物 和所积蓄的都要运过柳树河。

chapters.en:
For their outcry echoes to the border of Moab. Their wailing reaches Eglaim;
it is heard in Beer-elim.
chapters.zh: 哀声遍闻摩押的四境； 哀号的声音达到以基莲； 哀号的声音达到比珥‧以琳。

chapters.en: The waters of Dimon are full of blood, but I will bring more upon Dimon— a lion upon the fugitives of Moab and upon the remnant of the land.
chapters.zh: 底们的水充满了血； 我还要加增底们的〔灾难〕， 叫狮子来追上摩押逃脱的民 和那地上所余剩的人。

chapters.en: Send the tribute lambs to the ruler of the land, from Sela in the desert to the mount of Daughter Zion.
chapters.zh: 你们当将羊羔奉给那地掌权的， 从西拉往旷野，送到锡安城〔注：原文是女子〕的山。

chapters.en: Like fluttering birds pushed out of the nest, so are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon:
chapters.zh: 摩押的居民〔注：原文是女子〕在亚嫩渡口， 必像游飞的鸟，如拆窝的〔雏〕。

chapters.en: “Give us counsel; render a decision. Shelter us at noonday with shade as dark as night. Hide the refugees; do not betray the one who flees.
chapters.zh: 求你献谋略，行公平， 使你的影子在午间如黑夜， 隐藏被赶散的人，不可显露逃民。

chapters.en:
Let my fugitives stay with you; be a refuge for Moab from the destroyer.”
When the oppressor has gone, destruction has ceased, and the oppressors have vanished from the land,
chapters.zh: 求你容我这被赶散的人和你同居。 至于摩押，求你作他的隐密处， 脱离灭命者的面。 勒索人的归于无有， 毁灭的事止息了， 欺压人的从国中除灭了，

chapters.en: in loving devotion a throne will be established in the tent of David. A judge seeking justice and hastening righteousness will sit on it in faithfulness.
chapters.zh: 必有宝座因慈爱坚立； 必有一位诚诚实实坐在其上， 在大卫帐幕中施行审判， 寻求公平，速行公义。

chapters.en: We have heard of Moab’s pomposity, his exceeding pride and conceit, his overflowing arrogance. But his boasting is empty.
chapters.zh: 我们听说摩押人骄傲， 是极其骄傲； 听说他狂妄、骄傲、忿怒； 他夸大的话是虚空的。

chapters.en: Therefore let Moab wail; let them wail together for Moab. Moan for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, you who are utterly stricken.
chapters.zh: 因此，摩押人必为摩押哀号； 人人都要哀号。 你们摩押人要为吉珥‧哈列设的葡萄饼哀叹， 极其忧伤。

chapters.en: For the fields of Heshbon have withered, along with the grapevines of Sibmah. The rulers of the nations have trampled its choicest vines, which had reached as far as Jazer and spread toward the desert. Their shoots had spread out and passed over the sea.
chapters.zh: 因为希实本的田地 和西比玛的葡萄树都衰残了。 列国的君主折断其上美好的枝子； 这枝子长到雅谢延到旷野， 嫩枝向外探出，直探过盐海。

chapters.en: So I weep with Jazer for the vines of Sibmah; I drench Heshbon and Elealeh with my tears. Triumphant shouts have fallen silent over your summer fruit and your harvest.
chapters.zh: 因此，我要为西比玛的葡萄树哀哭， 与雅谢人哀哭一样。 希实本、以利亚利啊， 我要以眼泪浇灌你； 因为有〔交战〕吶喊的声音 临到你夏天的果子， 并你收割的庄稼。

chapters.en: Joy and gladness are removed from the orchard; no one sings or shouts in the vineyards. No one tramples the grapes in the winepresses; I have put an end to the cheering.
chapters.zh: 从肥美的田中夺去了欢喜快乐； 在葡萄园里必无歌唱，也无欢呼的声音。 踹酒的在酒醡中不得踹出酒来； 我使他欢呼的声音止息。

chapters.en: Therefore my heart laments for Moab like a harp, my inmost being for Kir-heres.
chapters.zh: 因此，我心腹为摩押哀鸣如琴； 我心肠为吉珥‧哈列设也是如此。

chapters.en: When Moab appears on the high place, when he wearies himself and enters his sanctuary to pray, it will do him no good.
chapters.zh: 摩押人朝见的时候，在高处疲乏，又到他圣所祈祷，也不蒙应允。

chapters.en: This is the message that the LORD spoke earlier concerning Moab.
chapters.zh: 这是耶和华从前论摩押的话。

chapters.en: And now the LORD says, “In three years, as a hired worker counts the years, Moab’s splendor will become an object of contempt, with all her many people. And those who are left will be few and feeble.”
chapters.zh: 但现在耶和华说：「三年之内，照雇工的年数，摩押的荣耀与他的群众必被藐视，余剩的人甚少无几。」

chapters.en:
This is the burden against Damascus:
“Behold, Damascus is no longer a city; it has become a heap of ruins.
chapters.zh: 论大马士革的默示： 看哪，大马士革已被废弃，不再为城， 必变作乱堆。

chapters.en:
The cities of Aroer are forsaken; they will be left to the flocks,
which will lie down with no one to fear.
chapters.zh: 亚罗珥的城邑已被撇弃， 必成为牧羊之处； 羊在那里躺卧，无人惊吓。

chapters.en: The fortress will disappear from Ephraim, and the sovereignty from Damascus. The remnant of Aram will be like the splendor of the Israelites,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
chapters.zh: 以法莲不再有保障； 大马士革不再有国权； 亚兰所剩下的 必像以色列人的荣耀消灭一样。 这是万军之耶和华说的。

chapters.en: “In that day the splendor of Jacob will fade, and the fat of his body will waste away,
chapters.zh: 到那日，雅各的荣耀必至枵薄； 他肥胖的身体必渐瘦弱。

chapters.en: as the reaper gathers the standing grain and harvests the ears with his arm, as one gleans heads of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.
chapters.zh: 就必像收割的人收敛禾稼， 用手割取穗子， 又像人在利乏音谷拾取遗落的穗子。

chapters.en: Yet gleanings will remain, like an olive tree that has been beaten— two or three berries atop the tree, four or five on its fruitful branches,” declares the LORD, the God of Israel.
chapters.zh: 其间所剩下的不多，好像人打橄榄树－ 在尽上的枝梢上只剩两三个果子； 在多果树的旁枝上只剩四五个果子。 这是耶和华－以色列的上帝说的。

chapters.en: In that day men will look to their Maker and turn their eyes to the Holy One of Israel.
chapters.zh: 当那日，人必仰望造他们的主，眼目重看以色列的圣者。

chapters.en: They will not look to the altars they have fashioned with their hands or to the Asherahs and incense altars they have made with their fingers.
chapters.zh: 他们必不仰望祭坛，就是自己手所筑的，也不重看自己指头所做的，无论是木偶是日像。

chapters.en: In that day their strong cities will be like forsaken thickets and summits, abandoned to the Israelites and to utter desolation.
chapters.zh: 在那日，他们的坚固城必像树林中和山顶上所撇弃的地方，就是从前在以色列人面前被人撇弃的。这样，地就荒凉了。

chapters.en: For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and failed to remember the Rock of your refuge. Therefore, though you cultivate delightful plots and set out cuttings from exotic vines—
chapters.zh: 因你忘记救你的上帝， 不记念你能力的磐石； 所以，你栽上佳美的树秧子， 插上异样的栽子。

chapters.en: though on the day you plant you make them grow, and on that morning you help your seed sprout— yet the harvest will vanish on the day of disease and incurable pain.
chapters.zh: 栽种的日子，你周围圈上篱笆， 又到早晨使你所种的开花； 但在愁苦极其伤痛的日子， 所收割的都飞去了。

chapters.en:
Alas, the tumult of many peoples; they rage like the roaring seas and clamoring nations;
they rumble like the crashing of mighty waters.
chapters.zh: 唉！多民鬨嚷，好像海浪匉訇； 列邦奔腾，好像猛水滔滔；

chapters.en: The nations rage like the rush of many waters. He rebukes them, and they flee far away, driven before the wind like chaff on the hills, like tumbleweeds before a gale.
chapters.zh: 列邦奔腾，好像多水滔滔； 但上帝斥责他们，他们就远远逃避， 又被追赶，如同山上的风前糠， 又如暴风前的旋风土。

chapters.en: In the evening, there is sudden terror! Before morning, they are no more! This is the portion of those who loot us and the lot of those who plunder us.
chapters.zh: 到晚上有惊吓，未到早晨他们就没有了。这是掳掠我们之人所得的分，是抢夺我们之人的报应。

chapters.en: Woe to the land of whirring wings, along the rivers of Cush,
chapters.zh: 唉！古实河外翅膀刷刷响声之地，

chapters.en:
which sends couriers by sea, in papyrus vessels on the waters.
Go, swift messengers, to a people tall and smooth-skinned,
to a people widely feared, to a powerful nation of strange speech, whose land is divided by rivers.
chapters.zh: 差遣使者在水面上， 坐蒲草船过海。 〔先知说〕：你们快行的使者， 要到高大光滑的民那里去。 自从开国以来，那民极其可畏， 是分〔地界〕践踏〔人〕的； 他们的地有江河分开。

chapters.en: All you people of the world and dwellers of the earth, when a banner is raised on the mountains, you will see it; when a ram’s horn sounds, you will hear it.
chapters.zh: 世上一切的居民和地上所住的人哪， 山上竖立大旗的时候你们要看； 吹角的时候你们要听。

chapters.en:
For this is what the LORD has told me:
“I will quietly look on from My dwelling place, like shimmering heat in the sunshine,
