chapters.zh: 我必使他们与我山的四围成为福源，我也必叫时雨落下，必有福〔如〕甘霖而降。

chapters.en: The trees of the field will give their fruit, and the land will yield its produce; My flock will be secure in their land. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I have broken the bars of their yoke and delivered them from the hands that enslaved them.
chapters.zh: 田野的树必结果，地也必有出产；他们必在故土安然居住。我折断他们所负的轭，救他们脱离那以他们为奴之人的手；那时，他们就知道我是耶和华。

chapters.en: They will no longer be prey for the nations, and the beasts of the earth will not consume them. They will dwell securely, and no one will frighten them.
chapters.zh: 他们必不再作外邦人的掠物，地上的野兽也不再吞吃他们；却要安然居住，无人惊吓。

chapters.en: And I will raise up for them a garden of renown, and they will no longer be victims of famine in the land or bear the scorn of the nations.
chapters.zh: 我必给他们兴起有名的植物；他们在境内不再为饥荒所灭，也不再受外邦人的羞辱，

chapters.en: Then they will know that I, the LORD their God, am with them, and that they, the house of Israel, are My people,’ declares the Lord GOD.
chapters.zh: 必知道我、耶和华－他们的上帝是与他们同在的，并知道他们－以色列家是我的民。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: ‘You are My flock, the sheep of My pasture, My people, and I am your God,’ declares the Lord GOD.”
chapters.zh: 你们作我的羊，我草场上的羊，乃是以色列人，我也是你们的上帝。这是主耶和华说的。」

chapters.en: Moreover, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
chapters.zh: 耶和华的话又临到我说：

chapters.en: “Son of man, set your face against Mount Seir and prophesy against it,
chapters.zh: 「人子啊，你要面向西珥山发预言，攻击它，

chapters.en:
and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says:
Behold, I am against you, O Mount Seir. I will stretch out My hand against you and make you a desolate waste.
chapters.zh: 对它说，主耶和华如此说：西珥山哪，我与你为敌，必向你伸手攻击你，使你荒凉，令人惊骇。

chapters.en:
I will turn your cities into ruins, and you will become a desolation.
Then you will know that I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 我必使你的城邑变为荒场，成为凄凉。你就知道我是耶和华。

chapters.en: Because you harbored an ancient hatred and delivered the Israelites over to the sword in the time of their disaster at the final stage of their punishment,
chapters.zh: 因为你永怀仇恨，在以色列人遭灾、罪孽到了尽头的时候，将他们交与刀剑，

chapters.en: therefore as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will give you over to bloodshed and it will pursue you. Since you did not hate bloodshed, it will pursue you.
chapters.zh: 所以主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，我必使你遭遇流血的报应，罪〔注：原文是血；本节同〕必追赶你；你既不恨恶杀人流血，所以这罪必追赶你。

chapters.en: I will make Mount Seir a desolate waste and will cut off from it those who come and go.
chapters.zh: 我必使西珥山荒凉，令人惊骇，来往经过的人我必剪除。

chapters.en: I will fill its mountains with the slain; those killed by the sword will fall on your hills, in your valleys, and in all your ravines.
chapters.zh: 我必使西珥山满有被杀的人。被刀杀的，必倒在你小山和山谷，并一切的溪水中。

chapters.en: I will make you a perpetual desolation, and your cities will not be inhabited. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 我必使你永远荒凉，使你的城邑无人居住，你的民就知道我是耶和华。

chapters.en: Because you have said, ‘These two nations and countries will be ours, and we will possess them,’ even though the LORD was there,
chapters.zh: 「因为你曾说：『这二国这二邦必归于我，我必得为业』（其实耶和华仍在那里），

chapters.en: therefore as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will treat you according to the anger and jealousy you showed in your hatred against them, and I will make Myself known among them when I judge you.
chapters.zh: 所以主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，我必照你的怒气和你从仇恨中向他们所发的嫉妒待你。我审判你的时候，必将自己显明在他们中间。

chapters.en: Then you will know that I, the LORD, have heard every contemptuous word you uttered against the mountains of Israel when you said, ‘They are desolate; they are given to us to devour!’
chapters.zh: 你也必知道我－耶和华听见了你的一切毁谤，就是你攻击以色列山的话，说：『这些山荒凉，是归我们吞灭的。』

chapters.en: You boasted against Me with your mouth and multiplied your words against Me. I heard it Myself!
chapters.zh: 你们也用口向我夸大，增添与我反对的话，我都听见了。

chapters.en: This is what the Lord GOD says: While the whole earth rejoices, I will make you desolate.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说：全地欢乐的时候，我必使你荒凉。

chapters.en: As you rejoiced when the inheritance of the house of Israel became desolate, so will I do to you. You will become a desolation, O Mount Seir, and so will all of Edom. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 你怎样因以色列家的地业荒凉而喜乐，我必照你所行的待你。西珥山哪，你和以东全地必都荒凉。你们就知道我是耶和华。」

chapters.en: “And you, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel and say: O mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 「人子啊，你要对以色列山发预言说：以色列山哪，要听耶和华的话。

chapters.en: This is what the Lord GOD says: Because the enemy has said of you, ‘Aha! The ancient heights have become our possession,’
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说：因仇敌说：『阿哈！这永久的山冈都归我们为业了！』

chapters.en: therefore prophesy and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: Because they have made you desolate and have trampled you on every side, so that you became a possession of the rest of the nations and were taken up in slander by the lips of their talkers,
chapters.zh: 所以要发预言说，主耶和华如此说：因为敌人使你荒凉，四围吞吃，好叫你归与其余的外邦人为业，并且多嘴多舌的人提起你来，百姓也说你有臭名。

chapters.en:
therefore, O mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD.
This is what the Lord GOD says to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys, to the desolate ruins and abandoned cities, which have become a spoil and a mockery to the rest of the nations around you.
chapters.zh: 故此，以色列山要听主耶和华的话。大山小冈、水沟山谷、荒废之地、被弃之城，为四围其余的外邦人所占据、所讥刺的，

chapters.en: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Surely in My burning zeal I have spoken against the rest of the nations, and against all Edom, who took My land as their own possession with wholehearted joy and utter contempt, so that its pastureland became plunder.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华对你们如此说：我真发愤恨如火，责备那其余的外邦人和以东的众人。他们快乐满怀，心存恨恶，将我的地归自己为业，又看为被弃的掠物。

chapters.en: Therefore, prophesy concerning the land of Israel and tell the mountains and hills, the ravines and valleys, that this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I have spoken in My burning zeal because you have endured the reproach of the nations.
chapters.zh: 所以，你要指着以色列地说预言，对大山小冈、水沟山谷说，主耶和华如此说：我发愤恨和忿怒说，因你们曾受外邦人的羞辱，

chapters.en: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I have sworn with an uplifted hand that surely the nations around you will endure reproach of their own.
chapters.zh: 所以我起誓说：你们四围的外邦人总要担当自己的羞辱。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: But you, O mountains of Israel, will produce branches and bear fruit for My people Israel, for they will soon come home.
chapters.zh: 「以色列山哪，你必发枝条，为我的民以色列结果子，因为他们快要来到。

chapters.en: For behold, I am on your side; I will turn toward you, and you will be tilled and sown.
chapters.zh: 看哪，我是帮助你的，也必向你转意，使你得以耕种。

chapters.en: I will multiply the people upon you—the house of Israel in its entirety. The cities will be inhabited and the ruins rebuilt.
chapters.zh: 我必使以色列全家的人数在你上面增多，城邑有人居住，荒场再被建造。

chapters.en: I will fill you with people and animals, and they will multiply and be fruitful. I will make you as inhabited as you once were, and I will make you prosper more than before. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 我必使人和牲畜在你上面加增；他们必生养众多。我要使你照旧有人居住，并要赐福与你比先前更多，你就知道我是耶和华。

chapters.en: Yes, I will cause My people Israel to walk upon you; they will possess you, and you will be their inheritance, and you will no longer deprive them of their children.
chapters.zh: 我必使人，就是我的民以色列，行在你上面。他们必得你为业；你也不再使他们丧子。

chapters.en: For this is what the Lord GOD says: Because people say to you, ‘You devour men and deprive your nation of its children,’
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说：因为人对你说：『你是吞吃人的，又使国民丧子』，

chapters.en: therefore you will no longer devour men or deprive your nation of its children, declares the Lord GOD.
chapters.zh: 所以主耶和华说：你必不再吞吃人，也不再使国民丧子。

chapters.en: I will no longer allow the taunts of the nations to be heard against you, and you will no longer endure the reproach of the peoples or cause your nation to stumble, declares the Lord GOD.”
chapters.zh: 我使你不再听见各国的羞辱，不再受万民的辱骂，也不再使国民绊跌。这是主耶和华说的。」

chapters.en: Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
chapters.zh: 耶和华的话又临到我说：

chapters.en: “Son of man, when the people of Israel lived in their land, they defiled it by their own ways and deeds. Their behavior before Me was like the uncleanness of a woman’s impurity.
chapters.zh: 「人子啊，以色列家住在本地的时候，在行动作为上玷污那地。他们的行为在我面前，好像正在经期的妇人那样污秽。

chapters.en: So I poured out My wrath upon them because of the blood they had shed on the land, and because they had defiled it with their idols.
chapters.zh: 所以我因他们在那地上流人的血，又因他们以偶像玷污那地，就把我的忿怒倾在他们身上。

chapters.en: I dispersed them among the nations, and they were scattered throughout the lands. I judged them according to their ways and deeds.
chapters.zh: 我将他们分散在列国，四散在列邦，按他们的行动作为惩罚他们。

chapters.en: And wherever they went among the nations, they profaned My holy name, because it was said of them, ‘These are the people of the LORD, yet they had to leave His land.’
chapters.zh: 他们到了所去的列国，就使我的圣名被亵渎；因为人谈论他们说，这是耶和华的民，是从耶和华的地出来的。

chapters.en: But I had concern for My holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations to which they had gone.
chapters.zh: 我却顾惜我的圣名，就是以色列家在所到的列国中所亵渎的。

chapters.en: Therefore tell the house of Israel that this is what the Lord GOD says: It is not for your sake that I will act, O house of Israel, but for My holy name, which you profaned among the nations to which you went.
chapters.zh: 「所以，你要对以色列家说，主耶和华如此说：以色列家啊，我行这事不是为你们，乃是为我的圣名，就是在你们到的列国中所亵渎的。

chapters.en: I will show the holiness of My great name, which has been profaned among the nations—the name you have profaned among them. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the Lord GOD, when I show My holiness in you before their eyes.
chapters.zh: 我要使我的大名显为圣；这名在列国中已被亵渎，就是你们在他们中间所亵渎的。我在他们眼前，在你们身上显为圣的时候，他们就知道我是耶和华。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: For I will take you from among the nations and gather you out of all the countries, and I will bring you back into your own land.
chapters.zh: 我必从各国收取你们，从列邦聚集你们，引导你们归回本地。

chapters.en: I will also sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean. I will cleanse you from all your impurities and all your idols.
chapters.zh: 我必用清水洒在你们身上，你们就洁净了。我要洁净你们，使你们脱离一切的污秽，弃掉一切的偶像。

chapters.en: I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; I will remove your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
chapters.zh: 我也要赐给你们一个新心，将新灵放在你们里面，又从你们的肉体中除掉石心，赐给你们肉心。

chapters.en: And I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes and to carefully observe My ordinances.
chapters.zh: 我必将我的灵放在你们里面，使你们顺从我的律例，谨守遵行我的典章。

chapters.en: Then you will live in the land that I gave your forefathers; you will be My people, and I will be your God.
chapters.zh: 你们必住在我所赐给你们列祖之地。你们要作我的子民，我要作你们的上帝。

chapters.en: I will save you from all your uncleanness. I will summon the grain and make it plentiful, and I will not bring famine upon you.
chapters.zh: 我必救你们脱离一切的污秽，也必命五谷丰登，不使你们遭遇饥荒。

chapters.en: I will also make the fruit of the trees and the crops of the field plentiful, so that you will no longer bear reproach among the nations on account of famine.
chapters.zh: 我必使树木多结果子，田地多出土产，好叫你们不再因饥荒受外邦人的讥诮。

chapters.en: Then you will remember your evil ways and wicked deeds, and you will loathe yourselves for your iniquities and abominations.
chapters.zh: 那时，你们必追想你们的恶行和你们不善的作为，就因你们的罪孽和可憎的事厌恶自己。

chapters.en: It is not for your sake that I will act, declares the Lord GOD—let it be known to you. Be ashamed and disgraced for your ways, O house of Israel!
chapters.zh: 主耶和华说：你们要知道，我这样行不是为你们。以色列家啊，当为自己的行为抱愧蒙羞。

chapters.en: This is what the Lord GOD says: On the day I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will cause the cities to be resettled and the ruins to be rebuilt.
chapters.zh: 「主耶和华如此说：我洁净你们，使你们脱离一切罪孽的日子，必使城邑有人居住，荒场再被建造。

chapters.en: The desolate land will be cultivated instead of lying desolate in the sight of all who pass through.
chapters.zh: 过路的人虽看为荒废之地，现今这荒废之地仍得耕种。

chapters.en: Then they will say, ‘This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden. The cities that were once ruined, desolate, and destroyed are now fortified and inhabited.’
chapters.zh: 他们必说：『这先前为荒废之地，现在成如伊甸园；这荒废凄凉、毁坏的城邑现在坚固有人居住。』

chapters.en: Then the nations around you that remain will know that I, the LORD, have rebuilt what was destroyed, and I have replanted what was desolate. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.
chapters.zh: 那时，在你们四围其余的外邦人必知道我－耶和华修造那毁坏之处，培植那荒废之地。我－耶和华说过，也必成就。

chapters.en: This is what the Lord GOD says: Once again I will hear the plea of the house of Israel and do for them this: I will multiply their people like a flock.
chapters.zh: 「主耶和华如此说：我要加增以色列家的人数，多如羊群。他们必为这事向我求问，我要给他们成就。

chapters.en: Like the numerous flocks for sacrifices at Jerusalem during her appointed feasts, so the ruined cities will be filled with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷在守节作祭物所献的羊群怎样多，照样，荒凉的城邑必被人群充满。他们就知道我是耶和华。」

chapters.en: The hand of the LORD was upon me, and He brought me out by His Spirit and set me down in the middle of the valley, and it was full of bones.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的灵〔注：原文是手〕降在我身上。耶和华藉他的灵带我出去，将我放在平原中；这平原遍满骸骨。

chapters.en: He led me all around among them, and I saw a great many bones on the floor of the valley, and indeed, they were very dry.
chapters.zh: 他使我从骸骨的四围经过，谁知在平原的骸骨甚多，而且极其枯干。

chapters.en:
Then He asked me, “Son of man, can these bones come to life?”
“O Lord GOD,” I replied, “only You know.”
chapters.zh: 他对我说：「人子啊，这些骸骨能复活吗？」我说：「主耶和华啊，你是知道的。」

chapters.en: And He said to me, “Prophesy concerning these bones and tell them, ‘Dry bones, hear the word of the LORD!
chapters.zh: 他又对我说：「你向这些骸骨发预言说：枯干的骸骨啊，要听耶和华的话。

chapters.en: This is what the Lord GOD says to these bones: I will cause breath to enter you, and you will come to life.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华对这些骸骨如此说：『我必使气息进入你们里面，你们就要活了。

chapters.en: I will attach tendons to you and make flesh grow upon you and cover you with skin. I will put breath within you so that you will come to life. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’”
chapters.zh: 我必给你们加上筋，使你们长肉，又将皮遮蔽你们，使气息进入你们里面，你们就要活了；你们便知道我是耶和华。』」

chapters.en: So I prophesied as I had been commanded. And as I prophesied, there was suddenly a noise, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to bone.
chapters.zh: 于是，我遵命说预言。正说预言的时候，不料，有响声，有地震；骨与骨互相联络。

chapters.en: As I looked on, tendons appeared on them, flesh grew, and skin covered them; but there was no breath in them.
chapters.zh: 我观看，见骸骨上有筋，也长了肉，又有皮遮蔽其上，只是还没有气息。

chapters.en: Then He said to me, “Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and tell the breath that this is what the Lord GOD says: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe into these slain, so that they may live!”
chapters.zh: 主对我说：「人子啊，你要发预言，向风发预言，说主耶和华如此说：气息啊，要从四方〔注：原文是风〕而来，吹在这些被杀的人身上，使他们活了。」

chapters.en: So I prophesied as He had commanded me, and the breath entered them, and they came to life and stood on their feet—a vast army.
chapters.zh: 于是我遵命说预言，气息就进入骸骨，骸骨便活了，并且站起来，成为极大的军队。

chapters.en: Then He said to me, “Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. Look, they are saying, ‘Our bones are dried up, and our hope has perished; we are cut off.’
chapters.zh: 主对我说：「人子啊，这些骸骨就是以色列全家。他们说：『我们的骨头枯干了，我们的指望失去了，我们灭绝净尽了。』

chapters.en: Therefore prophesy and tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘O My people, I will open your graves and bring you up from them, and I will bring you back to the land of Israel.
chapters.zh: 所以你要发预言对他们说，主耶和华如此说：『我的民哪，我必开你们的坟墓，使你们从坟墓中出来，领你们进入以色列地。

chapters.en: Then you, My people, will know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves and bring you up from them.
chapters.zh: 我的民哪，我开你们的坟墓，使你们从坟墓中出来，你们就知道我是耶和华。

chapters.en: I will put My Spirit in you and you will live, and I will settle you in your own land. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it, declares the LORD.’”
chapters.zh: 我必将我的灵放在你们里面，你们就要活了。我将你们安置在本地，你们就知道我－耶和华如此说，也如此成就了。这是耶和华说的。』」

chapters.en: Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
chapters.zh: 耶和华的话又临到我说：

chapters.en: “And you, son of man, take a single stick and write on it: ‘Belonging to Judah and to the Israelites associated with him.’ Then take another stick and write on it: ‘Belonging to Joseph—the stick of Ephraim—and to all the house of Israel associated with him.’
chapters.zh: 「人子啊，你要取一根木杖，在其上写『为犹大和他的同伴以色列人』；又取一根木杖，在其上写『为约瑟，就是为以法莲，又为他的同伴以色列全家』。

chapters.en: Then join them together into one stick, so that they become one in your hand.
chapters.zh: 你要使这两根木杖接连为一，在你手中成为一根。

chapters.en: When your people ask you, ‘Won’t you explain to us what you mean by these?’
chapters.zh: 你本国的子民问你说：『这是什么意思？你不指示我们吗？』

chapters.en: you are to tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel associated with him, and I will put them together with the stick of Judah. I will make them into a single stick, and they will become one in My hand.’
chapters.zh: 你就对他们说：『主耶和华如此说：我要将约瑟和他同伴以色列支派的杖，就是那在以法莲手中的，与犹大的杖一同接连为一，在我手中成为一根。』

chapters.en: When the sticks on which you write are in your hand and in full view of the people,
chapters.zh: 你所写的那两根杖要在他们眼前拿在手中，

chapters.en: you are to tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will take the Israelites out of the nations to which they have gone, and I will gather them from all around and bring them into their own land.
chapters.zh: 要对他们说，主耶和华如此说：我要将以色列人从他们所到的各国收取，又从四围聚集他们，引导他们归回本地。

chapters.en: I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king will rule over all of them. Then they will no longer be two nations and will never again be divided into two kingdoms.
chapters.zh: 我要使他们在那地，在以色列山上成为一国，有一王作他们众民的王。他们不再为二国，决不再分为二国；

chapters.en: They will no longer defile themselves with their idols or detestable images, or with any of their transgressions. I will save them from all their apostasies by which they sinned, and I will cleanse them. Then they will be My people, and I will be their God.
chapters.zh: 也不再因偶像和可憎的物，并一切的罪过玷污自己。我却要救他们出离一切的住处，就是他们犯罪的地方；我要洁净他们，如此，他们要作我的子民，我要作他们的上帝。

chapters.en: My servant David will be king over them, and there will be one shepherd for all of them. They will follow My ordinances and keep and observe My statutes.
chapters.zh: 「我的仆人大卫必作他们的王；众民必归一个牧人。他们必顺从我的典章，谨守遵行我的律例。

chapters.en: They will live in the land that I gave to My servant Jacob, where your fathers lived. They will live there forever with their children and grandchildren, and My servant David will be their prince forever.
chapters.zh: 他们必住在我赐给我仆人雅各的地上，就是你们列祖所住之地。他们和他们的子孙，并子孙的子孙，都永远住在那里。我的仆人大卫必作他们的王，直到永远。

chapters.en: And I will make a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting covenant. I will establish them and multiply them, and I will set My sanctuary among them forever.
chapters.zh: 并且我要与他们立平安的约，作为永约。我也要将他们安置在〔本地〕，使他们的人数增多，又在他们中间设立我的圣所，直到永远。

chapters.en: My dwelling place will be with them; I will be their God, and they will be My people.
chapters.zh: 我的居所必在他们中间；我要作他们的上帝，他们要作我的子民。

chapters.en: Then the nations will know that I the LORD sanctify Israel, when My sanctuary is among them forever.’”
chapters.zh: 我的圣所在以色列人中间直到永远，外邦人就必知道我是叫以色列成为圣的耶和华。」

chapters.en: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
chapters.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：

chapters.en: “Son of man, set your face against Gog of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. Prophesy against him
chapters.zh: 「人子啊，你要面向玛各地的歌革，就是罗施、米设、土巴的王发预言攻击他，

chapters.en: and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
chapters.zh: 说主耶和华如此说：罗施、米设、土巴的王歌革啊，我与你为敌。

chapters.en: I will turn you around, put hooks in your jaws, and bring you out with all your army—your horses, your horsemen in full armor, and a great company armed with shields and bucklers, all brandishing their swords.
chapters.zh: 我必用钩子钩住你的腮颊，调转你，将你和你的军兵、马匹、马兵带出来，都披挂整齐，成了大队，有大小盾牌，各拿刀剑。

chapters.en: Persia, Cush, and Put will accompany them, all with shields and helmets,
chapters.zh: 波斯人、古实人，和弗人〔注：又作利比亚人〕，各拿盾牌，头上戴盔；

chapters.en: as well as Gomer with all its troops, and Beth-togarmah from the far north with all its troops—the many nations with you.
chapters.zh: 歌篾人和他的军队，北方极处的陀迦玛族和他的军队，这许多国的民都同着你。

chapters.en: Get ready; prepare yourself, you and all your company gathered around you; you will be their guard.
chapters.zh: 「那聚集到你这里的各队都当准备；你自己也要准备，作他们的大帅。

chapters.en: After a long time you will be summoned. In the latter years you will enter a land that has recovered from war, whose people were gathered from many nations to the mountains of Israel, which had long been desolate. They had been brought out from the nations, and all now dwell securely.
chapters.zh: 过了多日，你必被差派。到末后之年，你必来到脱离刀剑从列国收回之地，到以色列常久荒凉的山上；但那从列国中招聚出来的必在其上安然居住。

chapters.en: You and all your troops, and many peoples with you will go up, advancing like a thunderstorm; you will be like a cloud covering the land.
chapters.zh: 你和你的军队，并同着你许多国的民，必如暴风上来，如密云遮盖地面。」

chapters.en: This is what the Lord GOD says: On that day, thoughts will arise in your mind, and you will devise an evil plan.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「到那时，你心必起意念，图谋恶计，

chapters.en: You will say, ‘I will go up against a land of unwalled villages; I will come against a quiet people who dwell securely, all of them living without walls or bars or gates—
chapters.zh: 说：『我要上那无城墙的乡村，我要到那安静的民那里，他们都没有城墙，无门、无闩，安然居住。

chapters.en: in order to seize the spoil and carry off the plunder, to turn a hand against the desolate places now inhabited and against a people gathered from the nations, who have acquired livestock and possessions and who live at the center of the land.’
chapters.zh: 我去要抢财为掳物，夺货为掠物，反手攻击那从前荒凉、现在有人居住之地，又攻击那住世界中间、从列国招聚、得了牲畜财货的民。』

chapters.en: Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish with all its villages will ask, ‘Have you come to capture the plunder? Have you assembled your hordes to carry away loot, to make off with silver and gold, to take cattle and goods, to seize great spoil?’
chapters.zh: 示巴人、底但人、他施的客商，和其间的少壮狮子都必问你说：『你来要抢财为掳物吗？你聚集军队要夺货为掠物吗？要夺取金银，掳去牲畜、财货吗？要抢夺许多财宝为掳物吗？』

chapters.en: Therefore prophesy, son of man, and tell Gog that this is what the Lord GOD says: On that day when My people Israel are dwelling securely, will you not take notice of this?
chapters.zh: 「人子啊，你要因此发预言，对歌革说，主耶和华如此说：到我民以色列安然居住之日，你岂不知道吗？

chapters.en: And you will come from your place out of the far north—you and many peoples with you, all riding horses—a mighty horde, a huge army.
chapters.zh: 你必从本地，从北方的极处率领许多国的民来，都骑着马，乃一大队极多的军兵。

chapters.en: You will advance against My people Israel like a cloud covering the land. It will happen in the latter days, O Gog, that I will bring you against My land, so that the nations may know Me when I show Myself holy in you before their eyes.
chapters.zh: 歌革啊，你必上来攻击我的民以色列，如密云遮盖地面。末后的日子，我必带你来攻击我的地，到我在外邦人眼前，在你身上显为圣的时候，好叫他们认识我。

chapters.en: This is what the Lord GOD says: Are you the one of whom I have spoken in former days through My servants, the prophets of Israel, who in those times prophesied for years that I would bring you against them?
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说：我在古时藉我的仆人以色列的先知所说的，就是你吗？当日他们多年预言我必带你来攻击以色列人。」

chapters.en: Now on that day when Gog comes against the land of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, My wrath will flare up.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华说：「歌革上来攻击以色列地的时候，我的怒气要从鼻孔里发出。

chapters.en: In My zeal and fiery rage I proclaim that on that day there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel.
chapters.zh: 我发愤恨和烈怒如火说：那日在以色列地必有大震动，

chapters.en: The fish of the sea, the birds of the air, the beasts of the field, every creature that crawls upon the ground, and all mankind on the face of the earth will tremble at My presence. The mountains will be thrown down, the cliffs will collapse, and every wall will fall to the ground.
chapters.zh: 甚至海中的鱼、天空的鸟、田野的兽，并地上的一切昆虫，和其上的众人，因见我的面就都震动；山岭必崩裂，陡巖必塌陷，墙垣都必坍倒。」

chapters.en: And I will summon a sword against Gog on all My mountains, declares the Lord GOD, and every man’s sword will be against his brother.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华说：「我必命我的诸山发刀剑来攻击歌革；人都要用刀剑杀害弟兄。

chapters.en: I will execute judgment upon him with plague and bloodshed. I will pour out torrents of rain, hailstones, fire, and sulfur on him and on his troops and on the many nations with him.
chapters.zh: 我必用瘟疫和流血的事刑罚他。我也必将暴雨、大雹与火，并硫磺降与他和他的军队，并他所率领的众民。

chapters.en: I will magnify and sanctify Myself, and I will reveal Myself in the sight of many nations. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 我必显为大，显为圣，在多国人的眼前显现；他们就知道我是耶和华。」

chapters.en: “As for you, O son of man, prophesy against Gog and declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
chapters.zh: 「人子啊，你要向歌革发预言攻击他，说主耶和华如此说：罗施、米设、土巴的王歌革啊，我与你为敌。

chapters.en: I will turn you around, drive you along, bring you up from the far north, and send you against the mountains of Israel.
chapters.zh: 我必调转你，领你前往，使你从北方的极处上来，带你到以色列的山上。

chapters.en: Then I will strike the bow from your left hand and dash down the arrows from your right hand.
chapters.zh: 我必从你左手打落你的弓，从你右手打掉你的箭。

chapters.en: On the mountains of Israel you will fall—you and all your troops and the nations with you. I will give you as food to every kind of ravenous bird and wild beast.
chapters.zh: 你和你的军队，并同着你的列国人，都必倒在以色列的山上。我必将你给各类的鸷鸟和田野的走兽作食物。

chapters.en: You will fall in the open field, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.
chapters.zh: 你必倒在田野，因为我曾说过。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: I will send fire on Magog and on those who dwell securely in the coastlands, and they will know that I am the LORD.
chapters.zh: 我要降火在玛各和海岛安然居住的人身上，他们就知道我是耶和华。

chapters.en: So I will make My holy name known among My people Israel and will no longer allow it to be profaned. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel.
chapters.zh: 「我要在我民以色列中显出我的圣名，也不容我的圣名再被亵渎，列国人就知道我是耶和华－以色列中的圣者。

chapters.en: Yes, it is coming, and it will surely happen, declares the Lord GOD. This is the day of which I have spoken.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华说：这日事情临近，也必成就，乃是我所说的日子。

chapters.en: Then those who dwell in the cities of Israel will go out, kindle fires, and burn up the weapons—the bucklers and shields, the bows and arrows, the clubs and spears. For seven years they will use them for fuel.
chapters.zh: 「住以色列城邑的人必出去捡器械，就是大小盾牌、弓箭、梃杖、枪矛，都当柴烧火，直烧七年，

chapters.en: They will not gather wood from the countryside or cut it from the forests, for they will use the weapons for fuel. They will loot those who looted them and plunder those who plundered them, declares the Lord GOD.
chapters.zh: 甚至他们不必从田野捡柴，也不必从树林伐木；因为他们要用器械烧火，并且抢夺那抢夺他们的人，掳掠那掳掠他们的人。这是主耶和华说的。」

chapters.en: And on that day I will give Gog a burial place in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers, east of the Sea. It will block those who travel through, because Gog and all his hordes will be buried there. So it will be called the Valley of Hamon-gog.
chapters.zh: 「当那日，我必将以色列〔地〕的谷，就是海东人所经过的谷，赐给歌革为坟地，使经过的人到此停步。在那里人必葬埋歌革和他的群众，就称那地为哈们‧歌革谷。

chapters.en: For seven months the house of Israel will be burying them in order to cleanse the land.
chapters.zh: 以色列家的人必用七个月葬埋他们，为要洁净全地。

chapters.en: All the people of the land will bury them, and it will bring them renown on the day I display My glory, declares the Lord GOD.
chapters.zh: 全地的居民都必葬埋他们。当我得荣耀的日子，这事必叫他们得名声。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: And men will be employed to continually pass through the land to cleanse it by burying the invaders who remain on the ground. At the end of the seven months they will begin their search.
chapters.zh: 他们必分派人时常巡查遍地，与过路的人一同葬埋那剩在地面上的尸首，好洁净全地。过了七个月，他们还要巡查。

chapters.en: As they pass through the land, anyone who sees a human bone will set up a pillar next to it, until the gravediggers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog.
chapters.zh: 巡查遍地的人要经过全地，见有人的骸骨，就在旁边立一标记，等葬埋的人来将骸骨葬在哈们‧歌革谷。

chapters.en: (Even the city will be named Hamonah. ) And so they will cleanse the land.
chapters.zh: 他们必这样洁净那地，并有一城名叫哈摩那。

chapters.en: And as for you, son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: Call out to every kind of bird and to every beast of the field: ‘Assemble and come together from all around to the sacrificial feast that I am preparing for you, a great feast on the mountains of Israel. There you will eat flesh and drink blood.
chapters.zh: 「人子啊，主耶和华如此说：你要对各类的飞鸟和田野的走兽说：你们聚集来吧，要从四方聚到我为你们献祭之地，就是在以色列山上献大祭之地，好叫你们吃肉、喝血。

chapters.en: You will eat the flesh of the mighty and drink the blood of the princes of the earth as though they were rams, lambs, goats, and bulls—all the fattened animals of Bashan.
chapters.zh: 你们必吃勇士的肉，喝地上首领的血，就如吃公绵羊、羊羔、公山羊、公牛，都是巴珊的肥畜。

chapters.en: At the sacrifice I am preparing, you will eat fat until you are gorged and drink blood until you are drunk.
chapters.zh: 你们吃我为你们所献的祭，必吃饱了脂油，喝醉了血。

chapters.en: And at My table you will eat your fill of horses and riders, of mighty men and warriors of every kind,’ declares the Lord GOD.
chapters.zh: 你们必在我席上饱吃马匹和〔坐〕车〔的人〕，并勇士和一切的战士。这是主耶和华说的。」

chapters.en: I will display My glory among the nations, and all the nations will see the judgment that I execute and the hand that I lay upon them.
chapters.zh: 「我必显我的荣耀在列国中；万民就必看见我所行的审判与我在他们身上所加的手。

chapters.en: From that day forward the house of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God.
chapters.zh: 这样，从那日以后，以色列家必知道我是耶和华－他们的上帝。

chapters.en: And the nations will know that the house of Israel went into exile for their iniquity, because they were unfaithful to Me. So I hid My face from them and delivered them into the hands of their enemies, so that they all fell by the sword.
chapters.zh: 列国人也必知道以色列家被掳掠是因他们的罪孽。他们得罪我，我就掩面不顾，将他们交在敌人手中，他们便都倒在刀下。

chapters.en: I dealt with them according to their uncleanness and transgressions, and I hid My face from them.
chapters.zh: 我是照他们的污秽和罪过待他们，并且我掩面不顾他们。」

chapters.en: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Now I will restore Jacob from captivity and will have compassion on the whole house of Israel, and I will be jealous for My holy name.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「我要使雅各被掳的人归回，要怜悯以色列全家，又为我的圣名发热心。

chapters.en: They will forget their disgrace and all the treachery they committed against Me, when they dwell securely in their land, with no one to frighten them.
When I bring them back from the peoples and gather them out of the lands of their enemies, I will show My holiness in them in the sight of many nations.
chapters.zh: 他们在本地安然居住，无人惊吓，是我将他们从万民中领回，从仇敌之地召来。我在许多国的民眼前，在他们身上显为圣的时候，他们要担当自己的羞辱和干犯我的一切罪。

chapters.en: Then they will know that I am the LORD their God, when I regather them to their own land, not leaving any of them behind after their exile among the nations.
chapters.zh: 因我使他们被掳到外邦人中，后又聚集他们归回本地，他们就知道我是耶和华－他们的上帝；我必不再留他们一人在外邦。

chapters.en: And I will no longer hide My face from them, for I will pour out My Spirit on the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.”
chapters.zh: 我也不再掩面不顾他们，因我已将我的灵浇灌以色列家。这是主耶和华说的。」

chapters.en: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month—in the fourteenth year after Jerusalem had been struck down—on that very day the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He took me there.
chapters.zh: 我们被掳掠第二十五年，耶路撒冷城攻破后十四年，正在年初，月之初十日，耶和华的灵〔注：原文是手〕降在我身上，他把我带到以色列地。

chapters.en: In visions of God He took me to the land of Israel and set me on a very high mountain, on whose southern slope was a structure that resembled a city.
chapters.zh: 在上帝的异象中带我到以色列地，安置在至高的山上；在山上的南边有仿佛一座城建立。

chapters.en: So He took me there, and I saw a man whose appearance was like bronze. He was standing in the gateway with a linen cord and a measuring rod in his hand.
chapters.zh: 他带我到那里，见有一人，颜色〔注：原文是形状〕如铜，手拿麻绳和量度的竿，站在门口。

chapters.en: “Son of man,” he said to me, “look with your eyes, hear with your ears, and pay attention to everything I am going to show you, for that is why you have been brought here. Report to the house of Israel everything you see.”
chapters.zh: 那人对我说：「人子啊，凡我所指示你的，你都要用眼看，用耳听，并要放在心上。我带你到这里来，特为要指示你；凡你所见的，你都要告诉以色列家。」

chapters.en: And I saw a wall surrounding the temple area. Now the length of the measuring rod in the man’s hand was six long cubits (each measuring a cubit and a handbreadth), and he measured the wall to be one rod thick and one rod high.
chapters.zh: 我见殿四围有墙。那人手拿量度的竿，长六肘，每肘是一肘零一掌。他用竿量墙，厚一竿，高一竿。

chapters.en: Then he came to the gate facing east and climbed its steps. He measured the threshold of the gate to be one rod deep.
chapters.zh: 他到了朝东的门，就上门的台阶，量门的这槛，宽一竿；又量门的那槛，宽一竿。

chapters.en: Each gate chamber was one rod long and one rod wide, and there were five cubits between the gate chambers. The inner threshold of the gate by the portico facing inward was one rod deep.
chapters.zh: 又有卫房，每房长一竿，宽一竿，相隔五肘。门槛，就是挨着向殿的廊门槛，宽一竿。

chapters.en: Then he measured the portico of the gateway inside;
chapters.zh: 他又量向殿门的廊子，宽一竿。

chapters.en: it was eight cubits deep, and its jambs were two cubits thick. And the portico of the gateway faced the temple.
chapters.zh: 又量门廊，宽八肘，墙柱厚二肘；那门的廊子向着殿。

chapters.en: There were three gate chambers on each side of the east gate, each with the same measurements, and the gateposts on either side also had the same measurements.
chapters.zh: 东门洞有卫房：这旁三间，那旁三间，都是一样的尺寸；这边的柱子和那边的柱子，也是一样的尺寸。

chapters.en: And he measured the width of the gateway entrance to be ten cubits, and its length was thirteen cubits.
chapters.zh: 他量门口，宽十肘，长十三肘。

chapters.en: In front of each gate chamber was a wall one cubit high, and the gate chambers were six cubits square.
chapters.zh: 卫房前〔展出〕的境界：〔这边〕一肘，那边一肘；卫房这边六肘，那边六肘。

chapters.en: Then he measured the gateway from the roof of one gate chamber to the roof of the opposite one; the distance was twenty-five cubits from doorway to doorway.
chapters.zh: 又量门洞，从这卫房顶〔的后檐〕到那卫房顶〔的后檐〕，宽二十五肘；〔卫房〕门与门相对。

chapters.en: Next he measured the gateposts to be sixty cubits high. The gateway extended around to the gatepost of the courtyard.
chapters.zh: 又量〔注：原文是造〕廊子六十肘〔注：七十士译本是二十肘〕，墙柱外是院子，有廊为界，在门洞两边。

chapters.en: And the distance from the entrance of the gateway to the far end of its inner portico was fifty cubits.
chapters.zh: 从大门口到内廊前，共五十肘。

chapters.en: The gate chambers and their side pillars had beveled windows all around the inside of the gateway. The porticos also had windows all around on the inside. Each side pillar was decorated with palm trees.
chapters.zh: 卫房和门洞两旁柱间并廊子，都有严紧的窗櫺；里边都有窗櫺，柱上有雕刻的棕树。

chapters.en: Then he brought me into the outer court, and there were chambers and a pavement laid out all around the court. Thirty chambers faced the pavement,
chapters.zh: 他带我到外院，见院的四围有铺石地；铺石地上有屋子三十间。

chapters.en: which flanked the gateways and corresponded to the length of the gates; this was the lower pavement.
chapters.zh: 铺石地，就是矮铺石地在各门洞两旁，以门洞的长短为度。

chapters.en: Then he measured the distance from the front of the lower gateway to the outside of the inner court; it was a hundred cubits on the east side as well as on the north.
chapters.zh: 他从下门量到内院外，共宽一百肘，东面北面都是如此。

chapters.en: He also measured the length and width of the gateway of the outer court facing north.
chapters.zh: 他量外院朝北的门，长宽若干。

chapters.en: Its three gate chambers on each side, its side pillars, and its portico all had the same measurements as the first gate: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 门洞的卫房，这旁三间，那旁三间。门洞的柱子和廊子，与第一门的尺寸一样。门洞长五十肘，宽二十五肘。

chapters.en: Its windows, portico, and palm trees had the same measurements as those of the gate facing east. Seven steps led up to it, with its portico opposite them.
chapters.zh: 其窗櫺和廊子，并雕刻的棕树，与朝东的门尺寸一样。登七层台阶上到这门，前面有廊子。

chapters.en: There was a gate to the inner court facing the north gate, just as there was on the east. He measured the distance from gateway to gateway to be a hundred cubits.
chapters.zh: 内院有门与这门相对，北面东面都是如此。他从这门量到那门，共一百肘。

chapters.en: Then he led me to the south side, and I saw a gateway facing south. He measured its side pillars and portico, and they had the same measurements as the others.
chapters.zh: 他带我往南去，见朝南有门，又照先前的尺寸量门洞的柱子和廊子。

chapters.en: Both the gateway and its portico had windows all around, like the other windows. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 门洞两旁与廊子的周围都有窗櫺，和先量的窗櫺一样。门洞长五十肘，宽二十五肘。

chapters.en: Seven steps led up to it, and its portico was opposite them; it had palm trees on its side pillars, one on each side.
chapters.zh: 登七层台阶上到这门，前面有廊子；柱上有雕刻的棕树，这边一棵，那边一棵。

chapters.en: The inner court also had a gate facing south, and he measured the distance from gateway to gateway toward the south to be a hundred cubits.
chapters.zh: 内院朝南有门。从这门量到朝南的那门，共一百肘。

chapters.en: Next he brought me into the inner court through the south gate, and he measured the south gate; it had the same measurements as the others.
chapters.zh: 他带我从南门到内院，就照先前的尺寸量南门。

chapters.en: Its gate chambers, side pillars, and portico had the same measurements as the others. Both the gateway and its portico had windows all around; it was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 卫房和柱子，并廊子都照先前的尺寸。门洞两旁与廊子的周围都有窗櫺。门洞长五十肘，宽二十五肘。

chapters.en: (The porticoes around the inner court were twenty-five cubits long and five cubits deep. )
chapters.zh: 周围有廊子，长二十五肘，宽五肘。

chapters.en: Its portico faced the outer court, and its side pillars were decorated with palm trees. Eight steps led up to it.
chapters.zh: 廊子朝着外院，柱上有雕刻的棕树。登八层台阶上到这门。

chapters.en: And he brought me to the inner court on the east side, and he measured the gateway; it had the same measurements as the others.
chapters.zh: 他带我到内院的东面，就照先前的尺寸量东门。

chapters.en: Its gate chambers, side pillars, and portico had the same measurements as the others. Both the gateway and its portico had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 卫房和柱子，并廊子都照先前的尺寸。门洞两旁与廊子的周围都有窗櫺。门洞长五十肘，宽二十五肘。

chapters.en: Its portico faced the outer court, and its side pillars were decorated with palm trees on each side. Eight steps led up to it.
chapters.zh: 廊子朝着外院。门洞两旁的柱子都有雕刻的棕树。登八层台阶上到这门。

chapters.en: Then he brought me to the north gate and measured it. It had the same measurements as the others,
chapters.zh: 他带我到北门，就照先前的尺寸量那门，

chapters.en: as did its gate chambers, side pillars, and portico. It also had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 就是量卫房和柱子，并廊子。门洞周围都有窗櫺；门洞长五十肘，宽二十五肘。

chapters.en: Its portico faced the outer court, and its side pillars were decorated with palm trees on each side. Eight steps led up to it.
chapters.zh: 廊柱朝着外院。门洞两旁的柱子都有雕刻的棕树。登八层台阶上到这门。

chapters.en: There was a chamber with a doorway by the portico in each of the inner gateways. There the burnt offering was to be washed.
chapters.zh: 门洞的柱旁有屋子和门；祭司〔注：原文是他们〕在那里洗燔祭牲。

chapters.en: Inside the portico of the gateway were two tables on each side, on which the burnt offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings were to be slaughtered.
chapters.zh: 在门廊内，这边有两张桌子，那边有两张桌子，在其上可以宰杀燔祭牲、赎罪祭牲，和赎愆祭牲。

chapters.en: Outside, as one goes up to the entrance of the north gateway, there were two tables on one side and two more tables on the other side of the gate’s portico.
chapters.zh: 上到朝北的门口，这边有两张桌子，门廊那边也有两张桌子。

chapters.en: So there were four tables inside the gateway and four outside—eight tables in all—on which the sacrifices were to be slaughtered.
chapters.zh: 门这边有四张桌子，那边有四张桌子，共八张；在其上祭司宰杀〔牺牲〕。

chapters.en: There were also four tables of dressed stone for the burnt offering, each a cubit and a half long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit high. On these were placed the utensils used to slaughter the burnt offerings and the other sacrifices.
chapters.zh: 为燔祭牲有四张桌子，是凿过的石头做成的，长一肘半，宽一肘半，高一肘。祭司将宰杀燔祭牲和〔平安〕祭牲所用的器皿放在其上。

chapters.en: The double-pronged hooks, each a handbreadth long, were fastened all around the inside of the room, and the flesh of the offering was to be placed on the tables.
chapters.zh: 有钩子，宽一掌，钉在廊内的四围。桌子上有牺牲的肉。

chapters.en: Outside the inner gate, within the inner court, were two chambers, one beside the north gate and facing south, and another beside the south gate and facing north.
chapters.zh: 在北门旁，内院里有屋子，为歌唱的人而设。这屋子朝南；在南〔注：南：原文是东〕门旁，又有一间朝北。

chapters.en: Then the man said to me: “The chamber that faces south is for the priests who keep charge of the temple,
chapters.zh: 他对我说：「这朝南的屋子是为看守殿宇的祭司；

chapters.en: and the chamber that faces north is for the priests who keep charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, the only Levites who may approach the LORD to minister before Him.”
chapters.zh: 那朝北的屋子是为看守祭坛的祭司。这些祭司是利未人中撒督的子孙，近前来事奉耶和华的。」

chapters.en: Next he measured the court. It was square, a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide. And the altar was in front of the temple.
chapters.zh: 他又量内院，长一百肘，宽一百肘，是见方的。祭坛在殿前。

chapters.en: Then he brought me to the portico of the temple and measured the side pillars of the portico to be five cubits on each side. The width of the gateway was fourteen cubits and its sidewalls were three cubits on either side.
chapters.zh: 于是他带我到殿前的廊子，量廊子的墙柱。这面厚五肘，那面厚五肘。门两旁，这边三肘，那边三肘。

chapters.en: The portico was twenty cubits wide and twelve cubits deep, and ten steps led up to it. There were columns by the side pillars, one on each side.
chapters.zh: 廊子长二十肘，宽十一肘。上廊子有台阶。靠近墙柱又有柱子，这边一根，那边一根。

chapters.en: Then the man brought me into the outer sanctuary and measured the side pillars to be six cubits wide on each side.
chapters.zh: 他带我到殿那里量墙柱：这面厚六肘，那面厚六肘，宽窄与会幕相同。

chapters.en: The width of the entrance was ten cubits, and the sides of the entrance were five cubits on each side. He also measured the length of the outer sanctuary to be forty cubits, and the width to be twenty cubits.
chapters.zh: 门口宽十肘。门两旁，这边五肘，那边五肘。他量殿长四十肘，宽二十肘。

chapters.en: And he went into the inner sanctuary and measured the side pillars at the entrance to be two cubits wide. The entrance was six cubits wide, and the walls on each side were seven cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 他到内殿量墙柱，各厚二肘。门口宽六肘，门两旁各宽七肘。

chapters.en: Then he measured the room adjacent to the inner sanctuary to be twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. And he said to me, “This is the Most Holy Place. ”
chapters.zh: 他量内殿，长二十肘，宽二十肘。他对我说：「这是至圣所。」

chapters.en: Next he measured the wall of the temple to be six cubits thick, and the width of each side room around the temple was four cubits.
chapters.zh: 他又量殿墙，厚六肘；围着殿有旁屋，各宽四肘。

chapters.en: The side rooms were arranged one above another in three levels of thirty rooms each. There were ledges all around the wall of the temple to serve as supports for the side rooms, so that the supports would not be fastened into the wall of the temple itself.
chapters.zh: 旁屋有三层，层叠而上，每层排列三十间。旁屋〔的梁木〕搁在殿墙坎上，免得插入殿墙。

chapters.en: The side rooms surrounding the temple widened at each successive level, because the structure surrounding the temple ascended by stages corresponding to the narrowing of the temple wall as it rose upward. And so a stairway went up from the lowest story to the highest, through the middle one.
chapters.zh: 这围〔殿〕的旁屋越高越宽；因旁屋围殿悬叠而上，所以越上越宽，从下一层，由中一层，到上一层。

chapters.en: I saw that the temple had a raised base all around it, forming the foundation of the side rooms. It was the full length of a rod, six long cubits.
chapters.zh: 我又见围着殿有高月台。旁屋的根基，高足一竿，就是六大肘。

chapters.en: The outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits thick, and the open area between the side rooms of the temple
chapters.zh: 旁屋的外墙厚五肘。旁屋之外还有余地。

chapters.en: and the outer chambers was twenty cubits wide all around the temple.
chapters.zh: 在旁屋与对面的房屋中间有〔空地〕，宽二十肘。

chapters.en: The side rooms opened into this area, with one entrance on the north and another on the south. The open area was five cubits wide all around.
chapters.zh: 旁屋的门都向余地：一门向北，一门向南。周围的余地宽五肘。

chapters.en: Now the building that faced the temple courtyard on the west was seventy cubits wide, and the wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, with a length of ninety cubits.
chapters.zh: 在西面空地之后有房子，宽七十肘，长九十肘，墙四围厚五肘。

chapters.en: Then he measured the temple to be a hundred cubits long, and the temple courtyard and the building with its walls were also a hundred cubits long.
chapters.zh: 这样，他量殿，长一百肘，又量空地和那房子并墙，共长一百肘。

chapters.en: The width of the temple courtyard on the east, including the front of the temple, was a hundred cubits.
chapters.zh: 殿的前面和两旁的空地，宽一百肘。

chapters.en: Next he measured the length of the building facing the temple courtyard at the rear of the temple, including its galleries on each side; it was a hundred cubits. The outer sanctuary, the inner sanctuary, and the porticoes facing the court,
chapters.zh: 他量空地后面的那房子，并两旁的楼廊，共长一百肘。

chapters.en: as well as the thresholds and the beveled windows and the galleries all around with their three levels opposite the threshold, were overlaid with wood on all sides. They were paneled from the ground to the windows, and the windows were covered.
chapters.zh: 内殿、院廊、门槛、严紧的窗櫺，并对着门槛的三层楼廊，从地到窗櫺（窗櫺都有蔽子），

chapters.en: In the space above the outside of the entrance to the inner sanctuary on all the walls, spaced evenly around the inner and outer sanctuary,
chapters.zh: 直到门以上，就是到内殿和外殿内外四围墙壁，都按尺寸用木板遮蔽。

chapters.en: were alternating carved cherubim and palm trees. Each cherub had two faces:
chapters.zh: 墙上雕刻基路伯和棕树。每二基路伯中间有一棵棕树，每基路伯有二脸。

chapters.en: the face of a man was toward the palm tree on one side, and the face of a young lion was toward the palm tree on the other side. They were carved all the way around the temple.
chapters.zh: 这边有人脸向着棕树，那边有狮子脸向着棕树，殿内周围都是如此。

chapters.en: Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the outer sanctuary from the floor to the space above the entrance.
chapters.zh: 从地至门以上，都有基路伯和棕树。殿墙就是这样。

chapters.en: The outer sanctuary had a rectangular doorframe, and the doorframe of the sanctuary was similar.
chapters.zh: 殿的门柱是方的。至圣所的前面，形状和〔殿〕的形状一样。

chapters.en: There was an altar of wood three cubits high and two cubits square. Its corners, base, and sides were of wood. And the man told me, “This is the table that is before the LORD.”
chapters.zh: 坛是木头做的，高三肘，长二肘。坛角和坛面，并四旁，都是木头做的。他对我说：「这是耶和华面前的桌子。」

chapters.en: Both the outer sanctuary and the inner sanctuary had double doors,
chapters.zh: 殿和至圣所的门各有两扇。

chapters.en: and each door had two swinging panels. There were two panels for one door and two for the other.
chapters.zh: 每扇分两扇，这两扇是折叠的。这边门分两扇，那边门也分两扇。

chapters.en: Cherubim and palm trees like those on the walls were carved on the doors of the outer sanctuary, and there was a wooden canopy outside, on the front of the portico.
chapters.zh: 殿的门扇上雕刻基路伯和棕树，与刻在墙上的一般。在外头廊前有木槛。

chapters.en: There were beveled windows and palm trees on the sidewalls of the portico. The side rooms of the temple also had canopies.
chapters.zh: 廊这边那边都有严紧的窗櫺和棕树；殿的旁屋和槛就是这样。

chapters.en: Then the man led me out northward into the outer court, and he brought me to the group of chambers opposite the temple courtyard and the outer wall on the north side.
chapters.zh: 他带我出来向北，到外院，又带我进入圣屋；这圣屋一排顺着空地，一排与北边〔铺石地〕之屋相对。

chapters.en: The building with the door facing north was a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 这圣屋长一百肘，宽五十肘，有向北的门。

chapters.en: Gallery faced gallery in three levels opposite the twenty cubits that belonged to the inner court and opposite the pavement that belonged to the outer court.
chapters.zh: 对着内院那二十〔肘宽之空地〕，又对着外院的铺石地，在第三层楼上有楼廊对着楼廊。

chapters.en: In front of the chambers was an inner walkway ten cubits wide and a hundred cubits long. Their doors were on the north.
chapters.zh: 在圣屋前有一条夹道，宽十肘，长一百肘。房门都向北。

chapters.en: Now the upper chambers were smaller because the galleries took more space from the chambers on the lower and middle floors of the building.
chapters.zh: 圣屋因为楼廊佔去些地方，所以上层比中下两层窄些。

chapters.en: For they were arranged in three stories, and unlike the courts, they had no pillars. So the upper chambers were set back further than the lower and middle floors.
chapters.zh: 圣屋有三层，却无柱子，不像外院〔的屋子〕有柱子；所以〔上层〕比中下两层更窄。

chapters.en: An outer wall in front of the chambers was fifty cubits long and ran parallel to the chambers and the outer court.
chapters.zh: 圣屋外，东边有墙，靠着外院，长五十肘。

chapters.en: For the chambers on the outer court were fifty cubits long, while those facing the temple were a hundred cubits long.
chapters.zh: 靠着外院的圣屋长五十肘。殿北面〔的圣屋〕长一百肘。

chapters.en: And below these chambers was the entrance on the east side as one enters them from the outer court.
chapters.zh: 在圣屋以下，东头有进入之处，就是从外院进入之处。

chapters.en: On the south side along the length of the wall of the outer court were chambers adjoining the courtyard and opposite the building,
chapters.zh: 向南〔注：原文是东〕在内院墙里有圣屋，一排与铺石地之屋相对，一排顺着空地。

chapters.en: with a passageway in front of them, just like the chambers that were on the north. They had the same length and width, with similar exits and dimensions.
chapters.zh: 这圣屋前的夹道与北边圣屋的〔夹道〕长宽一样；出入之处与北屋门的样式相同。

chapters.en: And corresponding to the doors of the chambers that were facing south, there was a door in front of the walkway that was parallel to the wall extending eastward.
chapters.zh: 正在墙前、夹道的东头，有门可以进入，与向南圣屋的门一样。

chapters.en: Then the man said to me, “The north and south chambers facing the temple courtyard are the holy chambers where the priests who approach the LORD will eat the most holy offerings. There they will place the most holy offerings—the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings—for the place is holy.
chapters.zh: 他对我说：「顺着空地的南屋北屋，都是圣屋；亲近耶和华的祭司当在那里吃至圣的物，也当在那里放至圣的物，就是素祭、赎罪祭，和赎愆祭，因此处为圣。

chapters.en: Once the priests have entered the holy area, they must not go out into the outer court until they have left behind the garments in which they minister, for these are holy. They are to put on other clothes before they approach the places that are for the people.”
chapters.zh: 祭司进去出了圣所的时候，不可直到外院，但要在圣屋放下他们供职的衣服，因为是圣衣；要穿上别的衣服才可以到属民的〔外院〕。」

chapters.en: Now when the man had finished measuring the interior of the temple area, he led me out by the gate that faced east, and he measured the area all around:
chapters.zh: 他量完了内殿，就带我出朝东的门，量院的四围。

chapters.en: With a measuring rod he measured the east side to be five hundred cubits long.
chapters.zh: 他用量度的竿量四围，量东面五百肘〔注：原文是竿；本章下同〕，

chapters.en: He measured the north side to be five hundred cubits long.
chapters.zh: 用竿量北面五百肘，

chapters.en: He measured the south side to be five hundred cubits long.
chapters.zh: 用竿量南面五百肘，

chapters.en: And he came around and measured the west side to be five hundred cubits long.
chapters.zh: 又转到西面，用竿量五百肘。

chapters.en: So he measured the area on all four sides. It had a wall all around, five hundred cubits long and five hundred cubits wide, to separate the holy from the common.
chapters.zh: 他量四面，四围有墙，长五百〔肘〕，宽五百〔肘〕，为要分别圣地与俗地。

chapters.en: Then the man brought me back to the gate that faces east,
chapters.zh: 以后，他带我到一座门，就是朝东的门。

chapters.en: and I saw the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east. His voice was like the roar of many waters, and the earth shone with His glory.
chapters.zh: 以色列上帝的荣光从东而来。他的声音如同多水的声音；地就因他的荣耀发光。

chapters.en: The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when He came to destroy the city and like the visions I had seen by the River Kebar. I fell facedown,
chapters.zh: 其状如从前他来灭城的时候我所见的异象，那异象如我在迦巴鲁河边所见的异象，我就俯伏在地。

chapters.en: and the glory of the LORD entered the temple through the gate facing east.
chapters.zh: 耶和华的荣光从朝东的门照入殿中。

chapters.en: Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple.
chapters.zh: 灵将我举起，带入内院，不料，耶和华的荣光充满了殿。

chapters.en: While the man was standing beside me, I heard someone speaking to me from inside the temple,
chapters.zh: 我听见有一位从殿中对我说话。有一人站在我旁边。

chapters.en: and He said to me, “Son of man, this is the place of My throne and the place for the soles of My feet, where I will dwell among the Israelites forever. The house of Israel will never again defile My holy name—neither they nor their kings—by their prostitution and by the funeral offerings for their kings at their deaths.
chapters.zh: 他对我说：「人子啊，这是我宝座之地，是我脚掌所踏之地。我要在这里住，在以色列人中直到永远。以色列家和他们的君王必不再玷污我的圣名，就是行邪淫、在〔锡安的〕高处〔葬埋〕他们君王的尸首，

chapters.en: When they placed their threshold next to My threshold and their doorposts beside My doorposts, with only a wall between Me and them, they defiled My holy name by the abominations they committed. Therefore I have consumed them in My anger.
chapters.zh: 使他们的门槛挨近我的门槛，他们的门框挨近我的门框；他们与我中间仅隔一墙，并且行可憎的事，玷污了我的圣名，所以我发怒灭绝他们。

chapters.en: Now let them remove far from Me their prostitution and the funeral offerings for their kings, and I will dwell among them forever.
chapters.zh: 现在他们当从我面前远除邪淫和他们君王的尸首，我就住在他们中间直到永远。

chapters.en: As for you, son of man, describe the temple to the people of Israel, so that they may be ashamed of their iniquities. Let them measure the plan,
chapters.zh: 「人子啊，你要将这殿指示以色列家，使他们因自己的罪孽惭愧，也要他们量殿的尺寸。

chapters.en: and if they are ashamed of all they have done, then make known to them the design of the temple—its arrangement and its exits and entrances—its whole design along with all its statutes, forms, and laws. Write it down in their sight, so that they may keep its complete design and all its statutes and may carry them out.
chapters.zh: 他们若因自己所行的一切事惭愧，你就将殿的规模、样式、出入之处，和一切形状、典章、礼仪、法则指示他们，在他们眼前写上，使他们遵照殿的一切规模典章去做。

chapters.en: This is the law of the temple: All its surrounding territory on top of the mountain will be most holy. Yes, this is the law of the temple.
chapters.zh: 殿的法则乃是如此：殿在山顶上，四围的全界要称为至圣。这就是殿的法则。」

chapters.en:
These are the measurements of the altar in long cubits (a cubit and a handbreadth): Its gutter shall be a cubit deep and a cubit wide, with a rim of one span around its edge.
And this is the height of the altar:
chapters.zh: 以下量祭坛，是以肘为度（这肘是一肘零一掌）。底座高一肘，边宽一肘，四围起边高一掌，这是坛的座。

chapters.en: The space from the gutter on the ground to the lower ledge shall be two cubits, and the ledge one cubit wide. The space from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge shall be four cubits, and the ledge one cubit wide.
chapters.zh: 从底座到下层磴台，高二肘，边宽一肘。从小磴台到大磴台，高四肘，边宽一肘。

chapters.en: The altar hearth shall be four cubits high, and four horns shall project upward from the hearth.
chapters.zh: 坛上的供台，高四肘。供台的四拐角上都有角。

chapters.en: The altar hearth shall be square at its four corners, twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 供台长十二〔肘〕，宽十二肘，四面见方。

chapters.en: The ledge shall also be square, fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide, with a rim of half a cubit and a gutter of a cubit all around it. The steps of the altar shall face east.”
chapters.zh: 磴台长十四〔肘〕，宽十四肘，四面见方。四围起边高半肘，底座四围的边宽一肘。台阶朝东。

chapters.en: Then He said to me: “Son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘These are the statutes for the altar on the day it is constructed, so that burnt offerings may be sacrificed on it and blood may be splattered on it:
chapters.zh: 他对我说：「人子啊，主耶和华如此说：建造祭坛，为要在其上献燔祭洒血，造成的时候典章如下：

chapters.en: You are to give a young bull from the herd as a sin offering to the Levitical priests who are of the family of Zadok, who approach Me to minister before Me, declares the Lord GOD.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华说，你要将一只公牛犊作为赎罪祭，给祭司利未人撒督的后裔，就是那亲近我、事奉我的。

chapters.en: You are to take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the ledge, and all around the rim; thus you will cleanse the altar and make atonement for it.
chapters.zh: 你要取些公牛的血，抹在坛的四角和磴台的四拐角，并四围所起的边上。你这样洁净坛，坛就洁净了。

chapters.en: Then you are to take away the bull for the sin offering and burn it in the appointed part of the temple area outside the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 你又要将那作赎罪祭的公牛〔犊〕烧在殿外、圣地之外预定之处。

chapters.en: On the second day you are to present an unblemished male goat as a sin offering, and the altar is to be cleansed as it was with the bull.
chapters.zh: 次日，要将无残疾的公山羊献为赎罪祭；要洁净坛，像用公牛〔犊〕洁净的一样。

chapters.en: When you have finished the purification, you are to present a young, unblemished bull and an unblemished ram from the flock.
chapters.zh: 洁净了坛，就要将一只无残疾的公牛犊和羊群中一只无残疾的公绵羊

chapters.en: You must present them before the LORD; the priests are to sprinkle salt on them and sacrifice them as a burnt offering to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 奉到耶和华前。祭司要撒盐在其上，献与耶和华为燔祭。

chapters.en: For seven days you are to provide a male goat daily for a sin offering; you are also to provide a young bull and a ram from the flock, both unblemished.
chapters.zh: 七日内，每日要预备一只公山羊为赎罪祭，也要预备一只公牛犊和羊群中的一只公绵羊，都要没有残疾的。

chapters.en: For seven days the priests are to make atonement for the altar and cleanse it; so they shall consecrate it.
chapters.zh: 七日祭司洁净坛，坛就洁净了；要这样把坛分别为圣。

chapters.en: At the end of these days, from the eighth day on, the priests are to present your burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar. Then I will accept you, declares the Lord GOD.’”
chapters.zh: 满了七日，自八日以后，祭司要在坛上献你们的燔祭和平安祭；我必悦纳你们。这是主耶和华说的。」

chapters.en: The man then brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary that faced east, but it was shut.
chapters.zh: 他又带我回到圣地朝东的外门；那门关闭了。

chapters.en: And the LORD said to me, “This gate is to remain shut. It shall not be opened, and no man shall enter through it, because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it. Therefore it will remain shut.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对我说：「这门必须关闭，不可敞开，谁也不可由其中进入；因为耶和华－以色列的上帝已经由其中进入，所以必须关闭。

chapters.en: Only the prince himself may sit inside the gateway to eat in the presence of the LORD. He must enter by way of the portico of the gateway and go out the same way.”
chapters.zh: 至于王，他必按王的位分，坐在其内，在耶和华面前吃饼。他必由这门的廊而入，也必由此而出。」

chapters.en: Then the man brought me to the front of the temple by way of the north gate. I looked and saw the glory of the LORD filling His temple, and I fell facedown.
chapters.zh: 他又带我由北门来到殿前。我观看，见耶和华的荣光充满耶和华的殿，我就俯伏在地。

chapters.en: The LORD said to me: “Son of man, pay attention; look carefully with your eyes and listen closely with your ears to everything I tell you concerning all the statutes and laws of the house of the LORD. Take careful note of the entrance to the temple, along with all the exits of the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 耶和华对我说：「人子啊，我对你所说耶和华殿中的一切典章法则，你要放在心上，用眼看，用耳听，并要留心殿宇和圣地一切出入之处。

chapters.en: Tell the rebellious house of Israel that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I have had enough of all your abominations, O house of Israel.
chapters.zh: 你要对那悖逆的以色列家说，主耶和华如此说：以色列家啊，你们行一切可憎的事，当够了吧！

chapters.en: In addition to all your other abominations, you brought in foreigners uncircumcised in both heart and flesh to occupy My sanctuary; you defiled My temple when you offered My food—the fat and the blood; you broke My covenant.
chapters.zh: 你们把我的食物，就是脂油和血献上的时候，将身心未受割礼的外邦人领进我的圣地，玷污了我的殿；又背了我的约，在你们一切可憎的事上，加上〔这一层〕。

chapters.en: And you have not kept charge of My holy things, but have appointed others to keep charge of My sanctuary for you.’
chapters.zh: 你们也没有看守我的圣物，却派别人在圣地替你们看守我所吩咐你们的。

chapters.en: This is what the Lord GOD says: No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter My sanctuary—not even a foreigner who lives among the Israelites.
chapters.zh: 「主耶和华如此说：以色列中的外邦人，就是身心未受割礼的，都不可入我的圣地。」

chapters.en: Surely the Levites who wandered away from Me when Israel went astray, and who wandered away from Me after their idols, will bear the consequences of their iniquity.
chapters.zh: 「当以色列人走迷的时候，有利未人远离我，就是走迷离开我、随从他们的偶像，他们必担当自己的罪孽。

chapters.en: Yet they shall be ministers in My sanctuary, having charge of the gates of the temple and ministering there. They shall slaughter the burnt offerings and other sacrifices for the people and stand before them to minister to them.
chapters.zh: 然而他们必在我的圣地当仆役，照管殿门，在殿中供职；必为民宰杀燔祭牲和〔平安〕祭牲，必站在民前伺候他们。

chapters.en: Because they ministered before their idols and became a stumbling block of iniquity to the house of Israel, therefore I swore with an uplifted hand concerning them that they would bear the consequences of their iniquity, declares the Lord GOD.
chapters.zh: 因为这些利未人曾在偶像前伺候这民，成了以色列家罪孽的绊脚石，所以我向他们起誓：他们必担当自己的罪孽。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: They must not approach Me to serve Me as priests or come near any of My holy things or the most holy things. They will bear the shame of the abominations they have committed.
chapters.zh: 他们不可亲近我，给我供祭司的职分，也不可挨近我的一件圣物，就是至圣的物；他们却要担当自己的羞辱和所行可憎之事的报应。

chapters.en: Yet I will appoint them to keep charge of all the work for the temple and everything to be done in it.
chapters.zh: 然而我要使他们看守殿宇，办理其中的一切事，并做其内一切当做之工。」

chapters.en: But the Levitical priests, who are descended from Zadok and who kept charge of My sanctuary when the Israelites went astray from Me, are to approach Me to minister before Me. They will stand before Me to offer Me fat and blood, declares the Lord GOD.
chapters.zh: 「以色列人走迷离开我的时候，祭司利未人撒督的子孙仍看守我的圣所。他们必亲近我，事奉我，并且侍立在我面前，将脂油与血献给我。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: They alone shall enter My sanctuary and draw near to My table to minister before Me. They will keep My charge.
chapters.zh: 他们必进入我的圣所，就近我的桌前事奉我，守我所吩咐的。

chapters.en: When they enter the gates of the inner court, they are to wear linen garments; they must not wear anything made of wool when they minister at the gates of the inner court or inside the temple.
chapters.zh: 他们进内院门必穿细麻衣。在内院门和殿内供职的时候不可穿羊毛衣服。

chapters.en: They are to wear linen turbans on their heads and linen undergarments around their waists. They must not wear anything that makes them perspire.
chapters.zh: 他们头上要戴细麻布裹头巾，腰穿细麻布裤子；不可穿使身体出汗〔的衣服〕。

chapters.en: When they go out to the outer court, to the people, they are to take off the garments in which they have ministered, leave them in the holy chambers, and dress in other clothes so that they do not transmit holiness to the people with their garments.
chapters.zh: 他们出到外院的民那里，当脱下供职的衣服，放在圣屋内，穿上别的衣服，免得因圣衣使民成圣。

chapters.en: They must not shave their heads or let their hair grow long, but must carefully trim their hair.
chapters.zh: 不可剃头，也不可容发绺长长，只可剪发。

chapters.en: No priest may drink wine before he enters the inner court.
chapters.zh: 祭司进内院的时候都不可喝酒。

chapters.en: And they shall not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but must marry a virgin of the descendants of the house of Israel, or a widow of a priest.
chapters.zh: 不可娶寡妇和被休的妇人为妻，只可娶以色列后裔中的处女，或是祭司遗留的寡妇。

chapters.en: They are to teach My people the difference between the holy and the common and show them how to discern between the clean and the unclean.
chapters.zh: 他们要使我的民知道圣俗的分别，又使他们分辨洁净的和不洁净的。

chapters.en: In any dispute, they shall officiate as judges and judge according to My ordinances. They must keep My laws and statutes regarding all My appointed feasts, and they must keep My Sabbaths holy.
chapters.zh: 有争讼的事，他们应当站立判断，要按我的典章判断。在我一切的节期必守我的律法、条例，也必以我的安息日为圣日。

chapters.en: A priest must not defile himself by going near a dead person. However, for a father, a mother, a son, a daughter, a brother, or an unmarried sister, he may do so,
chapters.zh: 他们不可挨近死尸沾染自己，只可为父亲、母亲、儿子、女儿、弟兄，和未嫁人的姊妹沾染自己。

chapters.en: and after he is cleansed, he must count off seven days for himself.
chapters.zh: 祭司洁净之后，必再计算七日。

chapters.en: And on the day he goes into the sanctuary, into the inner court, to minister in the sanctuary, he must present his sin offering, declares the Lord GOD.
chapters.zh: 当他进内院，进圣所，在圣所中事奉的日子，要为自己献赎罪祭。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: In regard to their inheritance, I am their inheritance. You are to give them no possession in Israel, for I am their possession.
chapters.zh: 「祭司必有产业，我是他们的产业。不可在以色列中给他们基业；我是他们的基业。

chapters.en: They shall eat the grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings. Everything in Israel devoted to the LORD will belong to them.
chapters.zh: 素祭、赎罪祭，和赎愆祭他们都可以吃，以色列中一切永献的物都要归他们。

chapters.en: The best of all the firstfruits and of every contribution from all your offerings will belong to the priests. You are to give your first batch of dough to the priest, so that a blessing may rest upon your homes.
chapters.zh: 首先初熟之物和一切所献的供物都要归给祭司。你们也要用初熟的麦子磨面给祭司；这样，福气就必临到你们的家了。

chapters.en: The priests may not eat any bird or animal found dead or torn by wild beasts.
chapters.zh: 无论是鸟是兽，凡自死的，或是撕裂的，祭司都不可吃。」

chapters.en: “When you divide the land by lot as an inheritance, you are to set aside a portion for the LORD, a holy portion of the land 25,000 cubits long and 20,000 cubits wide. This entire tract of land will be holy.
chapters.zh: 你们拈鬮分地为业，要献上一分给耶和华为圣供地，长二万五千〔肘〕，宽一万〔肘〕。这分以内，四围都为圣地。

chapters.en: Within this area there is to be a section for the sanctuary 500 cubits square, with 50 cubits around it for open land.
chapters.zh: 其中有作为圣所之地，〔长〕五百〔肘〕，〔宽〕五百〔肘〕，四面见方。四围再有五十肘为郊野之地。

chapters.en: From this holy portion, you are to measure off a length of 25,000 cubits and a width of 10,000 cubits, and in it will be the sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
chapters.zh: 要以肘为度量地，长二万五千〔肘〕，宽一万〔肘〕。其中有圣所，是至圣的。

chapters.en: It will be a holy portion of the land to be used by the priests who minister in the sanctuary, who draw near to minister before the LORD. It will be a place for their houses, as well as a holy area for the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 这是全地的一分圣地，要归与供圣所职事的祭司，就是亲近事奉耶和华的，作为他们房屋之地与圣所之圣地。

chapters.en: An adjacent area 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide shall belong to the Levites who minister in the temple; it will be their possession for towns in which to live.
chapters.zh: 又有一分，长二万五千〔肘〕，宽一万〔肘〕，要归与在殿中供职的利未人，作为二十间房屋之业。

chapters.en: As the property of the city, you are to set aside an area 5,000 cubits wide and 25,000 cubits long, adjacent to the holy district. It will belong to the whole house of Israel.
chapters.zh: 也要分定属城的地业，宽五千〔肘〕，长二万五千〔肘〕，挨着那分圣供地，要归以色列全家。

chapters.en: Now the prince will have the area bordering each side of the area formed by the holy district and the property of the city, extending westward from the western side and eastward from the eastern side, running lengthwise from the western boundary to the eastern boundary and parallel to one of the tribal portions.
chapters.zh: 归王〔之地〕要在圣供地和属城之地的两旁，就是圣供地和属城之地的旁边，西至西头，东至东头，从西到东，其长与〔每支派的〕分一样。

chapters.en:
This land will be his possession in Israel.
And My princes will no longer oppress My people, but will give the rest of the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.
chapters.zh: 这地在以色列中必归王为业。我所立的王必不再欺压我的民，却要按支派将地分给以色列家。

chapters.en: For this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Enough, O princes of Israel! Cease your violence and oppression, and do what is just and right. Stop dispossessing My people, declares the Lord GOD.’
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「以色列的王啊，你们应当知足，要除掉强暴和抢夺的事，施行公平和公义，不再勒索我的民。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: You must use honest scales, a just ephah, and a just bath.
chapters.zh: 「你们要用公道天平、公道伊法、公道罢特。

chapters.en: The ephah and the bath shall be the same quantity so that the bath will contain a tenth of a homer, and the ephah a tenth of a homer; the homer will be the standard measure for both.
chapters.zh: 伊法与罢特大小要一样。罢特可盛贺梅珥十分之一，伊法也可盛贺梅珥十分之一，都以贺梅珥的大小为准。

chapters.en: The shekel will consist of twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels plus twenty-five shekels plus fifteen shekels will equal one mina.
chapters.zh: 舍客勒是二十季拉；二十舍客勒，二十五舍客勒，十五舍客勒，为你们的弥那。

chapters.en: This is the contribution you are to offer: a sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat, and a sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley.
chapters.zh: 「你们当献的供物乃是这样：一贺梅珥麦子要献伊法六分之一；一贺梅珥大麦要献伊法六分之一。

chapters.en: The prescribed portion of oil, measured by the bath, is a tenth of a bath from each cor (a cor consists of ten baths or one homer, since ten baths are equivalent to a homer).
chapters.zh: 你们献所分定的油，按油的罢特，一柯珥油要献罢特十分之一（原来十罢特就是一贺梅珥）。

chapters.en: And one sheep shall be given from each flock of two hundred from the well-watered pastures of Israel. These are for the grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings, to make atonement for the people, declares the Lord GOD.
chapters.zh: 从以色列滋润的草场上每二百羊中，要献一只羊羔。这都可作素祭、燔祭、平安祭，为民赎罪。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en: All the people of the land must participate in this contribution for the prince in Israel.
chapters.zh: 此地的民都要奉上这供物给以色列中的王。

chapters.en: And it shall be the prince’s part to provide the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings for the feasts, New Moons, and Sabbaths—for all the appointed feasts of the house of Israel. He will provide the sin offerings, grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings to make atonement for the house of Israel.
chapters.zh: 王的本分是在节期、月朔、安息日，就是以色列家一切的节期，奉上燔祭、素祭、奠祭。他要预备赎罪祭、素祭、燔祭，和平安祭，为以色列家赎罪。」

chapters.en: This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘On the first day of the first month you are to take a young bull without blemish and purify the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「正〔月〕初一〔日〕，你要取无残疾的公牛犊，洁净圣所。

chapters.en: And the priest is to take some of the blood from the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the temple, on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the gateposts of the inner court.
chapters.zh: 祭司要取些赎罪祭牲的血，抹在殿的门柱上和坛磴台的四角上，并内院的门框上。

chapters.en: You must do the same thing on the seventh day of the month for anyone who strays unintentionally or in ignorance. In this way you will make atonement for the temple.
chapters.zh: 本月初七日〔注：七十士译本是七月初一日〕也要为误犯罪的和愚蒙犯罪的如此行，为殿赎罪。

chapters.en: On the fourteenth day of the first month you are to observe the Passover, a feast of seven days, during which unleavened bread shall be eaten.
chapters.zh: 「正月十四日，你们要守逾越节，守节七日，要吃无酵饼。

chapters.en: On that day the prince shall provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people of the land.
chapters.zh: 当日，王要为自己和国内的众民预备一只公牛作赎罪祭。

chapters.en: Each day during the seven days of the feast, he shall provide seven bulls and seven rams without blemish as a burnt offering to the LORD, along with a male goat for a sin offering.
chapters.zh: 这节的七日，每日他要为耶和华预备无残疾的公牛七只、公绵羊七只为燔祭。每日又要预备公山羊一只为赎罪祭。

chapters.en: He shall also provide as a grain offering an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, along with a hin of olive oil for each ephah of grain.
chapters.zh: 他也要预备素祭，就是为一只公牛同献一伊法〔细面〕，为一只公绵羊同献一伊法〔细面〕，每一伊法〔细面〕加油一欣。

chapters.en: During the seven days of the feast that begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, he is to make the same provision for sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, and oil.’
chapters.zh: 七月十五日守节的时候，七日他都要如此行，照〔逾越节的〕赎罪祭、燔祭、素祭，和油的条例一样。」

chapters.en: “This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘The gate of the inner court that faces east must be kept shut during the six days of work, but on the Sabbath day and on the day of the New Moon it shall be opened.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「内院朝东的门，在办理事务的六日内必须关闭；惟有安息日和月朔必须敞开。

chapters.en: The prince is to enter from the outside through the portico of the gateway and stand by the gatepost, while the priests sacrifice his burnt offerings and peace offerings. He is to bow in worship at the threshold of the gate and then depart, but the gate must not be shut until evening.
chapters.zh: 王要从这门的廊进入，站在门框旁边。祭司要为他预备燔祭和平安祭，他就要在门槛那里敬拜，然后出去。这门直到晚上不可关闭。

chapters.en: On the Sabbaths and New Moons the people of the land are also to bow in worship before the LORD at the entrance to that gateway.
chapters.zh: 在安息日和月朔，国内的居民要在这门口，耶和华面前敬拜。

chapters.en: The burnt offering that the prince presents to the LORD on the Sabbath day shall be six unblemished male lambs and an unblemished ram.
chapters.zh: 安息日，王所献与耶和华的燔祭要用无残疾的羊羔六只，无残疾的公绵羊一只；

chapters.en: The grain offering with the ram shall be one ephah, and the grain offering with the lambs shall be as much as he is able, along with a hin of oil per ephah.
chapters.zh: 同献的素祭要为公绵羊献一伊法〔细面〕，为羊羔照他的力量而献，一伊法〔细面〕加油一欣。

chapters.en: On the day of the New Moon he shall offer a young, unblemished bull, six lambs, and a ram without blemish.
chapters.zh: 当月朔，要献无残疾的公牛犊一只，羊羔六只，公绵羊一只，都要无残疾的。

chapters.en: He is to provide a grain offering of an ephah with the bull, an ephah with the ram, and as much as he is able with the lambs, along with a hin of oil per ephah.
chapters.zh: 他也要预备素祭，为公牛献一伊法〔细面〕，为公绵羊献一伊法〔细面〕，为羊羔照他的力量而献，一伊法〔细面〕加油一欣。

chapters.en: When the prince enters, he shall go in through the portico of the gateway, and he shall go out the same way.
chapters.zh: 王进入的时候必由这门的廊而入，也必由此而出。

chapters.en: When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed feasts, whoever enters by the north gate to worship must go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate must go out by the north gate. No one is to return through the gate by which he entered, but each must go out by the opposite gate.
chapters.zh: 「在各节期，国内居民朝见耶和华的时候，从北门进入敬拜的，必由南门而出；从南门进入的，必由北门而出。不可从所入的门而出，必要直往前行，〔由对门〕而出。

chapters.en: When the people enter, the prince shall go in with them, and when they leave, he shall leave.
chapters.zh: 民进入，王也要在民中进入；民出去，王也要一同出去。

chapters.en: At the festivals and appointed feasts, the grain offering shall be an ephah with a bull, an ephah with a ram, and as much as one is able to give with the lambs, along with a hin of oil per ephah.
chapters.zh: 「在节期和圣会的日子同献的素祭，要为一只公牛献一伊法〔细面〕，为一只公绵羊献一伊法〔细面〕，为羊羔照他的力量而献，一伊法〔细面〕加油一欣。

chapters.en: When the prince makes a freewill offering to the LORD, whether a burnt offering or a peace offering, the gate facing east must be opened for him. He is to offer his burnt offering or peace offering just as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he shall go out, and the gate must be closed after he goes out.
chapters.zh: 王预备甘心献的燔祭或平安祭，就是向耶和华甘心献的，当有人为他开朝东的门。他就预备燔祭和平安祭，与安息日预备的一样，〔献毕〕就出去。他出去之后，当有人将门关闭。」

chapters.en: And you shall provide an unblemished year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the LORD; you are to offer it every morning.
chapters.zh: 「每日，你要预备无残疾一岁的羊羔一只，献与耶和华为燔祭；要每早晨预备。

chapters.en: You are also to provide with it every morning a grain offering of a sixth of an ephah with a third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour—a grain offering to the LORD. This is a permanent statute.
chapters.zh: 每早晨也要预备同献的素祭，〔细面〕一伊法六分之一，并油一欣三分之一，调和细面。这素祭要常献与耶和华为永远的定例。

chapters.en: Thus they shall provide the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil every morning as a regular burnt offering.’
chapters.zh: 每早晨要这样预备羊羔、素祭，并油为常献的燔祭。」

chapters.en: This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons as an inheritance, it will belong to his descendants. It will become their property by inheritance.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「王若将产业赐给他的儿子，就成了他儿子的产业，那是他们承受为业的。

chapters.en: But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it will belong to that servant until the year of freedom; then it will revert to the prince. His inheritance belongs only to his sons; it shall be theirs.
chapters.zh: 倘若王将一分产业赐给他的臣仆，就成了他臣仆的产业；到自由之年仍要归与王。至于王的产业，必归与他的儿子。

chapters.en: The prince must not take any of the inheritance of the people by evicting them from their property. He is to provide an inheritance for his sons from his own property, so that none of My people will be displaced from his property.’”
chapters.zh: 王不可夺取民的产业，以致驱逐他们离开所承受的；他要从自己的地业中，将产业赐给他儿子，免得我的民分散，各人离开所承受的。」

chapters.en: Then the man brought me through the entrance at the side of the gate into the holy chambers facing north, which belonged to the priests, and he showed me a place there at the far western end
chapters.zh: 那带我的，将我从门旁进入之处、领进为祭司预备的圣屋，是朝北的，见后头西边有一块地。

chapters.en: and said to me, “This is the place where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and where they shall bake the grain offering, so that they do not bring them into the outer court and transmit holiness to the people.”
chapters.zh: 他对我说：「这是祭司煮赎愆祭、赎罪祭，烤素祭之地，免得带到外院，使民成圣。」

chapters.en: Then he brought me into the outer court and led me around to its four corners, and I saw a separate court in each of its corners.
chapters.zh: 他又带我到外院，使我经过院子的四拐角，见每拐角各有一个院子。

chapters.en: In the four corners of the outer court there were enclosed courts, each forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide. Each of the four corner areas had the same dimensions.
chapters.zh: 院子四拐角的院子，周围有墙，每院长四十〔肘〕，宽三十〔肘〕。四拐角院子的尺寸都是一样，

chapters.en: Around the inside of each of the four courts was a row of masonry with ovens built at the base of the walls on all sides.
chapters.zh: 其中周围有一排房子，房子内有煮〔肉〕的地方。

chapters.en: And he said to me, “These are the kitchens where those who minister at the temple will cook the sacrifices offered by the people.”
chapters.zh: 他对我说：「这都是煮〔肉〕的房子，殿内的仆役要在这里煮民的祭物。」

chapters.en: Then the man brought me back to the entrance of the temple, and I saw water flowing from under the threshold of the temple toward the east (for the temple faced east). The water was coming down from under the south side of the temple, south of the altar.
chapters.zh: 他带我回到殿门，见殿的门槛下有水往东流出（原来殿面朝东）。这水从槛下，由殿的右边，在祭坛的南边往下流。

chapters.en: Next he brought me out through the north gate and led me around the outside to the outer gate facing east, and there I saw the water trickling out from the south side.
chapters.zh: 他带我出北门，又领我从外边转到朝东的外门，见水从右边流出。

chapters.en: As the man went eastward with a measuring line in his hand, he measured off a thousand cubits and led me through ankle-deep water.
chapters.zh: 他手拿准绳往东出去的时候，量了一千肘，使我诜过水，水到踝子骨。

chapters.en:
Then he measured off a thousand cubits and led me through knee-deep water.
Again he measured a thousand cubits and led me through waist-deep water.
chapters.zh: 他又量了一千〔肘〕，使我诜过水，水就到膝；再量了一千〔肘〕，使我诜过〔水〕，水便到腰；

chapters.en: Once again he measured off a thousand cubits, but now it was a river that I could not cross, because the water had risen and was deep enough for swimming—a river that could not be crossed on foot.
chapters.zh: 又量了一千〔肘〕，水便成了河，使我不能诜过。因为水势涨起，成为可洑的水，不可诜的河。

chapters.en: “Son of man, do you see this?” he asked. Then he led me back to the bank of the river.
chapters.zh: 他对我说：「人子啊，你看见了什么？」 他就带我回到河边。

chapters.en: When I arrived, I saw a great number of trees along both banks of the river.
chapters.zh: 我回到河边的时候，见在河这边与那边的岸上有极多的树木。

chapters.en: And he said to me, “This water flows out to the eastern region and goes down into the Arabah. When it empties into the Dead Sea, the water there becomes fresh.
chapters.zh: 他对我说：「这水往东方流去，必下到亚拉巴，直到海。所发出来的〔水〕必流入〔盐〕海，使水变甜〔注：原文是得医治；下同〕。

chapters.en: Wherever the river flows, there will be swarms of living creatures and a great number of fish, because it flows there and makes the waters fresh; so wherever the river flows, everything will flourish.
chapters.zh: 这河水所到之处，凡滋生的动物都必生活，并且因这流来的水必有极多的鱼，〔海水〕也变甜了。这河水所到之处，百物都必生活。

chapters.en: Fishermen will stand by the shore; from En-gedi to En-eglaim they will spread their nets to catch fish of many kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea.
chapters.zh: 必有渔夫站在河边，从隐‧基底直到隐‧以革莲，都作晒〔注：或译：张〕网之处。那鱼各从其类，好像大海的鱼甚多。

chapters.en: But the swamps and marshes will not become fresh; they will be left for salt.
chapters.zh: 只是泥泞之地与洼湿之处不得治好，必为盐地。

chapters.en: Along both banks of the river, fruit trees of all kinds will grow. Their leaves will not wither, and their fruit will not fail. Each month they will bear fruit, because the water from the sanctuary flows to them. Their fruit will be used for food and their leaves for healing.”
chapters.zh: 在河这边与那边的岸上必生长各类的树木；〔其果〕可作食物，叶子不枯干，果子不断绝。每月必结新果子，因为这水是从圣所流出来的。树上的果子必作食物，叶子乃为治病。」

chapters.en: This is what the Lord GOD says: “These are the boundaries by which you are to divide the land as an inheritance among the twelve tribes of Israel; Joseph shall receive two portions.
chapters.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「你们要照地的境界，按以色列十二支派分地为业。约瑟〔必得两〕分。

chapters.en: You are to divide it equally among them. Because I swore with an uplifted hand to give it to your forefathers, this land will fall to you as an inheritance.
chapters.zh: 你们承受这地为业，要彼此均分；因为我曾起誓应许将这地赐与你们的列祖；这地必归你们为业。

chapters.en:
This shall be the boundary of the land:
On the north side it will extend from the Great Sea by way of Hethlon through Lebo-hamath to Zedad,
chapters.zh: 「地的四界乃是如此：北界从大海往希特伦，直到西达达口。

chapters.en: Berothah, and Sibraim (which is on the border between Damascus and Hamath), as far as Hazer-hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
chapters.zh: 又往哈马、比罗他、西伯莲（西伯莲在大马士革与哈马两界中间），到浩兰边界的哈撒‧哈提干。

chapters.en: So the border will run from the Sea to Hazar-enan, along the northern border of Damascus, with the territory of Hamath to the north. This will be the northern boundary.
chapters.zh: 这样，境界从海边往大马士革地界上的哈萨‧以难，北边以哈马地为界。这是北界。

chapters.en: On the east side the border will run between Hauran and Damascus, along the Jordan between Gilead and the land of Israel, to the Eastern Sea and as far as Tamar. This will be the eastern boundary.
chapters.zh: 「东界在浩兰、大马士革、基列，和以色列地的中间，就是约旦河。你们要从〔北〕界量到东海。这是东界。

chapters.en: On the south side it will run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, and along the Brook of Egypt to the Great Sea. This will be the southern boundary.
chapters.zh: 「南界是从他玛到米利巴‧加低斯的水，延到〔埃及〕小河，直到大海。这是南界。

chapters.en: And on the west side, the Great Sea will be the boundary up to a point opposite Lebo-hamath. This will be the western boundary.
chapters.zh: 「西界就是大海，从〔南〕界直到哈马口对面之地。这是西界。
