chapters.en: You are to divide this land among yourselves according to the tribes of Israel.
chapters.zh: 「你们要按着以色列的支派彼此分这地。

chapters.en: You shall allot it as an inheritance for yourselves and for the foreigners who dwell among you and who have children. You are to treat them as native-born Israelites; along with you, they shall be allotted an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
chapters.zh: 要拈鬮分这地为业，归与自己和你们中间寄居的外人，就是在你们中间生养儿女的外人。你们要看他们如同以色列人中所生的一样；他们在以色列支派中要与你们同得地业。

chapters.en: In whatever tribe a foreigner dwells, you are to assign his inheritance there,” declares the Lord GOD.
chapters.zh: 外人寄居在哪支派中，你们就在那里分给他地业。这是主耶和华说的。」

chapters.en:
“Now these are the names of the tribes:
At the northern frontier, Dan will have one portion bordering the road of Hethlon to Lebo-hamath and running on to Hazar-enan on the border of Damascus with Hamath to the north, and extending from the east side to the west side.
chapters.zh: 众支派按名所得〔之地〕记在下面：从北头，由希特伦往哈马口，到大马士革地界上的哈萨‧以难。北边靠着哈马地（各支派〔的地〕都有东西的边界），是但的一〔分〕。

chapters.en: Asher will have one portion bordering the territory of Dan from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着但的地界，从东到西，是亚设的一〔分〕。

chapters.en: Naphtali will have one portion bordering the territory of Asher from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着亚设的地界，从东到西，是拿弗他利的一〔分〕。

chapters.en: Manasseh will have one portion bordering the territory of Naphtali from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着拿弗他利的地界，从东到西，是玛拿西的一〔分〕。

chapters.en: Ephraim will have one portion bordering the territory of Manasseh from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着玛拿西的地界，从东到西，是以法莲的一〔分〕。

chapters.en: Reuben will have one portion bordering the territory of Ephraim from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着以法莲的地界，从东到西，是吕便的一〔分〕。

chapters.en: Judah will have one portion bordering the territory of Reuben from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着吕便的地界，从东到西，是犹大的一〔分〕。

chapters.en: Bordering the territory of Judah, from east to west, will be the portion you are to set apart. It will be 25,000 cubits wide, and the length of a tribal portion from east to west. In the center will be the sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 挨着犹大的地界，从东到西，必有你们所当献的供地，宽二万五千〔肘〕。从东界到西界，长短与各分之地相同，圣地当在其中。

chapters.en: The special portion you set apart to the LORD shall be 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide.
chapters.zh: 你们献与耶和华的供地要长二万五千〔肘〕，宽一万〔肘〕。

chapters.en: This will be the holy portion for the priests. It will be 25,000 cubits long on the north side, 10,000 cubits wide on the west side, 10,000 cubits wide on the east side, and 25,000 cubits long on the south side. In the center will be the sanctuary of the LORD.
chapters.zh: 这圣供地要归与祭司，北〔长〕二万五千〔肘〕，西宽一万〔肘〕，东宽一万〔肘〕，南长二万五千〔肘〕。耶和华的圣地当在其中。

chapters.en: It will be for the consecrated priests, the descendants of Zadok, who kept My charge and did not go astray as the Levites did when the Israelites went astray.
chapters.zh: 这地要归与撒督的子孙中成为圣的祭司，就是那守我所吩咐的。当以色列人走迷的时候，他们不像那些利未人走迷了。

chapters.en: It will be a special portion for them set apart from the land, a most holy portion adjacent to the territory of the Levites.
chapters.zh: 这要归与他们为供地，是全地中至圣的。供地挨着利未人的地界。

chapters.en: Bordering the territory of the priests, the Levites shall have an area 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. The whole length will be 25,000 cubits, and the width 10,000 cubits.
chapters.zh: 利未人所得的地要长二万五千〔肘〕，宽一万〔肘〕，与祭司的地界相等，都长二万五千〔肘〕，宽一万〔肘〕。

chapters.en: They must not sell or exchange any of it, and they must not transfer this best part of the land, for it is holy to the LORD.
chapters.zh: 这地不可卖，不可换，初熟之物也不可归与别人，因为是归耶和华为圣的。

chapters.en: The remaining area, 5,000 cubits wide and 25,000 cubits long, will be for common use by the city, for houses, and for pastureland. The city will be in the center of it
chapters.zh: 这二万五千〔肘〕前面所剩下五千〔肘〕宽之地要作俗用，作为造城盖房郊野之地。城要在当中。

chapters.en: and will have these measurements: 4,500 cubits on the north side, 4,500 cubits on the south side, 4,500 cubits on the east side, and 4,500 cubits on the west side.
chapters.zh: 城的尺寸乃是如此：北面四千五百〔肘〕，南面四千五百〔肘〕，东面四千五百〔肘〕，西面四千五百〔肘〕。

chapters.en: The pastureland of the city will extend 250 cubits to the north, 250 cubits to the south, 250 cubits to the east, and 250 cubits to the west.
chapters.zh: 城必有郊野，向北二百五十〔肘〕，向南二百五十〔肘〕，向东二百五十〔肘〕，向西二百五十〔肘〕。

chapters.en: The remainder of the length bordering the holy portion and running adjacent to it will be 10,000 cubits on the east side and 10,000 cubits on the west side. Its produce will supply food for the workers of the city.
chapters.zh: 靠着圣供地的余地，东长一〔万〕肘，西长一万〔肘〕，要与圣供地相等；其中的土产要作城内工人的食物。

chapters.en: The workers of the city who cultivate it will come from all the tribes of Israel.
chapters.zh: 所有以色列支派中，在城内做工的，都要耕种这地。

chapters.en: The entire portion will be a square, 25,000 cubits by 25,000 cubits. You are to set apart the holy portion, along with the city property.
chapters.zh: 你们所献的圣供地连归城之地，是四方的：长二万五千〔肘〕，宽二万五千〔肘〕。

chapters.en: The remaining area on both sides of the holy portion and of the property of the city will belong to the prince. He will own the land adjacent to the tribal portions, extending eastward from the 25,000 cubits of the holy district toward the eastern border, and westward from the 25,000 cubits to the western border. And in the center of them will be the holy portion and the sanctuary of the temple.
chapters.zh: 圣供地连归城之地，两边的余地要归与王。供地东边，〔南北〕二万五千〔肘〕，东至东界，西边〔南北〕二万五千〔肘〕，西至西界，与各分之地相同，都要归王。圣供地和殿的圣地要在其中，

chapters.en: So the Levitical property and the city property will lie in the center of the area belonging to the prince—the area between the borders of Judah and Benjamin.
chapters.zh: 并且利未人之地，与归城之地的东西两边延长之地（这两地在王地中间），就是在犹大和便雅悯两界中间，要归与王。

chapters.en:
As for the rest of the tribes:
Benjamin will have one portion extending from the east side to the west side.
chapters.zh: 论到其余的支派，从东到西，是便雅悯的一〔分〕。

chapters.en: Simeon will have one portion bordering the territory of Benjamin from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着便雅悯的地界，从东到西，是西缅的一〔分〕。

chapters.en: Issachar will have one portion bordering the territory of Simeon from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着西缅的地界，从东到西，是以萨迦的一〔分〕。

chapters.en: Zebulun will have one portion bordering the territory of Issachar from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着以萨迦的地界，从东到西，是西布伦的一〔分〕。

chapters.en: And Gad will have one portion bordering the territory of Zebulun from east to west.
chapters.zh: 挨着西布伦的地界，从东到西，是迦得的一〔分〕。

chapters.en: The southern border of Gad will run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, then along the Brook of Egypt and out to the Great Sea.
chapters.zh: 迦得地的南界是从他玛到米利巴‧加低斯的水，延到埃及小河，直到大海。

chapters.en: This is the land you are to allot as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel, and these will be their portions,” declares the Lord GOD.
chapters.zh: 这就是你们要拈鬮分给以色列支派为业之地，乃是他们各支派所得之分。这是主耶和华说的。

chapters.en:
“These will be the exits of the city:
Beginning on the north side, which will be 4,500 cubits long,
chapters.zh: 城的北面四千五百〔肘〕。出城之处如下；

chapters.en: the gates of the city will be named after the tribes of Israel. On the north side there will be three gates: the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah, and the gate of Levi.
chapters.zh: 城的各门要按以色列支派的名字。北面有三门，一为吕便门，一为犹大门，一为利未门；

chapters.en: On the east side, which will be 4,500 cubits long, there will be three gates: the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin, and the gate of Dan.
chapters.zh: 东面四千五百〔肘〕，有三门，一为约瑟门，一为便雅悯门，一为但门；

chapters.en: On the south side, which will be 4,500 cubits long, there will be three gates: the gate of Simeon, the gate of Issachar, and the gate of Zebulun.
chapters.zh: 南面四千五百〔肘〕，有三门，一为西缅门，一为以萨迦门，一为西布伦门；

chapters.en: And on the west side, which will be 4,500 cubits long, there will be three gates: the gate of Gad, the gate of Asher, and the gate of Naphtali.
chapters.zh: 西面四千五百〔肘〕，有三门，一为迦得门，一为亚设门，一为拿弗他利门。

chapters.en:
The perimeter of the city will be 18,000 cubits, and from that day on the name of the city will be:
THE LORD IS THERE. ”
chapters.zh: 城四围共一万八千〔肘〕。从此以后，这城的名字必称为「耶和华的所在」。

chapters.en: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.
chapters.zh: 犹大王约雅敬在位第三年，巴比伦王尼布甲尼撒来到耶路撒冷，将城围困。

chapters.en: And the Lord delivered into his hand Jehoiakim king of Judah, along with some of the articles from the house of God. He carried these off to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, where he put them in the treasury of his god.
chapters.zh: 主将犹大王约雅敬，并上帝殿中器皿的几分交付他手。他就把这器皿带到示拿地，收入他神的庙里，放在他神的库中。

chapters.en: Then the king ordered Ashpenaz, the chief of his court officials, to bring in some Israelites from the royal family and the nobility—
chapters.zh: 王吩咐太监长亚施毗拿，从以色列人的宗室和贵胄中带进几个人来，

chapters.en: young men without blemish, handsome, gifted in all wisdom, knowledgeable, quick to understand, and qualified to serve in the king’s palace—and to teach them the language and literature of the Chaldeans.
chapters.zh: 就是年少没有残疾、相貌俊美、通达各样学问、知识聪明俱备、足能侍立在王宫里的，要教他们迦勒底的文字言语。

chapters.en: The king assigned them daily provisions of the royal food and wine. They were to be trained for three years, after which they were to enter the king’s service.
chapters.zh: 王派定将自己所用的膳和所饮的酒，每日赐他们一分，养他们三年。满了三年，好叫他们在王面前侍立。

chapters.en: Among these young men were some from Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
chapters.zh: 他们中间有犹大族的人：但以理、哈拿尼雅、米沙利、亚撒利雅。

chapters.en: The chief official gave them new names: To Daniel he gave the name Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.
chapters.zh: 太监长给他们起名：称但以理为伯提沙撒，称哈拿尼雅为沙得拉，称米沙利为米煞，称亚撒利雅为亚伯尼歌。

chapters.en: But Daniel made up his mind that he would not defile himself with the king’s food or wine. So he asked the chief official for permission not to defile himself.
chapters.zh: 但以理却立志不以王的膳和王所饮的酒玷污自己，所以求太监长容他不玷污自己。

chapters.en: Now God had granted Daniel favor and compassion from the chief official,
chapters.zh: 上帝使但以理在太监长眼前蒙恩惠，受怜悯。

chapters.en: but he said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who has assigned your food and drink. For why should he see your faces looking thinner than those of the other young men your age? You would endanger my head before the king!”
chapters.zh: 太监长对但以理说：「我惧怕我主我王，他已经派定你们的饮食，倘若他见你们的面貌比你们同岁的少年人肌瘦，怎么好呢？这样，你们就使我的头在王那里难保。」

chapters.en: Then Daniel said to the steward whom the chief official had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
chapters.zh: 但以理对太监长所派管理但以理、哈拿尼雅、米沙利、亚撒利雅的委办说：

chapters.en: “Please test your servants for ten days. Let us be given only vegetables to eat and water to drink.
chapters.zh: 「求你试试仆人们十天，给我们素菜吃，白水喝，

chapters.en: Then compare our appearances with those of the young men who are eating the royal food, and deal with your servants according to what you see.”
chapters.zh: 然后看看我们的面貌和用王膳那少年人的面貌，就照你所看的待仆人吧！」

chapters.en: So he consented to this and tested them for ten days.
chapters.zh: 委办便允准他们这件事，试看他们十天。

chapters.en: And at the end of ten days, they looked healthier and better nourished than all the young men who were eating the king’s food.
chapters.zh: 过了十天，见他们的面貌比用王膳的一切少年人更加俊美肥胖。

chapters.en: So the steward continued to withhold their choice food and the wine they were to drink, and he gave them vegetables instead.
chapters.zh: 于是委办撤去派他们用的膳，饮的酒，给他们素菜吃。

chapters.en: To these four young men God gave knowledge and understanding in every kind of literature and wisdom. And Daniel had insight into all kinds of visions and dreams.
chapters.zh: 这四个少年人，上帝在各样文字学问〔注：学问：原文是智慧〕上赐给他们聪明知识；但以理又明白各样的异象和梦兆。

chapters.en: Now at the end of the time specified by the king, the chief official presented them to Nebuchadnezzar.
chapters.zh: 尼布甲尼撒王预定带进少年人来的日期满了，太监长就把他们带到王面前。

chapters.en: And the king spoke with them, and among all the young men he found no one equal to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they entered the king’s service.
chapters.zh: 王与他们谈论，见少年人中无一人能比但以理、哈拿尼雅、米沙利、亚撒利雅，所以留他们在王面前侍立。

chapters.en: In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king consulted them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his entire kingdom.
chapters.zh: 王考问他们一切事，就见他们的智慧聪明比通国的术士和用法术的胜过十倍。

chapters.en: And Daniel remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.
chapters.zh: 到塞鲁士王元年，但以理还在。

chapters.en: In the second year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams that troubled his spirit, and sleep escaped him.
chapters.zh: 尼布甲尼撒在位第二年，他做了梦，心里烦乱，不能睡觉。

chapters.en: So the king gave orders to summon the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and astrologers to explain his dreams. When they came and stood before the king,
chapters.zh: 王吩咐人将术士、用法术的、行邪术的，和迦勒底人召来，要他们将王的梦告诉王，他们就来站在王前。

chapters.en: he said to them, “I have had a dream, and my spirit is anxious to understand it.”
chapters.zh: 王对他们说：「我做了一梦，心里烦乱，要知道这是什么梦。」

chapters.en: Then the astrologers answered the king in Aramaic, “O king, may you live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will give the interpretation.”
chapters.zh: 迦勒底人用亚兰的言语对王说：「愿王万岁！请将那梦告诉仆人，仆人就可以讲解。」

chapters.en: The king replied to the astrologers, “My word is final: If you do not tell me the dream and its interpretation, you will be cut into pieces and your houses will be reduced to rubble.
chapters.zh: 王回答迦勒底人说：「梦我已经忘了〔注：或译：我已定命；八节同〕，你们若不将梦和梦的讲解告诉我，就必被凌迟，你们的房屋必成为粪堆；

chapters.en: But if you tell me the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts and rewards and great honor. So tell me the dream and its interpretation.”
chapters.zh: 你们若将梦和梦的讲解告诉我，就必从我这里得赠品和赏赐，并大尊荣。现在你们要将梦和梦的讲解告诉我。」

chapters.en: They answered a second time, “Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will give the interpretation.”
chapters.zh: 他们第二次对王说：「请王将梦告诉仆人，仆人就可以讲解。」

chapters.en: The king replied, “I know for sure that you are stalling for time because you see that my word is final.
chapters.zh: 王回答说：「我准知道你们是故意迟延，因为你们知道那梦我已经忘了。

chapters.en: If you do not tell me the dream, there is only one decree for you. You have conspired to speak before me false and fraudulent words, hoping the situation will change. Therefore tell me the dream, and I will know that you can give me its interpretation.”
chapters.zh: 你们若不将梦告诉我，只有一法待你们；因为你们预备了谎言乱语向我说，要等候时势改变。现在你们要将梦告诉我，因我知道你们能将梦的讲解告诉我。」

chapters.en: The astrologers answered the king, “No one on earth can do what the king requests! No king, however great and powerful, has ever asked anything like this of any magician, enchanter, or astrologer.
chapters.zh: 迦勒底人在王面前回答说：「世上没有人能将王所问的事说出来；因为没有君王、大臣、掌权的向术士，或用法术的，或迦勒底人问过这样的事。

chapters.en: What the king requests is so difficult that no one can tell it to him except the gods, whose dwelling is not with mortals.”
chapters.zh: 王所问的事甚难。除了不与世人同居的神明，没有人在王面前能说出来。」

chapters.en: This response made the king so angry and furious that he gave orders to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
chapters.zh: 因此，王气忿忿地大发烈怒，吩咐灭绝巴比伦所有的哲士。

chapters.en: So the decree went out that the wise men were to be executed, and men went to look for Daniel and his friends to execute them.
chapters.zh: 于是命令发出，哲士将要见杀，人就寻找但以理和他的同伴，要杀他们。

chapters.en: When Arioch, the commander of the king’s guard, went out to execute the wise men of Babylon, Daniel responded with discretion and tact.
chapters.zh: 王的护卫长亚略出来，要杀巴比伦的哲士，但以理就用婉言回答他，

chapters.en:
“Why is the decree from the king so harsh?” he asked.
Then Arioch explained the situation to Daniel.
chapters.zh: 向王的护卫长亚略说：「王的命令为何这样紧急呢？」亚略就将情节告诉但以理。

chapters.en: So Daniel went in and asked the king to give him some time, so that he could give him the interpretation.
chapters.zh: 但以理遂进去求王宽限，就可以将〔梦的〕讲解告诉王。

chapters.en: Then Daniel returned to his house and explained the matter to his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
chapters.zh: 但以理回到他的居所，将这事告诉他的同伴哈拿尼雅、米沙利、亚撒利雅，

chapters.en: urging them to plead for mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his friends would not be killed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
chapters.zh: 要他们祈求天上的上帝施怜悯，将这奥祕的事指明，免得但以理和他的同伴与巴比伦其余的哲士一同灭亡。

chapters.en: During the night, the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision, and he blessed the God of heaven
chapters.zh: 这奥祕的事就在夜间异象中给但以理显明，但以理便称颂天上的上帝。

chapters.en:
and declared:
“Blessed be the name of God forever and ever, for wisdom and power belong to Him.
chapters.zh: 但以理说：「上帝的名是应当称颂的！从亘古直到永远，因为智慧能力都属乎他。

chapters.en: He changes the times and seasons; He removes kings and establishes them. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to the discerning.
chapters.zh: 他改变时候、日期，废王，立王，将智慧赐与智慧人，将知识赐与聪明人。

chapters.en:
He reveals the deep and hidden things; He knows what lies in darkness,
and light dwells with Him.
chapters.zh: 他显明深奥隐秘的事，知道暗中所有的，光明也与他同居。

chapters.en: To You, O God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because You have given me wisdom and power. And now You have made known to me what we have requested, for You have made known to us the dream of the king.”
chapters.zh: 我列祖的上帝啊，我感谢你，赞美你；因你将智慧才能赐给我，允准我们所求的，把王的事给我们指明。」

chapters.en: Therefore Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and said to him, “Do not execute the wise men of Babylon! Bring me before the king, and I will give him the interpretation.”
chapters.zh: 于是，但以理进去见亚略，就是王所派灭绝巴比伦哲士的，对他说：「不要灭绝巴比伦的哲士，求你领我到王面前，我要将〔梦的〕讲解告诉王。」

chapters.en: Arioch hastily brought Daniel before the king and said to him, “I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who will tell the king the interpretation.”
chapters.zh: 亚略就急忙将但以理领到王面前，对王说：「我在被掳的犹大人中遇见一人，他能将〔梦的〕讲解告诉王。」

chapters.en: The king responded to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Are you able to tell me what I saw in the dream, as well as its interpretation?”
chapters.zh: 王问称为伯提沙撒的但以理说：「你能将我所做的梦和梦的讲解告诉我吗？」

chapters.en: Daniel answered the king, “No wise man, enchanter, medium, or magician can explain to the king the mystery of which he inquires.
chapters.zh: 但以理在王面前回答说：「王所问的那奥祕事，哲士、用法术的、术士、观兆的都不能告诉王，

chapters.en: But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and He has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the latter days. Your dream and the visions that came into your mind as you lay on your bed were these:
chapters.zh: 只有一位在天上的上帝能显明奥祕的事。他已将日后必有的事指示尼布甲尼撒王。你的梦和你在床上脑中的异象是这样：

chapters.en: As you lay on your bed, O king, your thoughts turned to the future, and the Revealer of Mysteries made known to you what will happen.
chapters.zh: 王啊，你在床上想到后来的事，那显明奥祕事的主把将来必有的事指示你。

chapters.en: And to me this mystery has been revealed, not because I have more wisdom than any man alive, but in order that the interpretation might be made known to the king, and that you may understand the thoughts of your mind.
chapters.zh: 至于那奥祕的事显明给我，并非因我的智慧胜过一切活人，乃为使王知道〔梦的〕讲解和心里的思念。

chapters.en: As you, O king, were watching, a great statue appeared. A great and dazzling statue stood before you, and its form was awesome.
chapters.zh: 「王啊，你梦见一个大像，这像甚高，极其光耀，站在你面前，形状甚是可怕。

chapters.en: The head of the statue was pure gold, its chest and arms were silver, its belly and thighs were bronze,
chapters.zh: 这像的头是精金的，胸膛和膀臂是银的，肚腹和腰是铜的，

chapters.en: its legs were iron, and its feet were part iron and part clay.
chapters.zh: 腿是铁的，脚是半铁半泥的。

chapters.en: As you watched, a stone was cut out, but not by human hands. It struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay, and crushed them.
chapters.zh: 你观看，见有一块非人手凿出来的石头打在这像半铁半泥的脚上，把脚砸碎；

chapters.en: Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were shattered and became like chaff on the threshing floor in summer. The wind carried them away, and not a trace of them could be found. But the stone that had struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
chapters.zh: 于是金、银、铜、铁、泥都一同砸得粉碎，成如夏天禾场上的糠秕，被风吹散，无处可寻。打碎这像的石头变成一座大山，充满天下。

chapters.en: This was the dream; now we will tell the king its interpretation.
chapters.zh: 「这就是那梦；我们在王面前要讲解那梦。

chapters.en: You, O king, are the king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given sovereignty, power, strength, and glory.
chapters.zh: 王啊，你是诸王之王。天上的上帝已将国度、权柄、能力、尊荣都赐给你。

chapters.en: Wherever the sons of men or beasts of the field or birds of the air dwell, He has given them into your hand and has made you ruler over them all. You are that head of gold.
chapters.zh: 凡世人所住之地的走兽，并天空的飞鸟，他都交付你手，使你掌管这一切。你就是那金头。

chapters.en:
But after you, there will arise another kingdom, inferior to yours.
Next, a third kingdom, one of bronze, will rule the whole earth.
chapters.zh: 在你以后必另兴一国，不及于你；又有第三国，就是铜的，必掌管天下。

chapters.en: Finally, there will be a fourth kingdom as strong as iron; for iron shatters and crushes all things, and like iron that crushes all things, it will shatter and crush all the others.
chapters.zh: 第四国，必坚壮如铁，铁能打碎克制百物，又能压碎一切，那国也必打碎压制〔列国〕。

chapters.en: And just as you saw that the feet and toes were made partly of fired clay and partly of iron, so this will be a divided kingdom, yet some of the strength of iron will be in it—just as you saw the iron mixed with clay.
chapters.zh: 你既见像的脚和脚指头，一半是窑匠的泥，一半是铁，那国将来也必分开。你既见铁与泥搀杂，那国也必有铁的力量。

chapters.en: And as the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay, so this kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.
chapters.zh: 那脚指头，既是半铁半泥，那国也必半强半弱。

chapters.en: As you saw the iron mixed with clay, so the peoples will mix with one another but will not hold together any more than iron mixes with clay.
chapters.zh: 你既见铁与泥搀杂，那国民也必与各种人搀杂，却不能彼此相合，正如铁与泥不能相合一样。

chapters.en: In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will shatter all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but will itself stand forever.
chapters.zh: 当那列王在位的时候，天上的上帝必另立一国，永不败坏，也不归别国的人，却要打碎灭绝那一切国，这国必存到永远。

chapters.en:
And just as you saw a stone being cut out of the mountain without human hands, and it shattered the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold, so the great God has told the king what will happen in the future.
The dream is true, and its interpretation is trustworthy.”
chapters.zh: 你既看见非人手凿出来的一块石头从山而出，打碎金、银、铜、铁、泥，那就是至大的上帝把后来必有的事给王指明。这梦准是这样，这讲解也是确实的。」

chapters.en: At this, King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, paid homage to Daniel, and ordered that an offering and incense be presented to him.
chapters.zh: 当时，尼布甲尼撒王俯伏在地，向但以理下拜，并且吩咐人给他奉上供物和香品。

chapters.en: The king said to Daniel, “Your God is truly the God of gods and Lord of kings, the Revealer of Mysteries, since you were able to reveal this mystery.”
chapters.zh: 王对但以理说：「你既能显明这奥祕的事，你们的上帝诚然是万神之神、万王之主，又是显明奥祕事的。」

chapters.en: Then the king promoted Daniel and gave him many generous gifts. He made him ruler over the entire province of Babylon and chief administrator over all the wise men of Babylon.
chapters.zh: 于是王高抬但以理，赏赐他许多上等礼物，派他管理巴比伦全省，又立他为总理，掌管巴比伦的一切哲士。

chapters.en: And at Daniel’s request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to manage the province of Babylon, while Daniel remained in the king’s court.
chapters.zh: 但以理求王，王就派沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌管理巴比伦省的事务，只是但以理常在朝中侍立。

chapters.en: King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden statue sixty cubits high and six cubits wide, and he set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.
chapters.zh: 尼布甲尼撒王造了一个金像，高六十肘，宽六肘，立在巴比伦省杜拉平原。

chapters.en: Then King Nebuchadnezzar sent word to assemble the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the other officials of the provinces to attend the dedication of the statue he had set up.
chapters.zh: 尼布甲尼撒王差人将总督、钦差、巡抚、臬司、藩司、谋士、法官，和各省的官员都召了来，为尼布甲尼撒王所立的像行开光之礼。

chapters.en: So the satraps, prefects, governors, advisers, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the rulers of the provinces assembled for the dedication of the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood before it.
chapters.zh: 于是总督、钦差、巡抚、臬司、藩司、谋士、法官，和各省的官员都聚集了来，要为尼布甲尼撒王所立的像行开光之礼，就站在尼布甲尼撒所立的像前。

chapters.en: Then the herald loudly proclaimed, “O people of every nation and language, this is what you are commanded:
chapters.zh: 那时传令的大声呼叫说：「各方、各国、各族〔注：原文是舌；下同〕的人哪，有令传与你们：

chapters.en: As soon as you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music, you must fall down and worship the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
chapters.zh: 你们一听见角、笛、琵琶、琴、瑟、笙，和各样乐器的声音，就当俯伏敬拜尼布甲尼撒王所立的金像。

chapters.en: And whoever does not fall down and worship will immediately be thrown into the blazing fiery furnace.”
chapters.zh: 凡不俯伏敬拜的，必立时扔在烈火的窑中。」

chapters.en: Therefore, as soon as all the people heard the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, and all kinds of music, the people of every nation and language would fall down and worship the golden statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
chapters.zh: 因此各方、各国、各族的人民一听见角、笛、琵琶、琴、瑟，和各样乐器的声音，就都俯伏敬拜尼布甲尼撒王所立的金像。

chapters.en: At this time some astrologers came forward and maliciously accused the Jews,
chapters.zh: 那时，有几个迦勒底人进前来控告犹大人。

chapters.en: saying to King Nebuchadnezzar, “O king, may you live forever!
chapters.zh: 他们对尼布甲尼撒王说：「愿王万岁！

chapters.en: You, O king, have issued a decree that everyone who hears the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music must fall down and worship the golden statue,
chapters.zh: 王啊，你曾降旨说，凡听见角、笛、琵琶、琴、瑟、笙，和各样乐器声音的都当俯伏敬拜金像。

chapters.en: and that whoever does not fall down and worship will be thrown into the blazing fiery furnace.
chapters.zh: 凡不俯伏敬拜的，必扔在烈火的窑中。

chapters.en: But there are some Jews you have appointed to manage the province of Babylon—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego—who have ignored you, O king, and have refused to serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up.”
chapters.zh: 现在有几个犹大人，就是王所派管理巴比伦省事务的沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌；王啊，这些人不理你，不事奉你的神，也不敬拜你所立的金像。」

chapters.en: Then Nebuchadnezzar, furious with rage, summoned Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. So these men were brought before the king,
chapters.zh: 当时，尼布甲尼撒冲冲大怒，吩咐人把沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌带过来，他们就把那些人带到王面前。

chapters.en: and Nebuchadnezzar said to them, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, is it true that you do not serve my gods or worship the golden statue I have set up?
chapters.zh: 尼布甲尼撒问他们说：「沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌，你们不事奉我的神，也不敬拜我所立的金像，是故意的吗？

chapters.en: Now when you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipes, and all kinds of music, if you are ready to fall down and worship the statue I have made, very good. But if you refuse to worship, you will be thrown at once into the blazing fiery furnace. Then what god will be able to deliver you from my hands?”
chapters.zh: 你们再听见角、笛、琵琶、琴、瑟、笙，和各样乐器的声音，若俯伏敬拜我所造的像，却还可以；若不敬拜，必立时扔在烈火的窑中，有何神能救你们脱离我手呢？」

chapters.en: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego replied to the king, “O Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you in this matter.
chapters.zh: 沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌对王说：「尼布甲尼撒啊，这件事我们不必回答你，

chapters.en: If the God whom we serve exists, then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace and from your hand, O king.
chapters.zh: 即便如此，我们所事奉的上帝能将我们从烈火的窑中救出来。王啊，他也必救我们脱离你的手；

chapters.en: But even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up.”
chapters.zh: 即或不然，王啊，你当知道我们决不事奉你的神，也不敬拜你所立的金像。」

chapters.en: At this, Nebuchadnezzar was filled with rage, and the expression on his face changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He gave orders to heat the furnace seven times hotter than usual,
chapters.zh: 当时，尼布甲尼撒怒气填胸，向沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌变了脸色，吩咐人把窑烧热，比寻常更加七倍；

chapters.en: and he commanded some mighty men of valor in his army to tie up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and throw them into the blazing fiery furnace.
chapters.zh: 又吩咐他军中的几个壮士，将沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌捆起来，扔在烈火的窑中。

chapters.en: So they were tied up, wearing robes, trousers, turbans, and other clothes, and they were thrown into the blazing fiery furnace.
chapters.zh: 这三人穿着裤子、内袍、外衣，和〔别的〕衣服，被捆起来扔在烈火的窑中。

chapters.en: The king’s command was so urgent and the furnace so hot that the fiery flames killed the men who carried up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
chapters.zh: 因为王命紧急，窑又甚热，那抬沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌的人都被火焰烧死。

chapters.en: And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, firmly bound, fell into the blazing fiery furnace.
chapters.zh: 沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌这三个人都被捆着落在烈火的窑中。

chapters.en:
Suddenly King Nebuchadnezzar jumped up in amazement and asked his advisers, “Did we not throw three men, firmly bound, into the fire?”
“Certainly, O king,” they replied.
chapters.zh: 那时，尼布甲尼撒王惊奇，急忙起来，对谋士说：「我们捆起来扔在火里的不是三个人吗？」他们回答王说：「王啊，是。」

chapters.en: “Look!” he exclaimed. “I see four men, unbound and unharmed, walking around in the fire—and the fourth looks like a son of the gods! ”
chapters.zh: 王说：「看哪，我见有四个人，并没有捆绑，在火中游行，也没有受伤；那第四个的相貌好像神子。」

chapters.en:
Then Nebuchadnezzar approached the door of the blazing fiery furnace and called out, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out!”
So Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out of the fire,
chapters.zh: 于是，尼布甲尼撒就近烈火窑门，说：「至高上帝的仆人沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌出来，上这里来吧！」沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌就从火中出来了。

chapters.en: and when the satraps, prefects, governors, and royal advisers had gathered around, they saw that the fire had no effect on the bodies of these men. Not a hair of their heads was singed, their robes were unaffected, and there was no smell of fire on them.
chapters.zh: 那些总督、钦差、巡抚，和王的谋士一同聚集看这三个人，见火无力伤他们的身体，头发也没有烧焦，衣裳也没有变色，并没有火燎的气味。

chapters.en: Nebuchadnezzar declared, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent His angel and delivered His servants who trusted in Him. They violated the king’s command and risked their lives rather than serve or worship any god except their own God.
chapters.zh: 尼布甲尼撒说：「沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌的上帝是应当称颂的！他差遣使者救护倚靠他的仆人，他们不遵王命，舍去己身，在他们上帝以外不肯事奉敬拜别神。

chapters.en: Therefore I decree that the people of any nation or language who say anything offensive against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego will be cut into pieces and their houses reduced to rubble. For there is no other god who can deliver in this way.”
chapters.zh: 现在我降旨，无论何方、何国、何族的人，谤讟沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌之上帝的，必被凌迟，他的房屋必成粪堆，因为没有别神能这样施行拯救。」

chapters.en: Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
chapters.zh: 那时王在巴比伦省，高升了沙得拉、米煞、亚伯尼歌。

chapters.en:
King Nebuchadnezzar,
To the people of every nation and language who dwell in all the earth:
May your prosperity be multiplied.
chapters.zh: 尼布甲尼撒王晓谕住在全地各方、各国、各族的人说：「愿你们大享平安！

chapters.en: I am pleased to declare the signs and wonders that the Most High God has performed for me.
chapters.zh: 我乐意将至高的上帝向我所行的神迹奇事宣扬出来。

chapters.en: How great are His signs, how mighty His wonders! His kingdom is an eternal kingdom; His dominion endures from generation to generation.
chapters.zh: 他的神迹何其大！ 他的奇事何其盛！ 他的国是永远的； 他的权柄存到万代！

chapters.en: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and flourishing in my palace.
chapters.zh: 「我－尼布甲尼撒安居在宫中，平顺在殿内。

chapters.en: I had a dream, and it frightened me; while I was in my bed, the images and visions in my mind alarmed me.
chapters.zh: 我做了一梦，使我惧怕。我在床上的思念，并脑中的异象，使我惊惶。

chapters.en: So I issued a decree that all the wise men of Babylon be brought before me to interpret the dream for me.
chapters.zh: 所以我降旨召巴比伦的一切哲士到我面前，叫他们把梦的讲解告诉我。

chapters.en: When the magicians, enchanters, astrologers, and diviners came in, I told them the dream, but they could not interpret it for me.
chapters.zh: 于是那些术士、用法术的、迦勒底人、观兆的都进来，我将那梦告诉了他们，他们却不能把梦的讲解告诉我。

chapters.en: But at last, into my presence came Daniel (whose name is Belteshazzar after the name of my god, and in whom is the spirit of the holy gods). And I told him the dream:
chapters.zh: 末后那照我神的名，称为伯提沙撒的但以理来到我面前，他里头有圣神的灵，我将梦告诉他〔说〕：

chapters.en: “O Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and that no mystery baffles you. So explain to me the visions I saw in my dream, and their interpretation.
chapters.zh: 『术士的领袖伯提沙撒啊，因我知道你里头有圣神的灵，什么奥祕的事都不能使你为难。现在要把我梦中所见的异象和梦的讲解告诉我。』

chapters.en:
In these visions of my mind as I was lying in bed, I saw this come to pass:
There was a tree in the midst of the land, and its height was great.
chapters.zh: 「我在床上脑中的异象是这样：我看见地当中有一棵树，极其高大。

chapters.en: The tree grew large and strong; its top reached the sky, and it was visible to the ends of the earth.
chapters.zh: 那树渐长，而且坚固，高得顶天，从地极都能看见，

chapters.en:
Its leaves were beautiful, its fruit was abundant,
and upon it was food for all. Under it the beasts of the field found shelter, in its branches the birds of the air nested,
and from it every creature was fed.
chapters.zh: 叶子华美，果子甚多，可作众生的食物；田野的走兽卧在荫下，天空的飞鸟宿在枝上；凡有血气的都从这树得食。

chapters.en: As I lay on my bed, I also saw in the visions of my mind a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven.
chapters.zh: 「我在床上脑中的异象，见有一位守望的圣者从天而降。

chapters.en:
He called out in a loud voice:
‘Cut down the tree and chop off its branches; strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Let the beasts flee from under it, and the birds from its branches.
chapters.zh: 大声呼叫说：『伐倒这树！砍下枝子！摇掉叶子！抛散果子！使走兽离开树下，飞鸟躲开树枝。

chapters.en:
But leave the stump with its roots in the ground, with a band of iron and bronze around it,
in the tender grass of the field.
Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven and graze with the beasts on the grass of the earth.
chapters.zh: 树触却要留在地内，用铁圈和铜圈箍住，在田野的青草中让天露滴湿，使他与地上的兽一同吃草，

chapters.en:
Let his mind be changed from that of a man, and let him be given the mind of a beast
till seven times pass him by.
chapters.zh: 使他的心改变，不如人心，给他一个兽心，使他经过七期〔注：期：或译年；本章同〕。

chapters.en:
This decision is the decree of the watchers, the verdict declared by the holy ones,
so that the living will know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom He wishes,
setting over it the lowliest of men.’
chapters.zh: 这是守望者所发的命，圣者所出的令，好叫世人知道至高者在人的国中掌权，要将国赐与谁就赐与谁，〔或〕立极卑微的人执掌国权。』

chapters.en: This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. Now, Belteshazzar, tell me the interpretation, because none of the wise men of my kingdom can interpret it for me. But you are able, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you.”
chapters.zh: 「这是我－尼布甲尼撒王所做的梦。伯提沙撒啊，你要说明这〔梦的〕讲解；因为我国中的一切哲士都不能将〔梦〕的讲解告诉我，惟独你能，因你里头有圣神的灵。」

chapters.en:
For a time, Daniel, who was also known as Belteshazzar, was perplexed, and his thoughts alarmed him.
So the king said, “Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its interpretation alarm you.”
“My lord,” replied Belteshazzar, “may the dream apply to those who hate you, and its interpretation to your enemies!
chapters.zh: 于是称为伯提沙撒的但以理惊讶片时，心意惊惶。王说：「伯提沙撒啊，不要因梦和梦的讲解惊惶。」伯提沙撒回答说：「我主啊，愿这梦归与恨恶你的人，讲解归与你的敌人。

chapters.en: The tree you saw that grew large and strong, whose top reached the sky and was visible to all the earth,
chapters.zh: 你所见的树渐长，而且坚固，高得顶天，从地极都能看见；

chapters.en: whose foliage was beautiful and whose fruit was abundant, providing food for all, under which the beasts of the field lived, and in whose branches the birds of the air nested—
chapters.zh: 叶子华美，果子甚多，可作众生的食物；田野的走兽住在其下；天空的飞鸟宿在枝上。

chapters.en: you, O king, are that tree! For you have become great and strong; your greatness has grown to reach the sky, and your dominion extends to the ends of the earth.
chapters.zh: 「王啊，这渐长又坚固的树就是你。你的威势渐长及天，你的权柄管到地极。

chapters.en:
And you, O king, saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven and saying:
‘Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump with its roots in the ground, with a band of iron and bronze around it, in the tender grass of the field.
Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and graze with the beasts of the field
till seven times pass him by.’
chapters.zh: 王既看见一位守望的圣者从天而降，说：『将这树砍伐毁坏，树触却要留在地内，用铁圈和铜圈箍住；在田野的青草中，让天露滴湿，使他与地上的兽一同吃草，直到经过七期。』

chapters.en: This is the interpretation, O king, and this is the decree that the Most High has issued against my lord the king:
chapters.zh: 「王啊，讲解就是这样：临到我主我王的事是出于至高者的命。

chapters.en: You will be driven away from mankind, and your dwelling will be with the beasts of the field. You will feed on grass like an ox and be drenched with the dew of heaven, and seven times shall pass you by, until you acknowledge that the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom He wishes.
chapters.zh: 你必被赶出离开世人，与野地的兽同居，吃草如牛，被天露滴湿，且要经过七期。等你知道至高者在人的国中掌权，要将国赐与谁就赐与谁。

chapters.en: As for the command to leave the stump of the tree with its roots, your kingdom will be restored to you as soon as you acknowledge that Heaven rules.
chapters.zh: 守望者既吩咐存留树触，等你知道诸天掌权，以后你的国必定归你。

chapters.en: Therefore, may my advice be pleasing to you, O king. Break away from your sins by doing what is right, and from your iniquities by showing mercy to the oppressed. Perhaps there will be an extension of your prosperity.”
chapters.zh: 王啊，求你悦纳我的谏言，以施行公义断绝罪过，以怜悯穷人除掉罪孽，或者你的平安可以延长。」

chapters.en: All this happened to King Nebuchadnezzar.
chapters.zh: 这事都临到尼布甲尼撒王。

chapters.en: Twelve months later, as he was walking on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon,
chapters.zh: 过了十二个月，他游行在巴比伦王宫里〔注：原文是上〕。

chapters.en: the king exclaimed, “Is this not Babylon the Great, which I myself have built as a royal residence by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?”
chapters.zh: 他说：「这大巴比伦不是我用大能大力建为京都，要显我威严的荣耀吗？」

chapters.en: While the words were still in the king’s mouth, a voice came from heaven: “It is decreed to you, King Nebuchadnezzar, that the kingdom has departed from you.
chapters.zh: 这话在王口中尚未说完，有声音从天降下，〔说〕：「尼布甲尼撒王啊，有话对你说，你的国位离开你了。

chapters.en: You will be driven away from mankind to live with the beasts of the field, and you will feed on grass like an ox. And seven times will pass you by, until you acknowledge that the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind and gives it to whom He wishes.”
chapters.zh: 你必被赶出离开世人，与野地的兽同居，吃草如牛，且要经过七期。等你知道至高者在人的国中掌权，要将国赐与谁就赐与谁。」

chapters.en: At that moment the sentence against Nebuchadnezzar was fulfilled. He was driven away from mankind. He ate grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like the feathers of an eagle and his nails like the claws of a bird.
chapters.zh: 当时这话就应验在尼布甲尼撒的身上，他被赶出离开世人，吃草如牛，身被天露滴湿，头发长长，好像鹰〔毛〕；指甲长长，如同鸟〔爪〕。

chapters.en:
But at the end of those days I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven, and my sanity was restored to me. Then I praised the Most High, and I honored and glorified Him who lives forever:
“For His dominion is an everlasting dominion, and His kingdom endures from generation to generation.
chapters.zh: 日子满足，我－尼布甲尼撒举目望天，我的聪明复归于我，我便称颂至高者，赞美尊敬活到永远的〔上帝〕。 他的权柄是永有的； 他的国存到万代。

chapters.en:
All the peoples of the earth are counted as nothing, and He does as He pleases with the army of heaven
and the peoples of the earth. There is no one who can restrain His hand or say to Him, ‘What have You done?’”
chapters.zh: 世上所有的居民都算为虚无； 在天上的万军和世上的居民中， 他都凭自己的意旨行事。 无人能拦住他手， 或问他说，你做什么呢？

chapters.en: At the same time my sanity was restored, my honor and splendor returned to me for the glory of my kingdom. My advisers and nobles sought me out, and I was restored to my throne, and surpassing greatness was added to me.
chapters.zh: 那时，我的聪明复归于我，为我国的荣耀、威严，和光耀也都复归于我；并且我的谋士和大臣也来朝见我。我又得坚立在国位上，至大的权柄加增于我。

chapters.en: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of heaven, for all His works are true and all His ways are just. And He is able to humble those who walk in pride.
chapters.zh: 现在我－尼布甲尼撒赞美、尊崇、恭敬天上的王；因为他所做的全都诚实，他所行的也都公平。那行动骄傲的，他能降为卑。

chapters.en: Later, King Belshazzar held a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and he drank wine with them.
chapters.zh: 伯沙撒王为他的一千大臣设摆盛筵，与这一千人对面饮酒。

chapters.en: Under the influence of the wine, Belshazzar gave orders to bring in the gold and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken from the temple in Jerusalem, so that the king could drink from them, along with his nobles, his wives, and his concubines.
chapters.zh: 伯沙撒欢饮之间，吩咐人将他父〔注：或译：祖；下同〕尼布甲尼撒从耶路撒冷殿中所掠的金银器皿拿来，王与大臣、皇后、妃嫔好用这器皿饮酒。

chapters.en: Thus they brought in the gold vessels that had been taken from the temple, the house of God in Jerusalem, and the king drank from them, along with his nobles, his wives, and his concubines.
chapters.zh: 于是他们把耶路撒冷上帝殿〔库〕房中所掠的金器皿拿来，王和大臣、皇后、妃嫔就用这器皿饮酒。

chapters.en: As they drank the wine, they praised their gods of gold and silver, bronze and iron, wood and stone.
chapters.zh: 他们饮酒，赞美金、银、铜、铁、木、石所造的神。

chapters.en: At that moment the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall, near the lampstand in the royal palace. As the king watched the hand that was writing,
chapters.zh: 当时，〔忽〕有人的指头显出，在王宫与灯台相对的粉墙上写字。王看见写字的指头

chapters.en: his face grew pale and his thoughts so alarmed him that his hips gave way and his knees knocked together.
chapters.zh: 就变了脸色，心意惊惶，腰骨〔好像〕脱节，双膝彼此相碰，

chapters.en: The king called out for the enchanters, astrologers, and diviners to be brought in, and he said to these wise men of Babylon, “Whoever reads this inscription and tells me its interpretation will be clothed in purple and have a gold chain placed around his neck, and he will be made the third highest ruler in the kingdom.”
chapters.zh: 大声吩咐将用法术的和迦勒底人并观兆的领进来，对巴比伦的哲士说，谁能读这文字，把讲解告诉我，他必身穿紫袍，项带金鍊，在我国中位列第三。

chapters.en: So all the king’s wise men came in, but they could not read the inscription or interpret it for him.
chapters.zh: 于是王的一切哲士都进来，却不能读那文字，也不能把讲解告诉王。

chapters.en: Then King Belshazzar became even more terrified, his face grew even more pale, and his nobles were bewildered.
chapters.zh: 伯沙撒王就甚惊惶，脸色改变，他的大臣也都惊奇。

chapters.en: Hearing the outcry of the king and his nobles, the queen entered the banquet hall. “O king, may you live forever!” she said. “Do not let your thoughts terrify you, or your face grow pale.
chapters.zh: 太后〔注：或译：皇后；下同〕因王和他大臣所说的话，就进入宴宫，说：「愿王万岁！你心意不要惊惶，脸面不要变色。

chapters.en:
There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him. In the days of your father he was found to have insight, intelligence, and wisdom like that of the gods.
Your father, King Nebuchadnezzar, appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, astrologers, and diviners. Your own father, the king,
chapters.zh: 在你国中有一人，他里头有圣神的灵，你父在世的日子，这人心中光明，又有聪明智慧，好像神的智慧。你父尼布甲尼撒王，就是王的父，立他为术士、用法术的，和迦勒底人，并观兆的领袖。

chapters.en: did this because Daniel, the one he named Belteshazzar, was found to have an extraordinary spirit, as well as knowledge, understanding, and the ability to interpret dreams, explain riddles, and solve difficult problems. Summon Daniel, therefore, and he will give you the interpretation.”
chapters.zh: 在他里头有美好的灵性，又有知识聪明，能圆梦，释谜语，解疑惑。这人名叫但以理，尼布甲尼撒王又称他为伯提沙撒，现在可以召他来，他必解明这意思。」

chapters.en: So Daniel was brought before the king, who asked him, “Are you Daniel, one of the exiles my father the king brought from Judah?
chapters.zh: 但以理就被领到王前。王问但以理说：「你是被掳之犹大人中的但以理吗？就是我父王从犹大掳来的吗？

chapters.en: I have heard that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that you have insight, intelligence, and extraordinary wisdom.
chapters.zh: 我听说你里头有神的灵，心中光明，又有聪明和美好的智慧。

chapters.en: Now the wise men and enchanters were brought before me to read this inscription and interpret it for me, but they could not give its interpretation.
chapters.zh: 现在哲士和用法术的都领到我面前，为叫他们读这文字，把讲解告诉我，无奈他们都不能把讲解说出来。

chapters.en: But I have heard about you, that you are able to give interpretations and solve difficult problems. Therefore, if you can read this inscription and give me its interpretation, you will be clothed in purple and have a gold chain placed around your neck, and you will be made the third highest ruler in the kingdom.”
chapters.zh: 我听说你善于讲解，能解疑惑；现在你若能读这文字，把讲解告诉我，就必身穿紫袍，项戴金鍊，在我国中位列第三。」

chapters.en: In response, Daniel said to the king, “You may keep your gifts for yourself and give your rewards to someone else. Nevertheless, I will read the inscription for the king and interpret it for him.
chapters.zh: 但以理在王面前回答说：「你的赠品可以归你自己，你的赏赐可以归给别人；我却要为王读这文字，把讲解告诉王。

chapters.en: As for you, O king, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar sovereignty and greatness, glory and honor.
chapters.zh: 王啊，至高的上帝曾将国位、大权、荣耀、威严赐与你父尼布甲尼撒；

chapters.en: Because of the greatness that He bestowed on him, the people of every nation and language trembled in fear before him. He killed whom he wished and kept alive whom he wished; he exalted whom he wished and humbled whom he wished.
chapters.zh: 因上帝所赐他的大权，各方、各国、各族的人都在他面前战兢恐惧。他可以随意生杀，随意升降。

chapters.en: But when his heart became arrogant and his spirit was hardened with pride, he was deposed from his royal throne, and his glory was taken from him.
chapters.zh: 但他心高气傲，灵也刚愎，甚至行事狂傲，就被革去王位，夺去荣耀。

chapters.en: He was driven away from mankind, and his mind was like that of a beast. He lived with the wild donkeys and ate grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven until he acknowledged that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of mankind, setting over it whom He wishes.
chapters.zh: 他被赶出离开世人，他的心变如兽心，与野驴同居，吃草如牛，身被天露滴湿，等他知道至高的上帝在人的国中掌权，凭自己的意旨立人治国。

chapters.en: But you his son, O Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, even though you knew all this.
chapters.zh: 伯沙撒啊，你是他的儿子〔注：或译：孙子〕，你虽知道这一切，你心仍不自卑，

chapters.en: Instead, you have exalted yourself against the Lord of heaven. The vessels from His house were brought to you, and as you drank wine from them with your nobles, wives, and concubines, you praised your gods of silver and gold, bronze and iron, wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or understand. But you have failed to glorify the God who holds in His hand your very breath and all your ways.
chapters.zh: 竟向天上的主自高，使人将他殿中的器皿拿到你面前，你和大臣、皇后、妃嫔用这器皿饮酒。你又赞美那不能看、不能听、无知无识、金、银、铜、铁、木、石所造的神，却没有将荣耀归与那手中有你气息，管理你一切行动的上帝。

chapters.en: Therefore He sent the hand that wrote the inscription.
chapters.zh: 因此从上帝那里显出指头来写这文字。

chapters.en:
Now this is the inscription that was written:
MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN.
chapters.zh: 「所写的文字是：『弥尼，弥尼，提客勒，乌法珥新。』

chapters.en:
And this is the interpretation of the message:
MENE means that God has numbered the days of your reign and brought it to an end.
chapters.zh: 讲解是这样：弥尼，就是上帝已经数算你国的年日到此完毕。

chapters.en: TEKEL means that you have been weighed on the scales and found deficient.
chapters.zh: 提客勒，就是你被称在天平里，显出你的亏欠。

chapters.en: PERES means that your kingdom has been divided and given over to the Medes and Persians.”
chapters.zh: 毗勒斯〔注：与乌法珥新同义〕，就是你的国分裂，归与米底亚人和波斯人。」

chapters.en: Then Belshazzar gave the command, and they clothed Daniel in purple, placed a gold chain around his neck, and proclaimed him the third highest ruler in the kingdom.
chapters.zh: 伯沙撒下令，人就把紫袍给但以理穿上，把金鍊给他戴在颈项上，又传令使他在国中位列第三。

chapters.en: That very night Belshazzar king of the Chaldeans was slain,
chapters.zh: 当夜，迦勒底王伯沙撒被杀。

chapters.en: and Darius the Mede received the kingdom at the age of sixty-two.
chapters.zh: 米底亚人大流士年六十二岁，取了迦勒底国。

chapters.en: Now it pleased Darius to appoint 120 satraps to rule throughout the kingdom,
chapters.zh: 大流士随心所愿，立一百二十个总督，治理通国。

chapters.en: and over them three administrators, including Daniel, to whom these satraps were accountable so that the king would not suffer loss.
chapters.zh: 又在他们以上立总长三人（但以理在其中），使总督在他们三人面前回复事务，免得王受亏损。

chapters.en: Soon, by his extraordinary spirit, Daniel distinguished himself among the administrators and satraps. So the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.
chapters.zh: 因这但以理有美好的灵性，所以显然超乎其余的总长和总督，王又想立他治理通国。

chapters.en: Thus the administrators and satraps sought a charge against Daniel concerning the kingdom, but they could find no charge or corruption, because he was trustworthy, and no negligence or corruption was found in him.
chapters.zh: 那时，总长和总督寻找但以理误国的把柄，为要参他；只是找不着他的错误过失，因他忠心办事，毫无错误过失。

chapters.en: Finally these men said, “We will never find any charge against this Daniel unless we find something against him concerning the law of his God.”
chapters.zh: 那些人便说：「我们要找参这但以理的把柄，除非在他上帝的律法中就寻不着。」

chapters.en: So the administrators and satraps went together to the king and said, “O King Darius, may you live forever!
chapters.zh: 于是，总长和总督纷纷聚集来见王，说：「愿大流士王万岁！

chapters.en: All the royal administrators, prefects, satraps, advisers, and governors have agreed that the king should establish an ordinance and enforce a decree that for thirty days anyone who petitions any god or man except you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions.
chapters.zh: 国中的总长、钦差、总督、谋士，和巡抚彼此商议，要立一条坚定的禁令〔注：或译：求王下旨要立一条......〕，三十日内，不拘何人，若在王以外，或向神或向人求什么，就必扔在狮子坑中。

chapters.en: Therefore, O king, establish the decree and sign the document so that it cannot be changed—in accordance with the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed.”
chapters.zh: 王啊，现在求你立这禁令，加盖玉玺，使禁令决不更改；照米底亚和波斯人的例是不可更改的。」

chapters.en: Therefore King Darius signed the written decree.
chapters.zh: 于是大流士王立这禁令，加盖玉玺。

chapters.en: Now when Daniel learned that the document had been signed, he went into his house, where the windows of his upper room opened toward Jerusalem, and three times a day he got down on his knees, prayed, and gave thanks to his God, just as he had done before.
chapters.zh: 但以理知道这〔禁令〕盖了玉玺，就到自己家里（他楼上的窗户开向耶路撒冷），一日三次，双膝跪在他上帝面前，祷告感谢，与素常一样。

chapters.en: Then these men went as a group and found Daniel petitioning and imploring his God.
chapters.zh: 那些人就纷纷聚集，见但以理在他上帝面前祈祷恳求。

chapters.en:
So they approached the king and asked about his royal decree: “Did you not sign a decree that for thirty days any man who petitions any god or man except you, O king, will be thrown into the den of lions?”
The king replied, “According to the law of the Medes and Persians the order stands, and it cannot be repealed.”
chapters.zh: 他们便进到王前，提王的禁令，说：「王啊，三十日内不拘何人，若在王以外，或向神或向人求什么，必被扔在狮子坑中。王不是在这禁令上盖了玉玺吗？」王回答说：「实有这事，照米底亚和波斯人的例是不可更改的。」

chapters.en: Then they told the king, “Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah, shows no regard for you, O king, or for the decree that you have signed. He still makes his petition three times a day.”
chapters.zh: 他们对王说：「王啊，那被掳之犹大人中的但以理不理你，也不遵你盖了玉玺的禁令，他竟一日三次祈祷。」

chapters.en: As soon as the king heard this, he was deeply distressed and set his mind on delivering Daniel, and he labored until sundown to rescue him.
chapters.zh: 王听见这话，就甚愁烦，一心要救但以理，筹划解救他，直到日落的时候。

chapters.en: Then the men approached the king together and said to him, “Remember, O king, that by the law of the Medes and Persians no decree or ordinance established by the king can be changed.”
chapters.zh: 那些人就纷纷聚集来见王，说：「王啊，当知道米底亚人和波斯人有例，凡王所立的禁令和律例都不可更改。」

chapters.en:
So the king gave the order, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the den of lions.
The king said to Daniel, “May your God, whom you serve continually, deliver you!”
chapters.zh: 王下令，人就把但以理带来，扔在狮子坑中。王对但以理说：「你所常事奉的上帝，他必救你。」

chapters.en: A stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the rings of his nobles, so that nothing concerning Daniel could be changed.
chapters.zh: 有人搬石头放在坑口，王用自己的玺和大臣的印，封闭那坑，使惩办但以理的事毫无更改。

chapters.en: Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting. No entertainment was brought before him, and sleep fled from him.
chapters.zh: 王回宫，终夜禁食，无人拿乐器到他面前，并且睡不着觉。

chapters.en: At the first light of dawn, the king got up and hurried to the den of lions.
chapters.zh: 次日黎明，王就起来，急忙往狮子坑那里去。

chapters.en: When he reached the den, he cried out in a voice of anguish, “O Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to deliver you from the lions?”
chapters.zh: 临近坑边，哀声呼叫但以理，对但以理说：「永生上帝的仆人但以理啊，你所常事奉的上帝能救你脱离狮子吗？」

chapters.en: Then Daniel replied, “O king, may you live forever!
chapters.zh: 但以理对王说：「愿王万岁！

chapters.en: My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions. They have not hurt me, for I was found innocent in His sight, and I have done no wrong against you, O king.”
chapters.zh: 我的上帝差遣使者，封住狮子的口，叫狮子不伤我；因我在上帝面前无辜，我在王面前也没有行过亏损的事。」

chapters.en: The king was overjoyed and gave orders to lift Daniel out of the den, and when Daniel was lifted out of the den, no wounds whatsoever were found on him, because he had trusted in his God.
chapters.zh: 王就甚喜乐，吩咐人将但以理从坑里系上来。于是但以理从坑里被系上来，身上毫无伤损，因为信靠他的上帝。

chapters.en: At the command of the king, the men who had falsely accused Daniel were brought and thrown into the den of lions—they and their children and wives. And before they had reached the bottom of the den, the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
chapters.zh: 王下令，人就把那些控告但以理的人，连他们的妻子儿女都带来，扔在狮子坑中。他们还没有到坑底，狮子就抓住〔注：原文是胜了〕他们，咬碎他们的骨头。

chapters.en: Then King Darius wrote to the people of every nation and language throughout the land: “May your prosperity abound.
chapters.zh: 那时，大流士王传旨，晓谕住在全地各方、各国、各族的人说：「愿你们大享平安！

chapters.en:
I hereby decree that in every part of my kingdom, men are to tremble in fear before the God of Daniel:
For He is the living God, and He endures forever; His kingdom will never be destroyed, and His dominion will never end.
chapters.zh: 现在我降旨晓谕我所统辖的全国人民，要在但以理的上帝面前，战兢恐惧。 因为他是永远长存的活上帝， 他的国永不败坏； 他的权柄永存无极！

chapters.en:
He delivers and rescues; He performs signs and wonders
in the heavens and on the earth, for He has rescued Daniel from the power of the lions.”
chapters.zh: 他护庇人，搭救人， 在天上地下施行神迹奇事， 救了但以理脱离狮子的口。」

chapters.en: So Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
chapters.zh: 如此，这但以理，当大流士〔王〕在位的时候和波斯〔王〕塞鲁士在位的时候，大享亨通。

chapters.en: In the first year of the reign of Belshazzar over Babylon, Daniel had a dream, and visions passed through his mind as he lay on his bed. He wrote down the dream, and this is the summary of his account.
chapters.zh: 巴比伦王伯沙撒元年，但以理在床上做梦，见了脑中的异象，就记录这梦，述说其中的大意。

chapters.en: Daniel declared: “In my vision in the night I looked, and suddenly the four winds of heaven were churning up the great sea.
chapters.zh: 但以理说： 我夜里见异象，看见天的四风陡起，刮在大海之上。

chapters.en: Then four great beasts came up out of the sea, each one different from the others:
chapters.zh: 有四个大兽从海中上来，〔形状〕各有不同：

chapters.en: The first beast was like a lion, and it had the wings of an eagle. I watched until its wings were torn off and it was lifted up from the ground and made to stand on two feet like a man and given the mind of a man.
chapters.zh: 头一个像狮子，有鹰的翅膀；我正观看的时候，兽的翅膀被拔去，兽从地上得立起来，用两脚站立，像人一样，又得了人心。

chapters.en: Suddenly another beast appeared, which looked like a bear. It was raised up on one of its sides, and it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. So it was told, ‘Get up and gorge yourself on flesh!’
chapters.zh: 又有一兽如熊，就是第二兽，旁跨而坐，口齿内啣着三根肋骨。有吩咐这兽的说：「起来吞吃多肉。」

chapters.en: Next, as I watched, suddenly another beast appeared. It was like a leopard, and on its back it had four wings like those of a bird. The beast also had four heads, and it was given authority to rule.
chapters.zh: 此后我观看，又有一兽如豹，背上有鸟的四个翅膀；这兽有四个头，又得了权柄。

chapters.en: After this, as I watched in my vision in the night, suddenly a fourth beast appeared, and it was terrifying—dreadful and extremely strong—with large iron teeth. It devoured and crushed; then it trampled underfoot whatever was left. It was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.
chapters.zh: 其后我在夜间的异象中观看，见第四兽甚是可怕，极其强壮，大有力量，有大铁牙，吞吃嚼碎，所剩下的用脚践踏。这兽与前三兽大不相同，头有十角。

chapters.en: While I was contemplating the horns, suddenly another horn, a little one, came up among them, and three of the first horns were uprooted before it. This horn had eyes like those of a man and a mouth that spoke words of arrogance.
chapters.zh: 我正观看这些角，见其中又长起一个小角；先前的角中有三角在这角前，连根被牠拔出来。这角有眼，像人的眼，有口说夸大的话。

chapters.en:
As I continued to watch,
thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took His seat. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of His head was like pure wool. His throne was flaming with fire, and its wheels were all ablaze.
chapters.zh: 我观看， 见有宝座设立， 上头坐着亘古常在者。 他的衣服洁白如雪， 头发如纯净的羊毛。 宝座乃火焰， 其轮乃烈火。

chapters.en: A river of fire was flowing, coming out from His presence. Thousands upon thousands attended Him, and myriads upon myriads stood before Him. The court was convened, and the books were opened.
chapters.zh: 从他面前有火，像河发出； 事奉他的有千千， 在他面前侍立的有万万； 他坐着要行审判， 案卷都展开了。

chapters.en: Then I kept watching because of the arrogant words the horn was speaking. As I continued to watch, the beast was slain, and its body was destroyed and thrown into the blazing fire.
chapters.zh: 那时我观看，见那兽因小角说夸大话的声音被杀，身体损坏，扔在火中焚烧。

chapters.en: As for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was removed, but they were granted an extension of life for a season and a time.
chapters.zh: 其余的兽，权柄都被夺去，生命却仍存留，直到所定的时候和日期。

chapters.en:
In my vision in the night I continued to watch,
and I saw One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into His presence.
chapters.zh: 我在夜间的异象中观看， 见有一位像人子的， 驾着天云而来， 被领到亘古常在者面前，

chapters.en: And He was given dominion, glory, and kingship, that the people of every nation and language should serve Him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and His kingdom is one that will never be destroyed.
chapters.zh: 得了权柄、荣耀、国度， 使各方、各国、各族的人都事奉他。 他的权柄是永远的，不能废去； 他的国必不败坏。

chapters.en: I, Daniel, was grieved in my spirit, and the visions in my mind alarmed me.
chapters.zh: 至于我－但以理，我的灵在我里面愁烦，我脑中的异象使我惊惶。

chapters.en:
I approached one of those who were standing there, and I asked him the true meaning of all this.
So he told me the interpretation of these things:
chapters.zh: 我就近一位侍立者，问他这一切的真情。他就告诉我，将那事的讲解给我说明：

chapters.en: ‘These four great beasts are four kings who will arise from the earth.
chapters.zh: 这四个大兽就是四王将要在世上兴起。

chapters.en: But the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever—yes, forever and ever.’
chapters.zh: 然而，至高者的圣民，必要得国享受，直到永永远远。

chapters.en: Then I wanted to know the true meaning of the fourth beast, which was different from all the others—extremely terrifying—devouring and crushing with iron teeth and bronze claws, then trampling underfoot whatever was left.
chapters.zh: 那时我愿知道第四兽的真情，牠为何与那三兽的真情大不相同，甚是可怕，有铁牙铜爪，吞吃嚼碎，所剩下的用脚践踏；

chapters.en: I also wanted to know about the ten horns on its head and the other horn that came up, before which three of them fell—the horn whose appearance was more imposing than the others, with eyes and with a mouth that spoke words of arrogance.
chapters.zh: 头有十角和那另长的一角，在这角前有三角被牠打落。这角有眼，有说夸大话的口，形状强横，过于牠的同类。

chapters.en: As I watched, this horn was waging war against the saints and prevailing against them,
chapters.zh: 我观看，见这角与圣民争战，胜了他们。

chapters.en: until the Ancient of Days arrived and pronounced judgment in favor of the saints of the Most High, and the time came for them to possess the kingdom.
chapters.zh: 直到亘古常在者来给至高者的圣民伸冤，圣民得国的时候就到了。

chapters.en: This is what he said: ‘The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that will appear on the earth, different from all the other kingdoms, and it will devour the whole earth, trample it down, and crush it.
chapters.zh: 那侍立者这样说： 第四兽就是世上必有的第四国， 与一切国大不相同， 必吞吃全地， 并且践踏嚼碎。

chapters.en: And the ten horns are ten kings who will rise from this kingdom. After them another king, different from the earlier ones, will rise and subdue three kings.
chapters.zh: 至于那十角，就是从这国中必兴起的十王， 后来又兴起一王， 与先前的不同； 他必制伏三王。

chapters.en: He will speak out against the Most High and oppress the saints of the Most High, intending to change the appointed times and laws; and the saints will be given into his hand for a time, and times, and half a time.
chapters.zh: 他必向至高者说〔夸大的〕话， 必折磨至高者的圣民， 必想改变节期和律法。 圣民必交付他手一载、二载、半载。

chapters.en: But the court will convene, and his dominion will be taken away and completely destroyed forever.
chapters.zh: 然而，审判者必坐着行审判； 他的权柄必被夺去， 毁坏，灭绝，一直到底。

chapters.en: Then the sovereignty, dominion, and greatness of the kingdoms under all of heaven will be given to the people, the saints of the Most High. His kingdom will be an everlasting kingdom, and all rulers will serve and obey Him.’
chapters.zh: 国度、权柄，和天下诸国的大权 必赐给至高者的圣民。 他的国是永远的； 一切掌权的都必事奉他，顺从他。

chapters.en: Thus ends the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts troubled me greatly, and my face turned pale. But I kept the matter to myself.”
chapters.zh: 那事至此完毕。至于我－但以理，心中甚是惊惶，脸色也改变了，却将那事存记在心。

chapters.en: In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, subsequent to the one that had appeared to me earlier.
chapters.zh: 伯沙撒王在位第三年，有异象现与我－但以理，是在先前所见的异象之后。

chapters.en: And in the vision I saw myself in the citadel of Susa, in the province of Elam. I saw in the vision that I was beside the Ulai Canal.
chapters.zh: 我见了异象的时候，我〔以为〕在以拦省书珊城〔注：或译：宫〕中；我见异象又如在乌莱河边。

chapters.en: Then I lifted up my eyes and saw a ram with two horns standing beside the canal. The horns were long, but one was longer than the other, and the longer one grew up later.
chapters.zh: 我举目观看，见有双角的公绵羊站在河边，两角都高。这角高过那角，更高的是后长的。

chapters.en: I saw the ram charging toward the west and the north and the south. No animal could stand against him, and there was no deliverance from his power. He did as he pleased and became great.
chapters.zh: 我见那公绵羊往西、往北、往南牴触。兽在牠面前都站立不住，也没有能救护脱离牠手的；但牠任意而行，自高自大。

chapters.en: As I was contemplating all this, suddenly a goat with a prominent horn between his eyes came out of the west, crossing the surface of the entire earth without touching the ground.
chapters.zh: 我正思想的时候，见有一只公山羊从西而来，遍行全地，〔脚〕不沾尘。这山羊两眼当中有一非常的角。

chapters.en: He came toward the two-horned ram I had seen standing beside the canal and rushed at him with furious power.
chapters.zh: 牠往我所看见、站在河边有双角的公绵羊那里去，大发忿怒，向牠直闯。

chapters.en: I saw him approach the ram in a rage against him, and he struck the ram and shattered his two horns. The ram was powerless to stand against him, and the goat threw him to the ground and trampled him, and no one could deliver the ram from his power.
chapters.zh: 我见公山羊就近公绵羊，向牠发烈怒，牴触牠，折断牠的两角。绵羊在牠面前站立不住；牠将绵羊触倒在地，用脚践踏，没有能救绵羊脱离牠手的。

chapters.en: Thus the goat became very great, but at the height of his power, his large horn was broken off, and four prominent horns came up in its place, pointing toward the four winds of heaven.
chapters.zh: 这山羊极其自高自大，正强盛的时候，那大角折断了，又在角根上向天的四方〔注：原文是风〕长出四个非常的角来。

chapters.en: From one of these horns a little horn emerged and grew extensively toward the south and the east and toward the Beautiful Land.
chapters.zh: 四角之中有一角长出一个小角，向南、向东、向荣美之〔地〕，渐渐成为强大。

chapters.en: It grew as high as the host of heaven, and it cast down some of the host and some of the stars to the earth and trampled them.
chapters.zh: 牠渐渐强大，高及天象，将些天象和星宿抛落在地，用脚践踏。

chapters.en: It magnified itself, even to the Prince of the host; it removed His daily sacrifice and overthrew the place of His sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 并且牠自高自大，以为高及天象之君；除掉常献给君的〔燔祭〕，毁坏君的圣所。

chapters.en: And in the rebellion, the host and the daily sacrifice were given over to the horn, and it flung truth to the ground and prospered in whatever it did.
chapters.zh: 因罪过的缘故，有军旅和常献的〔燔祭〕交付牠。牠将真理抛在地上，〔任意〕而行，无不顺利。

chapters.en: Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to him, “How long until the fulfillment of the vision of the daily sacrifice, the rebellion that causes desolation, and the surrender of the sanctuary and of the host to be trampled?”
chapters.zh: 我听见有一位圣者说话，又有一位圣者问那说话的圣者说：「这〔除掉〕常献的〔燔祭〕和施行毁坏的罪过，将圣所与军旅〔注：或译：以色列的军〕践踏的异象，要到几时才〔应验〕呢？」

chapters.en: He said to me, “It will take 2,300 evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary will be properly restored.”
chapters.zh: 他对我说：「到二千三百日，圣所就必洁净。」

chapters.en: While I, Daniel, was watching the vision and trying to understand it, there stood before me one having the appearance of a man.
chapters.zh: 我－但以理见了这异象，愿意明白其中的意思。忽有一位形状像人的站在我面前。

chapters.en: And I heard the voice of a man calling from between the banks of the Ulai: “Gabriel, explain the vision to this man.”
chapters.zh: 我又听见乌莱河〔两岸〕中有人声呼叫说：「加百列啊，要使此人明白这异象。」

chapters.en:
As he came near to where I stood, I was terrified and fell facedown.
“Son of man,” he said to me, “understand that the vision concerns the time of the end.”
chapters.zh: 他便来到我所站的地方。他一来，我就惊慌俯伏在地；他对我说：「人子啊，你要明白，因为这是关乎末后的异象。」

chapters.en:
While he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground.
Then he touched me, helped me to my feet,
chapters.zh: 他与我说话的时候，我面伏在地沉睡；他就摸我，扶我站起来，

chapters.en: and said, “Behold, I will make known to you what will happen in the latter time of wrath, because it concerns the appointed time of the end.
chapters.zh: 说：「我要指示你恼怒临完必有的事，因为这是关乎末后的定期。

chapters.en: The two-horned ram that you saw represents the kings of Media and Persia.
chapters.zh: 你所看见双角的公绵羊，就是米底亚和波斯王。

chapters.en: The shaggy goat represents the king of Greece, and the large horn between his eyes is the first king.
chapters.zh: 那公山羊就是希腊王〔注：希腊：原文是雅完；下同〕；两眼当中的大角就是头一王。

chapters.en: The four horns that replaced the broken one represent four kingdoms that will rise from that nation but will not have the same power.
chapters.zh: 至于那折断了的角，在其根上又长出四角，这四角就是四国，必从这国里兴起来，只是权势都不及他。

chapters.en: In the latter part of their reign, when the rebellion has reached its full measure, an insolent king, skilled in intrigue, will come to the throne.
chapters.zh: 这四国末时，犯法的人罪恶满盈，必有一王兴起，面貌凶恶，能用双关的诈语。

chapters.en: His power will be great, but it will not be his own. He will cause terrible destruction and succeed in whatever he does. He will destroy the mighty men along with the holy people.
chapters.zh: 他的权柄必大，却不是因自己的能力；他必行非常的毁灭，事情顺利，〔任意〕而行；又必毁灭有能力的和圣民。

chapters.en: Through his craft and by his hand, he will cause deceit to prosper, and in his own mind he will make himself great. In a time of peace he will destroy many, and he will even stand against the Prince of princes. Yet he will be broken off, but not by human hands.
chapters.zh: 他用权术成就手中的诡计，心里自高自大，在人坦然无备的时候，毁灭多人；又要站起来攻击万君之君，至终却非因人手而灭亡。

chapters.en: The vision of the evenings and the mornings that has been spoken is true. Now you must seal up the vision, for it concerns the distant future.”
chapters.zh: 所说二千三百日的异象是真的，但你要将这异象封住，因为关乎〔后来〕许多的日子。」

chapters.en: I, Daniel, was exhausted and lay ill for days. Then I got up and went about the king’s business. I was confounded by the vision; it was beyond understanding.
chapters.zh: 于是我－但以理昏迷不醒，病了数日，然后起来办理王的事务。我因这异象惊奇，却无人能明白其中的意思。

chapters.en: In the first year of Darius son of Xerxes, a Mede by descent, who was made ruler over the kingdom of the Chaldeans —
chapters.zh: 米底亚族亚哈随鲁的儿子大流士立为迦勒底国的王元年，

chapters.en: in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the sacred books, according to the word of the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet, that the desolation of Jerusalem would last seventy years.
chapters.zh: 就是他在位第一年，我－但以理从书上得知耶和华的话临到先知耶利米，论耶路撒冷荒凉的年数，七十年为满。

chapters.en: So I turned my attention to the Lord God to seek Him by prayer and petition, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
chapters.zh: 我便禁食，披麻蒙灰，定意向主上帝祈祷恳求。

chapters.en: And I prayed to the LORD my God and confessed, “O, Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps His covenant of loving devotion to those who love Him and keep His commandments,
chapters.zh: 我向耶和华－我的上帝祈祷、认罪，说：「主啊，大而可畏的上帝，向爱主、守主诫命的人守约施慈爱。

chapters.en: we have sinned and done wrong. We have acted wickedly and rebelled. We have turned away from Your commandments and ordinances.
chapters.zh: 我们犯罪作孽，行恶叛逆，偏离你的诫命典章，

chapters.en: We have not listened to Your servants the prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings, leaders, fathers, and all the people of the land.
chapters.zh: 没有听从你仆人众先知奉你名向我们君王、首领、列祖，和国中一切百姓所说的话。

chapters.en: To You, O Lord, belongs righteousness, but this day we are covered with shame—the men of Judah, the people of Jerusalem, and all Israel near and far, in all the countries to which You have driven us because of our unfaithfulness to You.
chapters.zh: 主啊，你是公义的，我们是脸上蒙羞的；因我们犹大人和耶路撒冷的居民，并以色列众人，或在近处，或在远处，被你赶到各国的人，都得罪了你，正如今日一样。

chapters.en: O LORD, we are covered with shame—our kings, our leaders, and our fathers—because we have sinned against You.
chapters.zh: 主啊，我们和我们的君王、首领、列祖因得罪了你，就都脸上蒙羞。

chapters.en: To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness, even though we have rebelled against Him
chapters.zh: 主－我们的上帝是怜悯饶恕人的，我们却违背了他，

chapters.en: and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God to walk in His laws, which He set before us through His servants the prophets.
chapters.zh: 也没有听从耶和华－我们上帝的话，没有遵行他藉仆人众先知向我们所陈明的律法。

chapters.en: All Israel has transgressed Your law and turned away, refusing to obey Your voice; so the oath and the curse written in the Law of Moses the servant of God has been poured out on us, because we have sinned against You.
chapters.zh: 以色列众人都犯了你的律法，偏行，不听从你的话；因此，在你仆人摩西律法上所写的咒诅和誓言都倾在我们身上，因我们得罪了上帝。

chapters.en: You have carried out the words spoken against us and against our rulers by bringing upon us a great disaster. For under all of heaven, nothing has ever been done like what has been done to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 他使大灾祸临到我们，成就了警戒我们和审判我们官长的话；原来在普天之下未曾行过像在耶路撒冷所行的。

chapters.en: Just as it is written in the Law of Moses, all this disaster has come upon us, yet we have not sought the favor of the LORD our God by turning from our iniquities and giving attention to Your truth.
chapters.zh: 这一切灾祸临到我们身上是照摩西律法上所写的，我们却没有求耶和华－我们上帝的恩典，使我们回头离开罪孽，明白你的真理。

chapters.en: Therefore the LORD has kept the calamity in store and brought it upon us. For the LORD our God is righteous in all He does; yet we have not obeyed His voice.
chapters.zh: 所以耶和华留意使这灾祸临到我们身上，因为耶和华－我们的上帝在他所行的事上都是公义；我们并没有听从他的话。

chapters.en: Now, O Lord our God, who brought Your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, and who made for Yourself a name renowned to this day, we have sinned; we have acted wickedly.
chapters.zh: 主－我们的上帝啊，你曾用大能的手领你的子民出埃及地，使自己得了名，正如今日一样。我们犯了罪，作了恶。

chapters.en: O Lord, in keeping with all Your righteous acts, I pray that Your anger and wrath may turn away from Your city Jerusalem, Your holy mountain; for because of our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people are a reproach to all around us.
chapters.zh: 主啊，求你按你的大仁大义，使你的怒气和忿怒转离你的城耶路撒冷，就是你的圣山。耶路撒冷和你的子民，因我们的罪恶和我们列祖的罪孽被四围的人羞辱。

chapters.en: So now, our God, hear the prayers and petitions of Your servant. For Your sake, O Lord, cause Your face to shine upon Your desolate sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 我们的上帝啊，现在求你垂听仆人的祈祷恳求，为自己使脸光照你荒凉的圣所。

chapters.en: Incline Your ear, O my God, and hear; open Your eyes and see the desolation of the city that bears Your name. For we are not presenting our petitions before You because of our righteous acts, but because of Your great compassion.
chapters.zh: 我的上帝啊，求你侧耳而听，睁眼而看，〔眷顾〕我们荒凉〔之地〕和称为你名下的城。我们在你面前恳求，原不是因自己的义，乃因你的大怜悯。

chapters.en: O Lord, listen! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, hear and act! For Your sake, O my God, do not delay, because Your city and Your people bear Your name.”
chapters.zh: 求主垂听，求主赦免，求主应允而行，为你自己不要迟延。我的上帝啊，因这城和这民都是称为你名下的。」

chapters.en: While I was speaking, praying, confessing my sin and that of my people Israel, and presenting my petition before the LORD my God concerning His holy mountain—
chapters.zh: 我说话，祷告，承认我的罪和本国之民以色列的罪，为我上帝的圣山，在耶和华－我上帝面前恳求。

chapters.en: while I was still praying, Gabriel, the man I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight about the time of the evening sacrifice.
chapters.zh: 我正祷告的时候，先前在异象中所见的那位加百列，奉命迅速飞来，约在献晚祭的时候，按手在我身上。

chapters.en: He instructed me and spoke with me, saying: “O Daniel, I have come now to give you insight and understanding.
chapters.zh: 他指教我说：「但以理啊，现在我出来要使你有智慧，有聪明。

chapters.en: At the beginning of your petitions, an answer went out, and I have come to tell you, for you are highly precious. So consider the message and understand the vision:
chapters.zh: 你初恳求的时候，就发出命令，我来告诉你，因你大蒙眷爱；所以你要思想明白这〔以下的〕事和异象。

chapters.en: Seventy weeks are decreed for your people and your holy city to stop their transgression, to put an end to sin, to make atonement for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint the Most Holy Place.
chapters.zh: 「为你本国之民和你圣城，已经定了七十个七。要止住罪过，除净罪恶，赎尽罪孽，引进〔注：或译：彰显〕永义，封住异象和预言，并膏至圣者〔注：者：或译所〕。

chapters.en: Know and understand this: From the issuance of the decree to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until the Messiah, the Prince, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. It will be rebuilt with streets and a trench, but in times of distress.
chapters.zh: 你当知道，当明白，从出令重新建造耶路撒冷，直到有受膏君的时候，必有七个七和六十二个七。正在艰难的时候，耶路撒冷城连街带濠都必重新建造。

chapters.en:
Then after the sixty-two weeks the Messiah will be cut off and will have nothing.
Then the people of the prince who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. The end will come like a flood, and until the end there will be war; desolations have been decreed.
chapters.zh: 过了六十二个七，那〔注：或译：有〕受膏者必被剪除，一无所有；必有一王的民来毁灭这城和圣所，至终必如洪水冲没。必有争战，一直到底，荒凉的事已经定了。

chapters.en: And he will confirm a covenant with many for one week, but in the middle of the week he will put an end to sacrifice and offering. And on the wing of the temple will come the abomination that causes desolation, until the decreed destruction is poured out upon him. ”
chapters.zh: 一七之内，他必与许多人坚定盟约；一七之半，他必使祭祀与供献止息。那行毁坏可憎的〔注：或译：使地荒凉的〕如飞而来，并且有〔忿怒〕倾在那行毁坏的身上〔注：或译：倾在那荒凉之地〕，直到所定的结局。」

chapters.en: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a message was revealed to Daniel, who was called Belteshazzar. The message was true, and it concerned a great conflict. And the understanding of the message was given to him in a vision.
chapters.zh: 波斯王塞鲁士第三年，有事显给称为伯提沙撒的但以理。这事是真的，是指着大争战；但以理通达这事，明白这异象。

chapters.en: In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three full weeks.
chapters.zh: 当那时，我－但以理悲伤了三个七日。

chapters.en: I ate no rich food, no meat or wine entered my mouth, and I did not anoint myself with oil until the three weeks were completed.
chapters.zh: 美味我没有吃，酒肉没有入我的口，也没有用油抹我的身，直到满了三个七日。

chapters.en: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, as I was standing on the bank of the great river, the Tigris,
chapters.zh: 正月二十四日，我在底格里斯大河边，

chapters.en: I lifted up my eyes, and behold, there was a certain man dressed in linen, with a belt of fine gold from Uphaz around his waist.
chapters.zh: 举目观看，见有一人身穿细麻衣，腰束乌法精金带。

chapters.en: His body was like beryl, his face like the brilliance of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and legs like the gleam of polished bronze, and his voice like the sound of a multitude.
chapters.zh: 他身体如水苍玉，面貌如闪电，眼目如火把，手和脚如光明的铜，说话的声音如大众的声音。

chapters.en: Only I, Daniel, saw the vision; the men with me did not see it, but a great terror fell upon them, and they ran and hid themselves.
chapters.zh: 这异象惟有我－但以理一人看见，同着我的人没有看见。他们却大大战兢，逃跑隐藏，

chapters.en: So I was left alone, gazing at this great vision. No strength remained in me; my face grew deathly pale, and I was powerless.
chapters.zh: 只剩下我一人。我见了这大异象便浑身无力，面貌失色，毫无气力。

chapters.en: I heard the sound of his words, and as I listened, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground.
chapters.zh: 我却听见他说话的声音，一听见就面伏在地沉睡了。

chapters.en: Suddenly, a hand touched me and set me trembling on my hands and knees.
chapters.zh: 忽然，有一手按在我身上，使我用膝和手掌支持微起。

chapters.en:
He said to me, “Daniel, you are a man who is highly precious. Consider carefully the words that I am about to say to you. Stand up, for I have now been sent to you.”
And when he had said this to me, I stood up trembling.
chapters.zh: 他对我说：「大蒙眷爱的但以理啊，要明白我与你所说的话，只管站起来，因为我现在奉差遣来到你这里。」他对我说这话，我便战战兢兢地立起来。

chapters.en: “Do not be afraid, Daniel,” he said, “for from the first day that you purposed to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come in response to them.
chapters.zh: 他就说：「但以理啊，不要惧怕！因为从你第一日专心求明白〔将来的事〕，又在你上帝面前刻苦己心，你的言语已蒙应允；我是因你的言语而来。

chapters.en: However, the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, for I had been left there with the kings of Persia.
chapters.zh: 但波斯国的〔魔〕君拦阻我二十一日。忽然有大君〔注：就是天使长；二十一节同〕中的一位米迦勒来帮助我，我就停留在波斯诸王那里。

chapters.en: Now I have come to explain to you what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision concerns those days.”
chapters.zh: 现在我来，要使你明白本国之民日后必遭遇的事，因为这异象关乎后来〔许多的〕日子。」

chapters.en: While he was speaking these words to me, I set my face toward the ground and became speechless.
chapters.zh: 他向我这样说，我就脸面朝地，哑口无声。

chapters.en: And suddenly one with the likeness of a man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and said to the one standing before me, “My lord, because of the vision, I am overcome with anguish, and I have no strength.
chapters.zh: 不料，有一位像人的，摸我的嘴唇，我便开口向那站在我面前的说：「我主啊，因见这异象，我大大愁苦，毫无气力。

chapters.en: How can I, your servant, speak with you, my lord? Now I have no strength, nor is any breath left in me.”
chapters.zh: 我主的仆人怎能与我主说话呢？我〔一见异象〕就浑身无力，毫无气息。」

chapters.en: Again the one with the likeness of a man touched me and strengthened me.
chapters.zh: 有一位形状像人的又摸我，使我有力量。

chapters.en:
“Do not be afraid, you who are highly precious,” he said. “Peace be with you! Be strong now; be very strong!”
As he spoke with me, I was strengthened and said, “Speak, my lord, for you have strengthened me.”
chapters.zh: 他说：「大蒙眷爱的人哪，不要惧怕，愿你平安！你总要坚强。」他一向我说话，我便觉得有力量，说：「我主请说，因你使我有力量。」

chapters.en: “Do you know why I have come to you?” he said. “I must return at once to fight against the prince of Persia, and when I have gone forth, behold, the prince of Greece will come.
chapters.zh: 他就说：「你知道我为何来见你吗？现在我要回去与波斯的〔魔〕君争战，我去后，希腊〔注：原文是雅完〕的〔魔〕君必来。

chapters.en: But first I will tell you what is inscribed in the Book of Truth. Yet no one has the courage to support me against these, except Michael your prince.
chapters.zh: 但我要将那录在真确书上的事告诉你。除了你们的〔大〕君米迦勒之外，没有帮助我抵挡这两〔魔〕君的。」

chapters.en: “And I, in the first year of Darius the Mede, stood up to strengthen and protect him.
chapters.zh: 〔又说〕：「当米底亚王大流士元年，我曾起来扶助米迦勒，使他坚强。」

chapters.en: Now then, I will tell you the truth: Three more kings will arise in Persia, and then a fourth, who will be far richer than all the others. By the power of his wealth, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
chapters.zh: 现在我将真事指示你： 「波斯还有三王兴起，第四王必富足远胜诸王。他因富足成为强盛，就必激动大众攻击希腊国。

chapters.en: Then a mighty king will arise, who will rule with great authority and do as he pleases.
chapters.zh: 必有一个勇敢的王兴起，执掌大权，随意而行。

chapters.en: But as soon as he is established, his kingdom will be broken up and parceled out toward the four winds of heaven. It will not go to his descendants, nor will it have the authority with which he ruled, because his kingdom will be uprooted and given to others.
chapters.zh: 他兴起的时候，他的国必破裂，向天的四方〔注：方：原文是风〕分开，却不归他的后裔，治国的权势也都不及他；因为他的国必被拔出，归与他后裔之外的人。

chapters.en: The king of the South will grow strong, but one of his commanders will grow even stronger and will rule his own kingdom with great authority.
chapters.zh: 「南方的王必强盛，他将帅中必有一个比他更强盛，执掌权柄，他的权柄甚大。

chapters.en: After some years they will form an alliance, and the daughter of the king of the South will go to the king of the North to seal the agreement. But his daughter will not retain her position of power, nor will his strength endure. At that time she will be given up, along with her royal escort and her father and the one who supported her.
chapters.zh: 过些年后，他们必互相连合，南方王的女儿必就了北方王来立约；但这女子帮助之力存立不住，王和他所倚靠之力也不能存立。这女子和引导她来的，并生她的，以及当时扶助她的，都必交与〔死地〕。

chapters.en: But one from her family line will rise up in his place, come against the army of the king of the North, and enter his fortress, fighting and prevailing.
chapters.zh: 但这女子的本家〔注：原文是根〕必另生一子〔注：子：原文是枝〕继续王位，他必率领军队进入北方王的保障，攻击他们，而且得胜；

chapters.en: He will take even their gods captive to Egypt, with their metal images and their precious vessels of silver and gold. For some years he will stay away from the king of the North,
chapters.zh: 并将他们的神像和铸成的偶像，与金银的宝器掠到埃及去。数年之内，他不去攻击北方的王。

chapters.en: who will invade the realm of the king of the South and then return to his own land.
chapters.zh: 北方的王〔注：原文是他〕必入南方王的国，却要仍回本地。

chapters.en: But his sons will stir up strife and assemble a great army, which will advance forcefully, sweeping through like a flood, and will again carry the battle as far as his fortress.
chapters.zh: 「北方王〔注：原文是他〕的二子必动干戈，招聚许多军兵。这军兵前去，如洪水泛滥，又必再去争战，直到南方王的保障。

chapters.en: In a rage, the king of the South will march out to fight the king of the North, who will raise a large army, but it will be delivered into the hand of his enemy.
chapters.zh: 南方王必发烈怒，出来与北方王争战，摆列大军；北方王的军兵必交付他手。

chapters.en: When the army is carried off, the king of the South will be proud in heart and will cast down tens of thousands, but he will not triumph.
chapters.zh: 他的众军高傲，他的心也必自高；他虽使数万人仆倒，却不得〔常〕胜。

chapters.en: For the king of the North will raise another army, larger than the first, and after some years he will advance with a great army and many supplies.
chapters.zh: 「北方王必回来摆列大军，比先前的更多。满了所定的年数，他必率领大军，带极多的军装来。

chapters.en: In those times many will rise up against the king of the South. Violent ones among your own people will exalt themselves in fulfillment of the vision, but they will fail.
