chapters.en: “Do not tell anyone,” Jesus instructed him. “But go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣嘱咐他：「你切不可告诉人，只要去把身体给祭司察看，又要为你得了洁净，照摩西所吩咐的献上〔礼物〕，对众人作证据。」

chapters.en: But the news about Jesus spread all the more, and great crowds came to hear Him and to be healed of their sicknesses.
chapters.zh: 但耶稣的名声越发传扬出去。有极多的人聚集来听道，也指望医治他们的病。

chapters.en: Yet He frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray.
chapters.zh: 耶稣却退到旷野去祷告。

chapters.en: One day Jesus was teaching, and the Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. People had come from Jerusalem and from every village of Galilee and Judea, and the power of the Lord was present for Him to heal the sick.
chapters.zh: 有一天，耶稣教训人，有法利赛人和教法师在旁边坐着；他们是从加利利各乡村和犹太并耶路撒冷来的。主的能力与耶稣同在，使他能医治病人。

chapters.en: Just then some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. They tried to bring him inside to set him before Jesus,
chapters.zh: 有人用褥子抬着一个瘫子，要抬进去放在耶稣面前，

chapters.en: but they could not find a way through the crowd. So they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the crowd, right in front of Jesus.
chapters.zh: 却因人多，寻不出法子抬进去，就上了房顶，从瓦间把他连褥子缒到当中，正在耶稣面前。

chapters.en: When Jesus saw their faith, He said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣见他们的信心，就对瘫子说：「你的罪赦了。」

chapters.en: But the scribes and Pharisees began thinking to themselves, “Who is this man who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
chapters.zh: 文士和法利赛人就议论说：「这说僭妄话的是谁？除了上帝以外，谁能赦罪呢？」

chapters.en: Knowing what they were thinking, Jesus replied, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?
chapters.zh: 耶稣知道他们所议论的，就说：「你们心里议论的是什么呢？

chapters.en: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
chapters.zh: 或说『你的罪赦了』，或说『你起来行走』，哪一样容易呢？

chapters.en: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic, “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
chapters.zh: 但要叫你们知道，人子在地上有赦罪的权柄。」就对瘫子说：「我吩咐你，起来，拿你的褥子回家去吧！」

chapters.en: And immediately the man stood up before them, took what he had been lying on, and went home glorifying God.
chapters.zh: 那人当众人面前立刻起来，拿着他所躺卧的〔褥子〕回家去，归荣耀与上帝。

chapters.en: Everyone was taken with amazement and glorified God. They were filled with awe and said, “We have seen remarkable things today.”
chapters.zh: 众人都惊奇，也归荣耀与上帝，并且满心惧怕，说：「我们今日看见非常的事了。」

chapters.en: After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him,
chapters.zh: 这事以后，耶稣出去，看见一个税吏，名叫利未，坐在税关上，就对他说：「你跟从我来。」

chapters.en: and Levi got up, left everything, and followed Him.
chapters.zh: 他就撇下所有的，起来，跟从了耶稣。

chapters.en: Then Levi hosted a great banquet for Jesus at his house. A large crowd of tax collectors was there, along with others who were eating with them.
chapters.zh: 利未在自己家里为耶稣大摆筵席，有许多税吏和别人与他们一同坐席。

chapters.en: But the Pharisees and their scribes complained to Jesus’ disciples, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
chapters.zh: 法利赛人和文士就向耶稣的门徒发怨言说：「你们为什么和税吏并罪人一同吃喝呢？」

chapters.en: Jesus answered, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他们说：「无病的人用不着医生；有病的人才用得着。

chapters.en: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.”
chapters.zh: 我来本不是召义人悔改，乃是召罪人悔改。」

chapters.en: Then they said to Him, “John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees frequently fast and pray, but Yours keep on eating and drinking.”
chapters.zh: 他们说：「约翰的门徒屡次禁食祈祷，法利赛人的〔门徒〕也是这样；惟独你的门徒又吃又喝。」

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “Can you make the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them?
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他们说：「新郎和陪伴之人同在的时候，岂能叫陪伴之人禁食呢？

chapters.en: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.”
chapters.zh: 但日子将到，新郎要离开他们，那日他们就要禁食了。」

chapters.en: He also told them a parable: “No one tears a piece of cloth from a new garment and sews it on an old one. If he does, he will tear the new garment as well, and the patch from the new will not match the old.
chapters.zh: 耶稣又设一个比喻，对他们说：「没有人把新衣服撕下一块来补在旧衣服上；若是这样，就把新的撕破了，并且所撕下来的那块新的和旧的也不相称。

chapters.en: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the skins, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined.
chapters.zh: 也没有人把新酒装在旧皮袋里；若是这样，新酒必将皮袋裂开，酒便漏出来，皮袋也就坏了。

chapters.en: Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.
chapters.zh: 但新酒必须装在新皮袋里。

chapters.en: And no one after drinking old wine wants new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’”
chapters.zh: 没有人喝了陈酒又想喝新的；他总说陈的好。」

chapters.en: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain, rub them in their hands, and eat them.
chapters.zh: 有一个安息日，耶稣从麦地经过。他的门徒掐了麦穗，用手搓着吃。

chapters.en: But some of the Pharisees asked, “Why are you doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?”
chapters.zh: 有几个法利赛人说：「你们为什么做安息日不可做的事呢？」

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他们说：「〔经上记着〕大卫和跟从他的人饥饿之时所做的事，连这个你们也没有念过吗？

chapters.en: He entered the house of God, took the consecrated bread and gave it to his companions, and ate what is lawful only for the priests to eat.”
chapters.zh: 他怎么进了上帝的殿，拿陈设饼吃，又给跟从的人吃？这饼除了祭司以外，别人都不可吃。」

chapters.en: Then Jesus declared, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
chapters.zh: 又对他们说：「人子是安息日的主。」

chapters.en: On another Sabbath Jesus entered the synagogue and was teaching, and a man was there whose right hand was withered.
chapters.zh: 又有一个安息日，耶稣进了会堂教训人，在那里有一个人右手枯干了。

chapters.en: Looking for a reason to accuse Jesus, the scribes and Pharisees were watching Him closely to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.
chapters.zh: 文士和法利赛人窥探耶稣，在安息日治病不治病，要得把柄去告他。

chapters.en: But Jesus knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand, “Get up and stand among us.” So he got up and stood there.
chapters.zh: 耶稣却知道他们的意念，就对那枯干一只手的人说：「起来！站在当中。」那人就起来，站着。

chapters.en: Then Jesus said to them, “I ask you, which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?”
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他们说：「我问你们，在安息日行善行恶，救命害命，哪样是可以的呢？」

chapters.en: And after looking around at all of them, He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and it was restored.
chapters.zh: 他就周围看着他们众人，对那人说：「伸出手来！」他把手一伸，手就复了原。

chapters.en: But the scribes and Pharisees were filled with rage and began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus.
chapters.zh: 他们就满心大怒，彼此商议怎样处治耶稣。

chapters.en: In those days Jesus went out to the mountain to pray, and He spent the night in prayer to God.
chapters.zh: 那时，耶稣出去，上山祷告，整夜祷告上帝；

chapters.en: When daylight came, He called His disciples to Him and chose twelve of them, whom He also designated as apostles:
chapters.zh: 到了天亮，叫他的门徒来，就从他们中间挑选十二个人，称他们为使徒。

chapters.en: Simon, whom He named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew;
chapters.zh: 〔这十二个人〕有西门（耶稣又给他起名叫彼得），还有他兄弟安得烈，又有雅各和约翰，腓力和巴多罗买，

chapters.en: Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus and Simon called the Zealot;
chapters.zh: 马太和多马，亚勒腓的儿子雅各和奋锐党的西门，

chapters.en: Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.
chapters.zh: 雅各的儿子〔注：或译：兄弟〕犹大，和卖主的加略人犹大。

chapters.en: Then Jesus came down with them and stood on a level place. A large crowd of His disciples was there, along with a great number of people from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon.
chapters.zh: 耶稣和他们下了山，站在一块平地上；同站的有许多门徒，又有许多百姓，从犹太全地和耶路撒冷，并泰尔、西顿的海边来，都要听他〔讲道〕，又指望医治他们的病；

chapters.en: They had come to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases, and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed.
chapters.zh: 还有被污鬼缠磨的，也得了医治。

chapters.en: The entire crowd was trying to touch Him, because power was coming from Him and healing them all.
chapters.zh: 众人都想要摸他；因为有能力从他身上发出来，医好了他们。

chapters.en:
Looking up at His disciples, Jesus said:
“Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.
chapters.zh: 耶稣举目看着门徒，说： 你们贫穷的人有福了！ 因为上帝的国是你们的。

chapters.en: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
chapters.zh: 你们饥饿的人有福了！ 因为你们将要饱足。 你们哀哭的人有福了！ 因为你们将要喜笑。

chapters.en: Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.
chapters.zh: 「人为人子恨恶你们，拒绝你们，辱骂你们，弃掉你们的名，以为是恶，你们就有福了！

chapters.en: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven. For their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.
chapters.zh: 当那日，你们要〔欢喜〕跳跃，因为你们在天上的赏赐是大的。他们的祖宗待先知也是这样。

chapters.en: But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort.
chapters.zh: 但你们富足的人有祸了！ 因为你们受过你们的安慰。

chapters.en: Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
chapters.zh: 你们饱足的人有祸了！ 因为你们将要饥饿。 你们喜笑的人有祸了！ 因为你们将要哀恸哭泣。

chapters.en: Woe to you when all men speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way.
chapters.zh: 「人都说你们好的时候，你们就有祸了！因为他们的祖宗待假先知也是这样。」

chapters.en: But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
chapters.zh: 「只是我告诉你们这听道的人，你们的仇敌，要爱他！恨你们的，要待他好！

chapters.en: bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
chapters.zh: 咒诅你们的，要为他祝福！凌辱你们的，要为他祷告！

chapters.en: If someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also. And if someone takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic as well.
chapters.zh: 有人打你这边的脸，连那边的脸也由他打。有人夺你的外衣，连里衣也由他拿去。

chapters.en: Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back.
chapters.zh: 凡求你的，就给他。有人夺你的东西去，不用再要回来。

chapters.en: Do to others as you would have them do to you.
chapters.zh: 你们愿意人怎样待你们，你们也要怎样待人。

chapters.en: If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.
chapters.zh: 你们若单爱那爱你们的人，有什么可酬谢的呢？就是罪人也爱那爱他们的人。

chapters.en: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.
chapters.zh: 你们若善待那善待你们的人，有什么可酬谢的呢？就是罪人也是这样行。

chapters.en: And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full.
chapters.zh: 你们若借给人，指望从他收回，有什么可酬谢的呢？就是罪人也借给罪人，要如数收回。

chapters.en: But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return. Then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High; for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.
chapters.zh: 你们倒要爱仇敌，也要善待他们，并要借给人不指望偿还，你们的赏赐就必大了，你们也必作至高者的儿子，因为他恩待那忘恩的和作恶的。

chapters.en: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
chapters.zh: 你们要慈悲，像你们的父慈悲一样。」

chapters.en: Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 「你们不要论断人，就不被论断；你们不要定人的罪，就不被定罪；你们要饶恕人，就必蒙饶恕〔注：饶恕：原文是释放〕；

chapters.en: Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you.”
chapters.zh: 你们要给人，就必有给你们的，并且用十足的升斗，连摇带按，上尖下流地倒在你们怀里；因为你们用什么量器量给人，也必用什么量器量给你们。」

chapters.en: Jesus also told them a parable: “Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?
chapters.zh: 耶稣又用比喻对他们说：「瞎子岂能领瞎子，两个人不是都要掉在坑里吗？

chapters.en: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.
chapters.zh: 学生不能高过先生；凡学成了的不过和先生一样。

chapters.en: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?
chapters.zh: 为什么看见你弟兄眼中有刺，却不想自己眼中有梁木呢？

chapters.en: How can you say, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while you yourself fail to see the beam in your own eye? You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
chapters.zh: 你不见自己眼中有梁木，怎能对你弟兄说：『容我去掉你眼中的刺』呢？你这假冒为善的人！先去掉自己眼中的梁木，然后才能看得清楚，去掉你弟兄眼中的刺。」

chapters.en: No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit.
chapters.zh: 「因为，没有好树结坏果子，也没有坏树结好果子。

chapters.en: For each tree is known by its own fruit. Indeed, figs are not gathered from thornbushes, nor grapes from brambles.
chapters.zh: 凡树木看果子，就可以认出它来。人不是从荆棘上摘无花果，也不是从蒺藜里摘葡萄。

chapters.en: The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart, and the evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his heart. For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks.
chapters.zh: 善人从他心里所存的善就发出善来；恶人从他〔心里〕所存的恶就发出恶来；因为心里所充满的，口里就说出来。」

chapters.en: Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ but do not do what I say?
chapters.zh: 「你们为什么称呼我『主啊，主啊』却不遵我的话行呢？

chapters.en: I will show you what he is like who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them:
chapters.zh: 凡到我这里来，听见我的话就去行的，我要告诉你们他像什么人：

chapters.en: He is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock. When the flood came, the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it, because it was well built.
chapters.zh: 他像一个人盖房子，深深地挖地，把根基安在磐石上；到发大水的时候，水冲那房子，房子总不能摇动，因为根基立在磐石上〔注：有古卷：因为盖造得好〕。

chapters.en: But the one who hears My words and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on ground without a foundation. The torrent crashed against that house, and immediately it fell—and great was its destruction!”
chapters.zh: 惟有听见不去行的，就像一个人在土地上盖房子，没有根基；水一冲，随即倒塌了，并且那房子坏的很大。」

chapters.en: When Jesus had concluded His discourse in the hearing of the people, He went to Capernaum.
chapters.zh: 耶稣对百姓讲完了这一切的话，就进了迦百农。

chapters.en: There a highly valued servant of a centurion was sick and about to die.
chapters.zh: 有一个百夫长所宝贵的仆人害病，快要死了。

chapters.en: When the centurion heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to ask Him to come and heal his servant.
chapters.zh: 百夫长风闻耶稣的事，就讬犹太人的几个长老去求耶稣来救他的仆人。

chapters.en: They came to Jesus and pleaded with Him earnestly, “This man is worthy to have You grant this,
chapters.zh: 他们到了耶稣那里，就切切地求他说：「你给他行这事是他所配得的；

chapters.en: for he loves our nation and has built our synagogue.”
chapters.zh: 因为他爱我们的百姓，给我们建造会堂。」

chapters.en: So Jesus went with them. But when He was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends with the message: “Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof.
chapters.zh: 耶稣就和他们同去。离那家不远，百夫长讬几个朋友去见耶稣，对他说：「主啊！不要劳动；因你到我舍下，我不敢当。

chapters.en: That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to You. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
chapters.zh: 我也自以为不配去见你，只要你说一句话，我的仆人就必好了。

chapters.en: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”
chapters.zh: 因为我在人的权下，也有兵在我以下，对这个说：『去！』他就去；对那个说：『来！』他就来；对我的仆人说：『你做这事！』他就去做。」

chapters.en: When Jesus heard this, He marveled at the centurion. Turning to the crowd following Him, He said, “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣听见这话，就希奇他，转身对跟随的众人说：「我告诉你们，这么大的信心，就是在以色列中，我也没有遇见过。」

chapters.en: And when the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant in good health.
chapters.zh: 那讬来的人回到百夫长家里，看见仆人已经好了。

chapters.en: Soon afterward, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd.
chapters.zh: 过了不多时〔注：有古卷：次日〕，耶稣往一座城去，这城名叫拿因，他的门徒和极多的人与他同行。

chapters.en: As He approached the town gate, He saw a dead man being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. And a large crowd from the town was with her.
chapters.zh: 将近城门，有一个死人被抬出来。这人是他母亲独生的儿子；他母亲又是寡妇。有城里的许多人同着寡妇送殡。

chapters.en: When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her and said, “Do not weep.”
chapters.zh: 主看见那寡妇，就怜悯她，对她说：「不要哭！」

chapters.en: Then He went up and touched the coffin, and those carrying it stood still. “Young man,” He said, “I tell you, get up!”
chapters.zh: 于是进前按着杠，抬的人就站住了。耶稣说：「少年人，我吩咐你，起来！」

chapters.en: And the dead man sat up and began to speak! Then Jesus gave him back to his mother.
chapters.zh: 那死人就坐起，并且说话。耶稣便把他交给他母亲。

chapters.en: A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God. “A great prophet has appeared among us!” they said. “God has visited His people!”
chapters.zh: 众人都惊奇，归荣耀与上帝，说：「有大先知在我们中间兴起来了！」又说：「上帝眷顾了他的百姓！」

chapters.en: And the news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region.
chapters.zh: 他这事的风声就传遍了犹太和周围地方。

chapters.en: Then John’s disciples informed him about all these things.
chapters.zh: 约翰的门徒把这些事都告诉约翰。

chapters.en: So John called two of his disciples and sent them to ask the Lord, “Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?”
chapters.zh: 他便叫了两个门徒来，打发他们到主那里去，说：「那将要来的是你吗？还是我们等候别人呢？」

chapters.en: When the men came to Jesus, they said, “John the Baptist sent us to ask, ‘Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?’”
chapters.zh: 那两个人来到耶稣那里，说：「施洗的约翰打发我们来问你：『那将要来的是你吗？还是我们等候别人呢？』」

chapters.en: At that very hour Jesus healed many people of their diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and He gave sight to many who were blind.
chapters.zh: 正当那时候，耶稣治好了许多有疾病的，受灾患的，被恶鬼附着的，又开恩叫好些瞎子能看见。

chapters.en: So He replied, “Go back and report to John what you have seen and heard: The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说：「你们去，把所看见所听见的事告诉约翰，就是瞎子看见，瘸子行走，长大痲疯的洁净，聋子听见，死人复活，穷人有福音传给他们。

chapters.en: Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me. ”
chapters.zh: 凡不因我跌倒的，就有福了！」

chapters.en: After John’s messengers had left, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?
chapters.zh: 约翰所差来的人既走了，耶稣就对众人讲论约翰说：「你们从前出去到旷野，是要看什么呢？要看风吹动的芦苇吗？

chapters.en: Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in palaces.
chapters.zh: 你们出去，到底是要看什么？要看穿细软衣服的人吗？那穿华丽衣服、宴乐度日的人是在王宫里。

chapters.en: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
chapters.zh: 你们出去，究竟是要看什么？要看先知吗？我告诉你们，是的，他比先知大多了。

chapters.en:
This is the one about whom it is written:
‘Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.’
chapters.zh: 〔经上〕记着说：『我要差遣我的使者在你前面预备道路』，所说的就是这个人。

chapters.en: I tell you, among those born of women there is no one greater than John, yet even the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，凡妇人所生的，没有一个大过约翰的；然而上帝国里最小的比他还大。」

chapters.en: All the people who heard this, even the tax collectors, acknowledged God’s justice. For they had received the baptism of John.
chapters.zh: 众百姓和税吏既受过约翰的洗，听见这话，就以上帝为义；

chapters.en: But the Pharisees and experts in the law rejected God’s purpose for themselves, because they had not been baptized by John.
chapters.zh: 但法利赛人和律法师没有受过约翰的洗，竟为自己废弃了上帝的旨意。〔注：29－30两节或译：众百姓和税吏听见了约翰的话，就受了他的洗，便以上帝为义；但法利赛人和律法师不受约翰的洗，竟为自己废弃了上帝的旨意。〕

chapters.en: “To what, then, can I compare the men of this generation? What are they like?
chapters.zh: 〔主又说〕：「这样，我可用什么比这世代的人呢？他们好像什么呢？

chapters.en:
They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another:
‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep.’
chapters.zh: 好像孩童坐在街市上，彼此呼叫说： 我们向你们吹笛， 你们不跳舞； 我们向你们举哀， 你们不啼哭。

chapters.en: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon!’
chapters.zh: 施洗的约翰来，不吃饼，不喝酒，你们说他是被鬼附着的。

chapters.en: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
chapters.zh: 人子来，也吃也喝，你们说他是贪食好酒的人，是税吏和罪人的朋友。

chapters.en: But wisdom is vindicated by all her children.”
chapters.zh: 但智慧之子都以智慧为是。」

chapters.en: Then one of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him, and He entered the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table.
chapters.zh: 有一个法利赛人请耶稣和他吃饭；耶稣就到法利赛人家里去坐席。

chapters.en: When a sinful woman from that town learned that Jesus was dining there, she brought an alabaster jar of perfume.
chapters.zh: 那城里有一个女人，是个罪人，知道耶稣在法利赛人家里坐席，就拿着盛香膏的玉瓶，

chapters.en: As she stood behind Him at His feet weeping, she began to wet His feet with her tears and wipe them with her hair. Then she kissed His feet and anointed them with the perfume.
chapters.zh: 站在耶稣背后，挨着他的脚哭，眼泪湿了耶稣的脚，就用自己的头发擦干，又用嘴连连亲他的脚，把香膏抹上。

chapters.en: When the Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, He would know who this is and what kind of woman is touching Him—for she is a sinner!”
chapters.zh: 请耶稣的法利赛人看见这事，心里说：「这人若是先知，必知道摸他的是谁，是个怎样的女人；乃是个罪人。」

chapters.en:
But Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to tell you.”
“Tell me, Teacher,” he said.
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他说：「西门！我有句话要对你说。」西门说：「夫子，请说。」

chapters.en: “Two men were debtors to a certain moneylender. One owed him five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
chapters.zh: 〔耶稣说〕：「一个债主有两个人欠他的债；一个欠五十两银子，一个欠五两银子；

chapters.en: When they were unable to repay him, he forgave both of them. Which one, then, will love him more?”
chapters.zh: 因为他们无力偿还，债主就开恩免了他们两个人的债。这两个人哪一个更爱他呢？」

chapters.en:
“I suppose the one who was forgiven more,” Simon replied.
“You have judged correctly,” Jesus said.
chapters.zh: 西门回答说：「我想是那多得恩免的人。」耶稣说：「你断的不错。」

chapters.en: And turning toward the woman, He said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? When I entered your house, you did not give Me water for My feet, but she wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
chapters.zh: 于是转过来向着那女人，便对西门说：「你看见这女人吗？我进了你的家，你没有给我水洗脚；但这女人用眼泪湿了我的脚，用头发擦干。

chapters.en: You did not greet Me with a kiss, but she has not stopped kissing My feet since I arrived.
chapters.zh: 你没有与我亲嘴；但这女人从我进来的时候就不住地用嘴亲我的脚。

chapters.en: You did not anoint My head with oil, but she has anointed My feet with perfume.
chapters.zh: 你没有用油抹我的头；但这女人用香膏抹我的脚。

chapters.en: Therefore I tell you, her many sins have been forgiven, for she has loved much. But he who has been forgiven little loves little.”
chapters.zh: 所以我告诉你，她许多的罪都赦免了，因为她的爱多；但那赦免少的，他的爱就少。」

chapters.en: Then Jesus said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
chapters.zh: 于是对那女人说：「你的罪赦免了。」

chapters.en: But those at the table began to say to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
chapters.zh: 同席的人心里说：「这是什么人，竟赦免人的罪呢？」

chapters.en: And Jesus told the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣对那女人说：「你的信救了你；平平安安回去吧！」

chapters.en: Soon afterward, Jesus traveled from one town and village to another, preaching and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God. The Twelve were with Him,
chapters.zh: 过了不多日，耶稣周游各城各乡传道，宣讲上帝国的福音。和他同去的有十二个门徒，

chapters.en: as well as some women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
chapters.zh: 还有被恶鬼所附、被疾病所累、已经治好的几个妇女，内中有称为抹大拉的马利亚（曾有七个鬼从她身上赶出来），

chapters.en: Joanna the wife of Herod’s household manager Chuza, Susanna, and many others. These women were ministering to them out of their own means.
chapters.zh: 又有希律的家宰苦撒的妻子约亚拿，并苏撒拿，和好些别的妇女，都是用自己的财物供给耶稣和门徒。

chapters.en: While a large crowd was gathering and people were coming to Jesus from town after town, He told them this parable:
chapters.zh: 当许多人聚集、又有人从各城里出来见耶稣的时候，耶稣就用比喻说：

chapters.en: “A farmer went out to sow his seed. And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, where it was trampled, and the birds of the air devoured it.
chapters.zh: 「有一个撒种的出去撒种。撒的时候，有落在路旁的，被人践踏，天上的飞鸟又来吃尽了。

chapters.en: Some fell on rocky ground, and when it came up, the seedlings withered because they had no moisture.
chapters.zh: 有落在磐石上的，一出来就枯干了，因为得不着滋润。

chapters.en: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up with it and choked the seedlings.
chapters.zh: 有落在荆棘里的，荆棘一同生长，把它挤住了。

chapters.en:
Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprang up and produced a crop—a hundredfold.”
As Jesus said this, He called out, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
chapters.zh: 又有落在好土里的，生长起来，结实百倍。」耶稣说了这些话，就大声说：「有耳可听的，就应当听！」

chapters.en: Then His disciples asked Him what this parable meant.
chapters.zh: 门徒问耶稣说：「这比喻是什么意思呢？」

chapters.en:
He replied, “The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to others I speak in parables, so that,
‘though seeing, they may not see; though hearing, they may not understand.’
chapters.zh: 他说：「上帝国的奥祕只叫你们知道；至于别人，就用比喻，叫他们看也看不见，听也听不明。」

chapters.en: Now this is the meaning of the parable: The seed is the word of God.
chapters.zh: 「这比喻乃是这样：种子就是上帝的道。

chapters.en: The seeds along the path are those who hear, but the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.
chapters.zh: 那些在路旁的，就是人听了道，随后魔鬼来，从他们心里把道夺去，恐怕他们信了得救。

chapters.en: The seeds on rocky ground are those who hear the word and receive it with joy, but they have no root. They believe for a season, but in the time of testing, they fall away.
chapters.zh: 那些在磐石上的，就是人听道，欢喜领受，但心中没有根，不过暂时相信，及至遇见试炼就退后了。

chapters.en: The seeds that fell among the thorns are those who hear, but as they go on their way, they are choked by the worries, riches, and pleasures of this life, and their fruit does not mature.
chapters.zh: 那落在荆棘里的，就是人听了道，走开以后，被今生的思虑、钱财、宴乐挤住了，便结不出成熟的子粒来。

chapters.en: But the seeds on good soil are those with a noble and good heart, who hear the word, cling to it, and by persevering produce a crop.
chapters.zh: 〔那落〕在好土里的，就是人听了道，持守在诚实善良的心里，并且忍耐着结实。」

chapters.en: No one lights a lamp and covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.
chapters.zh: 「没有人点灯用器皿盖上，或放在床底下，乃是放在灯台上，叫进来的人看见亮光。

chapters.en: For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be made known and brought to light.
chapters.zh: 因为掩藏的事没有不显出来的；隐瞒的事没有不露出来被人知道的。

chapters.en: Pay attention, therefore, to how you listen. Whoever has will be given more, but whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him.”
chapters.zh: 所以，你们应当小心怎样听；因为凡有的，还要加给他；凡没有的，连他自以为有的，也要夺去。」

chapters.en: Then Jesus’ mother and brothers came to see Him, but they were unable to reach Him because of the crowd.
chapters.zh: 耶稣的母亲和他弟兄来了，因为人多，不得到他跟前。

chapters.en: He was told, “Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see You.”
chapters.zh: 有人告诉他说：「你母亲和你弟兄站在外边，要见你。」

chapters.en: But He replied, “My mother and brothers are those who hear the word of God and carry it out.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说：「听了上帝之道而遵行的人就是我的母亲，我的弟兄了。」

chapters.en: One day Jesus said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.” So He got into a boat with them and set out.
chapters.zh: 有一天，耶稣和门徒上了船，对门徒说：「我们可以渡到湖那边去。」他们就开了船。

chapters.en: As they sailed, He fell asleep, and a windstorm came down on the lake, so that the boat was being swamped, and they were in great danger.
chapters.zh: 正行的时候，耶稣睡着了。湖上忽然起了暴风，船将满了〔水〕，甚是危险。

chapters.en:
The disciples went and woke Him, saying, “Master, Master, we are perishing!”
Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the raging waters, and they subsided, and all was calm.
chapters.zh: 门徒来叫醒了他，说：「夫子！夫子！我们丧命啦！」耶稣醒了，斥责那狂风大浪；风浪就止住，平静了。

chapters.en:
“Where is your faith?” He asked.
Frightened and amazed, they asked one another, “Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him!”
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他们说：「你们的信心在哪里呢？」他们又惧怕又希奇，彼此说：「这到底是谁？他吩咐风和水，连风和水也听从他了。」

chapters.en: Then they sailed to the region of the Gerasenes, across the lake from Galilee.
chapters.zh: 他们到了格拉森〔注：有古卷：加大拉〕人的地方，就是加利利的对面。

chapters.en: When Jesus stepped ashore, He was met by a demon-possessed man from the town. For a long time this man had not worn clothing or lived in a house, but he stayed in the tombs.
chapters.zh: 耶稣上了岸，就有城里一个被鬼附着的人迎面而来。这个人许久不穿衣服，不住房子，只住在坟茔里。

chapters.en: When the man saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before Him, shouting in a loud voice, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You not to torture me!”
chapters.zh: 他见了耶稣，就俯伏在他面前，大声喊叫，说：「至高上帝的儿子耶稣，我与你有什么相干？求你不要叫我受苦！」

chapters.en: For Jesus had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him, and though he was bound with chains and shackles, he had broken the chains and been driven by the demon into solitary places.
chapters.zh: 是因耶稣曾吩咐污鬼从那人身上出来。原来这鬼屡次抓住他；他常被人看守，又被铁鍊和脚镣捆锁，他竟把锁鍊挣断，被鬼赶到旷野去。

chapters.en:
“What is your name?” Jesus asked.
“Legion,” he replied, because many demons had gone into him.
chapters.zh: 耶稣问他说：「你名叫什么？」他说：「我名叫『群』」；这是因为附着他的鬼多。

chapters.en: And the demons kept begging Jesus not to order them to go into the Abyss.
chapters.zh: 鬼就央求耶稣，不要吩咐他们到无底坑里去。

chapters.en: There on the hillside a large herd of pigs was feeding. So the demons begged Jesus to let them enter the pigs, and He gave them permission.
chapters.zh: 那里有一大群猪在山上吃食。鬼央求耶稣，准他们进入猪里去。耶稣准了他们，

chapters.en: Then the demons came out of the man and went into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.
chapters.zh: 鬼就从那人出来，进入猪里去。于是那群猪闯下山崖，投在湖里淹死了。

chapters.en: When those tending the pigs saw what had happened, they ran off and reported this in the town and countryside.
chapters.zh: 放猪的看见这事就逃跑了，去告诉城里和乡下的人。

chapters.en: So the people went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man whom the demons had left, sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
chapters.zh: 众人出来要看是什么事；到了耶稣那里，看见鬼所离开的那人，坐在耶稣脚前，穿着衣服，心里明白过来，他们就害怕。

chapters.en: Meanwhile, those who had seen it reported how the demon-possessed man had been healed.
chapters.zh: 看见这事的便将被鬼附着的人怎么得救告诉他们。

chapters.en: Then all the people of the region of the Gerasenes asked Jesus to depart from them, because great fear had taken hold of them. So He got into the boat and started back.
chapters.zh: 格拉森四围的人，因为害怕得很，都求耶稣离开他们；耶稣就上船回去了。

chapters.en: The man whom the demons had left begged to go with Jesus. But He sent him away, saying,
chapters.zh: 鬼所离开的那人恳求和耶稣同在；耶稣却打发他回去，说：

chapters.en: “Return home and describe how much God has done for you.” So the man went away and proclaimed all over the town how much Jesus had done for him.
chapters.zh: 「你回家去，传说上帝为你做了何等大的事。」他就去，满城里传扬耶稣为他做了何等大的事。

chapters.en: When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed Him, for they had all been waiting for Him.
chapters.zh: 耶稣回来的时候，众人迎接他，因为他们都等候他。

chapters.en: Just then a synagogue leader named Jairus came and fell at Jesus’ feet. He begged Him to come to his house,
chapters.zh: 有一个管会堂的，名叫睚鲁，来俯伏在耶稣脚前，求耶稣到他家里去；

chapters.en:
because his only daughter, who was about twelve, was dying.
As Jesus went with him, the crowds pressed around Him,
chapters.zh: 因他有一个独生女儿，约有十二岁，快要死了。 耶稣去的时候，众人拥挤他。

chapters.en: including a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years. She had spent all her money on physicians, but no one was able to heal her.
chapters.zh: 有一个女人，患了十二年的血漏，在医生手里花尽了她一切养生的，并没有一人能医好她。

chapters.en: She came up behind Jesus and touched the fringe of His cloak, and immediately her bleeding stopped.
chapters.zh: 她来到耶稣背后，摸他的衣裳繸子，血漏立刻就止住了。

chapters.en:
“Who touched Me?” Jesus asked.
But they all denied it. “Master,” said Peter, “the people are crowding and pressing against You.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「摸我的是谁？」众人都不承认。彼得和同行的人都说：「夫子，众人拥拥挤挤紧靠着你。〔注：有古卷加：你还问摸我的是谁吗？〕」

chapters.en: But Jesus declared, “Someone touched Me, for I know that power has gone out from Me.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「总有人摸我，因我觉得有能力从我身上出去。」

chapters.en: Then the woman, seeing that she could not escape notice, came trembling and fell down before Him. In the presence of all the people, she explained why she had touched Him and how she had immediately been healed.
chapters.zh: 那女人知道不能隐藏，就战战兢兢地来俯伏在耶稣脚前，把摸他的缘故和怎样立刻得好了，当着众人都说出来。

chapters.en: “Daughter,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣对她说：「女儿，你的信救了你；平平安安地去吧！」

chapters.en: While He was still speaking, someone arrived from the house of the synagogue leader. “Your daughter is dead,” he told Jairus. “Do not bother the Teacher anymore.”
chapters.zh: 还说话的时候，有人从管会堂的家里来，说：「你的女儿死了，不要劳动夫子。」

chapters.en: But Jesus overheard them and said to Jairus, “Do not be afraid; just believe, and she will be healed.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣听见就对他说：「不要怕，只要信！你的女儿就必得救。」

chapters.en: When He entered the house, He did not allow anyone to go in with Him except Peter, John, James, and the child’s father and mother.
chapters.zh: 耶稣到了他的家，除了彼得、约翰、雅各，和女儿的父母，不许别人同他进去。

chapters.en: Meanwhile, everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But Jesus said, “Stop weeping; she is not dead but asleep.”
chapters.zh: 众人都为这女儿哀哭捶胸。耶稣说：「不要哭！她不是死了，是睡着了。」

chapters.en: And they laughed at Him, knowing that she was dead.
chapters.zh: 他们晓得女儿已经死了，就嗤笑耶稣。

chapters.en: But Jesus took her by the hand and called out, “Child, get up!”
chapters.zh: 耶稣拉着她的手，呼叫说：「女儿，起来吧！」

chapters.en: Her spirit returned, and at once she got up. And He directed that she be given something to eat.
chapters.zh: 她的灵魂便回来，她就立刻起来了。耶稣吩咐给她东西吃。

chapters.en: Her parents were astounded, but Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone what had happened.
chapters.zh: 她的父母惊奇得很；耶稣嘱咐他们，不要把所做的事告诉人。

chapters.en: Then Jesus called the Twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and power to cure diseases.
chapters.zh: 耶稣叫齐了十二个门徒，给他们能力、权柄，制伏一切的鬼，医治各样的病，

chapters.en: And He sent them out to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
chapters.zh: 又差遣他们去宣传上帝国〔的道〕，医治病人，

chapters.en: “Take nothing for the journey,” He told them, “no staff, no bag, no bread, no money, no second tunic.
chapters.zh: 对他们说：「行路的时候，不要带柺杖和口袋，不要带食物和银子，也不要带两件褂子。

chapters.en: Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that area.
chapters.zh: 无论进哪一家，就住在那里，也从那里起行。

chapters.en: If anyone does not welcome you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that town, as a testimony against them.”
chapters.zh: 凡不接待你们的，你们离开那城的时候，要把脚上的尘土跺下去，见证他们的不是。」

chapters.en: So they set out and went from village to village, preaching the gospel and healing people everywhere.
chapters.zh: 门徒就出去，走遍各乡宣传福音，到处治病。

chapters.en: When Herod the tetrarch heard about all that was happening, he was perplexed. For some were saying that John had risen from the dead,
chapters.zh: 分封的王希律听见耶稣所做的一切事，就游移不定；因为有人说：「是约翰从死里复活」；

chapters.en: others that Elijah had appeared, and still others that a prophet of old had arisen.
chapters.zh: 又有人说：「是以利亚显现」；还有人说：「是古时的一个先知又活了。」

chapters.en: “I beheaded John,” Herod said, “but who is this man I hear such things about?” And he kept trying to see Jesus.
chapters.zh: 希律说：「约翰我已经斩了，这却是什么人？我竟听见他这样的事呢？」就想要见他。

chapters.en: Then the apostles returned and reported to Jesus all that they had done. Taking them away privately, He withdrew to a town called Bethsaida.
chapters.zh: 使徒回来，将所做的事告诉耶稣，耶稣就带他们暗暗地离开那里，往一座城去；那城名叫伯赛大。

chapters.en: But the crowds found out and followed Him. He welcomed them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and He healed those who needed healing.
chapters.zh: 但众人知道了，就跟着他去；耶稣便接待他们，对他们讲论上帝国〔的道〕，医治那些需医的人。

chapters.en: As the day neared its end, the Twelve came to Jesus and said, “Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding villages and countryside for lodging and provisions. For we are in a desolate place here.”
chapters.zh: 日头快要平西，十二个门徒来对他说：「请叫众人散开，他们好往四面乡村里去借宿找吃的，因为我们这里是野地。」

chapters.en:
But Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.”
“We have only five loaves of bread and two fish,” they answered, “unless we go and buy food for all these people.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「你们给他们吃吧！」门徒说：「我们不过有五个饼，两条鱼，若不去为这许多人买食物就不够。」

chapters.en:
(There were about five thousand men.)
He told His disciples, “Have them sit down in groups of about fifty each.”
chapters.zh: 那时，人数约有五千。耶稣对门徒说：「叫他们一排一排地坐下，每排大约五十个人。」

chapters.en: They did so, and everyone was seated.
chapters.zh: 门徒就如此行，叫众人都坐下。

chapters.en: Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, Jesus spoke a blessing and broke them. Then He gave them to the disciples to set before the people.
chapters.zh: 耶稣拿着这五个饼，两条鱼，望着天祝福，擘开，递给门徒，摆在众人面前。

chapters.en: They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
chapters.zh: 他们就吃，并且都吃饱了；把剩下的零碎收拾起来，装满了十二篮子。

chapters.en: One day as Jesus was praying in private and the disciples were with Him, He questioned them: “Who do the crowds say I am?”
chapters.zh: 耶稣自己祷告的时候，门徒也同他在那里。耶稣问他们说：「众人说我是谁？」

chapters.en: They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, that a prophet of old has arisen.”
chapters.zh: 他们说：「有人说是施洗的约翰；有人说是以利亚；还有人说是古时的一个先知又活了。」

chapters.en:
“But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?”
Peter answered, “The Christ of God.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「你们说我是谁？」彼得回答说：「是上帝所立的基督。」

chapters.en: Jesus strictly warned them not to tell this to anyone.
chapters.zh: 耶稣切切地嘱咐他们，不可将这事告诉人，

chapters.en: “The Son of Man must suffer many things,” He said. “He must be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and He must be killed and on the third day be raised to life.”
chapters.zh: 又说：「人子必须受许多的苦，被长老、祭司长，和文士弃绝，并且被杀，第三日复活。」

chapters.en: Then Jesus said to all of them, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow Me.
chapters.zh: 耶稣又对众人说：「若有人要跟从我，就当舍己，天天背起他的十字架来跟从我。

chapters.en: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake will save it.
chapters.zh: 因为，凡要救自己生命〔注：生命：或译灵魂；下同〕的，必丧掉生命；凡为我丧掉生命的，必救了生命。

chapters.en: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet lose or forfeit his very self?
chapters.zh: 人若赚得全世界，却丧了自己，赔上自己，有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when He comes in His glory and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.
chapters.zh: 凡把我和我的道当作可耻的，人子在自己的荣耀里，并天父与圣天使的荣耀里降临的时候，也要把那人当作可耻的。

chapters.en: But I tell you truly, some who are standing here will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God.”
chapters.zh: 我实在告诉你们，站在这里的，有人在没尝死味以前，必看见上帝的国。」

chapters.en: About eight days after Jesus had said these things, He took with Him Peter, John, and James, and went up on a mountain to pray.
chapters.zh: 说了这话以后约有八天，耶稣带着彼得、约翰、雅各上山去祷告。

chapters.en: And as He was praying, the appearance of His face changed, and His clothes became radiantly white.
chapters.zh: 正祷告的时候，他的面貌就改变了，衣服洁白放光。

chapters.en: Suddenly two men, Moses and Elijah, began talking with Jesus.
chapters.zh: 忽然有摩西、以利亚两个人同耶稣说话；

chapters.en: They appeared in glory and spoke about His departure, which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 他们在荣光里显现，谈论耶稣去世的事，就是他在耶路撒冷将要成的事。

chapters.en: Meanwhile Peter and his companions were overcome by sleep, but when they awoke, they saw Jesus’ glory and the two men standing with Him.
chapters.zh: 彼得和他的同伴都打盹，既清醒了，就看见耶稣的荣光，并同他站着的那两个人。

chapters.en: As Moses and Elijah were leaving, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters —one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” (He did not know what he was saying.)
chapters.zh: 二人正要和耶稣分离的时候，彼得对耶稣说：「夫子，我们在这里真好！可以搭三座棚，一座为你，一座为摩西，一座为以利亚。」他却不知道所说的是什么。

chapters.en: While Peter was speaking, a cloud appeared and enveloped them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
chapters.zh: 说这话的时候，有一朵云彩来遮盖他们；他们进入云彩里就惧怕。

chapters.en: And a voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is My Son, whom I have chosen. Listen to Him!”
chapters.zh: 有声音从云彩里出来，说：「这是我的儿子，我所拣选的〔注：有古卷：这是我的爱子〕，你们要听他。」

chapters.en: After the voice had spoken, only Jesus was present with them. The disciples kept this to themselves, and in those days they did not tell anyone what they had seen.
chapters.zh: 声音住了，只见耶稣一人在那里。当那些日子，门徒不提所看见的事，一样也不告诉人。

chapters.en: The next day, when they came down from the mountain, Jesus was met by a large crowd.
chapters.zh: 第二天，他们下了山，就有许多人迎见耶稣。

chapters.en: Suddenly a man in the crowd cried out, “Teacher, I beg You to look at my son, for he is my only child.
chapters.zh: 其中有一人喊叫说：「夫子！求你看顾我的儿子，因为他是我的独生子。

chapters.en: A spirit keeps seizing him, and he screams abruptly. It throws him into convulsions so that he foams at the mouth. It keeps mauling him and rarely departs from him.
chapters.zh: 他被鬼抓住就忽然喊叫；鬼又叫他抽疯，口中流沫，并且重重地伤害他，难以离开他。

chapters.en: I begged Your disciples to drive it out, but they were unable.”
chapters.zh: 我求过你的门徒，把鬼赶出去，他们却是不能。」

chapters.en: “O unbelieving and perverse generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you and put up with you? Bring your son here.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「嗳！这又不信又悖谬的世代啊，我在你们这里，忍耐你们要到几时呢？将你的儿子带到这里来吧！」

chapters.en: Even while the boy was approaching, the demon slammed him to the ground in a convulsion. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
chapters.zh: 正来的时候，鬼把他摔倒，叫他重重地抽疯。耶稣就斥责那污鬼，把孩子治好了，交给他父亲。

chapters.en:
And they were all astonished at the greatness of God.
While everyone was marveling at all that Jesus was doing, He said to His disciples,
chapters.zh: 众人都诧异上帝的大能〔注：大能：或译威荣〕。 耶稣所做的一切事，众人正希奇的时候，耶稣对门徒说：

chapters.en: “Let these words sink into your ears: The Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men.”
chapters.zh: 「你们要把这些话存在耳中，因为人子将要被交在人手里。」

chapters.en: But they did not understand this statement. It was veiled from them so that they could not comprehend it, and they were afraid to ask Him about it.
chapters.zh: 他们不明白这话，意思乃是隐藏的，叫他们不能明白，他们也不敢问这话的意思。

chapters.en: Then an argument started among the disciples as to which of them would be the greatest.
chapters.zh: 门徒中间起了议论，谁将为大。

chapters.en: But Jesus, knowing the thoughts of their hearts, had a little child stand beside Him.
chapters.zh: 耶稣看出他们心中的议论，就领一个小孩子来，叫他站在自己旁边，

chapters.en: And He said to them, “Whoever welcomes this little child in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes the One who sent Me. For whoever is the least among all of you, he is the greatest.”
chapters.zh: 对他们说：「凡为我名接待这小孩子的，就是接待我；凡接待我的，就是接待那差我来的。你们中间最小的，他便为大。」

chapters.en: “Master,” said John, “we saw someone driving out demons in Your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not accompany us.”
chapters.zh: 约翰说：「夫子，我们看见一个人奉你的名赶鬼，我们就禁止他，因为他不与我们一同跟从〔你〕。」

chapters.en: “Do not stop him,” Jesus replied, “for whoever is not against you is for you.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「不要禁止他；因为不敌挡你们的，就是帮助你们的。」

chapters.en: As the day of His ascension approached, Jesus resolutely set out for Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 耶稣被接上升的日子将到，他就定意向耶路撒冷去，

chapters.en: He sent messengers on ahead, who went into a village of the Samaritans to make arrangements for Him.
chapters.zh: 便打发使者在他前头走。他们到了撒马利亚的一个村庄，要为他预备。

chapters.en: But the people there refused to welcome Him, because He was heading for Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 那里的人不接待他，因他面向耶路撒冷去。

chapters.en: When the disciples James and John saw this, they asked, “Lord, do You want us to call down fire from heaven to consume them?”
chapters.zh: 他的门徒雅各、约翰看见了，就说：「主啊，你要我们吩咐火从天上降下来烧灭他们，像以利亚所做的〔注：有古卷没有像以利亚所做的这几个字〕吗？」

chapters.en: But Jesus turned and rebuked them.
chapters.zh: 耶稣转身责备两个门徒，说：「你们的心如何，你们并不知道。

chapters.en: And He and His disciples went on to another village.
chapters.zh: 人子来不是要灭人的性命〔注：性命：或译灵魂；下同〕，是要救人的性命。」说着就往别的村庄去了〔注：有古卷只有五十五节首句，五十六节末句〕。

chapters.en: As they were walking along the road, someone said to Jesus, “I will follow You wherever You go.”
chapters.zh: 他们走路的时候，有一人对耶稣说：「你无论往哪里去，我要跟从你。」

chapters.en: Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「狐狸有洞，天空的飞鸟有窝，只是人子没有枕头的地方。」

chapters.en:
Then He said to another man, “Follow Me.”
The man replied, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”
chapters.zh: 又对一个人说：「跟从我来！」那人说：「主，容我先回去埋葬我的父亲。」

chapters.en: But Jesus told him, “Let the dead bury their own dead. You, however, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「任凭死人埋葬他们的死人，你只管去传扬上帝国〔的道〕。」

chapters.en: Still another said, “I will follow You, Lord; but first let me bid farewell to my family.”
chapters.zh: 又有一人说：「主，我要跟从你，但容我先去辞别我家里的人。」

chapters.en: Then Jesus declared, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「手扶着诓向后看的，不配进上帝的国。」

chapters.en: After this, the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them two by two ahead of Him to every town and place He was about to visit.
chapters.zh: 这事以后，主又设立七十个人，差遣他们两个两个地在他前面，往自己所要到的各城各地方去，

chapters.en: And He told them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.
chapters.zh: 就对他们说：「要收的庄稼多，做工的人少。所以，你们当求庄稼的主打发工人出去收他的庄稼。

chapters.en: Go! I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.
chapters.zh: 你们去吧！我差你们出去，如同羊羔进入狼群。

chapters.en: Carry no purse or bag or sandals. Do not greet anyone along the road.
chapters.zh: 不要带钱囊，不要带口袋，不要带鞋；在路上也不要问人的安。

chapters.en: Whatever house you enter, begin by saying, ‘Peace to this house.’
chapters.zh: 无论进哪一家，先要说：『愿这一家平安。』

chapters.en: If a man of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it will return to you.
chapters.zh: 那里若有当得平安的人〔注：当得平安的人：原文是平安之子〕，你们所求的平安就必临到那家；不然，就归与你们了。

chapters.en: Stay at the same house, eating and drinking whatever you are offered. For the worker is worthy of his wages. Do not move around from house to house.
chapters.zh: 你们要住在那家，吃喝他们所供给的，因为工人得工价是应当的；不要从这家搬到那家。

chapters.en: If you enter a town and they welcome you, eat whatever is set before you.
chapters.zh: 无论进哪一城，人若接待你们，给你们摆上什么，你们就吃什么。

chapters.en: Heal the sick who are there and tell them, ‘The kingdom of God is near you.’
chapters.zh: 要医治那城里的病人，对他们说：『上帝的国临近你们了。』

chapters.en: But if you enter a town and they do not welcome you, go into the streets and declare,
chapters.zh: 无论进哪一城，人若不接待你们，你们就到街上去，

chapters.en: ‘Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet, we wipe off as a testimony against you. Yet be sure of this: The kingdom of God is near.’
chapters.zh: 说：『就是你们城里的尘土黏在我们的脚上，我们也当着你们擦去。虽然如此，你们该知道上帝的国临近了。』

chapters.en: I tell you, it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town.
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，当审判的日子，所多玛所受的，比那城还容易受呢！」

chapters.en: Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
chapters.zh: 「哥拉汛哪，你有祸了！伯赛大啊，你有祸了！因为在你们中间所行的异能若行在泰尔、西顿，他们早已披麻蒙灰，坐在地上悔改了。

chapters.en: But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.
chapters.zh: 当审判的日子，泰尔、西顿所受的，比你们还容易受呢！

chapters.en: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades!
chapters.zh: 迦百农啊，你已经升到天上〔注：或译：你将要升到天上吗〕，将来必推下阴间。」

chapters.en: Whoever listens to you listens to Me; whoever rejects you rejects Me; and whoever rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me.”
chapters.zh: 〔又对门徒说〕：「听从你们的就是听从我；弃绝你们的就是弃绝我；弃绝我的就是弃绝那差我来的。」

chapters.en: The seventy-two returned with joy and said, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in Your name.”
chapters.zh: 那七十个人欢欢喜喜地回来，说：「主啊！因你的名，就是鬼也服了我们。」

chapters.en: So He told them, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他们说：「我曾看见撒但从天上坠落，像闪电一样。

chapters.en: Behold, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will harm you.
chapters.zh: 我已经给你们权柄可以践踏蛇和蠍子，又胜过仇敌一切的能力，断没有什么能害你们。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”
chapters.zh: 然而，不要因鬼服了你们就欢喜，要因你们的名记录在天上欢喜。」

chapters.en: At that time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.
chapters.zh: 正当那时，耶稣被圣灵感动就欢乐，说：「父啊，天地的主，我感谢你！因为你将这些事向聪明通达人就藏起来，向婴孩就显出来。父啊！是的，因为你的美意本是如此。

chapters.en: All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.”
chapters.zh: 一切所有的都是我父交付我的；除了父，没有人知道子是谁；除了子和子所愿意指示的，没有人知道父是谁。」

chapters.en: Then Jesus turned to the disciples and said privately, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.
chapters.zh: 耶稣转身暗暗地对门徒说：「看见你们所看见的，那眼睛就有福了。

chapters.en: For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.”
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，从前有许多先知和君王要看你们所看的，却没有看见，要听你们所听的，却没有听见。」

chapters.en: One day an expert in the law stood up to test Him. “Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
chapters.zh: 有一个律法师起来试探耶稣，说：「夫子！我该做什么才可以承受永生？」

chapters.en: “What is written in the Law?” Jesus replied. “How do you read it?”
chapters.zh: 耶稣对他说：「律法上写的是什么？你念的是怎样呢？」

chapters.en: He answered, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind’ and ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ ”
chapters.zh: 他回答说：「你要尽心、尽性、尽力、尽意爱主－你的上帝；又要爱邻舍如同自己。」

chapters.en: “You have answered correctly,” Jesus said. “Do this and you will live.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「你回答的是；你这样行，就必得〔永〕生。」

chapters.en: But wanting to justify himself, he asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”
chapters.zh: 那人要显明自己有理，就对耶稣说：「谁是我的邻舍呢？」

chapters.en: Jesus took up this question and said, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he fell into the hands of robbers. They stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead.
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说：「有一个人从耶路撒冷下耶利哥去，落在强盗手中。他们剥去他的衣裳，把他打个半死，就丢下他走了。

chapters.en: Now by chance a priest was going down the same road, but when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
chapters.zh: 偶然有一个祭司从这条路下来，看见他就从那边过去了。

chapters.en: So too, when a Levite came to that spot and saw him, he passed by on the other side.
chapters.zh: 又有一个利未人来到这地方，看见他，也照样从那边过去了。

chapters.en: But a Samaritan on a journey came upon him, and when he saw him, he had compassion.
chapters.zh: 惟有一个撒马利亚人行路来到那里，看见他就动了慈心，

chapters.en: He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
chapters.zh: 上前用油和酒倒在他的伤处，包裹好了，扶他骑上自己的牲口，带到店里去照应他。

chapters.en: The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper. ‘Take care of him,’ he said, ‘and on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.’
chapters.zh: 第二天拿出二钱银子来，交给店主，说：『你且照应他；此外所费用的，我回来必还你。』

chapters.en: Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?”
chapters.zh: 你想，这三个人哪一个是落在强盗手中的邻舍呢？」

chapters.en:
“The one who showed him mercy,” replied the expert in the law.
Then Jesus told him, “Go and do likewise.”
chapters.zh: 他说：「是怜悯他的。」耶稣说：「你去照样行吧。」

chapters.en: As they traveled along, Jesus entered a village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home.
chapters.zh: 他们走路的时候，耶稣进了一个村庄。有一个女人，名叫马大，接他到自己家里。

chapters.en: She had a sister named Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message.
chapters.zh: 她有一个妹子，名叫马利亚，在耶稣脚前坐着听他的道。

chapters.en: But Martha was distracted by all the preparations to be made. She came to Jesus and said, “Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me!”
chapters.zh: 马大伺候的事多，心里忙乱，就进前来，说：「主啊，我的妹子留下我一个人伺候，你不在意吗？请吩咐她来帮助我。」

chapters.en: “Martha, Martha,” the Lord replied, “you are worried and upset about many things.
chapters.zh: 耶稣回答说：「马大！马大！你为许多的事思虑烦扰，

chapters.en: But only one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her.”
chapters.zh: 但是不可少的只有一件；马利亚已经选择那上好的福分，是不能夺去的。」

chapters.en: One day in a place where Jesus had just finished praying, one of His disciples requested, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣在一个地方祷告；祷告完了，有个门徒对他说：「求主教导我们祷告，像约翰教导他的门徒。」

chapters.en:
So Jesus told them, “When you pray, say:
‘Father, hallowed be Your name.
Your kingdom come.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「你们祷告的时候，要说： 我们在天上的父〔注：有古卷：父啊〕： 愿人都尊你的名为圣。 愿你的国降临； 愿你的旨意行在地上， 如同行在天上〔注：有古卷没有愿你的旨意…〕。

chapters.en: Give us each day our daily bread.
chapters.zh: 我们日用的饮食， 天天赐给我们。

chapters.en: And forgive us our sins, for we also forgive everyone who sins against us. And lead us not into temptation. ’”
chapters.zh: 赦免我们的罪， 因为我们也赦免凡亏欠我们的人。 不叫我们遇见试探； 救我们脱离凶恶〔注：有古卷没有末句〕。」

chapters.en: Then Jesus said to them, “Suppose one of you goes to his friend at midnight and says, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
chapters.zh: 耶稣又说：「你们中间谁有一个朋友半夜到他那里去，说：『朋友！请借给我三个饼；

chapters.en: because a friend of mine has come to me on a journey, and I have nothing to set before him.’
chapters.zh: 因为我有一个朋友行路，来到我这里，我没有什么给他摆上。』

chapters.en: And suppose the one inside answers, ‘Do not bother me. My door is already shut, and my children and I are in bed. I cannot get up to give you anything.’
chapters.zh: 那人在里面回答说：『不要搅扰我，门已经关闭，孩子们也同我在床上了，我不能起来给你。』

chapters.en: I tell you, even though he will not get up to provide for him because of his friendship, yet because of the man’s persistence, he will get up and give him as much as he needs.
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，虽不因他是朋友起来给他，但因他情词迫切地直求，就必起来照他所需用的给他。

chapters.en: So I tell you: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
chapters.zh: 我又告诉你们，你们祈求，就给你们；寻找，就寻见；叩门，就给你们开门。

chapters.en: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.
chapters.zh: 因为，凡祈求的，就得着；寻找的，就寻见；叩门的，就给他开门。

chapters.en: What father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead?
chapters.zh: 你们中间作父亲的，谁有儿子求饼，反给他石头呢？求鱼，反拿蛇当鱼给他呢？

chapters.en: Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?
chapters.zh: 求〔鸡〕蛋，反给他蠍子呢？

chapters.en: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!”
chapters.zh: 你们虽然不好，尚且知道拿好东西给儿女；何况天父，岂不更将圣灵给求他的人吗？」

chapters.en: One day Jesus was driving out a demon that was mute. And when the demon was gone, the man who had been mute spoke. The crowds were amazed,
chapters.zh: 耶稣赶出一个叫人哑巴的鬼；鬼出去了，哑巴就说出话来；众人都希奇。

chapters.en: but some of them said, “It is by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons, that He drives out demons.”
chapters.zh: 内中却有人说：「他是靠着鬼王别西卜赶鬼。」

chapters.en: And others tested Him by demanding a sign from heaven.
chapters.zh: 又有人试探耶稣，向他求从天上来的神迹。

chapters.en: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and a house divided against a house will fall.
chapters.zh: 他晓得他们的意念，便对他们说：「凡一国自相纷争，就成为荒场；凡一家自相纷争，就必败落。

chapters.en: If Satan is divided against himself, how can his kingdom stand? After all, you say that I drive out demons by Beelzebul.
chapters.zh: 若撒但自相纷争，他的国怎能站得住呢？因为你们说我是靠着别西卜赶鬼。

chapters.en: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.
chapters.zh: 我若靠着别西卜赶鬼，你们的子弟赶鬼又靠着谁呢？这样，他们就要断定你们的是非。

chapters.en: But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
chapters.zh: 我若靠着上帝的能力赶鬼，这就是上帝的国临到你们了。

chapters.en: When a strong man, fully armed, guards his house, his possessions are secure.
chapters.zh: 壮士披挂整齐，看守自己的住宅，他所有的都平安无事；

chapters.en: But when someone stronger attacks and overpowers him, he takes away the armor in which the man trusted, and then he divides up his plunder.
chapters.zh: 但有一个比他更壮的来，胜过他，就夺去他所倚靠的盔甲兵器，又分了他的赃。

chapters.en: He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters.
chapters.zh: 不与我相合的，就是敌我的；不同我收聚的，就是分散的。」

chapters.en: When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it. Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’
chapters.zh: 「污鬼离了人身，就在无水之地过来过去，寻求安歇〔之处〕；既寻不着，便说：『我要回到我所出来的屋里去。』

chapters.en: On its return, it finds the house swept clean and put in order.
chapters.zh: 到了，就看见〔里面〕打扫干净，修饰好了，

chapters.en: Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and dwell there. And the final plight of that man is worse than the first.”
chapters.zh: 便去另带了七个比自己更恶的鬼来，都进去住在那里。那人末后的景况比先前更不好了。」

chapters.en: As Jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said, “Blessed is the womb that bore You, and blessed are the breasts that nursed You!”
chapters.zh: 耶稣正说这话的时候，众人中间有一个女人大声说：「怀你胎的和乳养你的有福了！」

chapters.en: But He replied, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「是，却还不如听上帝之道而遵守的人有福。」

chapters.en: As the crowds were increasing, Jesus said, “This is a wicked generation. It demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of Jonah.
chapters.zh: 当众人聚集的时候，耶稣开讲说：「这世代是一个邪恶的世代。他们求看神迹，除了约拿的神迹以外，再没有神迹给他们看。

chapters.en: For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.
chapters.zh: 约拿怎样为尼尼微人成了神迹，人子也要照样为这世代的人成了神迹。

chapters.en: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here.
chapters.zh: 当审判的时候，南方的女王要起来定这世代的罪；因为她从地极而来，要听所罗门的智慧话。看哪，在这里有一人比所罗门更大。

chapters.en: The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here.
chapters.zh: 当审判的时候，尼尼微人要起来定这世代的罪，因为尼尼微人听了约拿所传的就悔改了。看哪，在这里有一人比约拿更大。」

chapters.en: No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.
chapters.zh: 「没有人点灯放在地窨子里，或是斗底下，总是放在灯台上，使进来的人得见亮光。

chapters.en: Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eyes are good, your whole body also is full of light. But when they are bad, your body is full of darkness.
chapters.zh: 你眼睛就是身上的灯。你的眼睛若瞭亮，全身就光明；眼睛若昏花，全身就黑暗。

chapters.en: Be careful, then, that the light within you is not darkness.
chapters.zh: 所以，你要省察，恐怕你里头的光或者黑暗了。

chapters.en: So if your whole body is full of light, with no part of it in darkness, you will be radiant, as though a lamp were shining on you.”
chapters.zh: 若是你全身光明，毫无黑暗，就必全然光明，如同灯的明光照亮你。」

chapters.en: As Jesus was speaking, a Pharisee invited Him to dine with him; so He went in and reclined at the table.
chapters.zh: 说话的时候，有一个法利赛人请耶稣同他吃饭，耶稣就进去坐席。

chapters.en: But the Pharisee was surprised to see that Jesus did not first wash before the meal.
chapters.zh: 这法利赛人看见耶稣饭前不洗〔手〕便诧异。

chapters.en: Then the Lord said, “Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside you are full of greed and wickedness.
chapters.zh: 主对他说：「如今你们法利赛人洗净杯盘的外面，你们里面却满了勒索和邪恶。

chapters.en: You fools! Did not the One who made the outside make the inside as well?
chapters.zh: 无知的人哪，造外面的，不也造里面吗？

chapters.en: But give as alms the things that are within you, and behold, everything will be clean for you.
chapters.zh: 只要把里面的施舍给人，凡物于你们就都洁净了。

chapters.en: Woe to you Pharisees! For you pay tithes of mint, rue, and every herb, but you disregard justice and the love of God. You should have practiced the latter without neglecting the former.
chapters.zh: 「你们法利赛人有祸了！因为你们将薄荷、芸香并各样菜蔬献上十分之一，那公义和爱上帝的事反倒不行了。这原是你们当行的；那也是不可不行的。

chapters.en: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
chapters.zh: 你们法利赛人有祸了！因为你们喜爱会堂里的首位，又喜爱人在街市上问你们的安。

chapters.en: Woe to you! For you are like unmarked graves, which men walk over without even noticing.”
chapters.zh: 你们有祸了！因为你们如同不显露的坟墓，走在上面的人并不知道。」

chapters.en: One of the experts in the law told Him, “Teacher, when You say these things, You insult us as well.”
chapters.zh: 律法师中有一个回答耶稣说：「夫子！你这样说也把我们糟蹋了。」

chapters.en: “Woe to you as well, experts in the law!” He replied. “For you weigh men down with heavy burdens, but you yourselves will not lift a finger to lighten their load.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「你们律法师也有祸了！因为你们把难担的担子放在人身上，自己一个指头却不肯动。

chapters.en: Woe to you! For you build tombs for the prophets, but it was your fathers who killed them.
chapters.zh: 你们有祸了！因为你们修造先知的坟墓，那先知正是你们的祖宗所杀的。

chapters.en: So you are witnesses consenting to the deeds of your fathers: They killed the prophets, and you build their tombs.
chapters.zh: 可见你们祖宗所做的事，你们又证明又喜欢；因为他们杀了先知，你们修造〔先知的坟墓〕。

chapters.en: Because of this, the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send them prophets and apostles; some of them they will kill and others they will persecute.’
chapters.zh: 所以上帝用智慧〔注：用智慧：或译的智者〕曾说：『我要差遣先知和使徒到他们那里去，有的他们要杀害，有的他们要逼迫』，

chapters.en: As a result, this generation will be charged with the blood of all the prophets that has been shed since the foundation of the world,
chapters.zh: 使创世以来所流众先知血的罪都要问在这世代的人身上，

chapters.en: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, all of it will be charged to this generation.
chapters.zh: 就是从亚伯的血起，直到被杀在坛和殿中间撒迦利亚的血为止。我实在告诉你们，这都要问在这世代的人身上。

chapters.en: Woe to you experts in the law! For you have taken away the key to knowledge. You yourselves have not entered, and you have hindered those who were entering.”
chapters.zh: 你们律法师有祸了！因为你们把知识的钥匙夺了去，自己不进去，正要进去的人你们也阻挡他们。」

chapters.en: As Jesus went on from there, the scribes and Pharisees began to oppose Him bitterly and to ply Him with questions about many things,
chapters.zh: 耶稣从那里出来，文士和法利赛人就极力地催逼他，引动他多说话，

chapters.en: waiting to catch Him in something He might say.
chapters.zh: 私下窥听，要拿他的话柄。

chapters.en: In the meantime, a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so that they were trampling one another. Jesus began to speak first to His disciples: “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
chapters.zh: 这时，有几万人聚集，甚至彼此践踏。耶稣开讲，先对门徒说：「你们要防备法利赛人的酵，就是假冒为善。

chapters.en: There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.
chapters.zh: 掩盖的事没有不露出来的；隐藏的事没有不被人知道的。

chapters.en: What you have spoken in the dark will be heard in the daylight, and what you have whispered in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the housetops.
chapters.zh: 因此，你们在暗中所说的，将要在明处被人听见；在内室附耳所说的，将要在房上被人宣扬。」

chapters.en: I tell you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more.
chapters.zh: 「我的朋友，我对你们说，那杀身体以后不能再做什么的，不要怕他们。

chapters.en: But I will show you whom you should fear: Fear the One who, after you have been killed, has authority to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear Him!
chapters.zh: 我要指示你们当怕的是谁：当怕那杀了以后又有权柄丢在地狱里的。我实在告诉你们，正要怕他。

chapters.en: Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.
chapters.zh: 五个麻雀不是卖二分银子吗？但在上帝面前，一个也不忘记；

chapters.en: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
chapters.zh: 就是你们的头发，也都被数过了。不要惧怕，你们比许多麻雀还贵重！」

chapters.en: I tell you, everyone who confesses Me before men, the Son of Man will also confess him before the angels of God.
chapters.zh: 「我又告诉你们，凡在人面前认我的，人子在上帝的使者面前也必认他；

chapters.en: But whoever denies Me before men will be denied before the angels of God.
chapters.zh: 在人面前不认我的，人子在上帝的使者面前也必不认他。

chapters.en: And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 凡说话干犯人子的，还可得赦免；惟独亵渎圣灵的，总不得赦免。

chapters.en: When you are brought before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.
chapters.zh: 人带你们到会堂，并官府和有权柄的人面前，不要思虑怎么分诉，说什么话；

chapters.en: For at that time the Holy Spirit will teach you what you should say.”
chapters.zh: 因为正在那时候，圣灵要指教你们当说的话。」

chapters.en: Someone in the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
chapters.zh: 众人中有一个人对耶稣说：「夫子！请你吩咐我的兄长和我分开家业。」

chapters.en: But Jesus replied, “Man, who appointed Me judge or executor between you?”
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「你这个人！谁立我作你们断事的官，给你们分家业呢？」

chapters.en: And He said to them, “Watch out! Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”
chapters.zh: 于是对众人说：「你们要谨慎自守，免去一切的贪心，因为人的生命不在乎家道丰富。」

chapters.en: Then He told them a parable: “The ground of a certain rich man produced an abundance.
chapters.zh: 就用比喻对他们说：「有一个财主田产丰盛；

chapters.en: So he thought to himself, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to store my crops?’
chapters.zh: 自己心里思想说：『我的出产没有地方收藏，怎么办呢？』

chapters.en: Then he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and will build bigger ones, and there I will store up all my grain and my goods.
chapters.zh: 又说：『我要这么办：要把我的仓房拆了，另盖更大的，在那里好收藏我一切的粮食和财物，

chapters.en: Then I will say to myself, “You have plenty of good things laid up for many years. Take it easy. Eat, drink, and be merry!”’
chapters.zh: 然后要对我的灵魂说：灵魂哪，你有许多财物积存，可作多年的费用，只管安安逸逸地吃喝快乐吧！』

chapters.en: But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life will be required of you. Then who will own what you have accumulated?’
chapters.zh: 上帝却对他说：『无知的人哪，今夜必要你的灵魂；你所预备的要归谁呢？』

chapters.en: This is how it will be for anyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.”
chapters.zh: 凡为自己积财，在上帝面前却不富足的，也是这样。」

chapters.en: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
chapters.zh: 耶稣又对门徒说：「所以我告诉你们，不要为生命忧虑吃什么，为身体忧虑穿什么；

chapters.en: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothes.
chapters.zh: 因为生命胜于饮食，身体胜于衣裳。

chapters.en: Consider the ravens: They do not sow or reap, they have no storehouse or barn; yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!
chapters.zh: 你想乌鸦，也不种也不收，又没有仓又没有库，上帝尚且养活牠。你们比飞鸟是何等地贵重呢！

chapters.en: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
chapters.zh: 你们哪一个能用思虑使寿数多加一刻呢〔注：或译：使身量多加一肘呢〕？

chapters.en: So if you cannot do such a small thing, why do you worry about the rest?
chapters.zh: 这最小的事，你们尚且不能做，为什么还忧虑其余的事呢？

chapters.en: Consider how the lilies grow: They do not labor or spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.
chapters.zh: 你想百合花怎么长起来；它也不劳苦，也不纺线。然而我告诉你们，就是所罗门极荣华的时候，他所穿戴的，还不如这花一朵呢！

chapters.en: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, how much more will He clothe you, O you of little faith!
chapters.zh: 你们这小信的人哪，野地里的草今天还在，明天就丢在炉里，上帝还给它这样的妆饰，何况你们呢！

chapters.en: And do not be concerned about what you will eat or drink. Do not worry about it.
chapters.zh: 你们不要求吃什么，喝什么，也不要挂心；

chapters.en: For the Gentiles of the world strive after all these things, and your Father knows that you need them.
chapters.zh: 这都是外邦人所求的。你们必须用这些东西，你们的父是知道的。

chapters.en: But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you.
chapters.zh: 你们只要求他的国，这些东西就必加给你们了。

chapters.en: Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.
chapters.zh: 你们这小群，不要惧怕，因为你们的父乐意把国赐给你们。

chapters.en: Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Provide yourselves with purses that will not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.
chapters.zh: 你们要变卖所有的赒济人，为自己预备永不坏的钱囊，用不尽的财宝在天上，就是贼不能近、虫不能蛀的地方。

chapters.en: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
chapters.zh: 因为，你们的财宝在哪里，你们的心也在那里。」

chapters.en: Be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning.
chapters.zh: 「你们腰里要束上带，灯也要点着，

chapters.en: Then you will be like servants waiting for their master to return from the wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him at once.
chapters.zh: 自己好像〔仆〕人等候主人从婚姻的筵席上回来。他来到，叩门，就立刻给他开门。

chapters.en: Blessed are those servants whom the master finds on watch when he returns. Truly I tell you, he will dress himself to serve and will have them recline at the table, and he himself will come and wait on them.
chapters.zh: 主人来了，看见仆人警醒，那仆人就有福了。我实在告诉你们，主人必叫他们坐席，自己束上带，进前伺候他们。

chapters.en: Even if he comes in the second or third watch of the night and finds them alert, those servants will be blessed.
chapters.zh: 或是二更天来，或是三更天来，看见仆人这样，那仆人就有福了。

chapters.en: But understand this: If the homeowner had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.
chapters.zh: 家主若知道贼什么时候来，就必警醒，不容贼挖透房屋，这是你们所知道的。

chapters.en: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.”
chapters.zh: 你们也要预备；因为你们想不到的时候，人子就来了。」

chapters.en: “Lord,” said Peter, “are You addressing this parable to us, or to everyone else as well?”
chapters.zh: 彼得说：「主啊，这比喻是为我们说的呢？还是为众人呢？」

chapters.en: And the Lord answered, “Who then is the faithful and wise manager, whom the master puts in charge of his servants to give them their portion at the proper time?
chapters.zh: 主说：「谁是那忠心有见识的管家，主人派他管理家里的人，按时分粮给他们呢？

chapters.en: Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.
chapters.zh: 主人来到，看见仆人这样行，那仆人就有福了。

chapters.en: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
chapters.zh: 我实在告诉你们，主人要派他管理一切所有的。

chapters.en: But suppose that servant says in his heart, ‘My master will be a long time in coming,’ and he begins to beat the menservants and maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk.
chapters.zh: 那仆人若心里说：『我的主人必来得迟』，就动手打仆人和使女，并且吃喝醉酒；

chapters.en: The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate. Then he will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the unbelievers.
chapters.zh: 在他想不到的日子，不知道的时辰，那仆人的主人要来，重重地处治他〔注：或译：把他腰斩了〕，定他和不忠心的人同罪。

chapters.en: That servant who knows his master’s will but does not get ready or follow his instructions will be beaten with many blows.
chapters.zh: 仆人知道主人的意思，却不预备，又不顺他的意思行，那仆人必多受责打；

chapters.en: But the one who unknowingly does things worthy of punishment will be beaten with few blows. From everyone who has been given much, much will be required; and from him who has been entrusted with much, even more will be demanded.
chapters.zh: 惟有那不知道的，做了当受责打的事，必少受责打；因为多给谁，就向谁多取；多讬谁，就向谁多要。」

chapters.en: I have come to ignite a fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!
chapters.zh: 「我来要把火丢在地上，倘若已经着起来，不也是我所愿意的吗？

chapters.en: But I have a baptism to undergo, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
chapters.zh: 我有当受的洗还没有成就，我是何等地迫切呢？

chapters.en: Do you think that I have come to bring peace to the earth? No, I tell you, but division.
chapters.zh: 你们以为我来，是叫地上太平吗？我告诉你们，不是，乃是叫人纷争。

chapters.en: From now on, five in one household will be divided, three against two and two against three.
chapters.zh: 从今以后，一家五个人将要纷争：三个人和两个人相争，两个人和三个人相争；

chapters.en: They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law. ”
chapters.zh: 父亲和儿子相争， 儿子和父亲相争； 母亲和女儿相争， 女儿和母亲相争； 婆婆和媳妇相争， 媳妇和婆婆相争。」

chapters.en: Then Jesus said to the crowds, “As soon as you see a cloud rising in the west, you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and that is what happens.
chapters.zh: 耶稣又对众人说：「你们看见西边起了云彩，就说：『要下一阵雨』；果然就有。

chapters.en: And when the south wind blows, you say, ‘It will be hot,’ and it is.
chapters.zh: 起了南风，就说：『将要燥热』；也就有了。

chapters.en: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and sky. Why don’t you know how to interpret the present time?
chapters.zh: 假冒为善的人哪，你们知道分辨天地的气色，怎么不知道分辨这时候呢？」

chapters.en: And why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?
chapters.zh: 「你们又为何不自己审量什么是合理的呢？

chapters.en: Make every effort to reconcile with your adversary while you are on your way to the magistrate. Otherwise, he may drag you off to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and the officer may throw you into prison.
chapters.zh: 你同〔告〕你的对头去见官，还在路上，务要尽力地和他了结；恐怕他拉你到官面前，官交付差役，差役把你下在监里。

chapters.en: I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the very last penny. ”
chapters.zh: 我告诉你，若有半文钱没有还清，你断不能从那里出来。」

chapters.en: At that time some of those present told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
chapters.zh: 正当那时，有人将彼拉多使加利利人的血搀杂在他们祭物中的事告诉耶稣。

chapters.en: To this He replied, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this way?
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「你们以为这些加利利人比众加利利人更有罪，所以受这害吗？

chapters.en: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，不是的！你们若不悔改，都要如此灭亡！

chapters.en: Or those eighteen who were killed when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them: Do you think that they were more sinful than all the others living in Jerusalem?
chapters.zh: 从前西罗亚楼倒塌了，压死十八个人；你们以为那些人比一切住在耶路撒冷的人更有罪吗？

chapters.en: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.”
chapters.zh: 我告诉你们，不是的！你们若不悔改，都要如此灭亡！」

chapters.en: Then Jesus told this parable: “A man had a fig tree that was planted in his vineyard. He went to look for fruit on it but did not find any.
chapters.zh: 于是用比喻说：「一个人有一棵无花果树栽在葡萄园里。他来到树前找果子，却找不着。

chapters.en: So he said to the keeper of the vineyard, ‘Look, for the past three years I have come to search for fruit on this fig tree and haven’t found any. Therefore cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?’
chapters.zh: 就对管园的说：『看哪，我这三年来到这无花果树前找果子，竟找不着。把它砍了吧，何必白佔地土呢！』

chapters.en: ‘Sir,’ the man replied, ‘leave it alone again this year, until I dig around it and fertilize it.
chapters.zh: 管园的说：『主啊，今年且留着，等我周围掘开土，加上粪；

chapters.en: If it bears fruit next year, fine. But if not, you can cut it down.’”
chapters.zh: 以后若结果子便罢，不然再把它砍了。』」

chapters.en: One Sabbath Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues,
chapters.zh: 安息日，耶稣在会堂里教训人。

chapters.en: and a woman there had been disabled by a spirit for eighteen years. She was hunched over and could not stand up straight.
chapters.zh: 有一个女人被鬼附着，病了十八年，腰弯得一点直不起来。

chapters.en: When Jesus saw her, He called her over and said, “Woman, you are set free from your disability.”
chapters.zh: 耶稣看见，便叫过她来，对她说：「女人，你脱离这病了！」

chapters.en: Then He placed His hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and began to glorify God.
chapters.zh: 于是用两只手按着她；她立刻直起腰来，就归荣耀与上帝。

chapters.en: But the synagogue leader was indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. “There are six days for work,” he told the crowd. “So come and be healed on those days and not on the Sabbath.”
chapters.zh: 管会堂的因为耶稣在安息日治病，就气忿忿地对众人说：「有六日应当做工；那六日之内可以来求医，在安息日却不可。」

chapters.en: “You hypocrites!” the Lord replied. “Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the stall and lead it to water?
chapters.zh: 主说：「假冒为善的人哪，难道你们各人在安息日不解开槽上的牛、驴，牵去饮吗？

chapters.en: Then should not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen long years, be released from her bondage on the Sabbath day?”
chapters.zh: 况且这女人本是亚伯拉罕的后裔，被撒但捆绑了这十八年，不当在安息日解开她的绑吗？」

chapters.en: When Jesus said this, all His adversaries were humiliated. And the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things He was doing.
chapters.zh: 耶稣说这话，他的敌人都惭愧了；众人因他所行一切荣耀的事，就都欢喜了。

chapters.en: Then Jesus asked, “What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「上帝的国好像什么？我拿什么来比较呢？

chapters.en: It is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches.”
chapters.zh: 好像一粒芥菜种，有人拿去种在园子里，长大成树，天上的飞鸟宿在它的枝上。」

chapters.en: Again He asked, “To what can I compare the kingdom of God?
chapters.zh: 又说：「我拿什么来比上帝的国呢？

chapters.en: It is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.”
chapters.zh: 好比面酵，有妇人拿来藏在三斗面里，直等全团都发起来。」

chapters.en: Then Jesus traveled throughout the towns and villages, teaching as He made His way toward Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 耶稣往耶路撒冷去，在所经过的各城各乡教训人。

chapters.en:
“Lord,” someone asked Him, “will only a few people be saved?”
Jesus answered,
chapters.zh: 有一个人问他说：「主啊，得救的人少吗？」

chapters.en: “Make every effort to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.
chapters.zh: 耶稣对众人说：「你们要努力进窄门。我告诉你们，将来有许多人想要进去，却是不能。

chapters.en:
After the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, ‘Lord, open the door for us.’
But he will reply, ‘I do not know where you are from.’
chapters.zh: 及至家主起来关了门，你们站在外面叩门，说：『主啊，给我们开门！』他就回答说：『我不认识你们，不晓得你们是哪里来的！』

chapters.en: Then you will say, ‘We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’
chapters.zh: 那时，你们要说：『我们在你面前吃过喝过，你也在我们的街上教训过人。』

chapters.en: And he will answer, ‘I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you evildoers.’
chapters.zh: 他要说：『我告诉你们，我不晓得你们是哪里来的。你们这一切作恶的人，离开我去吧！』

chapters.en: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves are thrown out.
chapters.zh: 你们要看见亚伯拉罕、以撒、雅各，和众先知都在上帝的国里，你们却被赶到外面，在那里必要哀哭切齿了。

chapters.en: People will come from east and west and north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.
chapters.zh: 从东、从西、从南、从北将有人来，在上帝的国里坐席。

chapters.en: And indeed, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.”
chapters.zh: 只是有在后的，将要在前；有在前的，将要在后。」

chapters.en: At that very hour, some Pharisees came to Jesus and told Him, “Leave this place and get away, because Herod wants to kill You.”
chapters.zh: 正当那时，有几个法利赛人来对耶稣说：「离开这里去吧，因为希律想要杀你。」

chapters.en: But Jesus replied, “Go tell that fox, ‘Look, I will keep driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will reach My goal.’
chapters.zh: 耶稣说：「你们去告诉那个狐狸说：『今天、明天我赶鬼治病，第三天我的事就成全了。』

chapters.en: Nevertheless, I must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day, for it is not admissible for a prophet to perish outside of Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 虽然这样，今天、明天、后天，我必须前行，因为先知在耶路撒冷之外丧命是不能的。

chapters.en: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!
chapters.zh: 耶路撒冷啊！耶路撒冷啊！你常杀害先知，又用石头打死那奉差遣到你这里来的人。我多次愿意聚集你的儿女，好像母鸡把小鸡聚集在翅膀底下；只是你们不愿意。

chapters.en: Look, your house is left to you desolate. And I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’ ”
chapters.zh: 看哪，你们的家成为荒场留给你们。我告诉你们，〔从今以后〕你们不得再见我，直等到你们说：『奉主名来的是应当称颂的。』」

chapters.en: One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat in the home of a leading Pharisee, and those in attendance were watching Him closely.
chapters.zh: 安息日，耶稣到一个法利赛人的首领家里去吃饭，他们就窥探他。

chapters.en: Right there before Him was a man with dropsy.
chapters.zh: 在他面前有一个患水臌的人。

chapters.en: So Jesus asked the experts in the law and the Pharisees, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?”
chapters.zh: 耶稣对律法师和法利赛人说：「安息日治病可以不可以？」

chapters.en:
But they remained silent.
Then Jesus took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him on his way.
chapters.zh: 他们却不言语。耶稣就治好那人，叫他走了；

chapters.en: And He asked them, “Which of you whose son or ox falls into a pit on the Sabbath day will not immediately pull him out?”
chapters.zh: 便对他们说：「你们中间谁有驴或有牛，在安息日掉在井里，不立时拉牠上来呢？」

chapters.en: And they were unable to answer these questions.
chapters.zh: 他们不能对答这话。

chapters.en: When Jesus noticed how the guests chose the places of honor, He told them a parable:
chapters.zh: 耶稣见所请的客拣择首位，就用比喻对他们说：

chapters.en: “When you are invited to a wedding banquet, do not sit in the place of honor, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited.
chapters.zh: 「你被人请去赴婚姻的筵席，不要坐在首位上，恐怕有比你尊贵的客被他请来；

chapters.en: Then the host who invited both of you will come and tell you, ‘Give this man your seat.’ And in humiliation, you will have to take the last place.
chapters.zh: 那请你们的人前来对你说：『让座给这一位吧！』你就羞羞惭惭地退到末位上去了。

chapters.en: But when you are invited, go and sit in the last place, so that your host will come and tell you, ‘Friend, move up to a better place.’ Then you will be honored in front of everyone at the table with you.
chapters.zh: 你被请的时候，就去坐在末位上，好叫那请你的人来对你说：『朋友，请上座。』那时，你在同席的人面前就有光彩了。

chapters.en: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
chapters.zh: 因为，凡自高的，必降为卑；自卑的，必升为高。」
