chapters.en: ‘After this I will return and rebuild the fallen tent of David. Its ruins I will rebuild, and I will restore it,
chapters.zh: 正如〔经上〕所写的： 此后，我要回来， 重新修造大卫倒塌的帐幕， 把那破坏的重新修造建立起来，

chapters.en: so that the remnant of men may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles who are called by My name, says the Lord who does these things
chapters.zh: 叫余剩的人， 就是凡称为我名下的外邦人， 都寻求主。

chapters.en: that have been known for ages.’
chapters.zh: 这话是从创世以来显明这事的主说的。

chapters.en: It is my judgment, therefore, that we should not cause trouble for the Gentiles who are turning to God.
chapters.zh: 「所以据我的意见，不可难为那归服上帝的外邦人；

chapters.en: Instead, we should write and tell them to abstain from food polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from the meat of strangled animals, and from blood.
chapters.zh: 只要写信，吩咐他们禁戒偶像的污秽和奸淫，并勒死的牲畜和血。

chapters.en: For Moses has been proclaimed in every city from ancient times and is read in the synagogues on every Sabbath.”
chapters.zh: 因为从古以来，摩西〔的书〕在各城有人传讲，每逢安息日，在会堂里诵读。」

chapters.en: Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, decided to select men from among them to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, two leaders among the brothers,
chapters.zh: 那时，使徒和长老并全教会定意从他们中间拣选人，差他们和保罗、巴拿巴同往安提阿去；〔所拣选的〕就是称呼巴撒巴的犹大和西拉。这两个人在弟兄中是作首领的。

chapters.en:
and sent them with this letter:
The apostles and the elders, your brothers,
To the brothers among the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia:
Greetings.
chapters.zh: 于是写信交付他们，内中说：「使徒和作长老的弟兄们问安提阿、觜利亚、基利家外邦众弟兄的安。

chapters.en: It has come to our attention that some went out from us without our authorization and unsettled you, troubling your minds by what they said.
chapters.zh: 我们听说，有几个人从我们这里出去，用言语搅扰你们，惑乱你们的心。〔注：有古卷加：你们必须受割礼，守摩西的律法。〕其实我们并没有吩咐他们。

chapters.en: So we all agreed to choose men to send to you along with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
chapters.zh: 所以，我们同心定意，拣选几个人，差他们同我们所亲爱的巴拿巴和保罗往你们那里去。

chapters.en: men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 这二人是为我主耶稣基督的名不顾性命的。

chapters.en: Therefore we are sending Judas and Silas to tell you in person the same things we are writing.
chapters.zh: 我们就差了犹大和西拉，他们也要亲口诉说这些事。

chapters.en: It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to burden you with anything beyond these essential requirements:
chapters.zh: 因为圣灵和我们定意不将别的重担放在你们身上，惟有几件事是不可少的，

chapters.en:
You must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid these things.
Farewell.
chapters.zh: 就是禁戒祭偶像的物和血，并勒死的牲畜和奸淫。这几件你们若能自己禁戒不犯就好了。愿你们平安！」

chapters.en: So the men were sent off and went down to Antioch, where they assembled the congregation and delivered the letter.
chapters.zh: 他们既奉了差遣，就下安提阿去，聚集众人，交付书信。

chapters.en: When the people read it, they rejoiced at its encouraging message.
chapters.zh: 众人念了，因为信上安慰的话就欢喜了。

chapters.en: Judas and Silas, who themselves were prophets, said much to encourage and strengthen the brothers.
chapters.zh: 犹大和西拉也是先知，就用许多话劝勉弟兄，坚固他们。

chapters.en: After spending some time there, they were sent off by the brothers in peace to return to those who had sent them.
chapters.zh: 住了些日子，弟兄们打发他们平平安安地回到差遣他们的人那里去。
〔注：有古卷加：34 惟有西拉定意仍住在那里。〕

chapters.en: But Paul and Barnabas remained at Antioch, along with many others, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord.
chapters.zh: 但保罗和巴拿巴仍住在安提阿，和许多别人一同教训人，传主的道。

chapters.en: Some time later Paul said to Barnabas, “Let us go back and visit the brothers in every town where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.”
chapters.zh: 过了些日子，保罗对巴拿巴说：「我们可以回到从前宣传主道的各城，看望弟兄们景况如何。」

chapters.en: Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark.
chapters.zh: 巴拿巴有意要带称呼马可的约翰同去；

chapters.en: But Paul thought it best not to take him, because he had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not accompanied them in the work.
chapters.zh: 但保罗因为马可从前在旁非利亚离开他们，不和他们同去做工，就以为不可带他去。

chapters.en: Their disagreement was so sharp that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,
chapters.zh: 于是二人起了争论，甚至彼此分开。巴拿巴带着马可，坐船往塞浦路斯去；

chapters.en: but Paul chose Silas and left, commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.
chapters.zh: 保罗拣选了西拉，也出去，蒙弟兄们把他交于主的恩中。

chapters.en: And he traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
chapters.zh: 他就走遍觜利亚、基利家，坚固众教会。

chapters.en: Paul came to Derbe and then to Lystra, where he found a disciple named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father.
chapters.zh: 保罗来到特庇，又到路司得。在那里有一个门徒，名叫提摩太，是信主之犹太妇人的儿子，他父亲却是希腊人。

chapters.en: The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.
chapters.zh: 路司得和以哥念的弟兄都称赞他。

chapters.en: Paul wanted Timothy to accompany him, so he took him and circumcised him on account of the Jews in that area, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
chapters.zh: 保罗要带他同去，只因那些地方的犹太人都知道他父亲是希腊人，就给他行了割礼。

chapters.en: As they went from town to town, they delivered the decisions handed down by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem for the people to obey.
chapters.zh: 他们经过各城，把耶路撒冷使徒和长老所定的条规交给门徒遵守。

chapters.en: So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew daily in numbers.
chapters.zh: 于是众教会信心越发坚固，人数天天加增。

chapters.en: After the Holy Spirit had prevented them from speaking the word in the province of Asia, they traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia.
chapters.zh: 圣灵既然禁止他们在亚细亚讲道，他们就经过弗吕家、加拉太一带地方。

chapters.en: And when they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them.
chapters.zh: 到了每西亚的边界，他们想要往庇推尼去，耶稣的灵却不许。

chapters.en: So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.
chapters.zh: 他们就越过每西亚，下到特罗亚去。

chapters.en: During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia standing and pleading with him, “Come over to Macedonia and help us.”
chapters.zh: 在夜间有异象现与保罗。有一个马其顿人站着求他说：「请你过到马其顿来帮助我们。」

chapters.en: As soon as Paul had seen the vision, we got ready to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.
chapters.zh: 保罗既看见这异象，我们随即想要往马其顿去，以为上帝召我们传福音给那里的人听。

chapters.en: We sailed from Troas straight to Samothrace, and the following day on to Neapolis.
chapters.zh: 于是从特罗亚开船，一直行到撒摩特喇，第二天到了尼亚坡里。

chapters.en: From there we went to the Roman colony of Philippi, the leading city of that district of Macedonia. And we stayed there several days.
chapters.zh: 从那里来到腓立比，就是马其顿这一方的头一个城，也是〔罗马〕的驻防城。我们在这城里住了几天。

chapters.en: On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate along the river, where it was customary to find a place of prayer. After sitting down, we spoke to the women who had gathered there.
chapters.zh: 当安息日，我们出城门，到了河边，知道那里有一个祷告的地方，我们就坐下对那聚会的妇女讲道。

chapters.en: Among those listening was a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshiper of God. The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message.
chapters.zh: 有一个卖紫色布疋的妇人，名叫吕底亚，是推雅推喇城的人，素来敬拜上帝。她听见了，主就开导她的心，叫她留心听保罗所讲的话。

chapters.en: And when she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.” And she persuaded us.
chapters.zh: 她和她一家既领了洗，便求我们说：「你们若以为我是真信主的〔注：或译：你们若以为我是忠心事主的〕，请到我家里来住」；于是强留我们。

chapters.en: One day as we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination, who earned a large income for her masters by fortune-telling.
chapters.zh: 后来，我们往那祷告的地方去。有一个使女迎着面来，她被巫鬼所附，用法术，叫她主人们大得财利。

chapters.en: This girl followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation!”
chapters.zh: 她跟随保罗和我们，喊着说：「这些人是至高上帝的仆人，对你们传说救人的道。」

chapters.en: She continued this for many days. Eventually Paul grew so aggravated that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!” And the spirit left her at that very moment.
chapters.zh: 她一连多日这样喊叫，保罗就心中厌烦，转身对那鬼说：「我奉耶稣基督的名，吩咐你从她身上出来！」那鬼当时就出来了。

chapters.en: When the girl’s owners saw that their hope of making money was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities in the marketplace.
chapters.zh: 使女的主人们见得利的指望没有了，便揪住保罗和西拉，拉他们到市上去见首领；

chapters.en: They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil
chapters.zh: 又带到官长面前说：「这些人原是犹太人，竟骚扰我们的城，

chapters.en: by promoting customs that are unlawful for us Romans to adopt or practice.”
chapters.zh: 传我们罗马人所不可受不可行的规矩。」

chapters.en: The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped and beaten with rods.
chapters.zh: 众人就一同起来攻击他们。官长吩咐剥了他们的衣裳，用棍打；

chapters.en: And after striking them with many blows, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them securely.
chapters.zh: 打了许多棍，便将他们下在监里，嘱咐禁卒严紧看守。

chapters.en: On receiving this order, he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.
chapters.zh: 禁卒领了这样的命，就把他们下在内监里，两脚上了木狗。

chapters.en: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.
chapters.zh: 约在半夜，保罗和西拉祷告，唱诗赞美上帝，众囚犯也侧耳而听。

chapters.en: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the foundations of the prison. At once all the doors flew open and everyone’s chains came loose.
chapters.zh: 忽然，地大震动，甚至监牢的地基都摇动了，监门立刻全开，众囚犯的锁鍊也都松开了。

chapters.en: When the jailer woke up and saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, presuming that the prisoners had escaped.
chapters.zh: 禁卒一醒，看见监门全开，以为囚犯已经逃走，就拔刀要自杀。

chapters.en: But Paul called out in a loud voice, “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!”
chapters.zh: 保罗大声呼叫说：「不要伤害自己！我们都在这里。」

chapters.en: Calling for lights, the jailer rushed in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.
chapters.zh: 禁卒叫人拿灯来，就跳进去，战战兢兢地俯伏在保罗、西拉面前；

chapters.en: Then he brought them out and asked, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”
chapters.zh: 又领他们出来，说：「二位先生，我当怎样行才可以得救？」

chapters.en: They replied, “Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household.”
chapters.zh: 他们说：「当信主耶稣，你和你一家都必得救。」

chapters.en: Then Paul and Silas spoke the word of the Lord to him and to everyone in his house.
chapters.zh: 他们就把主的道讲给他和他全家的人听。

chapters.en: At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds. And without delay, he and all his household were baptized.
chapters.zh: 当夜，就在那时候，禁卒把他们带去，洗他们的伤；他和属乎他的人立时都受了洗。

chapters.en: Then he brought them into his home and set a meal before them. So he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God.
chapters.zh: 于是禁卒领他们上自己家里去，给他们摆上饭。他和全家，因为信了上帝，都很喜乐。

chapters.en: When daylight came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order: “Release those men.”
chapters.zh: 到了天亮，官长打发差役来，说：「释放那两个人吧。」

chapters.en: The jailer informed Paul: “The magistrates have sent orders to release you. Now you may go on your way in peace.”
chapters.zh: 禁卒就把这话告诉保罗说：「官长打发人来叫释放你们，如今可以出监，平平安安地去吧。」

chapters.en: But Paul said to the officers, “They beat us publicly without a trial and threw us into prison, even though we are Roman citizens. And now do they want to send us away secretly? Absolutely not! Let them come themselves and escort us out!”
chapters.zh: 保罗却说：「我们是罗马人，并没有定罪，他们就在众人面前打了我们，又把我们下在监里，现在要私下撵我们出去吗？这是不行的。叫他们自己来领我们出去吧！」

chapters.en: So the officers relayed this message to the magistrates, who were alarmed to hear that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.
chapters.zh: 差役把这话回禀官长。官长听见他们是罗马人，就害怕了，

chapters.en: They came to appease them and led them out, requesting that they leave the city.
chapters.zh: 于是来劝他们，领他们出来，请他们离开那城。

chapters.en: After Paul and Silas came out of the prison, they went to Lydia’s house to see the brothers and encourage them. Then they left the city.
chapters.zh: 二人出了监，往吕底亚家里去，见了弟兄们，劝慰他们一番，就走了。

chapters.en: When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
chapters.zh: 保罗和西拉经过暗妃坡里、亚波罗尼亚，来到帖撒罗尼迦，在那里有犹太人的会堂。

chapters.en: As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue, and on three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
chapters.zh: 保罗照他素常的规矩进去，一连三个安息日，本着圣经与他们辩论，

chapters.en: explaining and proving that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. “This Jesus I am proclaiming to you is the Christ,” he declared.
chapters.zh: 讲解陈明基督必须受害，从死里复活；又说：「我所传与你们的这位耶稣就是基督。」

chapters.en: Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women.
chapters.zh: 他们中间有些人听了劝，就附从保罗和西拉，并有许多虔敬的希腊人，尊贵的妇女也不少。

chapters.en: The Jews, however, became jealous. So they brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar. They raided Jason’s house in search of Paul and Silas, hoping to bring them out to the people.
chapters.zh: 但那〔不信的〕犹太人心里嫉妒，招聚了些市井匪类，搭伙成群，耸动合城的人闯进耶孙的家，要将保罗、西拉带到百姓那里。

chapters.en: But when they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials, shouting, “These men who have turned the world upside down have now come here,
chapters.zh: 找不着他们，就把耶孙和几个弟兄拉到地方官那里，喊叫说：「那搅乱天下的也到这里来了，

chapters.en: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. They are all defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!”
chapters.zh: 耶孙收留他们。这些人都违背凯撒的命令，说另有一个王耶稣。」

chapters.en: On hearing this, the crowd and city officials were greatly disturbed.
chapters.zh: 众人和地方官听见这话，就惊慌了；

chapters.en: And they collected bond from Jason and the others and then released them.
chapters.zh: 于是取了耶孙和其余之人的保状，就释放了他们。

chapters.en: As soon as night had fallen, the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving there, they went into the Jewish synagogue.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们随即在夜间打发保罗和西拉往庇哩亚去。二人到了，就进入犹太人的会堂。

chapters.en: Now the Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians, for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true.
chapters.zh: 这地方的人贤于帖撒罗尼迦的人，甘心领受这道，天天考查圣经，要晓得这道是与不是。

chapters.en: As a result, many of them believed, along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men.
chapters.zh: 所以他们中间多有相信的，又有希腊尊贵的妇女，男子也不少。

chapters.en: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul was also proclaiming the word of God in Berea, they went there themselves to incite and agitate the crowds.
chapters.zh: 但帖撒罗尼迦的犹太人知道保罗又在庇哩亚传上帝的道，也就往那里去，耸动搅扰众人。

chapters.en: The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast, but Silas and Timothy remained in Berea.
chapters.zh: 当时弟兄们便打发保罗往海边去，西拉和提摩太仍住在庇哩亚。

chapters.en: Those who escorted Paul brought him to Athens and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.
chapters.zh: 送保罗的人带他到了雅典，既领了保罗的命，叫西拉和提摩太速速到他这里来，就回去了。

chapters.en: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply disturbed in his spirit to see that the city was full of idols.
chapters.zh: 保罗在雅典等候他们的时候，看见满城都是偶像，就心里着急；

chapters.en: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and God-fearing Gentiles, and in the marketplace with those he met each day.
chapters.zh: 于是在会堂里与犹太人和虔敬的人，并每日在市上所遇见的人，辩论。

chapters.en: Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also began to debate with him. Some of them asked, “What is this babbler trying to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign gods.” They said this because Paul was proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.
chapters.zh: 还有伊壁鸠鲁和斯多亚两门的学士，与他争论。有的说：「这胡言乱语的要说什么？」有的说：「他似乎是传说外邦鬼神的。」这话是因保罗传讲耶稣与复活的道。

chapters.en: So they took Paul and brought him to the Areopagus, where they asked him, “May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting?
chapters.zh: 他们就把他带到亚略‧巴古，说：「你所讲的这新道，我们也可以知道吗？

chapters.en: For you are bringing some strange notions to our ears, and we want to know what they mean.”
chapters.zh: 因为你有些奇怪的事传到我们耳中，我们愿意知道这些事是什么意思。」

chapters.en: Now all the Athenians and foreigners who lived there spent their time doing nothing more than hearing and articulating new ideas.
chapters.zh: （雅典人和住在那里的客人都不顾别的事，只将新闻说说听听。）

chapters.en: Then Paul stood up in the meeting of the Areopagus and said, “Men of Athens, I see that in every way you are very religious.
chapters.zh: 保罗站在亚略‧巴古当中，说：「众位雅典人哪，我看你们凡事很敬畏鬼神。

chapters.en:
For as I walked around and examined your objects of worship, I even found an altar with this inscription:
TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.
Therefore what you worship as something unknown, I now proclaim to you.
chapters.zh: 我游行的时候，观看你们所敬拜的，遇见一座坛，上面写着『未识之神』。你们所不认识而敬拜的，我现在告诉你们。

chapters.en: The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples made by human hands.
chapters.zh: 创造宇宙和其中万物的上帝，既是天地的主，就不住人手所造的殿，

chapters.en: Nor is He served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.
chapters.zh: 也不用人手服事，好像缺少什么；自己倒将生命、气息、万物，赐给万人。

chapters.en: From one man He made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.
chapters.zh: 他从一本〔注：本：有古卷是血脉〕造出万族的人，住在全地上，并且预先定准他们的年限和所住的疆界，

chapters.en: God intended that they would seek Him and perhaps reach out for Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.
chapters.zh: 要叫他们寻求上帝，或者可以揣摩而得，其实他离我们各人不远；

chapters.en: ‘For in Him we live and move and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘We are His offspring.’
chapters.zh: 我们生活、动作、存留，都在乎他。就如你们作诗的，有人说：『我们也是他所生的。』

chapters.en: Therefore, being offspring of God, we should not think that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by man’s skill and imagination.
chapters.zh: 我们既是上帝所生的，就不当以为上帝的神性像人用手艺、心思所雕刻的金、银、石。

chapters.en: Although God overlooked the ignorance of earlier times, He now commands all people everywhere to repent.
chapters.zh: 世人蒙昧无知的时候，上帝并不监察，如今却吩咐各处的人都要悔改。

chapters.en: For He has set a day when He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”
chapters.zh: 因为他已经定了日子，要藉着他所设立的人按公义审判天下，并且叫他从死里复活，给万人作可信的凭据。」

chapters.en: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some began to mock him, but others said, “We want to hear you again on this topic.”
chapters.zh: 众人听见从死里复活的话，就有讥诮他的；又有人说：「我们再听你讲这个吧！」

chapters.en: At that, Paul left the Areopagus.
chapters.zh: 于是保罗从他们当中出去了。

chapters.en: But some joined him and believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others who were with them.
chapters.zh: 但有几个人贴近他，信了〔主〕，其中有亚略‧巴古的官丢尼修，并一个妇人，名叫大马哩，还有别人一同信从。

chapters.en: After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.
chapters.zh: 这事以后，保罗离了雅典，来到哥林多。

chapters.en: There he found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to visit them,
chapters.zh: 遇见一个犹太人，名叫亚居拉，他生在本都；因为克劳第命犹太人都离开罗马，新近带着妻百基拉，从意大利来。保罗就投奔了他们。

chapters.en: and he stayed and worked with them because they were tentmakers by trade, just as he was.
chapters.zh: 他们本是制造帐棚为业。保罗因与他们同业，就和他们同住做工。

chapters.en: Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade Jews and Greeks alike.
chapters.zh: 每逢安息日，保罗在会堂里辩论，劝化犹太人和希腊人。

chapters.en: And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself fully to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
chapters.zh: 西拉和提摩太从马其顿来的时候，保罗为道迫切，向犹太人证明耶稣是基督。

chapters.en: But when they opposed and insulted him, he shook out his garments and told them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”
chapters.zh: 他们既抗拒、毁谤，保罗就抖着衣裳，说：「你们的罪〔注：原文是血〕归到你们自己头上，与我无干〔注：原文是我却干净〕。从今以后，我要往外邦人那里去。」

chapters.en: So Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titus Justus, a worshiper of God.
chapters.zh: 于是离开那里，到了一个人的家中；这人名叫提多‧犹士都，是敬拜上帝的，他的家靠近会堂。

chapters.en: Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his whole household believed in the Lord. And many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized.
chapters.zh: 管会堂的基利司布和全家都信了主，还有许多哥林多人听了，就相信受洗。

chapters.en: One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: “Do not be afraid; keep on speaking; do not be silent.
chapters.zh: 夜间，主在异象中对保罗说：「不要怕，只管讲，不要闭口，

chapters.en: For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on you, because I have many people in this city.”
chapters.zh: 有我与你同在，必没有人下手害你，因为在这城里我有许多的百姓。」

chapters.en: So Paul stayed for a year and a half, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians.
chapters.zh: 保罗在那里住了一年零六个月，将上帝的道教训他们。

chapters.en: While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews coordinated an attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.
chapters.zh: 到迦流作亚该亚方伯的时候，犹太人同心起来攻击保罗，拉他到公堂，

chapters.en: “This man is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law,” they said.
chapters.zh: 说：「这个人劝人不按着律法敬拜上帝。」

chapters.en: But just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio told the Jews, “If this matter involved a wrongdoing or vicious crime, O Jews, it would be reasonable for me to hear your complaint.
chapters.zh: 保罗刚要开口，迦流就对犹太人说：「你们这些犹太人！如果是为冤枉或奸恶的事，我理当耐性听你们。

chapters.en: But since it is a dispute about words and names and your own law, settle it yourselves. I refuse to be a judge of such things.”
chapters.zh: 但所争论的，若是关乎言语、名目，和你们的律法，你们自己去办吧！这样的事我不愿意审问」；

chapters.en: And he drove them away from the judgment seat.
chapters.zh: 就把他们撵出公堂。

chapters.en: At this, the crowd seized Sosthenes the synagogue leader and beat him in front of the judgment seat. But none of this was of concern to Gallio.
chapters.zh: 众人便揪住管会堂的所提尼，在堂前打他。这些事迦流都不管。

chapters.en: Paul remained in Corinth for quite some time before saying goodbye to the brothers. He had his head shaved in Cenchrea to keep a vow he had made, and then he sailed for Syria, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila.
chapters.zh: 保罗又住了多日，就辞别了弟兄，坐船往觜利亚去；百基拉、亚居拉和他同去。他因为许过愿，就在坚革哩剪了头发。

chapters.en: When they reached Ephesus, Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He himself went into the synagogue there and reasoned with the Jews.
chapters.zh: 到了以弗所，保罗就把他们留在那里，自己进了会堂，和犹太人辩论。

chapters.en: When they asked him to stay for a while longer, he declined.
chapters.zh: 众人请他多住些日子，他却不允，

chapters.en: But as he left, he said, “I will come back to you if God is willing.” And he set sail from Ephesus.
chapters.zh: 就辞别他们，说：「上帝若许我，我还要回到你们这里」；于是开船离了以弗所。

chapters.en: When Paul had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem. Then he went down to Antioch.
chapters.zh: 在凯撒利亚下了船，就上〔耶路撒冷〕去问教会安，随后下安提阿去。

chapters.en: After Paul had spent some time in Antioch, he traveled from place to place throughout the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
chapters.zh: 住了些日子，又离开那里，挨次经过加拉太和弗吕家地方，坚固众门徒。

chapters.en: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.
chapters.zh: 有一个犹太人，名叫亚波罗，来到以弗所。他生在亚历山大，是有学问〔注：或译：口才〕的，最能讲解圣经。

chapters.en: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and was fervent in spirit. He spoke and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.
chapters.zh: 这人已经在主的道上受了教训，心里火热，将耶稣的事详细讲论教训人；只是他单晓得约翰的洗礼。

chapters.en: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately.
chapters.zh: 他在会堂里放胆讲道；百基拉、亚居拉听见，就接他来，将上帝的道给他讲解更加详细。

chapters.en: When Apollos resolved to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. On his arrival, he was a great help to those who by grace had believed.
chapters.zh: 他想要往亚该亚去，弟兄们就勉励他，并写信请门徒接待他〔注：或译：弟兄们就写信劝门徒接待他〕。他到了那里，多帮助那蒙恩信主的人，

chapters.en: For he powerfully refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
chapters.zh: 在众人面前极有能力驳倒犹太人，引圣经证明耶稣是基督。

chapters.en: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul passed through the interior and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples
chapters.zh: 亚波罗在哥林多的时候，保罗经过了上边一带地方，就来到以弗所；在那里遇见几个门徒，

chapters.en:
and asked them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?”
“No,” they answered, “we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
chapters.zh: 问他们说：「你们信的时候受了圣灵没有？」他们回答说：「没有，也未曾听见有圣灵〔赐下来〕。」

chapters.en:
“Into what, then, were you baptized?” Paul asked.
“The baptism of John,” they replied.
chapters.zh: 保罗说：「这样，你们受的是什么洗呢？」他们说：「是约翰的洗。」

chapters.en: Paul explained: “John’s baptism was a baptism of repentance. He told the people to believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Jesus.”
chapters.zh: 保罗说：「约翰所行的是悔改的洗，告诉百姓当信那在他以后要来的，就是耶稣。」

chapters.en: On hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
chapters.zh: 他们听见这话，就奉主耶稣的名受洗。

chapters.en: And when Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.
chapters.zh: 保罗按手在他们〔头〕上，圣灵便降在他们身上，他们就说方言，又说预言〔注：或译：又讲道〕。

chapters.en: There were about twelve men in all.
chapters.zh: 一共约有十二个人。

chapters.en: Then Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months, arguing persuasively about the kingdom of God.
chapters.zh: 保罗进会堂，放胆讲道，一连三个月，辩论上帝国的事，劝化众人。

chapters.en: But when some of them stubbornly refused to believe and publicly maligned the Way, Paul took his disciples and left the synagogue to conduct daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
chapters.zh: 后来，有些人心里刚硬不信，在众人面前毁谤这道，保罗就离开他们，也叫门徒与他们分离，便在推喇奴的学房天天辩论。

chapters.en: This continued for two years, so that everyone who lived in the province of Asia, Jews and Greeks alike, heard the word of the Lord.
chapters.zh: 这样有两年之久，叫一切住在亚细亚的，无论是犹太人，是希腊人，都听见主的道。

chapters.en: God did extraordinary miracles through the hands of Paul,
chapters.zh: 上帝藉保罗的手行了些非常的奇事；

chapters.en: so that even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick, and the diseases and evil spirits left them.
chapters.zh: 甚至有人从保罗身上拿手巾或围裙放在病人身上，病就退了，恶鬼也出去了。

chapters.en: Now there were some itinerant Jewish exorcists who tried to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those with evil spirits. They would say, “I command you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.”
chapters.zh: 那时，有几个游行各处、念咒赶鬼的犹太人，向那被恶鬼附的人擅自称主耶稣的名，说：「我奉保罗所传的耶稣觢令你们出来！」

chapters.en: Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.
chapters.zh: 做这事的，有犹太祭司长士基瓦的七个儿子。

chapters.en: But one day the evil spirit responded, “Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?”
chapters.zh: 恶鬼回答他们说：「耶稣我认识，保罗我也知道。你们却是谁呢？」

chapters.en: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all. The attack was so violent that they ran out of the house naked and wounded.
chapters.zh: 恶鬼所附的人就跳在他们身上，胜了其中二人，制伏他们，叫他们赤着身子受了伤，从那房子里逃出去了。

chapters.en: This became known to all the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, and fear came over all of them. So the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.
chapters.zh: 凡住在以弗所的，无论是犹太人，是希腊人，都知道这事，也都惧怕；主耶稣的名从此就尊大了。

chapters.en: Many who had believed now came forward, confessing and disclosing their deeds.
chapters.zh: 那已经信的，多有人来承认诉说自己所行的事。

chapters.en: And a number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books and burned them in front of everyone. When the value of the books was calculated, the total came to fifty thousand drachmas.
chapters.zh: 平素行邪术的，也有许多人把书拿来，堆积在众人面前焚烧。他们算计书价，便知道共合五万块钱。

chapters.en: So the word of the Lord powerfully continued to spread and prevail.
chapters.zh: 主的道大大兴旺，而且得胜，就是这样。

chapters.en: After these things had happened, Paul resolved in the Spirit to go to Jerusalem, passing through Macedonia and Achaia. “After I have been there,” he said, “I must see Rome as well.”
chapters.zh: 这些事完了，保罗心里定意经过了马其顿、亚该亚，就往耶路撒冷去；又说：「我到了那里以后，也必须往罗马去看看。」

chapters.en: He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he stayed for a time in the province of Asia.
chapters.zh: 于是从帮助他的人中打发提摩太、以拉都二人往马其顿去，自己暂时等在亚细亚。

chapters.en: About that time there arose a great disturbance about the Way.
chapters.zh: 那时，因为这道起的扰乱不小。

chapters.en: It began with a silversmith named Demetrius who made silver shrines of Artemis, bringing much business to the craftsmen.
chapters.zh: 有一个银匠，名叫底米丢，是制造亚底米神银龛的，他使这样手艺人生意发达。

chapters.en: Demetrius assembled the craftsmen, along with the workmen in related trades. “Men,” he said, “you know that this business is our source of prosperity.
chapters.zh: 他聚集他们和同行的工人，说：「众位，你们知道我们是倚靠这生意发财。

chapters.en: And you can see and hear that not only in Ephesus, but in nearly the whole province of Asia, this Paul has persuaded a great number of people to turn away. He says that man-made gods are no gods at all.
chapters.zh: 这保罗不但在以弗所，也几乎在亚细亚全地，引诱迷惑许多人，说：『人手所做的，不是神。』这是你们所看见所听见的。

chapters.en: There is danger not only that our business will fall into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be discredited and her majesty deposed—she who is worshiped by all the province of Asia and the whole world.”
chapters.zh: 这样，不独我们这事业被人藐视，就是大女神亚底米的庙也要被人轻忽，连亚细亚全地和普天下所敬拜的大女神之威荣也要消灭了。」

chapters.en: When the men heard this, they were enraged and began shouting, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
chapters.zh: 众人听见，就怒气填胸，喊着说：「大哉，以弗所人的亚底米啊！」

chapters.en: Soon the whole city was in disarray. They rushed together into the theatre, dragging with them Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul’s traveling companions from Macedonia.
chapters.zh: 满城都轰动起来。众人拿住与保罗同行的马其顿人该犹和亚里达古，齐心拥进戏园里去。

chapters.en: Paul wanted to go before the assembly, but the disciples would not allow him.
chapters.zh: 保罗想要进去，到百姓那里，门徒却不许他去。

chapters.en: Even some of Paul’s friends who were officials of the province of Asia sent word to him, begging him not to venture into the theatre.
chapters.zh: 还有亚细亚几位首领，是保罗的朋友，打发人来劝他，不要冒险到戏园里去。

chapters.en: Meanwhile the assembly was in turmoil. Some were shouting one thing and some another, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
chapters.zh: 聚集的人纷纷乱乱，有喊叫这个的，有喊叫那个的；大半不知道是为什么聚集。

chapters.en: The Jews in the crowd pushed Alexander forward to explain himself, and he motioned for silence so he could make his defense to the people.
chapters.zh: 有人把亚历山大从众人中带出来，犹太人推他往前，亚历山大就摆手，要向百姓分诉；

chapters.en: But when they realized that he was a Jew, they all shouted in unison for about two hours: “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
chapters.zh: 只因他们认出他是犹太人，就大家同声喊着说：「大哉！以弗所人的亚底米啊。」如此约有两小时。

chapters.en: Finally the city clerk quieted the crowd and declared, “Men of Ephesus, doesn’t everyone know that the city of Ephesus is guardian of the temple of the great Artemis and of her image, which fell from heaven?
chapters.zh: 那城里的书记安抚了众人，就说：「以弗所人哪，谁不知道以弗所人的城是看守大亚底米的庙和从宙斯那里落下来的〔像〕呢？

chapters.en: Since these things are undeniable, you ought to be calm and not do anything rash.
chapters.zh: 这事既是驳不倒的，你们就当安静，不可造次。

chapters.en: For you have brought these men here, though they have neither robbed our temple nor blasphemed our goddess.
chapters.zh: 你们把这些人带来，他们并没有偷窃庙中之物，也没有谤讟我们的女神。

chapters.en: So if Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen have a complaint against anyone, the courts are open and proconsuls are available. Let them bring charges against one another there.
chapters.zh: 若是底米丢和他同行的人有控告人的事，自有放告的日子〔注：或译：自有公堂〕，也有方伯可以彼此对告。

chapters.en: But if you are seeking anything beyond this, it must be settled in a legal assembly.
chapters.zh: 你们若问别的事，就可以照常例聚集断定。

chapters.en: For we are in jeopardy of being charged with rioting for today’s events, and we have no justification to account for this commotion.”
chapters.zh: 今日的扰乱本是无缘无故，我们难免被查问。论到这样聚众，我们也说不出所以然来。」

chapters.en: After he had said this, he dismissed the assembly.
chapters.zh: 说了这话，便叫众人散去。

chapters.en: When the uproar had ended, Paul sent for the disciples. And after encouraging them, he said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.
chapters.zh: 乱定之后，保罗请门徒来，劝勉他们，就辞别起行，往马其顿去。

chapters.en: After traveling through that area and speaking many words of encouragement, he arrived in Greece,
chapters.zh: 走遍了那一带地方，用许多话劝勉门徒〔注：或译：众人〕，然后来到希腊。

chapters.en: where he stayed three months. And when the Jews formed a plot against him as he was about to sail for Syria, he decided to go back through Macedonia.
chapters.zh: 在那里住了三个月，将要坐船往觜利亚去，犹太人设计要害他，他就定意从马其顿回去。

chapters.en: Paul was accompanied by Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.
chapters.zh: 同他到亚细亚去的，有庇哩亚人毕罗斯的儿子所巴特，帖撒罗尼迦人亚里达古和西公都，还有特庇人该犹，并提摩太，又有亚细亚人推基古和特罗非摩。

chapters.en: These men went on ahead and waited for us in Troas.
chapters.zh: 这些人先走，在特罗亚等候我们。

chapters.en: And after the Feast of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi, and five days later we rejoined them in Troas, where we stayed seven days.
chapters.zh: 过了除酵的日子，我们从腓立比开船，五天到了特罗亚，和他们相会，在那里住了七天。

chapters.en: On the first day of the week we came together to break bread. Since Paul was ready to leave the next day, he talked to them and kept on speaking until midnight.
chapters.zh: 七日的第一日，我们聚会擘饼的时候，保罗因为要次日起行，就与他们讲论，直讲到半夜。

chapters.en: Now there were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered.
chapters.zh: 我们聚会的那座楼上，有好些灯烛。

chapters.en: And a certain young man named Eutychus, seated in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on. When he was sound asleep, he fell from the third story and was picked up dead.
chapters.zh: 有一个少年人，名叫犹推古，坐在窗台上，困倦沉睡。保罗讲了多时，少年人睡熟了，就从三层楼上掉下去；扶起他来，已经死了。

chapters.en: But Paul went down, threw himself on the young man, and embraced him. “Do not be alarmed!” he said. “He is still alive!”
chapters.zh: 保罗下去，伏在他身上，抱着他，说：「你们不要发慌，他的灵魂还在身上。」

chapters.en: Then Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, and ate. And after speaking until daybreak, he departed.
chapters.zh: 保罗又上去，擘饼，吃了，谈论许久，直到天亮，这才走了。

chapters.en: And the people were greatly relieved to take the boy home alive.
chapters.zh: 有人把那童子活活地领来，得的安慰不小。

chapters.en: We went on ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos, where we were to take Paul aboard. He had arranged this because he was going there on foot.
chapters.zh: 我们先上船，开往亚朔去，意思要在那里接保罗；因为他是这样安排的，他自己打算要步行。

chapters.en: And when he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.
chapters.zh: 他既在亚朔与我们相会，我们就接他上船，来到米推利尼。

chapters.en: Sailing on from there, we arrived the next day opposite Chios. The day after that we arrived at Samos, and on the following day we came to Miletus.
chapters.zh: 从那里开船，次日到了基阿的对面；又次日，在撒摩靠岸；又次日，来到米利都。

chapters.en: Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus to avoid spending time in the province of Asia, because he was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost.
chapters.zh: 乃因保罗早已定意越过以弗所，免得在亚细亚耽延，他急忙前走，巴不得赶五旬节能到耶路撒冷。

chapters.en: From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church.
chapters.zh: 保罗从米利都打发人往以弗所去，请教会的长老来。

chapters.en: When they came to him, he said, “You know how I lived the whole time I was with you, from the first day I arrived in the province of Asia.
chapters.zh: 他们来了，保罗就说：「你们知道，自从我到亚细亚的日子以来，在你们中间始终为人如何，

chapters.en: I served the Lord with great humility and with tears, especially in the trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews.
chapters.zh: 服事主，凡事谦卑，眼中流泪，又因犹太人的谋害，经历试炼。

chapters.en: I did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to you as I taught you publicly and from house to house,
chapters.zh: 你们也知道，凡与你们有益的，我没有一样避讳不说的，或在众人面前，或在各人家里，我都教导你们；

chapters.en: testifying to Jews and Greeks alike about repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 又对犹太人和希腊人证明当向上帝悔改，信靠我主耶稣基督。

chapters.en: And now, compelled by the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there.
chapters.zh: 现在我往耶路撒冷去，心甚迫切〔注：原文是心被捆绑〕，不知道在那里要遇见什么事；

chapters.en: I only know that in town after town the Holy Spirit warns me that chains and afflictions await me.
chapters.zh: 但知道圣灵在各城里向我指证，说有捆锁与患难等待我。

chapters.en: But I consider my life of no value to me, if only I may finish my course and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus—the ministry of testifying to the good news of God’s grace.
chapters.zh: 我却不以性命为念，也不看为宝贵，只要行完我的路程，成就我从主耶稣所领受的职事，证明上帝恩惠的福音。

chapters.en: Now I know that none of you among whom I have preached the kingdom will see my face again.
chapters.zh: 「我素常在你们中间来往，传讲上帝国〔的道〕；如今我晓得，你们以后都不得再见我的面了。

chapters.en: Therefore I testify to you this day that I am innocent of the blood of all men.
chapters.zh: 所以我今日向你们证明，你们中间无论何人死亡，罪不在我身上〔注：原文是我于众人的血是洁净的〕。

chapters.en: For I did not shrink back from declaring to you the whole will of God.
chapters.zh: 因为上帝的旨意，我并没有一样避讳不传给你们的。

chapters.en: Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood.
chapters.zh: 圣灵立你们作全群的监督，你们就当为自己谨慎，也为全群谨慎，牧养上帝的教会，就是他用自己血所买来的〔注：或译：救赎的〕。

chapters.en: I know that after my departure, savage wolves will come in among you and will not spare the flock.
chapters.zh: 我知道，我去之后必有兇暴的豺狼进入你们中间，不爱惜羊群。

chapters.en: Even from your own number, men will rise up and distort the truth to draw away disciples after them.
chapters.zh: 就是你们中间，也必有人起来说悖谬的话，要引诱门徒跟从他们。

chapters.en: Therefore be alert and remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you night and day with tears.
chapters.zh: 所以你们应当警醒，记念我三年之久昼夜不住地流泪、劝戒你们各人。

chapters.en: And now I commit you to God and to the word of His grace, which can build you up and give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.
chapters.zh: 如今我把你们交讬上帝和他恩惠的道；这道能建立你们，叫你们和一切成圣的人同得基业。

chapters.en: I have not coveted anyone’s silver or gold or clothing.
chapters.zh: 我未曾贪图一个人的金、银、衣服。

chapters.en: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.
chapters.zh: 我这两只手常供给我和同人的需用，这是你们自己知道的。

chapters.en: In everything, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
chapters.zh: 我凡事给你们作榜样，叫你们知道应当这样劳苦，扶助软弱的人，又当记念主耶稣的话，说：『施比受更为有福。』」

chapters.en: When Paul had said this, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
chapters.zh: 保罗说完了这话，就跪下同众人祷告。

chapters.en: They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.
chapters.zh: 众人痛哭，抱着保罗的颈项，和他亲嘴。

chapters.en: They were especially grieved by his statement that they would never see his face again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.
chapters.zh: 叫他们最伤心的，就是他说「以后不能再见我的面」那句话，于是送他上船去了。

chapters.en: After we had torn ourselves away from them, we sailed directly to Cos, and the next day on to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
chapters.zh: 我们离别了众人，就开船一直行到哥士。第二天到了罗底，从那里到帕大喇，

chapters.en: Finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we boarded it and set sail.
chapters.zh: 遇见一只船要往腓尼基去，就上船起行。

chapters.en: After sighting Cyprus and passing south of it, we sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre, where the ship was to unload its cargo.
chapters.zh: 望见塞浦路斯，就从南边行过，往觜利亚去，我们就在泰尔上岸，因为船要在那里卸货。

chapters.en: We sought out the disciples in Tyre and stayed with them seven days. Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 找着了门徒，就在那里住了七天。他们被圣灵感动，对保罗说：「不要上耶路撒冷去。」

chapters.en: But when our time there had ended, we set out on our journey. All the disciples, with their wives and children, accompanied us out of the city and knelt down on the beach to pray with us.
chapters.zh: 过了这几天，我们就起身前行。他们众人同妻子儿女，送我们到城外，我们都跪在岸上祷告，彼此辞别。

chapters.en: And after we had said our farewells, we went aboard the ship, and they returned home.
chapters.zh: 我们上了船，他们就回家去了。

chapters.en: When we had finished our voyage from Tyre, we landed at Ptolemais, where we greeted the brothers and stayed with them for a day.
chapters.zh: 我们从泰尔行尽了水路，来到多利买，就问那里的弟兄安，和他们同住了一天。

chapters.en: Leaving the next day, we went on to Caesarea and stayed at the home of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the Seven.
chapters.zh: 第二天，我们离开那里，来到凯撒利亚，就进了传福音的腓利家里，和他同住。他是那七个〔执事〕里的一个。

chapters.en: He had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
chapters.zh: 他有四个女儿，都是处女，是说预言的。

chapters.en: After we had been there several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
chapters.zh: 我们在那里多住了几天，有一个先知，名叫亚迦布，从犹太下来，

chapters.en: Coming over to us, he took Paul’s belt, bound his own feet and hands, and said, “The Holy Spirit says: ‘In this way the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and hand him over to the Gentiles.’”
chapters.zh: 到了我们这里，就拿保罗的腰带捆上自己的手脚，说：「圣灵说：犹太人在耶路撒冷，要如此捆绑这腰带的主人，把他交在外邦人手里。」

chapters.en: When we heard this, we and the people there pleaded with Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 我们和那本地的人听见这话，都苦劝保罗不要上耶路撒冷去。

chapters.en: Then Paul answered, “Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”
chapters.zh: 保罗说：「你们为什么这样痛哭，使我心碎呢？我为主耶稣的名，不但被人捆绑，就是死在耶路撒冷也是愿意的。」

chapters.en: When he would not be dissuaded, we quieted down and said, “The Lord’s will be done.”
chapters.zh: 保罗既不听劝，我们便住了口，只说：「愿主的旨意成就」，便了。

chapters.en: After these days, we packed up and went on to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 过了几日，我们收拾行李上耶路撒冷去。

chapters.en: Some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied us, and they took us to stay at the home of Mnason the Cypriot, an early disciple.
chapters.zh: 有凯撒利亚的几个门徒和我们同去，带我们到一个久为〔注：久为：或译老〕门徒的家里，叫我们与他同住；他名叫拿孙，是塞浦路斯人。

chapters.en: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us joyfully.
chapters.zh: 到了耶路撒冷，弟兄们欢欢喜喜地接待我们。

chapters.en: The next day Paul went in with us to see James, and all the elders were present.
chapters.zh: 第二天，保罗同我们去见雅各；长老们也都在那里。

chapters.en: Paul greeted them and recounted one by one the things that God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
chapters.zh: 保罗问了他们安，便将上帝用他传教，在外邦人中间所行之事，一一地述说了。

chapters.en: When they heard this, they glorified God. Then they said to Paul, “You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews have believed, and all of them are zealous for the law.
chapters.zh: 他们听见，就归荣耀与上帝，对保罗说：「兄台，你看犹太人中信主的有多少万，并且都为律法热心。

chapters.en: But they are under the impression that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or observe our customs.
chapters.zh: 他们听见人说，你教训一切在外邦的犹太人离弃摩西，对他们说，不要给孩子行割礼，也不要遵行条规。

chapters.en: What then should we do? They will certainly hear that you have come.
chapters.zh: 众人必听见你来了，这可怎么办呢？

chapters.en: Therefore do what we advise you. There are four men with us who have taken a vow.
chapters.zh: 你就照着我们的话行吧！我们这里有四个人，都有愿在身。

chapters.en: Take these men, purify yourself along with them, and pay their expenses so they can have their heads shaved. Then everyone will know that there is no truth to these rumors about you, but that you also live in obedience to the law.
chapters.zh: 你带他们去，与他们一同行洁净的礼，替他们拿出规费，叫他们得以剃头。这样，众人就可知道，先前所听见你的事都是虚的；并可知道，你自己为人，循规蹈矩，遵行律法。

chapters.en: As for the Gentile believers, we have written to them our decision that they must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality.”
chapters.zh: 至于信主的外邦人，我们已经写信拟定，叫他们谨忌那祭偶像之物，和血，并勒死的牲畜，与奸淫。」

chapters.en: So the next day Paul took the men and purified himself along with them. Then he entered the temple to give notice of the date when their purification would be complete and the offering would be made for each of them.
chapters.zh: 于是保罗带着那四个人，第二天与他们一同行了洁净的礼，进了殿，报明洁净的日期满足，只等〔祭司〕为他们各人献祭。

chapters.en: When the seven days were almost over, some Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul at the temple. They stirred up the whole crowd and seized him,
chapters.zh: 那七日将完，从亚细亚来的犹太人看见保罗在殿里，就耸动了众人，下手拿他，

chapters.en: crying out, “Men of Israel, help us! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against our people and against our law and against this place. Furthermore, he has brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.”
chapters.zh: 喊叫说：「以色列人来帮助，这就是在各处教训众人糟践〔我们〕百姓和律法，并这地方的。他又带着希腊人进殿，污秽了这圣地。」

chapters.en: For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they assumed that Paul had brought him into the temple.
chapters.zh: （这话是因他们曾看见以弗所人特罗非摩同保罗在城里，以为保罗带他进了殿。）

chapters.en: The whole city was stirred up, and the people rushed together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple, and at once the gates were shut.
chapters.zh: 合城都震动，百姓一齐跑来，拿住保罗，拉他出殿，殿门立刻都关了。

chapters.en: While they were trying to kill him, the commander of the Roman regiment received a report that all Jerusalem was in turmoil.
chapters.zh: 他们正想要杀他，有人报信给营里的千夫长说：「耶路撒冷合城都乱了。」

chapters.en: Immediately he took some soldiers and centurions and ran down to the crowd. When the people saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
chapters.zh: 千夫长立时带着兵丁和几个百夫长，跑下去到他们那里。他们见了千夫长和兵丁，就止住不打保罗。

chapters.en: The commander came up and arrested Paul, ordering that he be bound with two chains. Then he asked who he was and what he had done.
chapters.zh: 于是千夫长上前拿住他，吩咐用两条铁鍊捆锁；又问他是什么人，做的是什么事。

chapters.en: Some in the crowd were shouting one thing, and some another. And since the commander could not get at the truth because of the uproar, he ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks.
chapters.zh: 众人有喊叫这个的，有喊叫那个的；千夫长因为这样乱嚷，得不着实情，就吩咐人将保罗带进营楼去。

chapters.en: When Paul reached the steps, he had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the mob.
chapters.zh: 到了台阶上，众人挤得兇猛，兵丁只得将保罗抬起来。

chapters.en: For the crowd that followed him kept shouting, “Away with him!”
chapters.zh: 众人跟在后面，喊着说：「除掉他！」

chapters.en:
As they were about to take Paul into the barracks, he asked the commander, “May I say something to you?”
“Do you speak Greek?” he replied.
chapters.zh: 将要带他进营楼，保罗对千夫长说：「我对你说句话可以不可以？」他说：「你懂得希腊话吗？

chapters.en: “Aren’t you the Egyptian who incited a rebellion some time ago and led four thousand members of the Assassins into the wilderness?”
chapters.zh: 你莫非是从前作乱、带领四千凶徒往旷野去的那埃及人吗？」

chapters.en: But Paul answered, “I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city. Now I beg you to allow me to speak to the people.”
chapters.zh: 保罗说：「我本是犹太人，生在基利家的大数，并不是无名小城的人。求你准我对百姓说话。」

chapters.en: Having received permission, Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the crowd. A great hush came over the crowd, and he addressed them in Hebrew:
chapters.zh: 千夫长准了。保罗就站在台阶上，向百姓摆手，他们都静默无声，保罗便用希伯来话对他们说：

chapters.en: “Brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense before you.”
chapters.zh: 「诸位父兄请听，我现在对你们分诉。」

chapters.en:
When they heard him speak to them in Hebrew, they became even more silent.
Then Paul declared,
chapters.zh: 众人听他说的是希伯来话，就更加安静了。

chapters.en: “I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but raised in this city. I was educated at the feet of Gamaliel in strict conformity to the law of our fathers. I was just as zealous for God as any of you are today.
chapters.zh: 保罗说：「我原是犹太人，生在基利家的大数，长在这城里，在迦玛列门下，按着我们祖宗严紧的律法受教，热心事奉上帝，像你们众人今日一样。

chapters.en: I persecuted this Way even to the death, detaining both men and women and throwing them into prison,
chapters.zh: 我也曾逼迫奉这道的人，直到死地，无论男女都锁拿下监。

chapters.en: as the high priest and the whole Council can testify about me. I even obtained letters from them to their brothers in Damascus, and I was on my way to apprehend these people and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
chapters.zh: 这是大祭司和众长老都可以给我作见证的。我又领了他们达与弟兄的书信，往大马士革去，要把在那里〔奉这道〕的人锁拿，带到耶路撒冷受刑。」

chapters.en: About noon as I was approaching Damascus, suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed around me.
chapters.zh: 「我将到大马士革，正走的时候，约在晌午，忽然从天上发大光，四面照着我。

chapters.en: I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?’
chapters.zh: 我就仆倒在地，听见有声音对我说：『扫罗！扫罗！你为什么逼迫我？』

chapters.en:
‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked.
‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting,’ He replied.
chapters.zh: 我回答说：『主啊，你是谁？』他说：『我就是你所逼迫的拿撒勒人耶稣。』

chapters.en: My companions saw the light, but they could not understand the voice of the One speaking to me.
chapters.zh: 与我同行的人看见了那光，却没有听明那位对我说话的声音。

chapters.en:
Then I asked, ‘What should I do, Lord?’
‘Get up and go into Damascus,’ He told me. ‘There you will be told all that you have been appointed to do.’
chapters.zh: 我说：『主啊，我当做什么？』主说：『起来，进大马士革去，在那里，要将所派你做的一切事告诉你。』

chapters.en: Because the brilliance of the light had blinded me, my companions led me by the hand into Damascus.
chapters.zh: 我因那光的荣耀不能看见，同行的人就拉着我手进了大马士革。

chapters.en: There a man named Ananias, a devout observer of the law who was highly regarded by all the Jews living there,
chapters.zh: 那〔里〕有一个人，名叫亚拿尼亚，按着律法是虔诚人，为一切住在那里的犹太人所称赞。

chapters.en: came and stood beside me. ‘Brother Saul,’ he said, ‘receive your sight.’ And at that moment I could see him.
chapters.zh: 他来见我，站在旁边，对我说：『兄弟扫罗，你可以看见。』我当时往上一看，就看见了他。

chapters.en: Then he said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will and to see the Righteous One and to hear His voice.
chapters.zh: 他又说：『我们祖宗的上帝拣选了你，叫你明白他的旨意，又得见那义者，听他口中所出的声音。

chapters.en: You will be His witness to everyone of what you have seen and heard.
chapters.zh: 因为你要将所看见的，所听见的，对着万人为他作见证。

chapters.en: And now what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized, and wash your sins away, calling on His name.’
chapters.zh: 现在你为什么耽延呢？起来，求告他的名受洗，洗去你的罪。』」

chapters.en: Later, when I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying at the temple, I fell into a trance
chapters.zh: 「后来，我回到耶路撒冷，在殿里祷告的时候，魂游象外，

chapters.en: and saw the Lord saying to me, ‘Hurry! Leave Jerusalem quickly, because the people here will not accept your testimony about Me.’
chapters.zh: 看见主向我说：『你赶紧地离开耶路撒冷，不可迟延；因你为我作的见证，这里的人必不领受。』

chapters.en: ‘Lord,’ I answered, ‘they know very well that in one synagogue after another I imprisoned and beat those who believed in You.
chapters.zh: 我就说：『主啊，他们知道我从前把信你的人收在监里，又在各会堂里鞭打他们。

chapters.en: And when the blood of Your witness Stephen was shed, I stood there giving my approval and watching over the garments of those who killed him.’
chapters.zh: 并且你的见证人司提反被害流血的时候，我也站在旁边欢喜；又看守害死他之人的衣裳。』

chapters.en: Then He said to me, ‘Go! I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’”
chapters.zh: 主向我说：『你去吧！我要差你远远地往外邦人那里去。』」

chapters.en: The crowd listened to Paul until he made this statement. Then they lifted up their voices and shouted, “Rid the earth of him! He is not fit to live!”
chapters.zh: 众人听他说到这句话，就高声说：「这样的人，从世上除掉他吧！他是不当活着的。」

chapters.en: As they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air,
chapters.zh: 众人喧嚷，摔掉衣裳，把尘土向空中扬起来。

chapters.en: the commander ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks. He directed that Paul be flogged and interrogated to determine the reason for this outcry against him.
chapters.zh: 千夫长就吩咐将保罗带进营楼去，叫人用鞭子拷问他，要知道他们向他这样喧嚷是为什么缘故。

chapters.en: But as they stretched him out to strap him down, Paul said to the centurion standing there, “Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman citizen without a trial?”
chapters.zh: 刚用皮条捆上，保罗对旁边站着的百夫长说：「人是罗马人，又没有定罪，你们就鞭打他，有这个例吗？」

chapters.en: On hearing this, the centurion went and reported it to the commander. “What are you going to do?” he said. “This man is a Roman citizen.”
chapters.zh: 百夫长听见这话，就去见千夫长，告诉他说：「你要做什么？这人是罗马人。」

chapters.en:
The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?”
“Yes,” he answered.
chapters.zh: 千夫长就来问保罗说：「你告诉我，你是罗马人吗？」保罗说：「是。」

chapters.en:
“I paid a high price for my citizenship,” said the commander.
“But I was born a citizen,” Paul replied.
chapters.zh: 千夫长说：「我用许多银子才入了罗马的民籍。」保罗说：「我生来就是。」

chapters.en: At once those who were about to interrogate Paul stepped back, and the commander himself was alarmed when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains.
chapters.zh: 于是那些要拷问保罗的人就离开他去了。千夫长既知道他是罗马人，又因为捆绑了他，也害怕了。

chapters.en: The next day the commander, wanting to learn the real reason Paul was accused by the Jews, released him and ordered the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin to assemble. Then he brought Paul down and had him stand before them.
chapters.zh: 第二天，千夫长为要知道犹太人控告保罗的实情，便解开他，吩咐祭司长和全公会的人都聚集，将保罗带下来，叫他站在他们面前。

chapters.en: Paul looked directly at the Sanhedrin and said, “Brothers, I have conducted myself before God in all good conscience to this day.”
chapters.zh: 保罗定睛看着公会的人，说：「弟兄们，我在上帝面前行事为人都是凭着良心，直到今日。」

chapters.en: At this, the high priest Ananias ordered those standing near Paul to strike him on the mouth.
chapters.zh: 大祭司亚拿尼亚就吩咐旁边站着的人打他的嘴。

chapters.en: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! You sit here to judge me according to the law, yet you yourself violate the law by commanding that I be struck.”
chapters.zh: 保罗对他说：「你这粉饰的墙，上帝要打你！你坐堂为的是按律法审问我，你竟违背律法，吩咐人打我吗？」

chapters.en: But those standing nearby said, “How dare you insult the high priest of God!”
chapters.zh: 站在旁边的人说：「你辱骂上帝的大祭司吗？」

chapters.en: “Brothers,” Paul replied, “I was not aware that he was the high priest, for it is written: ‘Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people.’ ”
chapters.zh: 保罗说：「弟兄们，我不晓得他是大祭司；〔经上〕记着说：『不可毁谤你百姓的官长。』」

chapters.en: Then Paul, knowing that some of them were Sadducees and the others Pharisees, called out in the Sanhedrin, “Brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee. It is because of my hope in the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial.”
chapters.zh: 保罗看出大众一半是撒都该人，一半是法利赛人，就在公会中大声说：「弟兄们，我是法利赛人，也是法利赛人的子孙。我现在受审问，是为盼望死人复活。」

chapters.en: As soon as he had said this, a dispute broke out between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.
chapters.zh: 说了这话，法利赛人和撒都该人就争论起来，会众分为两党。

chapters.en: For the Sadducees say that there is neither a resurrection nor angels nor spirits, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all.
chapters.zh: 因为撒都该人说，没有复活，也没有天使和鬼魂；法利赛人却说，两样都有。

chapters.en: A great clamor arose, and some scribes from the party of the Pharisees got up and contended sharply, “We find nothing wrong with this man. What if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?”
chapters.zh: 于是大大地喧嚷起来。有几个法利赛党的文士站起来争辩说：「我们看不出这人有什么恶处，倘若有鬼魂或是天使对他说过话，怎么样呢？」

chapters.en: The dispute grew so violent that the commander was afraid they would tear Paul to pieces. He ordered the soldiers to go down and remove him by force and bring him into the barracks.
chapters.zh: 那时大起争吵，千夫长恐怕保罗被他们扯碎了，就吩咐兵丁下去，把他从众人当中抢出来，带进营楼去。

chapters.en: The following night the Lord stood near Paul and said, “Take courage! As you have testified about Me in Jerusalem, so also you must testify in Rome.”
chapters.zh: 当夜，主站在保罗旁边，说：「放心吧！你怎样在耶路撒冷为我作见证，也必怎样在罗马〔为我〕作见证。」

chapters.en: When daylight came, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.
chapters.zh: 到了天亮，犹太人同谋起誓，说：「若不先杀保罗就不吃不喝。」

chapters.en: More than forty of them were involved in this plot.
chapters.zh: 这样同心起誓的有四十多人。

chapters.en: They went to the chief priests and elders and said, “We have bound ourselves with a solemn oath not to eat anything until we have killed Paul.
chapters.zh: 他们来见祭司长和长老，说：「我们已经起了一个大誓，若不先杀保罗就不吃什么。

chapters.en: Now then, you and the Sanhedrin petition the commander to bring him down to you on the pretext of examining his case more carefully. We are ready to kill him on the way.”
chapters.zh: 现在你们和公会要知会千夫长，叫他带下保罗到你们这里来，假作要详细察考他的事；我们已经预备好了，不等他来到跟前就杀他。」

chapters.en: But when the son of Paul’s sister heard about the plot, he went into the barracks and told Paul.
chapters.zh: 保罗的外甥听见他们设下埋伏，就来到营楼里告诉保罗。

chapters.en: Then Paul called one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him.”
chapters.zh: 保罗请一个百夫长来，说：「你领这少年人去见千夫长，他有事告诉他。」

chapters.en: So the centurion took him to the commander and said, “Paul the prisoner sent and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”
chapters.zh: 于是把他领去见千夫长，说：「被囚的保罗请我到他那里，求我领这少年人来见你；他有事告诉你。」

chapters.en: The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside, and asked, “What do you need to tell me?”
chapters.zh: 千夫长就拉着他的手，走到一旁，私下问他说：「你有什么事告诉我呢？」

chapters.en: He answered, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul to the Sanhedrin tomorrow on the pretext of acquiring more information about him.
chapters.zh: 他说：「犹太人已经约定，要求你明天带下保罗到公会里去，假作要详细查问他的事。

chapters.en: Do not let them persuade you, because more than forty men are waiting to ambush him. They have bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they have killed him; they are ready now, awaiting your consent.”
chapters.zh: 你切不要随从他们；因为他们有四十多人埋伏，已经起誓说，若不先杀保罗就不吃不喝。现在预备好了，只等你应允。」

chapters.en: So the commander dismissed the young man and instructed him, “Do not tell anyone that you have reported this to me.”
chapters.zh: 于是千夫长打发少年人走，嘱咐他说：「不要告诉人你将这事报给我了。」

chapters.en: Then he called two of his centurions and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea in the third hour of the night.
chapters.zh: 千夫长便叫了两个百夫长来，说：「预备步兵二百，马兵七十，长枪手二百，今夜亥初往凯撒利亚去；

chapters.en: Provide mounts for Paul to take him safely to Governor Felix.”
chapters.zh: 也要预备牲口叫保罗骑上，护送到巡抚腓力斯那里去。」

chapters.en: And he wrote the following letter:
chapters.zh: 千夫长又写了文书，

chapters.en:
Claudius Lysias,
To His Excellency, Governor Felix:
Greetings.
chapters.zh: 大略说：「克劳第‧吕西亚，请巡抚腓力斯大人安。

chapters.en: This man was seized by the Jews, and they were about to kill him when I came with my troops to rescue him. For I had learned that he is a Roman citizen,
chapters.zh: 这人被犹太人拿住，将要杀害，我得知他是罗马人，就带兵丁下去救他出来。

chapters.en: and since I wanted to understand their charges against him, I brought him down to their Sanhedrin.
chapters.zh: 因要知道他们告他的缘故，我就带他下到他们的公会去，

chapters.en: I found that the accusation involved questions about their own law, but there was no charge worthy of death or imprisonment.
chapters.zh: 便查知他被告是因他们律法的辩论，并没有什么该死该绑的罪名。

chapters.en: When I was informed that there was a plot against the man, I sent him to you at once. I also instructed his accusers to present their case against him before you.
chapters.zh: 后来有人把要害他的计谋告诉我，我就立时解他到你那里去，又吩咐告他的人在你面前告他。〔注：有古卷加：愿你平安！〕」

chapters.en: So the soldiers followed their orders and brought Paul by night to Antipatris.
chapters.zh: 于是，兵丁照所吩咐他们的，将保罗夜里带到安提帕底。

chapters.en: The next day they returned to the barracks and let the horsemen go on with him.
chapters.zh: 第二天，让马兵护送，他们就回营楼去。

chapters.en: When the horsemen arrived in Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and presented Paul to him.
chapters.zh: 马兵来到凯撒利亚，把文书呈给巡抚，便叫保罗站在他面前。

chapters.en: The governor read the letter and asked what province Paul was from. Learning that he was from Cilicia,
chapters.zh: 巡抚看了文书，问保罗是哪省的人，既晓得他是基利家人，

chapters.en: he said, “I will hear your case when your accusers arrive.” Then he ordered that Paul be kept under guard in Herod’s Praetorium.
chapters.zh: 就说：「等告你的人来到，我要细听你的事」；便吩咐人把他看守在希律的衙门里。

chapters.en: Five days later the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, who presented to the governor their case against Paul.
chapters.zh: 过了五天，大祭司亚拿尼亚同几个长老，和一个辩士帖土罗下来，向巡抚控告保罗。

chapters.en: When Paul had been called in, Tertullus opened the prosecution: “Because of you, we have enjoyed a lasting peace, and your foresight has brought improvements to this nation.
chapters.zh: 保罗被提了来，帖土罗就告他说：

chapters.en: In every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, we acknowledge this with all gratitude.
chapters.zh: 「腓力斯大人，我们因你得以大享太平，并且这一国的弊病，因着你的先见得以更正了；我们随时随地满心感谢不尽。

chapters.en: But in order not to delay you any further, I beg your indulgence to hear us briefly.
chapters.zh: 惟恐多说，你嫌烦絮，只求你宽容听我们说几句话。

chapters.en: We have found this man to be a pestilence, stirring up dissension among the Jews all over the world. He is a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,
chapters.zh: 我们看这个人，如同瘟疫一般，是鼓动普天下众犹太人生乱的，又是拿撒勒教党里的一个头目，

chapters.en: and he even tried to desecrate the temple; so we seized him.
chapters.zh: 连〔圣〕殿他也想要污秽；我们把他捉住了。〔注：有古卷加：要按我们的律法审问，7 不料，千夫长吕西亚前来，甚是强横，从我们手中把他夺去，吩咐告他的人到你这里来。〕

chapters.en: By examining him yourself, you will be able to learn the truth about all our charges against him.”
chapters.zh: 你自己究问他，就可以知道我们告他的一切事了。」

chapters.en: The Jews concurred, asserting that these charges were true.
chapters.zh: 众犹太人也随着告他说：「事情诚然是这样。」

chapters.en: When the governor motioned for Paul to speak, he began his response: “Knowing that you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I gladly make my defense.
chapters.zh: 巡抚点头叫保罗说话。他就说：「我知道你在这国里断事多年，所以我乐意为自己分诉。

chapters.en: You can verify for yourself that no more than twelve days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship.
chapters.zh: 你查问就可以知道，从我上耶路撒冷礼拜到今日不过有十二天。

chapters.en: Yet my accusers did not find me debating with anyone in the temple or riling up a crowd in the synagogues or in the city.
chapters.zh: 他们并没有看见我在殿里，或是在会堂里，或是在城里，和人辩论，耸动众人。

chapters.en: Nor can they prove to you any of their charges against me.
chapters.zh: 他们现在所告我的事并不能对你证实了。

chapters.en: I do confess to you, however, that I worship the God of our fathers according to the Way, which they call a sect. I believe everything that is laid down by the Law and written in the Prophets,
chapters.zh: 但有一件事，我向你承认，就是他们所称为异端的道，我正按着那道事奉我祖宗的上帝，又信合乎〔律法〕的和〔先知书〕上一切所记载的，

chapters.en: and I have the same hope in God that they themselves cherish, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.
chapters.zh: 并且靠着上帝，盼望死人，无论善恶，都要复活，就是他们自己也有这个盼望。

chapters.en: In this hope, I strive always to maintain a clear conscience before God and man.
chapters.zh: 我因此自己勉励，对上帝对人，常存无亏的良心。

chapters.en: After several years, then, I returned to Jerusalem to bring alms to my people and to present offerings.
chapters.zh: 过了几年，我带着赒济本国的捐项和供献的物上去。

chapters.en: At the time they found me in the temple, I was ceremonially clean and was not inciting a crowd or an uproar. But there are some Jews from the province of Asia
chapters.zh: 正献的时候，他们看见我在殿里已经洁净了，并没有聚众，也没有吵嚷，惟有几个从亚细亚来的犹太人。

chapters.en: who ought to appear before you and bring charges, if they have anything against me.
chapters.zh: 他们若有告我的事，就应当到你面前来告我。

chapters.en: Otherwise, let these men state for themselves any crime they found in me when I stood before the Sanhedrin,
chapters.zh: 即或不然，这些人若看出我站在公会前，有妄为的地方，他们自己也可以说明。

chapters.en: unless it was this one thing I called out as I stood in their presence: ‘It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.’”
chapters.zh: 纵然有，也不过一句话，就是我站在他们中间大声说：『我今日在你们面前受审，是为死人复活〔的道理〕。』」

chapters.en: Then Felix, who was well informed about the Way, adjourned the hearing and said, “When Lysias the commander comes, I will decide your case.”
chapters.zh: 腓力斯本是详细晓得这道，就支吾他们说：「且等千夫长吕西亚下来，我要审断你们的事。」

chapters.en: He ordered the centurion to keep Paul under guard, but to allow him some freedom and permit his friends to minister to his needs.
chapters.zh: 于是吩咐百夫长看守保罗，并且宽待他，也不拦阻他的亲友来供给他。

chapters.en: After several days, Felix returned with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess. He sent for Paul and listened to him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 过了几天，腓力斯和他夫人－犹太的女子土西拉－一同来到，就叫了保罗来，听他讲论信基督耶稣的道。

chapters.en: As Paul expounded on righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix became frightened and said, “You may go for now. When I find the time, I will call for you.”
chapters.zh: 保罗讲论公义、节制，和将来的审判。腓力斯甚觉恐惧，说：「你暂且去吧，等我得便再叫你来。」

chapters.en: At the same time, he was hoping that Paul would offer him a bribe. So he sent for Paul frequently and talked with him.
chapters.zh: 腓力斯又指望保罗送他银钱，所以屡次叫他来，和他谈论。

chapters.en: After two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. And wishing to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in prison.
chapters.zh: 过了两年，波求‧非斯都接了腓力斯的任；腓力斯要讨犹太人的喜欢，就留保罗在监里。

chapters.en: Three days after his arrival in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem,
chapters.zh: 非斯都到了任，过了三天，就从凯撒利亚上耶路撒冷去。

chapters.en: where the chief priests and Jewish leaders presented their case against Paul. They urged Festus
chapters.zh: 祭司长和犹太人的首领向他控告保罗，

chapters.en: to grant them a concession against Paul by summoning him to Jerusalem, because they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way.
chapters.zh: 又央告他，求他的情，将保罗提到耶路撒冷来，他们要在路上埋伏杀害他。

chapters.en: But Festus replied, “Paul is being held in Caesarea, and I myself am going there soon.
chapters.zh: 非斯都却回答说：「保罗押在凯撒利亚，我自己快要往那里去」；

chapters.en: So if this man has done anything wrong, let some of your leaders come down with me and accuse him there.”
chapters.zh: 又说：「你们中间有权势的人与我一同下去，那人若有什么不是，就可以告他。」

chapters.en: After spending no more than eight or ten days with them, Festus went down to Caesarea. The next day he sat on the judgment seat and ordered that Paul be brought in.
chapters.zh: 非斯都在他们那里住了不过十天八天，就下凯撒利亚去；第二天坐堂，吩咐将保罗提上来。

chapters.en: When Paul arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many serious charges that they could not prove.
chapters.zh: 保罗来了，那些从耶路撒冷下来的犹太人周围站着，将许多重大的事控告他，都是不能证实的。

chapters.en: Then Paul made his defense: “I have committed no offense against the law of the Jews or against the temple or against Caesar.”
chapters.zh: 保罗分诉说：「无论犹太人的律法，或是〔圣〕殿，或是凯撒，我都没有干犯。」

chapters.en: But Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, said to Paul, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem to stand trial before me on these charges?”
chapters.zh: 但非斯都要讨犹太人的喜欢，就问保罗说：「你愿意上耶路撒冷去，在那里听我审断这事吗？」

chapters.en: Paul replied, “I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where I ought to be tried. I have done nothing wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.
chapters.zh: 保罗说：「我站在凯撒的堂前，这就是我应当受审的地方。我向犹太人并没有行过什么不义的事，这也是你明明知道的。

chapters.en: If, however, I am guilty of anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die. But if there is no truth to their accusations against me, no one has the right to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!”
chapters.zh: 我若行了不义的事，犯了什么该死的罪，就是死，我也不辞。他们所告我的事若都不实，就没有人可以把我交给他们。我要上告于凯撒。」

chapters.en: Then Festus conferred with his council and replied, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!”
chapters.zh: 非斯都和议会商量了，就说：「你既上告于凯撒，可以往凯撒那里去。」

chapters.en: After several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice came down to Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.
chapters.zh: 过了些日子，亚基帕王和百妮基氏来到凯撒利亚，问非斯都安。

chapters.en: Since they were staying several days, Festus laid out Paul’s case before the king: “There is a certain man whom Felix left in prison.
chapters.zh: 在那里住了多日，非斯都将保罗的事告诉王，说：「这里有一个人，是腓力斯留在监里的。

chapters.en: While I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders of the Jews presented their case and requested a judgment against him.
chapters.zh: 我在耶路撒冷的时候，祭司长和犹太的长老将他的事禀报了我，求我定他的罪。

chapters.en: I told them that it is not the Roman custom to hand a man over before he has had an opportunity to face his accusers and defend himself against their charges.
chapters.zh: 我对他们说，无论什么人，被告还没有和原告对质，未得机会分诉所告他的事，就先定他的罪，这不是罗马人的条例。

chapters.en: So when they came here with me, I did not delay. The next day I sat on the judgment seat and ordered that the man be brought in.
chapters.zh: 及至他们都来到这里，我就不耽延，第二天便坐堂，吩咐把那人提上来。

chapters.en: But when his accusers rose to speak, they did not charge him with any of the crimes I had expected.
chapters.zh: 告他的人站着告他；所告的，并没有我所逆料的那等恶事。

chapters.en: They only had some contentions with him regarding their own religion and a certain Jesus who had died, but whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
chapters.zh: 不过是有几样辩论，为他们自己敬鬼神的事，又为一个人名叫耶稣，是已经死了，保罗却说他是活着的。

chapters.en: Since I was at a loss as to how to investigate these matters, I asked if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried there on these charges.
chapters.zh: 这些事当怎样究问，我心里作难，所以问他说：『你愿意上耶路撒冷去，在那里为这些事听审吗？』

chapters.en: But when Paul appealed to be held over for the decision of the Emperor, I ordered that he be held until I could send him to Caesar.”
chapters.zh: 但保罗求我留下他，要听皇上审断，我就吩咐把他留下，等我解他到凯撒那里去。」

chapters.en:
Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would like to hear this man myself.”
“Tomorrow you will hear him,” Festus declared.
chapters.zh: 亚基帕对非斯都说：「我自己也愿听这人辩论。」非斯都说：「明天你可以听。」

chapters.en: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the auditorium, along with the commanders and leading men of the city. And Festus ordered that Paul be brought in.
chapters.zh: 第二天，亚基帕和百妮基大张威势而来，同着众千夫长和城里的尊贵人进了公厅。非斯都吩咐一声，就有人将保罗带进来。

chapters.en: Then Festus said, “King Agrippa and all who are present with us, you see this man. The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him, both here and in Jerusalem, crying out that he ought not to live any longer.
chapters.zh: 非斯都说：「亚基帕王和在这里的诸位啊，你们看这人，就是一切犹太人，在耶路撒冷和这里，曾向我恳求、呼叫说：『不可容他再活着。』

chapters.en: But I found he had done nothing worthy of death, and since he has now appealed to the Emperor, I decided to send him.
chapters.zh: 但我查明他没有犯什么该死的罪，并且他自己上告于皇帝，所以我定意把他解去。

chapters.en: I have nothing definite to write to our sovereign about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after this inquiry I may have something to write.
chapters.zh: 论到这人，我没有确实的事可以奏明主上。因此，我带他到你们面前，也特意带他到你亚基帕王面前，为要在查问之后有所陈奏。

chapters.en: For it seems unreasonable to me to send on a prisoner without specifying the charges against him.”
chapters.zh: 据我看来，解送囚犯，不指明他的罪案是不合理的。」

chapters.en:
Agrippa said to Paul, “You have permission to speak for yourself.”
Then Paul stretched out his hand and began his defense:
chapters.zh: 亚基帕对保罗说：「准你为自己辩明。」于是保罗伸手分诉，说：「

chapters.en: “King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate to stand before you today to defend myself against all the accusations of the Jews,
chapters.zh: 亚基帕王啊，犹太人所告我的一切事，今日得在你面前分诉，实为万幸；

chapters.en: especially since you are acquainted with all the Jewish customs and controversies. I beg you, therefore, to listen to me patiently.
chapters.zh: 更可幸的，是你熟悉犹太人的规矩和他们的辩论；所以求你耐心听我。

chapters.en: Surely all the Jews know how I have lived from my earliest childhood among my own people, and also in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 我从起初在本国的民中，并在耶路撒冷，自幼为人如何，犹太人都知道。

chapters.en: They have known me for a long time and can testify, if they are willing, that I lived as a Pharisee, adhering to the strictest sect of our religion.
chapters.zh: 他们若肯作见证就晓得，我从起初是按着我们教中最严紧的教门作了法利赛人。

chapters.en: And now I stand on trial because of my hope in the promise that God made to our fathers,
chapters.zh: 现在我站在这里受审，是因为指望上帝向我们祖宗所应许的；

chapters.en: the promise our twelve tribes are hoping to see fulfilled as they earnestly serve God day and night. It is because of this hope, O king, that I am accused by the Jews.
chapters.zh: 这应许，我们十二个支派，昼夜切切地事奉〔上帝〕，都指望得着。王啊，我被犹太人控告，就是因这指望。

chapters.en: Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?
chapters.zh: 上帝叫死人复活，你们为什么看作不可信的呢？

chapters.en: So then, I too was convinced that I ought to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
chapters.zh: 从前我自己以为应当多方攻击拿撒勒人耶稣的名，

chapters.en: And that is what I did in Jerusalem. With authority from the chief priests I put many of the saints in prison, and when they were condemned to death, I cast my vote against them.
chapters.zh: 我在耶路撒冷也曾这样行了。既从祭司长得了权柄，我就把许多圣徒囚在监里。他们被杀，我也出名定案。

chapters.en: I frequently had them punished in the synagogues, and I tried to make them blaspheme. In my raging fury against them, I even went to foreign cities to persecute them.
chapters.zh: 在各会堂，我屡次用刑强逼他们说亵渎的话，又分外恼恨他们，甚至追逼他们，直到外邦的城邑。」

chapters.en: In this pursuit I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.
chapters.zh: 「那时，我领了祭司长的权柄和命令，往大马士革去。

chapters.en: About noon, O king, as I was on the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and my companions.
chapters.zh: 王啊，我在路上，晌午的时候，看见从天发光，比日头还亮，四面照着我并与我同行的人。

chapters.en: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice say to me in Hebrew, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
chapters.zh: 我们都仆倒在地，我就听见有声音用希伯来话向我说：『扫罗！扫罗！为什么逼迫我？你用脚踢刺是难的！』

chapters.en:
‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked.
‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,’ the Lord replied.
chapters.zh: 我说：『主啊，你是谁？』主说：『我就是你所逼迫的耶稣。

chapters.en: ‘But get up and stand on your feet. For I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and as a witness of what you have seen from Me and what I will show you.
chapters.zh: 你起来站着，我特意向你显现，要派你作执事，作见证，将你所看见的事和我将要指示你的事证明出来。

chapters.en: I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them
chapters.zh: 我也要救你脱离百姓和外邦人的手。

chapters.en: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in Me.’
chapters.zh: 我差你到他们那里去，要叫他们的眼睛得开，从黑暗中归向光明，从撒但权下归向上帝；又因信我，得蒙赦罪，和一切成圣的人同得基业。』」

chapters.en: So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.
chapters.zh: 「亚基帕王啊，我故此没有违背那从天上来的异象；

chapters.en: First to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, then to everyone in the region of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, I declared that they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds worthy of their repentance.
chapters.zh: 先在大马士革，后在耶路撒冷和犹太全地，以及外邦，劝勉他们应当悔改归向上帝，行事与悔改的心相称。

chapters.en: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple courts and tried to kill me.
chapters.zh: 因此，犹太人在殿里拿住我，想要杀我。

chapters.en: But I have had God’s help to this day, and I stand here to testify to small and great alike. I am saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen:
chapters.zh: 然而我蒙上帝的帮助，直到今日还站得住，对着尊贵、卑贱、老幼作见证；所讲的并不外乎众先知和摩西所说将来必成的事，

chapters.en: that the Christ would suffer, and as the first to rise from the dead, would proclaim light to our people and to the Gentiles.”
chapters.zh: 就是基督必须受害，并且因从死里复活，要首先把光明的道传给百姓和外邦人。」

chapters.en: At this stage of Paul’s defense, Festus exclaimed in a loud voice, “You are insane, Paul! Your great learning is driving you to madness!”
chapters.zh: 保罗这样分诉，非斯都大声说：「保罗，你癫狂了吧。你的学问太大，反叫你癫狂了！」

chapters.en: But Paul answered, “I am not insane, most excellent Festus; I am speaking words of truth and sobriety.
chapters.zh: 保罗说：「非斯都大人，我不是癫狂，我说的乃是真实明白话。

chapters.en: For the king knows about these matters, and I can speak freely to him. I am confident that none of this has escaped his notice, because it was not done in a corner.
chapters.zh: 王也晓得这些事，所以我向王放胆直言，我深信这些事没有一件向王隐藏的，因都不是在背地里做的。

chapters.en: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.”
chapters.zh: 亚基帕王啊，你信先知吗？我知道你是信的。」

chapters.en: Then Agrippa said to Paul, “Can you persuade me in such a short time to become a Christian?”
chapters.zh: 亚基帕对保罗说：「你想少微一劝，便叫我作基督徒啊〔注：或译：你这样劝我，几乎叫我作基督徒了〕！」

chapters.en: “Short time or long,” Paul replied, “I wish to God that not only you but all who hear me this day may become what I am, except for these chains.”
chapters.zh: 保罗说：「无论是少劝是多劝，我向上帝所求的，不但你一个人，就是今天一切听我的，都要像我一样，只是不要像我有这些锁鍊。」

chapters.en: Then the king and the governor rose, along with Bernice and those seated with them.
chapters.zh: 于是，王和巡抚并百妮基与同坐的人都起来，

chapters.en: On their way out, they said to one another, “This man has done nothing worthy of death or imprisonment.”
chapters.zh: 退到里面，彼此谈论说：「这人并没有犯什么该死该绑的罪。」

chapters.en: And Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
chapters.zh: 亚基帕又对非斯都说：「这人若没有上告于凯撒，就可以释放了。」

chapters.en: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.
chapters.zh: 〔非斯都〕既然定规了，叫我们坐船往意大利去，便将保罗和别的囚犯交给御营里的一个百夫长，名叫犹流。

chapters.en: We boarded an Adramyttian ship about to sail for ports along the coast of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.
chapters.zh: 有一只亚大米田的船，要沿着亚细亚一带地方的海边走，我们就上了那船开行；有马其顿的帖撒罗尼迦人亚里达古和我们同去。

chapters.en: The next day we landed at Sidon, and Julius treated Paul with consideration, allowing him to visit his friends and receive their care.
chapters.zh: 第二天，到了西顿；犹流宽待保罗，准他往朋友那里去，受他们的照应。

chapters.en: After putting out from there, we sailed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.
chapters.zh: 从那里又开船，因为风不顺，就贴着塞浦路斯背风岸行去。

chapters.en: And when we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra in Lycia.
chapters.zh: 过了基利家、旁非利亚前面的海，就到了吕家的每拉。

chapters.en: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.
chapters.zh: 在那里，百夫长遇见一只亚历山大的船，要往意大利去，便叫我们上了那船。

chapters.en: After sailing slowly for many days, we arrived off Cnidus. When the wind impeded us, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
chapters.zh: 一连多日，船行得慢，仅仅来到革尼土的对面。因为被风拦阻，就贴着克里特背风岸，从撒摩尼对面行过。

chapters.en: After we had moved along the coast with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.
chapters.zh: 我们沿岸行走，仅仅来到一个地方，名叫佳澳；离那里不远，有拉西亚城。

chapters.en: By now much time had passed, and the voyage had already become dangerous because it was after the Fast. So Paul advised them,
chapters.zh: 走的日子多了，已经过了禁食的节期，行船又危险，保罗就劝众人说：

chapters.en: “Men, I can see that our voyage will be filled with disaster and great loss, not only to ship and cargo, but to our own lives as well.”
chapters.zh: 「众位，我看这次行船，不但货物和船要受损伤，大遭破坏，连我们的性命也难保。」

chapters.en: But contrary to Paul’s advice, the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship.
chapters.zh: 但百夫长信从掌船的和船主，不信从保罗所说的。

chapters.en: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided to sail on, hoping that somehow they could reach Phoenix to winter there. Phoenix was a harbor in Crete facing both southwest and northwest.
chapters.zh: 且因在这海口过冬不便，船上的人就多半说，不如开船离开这地方，或者能到菲尼基过冬。菲尼基是克里特的一个海口，一面朝东北，一面朝东南。

chapters.en: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had their opportunity. So they weighed anchor and sailed along, hugging the coast of Crete.
chapters.zh: 这时，微微起了南风，他们以为得意，就起了锚，贴近克里特行去。

chapters.en: But it was not long before a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island.
chapters.zh: 不多几时，狂风从岛上扑下来；那风名叫「友拉革罗」。

chapters.en: Unable to head into the wind, the ship was caught up. So we gave way and let ourselves be driven along.
chapters.zh: 船被风抓住，敌不住风，我们就任风刮去。

chapters.en: Passing to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we barely managed to secure the lifeboat.
chapters.zh: 贴着一个小岛的背风岸奔行，那岛名叫高大，在那里仅仅收住了小船。

chapters.en: After hoisting it up, the crew used ropes to undergird the ship. And fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and were driven along.
chapters.zh: 既然把小船拉上来，就用缆索捆绑船底，又恐怕在赛耳底沙滩上搁了浅，就落下篷来，任船飘去。

chapters.en: We were tossed so violently that the next day the men began to jettison the cargo.
chapters.zh: 我们被风浪逼得甚急，第二天众人就把〔货物〕抛在海里。

chapters.en: On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.
chapters.zh: 到第三天，他们又亲手把船上的器具抛弃了。

chapters.en: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the great storm continued to batter us, we abandoned all hope of being saved.
chapters.zh: 太阳和星辰多日不显露，又有狂风大浪催逼，我们得救的指望就都绝了。

chapters.en: After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete. Then you would have averted this disaster and loss.
chapters.zh: 众人多日没有吃什么，保罗就出来站在他们中间，说：「众位，你们本该听我的话，不离开克里特，免得遭这样的伤损破坏。

chapters.en: But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because you will not experience any loss of life, but only of the ship.
chapters.zh: 现在我还劝你们放心，你们的性命一个也不失丧，惟独失丧这船。

chapters.en: For just last night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me
chapters.zh: 因我所属所事奉的上帝，他的使者昨夜站在我旁边，说：

chapters.en: and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And look, God has granted you the lives of all who sail with you.’
chapters.zh: 『保罗，不要害怕，你必定站在凯撒面前，并且与你同船的人，上帝都赐给你了。』

chapters.en: So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me.
chapters.zh: 所以众位可以放心，我信上帝他怎样对我说，事情也要怎样成就。

chapters.en: However, we must run aground on some island.”
chapters.zh: 只是我们必要撞在一个岛上。」

chapters.en: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.
chapters.zh: 到了第十四天夜间，船在亚得里亚海飘来飘去。约到半夜，水手以为渐近旱地，

chapters.en: They took soundings and found that the water was twenty fathoms deep. Going a little farther, they took another set of soundings that read fifteen fathoms.
chapters.zh: 就探深浅，探得有十二丈；稍往前行，又探深浅，探得有九丈。

chapters.en: Fearing that we would run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak.
chapters.zh: 恐怕撞在石头上，就从船尾抛下四个锚，盼望天亮。
