chapters.en: Meanwhile, the sailors attempted to escape from the ship. Pretending to lower anchors from the bow, they let the lifeboat down into the sea.
chapters.zh: 水手想要逃出船去，把小船放在海里，假作要从船头抛锚的样子。

chapters.en: But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved.”
chapters.zh: 保罗对百夫长和兵丁说：「这些人若不等在船上，你们必不能得救。」

chapters.en: So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set it adrift.
chapters.zh: 于是兵丁砍断小船的绳子，由它飘去。

chapters.en: Right up to daybreak, Paul kept urging them all to eat: “Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food.
chapters.zh: 天渐亮的时候，保罗劝众人都吃饭，说：「你们悬望忍饿不吃什么，已经十四天了。

chapters.en: So for your own preservation, I urge you to eat something, because not a single hair of your head will be lost.”
chapters.zh: 所以我劝你们吃饭，这是关乎你们救命的事；因为你们各人连一根头发也不至于损坏。」

chapters.en: After he had said this, Paul took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.
chapters.zh: 保罗说了这话，就拿着饼，在众人面前祝谢了上帝，擘开吃。

chapters.en: They were all encouraged and took some food themselves.
chapters.zh: 于是他们都放下心，也就吃了。

chapters.en: In all, there were 276 of us on board.
chapters.zh: 我们在船上的共有二百七十六个人。

chapters.en: After the men had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.
chapters.zh: 他们吃饱了，就把船上的麦子抛在海里，为要叫船轻一点。

chapters.en: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.
chapters.zh: 到了天亮，他们不认识那地方，但见一个海湾，有岸可登，就商议能把船拢进去不能。

chapters.en: Cutting away the anchors, they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.
chapters.zh: 于是砍断缆索，弃锚在海里；同时也松开舵绳，拉起头篷，顺着风向岸行去。

chapters.en: But the ship struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves.
chapters.zh: 但遇着两水夹流的地方，就把船搁了浅；船头胶住不动，船尾被浪的猛力冲坏。

chapters.en: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom.
chapters.zh: 兵丁的意思要把囚犯杀了，恐怕有洑水脱逃的。

chapters.en: But the centurion, wanting to spare Paul’s life, thwarted their plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.
chapters.zh: 但百夫长要救保罗，不准他们任意而行，就吩咐会洑水的，跳下水去先上岸；

chapters.en: The rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. In this way everyone was brought safely to land.
chapters.zh: 其余的人可以用板子或船上的零碎东西上岸。这样，众人都得了救，上了岸。

chapters.en: Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
chapters.zh: 我们既已得救，才知道那岛名叫马耳他。

chapters.en: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.
chapters.zh: 土人看待我们，有非常的情分；因为当时下雨，天气又冷，就生火接待我们众人。

chapters.en: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.
chapters.zh: 那时，保罗拾起一捆柴，放在火上，有一条毒蛇，因为热了出来，咬住他的手。

chapters.en: When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”
chapters.zh: 土人看见那毒蛇悬在他手上，就彼此说：「这人必是个凶手，虽然从海里救上来，天理还不容他活着。」

chapters.en: But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.
chapters.zh: 保罗竟把那毒蛇甩在火里，并没有受伤。

chapters.en: The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
chapters.zh: 土人想他必要肿起来，或是忽然仆倒死了；看了多时，见他无害，就转念，说：「他是个神。」

chapters.en: Nearby stood an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.
chapters.zh: 离那地方不远，有田产是岛长部百流的；他接纳我们，尽情款待三日。

chapters.en: The father of Publius was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man.
chapters.zh: 当时，部百流的父亲患热病和痢疾躺着。保罗进去，〔为他〕祷告，按手在他身上，治好了他。

chapters.en: After this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well.
chapters.zh: 从此，岛上其余的病人也来，得了医治。

chapters.en: The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail.
chapters.zh: 他们又多方地尊敬我们；到了开船的时候，也把我们所需用的送到船上。

chapters.en: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island. It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead.
chapters.zh: 过了三个月，我们上了亚历山大的船往前行；这船以「宙斯双子」为记，是在那海岛过了冬的。

chapters.en: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
chapters.zh: 到了觜拉古，我们停泊三日；

chapters.en: From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.
chapters.zh: 又从那里绕行，来到利基翁。过了一天，起了南风，第二天就来到部丢利。

chapters.en: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.
chapters.zh: 在那里遇见弟兄们，请我们与他们同住了七天。这样，我们来到罗马。

chapters.en: The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.
chapters.zh: 那里的弟兄们一听见我们的信息就出来，到亚比乌市和三馆地方迎接我们。保罗见了他们，就感谢上帝，放心壮胆。

chapters.en: When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.
chapters.zh: 进了罗马城，〔注：有古卷加：百夫长把众囚犯交给御营的统领，惟有〕保罗蒙准和一个看守他的兵另住在一处。

chapters.en: After three days, he called together the leaders of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them, “Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.
chapters.zh: 过了三天，保罗请犹太人的首领来。他们来了，就对他们说：「弟兄们，我虽没有做什么事干犯本国的百姓和我们祖宗的规条，却被锁绑，从耶路撒冷解在罗马人的手里。

chapters.en: They examined me and wanted to release me, because there was no basis for a death sentence against me.
chapters.zh: 他们审问了我，就愿意释放我；因为在我身上，并没有该死的罪。

chapters.en: But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, even though I have no charge to bring against my nation.
chapters.zh: 无奈犹太人不服，我不得已，只好上告于凯撒，并非有什么事要控告我本国的百姓。

chapters.en: So for this reason I have called to see you and speak with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.”
chapters.zh: 因此，我请你们来见面说话，我原为以色列人所指望的，被这鍊子捆锁。」

chapters.en: The leaders replied, “We have not received any letters about you from Judea, nor have any of the brothers from there reported or even mentioned anything bad about you.
chapters.zh: 他们说：「我们并没有接着从犹太来论你的信，也没有弟兄到这里来报给我们说你有什么不好处。

chapters.en: But we consider your views worth hearing, because we know that people everywhere are speaking against this sect.”
chapters.zh: 但我们愿意听你的意见如何；因为这教门，我们晓得是到处被毁谤的。」

chapters.en: So they set a day to meet with Paul, and many people came to the place he was staying. He expounded to them from morning to evening, testifying about the kingdom of God and persuading them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets.
chapters.zh: 他们和保罗约定了日子，就有许多人到他的寓处来。保罗从早到晚，对他们讲论这事，证明上帝国〔的道〕，引摩西的律法和先知的书，以耶稣的事劝勉他们。

chapters.en: Some of them were convinced by what he said, but others refused to believe.
chapters.zh: 他所说的话，有信的，有不信的。

chapters.en: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: “The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet:
chapters.zh: 他们彼此不合，就散了；未散以先，保罗说了一句话，说：「圣灵藉先知以赛亚向你们祖宗所说的话是不错的。

chapters.en:
‘Go to this people and say, “You will be ever hearing but never understanding;
you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.”
chapters.zh: 他说： 你去告诉这百姓说： 你们听是要听见，却不明白； 看是要看见，却不晓得；

chapters.en:
For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears,
and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears,
understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.’
chapters.zh: 因为这百姓油蒙了心， 耳朵发沉， 眼睛闭着； 恐怕眼睛看见， 耳朵听见， 心里明白，回转过来， 我就医治他们。

chapters.en: Be advised, therefore, that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!”
chapters.zh: 所以你们当知道，上帝这救恩，如今传给外邦人，他们也必听受。」
〔注：有古卷加：29 保罗说了这话，犹太人议论纷纷地就走了。〕

chapters.en: Paul stayed there two full years in his own rented house, welcoming all who came to visit him.
chapters.zh: 保罗在自己所租的房子里住了足足两年。凡来见他的人，他全都接待，

chapters.en: Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 放胆传讲上帝国〔的道〕，将主耶稣基督的事教导人，并没有人禁止。

chapters.en: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, and set apart for the gospel of God—
chapters.zh: 耶稣基督的仆人保罗，奉召为使徒，特派传上帝的福音。

chapters.en: the gospel He promised beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures,
chapters.zh: 这福音是上帝从前藉众先知在圣经上所应许的，

chapters.en: regarding His Son, who was a descendant of David according to the flesh,
chapters.zh: 论到他儿子－我主耶稣基督。按肉体说，是从大卫后裔生的；

chapters.en: and who through the Spirit of holiness was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.
chapters.zh: 按圣善的灵说，因从死里复活，以大能显明是上帝的儿子。

chapters.en: Through Him and on behalf of His name, we received grace and apostleship to call all those among the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith.
chapters.zh: 我们从他受了恩惠并使徒的职分，在万国之中叫人为他的名信服真道；

chapters.en: And you also are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 其中也有你们这蒙召属耶稣基督的人。

chapters.en:
To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 我写信给你们在罗马、为上帝所爱、奉召作圣徒的众人。愿恩惠、平安从我们的父上帝并主耶稣基督归与你们！

chapters.en: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed all over the world.
chapters.zh: 第一，我靠着耶稣基督，为你们众人感谢我的上帝，因你们的信德传遍了天下。

chapters.en: God, whom I serve with my spirit in preaching the gospel of His Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you
chapters.zh: 我在他儿子福音上，用心灵所事奉的上帝可以见证，我怎样不住地提到你们；

chapters.en: in my prayers at all times, asking that now at last by God’s will I may succeed in coming to you.
chapters.zh: 在祷告之间常常恳求，或者照上帝的旨意，终能得平坦的道路往你们那里去。

chapters.en: For I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you,
chapters.zh: 因为我切切地想见你们，要把些属灵的恩赐分给你们，使你们可以坚固；

chapters.en: that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.
chapters.zh: 这样，我在你们中间，因你与我彼此的信心，就可以同得安慰。

chapters.en: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, how often I planned to come to you (but have been prevented from visiting until now), in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我不愿意你们不知道，我屡次定意往你们那里去，要在你们中间得些果子，如同在其余的外邦人中一样；只是到如今仍有阻隔。

chapters.en: I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.
chapters.zh: 无论是希腊人、化外人、聪明人、愚拙人，我都欠他们的债，

chapters.en: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.
chapters.zh: 所以情愿尽我的力量，将福音也传给你们在罗马的人。

chapters.en: I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, first to the Jew, then to the Greek.
chapters.zh: 我不以福音为耻；这福音本是上帝的大能，要救一切相信的，先是犹太人，后是希腊人。

chapters.en: For the gospel reveals the righteousness of God that comes by faith from start to finish, just as it is written: “The righteous will live by faith.”
chapters.zh: 因为上帝的义正在这福音上显明出来；这义是本于信，以至于信。如〔经上〕所记：「义人必因信得生。」

chapters.en: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness.
chapters.zh: 原来，上帝的忿怒从天上显明在一切不虔不义的人身上，就是那些行不义阻挡真理的人。

chapters.en: For what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.
chapters.zh: 上帝的事情，人所能知道的，原显明在人心里，因为上帝已经给他们显明。

chapters.en: For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood from His workmanship, so that men are without excuse.
chapters.zh: 自从造天地以来，上帝的永能和神性是明明可知的，虽是眼不能见，但藉着所造之物就可以晓得，叫人无可推诿。

chapters.en: For although they knew God, they neither glorified Him as God nor gave thanks to Him, but they became futile in their thinking and darkened in their foolish hearts.
chapters.zh: 因为，他们虽然知道上帝，却不当作上帝荣耀他，也不感谢他。他们的思念变为虚妄，无知的心就昏暗了。

chapters.en: Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools,
chapters.zh: 自称为聪明，反成了愚拙，

chapters.en: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles.
chapters.zh: 将不能朽坏之上帝的荣耀变为偶像，仿佛必朽坏的人和飞禽、走兽、昆虫的样式。

chapters.en: Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity for the dishonoring of their bodies with one another.
chapters.zh: 所以，上帝任凭他们逞着心里的情欲行污秽的事，以致彼此玷辱自己的身体。

chapters.en: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is forever worthy of praise! Amen.
chapters.zh: 他们将上帝的真实变为虚谎，去敬拜事奉受造之物，不敬奉那造物的主－主乃是可称颂的，直到永远。阿们！

chapters.en: For this reason God gave them over to dishonorable passions. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.
chapters.zh: 因此，上帝任凭他们放纵可羞耻的情欲。他们的女人把顺性的用处变为逆性的用处；

chapters.en: Likewise, the men abandoned natural relations with women and burned with lust for one another. Men committed indecent acts with other men and received in themselves the due penalty for their error.
chapters.zh: 男人也是如此，弃了女人顺性的用处，欲火攻心，彼此贪恋，男和男行可羞耻的事，就在自己身上受这妄为当得的报应。

chapters.en: Furthermore, since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, He gave them up to a depraved mind, to do what ought not to be done.
chapters.zh: 他们既然故意不认识上帝，上帝就任凭他们存邪僻的心，行那些不合理的事；

chapters.en: They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, greed, and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and malice. They are gossips,
chapters.zh: 装满了各样不义、邪恶、贪婪、恶毒〔注：或译：阴毒〕；满心是嫉妒、凶杀、争竞、诡诈、毒恨；

chapters.en: slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, and boastful. They invent new forms of evil; they disobey their parents.
chapters.zh: 又是谗毁的、背后说人的、怨恨上帝的〔注：或译：被上帝所憎恶的〕、侮慢人的、狂傲的、自夸的、捏造恶事的、违背父母的、

chapters.en: They are senseless, faithless, heartless, merciless.
chapters.zh: 无知的、背约的、无亲情的、不怜悯人的。

chapters.en: Although they know God’s righteous decree that those who do such things are worthy of death, they not only continue to do these things, but also approve of those who practice them.
chapters.zh: 他们虽知道上帝判定行这样事的人是当死的，然而他们不但自己去行，还喜欢别人去行。

chapters.en: You, therefore, have no excuse, you who pass judgment on another. For on whatever grounds you judge the other, you are condemning yourself, because you who pass judgment do the same things.
chapters.zh: 你这论断人的，无论你是谁，也无可推诿。你在什么事上论断人，就在什么事上定自己的罪；因你这论断人的，自己所行却和别人一样。

chapters.en: And we know that God’s judgment against those who do such things is based on truth.
chapters.zh: 我们知道这样行的人，上帝必照真理审判他。

chapters.en: So when you, O man, pass judgment on others, yet do the same things, do you think you will escape God’s judgment?
chapters.zh: 你这人哪，你论断行这样事的人，自己所行的却和别人一样，你以为能逃脱上帝的审判吗？

chapters.en: Or do you disregard the riches of His kindness, tolerance, and patience, not realizing that God’s kindness leads you to repentance?
chapters.zh: 还是你藐视他丰富的恩慈、宽容、忍耐，不晓得他的恩慈是领你悔改呢？

chapters.en: But because of your hard and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath against yourself for the day of wrath, when God’s righteous judgment will be revealed.
chapters.zh: 你竟任着你刚硬不悔改的心，为自己积蓄忿怒，以致上帝震怒，显他公义审判的日子来到。

chapters.en: God “will repay each one according to his deeds.”
chapters.zh: 他必照各人的行为报应各人。

chapters.en: To those who by perseverance in doing good seek glory, honor, and immortality, He will give eternal life.
chapters.zh: 凡恒心行善、寻求荣耀、尊贵和不能朽坏〔之福〕的，就以永生报应他们；

chapters.en: But for those who are self-seeking and who reject the truth and follow wickedness, there will be wrath and anger.
chapters.zh: 惟有结党、不顺从真理、反顺从不义的，就以忿怒、恼恨报应他们；

chapters.en: There will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil, first for the Jew, then for the Greek;
chapters.zh: 将患难、困苦加给一切作恶的人，先是犹太人，后是希腊人，

chapters.en: but glory, honor, and peace for everyone who does good, first for the Jew, then for the Greek.
chapters.zh: 却将荣耀、尊贵、平安加给一切行善的人，先是犹太人，后是希腊人。

chapters.en: For God does not show favoritism.
chapters.zh: 因为上帝不偏待人。

chapters.en: All who sin apart from the law will also perish apart from the law, and all who sin under the law will be judged by the law.
chapters.zh: 凡没有律法犯了罪的，也必不按律法灭亡；凡在律法以下犯了罪的，也必按律法受审判。

chapters.en: For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but it is the doers of the law who will be declared righteous.
chapters.zh: （原来在上帝面前，不是听律法的为义，乃是行律法的称义。

chapters.en: Indeed, when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law.
chapters.zh: 没有律法的外邦人若顺着本性行律法上的事，他们虽然没有律法，自己就是自己的律法。

chapters.en: So they show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, their consciences also bearing witness, and their thoughts either accusing or defending them
chapters.zh: 这是显出律法的功用刻在他们心里，他们是非之心同作见证，并且他们的思念互相较量，或以为是，或以为非。）

chapters.en: on the day when God will judge men’s secrets through Christ Jesus, as proclaimed by my gospel.
chapters.zh: 就在上帝藉耶稣基督审判人隐祕事的日子，照着我的福音所言。

chapters.en: Now you, if you call yourself a Jew; if you rely on the law and boast in God;
chapters.zh: 你称为犹太人，又倚靠律法，且指着上帝夸口；

chapters.en: if you know His will and approve of what is superior because you are instructed by the law;
chapters.zh: 既从律法中受了教训，就晓得上帝的旨意，也能分别是非〔注：或译：也喜爱那美好的事〕；

chapters.en: if you are convinced that you are a guide for the blind, a light for those in darkness,
chapters.zh: 又深信自己是给瞎子领路的，是黑暗中人的光，

chapters.en: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, because you have in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth—
chapters.zh: 是蠢笨人的师傅，是小孩子的先生，在律法上有知识和真理的模范。

chapters.en: you, then, who teach others, do you not teach yourself? You who preach against stealing, do you steal?
chapters.zh: 你既是教导别人，还不教导自己吗？你讲说人不可偷窃，自己还偷窃吗？

chapters.en: You who forbid adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
chapters.zh: 你说人不可奸淫，自己还奸淫吗？你厌恶偶像，自己还偷窃庙中之物吗？

chapters.en: You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?
chapters.zh: 你指着律法夸口，自己倒犯律法、玷辱上帝吗？

chapters.en: As it is written: “God’s name is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.”
chapters.zh: 上帝的名在外邦人中，因你们受了亵渎，正如〔经上〕所记的。

chapters.en: Circumcision has value if you observe the law, but if you break the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
chapters.zh: 你若是行律法的，割礼固然于你有益；若是犯律法的，你的割礼就算不得割礼。

chapters.en: If a man who is not circumcised keeps the requirements of the law, will not his uncircumcision be regarded as circumcision?
chapters.zh: 所以那未受割礼的，若遵守律法的条例，他虽然未受割礼，岂不算是有割礼吗？

chapters.en: The one who is physically uncircumcised yet keeps the law will condemn you who, even though you have the written code and circumcision, are a lawbreaker.
chapters.zh: 而且那本来未受割礼的，若能全守律法，岂不是要审判你这有仪文和割礼竟犯律法的人吗？

chapters.en: A man is not a Jew because he is one outwardly, nor is circumcision only outward and physical.
chapters.zh: 因为外面作犹太人的，不是〔真〕犹太人；外面肉身的割礼，也不是〔真〕割礼。

chapters.en: No, a man is a Jew because he is one inwardly, and circumcision is a matter of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the written code. Such a man’s praise does not come from men, but from God.
chapters.zh: 惟有里面作的，才是〔真〕犹太人；〔真〕割礼也是心里的，在乎灵，不在乎仪文。这人的称赞不是从人来的，乃是从上帝来的。

chapters.en: What, then, is the advantage of being a Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision?
chapters.zh: 这样说来，犹太人有什么长处？割礼有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: Much in every way. First of all, they have been entrusted with the very words of God.
chapters.zh: 凡事大有好处：第一是上帝的圣言交讬他们。

chapters.en: What if some did not have faith? Will their lack of faith nullify God’s faithfulness?
chapters.zh: 即便有不信的，这有何妨呢？难道他们的不信就废掉上帝的信吗？

chapters.en:
Certainly not! Let God be true and every man a liar. As it is written:
“So that You may be proved right when You speak and victorious when You judge.”
chapters.zh: 断乎不能！不如说，上帝是真实的，人都是虚谎的。如〔经上〕所记： 你责备人的时候，显为公义； 被人议论的时候，可以得胜。

chapters.en: But if our unrighteousness highlights the righteousness of God, what shall we say? That God is unjust to inflict His wrath on us? I am speaking in human terms.
chapters.zh: 我且照着人的常话说，我们的不义若显出上帝的义来，我们可以怎么说呢？上帝降怒，是他不义吗？

chapters.en: Certainly not! In that case, how could God judge the world?
chapters.zh: 断乎不是！若是这样，上帝怎能审判世界呢？

chapters.en: However, if my falsehood accentuates God’s truthfulness, to the increase of His glory, why am I still condemned as a sinner?
chapters.zh: 若上帝的真实，因我的虚谎越发显出他的荣耀，为什么我还受审判，好像罪人呢？

chapters.en: Why not say, as some slanderously claim that we say, “Let us do evil that good may result”? Their condemnation is deserved!
chapters.zh: 为什么不说，我们可以作恶以成善呢？这是毁谤我们的人说我们有这话。这等人定罪是该当的。

chapters.en: What then? Are we any better? Not at all. For we have already made the charge that Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin.
chapters.zh: 这却怎么样呢？我们比他们强吗？决不是的！因我们已经证明：犹太人和希腊人都在罪恶之下。

chapters.en:
As it is written:
“There is no one righteous, not even one.
chapters.zh: 就如〔经上〕所记： 没有义人，连一个也没有。

chapters.en: There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God.
chapters.zh: 没有明白的； 没有寻求上帝的；

chapters.en: All have turned away, they have together become worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one.”
chapters.zh: 都是偏离正路， 一同变为无用。 没有行善的，连一个也没有。

chapters.en:
“Their throats are open graves; their tongues practice deceit.”
“The venom of vipers is on their lips.”
chapters.zh: 他们的喉咙是敞开的坟墓； 他们用舌头弄诡诈， 嘴唇里有虺蛇的毒气，

chapters.en: “Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness.”
chapters.zh: 满口是咒骂苦毒。

chapters.en: “Their feet are swift to shed blood;
chapters.zh: 杀人流血， 他们的脚飞跑，

chapters.en: ruin and misery lie in their wake,
chapters.zh: 所经过的路便行残害暴虐的事。

chapters.en: and the way of peace they have not known.”
chapters.zh: 平安的路，他们未曾知道；

chapters.en: “There is no fear of God before their eyes.”
chapters.zh: 他们眼中不怕上帝。

chapters.en: Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.
chapters.zh: 我们晓得律法上的话都是对律法以下之人说的，好塞住各人的口，叫普世的人都伏在上帝审判之下。

chapters.en: Therefore no one will be justified in His sight by works of the law. For the law merely brings awareness of sin.
chapters.zh: 所以凡有血气的，没有一个因行律法能在上帝面前称义，因为律法本是叫人知罪。

chapters.en: But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, as attested by the Law and the Prophets.
chapters.zh: 但如今，上帝的义在律法以外已经显明出来，有律法和先知为证：

chapters.en: And this righteousness from God comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all who believe. There is no distinction,
chapters.zh: 就是上帝的义，因信耶稣基督加给一切相信的人，并没有分别。

chapters.en: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
chapters.zh: 因为世人都犯了罪，亏缺了上帝的荣耀；

chapters.en: and are justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 如今却蒙上帝的恩典，因基督耶稣的救赎，就白白地称义。

chapters.en: God presented Him as an atoning sacrifice in His blood through faith, in order to demonstrate His righteousness, because in His forbearance He had passed over the sins committed beforehand.
chapters.zh: 上帝设立耶稣作挽回祭，是凭着耶稣的血，藉着人的信，要显明上帝的义；因为他用忍耐的心宽容人先时所犯的罪，

chapters.en: He did this to demonstrate His righteousness at the present time, so as to be just and to justify the one who has faith in Jesus.
chapters.zh: 好在今时显明他的义，使人知道他自己为义，也称信耶稣的人为义。

chapters.en: Where, then, is boasting? It is excluded. On what principle? On that of works? No, but on that of faith.
chapters.zh: 既是这样，哪里能夸口呢？没有可夸的了。用何法没有的呢？是用立功之法吗？不是，乃用信〔主〕之法。

chapters.en: For we maintain that a man is justified by faith apart from works of the law.
chapters.zh: 所以〔注：有古卷：因为〕我们看定了：人称义是因着信，不在乎遵行律法。

chapters.en: Is God the God of Jews only? Is He not the God of Gentiles too? Yes, of Gentiles too,
chapters.zh: 难道上帝只作犹太人的上帝吗？不也是作外邦人的上帝吗？是的，也作外邦人的上帝。

chapters.en: since there is only one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through that same faith.
chapters.zh: 上帝既是一位，他就要因信称那受割礼的为义，也要因信称那未受割礼的为义。

chapters.en: Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Certainly not! Instead, we uphold the law.
chapters.zh: 这样，我们因信废了律法吗？断乎不是！更是坚固律法。

chapters.en: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has discovered?
chapters.zh: 如此说来，我们的祖宗亚伯拉罕凭着肉体得了什么呢？

chapters.en: If Abraham was indeed justified by works, he had something to boast about, but not before God.
chapters.zh: 倘若亚伯拉罕是因行为称义，就有可夸的；只是在上帝面前并无可夸。

chapters.en: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”
chapters.zh: 经上说什么呢？说：「亚伯拉罕信上帝，这就算为他的义。」

chapters.en: Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation.
chapters.zh: 做工的得工价，不算恩典，乃是该得的；

chapters.en: However, to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is credited as righteousness.
chapters.zh: 惟有不做工的，只信称罪人为义的上帝，他的信就算为义。

chapters.en: And David speaks likewise of the blessedness of the man to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:
chapters.zh: 正如大卫称那在行为以外蒙上帝算为义的人是有福的。

chapters.en: “Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.
chapters.zh: 〔他〕说： 得赦免其过、遮盖其罪的， 这人是有福的。

chapters.en: Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him.”
chapters.zh: 主不算为有罪的， 这人是有福的。

chapters.en: Is this blessing only on the circumcised, or also on the uncircumcised? We have been saying that Abraham’s faith was credited to him as righteousness.
chapters.zh: 如此看来，这福是单加给那受割礼的人吗？不也是加给那未受割礼的人吗？因我们所说，亚伯拉罕的信，就算为他的义，

chapters.en: In what context was it credited? Was it after his circumcision, or before? It was not after, but before.
chapters.zh: 是怎么算的呢？是在他受割礼的时候呢？是在他未受割礼的时候呢？不是在受割礼的时候，乃是在未受割礼的时候。

chapters.en: And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that he had by faith while he was still uncircumcised. So then, he is the father of all who believe but are not circumcised, in order that righteousness might be credited to them.
chapters.zh: 并且他受了割礼的记号，作他未受割礼的时候因信称义的印证，叫他作一切未受割礼而信之人的父，使他们也算为义；

chapters.en: And he is also the father of the circumcised who not only are circumcised, but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.
chapters.zh: 又作受割礼之人的父，就是那些不但受割礼，并且按我们的祖宗亚伯拉罕未受割礼而信之踪迹去行的人。

chapters.en: For the promise to Abraham and his offspring that he would be heir of the world was not given through the law, but through the righteousness that comes by faith.
chapters.zh: 因为〔上帝〕应许亚伯拉罕和他后裔，必得承受世界，不是因律法，乃是因信而得的义。

chapters.en: For if those who live by the law are heirs, faith is useless and the promise is worthless,
chapters.zh: 若是属乎律法的人才得为后嗣，信就归于虚空，应许也就废弃了。

chapters.en: because the law brings wrath. And where there is no law, there is no transgression.
chapters.zh: 因为律法是惹动忿怒的〔注：或译：叫人受刑的〕；哪里没有律法，那里就没有过犯。

chapters.en: Therefore, the promise comes by faith, so that it may rest on grace and may be guaranteed to all Abraham’s offspring—not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham. He is the father of us all.
chapters.zh: 所以〔人得为后嗣〕是本乎信，因此就属乎恩，叫应许定然归给一切后裔；不但归给那属乎律法的，也归给那效法亚伯拉罕之信的。

chapters.en: As it is written: “I have made you a father of many nations.” He is our father in the presence of God, in whom he believed, the God who gives life to the dead and calls into being what does not yet exist.
chapters.zh: 亚伯拉罕所信的，是那叫死人复活、使无变为有的上帝，他在主面前作我们世人的父。如〔经上〕所记：「我已经立你作多国的父。」

chapters.en: Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed and so became the father of many nations, just as he had been told, “So shall your offspring be.”
chapters.zh: 他在无可指望的时候，因信仍有指望，就得以作多国的父，正如先前所说：「你的后裔将要如此。」

chapters.en: Without weakening in his faith, he acknowledged the decrepitness of his body (since he was about a hundred years old) and the lifelessness of Sarah’s womb.
chapters.zh: 他将近百岁的时候，虽然想到自己的身体如同已死，撒拉的生育已经断绝，他的信心还是不软弱；

chapters.en: Yet he did not waver through disbelief in the promise of God, but was strengthened in his faith and gave glory to God,
chapters.zh: 并且仰望上帝的应许，总没有因不信心里起疑惑，反倒因信心里得坚固，将荣耀归给上帝，

chapters.en: being fully persuaded that God was able to do what He had promised.
chapters.zh: 且满心相信上帝所应许的必能做成。

chapters.en: This is why “it was credited to him as righteousness.”
chapters.zh: 所以，这就算为他的义。

chapters.en: Now the words “it was credited to him” were written not only for Abraham,
chapters.zh: 「算为他义」的这句话不是单为他写的，

chapters.en: but also for us, to whom righteousness will be credited—for us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
chapters.zh: 也是为我们将来得算为义之人写的，就是我们这信上帝使我们的主耶稣从死里复活的人。

chapters.en: He was delivered over to death for our trespasses and was raised to life for our justification.
chapters.zh: 耶稣被交给人，是为我们的过犯；复活，是为叫我们称义〔注：或译：耶稣是为我们的过犯交付了，是为我们称义复活了〕。

chapters.en: Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
chapters.zh: 我们既因信称义，就藉着我们的主耶稣基督得与上帝相和。

chapters.en: through whom we have gained access by faith into this grace in which we stand. And we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God.
chapters.zh: 我们又藉着他，因信得进入现在所站的这恩典中，并且欢欢喜喜盼望上帝的荣耀。

chapters.en: Not only that, but we also rejoice in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance;
chapters.zh: 不但如此，就是在患难中也是欢欢喜喜的；因为知道患难生忍耐，

chapters.en: perseverance, character; and character, hope.
chapters.zh: 忍耐生老练，老练生盼望；

chapters.en: And hope does not disappoint us, because God has poured out His love into our hearts through the Holy Spirit, whom He has given us.
chapters.zh: 盼望不至于羞耻，因为所赐给我们的圣灵将上帝的爱浇灌在我们心里。

chapters.en: For at just the right time, while we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly.
chapters.zh: 因我们还软弱的时候，基督就按所定的日期为罪人死。

chapters.en: Very rarely will anyone die for a righteous man, though for a good man someone might possibly dare to die.
chapters.zh: 为义人死，是少有的；为仁人死，或者有敢做的。

chapters.en: But God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
chapters.zh: 惟有基督在我们还作罪人的时候为我们死，上帝的爱就在此向我们显明了。

chapters.en: Therefore, since we have now been justified by His blood, how much more shall we be saved from wrath through Him!
chapters.zh: 现在我们既靠着他的血称义，就更要藉着他免去〔上帝的〕忿怒。

chapters.en: For if, when we were enemies of God, we were reconciled to Him through the death of His Son, how much more, having been reconciled, shall we be saved through His life!
chapters.zh: 因为我们作仇敌的时候，且藉着上帝儿子的死，得与上帝和好；既已和好，就更要因他的生得救了。

chapters.en: Not only that, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.
chapters.zh: 不但如此，我们既藉着我主耶稣基督得与上帝和好，也就藉着他以上帝为乐。

chapters.en: Therefore, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death was passed on to all men, because all sinned.
chapters.zh: 这就如罪是从一人入了世界，死又是从罪来的，于是死就临到众人，因为众人都犯了罪。

chapters.en: For sin was in the world before the law was given; but sin is not taken into account when there is no law.
chapters.zh: 没有律法之先，罪已经在世上；但没有律法，罪也不算罪。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the way that Adam transgressed. He is a pattern of the One to come.
chapters.zh: 然而从亚当到摩西，死就作了王，连那些不与亚当犯一样罪过的，也在他的权下。亚当乃是那以后要来之人的预像。

chapters.en: But the gift is not like the trespass. For if the many died by the trespass of the one man, how much more did God’s grace and the gift that came by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many!
chapters.zh: 只是过犯不如恩赐，若因一人的过犯，众人都死了，何况上帝的恩典，与那因耶稣基督一人恩典中的赏赐，岂不更加倍地临到众人吗？

chapters.en: Again, the gift is not like the result of the one man’s sin: The judgment that followed one sin brought condemnation, but the gift that followed many trespasses brought justification.
chapters.zh: 因一人犯罪就定罪，也不如恩赐，原来审判是由一人而定罪，恩赐乃是由许多过犯而称义。

chapters.en: For if, by the trespass of the one man, death reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!
chapters.zh: 若因一人的过犯，死就因这一人作了王，何况那些受洪恩又蒙所赐之义的，岂不更要因耶稣基督一人在生命中作王吗？

chapters.en: So then, just as one trespass brought condemnation for all men, so also one act of righteousness brought justification and life for all men.
chapters.zh: 如此说来，因一次的过犯，众人都被定罪；照样，因一次的义行，众人也就被称义得生命了。

chapters.en: For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the one man the many will be made righteous.
chapters.zh: 因一人的悖逆，众人成为罪人；照样，因一人的顺从，众人也成为义了。

chapters.en: The law came in so that the trespass would increase; but where sin increased, grace increased all the more,
chapters.zh: 律法本是外添的，叫过犯显多；只是罪在哪里显多，恩典就更显多了。

chapters.en: so that, just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to bring eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
chapters.zh: 就如罪作王叫人死；照样，恩典也藉着义作王，叫人因我们的主耶稣基督得永生。

chapters.en: What then shall we say? Shall we continue in sin so that grace may increase?
chapters.zh: 这样，怎么说呢？我们可以仍在罪中、叫恩典显多吗？

chapters.en: Certainly not! How can we who died to sin live in it any longer?
chapters.zh: 断乎不可！我们在罪上死了的人岂可仍在罪中活着呢？

chapters.en: Or aren’t you aware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?
chapters.zh: 岂不知我们这受洗归入基督耶稣的人是受洗归入他的死吗？

chapters.en: We were therefore buried with Him through baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may walk in newness of life.
chapters.zh: 所以，我们藉着洗礼归入死，和他一同埋葬，原是叫我们一举一动有新生的样式，像基督藉着父的荣耀从死里复活一样。

chapters.en: For if we have been united with Him like this in His death, we will certainly also be united with Him in His resurrection.
chapters.zh: 我们若在他死的形状上与他联合，也要在他复活的形状上与他联合；

chapters.en: We know that our old self was crucified with Him so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, that we should no longer be slaves to sin.
chapters.zh: 因为知道我们的旧人和他同钉十字架，使罪身灭绝，叫我们不再作罪的奴仆；

chapters.en: For anyone who has died has been freed from sin.
chapters.zh: 因为已死的人是脱离了罪。

chapters.en: Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with Him.
chapters.zh: 我们若是与基督同死，就信必与他同活。

chapters.en: For we know that since Christ was raised from the dead, He cannot die again; death no longer has dominion over Him.
chapters.zh: 因为知道基督既从死里复活，就不再死，死也不再作他的主了。

chapters.en: The death He died, He died to sin once for all; but the life He lives, He lives to God.
chapters.zh: 他死是向罪死了，只有一次；他活是向上帝活着。

chapters.en: So you too must count yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 这样，你们向罪也当看自己是死的；向上帝在基督耶稣里，却当看自己是活的。

chapters.en: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its desires.
chapters.zh: 所以，不要容罪在你们必死的身上作王，使你们顺从身子的私欲。

chapters.en: Do not present the parts of your body to sin as instruments of wickedness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life; and present the parts of your body to Him as instruments of righteousness.
chapters.zh: 也不要将你们的肢体献给罪作不义的器具；倒要像从死里复活的人，将自己献给上帝，并将肢体作义的器具献给上帝。

chapters.en: For sin shall not be your master, because you are not under law, but under grace.
chapters.zh: 罪必不能作你们的主；因你们不在律法之下，乃在恩典之下。

chapters.en: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? Certainly not!
chapters.zh: 这却怎么样呢？我们在恩典之下，不在律法之下，就可以犯罪吗？断乎不可！

chapters.en: Do you not know that when you offer yourselves as obedient slaves, you are slaves to the one you obey, whether you are slaves to sin leading to death, or to obedience leading to righteousness?
chapters.zh: 岂不晓得你们献上自己作奴仆，顺从谁，就作谁的奴仆吗？或作罪的奴仆，以至于死；或作顺命的奴仆，以致成义。

chapters.en: But thanks be to God that, though you once were slaves to sin, you wholeheartedly obeyed the form of teaching to which you were committed.
chapters.zh: 感谢上帝！因为你们从前虽然作罪的奴仆，现今却从心里顺服了所传给你们道理的模范。

chapters.en: You have been set free from sin and have become slaves to righteousness.
chapters.zh: 你们既从罪里得了释放，就作了义的奴仆。

chapters.en: I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. Just as you used to offer the parts of your body in slavery to impurity and to escalating wickedness, so now offer them in slavery to righteousness leading to holiness.
chapters.zh: 我因你们肉体的软弱，就照人的常话对你们说。你们从前怎样将肢体献给不洁不法作奴仆，以至于不法；现今也要照样将肢体献给义作奴仆，以至于成圣。

chapters.en: For when you were slaves to sin, you were free of obligation to righteousness.
chapters.zh: 因为你们作罪之奴仆的时候，就不被义约束了。

chapters.en: What fruit did you reap at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? The outcome of those things is death.
chapters.zh: 你们现今所看为羞耻的事，当日有什么果子呢？那些事的结局就是死。

chapters.en: But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves to God, the fruit you reap leads to holiness, and the outcome is eternal life.
chapters.zh: 但现今，你们既从罪里得了释放，作了上帝的奴仆，就有成圣的果子，那结局就是永生。

chapters.en: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
chapters.zh: 因为罪的工价乃是死；惟有上帝的恩赐，在我们的主基督耶稣里，乃是永生。

chapters.en: Do you not know, brothers (for I am speaking to those who know the law), that the law has authority over a man only as long as he lives?
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我现在对明白律法的人说，你们岂不晓得律法管人是在活着的时候吗？

chapters.en: For instance, a married woman is bound by law to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is released from the law of marriage.
chapters.zh: 就如女人有了丈夫，丈夫还活着，就被律法约束；丈夫若死了，就脱离了丈夫的律法。

chapters.en: So then, if she is joined to another man while her husband is still alive, she is called an adulteress; but if her husband dies, she is free from that law and is not an adulteress if she marries another man.
chapters.zh: 所以丈夫活着，她若归于别人，便叫淫妇；丈夫若死了，她就脱离了丈夫的律法，虽然归于别人，也不是淫妇。

chapters.en: Therefore, my brothers, you also died to the law through the body of Christ, that you might belong to another, to Him who was raised from the dead, in order that we might bear fruit to God.
chapters.zh: 我的弟兄们，这样说来，你们藉着基督的身体，在律法上也是死了，叫你们归于别人，就是归于那从死里复活的，叫我们结果子给上帝。

chapters.en: For when we lived according to the flesh, the sinful passions aroused by the law were at work in our bodies, bearing fruit for death.
chapters.zh: 因为我们属肉体的时候，那因律法而生的恶欲就在我们肢体中发动，以致结成死亡的果子。

chapters.en: But now, having died to what bound us, we have been released from the law, so that we serve in the new way of the Spirit, and not in the old way of the written code.
chapters.zh: 但我们既然在捆我们的律法上死了，现今就脱离了律法，叫我们服事〔主〕，要按着心灵〔注：心灵：或译圣灵〕的新样，不按着仪文的旧样。

chapters.en: What then shall we say? Is the law sin? Certainly not! Indeed, I would not have been mindful of sin if not for the law. For I would not have been aware of coveting if the law had not said, “Do not covet.”
chapters.zh: 这样，我们可说什么呢？律法是罪吗？断乎不是！只是非因律法，我就不知何为罪。非律法说「不可起贪心」，我就不知何为贪心。

chapters.en: But sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, produced in me every kind of covetous desire. For apart from the law, sin is dead.
chapters.zh: 然而，罪趁着机会，就藉着诫命叫诸般的贪心在我里头发动；因为没有律法，罪是死的。

chapters.en: Once I was alive apart from the law; but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life and I died.
chapters.zh: 我以前没有律法是活着的；但是诫命来到，罪又活了，我就死了。

chapters.en: So I discovered that the very commandment that was meant to bring life actually brought death.
chapters.zh: 那本来叫人活的诫命，反倒叫我死；

chapters.en: For sin, seizing its opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through the commandment put me to death.
chapters.zh: 因为罪趁着机会，就藉着诫命引诱我，并且杀了我。

chapters.en: So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.
chapters.zh: 这样看来，律法是圣洁的，诫命也是圣洁、公义、良善的。

chapters.en: Did that which is good, then, become death to me? Certainly not! But in order that sin might be exposed as sin, it produced death in me through what was good, so that through the commandment sin might become utterly sinful.
chapters.zh: 既然如此，那良善的是叫我死吗？断乎不是！〔叫我死的乃是罪〕。但罪藉着那良善的叫我死，就显出真是罪，叫罪因着诫命更显出是恶极了。

chapters.en: We know that the law is spiritual; but I am unspiritual, sold as a slave to sin.
chapters.zh: 我们原晓得律法是属乎灵的，但我是属乎肉体的，是已经卖给罪了。

chapters.en: I do not understand what I do. For what I want to do, I do not do. But what I hate, I do.
chapters.zh: 因为我所做的，我自己不明白；我所愿意的，我并不做；我所恨恶的，我倒去做。

chapters.en: And if I do what I do not want to do, I admit that the law is good.
chapters.zh: 若我所做的，是我所不愿意的，我就应承律法是善的。

chapters.en: In that case, it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.
chapters.zh: 既是这样，就不是我做的，乃是住在我里头的罪做的。

chapters.en: I know that nothing good lives in me, that is, in my flesh; for I have the desire to do what is good, but I cannot carry it out.
chapters.zh: 我也知道，在我里头，就是我肉体之中，没有良善。因为，立志为善由得我，只是行出来由不得我。

chapters.en: For I do not do the good I want to do. Instead, I keep on doing the evil I do not want to do.
chapters.zh: 故此，我所愿意的善，我反不做；我所不愿意的恶，我倒去做。

chapters.en: And if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but it is sin living in me that does it.
chapters.zh: 若我去做所不愿意做的，就不是我做的，乃是住在我里头的罪做的。

chapters.en: So this is the principle I have discovered: When I want to do good, evil is right there with me.
chapters.zh: 我觉得有个律，就是我愿意为善的时候，便有恶与我同在。

chapters.en: For in my inner being I delight in God’s law.
chapters.zh: 因为按着我里面的意思〔注：原文是人〕，我是喜欢上帝的律；

chapters.en: But I see another law at work in my body, warring against the law of my mind and holding me captive to the law of sin that dwells within me.
chapters.zh: 但我觉得肢体中另有个律和我心中的律交战，把我掳去，叫我附从那肢体中犯罪的律。

chapters.en: What a wretched man I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?
chapters.zh: 我真是苦啊！谁能救我脱离这取死的身体呢？

chapters.en:
Thanks be to God, through Jesus Christ our Lord!
So then, with my mind I serve the law of God, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin.
chapters.zh: 感谢上帝，靠着我们的主耶稣基督〔就能脱离了〕。这样看来，我以内心顺服上帝的律，我肉体却顺服罪的律了。

chapters.en: Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 如今，那些在基督耶稣里的就不定罪了。

chapters.en: For in Christ Jesus the law of the Spirit of life set you free from the law of sin and death.
chapters.zh: 因为赐生命〔圣〕灵的律，在基督耶稣里释放了我，使我脱离罪和死的律了。

chapters.en: For what the law was powerless to do in that it was weakened by the flesh, God did by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful man, as an offering for sin. He thus condemned sin in the flesh,
chapters.zh: 律法既因肉体软弱，有所不能行的，上帝就差遣自己的儿子，成为罪身的形状，作了赎罪祭，在肉体中定了罪案，

chapters.en: so that the righteous standard of the law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.
chapters.zh: 使律法的义成就在我们这不随从肉体、只随从〔圣〕灵的人身上。

chapters.en: Those who live according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh; but those who live according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit.
chapters.zh: 因为，随从肉体的人体贴肉体的事；随从〔圣〕灵的人体贴〔圣〕灵的事。

chapters.en: The mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace,
chapters.zh: 体贴肉体的，就是死；体贴〔圣〕灵的，乃是生命、平安。

chapters.en: because the mind of the flesh is hostile to God: It does not submit to God’s law, nor can it do so.
chapters.zh: 原来体贴肉体的，就是与上帝为仇；因为不服上帝的律法，也是不能服，

chapters.en: Those controlled by the flesh cannot please God.
chapters.zh: 而且属肉体的人不能得上帝的喜欢。

chapters.en: You, however, are controlled not by the flesh, but by the Spirit, if the Spirit of God lives in you. And if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Christ.
chapters.zh: 如果上帝的灵住在你们心里，你们就不属肉体，乃属〔圣〕灵了。人若没有基督的灵，就不是属基督的。

chapters.en: But if Christ is in you, your body is dead because of sin, yet your spirit is alive because of righteousness.
chapters.zh: 基督若在你们心里，身体就因罪而死，心灵却因义而活。

chapters.en: And if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead is living in you, He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit, who lives in you.
chapters.zh: 然而，叫耶稣从死里复活者的灵若住在你们心里，那叫基督耶稣从死里复活的，也必藉着住在你们心里的〔圣〕灵，使你们必死的身体又活过来。

chapters.en: Therefore, brothers, we have an obligation, but it is not to the flesh, to live according to it.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，这样看来，我们并不是欠肉体的债去顺从肉体活着。

chapters.en: For if you live according to the flesh, you will die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.
chapters.zh: 你们若顺从肉体活着，必要死；若靠着〔圣〕灵治死身体的恶行，必要活着。

chapters.en: For all who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.
chapters.zh: 因为凡被上帝的灵引导的，都是上帝的儿子。

chapters.en: For you did not receive a spirit of slavery that returns you to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption to sonship, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”
chapters.zh: 你们所受的，不是奴仆的心，仍旧害怕；所受的，乃是儿子的心，因此我们呼叫：「阿爸！父！」

chapters.en: The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.
chapters.zh: 圣灵与我们的心同证我们是上帝的儿女；

chapters.en: And if we are children, then we are heirs: heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ—if indeed we suffer with Him, so that we may also be glorified with Him.
chapters.zh: 既是儿女，便是后嗣，就是上帝的后嗣，和基督同作后嗣。如果我们和他一同受苦，也必和他一同得荣耀。

chapters.en: I consider that our present sufferings are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed in us.
chapters.zh: 我想，现在的苦楚若比起将来要显于我们的荣耀就不足介意了。

chapters.en: The creation waits in eager expectation for the revelation of the sons of God.
chapters.zh: 受造之物切望等候上帝的众子显出来。

chapters.en: For the creation was subjected to futility, not by its own will, but because of the One who subjected it, in hope
chapters.zh: 因为受造之物服在虚空之下，不是自己愿意，乃是因那叫他如此的。

chapters.en: that the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to decay and brought into the glorious freedom of the children of God.
chapters.zh: 但受造之物仍然指望脱离败坏的辖制，得享〔注：享：原文是入〕上帝儿女自由的荣耀。

chapters.en: We know that the whole creation has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth until the present time.
chapters.zh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息，劳苦，直到如今。

chapters.en: Not only that, but we ourselves, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for our adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies.
chapters.zh: 不但如此，就是我们这有〔圣〕灵初结果子的，也是自己心里叹息，等候得着儿子的名分，乃是我们的身体得赎。

chapters.en: For in this hope we were saved; but hope that is seen is no hope at all. Who hopes for what he can already see?
chapters.zh: 我们得救是在乎盼望；只是所见的盼望不是盼望，谁还盼望他所见的呢〔注：有古卷：人所看见的何必再盼望呢〕？

chapters.en: But if we hope for what we do not yet see, we wait for it patiently.
chapters.zh: 但我们若盼望那所不见的，就必忍耐等候。

chapters.en: In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. For we do not know how we ought to pray, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groans too deep for words.
chapters.zh: 况且，我们的软弱有〔圣〕灵帮助；我们本不晓得当怎样祷告，只是〔圣〕灵亲自用说不出来的叹息替我们祷告。

chapters.en: And He who searches our hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God.
chapters.zh: 鉴察人心的，晓得〔圣〕灵的意思，因为〔圣〕灵照着上帝的〔旨意〕替圣徒祈求。

chapters.en: And we know that God works all things together for the good of those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose.
chapters.zh: 我们晓得万事都互相效力，叫爱上帝的人得益处，就是按他旨意被召的人。

chapters.en: For those God foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers.
chapters.zh: 因为他预先所知道的人，就预先定下效法他儿子的模样，使他儿子在许多弟兄中作长子。

chapters.en: And those He predestined, He also called; those He called, He also justified; those He justified, He also glorified.
chapters.zh: 预先所定下的人又召他们来；所召来的人又称他们为义；所称为义的人又叫他们得荣耀。

chapters.en: What then shall we say in response to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
chapters.zh: 既是这样，还有什么说的呢？上帝若帮助我们，谁能敌挡我们呢？

chapters.en: He who did not spare His own Son but gave Him up for us all, how will He not also, along with Him, freely give us all things?
chapters.zh: 上帝既不爱惜自己的儿子，为我们众人舍了，岂不也把万物和他一同白白地赐给我们吗？

chapters.en: Who will bring any charge against God’s elect? It is God who justifies.
chapters.zh: 谁能控告上帝所拣选的人呢？有上帝称他们为义了〔注：或译：是称他们为义的上帝吗〕。

chapters.en: Who is there to condemn us? For Christ Jesus, who died, and more than that was raised to life, is at the right hand of God—and He is interceding for us.
chapters.zh: 谁能定他们的罪呢？有基督耶稣已经死了，而且从死里复活，现今在上帝的右边，也替我们祈求〔注：有基督......或译：是已经死了，而且从死里复活，现今在上帝的右边，也替我们祈求的基督耶稣吗〕。

chapters.en: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Shall trouble or distress or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?
chapters.zh: 谁能使我们与基督的爱隔绝呢？难道是患难吗？是困苦吗？是逼迫吗？是饥饿吗？是赤身露体吗？是危险吗？是刀剑吗？

chapters.en:
As it is written:
“For Your sake we face death all day long; we are considered as sheep to be slaughtered.”
chapters.zh: 如〔经上〕所记： 我们为你的缘故终日被杀； 人看我们如将宰的羊。

chapters.en: No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.
chapters.zh: 然而，靠着爱我们的〔主〕，在这一切的事上已经得胜有余了。

chapters.en: For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers,
chapters.zh: 因为我深信无论是死，是生，是天使，是掌权的，是有能的，是现在的事，是将来的事，

chapters.en: neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
chapters.zh: 是高处的，是低处的，是别的受造之物，都不能叫我们与上帝的爱隔绝；这爱是在我们的主基督耶稣里的。

chapters.en: I speak the truth in Christ; I am not lying, as confirmed by my conscience in the Holy Spirit.
chapters.zh: 我在基督里说真话，并不谎言，有我良心被圣灵感动，给我作见证：

chapters.en: I have deep sorrow and unceasing anguish in my heart.
chapters.zh: 我是大有忧愁，心里时常伤痛；

chapters.en: For I could wish that I myself were cursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my own flesh and blood,
chapters.zh: 为我弟兄，我骨肉之亲，就是自己被咒诅，与基督分离，我也愿意。

chapters.en: the people of Israel. Theirs is the adoption as sons; theirs the divine glory and the covenants; theirs the giving of the law, the temple worship, and the promises.
chapters.zh: 他们是以色列人；那儿子的名分、荣耀、诸约、律法、礼仪、应许都是他们的。

chapters.en: Theirs are the patriarchs, and from them proceeds the human descent of Christ, who is God over all, forever worthy of praise! Amen.
chapters.zh: 列祖就是他们的祖宗；按肉体说，基督也是从他们出来的。他是在万有之上，永远可称颂的上帝。阿们！

chapters.en: It is not as though God’s word has failed. For not all who are descended from Israel are Israel.
chapters.zh: 这不是说上帝的话落了空。因为从以色列生的不都是以色列人，

chapters.en: Nor because they are Abraham’s descendants are they all his children. On the contrary, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”
chapters.zh: 也不因为是亚伯拉罕的后裔就都作他的儿女；惟独「从以撒生的才要称为你的后裔。」

chapters.en: So it is not the children of the flesh who are God’s children, but it is the children of the promise who are regarded as offspring.
chapters.zh: 这就是说，肉身所生的儿女不是上帝的儿女，惟独那应许的儿女才算是后裔。

chapters.en: For this is what the promise stated: “At the appointed time I will return, and Sarah will have a son.”
chapters.zh: 因为所应许的话是这样说：「到〔明年〕这时候我要来，撒拉必生一个儿子。」

chapters.en: Not only that, but Rebecca’s children were conceived by one man, our father Isaac.
chapters.zh: 不但如此，还有利百加，既从一个人，就是从我们的祖宗以撒怀了孕，

chapters.en: Yet before the twins were born or had done anything good or bad, in order that God’s plan of election might stand,
chapters.zh: （〔双子〕还没有生下来，善恶还没有做出来，只因要显明上帝拣选人的旨意，不在乎人的行为，乃在乎召人的〔主〕。）

chapters.en: not by works but by Him who calls, she was told, “The older will serve the younger.”
chapters.zh: 上帝就对利百加说：「将来，大的要服事小的。」

chapters.en: So it is written: “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”
chapters.zh: 正如〔经上〕所记：雅各是我所爱的；以扫是我所恶的。

chapters.en: What then shall we say? Is God unjust? Certainly not!
chapters.zh: 这样，我们可说什么呢？难道上帝有什么不公平吗？断乎没有！

chapters.en:
For He says to Moses:
“I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.”
chapters.zh: 因他对摩西说： 我要怜悯谁就怜悯谁， 要恩待谁就恩待谁。

chapters.en: So then, it does not depend on man’s desire or effort, but on God’s mercy.
chapters.zh: 据此看来，这不在乎那定意的，也不在乎那奔跑的，只在乎发怜悯的上帝。

chapters.en: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh: “I raised you up for this very purpose, that I might display My power in you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”
chapters.zh: 因为经上有话向法老说：「我将你兴起来，特要在你身上彰显我的权能，并要使我的名传遍天下。」

chapters.en: Therefore God has mercy on whom He wants to have mercy, and He hardens whom He wants to harden.
chapters.zh: 如此看来，上帝要怜悯谁就怜悯谁，要叫谁刚硬就叫谁刚硬。

chapters.en: One of you will say to me, “Then why does God still find fault? For who can resist His will?”
chapters.zh: 这样，你必对我说：「他为什么还指责人呢？有谁抗拒他的旨意呢？」

chapters.en: But who are you, O man, to talk back to God? Shall what is formed say to Him who formed it, “Why did You make me like this?”
chapters.zh: 你这个人哪，你是谁，竟敢向上帝强嘴呢？受造之物岂能对造他的说：「你为什么这样造我呢？」

chapters.en: Does not the potter have the right to make from the same lump of clay one vessel for special occasions and another for common use?
chapters.zh: 窑匠难道没有权柄从一团泥里拿一块做成贵重的器皿，又拿一块做成卑贱的器皿吗？

chapters.en: What if God, intending to show His wrath and make His power known, bore with great patience the vessels of His wrath, prepared for destruction?
chapters.zh: 倘若上帝要显明他的忿怒，彰显他的权能，就多多忍耐宽容那可怒、预备遭毁灭的器皿，

chapters.en: What if He did this to make the riches of His glory known to the vessels of His mercy, whom He prepared in advance for glory—
chapters.zh: 又要将他丰盛的荣耀彰显在那蒙怜悯、早预备得荣耀的器皿上。

chapters.en: including us, whom He has called not only from the Jews, but also from the Gentiles?
chapters.zh: 这〔器皿〕就是我们被上帝所召的，不但是从犹太人中，也是从外邦人中。这有什么不可呢？

chapters.en:
As He says in Hosea:
“I will call them ‘My People’ who are not My people, and I will call her ‘My Beloved’ who is not My beloved,”
chapters.zh: 就像上帝在何西阿书上说： 那本来不是我子民的， 我要称为「我的子民」； 本来不是蒙爱的， 我要称为「蒙爱的」。

chapters.en:
and,
“It will happen that in the very place where it was said to them, ‘You are not My people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’”
chapters.zh: 从前在什么地方对他们说： 你们不是我的子民， 将来就在那里称他们为「永生上帝的儿子」。

chapters.en:
Isaiah cries out concerning Israel:
“Though the number of the Israelites is like the sand of the sea, only the remnant will be saved.
chapters.zh: 以赛亚指着以色列人喊着说：「以色列人虽多如海沙，得救的不过是剩下的余数；

chapters.en: For the Lord will carry out His sentence on the earth thoroughly and decisively.”
chapters.zh: 因为主要在世上施行他的话，叫他的话都成全，速速地完结。」

chapters.en:
It is just as Isaiah foretold:
“Unless the Lord of Hosts had left us descendants, we would have become like Sodom,
we would have resembled Gomorrah.”
chapters.zh: 又如以赛亚先前说过： 若不是万军之主给我们存留余种， 我们早已像所多玛、蛾摩拉的样子了。

chapters.en: What then will we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have obtained it, a righteousness that is by faith;
chapters.zh: 这样，我们可说什么呢？那本来不追求义的外邦人反得了义，就是因信而得的义。

chapters.en: but Israel, who pursued a law of righteousness, has not attained it.
chapters.zh: 但以色列人追求律法的义，反得不着律法的义。

chapters.en: Why not? Because their pursuit was not by faith, but as if it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone,
chapters.zh: 这是什么缘故呢？是因为他们不凭着信心求，只凭着行为求；他们正跌在那绊脚石上。

chapters.en:
as it is written:
“See, I lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
chapters.zh: 就如经上所记： 我在锡安放一块绊脚的石头，跌人的磐石； 信靠他的人必不至于羞愧。

chapters.en: Brothers, my heart’s desire and prayer to God for the Israelites is for their salvation.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我心里所愿的，向上帝所求的，是要以色列人得救。

chapters.en: For I testify about them that they are zealous for God, but not on the basis of knowledge.
chapters.zh: 我可以证明，他们向上帝有热心，但不是按着真知识；

chapters.en: Because they were ignorant of God’s righteousness and sought to establish their own, they did not submit to God’s righteousness.
chapters.zh: 因为不知道上帝的义，想要立自己的义，就不服上帝的义了。

chapters.en: For Christ is the end of the law, to bring righteousness to everyone who believes.
chapters.zh: 律法的总结就是基督，使凡信他的都得着义。

chapters.en: For concerning the righteousness that is by the law, Moses writes: “The man who does these things will live by them.”
chapters.zh: 摩西写着说：「人若行那出于律法的义，就必因此活着。」

chapters.en: But the righteousness that is by faith says: “Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’ (that is, to bring Christ down)
chapters.zh: 惟有出于信心的义如此说：「你不要心里说：谁要升到天上去呢？（就是要领下基督来；）

chapters.en: or, ‘Who will descend into the Abyss?’ (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead).”
chapters.zh: 谁要下到阴间去呢？（就是要领基督从死里上来。）」

chapters.en: But what does it say? “The word is near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart,” that is, the word of faith we are proclaiming:
chapters.zh: 他到底怎么说呢？他说： 这道离你不远， 正在你口里，在你心里－ （就是我们所传信〔主〕的道。）

chapters.en: that if you confess with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.
chapters.zh: 你若口里认耶稣为主，心里信上帝叫他从死里复活，就必得救。

chapters.en: For with your heart you believe and are justified, and with your mouth you confess and are saved.
chapters.zh: 因为，人心里相信就可以称义，口里承认就可以得救。

chapters.en: It is just as the Scripture says: “Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
chapters.zh: 经上说：「凡信他的人必不至于羞愧。」

chapters.en: For there is no difference between Jew and Greek: The same Lord is Lord of all, and gives richly to all who call on Him,
chapters.zh: 犹太人和希腊人并没有分别，因为众人同有一位主；他也厚待一切求告他的人。

chapters.en: for, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.”
chapters.zh: 因为「凡求告主名的就必得救」。

chapters.en: How then can they call on the One in whom they have not believed? And how can they believe in the One of whom they have not heard? And how can they hear without someone to preach?
chapters.zh: 然而，人未曾信他，怎能求他呢？未曾听见他，怎能信他呢？没有传道的，怎能听见呢？

chapters.en: And how can they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!”
chapters.zh: 若没有奉差遣，怎能传道呢？如〔经〕上所记：「报福音、传喜信的人，他们的脚〔踪〕何等佳美！」

chapters.en: But not all of them welcomed the good news. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our message?”
chapters.zh: 只是人没有都听从福音，因为以赛亚说：「主啊，我们所传的有谁信呢？」

chapters.en: Consequently, faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of Christ.
chapters.zh: 可见，信道是从听道来的，听道是从基督的话来的。

chapters.en:
But I ask, did they not hear? Indeed they did:
“Their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.”
chapters.zh: 但我说，人没有听见吗？诚然听见了。 他们的声音传遍天下； 他们的言语传到地极。

chapters.en:
I ask instead, did Israel not understand? First, Moses says:
“I will make you jealous by those who are not a nation; I will make you angry by a nation without understanding.”
chapters.zh: 我再说，以色列人不知道吗？先有摩西说： 我要用那不成子民的惹动你们的愤恨； 我要用那无知的民触动你们的怒气。

chapters.en:
And Isaiah boldly says:
“I was found by those who did not seek Me; I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me.”
chapters.zh: 又有以赛亚放胆说： 没有寻找我的，我叫他们遇见； 没有访问我的，我向他们显现。

chapters.en:
But as for Israel he says:
“All day long I have held out My hands to a disobedient and obstinate people.”
chapters.zh: 至于以色列人，他说：「我整天伸手招呼那悖逆顶嘴的百姓。」

chapters.en: I ask then, did God reject His people? Certainly not! I am an Israelite myself, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.
chapters.zh: 我且说，上帝弃绝了他的百姓吗？断乎没有！因为我也是以色列人，亚伯拉罕的后裔，属便雅悯支派的。

chapters.en: God did not reject His people, whom He foreknew. Do you not know what the Scripture says about Elijah, how he appealed to God against Israel:
chapters.zh: 上帝并没有弃绝他预先所知道的百姓。你们岂不晓得经上论到以利亚是怎么说的呢？他在上帝面前怎样控告以色列人说：

chapters.en: “Lord, they have killed Your prophets and torn down Your altars. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well” ?
chapters.zh: 「主啊，他们杀了你的先知，拆了你的祭坛，只剩下我一个人；他们还要寻索我的命。」

chapters.en: And what was the divine reply to him? “I have reserved for Myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal.”
chapters.zh: 上帝的回话是怎么说的呢？〔他说〕：「我为自己留下七千人，是未曾向巴力屈膝的。」

chapters.en: In the same way, at the present time there is a remnant chosen by grace.
chapters.zh: 如今也是这样，照着拣选的恩典，还有所留的余数。

chapters.en: And if it is by grace, then it is no longer by works. Otherwise, grace would no longer be grace.
chapters.zh: 既是出于恩典，就不在乎行为；不然，恩典就不是恩典了。

chapters.en: What then? What Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain, but the elect did. The others were hardened,
chapters.zh: 这是怎么样呢？以色列人所求的，他们没有得着。惟有蒙拣选的人得着了；其余的就成了顽梗不化的。

chapters.en:
as it is written:
“God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that could not see,
and ears that could not hear, to this very day.”
chapters.zh: 如〔经上〕所记： 上帝给他们昏迷的心， 眼睛不能看见， 耳朵不能听见， 直到今日。

chapters.en:
And David says:
“May their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution to them.
chapters.zh: 大卫也说： 愿他们的筵席变为网罗，变为机槛， 变为绊脚石，作他们的报应。

chapters.en: May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.”
chapters.zh: 愿他们的眼睛昏矇，不得看见； 愿你时常弯下他们的腰。

chapters.en: I ask then, did they stumble so as to fall beyond recovery? Certainly not! However, because of their trespass, salvation has come to the Gentiles to make Israel jealous.
chapters.zh: 我且说，他们失脚是要他们跌倒吗？断乎不是！反倒因他们的过失，救恩便临到外邦人，要激动他们发愤。

chapters.en: But if their trespass means riches for the world, and their failure means riches for the Gentiles, how much greater riches will their fullness bring!
chapters.zh: 若他们的过失为天下的富足，他们的缺乏为外邦人的富足，何况他们的丰满呢？

chapters.en: I am speaking to you Gentiles. Inasmuch as I am the apostle to the Gentiles, I magnify my ministry
chapters.zh: 我对你们外邦人说这话；因我是外邦人的使徒，所以敬重〔注：原文是荣耀〕我的职分，

chapters.en: in the hope that I may provoke my own people to jealousy and save some of them.
chapters.zh: 或者可以激动我骨肉之亲发愤，好救他们一些人。

chapters.en: For if their rejection is the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?
chapters.zh: 若他们被丢弃，天下就得〔与上帝〕和好，他们被收纳，岂不是死而复生吗？

chapters.en: If the first part of the dough is holy, so is the whole batch; if the root is holy, so are the branches.
chapters.zh: 所献的新面若是圣洁，全团也就圣洁了；树根若是圣洁，树枝也就圣洁了。

chapters.en: Now if some branches have been broken off, and you, a wild olive shoot, have been grafted in among the others to share in the nourishment of the olive root,
chapters.zh: 若有几根枝子被折下来，你这野橄榄得接在其中，一同得着橄榄根的肥汁，

chapters.en: do not boast over those branches. If you do, remember this: You do not support the root, but the root supports you.
chapters.zh: 你就不可向〔旧〕枝子夸口；若是夸口，〔当知道〕不是你托着根，乃是根托着你。

chapters.en: You will say then, “Branches were broken off so that I could be grafted in.”
chapters.zh: 你若说，那枝子被折下来是特为叫我接上。

chapters.en: That is correct: They were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not be arrogant, but be afraid.
chapters.zh: 不错！他们因为不信，所以被折下来；你因为信，所以立得住；你不可自高，反要惧怕。

chapters.en: For if God did not spare the natural branches, He will certainly not spare you either.
chapters.zh: 上帝既不爱惜原来的枝子，也必不爱惜你。

chapters.en: Take notice, therefore, of the kindness and severity of God: severity to those who fell, but kindness to you, if you continue in His kindness. Otherwise you also will be cut off.
chapters.zh: 可见，上帝的恩慈和严厉向那跌倒的人是严厉的，向你是有恩慈的，只要你长久在他的恩慈里；不然，你也要被砍下来。

chapters.en: And if they do not persist in unbelief, they will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.
chapters.zh: 而且他们若不是长久不信，仍要被接上，因为上帝能够把他们重新接上。

chapters.en: For if you were cut from a wild olive tree, and contrary to nature were grafted into one that is cultivated, how much more readily will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree!
chapters.zh: 你是从那天生的野橄榄上砍下来的，尚且逆着性得接在好橄榄上，何况这本树的枝子，要接在本树上呢！

chapters.en: I do not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, brothers, so that you will not be conceited: A hardening in part has come to Israel, until the full number of the Gentiles has come in.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我不愿意你们不知道这奥祕（恐怕你们自以为聪明），就是以色列人有几分是硬心的，等到外邦人的数目添满了，

chapters.en:
And so all Israel will be saved, as it is written:
“The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will remove godlessness from Jacob.
chapters.zh: 于是以色列全家都要得救。如〔经上〕所记： 必有一位救主从锡安出来， 要消除雅各家的一切罪恶；

chapters.en: And this is My covenant with them when I take away their sins.”
chapters.zh: 又〔说〕：我除去他们罪的时候， 这就是我与他们所立的约。

chapters.en: Regarding the gospel, they are enemies on your account; but regarding election, they are loved on account of the patriarchs.
chapters.zh: 就着福音说，他们为你们的缘故是仇敌；就着拣选说，他们为列祖的缘故是蒙爱的。

chapters.en: For God’s gifts and His call are irrevocable.
chapters.zh: 因为上帝的恩赐和选召是没有后悔的。

chapters.en: Just as you who formerly disobeyed God have now received mercy through their disobedience,
chapters.zh: 你们从前不顺服上帝，如今因他们的不顺服，你们倒蒙了怜恤。

chapters.en: so they too have now disobeyed, in order that they too may now receive mercy through the mercy shown to you.
chapters.zh: 这样，他们也是不顺服，叫他们因着施给你们的怜恤，现在也就蒙怜恤。

chapters.en: For God has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone.
chapters.zh: 因为上帝将众人都圈在不顺服之中，特意要怜恤众人。

chapters.en: O, the depth of the riches of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments, and untraceable His ways!
chapters.zh: 深哉，上帝丰富的智慧和知识！ 他的判断何其难测！ 他的踪迹何其难寻！

chapters.en: “Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been His counselor?”
chapters.zh: 谁知道主的心？ 谁作过他的谋士呢？

chapters.en: “Who has first given to God, that God should repay him?”
chapters.zh: 谁是先给了他， 使他后来偿还呢？

chapters.en: For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever! Amen.
chapters.zh: 因为万有都是本于他， 倚靠他，归于他。 愿荣耀归给他，直到永远。阿们！

chapters.en: Therefore I urge you, brothers, on account of God’s mercy, to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual service of worship.
chapters.zh: 所以，弟兄们，我以上帝的慈悲劝你们，将身体献上，当作活祭，是圣洁的，是上帝所喜悦的；你们如此事奉乃是理所当然的。

chapters.en: Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.
chapters.zh: 不要效法这个世界，只要心意更新而变化，叫你们察验何为上帝的善良、纯全、可喜悦的旨意。

chapters.en: For by the grace given me I say to every one of you: Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think of yourself with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has given you.
chapters.zh: 我凭着所赐我的恩对你们各人说：不要看自己过于所当看的；要照着上帝所分给各人信心的大小，看得合乎中道。

chapters.en: Just as each of us has one body with many members, and not all members have the same function,
chapters.zh: 正如我们一个身子上有好些肢体，肢体也不都是一样的用处。

chapters.en: so in Christ we who are many are one body, and each member belongs to one another.
chapters.zh: 我们这许多人，在基督里成为一身，互相联络作肢体，也是如此。

chapters.en: We have different gifts according to the grace given us. If one’s gift is prophecy, let him use it in proportion to his faith;
chapters.zh: 按我们所得的恩赐，各有不同。或说预言，就当照着信心的程度说〔预言〕；

chapters.en: if it is serving, let him serve; if it is teaching, let him teach;
chapters.zh: 或作执事，就当〔专一〕执事；或作教导的，就当〔专一〕教导；

chapters.en: if it is encouraging, let him encourage; if it is giving, let him give generously; if it is leading, let him lead with diligence; if it is showing mercy, let him do it cheerfully.
chapters.zh: 或作劝化的，就当〔专一〕劝化；施舍的，就当诚实；治理的，就当殷勤；怜悯人的，就当甘心。

chapters.en: Love must be sincere. Detest what is evil; cling to what is good.
chapters.zh: 爱人不可虚假。恶，要厌恶；善，要亲近。

chapters.en: Be devoted to one another in brotherly love. Outdo yourselves in honoring one another.
chapters.zh: 爱弟兄，要彼此亲热；恭敬人，要彼此推让。

chapters.en: Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.
chapters.zh: 殷勤，不可懒惰；要心里火热，常常服事主。

chapters.en: Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.
chapters.zh: 在指望中要喜乐；在患难中要忍耐；祷告要恒切。

chapters.en: Share with the saints who are in need. Practice hospitality.
chapters.zh: 圣徒缺乏，要帮补；客，要一味地款待。

chapters.en: Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.
chapters.zh: 逼迫你们的，要给他们祝福；只要祝福，不可咒诅。

chapters.en: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
chapters.zh: 与喜乐的人要同乐；与哀哭的人要同哭。

chapters.en: Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but associate with the lowly. Do not be conceited.
chapters.zh: 要彼此同心；不要志气高大，倒要俯就卑微的人〔注：人：或译事〕。不要自以为聪明。

chapters.en: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.
chapters.zh: 不要以恶报恶；众人以为美的事要留心去做。

chapters.en: If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.
chapters.zh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

chapters.en: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
chapters.zh: 亲爱的弟兄，不要自己伸冤，宁可让步，听凭主怒〔注：或译：让人发怒〕；因为〔经上〕记着：「主说：『伸冤在我，我必报应。』」

chapters.en:
On the contrary,
“If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head.”
chapters.zh: 所以，「你的仇敌若饿了，就给他吃，若渴了，就给他喝；因为你这样行就是把炭火堆在他的头上。」

chapters.en: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
chapters.zh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

chapters.en: Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.
chapters.zh: 在上有权柄的，人人当顺服他，因为没有权柄不是出于上帝的。凡掌权的都是上帝所命的。

chapters.en: Consequently, whoever resists authority is opposing what God has set in place, and those who do so will bring judgment on themselves.
chapters.zh: 所以，抗拒掌权的就是抗拒上帝的命；抗拒的必自取刑罚。

chapters.en: For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad. Do you want to be unafraid of the one in authority? Then do what is right, and you will have his approval.
chapters.zh: 作官的原不是叫行善的惧怕，乃是叫作恶的惧怕。你愿意不惧怕掌权的吗？你只要行善，就可得他的称赞；

chapters.en: For he is God’s servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not carry the sword in vain. He is God’s servant, an agent of retribution to the wrongdoer.
chapters.zh: 因为他是上帝的用人，是与你有益的。你若作恶，却当惧怕，因为他不是空空地佩剑；他是上帝的用人，是伸冤的，刑罚那作恶的。

chapters.en: Therefore it is necessary to submit to authority, not only to avoid punishment, but also as a matter of conscience.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们必须顺服，不但是因为刑罚，也是因为良心。

chapters.en: This is also why you pay taxes. For the authorities are God’s servants, who devote themselves to their work.
chapters.zh: 你们纳粮，也为这个缘故；因他们是上帝的差役，常常特管这事。

chapters.en: Pay everyone what you owe him: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due.
chapters.zh: 凡人所当得的，就给他。当得粮的，给他纳粮；当得税的，给他上税；当惧怕的，惧怕他；当恭敬的，恭敬他。

chapters.en: Be indebted to no one, except to one another in love. For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.
chapters.zh: 凡事都不可亏欠人，惟有彼此相爱要常以为亏欠，因为爱人的就完全了律法。

chapters.en: The commandments “Do not commit adultery,” “Do not murder,” “Do not steal,” “Do not covet,” and any other commandments, are summed up in this one decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
chapters.zh: 像那不可奸淫，不可杀人，不可偷盗，不可贪婪，或有别的诫命，都包在爱人如己这一句话之内了。

chapters.en: Love does no wrong to its neighbor. Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
chapters.zh: 爱是不加害与人的，所以爱就完全了律法。

chapters.en: And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.
chapters.zh: 再者，你们晓得，现今就是该趁早睡醒的时候；因为我们得救，现今比〔初〕信的时候更近了。

chapters.en: The night is nearly over; the day has drawn near. So let us lay aside the deeds of darkness and put on the armor of light.
chapters.zh: 黑夜已深，白昼将近。我们就当脱去暗昧的行为，带上光明的兵器。

chapters.en: Let us behave decently, as in the daytime, not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy.
chapters.zh: 行事为人要端正，好像行在白昼。不可荒宴醉酒；不可好色邪荡；不可争竞嫉妒。

chapters.en: Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the desires of the flesh.
chapters.zh: 总要披戴主耶稣基督，不要为肉体安排，去〔放纵〕私欲。

chapters.en: Accept him whose faith is weak, without passing judgment on his opinions.
chapters.zh: 信心软弱的，你们要接纳，但不要辩论所疑惑的事。

chapters.en: For one person has faith to eat all things, while another, who is weak, eats only vegetables.
chapters.zh: 有人信百物都可吃；但那软弱的，只吃蔬菜。

chapters.en: The one who eats everything must not belittle the one who does not, and the one who does not eat everything must not judge the one who does, for God has accepted him.
chapters.zh: 吃的人不可轻看不吃的人；不吃的人不可论断吃的人；因为上帝已经收纳他了。

chapters.en: Who are you to judge someone else’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. And he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.
chapters.zh: 你是谁，竟论断别人的仆人呢？他或站住或跌倒，自有他的主人在；而且他也必要站住，因为主能使他站住。

chapters.en: One person regards a certain day above the others, while someone else considers every day alike. Each one should be fully convinced in his own mind.
chapters.zh: 有人看这日比那日强；有人看日日都是一样。只是各人心里要意见坚定。

chapters.en: He who observes a special day does so to the Lord; he who eats does so to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and he who abstains does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God.
chapters.zh: 守日的人是为主守的。吃的人是为主吃的，因他感谢上帝；不吃的人是为主不吃的，也感谢上帝。

chapters.en: For none of us lives to himself alone, and none of us dies to himself alone.
chapters.zh: 我们没有一个人为自己活，也没有一个人为自己死。

chapters.en: If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord. So whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
chapters.zh: 我们若活着，是为主而活；若死了，是为主而死。所以，我们或活或死总是主的人。

chapters.en: For this reason Christ died and returned to life, that He might be the Lord of both the dead and the living.
chapters.zh: 因此，基督死了，又活了，为要作死人并活人的主。

chapters.en: Why, then, do you judge your brother? Or why do you belittle your brother? For we will all stand before God’s judgment seat.
chapters.zh: 你这个人，为什么论断弟兄呢？又为什么轻看弟兄呢？因我们都要站在上帝的台前。

chapters.en:
It is written:
“As surely as I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow before Me; every tongue will confess to God.”
chapters.zh: 〔经上〕写着： 主说：我凭着我的永生起誓： 万膝必向我跪拜； 万口必向我承认。

chapters.en: So then, each of us will give an account of himself to God.
chapters.zh: 这样看来，我们各人必要将自己的事在上帝面前说明。

chapters.en: Therefore let us stop judging one another. Instead, make up your mind not to put any stumbling block or obstacle in your brother’s way.
chapters.zh: 所以，我们不可再彼此论断，宁可定意谁也不给弟兄放下绊脚跌人之物。

chapters.en: I am convinced and fully persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone regards something as unclean, then for him it is unclean.
chapters.zh: 我凭着主耶稣确知深信，凡物本来没有不洁净的；惟独人以为不洁净的，在他就不洁净了。

chapters.en: If your brother is distressed by what you eat, you are no longer acting in love. Do not by your eating destroy your brother, for whom Christ died.
chapters.zh: 你若因食物叫弟兄忧愁，就不是按着爱人的道理行。基督已经替他死，你不可因你的食物叫他败坏。

chapters.en: Do not allow what you consider good, then, to be spoken of as evil.
chapters.zh: 不可叫你的善被人毁谤；

chapters.en: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
chapters.zh: 因为上帝的国不在乎吃喝，只在乎公义、和平，并圣灵中的喜乐。

chapters.en: For whoever serves Christ in this way is pleasing to God and approved by men.
chapters.zh: 在这几样上服事基督的，就为上帝所喜悦，又为人所称许。

chapters.en: So then, let us pursue what leads to peace and to mutual edification.
chapters.zh: 所以，我们务要追求和睦的事与彼此建立〔德行〕的事。

chapters.en: Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All food is clean, but it is wrong for a man to let his eating be a stumbling block.
chapters.zh: 不可因食物毁坏上帝的工程。凡物固然洁净，但有人因食物叫人跌倒，就是他的罪了。

chapters.en: It is better not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything to cause your brother to stumble.
chapters.zh: 无论是吃肉是喝酒，是什么别的事，叫弟兄跌倒，一概不做才好。

chapters.en: Keep your belief about such matters between yourself and God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves.
chapters.zh: 你有信心，就当在上帝面前守着。人在自己以为可行的事上能不自责，就有福了。

chapters.en: But the one who has doubts is condemned if he eats, because his eating is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.
chapters.zh: 若有疑心而吃的，就必有罪，因为他吃不是出于信心。凡不出于信心的都是罪。

chapters.en: We who are strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak and not to please ourselves.
chapters.zh: 我们坚固的人应该担代不坚固人的软弱，不求自己的喜悦。

chapters.en: Each of us should please his neighbor for his good, to build him up.
chapters.zh: 我们各人务要叫邻舍喜悦，使他得益处，建立〔德行〕。

chapters.en: For even Christ did not please Himself, but as it is written: “The insults of those who insult You have fallen on Me.”
chapters.zh: 因为基督也不求自己的喜悦，如〔经上〕所记：「辱骂你人的辱骂都落在我身上。」

chapters.en: For everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and the encouragement of the Scriptures, we might have hope.
chapters.zh: 从前所写的〔圣经〕都是为教训我们写的，叫我们因圣经所生的忍耐和安慰可以得着盼望。

chapters.en: Now may the God who gives endurance and encouragement grant you harmony with one another in Christ Jesus,
chapters.zh: 但愿赐忍耐安慰的上帝叫你们彼此同心，效法基督耶稣，

chapters.en: so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 一心一口荣耀上帝－我们主耶稣基督的父！

chapters.en: Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们要彼此接纳，如同基督接纳你们一样，使荣耀归与上帝。

chapters.en: For I tell you that Christ has become a servant of the circumcised on behalf of God’s truth, to confirm the promises made to the patriarchs,
chapters.zh: 我说，基督是为上帝真理作了受割礼人的执事，要证实所应许列祖的话，

chapters.en:
so that the Gentiles may glorify God for His mercy. As it is written:
“Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles; I will sing hymns to Your name.”
chapters.zh: 并叫外邦人因他的怜悯荣耀上帝。如〔经上〕所记： 因此，我要在外邦中称赞你， 歌颂你的名；

chapters.en:
Again, it says:
“Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people.”
chapters.zh: 又说： 你们外邦人当与主的百姓一同欢乐；

chapters.en:
And again:
“Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and extol Him, all you peoples.”
chapters.zh: 又说： 外邦啊，你们当赞美主！ 万民哪，你们都当颂赞他！
又有以赛亚说： 将来有耶西的根， 就是那兴起来要治理外邦的； 外邦人要仰望他。

chapters.en: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe in Him, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
chapters.zh: 但愿使人有盼望的上帝，因信将诸般的喜乐、平安充满你们的心，使你们藉着圣灵的能力大有盼望！

chapters.en: I myself am convinced, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, brimming with knowledge, and able to instruct one another.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我自己也深信你们是满有良善，充足了诸般的知识，也能彼此劝戒。

chapters.en: However, I have written you a bold reminder on some points, because of the grace God has given me
chapters.zh: 但我稍微放胆写信给你们，是要提醒你们的记性，特因上帝所给我的恩典，

chapters.en: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles in the priestly service of the gospel of God, so that the Gentiles might become an offering acceptable to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
chapters.zh: 使我为外邦人作基督耶稣的仆役，作上帝福音的祭司，叫所献上的外邦人，因着圣灵成为圣洁，可蒙悦纳。

chapters.en: Therefore I exult in Christ Jesus in my service to God.
chapters.zh: 所以论到上帝的事，我在基督耶稣里有可夸的。

chapters.en: I will not presume to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me in leading the Gentiles to obedience by word and deed,
chapters.zh: 除了基督藉我做的那些事，我什么都不敢提，只提他藉我言语作为，用神迹奇事的能力，并圣灵的能力，使外邦人顺服；

chapters.en: by the power of signs and wonders, and by the power of the Spirit of God. So from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ.
chapters.zh: 甚至我从耶路撒冷，直转到以利哩古，到处传了基督的福音。

chapters.en: In this way I have aspired to preach the gospel where Christ was not known, so that I would not be building on someone else’s foundation.
chapters.zh: 我立了志向，不在基督的名被称过的地方传福音，免得建造在别人的根基上。

chapters.en:
Rather, as it is written:
“Those who were not told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”
chapters.zh: 就如〔经上〕所记： 未曾闻知他信息的，将要看见； 未曾听过的，将要明白。

chapters.en: That is why I have often been hindered from coming to you.
chapters.zh: 我因多次被拦阻，总不得到你们那里去。

chapters.en: But now that there are no further opportunities for me in these regions, and since I have longed for many years to visit you,
chapters.zh: 但如今，在这里再没有〔可传的〕地方，而且这好几年，我切心想望到西班牙去的时候，可以到你们那里，

chapters.en: I hope to see you on my way to Spain. And after I have enjoyed your company for a while, you can equip me for my journey.
chapters.zh: 盼望从你们那里经过，得见你们，先与你们彼此交往，心里稍微满足，然后蒙你们送行。

chapters.en: Now, however, I am on my way to Jerusalem to serve the saints there.
chapters.zh: 但现在，我往耶路撒冷去供给圣徒。

chapters.en: For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 因为马其顿和亚该亚人乐意凑出捐项给耶路撒冷圣徒中的穷人。

chapters.en: They were pleased to do it, and indeed they owe it to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual blessings, they are obligated to minister to them with material blessings.
chapters.zh: 这固然是他们乐意的，其实也算是所欠的债；因外邦人既然在他们属灵的好处上有分，就当把养身之物供给他们。

chapters.en: So after I have completed this service and have safely delivered this bounty to them, I will set off to Spain by way of you.
chapters.zh: 等我办完了这事，把这善果向他们交付明白，我就要路过你们那里，往西班牙去。

chapters.en: I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.
chapters.zh: 我也晓得，去的时候必带着基督丰盛的恩典而去。

chapters.en: Now I urge you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to join me in my struggle by praying to God for me.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我藉着我们主耶稣基督，又藉着〔圣〕灵的爱，劝你们与我一同竭力，为我祈求上帝，
