chapters.en: Pray that I may be delivered from the unbelievers in Judea, and that my service in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints there,
chapters.zh: 叫我脱离在犹太不顺从的人，也叫我为耶路撒冷所办的捐项可蒙圣徒悦纳，

chapters.en: so that by God’s will I may come to you with joy and together with you be refreshed.
chapters.zh: 并叫我顺着上帝的旨意，欢欢喜喜地到你们那里，与你们同得安息。

chapters.en: The God of peace be with all of you. Amen.
chapters.zh: 愿赐平安的上帝常和你们众人同在。阿们！

chapters.en: I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a servant of the church in Cenchrea.
chapters.zh: 我对你们举荐我们的姊妹非比；她是坚革哩教会中的女执事。

chapters.en: Welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her with anything she may need from you. For she has been a great help to many people, including me.
chapters.zh: 请你们为主接待她，合乎圣徒的体统。她在何事上要你们帮助，你们就帮助她；因她素来帮助许多人，也帮助了我。

chapters.en: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
chapters.zh: 问百基拉和亚居拉安。他们在基督耶稣里与我同工，

chapters.en: who have risked their lives for me. Not only I but all the churches of the Gentiles are grateful to them.
chapters.zh: 也为我的命将自己的颈项置之度外。不但我感谢他们，就是外邦的众教会也感谢他们。

chapters.en:
Greet also the church that meets at their house.
Greet my beloved Epenetus, who was the first convert to Christ in the province of Asia.
chapters.zh: 又问在他们家中的教会安。问我所亲爱的以拜尼土安；他在亚细亚是归基督初结的果子。

chapters.en: Greet Mary, who has worked very hard for you.
chapters.zh: 又问马利亚安；她为你们多受劳苦。

chapters.en: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my fellow countrymen and fellow prisoners. They are outstanding among the apostles, and they were in Christ before I was.
chapters.zh: 又问我亲属与我一同坐监的安多尼古和犹尼亚安；他们在使徒中是有名望的，也是比我先在基督里。

chapters.en: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
chapters.zh: 又问我在主里面所亲爱的暗伯利安。

chapters.en: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my beloved Stachys.
chapters.zh: 又问在基督里与我们同工的耳巴奴，并我所亲爱的士大古安。

chapters.en:
Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ.
Greet those who belong to the household of Aristobulus.
chapters.zh: 又问在基督里经过试验的亚比利安。问亚利多布家里的人安。

chapters.en:
Greet Herodion, my fellow countryman.
Greet those from the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
chapters.zh: 又问我亲属希罗天安。问拿其数家在主里的人安。

chapters.en:
Greet Tryphena and Tryphosa, women who have worked hard in the Lord.
Greet my beloved Persis, who has worked very hard in the Lord.
chapters.zh: 又问为主劳苦的土非拿氏和土富撒氏安。问可亲爱为主多受劳苦的彼息氏安。

chapters.en: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been a mother to me as well.
chapters.zh: 又问在主蒙拣选的鲁孚和他母亲安；他的母亲就是我的母亲。

chapters.en: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.
chapters.zh: 又问亚逊其土、弗勒干、黑米、八罗巴、黑马，并与他们在一处的弟兄们安。

chapters.en: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.
chapters.zh: 又问非罗罗古和犹利亚，尼利亚和他姊妹，同阿林巴并与他们在一处的众圣徒安。

chapters.en:
Greet one another with a holy kiss.
All the churches of Christ send you greetings.
chapters.zh: 你们亲嘴问安，彼此务要圣洁。基督的众教会都问你们安。

chapters.en: Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those who create divisions and obstacles that are contrary to the teaching you have learned. Turn away from them.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，那些离间你们、叫你们跌倒、背乎所学之道的人，我劝你们要留意躲避他们。

chapters.en: For such people are not serving our Lord Christ, but their own appetites. By smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive.
chapters.zh: 因为这样的人不服事我们的主基督，只服事自己的肚腹，用花言巧语诱惑那些老实人的心。

chapters.en: Everyone has heard about your obedience, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.
chapters.zh: 你们的顺服已经传于众人，所以我为你们欢喜；但我愿意你们在善上聪明，在恶上愚拙。

chapters.en: The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
chapters.zh: 赐平安的上帝快要将撒但践踏在你们脚下。愿我主耶稣基督的恩常和你们同在！

chapters.en: Timothy, my fellow worker, sends you greetings, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my fellow countrymen.
chapters.zh: 与我同工的提摩太，和我的亲属路求、耶孙、所西巴德，问你们安。

chapters.en: I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.
chapters.zh: 我这代笔写信的德提，在主里面问你们安。

chapters.en:
Gaius, who has hosted me and all the church, sends you greetings.
Erastus, the city treasurer, sends you greetings, as does our brother Quartus.
chapters.zh: 那接待我、也接待全教会的该犹问你们安。
城内管银库的以拉都和兄弟括土问你们安。

chapters.en: Now to Him who is able to strengthen you by my gospel and by the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery concealed for ages past
chapters.zh: 惟有上帝能照我所传的福音和所讲的耶稣基督，并照永古隐藏不言的奥祕，坚固你们的心。

chapters.en: but now revealed and made known through the writings of the prophets by the command of the eternal God, in order to lead all nations to the obedience that comes from faith —
chapters.zh: 这奥祕如今显明出来，而且按着永生上帝的命，藉众先知的书指示万国的民，使他们信服真道。

chapters.en: to the only wise God be glory forever through Jesus Christ! Amen.
chapters.zh: 愿荣耀，因耶稣基督，归与独一全智的上帝，直到永远。阿们！

chapters.en: Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and our brother Sosthenes,
chapters.zh: 奉上帝旨意，蒙召作耶稣基督使徒的保罗，同兄弟所提尼，

chapters.en: To the church of God in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy, together with all those everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:
chapters.zh: 写信给在哥林多上帝的教会，就是在基督耶稣里成圣、蒙召作圣徒的，以及所有在各处求告我主耶稣基督之名的人。基督是他们的〔主〕，也是我们的〔主〕。

chapters.en: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 愿恩惠、平安从上帝我们的父并主耶稣基督归与你们。

chapters.en: I always thank my God for you because of the grace He has given you in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 我常为你们感谢我的上帝，因上帝在基督耶稣里所赐给你们的恩惠；

chapters.en: For in Him you have been enriched in every way, in all speech and all knowledge,
chapters.zh: 又因你们在他里面凡事富足，口才、知识都全备，

chapters.en: because our testimony about Christ was confirmed in you.
chapters.zh: 正如〔我为〕基督〔作〕的见证，在你们心里得以坚固，

chapters.en: Therefore you do not lack any spiritual gift as you eagerly await the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 以致你们在恩赐上没有一样不及人的，等候我们的主耶稣基督显现。

chapters.en: He will sustain you to the end, so that you will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 他也必坚固你们到底，叫你们在我们主耶稣基督的日子无可责备。

chapters.en: God, who has called you into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ our Lord, is faithful.
chapters.zh: 上帝是信实的，你们原是被他所召，好与他儿子－我们的主耶稣基督一同得分。

chapters.en: I appeal to you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree together, so that there may be no divisions among you and that you may be united in mind and conviction.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我藉我们主耶稣基督的名劝你们都说一样的话。你们中间也不可分党，只要一心一意，彼此相合。

chapters.en: My brothers, some from Chloe’s household have informed me that there are quarrels among you.
chapters.zh: 因为革来氏〔家里〕的人曾对我提起弟兄们来，说你们中间有纷争。

chapters.en: What I mean is this: Individuals among you are saying, “I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos,” “I follow Cephas,” or “I follow Christ.”
chapters.zh: 我的意思就是你们各人说：「我是属保罗的」；「我是属亚波罗的」；「我是属矶法的」；「我是属基督的」。

chapters.en: Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Were you baptized into the name of Paul?
chapters.zh: 基督是分开的吗？保罗为你们钉了十字架吗？你们是奉保罗的名受了洗吗？

chapters.en: I thank God that I did not baptize any of you except Crispus and Gaius,
chapters.zh: 我感谢上帝，除了基利司布并该犹以外，我没有给你们一个人施洗，

chapters.en: so no one can say that you were baptized into my name.
chapters.zh: 免得有人说，你们是奉我的名受洗。

chapters.en: Yes, I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that I do not remember if I baptized anyone else.
chapters.zh: 我也给司提法那家施过洗，此外给别人施洗没有，我却记不清。

chapters.en: For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel, not with words of wisdom, lest the cross of Christ be emptied of its power.
chapters.zh: 基督差遣我，原不是为施洗，乃是为传福音，并不用智慧的言语，免得基督的十字架落了空。

chapters.en: For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
chapters.zh: 因为十字架的道理，在那灭亡的人为愚拙；在我们得救的人，却为上帝的大能。

chapters.en:
For it is written:
“I will destroy the wisdom of the wise; the intelligence of the intelligent I will frustrate.”
chapters.zh: 就如〔经上〕所记： 我要灭绝智慧人的智慧， 废弃聪明人的聪明。

chapters.en: Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the philosopher of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?
chapters.zh: 智慧人在哪里？文士在哪里？这世上的辩士在哪里？上帝岂不是叫这世上的智慧变成愚拙吗？

chapters.en: For since in the wisdom of God the world through its wisdom did not know Him, God was pleased through the foolishness of what was preached to save those who believe.
chapters.zh: 世人凭自己的智慧，既不认识上帝，上帝就乐意用〔人所当作〕愚拙的道理拯救那些信的人；这就是上帝的智慧了。

chapters.en: Jews demand signs and Greeks search for wisdom,
chapters.zh: 犹太人是要神迹，希腊人是求智慧，

chapters.en: but we preach Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,
chapters.zh: 我们却是传钉十字架的基督，在犹太人为绊脚石，在外邦人为愚拙；

chapters.en: but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.
chapters.zh: 但在那蒙召的，无论是犹太人、希腊人，基督总为上帝的能力，上帝的智慧。

chapters.en: For the foolishness of God is wiser than man’s wisdom, and the weakness of God is stronger than man’s strength.
chapters.zh: 因上帝的愚拙总比人智慧，上帝的软弱总比人强壮。

chapters.en: Brothers, consider the time of your calling: Not many of you were wise by human standards; not many were powerful; not many were of noble birth.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们哪，可见你们蒙召的，按着肉体有智慧的不多，有能力的不多，有尊贵的也不多。

chapters.en: But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise; God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.
chapters.zh: 上帝却拣选了世上愚拙的，叫有智慧的羞愧；又拣选了世上软弱的，叫那强壮的羞愧。

chapters.en: He chose the lowly and despised things of the world, and the things that are not, to nullify the things that are,
chapters.zh: 上帝也拣选了世上卑贱的，被人厌恶的，以及那无有的，为要废掉那有的，

chapters.en: so that no one may boast in His presence.
chapters.zh: 使一切有血气的，在上帝面前一个也不能自夸。

chapters.en: It is because of Him that you are in Christ Jesus, who has become for us wisdom from God: our righteousness, holiness, and redemption.
chapters.zh: 但你们得在基督耶稣里是本乎上帝，上帝又使他成为我们的智慧、公义、圣洁、救赎。

chapters.en: Therefore, as it is written: “Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.”
chapters.zh: 如〔经上〕所记：「夸口的，当指着主夸口。」

chapters.en: When I came to you, brothers, I did not come with eloquence or wisdom as I proclaimed to you the testimony about God.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，从前我到你们那里去，并没有用高言大智对你们宣传上帝的奥祕。

chapters.en: For I resolved to know nothing while I was with you except Jesus Christ and Him crucified.
chapters.zh: 因为我曾定了主意，在你们中间不知道别的，只知道耶稣基督并他钉十字架。

chapters.en: I came to you in weakness and fear, and with much trembling.
chapters.zh: 我在你们那里，又软弱，又惧怕又甚战兢。

chapters.en: My message and my preaching were not with persuasive words of wisdom, but with a demonstration of the Spirit’s power,
chapters.zh: 我说的话、讲的道，不是用智慧委婉的言语，乃是用圣灵和大能的明证，

chapters.en: so that your faith would not rest on men’s wisdom, but on God’s power.
chapters.zh: 叫你们的信不在乎人的智慧，只在乎上帝的大能。

chapters.en: Among the mature, however, we speak a message of wisdom—but not the wisdom of this age or of the rulers of this age, who are coming to nothing.
chapters.zh: 然而，在完全的人中，我们也讲智慧。但不是这世上的智慧，也不是这世上有权有位、将要败亡之人的智慧。

chapters.en: No, we speak of the mysterious and hidden wisdom of God, which He destined for our glory before time began.
chapters.zh: 我们讲的，乃是从前所隐藏、上帝奥祕的智慧，就是上帝在万世以前预定使我们得荣耀的。

chapters.en: None of the rulers of this age understood it. For if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
chapters.zh: 这智慧世上有权有位的人没有一个知道的，他们若知道，就不把荣耀的主钉在十字架上了。

chapters.en:
Rather, as it is written:
“No eye has seen, no ear has heard,
no heart has imagined, what God has prepared for those who love Him.”
chapters.zh: 如〔经上〕所记： 上帝为爱他的人所预备的 是眼睛未曾看见， 耳朵未曾听见， 人心也未曾想到的。

chapters.en:
But God has revealed it to us by the Spirit.
The Spirit searches all things, even the deep things of God.
chapters.zh: 只有上帝藉着圣灵向我们显明了，因为圣灵参透万事，就是上帝深奥的事也参透了。

chapters.en: For who among men knows the thoughts of man except his own spirit within him? So too, no one knows the thoughts of God except the Spirit of God.
chapters.zh: 除了在人里头的灵，谁知道人的事？像这样，除了上帝的灵，也没有人知道上帝的事。

chapters.en: We have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, that we may understand what God has freely given us.
chapters.zh: 我们所领受的，并不是世上的灵，乃是从上帝来的灵，叫我们能知道上帝开恩赐给我们的事。

chapters.en: And this is what we speak, not in words taught us by human wisdom, but in words taught by the Spirit, expressing spiritual truths in spiritual words.
chapters.zh: 并且我们讲说这些事，不是用人智慧所指教的言语，乃是用〔圣〕灵所指教的言语，将属灵的话解释属灵的事〔注：或译：将属灵的事讲与属灵的人〕。

chapters.en: The natural man does not accept the things that come from the Spirit of God. For they are foolishness to him, and he cannot understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.
chapters.zh: 然而，属血气的人不领会上帝〔圣〕灵的事，反倒以为愚拙，并且不能知道，因为这些事惟有属灵的人才能看透。

chapters.en: The spiritual man judges all things, but he himself is not subject to anyone’s judgment.
chapters.zh: 属灵的人能看透万事，却没有一人能看透了他。

chapters.en: “For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct Him?” But we have the mind of Christ.
chapters.zh: 谁曾知道主的心去教导他呢？但我们是有基督的心了。

chapters.en: Brothers, I could not address you as spiritual, but as worldly—as infants in Christ.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我从前对你们说话，不能把你们当作属灵的，只得把你们当作属肉体，在基督里为婴孩的。

chapters.en: I gave you milk, not solid food, for you were not yet ready for solid food. In fact, you are still not ready,
chapters.zh: 我是用奶餵你们，没有用饭餵你们。那时你们不能吃，就是如今还是不能。

chapters.en: for you are still worldly. For since there is jealousy and dissension among you, are you not worldly? Are you not walking in the way of man?
chapters.zh: 你们仍是属肉体的，因为在你们中间有嫉妒、纷争，这岂不是属乎肉体、照着世人的样子行吗？

chapters.en: For when one of you says, “I follow Paul,” and another, “I follow Apollos,” are you not mere men?
chapters.zh: 有说：「我是属保罗的」；有说：「我是属亚波罗的。」这岂不是你们和世人一样吗？

chapters.en: What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? They are servants through whom you believed, as the Lord has assigned to each his role.
chapters.zh: 亚波罗算什么？保罗算什么？无非是执事，照主所赐给他们各人的，引导你们相信。

chapters.en: I planted the seed and Apollos watered it, but God made it grow.
chapters.zh: 我栽种了，亚波罗浇灌了，惟有上帝叫他生长。

chapters.en: So neither he who plants nor he who waters is anything, but only God, who makes things grow.
chapters.zh: 可见栽种的，算不得什么，浇灌的，也算不得什么；只在那叫他生长的上帝。

chapters.en: He who plants and he who waters are one in purpose, and each will be rewarded according to his own labor.
chapters.zh: 栽种的和浇灌的，都是一样，但将来各人要照自己的工夫得自己的赏赐。

chapters.en: For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s field, God’s building.
chapters.zh: 因为我们是与上帝同工的；你们是上帝所耕种的田地，所建造的房屋。

chapters.en: By the grace God has given me, I laid a foundation as an expert builder, and someone else is building on it. But each one must be careful how he builds.
chapters.zh: 我照上帝所给我的恩，好像一个聪明的工头，立好了根基，有别人在上面建造；只是各人要谨慎怎样在上面建造。

chapters.en: For no one can lay a foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 因为那已经立好的根基就是耶稣基督，此外没有人能立别的根基。

chapters.en: If anyone builds on this foundation using gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw,
chapters.zh: 若有人用金、银、宝石、草木、禾诩在这根基上建造，

chapters.en: his workmanship will be evident, because the Day will bring it to light. It will be revealed with fire, and the fire will prove the quality of each man’s work.
chapters.zh: 各人的工程必然显露，因为那日子要将它表明出来，有火发现；这火要试验各人的工程怎样。

chapters.en: If what he has built survives, he will receive a reward.
chapters.zh: 人在那根基上所建造的工程若存得住，他就要得赏赐。

chapters.en: If it is burned up, he will suffer loss. He himself will be saved, but only as if through the flames.
chapters.zh: 人的工程若被烧了，他就要受亏损，自己却要得救；虽然得救，乃像从火里经过的一样。

chapters.en: Do you not know that you yourselves are God’s temple, and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?
chapters.zh: 岂不知你们是上帝的殿，上帝的灵住在你们里头吗？

chapters.en: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for God’s temple is holy, and you are that temple.
chapters.zh: 若有人毁坏上帝的殿，上帝必要毁坏那人；因为上帝的殿是圣的，这殿就是你们。

chapters.en: Let no one deceive himself. If any of you thinks he is wise in this age, he should become a fool, so that he may become wise.
chapters.zh: 人不可自欺。你们中间若有人在这世界自以为有智慧，倒不如变作愚拙，好成为有智慧的。

chapters.en: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness in God’s sight. As it is written: “He catches the wise in their craftiness.”
chapters.zh: 因这世界的智慧，在上帝看是愚拙。如〔经上〕记着说：「主叫有智慧的，中了自己的诡计」；

chapters.en: And again, “The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are futile.”
chapters.zh: 又说：「主知道智慧人的意念是虚妄的。」

chapters.en: Therefore, stop boasting in men. All things are yours,
chapters.zh: 所以无论谁，都不可拿人夸口，因为万有全是你们的。

chapters.en: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or the present or the future. All of them belong to you,
chapters.zh: 或保罗，或亚波罗，或矶法，或世界，或生，或死，或现今的事，或将来的事，全是你们的；

chapters.en: and you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.
chapters.zh: 并且你们是属基督的，基督又是属上帝的。

chapters.en: So then, men ought to regard us as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.
chapters.zh: 人应当以我们为基督的执事，为上帝奥祕事的管家。

chapters.en: Now it is required of stewards that they be found faithful.
chapters.zh: 所求于管家的，是要他有忠心。

chapters.en: I care very little, however, if I am judged by you or by any human court. In fact, I do not even judge myself.
chapters.zh: 我被你们论断，或被别人论断，我都以为极小的事；连我自己也不论断自己。

chapters.en: My conscience is clear, but that does not vindicate me. It is the Lord who judges me.
chapters.zh: 我虽不觉得自己有错，却也不能因此得以称义；但判断我的乃是主。

chapters.en: Therefore judge nothing before the appointed time; wait until the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and will expose the motives of men’s hearts. At that time each will receive his praise from God.
chapters.zh: 所以，时候未到，什么都不要论断，只等主来，他要照出暗中的隐情，显明人心的意念。那时，各人要从上帝那里得着称赞。

chapters.en: Brothers, I have applied these things to myself and Apollos for your benefit, so that you may learn from us not to go beyond what is written. Then you will not take pride in one man over another.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我为你们的缘故，拿这些事转比自己和亚波罗，叫你们效法我们不可过于〔圣经〕所记，免得你们自高自大，贵重这个，轻看那个。

chapters.en: For who makes you so superior? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you did not?
chapters.zh: 使你与人不同的是谁呢？你有什么不是领受的呢？若是领受的，为何自夸，仿佛不是领受的呢？

chapters.en: Already you have all you want. Already you have become rich. Without us, you have become kings. How I wish you really were kings, so that we might be kings with you!
chapters.zh: 你们已经饱足了！已经丰富了！不用我们，自己就作王了！我愿意你们果真作王，叫我们也得与你们一同作王。

chapters.en: For it seems to me that God has displayed us apostles at the end of the procession, like prisoners appointed for death. We have become a spectacle to the whole world, to angels as well as to men.
chapters.zh: 我想上帝把我们使徒明明列在末后，好像定死罪的囚犯；因为我们成了一台戏，给世人和天使观看。

chapters.en: We are fools for Christ, but you are wise in Christ. We are weak, but you are strong. You are honored, but we are dishonored.
chapters.zh: 我们为基督的缘故算是愚拙的，你们在基督里倒是聪明的；我们软弱，你们倒强壮；你们有荣耀，我们倒被藐视。

chapters.en: To this very hour we are hungry and thirsty, we are poorly clothed, we are brutally treated, we are homeless.
chapters.zh: 直到如今，我们还是又饥又渴，又赤身露体，又挨打，又没有一定的住处，

chapters.en: We work hard with our own hands. When we are vilified, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure it;
chapters.zh: 并且劳苦，亲手做工。被人咒骂，我们就祝福；被人逼迫，我们就忍受；

chapters.en: when we are slandered, we answer gently. Up to this moment we have become the scum of the earth, the refuse of the world.
chapters.zh: 被人毁谤，我们就善劝。直到如今，人还把我们看作世界上的污秽，万物中的渣滓。

chapters.en: I am not writing this to shame you, but to warn you as my beloved children.
chapters.zh: 我写这话，不是叫你们羞愧，乃是警戒你们，好像我所亲爱的儿女一样。

chapters.en: Even if you have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.
chapters.zh: 你们学基督的，师傅虽有一万，为父的却是不多，因我在基督耶稣里用福音生了你们。

chapters.en: Therefore I urge you to imitate me.
chapters.zh: 所以，我求你们效法我。

chapters.en: That is why I have sent you Timothy, my beloved and faithful child in the Lord. He will remind you of my way of life in Christ Jesus, which is exactly what I teach everywhere in every church.
chapters.zh: 因此我已打发提摩太到你们那里去。他在主里面，是我所亲爱、有忠心的儿子。他必提醒你们，记念我在基督里怎样行事，在各处各教会中怎样教导人。

chapters.en: Some of you have become arrogant, as if I were not coming to you.
chapters.zh: 有些人自高自大，以为我不到你们那里去；

chapters.en: But I will come to you shortly, if the Lord is willing, and then I will find out not only what these arrogant people are saying, but what power they have.
chapters.zh: 然而，主若许我，我必快到你们那里去，并且我所要知道的，不是那些自高自大之人的言语，乃是他们的权能。

chapters.en: For the kingdom of God is not a matter of talk but of power.
chapters.zh: 因为上帝的国不在乎言语，乃在乎权能。

chapters.en: Which do you prefer? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and with a gentle spirit?
chapters.zh: 你们愿意怎么样呢？是愿意我带着刑杖到你们那里去呢？还是要我存慈爱温柔的心呢？

chapters.en: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and of a kind that is intolerable even among pagans: A man has his father’s wife.
chapters.zh: 风闻在你们中间有淫乱的事。这样的淫乱连外邦人中也没有，就是有人收了他的继母。

chapters.en: And you are proud! Shouldn’t you rather have been stricken with grief and have removed from your fellowship the man who did this?
chapters.zh: 你们还是自高自大，并不哀痛，把行这事的人从你们中间赶出去。

chapters.en: Although I am absent from you in body, I am present with you in spirit, and I have already pronounced judgment on the one who did this, just as if I were present.
chapters.zh: 我身子虽不在你们那里，心却在你们那里，好像我亲自与你们同在，已经判断了行这事的人。

chapters.en: When you are assembled in the name of our Lord Jesus and I am with you in spirit, along with the power of the Lord Jesus,
chapters.zh: 就是你们聚会的时候，我的心也同在。奉我们主耶稣的名，并用我们主耶稣的权能，

chapters.en: hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the Day of the Lord.
chapters.zh: 要把这样的人交给撒但，败坏他的肉体，使他的灵魂在主耶稣的日子可以得救。

chapters.en: Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven works through the whole batch of dough?
chapters.zh: 你们这自夸是不好的。岂不知一点面酵能使全团发起来吗？

chapters.en: Get rid of the old leaven, that you may be a new unleavened batch, as you really are. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.
chapters.zh: 你们既是无酵的面，应当把旧酵除净，好使你们成为新团；因为我们逾越节的〔羔羊〕基督已经被杀献祭了。

chapters.en: Therefore let us keep the feast, not with the old bread, leavened with malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and of truth.
chapters.zh: 所以，我们守这节不可用旧酵，也不可用恶毒〔注：或译：阴毒〕、邪恶的酵，只用诚实真正的无酵饼。

chapters.en: I wrote you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.
chapters.zh: 我先前写信给你们说，不可与淫乱的人相交。

chapters.en: I was not including the sexually immoral of this world, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters. In that case you would have to leave this world.
chapters.zh: 此话不是指这世上一概行淫乱的，或贪婪的，勒索的，或拜偶像的；若是这样，你们除非离开世界方可。

chapters.en: But now I am writing you not to associate with anyone who claims to be a brother but is sexually immoral or greedy, an idolater or a verbal abuser, a drunkard or a swindler. With such a man do not even eat.
chapters.zh: 但如今我写信给你们说，若有称为弟兄是行淫乱的，或贪婪的，或拜偶像的，或辱骂的，或醉酒的，或勒索的，这样的人不可与他相交，就是与他吃饭都不可。

chapters.en: What business of mine is it to judge those outside the church? Are you not to judge those inside?
chapters.zh: 因为审判〔教〕外的人与我何干？〔教〕内的人岂不是你们审判的吗？

chapters.en: God will judge those outside. “Expel the wicked man from among you.”
chapters.zh: 至于外人有上帝审判他们。你们应当把那恶人从你们中间赶出去。

chapters.en: If any of you has a grievance against another, how dare he go to law before the unrighteous instead of before the saints!
chapters.zh: 你们中间有彼此相争的事，怎敢在不义的人面前求审，不在圣徒面前求审呢？

chapters.en: Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if you are to judge the world, are you not competent to judge trivial cases?
chapters.zh: 岂不知圣徒要审判世界吗？若世界为你们所审，难道你们不配审判这最小的事吗？

chapters.en: Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more the things of this life!
chapters.zh: 岂不知我们要审判天使吗？何况今生的事呢？

chapters.en: So if you need to settle everyday matters, do you appoint as judges those of no standing in the church?
chapters.zh: 既是这样，你们若有今生的事当审判，是派教会所轻看的人审判吗？

chapters.en: I say this to your shame. Is there really no one among you wise enough to arbitrate between his brothers?
chapters.zh: 我说这话是要叫你们羞耻。难道你们中间没有一个智慧人能审断弟兄们的事吗？

chapters.en: Instead, one brother goes to law against another, and this in front of unbelievers!
chapters.zh: 你们竟是弟兄与弟兄告状，而且告在不信〔主〕的人面前。

chapters.en: The very fact that you have lawsuits among you means that you are thoroughly defeated already. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be cheated?
chapters.zh: 你们彼此告状，这已经是你们的大错了。为什么不情愿受欺呢？为什么不情愿吃亏呢？

chapters.en: Instead, you yourselves cheat and do wrong, even against your own brothers!
chapters.zh: 你们倒是欺压人、亏负人，况且所欺压所亏负的就是弟兄。

chapters.en: Do you not know that the wicked will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: Neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men who submit to or perform homosexual acts,
chapters.zh: 你们岂不知不义的人不能承受上帝的国吗？不要自欺！无论是淫乱的、拜偶像的、奸淫的、作娈童的、亲男色的、

chapters.en: nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor verbal abusers, nor swindlers, will inherit the kingdom of God.
chapters.zh: 偷窃的、贪婪的、醉酒的、辱骂的、勒索的，都不能承受上帝的国。

chapters.en: And that is what some of you were. But you were washed, you were sanctified, you were justified, in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.
chapters.zh: 你们中间也有人从前是这样；但如今你们奉主耶稣基督的名，并藉着我们上帝的灵，已经洗净，成圣，称义了。

chapters.en: “Everything is permissible for me,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible for me,” but I will not be mastered by anything.
chapters.zh: 凡事我都可行，但不都有益处。凡事我都可行，但无论哪一件，我总不受它的辖制。

chapters.en: “Food for the stomach and the stomach for food,” but God will destroy them both. The body is not intended for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
chapters.zh: 食物是为肚腹，肚腹是为食物；但上帝要叫这两样都废坏。身子不是为淫乱，乃是为主；主也是为身子。

chapters.en: By His power God raised the Lord from the dead, and He will raise us also.
chapters.zh: 并且上帝已经叫主复活，也要用自己的能力叫我们复活。

chapters.en: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and unite them with a prostitute? Never!
chapters.zh: 岂不知你们的身子是基督的肢体吗？我可以将基督的肢体作为娼妓的肢体吗？断乎不可！

chapters.en: Or don’t you know that he who unites himself with a prostitute is one with her in body? For it is said, “The two will become one flesh.”
chapters.zh: 岂不知与娼妓联合的，便是与她成为一体吗？因为主说：「二人要成为一体。」

chapters.en: But he who unites himself with the Lord is one with Him in spirit.
chapters.zh: 但与主联合的，便是与主成为一灵。

chapters.en: Flee from sexual immorality. Every other sin a man can commit is outside his body, but he who sins sexually sins against his own body.
chapters.zh: 你们要逃避淫行。人所犯的，无论什么罪，都在身子以外，惟有行淫的，是得罪自己的身子。

chapters.en: Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have received from God? You are not your own;
chapters.zh: 岂不知你们的身子就是圣灵的殿吗？这圣灵是从上帝而来，住在你们里头的；并且你们不是自己的人，

chapters.en: you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God with your body.
chapters.zh: 因为你们是重价买来的。所以，要在你们的身子上荣耀上帝。

chapters.en: Now for the matters you wrote about: It is good to abstain from sexual relations.
chapters.zh: 论到你们信上所提的事，〔我说〕男不近女倒好。

chapters.en: But because there is so much sexual immorality, each man should have his own wife, and each woman her own husband.
chapters.zh: 但要免淫乱的事，男子当各有自己的妻子；女子也当各有自己的丈夫。

chapters.en: The husband should fulfill his marital duty to his wife, and likewise the wife to her husband.
chapters.zh: 丈夫当用合宜之分待妻子；妻子待丈夫也要如此。

chapters.en: The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband. Likewise the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife.
chapters.zh: 妻子没有权柄主张自己的身子，乃在丈夫；丈夫也没有权柄主张自己的身子，乃在妻子。

chapters.en: Do not deprive each other, except by mutual consent and for a time, so you may devote yourselves to prayer. Then come together again, so that Satan will not tempt you through your lack of self-control.
chapters.zh: 夫妻不可彼此亏负，除非两相情愿，暂时分房，为要专心祷告方可；以后仍要同房，免得撒但趁着你们情不自禁，引诱你们。

chapters.en: I say this as a concession, not as a command.
chapters.zh: 我说这话，原是准〔你们〕的，不是命〔你们〕的。

chapters.en: I wish that all men were as I am. But each man has his own gift from God; one has this gift, another has that.
chapters.zh: 我愿意众人像我一样；只是各人领受上帝的恩赐，一个是这样，一个是那样。

chapters.en: Now to the unmarried and widows I say this: It is good for them to remain unmarried, as I am.
chapters.zh: 我对着没有嫁娶的和寡妇说，若他们常像我就好。

chapters.en: But if they cannot control themselves, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to burn with passion.
chapters.zh: 倘若自己禁止不住，就可以嫁娶。与其欲火攻心，倒不如嫁娶为妙。

chapters.en: To the married I give this command (not I, but the Lord): A wife must not separate from her husband.
chapters.zh: 至于那已经嫁娶的，我吩咐他们；其实不是我吩咐，乃是主吩咐说：妻子不可离开丈夫，

chapters.en: But if she does, she must remain unmarried or else be reconciled to her husband. And a husband must not divorce his wife.
chapters.zh: 若是离开了，不可再嫁，或是仍同丈夫和好。丈夫也不可离弃妻子。

chapters.en: To the rest I say this (I, not the Lord): If a brother has an unbelieving wife and she is willing to live with him, he must not divorce her.
chapters.zh: 我对其余的人说（不是主说）：倘若某弟兄有不信的妻子，妻子也情愿和他同住，他就不要离弃妻子。

chapters.en: And if a woman has an unbelieving husband and he is willing to live with her, she must not divorce him.
chapters.zh: 妻子有不信的丈夫，丈夫也情愿和她同住，她就不要离弃丈夫。

chapters.en: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified through his believing wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified through her believing husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.
chapters.zh: 因为不信的丈夫就因着妻子成了圣洁，并且不信的妻子就因着丈夫〔注：原文是弟兄〕成了圣洁。不然，你们的儿女就不洁净，但如今他们是圣洁的了。

chapters.en: But if the unbeliever leaves, let him go. The believing brother or sister is not bound in such cases. God has called you to live in peace.
chapters.zh: 倘若那不信的人要离去，就由他离去吧！无论是弟兄，是姊妹，遇着这样的事都不必拘束。上帝召我们原是要我们和睦。

chapters.en: How do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
chapters.zh: 你这作妻子的，怎么知道不能救你的丈夫呢？你这作丈夫的，怎么知道不能救你的妻子呢？

chapters.en: Regardless, each one should lead the life that the Lord has assigned to him and to which God has called him. This is what I prescribe in all the churches.
chapters.zh: 只要照主所分给各人的，和上帝所召各人的而行。我吩咐各教会都是这样。

chapters.en: Was a man already circumcised when he was called? He should not become uncircumcised. Was a man still uncircumcised when called? He should not be circumcised.
chapters.zh: 有人已受割礼蒙召呢，就不要废割礼；有人未受割礼蒙召呢，就不要受割礼。

chapters.en: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing. Keeping God’s commandments is what counts.
chapters.zh: 受割礼算不得什么，不受割礼也算不得什么，只要守上帝的诫命就是了。

chapters.en: Each one should remain in the situation he was in when he was called.
chapters.zh: 各人蒙召的时候是什么身分，仍要守住这身分。

chapters.en: Were you a slave when you were called? Do not let it concern you—but if you can gain your freedom, take the opportunity.
chapters.zh: 你是作奴隸蒙召的吗？不要因此忧虑；若能以自由，就求自由更好。

chapters.en: For he who was a slave when he was called by the Lord is the Lord’s freedman. Conversely, he who was a free man when he was called is Christ’s slave.
chapters.zh: 因为作奴仆蒙召于主的，就是主所释放的人；作自由之人蒙召的，就是基督的奴仆。

chapters.en: You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of men.
chapters.zh: 你们是重价买来的，不要作人的奴仆。

chapters.en: Brothers, each one should remain in the situation he was in when God called him.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，你们各人蒙召的时候是什么身分，仍要在上帝面前守住这身分。

chapters.en: Now about virgins, I have no command from the Lord, but I give a judgment as one who by the Lord’s mercy is trustworthy.
chapters.zh: 论到童身的人，我没有主的命令，但我既蒙主怜恤能作忠心的人，就把自己的意见告诉〔你们〕。

chapters.en: Because of the present crisis, I think it is good for a man to remain as he is.
chapters.zh: 因现今的艰难，据我看来，人不如守素安常才好。

chapters.en: Are you committed to a wife? Do not seek to be released. Are you free of commitment? Do not look for a wife.
chapters.zh: 你有妻子缠着呢，就不要求脱离；你没有妻子缠着呢，就不要求妻子。

chapters.en: But if you do marry, you have not sinned. And if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. But those who marry will face troubles in this life, and I want to spare you this.
chapters.zh: 你若娶妻，并不是犯罪；处女若出嫁，也不是犯罪。然而这等人肉身必受苦难，我却愿意你们免这苦难。

chapters.en: What I am saying, brothers, is that the time is short. From now on those who have wives should live as if they had none;
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我对你们说：时候减少了。从此以后，那有妻子的，要像没有妻子；

chapters.en: those who weep, as if they did not; those who are joyful, as if they were not; those who make a purchase, as if they had nothing;
chapters.zh: 哀哭的，要像不哀哭；快乐的，要像不快乐；置买的，要像无有所得；

chapters.en: and those who use the things of this world, as if not dependent on them. For this world in its present form is passing away.
chapters.zh: 用世物的，要像不用世物，因为这世界的样子将要过去了。

chapters.en: I want you to be free from concern. The unmarried man is concerned about the work of the Lord, how he can please the Lord.
chapters.zh: 我愿你们无所挂虑。没有娶妻的，是为主的事挂虑，想怎样叫主喜悦。

chapters.en: But the married man is concerned about the affairs of this world, how he can please his wife,
chapters.zh: 娶了妻的，是为世上的事挂虑，想怎样叫妻子喜悦。

chapters.en: and his interests are divided. The unmarried woman or virgin is concerned about the work of the Lord, how she can be holy in both body and spirit. But the married woman is concerned about the affairs of this world, how she can please her husband.
chapters.zh: 妇人和处女也有分别。没有出嫁的，是为主的事挂虑，要身体、灵魂都圣洁；已经出嫁的，是为世上的事挂虑，想怎样叫丈夫喜悦。

chapters.en: I am saying this for your own good, not to restrict you, but in order to promote proper decorum and undivided devotion to the Lord.
chapters.zh: 我说这话是为你们的益处，不是要牢笼你们，乃是要叫你们行合宜的事，得以殷勤服事主，没有分心的事。

chapters.en: However, if someone thinks he is acting inappropriately toward his betrothed, and if she is beyond her youth and they ought to marry, let him do as he wishes; he is not sinning; they should get married.
chapters.zh: 若有人以为自己待他的女儿不合宜，女儿也过了年岁，事又当行，他就可随意办理，不算有罪，叫二人成亲就是了。

chapters.en: But the man who is firmly established in his heart and under no constraint, with control over his will and resolve in his heart not to marry the virgin, he will do well.
chapters.zh: 倘若人心里坚定，没有不得已的事，并且由得自己作主，心里又决定了留下女儿〔不出嫁〕，如此行也好。

chapters.en: So then, he who marries the virgin does well, but he who does not marry her does even better.
chapters.zh: 这样看来，叫自己的女儿出嫁是好，不叫她出嫁更是好。

chapters.en: A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, as long as he belongs to the Lord.
chapters.zh: 丈夫活着的时候，妻子是被约束的；丈夫若死了，妻子就可以自由，随意再嫁，只是要嫁这在主里面的人。

chapters.en: In my judgment, however, she is happier if she remains as she is. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God.
chapters.zh: 然而按我的意见，若常守节更有福气。我也想自己是被上帝的灵感动了。

chapters.en: Now about food sacrificed to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
chapters.zh: 论到祭偶像之物，我们晓得我们都有知识。但知识是叫人自高自大，惟有爱心能造就人。

chapters.en: The one who thinks he knows something does not yet know as he ought to know.
chapters.zh: 若有人以为自己知道什么，按他所当知道的，他仍是不知道。

chapters.en: But the one who loves God is known by God.
chapters.zh: 若有人爱上帝，这人乃是上帝所知道的。

chapters.en: So about eating food sacrificed to idols: We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is no God but one.
chapters.zh: 论到吃祭偶像之物，我们知道偶像在世上算不得什么，也知道上帝只有一位，再没有别的上帝。

chapters.en: For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth (as there are many so-called gods and lords),
chapters.zh: 虽有称为神的，或在天，或在地，就如那许多的神，许多的主；

chapters.en: yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things came and for whom we exist. And there is but one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things came and through whom we exist.
chapters.zh: 然而我们只有一位上帝，就是父－万物都本于他；我们也归于他－并有一位主，就是耶稣基督－万物都是藉着他有的；我们也是藉着他有的。

chapters.en: But not everyone has this knowledge. Some people are still so accustomed to idols that they eat such food as if it were sacrificed to an idol. And since their conscience is weak, it is defiled.
chapters.zh: 但人不都有这等知识。有人到如今因拜惯了偶像，就以为所吃的是祭偶像之物。他们的良心既然软弱，也就污秽了。

chapters.en: But food does not bring us closer to God: We are no worse if we do not eat, and no better if we do.
chapters.zh: 其实食物不能叫上帝看中我们，因为我们不吃也无损，吃也无益。

chapters.en: Be careful, however, that your freedom does not become a stumbling block to the weak.
chapters.zh: 只是你们要谨慎，恐怕你们这自由竟成了那软弱人的绊脚石。

chapters.en: For if someone with a weak conscience sees you who are well informed eating in an idol’s temple, will he not be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols?
chapters.zh: 若有人见你这有知识的，在偶像的庙里坐席，这人的良心若是软弱，岂不放胆去吃那祭偶像之物吗？

chapters.en: So this weak brother, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge.
chapters.zh: 因此，基督为他死的那软弱弟兄，也就因你的知识沉沦了。

chapters.en: By sinning against your brothers in this way and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
chapters.zh: 你们这样得罪弟兄们，伤了他们软弱的良心，就是得罪基督。

chapters.en: Therefore, if what I eat causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again, so that I will not cause him to stumble.
chapters.zh: 所以，食物若叫我弟兄跌倒，我就永远不吃肉，免得叫我弟兄跌倒了。

chapters.en: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you yourselves not my workmanship in the Lord?
chapters.zh: 我不是自由的吗？我不是使徒吗？我不是见过我们的主耶稣吗？你们不是我在主里面所做之工吗？

chapters.en: Even if I am not an apostle to others, surely I am to you. For you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
chapters.zh: 假若在别人，我不是使徒，在你们，我总是使徒，因为你们在主里正是我作使徒的印证。

chapters.en: This is my defense to those who scrutinize me:
chapters.zh: 我对那盘问我的人就是这样分诉：

chapters.en: Have we no right to food and to drink?
chapters.zh: 难道我们没有权柄〔靠福音〕吃喝吗？

chapters.en: Have we no right to take along a believing wife, as do the other apostles and the Lord’s brothers and Cephas?
chapters.zh: 难道我们没有权柄娶〔信主的〕姊妹为妻，带着一同往来，仿佛其余的使徒和主的弟兄并矶法一样吗？

chapters.en: Or are Barnabas and I the only apostles who must work for a living?
chapters.zh: 独有我与巴拿巴没有权柄不做工吗？

chapters.en: Who serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not drink of its milk?
chapters.zh: 有谁当兵自备粮饷呢？有谁栽葡萄园不吃园里的果子呢？有谁牧养牛羊不吃牛羊的奶呢？

chapters.en: Do I say this from a human perspective? Doesn’t the Law say the same thing?
chapters.zh: 我说这话，岂是照人的意见；律法不也是这样说吗？

chapters.en: For it is written in the Law of Moses: “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.” Is it about oxen that God is concerned?
chapters.zh: 就如摩西的律法记着说：「牛〔在场上〕踹谷的时候，不可笼住牠的嘴。」难道上帝所挂念的是牛吗？

chapters.en: Isn’t He actually speaking on our behalf? Indeed, this was written for us, because when the plowman plows and the thresher threshes, they should also expect to share in the harvest.
chapters.zh: 不全是为我们说的吗？分明是为我们说的。因为耕种的当存着指望去耕种；打场的也当存得〔粮〕的指望去打场。

chapters.en: If we have sown spiritual seed among you, is it too much for us to reap a material harvest from you?
chapters.zh: 我们若把属灵的种子撒在你们中间，就是从你们收割奉养肉身之物，这还算大事吗？

chapters.en: If others have this right to your support, shouldn’t we have it all the more? But we did not exercise this right. Instead, we put up with anything rather than hinder the gospel of Christ.
chapters.zh: 若别人在你们身上有这权柄，何况我们呢？ 然而，我们没有用过这权柄，倒凡事忍受，免得基督的福音被阻隔。

chapters.en: Do you not know that those who work in the temple eat of its food, and those who serve at the altar partake of its offerings?
chapters.zh: 你们岂不知为圣事劳碌的就吃殿中的物吗？伺候祭坛的就分领坛上的物吗？

chapters.en: In the same way, the Lord has prescribed that those who preach the gospel should receive their living from the gospel.
chapters.zh: 主也是这样命定，叫传福音的靠着福音养生。

chapters.en: But I have not used any of these rights. And I am not writing this to suggest that something be done for me. Indeed, I would rather die than let anyone nullify my boast.
chapters.zh: 但这权柄我全没有用过。我写这话，并非要你们这样待我，因为我宁可死也不叫人使我所夸的落了空。

chapters.en: Yet when I preach the gospel, I have no reason to boast, because I am obligated to preach. Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel!
chapters.zh: 我传福音原没有可夸的，因为我是不得已的。若不传福音，我便有祸了。

chapters.en: If my preaching is voluntary, I have a reward. But if it is not voluntary, I am still entrusted with a responsibility.
chapters.zh: 我若甘心做这事，就有赏赐；若不甘心，责任却已经托付我了。

chapters.en: What then is my reward? That in preaching the gospel I may offer it free of charge, and so not use up my rights in preaching it.
chapters.zh: 既是这样，我的赏赐是什么呢？就是我传福音的时候叫人不花钱得福音，免得用尽我传福音的权柄。

chapters.en: Though I am free of obligation to anyone, I make myself a slave to everyone, to win as many as possible.
chapters.zh: 我虽是自由的，无人辖管；然而我甘心作了众人的仆人，为要多得人。

chapters.en: To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win the Jews. To those under the law I became like one under the law (though I myself am not under the law), to win those under the law.
chapters.zh: 向犹太人，我就作犹太人，为要得犹太人；向律法以下的人，我虽不在律法以下，还是作律法以下的人，为要得律法以下的人。

chapters.en: To those without the law I became like one without the law (though I am not outside the law of God but am under the law of Christ), to win those without the law.
chapters.zh: 向没有律法的人，我就作没有律法的人，为要得没有律法的人；其实我在上帝面前，不是没有律法；在基督面前，正在律法之下。

chapters.en: To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people so that by all possible means I might save some.
chapters.zh: 向软弱的人，我就作软弱的人，为要得软弱的人。向什么样的人，我就作什么样的人。无论如何，总要救些人。

chapters.en: I do all this for the sake of the gospel, so that I may share in its blessings.
chapters.zh: 凡我所行的，都是为福音的缘故，为要与人同得这福音〔的好处〕。

chapters.en: Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way as to take the prize.
chapters.zh: 岂不知在场上赛跑的都跑，但得奖赏的只有一人？你们也当这样跑，好叫你们得着奖赏。

chapters.en: Everyone who competes in the games trains with strict discipline. They do it for a crown that is perishable, but we do it for a crown that is imperishable.
chapters.zh: 凡较力争胜的，诸事都有节制，他们不过是要得能坏的冠冕；我们却是要得不能坏的冠冕。

chapters.en: Therefore I do not run aimlessly; I do not fight like I am beating the air.
chapters.zh: 所以，我奔跑不像无定向的；我斗拳不像打空气的。

chapters.en: No, I discipline my body and make it my slave, so that after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified.
chapters.zh: 我是攻克己身，叫身服我，恐怕我传〔福音〕给别人，自己反被弃绝了。

chapters.en: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our forefathers were all under the cloud, and that they all passed through the sea.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我不愿意你们不晓得，我们的祖宗从前都在云下，都从海中经过，

chapters.en: They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
chapters.zh: 都在云里、海里受洗归了摩西；

chapters.en: They all ate the same spiritual food
chapters.zh: 并且都吃了一样的灵食，

chapters.en: and drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.
chapters.zh: 也都喝了一样的灵水。所喝的，是出于随着他们的灵磐石；那磐石就是基督。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, God was not pleased with most of them, for they were struck down in the wilderness.
chapters.zh: 但他们中间多半是上帝不喜欢的人，所以在旷野倒毙。

chapters.en: These things took place as examples to keep us from craving evil things as they did.
chapters.zh: 这些事都是我们的鉴戒，叫我们不要贪恋恶事，像他们那样贪恋的；

chapters.en: Do not be idolaters, as some of them were. As it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink and got up to indulge in revelry.”
chapters.zh: 也不要拜偶像，像他们有人拜的。如〔经上〕所记：「百姓坐下吃喝，起来玩耍。」

chapters.en: We should not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did, and in one day twenty-three thousand of them died.
chapters.zh: 我们也不要行奸淫，像他们有人行的，一天就倒毙了二万三千人；

chapters.en: We should not test Christ, as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.
chapters.zh: 也不要试探主〔注：有古卷：基督〕，像他们有人试探的，就被蛇所灭。

chapters.en: And do not complain, as some of them did, and were killed by the destroying angel.
chapters.zh: 你们也不要发怨言，像他们有发怨言的，就被灭命的所灭。

chapters.en: Now these things happened to them as examples and were written down as warnings for us, on whom the fulfillment of the ages has come.
chapters.zh: 他们遭遇这些事都要作为鉴戒，并且写〔在经上〕，正是警戒我们这末世的人。

chapters.en: So the one who thinks he is standing firm should be careful not to fall.
chapters.zh: 所以，自己以为站得稳的，须要谨慎，免得跌倒。

chapters.en: No temptation has seized you except what is common to man. And God is faithful; He will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, He will also provide an escape, so that you can stand up under it.
chapters.zh: 你们所遇见的试探，无非是人所能受的。上帝是信实的，必不叫你们受试探过于所能受的；在受试探的时候，总要给你们开一条出路，叫你们能忍受得住。

chapters.en: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
chapters.zh: 我所亲爱的〔弟兄〕啊，你们要逃避拜偶像的事。

chapters.en: I speak to reasonable people; judge for yourselves what I say.
chapters.zh: 我好像对明白人说的，你们要审察我的话。

chapters.en: Is not the cup of blessing that we bless a participation in the blood of Christ? And is not the bread that we break a participation in the body of Christ?
chapters.zh: 我们所祝福的杯，岂不是同领基督的血吗？我们所擘开的饼，岂不是同领基督的身体吗？

chapters.en: Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body; for we all partake of the one loaf.
chapters.zh: 我们虽多，仍是一个饼，一个身体，因为我们都是分受这一个饼。

chapters.en: Consider the people of Israel: Are not those who eat the sacrifices fellow partakers in the altar?
chapters.zh: 你们看属肉体的以色列人，那吃祭物的岂不是在祭坛上有分吗？

chapters.en: Am I suggesting, then, that food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?
chapters.zh: 我是怎么说呢？岂是说祭偶像之物算得什么呢？或说偶像算得什么呢？

chapters.en: No, but the sacrifices of pagans are offered to demons, not to God. And I do not want you to be participants with demons.
chapters.zh: 我乃是说，外邦人所献的祭是祭鬼，不是祭上帝。我不愿意你们与鬼相交。

chapters.en: You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons too; you cannot partake in the table of the Lord and the table of demons too.
chapters.zh: 你们不能喝主的杯又喝鬼的杯，不能吃主的筵席又吃鬼的筵席。

chapters.en: Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than He?
chapters.zh: 我们可惹主的愤恨吗？我们比他还有能力吗？

chapters.en: “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is edifying.
chapters.zh: 凡事都可行，但不都有益处。凡事都可行，但不都造就人。

chapters.en: No one should seek his own good, but the good of others.
chapters.zh: 无论何人，不要求自己的益处，乃要求别人的益处。

chapters.en: Eat anything sold in the meat market without raising questions of conscience,
chapters.zh: 凡市上所卖的，你们只管吃，不要为良心的缘故问什么话，

chapters.en: for, “The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof.”
chapters.zh: 因为地和其中所充满的都属乎主。

chapters.en: If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat anything set before you without raising questions of conscience.
chapters.zh: 倘有一个不信的人请你们〔赴席〕，你们若愿意去，凡摆在你们面前的，只管吃，不要为良心的缘故问什么话。

chapters.en: But if someone tells you, “This food was offered to idols,” then do not eat it, for the sake of the one who told you and for the sake of conscience—
chapters.zh: 若有人对你们说：「这是献过祭的物」，就要为那告诉你们的人，并为良心的缘故不吃。

chapters.en: the other one’s conscience, I mean, not your own. For why should my freedom be determined by someone else’s conscience?
chapters.zh: 我说的良心不是你的，乃是他的。我这自由为什么被别人的良心论断呢？

chapters.en: If I partake in the meal with thankfulness, why am I denounced because of that for which I give thanks?
chapters.zh: 我若谢恩而吃，为什么因我谢恩的物被人毁谤呢？

chapters.en: So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们或吃或喝，无论做什么，都要为荣耀上帝而行。

chapters.en: Do not become a stumbling block, whether to Jews or Greeks or the church of God—
chapters.zh: 不拘是犹太人，是希腊人，是上帝的教会，你们都不要使他跌倒；

chapters.en: as I also try to please everyone in all I do. For I am not seeking my own good, but the good of many, that they may be saved.
chapters.zh: 就好像我凡事都叫众人喜欢，不求自己的益处，只求众人的益处，叫他们得救。

chapters.en: You are to imitate me, just as I imitate Christ.
chapters.zh: 你们该效法我，像我效法基督一样。

chapters.en: Now I commend you for remembering me in everything and for maintaining the traditions, just as I passed them on to you.
chapters.zh: 我称赞你们，因你们凡事记念我，又坚守我所传给你们的。

chapters.en: But I want you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.
chapters.zh: 我愿意你们知道，基督是各人的头；男人是女人的头；上帝是基督的头。

chapters.en: Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.
chapters.zh: 凡男人祷告或是讲道〔注：或译：说预言；下同〕，若蒙着头，就羞辱自己的头。

chapters.en: And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is just as if her head were shaved.
chapters.zh: 凡女人祷告或是讲道，若不蒙着头，就羞辱自己的头，因为这就如同剃了头发一样。

chapters.en: If a woman does not cover her head, she should have her hair cut off. And if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut or shaved off, she should cover her head.
chapters.zh: 女人若不蒙着头，就该剪了头发；女人若以剪发、剃发为羞愧，就该蒙着头。

chapters.en: A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of man.
chapters.zh: 男人本不该蒙着头，因为他是上帝的形像和荣耀；但女人是男人的荣耀。

chapters.en: For man did not come from woman, but woman from man.
chapters.zh: 起初，男人不是由女人而出，女人乃是由男人而出；

chapters.en: Neither was man created for woman, but woman for man.
chapters.zh: 并且男人不是为女人造的，女人乃是为男人造的。

chapters.en: For this reason a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.
chapters.zh: 因此，女人为天使的缘故，应当在头上有服权柄的〔记号〕。

chapters.en: In the Lord, however, woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.
chapters.zh: 然而照主的安排，女也不是无男，男也不是无女。

chapters.en: For just as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman. But everything comes from God.
chapters.zh: 因为女人原是由男人而出，男人也是由女人而出；但万有都是出乎上帝。

chapters.en: Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
chapters.zh: 你们自己审察，女人祷告上帝，不蒙着头是合宜的吗？

chapters.en: Doesn’t nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him,
chapters.zh: 你们的本性不也指示你们，男人若有长头发，便是他的羞辱吗？

chapters.en: but that if a woman has long hair, it is her glory? For long hair is given to her as a covering.
chapters.zh: 但女人有长头发，乃是她的荣耀，因为这头发是给她作盖头的。

chapters.en: If anyone is inclined to dispute this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God.
chapters.zh: 若有人想要辩驳，我们却没有这样的规矩，上帝的众教会也是没有的。

chapters.en: In the following instructions I have no praise to offer, because your gatherings do more harm than good.
chapters.zh: 我现今吩咐你们的话，不是称赞你们；因为你们聚会不是受益，乃是招损。

chapters.en: First of all, I hear that when you come together as a church, there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it.
chapters.zh: 第一，我听说，你们聚会的时候彼此分门别类，我也稍微地信这话。

chapters.en: And indeed, there must be differences among you to show which of you are approved.
chapters.zh: 在你们中间不免有分门结党的事，好叫那些有经验的人显明出来。

chapters.en: Now then, when you come together, it is not the Lord’s Supper you eat.
chapters.zh: 你们聚会的时候，算不得吃主的晚餐；

chapters.en: For as you eat, each of you goes ahead without sharing his meal. While one remains hungry, another gets drunk.
chapters.zh: 因为吃的时候，各人先吃自己的饭，甚至这个饥饿，那个酒醉。

chapters.en: Don’t you have your own homes in which to eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? What can I say to you? Shall I praise you for this? No, I will not!
chapters.zh: 你们要吃喝，难道没有家吗？还是藐视上帝的教会，叫那没有的羞愧呢？我向你们可怎么说呢？可因此称赞你们吗？我不称赞！

chapters.en: For I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you: The Lord Jesus, on the night He was betrayed, took bread,
chapters.zh: 我当日传给你们的，原是从主领受的，就是主耶稣被卖的那一夜，拿起饼来，

chapters.en: and when He had given thanks, He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
chapters.zh: 祝谢了，就擘开，说：「这是我的身体，为你们舍〔注：有古卷：擘开〕的，你们应当如此行，为的是记念我。」

chapters.en: In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.”
chapters.zh: 饭后，也照样拿起杯来，说：「这杯是用我的血所立的新约，你们每逢喝的时候，要如此行，为的是记念我。」

chapters.en: For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.
chapters.zh: 你们每逢吃这饼，喝这杯，是表明主的死，直等到他来。

chapters.en: Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.
chapters.zh: 所以，无论何人，不按理吃主的饼，喝主的杯，就是干犯主的身、主的血了。

chapters.en: Each one must examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup.
chapters.zh: 人应当自己省察，然后吃这饼、喝这杯。

chapters.en: For anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the body eats and drinks judgment on himself.
chapters.zh: 因为人吃喝，若不分辨是〔主的〕身体，就是吃喝自己的罪了。

chapters.en: That is why many among you are weak and sick, and a number of you have fallen asleep.
chapters.zh: 因此，在你们中间有好些软弱的与患病的，死〔注：原文是睡〕的也不少。

chapters.en: Now if we judged ourselves properly, we would not come under judgment.
chapters.zh: 我们若是先分辨自己，就不至于受审。

chapters.en: But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined so that we will not be condemned with the world.
chapters.zh: 我们受审的时候，乃是被主惩治，免得我们和世人一同定罪。

chapters.en: So, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
chapters.zh: 所以我弟兄们，你们聚会吃的时候，要彼此等待。

chapters.en: If anyone is hungry, he should eat at home, so that when you come together it will not result in judgment. And when I come, I will give instructions about the remaining matters.
chapters.zh: 若有人饥饿，可以在家里先吃，免得你们聚会，自己取罪。其余的事，我来的时候再安排。

chapters.en: Now about spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be uninformed.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，论到属灵的〔恩赐〕，我不愿意你们不明白。

chapters.en: You know that when you were pagans, you were influenced and led astray to mute idols.
chapters.zh: 你们作外邦人的时候，随事被牵引，受迷惑，去服事那哑巴偶像，这是你们知道的。

chapters.en: Therefore I inform you that no one who is speaking by the Spirit of God says, “Jesus be cursed,” and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.
chapters.zh: 所以我告诉你们，被上帝的灵感动的，没有说「耶稣是可咒诅」的；若不是被〔圣〕灵感动的，也没有能说「耶稣是主」的。

chapters.en: There are different gifts, but the same Spirit.
chapters.zh: 恩赐原有分别，〔圣〕灵却是一位。

chapters.en: There are different ministries, but the same Lord.
chapters.zh: 职事也有分别，主却是一位。

chapters.en: There are different ways of working, but the same God works all things in all people.
chapters.zh: 功用也有分别，上帝却是一位，在众人里面运行一切的事。

chapters.en: Now to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.
chapters.zh: 〔圣〕灵显在各人身上，是叫人得益处。

chapters.en: To one there is given through the Spirit the message of wisdom, to another the message of knowledge by the same Spirit,
chapters.zh: 这人蒙〔圣〕灵赐他智慧的言语，那人也蒙这位〔圣〕灵赐他知识的言语，

chapters.en: to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by that one Spirit,
chapters.zh: 又有一人蒙这位〔圣〕灵赐他信心，还有一人蒙这位〔圣〕灵赐他医病的恩赐，

chapters.en: to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing between spirits, to another speaking in various tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues.
chapters.zh: 又叫一人能行异能，又叫一人能作先知，又叫一人能辨别诸灵，又叫一人能说方言，又叫一人能翻方言。

chapters.en: All these are the work of one and the same Spirit, who apportions them to each one as He determines.
chapters.zh: 这一切都是这位〔圣〕灵所运行、随己意分给各人的。

chapters.en: The body is a unit, though it is composed of many parts. And although its parts are many, they all form one body. So it is with Christ.
chapters.zh: 就如身子是一个，却有许多肢体；而且肢体虽多，仍是一个身子；基督也是这样。

chapters.en: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, slave or free, and we were all given one Spirit to drink.
chapters.zh: 我们不拘是犹太人，是希腊人，是为奴的，是自主的，都从一位〔圣〕灵受洗，成了一个身体，饮于一位〔圣〕灵。

chapters.en: For the body does not consist of one part, but of many.
chapters.zh: 身子原不是一个肢体，乃是许多肢体。

chapters.en: If the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.
chapters.zh: 设若脚说：「我不是手，所以不属乎身子，」它不能因此就不属乎身子。

chapters.en: And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.
chapters.zh: 设若耳说：「我不是眼，所以不属乎身子，」它也不能因此就不属乎身子。

chapters.en: If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be?
chapters.zh: 若全身是眼，从哪里听声呢？若全身是耳，从哪里闻味呢？

chapters.en: But in fact, God has arranged the members of the body, every one of them, according to His design.
chapters.zh: 但如今，上帝随自己的意思把肢体俱各安排在身上了。

chapters.en: If they were all one part, where would the body be?
chapters.zh: 若都是一个肢体，身子在哪里呢？

chapters.en: As it is, there are many parts, but one body.
chapters.zh: 但如今肢体是多的，身子却是一个。

chapters.en: The eye cannot say to the hand, “I do not need you.” Nor can the head say to the feet, “I do not need you.”
chapters.zh: 眼不能对手说：「我用不着你。」头也不能对脚说：「我用不着你。」

chapters.en: On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,
chapters.zh: 不但如此，身上肢体人以为软弱的，更是不可少的。

chapters.en: and the parts we consider less honorable, we treat with greater honor. And our unpresentable parts are treated with special modesty,
chapters.zh: 身上肢体，我们看为不体面的，越发给它加上体面；不俊美的，越发得着俊美。

chapters.en:
whereas our presentable parts have no such need.
But God has composed the body and has given greater honor to the parts that lacked it,
chapters.zh: 我们俊美的肢体，自然用不着装饰；但上帝配搭这身子，把加倍的体面给那有缺欠的肢体，

chapters.en: so that there should be no division in the body, but that its members should have mutual concern for one another.
chapters.zh: 免得身上分门别类，总要肢体彼此相顾。

chapters.en: If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it.
chapters.zh: 若一个肢体受苦，所有的肢体就一同受苦；若一个肢体得荣耀，所有的肢体就一同快乐。

chapters.en: Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it.
chapters.zh: 你们就是基督的身子，并且各自作肢体。

chapters.en: And in the church God has appointed first of all apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then workers of miracles, and those with gifts of healing, helping, administration, and various tongues.
chapters.zh: 上帝在教会所设立的：第一是使徒，第二是先知，第三是教师，其次是行异能的，再次是得恩赐医病的，帮助人的，治理事的，说方言的。

chapters.en: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?
chapters.zh: 岂都是使徒吗？岂都是先知吗？岂都是教师吗？岂都是行异能的吗？

chapters.en: Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
chapters.zh: 岂都是得恩赐医病的吗？岂都是说方言的吗？岂都是翻方言的吗？

chapters.en:
But eagerly desire the greater gifts.
And now I will show you the most excellent way.
chapters.zh: 你们要切切地求那更大的恩赐。 我现今把最妙的道指示你们。

chapters.en: If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.
chapters.zh: 我若能说万人的方言，并天使的话语，却没有爱，我就成了鸣的锣，响的钹一般。

chapters.en: If I have the gift of prophecy and can fathom all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.
chapters.zh: 我若有先知讲道〔之能〕，也明白各样的奥祕，各样的知识，而且有全备的信，叫我能够移山，却没有爱，我就算不得什么。

chapters.en: If I give all I possess to the poor and exult in the surrender of my body, but have not love, I gain nothing.
chapters.zh: 我若将所有的赒济〔穷人〕，又舍己身叫人焚烧，却没有爱，仍然与我无益。

chapters.en: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.
chapters.zh: 爱是恒久忍耐，又有恩慈；爱是不嫉妒；爱是不自夸，不张狂，

chapters.en: It is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no account of wrongs.
chapters.zh: 不做害羞的事，不求自己的益处，不轻易发怒，不计算〔人的〕恶，

chapters.en: Love takes no pleasure in evil, but rejoices in the truth.
chapters.zh: 不喜欢不义，只喜欢真理；

chapters.en: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
chapters.zh: 凡事包容，凡事相信，凡事盼望，凡事忍耐。

chapters.en: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be restrained; where there is knowledge, it will be dismissed.
chapters.zh: 爱是永不止息。先知讲道之能终必归于无有；说方言之能终必停止；知识也终必归于无有。

chapters.en: For we know in part and we prophesy in part,
chapters.zh: 我们现在所知道的有限，先知所讲的也有限，

chapters.en: but when the perfect comes, the partial passes away.
chapters.zh: 等那完全的来到，这有限的必归于无有了。

chapters.en: When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.
chapters.zh: 我作孩子的时候，话语像孩子，心思像孩子，意念像孩子，既成了人，就把孩子的事丢弃了。

chapters.en: Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face. Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known.
chapters.zh: 我们如今仿佛对着镜子观看，模糊不清〔注：原文是如同猜谜〕，到那时就要面对面了。我如今所知道的有限，到那时就全知道，如同主知道我一样。

chapters.en: And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love.
chapters.zh: 如今常存的有信，有望，有爱这三样，其中最大的是爱。

chapters.en: Earnestly pursue love and eagerly desire spiritual gifts, especially the gift of prophecy.
chapters.zh: 你们要追求爱，也要切慕属灵的〔恩赐〕，其中更要羨慕的，是作先知讲道〔注：原文作：是说预言；下同〕。

chapters.en: For he who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men, but to God. Indeed, no one understands him; he utters mysteries in the Spirit.
chapters.zh: 那说方言的，原不是对人说，乃是对上帝说，因为没有人听出来。然而，他在心灵里却是讲说各样的奥祕。

chapters.en: But he who prophesies speaks to men for their edification, encouragement, and comfort.
chapters.zh: 但作先知讲道的，是对人说，要造就、安慰、劝勉人。

chapters.en: The one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but the one who prophesies edifies the church.
chapters.zh: 说方言的，是造就自己；作先知讲道的，乃是造就教会。

chapters.en: I wish that all of you could speak in tongues, but I would rather have you prophesy. He who prophesies is greater than one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets so that the church may be edified.
chapters.zh: 我愿意你们都说方言，更愿意你们作先知讲道；因为说方言的，若不翻出来，使教会被造就，那作先知讲道的，就比他强了。

chapters.en: Now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I benefit you, unless I bring you some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我到你们那里去，若只说方言，不用启示，或知识，或预言，或教训，给你们讲解，我与你们有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: Even in the case of lifeless instruments, such as the flute or harp, how will anyone recognize the tune they are playing unless the notes are distinct?
chapters.zh: 就是那有声无气的物，或箫，或琴，若发出来的声音没有分别，怎能知道所吹所弹的是什么呢？

chapters.en: Again, if the trumpet sounds a muffled call, who will prepare for battle?
chapters.zh: 若吹无定的号声，谁能预备打仗呢？

chapters.en: So it is with you. Unless you speak intelligible words with your tongue, how will anyone know what you are saying? You will just be speaking into the air.
chapters.zh: 你们也是如此。舌头若不说容易明白的话，怎能知道所说的是什么呢？这就是向空说话了。

chapters.en: Assuredly, there are many different languages in the world, yet none of them is without meaning.
chapters.zh: 世上的声音，或者甚多，却没有一样是无意思的。

chapters.en: If, then, I do not know the meaning of someone’s language, I am a foreigner to the speaker, and he is a foreigner to me.
chapters.zh: 我若不明白那声音的意思，这说话的人必以我为化外之人，我也以他为化外之人。

chapters.en: It is the same with you. Since you are eager to have spiritual gifts, strive to excel in gifts that build up the church.
chapters.zh: 你们也是如此，既是切慕属灵的〔恩赐〕，就当求多得造就教会的恩赐。

chapters.en: Therefore, the one who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret.
chapters.zh: 所以那说方言的，就当求着能翻出来。

chapters.en: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.
chapters.zh: 我若用方言祷告，是我的灵祷告，但我的悟性没有果效。

chapters.en: What then shall I do? I will pray with my spirit, but I will also pray with my mind. I will sing with my spirit, but I will also sing with my mind.
chapters.zh: 这却怎么样呢？我要用灵祷告，也要用悟性祷告；我要用灵歌唱，也要用悟性歌唱。

chapters.en: Otherwise, if you speak a blessing in spirit, how can someone who is uninstructed say “Amen” to your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?
chapters.zh: 不然，你用灵祝谢，那在座不通方言的人，既然不明白你的话，怎能在你感谢的时候说「阿们」呢？

chapters.en: You may be giving thanks well enough, but the other one is not edified.
chapters.zh: 你感谢的固然是好，无奈不能造就别人。

chapters.en: I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
chapters.zh: 我感谢上帝，我说方言比你们众人还多。

chapters.en: But in the church, I would rather speak five coherent words to instruct others than ten thousand words in a tongue.
chapters.zh: 但在教会中，宁可用悟性说五句教导人的话，强如说万句方言。

chapters.en: Brothers, stop thinking like children. In regard to evil be infants, but in your thinking be mature.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，在心志上不要作小孩子。然而，在恶事上要作婴孩，在心志上总要作大人。

chapters.en:
It is written in the Law:
“By strange tongues and foreign lips I will speak to this people, but even then they will not listen to Me, says the Lord.”
chapters.zh: 律法上记着： 主说：我要用外邦人的舌头 和外邦人的嘴唇向这百姓说话； 虽然如此， 他们还是不听从我。

chapters.en: Tongues, then, are a sign, not for believers, but for unbelievers. Prophecy, however, is for believers, not for unbelievers.
chapters.zh: 这样看来，说方言不是为信的人作证据，乃是为不信的人；作先知讲道不是为不信的人〔作证据〕，乃是为信的人。

chapters.en: So if the whole church comes together and everyone speaks in tongues, and some who are uninstructed or some unbelievers come in, will they not say that you are out of your minds?
chapters.zh: 所以，全教会聚在一处的时候，若都说方言，偶然有不通方言的，或是不信的人进来，岂不说你们癫狂了吗？

chapters.en: But if an unbeliever or uninstructed person comes in while everyone is prophesying, he will be convicted and called to account by all,
chapters.zh: 若都作先知讲道，偶然有不信的，或是不通方言的人进来，就被众人劝醒，被众人审明，

chapters.en: and the secrets of his heart will be made known. So he will fall facedown and worship God, proclaiming, “God is truly among you!”
chapters.zh: 他心里的隐情显露出来，就必将脸伏地，敬拜上帝，说：「上帝真是在你们中间了。」

chapters.en: What then shall we say, brothers? When you come together, everyone has a psalm or a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. All of these must be done to build up the church.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，这却怎么样呢？你们聚会的时候，各人或有诗歌，或有教训，或有启示，或有方言，或有翻出来的话，凡事都当造就人。

chapters.en: If anyone speaks in a tongue, two, or at most three, should speak in turn, and someone must interpret.
chapters.zh: 若有说方言的，只好两个人，至多三个人，且要轮流着说，也要一个人翻出来。

chapters.en: But if there is no interpreter, he should remain silent in the church and speak only to himself and God.
chapters.zh: 若没有人翻，就当在会中闭口，只对自己和上帝说就是了。

chapters.en: Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should weigh carefully what is said.
chapters.zh: 至于作先知讲道的，只好两个人或是三个人，其余的就当〔慎思〕明辨。

chapters.en: And if a revelation comes to someone who is seated, the first speaker should stop.
chapters.zh: 若旁边坐着的得了启示，那先说话的就当闭口不言。

chapters.en: For you can all prophesy in turn so that everyone may be instructed and encouraged.
chapters.zh: 因为你们都可以一个一个地作先知讲道，叫众人学道理，叫众人得劝勉。

chapters.en: The spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.
chapters.zh: 先知的灵原是顺服先知的；

chapters.en: For God is not a God of disorder, but of peace—as in all the churches of the saints.
chapters.zh: 因为上帝不是叫人混乱，乃是叫人安静。

chapters.en: Women are to be silent in the churches. They are not permitted to speak, but must be in submission, as the law says.
chapters.zh: 妇女在会中要闭口不言，像在圣徒的众教会一样，因为不准她们说话。她们总要顺服，正如律法所说的。

chapters.en: If they wish to inquire about something, they are to ask their own husbands at home; for it is dishonorable for a woman to speak in the church.
chapters.zh: 她们若要学什么，可以在家里问自己的丈夫，因为妇女在会中说话原是可耻的。

chapters.en: Did the word of God originate with you? Or are you the only ones it has reached?
chapters.zh: 上帝的道理岂是从你们出来吗？岂是单临到你们吗？

chapters.en: If anyone considers himself a prophet or spiritual person, let him acknowledge that what I am writing you is the Lord’s command.
chapters.zh: 若有人以为自己是先知，或是属灵的，就该知道，我所写给你们的是主的命令。

chapters.en: But if anyone ignores this, he himself will be ignored.
chapters.zh: 若有不知道的，就由他不知道吧！

chapters.en: So, my brothers, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
chapters.zh: 所以我弟兄们，你们要切慕作先知讲道，也不要禁止说方言。

chapters.en: But everything must be done in a proper and orderly manner.
chapters.zh: 凡事都要规规矩矩地按着次序行。

chapters.en: Now, brothers, I want to remind you of the gospel I preached to you, which you received, and in which you stand firm.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我如今把先前所传给你们的福音告诉你们知道；这福音你们也领受了，又靠着站立得住，

chapters.en: By this gospel you are saved, if you hold firmly to the word I preached to you. Otherwise, you have believed in vain.
chapters.zh: 并且你们若不是徒然相信，能以持守我所传给你们的，就必因这福音得救。

chapters.en: For what I received I passed on to you as of first importance: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
chapters.zh: 我当日所领受又传给你们的：第一，就是基督照圣经所说，为我们的罪死了，

chapters.en: that He was buried, that He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
chapters.zh: 而且埋葬了；又照圣经所说，第三天复活了，

chapters.en: and that He appeared to Cephas and then to the Twelve.
chapters.zh: 并且显给矶法看，然后显给十二使徒看；

chapters.en: After that, He appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once, most of whom are still living, though some have fallen asleep.
chapters.zh: 后来一时显给五百多弟兄看，其中一大半到如今还在，却也有已经睡了的。

chapters.en: Then He appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
chapters.zh: 以后显给雅各看，再显给众使徒看，

chapters.en: And last of all He appeared to me also, as to one of untimely birth.
chapters.zh: 末了也显给我看；我如同未到产期而生的人一般。

chapters.en: For I am the least of the apostles and am unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
chapters.zh: 我原是使徒中最小的，不配称为使徒，因为我从前逼迫上帝的教会。

chapters.en: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and His grace to me was not in vain. No, I worked harder than all of them—yet not I, but the grace of God that was with me.
chapters.zh: 然而，我今日成了何等人，是蒙上帝的恩才成的，并且他所赐我的恩不是徒然的。我比众使徒格外劳苦；这原不是我，乃是上帝的恩与我同在。

chapters.en: Whether, then, it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.
chapters.zh: 不拘是我，是众使徒，我们如此传，你们也如此信了。

chapters.en: But if it is preached that Christ has been raised from the dead, how can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
chapters.zh: 既传基督是从死里复活了，怎么在你们中间有人说没有死人复活的事呢？

chapters.en: If there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised.
chapters.zh: 若没有死人复活的事，基督也就没有复活了。

chapters.en: And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is worthless, and so is your faith.
chapters.zh: 若基督没有复活，我们所传的便是枉然，你们所信的也是枉然；

chapters.en: In that case, we are also exposed as false witnesses about God. For we have testified about God that He raised Christ from the dead, but He did not raise Him if in fact the dead are not raised.
chapters.zh: 并且明显我们是为上帝妄作见证的，因我们见证上帝是叫基督复活了。若死人真不复活，上帝也就没有叫基督复活了。

chapters.en: For if the dead are not raised, then not even Christ has been raised.
chapters.zh: 因为死人若不复活，基督也就没有复活了。

chapters.en: And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.
chapters.zh: 基督若没有复活，你们的信便是徒然，你们仍在罪里。

chapters.en: Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
chapters.zh: 就是在基督里睡了的人也灭亡了。

chapters.en: If our hope in Christ is for this life alone, we are to be pitied more than all men.
chapters.zh: 我们若靠基督只在今生有指望，就算比众人更可怜。

chapters.en: But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
chapters.zh: 但基督已经从死里复活，成为睡了之人初熟的果子。

chapters.en: For since death came through a man, the resurrection of the dead comes also through a man.
chapters.zh: 死既是因一人而来，死人复活也是因一人而来。

chapters.en: For as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive.
chapters.zh: 在亚当里众人都死了；照样，在基督里众人也都要复活。

chapters.en: But each in his own turn: Christ the firstfruits; then at His coming, those who belong to Him.
chapters.zh: 但各人是按着自己的次序复活：初熟的果子是基督；以后，在他来的时候，是那些属基督的。

chapters.en: Then the end will come, when He hands over the kingdom to God the Father after He has destroyed all dominion, authority, and power.
chapters.zh: 再后，末期到了，那时基督既将一切执政的、掌权的、有能的都毁灭了，就把国交与父上帝。

chapters.en: For He must reign until He has put all His enemies under His feet.
chapters.zh: 因为基督必要作王，等上帝把一切仇敌都放在他的脚下。

chapters.en: The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
chapters.zh: 尽末了所毁灭的仇敌就是死。

chapters.en: For “God has put everything under His feet.” Now when it says that everything has been put under Him, this clearly does not include the One who put everything under Him.
chapters.zh: 因为〔经上〕说：「上帝叫万物都服在他的脚下。」既说万物都服了他，明显那叫万物服他的，不在其内了。

chapters.en: And when all things have been subjected to Him, then the Son Himself will be made subject to Him who put all things under Him, so that God may be all in all.
chapters.zh: 万物既服了他，那时子也要自己服那叫万物服他的，叫上帝在万物之上，为万物之主。

chapters.en: If these things are not so, what will those do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptized for them?
chapters.zh: 不然，那些为死人受洗的，将来怎样呢？若死人总不复活，因何为他们受洗呢？

chapters.en: And why do we endanger ourselves every hour?
chapters.zh: 我们又因何时刻冒险呢？

chapters.en: I face death every day, brothers, as surely as I boast about you in Christ Jesus our Lord.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我在我主基督耶稣里，指着你们所夸的口极力地说，我是天天〔冒〕死。

chapters.en:
If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus for human motives, what did I gain? If the dead are not raised,
“Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
chapters.zh: 我若当日像寻常人，在以弗所同野兽战斗，那于我有什么益处呢？若死人不复活， 我们就吃吃喝喝吧！ 因为明天要死了。

chapters.en: Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good character.”
chapters.zh: 你们不要自欺；滥交是败坏善行。

chapters.en: Sober up as you ought, and stop sinning; for some of you are ignorant of God. I say this to your shame.
chapters.zh: 你们要醒悟为善，不要犯罪，因为有人不认识上帝。我说这话是要叫你们羞愧。

chapters.en: But someone will ask, “How are the dead raised? With what kind of body will they come?”
chapters.zh: 或有人问：「死人怎样复活，带着什么身体来呢？」

chapters.en: You fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
chapters.zh: 无知的人哪，你所种的，若不死就不能生。

chapters.en: And what you sow is not the body that will be, but just a seed, perhaps of wheat or something else.
chapters.zh: 并且你所种的不是那将来的形体，不过是子粒，即如麦子，或是别样的谷。

chapters.en: But God gives it a body as He has designed, and to each kind of seed He gives its own body.
chapters.zh: 但上帝随自己的意思给他一个形体，并叫各等子粒各有自己的形体。

chapters.en: Not all flesh is the same: Men have one kind of flesh, animals have another, birds another, and fish another.
chapters.zh: 凡肉体各有不同：人是一样，兽又是一样，鸟又是一样，鱼又是一样。

chapters.en: There are also heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. But the splendor of the heavenly bodies is of one degree, and the splendor of the earthly bodies is of another.
chapters.zh: 有天上的形体，也有地上的形体；但天上形体的荣光是一样，地上形体的荣光又是一样。

chapters.en: The sun has one degree of splendor, the moon another, and the stars another; and star differs from star in splendor.
chapters.zh: 日有日的荣光，月有月的荣光，星有星的荣光；这星和那星的荣光也有分别。

chapters.en: So will it be with the resurrection of the dead: What is sown is perishable; it is raised imperishable.
chapters.zh: 死人复活也是这样：所种的是必朽坏的，复活的是不朽坏的；

chapters.en: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
chapters.zh: 所种的是羞辱的，复活的是荣耀的；所种的是软弱的，复活的是强壮的；

chapters.en: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
chapters.zh: 所种的是血气的身体，复活的是灵性的身体。若有血气的身体，也必有灵性的身体。

chapters.en: So it is written: “The first man Adam became a living being”; the last Adam a life-giving spirit.
chapters.zh: 〔经上〕也是这样记着说：「首先的人亚当成了有灵〔注：灵：或译血气〕的活人」；末后的亚当成了叫人活的灵。

chapters.en: The spiritual, however, was not first, but the natural, and then the spiritual.
chapters.zh: 但属灵的不在先，属血气的在先，以后才有属灵的。

chapters.en: The first man was of the dust of the earth, the second man from heaven.
chapters.zh: 头一个人是出于地，乃属土；第二个人是出于天。

chapters.en: As was the earthly man, so also are those who are of the earth; and as is the heavenly man, so also are those who are of heaven.
chapters.zh: 那属土的怎样，凡属土的也就怎样；属天的怎样，凡属天的也就怎样。

chapters.en: And just as we have borne the likeness of the earthly man, so also shall we bear the likeness of the heavenly man.
chapters.zh: 我们既有属土的形状，将来也必有属天的形状。

chapters.en: Now I declare to you, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我告诉你们说，血肉〔之体〕不能承受上帝的国，必朽坏的不能承受不朽坏的。

chapters.en: Listen, I tell you a mystery: We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed—
chapters.zh: 我如今把一件奥祕的事告诉你们：我们不是都要睡觉，乃是都要改变，

chapters.en: in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
chapters.zh: 就在一霎时，眨眼之间，号筒末次吹响的时候。因号筒要响，死人要复活成为不朽坏的，我们也要改变。

chapters.en: For the perishable must be clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with immortality.
chapters.zh: 这必朽坏的总要变成〔注：变成：原文是穿；下同〕不朽坏的，这必死的总要变成不死的。

chapters.en: When the perishable has been clothed with the imperishable and the mortal with immortality, then the saying that is written will come to pass: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
chapters.zh: 这必朽坏的既变成不朽坏的，这必死的既变成不死的，那时〔经上〕所记「死被得胜吞灭」的话就应验了。

chapters.en: “Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?”
chapters.zh: 死啊！你得胜的权势在哪里？ 死啊！你的毒钩在哪里？

chapters.en: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
chapters.zh: 死的毒钩就是罪，罪的权势就是律法。

chapters.en: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!
chapters.zh: 感谢上帝，使我们藉着我们的主耶稣基督得胜。

chapters.en: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast and immovable. Always excel in the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.
chapters.zh: 所以，我亲爱的弟兄们，你们务要坚固，不可摇动，常常竭力多做主工；因为知道，你们的劳苦在主里面不是徒然的。

chapters.en: Now about the collection for the saints, you are to do as I directed the churches of Galatia:
chapters.zh: 论到为圣徒捐钱，我从前怎样吩咐加拉太的众教会，你们也当怎样行。

chapters.en: On the first day of every week, each of you should set aside a portion of his income, saving it up, so that when I come no collections will be needed.
chapters.zh: 每逢七日的第一日，各人要照自己的进项抽出来留着，免得我来的时候现凑。

chapters.en: Then, on my arrival, I will send letters with those you recommend to carry your gift to Jerusalem.
chapters.zh: 及至我来到了，你们写信举荐谁，我就打发他们，把你们的捐资送到耶路撒冷去。

chapters.en: And if it is advisable for me to go also, they can travel with me.
chapters.zh: 若我也该去，他们可以和我同去。

chapters.en: After I go through Macedonia, however, I will come to you; for I will be going through Macedonia.
chapters.zh: 我要从马其顿经过；既经过了，就要到你们那里去，

chapters.en: Perhaps I will stay with you awhile, or even spend the winter, so that you can help me on my journey, wherever I go.
chapters.zh: 或者和你们同住几时，或者也过冬。无论我往哪里去，你们就可以给我送行。

chapters.en: For I do not want to see you now only in passing; I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permits.
chapters.zh: 我如今不愿意路过见你们；主若许我，我就指望和你们同住几时。

chapters.en: But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost,
chapters.zh: 但我要仍旧住在以弗所，直等到五旬节；

chapters.en: because a great door for effective work has opened to me, even though many oppose me.
chapters.zh: 因为有宽大又有功效的门为我开了，并且反对的人也多。

chapters.en: If Timothy comes, see to it that he has nothing to fear while he is with you, for he is doing the work of the Lord, just as I am.
chapters.zh: 若是提摩太来到，你们要留心，叫他在你们那里无所惧怕；因为他劳力做主的工，像我一样。

chapters.en: No one, then, should treat him with contempt. Send him on his way in peace so that he can return to me, for I am expecting him along with the brothers.
chapters.zh: 所以，无论谁都不可藐视他，只要送他平安前行，叫他到我这里来，因我指望他和弟兄们同来。

chapters.en: Now about our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to go to you with the brothers. He was not at all inclined to go now, but he will go when he has the opportunity.
chapters.zh: 至于兄弟亚波罗，我再三地劝他同弟兄们到你们那里去；但这时他决不愿意去，几时有了机会他必去。

chapters.en: Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong.
chapters.zh: 你们务要警醒，在真道上站立得稳，要作大丈夫，要刚强。

chapters.en: Do everything in love.
chapters.zh: 凡你们所做的都要凭爱心而做。

chapters.en: You know that Stephanas and his household were the first converts in Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the service of the saints. Now I urge you, brothers,
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，你们晓得司提法那一家，是亚该亚初结的果子，并且他们专以服事圣徒为念。

chapters.en: to submit to such as these, and to every fellow worker and laborer.
chapters.zh: 我劝你们顺服这样的人，并一切同工同劳的人。

chapters.en: I am glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus have arrived, because they have supplied what was lacking from you.
chapters.zh: 司提法那和福徒拿都，并亚该古到这里来，我很喜欢；因为你们待我有不及之处，他们补上了。

chapters.en: For they refreshed my spirit and yours as well. Show your appreciation, therefore, to such men.
chapters.zh: 他们叫我和你们心里都快活。这样的人，你们务要敬重。

chapters.en:
The churches in the province of Asia send you greetings.
Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, and so does the church that meets at their house.
chapters.zh: 亚细亚的众教会问你们安。亚居拉和百基拉并在他们家里的教会，因主多多地问你们安。

chapters.en: All the brothers here send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
chapters.zh: 众弟兄都问你们安。你们要亲嘴问安，彼此务要圣洁。

chapters.en: This greeting is in my own hand—Paul.
chapters.zh: 我－保罗亲笔问安。

chapters.en: If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be under a curse. Come, O Lord!
chapters.zh: 若有人不爱主，这人可诅可咒。主必要来！

chapters.en: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
chapters.zh: 愿主耶稣基督的恩〔常〕与你们众人同在！

chapters.en:
My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus.
Amen.
chapters.zh: 我在基督耶稣里的爱与你们众人同在。阿们！

chapters.en:
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother,
To the church of God in Corinth, together with all the saints throughout Achaia:
chapters.zh: 奉上帝旨意作基督耶稣使徒的保罗和兄弟提摩太，写信给在哥林多上帝的教会，并亚该亚遍处的众圣徒。

chapters.en: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 愿恩惠、平安从上帝我们的父和主耶稣基督归与你们！

chapters.en: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort,
chapters.zh: 愿颂赞归与我们的主耶稣基督的父上帝，就是发慈悲的父，赐各样安慰的上帝。

chapters.en: who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God.
chapters.zh: 我们在一切患难中，他就安慰我们，叫我们能用上帝所赐的安慰去安慰那遭各样患难的人。
