chapters.en: For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so also through Christ our comfort overflows.
chapters.zh: 我们既多受基督的苦楚，就靠基督多得安慰。

chapters.en: If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which accomplishes in you patient endurance of the same sufferings we experience.
chapters.zh: 我们受患难呢，是为叫你们得安慰，得拯救；我们得安慰呢，也是为叫你们得安慰；这安慰能叫你们忍受我们所受的那样苦楚。

chapters.en: And our hope for you is sure, because we know that just as you share in our sufferings, so also you will share in our comfort.
chapters.zh: 我们为你们所存的盼望是确定的，因为知道你们既是同受苦楚，也必同得安慰。

chapters.en: We do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the hardships we encountered in the province of Asia. We were under a burden far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired even of life.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我们不要你们不晓得，我们从前在亚细亚遭遇苦难，被压太重，力不能胜，甚至连活命的指望都绝了；

chapters.en: Indeed, we felt we were under the sentence of death, in order that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead.
chapters.zh: 自己心里也断定是必死的，叫我们不靠自己，只靠叫死人复活的上帝。

chapters.en: He has delivered us from such a deadly peril, and He will deliver us. In Him we have placed our hope that He will yet again deliver us,
chapters.zh: 他曾救我们脱离那极大的死亡，现在仍要救我们，并且我们指望他将来还要救我们。

chapters.en: as you help us by your prayers. Then many will give thanks on our behalf for the favor shown us in answer to their prayers.
chapters.zh: 你们以祈祷帮助我们，好叫许多人为我们谢恩，就是为我们因许多人所得的恩。

chapters.en: For this is our boast: Our conscience testifies that we have conducted ourselves in the world, and especially in relation to you, in the holiness and sincerity that are from God—not in worldly wisdom, but in the grace of God.
chapters.zh: 我们所夸的是自己的良心，见证我们凭着上帝的圣洁和诚实；在世为人不靠人的聪明，乃靠上帝的恩惠，向你们更是这样。

chapters.en: For we do not write you anything that is beyond your ability to read and understand. And I hope that you will understand us completely,
chapters.zh: 我们现在写给你们的话，并不外乎你们所念的、所认识的，我也盼望你们到底还是要认识；

chapters.en: as you have already understood us in part, that you may boast of us just as we will boast of you in the day of our Lord Jesus.
chapters.zh: 正如你们已经有几分认识我们，以我们夸口，好像我们在我们主耶稣的日子以你们夸口一样。

chapters.en: Confident of this, I planned to visit you first, so that you might receive a double blessing.
chapters.zh: 我既然这样深信，就早有意到你们那里去，叫你们再得益处；

chapters.en: I wanted to visit you on my way to Macedonia, and to return to you from Macedonia, and then to have you help me on my way to Judea.
chapters.zh: 也要从你们那里经过，往马其顿去，再从马其顿回到你们那里，叫你们给我送行往犹太去。

chapters.en: When I planned this, did I do it carelessly? Or do I make my plans by human standards, so as to say “Yes, yes” and also “No, no”?
chapters.zh: 我有此意，岂是反覆不定吗？我所起的意，岂是从情欲起的，叫我忽是忽非吗？

chapters.en: But as surely as God is faithful, our message to you is not “Yes” and “No.”
chapters.zh: 我指着信实的上帝说，我们向你们所传的道，并没有是而又非的。

chapters.en: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was proclaimed among you by me and Silvanus and Timothy, was not “Yes” and “No,” but in Him it has always been “Yes.”
chapters.zh: 因为我和西拉并提摩太，在你们中间所传上帝的儿子耶稣基督，总没有是而又非的，在他只有一是。

chapters.en: For all the promises of God are “Yes” in Christ. And so through Him, our “Amen” is spoken to the glory of God.
chapters.zh: 上帝的应许，不论有多少，在基督都是是的。所以藉着他也都是实在〔注：实在：原文是阿们〕的，叫上帝因我们得荣耀。

chapters.en: Now it is God who establishes both us and you in Christ. He anointed us,
chapters.zh: 那在基督里坚固我们和你们，并且膏我们的就是上帝。

chapters.en: placed His seal on us, and put His Spirit in our hearts as a pledge of what is to come.
chapters.zh: 他又用印印了我们，并赐〔圣〕灵在我们心里作凭据〔注：原文是质〕。

chapters.en: I call God as my witness that it was in order to spare you that I did not return to Corinth.
chapters.zh: 我呼吁上帝给我的心作见证，我没有往哥林多去是为要宽容你们。

chapters.en: Not that we lord it over your faith, but we are fellow workers with you for your joy, because it is by faith that you stand firm.
chapters.zh: 我们并不是辖管你们的信心，乃是帮助你们的快乐，因为你们凭信才站立得住。

chapters.en: So I made up my mind not to make another painful visit to you.
chapters.zh: 我自己定了主意再到你们那里去，必须大家没有忧愁。

chapters.en: For if I grieve you, who is left to cheer me but those whom I have grieved?
chapters.zh: 倘若我叫你们忧愁，除了我叫那忧愁的人以外，谁能叫我快乐呢？

chapters.en: I wrote as I did so that on my arrival I would not be grieved by those who ought to make me rejoice. I had confidence in all of you, that you would share my joy.
chapters.zh: 我曾把这事写给你们，恐怕我到的时候，应该叫我快乐的那些人，反倒叫我忧愁。我也深信，你们众人都以我的快乐为自己的快乐。

chapters.en: For through many tears I wrote you out of great distress and anguish of heart, not to grieve you but to let you know how much I love you.
chapters.zh: 我先前心里难过痛苦，多多地流泪，写信给你们，不是叫你们忧愁，乃是叫你们知道我格外地疼爱你们。

chapters.en: Now if anyone has caused grief, he has not grieved me but all of you—to some degree, not to overstate it.
chapters.zh: 若有叫人忧愁的，他不但叫我忧愁，也是叫你们众人有几分忧愁。我说几分，恐怕说得太重。

chapters.en: The punishment imposed on him by the majority is sufficient for him.
chapters.zh: 这样的人受了众人的责罚也就够了，

chapters.en: So instead, you ought to forgive and comfort him, so that he will not be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
chapters.zh: 倒不如赦免他，安慰他，免得他忧愁太过，甚至沉沦了。

chapters.en: Therefore I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.
chapters.zh: 所以我劝你们，要向他显出坚定不移的爱心来。

chapters.en: My purpose in writing you was to see if you would stand the test and be obedient in everything.
chapters.zh: 为此我先前也写信给你们，要试验你们，看你们凡事顺从不顺从。

chapters.en: If you forgive anyone, I also forgive him. And if I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven it in the presence of Christ for your sake,
chapters.zh: 你们赦免谁，我也赦免谁。我若有所赦免的，是在基督面前为你们赦免的，

chapters.en: in order that Satan should not outwit us. For we are not unaware of his schemes.
chapters.zh: 免得撒但趁着机会胜过我们，因我们并非不晓得他的诡计。

chapters.en: Now when I went to Troas to preach the gospel of Christ and a door stood open for me in the Lord,
chapters.zh: 我从前为基督的福音到了特罗亚，主也给我开了门。

chapters.en: I had no peace in my spirit, because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.
chapters.zh: 那时，因为没有遇见兄弟提多，我心里不安，便辞别那里的人往马其顿去了。

chapters.en: But thanks be to God, who always leads us triumphantly as captives in Christ and through us spreads everywhere the fragrance of the knowledge of Him.
chapters.zh: 感谢上帝！常率领我们在基督里夸胜，并藉着我们在各处显扬那因认识基督而有的香气。

chapters.en: For we are to God the sweet aroma of Christ among those who are being saved and those who are perishing.
chapters.zh: 因为我们在上帝面前，无论在得救的人身上或灭亡的人身上，都有基督馨香之气。

chapters.en: To the one we are an odor that brings death, to the other a fragrance that brings life. And who is qualified for such a task?
chapters.zh: 在这等人，就作了死的香气叫他死；在那等人，就作了活的香气叫他活。这事谁能当得起呢？

chapters.en: For we are not like so many others, who peddle the word of God for profit. On the contrary, in Christ we speak before God with sincerity, as men sent from God.
chapters.zh: 我们不像那许多人，为利混乱上帝的道；乃是由于诚实，由于上帝，在上帝面前凭着基督讲道。

chapters.en: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, like some people, letters of recommendation to you or from you?
chapters.zh: 我们岂是又举荐自己吗？岂像别人用人的荐信给你们或用你们的荐信给人吗？

chapters.en: You yourselves are our letter, inscribed on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
chapters.zh: 你们就是我们的荐信，写在我们的心里，被众人所知道所念诵的。

chapters.en: It is clear that you are a letter from Christ, the result of our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.
chapters.zh: 你们明显是基督的信，藉着我们修成的。不是用墨写的，乃是用永生上帝的灵写的；不是写在石版上，乃是写在心版上。

chapters.en: Such confidence before God is ours through Christ.
chapters.zh: 我们因基督，所以在上帝面前才有这样的信心。

chapters.en: Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim that anything comes from us, but our competence comes from God.
chapters.zh: 并不是我们凭自己能承担什么事；我们所能承担的，乃是出于上帝。

chapters.en: And He has qualified us as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
chapters.zh: 他叫我们能承当这新约的执事，不是凭着字句，乃是凭着精意；因为那字句是叫人死，精意〔注：或译：圣灵〕是叫人活。

chapters.en: Now if the ministry of death, which was engraved in letters on stone, came with such glory that the Israelites could not gaze at the face of Moses because of its fleeting glory,
chapters.zh: 那用字刻在石头上属死的职事尚且有荣光，甚至以色列人因摩西面上的荣光，不能定睛看他的脸；这荣光原是渐渐退去的，

chapters.en: will not the ministry of the Spirit be even more glorious?
chapters.zh: 何况那属灵的职事岂不更有荣光吗？

chapters.en: For if the ministry of condemnation was glorious, how much more glorious is the ministry of righteousness!
chapters.zh: 若是定罪的职事有荣光，那称义的职事荣光就越发大了。

chapters.en: Indeed, what was once glorious has no glory now in comparison to the glory that surpasses it.
chapters.zh: 那从前有荣光的，因这极大的荣光就算不得有荣光了；

chapters.en: For if what was fading away came with glory, how much greater is the glory of that which endures!
chapters.zh: 若那废掉的有荣光，这长存的就更有荣光了。

chapters.en: Therefore, since we have such a hope, we are very bold.
chapters.zh: 我们既有这样的盼望，就大胆讲说，

chapters.en: We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away.
chapters.zh: 不像摩西将帕子蒙在脸上，叫以色列人不能定睛看到那将废者〔的〕结局。

chapters.en: But their minds were closed. For to this day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant. It has not been lifted, because only in Christ can it be removed.
chapters.zh: 但他们的心地刚硬，直到今日诵读旧约的时候，这帕子还没有揭去。这帕子在基督里已经废去了。

chapters.en: And even to this day when Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts.
chapters.zh: 然而直到今日，每逢诵读摩西〔书〕的时候，帕子还在他们心上。

chapters.en: But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
chapters.zh: 但他们的心几时归向主，帕子就几时除去了。

chapters.en: Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
chapters.zh: 主就是那灵；主的灵在哪里，那里就得以自由。

chapters.en: And we, who with unveiled faces all reflect the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
chapters.zh: 我们众人既然敞着脸得以看见主的荣光，好像从镜子里返照，就变成主的形状，荣上加荣，如同从主的灵变成的。

chapters.en: Therefore, since God in His mercy has given us this ministry, we do not lose heart.
chapters.zh: 我们既然蒙怜悯，受了这职分，就不丧胆，

chapters.en: Instead, we have renounced secret and shameful ways. We do not practice deceit, nor do we distort the word of God. On the contrary, by open proclamation of the truth, we commend ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.
chapters.zh: 乃将那些暗昧可耻的事弃绝了；不行诡诈，不谬讲上帝的道理，只将真理表明出来，好在上帝面前把自己荐与各人的良心。

chapters.en: And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing.
chapters.zh: 如果我们的福音蒙蔽，就是蒙蔽在灭亡的人身上。

chapters.en: The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers, so they cannot see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
chapters.zh: 此等不信之人被这世界的神弄瞎了心眼，不叫基督荣耀福音的光照着他们。基督本是上帝的像。

chapters.en: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake.
chapters.zh: 我们原不是传自己，乃是传基督耶稣为主，并且自己因耶稣作你们的仆人。

chapters.en: For God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” made His light shine in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 那吩咐光从黑暗里照出来的上帝，已经照在我们心里，叫我们得知上帝荣耀的光显在耶稣基督的面上。

chapters.en: Now we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this surpassingly great power is from God and not from us.
chapters.zh: 我们有这宝贝放在瓦器里，要显明这莫大的能力是出于上帝，不是出于我们。

chapters.en: We are hard pressed on all sides, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;
chapters.zh: 我们四面受敌，却不被困住；心里作难，却不致失望；

chapters.en: persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed.
chapters.zh: 遭逼迫，却不被丢弃；打倒了，却不致死亡。

chapters.en: We always carry around in our body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
chapters.zh: 身上常带着耶稣的死，使耶稣的生也显明在我们身上。

chapters.en: For we who are alive are always consigned to death for Jesus’ sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our mortal body.
chapters.zh: 因为我们这活着的人是常为耶稣被交于死地，使耶稣的生在我们这必死的身上显明出来。

chapters.en: So then, death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
chapters.zh: 这样看来，死是在我们身上发动，生却在你们身上发动。

chapters.en: And in keeping with what is written, “I believed, therefore I have spoken,” we who have the same spirit of faith also believe and therefore speak,
chapters.zh: 但我们既有信心，正如〔经上〕记着说：「我因信，所以如此说话。」我们也信，所以也说话。

chapters.en: knowing that the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us with you in His presence.
chapters.zh: 自己知道那叫主耶稣复活的，也必叫我们与耶稣一同复活，并且叫我们与你们一同站在他面前。

chapters.en: All this is for your benefit, so that the grace that is extending to more and more people may cause thanksgiving to overflow, to the glory of God.
chapters.zh: 凡事都是为你们，好叫恩惠因人多越发加增，感谢格外显多，以致荣耀归与上帝。

chapters.en: Therefore we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.
chapters.zh: 所以，我们不丧胆。外体虽然毁坏，内心却一天新似一天。

chapters.en: For our light and momentary affliction is producing for us an eternal weight of glory that is far beyond comparison.
chapters.zh: 我们这至暂至轻的苦楚，要为我们成就极重无比、永远的荣耀。

chapters.en: So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.
chapters.zh: 原来我们不是顾念所见的，乃是顾念所不见的；因为所见的是暂时的，所不见的是永远的。

chapters.en: For we know that if the earthly tent we live in is dismantled, we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands.
chapters.zh: 我们原知道，我们这地上的帐棚若拆毁了，必得上帝所造，不是人手所造，在天上永存的房屋。

chapters.en: For in this tent we groan, longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling,
chapters.zh: 我们在这帐棚里叹息，深想得那从天上来的房屋，好像穿上〔衣服〕；

chapters.en: because when we are clothed, we will not be found naked.
chapters.zh: 倘若穿上，被遇见的时候就不至于赤身了。

chapters.en: For while we are in this tent, we groan under our burdens, because we do not wish to be unclothed but clothed, so that our mortality may be swallowed up by life.
chapters.zh: 我们在这帐棚里叹息劳苦，并非愿意脱下这个，乃是愿意穿上那个，好叫这必死的被生命吞灭了。

chapters.en: And it is God who has prepared us for this very purpose and has given us the Spirit as a pledge of what is to come.
chapters.zh: 为此，培植我们的就是上帝，他又赐给我们〔圣〕灵作凭据〔注：原文是质〕。

chapters.en: Therefore we are always confident, although we know that while we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord.
chapters.zh: 所以，我们时常坦然无惧，并且晓得我们住在身内，便与主相离。

chapters.en: For we walk by faith, not by sight.
chapters.zh: 因我们行事为人是凭着信心，不是凭着眼见。

chapters.en: We are confident, then, and would prefer to be away from the body and at home with the Lord.
chapters.zh: 我们坦然无惧，是更愿意离开身体与主同住。

chapters.en: So we aspire to please Him, whether we are at home in this body or away from it.
chapters.zh: 所以，无论是住在身内，离开身外，我们立了志向，要得主的喜悦。

chapters.en: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad.
chapters.zh: 因为我们众人必要在基督台前显露出来，叫各人按着本身所行的，或善或恶受报。

chapters.en: Therefore, since we know what it means to fear the Lord, we try to persuade men. What we are is clear to God, and I hope it is clear to your conscience as well.
chapters.zh: 我们既知道主是可畏的，所以劝人。但我们在上帝面前是显明的，盼望在你们的良心里也是显明的。

chapters.en: We are not commending ourselves to you again. Instead, we are giving you an occasion to be proud of us, so that you can answer those who take pride in appearances rather than in the heart.
chapters.zh: 我们不是向你们再举荐自己，乃是叫你们因我们有可夸之处，好对那凭外貌不凭内心夸口的人，有言可答。

chapters.en: If we are out of our mind, it is for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for you.
chapters.zh: 我们若果颠狂，是为上帝；若果谨守，是为你们。

chapters.en: For Christ’s love compels us, because we are convinced that One died for all, therefore all died.
chapters.zh: 原来基督的爱激励我们；因我们想，一人既替众人死，众人就都死了；

chapters.en: And He died for all, that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and was raised again.
chapters.zh: 并且他替众人死，是叫那些活着的人不再为自己活，乃为替他们死而复活的〔主〕活。

chapters.en: So from now on we regard no one according to the flesh. Although we once regarded Christ in this way, we do so no longer.
chapters.zh: 所以，我们从今以后，不凭着外貌〔注：原文是肉体；本节同〕认人了。虽然凭着外貌认过基督，如今却不再〔这样〕认他了。

chapters.en: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!
chapters.zh: 若有人在基督里，他就是新造的人，旧事已过，都变成新的了。

chapters.en: All this is from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:
chapters.zh: 一切都是出于上帝；他藉着基督使我们与他和好，又将劝人与他和好的职分赐给我们。

chapters.en: that God was reconciling the world to Himself in Christ, not counting men’s trespasses against them. And He has committed to us the message of reconciliation.
chapters.zh: 这就是上帝在基督里，叫世人与自己和好，不将他们的过犯归到他们身上，并且将这和好的道理托付了我们。

chapters.en: Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making His appeal through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ: Be reconciled to God.
chapters.zh: 所以，我们作基督的使者，就好像上帝藉我们劝你们一般。我们替基督求你们与上帝和好。

chapters.en: God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.
chapters.zh: 上帝使那无罪〔注：无罪：原文是不知罪〕的，替我们成为罪，好叫我们在他里面成为上帝的义。

chapters.en: As God’s fellow workers, then, we urge you not to receive God’s grace in vain.
chapters.zh: 我们与〔上帝〕同工的，也劝你们不可徒受他的恩典。

chapters.en:
For He says:
“In the time of favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you.”
Behold, now is the time of favor; now is the day of salvation!
chapters.zh: 因为他说：「在悦纳的时候，我应允了你；在拯救的日子，我搭救了你。」看哪，现在正是悦纳的时候！现在正是拯救的日子；

chapters.en: We put no obstacle in anyone’s way, so that no one can discredit our ministry.
chapters.zh: 我们凡事都不叫人有妨碍，免得这职分被人毁谤；

chapters.en: Rather, as servants of God we commend ourselves in every way: in great endurance; in troubles, hardships, and calamities;
chapters.zh: 反倒在各样的事上表明自己是上帝的用人，就如在许多的忍耐、患难、穷乏、困苦、

chapters.en: in beatings, imprisonments, and riots; in labor, sleepless nights, and hunger;
chapters.zh: 鞭打、监禁、扰乱、勤劳、警醒、不食、

chapters.en: in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness; in the Holy Spirit and in sincere love;
chapters.zh: 廉洁、知识、恒忍、恩慈、圣灵的感化、无伪的爱心、

chapters.en: in truthful speech and in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;
chapters.zh: 真实的道理、上帝的大能；仁义的兵器在左在右；

chapters.en: through glory and dishonor, slander and praise; viewed as imposters, yet genuine;
chapters.zh: 荣耀、羞辱，恶名、美名；似乎是诱惑人的，却是诚实的；

chapters.en: unknown, yet well-known; dying, and yet we live on; punished, yet not killed;
chapters.zh: 似乎不为人所知，却是人所共知的；似乎要死，却是活着的；似乎受责罚，却是不致丧命的；

chapters.en: sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, and yet possessing everything.
chapters.zh: 似乎忧愁，却是常常快乐的；似乎贫穷，却是叫许多人富足的；似乎一无所有，却是样样都有的。

chapters.en: We have spoken freely to you, Corinthians. Our hearts are open wide.
chapters.zh: 哥林多人哪，我们向你们，口是张开的，心是宽宏的。

chapters.en: It is not our affection, but yours, that is restrained.
chapters.zh: 你们狭窄，原不在乎我们，是在乎自己的心肠狭窄。

chapters.en: As a fair exchange—I speak as to my children—open wide your hearts also.
chapters.zh: 你们也要照样用宽宏的心报答我。我这话正像对自己的孩子说的。

chapters.en: Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership can righteousness have with wickedness? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?
chapters.zh: 你们和不信的原不相配，不要同负一轭。义和不义有什么相交呢？光明和黑暗有什么相通呢？

chapters.en: What harmony is there between Christ and Belial? Or what does a believer have in common with an unbeliever?
chapters.zh: 基督和彼列〔注：彼列就是撒但的别名〕有什么相和呢？信〔主〕的和不信〔主〕的有什么相干呢？

chapters.en:
What agreement can exist between the temple of God and idols? For we are the temple of the living God. As God has said:
“I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.”
chapters.zh: 上帝的殿和偶像有什么相同呢？因为我们是永生上帝的殿，就如上帝曾说： 我要在他们中间居住， 在他们中间来往； 我要作他们的上帝； 他们要作我的子民。

chapters.en: “Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.”
chapters.zh: 又说：你们务要从他们中间出来， 与他们分别； 不要沾不洁净的物，我就收纳你们。

chapters.en:
And:
“I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters,
says the Lord Almighty.”
chapters.zh: 我要作你们的父； 你们要作我的儿女。 这是全能的主说的。

chapters.en: Therefore, beloved, since we have these promises, let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
chapters.zh: 亲爱的〔弟兄〕啊，我们既有这等应许，就当洁净自己，除去身体、灵魂一切的污秽，敬畏上帝，得以成圣。

chapters.en: Make room for us in your hearts. We have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have exploited no one.
chapters.zh: 你们要心地宽大收纳我们。我们未曾亏负谁，未曾败坏谁，未曾佔谁的便宜。

chapters.en: I do not say this to condemn you. I have said before that you so occupy our hearts that we live and die together with you.
chapters.zh: 我说这话，不是要定你们的罪。我已经说过，你们常在我们心里，情愿与你们同生同死。

chapters.en: Great is my confidence in you; great is my pride in you; I am filled with encouragement; in all our troubles my joy overflows.
chapters.zh: 我大大地放胆，向你们说话；我因你们多多夸口，满得安慰；我们在一切患难中分外地快乐。

chapters.en: For when we arrived in Macedonia, our bodies had no rest, but we were pressed from every direction—conflicts on the outside, fears within.
chapters.zh: 我们从前就是到了马其顿的时候，身体也不得安宁，周围遭患难，外有争战，内有惧怕。

chapters.en: But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the arrival of Titus,
chapters.zh: 但那安慰丧气之人的上帝藉着提多来安慰了我们；

chapters.en: and not only by his arrival, but also by the comfort he had received from you. He told us about your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced all the more.
chapters.zh: 不但藉着他来，也藉着他从你们所得的安慰，安慰了我们；因他把你们的想念、哀恸，和向我的热心，都告诉了我，叫我更加欢喜。

chapters.en: Even if I caused you sorrow by my letter, I do not regret it. Although I did regret it—for I see that my letter caused you sorrow, but only for a short time—
chapters.zh: 我先前写信叫你们忧愁，我后来虽然懊悔，如今却不懊悔；因我知道，那信叫你们忧愁不过是暂时的。

chapters.en: yet now I rejoice, not because you were made sorrowful, but because your sorrow led you to repentance. For you felt the sorrow that God had intended, and so were not harmed in any way by us.
chapters.zh: 如今我欢喜，不是因你们忧愁，是因你们从忧愁中生出懊悔来。你们依着上帝的意思忧愁，凡事就不至于因我们受亏损了。

chapters.en: Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation without regret, but worldly sorrow brings death.
chapters.zh: 因为依着上帝的意思忧愁，就生出没有后悔的懊悔来，以致得救；但世俗的忧愁是叫人死。

chapters.en: Consider what this godly sorrow has produced in you: what earnestness, what eagerness to clear yourselves, what indignation, what alarm, what longing, what zeal, what vindication! In every way you have proved yourselves to be innocent in this matter.
chapters.zh: 你看，你们依着上帝的意思忧愁，从此就生出何等的殷勤、自诉、自恨、恐惧、想念、热心、责罚〔注：或译：自责〕。在这一切事上，你们都表明自己是洁净的。

chapters.en: So even though I wrote to you, it was not on account of the one who did wrong or the one who was harmed, but rather that your earnestness on our behalf would be made clear to you in the sight of God.
chapters.zh: 我虽然从前写信给你们，却不是为那亏负人的，也不是为那受人亏负的，乃要在上帝面前把你们顾念我们的热心表明出来。

chapters.en:
On account of this, we are encouraged.
In addition to our own encouragement, we were even more delighted by the joy of Titus. For his spirit has been refreshed by all of you.
chapters.zh: 故此，我们得了安慰。 并且在安慰之中，因你们众人使提多心里畅快欢喜，我们就更加欢喜了。

chapters.en: Indeed, I was not embarrassed by anything I had boasted to him about you. But just as everything we said to you was true, so our boasting to Titus has proved to be true as well.
chapters.zh: 我若对提多夸奖了你们什么，也觉得没有惭愧；因我对提多夸奖你们的话成了真的，正如我对你们所说的话也都是真的。

chapters.en: And his affection for you is even greater when he remembers that you were all obedient as you welcomed him with fear and trembling.
chapters.zh: 并且提多想起你们众人的顺服，是怎样恐惧战兢地接待他，他爱你们的心肠就越发热了。

chapters.en: I rejoice that I can have complete confidence in you.
chapters.zh: 我如今欢喜，能在凡事上为你们放心。

chapters.en: Now, brothers, we want you to know about the grace that God has given the churches of Macedonia.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我把上帝赐给马其顿众教会的恩告诉你们，

chapters.en: In the terrible ordeal they suffered, their abundant joy and deep poverty overflowed into rich generosity.
chapters.zh: 就是他们在患难中受大试炼的时候，仍有满足的快乐，在极穷之间还格外显出他们乐捐的厚恩。

chapters.en: For I testify that they gave according to their ability and even beyond it. Of their own accord,
chapters.zh: 我可以证明，他们是按着力量，而且也过了力量，自己甘心乐意地捐助，

chapters.en: they earnestly pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the saints.
chapters.zh: 再三地求我们，准他们在这供给圣徒的恩情上有分；

chapters.en: And not only did they do as we expected, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, through the will of God.
chapters.zh: 并且他们所做的，不但照我们所想望的，更照上帝的旨意先把自己献给主，又归附了我们。

chapters.en: So we urged Titus to help complete your act of grace, just as he had started it.
chapters.zh: 因此我劝提多，既然在你们中间开办这慈惠的事，就当办成了。

chapters.en: But just as you excel in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in complete earnestness, and in the love we inspired in you —see that you also excel in this grace of giving.
chapters.zh: 你们既然在信心、口才、知识、热心，和待我们的爱心上，都格外显出满足来，就当在这慈惠的事上也格外显出满足来。

chapters.en: I am not giving a command, but I am testing the sincerity of your love through the earnestness of others.
chapters.zh: 我说这话，不是吩咐你们，乃是藉着别人的热心试验你们爱心的实在。

chapters.en: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor, so that you through His poverty might become rich.
chapters.zh: 你们知道我们主耶稣基督的恩典：他本来富足，却为你们成了贫穷，叫你们因他的贫穷，可以成为富足。

chapters.en: And this is my opinion about what is helpful for you in this matter: Last year you were the first not only to give, but even to have such a desire.
chapters.zh: 我在这事上把我的意见告诉你们，是与你们有益；因为你们下手办这事，而且起此心意，已经有一年了，

chapters.en: Now finish the work, so that you may complete it with the same eager desire, according to your means.
chapters.zh: 如今就当办成这事。既有愿做的心，也当照你们所有的去办成。

chapters.en: For if the eagerness is there, the gift is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what he does not have.
chapters.zh: 因为人若有愿做的心，必蒙悦纳，乃是照他所有的，并不是照他所无的。

chapters.en: It is not our intention that others may be relieved while you are burdened, but that there may be equality.
chapters.zh: 我原不是要别人轻省，你们受累，

chapters.en: At the present time, your surplus will meet their need, so that in turn their surplus will meet your need. This way there will be equality.
chapters.zh: 乃要均平，就是要你们的富余，现在〔可以补〕他们的不足，使他们的富余，〔将来〕也可以〔补〕你们的不足，这就均平了。

chapters.en:
As it is written:
“He who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall.”
chapters.zh: 如〔经上〕所记： 多〔收〕的也没有余； 少〔收〕的也没有缺。

chapters.en: But thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same devotion I have for you.
chapters.zh: 多谢上帝，感动提多的心，叫他待你们殷勤，像我一样。

chapters.en: For not only did he welcome our appeal, but he is eagerly coming to you of his own volition.
chapters.zh: 他固然是听了我的劝，但自己更是热心，情愿往你们那里去。

chapters.en: Along with Titus we are sending the brother who is praised by all the churches for his work in the gospel.
chapters.zh: 我们还打发一位兄弟和他同去，这人在福音上得了众教会的称赞。

chapters.en: More than that, this brother was chosen by the churches to accompany us with the gracious offering we administer to honor the Lord Himself and to show our eagerness to help.
chapters.zh: 不但这样，他也被众教会挑选，和我们同行，把所讬与我们的这捐资送到了，可以荣耀主，又表明我们乐意的心。

chapters.en: We want to avoid any criticism of the way we administer this generous gift.
chapters.zh: 这就免得有人因我们收的捐银很多，就挑我们的不是。

chapters.en: For we are taking great care to do what is right, not only in the eyes of the Lord, but also in the eyes of men.
chapters.zh: 我们留心行光明的事，不但在主面前，就在人面前也是这样。

chapters.en: And we are sending along with them our brother who has proven his earnestness to us many times and in many ways, and now even more so by his great confidence in you.
chapters.zh: 我们又打发一位兄弟同去；这人的热心，我们在许多事上屡次试验过。现在他因为深信你们，就更加热心了。

chapters.en: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker among you. As for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, the glory of Christ.
chapters.zh: 论到提多，他是我的同伴，一同为你们劳碌的。论到那两位兄弟，他们是众教会的使者，是基督的荣耀。

chapters.en: In full view of the churches, then, show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们务要在众教会面前显明你们爱心的凭据，并我所夸奖你们的凭据。

chapters.en: Now about the service to the saints, there is no need for me to write to you.
chapters.zh: 论到供给圣徒的事，我不必写信给你们；

chapters.en: For I know your eagerness to help, and I have been boasting to the Macedonians that since last year you in Achaia were prepared to give. And your zeal has stirred most of them to do likewise.
chapters.zh: 因为我知道你们乐意的心，常对马其顿人夸奖你们，说亚该亚人预备好了，已经有一年了；并且你们的热心激动了许多人。

chapters.en: But I am sending the brothers in order that our boasting about you in this matter should not prove empty, but that you will be prepared, just as I said.
chapters.zh: 但我打发那几位弟兄去，要叫你们照我的话预备妥当，免得我们在这事上夸奖你们的话落了空。

chapters.en: Otherwise, if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—to say nothing of you—would be ashamed of having been so confident.
chapters.zh: 万一有马其顿人与我同去，见你们没有预备，就叫我们所确信的，反成了羞愧；你们羞愧，更不用说了。

chapters.en: So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers to visit you beforehand and make arrangements for the generous gift you had promised. This way, your gift will be prepared generously and not begrudgingly.
chapters.zh: 因此，我想不得不求那几位弟兄先到你们那里去，把从前所应许的捐资预备妥当，就显出你们所捐的是出于乐意，不是出于勉强。

chapters.en: Remember this: Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.
chapters.zh: 「少种的少收，多种的多收」，这话是真的。

chapters.en: Each one should give what he has decided in his heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.
chapters.zh: 各人要随本心所酌定的，不要作难，不要勉强，因为捐得乐意的人是上帝所喜爱的。

chapters.en: And God is able to make all grace abound to you, so that in all things, at all times, having all that you need, you will abound in every good work.
chapters.zh: 上帝能将各样的恩惠多多地加给你们，使你们凡事常常充足，能多行各样善事。

chapters.en:
As it is written:
“He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever.”
chapters.zh: 如〔经上〕所记： 他施舍〔钱财〕，赒济贫穷； 他的仁义存到永远。

chapters.en: Now He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your store of seed and will increase the harvest of your righteousness.
chapters.zh: 那赐种给撒种的，赐粮给人吃的，必多多加给你们种地的种子，又增添你们仁义的果子；

chapters.en: You will be enriched in every way to be generous on every occasion, and through us your generosity will produce thanksgiving to God.
chapters.zh: 叫你们凡事富足，可以多多施舍，就藉着我们使感谢归于上帝。

chapters.en: For this ministry of service is not only supplying the needs of the saints but is also overflowing in many expressions of thanksgiving to God.
chapters.zh: 因为办这供给的事，不但补圣徒的缺乏，而且叫许多人越发感谢上帝。

chapters.en: Because of the proof this ministry provides, the saints will glorify God for your obedient confession of the gospel of Christ, and for the generosity of your contribution to them and to all the others.
chapters.zh: 他们从这供给的事上得了凭据，知道你们承认基督顺服他的福音，多多地捐钱给他们和众人，便将荣耀归与上帝。

chapters.en: And their prayers for you will express their affection for you, because of the surpassing grace God has given you.
chapters.zh: 他们也因上帝极大的恩赐显在你们心里，就切切地想念你们，为你们祈祷。

chapters.en: Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!
chapters.zh: 感谢上帝，因他有说不尽的恩赐！

chapters.en: Now by the mildness and gentleness of Christ, I appeal to you—I, Paul, who am humble when face to face with you, but bold when away.
chapters.zh: 我－保罗，就是与你们见面的时候是谦卑的，不在你们那里的时候向你们是勇敢的，如今亲自藉着基督的温柔、和平劝你们。

chapters.en: I beg you that when I come I may not need to be as bold as I expect toward those who presume that we live according to the flesh.
chapters.zh: 有人以为我是凭着血气行事，我也以为必须用勇敢待这等人；求你们不要叫我在你们那里的时候，有这样的勇敢。

chapters.en: For though we live in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.
chapters.zh: 因为我们虽然在血气中行事，却不凭着血气争战。

chapters.en: The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the flesh. Instead, they have divine power to demolish strongholds.
chapters.zh: 我们争战的兵器本不是属血气的，乃是在上帝面前有能力，可以攻破坚固的营垒，

chapters.en: We demolish arguments and every presumption set up against the knowledge of God; and we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.
chapters.zh: 将各样的计谋，各样拦阻人认识上帝的那些自高之事，一概攻破了，又将人所有的心意夺回，使他都顺服基督。

chapters.en: And we will be ready to punish every act of disobedience, as soon as your obedience is complete.
chapters.zh: 并且我已经预备好了，等你们十分顺服的时候，要责罚那一切不顺服的人。

chapters.en: You are looking at outward appearances. If anyone is confident that he belongs to Christ, he should remind himself that we belong to Christ just as much as he does.
chapters.zh: 你们是看眼前的吗？倘若有人自信是属基督的，他要再想想，他如何属基督，我们也是如何属基督的。

chapters.en: For even if I boast somewhat excessively about the authority the Lord gave us for building you up rather than tearing you down, I will not be ashamed.
chapters.zh: 主赐给我们权柄，是要造就你们，并不是要败坏你们；我就是为这权柄稍微夸口，也不至于惭愧。

chapters.en: I do not want to seem to be trying to frighten you by my letters.
chapters.zh: 我〔说这话〕，免得你们以为我写信是要威吓你们；

chapters.en: For some say, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but his physical presence is unimpressive, and his speaking is of no account.”
chapters.zh: 因为有人说：「他的信又沉重又厉害，及至见面，却是气貌不扬，言语粗俗的。」

chapters.en: Such people should consider that what we are in our letters when absent, we will be in our actions when present.
chapters.zh: 这等人当想，我们不在那里的时候，信上的言语如何，见面的时候，行事也必如何。

chapters.en: We do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves. When they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they show their ignorance.
chapters.zh: 因为我们不敢将自己和那自荐的人同列相比。他们用自己度量自己，用自己比较自己，乃是不通达的。

chapters.en: We, however, will not boast beyond our limits, but only within the field of influence that God has assigned to us—a field that reaches even to you.
chapters.zh: 我们不愿意分外夸口，只要照上帝所量给我们的界限搆到你们那里。

chapters.en: We are not overstepping our bounds, as if we had not come to you. Indeed, we were the first to reach you with the gospel of Christ.
chapters.zh: 我们并非过了自己的界限，好像搆不到你们那里；因为我们早到你们那里，传了基督的福音。

chapters.en: Neither do we boast beyond our limits in the labors of others. But we hope that as your faith increases, our area of influence among you will greatly increase as well,
chapters.zh: 我们不仗着别人所劳碌的，分外夸口；但指望你们信心增长的时候，所量给我们的界限，就可以因着你们更加开展，

chapters.en: so that we can preach the gospel in the regions beyond you. Then we will not be boasting in the work already done in another man’s territory.
chapters.zh: 得以将福音传到你们以外的地方；并不是在别人界限之内，藉着他现成的事夸口。

chapters.en: Rather, “Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.”
chapters.zh: 但夸口的，当指着主夸口。

chapters.en: For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
chapters.zh: 因为蒙悦纳的，不是自己称许的，乃是主所称许的。

chapters.en: I hope you will put up with a little of my foolishness, but you are already doing that.
chapters.zh: 但愿你们宽容我这一点愚妄，其实你们原是宽容我的。

chapters.en: I am jealous for you with a godly jealousy. For I promised you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
chapters.zh: 我为你们起的愤恨，原是上帝那样的愤恨。因为我曾把你们许配一个丈夫，要把你们如同贞洁的童女，献给基督。

chapters.en: I am afraid, however, that just as Eve was deceived by the serpent’s cunning, your minds may be led astray from your simple and pure devotion to Christ.
chapters.zh: 我只怕你们的心或偏于邪，失去那向基督所存纯一清洁的心，就像蛇用诡诈诱惑了夏娃一样。

chapters.en: For if someone comes and proclaims a Jesus other than the One we proclaimed, or if you receive a different spirit than the One you received, or a different gospel than the one you accepted, you put up with it very easily.
chapters.zh: 假如有人来另传一个耶稣，不是我们所传过的；或者你们另受一个灵，不是你们所受过的；或者另得一个福音，不是你们所得过的；你们容让他也就罢了。

chapters.en: I consider myself in no way inferior to those “super-apostles.”
chapters.zh: 但我想，我一点不在那些最大的使徒以下。

chapters.en: Although I am not a polished speaker, I am certainly not lacking in knowledge. We have made this clear to you in every way possible.
chapters.zh: 我的言语虽然粗俗，我的知识却不粗俗。这是我们在凡事上向你们众人显明出来的。

chapters.en: Was it a sin for me to humble myself in order to exalt you, because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge?
chapters.zh: 我因为白白传上帝的福音给你们，就自居卑微，叫你们高升，这算是我犯罪吗？

chapters.en: I robbed other churches by accepting their support in order to serve you.
chapters.zh: 我亏负了别的教会，向他们取了工价来给你们效力。

chapters.en: And when I was with you and in need, I was not a burden to anyone; for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied my needs. I have refrained from being a burden to you in any way, and I will continue to do so.
chapters.zh: 我在你们那里缺乏的时候，并没有累着你们一个人；因我所缺乏的，那从马其顿来的弟兄们都补足了。我向来凡事谨守，后来也必谨守，总不至于累着你们。

chapters.en: As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting of mine will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.
chapters.zh: 既有基督的诚实在我里面，就无人能在亚该亚一带地方阻挡我这自夸。

chapters.en: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!
chapters.zh: 为什么呢？是因我不爱你们吗？这有上帝知道。

chapters.en: But I will keep on doing what I am doing, in order to undercut those who want an opportunity to be regarded as our equals in the things of which they boast.
chapters.zh: 我现在所做的，后来还要做，为要断绝那些寻机会人的机会，使他们在所夸的事上也不过与我们一样。

chapters.en: For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as apostles of Christ.
chapters.zh: 那等人是假使徒，行事诡诈，装作基督使徒的模样。

chapters.en: And no wonder, for Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light.
chapters.zh: 这也不足为怪，因为连撒但也装作光明的天使。

chapters.en: It is not surprising, then, if his servants masquerade as servants of righteousness. Their end will correspond to their actions.
chapters.zh: 所以他的差役，若装作仁义的差役，也不算希奇。他们的结局必然照着他们的行为。

chapters.en: I repeat: Let no one take me for a fool. But if you do, then receive me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
chapters.zh: 我再说，人不可把我看作愚妄的。纵然如此，也要把我当作愚妄人接纳，叫我可以略略自夸。

chapters.en: In this confident boasting of mine, I am not speaking as the Lord would, but as a fool.
chapters.zh: 我说的话不是奉主命说的，乃是像愚妄人放胆自夸；

chapters.en: Since many are boasting according to the flesh, I too will boast.
chapters.zh: 既有好些人凭着血气自夸，我也要自夸了。

chapters.en: For you gladly put up with fools, since you are so wise.
chapters.zh: 你们既是精明人，就能甘心忍耐愚妄人。

chapters.en: In fact, you even put up with anyone who enslaves you or exploits you or takes advantage of you or exalts himself or strikes you in the face.
chapters.zh: 假若有人强你们作奴仆，或侵吞你们，或掳掠你们，或侮慢你们，或打你们的脸，你们都能忍耐他。

chapters.en:
To my shame I concede that we were too weak for that!
Speaking as a fool, however, I can match what anyone else dares to boast about.
chapters.zh: 我说这话是羞辱自己，好像我们从前是软弱的。然而，人在何事上勇敢，（我说句愚妄话，）我也勇敢。

chapters.en: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.
chapters.zh: 他们是希伯来人吗？我也是。他们是以色列人吗？我也是。他们是亚伯拉罕的后裔吗？我也是。

chapters.en: Are they servants of Christ? (I am speaking as if I were out of my mind.) I am so much more: in harder labor, in more imprisonments, in worse beatings, in frequent danger of death.
chapters.zh: 他们是基督的仆人吗？（我说句狂话，）我更是。我比他们多受劳苦，多下监牢，受鞭打是过重的，冒死是屡次有的。

chapters.en: Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.
chapters.zh: 被犹太人鞭打五次，每次四十减去一下；

chapters.en: Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked. I spent a night and a day in the open sea.
chapters.zh: 被棍打了三次；被石头打了一次；遇着船坏三次，一昼一夜在深海里。

chapters.en: In my frequent journeys, I have been in danger from rivers and from bandits, in danger from my countrymen and from the Gentiles, in danger in the city and in the country, in danger on the sea and among false brothers,
chapters.zh: 又屡次行远路，遭江河的危险、盗贼的危险、同族的危险、外邦人的危险、城里的危险、旷野的危险、海中的危险、假弟兄的危险。

chapters.en: in labor and toil and often without sleep, in hunger and thirst and often without food, in cold and exposure.
chapters.zh: 受劳碌、受困苦，多次不得睡，又饥又渴，多次不得食，受寒冷，赤身露体。

chapters.en: Apart from these external trials, I face daily the pressure of my concern for all the churches.
chapters.zh: 除了这外面的事，还有为众教会挂心的事，天天压在我身上。

chapters.en: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led into sin, and I do not burn with grief?
chapters.zh: 有谁软弱，我不软弱呢？有谁跌倒，我不焦急呢？

chapters.en: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.
chapters.zh: 我若必须自夸，就夸那关乎我软弱的事便了。

chapters.en: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is forever worthy of praise, knows that I am not lying.
chapters.zh: 那永远可称颂之主耶稣的父上帝知道我不说谎。

chapters.en: In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas secured the city of the Damascenes in order to arrest me.
chapters.zh: 在大马士革的亚哩达王手下的提督把守大马士革城，要捉拿我，

chapters.en: But I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped his grasp.
chapters.zh: 我就从窗户中，在筐子里，从城墙上被人缒下去，脱离了他的手。

chapters.en: I must go on boasting. Although there is nothing to gain, I will go on to visions and revelations from the Lord.
chapters.zh: 我自夸固然无益，但我是不得已的。如今我要说到主的显现和启示。

chapters.en: I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago was caught up to the third heaven. Whether it was in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows.
chapters.zh: 我认得一个在基督里的人，他前十四年被提到第三层天上去；（或在身内，我不知道；或在身外，我也不知道；只有上帝知道。）

chapters.en: And I know that this man—whether in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows—
chapters.zh: 我认得这人；（或在身内，或在身外，我都不知道，只有上帝知道。）

chapters.en: was caught up to Paradise. The things he heard were inexpressible, things that man is not permitted to tell.
chapters.zh: 他被提到乐园里，听见隐祕的言语，是人不可说的。

chapters.en: I will boast about such a man, but I will not boast about myself, except in my weaknesses.
chapters.zh: 为这人，我要夸口；但是为我自己，除了〔我的〕软弱以外，我并不夸口。

chapters.en: Even if I wanted to boast, I would not be a fool, because I would be speaking the truth. But I refrain, so no one will credit me with more than he sees in me or hears from me,
chapters.zh: 我就是愿意夸口也不算狂，因为我必说实话；只是我禁止不说，恐怕有人把我看高了，过于他在我身上所看见、所听见的。

chapters.en:
or because of these surpassingly great revelations.
So to keep me from becoming conceited, I was given a thorn in my flesh, a messenger of Satan, to torment me.
chapters.zh: 又恐怕我因所得的启示甚大，就过于自高，所以有一根刺加在我肉体上，就是撒但的差役要攻击我，免得我过于自高。

chapters.en: Three times I pleaded with the Lord to take it away from me.
chapters.zh: 为这事，我三次求过主，叫这刺离开我。

chapters.en: But He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.
chapters.zh: 他对我说：「我的恩典够你用的，因为我的能力是在人的软弱上显得完全。」所以，我更喜欢夸自己的软弱，好叫基督的能力覆庇我。

chapters.en: That is why, for the sake of Christ, I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties. For when I am weak, then I am strong.
chapters.zh: 我为基督的缘故，就以软弱、凌辱、急难、逼迫、困苦为可喜乐的；因我什么时候软弱，什么时候就刚强了。

chapters.en: I have become a fool, but you drove me to it. In fact, you should have commended me, since I am in no way inferior to those “super-apostles,” even though I am nothing.
chapters.zh: 我成了愚妄人，是被你们强逼的。我本该被你们称许才是。我虽算不了什么，却没有一件事在那些最大的使徒以下。

chapters.en: The marks of a true apostle—signs, wonders, and miracles—were performed among you with great perseverance.
chapters.zh: 我在你们中间，用百般的忍耐，藉着神迹、奇事、异能显出使徒的凭据来。

chapters.en: In what way were you inferior to the other churches, except that I was not a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!
chapters.zh: 除了我不累着你们这一件事，你们还有什么事不及别的教会呢？这不公之处，求你们饶恕我吧。

chapters.en: See, I am ready to come to you a third time, and I will not be a burden, because I am not seeking your possessions, but you. For children should not have to save up for their parents, but parents for their children.
chapters.zh: 如今，我打算第三次到你们那里去，也必不累着你们；因我所求的是你们，不是你们的〔财物〕。儿女不该为父母积财，父母该为儿女积财。

chapters.en: And for the sake of your souls, I will most gladly spend my money and myself. If I love you more, will you love me less?
chapters.zh: 我也甘心乐意为你们的灵魂费财费力。难道我越发爱你们，就越发少得你们的爱吗？

chapters.en: Be that as it may, I was not a burden to you; but crafty as I am, I caught you by trickery.
chapters.zh: 罢了，我自己并没有累着你们，〔你们却有人说〕，我是诡诈，用心计牢笼你们。

chapters.en: Did I exploit you by anyone I sent you?
chapters.zh: 我所差到你们那里去的人，我藉着他们一个人佔过你们的便宜吗？

chapters.en: I urged Titus to visit you, and I sent our brother with him. Did Titus exploit you in any way? Did we not walk in the same Spirit and follow in the same footsteps?
chapters.zh: 我劝了提多〔到你们那里去〕，又差那位兄弟与他同去。提多佔过你们的便宜吗？我们行事，不同是一个心灵〔注：或译：圣灵〕吗？不同是一个脚踪吗？

chapters.en: Have you been thinking all along that we were making a defense to you? We speak before God in Christ, and all of this, beloved, is to build you up.
chapters.zh: 你们到如今，还想我们是向你们分诉；我们本是在基督里当上帝面前说话。亲爱的〔弟兄〕啊，一切的事都是为造就你们。

chapters.en: For I am afraid that when I come, I may not find you as I wish, and you may not find me as you wish. I fear that there may be quarreling, jealousy, rage, rivalry, slander, gossip, arrogance, and disorder.
chapters.zh: 我怕我再来的时候，见你们不合我所想望的，你们见我也不合你们所想望的；又怕有纷争、嫉妒、恼怒、结党、毁谤、谗言、狂傲、混乱的事。

chapters.en: I am afraid that when I come again, my God will humble me before you, and I will be grieved over many who have sinned earlier and have not repented of their acts of impurity, sexual immorality, and debauchery.
chapters.zh: 且怕我来的时候，我的上帝叫我在你们面前惭愧，又因许多人从前犯罪，行污秽、奸淫、邪荡的事不肯悔改，我就忧愁。

chapters.en: This is the third time I am coming to you. “Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.”
chapters.zh: 这是我第三次要到你们那里去。「凭两三个人的口作见证，句句都要定准。」

chapters.en: I already warned you the second time I was with you. So now in my absence I warn those who sinned earlier and everyone else: If I return, I will not spare anyone,
chapters.zh: 我从前说过，如今不在你们那里又说，正如我第二次见你们的时候所说的一样，就是对那犯了罪的和其余的人说：「我若再来，必不宽容。」

chapters.en: since you are demanding proof that Christ is speaking through me. He is not weak in dealing with you but is powerful among you.
chapters.zh: 你们既然寻求基督在我里面说话的凭据，〔我必不宽容〕。因为，基督在你们身上不是软弱的，在你们里面是有大能的。

chapters.en: For He was indeed crucified in weakness, yet He lives by God’s power. For we are also weak in Him, yet by God’s power we will live with Him concerning you.
chapters.zh: 他因软弱被钉在十字架上，却因上帝的大能仍然活着。我们也是这样同他软弱，但因上帝向你们所显的大能，也必与他同活。

chapters.en: Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves. Do you not realize that Jesus Christ is in you—unless you fail the test?
chapters.zh: 你们总要自己省察有信心没有，也要自己试验。岂不知你们若不是可弃绝的，就有耶稣基督在你们心里吗？

chapters.en: And I hope you will realize that we have not failed the test.
chapters.zh: 我却盼望你们晓得，我们不是可弃绝的人。

chapters.en: Now we pray to God that you will not do anything wrong—not that we will appear to have stood the test, but that you will do what is right, even if we appear to have failed.
chapters.zh: 我们求上帝，叫你们一件恶事都不做；这不是要显明我们是蒙悦纳的，是要你们行事端正，任凭人看我们是被弃绝的吧！

chapters.en: For we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth.
chapters.zh: 我们凡事不能敌挡真理，只能扶助真理。

chapters.en: In fact, we rejoice when we are weak but you are strong, and our prayer is for your perfection.
chapters.zh: 即便我们软弱，你们刚强，我们也欢喜；并且我们所求的，就是你们作完全人。

chapters.en: This is why I write these things while absent, so that when I am present I will not need to be severe in my use of the authority that the Lord gave me for building you up, not for tearing you down.
chapters.zh: 所以，我不在你们那里的时候，把这话写给你们，好叫我见你们的时候，不用照主所给我的权柄严厉地待你们。这权柄原是为造就人，并不是为败坏人。

chapters.en: Finally, brothers, rejoice! Aim for perfect harmony, encourage one another, be of one mind, live in peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you.
chapters.zh: 还有末了的话：愿弟兄们都喜乐。要作完全人；要受安慰；要同心合意；要彼此和睦。如此，仁爱和平的上帝必常与你们同在。

chapters.en: Greet one another with a holy kiss.
chapters.zh: 你们亲嘴问安，彼此务要圣洁。

chapters.en: All the saints send you greetings.
chapters.zh: 众圣徒都问你们安。

chapters.en: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.
chapters.zh: 愿主耶稣基督的恩惠、上帝的慈爱、圣灵的感动〔常〕与你们众人同在！

chapters.en: Paul, an apostle—sent not from men nor by man, but by Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Him from the dead—
chapters.zh: 作使徒的保罗（不是由于人，也不是藉着人，乃是藉着耶稣基督，与叫他从死里复活的父上帝）

chapters.en:
and all the brothers with me,
To the churches of Galatia:
chapters.zh: 和一切与我同在的众弟兄，写信给加拉太的各教会。

chapters.en: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,
chapters.zh: 愿恩惠、平安从父上帝与我们的主耶稣基督归与你们！

chapters.en: who gave Himself for our sins to rescue us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,
chapters.zh: 基督照我们父上帝的旨意，为我们的罪舍己，要救我们脱离这罪恶的世代。

chapters.en: to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
chapters.zh: 但愿荣耀归于上帝，直到永永远远。阿们！

chapters.en: I am amazed how quickly you are deserting the One who called you by the grace of Christ and are turning to a different gospel—
chapters.zh: 我希奇你们这么快离开那藉着基督之恩召你们的，去从别的福音。

chapters.en: which is not even a gospel. Evidently some people are troubling you and trying to distort the gospel of Christ.
chapters.zh: 那并不是〔福音〕，不过有些人搅扰你们，要把基督的福音更改了。

chapters.en: But even if we or an angel from heaven should preach a gospel contrary to the one we preached to you, let him be under a curse!
chapters.zh: 但无论是我们，是天上来的使者，若传福音给你们，与我们所传给你们的不同，他就应当被咒诅。

chapters.en: As we have said before, so now I say again: If anyone is preaching to you a gospel contrary to the one you received, let him be under a curse!
chapters.zh: 我们已经说了，现在又说，若有人传福音给你们，与你们所领受的不同，他就应当被咒诅。

chapters.en: Am I now seeking the approval of men, or of God? Or am I striving to please men? If I were still trying to please men, I would not be a servant of Christ.
chapters.zh: 我现在是要得人的心呢？还是要得上帝的心呢？我岂是讨人的喜欢吗？若仍旧讨人的喜欢，我就不是基督的仆人了。

chapters.en: For I want you to know, brothers, that the gospel I preached was not devised by man.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我告诉你们，我素来所传的福音不是出于人的意思。

chapters.en: I did not receive it from any man, nor was I taught it; rather, I received it by revelation from Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 因为我不是从人领受的，也不是人教导我的，乃是从耶稣基督启示来的。

chapters.en: For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how severely I persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it.
chapters.zh: 你们听见我从前在犹太教中所行的事，怎样极力逼迫残害上帝的教会。

chapters.en: I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries and was extremely zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
chapters.zh: 我又在犹太教中，比我本国许多同岁的人更有长进，为我祖宗的遗传更加热心。

chapters.en: But when God, who set me apart from my mother’s womb and called me by His grace, was pleased
chapters.zh: 然而，那把我从母腹里分别出来、又施恩召我的上帝，

chapters.en: to reveal His Son in me so that I might preach Him among the Gentiles, I did not rush to consult with flesh and blood,
chapters.zh: 既然乐意将他儿子启示在我心里，叫我把他传在外邦人中，我就没有与属血气的人商量，

chapters.en: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to the apostles who came before me, but I went into Arabia and later returned to Damascus.
chapters.zh: 也没有上耶路撒冷去见那些比我先作使徒的，惟独往阿拉伯去，后又回到大马士革。

chapters.en: Only after three years did I go up to Jerusalem to confer with Cephas, and I stayed with him fifteen days.
chapters.zh: 过了三年，才上耶路撒冷去见矶法，和他同住了十五天。

chapters.en: But I saw none of the other apostles except James, the Lord’s brother.
chapters.zh: 至于别的使徒，除了主的兄弟雅各，我都没有看见。

chapters.en: I assure you before God that what I am writing to you is no lie.
chapters.zh: 我写给你们的不是谎话，这是我在上帝面前说的。

chapters.en: Later I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
chapters.zh: 以后我到了觜利亚和基利家境内。

chapters.en: I was personally unknown, however, to the churches of Judea that are in Christ.
chapters.zh: 那时，犹太信基督的各教会都没有见过我的面。

chapters.en: They only heard the account: “The man who formerly persecuted us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy.”
chapters.zh: 不过听说那从前逼迫我们的，现在传扬他原先所残害的真道。

chapters.en: And they glorified God because of me.
chapters.zh: 他们就为我的缘故，归荣耀给上帝。

chapters.en: Fourteen years later I went up again to Jerusalem, accompanied by Barnabas. I took Titus along also.
chapters.zh: 过了十四年，我同巴拿巴又上耶路撒冷去，并带着提多同去。

chapters.en: I went in response to a revelation and set before them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles. But I spoke privately to those recognized as leaders, for fear that I was running or had already run in vain.
chapters.zh: 我是奉启示上去的，把我在外邦人中所传的福音对弟兄们陈说；却是背地里对那有名望之人说的，惟恐我现在，或是从前，徒然奔跑。

chapters.en: Yet not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised, even though he was a Greek.
chapters.zh: 但与我同去的提多，虽是希腊人，也没有勉强他受割礼；

chapters.en: This issue arose because some false brothers had come in under false pretenses to spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus, in order to enslave us.
chapters.zh: 因为有偷着引进来的假弟兄，私下窥探我们在基督耶稣里的自由，要叫我们作奴仆。

chapters.en: We did not give in to them for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel would remain with you.
chapters.zh: 我们就是一刻的工夫也没有容让顺服他们，为要叫福音的真理仍存在你们中间。

chapters.en: But as for the highly esteemed—whatever they were makes no difference to me; God does not show favoritism —those leaders added nothing to me.
chapters.zh: 至于那些有名望的，不论他是何等人，都与我无干。上帝不以外貌取人。那些有名望的，并没有加增我什么，

chapters.en: On the contrary, they saw that I had been entrusted to preach the gospel to the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been to the circumcised.
chapters.zh: 反倒看见了主讬我传福音给那未受割礼的人，正如讬彼得传福音给那受割礼的人。

chapters.en: For the One who was at work in Peter’s apostleship to the circumcised was also at work in my apostleship to the Gentiles.
chapters.zh: （那感动彼得、叫他为受割礼之人作使徒的，也感动我，叫我为外邦人作使徒；）

chapters.en: And recognizing the grace that I had been given, James, Cephas, and John—those reputed to be pillars—gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, so that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.
chapters.zh: 又知道所赐给我的恩典，那称为〔教会〕柱石的雅各、矶法、约翰，就向我和巴拿巴用右手行相交之礼，叫我们往外邦人那里去，他们往受割礼的人那里去。

chapters.en: They only asked us to remember the poor, the very thing I was eager to do.
chapters.zh: 只是愿意我们记念穷人；这也是我本来热心去行的。

chapters.en: When Cephas came to Antioch, however, I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned.
chapters.zh: 后来，矶法到了安提阿；因他有可责之处，我就当面抵挡他。

chapters.en: For before certain men came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they arrived, he began to draw back and separate himself, for fear of those in the circumcision group.
chapters.zh: 从雅各那里来的人未到以先，他和外邦人一同吃饭，及至他们来到，他因怕奉割礼的人，就退去与外邦人隔开了。

chapters.en: The other Jews joined him in his hypocrisy, so that by their hypocrisy even Barnabas was led astray.
chapters.zh: 其余的犹太人也都随着他装假，甚至连巴拿巴也随伙装假。

chapters.en: When I saw that they were not walking in line with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of them all, “If you, who are a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?”
chapters.zh: 但我一看见他们行的不正，与福音的真理不合，就在众人面前对矶法说：「你既是犹太人，若随外邦人行事，不随犹太人行事，怎么还勉强外邦人随犹太人呢？」

chapters.en: We who are Jews by birth and not Gentile “sinners”
chapters.zh: 我们这生来的犹太人，不是外邦的罪人；

chapters.en: know that a man is not justified by works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ. So we, too, have believed in Christ Jesus, that we may be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no one will be justified.
chapters.zh: 既知道人称义不是因行律法，乃是因信耶稣基督，连我们也信了基督耶稣，使我们因信基督称义，不因行律法称义；因为凡有血气的，没有一人因行律法称义。

chapters.en: But if, while we seek to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, does that make Christ a minister of sin? Certainly not!
chapters.zh: 我们若求在基督里称义，却仍旧是罪人，难道基督是叫人犯罪的吗？断乎不是！

chapters.en: If I rebuild what I have already torn down, I prove myself to be a lawbreaker.
chapters.zh: 我素来所拆毁的，若重新建造，这就证明自己是犯罪的人。

chapters.en: For through the law I died to the law so that I might live to God.
chapters.zh: 我因律法，就向律法死了，叫我可以向上帝活着。

chapters.en: I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I live in the body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself up for me.
chapters.zh: 我已经与基督同钉十字架，现在活着的不再是我，乃是基督在我里面活着；并且我如今在肉身活着，是因信上帝的儿子而活；他是爱我，为我舍己。

chapters.en: I do not set aside the grace of God. For if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died for nothing.
chapters.zh: 我不废掉上帝的恩；义若是藉着律法得的，基督就是徒然死了。

chapters.en: O foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you? Before your very eyes Jesus Christ was clearly portrayed as crucified.
chapters.zh: 无知的加拉太人哪，耶稣基督钉十字架，已经活画在你们眼前，谁又迷惑了你们呢？

chapters.en: I would like to learn just one thing from you: Did you receive the Spirit by works of the law, or by hearing with faith?
chapters.zh: 我只要问你们这一件：你们受了〔圣〕灵，是因行律法呢？是因听信〔福音〕呢？

chapters.en: Are you so foolish? After starting in the Spirit, are you now finishing in the flesh?
chapters.zh: 你们既靠〔圣〕灵入门，如今还靠肉身成全吗？你们是这样的无知吗？

chapters.en: Have you suffered so much for nothing, if it really was for nothing?
chapters.zh: 你们受苦如此之多，都是徒然的吗？难道果真是徒然的吗？

chapters.en: Does God lavish His Spirit on you and work miracles among you because you practice the law, or because you hear and believe?
chapters.zh: 那赐给你们〔圣〕灵，又在你们中间行异能的，是因你们行律法呢？是因你们听信〔福音〕呢？

chapters.en: So also, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”
chapters.zh: 正如「亚伯拉罕信上帝，这就算为他的义」。

chapters.en: Understand, then, that those who have faith are sons of Abraham.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们要知道：那以信为本的人，就是亚伯拉罕的子孙。

chapters.en: The Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, and foretold the gospel to Abraham: “All nations will be blessed through you.”
chapters.zh: 并且圣经既然预先看明，上帝要叫外邦人因信称义，就早已传福音给亚伯拉罕，〔说〕：「万国都必因你得福。」

chapters.en: So those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.
chapters.zh: 可见那以信为本的人和有信心的亚伯拉罕一同得福。

chapters.en: All who rely on works of the law are under a curse. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who does not continue to do everything written in the Book of the Law.”
chapters.zh: 凡以行律法为本的，都是被咒诅的；因为〔经上〕记着：「凡不常照律法书上所记一切之事去行的，就被咒诅。」

chapters.en: Now it is clear that no one is justified before God by the law, because, “The righteous will live by faith.”
chapters.zh: 没有一个人靠着律法在上帝面前称义，这是明显的；因为〔经上〕说：「义人必因信得生。」

chapters.en: The law, however, is not based on faith; on the contrary, “The man who does these things will live by them.”
chapters.zh: 律法原不本乎信，只〔说〕：「行这些事的，就必因此活着。」

chapters.en: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. For it is written: “Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree.”
chapters.zh: 基督既为我们受〔注：原文是成〕了咒诅，就赎出我们脱离律法的咒诅；因为〔经上〕记着：「凡挂在木头上都是被咒诅的。」

chapters.en: He redeemed us in order that the blessing promised to Abraham would come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, so that by faith we might receive the promise of the Spirit.
chapters.zh: 这便叫亚伯拉罕的福，因基督耶稣可以临到外邦人，使我们因信得着所应许的〔圣〕灵。

chapters.en: Brothers, let me put this in human terms. Even a human covenant, once it is ratified, cannot be canceled or amended.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我且照着人的常话说：虽然是人的文约，若已经立定了，就没有能废弃或加增的。

chapters.en: The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. The Scripture does not say, “and to seeds,” meaning many, but “and to your seed,” meaning One, who is Christ.
chapters.zh: 所应许的原是向亚伯拉罕和他子孙说的。上帝并不是说「众子孙」，指着许多人，乃是说「你那一个子孙」，指着一个人，就是基督。

chapters.en: What I mean is this: The law that came 430 years later does not revoke the covenant previously established by God, so as to nullify the promise.
chapters.zh: 我是这么说，上帝预先所立的约，不能被那四百三十年以后的律法废掉，叫应许归于虚空。

chapters.en: For if the inheritance depends on the law, then it no longer depends on a promise; but God freely granted it to Abraham through a promise.
chapters.zh: 因为承受产业，若本乎律法，就不本乎应许；但上帝是凭着应许把产业赐给亚伯拉罕。

chapters.en: Why then was the law given? It was added because of transgressions, until the arrival of the seed to whom the promise referred. It was administered through angels by a mediator.
chapters.zh: 这样说来，律法是为什么有的呢？原是为过犯添上的，等候那蒙应许的子孙来到，并且是藉天使经中保之手设立的。

chapters.en: A mediator is unnecessary, however, for only one party; but God is one.
chapters.zh: 但中保本不是为一面作的；上帝却是一位。

chapters.en: Is the law, then, opposed to the promises of God? Certainly not! For if a law had been given that could impart life, then righteousness would certainly have come from the law.
chapters.zh: 这样，律法是与上帝的应许反对吗？断乎不是！若曾传一个能叫人得生的律法，义就诚然本乎律法了。

chapters.en: But the Scripture pronounces all things confined by sin, so that by faith in Jesus Christ the promise might be given to those who believe.
chapters.zh: 但圣经把众人都圈在罪里，使所应许的〔福〕因信耶稣基督，归给那信的人。

chapters.en: Before this faith came, we were held in custody under the law, locked up until faith should be revealed.
chapters.zh: 但这〔因〕信〔得救的理〕还未来以先，我们被看守在律法之下，直圈到那将来的真道显明出来。

chapters.en: So the law became our guardian to lead us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith.
chapters.zh: 这样，律法是我们训蒙的师傅，〔引我们〕到基督那里，使我们因信称义。

chapters.en: Now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.
chapters.zh: 但这〔因〕信〔得救的理〕既然来到，我们从此就不在师傅的手下了。

chapters.en: You are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们因信基督耶稣都是上帝的儿子。

chapters.en: For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
chapters.zh: 你们受洗归入基督的都是披戴基督了。

chapters.en: There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 并不分犹太人、希腊人，自主的、为奴的，或男或女，因为你们在基督耶稣里都成为一了。

chapters.en: And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s seed and heirs according to the promise.
chapters.zh: 你们既属乎基督，就是亚伯拉罕的后裔，是照着应许承受产业的了。

chapters.en: What I am saying is that as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave, although he is the owner of everything.
chapters.zh: 我说那承受产业的，虽然是全业的主人，但为孩童的时候却与奴仆毫无分别，

chapters.en: He is subject to guardians and trustees until the date set by his father.
chapters.zh: 乃在师傅和管家的手下，直等他父亲预定的时候来到。

chapters.en: So also, when we were children, we were enslaved under the basic principles of the world.
chapters.zh: 我们为孩童的时候，受管于世俗小学之下，也是如此。

chapters.en: But when the time had fully come, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
chapters.zh: 及至时候满足，上帝就差遣他的儿子，为女子所生，且生在律法以下，

chapters.en: to redeem those under the law, that we might receive our adoption as sons.
chapters.zh: 要把律法以下的人赎出来，叫我们得着儿子的名分。

chapters.en: And because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, “Abba, Father!”
chapters.zh: 你们既为儿子，上帝就差他儿子的灵进入你们〔注：原文是我们〕的心，呼叫：「阿爸！父！」

chapters.en: So you are no longer a slave, but a son; and since you are a son, you are also an heir through God.
chapters.zh: 可见，从此以后，你不是奴仆，乃是儿子了；既是儿子，就靠着上帝为后嗣。

chapters.en: Formerly, when you did not know God, you were slaves to those who by nature are not gods.
chapters.zh: 但从前你们不认识上帝的时候，是给那些本来不是神的作奴仆；

chapters.en: But now that you know God, or rather are known by God, how is it that you are turning back to those weak and worthless principles? Do you wish to be enslaved by them all over again?
chapters.zh: 现在你们既然认识上帝，更可说是被上帝所认识的，怎么还要归回那懦弱无用的小学，情愿再给他作奴仆呢？

chapters.en: You are observing special days and months and seasons and years!
chapters.zh: 你们谨守日子、月份、节期、年份，

chapters.en: I fear for you, that my efforts for you may have been in vain.
chapters.zh: 我为你们害怕，惟恐我在你们身上是枉费了工夫。

chapters.en: I beg you, brothers, become like me, for I became like you. You have done me no wrong.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我劝你们要像我一样，因为我也像你们一样。你们一点没有亏负我。

chapters.en: You know that it was because of an illness that I first preached the gospel to you.
chapters.zh: 你们知道我头一次传福音给你们，是因为身体有疾病。

chapters.en: And although my illness was a trial to you, you did not despise or reject me. Instead, you welcomed me as if I were an angel of God, as if I were Christ Jesus Himself.
chapters.zh: 你们为我身体的缘故受试炼，没有轻看我，也没有厌弃我，反倒接待我，如同上帝的使者，如同基督耶稣。

chapters.en: What then has become of your blessing? For I can testify that, if it were possible, you would have torn out your eyes and given them to me.
chapters.zh: 你们当日所夸的福气在哪里呢？那时你们若能行，就是把自己的眼睛剜出来给我，也都情愿。这是我可以给你们作见证的。

chapters.en: Have I now become your enemy by telling you the truth?
chapters.zh: 如今我将真理告诉你们，就成了你们的仇敌吗？

chapters.en: Those people are zealous for you, but not in a good way. Instead, they want to isolate you from us, so that you may be zealous for them.
chapters.zh: 那些人热心待你们，却不是好意，是要离间你们〔注：原文是把你们关在外面〕，叫你们热心待他们。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, it is good to be zealous if it serves a noble purpose—at any time, and not only when I am with you.
chapters.zh: 在善事上，常用热心待人原是好的，却不单我与你们同在的时候才这样。

chapters.en: My children, for whom I am again in the pains of childbirth until Christ is formed in you,
chapters.zh: 我小子啊，我为你们再受生产之苦，直等到基督成形在你们心里。

chapters.en: how I wish I could be with you now and change my tone, because I am perplexed about you.
chapters.zh: 我巴不得现今在你们那里，改换口气，因我为你们心里作难。

chapters.en: Tell me, you who want to be under the law, do you not understand what the law says?
chapters.zh: 你们这愿意在律法以下的人，请告诉我，你们岂没有听见律法吗？

chapters.en: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and the other by the free woman.
chapters.zh: 因为〔律法上〕记着，亚伯拉罕有两个儿子，一个是使女生的，一个是自主之妇人生的。

chapters.en: His son by the slave woman was born according to the flesh, but his son by the free woman was born through the promise.
chapters.zh: 然而，那使女所生的是按着血气生的；那自主之妇人所生的是凭着应许生的。

chapters.en: These things serve as illustrations, for the women represent two covenants. One covenant is from Mount Sinai and bears children into slavery: This is Hagar.
chapters.zh: 这都是比方：那两个妇人就是两约。一约是出于西奈山，生子为奴，乃是夏甲。

chapters.en: Now Hagar stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia and corresponds to the present-day Jerusalem, because she is in slavery with her children.
chapters.zh: 这夏甲二字是指着阿拉伯的西奈山，与现在的耶路撒冷同类，因耶路撒冷和她的儿女都是为奴的。

chapters.en: But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother.
chapters.zh: 但那在上的耶路撒冷是自主的，她是我们的母。

chapters.en:
For it is written:
“Rejoice, O barren woman, who bears no children; break forth and cry aloud, you who have never travailed; because more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has a husband.”
chapters.zh: 因为〔经上〕记着： 不怀孕、不生养的，你要欢乐； 未曾经过产难的，你要高声欢呼； 因为没有丈夫的，比有丈夫的儿女更多。

chapters.en: Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of promise.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我们是凭着应许作儿女，如同以撒一样。

chapters.en: At that time, however, the son born by the flesh persecuted the son born by the Spirit. It is the same now.
chapters.zh: 当时，那按着血气生的逼迫了那按着〔圣〕灵生的，现在也是这样。

chapters.en: But what does the Scripture say? “Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with the free woman’s son.”
chapters.zh: 然而经上是怎么说的呢？〔是说〕：「把使女和她儿子赶出去！因为使女的儿子不可与自主妇人的儿子一同承受产业。」

chapters.en: Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，这样看来，我们不是使女的儿女，乃是自主妇人的儿女了。

chapters.en: It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery.
chapters.zh: 基督释放了我们，叫我们得以自由。所以要站立得稳，不要再被奴仆的轭挟制。

chapters.en: Take notice: I, Paul, tell you that if you let yourselves be circumcised, Christ will be of no value to you at all.
chapters.zh: 我－保罗告诉你们，若受割礼，基督就与你们无益了。

chapters.en: Again I testify to every man who gets himself circumcised that he is obligated to obey the whole law.
chapters.zh: 我再指着凡受割礼的人确实地说，他是欠着行全律法的债。

chapters.en: You who are trying to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ; you have fallen away from grace.
chapters.zh: 你们这要靠律法称义的，是与基督隔绝，从恩典中坠落了。

chapters.en: But by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness.
chapters.zh: 我们靠着〔圣〕灵，凭着信心，等候所盼望的义。

chapters.en: For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value. What matters is faith expressing itself through love.
chapters.zh: 原来在基督耶稣里，受割礼不受割礼全无功效，惟独使人生发仁爱的信心才有功效。

chapters.en: You were running so well. Who has obstructed you from obeying the truth?
chapters.zh: 你们向来跑得好，有谁拦阻你们，叫你们不顺从真理呢？

chapters.en: Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you.
chapters.zh: 这样的劝导不是出于那召你们的。

chapters.en: A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough.
chapters.zh: 一点面酵能使全团都发起来。

chapters.en: I am confident in the Lord that you will take no other view. The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be.
chapters.zh: 我在主里很信你们必不怀别样的心；但搅扰你们的，无论是谁，必担当他的罪名。

chapters.en: Now, brothers, if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? In that case the offense of the cross has been abolished.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我若仍旧传割礼，为什么还受逼迫呢？若是这样，那十字架讨厌的地方就没有了。

chapters.en: As for those who are agitating you, I wish they would proceed to emasculate themselves!
chapters.zh: 恨不得那搅乱你们的人把自己割绝了。

chapters.en: For you, brothers, were called to freedom; but do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh. Rather, serve one another in love.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，你们蒙召是要得自由，只是不可将你们的自由当作放纵情欲的机会，总要用爱心互相服事。

chapters.en: The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: “Love your neighbor as yourself.”
chapters.zh: 因为全律法都包在「爱人如己」这一句话之内了。

chapters.en: But if you keep on biting and devouring one another, watch out, or you will be consumed by one another.
chapters.zh: 你们要谨慎，若相咬相吞，只怕要彼此消灭了。

chapters.en: So I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh.
chapters.zh: 我说，你们当顺着〔圣〕灵而行，就不放纵肉体的情欲了。

chapters.en: For the flesh craves what is contrary to the Spirit, and the Spirit what is contrary to the flesh. They are opposed to each other, so that you do not do what you want.
chapters.zh: 因为情欲和〔圣〕灵相争，〔圣〕灵和情欲相争，这两个是彼此相敌，使你们不能做所愿意做的。

chapters.en: But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law.
chapters.zh: 但你们若被〔圣〕灵引导，就不在律法以下。

chapters.en: The acts of the flesh are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity, and debauchery;
chapters.zh: 情欲的事都是显而易见的，就如奸淫、污秽、邪荡、

chapters.en: idolatry and sorcery; hatred, discord, jealousy, and rage; rivalries, divisions, factions,
chapters.zh: 拜偶像、邪术、仇恨、争竞、忌恨、恼怒、结党、纷争、异端、

chapters.en: and envy; drunkenness, orgies, and the like. I warn you, as I did before, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
chapters.zh: 嫉妒〔注：有古卷加：凶杀二字〕、醉酒、荒宴等类。我从前告诉你们，现在又告诉你们，行这样事的人必不能承受上帝的国。

chapters.en: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
chapters.zh: 圣灵所结的果子，就是仁爱、喜乐、和平、忍耐、恩慈、良善、信实、

chapters.en: gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
chapters.zh: 温柔、节制。这样的事没有律法禁止。

chapters.en: Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
chapters.zh: 凡属基督耶稣的人，是已经把肉体连肉体的邪情私欲同钉在十字架上了。

chapters.en: Since we live by the Spirit, let us walk in step with the Spirit.
chapters.zh: 我们若是靠〔圣〕灵得生，就当靠〔圣〕灵行事。

chapters.en: Let us not become conceited, provoking and envying one another.
chapters.zh: 不要贪图虚名，彼此惹气，互相嫉妒。

chapters.en: Brothers, if someone is caught in a trespass, you who are spiritual should restore him with a spirit of gentleness. But watch yourself, or you also may be tempted.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，若有人偶然被过犯所胜，你们属灵的人就当用温柔的心把他挽回过来；又当自己小心，恐怕也被引诱。

chapters.en: Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
chapters.zh: 你们各人的重担要互相担当，如此，就完全了基督的律法。

chapters.en: If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
chapters.zh: 人若无有，自己还以为有，就是自欺了。

chapters.en: Each one should test his own work. Then he will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not in someone else.
chapters.zh: 各人应当察验自己的行为；这样，他所夸的就专在自己，不在别人了，

chapters.en: For each one should carry his own load.
chapters.zh: 因为各人必担当自己的担子。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, the one who receives instruction in the word must share in all good things with his instructor.
chapters.zh: 在道理上受教的，当把一切需用的供给施教的人。

chapters.en: Do not be deceived: God is not to be mocked. Whatever a man sows, he will reap in return.
chapters.zh: 不要自欺，上帝是轻慢不得的。人种的是什么，收的也是什么。

chapters.en: The one who sows to please his flesh, from the flesh will reap destruction; but the one who sows to please the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal life.
chapters.zh: 顺着情欲撒种的，必从情欲收败坏；顺着〔圣〕灵撒种的，必从〔圣〕灵收永生。

chapters.en: Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.
chapters.zh: 我们行善，不可丧志；若不灰心，到了时候就要收成。

chapters.en: Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, and especially to the family of faith.
chapters.zh: 所以，有了机会就当向众人行善，向信徒一家的人更当这样。

chapters.en: See what large letters I am using to write to you with my own hand!
chapters.zh: 请看我亲手写给你们的字是何等的大呢！

chapters.en: Those who want to make a good impression outwardly are trying to compel you to be circumcised. They only do this to avoid persecution for the cross of Christ.
chapters.zh: 凡希图外貌体面的人都勉强你们受割礼，无非是怕自己为基督的十字架受逼迫。

chapters.en: For the circumcised do not even keep the law themselves, yet they want you to be circumcised that they may boast in your flesh.
chapters.zh: 他们那些受割礼的，连自己也不守律法；他们愿意你们受割礼，不过要藉着你们的肉体夸口。

chapters.en: But as for me, may I never boast, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
chapters.zh: 但我断不以别的夸口，只夸我们主耶稣基督的十字架；因这十字架，就我而论，世界已经钉在十字架上；就世界而论，我已经钉在十字架上。

chapters.en: For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything. What counts is a new creation.
chapters.zh: 受割礼不受割礼都无关紧要，要紧的就是作新造的人。

chapters.en: Peace and mercy to all who walk by this rule, even to the Israel of God.
chapters.zh: 凡照此理而行的，愿平安、怜悯加给他们，和上帝的以色列民。

chapters.en: From now on let no one cause me trouble, for I bear on my body the marks of Jesus.
chapters.zh: 从今以后，人都不要搅扰我，因为我身上带着耶稣的印记。

chapters.en:
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers.
Amen.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，愿我主耶稣基督的恩〔常〕在你们心里。阿们！

chapters.en:
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God,
To the saints in Ephesus, the faithful in Christ Jesus:
chapters.zh: 奉上帝旨意，作基督耶稣使徒的保罗，写信给在以弗所的圣徒，就是在基督耶稣里有忠心的人。

chapters.en: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 愿恩惠、平安从上帝我们的父和主耶稣基督归与你们！

chapters.en: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly realms.
chapters.zh: 愿颂赞归与我们主耶稣基督的父上帝！他在基督里曾赐给我们天上各样属灵的福气：

chapters.en: For He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless in His presence. In love
chapters.zh: 就如上帝从创立世界以前，在基督里拣选了我们，使我们在他面前成为圣洁，无有瑕疵；

chapters.en: He predestined us for adoption as His sons through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of His will,
chapters.zh: 又因爱我们，就按着自己的意旨所喜悦的，预定我们藉着耶稣基督得儿子的名分，

chapters.en: to the praise of His glorious grace, which He has freely given us in the Beloved One.
chapters.zh: 使他荣耀的恩典得着称赞；这恩典是他在爱子里所赐给我们的。

chapters.en: In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of His grace
chapters.zh: 我们藉这爱子的血得蒙救赎，过犯得以赦免，乃是照他丰富的恩典。

chapters.en: that He lavished on us with all wisdom and understanding.
chapters.zh: 这恩典是上帝用诸般智慧聪明，充充足足赏给我们的；

chapters.en: And He has made known to us the mystery of His will according to His good pleasure, which He purposed in Christ
chapters.zh: 都是照他自己所预定的美意，叫我们知道他旨意的奥祕，

chapters.en: as a plan for the fullness of time, to bring all things in heaven and on earth together in Christ.
chapters.zh: 要照所安排的，在日期满足的时候，使天上、地上、一切所有的都在基督里面同归于一。

chapters.en: In Him we were also chosen as God’s own, having been predestined according to the plan of Him who works out everything by the counsel of His will,
chapters.zh: 我们也在他里面得〔注：得：或译成〕了基业；这原是那位随己意行、做万事的，照着他旨意所预定的，

chapters.en: in order that we, who were the first to hope in Christ, would be for the praise of His glory.
chapters.zh: 叫他的荣耀从我们这首先在基督里有盼望的人可以得着称赞。

chapters.en: And in Him, having heard and believed the word of truth—the gospel of your salvation—you were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit,
chapters.zh: 你们既听见真理的道，就是那叫你们得救的福音，也〔信了〕基督，既然信他，就受了所应许的圣灵为印记。

chapters.en: who is the pledge of our inheritance until the redemption of those who are God’s possession, to the praise of His glory.
chapters.zh: 这圣灵是我们得基业的凭据〔注：原文是质〕，直等到〔上帝〕之民〔注：民：原文是产业〕被赎，使他的荣耀得着称赞。

chapters.en: For this reason, ever since I heard about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints,
chapters.zh: 因此，我既听见你们信从主耶稣，亲爱众圣徒，

chapters.en: I have not stopped giving thanks for you, remembering you in my prayers,
chapters.zh: 就为你们不住地感谢上帝。祷告的时候，常提到你们，

chapters.en: that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the glorious Father, may give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in your knowledge of Him.
chapters.zh: 求我们主耶稣基督的上帝，荣耀的父，将那赐人智慧和启示的灵赏给你们，使你们真知道他，

chapters.en: I ask that the eyes of your heart may be enlightened, so that you may know the hope of His calling, the riches of His glorious inheritance in the saints,
chapters.zh: 并且照明你们心中的眼睛，使你们知道他的恩召有何等指望，他在圣徒中得的基业有何等丰盛的荣耀；

chapters.en: and the surpassing greatness of His power to us who believe. These are in accordance with the working of His mighty strength,
chapters.zh: 并〔知道〕他向我们这信的人所显的能力是何等浩大，

chapters.en: which He exerted in Christ when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly realms,
chapters.zh: 就是照他在基督身上所运行的大能大力，使他从死里复活，叫他在天上坐在自己的右边，

chapters.en: far above all rule and authority, power and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in the present age but also in the one to come.
chapters.zh: 远超过一切执政的、掌权的、有能的、主治的，和一切有名的；不但是今世的，连来世的也都超过了。

chapters.en: And God put everything under His feet and made Him head over everything for the church,
chapters.zh: 又将万有服在他的脚下，使他为教会作万有之首。

chapters.en: which is His body, the fullness of Him who fills all in all.
chapters.zh: 教会是他的身体，是那充满万有者所充满的。

chapters.en: And you were dead in your trespasses and sins,
chapters.zh: 你们死在过犯罪恶之中，〔他叫你们活过来〕。

chapters.en: in which you used to walk when you conformed to the ways of this world and of the ruler of the power of the air, the spirit who is now at work in the sons of disobedience.
chapters.zh: 那时，你们在其中行事为人，随从今世的风俗，顺服空中掌权者的首领，就是现今在悖逆之子心中运行的〔邪〕灵。

chapters.en: All of us also lived among them at one time, fulfilling the cravings of our flesh and indulging its desires and thoughts. Like the rest, we were by nature children of wrath.
chapters.zh: 我们从前也都在他们中间，放纵肉体的私欲，随着肉体和心中所喜好的去行，本为可怒之子，和别人一样。

chapters.en: But because of His great love for us, God, who is rich in mercy,
chapters.zh: 然而，上帝既有丰富的怜悯，因他爱我们的大爱，

chapters.en: made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in our trespasses. It is by grace you have been saved!
chapters.zh: 当我们死在过犯中的时候，便叫我们与基督一同活过来。你们得救是本乎恩。

chapters.en: And God raised us up with Christ and seated us with Him in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus,
chapters.zh: 他又叫我们与基督耶稣一同复活，一同坐在天上，

chapters.en: in order that in the coming ages He might display the surpassing riches of His grace, demonstrated by His kindness to us in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 要将他极丰富的恩典，就是他在基督耶稣里向我们所施的恩慈，显明给后来的世代看。

chapters.en: For it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God,
chapters.zh: 你们得救是本乎恩，也因着信；这并不是出于自己，乃是上帝所赐的；

chapters.en: not by works, so that no one can boast.
chapters.zh: 也不是出于行为，免得有人自夸。

chapters.en: For we are God’s workmanship, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance as our way of life.
chapters.zh: 我们原是他的工作，在基督耶稣里造成的，为要叫我们行善，就是上帝所预备叫我们行的。

chapters.en: Therefore remember that formerly you who are Gentiles in the flesh and called uncircumcised by the so-called circumcision (that done in the body by human hands)—
chapters.zh: 所以你们应当记念：你们从前按肉体是外邦人，是称为没受割礼的；这名原是那些凭人手在肉身上称为受割礼之人所起的。

chapters.en: remember that at that time you were separate from Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers to the covenants of the promise, without hope and without God in the world.
chapters.zh: 那时，你们与基督无关，在以色列国民以外，在所应许的诸约上是局外人，并且〔活〕在世上没有指望，没有上帝。

chapters.en: But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far away have been brought near through the blood of Christ.
chapters.zh: 你们从前远离〔上帝〕的人，如今却在基督耶稣里，靠着他的血，已经得亲近了。

chapters.en: For He Himself is our peace, who has made the two one and has torn down the dividing wall of hostility
chapters.zh: 因他使我们和睦〔注：原文是因他是我们的和睦〕，将两下合而为一，拆毁了中间隔断的墙；

chapters.en: by abolishing in His flesh the law of commandments and decrees. He did this to create in Himself one new man out of the two, thus making peace
chapters.zh: 而且以自己的身体废掉冤仇，就是那〔记〕在律法上的规条，为要将两下藉着自己造成一个新人，〔如此〕便成就了和睦。

chapters.en: and reconciling both of them to God in one body through the cross, by which He put to death their hostility.
chapters.zh: 既在十字架上灭了冤仇，便藉这十字架使两下归为一体，与上帝和好了，

chapters.en: He came and preached peace to you who were far away and peace to those who were near.
chapters.zh: 并且来传和平的福音给你们远处的人，也给那近处的人。

chapters.en: For through Him we both have access to the Father by one Spirit.
chapters.zh: 因为我们两下藉着他被一个〔圣〕灵所感，得以进到父面前。

chapters.en: Therefore you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of God’s household,
chapters.zh: 这样，你们不再作外人和客旅，是与圣徒同国，是上帝家里的人了；

chapters.en: built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus Himself as the cornerstone.
chapters.zh: 并且被建造在使徒和先知的根基上，有基督耶稣自己为房角石，

chapters.en: In Him the whole building is fitted together and grows into a holy temple in the Lord.
chapters.zh: 各〔注：或译：全〕房靠他联络得合式，渐渐成为主的圣殿。

chapters.en: And in Him you too are being built together into a dwelling place for God in His Spirit.
chapters.zh: 你们也靠他同被建造，成为上帝藉着圣灵居住的所在。

chapters.en: For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for the sake of you Gentiles...
