chapters.zh: 又愿女人廉耻、自守，以正派衣裳为妆饰，不以编发、黄金、珍珠，和贵价的衣裳为妆饰，

chapters.en: but with good deeds, as is proper for women who profess to worship God.
chapters.zh: 只要有善行，这才与自称是敬上帝的女人相宜。

chapters.en: A woman must learn in quietness and full submissiveness.
chapters.zh: 女人要沉静学道，一味地顺服。

chapters.en: I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man; she is to remain quiet.
chapters.zh: 我不许女人讲道，也不许她辖管男人，只要沉静。

chapters.en: For Adam was formed first, and then Eve.
chapters.zh: 因为先造的是亚当，后造的是夏娃，

chapters.en: And it was not Adam who was deceived, but the woman who was deceived and fell into transgression.
chapters.zh: 且不是亚当被引诱，乃是女人被引诱，陷在罪里。

chapters.en: Women, however, will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith, love, and holiness, with self-control.
chapters.zh: 然而，女人若常存信心、爱心，又圣洁自守，就必在生产上得救。

chapters.en: This is a trustworthy saying: If anyone aspires to be an overseer, he desires a noble task.
chapters.zh: 「人若想要得监督的职分，就是羨慕善工。」 这话是可信的。

chapters.en: An overseer, then, must be above reproach, the husband of but one wife, temperate, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach,
chapters.zh: 作监督的，必须无可指责，只作一个妇人的丈夫，有节制，自守，端正，乐意接待远人，善于教导；

chapters.en: not dependent on wine, not violent but gentle, peaceable, and free of the love of money.
chapters.zh: 不因酒滋事，不打人，只要温和，不争竞，不贪财；

chapters.en: An overseer must manage his own household well and keep his children under control, with complete dignity.
chapters.zh: 好好管理自己的家，使儿女凡事端庄顺服〔注：或译：端端庄庄地使儿女顺服〕。

chapters.en: For if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how can he care for the church of God?
chapters.zh: 人若不知道管理自己的家，焉能照管上帝的教会呢？

chapters.en: He must not be a recent convert, or he may become conceited and fall under the same condemnation as the devil.
chapters.zh: 初入教的不可作监督，恐怕他自高自大，就落在魔鬼〔所受〕的刑罚里。

chapters.en: Furthermore, he must have a good reputation with outsiders, so that he will not fall into disgrace and into the snare of the devil.
chapters.zh: 监督也必须在教外有好名声，恐怕被人毁谤，落在魔鬼的网罗里。

chapters.en: Deacons likewise must be dignified, not double-tongued or given to much wine or greedy for money.
chapters.zh: 作执事的，也是如此：必须端庄，不一口两舌，不好喝酒，不贪不义之财；

chapters.en: They must hold to the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.
chapters.zh: 要存清洁的良心，固守真道的奥祕。

chapters.en: Additionally, they must first be tested. Then, if they are above reproach, let them serve as deacons.
chapters.zh: 这等人也要先受试验，若没有可责之处，然后叫他们作执事。

chapters.en: In the same way, the women must be dignified, not slanderers, but temperate and faithful in all things.
chapters.zh: 女执事〔注：原文是女人〕也是如此：必须端庄，不说谗言，有节制，凡事忠心。

chapters.en: A deacon must be the husband of but one wife, a good manager of his children and of his own household.
chapters.zh: 执事只要作一个妇人的丈夫，好好管理儿女和自己的家。

chapters.en: For those who have served well as deacons acquire for themselves a high standing and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 因为善作执事的，自己就得到美好的地步，并且在基督耶稣里的真道上大有胆量。

chapters.en: Although I hope to come to you soon, I am writing you these things
chapters.zh: 我指望快到你那里去，所以先将这些事写给你。

chapters.en: in case I am delayed, so that you will know how each one must conduct himself in God’s household, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.
chapters.zh: 倘若我耽延日久，你也可以知道在上帝的家中当怎样行。这家就是永生上帝的教会，真理的柱石和根基。

chapters.en:
By common confession, the mystery of godliness is great:
He appeared in the flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, was seen by angels, was proclaimed among the nations, was believed in throughout the world, was taken up in glory.
chapters.zh: 大哉，敬虔的奥祕，无人不以为然！ 就是上帝在肉身显现， 被圣灵称义〔注：或译：在灵性称义〕， 被天使看见， 被传于外邦， 被世人信服， 被接在荣耀里。

chapters.en: Now the Spirit expressly states that in later times some will abandon the faith to follow deceitful spirits and the teachings of demons,
chapters.zh: 圣灵明说，在后来的时候，必有人离弃真道，听从那引诱人的〔邪〕灵和鬼魔的道理。

chapters.en: influenced by the hypocrisy of liars, whose consciences are seared with a hot iron.
chapters.zh: 这是因为说谎之人的假冒；这等人的良心如同被热铁烙惯了一般。

chapters.en: They will prohibit marriage and require abstinence from certain foods that God has created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
chapters.zh: 他们禁止嫁娶，又禁戒食物〔注：或译：又叫人戒荤〕，就是上帝所造、叫那信而明白真道的人感谢着领受的。

chapters.en: For every creation of God is good, and nothing that is received with thanksgiving should be rejected,
chapters.zh: 凡上帝所造的物都是好的，若感谢着领受，就没有一样可弃的，

chapters.en: because it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.
chapters.zh: 都因上帝的道和人的祈求成为圣洁了。

chapters.en: By pointing out these things to the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of faith and sound instruction that you have followed.
chapters.zh: 你若将这些事提醒弟兄们，便是基督耶稣的好执事，在真道的话语和你向来所服从的善道上得了教育。

chapters.en: But reject irreverent, silly myths. Instead, train yourself for godliness.
chapters.zh: 只是要弃绝那世俗的言语和老妇荒渺的话，在敬虔上操练自己。

chapters.en: For physical exercise is of limited value, but godliness is valuable in every way, holding promise for the present life and for the one to come.
chapters.zh: 「操练身体，益处还少；惟独敬虔，凡事都有益处，因有今生和来生的应许。」

chapters.en: This is a trustworthy saying, worthy of full acceptance.
chapters.zh: 这话是可信的，是十分可佩服的。

chapters.en: To this end we labor and strive, because we have set our hope on the living God, who is the Savior of everyone, and especially of those who believe.
chapters.zh: 我们劳苦努力，正是为此，因我们的指望在乎永生的上帝；他是万人的救主，更是信徒的救主。

chapters.en: Command and teach these things.
chapters.zh: 这些事，你要吩咐人，也要教导人。

chapters.en: Let no one despise your youth, but set an example for the believers in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
chapters.zh: 不可叫人小看你年轻，总要在言语、行为、爱心、信心、清洁上，都作信徒的榜样。

chapters.en: Until I come, devote yourself to the public reading of Scripture, to exhortation, and to teaching.
chapters.zh: 你要以宣读、劝勉、教导为念，直等到我来。

chapters.en: Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given you through the prophecy spoken over you at the laying on of the hands of the elders.
chapters.zh: 你不要轻忽所得的恩赐，就是从前藉着预言、在众长老按手的时候赐给你的。

chapters.en: Be diligent in these matters and absorbed in them, so that your progress will be evident to all.
chapters.zh: 这些事你要殷勤去做，并要在此专心，使众人看出你的长进来。

chapters.en: Pay close attention to your life and to your teaching. Persevere in these things, for by so doing you will save both yourself and those who hear you.
chapters.zh: 你要谨慎自己和自己的教训，要在这些事上恒心；因为这样行，又能救自己，又能救听你的人。

chapters.en:
Do not rebuke an older man, but appeal to him as to a father.
Treat younger men as brothers,
chapters.zh: 不可严责老年人，只要劝他如同父亲；劝少年人如同弟兄；

chapters.en: older women as mothers, and younger women as sisters, with absolute purity.
chapters.zh: 劝老年妇女如同母亲；劝少年妇女如同姊妹；总要清清洁洁的。

chapters.en: Honor the widows who are truly widows.
chapters.zh: 要尊敬那真为寡妇的。

chapters.en: But if a widow has children or grandchildren, they must first learn to show godliness to their own family and repay their parents, for this is pleasing in the sight of God.
chapters.zh: 若寡妇有儿女，或有孙子孙女，便叫他们先在自己家中学着行孝，报答亲恩，因为这在上帝面前是可悦纳的。

chapters.en: The widow who is truly in need and left all alone puts her hope in God and continues night and day in her petitions and prayers.
chapters.zh: 那独居无靠、真为寡妇的，是仰赖上帝，昼夜不住地祈求祷告。

chapters.en: But she who lives for pleasure is dead even while she is still alive.
chapters.zh: 但那好宴乐的寡妇正活着的时候也是死的。

chapters.en: Give these instructions to the believers, so that they will be above reproach.
chapters.zh: 这些事你要嘱咐她们，叫她们无可指责。

chapters.en: If anyone does not provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
chapters.zh: 人若不看顾亲属，就是背了真道，比不信的人还不好，不看顾自己家里的人，更是如此。

chapters.en: A widow should be enrolled if she is at least sixty years old, faithful to her husband,
chapters.zh: 寡妇记在册子上，必须年纪到六十岁，从来只作一个丈夫的妻子，

chapters.en: and well known for good deeds such as bringing up children, entertaining strangers, washing the feet of the saints, imparting relief to the afflicted, and devoting herself to every good work.
chapters.zh: 又有行善的名声，就如养育儿女，接待远人，洗圣徒的脚，救济遭难的人，竭力行各样善事。

chapters.en: But refuse to enroll younger widows. For when their passions draw them away from Christ, they will want to marry,
chapters.zh: 至于年轻的寡妇，就可以辞她；因为她们的情欲发动，违背基督的时候就想要嫁人。

chapters.en: and thus will incur judgment because they are setting aside their first faith.
chapters.zh: 她们被定罪，是因废弃了当初所许的愿；

chapters.en: At the same time they will also learn to be idle, going from house to house and being not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, discussing things they should not mention.
chapters.zh: 并且她们又习惯懒惰，挨家闲游；不但是懒惰，又说长道短，好管闲事，说些不当说的话。

chapters.en: So I advise the younger widows to marry, have children, and manage their households, denying the adversary occasion for slander.
chapters.zh: 所以我愿意年轻的〔寡妇〕嫁人，生养儿女，治理家务，不给敌人辱骂的把柄。

chapters.en: For some have already turned aside to follow Satan.
chapters.zh: 因为已经有转去随从撒但的。

chapters.en: If any believing woman has dependent widows, she must assist them and not allow the church to be burdened, so that it can help the widows who are truly in need.
chapters.zh: 信〔主〕的妇女，若家中有寡妇，自己就当救济她们，不可累着教会，好使教会能救济那真〔无倚靠的〕寡妇。

chapters.en: Elders who lead effectively are worthy of double honor, especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching.
chapters.zh: 那善于管理教会的长老，当以为配受加倍的敬奉；那劳苦传道教导人的，更当如此。

chapters.en: For the Scripture says, “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain,” and, “The worker is worthy of his wages.”
chapters.zh: 因为经上说：「牛〔在场上〕踹谷的时候，不可笼住牠的嘴」；又说：「工人得工价是应当的。」

chapters.en: Do not entertain an accusation against an elder, except on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
chapters.zh: 控告长老的呈子，非有两三个见证就不要收。

chapters.en: But those who persist in sin should be rebuked in front of everyone, so that the others will stand in fear of sin.
chapters.zh: 犯罪的人，当在众人面前责备他，叫其余的人也可以惧怕。

chapters.en: I solemnly charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels to maintain these principles without bias, and to do nothing out of partiality.
chapters.zh: 我在上帝和基督耶稣并蒙拣选的天使面前嘱咐你：要遵守这些话，不可存成见，行事也不可有偏心。

chapters.en: Do not be too quick in the laying on of hands and thereby share in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.
chapters.zh: 给人行按手的礼，不可急促；不要在别人的罪上有分，要保守自己清洁。

chapters.en: Stop drinking only water and use a little wine instead, because of your stomach and your frequent ailments.
chapters.zh: 因你胃口不清，屡次患病，再不要照常喝水，可以稍微用点酒。

chapters.en: The sins of some men are obvious, going ahead of them to judgment; but the sins of others do not surface until later.
chapters.zh: 有些人的罪是明显的，〔如同〕先到审判案前；有些人的罪是随后跟了去的。

chapters.en: In the same way, good deeds are obvious, and even the ones that are inconspicuous cannot remain hidden.
chapters.zh: 这样，善行也有明显的，那不明显的也不能隐藏。

chapters.en: All who are under the yoke of slavery should regard their masters as fully worthy of honor, so that God’s name and our teaching will not be discredited.
chapters.zh: 凡在轭下作仆人的，当以自己主人配受十分的恭敬，免得上帝的名和道理被人亵渎。

chapters.en: Those who have believing masters should not show disrespect because they are brothers, but should serve them all the more, since those receiving their good service are beloved believers. Teach and encourage these principles.
chapters.zh: 仆人有信道的主人，不可因为与他是弟兄就轻看他；更要加意服事他；因为得服事之益处的，是信道蒙爱的。 你要以此教训人，劝勉人。

chapters.en: If anyone teaches another doctrine and disagrees with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and with godly teaching,
chapters.zh: 若有人传异教，不服从我们主耶稣基督纯正的话与那合乎敬虔的道理，

chapters.en: he is conceited and understands nothing. Instead, he has an unhealthy interest in controversies and disputes about words, out of which come envy, strife, abusive talk, evil suspicions,
chapters.zh: 他是自高自大，一无所知，专好问难，争辩言词，从此就生出嫉妒、纷争、毁谤、妄疑，

chapters.en: and constant friction between men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth. These men regard godliness as a means of gain.
chapters.zh: 并那坏了心术、失丧真理之人的争竞。他们以敬虔为得利的门路。

chapters.en: Of course, godliness with contentment is great gain.
chapters.zh: 然而，敬虔加上知足的心便是大利了；

chapters.en: For we brought nothing into the world, so we cannot carry anything out of it.
chapters.zh: 因为我们没有带什么到世上来，也不能带什么去。

chapters.en: But if we have food and clothing, we will be content with these.
chapters.zh: 只要有衣有食，就当知足。

chapters.en: Those who want to be rich, however, fall into temptation and become ensnared by many foolish and harmful desires that plunge them into ruin and destruction.
chapters.zh: 但那些想要发财的人，就陷在迷惑、落在网罗和许多无知有害的私欲里，叫人沉在败坏和灭亡中。

chapters.en: For the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil. By craving it, some have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many sorrows.
chapters.zh: 贪财是万恶之根。有人贪恋钱财，就被引诱离了真道，用许多愁苦把自己刺透了。

chapters.en: But you, O man of God, flee from these things and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness.
chapters.zh: 但你这属上帝的人要逃避这些事，追求公义、敬虔、信心、爱心、忍耐、温柔。

chapters.en: Fight the good fight of the faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called when you made the good confession before many witnesses.
chapters.zh: 你要为真道打那美好的仗，持定永生。你为此被召，也在许多见证人面前，已经作了那美好的见证。

chapters.en: I charge you in the presence of God, who gives life to all things, and of Christ Jesus, who made the good confession in His testimony before Pontius Pilate:
chapters.zh: 我在叫万物生活的上帝面前，并在向本丢‧彼拉多作过那美好见证的基督耶稣面前嘱咐你：

chapters.en: Keep this commandment without stain or reproach until the appearance of our Lord Jesus Christ,
chapters.zh: 要守这命令，毫不玷污，无可指责，直到我们的主耶稣基督显现。

chapters.en: which the blessed and only Sovereign One—the King of kings and Lord of lords—will bring about in His own time.
chapters.zh: 到了日期，那可称颂、独有权能的万王之王、万主之主，

chapters.en: He alone is immortal and dwells in unapproachable light. No one has ever seen Him, nor can anyone see Him. To Him be honor and eternal dominion! Amen.
chapters.zh: 就是那独一不死、住在人不能靠近的光里，是人未曾看见、也是不能看见的，要将他显明出来。但愿尊贵和永远的权能都归给他。阿们！

chapters.en: Instruct those who are rich in the present age not to be conceited and not to put their hope in the uncertainty of wealth, but in God, who richly provides all things for us to enjoy.
chapters.zh: 你要嘱咐那些今世富足的人，不要自高，也不要倚靠无定的钱财；只要倚靠那厚赐百物给我们享受的上帝。

chapters.en: Instruct them to do good, to be rich in good works, and to be generous and ready to share,
chapters.zh: 又要嘱咐他们行善，在好事上富足，甘心施舍，乐意供给〔注：或译：体贴〕人，

chapters.en: treasuring up for themselves a firm foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of that which is truly life.
chapters.zh: 为自己积成美好的根基，预备将来，叫他们持定那真正的生命。

chapters.en: O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you. Avoid irreverent, empty chatter and the opposing arguments of so-called “knowledge,”
chapters.zh: 提摩太啊，你要保守所托付你的，躲避世俗的虚谈和那敌真道、似是而非的学问。

chapters.en:
which some have professed and thus swerved away from the faith.
Grace be with you all.
chapters.zh: 已经有人自称有这学问，就偏离了真道。 愿恩惠〔常〕与你们同在！

chapters.en: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, according to the promise of life in Christ Jesus,
chapters.zh: 奉上帝旨意，照着在基督耶稣里生命的应许，作基督耶稣使徒的保罗

chapters.en:
To Timothy, my beloved child:
Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
chapters.zh: 写信给我亲爱的儿子提摩太。愿恩惠、怜悯、平安从父上帝和我们主基督耶稣归与你！

chapters.en: I thank God, whom I serve with a clear conscience as did my forefathers, as I constantly remember you night and day in my prayers.
chapters.zh: 我感谢上帝，就是我接续祖先用清洁的良心所事奉的上帝。祈祷的时候，不住的想念你，

chapters.en: Recalling your tears, I long to see you so that I may be filled with joy.
chapters.zh: 记念你的眼泪，昼夜切切地想要见你，好叫我满心快乐。

chapters.en: I am reminded of your sincere faith, which first dwelt in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am convinced is in you as well.
chapters.zh: 想到你心里无伪之信，这信是先在你外祖母罗以和你母亲友妮基心里的，我深信也在你的心里。

chapters.en: For this reason I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God, which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
chapters.zh: 为此我提醒你，使你将上帝藉我按手所给你的恩赐再如火挑旺起来。

chapters.en: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
chapters.zh: 因为上帝赐给我们，不是胆怯的心，乃是刚强、仁爱、谨守的心。

chapters.en: So do not be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, or of me, His prisoner. Instead, join me in suffering for the gospel by the power of God.
chapters.zh: 你不要以给我们的主作见证为耻，也不要以我这为主被囚的为耻；总要按上帝的能力，与我为福音同受苦难。

chapters.en: He has saved us and called us to a holy calling, not because of our works, but by His own purpose and by the grace He granted us in Christ Jesus before time began.
chapters.zh: 上帝救了我们，以圣召召我们，不是按我们的行为，乃是按他的旨意和恩典；这恩典是万古之先，在基督耶稣里赐给我们的，

chapters.en: And now He has revealed this grace through the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus, who has abolished death and illuminated the way to life and immortality through the gospel,
chapters.zh: 但如今藉着我们救主基督耶稣的显现才表明出来了。他已经把死废去，藉着福音，将不能坏的生命彰显出来。

chapters.en: to which I was appointed as a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher.
chapters.zh: 我为这福音奉派作传道的，作使徒，作师傅。

chapters.en: For this reason, even though I suffer as I do, I am not ashamed; for I know whom I have believed, and I am convinced that He is able to guard what I have entrusted to Him for that day.
chapters.zh: 为这缘故，我也受这些苦难。然而我不以为耻；因为知道我所信的是谁，也深信他能保全我所交付他的〔注：或译：他所交讬我的〕，直到那日。

chapters.en: Hold on to the pattern of sound teaching you have heard from me, with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 你从我听的那纯正话语的规模，要用在基督耶稣里的信心和爱心，常常守着。

chapters.en: Guard the treasure entrusted to you, with the help of the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
chapters.zh: 从前所交讬你的善道，你要靠着那住在我们里面的圣灵牢牢地守着。

chapters.en: You know that everyone in the Province of Asia has deserted me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.
chapters.zh: 凡在亚细亚的人都离弃我，这是你知道的，其中有腓吉路和黑摩其尼。

chapters.en: May the Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he has often refreshed me and was unashamed of my chains.
chapters.zh: 愿主怜悯阿尼色弗一家的人；因他屡次使我畅快，不以我的锁鍊为耻，

chapters.en: Indeed, when he arrived in Rome, he searched diligently until he found me.
chapters.zh: 反倒在罗马的时候，殷勤地找我，并且找着了。

chapters.en: May the Lord grant Onesiphorus His mercy on that day. You know very well how much he ministered to me in Ephesus.
chapters.zh: 愿主使他在那日得主的怜悯。他在以弗所怎样多多地服事我，是你明明知道的。

chapters.en: You therefore, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 我儿啊，你要在基督耶稣的恩典上刚强起来。

chapters.en: And the things that you have heard me say among many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men who will be qualified to teach others as well.
chapters.zh: 你在许多见证人面前听见我所教训的，也要交讬那忠心能教导别人的人。

chapters.en: Join me in suffering, like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 你要和〔我〕同受苦难，好像基督耶稣的精兵。

chapters.en: A soldier refrains from entangling himself in civilian affairs, in order to please the one who enlisted him.
chapters.zh: 凡在军中当兵的，不将世务缠身，好叫那招他当兵的人喜悦。

chapters.en: Likewise, a competitor does not receive the crown unless he competes according to the rules.
chapters.zh: 人若在场上比武，非按规矩，就不能得冠冕。

chapters.en: The hardworking farmer should be the first to partake of the crops.
chapters.zh: 劳力的农夫理当先得粮食。

chapters.en: Consider what I am saying, for the Lord will give you insight into all things.
chapters.zh: 我所说的话，你要思想，因为凡事主必给你聪明。

chapters.en: Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David, as proclaimed by my gospel,
chapters.zh: 你要记念耶稣基督乃是大卫的后裔，他从死里复活，正合乎我所传的福音。

chapters.en: for which I suffer to the extent of being chained like a criminal. But the word of God cannot be chained!
chapters.zh: 我为这福音受苦难，甚至被捆绑，像犯人一样。然而上帝的道却不被捆绑。

chapters.en: For this reason I endure all things for the sake of the elect, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
chapters.zh: 所以，我为选民凡事忍耐，叫他们也可以得着那在基督耶稣里的救恩和永远的荣耀。

chapters.en:
This is a trustworthy saying:
If we died with Him, we will also live with Him;
chapters.zh: 有可信的话说： 我们若与基督同死，也必与他同活；

chapters.en: if we endure, we will also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He will also deny us;
chapters.zh: 我们若〔能〕忍耐，也必和他一同作王。 我们若不认他，他也必不认我们；

chapters.en:
if we are faithless, He remains faithful,
for He cannot deny Himself.
chapters.zh: 我们纵然失信，他仍是可信的， 因为他不能背乎自己。

chapters.en: Remind the believers of these things, charging them before God to avoid quarreling over words, which succeeds only in leading the listeners to ruin.
chapters.zh: 你要使众人回想这些事，在主面前嘱咐他们：不可为言语争辩；这是没有益处的，只能败坏听见的人。

chapters.en: Make every effort to present yourself approved to God, an unashamed workman who accurately handles the word of truth.
chapters.zh: 你当竭力在上帝面前得蒙喜悦，作无愧的工人，按着正意分解真理的道。

chapters.en: But avoid irreverent, empty chatter, which will only lead to more ungodliness,
chapters.zh: 但要远避世俗的虚谈，因为这等人必进到更不敬虔的地步。

chapters.en: and the talk of such men will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
chapters.zh: 他们的话如同毒疮，越烂越大；其中有许米乃和腓理徒，

chapters.en: who have deviated from the truth. They say that the resurrection has already occurred, and they undermine the faith of some.
chapters.zh: 他们偏离了真道，说复活的事已过，就败坏好些人的信心。

chapters.en: Nevertheless, God’s firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity.”
chapters.zh: 然而，上帝坚固的根基立住了；上面有这印记说：「主认识谁是他的人」；又说：「凡称呼主名的人总要离开不义。」

chapters.en: A large house contains not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay. Some indeed are for honorable use, but others are for common use.
chapters.zh: 在大户人家，不但有金器银器，也有木器瓦器；有作为贵重的，有作为卑贱的。

chapters.en: So if anyone cleanses himself of what is unfit, he will be a vessel for honor: sanctified, useful to the Master, and prepared for every good work.
chapters.zh: 人若自洁，脱离卑贱的事，就必作贵重的器皿，成为圣洁，合乎主用，预备行各样的善事。

chapters.en: Flee from youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.
chapters.zh: 你要逃避少年的私欲，同那清心祷告主的人追求公义、信德、仁爱、和平。

chapters.en: But reject foolish and ignorant speculation, for you know that it breeds quarreling.
chapters.zh: 惟有那愚拙无学问的辩论，总要弃绝，因为知道这等事是起争竞的。

chapters.en: And a servant of the Lord must not be quarrelsome, but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, and forbearing.
chapters.zh: 然而主的仆人不可争竞，只要温温和和地待众人，善于教导，存心忍耐，

chapters.en: He must gently reprove those who oppose him, in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth.
chapters.zh: 用温柔劝戒那抵挡的人；或者上帝给他们悔改的心，可以明白真道，

chapters.en: Then they will come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil, who has taken them captive to his will.
chapters.zh: 叫他们这已经被魔鬼任意掳去的，可以醒悟，脱离他的网罗。

chapters.en: But understand this: In the last days terrible times will come.
chapters.zh: 你该知道，末世必有危险的日子来到。

chapters.en: For men will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, unholy,
chapters.zh: 因为那时，人要专顾自己，贪爱钱财，自夸，狂傲，谤讟，违背父母，忘恩负义，心不圣洁，

chapters.en: unloving, unforgiving, slanderous, without self-control, brutal, without love of good,
chapters.zh: 无亲情，不解怨，好说谗言，不能自约，性情凶暴，不爱良善，

chapters.en: traitorous, reckless, conceited, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,
chapters.zh: 卖主卖友，任意妄为，自高自大，爱宴乐，不爱上帝，

chapters.en: having a form of godliness but denying its power. Turn away from such as these!
chapters.zh: 有敬虔的外貌，却背了敬虔的实意；这等人你要躲开。

chapters.en: They are the kind who worm their way into households and captivate vulnerable women who are weighed down with sins and led astray by various passions,
chapters.zh: 那偷进人家、牢笼无知妇女的，正是这等人。这些妇女担负罪恶，被各样的私欲引诱，

chapters.en: who are always learning but never able to come to a knowledge of the truth.
chapters.zh: 常常学习，终久不能明白真道。

chapters.en: Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so also these men oppose the truth. They are depraved in mind and disqualified from the faith.
chapters.zh: 从前雅尼和佯庇怎样敌挡摩西，这等人也怎样敌挡真道。他们的心地坏了，在真道上是可废弃的。

chapters.en: But they will not advance much further. For just like Jannes and Jambres, their folly will be plain to everyone.
chapters.zh: 然而他们不能再这样敌挡；因为他们的愚昧必在众人面前显露出来，像那二人一样。

chapters.en: You, however, have observed my teaching, my conduct, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love, my perseverance,
chapters.zh: 但你已经服从了我的教训、品行、志向、信心、宽容、爱心、忍耐，

chapters.en: my persecutions, and the sufferings that came upon me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. What persecutions I endured! Yet the Lord rescued me from all of them.
chapters.zh: 以及我在安提阿、以哥念、路司得所遭遇的逼迫、苦难。我所忍受是何等的逼迫；但从这一切苦难中，主都把我救出来了。

chapters.en: Indeed, all who desire to live godly lives in Christ Jesus will be persecuted,
chapters.zh: 不但如此，凡立志在基督耶稣里敬虔度日的也都要受逼迫。

chapters.en: while evil men and imposters go from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived.
chapters.zh: 只是作恶的和迷惑人的，必越久越恶，他欺哄人，也被人欺哄。

chapters.en: But as for you, continue in the things you have learned and firmly believed, since you know from whom you have learned them.
chapters.zh: 但你所学习的，所确信的，要存在心里；因为你知道是跟谁学的，

chapters.en: From infancy you have known the Holy Scriptures, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
chapters.zh: 并且知道你是从小明白圣经，这圣经能使你因信基督耶稣，有得救的智慧。

chapters.en: All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for instruction, for conviction, for correction, and for training in righteousness,
chapters.zh: 圣经都是上帝所默示的〔注：或译：凡上帝所默示的圣经〕，于教训、督责、使人归正、教导人学义都是有益的，

chapters.en: so that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.
chapters.zh: 叫属上帝的人得以完全，预备行各样的善事。

chapters.en: I charge you in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus, who will judge the living and the dead, and in view of His appearing and His kingdom:
chapters.zh: 我在上帝面前，并在将来审判活人死人的基督耶稣面前，凭着他的显现和他的国度嘱咐你：

chapters.en: Preach the word; be prepared in season and out of season; reprove, rebuke, and encourage with every form of patient instruction.
chapters.zh: 务要传道，无论得时不得时，总要专心，并用百般的忍耐、各样的教训责备人，警戒人，劝勉人。

chapters.en: For the time will come when men will not tolerate sound doctrine, but with itching ears they will gather around themselves teachers to suit their own desires.
chapters.zh: 因为时候要到，人必厌烦纯正的道理，耳朵发痒，就随从自己的情欲增添好些师傅，

chapters.en: So they will turn their ears away from the truth and turn aside to myths.
chapters.zh: 并且掩耳不听真道，偏向荒渺的言语。

chapters.en: But you, be sober in all things, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry.
chapters.zh: 你却要凡事谨慎，忍受苦难，做传道的工夫，尽你的职分。

chapters.en: For I am already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time of my departure is at hand.
chapters.zh: 我现在被浇奠，我离世的时候到了。

chapters.en: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
chapters.zh: 那美好的仗我已经打过了，当跑的路我已经跑尽了，所信的道我已经守住了。

chapters.en: From now on there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, will award to me on that day—and not only to me, but to all who crave His appearing.
chapters.zh: 从此以后，有公义的冠冕为我存留，就是按着公义审判的主到了那日要赐给我的；不但赐给我，也赐给凡爱慕他显现的人。

chapters.en: Make every effort to come to me quickly,
chapters.zh: 你要赶紧地到我这里来。

chapters.en: because Demas, in his love of this world, has deserted me and gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.
chapters.zh: 因为底马贪爱现今的世界，就离弃我往帖撒罗尼迦去了；革勒士往加拉太去；提多往挞马太去；

chapters.en: Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, because he is useful to me in the ministry.
chapters.zh: 独有路加在我这里。你来的时候，要把马可带来，因为他在传道〔注：或译：服事我〕的事上于我有益处。

chapters.en: Tychicus, however, I have sent to Ephesus.
chapters.zh: 我已经打发推基古往以弗所去。

chapters.en: When you come, bring the cloak that I left with Carpus at Troas, and my scrolls, especially the parchments.
chapters.zh: 我在特罗亚留于加布的那件外衣，你来的时候可以带来，那些书也要带来，更要紧的是那些皮卷。

chapters.en: Alexander the coppersmith did great harm to me. The Lord will repay him according to his deeds.
chapters.zh: 铜匠亚历山大多多地害我；主必照他所行的报应他。

chapters.en: You too should beware of him, for he has vigorously opposed our message.
chapters.zh: 你也要防备他，因为他极力敌挡了我们的话。

chapters.en: At my first defense, no one stood with me, but everyone deserted me. May it not be charged against them.
chapters.zh: 我初次申诉，没有人前来帮助，竟都离弃我；但愿这罪不归与他们。

chapters.en: But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the message would be fully proclaimed, and all the Gentiles would hear it. So I was delivered from the mouth of the lion.
chapters.zh: 惟有主站在我旁边，加给我力量，使福音被我尽都传明，叫外邦人都听见；我也从狮子口里被救出来。

chapters.en: And the Lord will rescue me from every evil action and bring me safely into His heavenly kingdom. To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
chapters.zh: 主必救我脱离诸般的凶恶，也必救我进他的天国。愿荣耀归给他，直到永永远远。阿们。

chapters.en: Greet Prisca and Aquila, as well as the household of Onesiphorus.
chapters.zh: 问百基拉、亚居拉，和阿尼色弗一家的人安。

chapters.en: Erastus has remained at Corinth, and Trophimus I left sick in Miletus.
chapters.zh: 以拉都在哥林多住下了。特罗非摩病了，我就留他在米利都。

chapters.en:
Make every effort to come to me before winter.
Eubulus sends you greetings, as do Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers.
chapters.zh: 你要赶紧在冬天以前到我这里来。有友布罗、布田、利奴、革老底亚，和众弟兄都问你安。

chapters.en: The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all.
chapters.zh: 愿主与你的灵同在！愿恩惠〔常〕与你们同在！

chapters.en: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ for the faith of God’s elect and their knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness,
chapters.zh: 上帝的仆人，耶稣基督的使徒保罗，凭着上帝选民的信心与敬虔真理的知识，

chapters.en: in the hope of eternal life, which God, who cannot lie, promised before time began.
chapters.zh: 盼望那无谎言的上帝在万古之先所应许的永生，

chapters.en: In His own time He has made His word evident in the proclamation entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior.
chapters.zh: 到了日期，藉着传扬的工夫把他的道显明了；这传扬〔的责任〕是按着上帝－我们救主的命令交讬了我。

chapters.en:
To Titus, my true child in our common faith:
Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
chapters.zh: 〔现在〕写信给提多，就是照着我们共信之道作我真儿子的。愿恩惠、平安从父上帝和我们的救主基督耶稣归与你！

chapters.en: The reason I left you in Crete was that you would set in order what was unfinished and appoint elders in every town, as I directed you.
chapters.zh: 我从前留你在克里特，是要你将那没有办完的事都办整齐了，又照我所吩咐你的，在各城设立长老。

chapters.en: An elder must be blameless, the husband of but one wife, having children who are believers and who are not open to accusation of indiscretion or insubordination.
chapters.zh: 若有无可指责的人，只作一个妇人的丈夫，儿女也是信主的，没有人告他们是放荡不服约束的，〔就可以设立〕。

chapters.en: As God’s steward, an overseer must be above reproach—not self-willed, not quick-tempered, not given to drunkenness, not violent, not greedy for money.
chapters.zh: 监督既是上帝的管家，必须无可指责，不任性，不暴躁，不因酒滋事，不打人，不贪无义之财；

chapters.en: Instead, he must be hospitable, a lover of good, self-controlled, upright, holy, and disciplined.
chapters.zh: 乐意接待远人，好善，庄重，公平，圣洁自持；

chapters.en: He must hold firmly to the faithful word as it was taught, so that he can encourage others by sound teaching and refute those who contradict it.
chapters.zh: 坚守所教真实的道理，就能将纯正的教训劝化人，又能把争辩的人驳倒了。

chapters.en: For many are rebellious and full of empty talk and deception, especially those of the circumcision,
chapters.zh: 因为有许多人不服约束，说虚空话欺哄人；那奉割礼的更是这样。

chapters.en: who must be silenced. For the sake of dishonorable gain, they undermine entire households and teach things they should not.
chapters.zh: 这些人的口总要堵住。他们因贪不义之财，将不该教导的教导人，败坏人的全家。

chapters.en: As one of their own prophets has said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons.”
chapters.zh: 有克里特人中的一个本地先知说：「克里特人常说谎话，乃是恶兽，又馋又懒。」

chapters.en: This testimony is true. Therefore rebuke them sternly, so that they will be sound in the faith
chapters.zh: 这个见证是真的。所以，你要严严地责备他们，使他们在真道上纯全无疵，

chapters.en: and will pay no attention to Jewish myths or to the commands of men who have rejected the truth.
chapters.zh: 不听犹太人荒渺的言语和离弃真道之人的诫命。

chapters.en: To the pure, all things are pure; but to the defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure. Indeed, both their minds and their consciences are defiled.
chapters.zh: 在洁净的人，凡物都洁净；在污秽不信的人，什么都不洁净，连心地和天良也都污秽了。

chapters.en: They profess to know God, but by their actions they deny Him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good deed.
chapters.zh: 他们说是认识上帝，行事却和他相背；本是可憎恶的，是悖逆的，在各样善事上是可废弃的。

chapters.en: But as for you, speak the things that are consistent with sound doctrine.
chapters.zh: 但你所讲的总要合乎那纯正的道理。

chapters.en: Older men are to be temperate, dignified, self-controlled, and sound in faith, love, and perseverance.
chapters.zh: 劝老年人要有节制、端庄、自守，在信心、爱心、忍耐上都要纯全无疵。

chapters.en: Older women, likewise, are to be reverent in their behavior, not slanderers or addicted to much wine, but teachers of good.
chapters.zh: 又劝老年妇人，举止行动要恭敬，不说谗言，不给酒作奴仆，用善道教训人，

chapters.en: In this way they can train the young women to love their husbands and children,
chapters.zh: 好指教少年妇人，爱丈夫，爱儿女，

chapters.en: to be self-controlled, pure, managers of their households, kind, and submissive to their own husbands, so that the word of God will not be discredited.
chapters.zh: 谨守，贞洁，料理家务，待人有恩，顺服自己的丈夫，免得上帝的道理被毁谤。

chapters.en: In the same way, urge the younger men to be self-controlled.
chapters.zh: 又劝少年人要谨守。

chapters.en: In everything, show yourself to be an example by doing good works. In your teaching show integrity, dignity,
chapters.zh: 你自己凡事要显出善行的榜样；在教训上要正直、端庄，

chapters.en: and wholesome speech that is above reproach, so that anyone who opposes us will be ashamed, having nothing bad to say about us.
chapters.zh: 言语纯全，无可指责，叫那反对的人，既无处可说我们的不是，便自觉羞愧。

chapters.en: Slaves are to submit to their own masters in everything, to be well-pleasing, not argumentative,
chapters.zh: 〔劝〕仆人要顺服自己的主人，凡事讨他的喜欢，不可顶撞他，

chapters.en: not stealing from them, but showing all good faith, so that in every respect they will adorn the teaching about God our Savior.
chapters.zh: 不可私拿东西，要显为忠诚，以致凡事尊荣我们救主－上帝的道。

chapters.en: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to everyone.
chapters.zh: 因为上帝救众人的恩典已经显明出来，

chapters.en: It instructs us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live sensible, upright, and godly lives in the present age,
chapters.zh: 教训我们除去不敬虔的心和世俗的情欲，在今世自守、公义、敬虔度日，

chapters.en: as we await the blessed hope and glorious appearance of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 等候所盼望的福，并等候至大的上帝和我们〔注：或译：上帝－我们〕救主耶稣基督的荣耀显现。

chapters.en: He gave Himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for Himself a people for His own possession, zealous for good deeds.
chapters.zh: 他为我们舍了自己，要赎我们脱离一切罪恶，又洁净我们，特作自己的子民，热心为善。

chapters.en: Speak these things as you encourage and rebuke with all authority. Let no one despise you.
chapters.zh: 这些事你要讲明，劝戒人，用各等权柄责备人；不可叫人轻看你。

chapters.en: Remind the believers to submit to rulers and authorities, to be obedient and ready for every good work,
chapters.zh: 你要提醒众人，叫他们顺服作官的、掌权的，遵他的命，预备行各样的善事。

chapters.en: to malign no one, and to be peaceable and gentle, showing full consideration to everyone.
chapters.zh: 不要毁谤，不要争竞，总要和平，向众人大显温柔。

chapters.en: For at one time we too were foolish, disobedient, misled, and enslaved to all sorts of desires and pleasures—living in malice and envy, being hated and hating one another.
chapters.zh: 我们从前也是无知、悖逆、受迷惑、服事各样私欲，和宴乐，常存恶毒〔注：或译：阴毒〕嫉妒的心，是可恨的，又是彼此相恨。

chapters.en: But when the kindness of God our Savior and His love for mankind appeared,
chapters.zh: 但到了上帝－我们救主的恩慈和他向人所施的慈爱显明的时候，

chapters.en: He saved us, not by the righteous deeds we had done, but according to His mercy, through the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.
chapters.zh: 他便救了我们；并不是因我们自己所行的义，乃是照他的怜悯，藉着重生的洗和圣灵的更新。

chapters.en: This is the Spirit He poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
chapters.zh: 圣灵就是上帝藉着耶稣基督－我们救主厚厚浇灌在我们身上的，

chapters.en: so that, having been justified by His grace, we would become heirs with the hope of eternal life.
chapters.zh: 好叫我们因他的恩得称为义，可以凭着永生的盼望成为后嗣〔注：或译：可以凭着盼望承受永生〕。

chapters.en: This saying is trustworthy. And I want you to emphasize these things, so that those who have believed God will take care to devote themselves to good deeds. These things are excellent and profitable for the people.
chapters.zh: 这话是可信的。 我也愿你把这些事切切实实地讲明，使那些已信上帝的人留心做正经事业〔注：或译：留心行善〕。这都是美事，并且与人有益。

chapters.en: But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, arguments, and quarrels about the law, because these things are pointless and worthless.
chapters.zh: 要远避无知的辩论和家谱〔的空谈〕，以及纷争，并因律法而起的争竞，因为这都是虚妄无益的。

chapters.en: Reject a divisive man after a first and second admonition,
chapters.zh: 分门结党的人，警戒过一两次，就要弃绝他。

chapters.en: knowing that such a man is corrupt and sinful; he is self-condemned.
chapters.zh: 因为知道这等人已经背道，犯了罪，自己明知不是，还是去做。

chapters.en: As soon as I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, make every effort to come to me at Nicopolis, because I have decided to winter there.
chapters.zh: 我打发亚提马或是推基古到你那里去的时候，你要赶紧往尼哥坡里去见我，因为我已经定意在那里过冬。

chapters.en: Do your best to equip Zenas the lawyer and Apollos, so that they will have everything they need.
chapters.zh: 你要赶紧给律师西纳和亚波罗送行，叫他们没有缺乏。

chapters.en: And our people must also learn to devote themselves to good works in order to meet the pressing needs of others, so that they will not be unfruitful.
chapters.zh: 并且我们的人要学习正经事业〔注：或译：要学习行善〕，预备所需用的，免得不结果子。

chapters.en:
All who are with me send you greetings.
Greet those who love us in the faith.
Grace be with all of you.
chapters.zh: 同我在一处的人都问你安。请代问那些因有信心爱我们的人安。愿恩惠〔常〕与你们众人同在！

chapters.en:
Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother,
To Philemon our beloved fellow worker,
chapters.zh: 为基督耶稣被囚的保罗，同兄弟提摩太写信给我们所亲爱的同工腓利门，

chapters.en: to Apphia our sister, to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets at your house:
chapters.zh: 和妹子亚腓亚并与我们同当兵的亚基布，以及在你家的教会。

chapters.en: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 愿恩惠、平安从上帝我们的父和主耶稣基督归与你们！

chapters.en: I always thank my God, remembering you in my prayers,
chapters.zh: 我祷告的时候提到你，常为你感谢我的上帝；

chapters.en: because I hear about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints.
chapters.zh: 因听说你的爱心并你向主耶稣和众圣徒的信心〔注：或译：因听说你向主耶稣和众圣徒有爱心有信心〕。

chapters.en: I pray that your partnership in the faith may become effective as you fully acknowledge every good thing that is ours in Christ.
chapters.zh: 愿你与人所同有的信心显出功效，使人知道你们各样善事都是为基督做的。

chapters.en: I take great joy and encouragement in your love, because you, brother, have refreshed the hearts of the saints.
chapters.zh: 兄弟啊，我为你的爱心，大有快乐，大得安慰，因众圣徒的心从你得了畅快。

chapters.en: So although in Christ I am bold enough to order you to do what is proper,
chapters.zh: 我虽然靠着基督能放胆吩咐你合宜的事，

chapters.en: I prefer to appeal on the basis of love. For I, Paul, am now aged, and a prisoner of Christ Jesus as well.
chapters.zh: 然而像我这有年纪的保罗，现在又是为基督耶稣被囚的，宁可凭着爱心求你，

chapters.en: I appeal to you for my child Onesimus, whose father I became while I was in chains.
chapters.zh: 就是为我在捆锁中所生的儿子阿尼西谋〔注：就是有益处的意思〕求你。

chapters.en: Formerly he was useless to you, but now he has become useful both to you and to me.
chapters.zh: 他从前与你没有益处，但如今与你我都有益处。

chapters.en: I am sending back to you him who is my very heart.
chapters.zh: 我现在打发他亲自回你那里去；他是我心上的人。

chapters.en: I would have liked to keep him with me, so that on your behalf he could minister to me in my chains for the gospel.
chapters.zh: 我本来有意将他留下，在我为福音所受的捆锁中替你伺候我。

chapters.en: But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your goodness will not be out of compulsion, but by your own free will.
chapters.zh: 但不知道你的意思，我就不愿意这样行，叫你的善行不是出于勉强，乃是出于甘心。

chapters.en: For perhaps this is why he was separated from you for a while, so that you might have him back for good—
chapters.zh: 他暂时离开你，或者是叫你永远得着他，

chapters.en: no longer as a slave, but better than a slave, as a beloved brother. He is especially beloved to me, but even more so to you, both in person and in the Lord.
chapters.zh: 不再是奴仆，乃是高过奴仆，是亲爱的兄弟。在我实在是如此，何况在你呢！这也不拘是按肉体说，是按主说。

chapters.en: So if you consider me a partner, receive him as you would receive me.
chapters.zh: 你若以我为同伴，就收纳他，如同收纳我一样。

chapters.en: But if he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
chapters.zh: 他若亏负你，或欠你什么，都归在我的帐上；

chapters.en: I, Paul, write this with my own hand. I will repay it—not to mention that you owe me your very self.
chapters.zh: 我必偿还，这是我－保罗亲笔写的。我并不用对你说，连你自己也是亏欠于我。

chapters.en: Yes, brother, let me have some benefit from you in the Lord. Refresh my heart in Christ.
chapters.zh: 兄弟啊，望你使我在主里因你得快乐〔注：或译：益处〕，并望你使我的心在基督里得畅快。

chapters.en: Confident of your obedience, I write to you, knowing that you will do even more than I ask.
chapters.zh: 我写信给你，深信你必顺服，知道你所要行的必过于我所说的。

chapters.en: In the meantime, prepare a guest room for me, because I hope that through your prayers I will be restored to you.
chapters.zh: 此外你还要给我预备住处；因为我盼望藉着你们的祷告，必蒙恩到你们那里去。

chapters.en: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you greetings,
chapters.zh: 为基督耶稣与我同坐监的以巴弗问你安。

chapters.en: as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.
chapters.zh: 与我同工的马可、亚里达古、底马、路加也都问你安。

chapters.en: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
chapters.zh: 愿我们主耶稣基督的恩〔常〕在你的心里。阿们！

chapters.en: On many past occasions and in many different ways, God spoke to our fathers through the prophets.
chapters.zh: 上帝既在古时藉着众先知多次多方地晓谕列祖，

chapters.en: But in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, and through whom He made the universe.
chapters.zh: 就在这末世藉着他儿子晓谕我们；又早已立他为承受万有的，也曾藉着他创造诸世界。

chapters.en: The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His nature, upholding all things by His powerful word. After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.
chapters.zh: 他是上帝荣耀所发的光辉，是上帝本体的真像，常用他权能的命令托住万有。他洗净了人的罪，就坐在高天至大者的右边。

chapters.en: So He became as far superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is excellent beyond theirs.
chapters.zh: 他所承受的名，既比天使的名更尊贵，就远超过天使。

chapters.en:
For to which of the angels did God ever say:
“You are My Son; today I have become Your Father” ?
Or again:
“I will be His Father, and He will be My Son” ?
chapters.zh: 所有的天使，上帝从来对哪一个说： 你是我的儿子， 我今日生你？ 又指着哪一个说： 我要作他的父， 他要作我的子？

chapters.en:
And again, when God brings His firstborn into the world, He says:
“Let all God’s angels worship Him.”
chapters.zh: 再者，上帝使长子到世上来的时候〔注：或译：上帝再使长子到世上来的时候〕，就说： 上帝的使者都要拜他。

chapters.en:
Now about the angels He says:
“He makes His angels winds, His servants flames of fire.”
chapters.zh: 论到使者，又说： 上帝以风为使者， 以火焰为仆役；

chapters.en:
But about the Son He says:
“Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.
chapters.zh: 论到子却说： 上帝啊，你的宝座是永永远远的； 你的国权是正直的。

chapters.en: You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, Your God, has anointed You above Your companions with the oil of joy.”
chapters.zh: 你喜爱公义，恨恶罪恶； 所以上帝，就是你的上帝，用喜乐油膏你， 胜过膏你的同伴；

chapters.en:
And:
“In the beginning, O Lord, You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.
chapters.zh: 又说：主啊，你起初立了地的根基； 天也是你手所造的。

chapters.en: They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment.
chapters.zh: 天地都要灭没，你却要长存。 天地都要像衣服渐渐旧了；

chapters.en: You will roll them up like a robe; like a garment they will be changed; but You remain the same, and Your years will never end.”
chapters.zh: 你要将天地卷起来，像一件外衣， 天地就都改变了。 惟有你永不改变； 你的年数没有穷尽。

chapters.en:
Yet to which of the angels did God ever say:
“Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet” ?
chapters.zh: 所有的天使，上帝从来对哪一个说： 你坐在我的右边， 等我使你仇敌作你的脚凳？

chapters.en: Are not the angels ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation?
chapters.zh: 天使岂不都是服役的灵、奉差遣为那将要承受救恩的人效力吗？

chapters.en: We must pay closer attention, therefore, to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.
chapters.zh: 所以，我们当越发郑重所听见的道理，恐怕我们随流失去。

chapters.en: For if the message spoken by angels was binding, and every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment,
chapters.zh: 那藉着天使所传的话既是确定的；凡干犯悖逆的都受了该受的报应。

chapters.en:
how shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation?
This salvation was first announced by the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard Him,
chapters.zh: 我们若忽略这么大的救恩，怎能逃罪呢？这救恩起先是主亲自讲的，后来是听见的人给我们证实了。

chapters.en: and was affirmed by God through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will.
chapters.zh: 上帝又按自己的旨意，用神迹、奇事和百般的异能，并圣灵的恩赐，同他们作见证。

chapters.en: For it is not to angels that He has subjected the world to come, about which we are speaking.
chapters.zh: 我们所说将来的世界，上帝原没有交给天使管辖。

chapters.en:
But somewhere it is testified in these words:
“What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?
chapters.zh: 但有人在〔经上〕某处证明说： 人算什么，你竟顾念他？ 世人算什么，你竟眷顾他？

chapters.en: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor
chapters.zh: 你叫他比天使微小一点〔注：或译：你叫他暂时比天使小〕， 赐他荣耀尊贵为冠冕， 并将你手所造的都派他管理，

chapters.en:
and placed everything under his feet.”
When God subjected all things to him, He left nothing outside of his control. Yet at present we do not see everything subject to him.
chapters.zh: 叫万物都服在他的脚下。 既叫万物都服他，就没有剩下一样不服他的。只是如今我们还不见万物都服他。

chapters.en: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because He suffered death, so that by the grace of God He might taste death for everyone.
chapters.zh: 惟独见那成为比天使小一点的耶稣〔注：或译：惟独见耶稣暂时比天使小〕；因为受死的苦，就得了尊贵荣耀为冠冕，叫他因着上帝的恩，为人人尝了死味。

chapters.en: In bringing many sons to glory, it was fitting for God, for whom and through whom all things exist, to make the author of their salvation perfect through suffering.
chapters.zh: 原来那为万物所属、为万物所本的，要领许多的儿子进荣耀里去，使救他们的元帅，因受苦难得以完全，本是合宜的。

chapters.en: For both the One who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are of the same family. So Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers.
chapters.zh: 因那使人成圣的和那些得以成圣的，都是出于一。所以，他称他们为弟兄也不以为耻，

chapters.en:
He says:
“I will proclaim Your name to My brothers; I will sing Your praises in the assembly.”
chapters.zh: 说： 我要将你的名传与我的弟兄， 在会中我要颂扬你；

chapters.en:
And again:
“I will put My trust in Him.”
And once again:
“Here am I, and the children God has given Me.”
chapters.zh: 又说： 我要倚赖他； 又说： 看哪，我与上帝所给我的儿女。

chapters.en: Now since the children have flesh and blood, He too shared in their humanity, so that by His death He might destroy him who holds the power of death, that is, the devil,
chapters.zh: 儿女既同有血肉之体，他也照样亲自成了血肉之体，特要藉着死败坏那掌死权的，就是魔鬼，

chapters.en: and free those who all their lives were held in slavery by their fear of death.
chapters.zh: 并要释放那些一生因怕死而为奴仆的人。

chapters.en: For surely it is not the angels He helps, but the descendants of Abraham.
chapters.zh: 他并不救拔天使，乃是救拔亚伯拉罕的后裔。

chapters.en: For this reason He had to be made like His brothers in every way, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God, in order to make atonement for the sins of the people.
chapters.zh: 所以，他凡事该与他的弟兄相同，为要在上帝的事上成为慈悲忠信的大祭司，为百姓的罪献上挽回祭。

chapters.en: Because He Himself suffered when He was tempted, He is able to help those who are being tempted.
chapters.zh: 他自己既然被试探而受苦，就能搭救被试探的人。

chapters.en: Therefore, holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling, set your focus on Jesus, the apostle and high priest whom we confess.
chapters.zh: 同蒙天召的圣洁弟兄啊，你们应当思想我们所认为使者、为大祭司的耶稣。

chapters.en: He was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just as Moses was faithful in all God’s house.
chapters.zh: 他为那设立他的尽忠，如同摩西在上帝的全家尽忠一样。

chapters.en: For Jesus has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has greater honor than the house itself.
chapters.zh: 他比摩西算是更配多得荣耀，好像建造房屋的比房屋更尊荣；

chapters.en: And every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.
chapters.zh: 因为房屋都必有人建造，但建造万物的就是上帝。

chapters.en: Now Moses was faithful as a servant in all God’s house, testifying to what would be spoken later.
chapters.zh: 摩西为仆人，在上帝的全家诚然尽忠，为要证明将来必传说的事。

chapters.en: But Christ is faithful as the Son over God’s house. And we are His house, if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope of which we boast.
chapters.zh: 但基督为儿子，治理上帝的家；我们若将可夸的盼望和胆量坚持到底，便是他的家了。

chapters.en:
Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says:
“Today, if you hear His voice,
chapters.zh: 圣灵有话说： 你们今日若听他的话，

chapters.en: do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion, in the day of testing in the wilderness,
chapters.zh: 就不可硬着心， 像在旷野惹他发怒、 试探他的时候一样。

chapters.en: where your fathers tested and tried Me, and for forty years saw My works.
chapters.zh: 在那里，你们的祖宗试我探我， 并且观看我的作为有四十年之久。

chapters.en: Therefore I was angry with that generation, and I said, ‘Their hearts are always going astray, and they have not known My ways.’
chapters.zh: 所以，我厌烦那世代的人，说： 他们心里常常迷糊， 竟不晓得我的作为！

chapters.en: So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’”
chapters.zh: 我就在怒中起誓说： 他们断不可进入我的安息。

chapters.en: See to it, brothers, that none of you has a wicked heart of unbelief that turns away from the living God.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，你们要谨慎，免得你们中间或有人存着不信的恶心，把永生上帝离弃了。

chapters.en: But exhort one another daily, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by sin’s deceitfulness.
chapters.zh: 总要趁着还有今日，天天彼此相劝，免得你们中间有人被罪迷惑，心里就刚硬了。

chapters.en: We have come to share in Christ if we hold firmly to the end the assurance we had at first.
chapters.zh: 我们若将起初确实的信心坚持到底，就在基督里有分了。

chapters.en:
As it has been said:
“Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion.”
chapters.zh: 〔经上〕说：「你们今日若听他的话，就不可硬着心，像惹他发怒的日子一样。」

chapters.en: For who were the ones who heard and rebelled? Were they not all those Moses led out of Egypt?
chapters.zh: 那时，听见他话惹他发怒的是谁呢？岂不是跟着摩西从埃及出来的众人吗？

chapters.en: And with whom was God angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
chapters.zh: 上帝四十年之久，又厌烦谁呢？岂不是那些犯罪、尸首倒在旷野的人吗？

chapters.en: And to whom did He swear that they would never enter His rest? Was it not to those who disobeyed?
chapters.zh: 又向谁起誓，不容他们进入他的安息呢？岂不是向那些不信从的人吗？

chapters.en: So we see that it was because of their unbelief that they were unable to enter.
chapters.zh: 这样看来，他们不能进入〔安息〕是因为不信的缘故了。

chapters.en: Therefore, while the promise of entering His rest still stands, let us be careful that none of you be deemed to have fallen short of it.
chapters.zh: 我们既蒙留下，有进入他安息的应许，就当畏惧，免得我们〔注：原文是你们〕中间或有人似乎是赶不上了。

chapters.en: For we also received the good news just as they did; but the message they heard was of no value to them, since they did not share the faith of those who comprehended it.
chapters.zh: 因为有福音传给我们，像传给他们一样；只是所听见的道与他们无益，因为他们没有信心与所听见的道调和。

chapters.en:
Now we who have believed enter that rest. As for the others, it is just as God has said:
“So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’”
And yet His works have been finished since the foundation of the world.
chapters.zh: 但我们已经相信的人得以进入那安息，正如上帝所说：「我在怒中起誓说：『他们断不可进入我的安息！』」其实造物之工，从创世以来已经成全了。

chapters.en: For somewhere He has spoken about the seventh day in this manner: “And on the seventh day God rested from all His works.”
chapters.zh: 论到第七日，有一处说：「到第七日，上帝就歇了他一切的工。」

chapters.en: And again, as He says in the passage above: “They shall never enter My rest.”
chapters.zh: 又有一处说：「他们断不可进入我的安息！」

chapters.en: Since, then, it remains for some to enter His rest, and since those who formerly heard the good news did not enter because of their disobedience,
chapters.zh: 既有必进安息的人，那先前听见福音的，因为不信从，不得进去。

chapters.en: God again designated a certain day as “Today,” when a long time later He spoke through David as was just stated: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”
chapters.zh: 所以过了多年，就在大卫的书上，又限定一日，如以上所引的说：「你们今日若听他的话，就不可硬着心。」

chapters.en: For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.
chapters.zh: 若是约书亚已叫他们享了安息，后来上帝就不再提别的日子了。

chapters.en: There remains, then, a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
chapters.zh: 这样看来，必另有一安息日的安息为上帝的子民存留。

chapters.en: For whoever enters God’s rest also rests from his own work, just as God did from His.
chapters.zh: 因为那进入安息的，乃是歇了自己的工，正如上帝歇了他的工一样。

chapters.en: Let us, therefore, make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one will fall by following the same pattern of disobedience.
chapters.zh: 所以，我们务必竭力进入那安息，免得有人学那不信从的样子跌倒了。

chapters.en: For the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it pierces even to dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
chapters.zh: 上帝的道是活泼的，是有功效的，比一切两刃的剑更快，甚至魂与灵，骨节与骨髓，都能刺入、剖开，连心中的思念和主意都能辨明。

chapters.en: Nothing in all creation is hidden from God’s sight; everything is uncovered and exposed before the eyes of Him to whom we must give account.
chapters.zh: 并且被造的没有一样在他面前不显然的；原来万物在那与我们有关系的主眼前，都是赤露敞开的。

chapters.en: Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to what we profess.
chapters.zh: 我们既然有一位已经升入高天尊荣的大祭司，就是上帝的儿子耶稣，便当持定所承认的道。

chapters.en: For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin.
chapters.zh: 因我们的大祭司并非不能体恤我们的软弱。他也曾凡事受过试探，与我们一样，只是他没有犯罪。

chapters.en: Let us then approach the throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.
chapters.zh: 所以，我们只管坦然无惧地来到施恩的宝座前，为要得怜恤，蒙恩惠，作随时的帮助。

chapters.en: Every high priest is appointed from among men to represent them in matters relating to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
chapters.zh: 凡从人间挑选的大祭司，是奉派替人办理属上帝的事，为要献上礼物和赎罪祭〔注：或译：要为罪献上礼物和祭物〕。

chapters.en: He is able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and misguided, since he himself is subject to weakness.
chapters.zh: 他能体谅那愚蒙的和失迷的人，因为他自己也是被软弱所困。

chapters.en: That is why he is obligated to offer sacrifices for his own sins, as well as for the sins of the people.
chapters.zh: 故此，他理当为百姓和自己献祭赎罪。

chapters.en: No one takes this honor upon himself; he must be called by God, just as Aaron was.
chapters.zh: 这〔大祭司的〕尊荣，没有人自取。惟要蒙上帝所召，像亚伦一样。

chapters.en:
So also Christ did not take upon Himself the glory of becoming a high priest, but He was called by the One who said to Him:
“You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.”
chapters.zh: 如此，基督也不是自取荣耀作大祭司，乃是在乎向他说「你是我的儿子，我今日生你」的那一位；

chapters.en:
And in another passage God says:
“You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”
chapters.zh: 就如〔经上〕又有一处说：「你是照着麦基洗德的等次永远为祭司。」

chapters.en: During the days of Jesus’ earthly life, He offered up prayers and petitions with loud cries and tears to the One who could save Him from death, and He was heard because of His reverence.
chapters.zh: 基督在肉体的时候，既大声哀哭，流泪祷告，恳求那能救他免死的主，就因他的虔诚蒙了应允。

chapters.en: Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from what He suffered.
chapters.zh: 他虽然为儿子，还是因所受的苦难学了顺从。

chapters.en: And having been made perfect, He became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him
chapters.zh: 他既得以完全，就为凡顺从他的人成了永远得救的根源，

chapters.en: and was designated by God as high priest in the order of Melchizedek.
chapters.zh: 并蒙上帝照着麦基洗德的等次称他为大祭司。

chapters.en: We have much to say about this, but it is hard to explain, because you are dull of hearing.
chapters.zh: 论到麦基洗德，我们有好些话，并且难以解明，因为你们听不进去。

chapters.en: Although by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to reteach you the basic principles of God’s word. You need milk, not solid food!
chapters.zh: 看你们学习的工夫，本该作师傅，谁知还得有人将上帝圣言小学的开端另教导你们，并且成了那必须吃奶、不能吃干粮的人。

chapters.en: For everyone who lives on milk is still an infant, inexperienced in the message of righteousness.
chapters.zh: 凡只能吃奶的都不熟练仁义的道理，因为他是婴孩；

chapters.en: But solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained their senses to distinguish good from evil.
chapters.zh: 惟独长大成人的才能吃干粮；他们的心窍习练得通达，就能分辨好歹了。

chapters.en: Therefore let us leave the elementary teachings about Christ and go on to maturity, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith in God,
chapters.zh: 所以，我们应当离开基督道理的开端，竭力进到完全的地步，不必再立根基，就如那懊悔死行、信靠上帝、

chapters.en: instruction about baptisms, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
chapters.zh: 各样洗礼、按手之礼、死人复活，以及永远审判各等教训。

chapters.en: And this we will do, if God permits.
chapters.zh: 上帝若许我们，我们必如此行。

chapters.en: It is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, who have shared in the Holy Spirit,
chapters.zh: 论到那些已经蒙了光照、尝过天恩的滋味、又于圣灵有分，

chapters.en: who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age—
chapters.zh: 并尝过上帝善道的滋味、觉悟来世权能的人，

chapters.en: and then have fallen away—to be restored to repentance, because they themselves are crucifying the Son of God all over again and subjecting Him to open shame.
chapters.zh: 若是离弃〔道〕理，就不能叫他们重新懊悔了。因为他们把上帝的儿子重钉十字架，明明地羞辱他。

chapters.en: For land that drinks in the rain often falling on it and that produces a crop useful to those for whom it is tended receives the blessing of God.
chapters.zh: 就如一块田地，吃过屡次下的雨水，生长菜蔬，合乎耕种的人用，就从上帝得福；

chapters.en: But land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless, and its curse is imminent. In the end it will be burned.
chapters.zh: 若长荆棘和蒺藜，必被废弃，近于咒诅，结局就是焚烧。

chapters.en: Even though we speak like this, beloved, we are convinced of better things in your case—things that accompany salvation.
chapters.zh: 亲爱的弟兄们，我们虽是这样说，却深信你们的行为强过这些，而且近乎得救。

chapters.en: For God is not unjust. He will not forget your work and the love you have shown for His name as you have ministered to the saints and continue to do so.
chapters.zh: 因为上帝并非不公义，竟忘记你们所做的工和你们为他名所显的爱心，就是先前伺候圣徒，如今还是伺候。

chapters.en: We want each of you to show this same diligence to the very end, in order to make your hope sure.
chapters.zh: 我们愿你们各人都显出这样的殷勤，使你们有满足的指望，一直到底。

chapters.en: Then you will not be sluggish, but will imitate those who through faith and patience inherit what has been promised.
chapters.zh: 并且不懈怠，总要效法那些凭信心和忍耐承受应许的人。

chapters.en: When God made His promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater to swear by, He swore by Himself,
chapters.zh: 当初上帝应许亚伯拉罕的时候，因为没有比自己更大可以指着起誓的，就指着自己起誓，说：

chapters.en: saying, “I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants.”
chapters.zh: 「论福，我必赐大福给你；论子孙，我必叫你的子孙多起来。」

chapters.en: And so Abraham, after waiting patiently, obtained the promise.
chapters.zh: 这样，亚伯拉罕既恒久忍耐，就得了所应许的。

chapters.en: Men swear by someone greater than themselves, and their oath serves as a confirmation to end all argument.
chapters.zh: 人都是指着比自己大的起誓，并且以起誓为实据，了结各样的争论。

chapters.en: So when God wanted to make the unchanging nature of His purpose very clear to the heirs of the promise, He guaranteed it with an oath.
chapters.zh: 照样，上帝愿意为那承受应许的人格外显明他的旨意是不更改的，就起誓为证。

chapters.en: Thus by two unchangeable things in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled to take hold of the hope set before us may be strongly encouraged.
chapters.zh: 藉这两件不更改的事，上帝决不能说谎，好叫我们这逃往避难所、持定摆在我们前头指望的人可以大得勉励。

chapters.en: We have this hope as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure. It enters the inner sanctuary behind the curtain,
chapters.zh: 我们有这指望，如同灵魂的锚，又坚固又牢靠，且通入幔内。

chapters.en: where Jesus our forerunner has entered on our behalf. He has become a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.
chapters.zh: 作先锋的耶稣，既照着麦基洗德的等次成了永远的大祭司，就为我们进入幔内。

chapters.en: This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
chapters.zh: 这麦基洗德就是撒冷王，又是至高上帝的祭司，本是长远为祭司的。他当亚伯拉罕杀败诸王回来的时候，就迎接他，给他祝福。

chapters.en: and Abraham apportioned to him a tenth of everything. First, his name means “king of righteousness.” Then also, “king of Salem” means “king of peace.”
chapters.zh: 亚伯拉罕也将自己所得来的，取十分之一给他。他头一个名翻出来就是仁义王，他又名撒冷王，就是平安王的意思。

chapters.en: Without father or mother or genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life, like the Son of God, he remains a priest for all time.
chapters.zh: 他无父，无母，无族谱，无生之始，无命之终，乃是与上帝的儿子相似。

chapters.en: Consider how great Melchizedek was: Even the patriarch Abraham gave him a tenth of the plunder.
chapters.zh: 你们想一想，先祖亚伯拉罕将自己所掳来上等之物取十分之一给他，这人是何等尊贵呢！

chapters.en: Now the law commands the sons of Levi who become priests to collect a tenth from the people—that is, from their brothers—though they too are descended from Abraham.
chapters.zh: 那得祭司职任的利未子孙，领命照例向百姓取十分之一，这百姓是自己的弟兄，虽是从亚伯拉罕身〔注：原文是腰〕中生的，还是照例〔取十分之一〕。

chapters.en: But Melchizedek, who did not trace his descent from Levi, collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed him who had the promises.
chapters.zh: 独有麦基洗德，不与他们同谱，倒收纳亚伯拉罕的十分之一，为那蒙应许的亚伯拉罕祝福。

chapters.en: And indisputably, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
chapters.zh: 从来位分大的给位分小的祝福，这是驳不倒的理。

chapters.en: In the case of the Levites, mortal men collect the tenth; but in the case of Melchizedek, it is affirmed that he lives on.
chapters.zh: 在这里收十分之一的都是必死的人；但在那里收十分之一的，有为他作见证的说，他是活的；

chapters.en: And so to speak, Levi, who collects the tenth, paid the tenth through Abraham.
chapters.zh: 并且可说那受十分之一的利未，也是藉着亚伯拉罕纳了十分之一。

chapters.en: For when Melchizedek met Abraham, Levi was still in the loin of his ancestor.
chapters.zh: 因为麦基洗德迎接亚伯拉罕的时候，利未已经在他先祖的身〔注：原文是腰〕中。

chapters.en: Now if perfection could have been attained through the Levitical priesthood (for on this basis the people received the law), why was there still need for another priest to appear—one in the order of Melchizedek and not in the order of Aaron?
chapters.zh: 从前百姓在利未人祭司职任以下受律法，倘若藉这职任能得完全，又何用另外兴起一位祭司，照麦基洗德的等次，不照亚伦的等次呢？

chapters.en: For when the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed as well.
chapters.zh: 祭司的职任既已更改，律法也必须更改。

chapters.en: He of whom these things are said belonged to a different tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.
chapters.zh: 因为这话所指的人本属别的支派，那支派里从来没有一人伺候祭坛。

chapters.en: For it is clear that our Lord descended from Judah, a tribe as to which Moses said nothing about priests.
chapters.zh: 我们的主分明是从犹大出来的；但这支派，摩西并没有提到祭司。

chapters.en: And this point is even more clear if another priest like Melchizedek appears,
chapters.zh: 倘若照麦基洗德的样式，另外兴起一位祭司来，〔我的话〕更是显而易见的了。

chapters.en: one who has become a priest not by a law of succession, but by the power of an indestructible life.
chapters.zh: 他成为祭司，并不是照属肉体的条例，乃是照无穷〔注：原文是不能毁坏〕之生命的大能。

chapters.en:
For it is testified:
“You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”
chapters.zh: 因为有给他作见证的说：「你是照着麦基洗德的等次永远为祭司。」

chapters.en: So the former commandment is set aside because it was weak and useless
chapters.zh: 先前的条例，因软弱无益，所以废掉了，

chapters.en: (for the law made nothing perfect), and a better hope is introduced, by which we draw near to God.
chapters.zh: （律法原来一无所成）就引进了更美的指望；靠这指望，我们便可以进到上帝面前。

chapters.en: And none of this happened without an oath. For others became priests without an oath,
chapters.zh: 再者，〔耶稣为祭司〕，并不是不起誓立的。

chapters.en:
but Jesus became a priest with an oath by the One who said to Him:
“The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: ‘You are a priest forever.’”
chapters.zh: 至于那些祭司，原不是起誓立的，只有耶稣是起誓立的；因为那立他的对他说：「主起了誓，决不后悔，你是永远为祭司。」

chapters.en: Because of this oath, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.
chapters.zh: 既是起誓立的，耶稣就作了更美之约的中保。

chapters.en: Now there have been many other priests, since death prevented them from continuing in office.
chapters.zh: 那些成为祭司的，数目本来多，是因为有死阻隔，不能长久。

chapters.en: But because Jesus lives forever, He has a permanent priesthood.
chapters.zh: 这位既是永远常存的，他祭司的职任就长久不更换。

chapters.en: Therefore He is able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them.
chapters.zh: 凡靠着他进到上帝面前的人，他都能拯救到底；因为他是长远活着，替他们祈求。

chapters.en: Such a high priest truly befits us—One who is holy, innocent, undefiled, set apart from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.
chapters.zh: 像这样圣洁、无邪恶、无玷污、远离罪人、高过诸天的大祭司，原是与我们合宜的。

chapters.en: Unlike the other high priests, He does not need to offer daily sacrifices, first for His own sins and then for the sins of the people; He sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself.
chapters.zh: 他不像那些大祭司，每日必须先为自己的罪，后为百姓的罪献祭；因为他只一次将自己献上，就把这事成全了。

chapters.en: For the law appoints as high priests men who are weak; but the oath, which came after the law, appointed the Son, who has been made perfect forever.
chapters.zh: 律法本是立软弱的人为大祭司；但在律法以后起誓的话，是立儿子为大祭司，乃是成全到永远的。

chapters.en: The point of what we are saying is this: We do have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven,
chapters.zh: 我们所讲的事，其中第一要紧的，就是我们有这样的大祭司，已经坐在天上至大者宝座的右边，

chapters.en: and who ministers in the sanctuary and true tabernacle set up by the Lord, not by man.
chapters.zh: 在圣所，就是真帐幕里，作执事；这帐幕是主所支的，不是人所支的。

chapters.en: And since every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices, it was necessary for this One also to have something to offer.
chapters.zh: 凡大祭司都是为献礼物和祭物设立的，所以这位大祭司也必须有所献的。

chapters.en: Now if He were on earth, He would not be a priest, since there are already priests who offer gifts according to the law.
chapters.zh: 他若在地上，必不得为祭司，因为已经有照律法献礼物的〔祭司〕。

chapters.en: The place where they serve is a copy and shadow of what is in heaven. This is why Moses was warned when he was about to build the tabernacle: “See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.”
chapters.zh: 他们供奉的事本是天上事的形状和影像，正如摩西将要造帐幕的时候，蒙〔上帝〕警戒他，说：「你要谨慎，作各样的物件都要照着在山上指示你的样式。」

chapters.en: Now, however, Jesus has received a much more excellent ministry, just as the covenant He mediates is better and is founded on better promises.
chapters.zh: 如今耶稣所得的职任是更美的，正如他作更美之约的中保；这约原是凭更美之应许立的。

chapters.en: For if that first covenant had been without fault, no place would have been sought for a second.
chapters.zh: 那前约若没有瑕疵，就无处寻求后约了。

chapters.en:
But God found fault with the people and said:
“Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
chapters.zh: 所以主指责他的百姓说〔注：或译：所以主指前约的缺欠说〕： 日子将到， 我要与以色列家和犹大家另立新约，

chapters.en: It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not abide by My covenant, and I disregarded them, declares the Lord.
chapters.zh: 不像我拉着他们祖宗的手， 领他们出埃及的时候， 与他们所立的约。 因为他们不恒心守我的约， 我也不理他们。 这是主说的。

chapters.en: For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the Lord. I will put My laws in their minds and inscribe them on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be My people.
chapters.zh: 主又说： 那些日子以后， 我与以色列家所立的约乃是这样： 我要将我的律法放在他们里面， 写在他们心上； 我要作他们的上帝； 他们要作我的子民。

chapters.en: No longer will each one teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.
chapters.zh: 他们不用各人教导自己的乡邻和自己的弟兄， 说：你该认识主； 因为他们从最小的到至大的，都必认识我。

chapters.en: For I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more.”
chapters.zh: 我要宽恕他们的不义， 不再记念他们的罪愆。

chapters.en: By speaking of a new covenant, He has made the first one obsolete; and what is obsolete and aging will soon disappear.
chapters.zh: 既说新约，就以前约为旧了；但那渐旧渐衰的，就必快归无有了。

chapters.en: Now the first covenant had regulations for worship and also an earthly sanctuary.
chapters.zh: 原来前约有礼拜的条例和属世界的圣幕。

chapters.en: A tabernacle was prepared. In its first room were the lampstand, the table, and the consecrated bread. This was called the Holy Place.
chapters.zh: 因为有预备的帐幕，头一层叫作圣所，里面有灯台、桌子，和陈设饼。

chapters.en: Behind the second curtain was a room called the Most Holy Place,
chapters.zh: 第二幔子后又有一层帐幕，叫作至圣所，

chapters.en: containing the golden altar of incense and the gold-covered ark of the covenant. Inside the ark were the gold jar of manna, Aaron’s staff that had budded, and the stone tablets of the covenant.
chapters.zh: 有金香炉〔注：炉：或译坛〕，有包金的约柜，柜里有盛吗哪的金罐和亚伦发过芽的杖，并两块约版；

chapters.en: Above the ark were the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the mercy seat. But we cannot discuss these things in detail now.
chapters.zh: 柜上面有荣耀基路伯的影罩着施恩〔注：施恩：原文是蔽罪〕座。这几件我现在不能一一细说。

chapters.en: When everything had been prepared in this way, the priests entered regularly into the first room to perform their sacred duties.
chapters.zh: 这些物件既如此预备齐了，众祭司就常进头一层帐幕，行拜上帝的礼。

chapters.en: But only the high priest entered the second room, and then only once a year, and never without blood, which he offered for himself and for the sins the people had committed in ignorance.
chapters.zh: 至于第二层帐幕，惟有大祭司一年一次独自进去，没有不带着血为自己和百姓的过错献上。

chapters.en: By this arrangement the Holy Spirit was showing that the way into the Most Holy Place had not yet been disclosed as long as the first tabernacle was still standing.
chapters.zh: 圣灵用此指明，头一层帐幕仍存的时候，进入至圣所的路还未显明。

chapters.en: It is an illustration for the present time, because the gifts and sacrifices being offered were unable to cleanse the conscience of the worshiper.
chapters.zh: 那头一层帐幕作现今的一个表样，所献的礼物和祭物，就着良心说，都不能叫礼拜的人得以完全。

chapters.en: They consist only in food and drink and special washings—external regulations imposed until the time of reform.
chapters.zh: 这些事，连那饮食和诸般洗濯的规矩，都不过是属肉体的条例，命定到振兴的时候为止。

chapters.en: But when Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come, He went through the greater and more perfect tabernacle that is not made by hands and is not a part of this creation.
chapters.zh: 但现在基督已经来到，作了将来美事的大祭司，经过那更大更全备的帐幕，不是人手所造，也不是属乎这世界的；

chapters.en: He did not enter by the blood of goats and calves, but He entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption.
chapters.zh: 并且不用山羊和牛犊的血，乃用自己的血，只一次进入圣所，成了永远赎罪的事。

chapters.en: For if the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean sanctify them so that their bodies are clean,
chapters.zh: 若山羊和公牛的血，并母牛犊的灰，洒在不洁的人身上，尚且叫人成圣，身体洁净，

chapters.en: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, purify our consciences from works of death, so that we may serve the living God!
chapters.zh: 何况基督藉着永远的灵，将自己无瑕无疵献给上帝，他的血岂不更能洗净你们的心〔注：原文是良心〕，除去你们的死行，使你们事奉那永生上帝吗？

chapters.en: Therefore Christ is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance, now that He has died to redeem them from the transgressions committed under the first covenant.
chapters.zh: 为此，他作了新约的中保，既然受死赎了人在前约之时所犯的罪过，便叫蒙召之人得着所应许永远的产业。

chapters.en: In the case of a will, it is necessary to establish the death of the one who made it,
chapters.zh: 凡有遗命必须等到留遗命〔注：遗命：原文与约字同〕的人死了；

chapters.en: because a will does not take effect until the one who made it has died; it cannot be executed while he is still alive.
chapters.zh: 因为人死了，遗命才有效力，若留遗命的尚在，那遗命还有用处吗？

chapters.en: That is why even the first covenant was not put into effect without blood.
chapters.zh: 所以，前约也不是不用血立的；

chapters.en: For when Moses had proclaimed every commandment of the law to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, along with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled the scroll and all the people,
chapters.zh: 因为摩西当日照着律法将各样诫命传给众百姓，就拿朱红色绒和牛膝草，把牛犊山羊的血和水洒在书上，又洒在众百姓身上，说：

chapters.en: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant, which God has commanded you to keep.”
chapters.zh: 「这血就是上帝与你们立约〔的凭据〕。」

chapters.en: In the same way, he sprinkled with blood the tabernacle and all the vessels used in worship.
chapters.zh: 他又照样把血洒在帐幕和各样器皿上。

chapters.en: According to the law, in fact, nearly everything must be purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
chapters.zh: 按着律法，凡物差不多都是用血洁净的；若不流血，罪就不得赦免了。

chapters.en: So it was necessary for the copies of the heavenly things to be purified with these sacrifices, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
chapters.zh: 照着天上样式做的物件必须用这些祭物去洁净；但那天上的本物自然当用更美的祭物去洁净。

chapters.en: For Christ did not enter a man-made copy of the true sanctuary, but He entered heaven itself, now to appear on our behalf in the presence of God.
chapters.zh: 因为基督并不是进了人手所造的圣所（这不过是真圣所的影像），乃是进了天堂，如今为我们显在上帝面前；

chapters.en: Nor did He enter heaven to offer Himself again and again, as the high priest enters the Most Holy Place every year with blood that is not his own.
chapters.zh: 也不是多次将自己献上，像那大祭司每年带着牛羊的血〔注：牛羊的血：原文作不是自己的血〕进入圣所，

chapters.en: Otherwise, Christ would have had to suffer repeatedly since the foundation of the world. But now He has appeared once for all at the end of the ages to do away with sin by the sacrifice of Himself.
chapters.zh: 如果这样，他从创世以来，就必多次受苦了。但如今在这末世显现一次，把自己献为祭，好除掉罪。

chapters.en: Just as man is appointed to die once, and after that to face judgment,
chapters.zh: 按着定命，人人都有一死，死后且有审判。

chapters.en: so also Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many; and He will appear a second time, not to bear sin, but to bring salvation to those who eagerly await Him.
chapters.zh: 像这样，基督既然一次被献，担当了多人的罪，将来要向那等候他的人第二次显现，并与罪无关，乃是为拯救他们。

chapters.en: For the law is only a shadow of the good things to come, not the realities themselves. It can never, by the same sacrifices offered year after year, make perfect those who draw near to worship.
chapters.zh: 律法既是将来美事的影儿，不是本物的真像，总不能藉着每年常献一样的祭物叫那近前来的人得以完全。

chapters.en: If it could, would not the offerings have ceased? For the worshipers would have been cleansed once for all, and would no longer have felt the guilt of their sins.
chapters.zh: 若不然，献祭的事岂不早已止住了吗？因为礼拜的人，良心既被洁净，就不再觉得有罪了。

chapters.en: Instead, those sacrifices are an annual reminder of sins,
chapters.zh: 但这些〔祭物〕是叫人每年想起罪来；

chapters.en: because it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
chapters.zh: 因为公牛和山羊的血，断不能除罪。

chapters.en:
Therefore, when Christ came into the world, He said:
“Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You prepared for Me.
chapters.zh: 所以基督到世上来的时候，就说： 〔上帝啊〕，祭物和礼物是你不愿意的； 你曾给我预备了身体。

chapters.en: In burnt offerings and sin offerings You took no delight.
chapters.zh: 燔祭和赎罪〔祭〕是你不喜欢的。

chapters.en: Then I said, ‘Here I am, it is written about Me in the scroll: I have come to do Your will, O God.’”
chapters.zh: 那时我说：上帝啊，我来了， 为要照你的旨意行； 我的事在经卷上已经记载了。

chapters.en: In the passage above He says, “Sacrifices and offerings, burnt offerings and sin offerings You did not desire, nor did You delight in them” (although they are offered according to the law).
chapters.zh: 以上说：「祭物和礼物，燔祭和赎罪祭，是你不愿意的，也是你不喜欢的（这都是按着律法献的）」；

chapters.en: Then He adds, “Here I am, I have come to do Your will.” He takes away the first to establish the second.
chapters.zh: 后又说：「我来了为要照你的旨意行」；〔可见〕他是除去在先的，为要立定在后的。

chapters.en: And by that will, we have been sanctified through the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
chapters.zh: 我们凭这旨意，靠耶稣基督，只一次献上他的身体，就得以成圣。

chapters.en: Day after day every priest stands to minister and to offer again and again the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.
chapters.zh: 凡祭司天天站着事奉〔上帝〕，屡次献上一样的祭物，这祭物永不能除罪。

chapters.en: But when this Priest had offered for all time one sacrifice for sins, He sat down at the right hand of God.
chapters.zh: 但基督献了一次永远的赎罪祭，就在上帝的右边坐下了。

chapters.en: Since that time, He waits for His enemies to be made a footstool for His feet,
chapters.zh: 从此，等候他仇敌成了他的脚凳。

chapters.en: because by a single offering He has made perfect for all time those who are being sanctified.
chapters.zh: 因为他一次献祭，便叫那得以成圣的人永远完全。

chapters.en: The Holy Spirit also testifies to us about this. First He says:
chapters.zh: 圣灵也对我们作见证；因为他既已说过：

chapters.en: “This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, declares the Lord. I will put My laws in their hearts and inscribe them on their minds.”
chapters.zh: 主说：那些日子以后， 我与他们所立的约乃是这样： 我要将我的律法写在他们心上， 又要放在他们的里面。

chapters.en:
Then He adds:
“Their sins and lawless acts I will remember no more.”
chapters.zh: 〔以后就说〕： 我不再记念他们的罪愆和他们的过犯。

chapters.en: And where these have been forgiven, an offering for sin is no longer needed.
chapters.zh: 这些罪过既已赦免，就不用再为罪献祭了。

chapters.en: Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus,
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我们既因耶稣的血得以坦然进入至圣所，

chapters.en: by the new and living way opened for us through the curtain of His body,
chapters.zh: 是藉着他给我们开了一条又新又活的路，从幔子经过，这幔子就是他的身体。

chapters.en: and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
chapters.zh: 又有一位大祭司治理上帝的家，

chapters.en: let us draw near with a sincere heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled to cleanse us from a guilty conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
chapters.zh: 并我们心中天良的亏欠已经洒去，身体用清水洗净了，就当存着诚心和充足的信心来到上帝面前；

chapters.en: Let us hold resolutely to the hope we profess, for He who promised is faithful.
chapters.zh: 也要坚守我们所承认的指望，不致摇动，因为那应许我们的是信实的。

chapters.en: And let us consider how to spur one another on to love and good deeds.
chapters.zh: 又要彼此相顾，激发爱心，勉励行善。

chapters.en: Let us not neglect meeting together, as some have made a habit, but let us encourage one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.
chapters.zh: 你们不可停止聚会，好像那些停止惯了的人，倒要彼此劝勉，既知道〔注：原文是看见〕那日子临近，就更当如此。

chapters.en: If we deliberately go on sinning after we have received the knowledge of the truth, no further sacrifice for sins remains,
chapters.zh: 因为我们得知真道以后，若故意犯罪，赎罪的祭就再没有了；

chapters.en: but only a fearful expectation of judgment and of raging fire that will consume all adversaries.
chapters.zh: 惟有战惧等候审判和那烧灭众敌人的烈火。

chapters.en: Anyone who rejected the law of Moses died without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
chapters.zh: 人干犯摩西的律法，凭两三个见证人，尚且不得怜恤而死，

chapters.en: How much more severely do you think one deserves to be punished who has trampled on the Son of God, profaned the blood of the covenant that sanctified him, and insulted the Spirit of grace?
chapters.zh: 何况人践踏上帝的儿子，将那使他成圣之约的血当作平常，又亵慢施恩的〔圣〕灵，你们想，他要受的刑罚该怎样加重呢！

chapters.en: For we know Him who said, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay,” and again, “The Lord will judge His people.”
chapters.zh: 因为我们知道谁说：「伸冤在我，我必报应」；又〔说〕：「主要审判他的百姓。」

chapters.en: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
chapters.zh: 落在永生上帝的手里，真是可怕的！

chapters.en: Remember the early days that you were in the light. In those days, you endured a great conflict in the face of suffering.
chapters.zh: 你们要追念往日，蒙了光照以后所忍受大争战的各样苦难：

chapters.en: Sometimes you were publicly exposed to ridicule and persecution; at other times you were partners with those who were so treated.
chapters.zh: 一面被毁谤，遭患难，成了戏景，叫众人观看；一面陪伴那些受这样苦难的人。

chapters.en: You sympathized with those in prison and joyfully accepted the confiscation of your property, knowing that you yourselves had a better and permanent possession.
chapters.zh: 因为你们体恤了那些被捆锁的人，并且你们的家业被人抢去，也甘心忍受，知道自己有更美长存的家业。

chapters.en: So do not throw away your confidence; it holds a great reward.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们不可丢弃勇敢的心；存这样的心必得大赏赐。

chapters.en: You need to persevere, so that after you have done the will of God, you will receive what He has promised.
chapters.zh: 你们必须忍耐，使你们行完了上帝的旨意，就可以得着所应许的。

chapters.en:
For,
“In just a little while, He who is coming will come and will not delay.
chapters.zh: 因为还有一点点时候， 那要来的就来，并不迟延；

chapters.en:
But My righteous one will live by faith; and if he shrinks back,
I will take no pleasure in him.”
chapters.zh: 只是义人〔注：有古卷：我的义人〕必因信得生。 他若退后，我心里就不喜欢他。

chapters.en: But we are not of those who shrink back and are destroyed, but of those who have faith and preserve their souls.
chapters.zh: 我们却不是退后入沉沦的那等人，乃是有信心以致灵魂得救的人。

chapters.en: Now faith is the assurance of what we hope for and the certainty of what we do not see.
chapters.zh: 信就是所望之事的实底，是未见之事的确据。

chapters.en: This is why the ancients were commended.
chapters.zh: 古人在这信上得了美好的证据。

chapters.en: By faith we understand that the universe was formed at God’s command, so that what is seen was not made out of what was visible.
chapters.zh: 我们因着信，就知道诸世界是藉上帝话造成的；这样，所看见的，并不是从显然之物造出来的。

chapters.en: By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. By faith he was commended as righteous when God gave approval to his gifts. And by faith he still speaks, even though he is dead.
chapters.zh: 亚伯因着信，献祭与上帝，比该隐所献的更美，因此便得了称义的见证，就是上帝指他礼物作的见证。他虽然死了，却因这信，仍旧说话。

chapters.en: By faith Enoch was taken up so that he did not see death: “He could not be found, because God had taken him away.” For before he was taken, he was commended as one who pleased God.
chapters.zh: 以诺因着信，被接去，不至于见死，人也找不着他，因为上帝已经把他接去了；只是他被接去以先，已经得了上帝喜悦他的明证。

chapters.en: And without faith it is impossible to please God. For anyone who approaches Him must believe that He exists and that He rewards those who earnestly seek Him.
chapters.zh: 人非有信，就不能得上帝的喜悦；因为到上帝面前来的人必须信有上帝，且信他赏赐那寻求他的人。
