chapters.en: By faith Noah, when warned about things not yet seen, in godly fear built an ark to save his family. By faith he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.
chapters.zh: 挪亚因着信，既蒙〔上帝〕指示他未见的事，动了敬畏的心，预备了一只方舟，使他全家得救。因此就定了那世代的罪，自己也承受了那从信而来的义。

chapters.en: By faith Abraham, when called to go to a place he would later receive as his inheritance, obeyed and went, without knowing where he was going.
chapters.zh: 亚伯拉罕因着信，蒙召的时候就遵命出去，往将来要得为业的地方去；出去的时候，还不知往哪里去。

chapters.en: By faith he dwelt in the promised land as a stranger in a foreign country. He lived in tents, as did Isaac and Jacob, who were heirs with him of the same promise.
chapters.zh: 他因着信，就在所应许之地作客，好像在异地居住帐棚，与那同蒙一个应许的以撒、雅各一样。

chapters.en: For he was looking forward to the city with foundations, whose architect and builder is God.
chapters.zh: 因为他等候那座有根基的城，就是上帝所经营所建造的。

chapters.en: By faith Sarah, even though she was barren and beyond the proper age, was enabled to conceive a child, because she considered Him faithful who had promised.
chapters.zh: 因着信，连撒拉自己，虽然过了生育的岁数，还能怀孕，因她以为那应许她的是可信的。

chapters.en: And so from one man, and he as good as dead, came descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as countless as the sand on the seashore.
chapters.zh: 所以从一个仿佛已死的人就生出〔子孙〕，如同天上的星那样众多，海边的沙那样无数。

chapters.en: All these people died in faith, without having received the things they were promised. However, they saw them and welcomed them from afar. And they acknowledged that they were strangers and exiles on the earth.
chapters.zh: 这些人都是存着信心死的，并没有得着所应许的；却从远处望见，且欢喜迎接，又承认自己在世上是客旅，是寄居的。

chapters.en: Now those who say such things show that they are seeking a country of their own.
chapters.zh: 说这样话的人是表明自己要找一个家乡。

chapters.en: If they had been thinking of the country they had left, they would have had opportunity to return.
chapters.zh: 他们若想念所离开的家乡，还有可以回去的机会。

chapters.en: Instead, they were longing for a better country, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for He has prepared a city for them.
chapters.zh: 他们却羨慕一个更美的家乡，就是在天上的。所以上帝被称为他们的上帝，并不以为耻，因为他已经给他们预备了一座城。

chapters.en: By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac on the altar. He who had received the promises was ready to offer his one and only son,
chapters.zh: 亚伯拉罕因着信，被试验的时候，就把以撒献上；这便是那欢喜领受应许的，将自己独生的儿子献上。

chapters.en: even though God had said to him, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”
chapters.zh: 〔论到这儿子〕，曾有话说：「从以撒生的才要称为你的后裔。」

chapters.en: Abraham reasoned that God could raise the dead, and in a sense, he did receive Isaac back from death.
chapters.zh: 他以为上帝还能叫人从死里复活；他也仿佛从死中得回他的儿子来。

chapters.en: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning the future.
chapters.zh: 以撒因着信，就指着将来的事给雅各、以扫祝福。

chapters.en: By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of Joseph’s sons and worshiped as he leaned on the top of his staff.
chapters.zh: 雅各因着信，临死的时候，给约瑟的两个儿子各自祝福，扶着杖头敬拜上帝。

chapters.en: By faith Joseph, when his end was near, spoke about the exodus of the Israelites and gave instructions about his bones.
chapters.zh: 约瑟因着信，临终的时候，提到以色列族将来要出〔埃及〕，并为自己的骸骨留下遗命。

chapters.en: By faith Moses’ parents hid him for three months after his birth, because they saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were unafraid of the king’s edict.
chapters.zh: 摩西生下来，他的父母见他是个俊美的孩子，就因着信，把他藏了三个月，并不怕王命。

chapters.en: By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.
chapters.zh: 摩西因着信，长大了就不肯称为法老女儿之子。

chapters.en: He chose to suffer oppression with God’s people rather than to experience the fleeting enjoyment of sin.
chapters.zh: 他宁可和上帝的百姓同受苦害，也不愿暂时享受罪中之乐。

chapters.en: He valued disgrace for Christ above the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to his reward.
chapters.zh: 他看为基督受的凌辱比埃及的财物更宝贵，因他想望所要得的赏赐。

chapters.en: By faith Moses left Egypt, not fearing the king’s anger; he persevered because he saw Him who is invisible.
chapters.zh: 他因着信，就离开埃及，不怕王怒；因为他恒心忍耐，如同看见那不能看见的〔主〕。

chapters.en: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch Israel’s own firstborn.
chapters.zh: 他因着信，就守〔注：或译：立〕逾越节，行洒血的礼，免得那灭长子的临近以色列人。

chapters.en: By faith the people passed through the Red Sea as on dry land; but when the Egyptians tried to follow, they were drowned.
chapters.zh: 他们因着信，过红海如行干地；埃及人试着要过去，就被吞灭了。

chapters.en: By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after the people had marched around them for seven days.
chapters.zh: 以色列人因着信，围绕耶利哥城七日，城墙就倒塌了。

chapters.en: By faith the prostitute Rahab, because she welcomed the spies in peace, did not perish with those who were disobedient.
chapters.zh: 妓女喇合因着信，曾和和平平地接待探子，就不与那些不顺从的人一同灭亡。

chapters.en: And what more shall I say? Time will not allow me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets,
chapters.zh: 我又何必再说呢？若要一一细说，基甸、巴拉、参孙、耶弗他、大卫、撒母耳，和众先知的事，时候就不够了。

chapters.en: who through faith conquered kingdoms, administered justice, and gained what was promised; who shut the mouths of lions,
chapters.zh: 他们因着信，制伏了敌国，行了公义，得了应许，堵了狮子的口，

chapters.en: quenched the raging fire, and escaped the edge of the sword; who gained strength from weakness, became mighty in battle, and put foreign armies to flight.
chapters.zh: 灭了烈火的猛势，脱了刀剑的锋刃；软弱变为刚强，争战显出勇敢，打退外邦的全军。

chapters.en: Women received back their dead, raised to life again. Others were tortured and refused their release, so that they might gain a better resurrection.
chapters.zh: 有妇人得自己的死人复活。又有人忍受严刑，不肯苟且得释放〔注：原文是赎〕，为要得着更美的复活。

chapters.en: Still others endured mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.
chapters.zh: 又有人忍受戏弄、鞭打、捆锁、监禁、各等的磨炼，

chapters.en: They were stoned, they were sawed in two, they were put to death by the sword. They went around in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, oppressed, and mistreated.
chapters.zh: 被石头打死，被锯锯死，受试探，被刀杀，披着绵羊、山羊的皮各处奔跑，受穷乏、患难、苦害，

chapters.en: The world was not worthy of them. They wandered in deserts and mountains, and hid in caves and holes in the ground.
chapters.zh: 在旷野、山岭、山洞、地穴，飘流无定，本是世界不配有的人。

chapters.en: These were all commended for their faith, yet they did not receive what was promised.
chapters.zh: 这些人都是因信得了美好的证据，却仍未得着所应许的；

chapters.en: God had planned something better for us, so that together with us they would be made perfect.
chapters.zh: 因为上帝给我们预备了更美的事，叫他们若不与我们同得，就不能完全。

chapters.en: Therefore, since we are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, let us throw off every encumbrance and the sin that so easily entangles, and let us run with endurance the race set out for us.
chapters.zh: 我们既有这许多的见证人，如同云彩围着我们，就当放下各样的重担，脱去容易缠累我们的罪，存心忍耐，奔那摆在我们前头的路程，

chapters.en: Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy set before Him endured the cross, scorning its shame, and sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
chapters.zh: 仰望为我们信心创始成终的耶稣〔注：或译：仰望那将真道创始成终的耶稣〕。他因那摆在前面的喜乐，就轻看羞辱，忍受了十字架〔的苦难〕，便坐在上帝宝座的右边。

chapters.en: Consider Him who endured such hostility from sinners, so that you will not grow weary and lose heart.
chapters.zh: 那忍受罪人这样顶撞的，你们要思想，免得疲倦灰心。

chapters.en: In your struggle against sin, you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood.
chapters.zh: 你们与罪恶相争，还没有抵挡到流血的地步。

chapters.en:
And you have forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons:
“My son, do not take lightly the discipline of the Lord, and do not lose heart when He rebukes you.
chapters.zh: 你们又忘了那劝你们如同劝儿子的话，说： 我儿，你不可轻看主的管教， 被他责备的时候也不可灰心；

chapters.en: For the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and He chastises every son He receives.”
chapters.zh: 因为主所爱的，他必管教， 又鞭打凡所收纳的儿子。

chapters.en: Endure suffering as discipline; God is treating you as sons. For what son is not disciplined by his father?
chapters.zh: 你们所忍受的，是上帝管教你们，待你们如同待儿子。焉有儿子不被父亲管教的呢？

chapters.en: If you do not experience discipline like everyone else, then you are illegitimate children and not true sons.
chapters.zh: 管教原是众子所共受的。你们若不受管教，就是私子，不是儿子了。

chapters.en: Furthermore, we have all had earthly fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them. Should we not much more submit to the Father of our spirits and live?
chapters.zh: 再者，我们曾有生身的父管教我们，我们尚且敬重他，何况万灵的父，我们岂不更当顺服他得生吗？

chapters.en: Our fathers disciplined us for a short time as they thought best, but God disciplines us for our good, so that we may share in His holiness.
chapters.zh: 生身的父都是暂随己意管教我们；惟有万灵的父管教我们，是要我们得益处，使我们在他的圣洁上有分。

chapters.en: No discipline seems enjoyable at the time, but painful. Later on, however, it yields a harvest of righteousness and peace to those who have been trained by it.
chapters.zh: 凡管教的事，当时不觉得快乐，反觉得愁苦；后来却为那经练过的人结出平安的果子，就是义。

chapters.en: Therefore strengthen your limp hands and weak knees.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们要把下垂的手、发酸的腿挺起来；

chapters.en: Make straight paths for your feet, so that the lame may not be disabled, but rather healed.
chapters.zh: 也要为自己的脚，把道路修直了，使瘸子不致歪脚〔注：或译：差路〕，反得痊愈。

chapters.en: Pursue peace with everyone, as well as holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.
chapters.zh: 你们要追求与众人和睦，并要追求圣洁；非圣洁没有人能见主。

chapters.en: See to it that no one falls short of the grace of God, and that no root of bitterness springs up to cause trouble and defile many.
chapters.zh: 又要谨慎，恐怕有人失了上帝的恩；恐怕有毒根生出来扰乱你们，因此叫众人沾染污秽；

chapters.en: See to it that no one is sexually immoral, or is godless like Esau, who for a single meal sold his birthright.
chapters.zh: 恐怕有淫乱的，有贪恋世俗如以扫的，他因一点食物把自己长子的名分卖了。

chapters.en: For you know that afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected. He could find no ground for repentance, though he sought the blessing with tears.
chapters.zh: 后来想要承受父所祝的福，竟被弃绝，虽然号哭切求，却得不着门路使他〔父亲〕的心意回转。这是你们知道的。

chapters.en: For you have not come to a mountain that can be touched and that is burning with fire; to darkness, gloom, and storm;
chapters.zh: 你们原不是来到那能摸的山；此山有火焰、密云、黑暗、暴风、

chapters.en: to a trumpet blast or to a voice that made its hearers beg that no further word be spoken.
chapters.zh: 角声与说话的声音。那些听见这声音的，都求不要再向他们说话；

chapters.en: For they could not bear what was commanded: “If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned.”
chapters.zh: 因为他们当不起所命他们的话，说：「靠近这山的，即便是走兽，也要用石头打死。」

chapters.en: The sight was so terrifying that even Moses said, “I am trembling with fear.”
chapters.zh: 所见的极其可怕，甚至摩西说：「我甚是恐惧战兢。」

chapters.en: Instead, you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. You have come to myriads of angels
chapters.zh: 你们乃是来到锡安山，永生上帝的城邑，就是天上的耶路撒冷。那里有千万的天使，

chapters.en: in joyful assembly, to the congregation of the firstborn, enrolled in heaven. You have come to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of the righteous made perfect,
chapters.zh: 有名录在天上诸长子之会所共聚的总会，有审判众人的上帝和被成全之义人的灵魂，

chapters.en: to Jesus the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.
chapters.zh: 并新约的中保耶稣，以及所洒的血；这血所说的比亚伯的血所说的更美。

chapters.en: See to it that you do not refuse Him who speaks. For if the people did not escape when they refused Him who warned them on earth, how much less will we escape if we reject Him who warns us from heaven?
chapters.zh: 你们总要谨慎，不可弃绝那向你们说话的。因为，那些弃绝在地上警戒他们的尚且不能逃罪，何况我们违背那从天上警戒我们的呢？

chapters.en: At that time His voice shook the earth, but now He has promised, “Once more I will shake not only the earth, but heaven as well.”
chapters.zh: 当时他的声音震动了地，但如今他应许说：「再一次我不单要震动地，还要震动天。」

chapters.en: The words “Once more” signify the removal of what can be shaken—that is, created things—so that the unshakable may remain.
chapters.zh: 这再一次的话，是指明被震动的，就是受造之物都要挪去，使那不被震动的常存。

chapters.en: Therefore, since we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us be filled with gratitude, and so worship God acceptably with reverence and awe.
chapters.zh: 所以我们既得了不能震动的国，就当感恩，照上帝所喜悦的，用虔诚、敬畏的心事奉上帝。

chapters.en: “For our God is a consuming fire.”
chapters.zh: 因为我们的上帝乃是烈火。

chapters.en: Continue in brotherly love.
chapters.zh: 你们务要常存弟兄相爱的心。

chapters.en: Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have entertained angels without knowing it.
chapters.zh: 不可忘记用爱心接待客旅；因为曾有接待客旅的，不知不觉就接待了天使。

chapters.en: Remember those in prison as if you were bound with them, and those who are mistreated as if you were suffering with them.
chapters.zh: 你们要记念被捆绑的人，好像与他们同受捆绑；也要记念遭苦害的人，想到自己也在肉身之内。

chapters.en: Marriage should be honored by all and the marriage bed kept undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.
chapters.zh: 婚姻，人人都当尊重，床也不可污秽；因为苟合行淫的人，上帝必要审判。

chapters.en:
Keep your lives free from the love of money and be content with what you have, for God has said:
“Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you.”
chapters.zh: 你们存心不可贪爱钱财，要以自己所有的为足；因为主曾说：「我总不撇下你，也不丢弃你。」

chapters.en:
So we say with confidence:
“The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?”
chapters.zh: 所以我们可以放胆说： 主是帮助我的，我必不惧怕； 人能把我怎么样呢？

chapters.en: Remember your leaders who spoke the word of God to you. Consider the outcome of their way of life and imitate their faith.
chapters.zh: 从前引导你们、传上帝之道给你们的人，你们要想念他们，效法他们的信心，留心看他们为人的结局。

chapters.en: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
chapters.zh: 耶稣基督昨日、今日、一直到永远，是一样的。

chapters.en: Do not be carried away by all kinds of strange teachings, for it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace and not by foods of no value to those devoted to them.
chapters.zh: 你们不要被那诸般怪异的教训勾引了去；因为人心靠恩得坚固才是好的，并不是靠饮食。那在饮食上专心的从来没有得着益处。

chapters.en: We have an altar from which those who serve at the tabernacle have no right to eat.
chapters.zh: 我们有一祭坛，上面的祭物是那些在帐幕中供职的人不可同吃的。

chapters.en: Although the high priest brings the blood of animals into the Holy Place as a sacrifice for sin, the bodies are burned outside the camp.
chapters.zh: 原来牲畜的血被大祭司带入圣所作赎罪祭；牲畜的身子被烧在营外。

chapters.en: And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate, to sanctify the people by His own blood.
chapters.zh: 所以，耶稣要用自己的血叫百姓成圣，也就在城门外受苦。

chapters.en: Therefore let us go to Him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace He bore.
chapters.zh: 这样，我们也当出到营外，就了他去，忍受他所受的凌辱。

chapters.en: For here we do not have a permanent city, but we are looking for the city that is to come.
chapters.zh: 我们在这里本没有常存的城，乃是寻求那将来的城。

chapters.en: Through Jesus, therefore, let us continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that confess His name.
chapters.zh: 我们应当靠着耶稣，常常以颂赞为祭献给上帝，这就是那承认主名之人嘴唇的果子。

chapters.en: And do not neglect to do good and to share with others, for with such sacrifices God is pleased.
chapters.zh: 只是不可忘记行善和捐输的事，因为这样的祭是上帝所喜悦的。

chapters.en: Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they watch over your souls as those who must give an account. To this end, allow them to lead with joy and not with grief, for that would be of no advantage to you.
chapters.zh: 你们要依从那些引导你们的，且要顺服；因他们为你们的灵魂时刻警醒，好像那将来交帐的人。你们要使他们交的时候有快乐，不致忧愁；若忧愁就与你们无益了。

chapters.en: Pray for us; we are convinced that we have a clear conscience and desire to live honorably in every way.
chapters.zh: 请你们为我们祷告，因我们自觉良心无亏，愿意凡事按正道而行。

chapters.en: And I especially urge you to pray that I may be restored to you soon.
chapters.zh: 我更求你们为我祷告，使我快些回到你们那里去。

chapters.en: Now may the God of peace, who through the blood of the eternal covenant brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great Shepherd of the sheep,
chapters.zh: 但愿赐平安的上帝，就是那凭永约之血、使群羊的大牧人－我主耶稣从死里复活的上帝，

chapters.en: equip you with every good thing to do His will. And may He accomplish in us what is pleasing in His sight through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
chapters.zh: 在各样善事上成全你们，叫你们遵行他的旨意；又藉着耶稣基督在你们心里行他所喜悦的事。愿荣耀归给他，直到永永远远。阿们！

chapters.en: I urge you, brothers, to bear with my word of exhortation, for I have only written to you briefly.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，我略略写信给你们，望你们听我劝勉的话。

chapters.en: Be aware that our brother Timothy has been released. If he arrives soon, I will come with him to see you.
chapters.zh: 你们该知道，我们的兄弟提摩太已经释放了；他若快来，我必同他去见你们。

chapters.en:
Greet all your leaders and all the saints.
Those from Italy send you greetings.
chapters.zh: 请你们问引导你们的诸位和众圣徒安。从意大利来的人也问你们安。

chapters.en: Grace be with all of you.
chapters.zh: 愿恩惠〔常〕与你们众人同在。阿们！

chapters.en:
James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ,
To the twelve tribes of the Dispersion:
Greetings.
chapters.zh: 作上帝和主耶稣基督仆人的雅各请散住十二个支派之人的安。

chapters.en: Consider it pure joy, my brothers, when you encounter trials of many kinds,
chapters.zh: 我的弟兄们，你们落在百般试炼中，都要以为大喜乐；

chapters.en: because you know that the testing of your faith develops perseverance.
chapters.zh: 因为知道你们的信心经过试验，就生忍耐。

chapters.en: Allow perseverance to finish its work, so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything.
chapters.zh: 但忍耐也当成功，使你们成全、完备，毫无缺欠。

chapters.en: Now if any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to him.
chapters.zh: 你们中间若有缺少智慧的，应当求那厚赐与众人、也不斥责人的上帝，〔主〕就必赐给他。

chapters.en: But he must ask in faith, without doubting, because he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.
chapters.zh: 只要凭着信心求，一点不疑惑；因为那疑惑的人，就像海中的波浪，被风吹动翻腾。

chapters.en: That man should not expect to receive anything from the Lord.
chapters.zh: 这样的人不要想从主那里得什么。

chapters.en: He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
chapters.zh: 心怀二意的人，在他一切所行的路上都没有定见。

chapters.en: The brother in humble circumstances should exult in his high position.
chapters.zh: 卑微的弟兄升高，就该喜乐；

chapters.en: But the one who is rich should exult in his low position, because he will pass away like a flower of the field.
chapters.zh: 富足的降卑，也该如此；因为他必要过去，如同草上的花一样。

chapters.en: For the sun rises with scorching heat and withers the plant; its flower falls and its beauty is lost. So too, the rich man will fade away in the midst of his pursuits.
chapters.zh: 太阳出来，热风刮起，草就枯干，花也凋谢，美容就消没了；那富足的人，在他所行的事上也要这样衰残。

chapters.en: Blessed is the man who perseveres under trial, because when he has stood the test, he will receive the crown of life that God has promised to those who love Him.
chapters.zh: 忍受试探的人是有福的，因为他经过试验以后，必得生命的冠冕；这是〔主〕应许给那些爱他之人的。

chapters.en: When tempted, no one should say, “God is tempting me.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone.
chapters.zh: 人被试探，不可说：「我是被上帝试探」；因为上帝不能被恶试探，他也不试探人。

chapters.en: But each one is tempted when by his own evil desires he is lured away and enticed.
chapters.zh: 但各人被试探，乃是被自己的私欲牵引诱惑的。

chapters.en: Then after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.
chapters.zh: 私欲既怀了胎，就生出罪来；罪既长成，就生出死来。

chapters.en: Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.
chapters.zh: 我亲爱的弟兄们，不要看错了。

chapters.en: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.
chapters.zh: 各样美善的恩赐和各样全备的赏赐都是从上头来的，从众光之父那里降下来的；在他并没有改变，也没有转动的影儿。

chapters.en: He chose to give us birth through the word of truth, that we would be a kind of firstfruits of His creation.
chapters.zh: 他按自己的旨意，用真道生了我们，叫我们在他所造的万物中好像初熟的果子。

chapters.en: My beloved brothers, understand this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger,
chapters.zh: 我亲爱的弟兄们，这是你们所知道的。但你们各人要快快地听，慢慢地说，慢慢地动怒，

chapters.en: for man’s anger does not bring about the righteousness that God desires.
chapters.zh: 因为人的怒气并不成就上帝的义。

chapters.en: Therefore, get rid of all moral filth and every expression of evil, and humbly accept the word planted in you, which can save your souls.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们要脱去一切的污秽和盈余的邪恶，存温柔的心领受那所栽种的道，就是能救你们灵魂的道。

chapters.en: Be doers of the word, and not hearers only. Otherwise, you are deceiving yourselves.
chapters.zh: 只是你们要行道，不要单单听道，自己欺哄自己。

chapters.en: For anyone who hears the word but does not carry it out is like a man who looks at his face in a mirror,
chapters.zh: 因为听道而不行道的，就像人对着镜子看自己本来的面目，

chapters.en: and after observing himself goes away and immediately forgets what he looks like.
chapters.zh: 看见，走后，随即忘了他的相貌如何。

chapters.en: But the one who looks intently into the perfect law of freedom, and continues to do so—not being a forgetful hearer, but an effective doer—he will be blessed in what he does.
chapters.zh: 惟有详细察看那全备、〔使人〕自由之律法的，并且时常如此，这人既不是听了就忘，乃是实在行出来，就在他所行的事上必然得福。

chapters.en: If anyone considers himself religious and yet does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his heart and his religion is worthless.
chapters.zh: 若有人自以为虔诚，却不勒住他的舌头，反欺哄自己的心，这人的虔诚是虚的。

chapters.en: Pure and undefiled religion before our God and Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their distress, and to keep oneself from being polluted by the world.
chapters.zh: 在上帝我们的父面前，那清洁没有玷污的虔诚，就是看顾在患难中的孤儿寡妇，并且保守自己不沾染世俗。

chapters.en: My brothers, as you hold out your faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, do not show favoritism.
chapters.zh: 我的弟兄们，你们信奉我们荣耀的主耶稣基督，便不可按着外貌待人。

chapters.en: Suppose a man comes into your meeting wearing a gold ring and fine clothes, and a poor man in shabby clothes also comes in.
chapters.zh: 若有一个人带着金戒指，穿着华美衣服，进你们的会堂去；又有一个穷人穿着肮脏衣服也进去；

chapters.en: If you lavish attention on the man in fine clothes and say, “Here is a seat of honor,” but say to the poor man, “You must stand” or “Sit at my feet,”
chapters.zh: 你们就重看那穿华美衣服的人，说：「请坐在这好位上」；又对那穷人说：「你站在那里」，或「坐在我脚凳下边。」

chapters.en: have you not discriminated among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
chapters.zh: 这岂不是你们偏心待人，用恶意断定人吗？

chapters.en: Listen, my beloved brothers: Has not God chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom He promised those who love Him?
chapters.zh: 我亲爱的弟兄们，请听，上帝岂不是拣选了世上的贫穷人，叫他们在信上富足，并承受他所应许给那些爱他之人的国吗？

chapters.en: But you have dishonored the poor. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into court?
chapters.zh: 你们反倒羞辱贫穷人。那富足人岂不是欺压你们、拉你们到公堂去吗？

chapters.en: Are they not the ones who blaspheme the noble name by which you have been called?
chapters.zh: 他们不是亵渎你们所敬奉〔注：所敬奉：或译被称〕的尊名吗？

chapters.en: If you really fulfill the royal law stated in Scripture, “Love your neighbor as yourself,” you are doing well.
chapters.zh: 经上记着说：「要爱人如己。」你们若全守这至尊的律法才是好的。

chapters.en: But if you show favoritism, you sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors.
chapters.zh: 但你们若按外貌待人，便是犯罪，被律法定为犯法的。

chapters.en: Whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles at just one point is guilty of breaking all of it.
chapters.zh: 因为凡遵守全律法的，只在一条上跌倒，他就是犯了众条。

chapters.en: For He who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not murder.” If you do not commit adultery, but do commit murder, you have become a lawbreaker.
chapters.zh: 原来那说「不可奸淫」的，也说「不可杀人」；你就是不奸淫，却杀人，仍是成了犯律法的。

chapters.en: Speak and act as those who are going to be judged by the law that gives freedom.
chapters.zh: 你们既然要按〔使人〕自由的律法受审判，就该照这律法说话行事。

chapters.en: For judgment without mercy will be shown to anyone who has not been merciful. Mercy triumphs over judgment.
chapters.zh: 因为那不怜悯人的，也要受无怜悯的审判；怜悯原是向审判夸胜。

chapters.en: What good is it, my brothers, if someone claims to have faith, but has no deeds? Can such faith save him?
chapters.zh: 我的弟兄们，若有人说自己有信心，却没有行为，有什么益处呢？这信心能救他吗？

chapters.en: Suppose a brother or sister is without clothes and daily food.
chapters.zh: 若是弟兄或是姊妹，赤身露体，又缺了日用的饮食；

chapters.en: If one of you tells him, “Go in peace; stay warm and well fed,” but does not provide for his physical needs, what good is that?
chapters.zh: 你们中间有人对他们说：「平平安安地去吧！愿你们穿得暖，吃得饱」，却不给他们身体所需用的，这有什么益处呢？

chapters.en: So too, faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead.
chapters.zh: 这样，信心若没有行为就是死的。

chapters.en: But someone will say, “You have faith and I have deeds.” Show me your faith without deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds.
chapters.zh: 必有人说：「你有信心，我有行为；你将你没有行为的信心指给我看，我便藉着我的行为，将我的信心指给你看。」

chapters.en: You believe that God is one. Good for you! Even the demons believe that—and shudder.
chapters.zh: 你信上帝只有一位，你信的不错；鬼魔也信，却是战惊。

chapters.en: O foolish man, do you want evidence that faith without deeds is worthless?
chapters.zh: 虚浮的人哪，你愿意知道没有行为的信心是死的吗？

chapters.en: Was not our father Abraham justified by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?
chapters.zh: 我们的祖宗亚伯拉罕把他儿子以撒献在坛上，岂不是因行为称义吗？

chapters.en: You see that his faith was working with his actions, and his faith was perfected by what he did.
chapters.zh: 可见，信心是与他的行为并行，而且信心因着行为才得成全。

chapters.en: And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,” and he was called a friend of God.
chapters.zh: 这就应验经上所说：「亚伯拉罕信上帝，这就算为他的义。」他又得称为上帝的朋友。

chapters.en: As you can see, a man is justified by his deeds and not by faith alone.
chapters.zh: 这样看来，人称义是因着行为，不是单因着信。

chapters.en: In the same way, was not even Rahab the prostitute justified by her actions when she welcomed the spies and sent them off on another route?
chapters.zh: 妓女喇合接待使者，又放他们从别的路上出去，不也是一样因行为称义吗？

chapters.en: As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead.
chapters.zh: 身体没有灵魂是死的，信心没有行为也是死的。

chapters.en: Not many of you should become teachers, my brothers, because you know that we who teach will be judged more strictly.
chapters.zh: 我的弟兄们，不要多人作师傅，因为晓得我们要受更重的判断。

chapters.en: We all stumble in many ways. If anyone is never at fault in what he says, he is a perfect man, able to control his whole body.
chapters.zh: 原来我们在许多事上都有过失；若有人在话语上没有过失，他就是完全人，也能勒住自己的全身。

chapters.en: When we put bits into the mouths of horses to make them obey us, we can guide the whole animal.
chapters.zh: 我们若把嚼环放在马嘴里，叫牠顺服，就能调动牠的全身。

chapters.en: Consider ships as well. Although they are so large and are driven by strong winds, they are steered by a very small rudder wherever the pilot is inclined.
chapters.zh: 看哪，船只虽然甚大，又被大风催逼，只用小小的舵，就随着掌舵的意思转动。

chapters.en: In the same way, the tongue is a small part of the body, but it boasts of great things. Consider how small a spark sets a great forest ablaze.
chapters.zh: 这样，舌头在百体里也是最小的，却能说大话。 看哪，最小的火能点着最大的树林。

chapters.en: The tongue also is a fire, a world of wickedness among the parts of the body. It pollutes the whole person, sets the course of his life on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.
chapters.zh: 舌头就是火，在我们百体中，舌头是个罪恶的世界，能污秽全身，也能把生命的轮子点起来，并且是从地狱里点着的。

chapters.en: All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and creatures of the sea are being tamed and have been tamed by man,
chapters.zh: 各类的走兽、飞禽、昆虫、水族，本来都可以制伏，也已经被人制伏了；

chapters.en: but no man can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
chapters.zh: 惟独舌头没有人能制伏，是不止息的恶物，满了害死人的毒气。

chapters.en: With the tongue we bless our Lord and Father, and with it we curse men, who have been made in God’s likeness.
chapters.zh: 我们用舌头颂赞那为主、为父的，又用舌头咒诅那照着上帝形像被造的人。

chapters.en: Out of the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, this should not be!
chapters.zh: 颂赞和咒诅从一个口里出来！我的弟兄们，这是不应当的！

chapters.en: Can both fresh water and salt water flow from the same spring?
chapters.zh: 泉源从一个眼里能发出甜苦两样的水吗？

chapters.en: My brothers, can a fig tree grow olives, or a grapevine bear figs? Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water.
chapters.zh: 我的弟兄们，无花果树能生橄榄吗？葡萄树能结无花果吗？咸水里也不能发出甜水来。

chapters.en: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show it by his good conduct, by deeds done in the humility that comes from wisdom.
chapters.zh: 你们中间谁是有智慧有见识的呢？他就当在智慧的温柔上显出他的善行来。

chapters.en: But if you harbor bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your hearts, do not boast in it or deny the truth.
chapters.zh: 你们心里若怀着苦毒的嫉妒和纷争，就不可自夸，也不可说谎话抵挡真道。

chapters.en: Such wisdom does not come from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, demonic.
chapters.zh: 这样的智慧不是从上头来的，乃是属地的，属情欲的，属鬼魔的。

chapters.en: For where jealousy and selfish ambition exist, there will be disorder and every evil practice.
chapters.zh: 在何处有嫉妒、纷争，就在何处有扰乱和各样的坏事。

chapters.en: But the wisdom from above is first of all pure, then peace-loving, gentle, accommodating, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, and sincere.
chapters.zh: 惟独从上头来的智慧，先是清洁，后是和平，温良柔顺，满有怜悯，多结善果，没有偏见，没有假冒。

chapters.en: Peacemakers who sow in peace reap the fruit of righteousness.
chapters.zh: 并且使人和平的，是用和平所栽种的义果。

chapters.en: What causes conflicts and quarrels among you? Don’t they come from the passions at war within you?
chapters.zh: 你们中间的争战斗殴是从哪里来的呢？不是从你们百体中战斗之私欲来的吗？

chapters.en: You crave what you do not have; you kill and covet, but are unable to obtain it. You quarrel and fight. You do not have, because you do not ask.
chapters.zh: 你们贪恋，还是得不着；你们杀害嫉妒，又斗殴争战，也不能得。你们得不着，是因为你们不求。

chapters.en: And when you do ask, you do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, that you may squander it on your pleasures.
chapters.zh: 你们求也得不着，是因为你们妄求，要浪费在你们的宴乐中。

chapters.en: You adulteresses! Do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Therefore, whoever chooses to be a friend of the world renders himself an enemy of God.
chapters.zh: 你们这些淫乱的人〔注：原文是淫妇〕哪，岂不知与世俗为友就是与上帝为敌吗？所以凡想要与世俗为友的，就是与上帝为敌了。

chapters.en: Or do you think the Scripture says without reason that the Spirit He caused to dwell in us yearns with envy?
chapters.zh: 你们想经上所说是徒然的吗？上帝所赐、住在我们里面的灵，是恋爱至于嫉妒吗？

chapters.en:
But He gives us more grace. This is why it says:
“God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
chapters.zh: 但他赐更多的恩典，所以经上说： 上帝阻挡骄傲的人， 赐恩给谦卑的人。

chapters.en: Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
chapters.zh: 故此，你们要顺服上帝。务要抵挡魔鬼，魔鬼就必离开你们逃跑了。

chapters.en: Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.
chapters.zh: 你们亲近上帝，上帝就必亲近你们。有罪的人哪，要洁净你们的手！心怀二意的人哪，要清洁你们的心！

chapters.en: Grieve, mourn, and weep. Turn your laughter to mourning, and your joy to gloom.
chapters.zh: 你们要愁苦、悲哀、哭泣，将喜笑变作悲哀，欢乐变作愁闷。

chapters.en: Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you.
chapters.zh: 务要在主面前自卑，主就必叫你们升高。

chapters.en: Brothers, do not slander one another. Anyone who speaks against his brother or judges him speaks against the law and judges it. And if you judge the law, you are not a practitioner of the law, but a judge of it.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，你们不可彼此批评。人若批评弟兄，论断弟兄，就是批评律法，论断律法。你若论断律法，就不是遵行律法，乃是判断人的。

chapters.en: There is only one Lawgiver and Judge, the One who is able to save and destroy. But who are you to judge your neighbor?
chapters.zh: 设立律法和判断人的，只有一位，就是那能救人也能灭人的。你是谁，竟敢论断别人呢？

chapters.en: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, spend a year there, carry on business, and make a profit.”
chapters.zh: 嗐！你们有话说：「今天明天我们要往某城里去，在那里住一年，做买卖得利。」

chapters.en: You do not even know what will happen tomorrow! What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.
chapters.zh: 其实明天如何，你们还不知道。你们的生命是什么呢？你们原来是一片云雾，出现少时就不见了。

chapters.en: Instead, you ought to say, “If the Lord is willing, we will live and do this or that.”
chapters.zh: 你们只当说：「主若愿意，我们就可以活着，也可以做这事，或做那事。」

chapters.en: As it is, you boast in your proud intentions. All such boasting is evil.
chapters.zh: 现今你们竟以张狂夸口；凡这样夸口都是恶的。

chapters.en: Anyone, then, who knows the right thing to do, yet fails to do it, is guilty of sin.
chapters.zh: 人若知道行善，却不去行，这就是他的罪了。

chapters.en: Come now, you who are rich, weep and wail over the misery to come upon you.
chapters.zh: 嗐！你们这些富足人哪，应当哭泣、号咷，因为将有苦难临到你们身上。

chapters.en: Your riches have rotted and moths have eaten your clothes.
chapters.zh: 你们的财物坏了，衣服也被虫子咬了。

chapters.en:
Your gold and silver are corroded. Their corrosion will testify against you and consume your flesh like fire.
You have hoarded treasure in the last days.
chapters.zh: 你们的金银都长了锈；那锈要证明你们的不是，又要吃你们的肉，如同火烧。你们在这末世只知积攒钱财。

chapters.en: Look, the wages you withheld from the workmen who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.
chapters.zh: 工人给你们收割庄稼，你们亏欠他们的工钱，这工钱有声音呼叫，并且那收割之人的冤声已经入了万军之主的耳了。

chapters.en: You have lived on earth in luxury and self-indulgence. You have fattened your hearts in the day of slaughter.
chapters.zh: 你们在世上享美福，好宴乐，当宰杀的日子竟娇养你们的心。

chapters.en: You have condemned and murdered the righteous, who did not resist you.
chapters.zh: 你们定了义人的罪，把他杀害，他也不抵挡你们。

chapters.en: Be patient, then, brothers, until the Lord’s coming. See how the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the soil—how patient he is for the fall and spring rains.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们哪，你们要忍耐，直到主来。看哪，农夫忍耐等候地里宝贵的出产，直到得了秋雨春雨。

chapters.en: You, too, be patient and strengthen your hearts, because the Lord’s coming is near.
chapters.zh: 你们也当忍耐，坚固你们的心，因为主来的日子近了。

chapters.en: Do not complain about one another, brothers, so that you will not be judged. Look, the Judge is standing at the door!
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，你们不要彼此埋怨，免得受审判。看哪，审判的〔主〕站在门前了。

chapters.en: Brothers, as an example of patience in affliction, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，你们要把那先前奉主名说话的众先知当作能受苦能忍耐的榜样。

chapters.en: See how blessed we consider those who have persevered. You have heard of Job’s perseverance and have seen the outcome from the Lord. The Lord is full of compassion and mercy.
chapters.zh: 那先前忍耐的人，我们称他们是有福的。你们听见过约伯的忍耐，也知道主〔给他〕的结局，明显主是满心怜悯，大有慈悲。

chapters.en: Above all, my brothers, do not swear, not by heaven or earth or by any other oath. Simply let your “Yes” be yes, and your “No,” no, so that you will not fall under judgment.
chapters.zh: 我的弟兄们，最要紧的是不可起誓；不可指着天起誓，也不可指着地起誓，无论何誓都不可起。你们说话，是，就说是；不是，就说不是，免得你们落在审判之下。

chapters.en: Is any one of you suffering? He should pray. Is anyone cheerful? He should sing praises.
chapters.zh: 你们中间有受苦的呢，他就该祷告；有喜乐的呢，他就该歌颂。

chapters.en: Is any one of you sick? He should call the elders of the church to pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.
chapters.zh: 你们中间有病了的呢，他就该请教会的长老来；他们可以奉主的名用油抹他，为他祷告。

chapters.en: And the prayer offered in faith will restore the one who is sick. The Lord will raise him up. If he has sinned, he will be forgiven.
chapters.zh: 出于信心的祈祷要救那病人，主必叫他起来；他若犯了罪，也必蒙赦免。

chapters.en: Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous man has great power to prevail.
chapters.zh: 所以你们要彼此认罪，互相代求，使你们可以得医治。义人祈祷所发的力量是大有功效的。

chapters.en: Elijah was a man just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three and a half years.
chapters.zh: 以利亚与我们是一样性情的人，他恳切祷告，求不要下雨，雨就三年零六个月不下在地上。

chapters.en: Again he prayed, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth yielded its crops.
chapters.zh: 他又祷告，天就降下雨来，地也生出土产。

chapters.en: My brothers, if one of you should wander from the truth and someone should bring him back,
chapters.zh: 我的弟兄们，你们中间若有失迷真道的，有人使他回转，

chapters.en: consider this: Whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death and cover over a multitude of sins.
chapters.zh: 这人该知道：叫一个罪人从迷路上转回便是救一个灵魂不死，并且遮盖许多的罪。

chapters.en:
Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ,
To the elect who are exiles of the Dispersion throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, chosen
chapters.zh: 耶稣基督的使徒彼得写信给那分散在本都、加拉太、加帕多家、亚细亚、庇推尼寄居的，

chapters.en:
according to the foreknowledge of God the Father and sanctified by the Spirit for obedience to Jesus Christ and sprinkling by His blood:
Grace and peace be yours in abundance.
chapters.zh: 就是照父上帝的先见被拣选，藉着〔圣〕灵得成圣洁，以致顺服耶稣基督，又蒙他血所洒的人。愿恩惠、平安多多地加给你们。

chapters.en: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! By His great mercy He has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
chapters.zh: 愿颂赞归与我们主耶稣基督的父上帝！他曾照自己的大怜悯，藉耶稣基督从死里复活，重生了我们，叫我们有活泼的盼望，

chapters.en: and into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, reserved in heaven for you,
chapters.zh: 可以得着不能朽坏、不能玷污、不能衰残、为你们存留在天上的基业。

chapters.en: who through faith are shielded by God’s power for the salvation that is ready to be revealed in the last time.
chapters.zh: 你们这因信蒙上帝能力保守的人，必能得着所预备、到末世要显现的救恩。

chapters.en: In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while you may have had to suffer grief in various trials
chapters.zh: 因此，你们是大有喜乐；但如今，在百般的试炼中暂时忧愁，

chapters.en: so that the proven character of your faith—more precious than gold, which perishes even though refined by fire—may result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 叫你们的信心既被试验，就比那被火试验仍然能坏的金子更显宝贵，可以在耶稣基督显现的时候得着称赞、荣耀、尊贵。

chapters.en: Though you have not seen Him, you love Him; and though you do not see Him now, you believe in Him and rejoice with an inexpressible and glorious joy,
chapters.zh: 你们虽然没有见过他，却是爱他；如今虽不得看见，却因信他就有说不出来、满有荣光的大喜乐；

chapters.en: now that you are receiving the goal of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
chapters.zh: 并且得着你们信心的果效，就是灵魂的救恩。

chapters.en: Concerning this salvation, the prophets who foretold the grace to come to you searched and investigated carefully,
chapters.zh: 论到这救恩，那预先说你们要得恩典的众先知早已详细地寻求考察，

chapters.en: trying to determine the time and setting to which the Spirit of Christ in them was pointing when He predicted the sufferings of Christ and the glories to follow.
chapters.zh: 就是考察在他们心里基督的灵，预先证明基督受苦难，后来得荣耀，是指着什么时候，并怎样的时候。

chapters.en: It was revealed to them that they were not serving themselves, but you, when they foretold the things now announced by those who preached the gospel to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven. Even angels long to look into these things.
chapters.zh: 他们得了启示，知道他们所传讲〔注：原文是服事〕的一切事，不是为自己，乃是为你们。那靠着从天上差来的圣灵传福音给你们的人，现在将这些事报给你们；天使也愿意详细察看这些事。

chapters.en: Therefore prepare your minds for action. Be sober-minded. Set your hope fully on the grace to be given you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 所以要约束你们的心〔注：原文是束上你们心中的腰〕，谨慎自守，专心盼望耶稣基督显现的时候所带来给你们的恩。

chapters.en: As obedient children, do not conform to the passions of your former ignorance.
chapters.zh: 你们既作顺命的儿女，就不要效法从前蒙昧无知的时候那放纵私欲的样子。

chapters.en: But just as He who called you is holy, so be holy in all you do,
chapters.zh: 那召你们的既是圣洁，你们在一切所行的事上也要圣洁。

chapters.en: for it is written: “Be holy, because I am holy.”
chapters.zh: 因为〔经上〕记着说：「你们要圣洁，因为我是圣洁的。」

chapters.en: Since you call on a Father who judges each one’s work impartially, conduct yourselves in reverent fear during your stay as foreigners.
chapters.zh: 你们既称那不偏待人、按各人行为审判人的〔主〕为父，就当存敬畏的心度你们在世寄居的日子，

chapters.en: For you know that it was not with perishable things such as silver or gold that you were redeemed from the empty way of life you inherited from your forefathers,
chapters.zh: 知道你们得赎，脱去你们祖宗所传流虚妄的行为，不是凭着能坏的金银等物，

chapters.en: but with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or spot.
chapters.zh: 乃是凭着基督的宝血，如同无瑕疵、无玷污的羔羊之血。

chapters.en: He was known before the foundation of the world, but was revealed in the last times for your sake.
chapters.zh: 基督在创世以前是预先被〔上帝〕知道的，却在这末世才为你们显现。

chapters.en: Through Him you believe in God, who raised Him from the dead and glorified Him; and so your faith and hope are in God.
chapters.zh: 你们也因着他，信那叫他从死里复活、又给他荣耀的上帝，叫你们的信心和盼望都在于上帝。

chapters.en: Since you have purified your souls by obedience to the truth so that you have a genuine love for your brothers, love one another deeply, from a pure heart.
chapters.zh: 你们既因顺从真理，洁净了自己的心，以致爱弟兄没有虚假，就当从心里〔注：从心里：有古卷是从清洁的心〕彼此切实相爱。

chapters.en: For you have been born again, not of perishable seed, but of imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God.
chapters.zh: 你们蒙了重生，不是由于能坏的种子，乃是由于不能坏的种子，是藉着上帝活泼常存的道。

chapters.en:
For,
“All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field; the grass withers and the flowers fall,
chapters.zh: 因为 凡有血气的，尽都如草； 他的美荣都像草上的花。 草必枯干，花必凋谢；

chapters.en:
but the word of the Lord stands forever.”
And this is the word that was proclaimed to you.
chapters.zh: 惟有主的道是永存的。 所传给你们的福音就是这道。

chapters.en: Rid yourselves, therefore, of all malice, deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and slander.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们既除去一切的恶毒〔注：或译：阴毒〕、诡诈，并假善、嫉妒，和一切毁谤的话，

chapters.en: Like newborn babies, crave pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow up in your salvation,
chapters.zh: 就要爱慕那纯净的灵奶，像才生的婴孩爱慕奶一样，叫你们因此渐长，以致得救。

chapters.en: now that you have tasted that the Lord is good.
chapters.zh: 你们若尝过主恩的滋味，〔就必如此〕。

chapters.en: As you come to Him, the living stone, rejected by men but chosen and precious in God’s sight,
chapters.zh: 主乃活石，固然是被人所弃的，却是被上帝所拣选、所宝贵的。

chapters.en: you also, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house to be a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 你们来到主面前，也就像活石，被建造成为灵宫，作圣洁的祭司，藉着耶稣基督奉献上帝所悦纳的灵祭。

chapters.en:
For it stands in Scripture:
“See, I lay in Zion a stone, a chosen and precious cornerstone; and the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.”
chapters.zh: 因为经上说： 看哪，我把所拣选、 所宝贵的房角石安放在锡安； 信靠他的人必不至于羞愧。

chapters.en:
To you who believe, then, this stone is precious. But to those who do not believe,
“The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,”
chapters.zh: 所以，他在你们信的人就为宝贵，在那不信的人〔有话说〕： 匠人所弃的石头 已作了房角的头块石头。

chapters.en:
and,
“A stone of stumbling and a rock of offense.”
They stumble because they disobey the word—and to this they were appointed.
chapters.zh: 又说：作了绊脚的石头，跌人的磐石。他们既不顺从，就在道理上绊跌〔注：或译：他们绊跌都因不顺从道理〕；他们这样绊跌也是预定的。

chapters.en: But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, to proclaim the virtues of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.
chapters.zh: 惟有你们是被拣选的族类，是有君尊的祭司，是圣洁的国度，是属〔上帝〕的子民，要叫你们宣扬那召你们出黑暗入奇妙光明者的美德。

chapters.en: Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God; once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.
chapters.zh: 你们从前算不得子民， 现在却作了上帝的子民； 从前未曾蒙怜恤， 现在却蒙了怜恤。

chapters.en: Beloved, I urge you, as foreigners and exiles, to abstain from the desires of the flesh, which war against your soul.
chapters.zh: 亲爱的〔弟兄〕啊，你们是客旅，是寄居的。我劝你们要禁戒肉体的私欲；这私欲是与灵魂争战的。

chapters.en: Conduct yourselves with such honor among the Gentiles that, though they slander you as evildoers, they may see your good deeds and glorify God on the day He visits us.
chapters.zh: 你们在外邦人中，应当品行端正，叫那些毁谤你们是作恶的，因看见你们的好行为，便在鉴察〔注：或译：眷顾〕的日子归荣耀给上帝。

chapters.en: Submit yourselves for the Lord’s sake to every human institution, whether to the king as the supreme authority,
chapters.zh: 你们为主的缘故，要顺服人的一切制度，或是在上的君王，

chapters.en: or to governors as those sent by him to punish those who do wrong and to praise those who do right.
chapters.zh: 或是君王所派罚恶赏善的臣宰。

chapters.en: For it is God’s will that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish men.
chapters.zh: 因为上帝的旨意原是要你们行善，可以堵住那糊涂无知人的口。

chapters.en: Live in freedom, but do not use your freedom as a cover-up for evil; live as servants of God.
chapters.zh: 你们虽是自由的，却不可藉着自由遮盖恶毒〔注：或译：阴毒〕，总要作上帝的仆人。

chapters.en: Treat everyone with high regard: Love the brotherhood of believers, fear God, honor the king.
chapters.zh: 务要尊敬众人，亲爱教中的弟兄，敬畏上帝，尊敬君王。

chapters.en: Servants, submit yourselves to your masters with all respect, not only to those who are good and gentle, but even to those who are unreasonable.
chapters.zh: 你们作仆人的，凡事要存敬畏的心顺服主人；不但顺服那善良温和的，就是那乖僻的也要顺服。

chapters.en: For if anyone endures the pain of unjust suffering because he is conscious of God, this is to be commended.
chapters.zh: 倘若人为叫良心对得住上帝，就忍受冤屈的苦楚，这是可喜爱的。

chapters.en: How is it to your credit if you are beaten for doing wrong and you endure it? But if you suffer for doing good and you endure it, this is commendable before God.
chapters.zh: 你们若因犯罪受责打，能忍耐，有什么可夸的呢？但你们若因行善受苦，能忍耐，这在上帝看是可喜爱的。

chapters.en: For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example, that you should follow in His footsteps:
chapters.zh: 你们蒙召原是为此；因基督也为你们受过苦，给你们留下榜样，叫你们跟随他的脚踪行。

chapters.en: “He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in His mouth.”
chapters.zh: 他并没有犯罪，口里也没有诡诈。

chapters.en: When they heaped abuse on Him, He did not retaliate; when He suffered, He made no threats, but entrusted Himself to Him who judges justly.
chapters.zh: 他被骂不还口；受害不说威吓的话，只将自己交讬那按公义审判人的〔主〕。

chapters.en: He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree, so that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. “By His stripes you are healed.”
chapters.zh: 他被挂在木头上，亲身担当了我们的罪，使我们既然在罪上死，就得以在义上活。因他受的鞭伤，你们便得了医治。

chapters.en: For “you were like sheep going astray,” but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
chapters.zh: 你们从前好像迷路的羊，如今却归到你们灵魂的牧人监督了。

chapters.en: Wives, in the same way, submit yourselves to your husbands, so that even if they refuse to believe the word, they will be won over without words by the behavior of their wives
chapters.zh: 你们作妻子的要顺服自己的丈夫；这样，若有不信从道理的丈夫，他们虽然不听道，也可以因妻子的品行被感化过来；

chapters.en: when they see your pure and reverent demeanor.
chapters.zh: 这正是因看见你们有贞洁的品行和敬畏的心。

chapters.en: Your beauty should not come from outward adornment, such as braided hair or gold jewelry or fine clothes,
chapters.zh: 你们不要以外面的辫头发，戴金饰，穿美衣为妆饰，

chapters.en: but from the inner disposition of your heart, the unfading beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is precious in God’s sight.
chapters.zh: 只要以里面存着长久温柔、安静的心为妆饰；这在上帝面前是极宝贵的。

chapters.en: For this is how the holy women of the past adorned themselves. They put their hope in God and were submissive to their husbands,
chapters.zh: 因为古时仰赖上帝的圣洁妇人正是以此为妆饰，顺服自己的丈夫，

chapters.en: just as Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord. And you are her children if you do what is right and refuse to give way to fear.
chapters.zh: 就如撒拉听从亚伯拉罕，称他为主。你们若行善，不因恐吓而害怕，便是撒拉的女儿了。

chapters.en: Husbands, in the same way, treat your wives with consideration as a delicate vessel, and with honor as fellow heirs of the gracious gift of life, so that your prayers will not be hindered.
chapters.zh: 你们作丈夫的也要按情理〔注：原文是知识〕和〔妻子〕同住；因她比你软弱〔注：比你软弱：原文作是软弱的器皿〕，与你一同承受生命之恩的，所以要敬重她。这样，便叫你们的祷告没有阻碍。

chapters.en: Finally, all of you, be like-minded and sympathetic, love as brothers, be tenderhearted and humble.
chapters.zh: 总而言之，你们都要同心，彼此体恤，相爱如弟兄，存慈怜谦卑的心。

chapters.en: Do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult, but with blessing, because to this you were called so that you may inherit a blessing.
chapters.zh: 不以恶报恶，以辱骂还辱骂，倒要祝福；因你们是为此蒙召，好叫你们承受福气。

chapters.en:
For,
“Whoever would love life and see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from deceitful speech.
chapters.zh: 因为〔经上〕说： 人若爱生命， 愿享美福， 须要禁止舌头不出恶言， 嘴唇不说诡诈的话；

chapters.en: He must turn from evil and do good; he must seek peace and pursue it.
chapters.zh: 也要离恶行善， 寻求和睦，一心追赶。

chapters.en: For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and His ears are inclined to their prayer. But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”
chapters.zh: 因为，主的眼看顾义人； 主的耳听他们的祈祷。 惟有行恶的人，主向他们变脸。

chapters.en: Who can harm you if you are zealous for what is good?
chapters.zh: 你们若是热心行善，有谁害你们呢？

chapters.en: But even if you should suffer for what is right, you are blessed. “Do not fear what they fear; do not be shaken.”
chapters.zh: 你们就是为义受苦，也是有福的。不要怕人的威吓〔注：的威吓：或译所怕的〕，也不要惊慌；

chapters.en: But in your hearts sanctify Christ as Lord. Always be prepared to give a defense to everyone who asks you the reason for the hope that is in you. But respond with gentleness and respect,
chapters.zh: 只要心里尊主基督为圣。有人问你们心中盼望的缘由，就要常作准备，以温柔、敬畏的心回答各人；

chapters.en: keeping a clear conscience, so that those who slander you may be put to shame by your good behavior in Christ.
chapters.zh: 存着无亏的良心，叫你们在何事上被毁谤，就在何事上可以叫那诬赖你们在基督里有好品行的人自觉羞愧。

chapters.en: For it is better, if it is God’s will, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil.
chapters.zh: 上帝的旨意若是叫你们因行善受苦，总强如因行恶受苦。

chapters.en: For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit,
chapters.zh: 因基督也曾一次为罪受苦〔注：有古卷：受死〕，就是义的代替不义的，为要引我们到上帝面前。按着肉体说，他被治死；按着灵性说，他复活了。

chapters.en: in whom He also went and preached to the spirits in prison
chapters.zh: 他藉这灵曾去传道给那些在监狱里的灵听，

chapters.en:
who disobeyed long ago when God waited patiently in the days of Noah while the ark was being built.
In the ark a few people, only eight souls, were saved through water.
chapters.zh: 就是那从前在挪亚预备方舟、上帝容忍等待的时候，不信从的人。当时进入方舟，藉着水得救的不多，只有八个人。

chapters.en: And this water symbolizes the baptism that now saves you also—not the removal of dirt from the body, but the pledge of a clear conscience toward God—through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
chapters.zh: 这水所表明的洗礼，现在藉着耶稣基督复活也拯救你们；〔这洗礼〕本不在乎除掉肉体的污秽，只求在上帝面前有无亏的良心。

chapters.en: who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels, authorities, and powers subject to Him.
chapters.zh: 耶稣已经进入天堂，在上帝的右边；众天使和有权柄的，并有能力的，都服从了他。

chapters.en: Therefore, since Christ suffered in His body, arm yourselves with the same resolve, because anyone who has suffered in his body is done with sin.
chapters.zh: 基督既在肉身受苦，你们也当将这样的心志作为兵器，因为在肉身受过苦的，就已经与罪断绝了。

chapters.en: Consequently, he does not live out his remaining time on earth for human passions, but for the will of God.
chapters.zh: 你们存这样的心，从今以后就可以不从人的情欲，只从上帝的旨意在世度余下的光阴。

chapters.en: For you have spent enough time in the past carrying out the same desires as the Gentiles: living in debauchery, lust, drunkenness, orgies, carousing, and detestable idolatry.
chapters.zh: 因为往日随从外邦人的心意行邪淫、恶欲、醉酒、荒宴、群饮，并可恶拜偶像的事，时候已经够了。

chapters.en: Because of this, they consider it strange of you not to plunge with them into the same flood of reckless indiscretion, and they heap abuse on you.
chapters.zh: 他们在这些事上，见你们不与他们同奔那放荡无度的路，就以为怪，毁谤你们。

chapters.en: But they will have to give an account to Him who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
chapters.zh: 他们必在那将要审判活人死人的主面前交帐。

chapters.en: That is why the gospel was preached even to those who are now dead, so that they might be judged as men in the flesh, but live according to God in the spirit.
chapters.zh: 为此，就是死人也曾有福音传给他们，要叫他们的肉体按着人受审判，他们的灵性却靠上帝活着。

chapters.en: The end of all things is near. Therefore be clear-minded and sober, so that you can pray.
chapters.zh: 万物的结局近了。所以，你们要谨慎自守，警醒祷告。

chapters.en: Above all, love one another deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.
chapters.zh: 最要紧的是彼此切实相爱，因为爱能遮掩许多的罪。

chapters.en: Show hospitality to one another without complaining.
chapters.zh: 你们要互相款待，不发怨言。

chapters.en: As good stewards of the manifold grace of God, each of you should use whatever gift he has received to serve one another.
chapters.zh: 各人要照所得的恩赐彼此服事，作上帝百般恩赐的好管家。

chapters.en: If anyone speaks, he should speak as one conveying the words of God. If anyone serves, he should serve with the strength God provides, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.
chapters.zh: 若有讲道的，要按着上帝的圣言讲；若有服事〔人〕的，要按着上帝所赐的力量服事，叫上帝在凡事上因耶稣基督得荣耀。〔原来〕荣耀、权能都是他的，直到永永远远。阿们！

chapters.en: Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery trial that has come upon you, as though something strange were happening to you.
chapters.zh: 亲爱的〔弟兄〕啊，有火炼的试验临到你们，不要以为奇怪（似乎是遭遇非常的事），

chapters.en: But rejoice that you share in the sufferings of Christ, so that you may be overjoyed at the revelation of His glory.
chapters.zh: 倒要欢喜；因为你们是与基督一同受苦，使你们在他荣耀显现的时候，也可以欢喜快乐。

chapters.en: If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you.
chapters.zh: 你们若为基督的名受辱骂，便是有福的；因为上帝荣耀的灵常住在你们身上。

chapters.en: Indeed, none of you should suffer as a murderer or thief or wrongdoer, or even as a meddler.
chapters.zh: 你们中间却不可有人因为杀人、偷窃、作恶、好管闲事而受苦。

chapters.en: But if you suffer as a Christian, do not be ashamed, but glorify God that you bear that name.
chapters.zh: 若为作基督徒受苦，却不要羞耻，倒要因这名归荣耀给上帝。

chapters.en: For it is time for judgment to begin with the family of God; and if it begins with us, what will the outcome be for those who disobey the gospel of God?
chapters.zh: 因为时候到了，审判要从上帝的家起首。若是先从我们起首，那不信从上帝福音的人将有何等的结局呢？

chapters.en:
And,
“If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?”
chapters.zh: 若是义人仅仅得救，那不虔敬和犯罪的人将有何地可站呢？

chapters.en: So then, those who suffer according to God’s will should entrust their souls to their faithful Creator and continue to do good.
chapters.zh: 所以，那照上帝旨意受苦的人要一心为善，将自己灵魂交与那信实的造化之主。

chapters.en: As a fellow elder, a witness of Christ’s sufferings, and a partaker of the glory to be revealed, I appeal to the elders among you:
chapters.zh: 我这作长老、作基督受苦的见证、同享后来所要显现之荣耀的，劝你们中间与我同作长老的人：

chapters.en: Be shepherds of God’s flock that is among you, watching over them not out of compulsion, but willingly, as God would have you; not out of greed, but out of eagerness;
chapters.zh: 务要牧养在你们中间上帝的群羊，按着上帝〔旨意〕照管他们；不是出于勉强，乃是出于甘心；也不是因为贪财，乃是出于乐意；

chapters.en: not lording it over those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock.
chapters.zh: 也不是辖制所托付你们的，乃是作群羊的榜样。

chapters.en: And when the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the crown of glory that will never fade away.
chapters.zh: 到了牧长显现的时候，你们必得那永不衰残的荣耀冠冕。

chapters.en:
Young men, in the same way, submit yourselves to your elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because,
“God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
chapters.zh: 你们年幼的，也要顺服年长的。就是你们众人也都要以谦卑束腰，彼此顺服；因为 上帝阻挡骄傲的人， 赐恩给谦卑的人。

chapters.en: Humble yourselves, therefore, under God’s mighty hand, so that in due time He may exalt you.
chapters.zh: 所以，你们要自卑，服在上帝大能的手下，到了时候，他必叫你们升高。

chapters.en: Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.
chapters.zh: 你们要将一切的忧虑卸给上帝，因为他顾念你们。

chapters.en: Be sober-minded and alert. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.
chapters.zh: 务要谨守，警醒。〔因为〕你们的仇敌魔鬼，如同吼叫的狮子，遍地游行，寻找可吞吃的人。

chapters.en: Resist him, standing firm in your faith and in the knowledge that your brothers throughout the world are undergoing the same kinds of suffering.
chapters.zh: 你们要用坚固的信心抵挡他，因为知道你们在世上的众弟兄也是经历这样的苦难。

chapters.en: And after you have suffered for a little while, the God of all grace, who has called you to His eternal glory in Christ, will Himself restore you, secure you, strengthen you, and establish you.
chapters.zh: 那赐诸般恩典的上帝曾在基督里召你们，得享他永远的荣耀，等你们暂受苦难之后，必要亲自成全你们，坚固你们，赐力量给你们。

chapters.en: To Him be the power forever and ever. Amen.
chapters.zh: 愿权能归给他，直到永永远远。阿们！

chapters.en: Through Silvanus, whom I regard as a faithful brother, I have written to you briefly, encouraging you and testifying that this is the true grace of God. Stand firm in it.
chapters.zh: 我略略地写了这信，讬我所看为忠心的兄弟西拉转交你们，劝勉你们，又证明这恩是上帝的真恩。你们务要在这恩上站立得住。

chapters.en: The church in Babylon, chosen together with you, sends you greetings, as does my son Mark.
chapters.zh: 在巴比伦与你们同蒙拣选的教会问你们安。我儿子马可也问你们安。

chapters.en:
Greet one another with a kiss of love.
Peace to all of you who are in Christ.
chapters.zh: 你们要用爱心彼此亲嘴问安。愿平安归与你们凡在基督里的人！

chapters.en:
Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ,
To those who through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ have received a faith as precious as ours:
chapters.zh: 作耶稣基督仆人和使徒的西门‧彼得写信给那因我们的上帝和〔注：有古卷没有和字〕救主耶稣基督之义、与我们同得一样宝贵信心的人。

chapters.en: Grace and peace be multiplied to you through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
chapters.zh: 愿恩惠、平安，因你们认识上帝和我们主耶稣，多多地加给你们。

chapters.en: His divine power has given us everything we need for life and godliness through the knowledge of Him who called us by His own glory and excellence.
chapters.zh: 上帝的神能已将一切关乎生命和虔敬的事赐给我们，皆因我们认识那用自己荣耀和美德召我们的主。

chapters.en: Through these He has given us His precious and magnificent promises, so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature, now that you have escaped the corruption in the world caused by evil desires.
chapters.zh: 因此，他已将又宝贵又极大的应许赐给我们，叫我们既脱离世上从情欲来的败坏，就得与上帝的性情有分。

chapters.en: For this very reason, make every effort to add to your faith virtue; and to virtue, knowledge;
chapters.zh: 正因这缘故，你们要分外地殷勤；有了信心，又要加上德行；有了德行，又要加上知识；

chapters.en: and to knowledge, self-control; and to self-control, perseverance; and to perseverance, godliness;
chapters.zh: 有了知识，又要加上节制；有了节制，又要加上忍耐；有了忍耐，又要加上虔敬；

chapters.en: and to godliness, brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness, love.
chapters.zh: 有了虔敬，又要加上爱弟兄的心；有了爱弟兄的心，又要加上爱〔众人的心〕。

chapters.en: For if you possess these qualities and continue to grow in them, they will keep you from being ineffective and unproductive in your knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 你们若充充足足地有这几样，就必使你们在认识我们的主耶稣基督上不至于闲懒不结果子了。

chapters.en: But whoever lacks these traits is nearsighted to the point of blindness, having forgotten that he has been cleansed from his past sins.
chapters.zh: 人若没有这几样，就是眼瞎，只看见近处的，忘了他旧日的罪已经得了洁净。

chapters.en: Therefore, brothers, strive to make your calling and election sure. For if you practice these things you will never stumble,
chapters.zh: 所以弟兄们，应当更加殷勤，使你们所蒙的恩召和拣选坚定不移。你们若行这几样，就永不失脚；

chapters.en: and you will receive a lavish reception into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 这样，必叫你们丰丰富富地得以进入我们主－救主耶稣基督永远的国。

chapters.en: Therefore I will always remind you of these things, even though you know them and are established in the truth you now have.
chapters.zh: 你们虽然晓得这些事，并且在你们已有的真道上坚固，我却要将这些事常常提醒你们。

chapters.en: I think it is right to refresh your memory as long as I live in the tent of my body,
chapters.zh: 我以为应当趁我还在这帐棚的时候提醒你们，激发你们；

chapters.en: because I know that this tent will soon be laid aside, as our Lord Jesus Christ has made clear to me.
chapters.zh: 因为知道我脱离这帐棚的时候快到了，正如我们主耶稣基督所指示我的。

chapters.en: And I will make every effort to ensure that after my departure, you will be able to recall these things at all times.
chapters.zh: 并且，我要尽心竭力，使你们在我去世以后时常记念这些事。

chapters.en: For we did not follow cleverly devised fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of His majesty.
chapters.zh: 我们从前将我们主耶稣基督的大能和他降临的事告诉你们，并不是随从乖巧捏造的虚言，乃是亲眼见过他的威荣。

chapters.en: For He received honor and glory from God the Father when the voice came to Him from the Majestic Glory, saying, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”
chapters.zh: 他从父上帝得尊贵荣耀的时候，从极大荣光之中有声音出来，向他说：「这是我的爱子，我所喜悦的。」

chapters.en: And we ourselves heard this voice from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain.
chapters.zh: 我们同他在圣山的时候，亲自听见这声音从天上出来。

chapters.en: We also have the word of the prophets as confirmed beyond doubt. And you will do well to pay attention to it, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.
chapters.zh: 我们并有先知更确的预言，如同灯照在暗处。你们在这预言上留意，直等到天发亮，晨星在你们心里出现的时候，才是好的。

chapters.en: Above all, you must understand that no prophecy of Scripture comes from one’s own interpretation.
chapters.zh: 第一要紧的，该知道经上所有的预言没有可随私意解说的；

chapters.en: For no such prophecy was ever brought forth by the will of man, but men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit.
chapters.zh: 因为预言从来没有出于人意的，乃是人被圣灵感动，说出上帝的话来。

chapters.en: Now there were also false prophets among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you. They will secretly introduce destructive heresies, even denying the Master who bought them—bringing swift destruction on themselves.
chapters.zh: 从前在百姓中有假先知起来，将来在你们中间也必有假师傅，私自引进陷害人的异端，连买他们的主他们也不承认，自取速速地灭亡。

chapters.en: Many will follow in their depravity, and because of them the way of truth will be defamed.
chapters.zh: 将有许多人随从他们邪淫的行为，便叫真道因他们的缘故被毁谤。

chapters.en: In their greed, these false teachers will exploit you with deceptive words. The longstanding verdict against them remains in force, and their destruction does not sleep.
chapters.zh: 他们因有贪心，要用捏造的言语在你们身上取利。他们的刑罚，自古以来并不迟延；他们的灭亡也必速速来到〔注：原文是也不打盹〕。

chapters.en: For if God did not spare the angels when they sinned, but cast them deep into hell, placing them in chains of darkness to be held for judgment;
chapters.zh: 就是天使犯了罪，上帝也没有宽容，曾把他们丢在地狱，交在黑暗坑中，等候审判。

chapters.en: if He did not spare the ancient world when He brought the flood on its ungodly people, but preserved Noah, a preacher of righteousness, among the eight;
chapters.zh: 上帝也没有宽容上古的世代，曾叫洪水临到那不敬虔的世代，却保护了传义道的挪亚一家八口。

chapters.en: if He condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to destruction, reducing them to ashes as an example of what is coming on the ungodly;
chapters.zh: 又判定所多玛、蛾摩拉，将二城倾覆，焚烧成灰，作为后世不敬虔人的鉴戒；

chapters.en: and if He rescued Lot, a righteous man distressed by the depraved conduct of the lawless
chapters.zh: 只搭救了那常为恶人淫行忧伤的义人罗得。

chapters.en: (for that righteous man, living among them day after day, was tormented in his righteous soul by the lawless deeds he saw and heard)—
chapters.zh: （因为那义人住在他们中间，看见听见他们不法的事，他的义心就天天伤痛。）

chapters.en: if all this is so, then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trials and to hold the unrighteous for punishment on the day of judgment.
chapters.zh: 主知道搭救敬虔的人脱离试探，把不义的人留在刑罚之下，等候审判的日子。

chapters.en: Such punishment is specially reserved for those who indulge the corrupt desires of the flesh and despise authority. Bold and self-willed, they are unafraid to slander glorious beings.
chapters.zh: 那些随肉身、纵污秽的情欲、轻慢主治之人的，更是如此。 他们胆大任性，毁谤在尊位的，也不知惧怕。

chapters.en: Yet not even angels, though greater in strength and power, dare to bring such slanderous charges against them before the Lord.
chapters.zh: 就是天使，虽然力量权能更大，还不用毁谤的话在主面前告他们。

chapters.en: These men are like irrational animals, creatures of instinct, born to be captured and destroyed. They blaspheme in matters they do not understand, and like such creatures, they too will be destroyed.
chapters.zh: 但这些人好像没有灵性，生来就是畜类，以备捉拿宰杀的。他们毁谤所不晓得的事，正在败坏人的时候，自己必遭遇败坏。

chapters.en:
The harm they will suffer is the wages of their wickedness.
They consider it a pleasure to carouse in broad daylight. They are blots and blemishes, reveling in their deception as they feast with you.
chapters.zh: 行的不义，就得了不义的工价。这些人喜爱白昼宴乐，他们已被玷污，又有瑕疵，正与你们一同坐席，就以自己的诡诈为快乐。

chapters.en: Their eyes are full of adultery; their desire for sin is never satisfied; they seduce the unstable. They are accursed children with hearts trained in greed.
chapters.zh: 他们满眼是淫色〔注：原文是淫妇〕，止不住犯罪，引诱那心不坚固的人，心中习惯了贪婪，正是被咒诅的种类。

chapters.en: They have left the straight way and wandered off to follow the way of Balaam son of Beor, who loved the wages of wickedness.
chapters.zh: 他们离弃正路，就走差了，随从比珥之子巴兰的路。巴兰就是那贪爱不义之工价的〔先知〕，

chapters.en: But he was rebuked for his transgression by a donkey, otherwise without speech, that spoke with a man’s voice and restrained the prophet’s madness.
chapters.zh: 他却为自己的过犯受了责备；那不能说话的驴以人言拦阻先知的狂妄。

chapters.en: These men are springs without water and mists driven by a storm. Blackest darkness is reserved for them.
chapters.zh: 这些人是无水的井，是狂风催逼的雾气，有墨黑的幽暗为他们存留。

chapters.en: With lofty but empty words, they appeal to the sensual passions of the flesh and entice those who are just escaping from others who live in error.
chapters.zh: 他们说虚妄矜夸的大话，用肉身的情欲和邪淫的事引诱那些刚才脱离妄行的人。

chapters.en: They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves to depravity. For a man is a slave to whatever has mastered him.
chapters.zh: 他们应许人得以自由，自己却作败坏的奴仆，因为人被谁制伏就是谁的奴仆。

chapters.en: If indeed they have escaped the corruption of the world through the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, only to be entangled and overcome by it again, their final condition is worse than it was at first.
chapters.zh: 倘若他们因认识主－救主耶稣基督，得以脱离世上的污秽，后来又在其中被缠住、制伏，他们末后的景况就比先前更不好了。

chapters.en: It would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than to have known it and then to turn away from the holy commandment passed on to them.
chapters.zh: 他们晓得义路，竟背弃了传给他们的圣命，倒不如不晓得为妙。

chapters.en: Of them the proverbs are true: “A dog returns to its vomit,” and, “A sow that is washed goes back to her wallowing in the mud.”
chapters.zh: 俗语说得真不错： 狗所吐的，牠转过来又吃； 猪洗净了又回到泥里去滚； 这话在他们身上正合式。

chapters.en: Beloved, this is now my second letter to you. Both of them are reminders to stir you to wholesome thinking
chapters.zh: 亲爱的〔弟兄〕啊，我现在写给你们的是第二封信。这两封都是提醒你们，激发你们诚实的心，

chapters.en: by recalling what was foretold by the holy prophets and commanded by our Lord and Savior through your apostles.
chapters.zh: 叫你们记念圣先知预先所说的话和主救主的命令，就是使徒所传给你们的。

chapters.en: Most importantly, you must understand that in the last days scoffers will come, scoffing and following their own evil desires.
chapters.zh: 第一要紧的，该知道在末世必有好讥诮的人随从自己的私欲出来讥诮说：

chapters.en: “Where is the promise of His coming?” they will ask. “Ever since our fathers fell asleep, everything continues as it has from the beginning of creation.”
chapters.zh: 「主要降临的应许在哪里呢？因为从列祖睡了以来，万物与起初创造的时候仍是一样。」

chapters.en: But they deliberately overlook the fact that long ago by God’s word the heavens existed and the earth was formed out of water and by water,
chapters.zh: 他们故意忘记，从太古，凭上帝的命有了天，并从水而出、藉水而成的地。

chapters.en: through which the world of that time perished in the flood.
chapters.zh: 故此，当时的世界被水淹没就消灭了。

chapters.en: And by that same word, the present heavens and earth are reserved for fire, being kept for the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly men.
chapters.zh: 但现在的天地还是凭着那命存留，直留到不敬虔之人受审判遭沉沦的日子，用火焚烧。

chapters.en: Beloved, do not let this one thing escape your notice: With the Lord a day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a day.
chapters.zh: 亲爱的〔弟兄〕啊，有一件事你们不可忘记，就是主看一日如千年，千年如一日。

chapters.en: The Lord is not slow in keeping His promise as some understand slowness, but is patient with you, not wanting anyone to perish but everyone to come to repentance.
chapters.zh: 主所应许的〔尚未成就〕，有人以为他是耽延，其实不是耽延，乃是宽容你们，不愿有一人沉沦，乃愿人人都悔改。

chapters.en: But the Day of the Lord will come like a thief. The heavens will disappear with a roar, the elements will be destroyed by fire, and the earth and its works will be laid bare.
chapters.zh: 但主的日子要像贼来到一样。那日，天必大有响声废去，有形质的都要被烈火销化，地和其上的物都要烧尽了。

chapters.en: Since everything will be destroyed in this way, what kind of people ought you to be? You ought to conduct yourselves in holiness and godliness
chapters.zh: 这一切既然都要如此销化，你们为人该当怎样圣洁，怎样敬虔，

chapters.en: as you anticipate and hasten the coming of the day of God, when the heavens will be destroyed by fire and the elements will melt in the heat.
chapters.zh: 切切仰望上帝的日子来到。在那日，天被火烧就销化了，有形质的都要被烈火镕化。

chapters.en: But in keeping with God’s promise, we are looking forward to a new heaven and a new earth, where righteousness dwells.
chapters.zh: 但我们照他的应许，盼望新天新地，有义居在其中。

chapters.en: Therefore, beloved, as you anticipate these things, make every effort to be found at peace—spotless and blameless in His sight.
chapters.zh: 亲爱的〔弟兄〕啊，你们既盼望这些事，就当殷勤，使自己没有玷污，无可指摘，安然见主；

chapters.en: Consider also that our Lord’s patience brings salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote you with the wisdom God gave him.
chapters.zh: 并且要以我主长久忍耐为得救的因由，就如我们所亲爱的兄弟保罗，照着所赐给他的智慧写了信给你们。

chapters.en: He writes this way in all his letters, speaking in them about such matters. Some parts of his letters are hard to understand, which ignorant and unstable people distort, as they do the rest of the Scriptures, to their own destruction.
chapters.zh: 他一切的信上也都是讲论这事。信中有些难明白的，那无学问、不坚固的人强解，如强解别的经书一样，就自取沉沦。

chapters.en: Therefore, beloved, since you already know these things, be on your guard so that you will not be carried away by the error of the lawless and fall from your secure standing.
chapters.zh: 亲爱的〔弟兄〕啊，你们既然预先知道这事，就当防备，恐怕被恶人的错谬诱惑，就从自己坚固的地步上坠落。

chapters.en:
But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be the glory both now and to the day of eternity.
Amen.
chapters.zh: 你们却要在我们主－救主耶稣基督的恩典和知识上有长进。愿荣耀归给他，从今直到永远。阿们！

chapters.en: That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our own eyes, which we have gazed upon and touched with our own hands—this is the Word of life.
chapters.zh: 论到从起初原有的生命之道，就是我们所听见、所看见、亲眼看过、亲手摸过的。

chapters.en: And this is the life that was revealed; we have seen it and testified to it, and we proclaim to you the eternal life that was with the Father and was revealed to us.
chapters.zh: （这生命已经显现出来，我们也看见过，现在又作见证，将原与父同在、且显现与我们那永远的生命传给你们。）

chapters.en: We proclaim to you what we have seen and heard, so that you also may have fellowship with us. And this fellowship of ours is with the Father and with His Son, Jesus Christ.
chapters.zh: 我们将所看见、所听见的传给你们，使你们与我们相交。我们乃是与父并他儿子耶稣基督相交的。

chapters.en: We write these things so that our joy may be complete.
chapters.zh: 我们将这些话写给你们，使你们〔注：有古卷：我们〕的喜乐充足。

chapters.en: And this is the message we have heard from Him and announce to you: God is light, and in Him there is no darkness at all.
chapters.zh: 上帝就是光，在他毫无黑暗。这是我们从主所听见、又报给你们的信息。

chapters.en: If we say we have fellowship with Him yet walk in the darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth.
chapters.zh: 我们若说是与上帝相交，却仍在黑暗里行，就是说谎话，不行真理了。

chapters.en: But if we walk in the light as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin.
chapters.zh: 我们若在光明中行，如同上帝在光明中，就彼此相交，他儿子耶稣的血也洗净我们一切的罪。

chapters.en: If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
chapters.zh: 我们若说自己无罪，便是自欺，真理不在我们心里了。

chapters.en: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
chapters.zh: 我们若认自己的罪，上帝是信实的，是公义的，必要赦免我们的罪，洗净我们一切的不义。

chapters.en: If we say we have not sinned, we make Him out to be a liar, and His word is not in us.
chapters.zh: 我们若说自己没有犯过罪，便是以上帝为说谎的，他的道也不在我们心里了。

chapters.en: My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you will not sin. But if anyone does sin, we have an advocate before the Father—Jesus Christ, the Righteous One.
chapters.zh: 我小子们哪，我将这些话写给你们，是要叫你们不犯罪。若有人犯罪，在父那里我们有一位中保，就是那义者耶稣基督。

chapters.en: He Himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the sins of the whole world.
chapters.zh: 他为我们的罪作了挽回祭，不是单为我们的罪，也是为普天下人的罪。

chapters.en: By this we can be sure that we have come to know Him: if we keep His commandments.
chapters.zh: 我们若遵守他的诫命，就晓得是认识他。

chapters.en: If anyone says, “I know Him,” but does not keep His commandments, he is a liar, and the truth is not in him.
chapters.zh: 人若说「我认识他」，却不遵守他的诫命，便是说谎话的，真理也不在他心里了。

chapters.en: But if anyone keeps His word, the love of God has been truly perfected in him. By this we know that we are in Him:
chapters.zh: 凡遵守主道的，爱上帝的心在他里面实在是完全的。从此，我们知道我们是在主里面。

chapters.en: Whoever claims to abide in Him must walk as Jesus walked.
chapters.zh: 人若说他住在主里面，就该自己照主所行的去行。

chapters.en: Beloved, I am not writing to you a new commandment, but an old one, which you have had from the beginning. This commandment is the message you have heard.
chapters.zh: 亲爱的〔弟兄〕啊，我写给你们的，不是一条新命令，乃是你们从起初所受的旧命令；这旧命令就是你们所听见的道。

chapters.en: Then again, I am also writing to you a new commandment, which is true in Him and also in you. For the darkness is fading and the true light is already shining.
chapters.zh: 再者，我写给你们的，是一条新命令，在主是真的，在你们也是真的；因为黑暗渐渐过去，真光已经照耀。

chapters.en: If anyone claims to be in the light but hates his brother, he is still in the darkness.
chapters.zh: 人若说自己在光明中，却恨他的弟兄，他到如今还是在黑暗里。

chapters.en: Whoever loves his brother remains in the light, and there is no cause of stumbling in him.
chapters.zh: 爱弟兄的，就是住在光明中，在他并没有绊跌的缘由。

chapters.en: But whoever hates his brother is in the darkness and walks in the darkness. He does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.
chapters.zh: 惟独恨弟兄的，是在黑暗里，且在黑暗里行，也不知道往哪里去，因为黑暗叫他眼睛瞎了。

chapters.en: I am writing to you, little children, because your sins have been forgiven through His name.
chapters.zh: 小子们哪，我写信给你们， 因为你们的罪藉着主名得了赦免。

chapters.en:
I am writing to you, fathers, because you know Him who is from the beginning.
I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one.
I have written to you, children, because you know the Father.
chapters.zh: 父老啊，我写信给你们， 因为你们认识那从起初原有的。 少年人哪，我写信给你们， 因为你们胜了那恶者。

chapters.en:
I have written to you, fathers, because you know Him who is from the beginning.
I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, and you have overcome the evil one.
chapters.zh: 小子们哪，我曾写信给你们， 因为你们认识父。 父老啊，我曾写信给你们， 因为你们认识那从起初原有的。 少年人哪，我曾写信给你们； 因为你们刚强， 上帝的道常存在你们心里； 你们也胜了那恶者。

chapters.en: Do not love the world or anything in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
chapters.zh: 不要爱世界和世界上的事。人若爱世界，爱父的心就不在他里面了。

chapters.en: For all that is in the world—the desires of the flesh, the desires of the eyes, and the pride of life—is not from the Father but from the world.
chapters.zh: 因为，凡世界上的事，就像肉体的情欲、眼目的情欲，并今生的骄傲，都不是从父来的，乃是从世界来的。

chapters.en: The world is passing away, along with its desires; but whoever does the will of God remains forever.
chapters.zh: 这世界和其上的情欲都要过去，惟独遵行上帝旨意的，是永远常存。

chapters.en: Children, it is the last hour; and just as you have heard that the antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have appeared. This is how we know it is the last hour.
chapters.zh: 小子们哪，如今是末时了。你们曾听见说，那敌基督的要来；现在已经有好些敌基督的出来了，从此我们就知道如今是末时了。

chapters.en: They went out from us, but they did not belong to us. For if they had belonged to us, they would have remained with us. But their departure made it clear that none of them belonged to us.
chapters.zh: 他们从我们中间出去，却不是属我们的；若是属我们的，就必仍旧与我们同在；〔他们出去〕，显明都不是属我们的。

chapters.en: You, however, have an anointing from the Holy One, and all of you know the truth.
chapters.zh: 你们从那圣者受了〔恩〕膏，并且知道这一切的事〔注：或译：都有知识〕。

chapters.en: I have not written to you because you lack knowledge of the truth, but because you have it, and because no lie comes from the truth.
chapters.zh: 我写信给你们，不是因你们不知道真理，正是因你们知道，并且知道没有虚谎是从真理出来的。

chapters.en: Who is the liar, if it is not the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son.
chapters.zh: 谁是说谎话的呢？不是那不认耶稣为基督的吗？不认父与子的，这就是敌基督的。

chapters.en: Whoever denies the Son does not have the Father, but whoever confesses the Son has the Father as well.
chapters.zh: 凡不认子的，就没有父；认子的，连父也有了。

chapters.en: As for you, let what you have heard from the beginning remain in you. If it does, you will also remain in the Son and in the Father.
chapters.zh: 论到你们，务要将那从起初所听见的，常存在心里。若将从起初所听见的存在心里，你们就必住在子里面，也必住在父里面。

chapters.en: And this is the promise that He Himself made to us: eternal life.
chapters.zh: 主所应许我们的就是永生。

chapters.en: I have written these things to you about those who are trying to deceive you.
chapters.zh: 我将这些话写给你们，是指着那引诱你们的人说的。

chapters.en: And as for you, the anointing you received from Him remains in you, and you do not need anyone to teach you. But just as His true and genuine anointing teaches you about all things, so remain in Him as you have been taught.
chapters.zh: 你们从主所受的〔恩〕膏常存在你们心里，并不用人教训你们，自有主的〔恩〕膏在凡事上教训你们。这〔恩〕膏是真的，不是假的；你们要按这〔恩〕膏的教训住在主里面。

chapters.en: And now, little children, remain in Christ, so that when He appears, we may be confident and unashamed before Him at His coming.
chapters.zh: 小子们哪，你们要住在主里面。这样，他若显现，我们就可以坦然无惧；当他来的时候，在他面前也不至于惭愧。

chapters.en: If you know that He is righteous, you also know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of Him.
chapters.zh: 你们若知道他是公义的，就知道凡行公义之人都是他所生的。

chapters.en: Behold what manner of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God. And that is what we are! The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know Him.
chapters.zh: 你看父赐给我们是何等的慈爱，使我们得称为上帝的儿女；我们也真是他的儿女。世人所以不认识我们，是因未曾认识他。

chapters.en: Beloved, we are now children of God, and what we will be has not yet been revealed. We know that when Christ appears, we will be like Him, for we will see Him as He is.
chapters.zh: 亲爱的〔弟兄〕啊，我们现在是上帝的儿女，将来如何，还未显明；但我们知道，主若显现，我们必要像他，因为必得见他的真体。

chapters.en: And everyone who has this hope in Him purifies himself, just as Christ is pure.
chapters.zh: 凡向他有这指望的，就洁净自己，像他洁净一样。

chapters.en: Everyone who practices sin practices lawlessness as well. Indeed, sin is lawlessness.
chapters.zh: 凡犯罪的，就是违背律法；违背律法就是罪。

chapters.en: But you know that Christ appeared to take away sins, and in Him there is no sin.
chapters.zh: 你们知道主曾显现，是要除掉人的罪，在他并没有罪。

chapters.en: No one who remains in Him keeps on sinning. No one who continues to sin has seen Him or known Him.
chapters.zh: 凡住在他里面的，就不犯罪；凡犯罪的，是未曾看见他，也未曾认识他。

chapters.en: Little children, let no one deceive you: The one who practices righteousness is righteous, just as Christ is righteous.
chapters.zh: 小子们哪，不要被人诱惑。行义的才是义人，正如主是义的一样。

chapters.en: The one who practices sin is of the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the very start. This is why the Son of God was revealed, to destroy the works of the devil.
chapters.zh: 犯罪的是属魔鬼，因为魔鬼从起初就犯罪。上帝的儿子显现出来，为要除灭魔鬼的作为。

chapters.en: Anyone born of God refuses to practice sin, because God’s seed abides in him; he cannot go on sinning, because he has been born of God.
chapters.zh: 凡从上帝生的，就不犯罪，因上帝的道〔注：原文是种〕存在他心里；他也不能犯罪，因为他是由上帝生的。

chapters.en: By this the children of God are distinguished from the children of the devil: Anyone who does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is anyone who does not love his brother.
chapters.zh: 从此就显出谁是上帝的儿女，谁是魔鬼的儿女。凡不行义的就不属上帝，不爱弟兄的也是如此。

chapters.en: This is the message you have heard from the beginning: We should love one another.
chapters.zh: 我们应当彼此相爱。这就是你们从起初所听见的命令。

chapters.en: Do not be like Cain, who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother. And why did Cain slay him? Because his own deeds were evil, while those of his brother were righteous.
chapters.zh: 不可像该隐；他是属那恶者，杀了他的兄弟。为什么杀了他呢？因自己的行为是恶的，兄弟的行为是善的。

chapters.en: So do not be surprised, brothers, if the world hates you.
chapters.zh: 弟兄们，世人若恨你们，不要以为希奇。

chapters.en: We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love our brothers. The one who does not love remains in death.
chapters.zh: 我们因为爱弟兄，就晓得是已经出死入生了。没有爱心的，仍住在死中。

chapters.en: Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that eternal life does not reside in a murderer.
chapters.zh: 凡恨他弟兄的，就是杀人的；你们晓得凡杀人的，没有永生存在他里面。

chapters.en: By this we know what love is: Jesus laid down His life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers.
chapters.zh: 主为我们舍命，我们从此就知道何为爱；我们也当为弟兄舍命。

chapters.en: If anyone with earthly possessions sees his brother in need, but withholds his compassion from him, how can the love of God abide in him?
chapters.zh: 凡有世上财物的，看见弟兄穷乏，却塞住怜恤的心，爱上帝的心怎能存在他里面呢？

chapters.en: Little children, let us love not in word and speech, but in action and truth.
chapters.zh: 小子们哪，我们相爱，不要只在言语和舌头上，总要在行为和诚实上。

chapters.en: And by this we will know that we belong to the truth, and will assure our hearts in His presence:
chapters.zh: 从此就知道我们是属真理的，并且我们的心在上帝面前可以安稳。

chapters.en: Even if our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts, and He knows all things.
chapters.zh: 我们的心若责备我们，上帝比我们的心大，一切事没有不知道的。

chapters.en: Beloved, if our hearts do not condemn us, we have confidence before God,
chapters.zh: 亲爱的〔弟兄〕啊，我们的心若不责备我们，就可以向上帝坦然无惧了。

chapters.en: and we will receive from Him whatever we ask, because we keep His commandments and do what is pleasing in His sight.
chapters.zh: 并且我们一切所求的，就从他得着；因为我们遵守他的命令，行他所喜悦的事。

chapters.en: And this is His commandment: that we should believe in the name of His Son, Jesus Christ, and we should love one another just as He commanded us.
chapters.zh: 上帝的命令就是叫我们信他儿子耶稣基督的名，且照他所赐给我们的命令彼此相爱。

chapters.en: Whoever keeps His commandments remains in God, and God in him. And by this we know that He remains in us: by the Spirit He has given us.
chapters.zh: 遵守上帝命令的，就住在上帝里面，上帝也住在他里面。我们所以知道上帝住在我们里面是因他所赐给我们的〔圣〕灵。

chapters.en: Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God. For many false prophets have gone out into the world.
chapters.zh: 亲爱的〔弟兄〕啊，一切的灵，你们不可都信，总要试验那些灵是出于上帝的不是，因为世上有许多假先知已经出来了。

chapters.en: By this you will know the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God,
chapters.zh: 凡灵认耶稣基督是成了肉身来的，就是出于上帝的；从此你们可以认出上帝的灵来。

chapters.en: and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you have heard is coming and which is already in the world at this time.
chapters.zh: 凡灵不认耶稣，就不是出于上帝，这是那敌基督者的灵。你们从前听见他要来，现在已经在世上了。

chapters.en: You, little children, are from God and have overcome them, because greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world.
chapters.zh: 小子们哪，你们是属上帝的，并且胜了他们；因为那在你们里面的，比那在世界上的更大。

chapters.en: They are of the world. That is why they speak from the world’s perspective, and the world listens to them.
chapters.zh: 他们是属世界的，所以论世界的事，世人也听从他们。
